incident_description:
On August 26, 2025, I arrived at my office and heard a constant beeping from our Kidde carbon monoxide and smoke alarm, model number P40110DCSC0. There was no fire, and the smoke alarm was stored in its original box without being used.  The smoke alarm was stored in an air-conditioned office building. I contacted the manufacturer to report this issue. The smoke alarm was manufactured in July 2019. 

The manufacturer informed me that they would not replace the failed smoke alarm because it had not been activated within a year of its manufacture. They also stated that the battery would drain faster when the alarm is in the standby (off) position if not used. According to them, the battery would last longer if the alarm were used, which does not make sense given that these smoke alarms are designed to be interconnected wirelessly to multiple smoke alarms and cannot be recharged. 

This is a significant issue for consumers' safety and a false sense of security, as the battery does not last 10 years, even when in standby mode. The manufacturer offered no replacement or support and placed the blame on the consumer for not turning it on.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning smoke alarm without any actual fire or injury, but it raises safety concerns.

Subject: Formal Complaint Regarding Whirlpool Washer Model WTW4855HW3  Serial CC1501839

To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally express my strong dissatisfaction with the Whirlpool top-load washer, model WTW4855HW3, serial number CC1501839, which I acquired  in September 2023 as part of a new home purchase through a new home builder. The. appliance was included as a promotion with the purchase of a house and presented as a reliable, brand-new unit intended to meet the needs of a modern household.

Unfortunately, less than two years after installation, the washer has completely failed. The issues are as follows:

1. The unit becomes stuck in the drain/spin cycle immediately upon being plugged into an outlet.
2. None of the wash cycles can be startedbuttons are unresponsive.
3. Once powered, no wash cycle can be stopped or reset.
4. The lid no longer locks while in use.
5. The machine is constantly running when plugged (which could cause the outlet to overheat).

These failures render the washer unusable and suggest a serious defect in either the control board or pressure sensor system. I have since learned that Whirlpool issued Technical Service Pointer W11766193 in March 2025 for models with serial numbers beginning in CC, which includes mine. The bulletin reportedly addresses pressure sensor and drain pump issues consistent with my experience.

I believe it is deceptive and unfair to sell or distribute a product with such a short lifespan, especially when consumers reasonably expect major appliances to last 812 years. This situation has caused me significant inconvenience and undermined my trust in Whirlpool products.

I am requesting the following:
- A full replacement of the defective unit or reimbursement for a comparable washer
- A formal acknowledgment of the issue and confirmation of whether my unit qualifies under the service bulletin
After calling Whirlpool, they do not want to help resolve the matter.  They only want to sell me more products at added costs.  This is the reason for filing the report. The washing machine was being used by the family of four, including adults, and children over the age of ten with adult supervision.  The product was being used in a normal manner, washing loads that were typically less than 2.9 cu ft anywhere from once a week to three times/ week. Injuries that could have happened include fire hazards.
Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.

Sincerely,  
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
I own a GE Monogram 48 inch kitchen range vent hood and noticed that the grease baffle filters provided with the hood do not cover the entire air intake opening of the hood. I contacted GE regarding my vent hood, model ZV48SSF1SS, in which is found three 12.75 inch x 15 inch x 1 inch (25mm) [REDACTED] baffle grease filters, rated for fire prevention, and which according to the parts diagram of the hood should have only have three filters. The parts diagram states that the filters are GE part #WB02X10877. GE confirmed that the part number is correct, but upon pressing them for the dimensions they stated 13.5 inch x 16.5 inch x 2.25 inch which is clearly not the size of the filters I have. I then looked up the part number at repairclinic.com where a nice image of the filter laid on a grid confirms that the filter is 12.75 inches x 15 inches. I also confirmed that an internal ledge within the vent hood will not allow a filter greater than 30mm in thickness. So GE does not know what filter fits my vent hood and GE was not aware that three filters with a width of 12.75 inch each can only cover 38.25 inches of the vent hood opening leaving 7 inches of the 45.25 inch wide opening uncovered by a grease filter. This leads me to believe that when GE contracted with [REDACTED] for 48 vent hood filters they either transmitted an erroneous specification or thought they could get away using a filter for a narrower hood in the 48 hood. 

As you know know grease baffle filters must cover the entire opening of a vent hood to keep grease out of the vent exhaust duct that passes through an attic before exiting a roof. When the filters do not cover the entire opening, there are manufacturers who may provide spacers to fill in the gaps. Notably GE does not provide spacers. Because the filters serve to prevent a fire from passing up the duct, a gap may allow fire to travel into a duct and ignite grease in the duct which of course will burn down a home. 

This was a major design error on the part of GE. [REDACTED] provided what GE requested. Had GE provided three 15 inches x 15 inches  x 1 inch filters, homes could have been spared from burning down. A GE rep told me that there were no recalls on the vent hood; however, the lack of recalls provides no certainty that fires did not occur and that lives have not been lost because the causes of a major fire are often difficult to determine given the destruction of responsible factors. With respect to fires and there causes, I speak from experience as a former US Navy engineering officer responsible for fire prevention and fire fighting aboard a guided missile destroyer.

Of course having uncovered these facts, I will have to take 3 measures. Firstly, I will be engaging a consumer products tort lawyer for his opinion on the viability of a civil lawsuit. Secondly, I will be engaging the US Consumer Products Safety Commission (you guys whom I hope will take my concerns seriously) which has regulatory tools to uncover what injuries may have occurred and force GE to provide remediation. Thirdly, I will be engaging my own insurance company, [REDACTED], which is very interested in mitigating fire risks.

UPDATE 7/29/2025:
Dear CPSC Clearing House,

I have communicated with the maker of the baffle grease filters intended to keep fires from entering vent hood ductwork and they have informed me that the orientation of the filters in the image I provided you was incorrect. Both the prior owner and myself who followed his practice had the baffles incorrectly horizontally oriented.  When I rotated the filters 90 degrees such that the baffles were vertically oriented the gaps disappeared. 

I now see that on p 15 of the hood installation manual, which I recently downloaded only because I was searching for an electrical parts diagram, the orientation of correctly installed filters is depicted. As noted above, I also realize that they were installed incorrectly by the former owner of my home. I simply followed his practice and never thought about the gap until I began to wonder why there was a gap. Because it is obvious that filters can be installed incorrectly and not fall onto the range, perhaps GE could have provided a warning in the manual stating that filters must be installed as seen in the picture and that no gap should be present between filters when they are installed correctly. I installed them incorrectly just as the former owner did and I would never have noticed my mistake but for my conversations with the maker of the filters [REDACTED]. It is a wonder that the prior owner of my home didnÃÂt burn the house down because he grilled meat on a gas range under the hood. Because purchasers of homes are also unlikely to be provided installation manuals on preexisting appliances, a permanent warning label on the hood and the filters would be a nice safety feature.

I have looked at manuals of current versions of the same GE hood and although they contain a diagram showing the vertical orientation of the baffles they do not contain warnings regarding incorrect filter baffle orientation and the necessity of not having gaps between filters caused by incorrect orientation of rectangular filters because the gaps create a risk of fires entering the vent ductwork. I am also concerned that the GE parts folks gave me the wrong dimensions of the filter after they confirmed that the filter part number was correct, and I am concerned that none of them could inform me that incorrect filter orientation was the cause of the gaps. It is only because I communicated with the USA rep of the Italian company which made the fire rated filters that I understood that the gap was due to an error by the prior owner and myself to properly install the filters. How not to do something is an important instruction that should accompany any instruction on how to do something. Unfortunately that type of instruction - which is necessary whenever it is physically possible to do something incorrectly - is rarely provided.  Image 2417 is an incorrect but physically possible  installation with gaps between filters apparent, and image 2422 is correct installation with no gaps. 

Thus, my only recommendation is that whenever fire is a risk, clearly worded warning labels with diagrams of correct and incorrect part orientations to advise users on proper installation be provided on or next to parts that can be improperly installed.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard due to incorrect filter orientation, but no actual incident, injury, or death occurred.

incident_description:
I am reporting a serious safety hazard involving the Samsung 5.3 cu. ft. Bespoke AI Ventless All-in-One Washer Dryer Combo. The product is marketed as ventless and low-maintenance. However, after approximately six months of use, I began noticing that loads were coming out damp at the end of a full wash/dry cycle. I followed all manufacturer recommendations, including cleaning the heat exchange coils and the lint trap, but the issue persisted.

A Samsung-authorized technician inspected the unit and found no issues, merely recommending that I rinse the lint filter regularly to prevent buildup. Despite this, the unit continued to underperform, requiring multiple drying cycles per load, leading to excessive energy usage and difficulty managing laundry for our six-person household.

Out of concern and frustration, I researched online forums and eventually found a video demonstrating how to disassemble the unit and access a hidden section of the internal lint chute  a location not mentioned in Samsungs maintenance instructions and not accessible without partial disassembly. When I opened the unit, I discovered a massive amount of compacted lint clogging the internal chute that is supposed to carry lint to the filter. The buildup had almost completely obstructed airflow and directly contributed to the units poor performance.

This represents a critical design flaw: lint is accumulating in an inaccessible area that consumers cannot clean during regular maintenance, and that Samsungs own technicians do not appear trained or authorized to inspect. This hidden lint buildup poses a serious fire hazard, especially since this is a heat-generating appliance being run for extended cycles, often unsupervised or overnight.

The only way to clean this hazardous buildup is to partially disassemble the machine, a process that is not safe or reasonable for average consumers. No warning is provided by Samsung, nor is any official method outlined for safely maintaining this area. I have attached a photo of the lint I removed for reference.

This situation is particularly alarming given the fire risk associated with dryers. According to the U.S. Fire Administration and Consumer Affairs, dryers cause an estimated 13,820 fires annually. Samsungs failure to properly design for lint management  or provide consumer access for maintenance  increases this risk significantly for every owner of this model.

I believe this unit poses a widespread and potentially fatal safety risk to other households, and I urge the CPSC to investigate this matter as a possible defect in design or failure to provide adequate safety information to consumers.
justification: The incident describes a serious fire hazard due to a design flaw, which could potentially lead to injury or death if a fire occurs.

incident_description:
Here is a run down of what happened.

Subject: Safety Incident Involving Milwaukee "Hole Dozer" Hole Saw


On June 28th, I purchased a Milwaukee "Hole Dozer" hole saw kit. I assembled the tool according to the provided instructions and began using it shortly thereafter. Within approximately 10 seconds of use, the hole saw detached from the arbor due to a design flaw. While the arbor tightens during operation, it lacks a proper locking mechanism or securing pins. Once the drill trigger is released, the centrifugal force allows the saw to spin off the arbor.

This unexpected detachment caused the saw to become a projectile. In an attempt to shield my face, I blocked it with my hand and sustained deep lacerations in three areas. The incident also caused me to fall from a ladder, resulting in a significant ankle injury. I had a medical appointment today. Tomorrow will be including an X-ray, scheduled to assess the extent of the damage.

The Home Depot website  the sole retailer of this specific kit  contains at least 15 reviews, dating back over a year, describing the exact same issue with the saw detaching unexpectedly.

As a construction professional with over 20 years of experience, I am very familiar with the safe and proper use of hole saws. This incident was not due to user error, but rather a hazardous product flaw.
justification: The incident resulted in deep lacerations and a significant ankle injury, requiring medical attention, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple similar reports of the same issue over a year.

incident_description:
Dear Consumer Product Safety Commission,

I am writing to report a serious incident involving a hazardous chemical product that has caused me significant health issues and emotional trauma. I believe it highlights a dangerous gap in product safety and labeling that leaves consumers vulnerable to severe harm.

I was exposed to Triple S Strong Arm Heavy Duty Clinging Bowl and Restroom Cleaner, which is labeled For Industrial and Institutional Use Only. Despite this label, the product is easily purchased online by consumers with no meaningful barriers to access. A friend who works in commercial cleaning recommended it and assured me it was safe for home use.

After using the product to clean my bathroom, I experienced:
		Constant burning skin, swelling, and severe allergic reactions.
		My potassium levels dropped to a dangerously low level, resulting in a critically low heart rate that required emergency medical care.
		The chemical spread throughout my apartment, contaminating my bedding, clothing, carpet, appliances, and other surfaces. I was trapped in my own home for 40 days with constant exposure.
		Even after professional decontamination, I continue to fear my home, living with ongoing anxiety and trauma.

I believe this product poses a serious risk to consumers, especially given its easy online availability despite its labeling. I am requesting:
	1.	That the CPSC investigate the products labeling and sales practices to ensure it is not accessible to untrained consumers.
	2.	That the CPSC review whether the products labeling, warnings, and instructions are adequate to prevent harm in residential settings.
	3.	That the CPSC consider regulatory or enforcement actions to protect consumers from hazardous products labeled for industrial use.

I can provide documentation, medical records, and photos if needed. Please let me know how best to submit them.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

Midea 50 Pint Cube Dehumidifier Model #MAD50PS1QGR, manufactured 05/2021

Item was in use in basement area to dehumidify living space.

Disconnected the unit from power after it began to show signs of overheating again (burning smell).

Dehumidifier was used around 12 hours a day, 6 months out of the year. 4th year that we've owned this particular unit and this is the first major failure we've experienced with the model.

No injuries or property damage to report, however this is solely due to the fact I was present at home when the unit began to malfunction. If I had been away for a few hours or if this had happened overnight there is a strong possibility that the unit could have continued to overheat and started a fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dehumidifier that could have led to a fire, but no actual injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
1. Introduction and Summary of Safety Concern
This complaint concerns the improper indoor application and misleading marketing of OSI QUAD
Advanced, a solvent-based construction sealant manufactured by Henkel and distributed through
major retailers including Lowe's, [REDACTED]. The product was applied inside my
home during a Lowe's window installation project, despite being intended solely for exterior use. The
chemical exposure required subsequent product removal. Manufacturer documentation and
misleading retail advertisements present a serious risk to consumer safety, especially when
installations occur indoors.
2. Background and Incident Summary
In 2022, I hired Lowe's to perform a full window replacement at my residence. The installation was
subcontracted to a third party, and solvent-based OSI QUAD Advanced was used to fill large interior
gaps around 24 windows without my knowledge or consent. I later learned that Lowe's
subcontractor had reportedly used this sealant indoors on every window installation he performed
for the company. This was confirmed to me in a phone call with Lowe's Installation Support. Shortly
after the installation, I contacted the manufacturer, Henkel, regarding the strong odor in my home.
Henkel later confirmed in writing that OSI QUAD Advanced is not approved for interior use and must
be fully removed if applied indoors, as covering it with other sealants will not mitigate the chemical
exposure.
Lowe's initially denied responsibility but eventually removed most of the product after inspection.
Nearly two years later, I discovered that multiple retailers had advertised the product as suitable for
both "interior and exterior windows"-a claim directly contradicted by the manufacturer's safety
guidance. Lowe's later admitted this in writing and quietly revised its website.
3. Timeline of Events
- August-November 2022: Lowe's subcontractor applied OSI QUAD Advanced indoors on 24
windows.
- January 3-10, 2023: Improper use confirmed by Lowe's during inspection and documented by a
representative.
- January 19-20, 2023: Lowe's representative personally removed most of the interior sealant.
- April 17, 2025: I alerted Lowe's to misleading online advertising of the product.
- May 5, 2025: Lowe's responded in writing, confirmed the sealant was not for interior use, and
blamed the subcontractor.
- May 2-6, 2025: Lowe's revised its website to remove misleading "interior/exterior" usage claims.
4. Safety Issues
According to the Henkel-issued Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for OSI QUAD Advanced, the product
contains hazardous volatile organic compounds (VOCs) not suitable for interior application. Lowe's
application of the sealant indoors, without consent or warning, introduced unsafe chemical
exposure. I experienced headaches and dizziness following the installation and have preexisting
autoimmune conditions affecting red blood cell production, which may heighten my sensitivity to
such exposures.
Moreover, the sealant was applied in thick layers across wide 1"+ interior gaps in 24 windows,
significantly increasing the volume of chemical material present indoors. No interior-safe alternative
was offered. Despite Henkel's SDS clearly stating the product is intended for exterior use only,
multiple retailers marketed it as appropriate for "interior/exterior windows," potentially misleading
both consumers and installers.
5. Manufacturer Responsibility and Retail Advertising
Henkel's product labeling and SDS documentation directly contradict the advertising language used
on multiple retailer websites. The manufacturer failed to promptly correct this misinformation or
prevent mass distribution of the sealant under misleading use cases. Henkel's emails to me confirm
that the sealant is not approved for indoor use and that complete removal is necessary if used
improperly.
6. Shared Accountability
Lowe's approved the materials list for this installation and created the scope of work. Their
subcontractor's repeated use of OSI QUAD indoors-including in my home-was confirmed by Lowe's
own customer service personnel. Henkel manufactured the product and failed to correct years-long
retailer misstatements. National retailers advertised it falsely. These actions jointly enabled
widespread indoor misuse.
7. Public Risk and Exposure
The false advertising of OSI QUAD Advanced as suitable for "interior/exterior windows" persisted for
years and remains live on retailer websites like [REDACTED]. This occurred during a
time when millions of Americans were spending extended time indoors due to COVID-19 lockdowns
and holidays. Many families may have been unknowingly exposed to VOCs and solvent emissions
in enclosed spaces, particularly if installers followed similar practices.
8. Relief Requested from the CPSC
I respectfully request that the Consumer Product Safety Commission:
- A. Investigate the chemical safety of OSI QUAD Advanced, particularly when used indoors.
- B. Review Henkel's product labeling and oversight of retailer advertising to determine whether
corrections or recalls are necessary.
- C. Identify the extent of public exposure caused by widespread indoor misuse.
- D. Mandate revised labeling, safety alerts, and retailer disclosures for any remaining inventory.
- E. Issue guidance for contractors and installers regarding proper product use and safer
alternatives.
9. Supporting Evidence and Documentation
I am prepared to submit the following materials upon request:
- Manufacturer emails confirming indoor use is prohibited and requires full removal.
- Archived screenshots of misleading retailer listings.
- Email admissions from Lowe's acknowledging misuse.
- Photos showing installation damage and improperly applied OSI QUAD.
- Timeline and inspection summaries documenting the issue and its correction.
Example Advertising References:
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved improper indoor application of a hazardous sealant, leading to chemical exposure and health effects like headaches and dizziness, indicating an injury.

Independent third-party laboratory testing conducted by [REDACTED] in June 2025 revealed that multiple paracord rope products sold by the Amazon seller [REDACTED] were falsely advertised as having a 1,000 lb breaking strength and being made of 100% nylon. Testing confirmed significantly lower strength ratings and revealed that the material is 100% polyester. These discrepancies present serious safety risks for consumers relying on this product for survival, emergency, or load-bearing purposes.

What type of product(s) were being used?
Paracord rope marketed and sold as 1000 lb Paracord and 100% Nylon on Amazon.com by seller [REDACTED]. 

Specifically:
B0B1N3HS5V (Green)
B0B1N7T1J8 (Black)
B0B1N18LH1 (Blue)

Who was using the product(s)?
This product is marketed to and available to the general public through Amazon.com. It is commonly used by outdoor enthusiasts, survivalists, emergency preparedness professionals, and general consumers.

How were the product(s) being used?
These types of paracord products are generally used for emergency situations, securing gear, climbing, rigging, survival situations, and load-bearing applications, based on their labeled tensile strength and material.

They said there are more chemicals, including formaldehyde, in our 21-year-old plywood subfloor than in their product. They said their product makes our home healthier than being without it.
 The installer/store owner told us that he was more convinced than ever, after the phone conversation with Lauzon, that he made the right choice of installing Lauzon flooring in his home, too, because Lauzon was so adamant about how pure their product was. In fact, the flooring has a finish on it that Lauzon named Pure Genius that they claim passively cleans the air, reducing VOCs, including formaldehyde. Lauzon never asked to speak to me, they never asked for a sample of the floor, they rejected giving us a refund, they never followed up on the status of our floor.
Convinced by Lauzon, that the flooring wasnt the problem, our installer offered to seal the floor in food grade plastic so that it would give us time to figure out what was causing our symptoms. It has adversely affected our health, our quality of life, our finances and our personal propertytoo lengthy to discuss here. We are still living with the impact.   We trusted Lauzon, we believed their advertising, we wanted to protect our family from the array of toxic chemicals flooding the consumer goods market. We just wanted healthy flooring.

What type of product(s) were being used?
Both products are APC BR1000MS Back-UPS Pro 1000VA uninterruptible power supply units.

Who was using the product(s)?
The products were used by myself, an adult homeowner, in a home office environment.

How were the product(s) being used?
The UPS units were used as intended: providing backup power and surge protection for home office electronics (computers, networking equipment, etc.). The maximum load connected to either unit was approximately 500W, well below the rated capacity. The units were operated in a climate-controlled environment (6873F), and batteries were tested and confirmed to be in good condition.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
No physical injuries occurred. However, the unit that caught fire could have caused burns or started a larger fire if not contained within the devices enclosure.

How did any injuries occur?
No injuries occurred, but there was significant risk due to the internal fire and release of smoke and fumes.

Additional details:

Both units were purchased new and put into service around March 2021.

The serial numbers are very close, suggesting the same production batch.

I contacted APC support ([REDACTED]). They were thorough but ultimately recommended disposal or third-party repair and encouraged me to report this incident to the CPSC.

I have photos and documentation available upon request.

Product Identification:

Model: APC BR1000MS

Serial Numbers: 4B2052P40811 (error/F02/F04), 4B2052P48282 (internal fire)

Manufacturing Date: December 29, 2020 (confirmed by attached quality assurance slip and APC support)

I have attached a photo of the quality assurance slip from one unit showing the manufacturing date and serial number. The other unit was manufactured in the same batch; the label was removed after the fire but this was confirmed by APC support.

Both units were purchased new and put into service in March 2021.

incident_description:
Smoke/CO detector can fail to stay activated silently and provide false positives of functioning properly.

This product turns on when attached to it's mount.  The on/off switch is actuated during the twisting motion that occurs when connecting the detector to it's mount.

Over multiple installs the on/off switch wears out causing a weak connection of the switch.

When a worn product is installed the smoke detector will blink as if it was successful and good battery.  The test button can even work and beep the alarm for you.  But when the detector relaxes and is unstrained the on/off button can be disconnected disabling the product.

This product is a 10-year battery life smoke detector, so there is less interaction from the user ensuring it is functional.  Additionally 3 out of 6 that I purchased had this problem.  The new version of the product does change the on/off switch.

A related concern is how the mount itself isnt stiff enough to ensure proper engagement of the on/off switch.  The mount has to be secured against a firm surface to ensure the mount isnt able to flex and turn the unit off.

To explain a bit more of the relaxing of the unit.  By pressing the test button you compress the entire unit that in turn provides additional pressure to the internal on/off switch.  This action will cause the unit to beep.  Once the test button is released, the additional pressure is removed from the on/off switch turning the unit off.
justification: The incident describes a failure in the smoke/CO detector that could lead to it being non-functional without the user's knowledge, posing a potential safety risk. Given that 3 out of 6 units had this issue, the occurrence likelihood is high.

incident_description:
My father purchased an Ougist fire extinguisher, Model: MSWJ620, from Amazon (Link: https://www.amazon.com/Extinguisher-Re-ignition-Extinguishing-Combustible-Electrically/dp/B09SCKL79L).

The product description for this fire extinguisher makes a highly concerning and potentially dangerous claim: It states the extinguishing agent is "97% Negative Ion Water, 3% Fire Extinguishing Agent" and that it is capable of safely extinguishing Class A (ordinary combustibles), Class B (flammable liquids), Class C (charged electrical fires), and Class K (grease fires).

However, the fire extinguisher canister itself explicitly states the "Extinguishing agent: S-6-AB." Research into "S-6-AB" indicates it is a protein foam concentrate (typically 6 parts protein foam concentrate to 94 parts water).

This is a critical contradiction. A protein foam extinguisher, like the one indicated on the canister, is NOT safe for use on energized electrical (Class C) fires due to conductivity, and is generally NOT recommended or effective for grease (Class K) fires, potentially causing dangerous splash-back or fire spread. The claim that a "water-based" (especially if it's foam-based) extinguisher is safe for these fire types is contrary to established fire safety standards and poses a severe risk of injury or death to users, including electrocution or worsening of a grease fire.


The Ougist company website (https://ougist.com/pages/about-us) provides no verifiable safety certifications relevant to US standards (e.g., UL) and contains significant amounts of dummy "Lorem Ipsum" text, indicating a lack of professional oversight. While the canister displays Chinese certifications (Metrology Accreditation (MA), China National Accreditation Service for Conformity Assessment (CNAS), China Compulsory Certification (CCC), and International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation - Mutual Recognition Arrangement (ilac MRA)), these do not guarantee safety or efficacy for all claimed fire types, especially given the contradictory agent information and the absence of US-recognized safety certifications like UL.

The product has not been used for any purpose yet, and no injuries have occurred. However, my concern is that if this product were to be used as advertised on an electrical or grease fire, it would very likely lead to serious injury or property damage due to the dangerous misinformation regarding its capabilities. It creates a false sense of security for consumers.
justification: The product has not been used yet, so no injury has occurred, but the misleading claims pose a significant risk if used incorrectly.

The Live Fine Towel Warmer (Model LFHTTWL01) in my master bathroom had a malfunction and melted down overnight. 

I woke up at 3 am and smelled a burning smell, not quite like a home fire but still very strong. I walked throughout my house but couldn't find the source. Once I got up hours later, the smell was much stronger and so repugnant that I searched again. I finally realized it was my towel warmer in my master bathroom. I had placed several shirts on top of the unit (on the lid) which is why I didn't immediately see the issue. I videod once I discovered what was happening. 

The top lid had melted into the unit. It was still dripping the melted lid material into the base of the towel warmer when I found it. I wanted to remove it from my house immediately, but even the outside of the unit was so hot I couldn't touch it. After unplugging, I waited a few minutes and used a towel to carry it outside. 

The unit was not turned on, and even if it had been, there is an automatic turn off switch that should've prevented this from occurring. I did not use the towel warmer the previous night before going to bed. I verified by looking at the unit that it was turned off and took pictures. The electrical cord itself had no damage and was not hot to the touch. 

So the malfunction was on the inside of the unit. I was very concerned since it was so hot and could've caught fire especially with the couple shirts I had placed on the top of the unit (which I've done many times before and never had an issue). The shirt on the bottom closest to the lid had discoloration from the burning and all items were very hot to the touch. And the smell lingered for several days despite using many types of sanitizers. While there were no injuries, thankfully, the smell triggered my asthma and caused some breathing difficulties. 

I've had the towel warmer for about 2 years and never had an issue before this unexpected problem occurred. I live in a senior living community and have very elderly neighbors who are not very mobile. Besides worry for myself, as it was in the bathroom in my master suite, if it had caught fire and spread could've been very difficult for my neighbors.

incident_description:
I am submitting a complaint regarding an unsafe and misleadingly advertised product currently being sold on Amazon by the seller VVAAGG.
Product Details: Paracord Rope 1000 lb
Product Listing Links:
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D5B6QEDF
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D5B5G8H8
The product listings referenced here make two key representations:
Breaking Strength: 1000 lbs
Material Composition: 100% Nylon
However, independent lab testing ([REDACTED] report attached as [REDACTED]) demonstrates the following:
Actual Breaking Strength: Only 324 lbs for the Army color and 361.2 lbs for the black color, well below the 1000 lb claim
Actual Material Composition: 0% Nylon; the rope consists of 100% polyester (inner core) and 100% polypropylene (outer sheath).
Testing.
The FTC requirement is 100% nylon for both inner and outer fibers. 
This discrepancy is severe and poses a material risk to consumers who may rely on this product for critical weight-bearing applications such as climbing, rescue, or survival gear.
Applicable Violations:
False Advertising: Misrepresentation of strength and materials is a violation of Section 5 of the FTC Act (unfair and deceptive practices).
Product Safety Concern: The grossly exaggerated strength rating creates a serious safety hazard to consumers who depend on the product's advertised capabilities.
Labeling Concerns: Initial review indicates that the product lacks compliant labeling as required under federal law, including the Fair Packaging and Labeling Act (FPLA) and the Textile Fiber Products Identification Act (TFPIA).

incident_description:
In October I received FEMA relief funding for the purpose of restoring my electrical utilities due to the loss of equipment and utility related hurricane Helene

I made the purchase off Amazon for 4x2 (8 total) 300w (2400w total) solar panels with the influence of the "Amazon's Top Choice" badge next to the listing. 

After receiving the 8 panels I reported 2 of them as being messed up possibly from shipping. I was given a refund for half the transaction. 

I install the panels, install the new equipment and begin monitoring solar production. The PwM charge controller I was using claimed 44v and 80a output based on my 4p2s configuration. This means I am getting 22.2v and 20a per panel in the 2 strings combining them in series to make the above number. 

I had consistent failures with my solar system due to the battery bank being nearly dead and shutting off by nearly 2am. This continues for months, me spending additional funds and the refund I received on advanced equipment and measurement tools. 

Upon further investigation after replacing every component besides the battery and the panels I discovered an anomaly about the panels themselves. They each had on each polarity junction box a JFET-R voltage regulator which is not a standard blocking diode as other panels have.

Further investigation into this anomaly with more advanced equipment and expert review of the set up determined the JFET-R components are actually hidden Amplifier IC nodes used to amplify the gain of the signal emitted by the solar panels before it can reach measuring equipment so that it reads a false highly inflated number 

A typical solar panel of 300w class is twice the weight of the ones I received, half the amperage output and double the voltage as well as some fair bit larger length or width wise. 

The sticker on the back of the panel had no manufacturer name or information but touted safety and compliance certification badges and the false output of 18.8v and 16a

Further research indicates even a panel of twice the power a typical 300w class photovoltaic cell in the class of 600w output only have a voltage and current reading of 30(some odd)  and 17a with a short circuit of 18 meaning this 300w panel has an isc that outclasses anything in the market at all

The purpose of the purchase was to restore my electrical utilities after hurricane Helene. I am sensitive to heat as a cancer survivor and live year round in a camper. Summer is the time of year I absolutely for medical reasons need to have a method of cooling my environment. Without the full 2400w of solar panels I can not directly power my HVAC system of 18000btu 

I complained to Amazon executive customer relations and received the additional half of my purchase refund at this point it was conveyed in no uncertain terms that I should pursue the manufacturer and I won't be receiving Amazon support for the additional losses related to uncovering the deceptive and fraudulent products. 

In compliance with Amazons statement I research deeply for the manufacturer eco-baeerss according to the seller on the Amazon platform. They can not be found. They are a fabricated manufacturer 

I made the conscious effort to purchase additional equipment equal to inadequate solutions to ensuring I endure the upcoming summer in a albiet extremely suffering but somewhat neutral health condition 

This event has left me to abandon my recovery plan for full restoration of my electrical utilities.  

If I had continued to believe the deception that there is no misrepresentation of the output of the solar array then by the time full peak summer arrived it could have lead to a death of my pet, heat stroke or death in me or my wife. 

That said I am out the allocated relief funding and still do not have adequate utilities even though the purchase of 2400w of panels would indeed have been enough.

UPDATED ON 5/15/2025: [I also was able to find the original manufacturer of the panels who admit the seller and manufacturer on the Amazon site are indeed ficticious as well as acknowledgement of the brand of panel does in fact belong to them

i would be more than happy just to recieve the 2400w i paid for or equivalent with a warranty and at least 50% of the extraordinary purchases made in trying to troubleshoot the falsely labeled panels i did overpay for ]
justification: The incident involved financial loss and potential health risks due to fraudulent solar panels, but no actual injury or death occurred.

What Happened?
I am reporting a safety concern related to a Carrier HVAC system with the Infinity System Control (-C controller) installed in my home in April 2024. The system was functioning properly until Carrier pushed a firmware update that caused a blower malfunction, resulting in erratic and unreliable operation.

The malfunction occurs specifically when the system is in Auto or Heat mode, which could potentially compromise the systems ability to maintain safe indoor temperaturesespecially when the home is unoccupied.

What Type of Product(s) Were Being Used?
The product in question is a Carrier HVAC system equipped with the Infinity System Control (-C controller). Carrier has acknowledged that the blower malfunction was caused by their own firmware update, but has failed to provide a permanent solution.

Who Was Using the Product(s)?
The HVAC system was being used by my family, including my spouse and young child, to regulate the temperature and maintain a safe living environment in our home. The system is also used to ensure the safety of our pets while we are traveling, as we frequently have a house sitter who relies on the systems proper operation.

How Were the Product(s) Being Used?
The system was being used in normal residential conditions, with the thermostat set to maintain a comfortable temperature during both heating and cooling seasons. The issue primarily arises when the system is placed in Auto or Heat mode, leading to inconsistent blower operation and reduced system performance.

Were There Any Injuries That Happened or May Have Happened While Using the Product?
While there have been no physical injuries yet, the defective system poses a potential safety hazard. Since my family travels frequently, the malfunction increases the risk of unsafe indoor temperatures that could lead to:

Heat exhaustion or hypothermia for our pets and house sitter during extreme weather.

Potential damage to the home caused by prolonged exposure to excessive heat, cold, or humidity.

Given the unreliable performance of the blower, there is a heightened risk of system failure during critical periods when the home is unoccupied.

How Did Any Injuries Occur?
While no direct injuries have occurred, the potential for harm arises from the systems inability to maintain safe indoor temperatures due to the blower malfunction. This situation creates unsafe living conditions and exposes both occupants and pets to risk, especially during periods of extreme heat or cold.

Why This is a Safety Concern:
Loss of Climate Control: Failure to maintain consistent temperatures can be dangerous, particularly for young children, elderly individuals, or pets.

Potential System Failure: Extended system malfunction may lead to complete failure of heating or cooling, creating unsafe home conditions.

I am reporting this to the CPSC because Carrier has failed to provide a permanent solution, despite acknowledging the defect caused by their firmware update.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning HVAC system with potential safety risks but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the acknowledged firmware issue and frequent system use.

incident_description:
What Happened?

On February 17, 2025, at midnight, a DeLonghi oil-filled radiator heater (model: EW7707CM-6A) suddenly exploded in a bedroom, causing hot oil to spray forcefully in one direction due to pressure buildup and leak onto the floor and surrounding area. The unit had been operating normally before the incident, with no prior signs of malfunction.

The heater was placed on a flat, wood floor, away from any obstructions, and was being used under normal operating conditions to heat a bedroom.

Damage & Health Concerns

The explosion caused oil to penetrate the engineered wood flooring, leaving irreversible damage despite extensive cleaning efforts. The room continues to emit a strong odor, raising serious concerns about potential health risks from prolonged exposure.

Impact on Household

The rooms occupant, a 12-year-old child, was present during the explosion. While no immediate physical injuries occurred, the sudden, violent explosion caused significant distress and fear, waking the entire household. Since the incident, the strong oil odor has made it difficult for the child to continue sleeping in the room, impacting her well-being and comfort.

Manufacturers Response & Safety Concerns

I reported the incident to DeLonghi customer service on February 18, 2025. The company acknowledged the failure but refused to provide written confirmation when I specifically asked whether the heater oil is non-toxic.

Additionally, DeLonghi has insisted on retrieving the damaged unit via regular [REDACTED] shipping, despite my concerns about further oil leakage during transport. They have ignored repeated requests for safe handling procedures and have not addressed potential exposure risks associated with the leaked oil.

Broader Consumer Risk

This product failure presents a serious safety concern that may impact other consumers using similar DeLonghi oil-filled heaters. I have found multiple reports of similar leaking, burning, and explosion incidents under reviews on Amazons product page:
https://www.amazon.com/DeLonghi-Comfort-Thermostat-Settings-Features/dp/B000TGDGLU?th=1
Given the potential fire hazard, exposure risks, and the manufacturers lack of transparency, I urge CPSC to investigate this matter to prevent further harm to consumers.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and distress but no physical injuries.

incident_description:
Aquasana, a subsidiary of A.O. Smith Corporation, misrepresented the capabilities of their whole house water filtration system. Multiple Aquasana employees, including Team Water Lead representatives, explicitly stated that their system would effectively remove both iron and manganese from my well water. I purchased and installed the system in December 2023 based on these representations.  The system became operational in January 2024.

After nearly a year of use, water testing revealed that the system failed to effectively remove manganese. The manganese levels in my water were approximately 11 times the EPA standard of 0.05 mg/L. This exposure lasted for almost a year, potentially putting my family at risk of health issues associated with high manganese intake.

The product in question is an Aquasana whole house water filtration system - Rhino Well with UV. It was being used as intended for all household water needs, including drinking, cooking, and bathing.

Aquasana's own website features an article detailing the risks associated with manganese in drinking water, demonstrating their awareness of the potential health hazards. Despite this knowledge, they failed to ensure their product effectively addressed this contaminant as promised.

Despite multiple attempts to resolve this issue with Aquasana and A.O. Smith, including requests for compensation and system replacement, the company has been unresponsive and unwilling to address the problem adequately.

This situation raises serious concerns about the accuracy of Aquasana's product claims and the potential for widespread misinformation affecting other consumers who may be unknowingly exposed to high levels of manganese.
justification: The incident involves misrepresentation and potential health risks due to prolonged exposure to high manganese levels, but no actual injury or death is reported.

So three defective units. Company Support via their toll-free line was mostly unhelpful until the 3rd call in - at which point they agreed to send out replacements.  With everything, and the fact that they DID NOT detect the smoke in a controlled test (I am not certified or licensed to test the units) it seems that there are other problems with these units and the company acted as if it was no big deal. While no injury (other than my nerves, back, and toes from jumping and stumbling out of bed as if there were a fire) were experienced, I do feel as if the products are unsafe and can stated without a doubt that I believe the company was being dismissive to my reports.

incident_description:
I own a Coleman/York 96% efficient furnace manufactured by Johnson Controls Heating and Cooling.  The clear condensate collector has cracked and developed several leaks (see attached pics). Leaking water is rusting the sheetmetal in the upper area of the furnace above the lower compartment which houses electronic circuitry for controlling it.  There are also electrical connectors in the pan that the water is leaking into.  According to the technician, if water reaches this area, it will cause the motor to short out.

Apparently there was a bulletin released that indicated a warranty issue if the part 'prematurely' cracked.  According to the Johnson rep, consumers were not notified of this issue and now that my warranty is 2 years past, the part is no longer covered.  Does that mean it is no longer a safety issue?? It seems that this is still a safety concern and a known defective part should be covered.  According to the technician, this issue probably started at least 2 years ago before my warranty expired. I called Johnson Control, they indicated that since the part did not leak prematurely, it would no longer be covered.  Also, when I spoke to the representative, she indicated that there never was a recall only a bulletin. However, there appears to be evidence from other sources (pictures attached) that there was a recall. Either way, I was never notified and had no way of mitigating the problem.
justification: The incident involves a cracked condensate collector leading to water leakage and potential electrical shorting, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
What happened that made you want to report? - Imported products from S. Korean company, which is also based in USA. They shipped 3 cargoes of defective saw blades. This company also has a subsidiary in USA, facing a lawsuit by the US government.
What type of product(s) were being used? - Diamond Segmented Saw blades 8" in diameter used for carving, grinding, and sawing granite
Who was using the product(s)? Our customers in India (all of them are granite processing factories)
How were the product(s) being used? The saw blades (also called Dry cutters) were used to grind and saw granite memorials for export to US and Europe
Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product? The tips (segments & steel teeth) broke off from the saw blades. Flew like bullets. Pierced the bodies of workers. Injured many. Workers stopped work in protest. Factories suffered a loss of production. We, as importers and suppliers, faced the wrath of factory owners, production managers, and workers. We want to warn and caution US users about the company since they operate in USA too.
How did any injuries occur? The segments, steep teeth break and fly off the saw blades like bullets. Workers were injured in their thigh, stomach, and groin regions.
The manufacturer SHINHAN DIAMOND,  Korea (also has a subsidiary in USA/ facing a lawsuit by the US government) for refused to acknowledge the seriousness of over 2000nos of defective saw blades shipped in three cargoes. They refused to acknowledge the extensive work we did for damage control. Recalling defective blades, replacing them with the second cargo, which again turned out to be defective, recalling a second time, and again replacing with the third cargo that once again turned out to be defective.
We paid for the import, freight, duties, taxes, free shipping to customers, free recall, and free replacement. Nothing was done by the manufacturer.
Instead, the manufacturer claimed anything can happen and that they are not responsible.
justification: Workers were injured by flying saw blade segments, indicating a severity level of 3. The repeated defects and injuries suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
On Sunday, Feb 16, I tried using the hot water maker, but it only provided cold water. The light under the sink was on, so I assumed it had power. After another attempt with no success, I smelled burning wires and saw smoke coming from under the kitchen sink. Opening the doors, I found the instant hot water maker smoking. incident_description:
I recently purchased a Speed Queen DR5 dryer in November of 2024.  After about the two months of use, the dryer ran twice without stopping, once for several hours and once for about 24 hours.  After looking up this problem, it has become apparent that there is a design flaw with the timer in this unit.  While the text above the timer dial plainly states to turn clockwise, it is natural for people to not notice the text or simply intuitively back the dial up a little bit should they spin it a little past the desired settings.  It seems as though the dials can malfunction when spun the counter clockwise.  The dial will freely rotate in a counterclockwise direction and there is no mechanical or other protection preventing the dial from being turned counter clockwise.  When the timer malfunctions, the dryer will run forever.  The technician who replaced my timer says he is well aware of this issue.  I called Speed Queen customer service and they acted like they had not heard of this problem, despite numerous reports being on this website with parent company Alliance even responding!  Further, I found many online accounts of this exact same problem.  Here is one example: [REDACTED]

If Speed Queen believes this isn't a design flaw and not a safety hazard because of other protections built into the dryer, then I humbly ask their executives to install and use these dryers in their own homes.  Speed Queen is marketed and sold as a premium machine and has a commensurate cost.  The design of their timer and failure mode of the machine is indeed a massive safety flaw and inexcusable in a product like this.  Speed Queen should at least redesign and offer an alternative part that remediates this issue.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw causing the dryer to run indefinitely, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

A 2-ton gantry crane, along with wheel locks and swivel locks that were recommended and sold separately for safety.

incident_description:
I have three Kidde KN-COPE-IC (interconnected combination photoelectric smoke/carbon monoxide detectors, 120V AC with 9V battery backup) that were purchased and installed on February 4, 2020.  They have a date of manufacture of October 24, 2019 and a date of replacement of February 4, 2030. They all have a Signaling Code of S1816 and an Issue Number of 0010023 on them. 


At approximately 3:30PM on January 10, 2025 I was sitting in the second floor of my home and noticed a strong, burning plastic smell. I went to the lower level and opened one of the doors at the bottom of the landing. Flames were visible 1 above the top of my water heater and smoke was banked down at least 1 foot from the ceiling. I yelled for my wife to bring me an extinguisher. She opened the other door at the bottom of the landing, that goes to her office, and the smoke detector in the room she came from sounded. 

I extinguished the fire and opened the windows and exterior doors. The fire department arrived soon after and mechanically ventilated the entire house and documented the fire. After we had calmed down somewhat I realized the smoke detector that was 7 feet away  horizontally or 8 feet away in a direct line away from the fire source hadn't sounded or alerted any of the other two interconnected detectors in the house. 

The detector on the second floor in the central stairway outside of the bedrooms also hadnt sounded when the lower door was opened. I went to the detector in the room of origin and the green AC light wasnt illuminated. I took the 9V battery out and checked it. It was a fully charged [REDACTED] 522 9v battery with a date of 12/26 on it but the detector still didnt sound an alarm. I removed the detector from its mounting bracket and saw that the power connector was fully seated in the detector prongs. It couldnt be pushed in farther. I removed the power connector from the detector and then reinserted it. There was no corrosion on any of the connections points, male or female. The green AC power light illuminated immediately. I did the exact same process on the upstairs detector with the same results. 

The upstairs detector also hadn't sounded during the fire and it was exposed to more smoke than the detector that did sound in the room on the lower level. The upper level detector also had a 9V [REDACTED] 522 battery with a date of 12/26 on it but that battery was fully depleted. The batteries in all three detectors were changed on daylight savings day, April 10, 2024, with brand new 9V [REDACTED] 522 batteries with dates of 12/26. All three batteries were tested with a voltage meter on November 3, 2024 and were all still fully charged. The detector on the second level obviously drained the backup battery sometime before January 10, 2025 without warning us that the battery was low. We have never been away from home for more than 6 hours in the previous year, since we work from home, so we would have noticed any warning of a low battery. It never alerted us of a low battery. 

After reinstalling the second detector I went to each detector and tested them. They all sounded and alerted the other interconnected detectors as designed to. I repeated this process three times with the same results every time. All of us now check the AC power light at least 10 times a day for every detector and look for the illuminated AC power light every time we walk by a detector and every night  before we go to sleep. Im sure we will be doing this same thing for the rest of our lives now. If the fire had occurred 8 hours later than it did there most definitely would have been fatalities from this event. 

I was a professional firefighter for 29 years and a fire inspector for part of my career. I was more upset with the smoke detectors not functioning than the fire occurring. The fact that the necessary life safety equipment that we have properly installed didnt perform is more concerning than the fire itself. That is the reason I am reporting this issue in the hopes that a tragedy can be averted for anyone else with these detectors properly installed in their homes. 

I tried to contact Kidde customer service on January 11, 2025 but they were closed due to a snowstorm the prior day. I contacted them as soon as they opened on January 13, 2025 and told them all of the above. They told me they would be replacing the two detectors that didnt work and I would be receiving them within 2 to 3 weeks minimum. 

I received an email from Kidde customer service on January 15, 2025 with a prepaid shipping label telling me to return both of the detectors within 7 to 10 business days. I told them that was insane and I would only return the detectors in question after I had installed the replacement detectors. My other recourse would be to purchase and install a different brand of detectors and then I would be sending these two detectors in question to the CPSC. They immediately emailed me that I could send the detectors back to them them after I had received the replacements.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no injuries, but the failure of smoke detectors could have led to fatalities under different circumstances.

Product Information:

Incident Summary:
I am submitting this report to inform the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) of a potentially hazardous product I recently purchased. The Non-slip rug pad I received from Amazon emitted a strong, noxious chemical odor upon installation that has persisted and spread throughout my home. The odor, which resembles raw sewage, has raised concerns regarding its origin and safety. Despite efforts to ventilate the house, the odor has remained pervasive, causing significant damage to my property.

What happened that made you want to report?
After receiving and installing the non-slip rug pad, I immediately noticed an unusually strong, offensive odor. I initially assumed this was normal off-gassing from a new product. However, the smell worsened overnight and spread throughout my entire house and I immediately disposed of the product. Since disposal of the product, the odor has not dissipated despite attempts to ventilate the space with open windows and fans. I have found that the odor has absorbed into the hardwood floors, and despite trying various cleaning solutions, the odor persists. Days after removing the rug pad, the room is still uninhabitable due to the overpowering chemical smell. I have since learned that I am not alone in this experience, as hundreds of Amazon customer reviews reference the same issue with this product, citing the same chemical smell.

What type of product(s) were being used?
The product in question is a Non-slip rug pad, typically used to keep rugs in place and prevent slipping. It is made from synthetic materials, but the specific components causing the odor remain unidentified.

Who was using the product(s)?
The product was used by myself and my family, including my pregnant wife, who has a heightened sensitivity to environmental conditions.

How were the product(s) being used?
The rug pad was unrolled and placed under a newly purchased area rug. The rug and a sectional couch were then placed on top of the pad in a residential living space.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
There were no immediate physical injuries reported. However, the long-lasting odor has raised significant health concerns due to its unknown source, especially considering the potential for toxic emissions. My pregnant wife is at risk of exposure to an unidentified chemical or biological hazard, and I am concerned about the long-term health effects of continued exposure to this substance in our home.

Health and Safety Concerns:
The odor emitted by the rug pad is highly unpleasant, resembling sewage, and it has filled every room in my house. Despite airing out the space with fans and open windows, the smell remains potent and pervasive. The odor has absorbed into the hardwood floors, and all attempts to clean it have failed. As of 48 hours after removing the rug pad, the room is still uninhabitable due to the overpowering smell. This situation poses a health risk, particularly due to the unknown nature of the chemicals or materials responsible for the odor. 

Customer Reviews:
Upon further research, I discovered that I am not alone in this issue. Hundreds of customer reviews on Amazon reference the same chemical or sewage-like smell emanating from the same rug pad. These reviews detail similar experiences, further supporting the concern that this is a widespread defect in the product.

Given the severity of the odor, the potential health risks, and the damage caused to my home and personal property, I urge the Consumer Product Safety Commission to investigate this matter and take appropriate action against the manufacturer of this defective product.

I appreciate your attention to this concern and look forward to your prompt review of this report.

Hello.  this is a written record of a Near Thermal Event PLEASE READ! My generator Westinghouse 7500, is kept in a temperature controlled garage year round and rolled out onto a cement pad partially enclosed out on the attached carport. The unit is well maintained. I had just recently changed oil and spark plug and cleaned air filter. I use good quality gas, stored in doors in approved containers.
     On this evening I move the unit out of the garage as I have done dozens of times. I connected the 30 amp cord and ground wire and with power feed switch off I turned on the gas and started the unit.  It never achieved full motor rpms it only chugged and created an impenetrable cloud of smoke.  I could neither get to the remote nor the off switch as the smoke was too toxic.  One breath and I would have been done.  This went on for about 40 seconds, it seemed longer. The machine was chugging and spewing a cloud of smoke.  I had just reached for my fire extinguisher when the engine stopped running.  As the smoke cleared I became aware that the unit was sitting in a puddle of oil and gas mixture. incident_description:
This is about 80 Gallon Hybrid American Water Heater Model number HPE10280H045DV. we had an almost boling water coming out of the water heater. As I investigated, I saw that the upper element was grounded. I immediately cut the power and applied it again to see what is going on. When power is applied, even before power button is pressed, the control board sends 240V to the upper element. If element is working fine, it cuts the 240V in a second or so. But if it is not working, like being grounded, it continues to send 240V. Remember that this happens even before power button is pressed.

So that 240V electricity finds its way from the element to the ground and heats the water, until the safety switch cuts the power.

I also checked if the relay to the upper element is stuck. So I changed the controller board first. It did the same thing. I changed the element, and everything went fine.

I believe this is a major safety issue.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning water heater that could cause scalding water, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On 12/22/24 we started to notice an acrid smell coming from all of our heating air ducts.  The smell lasted for two days and when a technician arrived on 12/24/24 the smell was gone. The technician checked the furnace to make sure that it was operating properly and also checked for any possible carbon monoxide. He could find nothing wrong at that time with the furnace. On 12/29/24 the smell returned, and a technician came out on 12/30/24. The furnace had been serviced by this same company in September 2024 for the winter season. The furnace and A/C system was installed new by this same company in September 2019. This company is in the local area and has been in business for 75 years. With further inspection by the technician on 12/30/24 it was determined that the plastic drain pan under the A/C evaporator coil was actually burning and scorching from the heat of the oil furnace. Our furnace and A/C iis called an up-flow setup. The A/C evaporator coil sits directly over the oil burner furnace enclosed by the furnace sides. This is a standard normal installation. It is incomprehensible to me why anyone would put a plastic drain pan over a heat source. I was told by the company that installed the furnace that plastic drain pans are the standard in the industry. In my opinion it should be made of aluminum like the evaporator coil. The pan is available separately from the coil, but my concern is that if they put in the same plastic pan, I will have the same problem a few years from now.  I am concerned of a possible fire hazard and health hazard from the fumes coming from the scorched and burning plastic.  The second time this happened on 12/30/24, I had a burning of my eyes and a slight headache. I read of a recall concerning other plastic drain pans manufactured by Goodman manufacturing. incident_description:
Subject: Urgent Appeal for Regulatory Action on the Toxicity Hazards of Aerosol Fire Extinguishers
I am writing to you following the recommendation of [REDACTED] at the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, to bring to your attention a critical and under-recognized issue regarding the toxicity hazards associated with aerosol fire extinguishers. This concern is particularly relevant to devices certified under NFPA 2010 and UL 2775 standards and produced by leading manufacturers such as FirePro and [REDACTED]. Current regulatory frameworks lack adequate safeguards, leaving a significant gap in toxicological oversight that directly endangers public and occupational safety.
Key Concerns
1. Absence of Mandatory Toxicological Testing  
   Current standards, including NFPA 2010 and UL 2775, do not mandate comprehensive toxicological assessments for aerosol fire extinguishers. This regulatory omission has allowed the approval and widespread deployment of devices without evaluation of their potential health hazards during activation.
2. Substituted Test Results  
   Investigations by the UKs Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MIAB) have documented instances where manufacturers submitted substituted toxicological test data to regulatory authorities. This malpractice perpetuates the use of devices that pose severe risks to human health. Refer to MIAB findings [REDACTED].
3. Lethal Hazards in Non-Fire Scenarios  
   Unintentional activation of aerosol fire extinguishers in confined spaces has been shown to release toxic gases at concentrations exceeding permissible exposure limits for carbon monoxide (CO) by up to 331 times. These incidents have caused fatalities due to asphyxiation, underscoring the immediate danger posed by such devices.
4. Increased Toxicity During Fires 
   When activated during fire events, aerosol extinguishers contribute toxic byproducts indistinguishable from standard combustion gases. This complicates investigations and conceals their role in fatalities, as deaths are often attributed solely to fire-related toxicants.
Proposed Actions
1. Mandatory Toxicological Testing  
   Introduce mandatory toxicological evaluations for aerosol extinguishers in both U.S. and international safety standards. These evaluations must establish stringent limits for toxic gas concentrations during and after discharge to ensure user safety.
2. Investigation of Standards Compliance  
   Conduct a thorough review of the testing data submitted by manufacturers for compliance with existing standards. Implement robust enforcement mechanisms to prevent approval of untested or misrepresented products.

3. Comprehensive Analysis of Incident Data  
   Undertake detailed reviews of fire-related fatalities involving aerosol extinguishers to differentiate their toxicological contributions from standard combustion byproducts. This data will be instrumental in addressing regulatory gaps.
Support and Collaboration
I am prepared to provide detailed documentation, including independent toxicological assessments, incident reports, and recommended testing protocols, to support your efforts in addressing this issue. Collaboration on these measures is essential to ensure the safety of individuals in workplaces, residences, and public spaces.
The Consequences of Inaction
Failure to address this critical safety gap will leave thousands of individuals, including sailors, miners, office workers, and passengers, exposed to preventable risks. Addressing this issue now will not only save lives but also enhance the credibility and effectiveness of fire safety regulations worldwide.
I respectfully urge you to prioritize this matter and welcome the opportunity to discuss how we can work together to implement these critical safety measures. Please do not hesitate to contact me to request additional information.
Sincerely,  
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The description reports fatalities due to toxic gas exposure from aerosol fire extinguishers, indicating a severity level of 4 (Death). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on documented incidents but not widespread frequency.

incident_description:
What happened:  My mother fell off a toilet seat when the Toilet Seat Riser that she was sitting on snapped off / out of place when she was getting up.
Product: Toilet Seat Riser - Manufactured for: Health Smart International / Waukegan, IL
Item #: 522-1508-1901 ('may also be listed as # 924-1508-1901)
Sold by: Amazon Fulfillment Services
Scenario:  My mom was sitting on this product and was injured when she tried to get up.  This product, unlike other riser seats that lock in to place with bolts, is held in place by a rubber gasket that fits snuggly (but not locked) in to the hole of the toilet seat itself.  If the person simple gets up (using their legs only) or pushes down with equal pressure (using their arms / hands) on both sides (left and right) of the seat there is no problem.  The problem can arise when the person gets up by only using one arm and pushes down on that one side.  When that happens, the person is putting all of the downward pressure on that one side of the seat riser.  My mom did exactly that.  When she did, that asymmetric pressure caused the seat to literally pop out of place, and it sent my mom flying on to the hard tile bathroom floor.  
Injury: Fractured hip
Reason for reporting this:  So that other users of this product aren't hurt (or worse) by it.  It is my hope that this product is recalled - before someone like my mom is injured or dies!
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured hip, which is a significant injury, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the design flaw that can cause the seat to pop out under asymmetric pressure.

incident_description:
**Subject: Urgent Assistance Required for Heating System Issues**

Dear Bryant,

I am writing to seek urgent assistance with our Bryant heating system, which is controlled by an Evolution thermostat. We moved into our new home in August 2024 and have been experiencing ongoing issues with both the air conditioning and heating systems.

During our initial inspection, we discovered that the air conditioning was not functioning properly. Additionally, the Evolution thermostat displayed a "system malfunction" error. We began using the heating system as the weather turned colder. Unfortunately, we found that the heat was not working correctly. We had to set the temperature to 80F or higher and keep the fan on high for the system to work temporarily. However, after a few hours, the heat would stop working, and we had to turn off the system and repeat the process.

We contacted Young HVAC LLC, whose contact information we found on your website. The first technician visit was on December 2, 2024. The technician noted the following:

"UNIT WAS FLASHING HIGH UNIT ERROR CODE UPON ARRIVAL. FOUND HIGH EFFICIENT FILTER INSTALLED BACKWARDS. FOUND SIGNS OF BURNERS CANDLING. ADJUSTED GAS PRESSURE ON MODULATING VALVE. RESTARTED UNIT, BURNERS NOW APPEAR NORMAL, ERROR CODE ALSO WENT AWAY. CUSTOMER WILL MONITOR UNIT AND CALL BACK IF PROBLEM PERSISTS. CUSTOMER PAID BY CREDIT CARD $135."

Despite monitoring the system, it did not work throughout the night, and we had to use portable heaters, causing significant discomfort for my family. I called Young HVAC LLC again the next day as an emergency, but the technician did not arrive until 6:30 PM. The technician's notes from this visit stated:

"UNINSTALLED EVOLUTION UNIT T'STAT PER CUSTOMER REQUEST. INSTALLED STANDARD PROGRAMMABLE T'STAT. RECONFIGURED WIRING AT FURNACE AND A/C FOR NON-COMMUNICATING T'STAT PER MANUFACTURER INSTRUCTIONS. PERFORMED START-UP ON HEAT CYCLE. HEAT CYCLE STARTED LIKE NORMAL; HOWEVER, INDUCER DRAFT MOTOR IS NOISY BUT WORKABLE. AFTER ABOUT 15-20 MINUTES OF RUN TIME ON HEAT CYCLE, HIGH LIMIT IS TRIPPING. UNABLE TO DETERMINE CAUSE AT THIS TIME. WILL NEED TO CALL SUPPORT TO FURTHER DIAGNOSE DURING NORMAL BUSINESS HOURS. CUSTOMER PAID BY CREDIT CARD $125."

The system worked for a short period but stopped again during the night, leaving us without heat. Upon calling the technician again, he mentioned that the gas pressure was low and advised us to contact the gas company. The gas company identified and removed some clogging. The technician returned but was unable to fix the issue, resulting in another night without heat.

We urgently need a resolution to this problem as my family continues to suffer from the lack of proper heating. Please prioritize our case and provide a permanent solution as soon as possible.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.
justification: The incident describes significant discomfort due to heating system failure but no reported injuries or deaths.
