incident_description:
I recently purchased a Qidi 3D printer called the Plus 4. This was a new model on the market and I ordered it at the end of September, receiving it October 1st. I used this printer for several weeks before discovering some serious safety issues. After two weeks of use, I noticed a very strong burning plastic smell from this device. On discussing the issue with other members on the official Qidi tech [REDACTED], I removed the back panel from my printer and discovered the line voltage Solid State Relay that controls power for the chamber heater had melted significantly. This began my attempts to get the company to recall the printer and fix the problem. Since then, the past few weeks have been a cluster of bad decisions from the manufacturer. I asked the company to send a notice to all purchasers that continued use of the chamber heater was unsafe. Several [REDACTED] videos have been made by other early users demonstrating the immediate need for a recall and replacement of this part. The manufacturer has put this off for weeks. They have responded that the tests weren't "fair", even when I presented my own evidence that this was a fire hazard. They sent out replacement parts only to people who specifically asked for them, and sent out the same defective part as original. 

They also updated the firmware on their printer, without telling any customers that this was required, to a setting which uses less power, but is still creating unsafe temperatures in this power supply. Upwards of 210C has been recorded on video by several people in testing. 

A few days ago they started shipping out a poorly made replacement that while it might work temporarily, it is probably not safe for long term use with the high current heater it controls. Today was the last straw. Instead of warning all of their customers of a potential fire hazard and to stop using this 3d printer, they sent out an email to some customers that said 

"We would like to inform you that some units of Plus4 may experience relay aging during use, which could lead to machine failure. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and for not informing you sooner."

This is unacceptable. Anyone using this printer is currently at risk of burning wires and this relay board on an unprotected line voltage heater. Nothing in this system will shut down the power input if this board catches fire or melts. They need to notify all buyers that use of the chamber heater must be stopped immediately. Since this part is directly connected to line voltage, it is unsafe to ask most customers to replace this part themselves, deserving at least a voluntary recall of all the printers to properly replace this part. 

I'm hoping that there have been numerous reports of this component failure, as many people I have discussed this with online have said they are filing similar complaints. I can return this printer or demand a refund, but they are not warning the thousands of unaware buyers of this product of the potential dangers involved. 

You can learn all about this issue with the following [REDACTED] videos.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
there are many more. 

I'm happy to provide the many emails they have sent me, quotes of what they have sent to others, whatever detailed information is required. 

Because the company is not doing the right thing to protect consumers, I'm hoping this agency will force their hand. All customers of the Qidi Plus 4 printer should be notified that using the chamber heater can lead to dangerous temperatures on the heater power supply, which can melt or burn the components. In an unmonitored situation, I have no doubt this will eventually cause a fire. Let's try to prevent that. 

They should offer every customer either a return for full refund, or send a properly engineered replacement part out and reimburse customers for having professional installation by a certified electrician. They are still shipping printers with the original defective part, they are shipping out a new part which has hand soldered components on it. None of these parts are safe for connecting to household electrical power, and asking untrained users to install the new ones without even a comprehensive installation guide is nuts. Someone is going to wire it up wrong and burn down their house!

incident_description: In September of '24 I bought a Qidi Tech Plus 4 3 D printer. This printer is capable of printing high-temperature materials such as Nylon, Polycarbonate, ASA, ABS, etc. In order to successfully print those materials the printer relies on a closed environment-achieved by a removable glass top and a glass door as well as a chamber heater. This heater circulates warm/hot air throughout the build chamber of the printer and maintains a fairly consistent temperature for the duration of the print cycle, which can vary in duration. Depending upon the size of the model being printed the print time can be 30 minutes to 24 hours or so. This chamber heater is controlled by an SSR which is located on the inside rear of the machine. This SSR is not suited for our 110v system and in many cases is overheating to the point of turning the coils black and making it smoke. As a remedy, Qidi has offered replacement SSRs for the affected machines. This option is not acceptable as it requires the consumer to either pay someone else to replace the defective unit or do it themselves. This exposes the consumer to risk of electrical shock if they are not knowledgeable in this type of repair work. Qidi needs to recall and/or replace the affected machines. The SSR in my Plus 4 unit has blackened coils and another part on the SSR shows signs of getting too hot as it appears to be partially melted.
justification: The SSR overheating and smoking poses a fire hazard and risk of electrical shock, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Qidi Tech, a Chinese-based 3d printer company recently released a new model printer ( the "Plus 4") that is susceptible to catching fire. 
Certain types of filament require hot air around them to print properly. To accomplish this the user programs the printer turn on it's "Chamber Heater." As the air inside the printer gets warm, the electronics that control the heater fail to adequately control the electric current and the circuit board becomes hot enough to ignite. 
The model that I own nearly caught fire as I was overseeing it operate.  
I then researched the issue and found many other consumers were experiencing the same issue. 
There are many posts and a few youtube videos by experienced creators that attest to this issue. 
Qidi has known this issue well over a week now. They instructed their customers to update the firmware in an attempt to mitigate the rise in temperature but astute customers rebuked this attempt with proof that the firmware update is not sufficient to lessen the risk of fire. Hardware components must be replaced with safer ones to adequately reduce the temperature rise on the circuit board. 
Several consumers in the Qidi message boards have offered "fixes" to this problem by suggesting the proper components & directions to replace the faulty ones. *THIS IS A VERY RISKY PROCESS FOR THOSE UNFAMILIAR WITH WORKING ON AC CURRENT SYSTEMS!*
A widespread, comprehensive recall needs to be initiated by Qidi Tech at Qidi Tech's cost.
justification: The incident involves a printer model susceptible to catching fire, with multiple reports and evidence of near-fire incidents, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence and potential for severe consequences.

incident_description: I purchased a runner rug for my hallway from Amazon and received it on October 29. I unsealed it, on my bed , on November 12 and then placed it in my upstairs hallway. Within a few hours I began to experience itching on my hands  and neck. As the evening continued the itching increased and I took a shower . At this point I did not think it may be the carpet that had caused this. I went to bed for the evening and was awoken by midnight with severe itching and welts on my head and neck. Again I showered and by 2:30 in the morning I went to the Emergency Room because of the hives , swelling of my neck and head and some lip swelling. I also had some abdominal discomfort. Upon arrival to the ER I was immediately treated for an anaphylactic reaction with steroids and epinephrine injection . I was sent home 5 hours later. I fell asleep at home on my bed , where the carpet had been unsealed , and woke up 2 hours later with even more extensive hives and swelling now encompassing my head, neck, hands , groin and legs. I returned to the emergency room and was once again treated for an anaphylactic reaction with 2 doses of epinephrine given and a higher dose of steroids. I was then admitted into the hospital. Within a few hours of admission I was quickly taken to the ICU for closer observation due to hoarseness in my throat and increased lip swelling and facial welts. I remained in the ICU for 3 days and required yet another epinephrine injection and continued steroids and antihistamines. I remained for an additional day on a medical surgical floor before before discharge. I missed 2 work shifts due to hospitalization and 2 further days to recover since my discharge.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring multiple emergency treatments and hospitalization, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such severe reactions to rugs are not common.

incident_description:
On October 14th I was using my laser to cut a template of a small purse. A 4.2mm MDF board was placed inside. The settings were as follows:  Power - 100%
              Speed - 7 (it usually self populates to "5", but since its a 40 watt, I always up the speed a bit)
              Passes - 1

The machine is located in my garage near the garage door so the smoke can exit via the hose. I keep my garage door open when using. The air extractor is programmed to turn on when the machine is turned on. So when I press the start button both the machine and the air extractor start.

I performed auto focus. When that was done (my laptop is in my kitchen just off the garage) I went out to the machine and pressed the start button.

I stayed right outside the garage door (which was open) and waited for a gentleman to pick up a driveway full of lumber I no longer needed/used. There was ALOT of pieces (some little, some 2x4x10'), so we were both picking them up and placing them in his pick up truck which was backed into my driveway; thus about 14 feet from the garage door. When he first arrived he looked at the machine and asked, "What's that?".  I presume it was because he saw some smoke coming out of the air extractor tube.I told him about my starting a laser engraving business. Then we proceeded to go back and forth to his truck with armfulls of lumber. About 10 minutes into doing so, as he turned he said, "Uhm...I think you have a problem...". I turned, screamed, "oh my God!".
Flames about 2 feet high were coming up out of the top of the machine and my garage was starting to fill with smoke.  I ran into the garage (its a 2 car garage) to retrieve a fire extinguisher. It was hard to see with the smoke, my eyes watering, and coughing. The man had put a thick piece of plywood over the top to subdue the flames which were continuously getting larger. The man could see and hear my panic and took the fire extinguisher and began spraying. It took a few minutes for the fire to somewhat subside, but then it would start again. I unplugged the machine and pulled out the water hose because the fire extinguisher was running out. That finally put the fire totally out. In the meantime, a neighbor had called the fire department. The fire was out by the time they arrived, but they inspected the machine and all the area around it including my ceiling for damage. The fire department pulled the table on which the laser sat (this was partially melted through...the table). Some wood sheets close to the machine, intended to be used in the laser, were burned and charred. As well as a project for my son's birthday and a friend's upcoming birthday.

The fire department instructed me to NOT  pull the table and the laser back INTO the garage under any circumstances. So it remains in my driveway. My garage and the main level of my home still smell of smoke and burnt plastic.

To say I was terrified is an understatement. I thank GOD that man was right there when it happened because I don't know if I could have saved my garage and house by myself before the fire department arrived. I had my 2 beloved dogs in my house which had me further panicked.
I ALERTED THE COMPANY, "WE CREATE" (Laser Vision 40 W machine) via email and confirmed this machine had NO built in excessive heat/fire alert or auto stop safety function. I assumed it had because nearly EVERY OTHER LASER ON THE MARKET HAS THIS!!!
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant damage to property and creating a hazardous situation, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
My family has had severe heath issues since moving in to our house with spray foam insulation in Oct 2023. After several months & many inspections, we suspected it was due to the spray foam.

We reached out to our builder, [REDACTED] but they ignored us for almost a year. Finally, we reached out to Carlisle, the spray foam manufacturer & they agreed to come out with the installer, Texas Insulation (formerly Best Insulation) to do an inspection & take samples for testing. 

On 3 Sep 2024, Carlisle and Texas Insulation, both confirmed issues with the spray foam based on their visual inspection. They said it appeared as though the foam was off-ratio (Isocyanate rich) and off gassing due to an installation error, but needed to do testing to verify the issue.  They took samples from my attic for testing and assured me that they were going to resolve the issue.  

When I tried following up with them to get the lab results, Carlisle told me that they weren't testing any of the samples until they received installation documents from Texas Insulation showing that it was Carlisle foam.  Texas Insulation claimed they could not find the documents, but then later said they found them and sent them to [REDACTED] & Carlisle who still maintain that they never received them.  

It has been two months since the inspection, and noone will take responsibility for the issue. The manufacturer says it appears to be an installation error, but the installer won't schedule the remediation of the spray foam in my home. 

My family hasn't been able to live in our house for over a year because of the severe impact it was having on our health, especially my baby & toddler who developed asthma, severe allergies, & other chronic respiratory issues.  We want to warn others about the hazards of this product and get help to resolve this issue.
justification: The incident involves severe health issues, including asthma and chronic respiratory problems in children, indicating injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the confirmed installation error and ongoing health impacts.

incident_description: Smoke detectors with 10 year Lithium batteries intermittent false alarms due Lithium battery Voltage instability. This happened with a few Kiddie Combo Smoke/CO detectors as well as a number of [REDACTED] Sound units. The problem is with the constant falsing many people remove and do not replace the detectors and/or ignore the alarms which can and will lead to unsafe situations and someone getting hurt or worse. This does not appear to be a model or manufacturer specific issue, I firmly belive it is due to the nature of Lithium cells that are unstable and have Voltage flucuations. Even when the detectors are AC powered witht he 10 year Lithium back up battery, I beleive the battery is causing many of the detectors to false on a random basis. This is a BIG issue and need to be investigate. Just search online and you will see thouands of complaints, but many may not realize the problem is likely due to the Lithium batteries.
justification: The incident describes potential injury or worse due to ignored alarms from faulty detectors, indicating a severity level of 3. The widespread complaints and random nature of false alarms suggest a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
This rug is emitting Toxic Odors!  After 3 years of owning this rug, it got wet for the first time when our dog peed on it. On 10-18-24,  my wife discovered the wet spot and started  to clean it up. She could not believe the toxic smell that was emitting from the rug!  She tried to clean it by blotting.  The strong, toxic odor remained.  She then used vinegar and baking soda.  The terrible smell remained.  She used a professional rug cleaning solution.  The potent stench persisted and permeated throughout the house. A few days later, I smelled the rug and started having breathing issues and light-headedness.  We had to remove the rug from the house because of the stench.  We hosed the rug with water and let it air dry outside.  The strong, noxious stench still persists!

Something is very wrong with this rug's materials. I am 60 years old and have had dogs for most of my life.  This is NOT a normal smell caused by a dog urinating.  I am worried about the health of anyone who has this rug in their home. I noticed several other complaints on noxious odors on this website.  I tried to contact the seller, but was unable to since I am past my Amazon Return window.
justification: The incident caused breathing issues and light-headedness, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar complaints exist but are not widespread.

incident_description: I purchased a large bottle of Pine Sol at Ace Hardware and it spilled all over the front floor of my car. There is not a safety seal on their bottles and the cap was not even tightly closed. I thought that was so strange for such strong  cleaner with a strong odor, so I went to Home Depot to purchase another one, since mine was completely empty, and again, no seal and loosely capped. Crazy! The smell is so strong that I had to have my car detailed twice, and it still has a strong odor. I am allergic to chemical/cleaning smells and only use organic cleaners in my house. I only bought Pine Sol becuase I read that flies do not like that smell so I spray it around my trash and yard waste bins in the summer. I contacted Pine Sol and they only offered a refund if I sent them the reciept, which I no longer had. I am out $150 for the car detailing and the lingering odor makes me cough and makes my eyes water. Even the least harmful products, such as many of my cosmetics have a protective seal!
justification: The incident caused allergic reactions (coughing, watery eyes) due to the strong odor, indicating injury.

incident_description: I purchased this Firman TOP7573 on December 23, 2022 because the power was out during a snow storm. I had to call Firman when i got home because the light for the CO2 sensor came on and the generator would not run and generate electricity. The Firman technician directed me to disconnect  a wire in a fitting, and I was able to use the generator for 2 days until the power returned. When I tested the unit the next summer I was unable to get the unit restarted because the Co2 alarm was activating,I took the unit to a Firman dealer in 2023 and was told there was nothing wrong with the unit.  It is well established that the CO2 alarm sensor system almost never work properly. There is no potential for human error on my part. I tried to get the unit started but it will not currently operate because the C02 sensor continues to trip.  With no more effort from me CPSC shall direct Firman to send me the parts and instruction to fix the generator. It is beyond human comprehension that CPSC has not recalled all of the generators with CO2 sensors. It is undeniable that the C02 systems rarely work properly It is  chilling that the government is requiring CO2 sensors on residential generators when it is known that they fail entirely too much. Consult [REDACTED] if you disagree with this
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning CO2 sensor preventing generator use, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Purchased a new kitchen faucet named Fairbury from American Standard plumbing products company. After about 6 months, the leeching of plastic tubing from the pull down water line to the spray head tasted like 'plastic whiskey', contacted American Standard, they sent me a brand new complete faucet. Installed that one, again, about 6 mos later, same taste. It occurs while water sits in the supply line to the head, not the supply lines from the shut off valves to the control cartridge. I eliminated the lines from shut offs, filter and concluded it is the supply line to the spray head. I'm sure we're not the only one's with the problem, suggest a line replacement to the head recall. To get rid of the taste, must run the water between 15-40 secs (approx). No injuries known, concerned with aftereffects of effluent leeching.
justification: The incident involves a recurring issue with plastic taste in water due to leeching, but no injuries or health effects are reported.

incident_description: We were testing out the Piccalio Mini Chef Foldable Helper Tower before giving it to our child. The top handlebar has a rod in the front and back which is designed to glide/move in order to collapse (as the tower is advertised as being foldable for storage). The front bar is positioned just at the height for a child to grab, generally a few inches below counter height. Once built, the bar feels rather secure and has some stick to it, making it seem like it is available for holding with some pressure. When testing it out, one of the adults held on to the front handlebar thinking it was secure and leaned over to look at the adjustable platform heights. The handlebar then gave way and the back bar came flying up, hitting the adult on the skull just along the eye socket with significant force. Thankfully the bar didn't hit the eye, though the adult had a significant bruise and swelling. If a child were to be placed on the top platform height and grabbed/leaned onto the front bar at all, the back bar would come up at just the right height to crash into the back of their head, potentially causing significant injury. Another adult, wanting to test out the handlebars against the cabinet to see if it would prevent any movement, bruised a finger when pushing down and realizing the circular path of the glide forces the bar forward, so even if the back bar doesn't cause any injuries, a child grabbing onto the front bar could seriously bruise their fingers when smashed between the front bar and cabinet or countertop. The issue could be solved with a simple removable pin or latch to keep the bars in place, which I recommended to the company in my email complaint.
justification: The incident resulted in significant bruising and swelling from the handlebar hitting an adult, indicating an injury. The description suggests that a child could suffer similar or worse injuries, making the occurrence likely.

incident_description: We were draining a recalled hot tub (the Saluspa Ibiza) so that we could move forward with the recall on the pump. I noticed tiny little wisps of smoke from the window, went outside to investigate, and the cord of the pump had burned and was continuing to burn a 6x3" hole through our back porch. It looked like a smoldering campfire. The hot tub was turned off, but still plugged in, and my husband was draining it. This left a roughly 6 inch by 3 inch hole burned between 2 deck boards on our back porch. I have no idea how long it had been burning, but it was fine at about 1:15 pm. (This occurred around 5 pm.) The cord was melted through, stuck to a side of one of the pieces of wood, and still actively burning. You couldn't smell or hear anything, even right in front of it, and you could only see the occasional wisp of smoke. Had I not noticed, my entire house could've caught fire.

incident_description: I purchased the "Purewell Gravity-Fed 1.5 Gallon Stainless Steel Countertop Water Filter System with Water Level Gauge Faucet" less than a year ago, and since then it has been the main water source for my family. Nothing besides city water has touched it. Upon looking inside last week, I was horrified. The metal nut and maybe bolt that was included to attach the spout (that is in the bottom reservoir where clean drinking water is to be dispensed from)  is leaching metal shards into our water we've been drinking! I rinsed the shards out, but you can see in my photos how the nut has a metal coating that is just sluffing off, contaminating our water. This is a huge lapse in quality control. We care about clean drinking water, but this item has caused us to drink water that is far more contaminated than before the filtration.
justification: The incident involves contamination of drinking water with metal shards, posing a potential health risk but no reported injury or death.

It is glaringly obvious that these faulty devices are unfit for the market, as is evident from numerous online reviews lamenting the same problem with this product.

Adding insult to injury, on 10/11 at approximately 3 AM, the nuisance alarm was activated yet again, leading to a harrowing incident where my 7-year-old daughter jolted out of bed, collided with a wall, and tumbled down the stairs, resulting in a distressing head contusion and sprained ankle. This is an abhorrent consequence that highlights the urgent need for these defective alarms to be immediately recalled

incident_description:
USG brand sheetrock easy sand 90 minute drywall compound was used in my home for some drywall repair and patching (relatively small areas). Start date September 6, 2024, last date of application in a series of small areas was September 16, 2024 . The product was mixed with pure water according to manufacturer's instructions and applied according to manufacturer's instructions. The product smelled terrible, but it was assumed that after the material cured completely it would have no odor (as claimed by the manufacturer. )

A mineral paint that had been tested by the homeowner (completely safe and no odor after a few hours) was applied over the patched areas which had been allowed to dry overnight before paint application.

As of todays date, October 8, 2024, the homeowner has been forced to relocate and has not been able to return to her home due to the toxic odor, which causes allergic reaction, anaphylaxis, migraine and vomiting. And the bottom line is - that if she is reacting to something- it is toxic, and neurotoxic to children, babies, pregnant women, elderly, sensitive, allergic, and immunocompromised individuals.

Homeowner has been in contact with USG since September 29, 2024 and has not been provided with any information (and company has thus far refused to provide information about) about ingredients simply called "binders" on the product's MSDS. The word "binder(s) " is not an ingredient name, it is the function of an undisclosed ingredient(s).

The homeowner has been forced to relocate into a shed outside of her home. The problem cannot be remedied until the problematic ingredient(s) have been identified.
justification: The homeowner experienced allergic reactions, anaphylaxis, migraine, and vomiting, indicating injury.

incident_description:
I bought a air freshener product by Proctor & Gamble called "Febreze" small spaces original. I had it on a table near my bed. 
I live alone.
This is not a spray, it has a volatile carrier that slowly evaporates out with fregrance, it's NOT a plug in.
I soon began to have trouble breathing, my bronchial went into spasms, I coughed up large amounts of flem from my lungs, I had heavy, painful coughing, I wheezed loudly & was short of breath. 
I lost 20 LBS in two weeks.
I went to the ER twice because I could not breath. The ER doctor said I had acute asthma & the info they gave me mentioned "triggers" that could set off asthma. 
I have never had asthma or allergies.
I have had to spend hundreds of dollars for overpriced asthma inhalers & drugs, I am a low income senior.
I finally found my "trigger", it was the "Febreze" air freshener for small spaces, once I removed that from my room, I began to feel better but I'm still feeling the effects of the toxic volatiles of that product. 

The only warning on this product is to not get the liquid in your eyes.
I am still short of breath, I feel weak, I still cough up flem but not as much as before.
justification: The individual experienced acute asthma symptoms requiring ER visits and ongoing health issues, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Dear Consumer Product Safety Commission,

I am writing to formally submit a safety complaint regarding a serious incident involving my Samsung FlexWash washer Serial Number WV60A9900AV/A5, purchased in March 2024. The issue I encountered has raised significant concerns about the safety of this product, posing a potential fire hazard that could endanger lives and property.

On September 20, 2024, my Samsung washer prompted me to perform a self-cleaning cycle. Following this prompt, I left my home for a couple of hours. When I returned, I was shocked to find that my smoke detector and fire alarm were blaring. I rushed to the laundry room to discover thick smoke pouring from the washer, accompanied by a strong burning odor. The machine was unresponsive, and I had to manually unplug it from the back to prevent a potential escalation into a fire.

This incident could have been catastrophic. Had I not returned home in time, the smoke could have turned into a fire, threatening my property and the lives of my family. I live with my wife, who is five months pregnant, and our bedrooms are located directly next to the laundry room. The risk posed by this defective product is unacceptable, and the safety of my home and family was in jeopardy.

After contacting Samsung Care, a technician inspected the washer and confirmed that the computer board was severely burned and charred. Despite the clear defect, my request for a refund or replacement was denied, and I was left with no choice but to accept a repair as my only option. The technician has now been to my home three times, and during the third visit, the replacement computer board they brought was also defective. The machine remains unusable, and I have lost all confidence in its safety.

Samsung has failed to provide any assurance that future repairs will prevent another potentially life-threatening incident. I am extremely frustrated with the companys handling of this situation, as I have been left without a functioning washer and with concerns about the safety of any future repairs.

Given the severity of this fire hazard, I feel that this product presents an ongoing danger to consumers, and I strongly urge the CPSC to investigate this matter. I believe that this washer could pose a serious risk of fire, especially if similar incidents are happening to other consumers who may not be as fortunate as I was in preventing a fire in time.

I also be able to provide the damaged computer board and the defective replacement part if needed . I am available to provide any further information you may need to conduct your investigation. Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I hope this will lead to appropriate action to protect consumers from this dangerous product.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning odor but no actual fire or injury occurred, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I'm using a gas furnace by Trane.  After a routine inspection, the tech found cracks in the heat exchanger which can cause carbon monoxide to leak into the house. The part is covered by a warranty HOWEVER the labor to fix is $2500-3000 which is not economical for most families. The tech made a comment (and showed me photos) about this problem being very common, stating that he sees it weekly on units much newer then mine. I did a [REDACTED] search and discovered the same, so I then called around to several heating and cooling places and they all mentioned this was typical with units as young as 3 years old but super common with those in the 10 year age.  I asked 3 different companies if they were aware of any recalls and they all said no. Of course when the labor nets these companies a few thousand dollars, they have no real incentive to report it either.  This is essentially a public health crisis that is hiding in plain sight. Either the techs find this problem to scare people into getting a new furnace or the problem is real and defective products are just out there slowly poisoning people. Worse is that its a failure of a warrantied component yet repairs is so costly, families have to risk the consequences. I sincerely hope that someone will investigate how common of an issue this is.

This cleaner is sold in the form of flakes and some of them leaked from the container and damaged the packaging.  The packaging got wet somewhere in transport and the consumer noted that water can cause the contents to activate and heat up during the process.  This also causes the drain cleaner to combustible.

The product was delivered to a work location and fortunately, no one was injured.

NOTE:  The product was not sealed in child-resistant packaging, and there were no warning labels on the packaging.

The consumer believes that JB Tools got hold of a bulk quantity of this product and did not include warning labels when the product was shipped.  Therefore, other people who purchase this product could be exposed to a similar risk.

(09/30/2024): This complaint concerns my order of a 2 lb size of Thrift Drift Drain Cleaner on Amazon, which was however shipped to me directly from JB Tools. Upon recieving and opening the package, I realized, to my alarm, that the cleaning agent - sodium hydroxide (aka lye, caustic soda), a powerful and extremely toxic, fume-producing substance whose dormant form here is small flakes that get activated by hot water- was only loosely packaged inside a cardboard box. The sodium hydroxide flakes in this package somehow had become exposed to moisture and had started to combust inside the package. Not only that, they were spilling out into the cardboard box, potentially to be touched by and unsuspecting customer, in this case me. They got on my hands but fortunately I was not injured. But such injury could easily happen to other future unsuspecting customers. Finally, there was no warning label on the package, as there is on the 1lb bottle. This is in violation of OSHA regulations. 

After I conveyed all of this information to the JB Tools customer service representative on August 10, I heard nothing from them beyond a minimal and impersonal message, through Amazon, saying that they would refund my purchase and saying simply "sorry for any inconvenience." My information was apparently not passed along to their management until I called them again and told them I'd made a complaint about them to the CPSC and that I'm also about to do so with the New York State Public Employee Safety and Health Bureau. 
-[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a hazardous material leak and potential combustion, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
I own a table saw manufactured by Laguna Tools of Grand Prarie, TX.  All table saws manufactured since 2008 are required to have a safety device called a riving knife, which prevents the cut part of the board from pinching together as it is passed through the saw.  If the "kerf" or cut portion of the board pinches together, it will cause the saw to bind, which can lead to the board being forcefully ejected back towards the operator at high speed.  In some cases it may even result in the operator's hand being drawn into the spinning saw blade.

The riving knife on my table saw, Laguna model Fusion F1, has become very loose, causing it to be misaligned with the blade.  This sets up a very dangerous operating condition.  When I contacted Laguna's tech support, their answer was "do not use the saw as it is dangerous to operate in this condition."  I asked them what the fix was and was told "to remove the riving knife clamp mechanism, clean and lubricate it, and re-install it."  I asked how I might go about doing that and was told "we don't have a published procedure because it is straight forward."  I pressed further on what the procedure was for doing what they suggested and got no answer, other than to suggest that "I am the first person to ever have a problem with this."  I hold a degree in mechanical engineering and am quite familiar with tools and machinery, and I can say that there is absolutely nothing self-explanatory or "straightforward" about performing this repair.  They are setting up an extremely dangerous condition with a table saw that they manufacture, and are being extremely negligent about addressing my concern.
justification: The loose riving knife creates a high risk of injury or death due to potential saw binding and ejection of material or operator's hand being drawn into the blade.

We moved in in December of 2023. The home was built with Jeld-Wen exterior windows and doors. The front door to the house is very large and heavy. It does not have a traditional latching mechanism. It has spring-tensioned rollers on the door that fit into detents on the door frame. It has a dead bolt for security. If the dead bolt is not engaged, you simply push on the door with enough force to overcome the spring tension to open the door. 
When we moved in, we discovered that the door would blow open with the force of a stiff breeze. Finding this unacceptable, we have had Window Visions come out and adjust the tension. They have diligently adjusted it several times and it is now very difficult to open. A child cannot open the door. Yet it continues to blow open. We walked to a neighbors home Friday, August 16th for dinner. During dinner, a storm came in and the power went out. We walked home after the rain had stopped and found the door had blown open and rain came into the interior hardwood floor. We cleaned up the water but now, a few days later, the hardwood floor is damaged and warped. A child cannot open the door from inside or out, and the door blows open in the wind. The manufacturer, JELD-WEN refuses to repair or replace the door.

incident_description:
I have a very serious safety issue with my Singer sewing machine. I have been sewing over 50 years so I have plenty of sewing experience.  In May of 2022 I purchased a new Singer Model #HD6800C serial number 131711071953. 
The problem is that the machine runs even when I am nowhere near it.  It takes off very fast and the only way to stop it is to unplug it.  It has happened about 5 times in the past and it happened again today.
I called Singer customer service some weeks ago and since the machine is no longer under warrantee, I was simply told to unplug the foot petal and use the hand feature on the machine to sew.  I was also told that I am not the first person to report this issue. I was too busy at the time to argue about the response with the customer service person but when the problem happened again today- when I was out of the room, I realized that this is a much greater concern than what I first imagined. 
Here is the huge issue - I am at risk of getting my fingers caught in the needle when this machine takes off.  I also have grandchildren that I am teaching to sew and I truly feel that this machine could seriously injure them if the machine suddenly took off when they were sewing.  I know enough to quickly unplug the machine but this is such a shocking and startling event that they may stick their little hands into the needle to stop it.  That thought terrifies me.
Today it started zooming when I was in the other room and I had to run in to stop it.  What if I was outdoors or left the machine plugged in and on and left the home. The least of the damage will be to foul the bobbin/needle mechanism and ruin the machine.  The worst would be to overheat and cause a fire.
I have thoroughly inspected the pressure foot petal and it is clean and free from any foreign object, dust or debris that could cause the petal to stick in an on position.  To be clear, the machine is unattended with this malfunction occurs.
This malfunction has happened enough for me to know that this cant go on without a resolution or action on the part of Singer/ SVP Corporation.  This is a serious equipment malfunction that can terribly injure the consumer even when using the product correctly.  This malfunction is a fire hazard that can lead to property damage or death.  This serious safety concern cannot continue and warrants notification and attention from the highest executives at the SVP corporation.
justification: The sewing machine's unexpected operation poses a risk of injury to fingers and potential fire hazard, with multiple occurrences reported.

incident_description: We have had a Schlage Encode Smart Wi-Fi Deadbolt (with Century Trim in Satin Nickel) electronic lock on our home's front door since around January 2024. This allows us to use a code to enter our door (so we don't have to carry a key). After a couple months, we precipitously had an issue with the electronics on the first lock (with no warning, it just stopped turning on, even when the batteries were replaced, but we could still manually turn the deadbolt, so it was a pain, but we could still get in and out of the door). We contacted Schlage and they sent us a replacement lock. It seemed like the new lock was working okay until today, again out of nowhere, we we unable to manually unlock the door. The deadbolt would not undo from the inside. All adults in the household tried. We were locked in. Thank goodness we have other doors in the household, and thank goodness my husband was present and knew how to uninstall the entire lock. Once he removed all electronic aspects of the lock and was down to just the deadbolt (with the hole for the locking mechanism open between the outside and the inside), he was able to manually unlock the door with a tool. If we have been trying to exit in an emergency, particularly a fire, we could have all died because of this serious malfunction. We are going to remove this electronic lock and return to a basic locking mechanism, but it's important that this major safety concern be known.
justification: The incident describes a serious malfunction that could have led to death in an emergency, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was standing on the 3rd stop from the top of my Werner A-frame fiberglass ladder, model 5908. I was working in front of myself. incident_description:
I am writing to express my concerns about the safety of my Samsung washing machine, Model: WA50R5400AV/US The machine has exhibited consistent issues related to balance during operation, particularly during the spin cycle. These issues have escalated to a point where I believe the appliance presents a serious safety hazard.

During most cycles, the washing machine becomes severely unbalanced, causing it to rock violently and bang loudly. The force of the movement is significant enough that the entire machine shifts from its original position. This rocking and banging not only damage the surrounding area but also create a high risk of injury to anyone standing near the machine.

Given the amount of force involved, I am deeply concerned that if someone were standing nearby, they could be hit by the machine or injured by debris resulting from its movement. The instability of the washing machine during operation makes it unsafe for use in any household.
justification: The washing machine's violent movement poses a high risk of injury to anyone nearby, though no injury is reported yet.

incident_description: I purchased a Greenwood 2 gallon sprayer at Harbor Freight.  The unit was new and had never been used.  I was spraying for ticks at my property in NW Arkansas.  I had the sprayer nearly pressurized when the bottom of the tank split.  The sudden release of the liquid forced the tank upwards with incredible force.  With my hand still in the pump handle,  it knocked out a front tooth and drove it through my upper lip and I found it lodged inside the wall of my right nostril.  My face was bruised, my right eye was swollen and bloody and teeth ripped open my right arm.   I was unable to drive our of the woods until the next day where I was treated and released from the local hospital.  To this day, I am blind in my right eye.  I see blurred images most of the time but other times see only color, usually brown.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including blindness in one eye, a knocked-out tooth, and other facial injuries, requiring hospital treatment.

incident_description:
I've had issues with the Simplehuman Triple Wall Mount Soap Pump. I mounted it to my shower tile according to the directions, cleaning the surface and allowing 24 hours for the adhesive to set and within a couple days, it fell while my son was taking a bath. I contacted customer service about this, and their response was to send a new backing plate because that was the only part that seemed to sustain any damage.

I tried with the new plate, and within one day, it fell again while my son was taking a bath. This is not only frustrating because I've found Simplehuman products to be very well made otherwise, but also because it could have hurt my son. And now I'm loathe to contact customer service again because I don't want another backing plate that doesn't work and is downright dangerous.
justification: The soap pump fell twice but no injury was reported, though there was potential for harm.

incident_description: I purchased a Westinghouse WGen 12000 generator. I was recently running it to power our home and when I stepped out to turn it off there was gasoline spewing out all over the ground. It appeared to be coming from the fuel pump. It could've easily caused property damage or bodily harm. I've contacted Westinghouse four times and have received no return calls from their tech support. The last time I called, the customer service rep told me that each time I call my name is put back at the bottom of the pile. I called two days ago and told me to not expect a return call from technical support until two or three weeks.
justification: Gasoline spewing from the generator poses a risk of property damage or bodily harm, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I went to the REI Co-op in Eugene, Oregon, and bought Bottle Bright Cleaning Tablets to try to remove a lingering smell of tea in a water bottle. I brought the product home and proceeded to use it, having taken a general look at the label. It mentioned using warm water if you wanted strong action. I figured, the hotter the better, and used my electric kettle to prepare some water. Just after the water boiled, I poured some of it into the bottle, then dropped a tablet into the bottle. The ingredients in the product reacted with hot water violently, and it fizzed back out onto the back of my right hand. I rinsed my hand and washed it. Soon after, I applied ice. It began to sting unless ice or cool water was directly applied. My husband became concerned, did some research into the ingredients, and called Poison Control. Poison Control recommended I go to the emergency room, so I did. The exam included photographs of my hand, which I have available. The back of my right hand was very irritated, a little reddish, and had a couple small blisters due to a chemical and thermal burn. The clinician recommended a tetanus booster, which I received. He also got me [REDACTED], which I applied for a couple days and was soothing and seemed to help. I am really aggravated the company designed the label to appear very natural seeming and low-risk, but mineral agents can be very reactive it turns out! I recommend they add a specific warning about the highest safe temperature to avoid fizzing of the product out of the bottle.
justification: The incident resulted in chemical and thermal burns with small blisters, requiring emergency room treatment, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) since misuse of cleaning products with hot water is not uncommon but not frequent.

incident_description:

Fast forward to today and I hear her making unusual noises so l look at her and see a piece of the soft foam on her mouth and another piece on her shirt. I'm so upset at myself for not removing the fan earlier. 
The legs of the fan have these hard plastic or rubber cover caps that my 9month old removed. I did not save these pieces so I do not have any photos to reference but you can clearly see them in the advertisement on Amazon. And you can clearly see they have been removed on the photos I sent to safeproducts.gov.
justification: The incident involved a choking hazard with no reported injury, but the potential for harm was present.

incident_description:
What happened that made you want to report? 
I experienced severe skin irritation upon touching the black cover of our outdoor air conditioner unit. A similar incident occurred with one of my children, indicating a recurring problem with this product.

What type of product(s) were being used? 
The product in question is an outdoor air conditioner unit, specifically the Lennox model XC25-048-230-01, installed in 2018.

Who was using the product(s)? 
The product is installed at my residence and is used by household members for indoor climate control.

How were the product(s) being used? 
The air conditioner unit is used as intended for home cooling purposes. The irritation occurred when the external fiberglass cover of the unit was touched.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product? 
Yes, both I and one of my children suffered skin irritations from contact with the deteriorating cover of the unit. The irritation was significant, causing discomfort and concern due to the difficulty in removing the fiberglass particles embedded in the skin.

How did any injuries occur? 
The injuries occurred due to direct skin contact with the fiberglass cover of the air conditioner unit, which has deteriorated to the point where it sheds thin, sharp fibers upon touch.

Given the potential for harm, especially to children, I believe this matter warrants urgent attention.

incident_description: Samsung Dryer (Model #: DVE50R8500V/A3 & Serial #: 0B1C5BBMB01054Z) located in a residential home and used for its intended purpose while always referencing the manufacturer guidelines for operation and care. Constant excessive internal and external lint with no repair fix after Appliance Service Center (Lowes Warranty Assurant local servicing company) technicians came out five separate times. Routine maintenance and cleaning upheld every use and was noted by multiple technicians as in compliance. All technicians observed excessive lint on the exterior surface as well as on internal components. Some components were replaced after multiple troubleshooting attempts but the issue continues to be a constant hazard. Technician noted excessive lint on the internal copper coils and stated "it is not a fire hazard". NPFA Code 69 (prevention and control of explosions in enclosures that contain flammable concentrations) states that this is most definitely a hazard and a solution must be rectified as quickly as possible to reduce risks. The warranty company will NOT replace the unit because they state that it is because of lack of routine maintenance which is far from the truth as the manufacturer's guidelines for cleaning and maintenance are always followed. The unit is unserviceable and a safety hazard. It requires immediate recall and replacement.
justification: Excessive lint accumulation poses a fire hazard, as indicated by NFPA Code 69, despite technician claims to the contrary.

incident_description: My home uses a SimpliSafe home security system. The intention of this is improved safety. This evening, one of their entry sensors became displaced from a window in my toddler's bedroom, just by me gently knocking into it while pulling down the window's shade. The sensor came apart (though the pieces did not break, the device's components just separated), and within it was a lithium ion "button battery" which came out and fell to the floor with the sensor and separated from it easily. My husband, who installed these devices, could not initially locate the button battery and asked for my help in finding it on the floor of my child's bedroom given the dangers we know it can cause if ingested. We located the battery, and given how easily it became dislodged from the sensor, I promptly removed them from the room. I have contacted the Simplisafe company to give them feedback on this. Luckily no harm came to anyone but if the battery was ingested by a child, damage could have been serious and deadly. I am a pediatrician myself (in addition to being a mother), and know the severity of button battery damage and risks of ingestion. Recently, Reese's Law was put into place by the CPSC to avoid such injuries.

incident_description: We were awoken in the early morning our with our carbon monoxide detector going off in our downstairs hallway. My husband changed the battery thinking that was the problem. We went back to bed and awoke around 9 a.m. with carbon monoxide alarm going off again. We woke up with a headache like a hard hangover even though we had not been drinking. We knew it wasn't the battery since he had just installed new ones. We opened the nearest window and placed a fan in the hall to blow carbon monoxide outside.   Several hours later we still did not feel normal, so we called the fire department to get us, and house checked.  Our downstairs measured 6-7, and near the attic door registered 43. The fireman didn't see the need of opening the attic door. He said it would only measure higher and we already knew the numbers were high.  They checked our levels and said it was within tolerance. So, we decided not to go to the hospital since the firemen said we should be fine.  The carbon monoxide detector went off again the following morning.  We did not call the fire department. We just did the same thing but stayed awake and went outside so it wouldn't have the same effect on us.  We purchased our Generac home standby almost a year ago and we have never had any issues until now.  I feel the protocol for installation should be changed so that the exhaust doesn't go up in the soffits of people's homes.  Two days after we had our issues a friend had the same exact problem with their home standby generac.  The installers said they followed the generac installation guidelines.
justification: The incident involved carbon monoxide exposure leading to headaches, indicating injury (severity 3). The recurrence with another household suggests the issue is likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: My glass shower door exploded spontaneously, just after I finished showering. I had turned off the water, moved the door to grab a towel and bang! Sounded like a gunshot. There were bits of glass everywhere in the bathroom and I had tiny pieces embedded in my skin. It took almost two hours to remove all the glass from my body with tweezers and tape. Even the tiniest flecks were very sharp, and would go into my skin while I was trying to remove them, leaving tiny spots of blood all over. Thankfully none in my eyes or sensitive areas, but my feet and hands had loads, as well as my right back and shoulders, which were facing the door. Where the towel covered me, it absorbed all the flecks of glass. Towel, broom, dustpan, bath mat, and all contents inside the shower had to be discarded because they were embedded with glass. Although the glass didn't form any large shards, the small bits were all extremely sharp and I have cut scabs everywhere. To be clear, the glass did not fall; in fact there was a top segment still remaining attached to the top rail. It just blew apart. Never again will I put glass shower doors in my home.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries from glass fragments embedded in the skin, requiring extensive removal and causing cuts and scabs, but no severe or life-threatening harm.

incident_description:
On Saturday, 06 July 2024, I was operating my Jet JPS-10TS table saw when, during the middle of a cut, the motor which powers the saw blade stopped working. Looked at the online instruction manual and found the need to press thermal reset switch on motor which is inside cavity of saw.  Pressed button, heard a click, went back to front of saw and pressed the "ON" button to complete my cut.  Later than day, the same thing occurred, and the motor stalled mid-cut.  Reached inside saw cavity to press reset button, heard the click, and the saw immediately started.  The blade made contact with my right hand and cut the right pinky finger.  Thankfully I was able to remove my hand from the saw cavity before any further damage occurred.  The outside edge of my right pinky had lost a small area of skin (1/4" by 1/4") and bled profusely.  Fortunately, no hospital visit was required, however it took nearly 24 hours for the bleeding to stop.  On Tuesday 09 July, I contacted manufacturer to ask why the saw immediately restarted after pressing the reset switch and to let them know I received a minor injury. The Jet representative was able to look up the machine in his database and determined the thermal reset switch for motor is mechanical.  This, when the reset button is pressed power will immediately start the motor and spin the blade. When I asked why this did not occur the first time the saw motor stalled, the representative said that because the reset switch in mechanical and not magnetic, the on/off switch needs to be powered off before pressing the reset switch. There is nothing in the owner's manual which gives instructions on the process to reset the motor.  The manual (Section 9.3) states: "If the saw becomes overloaded and the motor shuts off, push the reset button on the motor junction box (B, Figure 21) to restart."  However, on the saw I own, there is no motor junction box.  The reset switch is located on the actual motor which sits approximately 4 inches from the blade.  I did ask if there was a magnetic reset switch available (which would automatically turn the saw power off) and was told the newer models have them but the one I have (made in 2016) does not. I then asked about replacing the entire motor and switch assembly with the new style (which places the reset switch above the on/off switch and on the outside of the saw cavity. The representative said since the new saw style is not exactly the same as the one I own, retrofitting would not be possible.  The representative suggested I could contact an electrician who might be able to rewire the saw and relocate the reset switch.  Jet does not offer a trade in policy to purchase the upgraded model which has the reset switch located in a safer location and a magnetic style switch which will cut the power should the voltage drop during use.

Because of the actual location of the reset switch being so close to the saw blade, this really is a safety hazard.  Further, the owner's manual indicates the reset switch is in a different location than it actually is and makes no mention of a process to safely reset the switch. Due to the injury to myself, there is a risk that others may have a similar occurrence with the motor shutting off in the middle of a cut and upon pressing the reset switch may have a more serious injury than I received.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut to the pinky finger) but no hospital visit was required, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the described safety hazard and lack of proper instructions in the manual.

We opened the front of the dryer and it was full of burnt lint,including in the gas manifold where the fire goes.

incident_description:
Today for the second time in two weeks, my Yale/SmartRent "smart" front door lock locked me inside my apartment, with no mechanical fail safe, apparently due to low battery. This is a lock that can be opened via entering a key code and is installed on all doors in my building with no option to opt out. The deadbolt typically unlocks automatically when I turn the handle, but can also be toggled manually via a knob. In these two situations, neither option worked; the deadbolt would not disengage. Fortunately I have a second exit from my apartment directly onto the street (my unit is one of a very small percent with this feature) and I was able to exit without needing to unlock the door.

There were no injuries, but the lack of a mechanical fail safe on this device seems profoundly negligent. In the case of an emergency e.g. fire, earthquake, etc, this would be a massive safety issue.
justification: The incident caused no injury but poses a significant safety risk due to repeated lock failures and lack of mechanical fail-safe.

justification: The incident involved the hot water dispenser falling apart, posing a high risk of burns, but no injury occurred in this specific case. Reviews indicate similar incidents with some resulting in burns.

incident_description: Approximately 2AM, February 29th, 2024, our Generac whole house emergency generator turned on due to loss of mainline electrical power from [REDACTED]. Shortly thereafter, we were awakened to a huge noise coming from the kitchen. Upon heading to the kitchen, most of the lights were inoperative, even though we had a whole house generator. Only about 10% of the house lights turned on, and the ones that did were weak and/or surging. Most circuits were inoperative. Upon entering the kitchen, the [REDACTED] coffee maker had turned itself on and was spinning the water pump at a high shrill, well beyond the normal turn rate. It soon burned itself out and ceased operation. Upon checking the major appliances, minor appliances and lighting, over half of the house's systems were inoperative. We checked the 200AMP whole house circuit breaker panel and no breakers were tripped. The emergency generator was surging high and low upon inspection outside. We called our Generac installer electrician emergency on-call number and spoke to [REDACTED] from [REDACTED] (they also maintain the generator). [REDACTED] asked us to check various systems across the house and many were indeed inoperative, including some GFCI plugs would not reset. He had never heard of this happening and during the phone inspection, the mainline power returned and the Generac emergency generator powered down from the Automatic Transfer Switch. The light circuits returned across teh house, but about half of the appliances were burned out and inoperative. [REDACTED] came over at 7:30AM and then did an initial house inspection and appliance inspection. He determined the generator had low and high power outputs simultaneously being transmitted across both of its 2 phases. Generac eventually replaced the entire generator portion of the machine, since the motor was fine. Upon final inspections over the next month, the emergency generator caused surging electrical signals, both high and low and burned out most of our appliances and GFCI circuits to include: refrigerator, double electric oven, dishwasher, coffee maker, coffee brother, chandelier motor, 2 x alarm clocks, [REDACTED] bath pump and controls, gas heater glow plugs, lawn irrigation system, about 5 x GFCI switch panels, well pump, ultrasound cleaning pod, office paper shredder, plant LED lights, aura digital photo frame. Many of these appliances were "off". In addition, while no electrical fires occurred with the wiring, we are quite concerned the wiring itself has likely been heated/melted behind the walls somewhere and we have constant worry something else may happen. We have subsequently installed an emergency generator whole house surge protector at our own expense to attempt to stop any repeat from occurring. Generac Emergency Generator purchased through COSTCO, installed and maintained by [REDACTED] (a Generac-certified installer), 24KW with Automatic Transfer Switch, Model G0072090, Serial Number 3012186978.
justification: The incident caused significant damage to appliances and electrical systems but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I observed that our Harbor Breeze model fan was "listing" somewhat. Upon scaling a ladder and removing the decorative shroud around the "fan box" in the ceiling I observed that the fan had "slipped" one of its mounts in the mounting bracket over years of usage. I am unsure if the fan was improperly installed (a washer or screw with a wider head would have prevented the issue) or if the "slipping" through the mounting bracket was due to wear on the bracket from the screw during regular use. The entire fan assembly disengaged from the ceiling when I touched the mounting bracket. Had I not been up a ladder and waiting for it someone could have been killed.

This is a Harbor Breeze fan manufactured sometime between 2006 (year home was built) and 2017 (year we purchased the home). 

This was used about as typically as a fan could be. We did observe that it had a "rock" to it when operating shortly after moving in, but did not thing anything of it.

No injures thankfully, but it could have easily killed our toddler or infant if they had been under it when it fell.
justification: The fan disengaged and fell, but no injuries occurred. The potential for severe injury or death was present, especially for toddlers or infants.

When emptying the dryer, I got an electrical chock when I touched the inside of the drum while my elbow was in contact with  the rim of the opening. Using a multimeter I found that the drum is carrying full mains and after unplugging the dryer, that it is is connected to the hot lead of the plug. This can of course lead to a lethal electrical chock. The outer shell of the dryer is properly grounded. The dryer was previously under recall, as reported under [REDACTED] and was later serviced by LG. No other service has been performed on the dryer.

UPDATED ON 7/17/2024: [LG sent out a service technician on July 10th to see if they could make repairs to the dryer and IÃÂm assuming that they also wanted to collect additional information regarding the cause of the problem. I took a photo of the cause while the tech had the dryer opened, a photo of the same problem was also sent by the service tech to his supervisor at LG who also told him that they wouldnÃÂt repair the dryer as the damaged wiring harness no longer is available.

The attached photo shows the wiring harness that the previous LG tech forgot to clip in place, and which since has been rubbing against the outside of the drum until it wore through the insulation. Because the drum in this design is insulated and not grounded in any way, it ended up carrying the full 120V mains even with the dryer turned off. This is of course both a potentially lethal electrical hazard for anyone coming in contact with the drum and also a potential fire hazard if a buckle or other conductive object makes contact between the drum and the back or front which actually is grounded.

As of today (July 16) we have yet to hear back from LG regarding any additional actions from their side. We have been told  multiple times that their ÃÂPresidential LiaisonÃÂ will reach out, but they keep postponing any action from their side.]
justification: The incident involved an electrical shock but no injury was reported, and the potential for lethal shock or fire hazard is noted.

incident_description:
Hello,
 
Yesterday, [REDACTED], our pet cockatiel died. Our son, our family, is devastated. We need your help in determining if our new SPC flooring is safe even for us.
 
The SPC rigid core flooring is made by McMillan of Vancouver but produced in China. We bought 1000 square feet of this flooring from The Flooring Factory in Valencia, Ca. We chose the Serna XL design. As recommended, we used a 6 mil plastic sheeting as a moisture barrier. I installed the flooring myself since the process is simple and straightforward, especially using a vinyl plank chopper that was both quiet and clean compared to a saw.
 
The entire project took more than two months after the floor was delivered. Halfway through the installation, as I rounded the kitchen towards the family room where [REDACTED] cage is located, I heard him fall from his perch. As I checked on him, he was trying to move back up using his beak. My son and I knew something was terribly wrong and we decided to follow online advice to move him out of the house to my in-laws apartment. Within a few nervous hours, he recovered. By the following morning, [REDACTED] was back to his old self.
 
We decided to try to play it safe and move [REDACTED] back home to my sons upstairs room with his window wide open. We even blocked the bottom of the door with towels. This strategy worked and as we continued the project, we aired out the first floor by opening all our windows and sliding door. The flooring project was isolated on the first floor of our house.
 
I eventually finished the entire project in time for my sons graduation party held on Saturday, June 1.  With the house in order and cleaned with no more construction debris and dust, we decided to move [REDACTED] back to his cage in the family room. My son even wiped down his cage and organized it with fresh tray of bedding material made just for birds. Fresh food and water, his old toys and perches were organized into [REDACTED] home. My son was super excited to welcome him back to his home.
 
Yesterday, while in a meeting at work, I received a frantic call from my son saying that [REDACTED] was in trouble again. This time he was worst. I immediately drove home hoping and praying that [REDACTED] will bounce back once again.
 
I saw him with my son slumped down on a cloth bedding with one notable exception that my son pointed out to me- his legs were straight back. We were at the backyard at this point, trying desperately to give [REDACTED] fresh air to breathe. We moved him back to the proven safe place in my sons room because it was getting too hot outside.
 
A few minutes later, we heard the anguished cry from my son. My wife and I rushed upstairs to see our son with [REDACTED] lifeless body in his hands. He was inconsolable at that point. The same with my wife. My son had him since his freshman year in college, through out the pandemic, three universities, and most importantly, [REDACTED] was the one that held him together after our son lost {REDACTED], his weiner dog, to old age of 17 years last October.
 
Please help us in the following:
 
1. Determine what caused [REDACTED] death.
2. Is the manufacturer and distributor responsible.
3. Were regulations and standards of safety violated.
4. Should there be specific warnings about fumes and VOCs pertaining to birds and not just pets in general.
 
[REDACTED] was a very special pet. I believe my sons personality and amount of care and love he gives to all his pets contributed to [REDACTED] being so special. These two had a really strong and special bond. My son said that being an only child makes him rely on his pets even more. After losing [REDACTED], his dog, the loss of [REDACTED] is truly devastating. He kept on saying how young he was to pass. They, according to my son, live to their twenties. [REDACTED] was only seven years old. [REDACTED] is now at the vets clinic freezer waiting for cremation. I had a hold put on until we figure out what happened to him.
 
Please help us get answers for [REDACTED] and safety for other beloved pet birds.
 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a pet cockatiel, indicating the highest severity level for an animal.

incident_description:
I am reporting this incident because I was genuinely terrified. 

Product: Sun Squad Portable Fans (battery-operated handheld water misting fans). 

Both the fan blade and end cap popped off, exposing a blunt metal needle the length of an infant [REDACTED] syringe tip.

Full details of the event:
I purchased several Sun Squad handheld misting fans for a family party. It was purchased in-store at Target, beside Sun Squadpool toys and childrens flotation devices. I got these misting fans for the family (of varying ages, toddler to middle schooler). The end caps fell off during use but also easily pop off, exposing a protruding metal needle that spins. There are multiple hazards:

- The end caps can fall off, presenting a choking hazard.
- The caps are choking hazards.
- The protruding metal is a hazard.

There were no injuries during use, and I took them away. It was a terrifying experience. To be fair, you would think people would stop using a product when that happens, but they continued on. When the end caps came off, exposing the blunt needle, it didn't impact the functionality of the sprayer, so everyone continued using the product. 

The needle doesn't have a sharp tip. It is a metal needle the size of a syringe tip, protruding outward that doesn't retract. It could potentially injure an eye. The cap is a chocking hazard.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous product defect (exposed metal needle and choking hazard) but no injuries occurred during use.

Last week it brunt out the receiver it could have caused a fire in my condo I called the fire dept just to ask if I should be concerned but they said just shut off the switch so I did.  I had to replace that fan and pay again for installation.  This fan is dangerous and should not be sold to anyone.
justification: The fan malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred. The issue recurred multiple times, indicating a likely occurrence.
