incident_description:
Ordered rock crusher from Amazon. Product and seller in China. Product was so cheaply  made, it broke in several places over time. Six months in, the crusher is broken and the crushing plates won't stay in place and one of them shot out of the machine with force. It's dangerous and I feel Amazon isn't heading my warnings about this product. Here is the Amazon review I attempted to post but it disappeared. Also included is my latest chat conversation with Amazon Customer Service on two different occasions. I told Amazon a week ago, that the machine is disintegrating and not safe. It remains as of today, on their website. Here is the review I tried to submit:
I didn't want to do this but I feel compelled to after having tried to make the best of a bad situation over a period of about six months wherein this machine disassembled itself.
The seller refused to refund. Amazon refused to refund. I'm considering filing a complaint with the Consumer Safety office because the crushing plates won't stay in place and the rear one has flown out twice and once hit my husband's hand. 
First of all, the motor is not made for North American electrical standards and it doesn't come with a plug. After a couple of weeks of research and talking to an electrician, we put a plug on that worked. This wasn't mentioned clearly in the product description and after 300.00 dollars in shipping and handling costs.
NONE of the bolts or screws have lock washers and, after repeatedly tightening, one came out leading to damage to a bracket inside the chute that the ore is fed into. Debris kept jamming behind the bent bracket and became a constant problem.
Next, the adjustment knob for how fine rocks are crushed sheared. I went back and forth with the seller and finally agreed to a partial refund at that point and they sent us a new knob.
Next, the crushing plates began to come loose and detach completely. We tried everything to keep the bolts tight to no avail. The plates will NOT stay in. The rear plate came out of the crusher at a pretty high speed.
After dealing with the seller and Amazon denying us a refund of the balance - 700.00 - we have a 250 pound paperweight.

Garage Door Operators/Gate Operators | CPSC.gov

The Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act of 1990 (Improvement Act) mandated that automatic residential garage door operators (GDOs) manufactured on or after January 1, 1991 conform to the entrapment protection requirements of the 1988 version of UL 325. On June 19, 1991, the Commission issued the garage door operator standard (16 CFR Part 1211).
The Improvement Act provides that when UL makes changes to the entrapment protection provisions of UL 325, UL must notify the Commission of the proposed changes. Those changes must be incorporated into the Commission rule unless the Commission notifies UL within 30 days that the Commission has determined the revisions do not carry out the purposes of the Improvement Act. The mandatory safety rule has been changed two times since it was first issued in 1991.

Since 1991 garage doors have been required to come equipped with a mechanism that auto-reverses the door when it comes into contact with an object.  
Homeowners with automatic garage door openers that do not automatically reverse should repair or replace them with new openers which do reverse to prevent young children from being trapped and killed under closing garage doors.
According to reports received by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), approximately 60 children between the ages of 2 and 14 have been trapped and killed under automatic garage doors since March 1982. incident_description:
We installed a Taco 5000 mixing valve to regulate water coming out of our domestic hot water heater to a safe temperature. Even though the thermostat on the water heater is set to 120F, the thermostat's temperature sensor is located in the center of the tank, so, due to water heater stratification, when the tank sits unused for a few hours, the water at the top of the tank, where the water exits, can reach temperatures of 150F or more.


Water heater stratification is a common problem with water heaters. The usual solution is to install a valve, known as a mixing valve, to automatically mix the hot water with cold water to reduce the water temperature to a safe temperature of 120F or less.


There are many manufacturers of water mixing valves. I purchased one made by Taco, a large manufacturer of plumbing products with a good reputation. However, we had problems with this valve from the beginning, when we first installed the water heater and Taco 5000 mixing valve in 2006. The temperature of the mixed water coming out of the valve seemed to vary considerably, sometimes reaching levels of heat that were unsafe.


Thinking that our original valve was somehow not working properly I replaced it with a new version of the same valve two years ago, in 2019. But the problems persisted even with the new valve. I did note similar complaints from other users on various web sites.


I finally decided to investigate the problem by gathering data. I installed digital temperature sensors on the hot inlet and mixed outlet ports of the Taco 5000. I found that the valve does not perform in a safe manner, because, once activated by water flow, it takes more than two minutes for the valve to reduce the output temperature to 120F, and even when it reaches 120F it is quite unstable, varying plus or minus 5F.


I replaced the Taco 5000 mixing valve with a [REDACTED] mixing valve. The [REDACTED] valve works absolutely perfectly.


IÃÂve posted videos on [REDACTED] of the Taco 5000 and [REDACTED] mixing valves in operation. The videos demonstrate exactly what I am talking about.


Taco 5000: [REDACTED]

justification: Electrical burning and charred insulation indicate an incident with potential for injury, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Home Depot Milwaukee 1,000 lbs. Capacity 4-in-1 Hand Truck
Internet #203875537
Model #60137
Store SKU #1000000836
Store SO SKU #1000592977
Hand Truck Frame Latch releases when any torque is applied to the frame such as going over a threshold or up steps.  The load is launched forward causing damage to the product on the dolly and injury to the user.  This item is going to kill someone if it happens on a set of stairs with a heavy load.  Please get this VERY dangerous product off the market immediately before someone is killed trying to use it to lift 1,000lbs.  I had maybe 60lbs on the dolly and it let go striking me in the face and crashing the load to the ground.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that it snowed approximately four inches in his hometown and all grounds were covered in it. The consumer tried to open his patio sliding door to go outside however it would not budge as the track that the door slides on is located outside of his home and was blocked by the wet snow. 

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to informed him they could not assist him as that was the design of the door.

The consumer notes his previous sliding doors had the track inside his home thus he never experienced this issue. The consumer is concerned because the door could leave him and his family trapped inside in an emergency.

The consumer plans on keeping the sliding door for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involves a blocked sliding door due to snow, posing a potential safety risk but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(6/6/2020)The consumer stated that this is the third replacement for his original Whirlpool washing machine, He has had the same issue with all three. The lid lock malfunctions. When this happens, the consumer get a code. The consumer unplugs the unit at the outlet but when he plugs it back into the electrical outlet, sparks comes from the outlet.

The consumer stated that he has not been able to use his washing machine for four months.

The consumer contacted the firm who ordered a part. But they are now saying that the part in on back-order. The consumer thinks that he is being given the run-around.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washing machine causing sparks, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: My TRANE XV80 Furnace had a malfunction on January 9, 2021. An electronics diagram sticker, the size of a piece of paper, was inside of this device, came loose, and was being sucked into the blower fan. This furnace is installed at my house, in a basement room. We were made aware of the problem when the furnace turned on and was making a strange banging noise. The installing company was called to inspect the furnace, and they found the sticker in the blower area. No one was hurt in this process.  In my opinion, this sticker should not have been located inside the machine where it can come loose. My concern is that it might have damaged my machine or caught on fire if we had not turned off the device and made a service call.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction with no injury, and the likelihood of such an event is possible given the description of the sticker coming loose.

incident_description: Top of washer blew off while on spin cycle with minimal load in it. Washer top contacted wall on one side and the dryer on the other side in the process of blowing off the washer. Witness marks were noticed on surrounding materials.
justification: The washer top blew off and caused damage to surrounding materials, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I attempted to test the emergency release pull cord for the garage door opener at my elderly father's home.  The opener unit, and the original factory installed release cord are about 7 years old and in otherwise excellent condition. The pull cord immediately broke about 2 inches above the "T" handle.  I grabbed the remaining cord and tried again.  The cord broke a second time, and the remaining cord is about 7 feet off the floor, the same height as the garage door,.

This is a health and safety risk! We live in So. California, where wildfires and rolling blackouts can be a regular thing. This pull cord is bright red, and seems made of a synthetic fiber.  While is is subject to ambient temperatures that frequently exceed 100 degrees F in the closed garage in the summer, it is never in direct sunlight and never is subject to moisture.  I may in fact be the first person to ever try pulling the cord since it's original installation in about 2013.

My father worked in aerospace, where nylon parachute cord was in regular use.  I am an avid camper and backpacker.  We both know that quality materials would not degrade as this cord has.  Yet had I not tested it, my father, or others like him, could have become entrapped in their own homes without means to evacuate in an emergency because of this kind of defect. 

The garage door opener is a Marantec 4500e.
justification: The cord broke during testing, indicating a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that his air conditioner was on for about ten minutes when he noticed that it was smoking. The consumer immediately unplugged the unit and took it outside; by this time it had already stopped smoking.

Three weeks later the consumer inspected the air conditioner and noticed that the motherboard, several wires, and some fuses were burnt. The consumer tried to fix the unit and although it did hum, the fan or compressor would not turn on.

The consumer states that the unit is used during warmer months roughly three times per week for about two to three hours each use.

The consumer plans on keeping his air conditioner for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The air conditioner smoked but caused no injury, and the issue was contained without further incident.

incident_description: Laceration to foot/ toe resulted when I stepped onto the lowest step of our Cal Premium 30" - 3 tier spa steps. The step completely cracked in half and perpendicular to middle break.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The step cracking is a possible but not frequent occurrence.

incident_description: I bought a Werner 32' fiberglass extension ladder in 2019.  I used it three times in total and was always garage kept, out of weather and UV light.  While using the product on the 3rd time while hanging a security light on the house I noticed a crack in rail next to one of the rungs.   No injuries occurred as I got off the ladder immediately after noticing it.
justification: A crack was noticed in the ladder rail, but no injuries occurred as the user got off immediately.

incident_description: I have a 2013 Bullfrog spa that has the drain suction cover model #640-52xx.  they all have come off for no reason.  I checked them out and the screws are completely stripped out and will not tighten. My wife informed of this and when got in tub and tried to screw them back on the screw just slides in and out.
justification: The incident involves a mechanical failure (drain suction cover coming off) with no reported injury or harm.

incident_description: My laundry took fire due to the battery of the Dyson Cordless Vacuum exploded. This fire killed my dog. Fire investigator report said the fire was cause by the Dyson's battery. My insurance company ([REDACTED]) is currently with the Dyson doing a technical investigation. The Dyson was installed in the wall as per instructions. I had been using the vacuum daily.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a dog due to a fire caused by the Dyson vacuum's battery.

incident_description: Lennox natural gas fireplace exploded.  Fireplace was on and working when there was a loud pop and bang shattering the protective glass.  I turned off the gas to the fireplace immediately.  No injuries occurred.  Lennox model# DR3530CNM-2.  Lennox Serial # 6301J01373
justification: The fireplace exploded but no injuries occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I discovered a stress crack approximately 6 inches long in the aluminum alloy air tank of a Ryobi brand portable air compressor.  This air tank is rated to hold up to 150 psi of pressure. The crack is located on the top of the tank and if the tank is filled with compressed air as designed, it will eventually explosively rupture causing serious injury or death to the operator and any bystanders. Fortunately, I discovered the crack before operating the air compressor and pumping compressed air into the tank.  As this is a potentially lethal flaw in their product, I contacted Ryobi customer service immediately at 800-525-2579 on 9/21/2020.  I spoke with a customer service representative who acknowledged the seriousness of my concern and stated that a company safety representative would contact me shortly.  I received no contact from Ryobi so I again called their customer service number and spoke to a different representative on 10/1/2020.  She indicated that they had a record of my earlier call and that someone from their safety department would contact me.  When I told her that this was a potentially fatal defect in their product, she replied that the normal time to respond was two weeks and that they were "very busy".   I then informed her that I read the federal law related to potentially hazardous products and that Ryobi was required to inform the CPSC within 24 hours of receiving my report. She again stated that they were "very busy in the Safety Department" and that someone would contact me soon.  As of 10/15/2020, I have received no contact from anyone at Ryobi regarding their hazardous defective product.
justification: The stress crack in the air tank poses a severe risk of explosive rupture, which could lead to death or serious injury if the tank is pressurized, but no incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: Above stove steam cleaning Range hood water container melted
justification: The incident involved a melted water container, which is a material issue but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: I sprayed Folex spot remover on some spilled soy sauce. My 11 yr old granddaughter wiped it up with a clean damp rag and immediately experienced burning and redness on both hands. I contacted the company for an ingredient list in order to treat the reaction properly and was denied any information due to the ÃÂproprietary natureÃÂ of the product. Additionally, they deflected by saying it was not poisonous or toxic and that they have fulfilled their duty by including a ÃÂKeep out of the reach of childrenÃÂ warning on the bottle. Owner stated that he has bathed in and drank this product and nothing ever happened. I repeated multiple times that I just wanted to be sure I was treating the reaction safely by rinsing with water since the company fails to disclose any ingredients on their packaging or website regarding products manufactured prior to 2020. He even went so far as to question the contents of the bottle being his product! This company should be held to a standard in order to ensure the best chance for safety to users. Instead he deflects and blames the victim.

justification: The incident caused property damage (deck and fireplace) but no human injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but possible with faulty equipment.

incident_description: I want to report multiple failures of the Culligan WH-HD200-C Whole House Heavy Duty water filter.  This unit has failed and Culligan refuses to honor the 2 year warranty of the product. The failure is insidious and can go undetected until substantial water damage and mold has occurred. These units are installed at the main water line coming into houses and businesses and often in areas that are seldom visited. The leak starts with a very small pin prick from the plastic head unit that accepts the filter bowl. The leak then gets progressively faster and leaks more water.  I have contacted product support and they require me to hire a plumber to test the water pressure coming from a city water line.
justification: The incident describes property damage (water damage and mold) but no mention of injury or death, warranting a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the described progressive nature of the leak and potential for widespread installation.

incident_description: Lid on top-loading Maytag washer fails to stay in open position because lid underside is made of plastic and has completely deteriorated after only one year of use.  The machine is not safe and should be recalled because the defective lid can fall and injure an adult or child.  The lid needs to be replaced with a new lid made of a different material that will not deteriorate.  The small plastic parts also break off and fall into the washer and become attached to clothing.  Model MVWB865GC
justification: The deteriorating lid poses a risk of injury if it falls, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: I was using a Ryobi quarter sheet sander model number S651D when I heard a loud pop and felt a sharp pain. Part of the lower right side had blown out and hit me in the stomach.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (sharp pain from being hit by a blown-out part), but such failures are unlikely for most users.

incident_description: On 3/25/21 the heater was turned on and after a few seconds stopped working.  The plug was checked and showed the outlet has burn damage. Also the plug itself had burn damage around it's metal connection site.  See upload photos.
justification: The incident involved burn damage to the heater plug and outlet, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that in order to activate the preinstalled battery of his carbon monoxide alarm he needs to remove a tab. When the consumer pulled the tab, an explosive noise was immediately emitted and the consumer went deaf on both of his ears. Two weeks later his hearing had not improved so he visited the Veterans Affairs, where testing came back showing that he had severe hearing loss on his left ear that needed hearing aid. The consumer was fitted with hearing aid on both ears as his right ear was also damaged but not as much as his left one.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; a representative e-mailed him apologizing for what happened but indicating that they have no idea how what happened could have occurred.

The consumer notes that there is no warning information on the alarm on on its instructions manual about a possible sound hazard.

The consumer plans on keeping his alarm for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The consumer suffered severe hearing loss requiring hearing aids, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: Pittsburgh,PA  Purchased Lennox Model EL296UH090XE48C furnace on 12/2017. Exposed homeowner,young family of 5, to carbon monoxide poisoning 2020 thru March 2021. More toxic level in last 3 months.Family sickened, various health issues.  Admiral Heating installed 88,000BTU for a 60,000BTU house. Heat exchanger possibly cracked. Lennox only concerned for Admiral Heating since they purchase many furnaces. Not interested in investigating cause. Admiral Heating refused to replace with proper size furnace or refund.Lennox allowed Admiral to call the shots. Lennox offered contractor refund to give to injured party. Admiral Heating refused.
justification: The family experienced various health issues due to carbon monoxide poisoning, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description: My front door has an Arrow bolt lock, A62 3.  The bolt became disengaged from the arm that operates it within a cylinder.  Normally, this bolt can only be removed when the door is open.  The two screws holding a plate that is attached to the cylinder containing the bolt are removed and the assembly is pulled out.  In this case, since the bolt held the door closed could not be extracted, it was impossible to get the door open.  This is obviously a safety hazard since it would prevent escape from the home.  I was, with about an hour's effort, able to force the cylinder open and to back the bolt out so the door could be opened.  I contacted Arrow, but their technical person said this was a rare occurrence, but would not indicate how often it happens or what the consequences had been in other cases.
justification: The incident describes a safety hazard that could prevent escape, but no injury or death occurred. The manufacturer indicated it is a rare occurrence.

incident_description:
I scalded/burned my foot as I was placing the filled water tank back onto the base unit of the humidifier.  As I turned the newly filled tank of water over and held the handle, the handle separated from the tank and fell onto the base unit that still had hot water in it.  The base unit tipped over landing on my slippered foot, completely saturating my slipper with scalding hot water and after some confusion of not realizing what happened, I saw I burned my foot.
My foot was burned with what I think was a 1st to 2nd degree burn.
justification: The incident resulted in a 1st to 2nd degree burn, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: On 03/20/2021at approximately 2 P.M., while working on my deck at my home in Altha, Florida a safety malfunction occurred while using an angle grinder.  A 7-inch angle grinder malfunctioned causing injury to my left hand and nearly caused serious life threatening injury to my left leg.   Cummins made the 7-inch Angle Grinder number 6761 for sale at Harbor Freight Tools stores.  The grinder is several years old, not sure of year purchased.  While in a squatting position and holding the grinder with one hand, I plugged the grinder into a 110-volt extension cord.  As soon as the grinder was plugged in, the grinder started at its maximum speed.  The torque of the tool and the surprise of the tool starting caused the grinder to fall into my lap and caused me to fall backward onto my rear.  I had a 7-inch metal cutoff blade mounted onto the grinder, which started cutting through my double layer military style pants and leg.  I quickly raised my left hand up to protect myself and to push the running angle grinder from my lap.  I received a deep cut to the thumb on my left hand and various small cuts and lacerations to the area between my waist to my knees.  Some of the lacerations were near the femoral artery on my left leg and crotch area.  This malfunction could have been deadly sense there would have been catastrophic loss of blood due to the proximity to the femoral artery and crotch, and the fact that I am on blood thinners.  After returning home from receiving care at the emergency room, I examined the grinder to determine what caused the accident.  Examination revealed that the button used to lock the grinder trigger in the run position was stuck in the on position.  Normally if the ÃÂLock-onÃÂ button is engaged, by squeezing the trigger the ÃÂLock-onÃÂ button is supposed to disengage.  This did not happen because the ÃÂLock-onÃÂ button had malfunctioned and would not release.  I talked to the local manager of the Harbor Freight Store on 03/22/2021.  He said he could do nothing since there was no recall on these grinders and that it was older than 90 days old.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut to the thumb and multiple lacerations, indicating an injury, but no death occurred.

incident_description: Since having a NEW gas hot water tank installed 8/14/2015 I have experienced water leaking from my Pressure Relief valve.  I replaced Pressure Relief valve in 2017. I continue to have issues with leaking from Pressure Relief valve. Yesterday 02/21/2021, while checking PSI of my Utilitech Model: LET2 100 expansion tank air valve, water came out of air valve. I then knew my expansion tank bladder had failed. This is an extremely dangerous product failure that could possibly cause massive property damage, injury and/or death. VERY HIGH RISK OF EXPLOSION!
justification: The description indicates a potential for explosion, which could lead to injury or death, but no actual incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: Burning smell from hot water heater after it wasn't working well.
justification: Burning smell indicates a potential issue but no injury or damage reported.

incident_description: We have a Whirlpool range hood, model UXT5230BDS1, serial number XH92594764, that was installed in our new home in mid 2019 by Pulte Corporation. On December 1st I was at the stove cooking when the right hood light exploded sending glass shards in every direction. Fortunately I was not hurt. I reported it to Whirlpool and a case was opened, case # [REDACTED]. Whirlpool has indicated that they would replace the light but nothing has happened. This is a flaw with the type of glass used as the lens. It should be some type of safety glass. Had a shorter person like my wife been there more than likely she would have been seriously hurt. Possible glass in the eye.
justification: The incident involved an exploding light with no injury, but potential for serious harm if conditions were different.

incident_description: An adult male works in an elementary school cafeteria. He saw a product labeled "Cherry" sitting on the floor and put it inside the refrigerator. The next day he took it out to have a drink. He immediately noticed it was a cleaner.
justification: The adult male ingested a cleaner, which constitutes an injury due to potential harm from chemical exposure.

incident_description: The fan metal bracket broke causing the fan blade to sling off and put a humongous gash into wall.
justification: The incident caused property damage (a gash in the wall) but no injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased Item 62295, Cobalt High Speed Steel Drill Bit Set from Harbor Freight Inc. They state that they are also the manufacturer of the product. On 2 occasion, while drilling into steel pipe, the drill bit broke. One was a 1/2 inch and the other a 25/64 inch, and they were drilling straight without any sideways torque or angulation; one incident occurred when using a drill press, so the bit was unambiguously going straight down. On that occasion, since I was pressing down on the drill press handle, the broken end of the bit continued down and I suffered a severe injury to my thumb. These drill bits are hazardous and should not be for sale.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury to the thumb, which warrants a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue happened twice under normal usage conditions.

incident_description: Flames blow out of the front of the water heater when it lights and the flame runs with a sputtering sound.  The flames blew out directly in our faces as were were investigating the sputtering sound.  This water heater is already subject to recall, but two online registration attempts have been ignored and calls to the toll free number are either disconnected after a recording plays or you are left on indefinite hold that is never answered.
justification: Flames blew out directly in faces, indicating a hazardous incident but no reported injury.

incident_description:
(02/01/2021) The consumer stated that his wife put a load of clothes in the machine. They left the house. When they returned, the consumer was told by a person that was in the basement that there was a loud noise. The  person did not investigate the noise. 

When the consumer went to the laundry room to check, he saw that the outside of the washing machine was bent. When he looked inside of the product,  it looked as if the drum had come off of the track.  Everything on the inside of the product is busted and the washing machine door cannot be closed.
justification: The incident involved damage to the washing machine but no injuries or fatalities were reported.

incident_description:
We have a SAMSUNG front loader washing machine and dryer purchased 11/172020. During the self clean phase the glass in the door of the washer exploded spraying water and glass all over our laundry room

The SAMSUNG washer exploded blowing the glass door out.  This left glass and water all over the floor and glass water inside the machine.  This happened during the self- clean cycle.  Anyone walking by or in the laundry room would have been hit by the glass leading to, at a minimum, cuts over their body and possibly hospitalization.  

Purchased Model WF45T6000AW from Best Buy on 10 Nov 2020 received 17 Nov 2020. On 20 Feb 2021 I noticed the writing on the front panels of the washer had smeared.  Called in a request for Service appointment was set for 1 Mar 2021.  On 27 Feb after washing a load the machine flashed the self-clean button.  (This is supposed to be done after every 40 loads.).  I put the wet clothes in the dryer and then cut on the self-clean cycle.  I left the laundry room and five minutes later the machine exploded.  There was glass and water all over our laundry room floor and inside the machine.  I was thankful I was not in the room.  I called this in immediately after my husband and I cleaned up the laundry room.  The SAMSUNG rep told us he was amending our repair order to include this problem.  When the repair person arrived on 1 Mar, he didn't see anything about the explosion on his order, but he took pictures, forwarded them to SAMSUNG and waited on their guidance.  They would only replace the panel with the smeared writing.  They refused to authorize the repair of the rest of the machine.  I had to call several times after this to try and get the entire machine repaired or replaced or receive a complete refund.  The appliance repair company is scheduled to come out a second time on 11 March.  This machine scares us because no one at SAMSUNG seems concerned about WHY it exploded!  They told me since no one was hurt they must try and repair it instead of just issuing a refund.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing significant damage but no injuries, as no one was present in the room at the time.

incident_description: I bought a "4 pack of Magnetic Cord Holders". I got one out to use and left the other 3 in the package to use at a later time. My 20 month old daughter found the package and chewed on one causing her to ingest two magnets that easily came out, although I was unaware they could come out. There is no labeling on the package to include about  a warning of the magnets possibly able to come out, danger to children, choking hazard, NOTHING. Only a warning for "cancer and reproductive harm." This ended in my child having to go to the emergency room to be xrayed multiple times, transported by ambulance to a children's hospital in another state, and being admitted to the hospital for IV treatment and to be closely monitored. Luckily the two had joined together early to where they were stuck together and are currently passing through her intestines. This could have resulted in surgery to remove the magnets. I do not want this to happen to another child. Is there anything that can be done?
justification: The child ingested magnets, required emergency medical treatment, and was hospitalized, indicating a significant injury but no death.

incident_description: 6 month old water heater failed. Co suggested it's a part that they know isn't the problem, but the real problem part has failed in so many units, it's nationally back-ordered. They claimed it's the pilot light assembly, sent a warranty replacement, which did not fix the problem. They now claim to be "building" a gas control valve for me, which is the part that everyone but the consumer seems to know is the problem.
justification: The incident involves a product failure with no reported injury or death, but the issue is widespread and parts are back-ordered, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: Using a recently purchased outdoor patio heater, in a pyramid design.  Using it for the fourth time at night, was trying to confirm if it was producing any discernable heat (it wasn't).  Pretty visual with the burner at the base, a steel pyramid  tower on four sides with visible glass tube from the burner to the top of the unit where the heat is presumably intended to release.  Video taping flame simply because it looked cool.  Over course of taping flame observed greater intensity burning, which I first assumed meant the unit was finally working correctly and would produce proper heat.  Then I noticed that it appeared the flame was no longer coming from the burner but  from an area around the perimeter of the burner, within the housing of the unit.  Intensity increased.  I went to shut off the gas from the plastic valve that is part of the unit.  The fire continued.  At this point I saw that the fire was coming from the end of the regulator hose that had been attached to the unit.  The rubber hose was burning slowly .  I estimated I had sufficient time to reach in and turn-off the propane canister - which I did.  The flame at the end of the regulator hose extinguished.  I had a minor burn to my hand that did not require medical attention and is fine.  There was no property damage beyond the unit itself.  The unit was on our backyard stone patio, about 10-12 feet from our home.  (I tried to file this report the night of the incident but when I went to attached the video files the system crashed and I had to start all over again.  The videos are telling and I can try to provide them separately but not with this report.  I am the homeowner and I was the only one using the unit at the time of the incident.  The prospects of injury seemed high had the fire continued to burn given that the flame was coming directly from the hose/regulator assembly that attaches to the propane tank.  The manual with the unit is titled:  "Quartz Glass Tube Patio Heater."  Oddly, the manual itself has no contact information nor does it identify any business or other entity.  The item was purchased from the Amazon.com website.  The item is listed as "Pyramid Outdoor Patio Heater - 45000 BTU Stainless Steel Propane Heater with Cover, Glass Tube"  When I spoke to Amazon to obtain the seller contact information to advise of this incident I was told that the company name was just a trade name and they did not have (or could not provide) a seller's name to me.  Via an exchange  with the Seller on Amazon platform seller simply indicated a refund had been granted and they would "check with factory."  I replied that i had specific information and was concerned about the product remaining available and in use.  No reply.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn to the hand, which did not require medical attention, fitting the severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) given the described malfunction and potential for similar incidents with the product.

incident_description: Door chime broke apart with brittle plastic leaving metal prong exposed and creating risk of electric shock
justification: Exposed metal prong poses a risk of electric shock, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: My 2 story home was on fire, nothing left due to using the Lasko ceramic 1500 watt heater, model # 751320  My family is now homeless, I will not stop until every unit is off the shelfs and I will seek funding for a home for my family. incident_description: My family and I were relaxing at home one evening when we heard a loud explosion accompanied by the sound of crunching metal; like that of a vehicle collision. The whole house shook and the sound was so loud that my wife and I were immediately alarmed and ran to check on our young children. Upon investigation, I discovered that our top-load GE washing machine (GTW750CSL1WS) had violently spun around in our laundry room with enough force to significantly damage the dryer and utility sink that were on each side of the washer. It was evident that the washer's heavy drum had become separated from the unit during a spin cycle which caused the whole machine to explode. The top was blown off and the sides blasted outward with such force that they appear to be damaged beyond repair. Fortunately, no one was injured but I am filing this report out of concern for other consumers. I am shocked to know that if my one-year old or any other member of my family had been in the laundry room or in the doorway when this event had occurred, they could have been killed or seriously injured given the obvious, violent force of the washing machine explosion and spin. Also of concern, broken pieces of sharp plastic were found in the laundry room after having been forcefully ejected and some were even found in the room across the hallway from the laundry room door.  Furthermore, golf-ball sized plastic knobs that sit underneath the top of the washer had been thrown from the washer. The washing machine also flung a brown, smelly sludge over the clothes inside the drum and on the walls and floor of the laundry room. Finally, it is important to note that the cycle in the washing machine was just a normal, small load of white dish towels and underwear and this GE washing machine was only 19 months old.

So they don't move freely, there is some sort of tensioner inside where they connect that add tension and prevent the lid from moving freely and dropping. Only issue is these metal hinges are then housed inside the plastic lids and over time the plastic isn't strong enough to continue to house these metal hinges and it breaks down eventually to the point where the hinges just bust out of the plastic lid. I had just finished loading a wash and I went to close the lid to be able to start the load and the plastic area of the lid holding the hinge in pretty much cracked and popped open and the hinge busted through. When this happened plastic did shoot off and just barely missed shooting me in the eye. It instead hit my face and bounced off thankfully. At this time the glass lid was also freed from its housing within the lid unit and almost slipped and fell to the ground. Fortunately I was able to catch it in time. My belief is this issue causes a potential safety issue due to the fact the glass can break and cause serious injury as well as the projectile plastic shooting off when it breaks could cause injury to the face and or eyes. Since you cannot predict when this may occur the only way to be safe is to wear safety goggles while doing laundry. I also believe this is a defect in the design because after it happened I went to do research and found that it seemed to be a very common break on the machine and there were numerous complaints about this happening. It even seemed to happen more frequently with the left hinge and that's exactly the one thst burst out first in my case too. I have alerted Samsung to this defect but they have refused to acknowledge it as such and claimed that the damage was "extreme physical damage" due to user error and thus they would not originally cover the repair under my extended warranty I purchased. incident_description:
Following is my review of the Insinkerator SST instant hot water heater on the Walmart website, that explains the issue.  There were no injuries, but there is likely a potential for electric shock or  fire.  UPC number and manufacturing date are not shown on the product.  I can't remember where purchased--it was an on-line website.
"[Name Redacted], in his March 2020 review on the Walmart website, got it right:  the Insinkerator SST under-sink instant water heater has a design flaw, with the vinyl tube that is in contact with the hot water tank getting brittle and cracking, causing a water leak.  After reading the review, I opened up my ~5-year-old leaking SST unit and sure enough--the tube was exactly as described in the review:  discolored dark brown and had a hard scabby cracked area where it contacted the tank, that was the source of the leak (see photo).  The leak caused water to drip on the electrical components below the tank.  Any time that electrical components get wet, there is a presumed possibility of hazards such as shock and fire.  Not to mention water damage to kitchen cabinetry.
[Name Redacted] noted that he spliced a length of copper tube in place of the vinyl tube and has had several years of satisfactory leak-free service from his unit.  But it may not be a good idea to continue using any electrical device that has had its electrical components drenched in water.  I did some research, and it looks like vinyl tubing has a maximum temperature limit of around 140 to 160 degrees F, which makes it obvious that vinyl tubing is inappropriate for contact with a hot water tank at near-boiling water temperature (212 F).  The Insinkerator engineers couldn't figure this out?  Perhaps food-grade silicone tubing, with a temperature limit of over 400F, well above water boiling point, might be a better design choice."
justification: The description reports a design flaw causing water leaks and potential electrical hazards, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: I bought a Bissel vacuum about 2 months ago. Model number: 2492 Serial number: 2023301925e The other day, I was vacuuming and it started to smoke. incident_description: "Future Glue", purchased at Ace Hardware.  I opened the soft metal tube very carefully and thought I had none on my hands but as soon as I touched the tube, my fingers stuck to it and began to hurt as if I had a strong acid on them--minor problem. Next,  I applied glue to a plastic surface but it would not dry. Instructions mentioned that the glue does not work on two types of plastic but I had no idea what type I was working with. The glue would not dry on the plastic surface that I was working with. I tried blowing hot air on it. It immediately emitted a strong odor from a gas that came from the glue. I removed the hot air as fast as I could because I was afraid it would permeate the whole room. The gas reacted with my fingers, eyes, nose lining and lungs with a severe  burning sensation. This was not mild like getting soap in one's eyes. It was like the gas was chemically reacting to the areas it came in contact with and was very severe. To use this product safely, one would need to be wearing lots of safety equipment and be outside to safely use it.  It is hard for me to believe that the general public could use this stuff safely in their homes. I threw the remaining tube in the trash with some apprehension about what it might come in contact with in the environment. I find it hard to believe that this material could even be safely manufactured.
justification: The incident caused severe burning sensations in multiple body parts due to chemical reaction with the glue's gas, indicating injury.

incident_description:
Purchased a Bissell Crosswave (model 1785) in Dec of 2017. Had numerous problems with 1st machine, including giving me a small, stray electric shock when touching the revolving floor brush with machine plugged in, even though the machine was turned off. Bissell replaced the 1st machine. Second machine had several slightly-different problems in addition to the same small electric shock problem and failed within 6 months of replacing the 1st machine. Over the course of our two-year warranty from Bissell they  replaced the second and third machine under their warranty. Fortunately we purchased an extended warranty through [REDACTED] when we purchased the original Crosswave, so when the 4th Crosswave failed, we contacted [REDACTED], since Bissell's two-year warranty had just expired the month before the 4th machine failed. We expected [REDACTED] to repair our Crosswave, however [REDACTED] replaced it with a different Crosswave (our FIFTH Crosswave machine, possibly "factory refurbished", but I'm not sure of that).
This morning as I was using the latest Crosswave I thought I could smell smoke, but the machine was operating normally, so I continued to use it.  A few minutes later the Crosswave blew out a large puff of smoke, so I immediately shut it off. As soon as I shut it off I could hear a crackling sound coming from the lower part of the machine- the housing for the spinning floor brush. I then immediately unplugged the machine! 
A few minutes later after the crackling noise had stopped I removed the clear brush cover to check the spinning floor brush. Not only was the floor brush clean but it also spun freely, without any unusual resistance. In other words the floor brush was able to be spun normally.
I then plugged the machine back into a GFCI outlet, which immediately tripped. I unplugged the machine, reset the GFCI outlet and tried plugging the Crosswave in again, but the GFCI outlet again tripped off immediately.
It is now very obvious to me that our Crosswave would very likely have caught on FIRE if I hadn't unplugged it! The fact that it immediately tripped a GFCI outlet indicates that there is a serious electrical problem, which I firmly believe would have eventually caused our Crosswave to ignite and burn down our home!
This is not the first complaint that I have filed about these machines! I filed a similar complaint about the electric shock hazard, and had hoped to add this latest problem to that complaint, but I was unable to find it.
justification: The incident involved a machine emitting smoke and nearly catching fire, posing a serious risk, but no injury or death occurred.

I went to emergency where the treated me, then they sent me a referral to an ophthalmologist at Prisma health in Columbia SC. They tested my vision and I now need glasses. incident_description: My HoMedics UHE-WM350 Humidifier began to give off an electrical smell.  It was still running.  Since it sits on a Hardwood floor, I have an oval plant tray underneath in case of leaks.  The tray was full and slightly overflowing (maybe a pint of liquid).  I unplugged the unit.  I emptied the tanks and thoroughly dried the unit overnight.  I inspected the water channels under the tanks and the membrane for obvious cracks or leaks and found none.  I plugged the unit back in to see if it powered up.  It did.  I refilled the tanks, restarted it, and watched it carefully,  the same thing happened again.  I decided that the unit needed to be retired.  Out of curiousity,  I opened the fairing and discovered affected electronics from an unidentified internal leak.  The affected electronics were high in the compartment, and there is some sort of tray/cover that shows and ongoing leak.  The rust makes it appear that this was an ongoing issue, and a very likely fire hazard.  I contacted HoMedics via email with pictures. incident_description:
We had a Navien tankless  hot water heater, model number NPE 240-A, serial number 7414D1472181250. It was approximately six years old, and has now been replaced. On November 24, 2020 my wife was taking a shower, and called out to me that the water was getting cold. I immediately went into the utility room and saw that the water heater was running, apparently normally, but with an obvious (and red hot) burn mark on the cover. I immediately pulled the plug on the water heater and turned off the gas supply.
The sight glass had blown out, burning the cover and a wire. Had I not reacted quickly, it appears that the cover would have been burned clear through, I have no idea how far flame would have projected into the utility room, or what the consequences may have been, but it is quite clear from viewing the inside of the cover that this was going to happen. With no water being heated, the water heater controls would likely continue to call for heat, and the flame shooting into the utility room would have continued. Yet the reaction from Navien is not at all one of concern, but rather dismissal.  This could have resulted in a fire, and/or carbon monoxide poisoning. Had a plumber or service technician been working on this unit at the time, using the sight glass for its intended purpose, their face and eye would have been severely burned, rather than the steel cover. See the photo of the inside of the steel cover, and imagine if that had been someone's face instead. With just a quick internet search, I was able to determine that this is not a new or unique problem, as someone else had posted a photo more than a year earlier.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard and risk of severe injury, but no actual injury or death occurred.

This broke and cracked the lid. Now the left corner has done exactly the same thing. I use my washer on a daily basis. And I have only had it about 2 years. Nothing has been put on top of the washer and the lid stays shut when not in use. There is no logical reason for this to have happened. This is the 2nd samsung product purchased in the last five years that I have had issues with. I love this washer but dont feel I should have to replace the lid after only 2 years. incident_description: Our new Generac whole house standby generator was professionally installed in June of 2020 and was serviced on two occasions by an authorized Generac service company since that time. In our winter storms we experienced a few short power outages and 36 hours of run time accumulated. Recently we had a severe series of storms where power outages caused the generator to automatically start as designed and it ran continuously for over 24 hours. When power was restored, it automatically turned off but a strong odor of burnt oul was coming from the generator enclosure. When I opened the enclosure, the entire interior was dripping with oil that had obviously come from the engine. This motor oil had been atomized by the strong cooling fan of this air cooled unit and the oil had been burnt onto the hot exhaust manifold and muffler while running automatically at 3800 rpm. This could easily have resulted in a fire that would have consumed the plastic enclosure and spread to the residence structure only four feet away where we were sleeping. That loss of oil was over 50% of the engine capacity and a catastrophic failure could have ruptured natural gas lines causing a major explosion and fire. The Generac factory authorized service company showed me how the plastic oil filler cap was defectively designed whereby only one thread of the cap has purchase of the filler hole. During normal operation, vibration routinely causes these caps to fall out unnoticed and resulting in the condition that I experienced. There is no labeling on the unit of this situation and the oil filler cap is actually concealed by the enclosure when otherwise routinely checking the oil level on the dipstick. In my situation there were no actual injuries but the risk as explained is very real and I have a very big mess to clean up.
justification: The incident involved a significant risk of fire and explosion due to a design defect, but no actual injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I have one of the A. O. Smith recalled water heaters (Model Number 153.330290, Serial Number 1144T450775).  The water heater burner and controller were replaced via the CPSC recall process (CPSC Recall Number 19-029) on April 21, 2020.  In early November 2020, the water heater burner started to make a loud humming noise 10 seconds after the burner is ignited and lasts 2 seconds.  In early December 2020, it also started to make a second much louder humming sound after another 25 seconds that lasts 10 seconds.  I would not have expected a new burner to have this problem.  Either the burner is defective or the installation was not correctly done.  This is a serious issue because the burner is vibrating (humming) when it is heating, and it could eventually physically tear and cause a fire.

I send an e-mail to Ashland City Support (help@hotwater.com) who had originally provided the list of plumbers to perform the recall.  They responded that this is not their problem and to contact Sears at 888-287-9322.  Although the burner assembly was part of the recall, they claim that ÃÂOnly the gas control valve was part of the recall, we replaced the burner assembly as a courtesy.ÃÂ  Per the Consumer Product Safety Commission recall notice, "The water heater's gas burner screen develops tears.  The water heater's burner can then create excess radiant heat, posing a fire hazard if the water heater is installed directly on a wood or other combustible floor."  Thus, the burner assembly was part of the recall and not a ÃÂcourtesy.ÃÂ  Claiming that it was a ÃÂcourtesyÃÂ is a fraud.

The telephone number that they provided for Sears is a non-working number that is always busy.  After further e-mail exchanges, they said to contact Sears at 800-469-4663.  I have also called the telephone number for Sears (866-880-4661) on the CPSC recall notice, but I have not had any success in speaking to someone about the recall.  I am always transferred to a non-working number.

Sears had also failed in the recall process.  The CPSC recall notice was published on November 6, 2018, but Sears never contacted me even though they have my mailing address, e-mail address, and telephone number.  I only found out about the recall in April 2020.

Request that you direct A. O. Smith to properly redo the water heater burner recall that was not done properly the first time.  They need to determine if the replacement burner had been properly installed and if not, fix it.  If the replacement burner was installed properly, then they need to install another replacement burner.  Thank you for your assistance.

incident_description:
I had a Honeywell Non Programmable electric baseboard thermostat installed in my garage/workshop, model CT410B1017, that was approximately 2 years old.  The thermostat controlled 2 electric baseboard heaters at a total of 3500 watts. This thermostat is rated for up to 5280 watts. 

The thermostat was shut off. When I went in my garage/work shop the next day it was apparent that the thermostat was in an uncontrolled heating mode. The temperature in the garage was well in excess of 80 degrees. The thermostat was no longer functioning.

I shut off the  circuit breaker that controlled the two heaters . The heaters were 240 volts and 8 feet and 6 feet in length with a total  approximate amp  draw of  approximately 17 watts. The circuit breaker was  a Square D 20 Amp breaker. I removed the thermostat from the junction box for replacement. When I removed the  unit I discover that the wiring had burned and melted. One of the wire nuts had completed melted, exposing the spring from the wire nut that was still securing the wiring connection.  The wiring that was installed was rated for 240 watt service. 

On this wall, the covering  for my workshop was MDF plywood.  This defective product could have ignited this flammable wall covering, causing a very fast burning fire.  

I notified Honeywell of this incident.  Case number [REDACTED]

I took photographs and still have in my possession the defective thermostat.

incident_description:
Subject: Dangerously hot water from Triangle Tube Smart 50 water heater caused by inadequate installation instructions:

In 2006 we had a Triangle Tube Smart 50 indirect water heater for DHW (Domestic Hot Water) installed in our house.

One of the most mystifying problems that IÃÂve finally solved was that occasionally the DHW temperature at the house faucets was dangerously hot. This problem appeared immediately on installation, so I had a mix (anti-scald) valve installed directly between the cold inlet and the hot outlet for the water heater. That helped for 90% of the time, but there were still times, such as first thing in the morning, when the problem continued to occur.

I finally was able to diagnose the problem within the past couple of weeks by replacing the original thermo-mechanical thermostat with a digital one, and by installing digital temperature sensors on the hot inlet and outlet of the mix valve. What I found was that there can be a huge temperature gradient between the water temperature in the center of the storage tank, where the temperature sensor is designed to sit, and the temperature of the water at the top of the tank after it has been sitting undisturbed for a few hours, such as overnight. The water at the center will be 120F but the water at the top of the tank, where the outlet picks up the water, can rise to 150F overnight. So a mix valve should be mandatory, not merely "optional" as described in the installation manual.

Furthermore, after much searching on line, I found out that the mix valve MUST be installed with a heat trap loop and with a minimum of 20ÃÂ between the heat trap loop and the mix valve. If not installed in this manner, the mix valve itself will become hot throughout the valve body and the temperature regulation mechanism will not work properly. This was the case with our installation until I finally replumbed it a couple of weeks ago. It has worked perfectly ever since, and IÃÂve been monitoring the digital temperature sensors closely.

In the installation manual, the installation of a mix (anti-scald) valve, is suggested, but not required. Furthermore, the installation diagram makes no mention of the actual requirements for proper installation of a mix valve so that it works as intended.

I just downloaded the installation manual for Triangle TubeÃÂs current model of this water heater, and the installation instructions have not changed since 2006.

I suggest that you require Triangle Tube to rewrite the installation manual. Please see attached pdf.
justification: The incident describes dangerously hot water due to inadequate installation instructions, which could lead to scalding injuries if not addressed.

incident_description:
My furnace went out. My boyfriend and I used two Westinghouse ceramic heaters, model WHT0571, to heat my house until the furnace could be repaired. When one of the Westinghouse heaters stopped working, I gently tapped it on the floor and it started again. The second time it stopped, tapping it didn't work to restart it. It smelled like burnt plastic and never worked again.
The second heater worked well, until it, too, stopped yesterday. I tapped it on the floor, as I had done with the first heater. It started up again. A few hours later I noticed a strong smell of burning plastic. I didn't want to pick up the heater because that would shut it off. Once shut off, it might never start up again. So I pushed it across the floor a few inches. I saw a burn mark on my bathroom floor. The size of the burn mark was between a nickel and a quarter. I needed this heater to continue working to prevent my water pipes from freezing during the below-freezing temperatures we were experiencing here at night in Minnesota. So, rather than shutting off the heater, I decided to frequently push it a few inches  across my bathroom floor to prevent any one area from being burnt. I already knew my entire bathroom floor needed replacing because of the initial burn mark, and I didn't want my pipes to freeze, too.  Sometime before noon this morning, I smelled a horrible burnt plastic smell that permeated my entire house. I pushed the heater a couple inches and found the worst burn mark of all. If I hadn't been home I believe the heater would have started a fire.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burn marks on the floor) and a strong risk of fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

I checked the wheels and noticed that there were rubber pieces next to one of the wheels.  Looking closer it was apparent that the wheel was not functional.

incident_description:
I had a Bradford White 40 gallon natural gas water heater installed on 11/16/20 (model RG240T6N). I noticed gas coming from the household faucets for several days after installation. Suspecting any air that was introduced into the system should have dissipated, I was concerned some other gas could be involved.  I am a volunteer firefighter and have access to a gas meter. I placed the meter next to the open faucet and got a reading of hydrogen sulfide (13.5 ppm)  before water eventually flowed (got gas only for about 10 seconds).  I notified the plumber who did the initial installation. He advised he called the plumbing supplier and they told him they were aware of the issue. They indicated the magnesium anodes were "bad" and that they would supply him with a new anode which should fix the gas issue.  The plumber returned and replaced the anode. The original anode showed significant corrosion after only having been in use for a week (I have it for testing if needed).  The gas issue did resolve with the new anode. However, the tank water continues to show signs of particles from the corroded original anode in the water.
I have concerns about any lingering health consequences of the hydrogen sulfide passing through my household faucets and the impact of the continued presence of what I am assuming is magnesium in my water.  Additionally, I have at least one faucet impacted by reduced flow (likely from a particle getting stuck in the internal pipe of the faucet). I have contacted both Bradford White and my water utility (Suez Water) for assistance but have not gotten a response from either to date.  Any assistances you can provide would be greatly appreciated.

We had what started as a minor grease fire on our kitchen stove on 11/30/2020.  We attempted to extinguish the fire using a cover for the pan but the cover was not big enough.  My wife then attempted to use the Kiddie ABC fire extinguisher nearby but upon pulling the pin and squeezing the trigger, nothing happened.  I attempted as well, to no avail. My wife was evacuating our two daughters and dog from the house and I was starting to dial 911 when I remembered I had another extinguisher in my shop area. I grabbed it, returned within 30 seconds, and successfully put out the fire that had quickly grown to close to ceiling height.

Unfortunately, the time lost time allowed the fire to burn far longer than it would have, had my extinguisher worked properly.  As a direct result of the failure, my stove's control partially melted and the smoke damage to my ceiling is going to require the mineral fiber tiles it to be replaced. (The textured tiles we have are not expensive, but are not well suited to painting either.)  

After this near catastrophe, I looked into why the extinguisher failed and found that the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) had issued a recall ÃÂdue to failure to discharge and nozzle detachmentÃÂ.  I contracted Kiddie and they did promptly replace the device itself, but I am still left with what I would estimate to be $1,200 in property damage. 

Although I know this safety concern is known to the CPSC, I felt it important to report he property damage associated with this issue.  

Please feel free to contact me with any questions, or if any additional information is needed.  (e.g., fire extinguisher model, serial number, date code, damage photos, photo of fire, etc.)
justification: The incident involved property damage but no injuries or deaths, and the occurrence likelihood is considered possible given the recall and failure of the extinguisher.

incident_description: Installed new garage door opener. I have installed several and inspected thousands. This Chamberlain unit and another new one they sent, both will not detect an object that is near the center, and 4 to 6 inches above the floor which is well within the track of the safety beam which is 6 inches above the floor. After about 40 hours of troubleshooting over the course of 8 weeks involving Chamberlain sending me new sensors, new logic board and ultimately a whole new unit, the problem persists. They agree that there is a problem. The problem area is along the beam areas not close to a sensor. Today I discovered that the safety beam and sensor technology is not compatible with the basic 3 year old floor paint. ItÃÂs not shiny epoxy, just plain gray floor paint. I had a moment of genius and covered the floor with blankets along the door area and discovered that the safety system starts working as it should. I have a video to show this. I also tested the other new unit with bare concrete and it performs correctly. I have a video to show this too.  It is the relationship of the paint to the beam in a way best described as an absorption. The beam is hugging the painted floor and bypassing an obstruction that is not flush. There is another troubleshooting process issue that causes the beam breakage testing to not work by just watching the green light while the door is closed, the beam also hugs the door and sneaks past a reasonable obstruction. There is another issue too, the installation instructions say to test the safety beam with the box that the unit came in. This would be a good idea but in this case it causes a very serious safety issue to be overlooked by inexperienced garage door installers and home owners. In summary, these units are unsafe with painted garage floors. The correction may be a design change, or a more risky approach of just telling people about this. If the installation instructions and system remain the same there will be consumers with unsafe doors. Doors have been required to have fully operational safety beams since around 1993. I did get to speak with a supervisor after several weeks who was helpful but had not heard of this type of problem. An older unit by same company does not have a problem with the floor paint. These products should be compatible with floor paint six inches from the sensors. The problem persists even if the height of the sensors is lowered or raised.
justification: The incident describes a safety issue with garage door openers not detecting obstructions due to floor paint, which could lead to accidents but no injuries are reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Aeiusny 288 wh 500 W Emergency power station and UPS powered with lithium ion batteries from Amazon in August of 2019.  Aeiusny is a Japanese company with an office in Massachusetts.  I used the device in Pennsylvania.  It caught fire in my house on the evening of November 9, 2020.  I was in on a different floor when the Aieusny UPS/Generator caught on fire so I did not see it initiate.  I was fortunate to have just replaced my smoke detectors in my house so they were quick to sound off when the fire ignited and I was fortunate that I had a dry chemical ABC fire extinguisher in the room where I was using the device as a UPS with a light load (modem and router).  I was able to temporarily douse the flames on the burning generator with the dry chemical extinguisher and due to ignorance of the reaction that causes lithium batteries to burn, I unplugged the modem and router from the generator and the generator from the AC source and grabbed it by the handle with my bare hand and proceeded to run it out of my house.  It flared up again as I approached my patio door and scorched part of the door frame, the glass and burnt some holes in the screen door but I kept running a few more feet and dropped it on my concrete patio and fortunately suffered no burns but I did breath in burning lithium battery and plastic case fumes during this process.  I read later that my initial belief that I had permanently doused the lithium battery fire with an ABC extinguisher was wrong and running with it out of my house bare-handed was dangerous since it is almost impossible to stop a lithium battery fire once it begins.   Yesterday, as I was verifying that my Amazon review of the generator where I reported the event was posted, I noted that another customer reported a bigger fire event in August of 2020 where an entire room in the customer's house was burned up and the fire department was called.  So, this Japanese company had notice that their generators were unsafe yet I have not seen a recall for them.  I am sure that I and this other Amazon reviewer are not the only fires caused by their generator.  I am sure they are or at least were using the old unsafe lithium battery technology in their generators that they are selling in the US.   Amazon did remove the link to the generator in my account that I purchased in Aug 2019 so there is a possibility that Aieusny switched out the type of lithium batteries they were using to build the generator and assigned a new part number to it but they kept quiet about the danger of the prior version of the generator that they sold in the US because I have not received a recall notice from anyone about the Aieusny generator that I purchased.  I have not contacted a doctor yet about possible damage to my lungs from breathing in burnt lithium battery fumes but I am at this point in time planning on it.  I can't definitively state that I have any lung damage from my exposure to the lithium battery smoke.  In addition to the photos that I uploaded to this complaint I also have photos of the damage the fire caused to my furniture, drywall and patio door as well as a PDF of the Amazon receipt for this product.  Since they are more personal in nature I did not upload them in accordance with the directions for this electronic form.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage and potential lung injury from inhaling toxic fumes, though no immediate burns or death occurred.

incident_description:
For the last few days, my wife and I have been noticing a burning smell coming from the garage.  We couldn't determine the source of the smell until late yesterday when I was in the garage while my wife was taking a shower.  The smell was originating from our RHEEM Platinum Water Heater.  

I immediately shut off the breaker to the water heater and proceeded to open the digital control panel where I noticed smoke and black marks around one of the wires connected to the panel.  

I immediately went online to determine whether any one else may have reported a similar problem.  I immediately found information related to a recall with my very same water heater; however, when I enter the model and serial number, the site tells me my water heater is not part of the recall.  This simply is not true.  

My water heater is the same brand and it was purchased at a Home Depot.  Furthermore, my model number is the same as those listed XE50M12EC55U0 and my serial number A081520571 falls within the series of numbers displayed online "A0114XXXXX to A5214XXXXX".  

Again, this could have been a much more serious problem had I not been in the garage.  We have two kids and a dog and we could have easily lost all or a part of our home to a fire.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and visible smoke from a water heater, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The glass wall that was installed in the shower in our master bathroom exploded around 8:50am on 10/2/2020. No one was in the shower or bathroom at the time, and the last use of the bathroom was approximately ~1 hour earlier. The noise of the glass exploding was loud enough that when I entered the room, I expected to find that the ceiling or floor had collapsed. Glass shards--both large blocky pieces and small sharp shards--were scattered throughout the bathroom and on all surfaces in the bathroom, and were also spread into the adjacent bedroom. The shower itself was filled with broken glass.

After the explosion, large pieces of shattered glass remained in the floor and ceiling clamps as shown in the photos. Several pieces of glass have fallen from the overhead portion that was attached to the ceiling since then.

Fortunately, no one was in the room when the glass exploded, and there were no immediate injuries. Myself, my wife and my 23-mo. daughter are frequently in that bathroom, so we believe we are fairly fortunate to have not been in there at the time of the explosion. As mentioned above the last use of the shower was approximately 1-hour before the panel exploded. I did receive a few minor cuts on my hands during the clean-up, which is still ongoing while we wait for contractors to arrive to provide repair estimates. As we are not sure how to safely remove the overhead glass, we currently expect to engage a professional for that purpose. So far the other adjacent glass panel and door appear undamaged, but we have not been able to conduct a thorough inspection.
justification: The incident caused minor injuries during cleanup, but no one was present during the explosion.

incident_description:
I am writing to alert you all to a critical safety issue in connection the above referenced generator (Serial No.:  3001516885).  This generator was installed at the above address in or about the Spring of 2017.  Although I am no expert, as far as I can tell from reading the Installation Manual, it was installed consistent with the installation guidelines provided by Generac which I understand are based upon the standards of the National Fire Protection Association.   Most importantly, it seems to meet or exceeds the required installation clearances.  It is at about 7 feet away from the house.  The guidelines say it must be installed at least 5 feet away.  There are no obstructions around it, etc.

The power went out in our area on Tuesday, August 4th and the generator kicked on.  On Wednesday, August 5th at 11:30 pm, the carbon monoxide detectors went off in our house.  [REDACTED] police, fire and first aid responded.  The readings in the basement were well in excess of 100 PPM, if I recall they were 112 or 120.  This is well in the danger zone.  There were also positive readings on the other floors of the house ranging from 20-50 ppm, if I recall correctly.  Three of us were in the house at the time.  My daughter was administered oxygen.  Thankfully the carbon monoxide detectors functioned properly and we are all ok and unharmed.

I am attaching pictures.  As you can see, the exhaust from the unit is blowing directly onto the house.  Again, I am no expert.  However, it appears the CO was aggregating in the basement door and window wells, as well as was probably getting into the house via the three white HVAC exhaust cones on the house.  At the time the atmosphere/air was rather heavy and still; there was no wind.  It had been running for about 30 hours.

I am alerting you all to this because it is a critical safety hazard.  A family could have been killed.  This kind of thing should never happen again.

It seems clear that the NFPA and Generac should do an immediate review of their standards and installation guidelines to fix this situation.  At a minimum, it seems the exhaust from the unit should be directed away from the house.  You should also issue an immediate recall, update and critical safety bulletin about these installation standards.
justification: The incident involved carbon monoxide exposure with one person requiring oxygen, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific conditions described.
