incident_description: While showering (without even touching the shower head) and no warning signs heard or observed the Delta Faucet Shower Head and rod (Model #75174C) came crashing down just missing my head. The force of the product falling easily could have damaged my bathtub but luckily it did not.  When the product broke, water began shooting out from the broken part on the side of the attachment right up and over our shower curtain causing our bathroom to flood, water dripping down the walls and damage to furniture in the room (wooden towel shelf and rug). While the incident occurred, I was in my home alone, so nobody would have been able to help me had the product fallen and hit me in the head... which likely could have knocked me out.  I have pictures of the product and how it broke.  After calming down from what had occurred (and trying to clean my bathroom of the damage), I looked on Home Depots web site (where we purchased the shower head from approximately 1 year ago) to find other reviews of the exact same situation happening to other owners, with pictures to prove it... some complaints date back to 2019. I reached out to Delta Faucets Customer Service via [REDACTED] and received a response requesting that I provide them with my address, personal info, and date of installation.  I provided the requested information with the exception of the date of instillation (as this is not something that a home owner would typically document).  I stated that I am not comfortable using this product ever again as it seems I am not the only person who this has happened to and it is very dangerous and was very scary- especially being home alone.  The only way the company would consider me for a reimbursement is if I provided the following information: 1. proof of purchase 2. letter of explanation explaining what I am seeking and what led up to the damage 3. pictures of the damage stating that they must be able to see the damage up close and that pictures must show the location of the damages in the unit.  Pictures must also be in color, well lit and in focus. 4. Photographs of the entire installation site, including the bathtub, base, surround, floor, and walls around installation pocket area. 5.  Two estimates for like replacement on letterhead from licensed contractors.  6.  Request must be for like replacement. 7.  The estimates need to be on letter head from licensed contractors. They will not consider anything else. They indicated that if any information above is not provided that they will not even consider the claim.  I stated that this is not a reasonable request and that I was very disappointed with their customer service.  Their only other solution is to provide me with a free replacement of the clearly faulty model that had broken in my home and other reviewers home or offered me 70% off of a product replacement on their web site.  When looking on their site, I quickly realized that their prices were WELL ABOVE the prices of other stores, like Home Depot, for the same model number of their product.  I am very concerned that this product is going to end up severely injuring someone and/or damaging their home and things inside of it.  Not only that but the situation was very stressful, loud, and frightening.
justification: The incident caused property damage and a near-miss injury, but no actual injury occurred. The occurrence likelihood is high given multiple similar reports.

incident_description: in December 2019 I purchased and installed four Kidde model P3010L 10 year Living Area smoke alarms.  Within three weeks, one of these alarms (date of manufacture 2019, Aug. 20) went off in the middle of the night and would not stop.  There was no smoke or fire present.  I got out a ladder and took the alarm down and disabled it per the manufacturer's directions.  No dirt or insect presence was seen.  This unit was returned to Home Depot and replaced. Over the next month, the remaining three original smoke detectors and the replacement detector (manufacture date 2020 Jan 14)  all went off during the night, were disabled and returned to Home Depot for replacement.  By the end of March, three more of the replacements failed during the night and were disabled.  I finally gave up on this product and replaced all four units with Code One model i9070 battery operated smoke alarms.  There have been no false alarms from the i9070 smoke alarms in the four months since they were installed. I notified Kidde about the problems with the P3010L alarms and asked for a refund or gift card but their response was that they will replace defective products but they do not give refunds.  Why would I want to replace these with more of the same defective product?  My concern is that this product is dangerous because it generates many false alarms.  It is also dangerous to the consumer when you have to climb a ladder in the middle of the night just to silence the alarm.  I have read many product reviews and talked with contractors and it has become very clear that I am not the only one having a problem.  Just look at Amazon reviews for some examples.  I would expect that if Kidde would share product return information from retailers and consumers with your agency, the data would show an unreasonable percentage of this product was or still is defective.  It is a good idea to have a product that has no battery to change and will last 10 years, but only if it works.  This product does not work as advertised and is not safe

incident_description: I was sitting in my living room when my air purifier made a weird sound, and then it started to smoke and smell like an electrical fire. incident_description:
I filled the Devilbiss 5250 Powerback generator with fuel the morning after being hit by hurricane Laura and fuel started running out of corner of the fuel tank mounting location. Plastic tank is cracked and was not leaking before. Generator was in safe location during the hurricane and was not affected by storm. It would have caused a major fire and possible total loss of home and possible loss of life because leak was over the area above the muffler on the engine. Fuel leaked all over the generator and all over the ground and was very difficult to empty fuel from tank and minimize leakage at the same time and I was drenched in highly flammable gasoline. Found recall online that was dated in 1999. My generator manufacture date is 2005 and the fuel tanks still have the exact same problem after recall was published, so manufacturer did not fix problem, but accepted the risk as being more cost effective. I called the number listed in the 1999 recall and the company said they could not help, but said to call the number on the recall for repair (WHAT??? it's the same number I contacted him with). Typical corporate answer to get consumers to give up is placing them in a nonsensical loop where there is no resolution. Please help as I depend on this generator for electrical loss due to hurricane power line infrastructure damage that will take over eight weeks to restore. 

Previous recall number December 30, 1999 Release # 00-047
 WASHINGTON, D.C. - % joins DeVilbiss Air Power Company (DAPC) of Jackson , Tenn., in alerting consumers about gasoline tanks used on certain models of portable generators. About 295,000 of these generators were sold nationwide from February 1996 until June 1999. CPSC and DAPC are investigating whether the fuel tanks on the generators can crack where the tanks mount on the frame, posing a fire hazard. As a precaution until that evaluation is complete, consumers should not put more than three gallons of gasoline in the fuel tanks at any time.

The only generators affected by this notice have the following brand names: DeVilbiss Air Power Company, EX-CELL, PowerBack, [REDACTED]. The seven gallon tanks that are affected include only those tanks that bear dates prior to June 1, 1999. The date is on the serial barcode label found on one of the gasoline tank support rails and on the shipping carton label.

Any consumer who has seen leakage from the tank should not use the generator and should contact DAPC at (800) 888-2468, ext. 21 or at www.devap.com to obtain a free warranty replacement tank. Consumers with questions can contact DAPC directly rather than contacting retailers. Consumers also can contact CPSC at (800) 638-2772.
justification: The incident involved a fuel leak that posed a significant fire hazard, potentially leading to property loss and possible loss of life, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Fire started inside in our Kenmore 91383 7.4 cu. ft. Gas Dryer on 9.9.2020.
I had load of dried clothes inside of the dryer and put it on a 10 minute wrinkle release cycle to grab a shirt out of the dryer to wear.  When the cycle was complete; I grabbed the t-shirt out of the dryer and shut the door.  The dryer was off at this point.
About 1 hour later, there was a subtle burning smell in the house.  But I determined it was inconclusive, as nothing was powered on/ the stove was off/ and also, I live in California where there are currently fires burning.  I decided it was the smell of the fires in California and left the house/ as I couldn't locate where the smell was coming from.
Approx. 30 minutes later, my husband arrived home from a work interview.  He also detected a subtle burning smell but also had the same conclusion as I, because again, nothing was turned on in our house.  
I returned home 30 minutes after he had already been home and the smell I had detected before (2 hours previously) was no longer faint but more recognizable and I didn't believe it was from nearby fires.  I inspected the house and then came over to our laundry area where the smell was a bit stronger.  I opened the dryer (which had not been running for hours) and I opened the door to find a fire inside of the dryer.  Smoke came billowing out of the dryer with visual flames.  Our smoke detector then went off.  My husband called 9-1-1 as I began the process of trying to extinguish the flames as well as trying to get the clothes out of the dryer and onto our lawn.
The firefighters arrived <5 minutes post the realization of the fire.  And by then, I had been able to extinguish the fire.
We lost not only a $1000 Kenmore dryer that was <2 years old but also ~ $500-700 worth of our clothes.
Luckily, no one was injured and our house is still standing.  But the reason for this fire occurring remains a mystery.  
lives could have been lost and we are very grateful that this was not the case
justification: A fire occurred causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the unusual nature of the incident.

incident_description:
I sent a similar write-up to the Finish Corporate Offices, but this is what happened:  Monday night, 09/14/20, I was loading the dishwasher and using Finish Quantum Powerball pods.  

Two of them were stuck together and when I went to pull them apart, the blue and red liquid pods burst and went into my left eye.   I called my brother, who is an internal medicine doctor, and he had me rinse my eyes out immediately for about 20 minutes turning my eye in various directions.  

After I did that, he had me put a patch on my eye and every 15 minutes put saline solution in it, since he wanted to get the PH level back up.  After about 2 1/2 hours of that, I took the patch off and looked through my left eye - it was like driving in a deep fog.  I called my provider and poison control and they recommended I go to the emergency room.  While there they flushed my eye out with 3 liters of saline solution, over about a 3 hour period.  There were breaks between because it was so painful to do that.  I was told by the doctors there that what I had splashed in my eye was probably one of the worst things out there that could have been put into it, since it is so concentrated.  Poison control told me the same thing before I went down to the hospital. They put ointment in my eye and sent me home around 3:30 a.m.   

Tuesday morning, my eye was swelled shut and watering profusely, and very light sensitive.  It still looked like I was looking through fog.  I had an appointment with an ophthalmologist that day.  He said that it appears my epithelial layer of my eye has been burned off.  He does not yet know if I will have permanent damage or if the epithelial layer will eventually grow back.  He told me that everyone who has this product in their household should throw it out immediately.  He apparently has seen this over and over again.  He and the doctors last night said that this stuff is so concentrated and alkaline, it has immediate absorption and, when kids swallow it, it burns their entire insides as it goes down and causes permanent damage.    

He gave me some medicines to apply to my eye, so will see at my appointment on today (09/16/20).   He said that, only then will we know if I have permanent eye damage or not.  Either way, he said that this can lead to other things in the future, like glaucoma.   

I had not heard anything like this in the media, so I was shocked to find out that it was such a common occurrence and so well-known when I was talking with medical professionals.  

I am a licensed senior architect.  They do not do well blind.    
My questions are this: 
1. If these types of occurrences are so well known, and this product is so dangerous, then why is it on the market?  
2. Why is this not more well known by the public, so they can make informed choices about whether or not to have it in their homes? 
 3. If this is a possibility, and the pods have a tendency to stick together with the liners that contain the blue and red liquids, then, why in the world are they not packaged individually, instead of just all being thrown in the same bag?  

Hopefully I am not permanently blinded in my left eye here, but I want this on record with both the company and your agency, so that you can consider whether this product is safe enough to have in the public, without the safeguards of providing individual wrappings and having HUGE warnings on the label indicating what can happen.   There is a small warning label on the package that says "CAUTION: HARMFUL IF SWALLOWED OR PUT  IN MOUTH.  EYE IRRITANT. DO NOT get in eyes.  There is nothing that says that this can cause immediate long term damage if ingested or if splashed in eyes.  Had I known how caustic and dangerous this product was, I would not have used this product and would have probably stuck with the powdered versions that are out there.
justification: The incident resulted in significant eye injury with potential for permanent damage, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the ophthalmologist's statement that this is a common occurrence.

incident_description:
- On the morning of Tuesday September the 8th 2020, the [REDACTED] toilet that contained a Pressure Assist Flushmate series 503 Sloan power flush Exploded shattering both the Water Tank and Tank Lid propelling shards throughout the bathroom with pieces impacting and cutting my wife's foot and leg and a large chunk of the Lid clubbing her in the forehead above her Right eye resulting in a nasty goose-egg swelling with associated impact pain from this blunt force trauma injury. One of the large pieces of debris found on the floor was a smooth rounded corner of the Lid which is likely what hit her on the head as there was no external bleeding. Although the pain persisted for days the swelling gradually reduced (leaving a dent in her forehead) and purple and green colors advanced down her forehead and between her eyes. Sudden loud noises would cause her to jump and her heart to race. 
- It was only after this incident that I was prompted to research this type of product failure and found that the 501, 502, and 503 series Flushmates' ALL had reported cases of catastrophic failures that destroyed the toilet, caused damage to the home, and exposed the occupants to injury - some who sustained serious wounds. Had I been informed of the known risks of the past 501 and 502 series I never would have purchased 1 [REDACTED] and 1 [REDACTED] toilet with the 503 PA for use in our home. The [REDACTED] toilet that exploded was the newer of the 2. I immediately stopped using both toilets and had them replaced with conventional gravity flush toilets.
- During the same time I originally had these toilets installed in my home I also designed a commercial building for the company I worked for ([REDACTED]) and had 8 toilets with the Sloan PA installed. [REDACTED] is now assessing what corrective action is needed since they have been informed they are putting their employees in harms way of random explosion at any time.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the wife, including cuts and blunt force trauma, but no death occurred.

Regardless of the pending outcome of my complaint to my bank, I still feel obligated to report what I witnessed because the plug in to the unit is very close to the bottom, where leaking water could touch the plug in. This is a poor design.
justification: The incident involved a leaking product with potential shock hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased carpet in 5/2019, but it was defective.  She ordered a replacement carpet in 2019, but it never shipped.  The carpet being reported, was delivered 11/8/2019.  The consumer contacted the dealer about staining concerns and the flattening out of the carpet.


There is fuzzing on the nose of the carpet.  The carpet has flattened down on the stair portion.  Other locations of the carpet in the home, have also flattened out.

(5/7/2020) One technician from the dealer came out, inspected the carpet and filed a complain

(5/21/2020)  A dealer's technician came out and looked at the carpet.  Sometime later, the dealer filed a report with the carpet manufacturer.

(7/2020)  The carpet manufacturer sent an independent technician ([REDACTED], with [REDACTED]) came out to examine the carpet. 

The carpet measured between 4.0 - 3.0.  The parts that walked on, were lower than the rest of the carpet.  [REDACTED] told the consumer that this was within the approved variance for the use of carpet.

Later, the consumer's claim was denied.

(approx. 7/21/2020)  The consumer was walking down the stairs, when she slip and fell.  She was holding the stair's handrail at the time, but the smoothness of the carpet caused/contributed to the problem.  She caught herself, but fell down 3 - 4 steps, on her bottom.  She did not get injured.

The consumer has spoken with the dealer's owner, [REDACTED NAME].
Dealer address:  Molyneaux Tile & Carpet, 10 Plumb St., Verona, PA , 15147, Tel:  412-793-6100

The house is 2 stories with 12 steps connecting the 1st and 2nd floors.  As the bedroom main bath and TV/craft room are on the second floor.  On average, each of us will make 7-8 trips per day from 1st to 2nd floor.  Carpet continues to flatten thus becoming smooth and creating an even more of a safety hazard.  Each step is damaged.

incident_description:
I was using my Aarke II water carbonator when the the bottle exploded, shortly after starting the carbonation process. Shards of plastic flew all through my kitchen, and my face and hand were welted and cut with the plastic. The force of the blast hit my cabinet even breaking some dishes.

Range fan/vent hood with a glass overhang.

incident_description: Water coming out of our fixtures smells like diesel fuel/gas/car exhaust or a chemical.  The water has been tested from where it comes into the house from the city supply and it tests good there and no smell is present.  The water dept disconnected our water supply and plumbed our house into a neighbors house who has no odor or smell in their water and the smells were still coming out of our fixtures and toilets.  The water is picking up or absorbing something from the pex pipes as it travels through or sits in those pipes.  Some type of VOC or SVOC is being released from the plastic pipe into the water.

incident_description: Fire hazard. ClimateMaster model TES049 geothermal heat pump wiring shorted out during normal operation in the early morning of August 22, 2020. The wiring harness was positioned close to the copper refrigerant line going into the compressor. Electric sparks from the wiring arced against the copper refrigerant line causing a pinhole leak in the copper  line. R410A refrigerant escaped and filled the garage, where the heat pump was located, with freon gas. Prior to this incident, the heat pump was experiencing false high pressure/high temperature faults in the water loop system causing the unit to shutdown prematurely. The house could have caught on fire while the occupants were sleeping. This unit needs to be recalled immediately.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and refrigerant leak, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We installed a deck ladder this summer on our deck, after purchasing on Amazon.
Our family used the ladder to get into and out of our pond.
Our 7 year old granddaughter suffered a laceration on the underside of her big toe, from climbing up the ladder.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Opus International LLC Aroma Sense Shower head from Amazon.com.  After 3 months, the shower head blew apart hitting my wife on the head leaving a small lump.  I checked the reviews on Amazon and there are a number of consumers that have experienced the same issue.  I contacted the manufacturer to inform them of the issue and have not heard back from them.
justification: The shower head caused an injury (small lump) and similar incidents are reported by multiple consumers, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: Shortly after showering, while drying off, the glass shower door spontaneously shattered. The door was not being touched, bumped, or moved when this happened. It shattered explosively, with hardware, metal handle, and broken glass flying away from the shower and covering every surface of the bathroom. The flying hardware pieces damaged wall and floor tiles, and the broken glass caused injuries to our daughter, who was nearest the door at the time of the incident. She had to receive emergency care at the hospital for lacerations and embedded glass, including multiple x-rays, sedation, and wound care.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring emergency care, indicating a severity level of 3. The spontaneous nature of the glass shattering suggests an unlikely but possible occurrence.

incident_description: A Delta designed shower door uses a plastic hinge on the bottom of the door to hold the door on. This plastic piece deformed in normal use after 2.5 years, causing the door to fall off and almost causing injury to my wife. Luckily she was holding the door by the handle and was able to hold it from striking the tile floor and shattering. I was able to remove the door from my wife and safely place it where it would not shatter.
justification: The shower door fell off due to a deformed plastic hinge, but no injury occurred as it was caught in time.

incident_description: Just find out that this product was re-called back in 2016, was looking at the website of LOWES for an appliance re-call when I came across this product re-call. Was completely appalled due to the fact that the company never made the re-call. When I see the effects on immunocompromise Individuals, I'm furious I was about to use it again this weekend. But I recall using this product many times before and now I'm questioning my decline in health as I'm wheelchair-bound at the age of 57 and being home at all times while using this product. Why this and other companies allow to do that? What about my health and others. For the past 4 yrs., this has been in my home, my sanctuary, my peaceful home. What I'm supposed to do?
justification: The user reports potential health decline linked to a recalled product, indicating possible injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the product's recall history and the user's reported health issues.

incident_description: I am the assigned fire investigator for a house fire in Lacey, WA.  A ceiling fan manufactured by NuTone was involved in a house fire causing significant damage to the attic space and second floor of a home.  I believe that the fire was most likely caused by a mechanical failure of the unit.  It was wired as a whole house vent fan that operated on a schedule throughout the day to exhaust air from the single family residence.  The house was built in 2009 so the age of the fan was likely 11-12 years old.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no mention of injuries or death.

incident_description:
The Dreamline Infinity-72-inch semi-frameless door top track became faulty. While waiting for a replacement part, the entire door shattered while my husband was using it. We understand that we should not have been using the shower during this time and ordered a replacement door. 

During installation yesterday, the new glass door shattered in our handyman's hands while he was holding the door. Two of these glass frames have shattered in the course of two weeks.

incident_description:
(09/02/2020) The consumer was using the vacuum for about 10 minutes when the product burst into flames. The flames were about 8 to 10 inches high. The consumer was able to put the fire out.

The product had shorted out at the handle near the extender rod. 

 There were damages to a vinyl floor in the bathroom.

incident_description: Purchased the Vornado EXO51 fan after receiving open the top of the box pulling the fan from the box itself and noticed a sharp pain in my hand after further inspection I had several small cuts on my fingers was wondering why that happened from just pulling the fan out of the box normally you would pull or pick up something from where the handle would be but there are no handles on this unit there is a gap between the top and back that your hand would fit to normally to pick this unit up that is where my hand was placed, went ahead and assembled  the base unit to the fan went to pick up the fan again in the most convenient spot which is the same place and felt sharp pain in my fingers again after looking at the placement of where my hand was there are several sharp jagged edges along with seam line on both sides of where your hand would fit in to normally pick the unit up my concerns is the unit is unsafe to handle.

(08/14/2020) The consumer stated that her husband had a reaction to the product. He sprayed the product inside of his swim goggles and went swimming for about an hour. When he took the goggles off, his eyes were burning. He washed his eyes out with water, but in the middle of the night, his eyes were still burning.

The consumer stated that she called the Poison Control Center who advised her to go to the ER. When they got to the ER, her husband's eyes were sealed shut and had to be forced open. 

The chemicals in the defogger caused a corneal abrasion on her husband's right eye.

The consumer stated that her husband has used the product before but never under water. 

The consumer also stated that the warning on the label states that  the product is not recommended for swim goggles.

incident_description:
This is an A/C adapter designed to specifically connect to a thermal electric cooler, that is made by this same manufacturer.  The A/C adapter has a transformer on the plug that is attached to the unit.  When the adapter is plugged into the wall outlet and operated, the transformer gets extremely hot.  The consumer estimates that the excessive heat occurs within 15 ÃÂ 20 minutes of use.

The consumer used it one day and it damaged his wall outlet so severely that he had to replace the outlet.  He believes that the outletÃÂs terminals heated up and shrunk back down.  This affected the wires inside the outlet, which prevented them from working properly and caused them to quit working.

7/21/2020:  The consumer called the manufacturer, but their rep. (name unavailable) did not understand his concerns or take them as seriously as he thought that they should have.

The transformer itself is between the A/C plug and the 12 volt adapter.  On his unit, the adapter is connected directly to the plug and acts as a heat-sync.
justification: The incident caused damage to the wall outlet but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as the issue consistently arises within 15-20 minutes of use.

incident_description:
Window unit air conditioner has developed what appears to be mold on several internal parts including the fan blades.  The window unit was purchased and installed in the bedroom window in summer 2018. In August 2020, my wife complained about waking up in the morning with congestion and swollen eyes. She said it had been happening for several weeks but recent got worse.  Investigating the possible causes, she cleaned the filter on the window AC unit and found apparent mold. I removed a cover plate to access the fan area of the AC unit and saw that nearly every surface inside had black splotchy spots.  Using a cotton swab, I was able to wipe a sample of the black substance from a fan blade. We are reasonably certain the black substance is mold.  I disassembled the AC further with a plan to clean the contaminated surfaces, but I was not able to reach all of the internal surfaces that appeared to be contaminated with mold.  We decided to remove the AC unit from the window, and bought a new one.  Since replacing the AC unit, my wife has not experienced the congestion and swollen eyes in the mornings.   I will perform a necropsy on the old unit in my garage to see if I can clean and reassemble it. 
The AC unit worked great at cooling the bedroom, but we don't care for the exposure to mold allergens. This summer has been more humid than recent years. Mold is ubiquitous and should be expected in an AC unit where condensation occurs.  My complaint was that there was no way to effectively clean or prevent mold growth in hard-to-reach parts of the unit.
justification: The incident caused health issues (congestion and swollen eyes) due to mold exposure, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he has had the Honeywell control valve of his A.O. Smith water heater (Model Number: G6-S4040NVR400) replaced four times under the Manufacturer's warranty because they continue to leak gas.

07/18/2020 - The consumer had the water heater replaced under warranty however it was also leaking gas.

08/04/2020 - The gas company red-tagged the water heater. The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and another replacement control valve was installed.

08/08/2020 - The consumer shut off his gas as he smelled it round his home.

08/10/2020 - A gas company technician turned off the gas to the water heater and red-tagged the unit once more.

The consumer plans on contacting the warranty department once again.
justification: The incident involves repeated gas leaks from a water heater, posing a significant hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The consumer washes his bed spread every 2 days, because the dog slept on it.  He estimates that the spread has been washed hundreds of times.  

3/2019:  A halogen light or an [REDACTED] fell on the bed spread off of a nearby table (unknown how). The halogen light was a reading light.  The [REDACTED] that was on the table was being charged.

The consumer went down stairs for 10 minutes or less, and he noticed a lavender scent similar to an odor that is present when one is drying clothes.  The consumer checked the laundry room, but he was not drying any clothes.  He went back upstairs in his bed room and his entire bed was on fire.  The bed spread was not burning, but there were flames rolling on the top of the bed spread.

He tried to pull off the bed spread, but was unable to.  He burned his face, hands and a fleece jacket that he had on.  The spread was tucked in on the sides of the bed and could not be removed due to the fire.  He ran downstairs and got a large fire extinguisher.  The flames were extremely high.  He sprayed the extinguisher until he emptied it, but could not put out the fire.  The bed comforter and pillows were burning at this point.  He had to crawl out of the bedroom on his hands and knee due to the thick black smoke.  He immediately called the fire department.

They arrived within 5 minutes and put out the fire.  The upstairs in his home was totally black.  The consumer had a [REDACTED] mattress on the bed.  The upstairs of his home was a total loss and the downstairs area had extensive smoke damage.  The fire department threw everything outside.

The consumer took a 4' sheet and put it through the dryer with a bed sheet, approximately 25 times.  The consumer went through a cycle of washing it and then drying it, each time.  The consumer added detergent to the laundry.  He also added a liquid fabric softener to the wash each time.  He also added a fabric dryer sheet to the dryer each time.  

After the experiment, the consumer scraped the residue from inside of his dryer and placed it in a cup and lit it.  The fire was almost like lighting gun powder.

The consumer called the firm and reported his incident and his findings to them.  The consumer received a letter from the manufacturer (Reference # [REDACTED]), Dated- 1/9/2020.  The letter stated that they did not believe that it was their product that caused this problem.  The firm asked for the entire boxes of the remaining dryer sheets that he had and he said no.  He offered to send them a few from each box, but they wanted everything.

The consumer said he also discovered that children's pajamas may meet the flammability regulations when they are purchased, but after they are washed approximately 20 - 25 times with the use of fabric dryer sheets, they can then easily catch fire.


NOTE:  There was a white scaly film on the bed spread and the consumer said that it was the result of using this manufacturerÃÂs brand of dryer sheets.  The dog seemed to like the scent of the dryer sheets on the bed spread, which is one of the reasons he used them.  He noticed the white scaly film in the past, but said that it smelled really good.

The consumer had 2 different boxes of fabric softeners by this manufacturer:  Lavender scent & Water Lilly Jasmine scent.


The consumer did not see a physician for his injuries.  He applied a burn cream to his arms.  His face was blacken and the fire department offered to take him to the hospital, but he declined.  The burns were superficial.

After the fire the consumer was diagnosed with an AFib, which was determined  to be the result of stress from this incident.  He has had to take medication for this incident.
justification: The incident resulted in superficial burns and stress-related health issues, but no death or severe injury, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but have been documented.

No one was in the room when it happened, but my husband heard a loud thud, and came into the garage to find the washer 5-6 feet away from the wall. incident_description:
Dehumidifier was plugged into a regular electrical socket.  Appliance had been working normally, and filter was clean.   Appliance was being used in the closed garage to lower the humidity. Appliance had been running for less than two hours   Stopped working.  Thought the home fuse had tripped, but it was fine.  When I shook the cord, the appliance came back on. I unplugged the electrical device and saw a seriously corroded electrode. Only one electrode of the plug was impacted. The ground and the other electrode were fine. The corroded electrode was black and the plastic was melted around it. The area around the electrode was built up and not flat anymore.. The cord was also bent, suggesting that maybe the inside the cadding the wire was melting away.

When I unplugged the appliance.ade in China. I purchased two of these Emerson dehumidifiers from Brandsmart USA in West Palm Beach, Florida. Now I am concerned they are a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a corroded and melted electrode, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I bought a GE air condition model #AKQ06LZG1.  The installation instructions make no sense.  They refer to two different parts as the frame lock. On p. 12, they show installation of screws through the top frame of the air conditioner itself (for a vinyl window) as installing through the frame lock, but on p. 10, in the parts list, they show a small bracket called the lock frame. Which is it?  Even worse, in frame 5, they show installation of the lock frame bracket for a wooden window at the bottom of the frame, through the window sill, which will be useless if someone raises the window sash and the unit begins to pivot back and fall from the second floor window. Also in frame 5, they change terminology again, and call it the support bracket.  All in all, the instructions are just nonsense, when installation of an air conditioner in a second floor window is safety issue. When I call GE appliance I cannot get any assistance.  I believe GE should be sanctioned and be required to update the installation instructions.
justification: The incident describes confusing installation instructions that could lead to unsafe installation, but no actual injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: GE front load washing machine caught on fire. GE factory tech was out just a few hours before the fire and said it was safe to use.

While some of this water was captured by the tub around the washer, a significant amount escaped and damaged the floor and drywall in the area.  It also came close to electrical wiring, which could have resulted in shock or increased risk of fire.

This is in addition to earlier problems with the electronic control panel and the black mold issue in the rubber door molding.
justification: The incident caused property damage and posed a potential electrical hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Railing was installed on my deck by a licensed contractor and installation was properly done.  After 3 years the bottom rail on one of the sections warped down and the aluminum balusters became less secure to the point they actually could fall out with little pressure.  We have 11 grandkids who naturally look out the deck railing and pull on them.  One of the balusters did pull out.  When I checked later in the day I found that with little effort four adjacent balusters were easily be pushed out.  This could easily have caused a tragic fall off our deck.  I'm an engineer by training and this is a fundamental design flaw.  The southern yellow pine that the railings are made of very often warp with time and that warping can easily increase the separation between the top and bottom rails to the point the balusters in the center can fall out.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw that could lead to a fall, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

On closer inspection it seems that the cooling fan blade inside the drill had came apart and was throwing the plastic pieces out of the vents.  The plastic hit my arms and chest causing pain but no permanet injury.  Could have easily caused damage to eyes if drill was turned another way.  The drill was well maintained and had not been used very often.
justification: The incident caused pain from plastic pieces hitting the arms and chest, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the drill was well-maintained but still malfunctioned.

incident_description: Maxxima 1875 Watt 7 Button Countdown Timer Switch product #MEW-PT1800.  Multiple users, including myself, have found that this product randomly goes to the "on" state while unattended, providing power the attached load.  This switch is commonly used in bathrooms to control infrared heating lamps.  If the homeowner is away, the infrared lamps will stay on for hours or days, potentially leading to a fire.  If connected to a motorized device, the motorized device will start without warning, potentially leading to injury.

This saw was In good condition and lightly used, by me, since new.  I am now learning It was subject to a recall for this exact issue.

incident_description:
I use the Comfort Zone Dual Window Fan (that is placed at my window and that I purchased a while ago) only on occasion, so I was very surprised when I turned it on for the first time in a while and BOTH fan blades immediately splintered and shattered into tiny plastic bits when the fan spun up, sending shards of the fan blades flying. Clearly, the motors are still working, but the plastic has become brittle. On closer inspection, even the plastic on the window side (sun side of the window) near the handle has become brittle and is cracking. This is especially bad and frustrating because this fan is listed as a WINDOW fan - and that is where it was placed - at the window! This was advertised and marked as a WINDOW fan, and so was placed at a window. What is even more distressing is the fact that the smaller splinters and shards of the brittle plastic fan blade flew out of the fan and could have seriously injured my family. I emailed Comfort Zone, hoping they would take this issue seriously, send a proper replacement, but they do not see this as a SAFETY issue to be addressed.  Attached, please find images:

1 window fan label.JPG
2 window fan blades flew off motors.JPG
3 window fan blades flew off both motors _ big shards inside.JPG
4 window fan small shards flew out of fan.JPG
justification: The incident involved fan blades shattering and sending plastic shards flying, which could have caused injury but did not in this case.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that he experienced similar problems of recall #13-073.  Hazard: An unbalanced load can cause the washing machine to shake excessively and the drum to come loose during use, posing a risk of injury to consumers and property damage to the surrounding area.

Caller stated that while in use the washer seemed to have been torn apart from the wall , the drum case lose and water flooded the first floor of his house.  He stated that it looked like the washer had exploded internally.  Caller stated that he was never notified of the recall.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet but he plans to do so.
justification: The incident caused property damage and posed a risk of injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: How is this device allowed to be sold, if it allows a grounded cord device to be plugged into an ungrounded outlet without any warnings or provision to connect an external ground?
justification: The description highlights a potential safety issue but does not report any actual incidents, injuries, or deaths.

incident_description: I purchased the following step stool from Amazon.  It is still available there.  It is less than 2 years old and and is used very infrequently. Today I was standing on it and I heard a crack and it collapsed. The label on the product says it holds individuals up to 200 pounds.  Really?     I am a 4'11", 105 pound 66 year old grandmother and could have been hurt.
justification: The incident involved a step stool collapsing, but no injury was reported, aligning with severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as the product is used infrequently and the user's weight is well below the stated limit.

incident_description:
I purchased a GFCI outlet from Amazon in December 2018. The outlet failed last month (scorched, but did not cause a fire). When I took a closer look at the instructions/packaging and the outlet itself so I could report the failure to Amazon, I couldn't find a model number anywhere.  I thought this was unusual, so I started investigating.

The Amazon listing of this product, as well as the printed instructions, say that the product was Intertek ETL certified.  I contacted Intertek to confirm that the product actually passed their tests. I communicated with [[REDACTED NAME], CFE, Coordinator/Claims Associate, Electrical & Wireless ÃÂ Certification Department, ETL. Her contact info is [REDACTED CONTACT INFO] .  [REDACTED] confirmed that this was a counterfeit product that was not ETL certified.

I attempted to reach out to Amazon in several different ways.  First I sent an email that went unanswered. Then I started contacting Amazon customer service several times on the phone and through chat. They kept telling me "we will alert the proper department" but nobody gave me specifics. Nobody ever got back to me.  I've done quite a bit of [REDACTED] searching and some investigating on Amazon's site, and they don't seem to care too much about giving customers an easy way to report counterfeit products.

Since this is an electrical receptacle that's connected directly to a house's wiring, a failure could be catastrophic -- causing house fires.  I need to report this to someone, and keep Amazon from selling this product.

Here is the product I purchased. It's being sold in multiple listings on Amazon (close to 50 of them) by the same seller.  They're selling them in a 2-pack, a 5-pack, a 10-pack, different specs, etc.  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B077QRPXWV/.  They're all called ELECTEK (or in some places ELECTECK).  The packaging for the product says ELECTEK but the Amazon listing says ELECTECK -- yet another clue this isn't a legit product.

I have more information regarding this product that I'd be happy to share.  Product packaging, instructions, the units themselves, etc.  Plus my correspondence with Intertek.
justification: The outlet failed and scorched but did not cause a fire or injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood of such incidents is possible given the counterfeit nature and multiple listings.

incident_description: I purchased an Opolar F-531 rechargeable fan from Amazon on June 12, 2020.  I charged it using a USB cable that plugged into a wall receptacle.  I would charge it during the day and use the fan at night.  Wednesday, July 30, 2020 approximately 15 or 20 minutes after turning it on, there was an explosion about 2 feet away from our bed at about 12:15am.  Smoke instantly filled the room and we eventually discovered that the fan had exploded, burning the rug it was on, shooting a piece of metal about 6 feet away which scorched our wood floor and several minutes later we realized that one battery was missing and found it under our bed.  It was searing hot and had burned down about 1/8" into our wood floor.  I have photos of the damage.  The battery must have shot up in the air from the floor and come across our nightstand, as a stuffed animal I had on there got burned as well.  There are a few small burn marks on our wall and soot covered much of the room.  This explosion was very violent and we are lucky that a fire did not start and that no one got hurt and that the damage is repairable.  We do not want this to happen to any one else. I did contact Amazon yesterday (July 30, 2020) and they have taken this item down from their site.  But we imagine that these batteries are in use in other items.  If we had not been home when this happened, it could have burned our house down and killed our cats.  I am shocked that these batteries can explode like this and are in use in many items.  These could seriously injure people, animals and property.  I understand the instances are rare, but the fact that they can occur seems reason enough to not allow these batteries to be in use. I feel that there should certainly be a recall on these batteries.
justification: The incident involved a violent explosion causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, and the description notes such instances are rare.

incident_description:
The consumer has experienced many different health effects and her dog is also experiencing health issues.  

The consumer's dog has high liver enzymes.  The dog has to receive an allergy pill and get allergy drops.  He also has ulcers on his mouth.  He can sometimes experience break-outs on his belly.

The consumer began experiencing allergic symptoms 3 - 4 different years ago.  The consumer has been diagnosed with Cystitis.  She has changed laundry detergent, toilet tissue, but noting has eased her symptoms.  The consumer experiences sever food allergies and water allergies.  They cause or contribute to vaginal inflammation.


The consumer went to visit a relative 8 days ago and stayed for the entire 8 days.  While there, she did not experience any of the symptoms that she does at her own home.  She could eat any foods that she chose to and various types of water without experiencing any adverse symptoms.

The consumer had the flooring in her home replaced and several rooms and hallways painted.  The carpet was removed from the home and replaced with hardwood flooring.  The consumer was in and out of the home the whole time that this was being done (2 years ago).  The flooring was installed in June 2018.

11/2019:  The consumer went out of town during the Thanksgiving holidays and did not experience any of the symptoms that she does in her own home.
justification: The consumer and her dog are experiencing ongoing health issues (injury level), and the symptoms recur consistently when at home, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I noticed a smoke/burning like smell coming from the table saw. Upon examination of the saw, I noticed the 4 screws on the front of the saw, that hold the blade/housing in place, were all missing. Because they were there when I assembled the product after purchase, I assumed they had vibrated out. I replaced the screws with new ones. This fix kept the blade straight but the smoke/burning smell was still there when using. Though a [REDACTED] search on the table saw, I noticed that a recall was issued in 2019 for this table saw due to the possibility of it catching fire. I started to fill out the online recall form but stopped because Porter Cable will only offer $95 reimbursement. They also wanted me to submit pictures of the cord cut in 3 places before I could complete the claim. The $95 is not enough to cover the cost of a new saw and Porter Cable should either fix my saw properly or provide enough compensation to buy a new on of equal value to when I purchased this saw.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to missing screws and a recall notice, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was using the Casabella Wayclean Deluxe Broom with Dustpan yesterday when the green attachment point between the metal pole and brush head failed. This resulted in the broom head flying off my 16th floor balcony, landing on the ground below.

Fortunately, no one was struck or injured from the incident, but it was troubling to experience a sudden product failure. More concerning, there are multiple examples of the same point of failure reported on Target.com from other consumers.
justification: The incident involved a product failure causing the broom head to fall from a balcony, but no one was injured. Multiple similar failures reported suggest the issue is likely to occur again.

incident_description:
Scotch-Brite Copper Scrubbing Pads--metal shreds and causes splinters and can be ingested

I used as normal to clean pots and pans, etc.  The copper-coated metal shredded into 1/4 inch slivers and I got a splinter.  More dangerous, the slivers stick to utensils, dishes  and pans and get into food and can be ingested.  THIS IS EXTREMELY DANGEROUS. There are many similar complaints and comments on the product website.

incident_description: Turned on the washer on permanent press, cold water, high spin. After about 10 minutes the clothing washer made popping, sparking, banging sounds and had sparks and fire shooting out of the base of the machine. We quickly unplugged the machine. The machine locked and would not open.

incident_description:
Product name:  SystemThree Rotfix.  Manufacturer:  SystemThree (Lacy, WA  98503)
This is a two-part, liquid epoxy compound meant to strengthen rotted wood.

Issues: (1) Incomplete safety instructions:  After mixing the two liquids in the proportions according to the instructions, the product gets very hot and emits smoke after 15 minutes.  It partially melted and cracked the plastic container I used to mix the two components.  I had to move the container to an outside location on concrete away from my house.  The product instructions say nothing about this behavior or warnings about toxic vapors or smoke.

The company also does not provide any warnings about the type of container suitable for mixing this product.  A plastic paint mixing cup I used partially melted due to the heat from the product.  

(2) Poor customer support:  The company offers very limited product support.  I tried using a phone number listed on a brochure (800-333-5514), and given the choice between a person presenting a hard-sell sales pitch for a senior citizen safety monitor (option 1) or a disconnected phone call (option 2).  I tried contacting them thru their website systemthree.com, and received a response about a half-hour later.  This is while I'm dealing with a very hot, fuming substance about which I wasn't warned.
justification: The product emits smoke and gets very hot, posing a risk of burns or toxic exposure, but no injury was reported in this incident.

incident_description: Just four days after receiving this brand new safe from Walmart, I went to open it with the code I had set and the locking mechanism wouldn't budge. I had entered the correct code, as confirmed by flashing green lights and a faint buzz of the servo motor, but still the safe stayed fully closed. So, I grabbed the backup keys for the electronic safe, put it in the keyway and turned. No luck. The locking mechanism was completely jammed and both keys were only able to turn a quarter of a turn before being met with considerable force. No amount of jiggling, pounding, or pushing while turning the key was effective. Eventually, I had to purchase tools to force the safe open to get access to my passport, handgun, social security card, cash, and best-man gift from my brother (a beautiful wristwatch). All the banging and force required to open the safe had scratched up the watch and gun. In addition, the manufacturing company was unresponsive to calls and emails, despite offering a 3 year warranty on the safe. They finally responded to a support email 5 days after forcing the safe open, and 8 days after the request the same day the safe first sealed itself closed.
justification: The incident involved property damage (scratched watch and gun) and inconvenience, but no injury or death. The likelihood is possible given the reported issues with the safe's locking mechanism.

incident_description:
After about 15 minutes of vacuuming my carpet, my Kenmore vacuum cleaner started making a grinding noise and I noticed a flickering light.  I turned off the power switch, but the vacuum continued to operate.  I next pulled the power plug, which stopped the vacuum, but the flickering continued.  A few seconds later I smelled burning plastic and a flame burst out of the top of the vacuum cleaner.  The flame was about 6-9 inches in height.  I was able to put it out with water, but I was very upset that my vacuum cleaner could burst into flames.

Details:  Kenmore 12-amp upright vacuum cleaner, model 116-31069110, serial number ME1094022
justification: The vacuum cleaner caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: LG Washer Model # WT5101HV continues to knock around and will not wash clothes. Even small loads are showing error messages.

incident_description:
Hi,

I bought a Westinghouse 3200PSI Pressure Washer from Walmart a couple of weeks ago. I've used it for less than 10 hours so far, and have had the following problems related to the extreme heat that the unit reaches when in use.

-2 hoses with holes melted into them
-1 second degree burn on my forearm from just GRAZING the engine while adjusting the hose connection.

All three of these happened from just brief contact with the engine. Yes, there is a picture indicating that it can get hot, but the hose invariably grazes the engine while moving around, and just a few seconds can result in a ruined hose.

In the case of my arm, the contact was a split second, and a significant injury occurred. 

The design is dangerous, and also limits the functionality of the unit because I now have to replace the hose again in such short succession. This design should be pulled from the market, or a cover that can be attached to the engine should be sent to owners.

Westinghouse WPX3200 Gas Powered Pressure Washer
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn from brief contact with the engine, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: I purchased the Westinghouse Great Falls outdoor ceiling fan from Amazon in late May, installed it scrupulously according to the directions and used it for a month.  On Saturday, while my children were nearby, a blade broke near the base and came flying off, landing near them.  Upon inspection, two other of the plastic blades are cracked, and the fourth is showing signs of stress.  I have contacted Amazon, left a review, and have a call into Westinghouse to warn them.  The blades seem brittle vs. strong/resilient upon inspection.
justification: A blade broke and flew off near children, but no injury was reported. The incident suggests a potential hazard with the product.

incident_description:
Bought a Ryobi pole saw at Home Depot.  First saw lasted around two hour.  Method of failure was a plastic bar inset came apart entirely and no longer supported the main chainsaw bar.  This led to the angle of the chainsaw varying drastically, blades being thrown and ground, and a serious hazard.

Figured there must have been a defect, made an exchange.  Second saw lasted less than an hour.  This time the method of failure was a single nut inset in plastic came out.  This single nut was holding the entire bar assembly in place.  So, pole saw cut a branch, up in the air, entire bar comes off because someone thought using a thermoplastic as the primary means to support an essential part of a chainsaw was cost effective.

Additionally, the bar design has a tightener on one side of the blade that sits in one of the two structural support holes that applies uneven tension.  Never seen a chainsaw without both holes being used with bolts to support a bar.  The uneven tension leads to lots of thrown and ground blades, itÃÂs a major design flaw that people frequently list on the Home Depot site.

Background:  Each saw was run fully oiled.  Longest run without throwing a chain was around ten minutes.

Additional information:  multiple pictures are currently available on the Home Depot website showing each of the modes of failure.  The major risk one is the single nut encased in plastic that holds the entire blade assembly.
justification: The incident describes a serious hazard with the pole saw, including thrown blades and structural failures, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: The problems are the same on both my Electrolux washer and dryer.  The washer powers up at random times, often in the middle of the night.  The brains continue screwing up until I cycle the breaker and then its usually good for a week.  This has been happening for a year or more and I've emailed the company about the problems and while they acknowledge the email, they have done nothing more.

It sounded like someone crashed a car into our house. Upon discovery of the cause of the sound, we realized what happened and could smell burning and immediately unplugged it. The 22 lb cement counterweight came shooting out of the unit and into my wall. That weight was literally attached to the unit with a piece of plastic. Needless to say the washer is completely ruined and upon some easy google searching we found that this has happened numerous other times and yet Whirlpool refuses to address it.

incident_description: My wife, two daughters (23 month old and 7 weeks old), and mother-in-law were sitting in the living room at my mother-in-laws house when all of a sudden the entire Hunter ceiling fan fell straight out of the fan box and fan attachment straight on the floor, shattering broken glass all over and oil (the older fan motors have oil in them). Thankfully, my oldest daughter who was playing in the room was on the couch at that moment, and my newborn daughter was in my wifeÃÂs arms. They would have easily been killed given the weight of this fan and height it dropped from. It appears that the old fan attachments are much different than what is sold today (ball support type), and only involves a threaded shaft screwed into a nut with a small set screw tightened into the side to prevent it from loosening due to the torque of the spinning fan. I believe that all of these fan types should be recalled or advertised by the company to replace as they are very prone to faulty installation and have a poor safety design.
justification: The ceiling fan fell but no one was injured, though the potential for severe injury or death was high.

incident_description:
The aerosol can Of WD40 white lithium grease would not spray out the nozzle. While trying to work the nozzle into position with the nozzle pointed away from me, the can shot into my face. Fortunately I was wearing glasses. I normally would not stop to use safety glasses to lubricate a hinge. 
This nozzle is very temperamental and the failure mode sprays grease in unexpected directions.  I am an engineer and a mechanic and well versed in workplace safety. The old push button nozzle with a plastic tube was much, MUCH safer, IMHO.  At least you knew where the line of fire was.

incident_description: I opened the lid to our Samsung top-loading washer (Model 52M775). The left spring that holds the lid spontaneously broke and snapped into several pieces, which then led to the lid disengaging from the washer completely. This seems to be similar to problems that led to an earlier Samsung recall.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure (spring breaking) leading to the lid disengaging, but no injury was reported. The mention of a similar past recall suggests this is a known issue, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: Ecover Zero Dish Soap is deceivingly labeled and has contributed to flare ups of my allergic contact dermatitis due to the presence of methylisothiazolinone and methylchloroisothiazolinone. The Ecover website lists the following three ingredients in their Zero Dish Soap: denatonium benzoate, methylchloroisothiazolinone, and methylisothiazolinone. However, these three  ingredients are not listed on the label. This discrepancy in the labeling would lead the average consumer to believe the product is free from these allergens. The inaccurate label information is a danger to consumers because the preservatives left off the physical label can cause allergic reactions in many people. For example, methylisothiazolinone was labeled the "contact allergen of the year" in 2013 by the American Contact Dermatitis Society. Had the company included a full ingredients list on the label or noted that the ingredient list on the label was not complete, I would have been able to avoid experiencing a reaction from this product. However, because of the deceptive labeling practices, I was unaware that Ecover Zero contained one of my allergens and was using it regularly. From this product, I experienced painful hand rashes, which affected my ability to function and resulted in increased medical treatment costs.
justification: The incident caused painful hand rashes and required medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description: We purchased an Aquasana Countertop Water Filter several years ago.   Aquasana claims that the unit filters tap water, removing contaminants, 60% of the fluoride and 90%+ of the chlorine.  There is a diverter valve that diverts the water from the faucet into a hose.  Then the water goes to a prefilter and then travels into a housed unit with 2 large filters and out to a second tube that goes to the faucet as filtered water.  However the prefilter and the hoses have a faulty design that causes mold to form around and inside the prefilter and hoses.  The water that goes thru the prefilter into the hose is supposed to be filtered, but instead it picks up mold from the prefilter and carries it all the way to the hose leading back to the faucet.  You can actually see the mold in the hose.  So the good water coming out of the faucet presumably has mold in it.  We have replaced the housing, and diverter valve several times due to mold and leaking water problems.  The diverter valve has a tendency to fail causing tap water to leak into the filtered water.  The filter in the prefilter must be changed very often, but nothing we do can stop the mold from growing in the system.  Unfortunately, we did not notice the problem right away because of the opaque colored hose.  Even with the clearer hose, it is not obvious enough to see until quite a bit of mold has passed thru the system presumably into the filtered drinking water. I called Aquasana to tell them about the mold issue the first time I noticed it, but customer service was not helpful and insisted I buy another diverter valve.  So I tried it again, but this time the hoses were more clear colored.  That's how I was able to see mold growing again in the hose that leads directly to the clean filtered water and out the faucet for drinking.  I have been plagued by unusual health problems in the past several years, and we are wondering if the Aquasana unit with the moldy filtered water could have contributed to this.  Can you please advise.  We have not spoken to Aquasana.  I tried to phone but there was no answer.  I sent them an email, but have not heard back from them.  However, we do not expect this time to be any different than the way they handled it last time.  They completely disavow any responsibility for the mold growth due to the faulty design in their water filter.  They insist that we sign up for their Water for Life Program where they force consumers to buy replacement filters on a monthly basis even though the consumer specifies a less frequent replacement filter schedule.  As a Water for Life customer we would be "entitled" to free replacement parts and only pay shipping.  Thank you for your help.
justification: The incident involves mold contamination in drinking water, which poses a health risk but no confirmed injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Accidental gas fire inside snowmobile trailer.   Tried to extinguish with Kidde 1-A-10-BC extinguisher but nothing happened after the pin was pulled and the handle squeezed.    I intentionally broke the plastic top off the extinguisher and manually actuated the canister plunger to put out the fire.

I purchased a new Maytag washer

We used it 2-3 times a week  until it quit working around June 4, 2020.  When it quit there was a strong odor of burning plastic.   When a service technician came and took the control cover off there were burned wires and scorching. No explanation was provided by the technician.  Pictures and the part are available. incident_description:
I have a Samsung WA50F9A6DSW washer that was included in the home when we purchased it in July 2016.  It is located in the garage.

We started a load and were in the family room when we heard a loud bang.  The washer had twisted and moved (about 6 inches) and the sides were dented.  We could not see any other damage.

justification: The washer moved and flooded, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: Drilling hole into trees stump with newly purchased Chicago Electric drill.  Drill bit was [REDACTED] 1-1/4ÃÂ with [REDACTED] 12ÃÂ Quick Change Extension attached.  With 1st hole and 1st ever use of drill, bit entered stump wood to approximately 6ÃÂ depth without issue.  Drill bit continued to spin but could not be pulled free of the hole.  Flipped direction switch to reverse and pressed trigger.  Chuck and attached bit unscrewed from the drill.  Confused, I flipped direction switch to forward and aligned male threaded end of drill to female threaded end of chuck and pressed trigger.  As the chuck and drill threaded back together without resistance, the sudden force of the two pieces coming fully together, the embedded bit likely wrenched into a jammed state in the hole and spun the drill, dislocating and fracturing  my right ring finger. incident_description:
As a dog owner, I have accepted that in-home "accidents" can occur. As such, I have been a fairly loyal customer of the Nature's Miracle Enzymatic Cleaner [dog version] for a while. It is usually a satisfactory product, but my most recent purchase has been far, far from. The most-recent bottle I purchased [bought from Target--Winston-Salem, NC] has caused many issues in my household.

I used this product a few times to clean up various accidents over the last 4-5 months, and initially thought it worked well. However, a day or two later I would smell something very off in the rooms in which I cleaned with this product--I assumed the urine just hadn't been fully removed, so I used the product on the same spot(s). Again, I initially thought the product removed the smell, but a day or two later the horrible smell [and I mean it is FOUL] still lingered in those places. After a week or so, the odor seemed to fill the entire rooms (living room, guest bedroom) to the point where both myself and guests found it noticeable immediately upon entering these rooms. 

I had no idea what was happening, so I purchased a wet-vacuum and treated all rugs in my home. Smell still there. Over a month or so, anyone who came into my house would notice the smell and either 1) tell me they think the dog peed somewhere, or 2) whisper to other friends that the house had a terrible smell. It was so embarrassing. Eventually, the smell became so persistent that it would give me nausea--yes it was that bad. At one point, my mother spent the weekend with me and repeatedly complained about this issue. I decided to have my rugs professionally cleaned, but it did not work. The cleaning company even tried four times on one rug and three times on another in order to satisfy me, but the smell wasn't going anywhere [mind you, the cleaning cost me $440 and ultimately did nothing]. 

Fast forwarding to now [7/9/20], this odor, caused by Nature's Miracle, lingers. I had never actually opened the bottle I had, so myself and the carpet cleaner technician did it together and were horrified at what was inside; the liquid literally looked like and smelled like pure, yellow-brown urine. That is not an exaggeration. I couldn't believe it, so I went to Target and purchased another bottle to verify, but to my surprise the new bottle smelled and looked absolutely fine, just like other bottles I had purchased in the past. I couldn't believe it. 

What was wrong with that one specific bottle? Contamination? Some chemical change during potentially hot temperature transport? Accidental formulation error? Something had to happen. I looked at online [REDACTED] reviews--nearly all positive, but found in the 1-star ratings that numerous consumers have had this same problem, similarly reported nausea, similarly reported that the smell would not come out, regardless of what they did to remedy the issue. One person even said that she had to replace the entire carpet in one room of her home. I, too, am going to have to replace about $1200 worth of rugs, even after spending $440 to have them cleaned. 

I called Spectrum Brands, the parent company of this product, to file a complaint/claim. Upon telling the representative of the foul smell issue, he mentioned nearly immediately [emphasis on immediately] that maybe I should go to the website [REDACTED] to find a cleaning professional in my area. Hmm...who in the world knows right off the top of their head the exact website of a professional cleaning search tool--and it isn't for regular cleaning, it is ozonation cleaning specifically, which is pretty much a last resort option to remove smells, and even this still may not work. That was extremely fishy to me, and every person I have mentioned it to today completely agreed that it was not just a coincidence. I asked the representative how he randomly knew of this type of cleaning and how he knew the specific website and could repeat it so quickly. He said, "I just knew." He also maintained that neither he nor the company had never heard of this issue until now--a blatant lie. I know this is a lie as Nature's Miracle brand managers routinely comment back to consumers in response to their negative [REDACTED] reviews, AND I had already called and emailed in the past. There is no way that this problem was not known about until today. Absolutely false on behalf of Spectrum Brands. 

One thing I should note is that I am literally a sensory scientist and actively work as a taste and smell researcher for a consumer goods company...my undergraduate background is in food science with an emphasis on quality control...so of one thing I am certain: this odor is foul and this product is the culprit.
justification: The incident describes a foul smell and product failure causing significant inconvenience and financial loss, but no physical injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased an EO Smith Gas Water Heater from Lowe's ([REDACTED]) on March 14, 2020 and self installed the unit the following day.   
On May 16,  2020, after waking up to no hot water, I went to check the unit.  The unit is in the garage, and sometimes when the garage doors are open, a strong enough draft is created that it blows out the pilot light. Prior to re-lighting the pilot light, I inspected the unit and noticed that the mesh screen (air intake dust screen) around the bottom ring of the unit was heavily melted and completely detached from the ring (picture included).  The bottom of the unit was very hot to the touch.  I immediately shut off the unit, closed the gas valve, and contacted the manufacturer.
I informed the customer service representative that inside the access panel area of the bottom of the tank, the insulation between the tank and the outer steel jacket was hanging down at least an inch (see picture).  As I relayed to the customer service rep, the insulation appeared to be restricting airflow for proper ventilation, which had in turn made the bottom ring so hot that it melted the mesh screen.  
The customer service rep. stated that the issue posed a safety risk and advised me to shut off the unit and replace it with a new one.  The agent provided a replacement ID # to take to Lowe's so that I could swap it out. 
I went to exchange the unit at Lowe's the following day, May 17, 2020. When I returned home, I found the replacement unit's insulation was hanging down even lower, was at a significant angle, and a section of the insulation was hanging over the little window used to view the pilot light (see picture).   I called the manufacturer and they said since I didn't install it, then I could just return it to Lowe's for an exchange. 
This time, when picking up the 3rd unit, I requested a Lowe's employee open up the box and check the insulation before I get all the way home just to have to return the product again. They ended up opening at least 6 different EO Smith Gas Water Heaters of varying sizes (30, 40, and 50 gallon tanks), year rating (6, 9, and 12 year models), and styles (short units, tall units).... every single one had insulation hanging down so low that they posed a major safety/fire hazard.  
Lowe's only carry EO Smith brand water heaters in store.  I told them I would not put an EO Smith product in my house and requested that they ship me a comparable unit by a different manufacturer.  They agreed and stated that no other brands are carried in house and that they have to ship it to me.  As of writing this, I'm still without a hot water heater and still have no idea when the new one will be delivered. 
My fear is that there are countless others with these defective products in their houses not only in my community, but possibly all over the US.   It is only a matter of time before these units start a fire.
I have pictures of the first 2 defective units. I was unable to take photos of the units in the store that were also defective.
justification: The incident describes a safety risk with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.
