incident_description:
On February 26, 2020, I purchased a one gallon container of Sunnyside Paint Thinner, The product number is 701G1 and the UPC number under the bar code is 076542000303. The container is made of white plastic and the factory seal under the cap is still intact.

Over the course of the weeks since this purchase, I have noticed the odor of paint thinner in my basement whenever I went near the area where this paint thinner is stored. I have repetitively sniffed around my basement to determine the source of this odor as I am worried about causing explosive fumes to build up in my basement. I have an opened and partially used container of the same product as well as this new unopened container.

Each time I would notice the odor I would sniff for the source. But it was not the previously opened container of paint thinner that was emitting the odor each time I but the new unopened container. I even tried placing the new container of paint thinner in a different part of my basement and each time I find the odor of paint thinner is strongest next to the unopend container of paint thinner.  I have this container of paint thinner now sitting on my desk at my computer as I write this report to you. When I put my nose next to the container I can distinctly notice the outside of the container smells of paint thinner. Yet the container of paint thinner still has its intact seal under the cap.

Also, the plastic container has started to collapse inward as if some of the product has been removed and the container was squeezed to let the air out and then resealed again. But I assure you this container has never been opened. Any loss of liquid contents of this container must have occurred as a result of the out-gassing of the product through the walls of the plastic container after the container was filled and sealed at the factory. I would guess the perhaps about a half of cup of paint thinner has out-gassed so far from this sealed one gallon container of paint thinner judging from how much the container walls are sucked in.

I have also recently visited the same Menard's store where I purchased this product, and when I have gone by the paint department shelves containing this same product, I can also distinctly notice a fairly strong paint thinner odor in that area of the store. I even reported it to the paint department employee and had them come over to notice the odor but they didn't seem very concerned.

I am strongly concerned that the plastic that these containers are made out of is slightly gas permeable. I believe the paint thinner is slowly out-gassing through the walls of the container and evaporating but the air or nitrogen in the air space is not able to get through the container walls. Thus, the container is slowly collapsing inward as the paint thinner out-gasses through the container wall.

I believe that this is a safety hazard and should be investigated. Containers that are made to contain flammable solvents must be made of a plastic that is totally gas impermeable. I worry that millions of gallons of paint thinner are being sold all over the world in containers like this that are not totally impermeable to flammable solvents. Please respond to my concern and address this issue ASAP as I am sure that more of this product is sitting on store shelves all across the US waiting for purchase.  I will keep this container of paint thinner for a few weeks but must eventually return it if you do not contact me. The next time I buy paint thinner, I will purchase it in a tight sealing metal can.
justification: The incident describes a potential safety hazard with out-gassing paint thinner, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
Applying interior latex paint throughout house. Immediately noticed severe congestion , sneezing and asthma-like symptoms. Used nasal spray for 3 days per the label with temporary relief of congestion as a result. As the nasal spray wore off, congestion would return. After a few weeks (with continued painting) a rash around my eyes started to develop. I suspected an allergy to something in the paint. I had casually glanced through the Product Safety Data Sheets at the first onset and missed the single brief mention of isothiazolinones in the ingredients. It was not listed on the paint can label. About 8 years ago, I had a reaction to some sunscreen I was using that had methylchloroisothiazolinone in it. My dermatologist performed a patch test and that was the only item I had a positive reaction (allergy) to. In order to gain some relief, I visited my dermatologist and received 2 steroid injections.

Upon researching further, I understand that isothiazolinones were identified as the "allergen of the year" in 2013, and that their use in cosmetics is stricter, but also that it is in decline. It must be listed in the ingredients, so that makes it relatively easy to avoid.

Isothiazolinones are used in about 95% of the latex paint products on the market today, but are NOT required to be listed on the product label and MAY NOT be listed on the SDS forms. This includes products noted as "Low-VOC" or "No-VOC", which implies that they are healthier than products with higher VOC content.

For people with sensitivities to isothiazolinones such as myself, it presents a false sense of security. I happened to know what product to be looking for due to my previous positive test. Someone without this knowledge could postpone treatment until their reactions are much more severe.

Additionally, there is no real remedy with this product. It isn't like I can paint over the walls with another paint that doesn't have isothiazolinones in them as there are very few manufacturers available.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (asthma-like symptoms, rash, and requiring steroid injections) due to an allergic reaction to paint ingredients.

incident_description: Purchased several Tornado Vacuum Taskforce CFV 10 HEPA vacuums based on company's claim of "These units employ a multi-stage filtration process and uses a certified HEPA filter to capture particles down to .03 microns, resulting in a 99.97% efficiency rating." (see webpage https://tornadovac.com/store/product.aspx?pid=272).  Had these vacuums aerosol tested by a certified testing company to verify HEPA specifications and they failed miserably (less than 97% efficiency).  While the vacuums contain a certified HEPA filter, the housing for the filter is not designed correctly and does not seal, thereby allowing air to flow around the filter rather than through it.  These vacuums are marketed for "health care, abatement, and industrial uses" and claim to be "the answer for containing environmental waste in accordance with strict safety standards, such as the Renovation, Repair and Painting (RRP) Program..  This provides for a dangerous situation of the consumer assuming that the vacuum is removing 99.97% of dangerous particles when it is not.
justification: The incident involves a product failing to meet advertised safety standards, posing potential health risks, but no actual injury or death is reported.

It sounded like the compressor was still running but the fan was off.  Very hot air was coming from the top of the unit and it smelled like a burning electric motor.  I shut the unit off and waited until the next day.  I decided to try it again but would only have it running when I was in the basement. Vacuum builds a static charge so large that:
a) When one touches the vacuum, the discharge is strong enough to move one's arm
b) The unit must be touched several times to completely discharge the built up charge.
     Example: If I use an alligator clip on a plastic part and touch a grounded surface, such as
       a cold water pipe or receptacle outlet ground prong, the spark is large and visible in
      daylight. The clip must be held on the grounded item for several seconds before the
      charge is completely dissipated.
c) The charge is also evidenced by the large amount of airborne dust, hair and lint that
    clings to the unit.
d) On one occasion, gypsum dust which was attracted to, and clung to, vacuum exploded in
    a small "pop".

If I leave a cord clipped to the vacuum body with the other end solidly grounded, no charge builds up.

Thank You for taking time to review this report. I appreciate your efforts to ensure safe products.
justification: The incident involves a significant static charge causing physical movement and visible sparks, but no injury is reported.

The boiler chamber where the gas is ignited appears to have a flaw.  When burning the the side of the boiler chamber inside the boiler heats up so much that it glows bright orange.  Bosch confirmed this is not supposed to happen.  It melts the wiring inside the unit.  It has also melted the insulation inside the boiler.  The first unit stopped working because the wiring was melted completely.  The second unit we caught the issues as we smelled and saw smoke from the unit.  

This is a major fire hazard,  Most people would never check on their boilers.  These run at all hours and I would hate to think what would have happened if this caught fire while we were sleeping.  

There must be a design or manufacturing flaw as we have had the exact same issue happen on two boilers.    We have photos of the boilers.

incident_description:
WHEN I TESTED THE BABY RESCUE FIRE BAG for babies and children (which is for lowering a child down during a fire), IT BROKE AND FELL 3 STORIES. IT WILL KILL YOUR CHILD! 

I just tested my Baby Rescue Emergency Rapid Evacuation Device and IT SNAPPED IMMEDIATELY. If my child had been inside it would have killed him! Two hours later, IÃÂm still shaking. Here is what happened: I wanted to test the bag before an emergency so I filled it with 22 pounds of heavy material. I wrapped the rope around my wrist about 5 feet up from the bag, braced myself, then pushed the 22 pound bag out out window. It free-fell a few feet then snapped immediately and the baby bag dropped 3 stories to the ground. Thankfully no one was walking by or it probably would have killed them. It definitely would have killed my baby inside. 

Note, I wanted to let it free-fall for about 5 feet as I figured this is would would happen in a true emergency. My son is 45 pounds (5 years old) and the window is on the higher side. I was trying to simulate how I would get him out of the window. I am not tall enough to lower him slowly at the beginning (even though I'm 5 foot 9 in) so I figured I'd have to put the bag on the sill, brace myself, then ÃÂpushÃÂ him in the bag out the window while holding the rope or securing it around a piece of heavy furniture.

Anyway, when I checked out what happened, the thread broke (which was sewn from the bag to the rope). IÃÂll attach pictures. Looking now, I see that the thread doesnÃÂt look reinforced or thick at all. The rope is unimpressive, but the thread is worse. In fact, all the strings look cheaply sewn up and down the line on the ÃÂloopsÃÂ too. These loops would be what you would naturally hold onto or loop around something to secure the line. Likely these threads would spit at many points. There are hundreds of ÃÂweak pointsÃÂ all over this product. No rock climber would dare use this. It also wouldnÃÂt take a fireman much to look at the line and see how flimsy it is. I am guessing these products are not individually checked. I canÃÂt imagine not double checking a factory produced product when telling you that you should lower your baby 30+ feet in it. And to think that no one will know this until there is a fire and they fling their baby out the window and watch him free fall. At a cost of $118, a pretty high price, the consumer would never expect such a poorly made and sure-to-break product. As well, there is a statement in the instructions that tell you NOT to test it (or the rope wonÃÂt wind up again correctly) so perhaps no one has figured this out.
justification: The product failure would likely result in death if used in an emergency, and the poor construction suggests a high likelihood of failure.

I purchased a two pack of First Alert, Smoke and CO detectors, model number PC1210V on January 6, 2020 from Costco.  About 2 weeks ago one started beeping during the day, I took it down and reset it and it appeared to work.  This morning at 1:45 AM it went off and sounded an audible alert, thank G-d there was no issue.  I removed it and attempted to disable the device.  Following instructions on device back I was unsuccessful at disabling the device (as noted by items 1 and 2 in picture below).  I broke off portion of tab noted (the bottom one).  That was unsuccessful at silencing the alarm.  I then attempted to take apart the device, it was very difficult.  I used two 3/8ÃÂ long slotted screwdrivers and a hammer to break apart the device.  Fortunately, I did not hit the lithium battery and start a fire.
Believe these devices should be recalled.
ÃÂ	I am concerned others may experience similar issues with this smoke/CO detector and be unsuccessful in turning it off.  Then they may attempt to silence it by tearing it apart or by smashing it with a hammer/mallet.  This could cause a Lithium fire.  
ÃÂ	Per further exploration I surmised I was supposed to tear away/break away something located a few inches from the  ÃÂDEACTIVATEÃÂ instructions and arrow.  This is noted by items 3 & 4 noted on pictures.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning smoke/CO detector that caused a nuisance alarm but no actual injury or fire.

incident_description:
On 1.16.2019, I ordered two pairs of Baldarassario glass sliding doors from Wayfair.com, order #[REDACTED].  Then on 3.18.2020, about 15 minutes past midnight, my wife got out of bed and due to one of her legs being asleep, fell into one side of the closet door pair in which it shattered.  She cut her forehead and lip and sustained a bad sprained right ankle and foot.

The glass was advertised as "tempered" but while the majority broke as with safety glass, there were many long shards of glass (4-5" in length) still remaining that were potentially very dangerous.  

I contacted Wayfair via email and voicemail asking for an investigation into this product that they continue to sell without any response.  I did not want this to happen to anyone else in which those long shards of glass would cause great damage.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cut forehead and lip, sprained ankle) due to the glass shattering, but no death occurred.

incident_description: My two year old son was in his toddler tower from Simplay3 at our island in the kitchen.  The nanny and I were at the island with him, but we were on the other side of the island opposite of my son.  My son was playing with his toy cars, when he reached over to grab one from his left hand side, and his weight caused the tower to tip over, allowing my son to fall onto our hardwood floors.  He severely bumped his head, forcing us to rush him to the hospital.  This product is very unsafe because there are no stabilizers on the side, bracing a fall, if the toddler shifts his weight enough causing the toddler tower to tip over.  These toddler towers can be bought online at various retailers.

So we utilized it, following the directions on the package. We made ten different containers of soap, one to turn in as his project and the others to give out to family and friends. incident_description: On the evening of March 2, 2020, my 11 year old son got into the shower in our downstairs bathroom.  Nothing out of the ordinary occurred.  He started the shower, and when it was warm, he got in and closed the door.  He estimates that he had been in the shower for about 15 minutes when the glass door suddenly exploded.  He had his back turned to the door at the time to let the water hit the right side of his body, so he did not see the glass shatter, only heard it.  He says it was a very loud boom.  He turned around and saw glass everywhere, and at that time realized that he was bleeding very badly from a large, deep laceration on his left lower leg. He had to walk over the broken glass to get out, which caused multiple smaller lacerations on his feet.  My husband was able to place a tourniquet on his leg and then apply pressure to the wound while I called paramedics.  He was taken to the Emergency Department and treated for a laceration on his left calf that was approximately three inches long, gaped open widely, and extended through the full thickness of the dermal and subcutaneous tissues and about 1/2" into his gastrocnemius muscle.  Clearly the chunk of glass that hit his leg hit with significant force.  If it had hit him on a more vital part of his body, such as his abdomen, neck, or face, or if it had been one of our smaller children in the shower that night, it could easily have been fatal.  We are concerned that the glass company that installed the door may have done something that weakened the glass and made it more prone to shattering.  When the door was initially installed sometime in December, it didn't fit well and rubbed with opening and closing.  The glass installers took the door down, took it back to their shop, and "polished" the edge down to make it fit better.  We have learned through our research since this event that grinding down the edge of tempered glass can cause damage that makes it more prone to spontaneously shattering.  We are very concerned that they are not taking this seriously and are simply shrugging their shoulders and saying "we have no idea why this happened, we've never heard of such a thing."
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration requiring emergency medical treatment, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: About 6 months after my dad bought this product [air purifier], he passed away suddenly and very unexpected. Since the day he died I have beat myself up on what truly happened considering my kids and I were just there for the weekend and he passed that Monday at about noon. Everything was left up to me to deal with paperwork wise, his stuff, the house, etc. then about 2 months ago I came across this air purifier again. I had read the instructions when it first happened and it sounded dangerous and scared me so I just put it in storage. Well I started researching it for the last month and I believe it could have had something to do with his death. He had COPD, a stroke history and diabetes for sure. He wasn't always truthful with me about his health trying not to make me worry. Anyways, y'all ruled it to be COPD and complications from diabetes mellitus.I remember after he bought that and we would go over there, the smell in the house was completely changed. He ran it nonstop and he went downhill cognitively very fast afterward but I thought it was just a regular air purifier. I always wondered why I felt weird over there like lightheaded and confused until I left. Well it was a bit more than that. It is one that releases ozone in the air. I still don't know too much about it because I just recently learned of these kinds of products. I ran it here and it made my mom's house smell the same way. I only tried it 1 day and decided it was a dangerous product especially for my mom (67) and my 3 young children putting ozone in the air and shocking you if the back gets touched. I decided to call the company who made it and 2 different people couldn't give me any information on it and claimed they could not find it in the system so they would have a supervisor contact me but that never happened. I also read a warning on the back saying it was not for people with respiratory problems but the warning is written so small I didn't even see it until I looked the product all over.
justification: The incident resulted in a death, with evidence suggesting the air purifier's ozone emission may have contributed to the individual's decline in health.

incident_description: I bought a Ryobi RY907022FI generator based on the recommendation of [REDACTED]. I purchased the generator through Home Depot. When I started assembling the generator I ran across a manufacturing defect in step 3 where you attach the positive red cable to the battery. Per the assembly diagram the positive cable has another red wire bound with it and they are supposed to come around the front of the battery to be attached. The unit I received the second red wire was too short to be attached in this manner. The only way to attach it was over the top of the battery. The second red wire was so short that if you attached the cables the second red wire was snug against the housing of the generator. I consider this a safety defect since the housing will get hot and eventually melt the plastic covering of the wire. The wire will then come in direct contact with the housing. I don't know what will happen if that happens. Hopeful the unit will just short out and stop operating. I called Ryobi and they said to just return the item and reorder it. Home Depot picked up the defective unit and I reordered the exact same model. The second unit came with the same manufacturing defect.
justification: The defect poses a potential safety hazard due to the wire being too short and possibly melting, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
LEVO I - Small Batch Oil and Butter Herbal Infusion Machine - Precise Time and Temperature Controls For Easy and Mess-Free Homemade Infusions - Dishwasher Safe Components - Basalt 
Bought on Amazon.

Product requires holding down a "Load" button while inserting metal basket.  Was meeting with resistance while holding down button and inserting basket.
We were infusing olive oil.  Ran for 3 hours at 165 as the directions on Levo's website, there's a calculator, suggested to run for.
When done, pressing the "Release" button for the oil to come out did nothing.  Even tho it's olive oil and very thin, not viscous, we thought it must have gotten stuck in the rubber release tube.  So we opened the lid, it was very liquid, the release button didn't release a single drop.
We ran machine another 10 minutes in case olive oil was stuck, it was not, it still didn't want to come out of infusion chamber, and it's been cooking, so it's hot.  We held down the button over the course of 20 minutes to try to remove the oil.  Then it seemed done, no oil left.
A few minutes later, we looked on counter, entire counter was covered with infused olive oil!!!
It was underneath the LEVO I and all around this appliance, sitting in a giant puddle of oil.  All over our counters and then it seeped down front of kitchen cabinets.  A huge mess!  Hot oil.
So now I just tried to run it next to sink with nothing but water, see if it's leaking.
Sure enough!  This ELECTRIC appliance that gets very hot was throwing the water all over the place!
Looking closer, there's some kind of tiny air holes next to larger hole where the product is supposed to come out.  It was going out those holes.
Even worse!  It does seem to be coming from UNDER the machine, and the empty space in the back.
Nothing you are infusing should be in the empty panel along the back or UNDER the machine.  This thing is dumping the product you put in the holder out the tiny holes, under the machine, and all around the sides, everywhere except where it's SUPPOSED to be coming out!!!
I took videos and photos to show this.
The LEVO I has made a HUGE mess of our kitchen.  It is unreliable, dangerous, it's running on electricity, it creates very HOT liquid.
This thing should be recalled!  Sold thru Amazon, it's very dangerous.  I'm returning the whole stupid thing!
justification: The incident involved a significant mess and potential danger from hot oil, but no injury was reported.

I vapor-proofed the entire inside of my singlewide and also have a fresh air heat recovery ventilator with duct work putting fresh air right in where I sleep.  This problem is not formaldehyde vapor because formaldehyde vapor causes my nasal membranes to close up as if I had a cold, making it difficult to even breathe. This problem is different.  I can breathe OK but my lungs are getting irritated right at the top at the bronchial tubes right where the air first enters.  I quit using both units and felt better within hours.  I didnÃÂt realize I had a problem with the first unit.  It mustÃÂve been something that was accumulating.  I was only using the first unit during the day under my table in the kitchen and then I was using the [REDACTED] at night.  But I noticed both a reduced ability to breathe as well as the lung soreness in the morning.  But I attributed it all to the [REDACTED] infrared heater.

Then at night I used the first unit until my symptoms got so bad that I decided to quit using both units and just go back to my [REDACTED] 1500 watt model. I am NOT trying to return either unit.  IÃÂll probably eventually just disassemble them to at least recycle the metal. I noticed on your site that this same PTC heater element is used in several models, including the new smaller 1500 watt [REDACTED] heater that is about 12 inches by 9 inches by 9 inches.  So I donÃÂt think I should get that model.  Right now the only model I would trust is another one with the six heater tubes, the 1500 watt model.

Then there was the formaldehyde problem with flooring from [REDACTED] that was in the news not all that long ago.  That flooring was manufactured in China.  The manufacturers in China like to cut corners to bring down the price.  But a bargain on something that you just canÃÂt use is not a bargain at all.  IÃÂve always been more concerned about indoor air quality than price which is why I got the [REDACTED] in the first place.  
I was really excited about the Comfort Deluxe at first and even gave it a very good review at Amazon, even though I bought both units directly from AirNmore.  IÃÂm going back to Amazon to adjust that review but IÃÂm guessing that Amazon wonÃÂt post it.  I had a problem with some [REDACTED] blankets and they wouldnÃÂt post that poor review.  They only want to post the good reviews.  I disassembled my second unit last night and it is not that much easier to remove that single fined copper PTC element than it is to replace six heater tubes in the [REDACTED].  I had to remove both right and left sides to remove that copper PTC element.  I put everything back together and it worked OK again. So there is no doubt in my mind that something is wrong with the copper PTC heater element.  Again, both units give me the symptoms.  
So if the manufacturer recognizes the problem and comes up with a new heater element then IÃÂd be interested in putting in the new copper PTC heater element and trying that out. I admit that my lungs are more sensitive after living with formaldehyde in my singlewide for so long.  So perhaps IÃÂm the first person to let you know that there is definitely a problem.  That is what needs to be addressed.  Perhaps they could make a glass-enclosed filament surrounded by the finned copper of the same size so I could just swap it into the two units that I already have.  
So, again, I just wanted to give you a heads up.  I am NOT trying to get a refund. Win some and lose some as they say.

incident_description:
I bought a Bissell Cleanview Swivel Pet Upright Bagless Vacuum Cleaner, Green, 2252 on Amazon on 1-4-20 and it was delivered shortly thereafter. I put it together and started using it soon after that. It worked wonderfully well at first, but within 3 or 4 uses the roller brush stopped turning and I noticed a burning smell. Upon investigation, I discovered that a mass of pet hair and other debris had collected around the motor spindle that turns the belt, which was causing the belt to slip and then to start melting from the friction caused by the spindle continuing to turn against the now stationary belt. I took it apart and cleaned it well, and used it a couple more times before it happened again.
People have reported in the product's reviews on Amazon that this design flaw- where the debris that is supposed to be channeled into the collection receptacle instead leaks into the belt housing- has caused their machines to malfunction, break, and/or catch fire. I had read some reviews on Amazon before making the purchase, but didn't see the ones warning of this problem, which appear to number in the hundreds as of today (one of which is mine). 
Many have also reported difficulty trying to obtain help from Bissell and/or Amazon, although Bissell has left replies to many of the complaints that the person should call them and they will be happy to help.
This product, which the manufacturer and Amazon appear to have known for at least a year poses a fire hazard under normal operation, is still on the market.
Please do something about this.
justification: The incident describes a malfunction leading to potential fire hazard but no injury or death reported.

incident_description: I bought a front loading washing machine in late 2008.  It is a higher end brand, Bosch.  I have done all of the recommended things to keep the mold from growing and the washer from smelling including leaving the door open after each wash, cleaning the gasket regularly (almost with every wash), cleaning out the drain, running it with vinegar, running a wash with bleach and not only does it still smell in the washer, now continually, but my clothes are starting to smell.  I'm concerned our family's consistent sore throats and other symptoms may be a result of the mold.  I have also been dealing with the cycles not finishing and giving me an error code that, per the manual, indicates the drain needs to be cleaned. There's never much in there and cleaning it does not clear the code for more than a few washes, which may not even be due to the cleaning as it is not consistent with each wash to begin with. Not only should consumers not have to go through so much for a load of laundry, but we certainly should not look forward to having to scrap a functioning appliance due to mold, mildew, and smell!  I often return to the internet to see if anything new has been suggested, what I find is more and more complaints and lawsuits.  Why are the appliance manufacturers allowed to continue peddling such products that have clearly had the same issues since their inception?
justification: The description indicates persistent mold and smell issues with the washing machine, leading to family members experiencing sore throats and other symptoms, suggesting potential health impacts.

incident_description:
I experienced a chemical burn from using Easy-Off oven cleaner (the yellow can) to both my left and right ear canal. This occurred while spraying the chemical and having flash burn back from the spray. Thankfully I had my eyes protected (wearing protective glasses) and my hands with wearing gloves (as directed on the can). I read the instructions numerous times and never did it warn about possible burn to your ears. I got spray on my face and hair which I wiped off right away. I didn't realize how much had got into my ears until I looked in the mirror and saw they were black. This was scary. 

I was taken to the [REDACTED] burn unit via ambulance from [REDACTED] on Friday. The burn unit diagnosed my burn and determined it was a chemical burn. I am to return to the Burn Unit Clinic for Grafting treatment for my ears.

At this time my left ear is partial hearing and my right no hearing. Not sure what damage was done to my ear drum as the doctors and burn unit were not able to see into my ear canal due to the damage and swelling from the chemical burn.

I have photos of my ears, the can used, the glasses worn. In my medical charts (which I can get copies) it will state I had 2nd degree burns in both my ear canals that I would like to send to you. I have damage to my ear drum (to what degree we still don't know). I am unable to hear from my right ear and distorted hearing from my left ear. Pain is horrible. Taking medication to help relieve pain.
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd degree chemical burns, partial hearing loss, and significant pain, requiring medical treatment and grafting, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: The Molekule was used in my office. One day my lungs burned as I breathed, became very dizzy and felt like I would pass out, tremors and tachycardia was starting. There was a sensation of inhaling a chemical but I could not smell anything. Leaving my office alleviated the symptoms and would return in my office. I could not figure out where it was coming from and the air purifier was my last guess. The symptoms would reoccur the first hour of the day and right after lunch more strikingly (my door would be shut while absent). I finally decided to turn off the Molekule and my symptoms resolved. Since removing the Molekule from my office, I have not had any symptoms. I did, however, have severe nerve damage/inflammation, became more difficult for me to breath generally, and I have high levels of inflammation that I could not get down for 2 months. I have a rare disease and when I went online to a support group, many people in the group said they reacted to the chemicals released from the machine. I believe my incident was a sudden malfunction as I had it for 2 years. I wrote the company and they were in denial that their machine could possibly cause any issue. They refused to receive my unit and investigate it, I was told to recycle it. I did not want to sue or even replace, I just wanted the company to do the right thing and investigate. Research turned up that the destruction of antigens by the Molekule releases hydroxyls, which are dangerous to any person's health, but especially those of us who are immune compromised and would rely on equipment like Molekule
justification: The incident caused severe nerve damage, inflammation, and breathing difficulties, which qualify as an injury.

incident_description:
My wife noticed that our washing machine had brown and white flakes floating the the wash water and deposited on clothes after cycle was finished. We ran a self-cleaning cycle and the water in the washer had a significant amount of scum floating in the water during this cycle. Knowing that we had mold or mildew in our washer and that we are washing our 8-month old daughter's clothes, we could not use the washer until this is issue was resolved. We have run self-cleaning cycles per the owners manual since we bought this washer, always dry the tub and detergent tray following use and leave the door on the washer open at all times when it is not running. 

A simple online search returns hundreds of results on Samsung's online forum showing that this is a well-known and ongoing problem with certain models of these washing machines. I disassembled the washer by removing the washplate and basket. Removing the drum revealed gray/brown scum lining the inner plastic drum, the base plate of the basket, and the bottom of the washplate. We cleaned all parts with bleach and reassembled. 

After running three self-cleaning cycles, the wash water was still filled with scum. After additional research online I found several accounts that the washplate (Samsung Washer Washplate #SAM-DC97-18154A) may still have mold inside of it. The washplate on these washers is a plastic base with a metal overlay crimped onto the base. There is a small gap between the plastic and metal where water gets trapped and mold forms. Since the metal plate is not removable, there is no easy way for a consumer to clean or maintain the washer effectively. A self-clean cycle will not remove the buildup between these two pieces. 

It appears that the washplate is poorly designed (see attached photos). Simply gluing the two pieces together would eliminate ingress of water. A one piece design could also solve this issue. After removing the basket it also appears that the baseplate of the basket could have been designed to shed water so that another place for mold to grow was eliminated. Samsung has been receiving complaints online about this product for years and it is seems that the typical action is to recommend a service tech visit which is costly and cannot solve the problem in the long-term. 

This is a known problem to consumers and should be known to Samsung by now. It is my opinion that this issue stems from several design flaws that can render the appliance useless and/or unsafe. Many consumers do not have the time or ability to fully disassemble their washer to clean it and may not have the time or money to chase down a solution with Samsung. Consumers should not have to pay for costly repairs or do it themselves based on a poorly designed product.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw causing mold in the washing machine, posing a hygiene issue but no direct injury or death.

incident_description:
Crucial Power Systems
Model ES1.5 A0100 N1-S
S/N ES1562
This is an emergency lighting system designed to provide emergency egress lighting in the event of a utility power failure. The equipment consists of a power inverter, controller, touch screen control/monitor and batteries contained in a cabinet. The system uses one 120V AC circuit for input power and distributes output power to up to six 120V circuits. In the event of a utility power failure the system is designed to provide un-interrupted output power for egress lighting for a minimum of 90 minutes to be in compliance with current life safety codes. This particular system failed recently and shutdown output power to the egress lighting throughout the building. The lights were out until an electrician got to the site and temporarily bypassed the system and directly connected the loads to the line feed. Under certain circumstances this could be a hazardous situation. The building egress path was completely in the dark. The system should either fail to "lights on" or be provided with a bypass switch as a standard feature. The bypass switch is offered as an option.
justification: The emergency lighting system failed, leaving the building egress path in the dark, which is a hazardous situation but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
This report is in relation to fragrant laundry products every day, especially those emitted from dryer vents into the air I must breathe. Millions of people with MCS suffer negative impacts from fragrant laundry product emissions, as well as people who are active outdoors. I am unable to provide a specific brand name or manufacturer because this problem is similar to second-hand smoke; someone else is purchasing and using the products and impacting everyone around them.

Fragrant consumer product emissions are a serious problem that impacts the lives of millions of people. People with multiple chemical sensitivity (MCS) and also people who have not yet developed an injury from common scented household products suffer adverse effects from inhaling the fumes from fragrant consumer products. People with MCS are injured in multiple ways; they are unable to keep jobs and often become shut-ins to avoid exposures that have a negative impact on their health; they lose friends and family members who are unwilling to discontinue the use of fragrant consumer products; and they often suffer vicious attacks from neighbors who are addicted to fragrant consumer products. There are many people with MCS that are shut-ins, or are forced to live in cars or tents in the country to avoid exposures to fragrant consumer products. This is a tragedy that is unthinkable. 
We are forgotten and outcast like lepers. No employer wants to make accommodations even though this is an ADA disability; no landlord wants to make accommodations; and even our neighbors tell us we should move or go somewhere else. This does not work, the problems due to chemicals in fragrant consumer products are present everywhere and we desperately need the governing agencies to investigate the formulas, set safe limits, ban/recall products, and instigate better, more highly visible, warning labels. It is the synthetic chemicals that are at issue and not natural scents produced by flowers or food.

We are healthy and normal as long as we are not exposed to the toxins in fragrant products. All we need is clean air to breathe. Fragrances are designed to impact the limbic system and the amygdala in the brain (i.e; soothe, relax, energize...). They also stimulate the brain and nervous system in negative and harmful ways; but revealing this information is not a good marketing tool, nor is informing consumers that products contain phthalates, benzenes, toluene, formaldehyde or other toxic chemicals that are known carcinogens, reproductive toxins, respiratory irritants/sensitizers, or mutagens. 

I am not certain how much fragrance remains on laundry after the rinse cycle, but dryer sheets and essential oils can be extreme. These fragrances (or the chemicals in them) expand when heated in the dryer and their emissions pollute the air into which they are vented. These scents do not remain near the dryer vent, they expand to nearby homes and I have encountered them as far as two blocks from the source. Millions of homes emitting these chemicals is no different than factory emissions, and laundromats containing a large number of dryers running at once are even worse. Consumers seeking strong fragrance in their laundry don't follow instructions and even if they do, the new stronger, longer lasting products are presenting a consumer safety issue.

Manufacturers of these products, and the [REDACTED], are on a quest to create stronger, longer lasting fragrances simply because they generate sales and are not considering the health consequences. There are now laundry products (i.e.; Downy Unstoppable) that are made to last as long as three weeks). Fabrics are not the only thing these fragrances attach to, they are also attaching to hair, skin, eyes, nasal passages, olfactory nerves, throats and lungs. Simply being exposed to clothes that contain these chemical fragrances cause adverse effects and can trigger an asthma attack.

When I open my door, I have experienced headaches, migraines, respiratory irritation, flu-like symptoms, chest pain, vocal cord dysfunction, difficulty breathing, temporary dementia, muscle spasms, and non-fatal heart attacks. Migraines and chest pain are the most common symptoms I experience. Please don't suggest wearing a mask, we were not created to breathe chemicals and the U.S. should not be like India or China. We are better than that.

Since fragrances are regulated by multiple agencies (FDA, EPA, OSHA and CPSC) depending on the product to which they are added, I must address each agency respectively.  However, the number of products containing fragrances is growing; including consumer products like garbage bags. I am glad to see the actions CPSC has taken on numerous hazardous consumer products. However, there is a dire need for the CPSC to set restrictions on fragrant products whose use impacts multiple, unwilling, people. Proposed actions include initiating inspections, banning/recalling products, and mandating labeling for fragrant consumer products that inform consumers to the hazards of their use.

Please put fragrant laundry products, especially fabric softeners and essential oils on your immediate agenda. Millions of people will thank you, especially those of us with MCS.
I will submit additional requests for essential oils, diffusers, fragrance warmers, and scented candles.

Best regards,

[REDACTED]
justification: The description details significant health impacts including respiratory issues, migraines, and non-fatal heart attacks, indicating injury (severity 3). The widespread use of fragrant products suggests occurrence is likely (4).

incident_description:
Upon replacing batteries in my smoke detectors, I found that most of them would not operate with the fresh batteries.  I have 5 smoke detectors all of the same brand, model and date of manufacture.
The same battery terminal has oxidation on most of the detectors.  The name brand batteries I removed were only a year old and not corroded.
To make these detectors work, I had to scrape the terminal with the end of a screwdriver then sand with emery cloth.  It took several attempts to get a few of these detectors working again.  I almost gave up.
I know most people would not know how to aggressively clean terminals like this.  It may mean that some people assume their detectors are working when they are not.  This is obviously a dangerous situation.
I am also concerned that with the plating removed from the contacts after sanding, that the battery connection through the terminal may cease at any time due to more oxidation forming.  This would leave the device non-functional.
The issue is probably the plating used on the terminals or the application of the plating.
After an hour or more of concerted effort, my 5 detectors are working.  The question is for how long.
justification: The incident describes a potential failure of smoke detectors due to terminal oxidation, which could lead to non-functioning devices and increased fire risk, though no injury or death is reported.

When the machine stopped, we opened the lid and one set of queen sheets was clumped together.  My wife noticed shredded rubber on the floor on the right side of the machine.  We called Whirlpool this afternoon and reported what had happened.  They referred me to the Safety Department.  Again I repeated what had happened and they set up a service call with GUINCO.  I asked the woman in the Safety Department why this machine didn't have an out of balance sensor and buzzer to notify the user.  She replied that she wasn't an engineer and could not answer this question.  She admitted that these machines tend to jump around but are built to take it.  In my opinion, this is a safety issue.  The machine should have some way of shutting itself down.  Imagine if we had been away when this happened.  Who knows what might have happened?  This seems to be a design issue and a violation of the Fitness for Particular Purpose.  I request that you investigate this issue.

incident_description:
Yesterday I started a load of clothing in my Whirlpool Calypso electric dryer (model GEW9868KQ3). Immediately after I pushed the start button, sparks and smoke started coming from the control panel area. I disconnected the dryer from the power source, grabbed a fire extinguisher and opened the control panel. The inspection revealed that we had been incredibly lucky. The "technician service manual" that had been taped to the inside of the control panel wall had come loose and made contact with the control panel itself. The manual was on fire and so was the control panel. 

This fire was not due to negligence, lack of maintenance or improper use. It was due to a dangerous practice of taping a paper manual less than one inch from the circuit board. Upon reviewing other complaints filed with the CPSC, apparently Whirlpool has done this with multiple models. In this instance, we were very fortunate that the fire did not spread, mainly because we were home at the time and put it out immediately. Had this happened when we were not at home, the fire could have destroyed our entire house. 

This is a dangerous oversight that can, thankfully, be corrected if Whirlpool addresses it. I urge the CPSC or other oversight bodies to address this immediately before someone loses their home or life to a completely preventable fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was quickly contained, resulting in no injuries or deaths, but posed a significant risk of property damage.

I was tinning and soldering some wires for my car stereo project.  I needed a different gauge wire for the next step so I turned torch off and set it on my work table to get some wires from my cabinet behind me.  When the turned around to continue my work, the torch was still on.  I just taught and said to myself that maybe I didn't turn it off and left it at that.

Approximately two or three months after that incident, I was using the torch on some heat shrink tubing and something worse happened.  As I was using the torch as a heat blower to shrink some tubing,  my phone rang.  Again, I turned the Ronson Torch off and set it on my work table.  I went to our living room to answer my cell.  After hanging up, I headed back to my work table.  I was maybe 10 feet away when I noticed that the torch was still on.  And at that exact moment, I heard a sound that resembles something like a combination of air coming out when you get a puncture in your tire and water heater being turned on.  And then a big ball of flame (approx 2 feet) which knocked down the torch which also fell on the floor still lit.  But this time, the flame was coming inside the torch body.  And you can tell the flame was pressurized.  Since it was burning on a concrete floor with nothing flammable around it,  I didn't even bother trying to put it out.  I figured it will soon extinguish by itself when the butane runs out, which it did. 

I could not have been on the phone that long (10 -15 min).  And even if I was on the phone longer than that, the torch should not have exploded like that and it should have turned off and release the flame hold lock.
justification: The incident involved a torch malfunction leading to a fireball, but no injuries or damage occurred.

incident_description: Water heater (whirlpool) from 2014 (here when we bought the house spring 2018) shut off in the middle of the night between Jan 1 2020 and Jan 2 2020. When I woke up in the morning I followed the instructions to relight but was unable to get the pilot going. I called the Whirlpool service hotline after several attempts because our water heater was still under warranty. They took me though all the steps several times, but could not get it to light. They said they would send me out a gas control valve. Days later it arrived and I replaced the gas control valve, but still could not get the pilot to light. After calling back the service line they told me they would send me a Thermopyle and the rest of the electronics. After taking apart the front of the unit I discover that the old igniter was melted and shorting out against the air intake tube. After replacing the igniter wire I successfully got the pilot to ignite. I then turned the gas valve to low which lit, but glowed a dull hazy orange flame for about thirty seconds at which point a blue flame began backfiring out the air intake tube repeatedly which sounded like a jet engine. I immediately shut the gas off and called again the hotline. They told me that my intake screen was dirty or my air flow was being restricted through the vent tube leaving my residence. I took apart the entire burner which I noticed had holes in the top of the screen. I used a shop vac to clean the screens (which looked clean already) and I inspected the air exhaust vent which looked clean and flowed freely. At this point I reassembled the unit and relit the heater only to have a blue fireball erupt out of the air intake orifice. I googled water heater backfire and found a youtube video that showed the exact problem that I was experiencing which said that the burner had failed and to get it replaced. I called the hotline again and spoke with a gentleman named [REDACTED] who was the most helpful and friendly. He was the first person who told me my water heater was recalled and that it was a part defect and that I needed to shut off the gas and call a professional. I am extremely upset that I called the hotline at least 5 times and gave my serial number but nobody except [REDcted] told me that my heater was recalled and could potentially hurt my family. I am more than disappointed that nobody thought to share that with me and they let me attempt to fix my heater putting me at risk.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning water heater with potential safety risks, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My wife bought me a Sharper Image battery-powered (rechargeable) tire inflator for Christmas 2018.  Its appearance is similar to a cordless drill but instead of a drill bit protruding from its nozzle, there is a short flexible tire hose with a valve that fits the standard Schroeder type used by all vehicles and most recreational products that have pneumatic tires on them.  It is in reality, a portable air compressor.

It features a digital readout which allows you to manually set your desired pressure.  Once set, you pull the trigger and let it run until the target pressure is reached. I had used it a number of times on my family's vehicles and enjoyed its convenience and efficiency.  

On one occasion I attached it to a deflated tire on a lightweight twin wheeled wheel barrow. I set the 22psi pressure recommended and left it alone to run until completed.  It ran for about 4 minutes and then stopped, having reached the desired pressure.  Instead of detaching the unit from my wheelbarrow tire, I left it there. No harm I assumed; job done.

A while later I set off my nearby lawn sprinkler.  Thinking nothing more about the lawn or the inflator after approx 10 mins, I was puzzled by a sound I thought may be at first was air caught up in the garden hose.  It was soon apparent that it was the SI inflator/compressor.  Realizing that I'd heard the noise for a while, I approached the valve with caution. When I tried to release the trigger, there was an almighty BANG!  It was so loud, my wife came running around from the front of the house thinking that a shotgun had fired very close to us!  

My assumption is that the water from the sprinkler shorted out the inflator's preset internal max pressure setting and allowed it continue until the battery would expire.  It completely ripped apart both the tube and the tire. 

Reporting the incident to Sharper Image, they, at first seemed concerned, telling me that they'd forward my unit to a special department. However,  their response to  a couple of follow up calls was ultimately to forward me a refund in the form of a credit.

In our town about 12 years ago, one tire dealer was killed when a regular hose was left on a wheel barrow tire that did not have the required safety cage over it.  Had this been set on a higher capacity tire typically found on a regular car or truck, the result could have been similarly catastrophic.

I belief that this product had not been thoroughly tested  prior to it being available for sale and so is extremely dangerous.  I also believe that other retailers sell the same unit under different names.
justification: The incident caused property damage (tire and inflator) but no injury, and similar incidents are unlikely under normal use conditions.

incident_description: [redacted****] Fire Department responded to a reported fire within a building on December 6, 2019. Upon arrival, we found that a fixed electrical ceiling mounted heater had been on fire and was extinguished by an occupant [redacted*] with a portable dry chemical fire extinguisher. After extinguishment, the circuit breaker had been turned off by the occupant. The fire appeared to originate at the heating element. The heater was photographed and left in place. The property has two identical buildings on it, which are used for servicing and washing of rental vehicles. Each building has two vestibules, with identical ceiling heaters in each vestibule. The occupant, [redacted**] stated that one of the other heaters had a previous fire early in the summer. That heater was still in place, with the circuit breaker turned off. I examined that heater and photographed it. The fire damage was not as extensive as this fire, but appeared to have originated in the heating element in a similar fashion. The occupant stated that the other two heaters, which did not have fire damage, have not been used and their circuit breakers have been off. The heaters are manufactured by [redacted***] and are model #F48483. The heaters have date codes of 0214. Because of the similar nature of the fires, of two identical models of the same heater, this is being reported for follow up by the CPSC and/or the manufacture for further investigation.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased an LG washing machine from Sears in 2011 and have been using it with no problems for the past 8 1/2 years.  On December 4, 2019, I was washing two pillow cases, two towels and a mattress cover. My washing machine is on the main floor and I was upstairs.  Suddenly, I heard a very loud explosion.  When I got downstairs, the bi-fold door in front of my washer was standing in the hallway.  The top of the washer had blown off, the sides were bent outward, and there was a hole in the wall behind the washer.   I reached out to LG  that same day and they sent me an email the next day asking me for pictures, a copy of the purchase receipt, the serial, product and model numbers of the washer.  I sent all but the serial number because it was behind the washer and I was unable to move the washer.  When my husband returned home, we were able to move the washer to get the serial number which I sent to LG on December 9th.  As of today, December 13th, I have not heard anything from them.  After doing some research, we have learned that there was a recall on this model.  We never received notice of the recall.  I don't know about later models, but this model is very dangerous and more should have been done to make the consumers aware of the danger.  I was fortunate enough to be upstairs when the explosion occurred.  Had I been downstairs taking clothes out the the dryer, I could have been injured or killed.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries, as the user was upstairs during the explosion.

incident_description:
The product was being used to dry clothes.

We believe there is a product safety issue with Whirlpool Cabrio Dryers.
>>>> There was a Class action Lawsuit against Whirlpool, and we believe this was dismissed. Unfortunately, everything we see regarding these dryers is what happened with ours. We hope and pray you will investigate this. Since we have purchased this dryer, we have had trouble with the heating element. It just stops heating. We realize now; it stops heating because there has been a fire, and it automatically trips an internal shutoff. Unfortunately, this takes place after it smells like we have had a fire in it. We have had at least three visits to our home in the last five years to fix this dryer. The technician fixed the unit the first two times. However, this last time, it was a significant fire. When the technician pulled the inside of the dryer out, there were at least 4-5 inches of lint build-up. Lint was all over the inside of the bottom and on different parts of our dryer. There was nowhere for the lint to go. It was apparent the vent unit in the dryer never worked correctly. The way the dryer was designed did not allow for appropriate venting. We previously had an [REDACTED] dryer, and we never had issues like this before. When seeing if our outside vent was blocked, air quickly passed through our homes vent. We are concerned about this model of dryer and believe it should be immediately recalled. With this fire we could have lost our children, spouse, animals, our home, and belongings. We have a hard time understanding with so much documentation online, and with the danger of this product, why it has not been recalled yet. If you could please investigate this and consider a recall, we would appreciate it.
justification: The incident involved a significant fire in the dryer due to lint build-up and design flaws, posing a severe risk to life and property, though no actual injury or death was reported.

Had a second plumber come out and verify install was correct including gas pressure and venting.  Also noticed the burner appeared to have a leak in the supply tube under the burner.  Contacted Rheem and had a new burner and TRD sent out.  They last until yesterday November 30th 2019 when the third TRD failed.  Appears to be some serious lack of quality control which causes fires from under the burner pan.

incident_description: This report is about a Kenmore Elite Oasis Type 580, model 110.27062600 top loading washing machine. Last night I was running a load of laundry in the washing machine. My family and I were in a different area of the house. We heard a sound like loud thunder followed immediately by what sounded like a bomb exploding and the house shook. I ran toward the source of the sound and saw the washing machine looked like it had exploded, with the sheet metal sides twisted and forced outward. The back steel panel was blown loose, and the lid and top frame were attached only at the back corner. There were machine parts and broken pieces of shrapnel scattered throughout the room, along with dirt and lubricating grease from the washer parts. Some of the wet clothes were located on the floor behind the drum. The tray for dispensing detergent and softener was ejected forward onto the floor. The washer rotated sideways and punched a 12 inches wide by 8 inches tall hole in the wall, and there was another smaller hole by the baseboard below. The gas dryer had serious damage from the impact and is inoperable. Next to the far side of the dryer there was a steel clothes rack that had a leg broken by the force of the dryer impacting it. After seeing the damaged dryer, I ran to the basement to shut off the gas and then came back and turned off the water supply lines and unplugged the power cords. The washer had been functioning normally and there was no warning or sound before the incident occurred. This washing machine normally is very quiet. We are in a tight spot financially with needing a new washing machine and dryer, hiring someone to repair the wall, needing to replace some damaged and stained clothes, and taking off work to clean up and go shopping. My family was shook up by the experience but we are grateful that no one was in that room when it happened and no one was hurt.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries, as the family was not in the room when the washing machine exploded.

incident_description: My report is to let the public know the consequences of being around during and after spray foam insulation installation in the home.  On 9/20/19 we were having our home repaired with Natural Therm Lapolla Foam - Lock 500 being sprayed in the kitchen ceiling and master bedroom and bath ceilings.  This is a second home which is very small about 1100 square feet.  My husband was in the family room during the process until they told him not to be in there, I was outside.  Afterwards we all entered the home to review the job and make sure we were happy.  This is when I asked about the toxicity of the product and how long it would take to be safe in the home since we were planning on sleeping in the family room which is openly next to the kitchen.  We were told when the smell was gone it would be safe to be in the home.  I was then told to open windows and doors in the upper master bedroom to let this floating molecule out of the house.  I went into that bedroom several times to open, close, and open again windows and doors.  We then left the house and came back later in the day to sleep in the house.  We both have suffered immediate health consequences from this incident.  My throat and tongue felt as if it were coated in a thick yellow substance.  I had a minty and tingling feeling in my throat, roof of mouth and tongue.  Over the next month, these symptoms felt worse and other symptoms began, vision impairment, puffy feeling in top and sides of throat, white lesion deep in throat, loss of taste, large bumps in back and on sides of tongue, hoarseness, continued minty or metal feeling all over tongue, eyelid puffiness, extremely dry mouth.  I had hoped these symptoms would go away.  They did not.  After looking in my mouth with a flashlight, I was frightened by what I saw.  Everything was yellow and looking inflamed.  I immediately went to a primary care doctor who did not know how to help me but treated me for thrush in case it helped.  I then went to an ENT who totally refused to acknowledge my concerns of my exposure to isocyanates and told me I had burning mouth syndrome.  I then contacted CDC and local poison control who were not helpful.  I of course know that my exposure to this chemical cannot be undone but am very concerned if cancer will be in my future.  Also the fact that doctors don't seem to be very aware of how to treat someone with a chemical exposure, or at least tell you where to go and what to do, was surprising to me.  It seems to me that this chemical is very dangerous during application and during it's airing out time and should be emphasized to home owners, do not be in the house at all!!  The info online only addresses workplace exposure and the health impacts were death from extreme exposure, the milder symptoms were skin irritation and asthma.  Nothing online addressed my symptoms.  My husband is also experiencing many of the symptoms that I have.
justification: Both individuals suffered immediate and prolonged health consequences from chemical exposure, including throat and tongue issues, vision impairment, and other symptoms, indicating injury.

incident_description:
The first day of November 2016. That was the day I gave birth to my baby boy. An hour later, my husband and I said our final goodbye to him. My son was born with Anencephaly, A serious birth defect where the baby is born missing parts of the brain and skull. Thankfully, we were prepared for this terrible event, having learned about his condition at an earlier sonogram. One of the known causes for this tragic condition is exposure to toxic chemicals in early pregnancy. I would like to share my story in the hope that other readers will understand the dangers of Moisture Cure Urethane (MCU) hardwood floor finish. When we decided to scrape the floors in our home, wanting to do our due diligence, we asked Mr. [REDACTED]- a man who is very educated about toxic chemicals that are used  in paint and floor finish - for his advice. He warned us not to do it as it was potentially dangerous, especially to an unborn baby. At this time, I was not yet aware that I was expecting, so we chose to go ahead with it, in spite of the advice he gave us. Incredibly, the scrapers who did the work told us that MCU is safe. In case there are those who suspect that there might have been other causes for my son's condition, I need to note that I had no infections or viruses throughout the entire time. This medical condition also has no genetic explanation, and I took plenty of folic acid throughout. I believe that my child condition was of MCU, and I hope that in the zechus of my doing my part in bringing awareness of this issue, and thereby, I hope my story will serve as a wake-up call. 
*P.S. Moisture Cure Urethane ingredients are Xylene, Toluene Dilsocyanate TDI, Erhyl Benzene, Ethyoxy Ethanol Acetate, Parachloro Benzotri Flouride, Tert Bityl Acetate, Aromatic Hydrocarbons and more.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a newborn due to a serious birth defect linked to exposure to toxic chemicals.

incident_description: At approximately 10:30pm pst, a hallway smoke alarm located on the ceiling above the emerson unit, was triggered. Upon investigation the top of the emerson thermostat was on fire. The flame was about 4 to 5 inches high and burned a CO2 detector located above it. The wall has sustained some damage, mostly to the exterior.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing damage to equipment and the wall, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: My wife was using the space heater in the living room to provide supplemental heat when she heard a pop, and an unusual noise.  She immediately turned it of and unplugged it.  There is a small electrical burn hole in the bottom/base of the heater.  I took off the back cover and discovered that the wiring where the external power cord was connected to the interior electronics (connected by wiring caps) was charred/burnt and melted.  This heater was being used for everyday household use and wasn't being abused.  I believe this heater would have most certainly started a fire in the house if it was left unattended.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual injury or death, but significant damage to the heater.

incident_description: September 5th, 2019 my son was in the bathtub and suffered two lacerated tendons and ligament in his right hand due to a shattered Delta brand shower door.  He was in the tub when one of the two rollers fell off the track above.  One corner of the shower door was resting on the side of the tub. When touched the shower door to raise it back up, it shattered completely.  Instead of small, pebble-sized glass shards, many pieces did not break and fell in hockey puck sized shards, one of which severely cut his right hand.  A visit to the emergency room was required, followed by surgical repair, and weeks of physical therapy.  A follow up procedure is likely in order for him to regain complete mobility in his hand.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries requiring emergency room visit, surgery, and physical therapy, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances described.

justification: The washing machine malfunctioned violently but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My wife and I purchased a Jotul Katahdin GI 450 DV II TSI, serial # 30878, on December 21, 2015. This is a gas fireplace insert that was bought from and installed by KC Stoves and Fireplaces of Alburtis, Pennsylvania. The fireplace insert would not start when we tried to start it on October 14, 2018. We went to KC Stoves on October 16, 2018 and [REDACTED], the owner, told me to replace the batteries. All batteries were replaced the day before. [REDACTED] then told me to look for a broken wire in the lower, control section of the fireplace. I asked why a wire would just break but I got no response. I looked in this area, behind a narrow door, and didn't see a broken wire. We had problems starting the insert off and on throughout the winter of 2018-19. We returned once more during the season, and were told to again look for a broken wire. On August 21,2019 we changed all batteries and tried to start the fireplace. It would not start. We went to KC Stoves the same day and again he told us to look for a broken wire. We returned home and this is when I checked the CPSC web site. Immediately I saw our fireplace was recalled in December 2012. The date on our Operating Booklet that came with the insert is 2012 and the serial # indicates 2012. Why were we sold a recalled fireplace that was 3 years old ? We went to KC Stoves on September 11, 2019 and showed [REDACTED] the recall notice. He made copies and said he would contact Jotul. On 9-24-2019 [REDACTED] from KC called and said she just faxed the info to Jotul. On 10-01-2019 [REDACTED] from KC called and left a message that was hard to understand. My wife called back and we were told we could come to their store and pick up the repair kit or if they came out to do the repair there would be a service charge. The fireplace is unplugged. When I look behind the door with a very bright light I can see that a wire connected to the pilot light switch is frayed and is contacting the metal base. We are afraid to use this recalled fireplace insert.
justification: The incident involves a recalled fireplace with a frayed wire posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
Our Vertex domestic hot water heater by AO Smith Corporation of McBee, South Carolina, was installed two years ago.  It is a high-efficiency natural gas unit used for domestic hot water and heating our house. 
It was installed new Oct 2017, and began having explosive starts in late July 2019.  Once the explosive starts begin, they continue every time it starts.  
When it calls for heating water, it starts the heating phase with a loud bang from an explosion of the gas. Servicemen have come to repair it and consulted extensively with the mfgrÃÂs Tech Service, yet it repeatedly reverts to explosive starts, which have gotten more powerful.
I have more than average homeowner experience with hot water heaters and their installation and maintenance.  My diagnosis is that the ignition is delayed while gas builds up in the combustion chamber.  Then, when the ignition kicks in, there is excess gas in the chamber which ignites and causes the explosion.   When it was serviced in August for this problem, the plumber, working with the AO Smith technical service line replaced the ignition components. 
In a subsequent call, the manufacturerÃÂs technical service said there was likely a problem with the air intake or exhaust, but after tearing them apart, no obstruction was found.  Note that a prior version of the Vertex hot water heater had served in the exact same location WITH THE SAME AIR SUPPLY AND EXHAUST for over seven years with NO problem. 
We also had the houseÃÂs gas supply line and regulator tested twice and each time it has been perfect. 
When this first started in July, the noise of the explosion was distinct and loud.  But it has gotten worse.
Yesterday, the explosion was so powerful that I thought a car hit our house.  
When this happened in September, I turned it off to stop the explosive starts.  Our plumber could not come immediately and we needed hot water so I temporarily turned it back on after it had been off for a day.  It started without incident, and so I let it run, and it operated for several weeks without a problem until yesterday.
After the very loud explosions that happened every time it started yesterday, I turned it off again and let it sit.  Based on the experience from September, I turned it back on this evening, and it started properly, and has been running through a cycle without incident.  
Based on past experience, it could run for weeks without problem, but then start back up with explosive starts without warning, which will continue until it is shut down to rest.  
I have begun to turn it off if IÃÂm going to be away for a day or more.  But as cold weather approaches, I canÃÂt risk that any longer.  But I also canÃÂt risk having these unpredictable, stunning explosions which are getting worse. 
I called the manufacturerÃÂs Technical Service several times, starting last July and again today.  They have no suggestions other than things that have already been tried at least twice already.  They blame everyone and everything but themselves for this defective product.
justification: The incident involves explosive starts of a water heater, which are dangerous but have not yet caused injury or death.

incident_description: I smelled a burning smell when I went into my garage and after looking around realized it was our solar inverter. It smelled like it was burning inside and was hot to the touch. I called the number listed on the box and they instructed me on how to shut the power off to it so hopefully it would stop burning. They were the installer of the product but not the manufacturer. Sunpower the installer came out for a service call a week later and saw that the inverter had caught fire inside the box but since it was out of warranty said there was nothing they could do. I then called a repair person out and they told me this product was recalled because of this issue. I was never notified of this, you would assume the installer would have note of this for this product but never said anything. I have attempted to contact the manufacturer schneider electric multiple times with no response.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and a fire inside the inverter, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
2 identical Artic King Dehumidifiers model WDP70AE7N failed within 1 month of each other leaking water all over carpet and walls.  Both units worked as advertised approximately 1 year into their purchase date.   Both units were manufactured 5/2017 and were purchased new from Walmart.  The water would suddenly and without warning leak out within the inside of the dehumidifiers instead of emptying into the buckets. This was disturbing as a electrical shock was very possible.  When the first unit failed we thought it was a fluke but when the second unit failed exactly the same way we contacted the company.   The Artic King company admitted they were "manufactured defects" but took no responsibility and strung us along with request of damaged pictures and a estimate of damage.  Once we did all the leg work with pics and professional estimates of documenting the damage, the company had pushed a low ranking operator to say they were not responsible as the units were used "improper"??   This was after multiple pictures and the company admitting they were manufactured defects.  To add insult to injury they recommended we could still salvage the 2 defective dehumidifiers by running a hose out the back instead of using the front buckets.  This was absolutely shocking and disgraceful.
   At this point we brand new carpet that is destroyed as well as mold damage on carpet and baseboards.
justification: The incident involved property damage (carpet and walls) and potential electrical shock risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer estimates that he uses the drill 10 times per month and may have used it for a total of 30 days since he purchased it.

10/1/2019:  The consumer used the drill for approximately 30 minutes (off and on), when parts of the drill separated.  The consumer heard a grinding type of noise and stopped using it.  He saw a few small pieces of plastic on his hand.   He held the drill up for further examination, but didn't see any damage.  He pulled the trigger to start the drill and the grinding noise continued and that is also when small plastic parts shot from inside the drill and hit him in the face.

The consumer was wearing his regular eye glasses and he was not injured.


There is a plastic ring, approximately the size of a silver dollar inside the drill and that is where the plastic pieces separated from.

The drill does not appear to be included in any CPSC recall.
justification: The incident involved parts of the drill separating and small plastic pieces hitting the consumer's face, but no injury occurred as the consumer was wearing eye glasses.

When it touched the wood it was going so fast it bounced off of the wood and hit my knee and split it wide open. incident_description: The dehumidifier was being used in the basement to take moisture out of the air.  The basement is completely finished and has baby grand in room so humidity needs to be in check.  The dehumidifier quit removing moisture and found that it had been recalled due to fire hazard.  The back of the unit was very hot to the touch when I shut it off and ceased use.  Would like full refund of $289.00 be sent to me being this unit was recalled and I was very fortunate that I averted a house fire.
