incident_description:
On 04/14/16, Thermoseal 500 foam was installed in the ceiling of my attic. The outside temperature was about 35 to 40 degrees Fahrenheit. The supply lines were laid in snow for a distance of about 30'. The temperature in the attic was 45 to 50 degrees. Two boys sprayed at the same time in a 24x48 attic. The foam was installed, in a haphazard manner with no uniform thickness to a depth from 8" to 12" (est.). There was no pause between passes, just continuous spraying. During the operation one of the guns broke and big chunks of foam were sprayed in part of my attic. My wife and I and our pets were present during the install. 
We were told that the chemical smell would be gone in a couple of days. The smell is still here and becoming more noxious as time goes by. The odor is more apparent now because I had air conditioning installed and the windows are all closed. The foam insulation was in preparation for the AC, since we didn't want to cool the attic. After a 6K bill for foam it took time to save for the AC.
My wife has an almost constant cough and my nose runs constantly.
justification: The incident describes improper installation of foam insulation leading to health symptoms (cough, runny nose) but no severe injury or death.

incident_description: Used Tide Original HE liquid detergent in my washer as I have for years.  Noticed a strong perfume smell.  My daughter and I both got headaches.  Finally figured out it was the detergent.  Nothing on the container notes that formulation has changed.  Contacted the company which noted they changed the scent earlier this year.  Unsafe to market this as ÃÂ originalÃÂ, as it is obviously not original.  Others may develop more severe allergic reactions than us.  Company admits they changed the scent.  They need to change the packaging to reflect this change.
justification: The incident caused headaches (injury) due to the changed detergent scent, but no severe allergic reactions or death occurred.

incident_description: We have an issue with insulation that was installed in our home. It was installed in the attic and walls at the end of July and that was the last day we were able to live in our home due to a variety of symptoms upon re-entry into the residence which include:. Burning tongue, eyes, headache, and nausea. We have been staying in a temporary residence. We have a 8 month old (6 months at the time). I sent my husband to get her crib and items from the house and everything weve brought from there has the smell and accompanying symptoms. We took items back to our house but the temporary reaidence maintained the smell. We are now with another family member. We had air quality testing done at 6 weeks from the install date. We received results and there are a variety of VOCs present in the home at levels higher than (and in some cases double) acceptable standards according to state or federal guidelines. There is also formaldehyde at levels.. Poison control doesn't think we should be living in our house with levels where they are.
justification: The incident caused multiple health symptoms (burning tongue, eyes, headache, nausea) and required relocation, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the presence of high VOC and formaldehyde levels.

incident_description: My son got hurt by shattered glass shower door while taking a shower.

incident_description:
The submitter is reporting the product for posing a health hazard. She claims the product emits a harmful fume that caused her adverse health effects.

She said the independent neighborhood painter painted her apartment on March 24-26 and shortly after she began experiencing adverse health effects. She also said there was a strong chemical odor in the apartment that she believes was due to the paint or tint in the paint. Her symptoms included headaches, nausea, fatigue, a chemical taste in her mouth and pain in her nostrils. 

She believes the tinted paint emits a harmful fume. She said the health symptoms and fumes did not diminish until 4 months later when she repainted her apartment. 

She contacted the firm (800-454-3336) and reported her concerns sometime on April 15, 2019 (Case # [REDACTED]). The firm Reps claimed the paint had nothing harmful. She spoke with Senior Tech Service Rep., [REDACTED], who took the information and said he would get back to her but he didnÃÂt. She then called back and spoke with [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] provided instructions for airing out the apartment then said she would look into the matter and get back to her but she didnÃÂt. 

She also contacted the retailer both Home Depot and Glidden paint and reported the concerns but they referred her to the firm. 

She has been seeking treatment with her allergist, her cardiologist and primary care. She said she is waiting to hear about her blood work and whether her liver was affected by the fumes. My liver was not affected however I do not know if recent dx of heart arythemia is related to stress due to this issue
justification: The submitter experienced adverse health effects including headaches, nausea, and fatigue, which qualify as an injury.

incident_description:
While using a jobsite table saw for dado groove cutting in a 1x2 piece of wood for a cabinet drawer I was making, the workpiece moved unexpectedly and shot back at me, pulling my left hand's thumb interior and ring finger nail area into the blade.

I rushed to a local urgent care and was given 9 stitches on the thumb and 3 on the ring finger. I was not using the kickback device as the workpiece was too small (approx 6" long), and the cut I was attempted prevented me from using the provided plastic push stick (again, too small workpiece).

I had purchased this saw with knowledge of the SawStop technology which would have prevented this injury, but with it's cost of $1300 vs the $279 for my saw, the cost difference was the deciding factor.. and assumption I could use the basic saw safely.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible (3) given the described circumstances and lack of safety measures.

incident_description: Craftsmen folding knife purchased at Lowe's. First time I went to use the knife to open a package, the locking mechanism that keeps the blade open did not work. The blade came down on my right index finger cutting it to the bone. It required immediate medical attention. I called Craftsmen, they said to return the knife to Lowe's which I did. incident_description: I used Mrs. Meyers Dish Soap to wash up after working in the yard. It came into contact with the back of my neck, my hands, arms, and lower legs. incident_description: The Hoover UH71013 cleaner I bought in the Fall of 2017 has a defective on/off switch. The original switch fell apart. I took it out and the plastic body was melted and the plastic insulators around the switch lead terminals were black. I ordered a replacement switch and installed and tested it. I ran the vacuum before mounting it on the handle to test it. I noticed the switch body and terminals were hot to the touch after only five minutes of operation. I then took the switch off the leads and clipped them directly together and ran machine for ten minutes. The terminals and wires were cool to the touch confirming the switch was too weak for the circuit. The cleaner is rated at 12 amps. I took the old switch apart and noticed the contacts were very tiny: about the size of a pinhead. This switch seems a bad design for this product.  This product should be recalled.
justification: The defective switch poses a risk of overheating but no injury or death was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the switch's poor design and observed overheating.

incident_description:
Re: Health issue
Bought a Sears window air conditioner in June 2017, ran fine, maintained that year.  2018, ran fine, maintained but found what looked like black spots on grill area and cleaned.  2019 (September)  lady stopped and said she smelled mold in the air. In checking we found not only the grill but fan blade and floor of unit was just covered with mold.  Cleaned it.  Thinking the cause was the drain hole might be plugged, checked and found no drain hole.  Checked manual, they indicated water from condensate/rain is tossed around by design to cool the condenser and mentioned that drilling a hole would end any warranty.
Bothersome!   we checked the rear of the unit and could see water deposits on fins out side that would indicate standing water.  Contacted sears and they kept going back to the fact the unit is designed to handle water....which might be right in northern climate but when in humid areas, how will that volume of water from condensation and rain get removed......STANDING WATER FEEDS MOLD AND MILDEW.  To make it safe at this point, we examined the inside and found an area that we could safely drill a hole....and have to tell you, water that ran out (and continues as it should) would blow your mind.....it means the standing water do to the design by the manufacturer is causing mold and mildew to form.   Now, in my conversation and letter to Sears Holding, I suggested that maybe they are not aware of an issue with standing water but, they need to at last replace the unit with one with a drain hole or we need to contact CPSC to let them know their product is a health hazard by design and should not be sold!  Again, the design might work well up north where humidity levels are low but in the south the amount of water from condensation is overwhelming and unless it can get out of the unit, is feeds mold and mildew which is a dangerous issue.   I have not heard from Sears and told them that if I do not I need to address the issue with you so this unit can be replaced and more importantly they look at the construction and make sure a drain hole is available for those areas where their present design will not allow standing water sit in the unit and create mold and mildew.  Any further questions someone can call me on my cell: [REDACTED].  Have been told now that regardless of the fact that the  hole we provided is draining he unit as it should....we should not have  drilled the hole. incident_description:
We have several Kidde P4010 series smoke (and smoke/CO) alarms in our home.  One in each bedroom, one outside each bedroom, and in common spaces on all floors.  We have had this issue with both wired and battery-operated devices, as well as with both smoke-only and smoke/CO combination devices.

Since we purchased these, and installed them carefully according to the manual, we have had a steady stream of false alarms as well as the devices losing communication with each other.

The false alarms are dangerous because they can desensitize occupants to the alarm and cause them to be ignored.  Some people might disconnect or remove the detectors.

The failure of the wireless interconnect is dangerous because we rely on interconnection to alert occupants in other parts of the home of an issue.  If the interconnect is unreliable, sleeping occupants of a bedroom may not know of an issue in another part of the structure.

Regarding false alarms, we have had the false alarms from units in multiple locations in our home, and the units are installed according to the manual.  There are no obvious explanations for the nuisance alarms.

Regarding the interconnect failure, we have followed the instructions regarding antenna orientation and coordinator selection from KIdde.  But we even have had a unit 5 feet (as well as 10, 15..) feet from the coordinator stop working.  There are no obvious factors at play, and we are hardly pushing the boundary with these specific units.

We have worked with Kidde support to try to resolve the issue but it has continued.  In reviewing online reviews of the product, we see many people with the same issue.
justification: False alarms and interconnect failures pose a risk of desensitization and delayed response to actual emergencies, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

At that moment, she heard a "gunshot" noise, the top separated from the motor housing, and a metal disk in the motor essentially exploded, sending bits of metal shrapnel flying in all directions.

incident_description: I was using this saw to cut down some parts for a project that I was building. But, the saw did not actually turn off. I repeated reaching down and turning the switch off a couple of more times with the thought in the moment that I had missed pressing the switch. When the saw still did not turn off I physically looked down at the switch, which is below normal eye line when operating the saw, and found that it was physically in the off position even though the saw was continuing to run. This fact necessitated actually pulling the plug from the socket to get the saw to turn off. Fortunately due to the layout of my workshop; reaching and pulling the plug was reasonably easy and the incident did not cause any injury or damage. However, if someone else were to encounter this issue and they were in a position where the saw had to be physically moved in order to reach the power cord; this would pose a significant danger to that person.

When working properly, you turn a power switch on, then you press the gun against a surface, then you pull the trigger and a staple is fired at high velocity into the material. When working properly the trigger will not fire a staple unless the gun is pressed into the material surface (which depresses a safety switch).

Literally the act of turning the gun on caused it to start firing staples until the gun ran out of staples. I was lucky that the gun was pointed away from me or it would have fired several staples into my foot, leg, or face before I would have had time to react. This is HORRIBLY dangerous.

I hope you can help me reach out to the company and help them imporoe their product.
justification: The incident resulted in a chemical burn to the eye, ongoing treatment, and vision impairment, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described fragility of the pods and the circumstances of the incident.

incident_description:
This past summer, in early July, we had the floors in our dining room and living room refinished with the product: Sampson professional urethane seal, satin clear, product 020933. The work had to be done in two stages, so furniture could be moved back and forth, and lasted July 1-3, and 8-9. The refinishers had told us to leave the air conditioner on while they worked, to lower humidity. I asked multiple times whether it was safe to stay in the house, and was told each time that there was no problem. 
Their answer: ÃÂrun the a/c. Do not open the windows. The humidity levels are high. There is not a health risk to you. If you are sensitive to smells, sometimes can give you a headache. You are fine.ÃÂ 
I stayed upstairs with the bottom of the door sealed and windows open. For most of the time I was fine, with only a small reaction at the back of my throat when breathing the air on the first floor. On the Monday, July 8th, my throat was feeling a bit raw when I breathed. On Tuesday, I realized that I had an enormous, horrible, raging raw feeling at the back of my throat and down my windpipe when I tried to breathe. I went outside, and could not force myself to reenter my house. We moved out for that night, and came back only when we were able to leave windows open throughout the house. The raw feeling calmed a bit, but was still there one and a half months later, so I went to a doctor on August 21. The airways looked irritated. After 3 (THREE!) courses of [REDACTED], my throat is recovering, although still somewhat sore and not fully recovered, , and my voice is still hoarse. I would like several things:

incident_description: I notified Samsung last Thursday in regards to black mold being discovered in between the layers of the washer drum as well as under the agitator plate on my top loading washer model #WA5471ABP/X.  Samsung noticed that there had been a previous recall regarding balance issues leading to exploding lids when used in the spin cycle for this particular model washer.  They refused to take any action in regards to the mold issue that upon further research is caused from a design flaw in manufacturing that causes the washer to accumulate moisture in above noted areas leading to growth of toxic black mold.  A service for the recall was made the following day 8/30 in order to expedite the ticket for manufacturer defect causing mold growth.  I explained to Samsung that the washer was purchased in March 2012 and my youngest daughter was born in April 2012, since she was born she has had numerous types of unexplained rashes as well as numerous visits for upper respiratory infections, all documented with her physician.  All with unexplained cause that is until the mold growth was discovered.  It is well known that exposure to black mold can lead to various skin rashes, upper respiratory issues, headaches, as well as many other complaints.  It is noted to Samsung that our washer is located in a laundry closet in our main living area of our house and also near our daughters bedroom.  Her clothes were continually washed in the contaminated washer, some being left to air dry.  It was noted that laundry often had a musty smell (another sign of mold growth) after washing, even after immediate removal once wash cycle complete.  I have taken samples of the mold growth to send to lab if needed.  I will also reach out to my daughters physician to see if any blood work is needed in regards to mold exposure.  We have since stopped using the washer and dryer due to concerns of any cross continuation it may now have.  Samsung's response to this issue is concerning, especially given the hundreds of complaints that are noted on their community support page on their website in regards to this exact issue.  Samsung's blatant disregard to the health and safety of their consumers in regards to using known faulty manufactured appliances is alarming.  They're insisting upon repair, which does not remove the current presence of mold nor does it prevent future accumulation of mold because as noted this is a flaw in the design of washing machine.  I'm asking for refund for my washer, as well as my compromised dryer.  Due to their insistence on having it serviced I must now continue to house an unhealthy and unsafe appliance within range of my family including my child who already shows signs of mold exposure.  We were out of the house Sat-Mon with no signs of sickness during that time and within 24 hrs of being back in our house my youngest daughter developed a rash on her arms, upper torso and cheeks, as well as sneezing and coughing.  I can't help but know in my gut that this is due to her exposure to black mold.  This health and safety concern needs to be addressed!! I have filed a complaint with the New Jersey BBB in regards to Samsung's negligence on this matter.
justification: The incident involves exposure to toxic black mold leading to documented health issues in a child, including rashes and respiratory infections, which aligns with severity level 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the design flaw and numerous similar complaints.

incident_description:
I own a Ridgid 12 inch Sliding Compound Miter Saw - R4221. The saw was purchased in June, 2018 and put in to use the same month.  The saw was put to use with mostly softwood products and used and service in accordance to the owner's manual.

I immediately noticed blade wobble, I purchased a new blade for the saw and the minor blade wobble condition persisted.  Both blades (the one that was included with the saw and the[REDACTED] 12inch 94 tooth finishing blade) have been tested on two other miter saws ([REDACTED] and a [REDACTED]) with no visible wobble detected. 

A Ridgid associate took my serial number over the phone and told me wobble is not an issue on my saw.  On the evening of August 4th, 2019 while the saw was in use a total failure event occurred.  A whiteboard 2x4 was being cut with no knots or foreign material in the blade path. Prior cuts were successfully made before the event occurred. The blade has penetrated roughly 1/4" of the wood when a loud 'BANG' was heard, the saw immediately seized, and would have jumped if it was not fastened to the work surface.  The failure occurred when the blade struck the brake.  The blade impacting a part of the saw was extremely loud and destroyed the saw.  

The issue with blade wobble and the R4221 miter saw is well documented and Ridgid is doing everything they can to hide this problem from consumers.  The R4221 is a very dangerous saw and they need to correct this issue. Home Depot deleted my review of the saw that was written.
justification: The incident involved a saw failure with no reported injury, but potential for harm exists.

incident_description:
I received an electrical shock from the water heater listed below, in May, 2019, and  determined there is a possible grounding flaw with the design, that can cause injury or death. I shipped the unit back to the manufacturer in May, 2019, for evaluation of this issue and they notified me on 8/15/2019, that they are refusing to test the grounding; with my old unit which is in their possession or one of their new units. ([REDACTED] of A.O. Smith, Claims Manager sent me an email on 8/14/2019 stating that "If you feel our design that UL approves is faulty there are steps to bring it to ULÃÂs attention. There is nothing more I can offer you.")  Prior to that, I had spent several hours on the phone and email exchanges explaining my concern to my first their tech support department, then my risk management contact, [REDACTED], and she apparently referred the case to [REDACTED], who emailed me for the first time with this news that they are unwilling to test the grounding. The test would take about 1-minute and will confirm that there is no electrical continuity between the metal jacket, other metal surfaces, and the green equipment ground screw. This would confirm that the unit is not properly grounded. Per [REDACTED] request, I sent them several pages of emails and photos, as well as several phone conversations explaining my concern and exactly how they can perform this simple test.

The unit was purchased from Lowes: Item # 816193 Model # HP10-50H45DV A.O. Smith Signature Premier 50-Gallon Tall 10-year Limited 4500-Watt Double Element Electric Water Heater with Hybrid Heat Pump

My assumption is that the reason that this flaw was not previously discovered is that with my unit, the heating element became corroded and caused a water leak which exposed live heating element wires and the water transferred the electricity to the jacket and other metal components; and the purpose of the ground is to protect the user and service personal from electrical shock. In this case my house ground wire was correctly terminated on the green grounding screw on the junction box but failed to ground the unit, since the junction box is not electrically connected to the jacket and other metal. With units that are working properly, the unit will function as normal without proper grounding, as the grounding is only used during an equipment failure like in my case, to protect the user and service personnel from electrical shock hazard.

I am the owner of [REDACTED] which is a licensed electrical contractor in the State of California, California State Contractors Board License # [REDACTED], C-10 Electrical. I also have an 4-year technology degree from from [REDACTED] with a concentration in Electronics, an AA Degree in Electronics from [REDACTED] in [REDACTED] and a vocational certificate in Electronics from [REDACTED]. I graduated from [REDACTED] in 1983 and held various technical and electronics engineering positions at [REDACTED] for the next 24-years, and accepted early retirement  2007, then founded [REDACTED] shortly afterwards.

Therefore, I feel that I am not only a consumer that received an electrical shock from a faulty unit, but I was able to verify exactly why I was shocked and determine exactly why the safety ground failed to protect me from electrical shock. I performed the testing by using a voltmeter to verify that there was approximately 120V on all of the water heater's metal components. And obviously in that state it could hurt or kill anybody that touches it, especially since it was leaking water at the same time. I then switched off the unit and used an Ohm meter to check continuity from the green equipment grounding screw to the metal components. And what I found was an open circuit, the green equipment ground screw is not connected to the water heater's metal components.  

FYI; I also filed a case with Lowes vendor safety department today and while awaiting their response I expect to receive next week, I will contact the City of San Diego Building Division and recommend that they test the unit for safety, prior to issuing city installation permits for this product. 

Thank you for investigating this issue. My primary concern is safety of others and I am extremely frustrated with the lack of concern from the manufacturer regarding this issue. And at the same I have spent countless hours and 3-months trying to bring this to their attention and at this point hit a "dead end", and appreciate the work of your agency. Your agency obviously exists because of manufactures like this, that refuse to take even a few minutes to investigate safety claims of their products, even after one of their consumers gets shocked from a grounding flaw. Apparently it will take a multi million dollar claim from a death and/or a class action suit for them to take any action. My other theory is that they performed the test, determined the unit is not properly grounded and are unwilling to acknowledge the flaw to me for legal reasons. As I know the remedy will be a costly recall, and they will have to remove the products from the Lowes shelves until they correct the issue. 
Thanks again,
[REDACTED]
Cell: [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an electrical shock from a faulty water heater, indicating an injury occurred. The design flaw suggests a possible risk of recurrence.

incident_description:
On 8-8-19, my husband, [REDACTED],  purchased for the very first time, Arm & Hammer product Pet Fresh Carpet Odor Eliminator and in the evening, our pet dog urinated on the rug in our bedroom.  My husband followed the directions on the package and soaked up the urine and let it dry overnight.  

In the morning, about 6:00 a.m. he sprinkled the product on the carpet area which was about a 12" across and waited 15 min. as directed.  The next step was to vacuum the carpet.  As soon as he turned on the vacuum and disturbed the product, the odor produced was totally overwhelming and triggered in me an asthma attack.  

I immediately left the bedroom, closed the door behind me and took my inhaler to help me breathe.  My husband immediately turned off the vacuum and opened all the windows in the bedroom and turned on the fan to help remove the product from the room.  Then, he vacuumed the carpet area for about 5 minutes to remove the product.  The odor continued to be overwhelming!

He then called the Arm & Hammer customer service to report the incident and to find out if there was a way to neutralize the product to help clear the bedroom air.  By this time, [REDACTED] was beginning to feel a tightness in his chest and he does not have asthma.  

The customer service rep. could not find any information on how to neutralize the product and suggested cleaning the area but not to introduce a new product.  My husband inquired about using regular baking soda and the rep. thought it might work.  

My comment was to label the product SCENTED and to put a warning on the label that it is not to be used by customers who have asthma or allergies to scents.

Next, [REDACTED] called the Arm & Hammer Medical Line and reported the incident.  This rep. also could not find any information on how to neutralize the odor but suggested cleaning the area with dish soap & lots of water, soaking it up and letting it dry.  This was 3.5 hours later and the smell in the bedroom is still very strong.  Since the incident, we have opened every window and door in the entire house and have stood outside to clear our lungs.

It is now 5 hours later and [REDACTED] has cleaned the carpet with dish soap and warm water.  Then he sprinkled baking soda on the area and let it sit for an hour.  The odor is starting to dissipate.

I believe that if I would have been directly involved with this product, I would have ended up in the ER receiving medical treatment for my asthma attack.

No product should create a situation that causes an asthma reaction and takes 5 hours with additional cleaning for the odor to begin to dissipate!!!

The ingredients that creates this product need to be analyzed for health issues - I may not be the only customer that has had a severe asthma reaction to this product.

If the ingredients are not harmful to consumers, then this product definitely needs to be labeled SCENTED and carry a warning label that says that it causes allergy and asthma reactions!
justification: The incident triggered an asthma attack and caused chest tightness, indicating injury.

incident_description:
General Electric Dryer
Model - GFDR270EH0WW
Serial - ZD102239G


On April 20th, 2019, I placed some clean sheets into our clothes dryer, which was purchased 4 years ago. I pushed the "Power" button, then the "Start" button.  
When I pushed the "Start" button, instead of the dryer starting to spin, I could see a bright light emanating from a space between the control panel and the dryer frame and a sound similar to a short circuit. Then, I could see black smoke coming through a space between the control panel and the dryer frame with a pungent burning smell.
I immediately turned off the dryer as well as quickly unplugged it from the wall to make certain that there would be no chance of the machine, the short circuit or anything else related to the dryer could start again and potentially start a fire in my house.
On April 21st, I contacted General Electric through their Facebook page outlining my frustration with the product, mainly concerned with the safety of my family. They had arranged for someone to come out to my house on May 1st to look at the dryer. At that time, they were willing to forgo the trip charge of $109.95.
The service person came out May 1st and diagnosed the problem very quickly - the main control board had shorted out from what anyone could tell, for no reason.  The technician initially indicated the initial cost to replace was around $800.  But when we explained what happened and the danger of what occurred, he was able to get the price of repair down to $310.00

Though I acknowledge General Electric stepped up and waived fees and the service person reduced the fee as much as possible, we have heard of other people experiencing something of a similar nature. The technician was aware of a few other times he had seen this same issue, but when we commented that perhaps it is a bigger problem, he stated that if there was a bigger issue, there would be a recall. While that may be the case, it takes enough people reporting an issue in order for them to know and take action. We are filling this out in the hope of a record of our experience is added to your database so that it is on record with your organization.

It should be noted that we did file a complaint with the Arizona Attorney General's office.  Since the complaint, General Electric did step-up and reimburse us for the cost of the dryer repair.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit and smoke but no injury or death, and the technician indicated awareness of similar issues occurring occasionally.

After researching and reading the manual, I have run the self-clean cycle many, many times and tried a washing machine cleaner several times.  The deposits remain -- I have pictures I will attach.  

When I have looked online for recommendations, some people have taken their washer apart to clear out the mildew, but I do not have the expertise for that nor do I want to have ANOTHER repairman out AGAIN for a Samsung product. Because they are Samsung products I can only have certain repair-people out, and the nearest Samsung repair shop is not local NOR are they efficient (hence having to have the fridge repaired three times in several months).

Because of the washer lid problems (even after the recall repair), any bed linens must be washed on a cycle with barely any spin, which means they take longer to dry.  This washer is only 4 years old and has been nothing but trouble (along with the fridge).

I am filling out this information in the hopes that even though I am stuck with a bad washer, that the problem will be fixed in future Samsung appliances.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washer causing inconvenience and dissatisfaction, but no injury or death.

incident_description: Keen Home Smart Vents - these are ceiling mounted HVAC vents that open and close via temp sensors through a vent to close off/on HVAC throughout a room.  They weigh 2 to 4 pounds and have (4) AA batteries of weight too.    These vents are manufactured in two pieces with one piece being the actual vent portion mated with a housing type bracket that is installed into a trim kit and then mounted on a ceiling or wall.  The housing and vent are mated together with just (6) strips of double sided tape.  So over time, 12 to 18 months the tape fails to hold the vent in the housing - and the entire assembly just falls crashing down on top of whatever is under it.   If it's a pet, elderly person or small child they could be easily injured.  There is also a deco vent cover held on by 4 magnents - these magnets are glued and the glue fails too - on cases where the vent hasn't totally fallen out, the vent deco cover ha when the glued magnets fail.  Two of four of these vents failed in my home and crashed to the floor.  I notified Keen Home twice and they refused to respond.  Also, their eCommerce site, doesn't have a place to open help requests and there isn't a phone number.   http://help.keenhome.io/en/     The company doesn't want to be bothered with or cares if someone using their product is hurt.    I feel this product is a safety hazard.  I had two incidents, no injuries.  One was April 12th 2019 and July 1 2019

incident_description: In August 2018, we purchased Quaker Low-E windows that were installed by a small business.  We believe they were installed to specification and Quaker does not dispute this.  In June 2019, we installed a vinyl pool liner in our newly remodeled pool.  The morning after the installalation of the liner, we observed a 5 inch area of the liner above the water line that appeared to have been melted.  The pool company was called to inspect the area and determined that this was not an issue the originated in the pool area (no wires, no electrical, no metal of any kind in that area.)  Upon further inspection and after an experiment the next morning, we determined that the vinyl melted due to extreme, concentrated heat from the reflection off of the low-E windows. We have video evidence of this occurring the following morning when we placed a plastic coffee can lid in the path of this reflection and melted a hole in it.  We measured this with a handheld laser thermometer which indicated the plastic lid was reaching 278deg F.  We have also performed other experiments to show this phenomenon.  A Quaker windows manufacturer's representative visited us on 7/2 and stated that, though they do not dispute the claim, they will not take responsibility for the issue and advised us to purchase an awning or a shade to cover the windows.  They further recommended that we could contact the glass manufacturer, Cardinal Glass.  This will not likely be resolved anytime soon and we will continue to gather video evidence of the issue and attempt to protect our pool and patio area from damage as well as try to ensure that our property does not catch fire.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted pool liner) but no injury or death. The likelihood is possible as it requires specific conditions (extreme, concentrated heat reflection).

incident_description:
I bought Nice! drain cleaner from Walgreens and I dropped my shopping bag on a table when I came home and went to the bathroom. While in the bathroom, I heard a leaking sound. I ran out to discover the "child-proof cap" had come off when I dropped the bag and it had leaked everywhere. I immediately opened my windows and proceeded to clean the spill with a baking soda solution and then an ammonia solution. I still came into contact with the corrosive liquid at times which caused me to have to flush my skin with large amounts of cold water and then wash my hands thoroughly.
My concern is that a child-proof cap should not be able to come off the way it did, from such a normal activity as dropping a shopping bag on a table. It could happen to anyone and while I have no children or pets, this product presents a real danger to anyone who does. All I suffered was property damage and bouts of lightheadedness easily fixed by breathing closer to a window. What others could suffer is unnecessary harm to children and pets.
Upon going to the store to buy ammonia, I discovered that the ammonia I had purchased had a pressure or tamper-proof seal that could have prevented a spill like this. It is my belief that Walgreens should have to package corrosive liquids more securely, whether that means improving on their lid design or adding a seal to the bottle. Either way, the Poison Prevention Packaging Act should address this problem. Thank you for your time and I hope Walgreens Co. is held to full account.
justification: The incident involved property damage and minor health effects (lightheadedness) but no serious injury, warranting a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the faulty child-proof cap design, making spills likely under normal handling conditions.

It is scary to even get close enough to the machine to  push this stop button. The machine is balanced and on solid tile. 

We have talked with a Whirlpool representative and they say they can find no information about their machine having an automatic cutoff. This is a dangerous situation that can easily be prevented with an automatic stop switch to stop the machine when it begins to violently vibrate.  We have seen pictures and read stories about these machines exploding and even causing bodily injury, so this is not an isolated incident. This is a safety problem.

incident_description:
I ordered Basco Shower Doors, frameless, from Tile-Redi in March 2019 for a bathroom/shower I was building in my house.  By June 18, 2019 I had the shower complete and the frame installed for the doors.  I removed the door from the box and proceeded to lift the door into the track. The doors did not require any prep to be done as the hanger brackets are factory installed.   While holding the door it exploded in my hands sending glass shards everywhere.  The door literally exploded into thousands of pieces, scratching the surrounding metal frame.  I received cuts on my wrists and hands but did not require medical attention.  The door had not been dropped or otherwise damaged in any way.
I immediately called Tile-Redi and provided information but they could not put me in touch with someone immediately to rectify the problem, so I called Basco Shower Doors directly.  They told me the doors were warranted and agreed to ship out two doors as I was concerned that neither of the two doors they originally shipped me had the proper temper done to the glass.  
On July 1, 2019 I received the new shipment of doors, and gingerly installed the first door.  The second door, again lifting it into the frame, exploded in my hands, causing small cuts and embedded shards of glass in my arm.  I required first aid but not medical attention.  This door reacted identically as the first shipment.  I contacted Basco Shower Doors again and they agreed to send me another set of doors.  At this point I have two of their shower doors installed but am extremely wary of their safety and quality.  Neither door was hit, twisted or jammed, each exploded with a great deal of energy with just minor handling, lifting them gently into the frame.  
There is something very wrong with these doors, either the temper is not correct or the hangers, installed at the factory, are creating pressure or damage to the glass causing them to be bombs waiting to go off.
I will not purchase Basco Doors again and if these doors shatter I will take my loss and have them locally made.  I am considering removing these doors and having framed doors made as I am concerned with another explosion occurring while using the shower.
Having a heavy glass door explode in your hands is a jarring experience.  The glass does not just break, it blows apart hitting everything surrounding it, including the person holding it.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts and embedded glass shards) but did not require medical attention, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the issue happened twice with the same product under normal handling conditions.

incident_description: While drying laundry we started noticing a strong gas odor coming from the dryer (LG Model DLG2051W, Serial #: 912KWUC00846) . The problem could be either with the underlayment or the wood itself which may be disintegrating from within.  The problem is worst where we step on the floor as the boards give a little each time.

We are probably not the only people exposed to this problem.  The company does not have a stellar reputation and has been in trouble  in the past for the materials used in its flooring.

incident_description:
Swimming pool acid (muriatic acid) comes in gallon jugs.  The jugs have a safety seal.  This seal consists of two layers - paper or thin foam on top, and a thin layer of cellophane plastic onderneath.  The seal has no tab, meaning that the consumer must use a fingernail to remove the seal,   Often the foam layer separates from the cellophane, the underside of which usually has acid on it.

Removing the safety seal without a tool, unless managed very carefully, will result in the consumer getting concentrated muriatic acid on their fingertips.

This problem was noted on Brenntag Mid-South Muriatic Acid, but I believe this problem is consistent across the industry.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw that can lead to exposure to concentrated acid, which is likely to cause injury if not managed carefully.

incident_description:
This smoke alarm started blaring a full emergency (NOT a low battery) at approximately 4:00am on June 11, 2019. I immediately went to find the source of the fire, as nobody in the house was awake, and no one had been for many hours at that time to cause a false alarm from things like steam or burning food. 

After a moment of panic that seemed like hours, I determined that there was no emergency. Unfortunately I then fell getting the alarm off the ceiling and was knocked unconscious for a minute or two. Besides a head injury, I had injuries to my legs where I hit while going down. 

While I was relieved to find that my house was *not* in fact on fire, I'm extremely concerned that this alarm would malfunction in such a way as to go into full emergency mode without any smoke or fire whatsoever. It was located in the hallway, a normally occupied area of the house, and was not dusty or dirty. 

Smoke alarms simply should not sound at random in clear air. Like most people would do, I immediately removed the batteries. However, as you certainly know, dead or missing batteries in smoke detectors are a leading cause of fire deaths in the United States. Thus, it is imperative that smoke alarms function correctly. I also would not have been injured and knocked unconscious if I didn't have to get the screaming alarm off the ceiling in a time of panic and adrenaline. 

I would like the CPSC to investigate and see if a full recall is warranted on this type of alarm. If you would like me to send you the unit in question that malfunctioned, I kept it and am willing to ship it for further investigation.
justification: The incident resulted in a head injury and leg injuries from a fall, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific circumstances of the malfunctioning smoke alarm leading to injury.

incident_description:
I am writing to identify dangerous design flaws in three products. The products are the following, and the flaw is the same in all of them.

Ceptics Brazil Travel Adapter Plug with Dual Usa Input - Type N (3 Pack - Ultra Compact
https://www.amazon.com/Ceptics-Brazil-Travel-Adapter-Plug/dp/B01N6UAWQF/

Ceptics Brazil Travel Plug Adapter (Type N) - 3 Pack
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0197VRX8Y/


[REDACTED]

These adapters incorrectly wire the neutral socket to the pin which enters the hot socket on a Brazilian wall outlet, and they wire the hot socket to the pin which enters the neutral socket on the wall outlet. This results in reversed polarity, which is a dangerous condition that may cause your device to fry or may even cause electrocution!

The condition may go unnoticed because almost all contemporary devices will still work when they are connected to power and neutral on the wrong pins. But it is easy to verify by testing the circuit either with a multimeter, an electrical tester, or even a surge suppressor that has an LED to indicate when there is a wiring fault.

I bought more than Ceptics adapters and several more [REDACTED] adapters for my American devices before moving to Brazil, and am dismayed these adapters have this inexcusable flaw!

I first noticed this when my surge suppressors complained of a wiring fault, and then confirmed it with a multimeter. In the US, in a typical type C outlet, the left socket is taller and is intended for netural, the right socket is shorter and is intended for power, and the middle socket is round and offset below the others and intended for ground. In Brazil, in a typical type N outlet, all sockets are the same shape, which can lead to confusion. But the spec clearly states that the left socket should be wired for neutral, the right socket for power, and the middle socket is for ground. However, unlike in the US, where the ground socket is offset below the two others, the Brazilian ground socket is offset above the other two.

The people at Ceptics and [REDACTED clearly misunderstood this, and designed the pins upside down, as if the ground socket should be below the others like in the US, not above the others where in Brazil it belongs. These adapters put the pins into the wall socket are UPSIDE DOWN!

This causes reversed polarity, and it puts all devices that are plugged into these adapters, and everyone who may touch them, at risk.

It should not be a surprise, one of my [REDACTED adapters also sparked and burned when I turned on a night light on that was plugged into it.

These adapters should be pulled off the market due to the danger they cause!

Note that I am now living in Brazil, but I maintain a US mailing address. For simplicity's sake I will provide my US address in the form below.
justification: The adapters have a dangerous design flaw causing reversed polarity, which can lead to device damage or electrocution, as evidenced by a sparking and burning incident.

incident_description:
Consumer complains that a generator was sold with a potential leak but consumers have to pay to get it inspected to find out if the fuel plenum is corroded and many won't pay for the service to find out if the generator is dangerous.

Generac has sent a letter to customers of this 14kw generator saying that a defect or deterioration in the fuel
system may cause the Generator to catch fire. It says that it will be responsible for repairing the problem,but
only after the consumer has paid a Generac designated contractor 80.00 to inspect the generator. It will
reimburse the 80.00 only if the part has been found to be defective. It took two calls to Generac to get them
to agree to pay the 80.00. The service call was made, and required about 30 seconds of sticking a gauge into
the housing. Mine was found to be okay, but the technician told me that the part involved was inherently
defective and subject to deterioration in moist climates. He said that the replacement part was of the same
design and manufacture. So the problem can show itself again, and although mine is okay now, it may not be a
year from now.

I have told Generac that although my generator is not defective at this time, I have filed this complaint with
CPSC, and that if it is going to take responsibility for fixing the problem it needs to take full responsibility,
including paying for each inspection, and replacing each potentially dangerous part. I expect that many
people, seeing that they need to pay a contractor to inspect the unit will probably not do so, and the hazard
will remain. When we receive an auto recall notice we are not asked to pay the dealer to inspect the car
before replacing the part if needed. This is a $5000 product that the manufacturer has admitted may catch
fire. It needs to be fully responsible.

This $5000 unit, incidentally, has cost us about $1700 for maintenance and repair over 8 years and
approximately two weeks of use.
justification: The generator has a potential fire hazard due to a defective fuel system, but no actual incidents or injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description:
Over the past 5 days my house has had a nasty perfume smell in it and I have had an allergic reaction along with a migraine from it.   It took me a few days to figure out the cause of the sudden stench, but it turns out the cause is my laundry detergent. I have been using Tide Original scent laundry detergent for as long as I can remember.   5 days ago I used a new container and I checked the packaging several times, but there were no indications on the package that would lead me to believe that it was the cause, so I kept using it and examined every other possibility for the cause. 

I finally figured out that it was indeed the Tide by going and buying a package from a different store and trying it. I assumed they had a glitch in their packaging process.

I just got off the phone with the Tide consumer help line and the woman who helped me informed me that they "updated" the scent in February of 2019 to make it "more floral" but did not do ANYTHING to the package labeling to warn consumers.

I am extremely sensitive to smells and fragrances and this change P&G decided to make has made my home a toxic environment.  They have refunded my money, but that is going to take care of the least of my worries.   

Their suggestion for eliminating the smell was to use their washer cleaner and after checking the ingredients the product also has perfume in it.  

I am blown away by the fact that a company such as P&G could consider the decision of changing the product without changing the package, forget actually doing it.  

It was irresponsible, negligent and has directly caused my home to become toxic to me.
justification: The incident caused an allergic reaction and migraine, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as scent changes in products are not uncommon but may not always cause such reactions.

incident_description:
I ordered a new Ford 3100 Gasoline Pressure Washer from Amazon. (Model # FPWG3100H-J)  I used it for the for the first time on Saturday - two days ago.  After about 5 hours of use, I looked back at the pressure washer and realized that the washer was no longer attached to the frame which is supposed to hold it - the engine was still running, and the whole engine was resting on it's side - of of the frame.  I tried to grab the engine and lift it back onto the frame - at which point I burned myself on the hot exhaust.  Concerned that it was resting on the gas tank, and that gas would begin leaking out, I hi the off switch and got it stopped.

Upon inspection, I realized that all four of the rubber engine mounts - the sole items which hold the engine to the frame - had all failed.  The engine is entirely loose from any mounting.

There is some basic assembly required on the power washer, but the engine comes attached to the frame, and these engine mounts are not an item which I installed, adjusted or worked on in any fashion.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from the hot exhaust, and there was a potential for gas leakage, indicating a moderate severity. The failure of all four engine mounts suggests a possible manufacturing defect, making recurrence likely.

incident_description:
MEMO TO THE FILE
04/17/2019

EVENT TIME LINE AND INFORMATION RELATING TO FIRE EXPLOSION FROM FLEX SEAL RUBBER SPRAY SEALANT
For


This event occurred on Monday, April 15, 2019 at approximately 3:00 pm at the residence of 
Background to Event:  We have a large flower pot in our back yard which is used for a water feature.  Over the years on a couple occasions we have sprayed the inside of the pot with a rubberized spray substance from an aerosol can.  This has worked out well to ensure that there were no leaks from the pot.  Over the winter we store the pot in the back yard location in an upside down configuration. (No water inside).  I decided this year to apply a secondary coat of the well advertised FLEX SEAL rubberized spray to the interior of the flower pot.  I ordered two 14 oz cans of FLEX SEAL from Amazon which was received on or about April 14, 2019.  This product was stored in my inside garage area until April 15, 2019, the day that we were to use it. On the day of use the weather was clear and there was sunshine with temperatures in the 60ÃÂs.  The flower pot was positioned completely in the open area in my rear yard ÃÂ nothing around it but space. There was no metal, electronic equipment or anything around that could possibly cause an ignition spark. Subsequently, on the above event day I opened the top of one of the 14 oz cans and began to spray the interior of the pot.  About 30 seconds into the spray operation (estimated) there was a loud pop sound coupled with a spontaneous combustion continuous fire flash which burned my face, arms and hair. Alarmed and with total shock, my normal reflex moved me away from the pot as I attempted to brush away the fire from my face & hair. My wife relates that my face and hair was covered in a black substance.  In concert with this I observed that the fire continued burning in an open flame manner for approximately 30 ÃÂ 45 seconds - then went out. My wife was working in the yard approximately 15 ft from where the incident occurred and in open view of the incident.  She immediately came to help. Moreover, my neighbor, [REDACTED] had just come out into his yard and observed, as he has recently related, that my face was burned, plus my normally white hair was now yellow. Upon examination I discovered that my eye lashes were singed off, eye brows burned, hair burned, both arms were burned with first and second degree burns along with blisters on my fingers and arm, my complete face, forehead and hair were damaged beyond belief with first and second degree burns.  I have very white hair and now as earlier related ÃÂ it was yellow.   I immediately came into the home and took a quick very cold face shower to help alleviate some of the burning.  We then chose to go to the Chattanooga CHI Memorial Primary Care office, [REDACTED].  Upon arriving at the front desk they took a quick look (we never register in) and were told to go to the Memorial North Park Emergency Room.  Afterward, not realizing our danger, we visited the Physicians Care office at [REDACTED] and were, (without registering in) were also instructed to get to the Emergency Room.  In a state of fright we grasp that our problem was very severe.  We then went to the Memorial North Park Emergency room where we were seen very quickly by a [REDACTED].  He did some of the preliminary testing and gave me shots for pain.  By this time the burning in the face and arm was crushing. However, the pain shots were most helpful.  After a brief period of time [REDACTED] said we have a lot to talk about I will be back shortly.  He came back into the room sat down with my wife and me, once more stating we need to have a serious talk.  He was concerned about the face being damaged therefore, was fearful that the airway passages could be affected as swelling would most certainly occur.  After our talk we followed his recommendations and he made arrangements for me to be transported via Memorial Hospital ambulance to the UAB Burn Center in Birmingham,AL    Some 2.5 hours later we arrived at a waiting Trauma center at the facility where I was triaged and sent on to the burn floor.  I arrived at my room in the burn center around midnight.  During the night multiple medical people along with attendants came in at all hours to do tests, take blood and multiple other functions.  Approximately, 3:00 a.m. an eye doctor came in and did an examination of my eyes ÃÂseveral tests were involved.  He did notice some, what seemed to be, burn residue in both my eyes apparently originated from the fire incident - he then proceed to irrigate both eyes.  Moving forward, a large amount of personalized care followed incorporating a steady flow of medical people entering and performing various medical burn functions. I was on an IV drip bag continually.   On Tuesday mid - morning April 16, 2019 the burn surgeon and his team of about six people came into see me, after conversation he proceeded to communicate he was going to be able to release me to come home.  Moreover, detailed instructions were communicated for wound care, along with scheduling a one week follow up appointment for a return visit to the burn clinic in Birmingham.  Upon the doctor telling me he would release me that evening, I called my wife and she drove down the Birmingham to pick me up.  We arrived back home in Chattanooga, Tennessee late evening. My face was saturated with [REDACTED] ointment and I was very, very tired, and after taking 1000 mg of acetaminophen went to bed and rested fairly well.  The Burn Center provided me with clear instruction for how to continue caring for the burns.  In addition, since we lived 2.5 hours from Birmingham, AL they told me it would be ok to transfer patient care to my local medical provider ÃÂ too wanted me to have a follow up eye exam with my local eye doctor. I was given prescriptions for pain and double antibiotic ointment ([REDACTED]) accompanied by instructions to thickly apply three times each day to the burn wounds - arms and face.  Additionally, they provided me with a supply of [REDACTED], 4ÃÂx4ÃÂ Gauze pads, tongue blades (for applying the medicine) and tape. 
________________________________________

On page 14 (under "Troubleshooting") of the Operators Manual for the SunJoe SPX4000 Electric Pressure Washer, it recommends that if a 'fuse' blows when using this device, the owner should replace the 'fuse' with one of a higher amp rating. If an owner does this it could easily result in overheating of the electrical wiring due to the new 'fuse' allowing more current to pass than the wiring was originally designed for. With enough of a current draw, this could create a fire at some point in the circuit, causing severe damage or even a life threatening situation.
     While there has been no incident due to this to my knowledge, I believe this recommendation could be quite dangerous for anyone to follow. Thank you.
justification: The recommendation could lead to a fire, posing a life-threatening situation, though no incidents have been reported yet.

incident_description:
In March, 2019, I received a recall notice respecting the Flushmate II 501-B units with which our toilets came equipped. Although we had not had any problems with these units during the 20 years we had owned them, we were advised that they were at risk of bursting at the weld seam, which could "lift the tank lid and shatter the tank, posing impact and laceration hazards to consumers and property damage." I contacted the company on March 7, 2019 and was told that they would send us replacement units for our six toilets that contained the faulty pressure systems, and that the company would send a technician to our house to install the units. The replacements arrived promptly, and the technician came out on April 5, 2019, and installed the units.

On April 20, 2019, my husband used one of the toilets containing the new replacement Flushmate unites, and when he flushed the toilet, the unit burst, spewing water all over the bathroom, and fracturing the china of the toilet, in this case, not the lid but the base.

My husband was not injured, but it is clear that a person might be from this type of explosion. The toilet is of course completely unusable and will have to be replaced.

incident_description:
Samsung Washing Machine Model WA45K7600A / WA45K7100A

Washer has a top loading lid, with a "built in sink." This sink is a separate blue plastic basin that remains over the tub when the lid is raised to provide a shallow basin to pre-treat or pre-wash soiled items.  

First problem:
At the end of the wash cycle, I need to raise the lid (with the plastic basin attached) in order to remove the cleaned clothes.  However, this raised lid/basin combination is top heavy and unstable.  It will close after the slightest disturbance.  Since I am required, by design, to stick my head under this unstable lid/basin to reach the laundry in the deep tub, I have several times had the lid close on my head, face or arms.

The latest occurrence (and final straw) happened on or about April 1 when the lid/basin fell unexpectedly and struck the bridge of my nose.  The result:  significant bleeding, an obvious wound, a scab with resulting scar, and finally, the inconvenience and indignity of rewashing an otherwise clean load. incident_description:
I purchased a Bissell Crosswave floor cleaner in December of 2017.
These machines are a type of vacuum that uses a terrycloth roller brush to sweep debris into the mouth of the vacuum while dispensing short pulses of cleaning solution onto the spinning roller brush.
The idea is that the spinning terrycloth roller brush will wash the floor and then pick up most of the dirty cleaning solution and sling the dirty cleaaning solution into the mouth of the vacuum where the dirty cleaning solution is eventually deposited into a receiving tank, which is eventually removed from the machine and emptied.
Since buying this machine we have had to have it replaced by Bissell twice so far, and the third machine is in our dining room waiting for yet another replacement machine. Each machine has failed but for different problems. ALL THREE of these machines have a common problem, which Bissell chooses to ignore. ALL THREE of these machines have shocked me with a mild electric charge!
These machines do not suck up all of the cleaning solution! They are not only not capable, but not expected to suck up all of the cleaning solution. The floor is still slightly wet. Not just damp, but wet!
I have many times had to remove the front see-thru housing that encloses the floor brush to remove minor clogs; small twigs and long pine needles that the vacuum can't pick up are common in our home. When I touch the wet terrycloth roller brush I get SHOCKED! The only way to prevent this is to unplug the machine, but I don't think these machines should be shocking me even when it IS plugged in!
The flooring that we use this machine on range from sheet vinyl, real wood flooring, and "click-lock" flooring that is 95% PVC plastic with a very thin foam rubber backing. I have been shocked in all three rooms, on all three types of flooring! The machine has shocked me when plugged into  properly grounded outlets in each room, and I have even experienced being shocked when the machine was plugged into BOTH GFCI outlets! This happens in ANY outlet!
This electric charge has so far not been strong enough to hurt me, but strong enough to startle me! I find it very disturbing that ALL THREE of these machines have had this same problem!
justification: The incident involves repeated electric shocks from the machine, which are startling but not causing injury.

To verify that it was wired correctly, I plugged a [REDACTED] receptacle tester into the output receptacle (the plug-in location for the router). The tester reported an open neutral with the power switch in the "OFF" position. Further testing with a multimeter revealed that regardless of the switch location, the hot channel is never shut off (testing from hot to ground). Open of the router control confirmed my suspicions: The off switch is on the neutral side. The 15A fuse is the only wiring on the hot side of the circuit.

Putting the off switch on the neutral side creates a potentially hazardous situation: Any connected device will appear to be off but will actually be powered. The neutral line will also become hot. This unusual and unsafe wiring arrangement is not disclosed in the included technical manual.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous wiring arrangement that could lead to unsafe conditions, but no actual injury or death occurred.

The consumer went to the recall web site and answered the series of questions. Because his water heater was on a metal pan under it, the response was that he did not qualify for a retrofit.

On 3/1 , the water heater stopped working. When the consumer 
re-lit the water heater, flames exploded out of the side of the product. This happened three different times. 

The consumer went to the web site again and indicated that the product was not siting on a metal pan. This time the response was that he qualified for a retrofit.

It is the consumer's opinion that the recall is too focused on the metal pan. 

The consumer contacted Kenmore who referred him to A.O. Smith. The consumer contacted A.O. Smith on 3-5. The firm could see on their web site when he had checked for the recall about a month ago.

incident_description: On January 31, 2019, I purchased a Vornado AVH10 Vortex heater. After using the heater for about a month, on March 4, 2019, the heater stopped working. When I inspected the heater, I discovered that on the back panel, the vent had partially melted towards the top of the unit. This was alarming to me considering that I only used the heater for about two or three hours at a time at a temperature of no more than 72 degrees. (For reference, the lowest temperature of the heater is 65 degrees.) If I had been using this heater for longer periods of time or at higher temperatures, it's possible that the casing of the heater could have melted further and dripped into the heater itself, possibly causing a fire - or at least a fire hazard. I did some research online to see if anyone else has had a similar experience with their heaters of the same model. There are many complaints regarding the same issue posted by many reviewers on the product page for the unit on Amazon, where I purchased the heater. Some reviews include pictures showing damage from melting that is very similar to what I saw on my heater. A brand new heater should not be melting after one month of use for reasonable periods of time at relatively low temperatures. It appears that the problems that caused another Vornado heater to be recalled last year are still present in other units currently being sold. I would like for this issue to be investigated to ensure that this heater does not pose safety hazards to consumers. (Also, I have pictures, but this website will not allow me to attach them because I receive an error message each time.)
justification: The heater malfunctioned with a melted vent, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Buderus - Bosch Wall Hung Heater (Gas Home Furnace)
Epidemic failure of vent adapter causes CO fumes to exhaust directly into living space.
My Buderus Model GB142 furnace is 4-5 years old  and was properly installed by an authorized Buderus Agent. Similar models to the GB-142 are 24/30/45/60. I recently scheduled a cleaning but the service person (not a Buderus Agent) found that the vent adapter was rotted away and that carbon-monoxide-rich exhaust was flowing directly into our basement (maybe explaining a recent surge in headaches). Further research finds that Buderus (a division of Bosch) is aware of the problem, has redesigned the failing component, and has issued an internal "Product Notice" (https://www.bosch-climate.us/files/PIN_GB142_Vent_Adaptor_Inspection_US.pdf). Yet they have not notified consumers and have apparently not reported the problem to the CPSC. They offered to replace the part for free (only if I had registered the warranty when I bought the furnace and follow the very complicated re-imbursement procedure) but I will still need to pay the several hundred dollars to have their authorized service agent install it. 
The photo in the Product Notice shows a failure that is identical to mine and the gaping hole depicted makes clear the danger of the problem... That hole is in the exhaust pipe and an internal blower is forcing the exhaust under and pressure through that hole and into our home!!!!  People who have these furnaces in their homes are going to start dying from CO poisoning unless the CPSC steps in and forces Buderus to more actively correct this problem!!!!
justification: The incident involves CO fumes entering living spaces, causing headaches, which indicates injury (severity 3). The widespread failure and potential for CO poisoning make occurrence likely (4).

I have taken in my Honda EU2200i and Honda EU2200i Companion generators several times each because of fuel related problems; the worst one being leaking fuel.  We had them sitting in our laundry room and woke in the night to the smell of gasoline, and found them sitting in a puddle of gas!  We stopped use and took them in to a different authorized service center and they said nothing looked out of place and they could not replicate the problem.  Then we had a repeat over the last few days of leaking fuel again.

These things are dangerous and I need generators for daily life because I am off-grid in Alaska!  Please get these pulled and repaired!? Honda says they are waiting on CPSR to approve the recall and repair plan.  PLEASE HELP!?

incident_description:
I filed one report, but cannot find it on the web site.  So, I am filing the report again.  Our family had the horror of being a home with a Federal Pacific Electric Company circuit breaker panel box.  It dated from a previous owner add-on in the early 1960s, and by the 1990s, spot outlet fires began to occur.  Audible hums from the walls and dimming of lights while those had occurred, along with flickering lights when the washing machine was running were thought of as strange, but not anything was thought to be coming from the circuit breaker panel box.  

This changed, however, when in December 2016, a burning odor began emanating from the circuit breaker panel box itself when an upright vacuum cleaner was in use, and later on, when a circuit breaker had tripped, and an electrical burning odor was noticed.  The circuit appeared to not have functioned properly.  Power was out to certain parts of the house, but the burning odor was there.  No flames were noted.

However, a power strip in an adjacent room had partially melted and had black scorch marks.  

Two electricians in 2006 had identified faulty circuit breakers, but replaced them with used Federal Pacific circuit breakers.

This time, in 2016, a good electrician had recognized the name Federal Pacific, and knew that the breakers and the panel box had to be removed and replaced.

I had looked on the Internet and had found that there was a dark history to that company and that we now knew why all of the previous events had happened.  The Consumer Product Safety Commission had investigated the company from 1980 to 1983, and found that they had falsified testing results in the early 1950s to skirt around getting an Underwriters Laboratories seal of approval.  

According to reliable sources on the Internet, including news clips from NBC San Francisco and NBC New York City, WNBC-TV, Angie's List, and electrician websites, these products are in 28 million American homes and were manufactured up until 1988 and installed in homes as late as the early 1990s.  Ours was from the 1960s era.  A formal recall was never issued, due to budget constraints with the CPSC in 1983.  An amended statement was issued in 2011 by the CPSC.  

According to the information on the news reports and websites, 2,800 fires and 13 deaths each year are attributed in the United States to these products.  It is my belief that, even though the company is defunct and has been for 30 years, that the CPSC should issue a press release to widely publicize the removal of these hazardous products from American homes and wherever else they might be found.  One reference on the Internet indicated that some older schools have these still in use.

Why jeopardize any lives, when the facts are known?  These products need to be removed and not used ever again.  Ours was removed, but saved for proof that it was there.  I have called the CSPC and they have told me that since the company no longer exists, that a recall cannot be issued.  But, surely, better publicity could be done to inform the public that might not have tracked this down on the Internet that these products were intentionally made to be defective and have caused property and human loss.  That is inexcusable, especially since the company is defunct.  No risks of reprisals or lawsuits, such as they had feared in the early 1980s, when the company was still in existence.  It is time for action to alert the public about the dangerous legacy that this company left behind.  We ourselves were unaware until December 2016 of the dangers and it went a long way in explaining what had happened with the previous incidents as well.

I am electrically sensitive, and I believe that the faulty product had effects on my nervous system over the years.  These products should be made known to be faulty and removed and replaced with safe equipment, as ours was, with Murray Siemens in our case.  This is an unusual case, as the company is out of business, but their products are still causing property damage, loss, and loss of human life, according to Internet and television reports.
justification: The incident involved a faulty circuit breaker panel causing electrical issues and a melted power strip, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
My wife noticed that there was a brown spot on the side of one of white smoke alarms on the ceiling.  It looked like the plastic was starting to burn.  I pulled the smoke alarm apart and found that a large resistor, labeled D7 on the circuit board, was where the heat was originating from.  The green circuit board was black covering a couple square inches of circuit board around it.  I then went and checked the other 13 smoke alarms in the house and 12 had similar brown spots on the exterior white plastic.  One had just slightly discolored plastic (barely noticeable) and I opened it up too and found the circuit board also blackened around that same resistor, but in this case the resistor looked very different.  It was a different brand, but similar size to the orignal one.  I found that the build date of this smoke alarm was 4/30/2010 whereas the original one I had looked at had a build date was 5/5/2009.

These smoke alarms are Kidde brand, model i12040, with build dates of 5/5/2009 and 4/30/2010 (I checked all 14 smoke alarms).  Upon removal they do feel hot on their rear side (goes against the ceiling) in the location of where the resistor is inside.

I contacted Kidde, sent them pictures of the brown spots on all of the smoke alarms along with detailed pictures showing the resistor and both sides of the circuit board inside.  A product support representative by the name of [REDACTED], forwarded the info to  an engineer there who responded, "The photos you send are typical for alarms that have been in service for 8 to 10 years. The power supply in the smoke alarm does generate some heat which will discolor the circuit board and possibly the plastic over time. This is a normal occurrence and not a design concern and does not affect the operation of the alarm."

My concern is that this issue may be a fire hazard as  I can't imagine any properly designed circuit board which gets hot enough to char the circuit board and cause burn marks on the plastic housing.  

I can send pictures if provided an email address or repository to send them to.
justification: The incident involves potential fire hazard due to overheating components in smoke alarms, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I purschased a Rheem Tankless Gas Water Heater at the Home Depot on 11/11/2018 and installed it myself. It was replacing another Tankless Gas Water Heater that I already had. Immediately after installing it, intermittently I would hear this loud popping & banging sound coming out of the water heater. It would only happen on ignition. Once the heater was running it was fine. And it only happens about 50% of the time. I thought well maybe this is the way this one functions as it was different from my last Tankless heater. But then it got worse; louder and more frequent. I called Rheem. They told my they thought I didn't have the discharge vent constructed properly however I told them it was within the specifications listed in their installation manual. They told me I had the wrong instructions so I changed the discharge ventilation to meet what they said. That did not fix the problems. I called them back. I then had to get a certified plumber to come and measure the natural gas pressures for them. That cost me $99. It was then determined that the heater has a bad gas valve that is leaking natural gas into my house even when there is no call for the heater to heat water. It's call "Bleed thru" as the gas is leaking thru a closed valve. That popping and bangin that I'm hearing is because of an excessive amount of natural gas in the combustion chamber being ignited when the heater turns on. MY HOUSE COULD BLOW UP!!!!!!!!!!!. Rheem in turn just sent me a new valve and it's going to cost me almost $200 to have it change. They are only reimbursing me for$125 of it. That's not the point. The point is they're acting like it's no big deal having natural gas leaking from the heater when it's not supposed to!!! The heaters with this valve need recalled and checked to make sure they have gas valves that are functioning properly and aren't leaking natural gas when they're not supposed to!!!!!!!!! Having the valve changed on 1/30/2019 (the earliest the plumber could do it).
justification: The incident involves a gas leak which poses a significant risk of explosion, but no injury or death has occurred yet.
