incident_description:
I have an Emerson Sensi Wifi thermostat purchased in 2015. I received the following email:

from: Sensi Support sensirecall@realtimeresults.net via [REDACTED]
Thu, Dec 20, 2018, 10:24 AM

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTICE

White-Rodgers Announces Voluntary Corrective Action on
Emerson-Branded Sensi WiFi Thermostats

December 12, 2018

Our records indicate you have an Emerson-branded Sensi Wi-Fi thermostat. In cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, White-Rodgers is implementing a corrective action plan that affects a limited number of those thermostats.

The affected thermostats are vulnerable to damage during service or replacement of your heating or cooling system. Accidental contact between the thermostat wires and line voltage by a service person can damage the thermostat and create a potential fire hazard, which can occur several days later.

Identifying an affected Thermostat

Potentially affected thermostats have ÃÂEmersonÃÂ printed on the front. Thermostats with ÃÂSensiÃÂ printed on the front are not affected. This corrective action involves model 1F86U-42WF and UP500W thermostats that have date codes from 1416 to 1536 AND are powered by a wire connected to the C terminal on the thermostat base plate.

HereÃÂs a step-by-step guide to determine if your thermostat is affected.

Step 1: Remove your thermostat from the wall by pulling the thermostat straight toward you; the back plate will remain attached to the wall.

Step 2: Check the product label located in the upper left of the backside of the thermostat for the model number and date code. Model numbers 1F86U-42WF and UP500W with date codes from 1416 to 1536 might be impacted.

o    If the product label indicates a different model number or date code outside of this range, no further action is required.

o   If the product label indicates either of these model numbers AND a date code within this range, please proceed to the next step.

Step 3: Check to see if you have a wire connected to the terminal labeled ÃÂCÃÂ on base plate on the wall.

o   If there is no wire connected to the terminal labeled ÃÂCÃÂ, no further action is required.

o   If there is a wire connected to the terminal labeled ÃÂCÃÂ, please proceed to the next step.

Step 4: Register your thermostat with White-Rodgers by visiting www.recallrtr.com/emersonthermostat or by calling 1-888-847-8742 between 7 a.m. and 6 p.m. (Central Time) Monday through Friday.

Step 5: Locate the pin labeled C at the bottom right on the backside of the thermostat. Bend the pin down to a 90-degree angle. For additional guidance and a demo, please watch a video at [REDACTED].

Step 6: Place the thermostat back on the base plate on the wall and continue to use your thermostat.

If you have any questions, please call 1-888-847-8742 between 7 a.m. and 6 p.m. (Central Time) Monday through Friday.

This completes the corrective action for most customers. In most installations, a connection to the C terminal is not necessary because your Sensi thermostat will still receive power from the heating/cooling system using the patented ÃÂpower-sharingÃÂ feature in the Sensi. The function of your thermostat should not be impacted, and there is no need to reprogram it.

If your thermostat is connected to Wi-Fi and your system has only heating or only cooling, or if you begin to experience shortened battery life, please contact White-Rodgers for assistance.

This corrective action will disable the continuous backlight feature of the Sensi thermostat. If you use this feature and wish to continue doing so, please contact White-Rodgers for further information.

To contact White-Rodgers, call 1-888-847-8742 between 7 a.m. and 6 p.m. (Central Time) Monday through Friday or visit www.recallrtr.com/emersonthermostat.

If you have already registered and completed the corrective action, no further action on your part is required
 ----------------------------- (end of email, pictures did not copy into this) -------

I performed the instructions. After bending the pin corresponding to the C-wire, the thermostat would no longer fire heat when called upon, after increasing the heat and waiting several minutes. I bent the pin back carefully and was able to restore functionality to the thermostat, but presumably whatever fire hazard was now a possibility. I wrote to the company, ending in a decision to buy another product, which is now installed and working, after the company could not explain what was happening, and would not reimburse me for the purchase from 2015. 

I wrote that I can not trust a company to give me another thermostat under the circumstances: the disclosed instructions rendered my thermostat inoperable. How can I trust anything this company puts out? I want reimbursement for the product. 

Someone from Emerson wrote that they would forward this request for reimbursement but never got back to me with information confirming that this would happen.

At this point they are not responding to my email after a weeks passing.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning thermostat due to corrective action, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood of recurrence is unlikely as the issue was resolved by replacing the product.

incident_description:
I purchased a
        "HUBEST 3 Speed Mini Drill Press Machine 150W Mini Bench Table Drill For Craft Jewelers & Hobbyists,  Sold by [REDACTED]" from Amazon.com on December 12th, 2018.

I am convinced it has a dangerous problem.

The motor within the drill head unit is not fixed and can swivel to either side.  It is obvious the manufacturer is aware of this since there is a piece of stick-on foam tape on either side of the aluminum casting where the motor would touch after it shifts.  The motor torque tries to shift the motor to the left as viewed from the front.

The problem arises from a ground wire attached to the left-inside of the case.  The brass wire termination is somewhat sharp-edged, and one of the blue power wires to the drill motor presses against it when the motor shifts to the left.  When the drill press handle is operated, the  motor moves up and down and the blue wire rubs quite aggressively against the sharp edge.  The result is the scraping of insulation off of a live 120VAC wire that will eventually results in a contact to the drill press frame.  The frame is grounded, which helps, but the contact could still cause a fire, or if the unit was plugged in an ungrounded socket, result in a "hot" device.

I discovered this problem when I removed the top cover of the drill head, which is necessary to change the motor speed by moving the drive belt to a different pulley.  I noticed that the drill seemed to hang-up slightly as I moved the drill press up/down, and this led me look closely at the motor assembly.  Further inspection showed it was the interference of the wire causing the problem, and that revealed the scraped insulation.

Please note that I never used the drill press.  I was just testing it on my bench to ascertain the run-out of the spindle and how smoothly the handle worked.  I probably never cranked the handle up/down more than a dozen times, and that was sufficient to cause the insulation problem.

Unfortunately, the Hubest model may not be the only one with this problem.  This drill press appears to be a generic Chinese-made tool sold by various companies that apply their label to it.  For example,
[REDACTED], and
[REDACTED]
on the Amazon website look to be identical.

I am an electrical engineer and have worked in multiple safety-critical areas, including medical equipment.  The problem described above is a definite safety hazard and the unit should not be sold until you can verify the problem has been rectified.  I would also HIGHLY recommend that existing units be recalled.
justification: The incident describes a potential electrical hazard that could lead to fire or electric shock, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
On 9/2/18, my fiance and I purchased two 1-gallon containers of Zep brand "Mold Stain & Mildew Stain Remover" from a local store. These containers were placed in the trunk of the car for transit home. Once at home and parked in the driveway, we began to smell a very strong bleach smell and noticed that from the back right corner of the car, a clearish liquid was steadily dripping to the ground and forming a foamy puddle. When we opened the trunk, we discovered that one of the bottles had fallen on its side and the cap was lying a few inches away from the bottle. Half or more of the contents had spilled from the bottle.

Despite trying to soak up as much of the product as we could, the car maintained a noxious bleach smell for over a week--it was impossible to drive it due to the fumes (which irritated our nasal passages, throats, and eyes), unless the windows were rolled down (in 80-90 degree weather). 

The most disturbing part of all this is that when we tested the white cap on the other bottle, WHICH WAS LABELED AS BEING "CHILD-PROOF," we found out that the cap was not at all child-proof and could be easily unscrewed (or easily popped off, as it did in the back of our trunk). In addition, when we turned over the second container (which did not fall over in the trunk) to look for serial/model numbers days later, liquid steadily leaked out from the cap. So the major issue here is the fact that this product is being sold with supposedly-child-proof caps that are NOT AT ALL child-proof. We pointed this out to the manager at the store where we bought it (when we took the bottle that spilled back for a replacement), and he said he would pass it along to the company so that they could address it. However, I have reason to believe they have not addressed it, and that is why I am filing this report.
justification: The incident caused irritation to nasal passages, throats, and eyes, which qualifies as injury. The likelihood is possible due to the product's faulty cap design.

incident_description:
Blueskin Butyl Flashing by Henry was used in the installation of windows in our home November 5 and 6th. The flashing is applied on the inside and outside of the house. [REDACTED] adhesive was used on the flashing on the outside of our home between the flashing and the nail in windows. From the first day forward a strong chemical off-gassing came from the windows. It grew worse once the exterior wood was placed over the windows. After over two months the off-gassing has NOT subsided. We have been unable to be in our home for more than a few minutes at a time. We have symptoms of headaches (migraines), confusion, short term memory loss, sore throat, and difficulty breathing which seemed to be more cardiac than pulmonary from exposure. The loss of short term memory seems to be the longest symptom to resolve and I am still having symptoms. I have stopped entering my house for this reason.

My husband clipped off a piece of the Blueskin Butyl Flashing from the inside of the house and put it in a sealed jar. This clipped had been stuck on the wood frame of the window, but not other adhesive used on this portion according to our window installer.  We opened the jar outside the home and identified this as the same chemical that is permeating our home. Our concern is that the volatiles are in all the contents of our home including drywall and insulation at this point.

The Blueskin Flashing was approved for use without the company divulging the major ingredients of the product. No information is available on the SDS regarding the volatile compounds used. It only lists it as" butyl compounds". We contacted them and they claim it does not smell, which is clearly false. They do not know what chemicals it interacts with or are safe to use with the product even though it is routinely used in homes along with other adhesives in the flashing. 

We had to move out of our home with our three children. We have had both financial, emotion and mental stress. We have had no help around how to mitigate the dangerous chemicals in our home. We are very upset that the building industry is so poorly regulated and endangers the health and lives of our citizens.
justification: The incident caused multiple health symptoms including migraines, confusion, and difficulty breathing, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances of the product's use and the reported symptoms.

incident_description: I purchased a Master Industrial Products kerosene space heater model MH-75T-KFA, S/N 170722309.  The fuel tank's cap is made of a plastic that appears to be incompatible with kerosene.  What happens is that the portion of the cap that is inside the tank swells making it very difficult to remove.  Once you successfully pry it off the tank, you cannot get it back on because the "nose" of the cap is larger than the hole it goes in due to the swelling of the plastic.  So one has to operate the heater with an OPEN fuel tank or you can modify the cap by sanding off the swollen area of the cap to get it to fit for a short time, which most consumers would not think to try to do.  The locking pin in the cap's nose also falls out due to the swelling of the plastic.  The plastic continues to deteriorate due to being incompatible with kerosene, even after a sanding modification.  I called the manufacturer and found out that they offer a metal cap that you can purchase (they won't provide for free) which on face value, seems to indicate they know they have a problem with their plastic fuel cap.  This model (or the entire series that uses these plastic caps) should be subject to a recall before serious fires occur from people operating these heaters without the fuel cap.  I have the faulty cap in my possession.
justification: The incident involves a faulty fuel cap that could lead to an open fuel tank, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has been reported yet.

I did contact the manufacturer of the knobs (Kwikset) to ask them about the issue and get a replacement knob. However, they did decline to replace the units for me as they indicated they were out of warranty.  I did inform them of the safety hazard condition this presented.  In this case it was just a child stuck in a closet, which is scary for them, but it could be someone trying to escape a fire in a house. justification: The incident involved a child being trapped in a closet due to a faulty door knob, which is a safety hazard but did not result in injury or death.

The unit itself lifted off the ground and landed onto the 4" diameter dryer vent which was laying on the ground in the back of the machine.  The washer moved forward dragging the vent approximately 18" blocking the exit door.  With the door blown open, the tub continued to spin at a very high rate and the machine continued to shake and move.  It was only stopped when the power was shut down.  No one was in the laundry room at the time. The unit has now been moved back to its original location to allow clear access to the door.

incident_description: I bought one of the Red Stone 30,000 btu vent free gas wall heaters several years ago from Tractor Supply. The model number is MD300TBA-RS Serial #12542450. They are set up to use either Natural Gas or Propane depending on how you need it. Ours was natural gas. After the first couple years, it started flaring up in an uncontrolled manner, and luckily I caught it in time, so I contacted the company. They wouldn't make it right, but they did sell me a new gas control valve body to replace the original defective one. The unit functioned perfectly after that until today when the unit started venting raw, unburned natural gas into our garage and filled our house up. I was in the basement and didn't discover it until I came upstairs and went into the garage and heard and smelled it.. I don't know where the gas was coming from, but it stopped when I turned the burner control to the off position. The pilot light was still lit, but it failed to ignite the gas, so I think the gas must have been coming from a different place than the correct one. It was a miracle that I found it when I did, and it didn't happen during the night, or there would be 3 dead people due to this defective product. I was probably less than 10 minutes from the gas level coming down to ignite on the still lit pilot light. This heater has got to have a inherent design flaw for two different controllers to malfunction twice.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous gas leak that could have led to death, but no actual injuries or deaths occurred.

I am going to have to have the roof deck pulled off and replaced with a roof deck with built in insulation.  I would recommend that spray foam never be used. incident_description:
My 6 yr old AO Smith natural gas water heater lost its pilot light overnight. I turned off my garage lights to view the combustion chamber while I relighted the pilot in  the normal fashion. It had no problem at this step, but upon turning the valve to main burner, the ignition of the burner came in loud explosions of machine-gun quick bursts of flame, escaping the combustion chamber and extending out the perimeter of the heater and upward about 12". This continued until I turned off the gas at the main valve. Please note that my water heater had been inspected and approved by a Livermore Building Inspector at installation.
  
I removed the burner to discover the cause to be a hole that had burned through the wire mesh burner diffuser, which allowed unburned gas to accumulate rather than to be immediately exposed to the pilot light. It is unknown how long the condition had taken to eventually blow out the pilot light. 

AO Smith was quick to send a replacement burner under warranty, but was unresponsive to my request for a review of safety issues, and specifically, a replacement with a traditional cast iron type burner. Phone calls and emails were stonewalled. 
 
My request of you is to assist me in registering a public safety complaint against this type of burner, as of course, no matter how old a water heater is, it should never experience catastrophic failure.
 Please see the enclosed pictures.
 
Thank you,
 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a dangerous gas explosion but resulted in no injury or death, hence severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the described failure mechanism and lack of manufacturer response.

incident_description:
I recently installed a Rheem gas water heater to as a replacement for an older heater. I attached the supplied draft vent hood to my existing 4 inch diameter flue. I performed the recommended draft test using a match and found sufficient draft for the operation of the appliance. After allowing the unit to operate overnight, I went to check the water connections for leaks. I observed that the plastic escutcheons and a plastic label on the top of the unit were melted. I contacted Rheem customer support and was instructed to perform the draft test again. Sufficient draft was present.
While the Rheem supplied draft hood accepts a 4 inch flue, the opening for the flue gasses is 3 inches. It doesn't appear that this restricts the flow of the gasses, but does appear to reflect enough heat to melt the plastic components on the top of the unit.
I've temporarily replaced the Rheem draft hood with one that has a true 4 inch opening and the melting condition has stopped. The CO detector in the basement hasn't activated, so I'm confident that the replacement draft hood is working properly.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic components due to heat reflection, but no injury or CO exposure was reported.

incident_description:
This furnace failed in the exact same manner as the one in Report# 20180907-68F7A-1791007..


The consumer believes that this unit had the exact same model & serial number as the previous unit, by the same mfr.  The consumer said that there were no design changes to remove the poloypropolene liner in this 2006 unit, so when they replaced this 2015 unit, it was the identical to the prior one.  

The consumer wrote:  "The first furnace was installed by a local plumbing company and I believe the distributor, at the time, was Blodgett.  When the second furnace failed in 2015 (the one in this report), the propane Service Provider, Blanchard Oil, installed and maintained the unit.  Blodgett also ordered and shipped the parts.  Homens is their new distributor.  Originally, I was told that I would be receiving a $ 600 gift card but all of that went out the window and I had to purchase a new furnace from a different company.  Based on the reviews from Blanchard and FredÃÂs Plumbing, I purchased a Napoleon Furnace.  I canÃÂt take any more risks of Bryant Furnace failures in Vermont Winter months."  

This furnace failed during Winter months and the consumer was home both times.  The consumer contacted Blanchard who put a portable propane Rinnai heater in the basement to keep the pipes from freezing. The consumer was able to burn wood inside the house.  In the evenings, the home temperature plunged to 50 degrees, but there was no damage to the home.  ?

The consumer wrote, "According to [REDACTED] at Blodgett supply in Newport Vermont, because the Flame Rollout Switch (and error code on the furnace) functioned properly, basically shutting down the furnace, it prevented any problems with harmful fumes or exhaust from entering the home.   Had that also stopped working, we would have had serious issues.  When the furnace begins to fail, a strange smell is emitted.  It smells like propane inside the home and it makes you nauseous, but I donÃÂt think there were long term health issues associated with that.   There was a great deal of stress during both failures.  When you donÃÂt have a working furnace in the winter and during sub zero weather, it is very upsetting."  

There was an odor that can best be described as a propane gas smell inside the house as the furnace became compromised and before final failure.  When the consumer smelled this again in 2018, they knew immediately that the furnace was beginning to fail.  When it did finally stop working, they contacted Bryant to open the second ticket.  That is when Bryant told them that they shipped the consumer the same furnace with the same design issue so it is no wonder it failed just 3 years later.  

The unit was charred ÃÂ this can see that in the attached pictures. The first picture is from 2018, the one below that is from 2015.   Unfortunately, this side of the furnace is not able to be seen when it is installed in the housing cabinet.  It needs to be removed to be able to see the damage from the unit being plugged or blocked.   The consumer attached pictures from the back of the furnace in 2015 and again in 2018.  They look exactly the same.  
 
Also, Bryant is now suggesting that the size of the unit in terms of BTUs was too large for the home.  Had that been the case, the furnace itself would have issued a fan high limit switch error code, which it did not.  It issued the Flame Rollout Switch which indicates the unit is plugged.  Blodgett also conducted a test to size the unit.   Unfortunately, they did not keep a copy, but they have refuted BryantÃÂs claim on the sizing of the furnace.  They have also sized the replacement [REDACTED] Unit and it is the same exact size.  Bryant claims the unit was too large for the square footage of the home.  According to Blodgett, you canÃÂt just use Square Footage ÃÂ you must also account for number of window and glass square footage and quality, type of walls, type of insulation, flooring, cold floor space (crawl space vs. basement, etc.)  They performed the calculation in 2006/2007 and again in 2018 and have said the size of the Bryant and Napoleon furnaces are correct.  
  
The consumer is concerned that both units may have presented a fire, a CO  or some other type of hazard.
justification: The incident involved furnace failure and hazardous odors, but no injury or death occurred. The recurrence of similar failures suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased the Samsung top load washer (Model: WA52J8700AP/A2) (Serial Number: 0E6H5AUH100175D) approximately less than two years ago.  Unfortunately, shortly after my fiancÃÂ© was injured in the Marines during a deployment to Iraq. Due to the financial strain from his injuries we were forced to sell our house and move to an apartment that was more affordable for the time being. Our brand new washer & dryer went to our storage unit until August of 2017 when we purchased our home. Our washer started acting up (excessive vibration, multiple error codes, loud noises, etc) in April 2018, so I went online to troubleshoot and quickly discovered it was recalled. 
Due to the move and chaos surrounding the time of purchase we no longer have our receipt so I called the recall rebate customer assistance to make sure that wouldn't cause an issue. I was told that wouldn't be a problem and was offered two options for this issue: (1) To have the washer repaired at their cost which would extend the manufacture warranty for one year OR (2) to purchase a new washer in exchange for the recalled washer.  The recall rebate form offered $544 for a new non-Samsung brand and they offered an additional $150 if you purchased another Samsung washer for a total of $694 plus any installation/removal fees as long as they were on the sales receipt for the new unit.  We definitely didn't have the extra money to purchase a new washer at the time so we had planned on opting for the repair, however, there were no "authorized agents" in my area to make the repair so the rebate was my only option.  

We were extremely disappointed and angry about having to fork out the extra money to purchase a new washer when ours was less than two years old, but were assured we'd receive our rebate in 4-6 weeks.  We made the purchase of the comparable Samsung model from Lowes on 8/1/18 for a total of $881.68 and delivered on 8/8/18.  Our recalled model washer that matched our dryer was platinum silver in color and of course, Samsung discontinued that color so we no longer have a matching set as we ordered (to which they told us "too bad").

On 8/11/18, I sent in the completed rebate form with all of the requirements included.  After six weeks of still not receiving the rebate (or any type of communication at all) I contacted Samsung to obtain the status of my rebate check and was told that someone had already claimed the rebate for my serial number.  I was floored!  I asked how this possibly could have happened when I've been in possession of the washer since I purchased in early 2017.  The agent told me that when the recall was first issued some of the recalled washers that were returned were mistakenly placed back on the sales floor.  So, I asked what I needed to do to receive the $694 as promised and was told they would need to "conduct an investigation" but they couldn't tell me an estimated time of when this would be completed and just said "it can take a very long time".  I have spoke to various different agents on the phone, written countless emails/complaints and exhausted every avenue of trying to get this issue resolved.  I am now completely out my recalled washer (that was not even 2 years old and was over $1000) that I was forced to replace because of their lack of agents but also the cost of another $900 washer in less than 24 months.  I understand that mistakes happen but it wasn't OUR mistake and Samsung is doing nothing to justify this error on their behalf.  I continue to get the same response that "they will have to investigate", no timeline of events of what to expect, continuous runaround, and excuses.  I have researched this issue in great lengths and have found that my experience is very similar to many others and I'm extremely frustrated, disappointed and down right angry in the lack of service and support from Samsung.  It was the recommendation of several agents I've spoke to regarding this situation to bring attention to the issue to CPSC.  I pray that this will help get my rebate issued immediately as originally promised by Samsung.  Thank  you in advance for you time.
justification: The incident describes financial and customer service issues without any physical injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the reported frequency of similar complaints.

I was able to get a second Samsung technician over and he told me that all washers are like this nowadays and the only way to have clean clothes is to wash the washer regularly with tide washer cleaner. It is certainly against the manual. Bottom line, I had to start using them, although I donÃÂt like to use those strong chemicals in my house, mostly having a small child. Well, our allergies got worse and I fear for my daughter lungs as at times I smell a mold type of smell on her clothes. 
We owned a front load washer before. We always kept the door opened and always wiped the door and around it. This maintenance doesnÃÂt help with this washer. I suspect there is something inside the washer that gets moldy from time to time. Fighting it with chemicals only helps for so long. ItÃÂs so sad!

incident_description:
We had this washing machine only 18 months or so when we started to notice small black spots on our clothes. We initially ignored it and just assumed something was left in a pocket, but the spots persisted and then became accompanied by a moldy/musty smell - clothes, towels, sheets, everything. After investigating, I discovered that there was an enormous amount of mold growing underneath and within the agitator as well as under the tub itself.  Both the tub and agitator are stainless steel on the inside (where the clothes make contact and plastic on the outside. The issue is that water remains between these two layers and the mold began growing (despite maintaining as recommended by the manufacturer and even running extra vinegar cycles monthly). We've been battling this issue for about a year now and are at a loss - I've even taken the agitator out and the steel and plastic pieces are fused together, so you can't even separate them to bleach or clean separately. We're at a point that this machine is now completely useless to us and a health hazard - we have a 5 yr old who's been wearing clothes with black mold on them for over a year and we can no longer risk her health nor ours.  If you search Samsung's support pages, there are 50+ pages comprising literally hundreds of reports from consumers having this same issue and Samsung refuses to call it a defect nor address the issue, so I'm reaching out in the hope that you can help since we're in an unsafe situation and the manufacturer refuses to do anything about it.  Thank you for your help.
-[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves mold exposure from a washing machine, posing a health hazard, especially to a child, but no direct injury is reported.

incident_description:
The furnace failed during the winter months.  The consumer contacted a local service company (Blanchard), who put a portable propane [REDACTED] heater in the basement to keep the pipes from freezing.  The consumer was able to burn wood inside the house.  In the evenings, the home temperature plunged to 50 degrees, but there was no damage to the home.  

There were no injuries as a result of this issue.  There was a smell that can best be described as a propane gas odor inside the house as the furnace is became compromised and before final failure occurred.    

The unit was charred.  Unfortunately, this side of the furnace is not able to be seen when it is installed in the housing cabinet.  It needs to be removed to be able to see the damage from the unit being plugged or blocked.   
 
A technician from the distributor (Blodgett) conducted a test to size the unit.  The calculations were performed in 2006/2007.
justification: No injuries occurred, but there was a propane gas odor and the furnace was charred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Electri-Cord brand power cord attached to a Weller W100PG solder iron that I just purchased with date stamp of (19/18).  Removing it from the packaging and limbering the cord from it's twist-tied folding caused splits along the thin black jacket overwrap where it had been most tightly curved to fit in the blister card.  This is an electric shock hazard, particularly if cord draped into conductive fluids.

Cord is marked with white imprint "(UL) VW-1 E46194 (M) SVTO 3/C 18 AWG (0.824mm2)   105'C 300V  FT1, FT2 LL90458 (M)" and with emboss "Made in Mexico" "E.S.Electri-Cord" "c(UL)us" on the plug head.

The thin 'shrinkwrap' black electrical isolation jacket on cord is too thin and flimsy and seems to have a seam running the length of it, which is where these splits are occurring and from which the white fibrous contents is spilling out.

With those splits, which I'm sure will extend in length and increase in number with time and any use, and gaps to the white fibrous interior, I'm sure this fails to meet UL rating because of electric shock hazard.

My older, same model iron with date stamp (02/14) has a similar Electri-Cord power cord, except that the codes is DEBOSSED on the black jacket and it is "SVT", not "SVTO".

I do not know the details of these different codings, but I've used this older one for years and it's cord jacket is thicker (you cannot see cord contents texture 'telegraph' through, like on this new one) and more rubbery and more pliable.  It's what I'd expect in a cord for a handheld heating tool.

Already communicated with Weller, Electri-Cord and UL about this problem.
justification: The power cord's damaged insulation presents an electric shock hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

He said the shower handle was shocking him.  I went and checked and it most definantley was charged with electricity.   Not long after that the water heater started beeping and has an A104 Error Code displayed.   There are no visible leaks on the unit but must have a leak inside the tank allowing it to become electrically charged.   So I immediately turned the unit off and our shower is no longer charged.   The water heater unit is fairly new.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock to a child, which constitutes an injury, and the likelihood is possible given the description of the faulty water heater.

incident_description: Have been sick periodically on and off since Mitsubishi split system a/c and heat pump system was installed in 2015 but condition has become chronic with congestion, coughing and chest tightening in last couple of months.  My husband also has the same cough and is suffering from leukemia.  We couldn't figure out what was wrong and neither could the doctors until I went to change the direction of the air flow from the unit and saw black mold on the vanes which I wiped off.  While on the ladder and having the vanes in the open position I saw to the back of the unit and noticed a heavy infestation of black mold across the area.  I have cleaned the filters in this unit religiously and never noticed this because the unit was off and the vanes were closed while cleaning them.  I immediately shut off the unit and it has been off since then (11/23/18). My congestion and coughing and my husband's sneezing and coughing is nearly gone and I have been cleaning everything to eliminate whatever mold spores may be remaining.  I contacted the installing dealer and was told the problem was merely dirt not mold and the "unit was definitely safe to use, don't worry" even though they hadn't actually seen the unit. I am a nurse and know the difference between dirt and mold and it is definitely mold.  They wanted over $300 to clean the unit but I am sure this will be a recurring problem which the literature doesn't mention.   Meanwhile I have a $5000 unit unused an am waiting to hear back from Mitsubishi.

incident_description:
This 68 year old consumer contacted the CPSC Hotline to report that the dehumidifier he purchased online June 10, 2016 had overheated and repeats the overheating very quickly.
He is reporting this unit as a severe fire hazard and is asking that it become one of the recalled units.
Around October 9th, 2018 the caller and his family went out for about three or four hours  but when they returned to their home there was a burning odor throughout it.
The caller went to the basement because it seemed to be coming from there to discover that it was his 70 pint dehumidifier that was overheating and was exceedingly hot.
He immediately unplugged it and allowed it to cool off.
The filter was clean due to having been changed recently and all else was up to care specifications. 
He waited for several days then plugged the dehumidifier back in and remained with it, however after only one half hour the fan stopped and the dehumidifier began instantly heating to a high heat.
He repeated this a couple of days later and it repeated that same process and is not being used at all.
There are no injuries being reported.
The caller does still have the product.
The consumer contacted the manufacturer and the distributor October 15th, 2018 and he was advised that he was outside of the warranty process and there was no assistance.
justification: The dehumidifier overheated multiple times, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Last spring (March or April 2018) I bought a HeatMate HMC-23K kerosene heater. 

This heater is intended for use inside homes. 

The shut-off switch never worked very well, but I could get it to shut off if I repeatedly wiggled the flame adjustment knob while actuating the shut off switch multiple times. According to the users manual, this was not how it is meant to be shutoff. Shut off should occur by simply depressing the shut off lever. 

I probably should have taken it back to the retailer when I first got it, as it would be a safety hazard if you needed to extinguish the flame quickly. However, I made due with it as it was.

Now, the flame adjustment know has completely broken, making the shut off nearly impossible. It is only possible with use of a heavy pair of pliers. 

To me, this is clearly a defective and dangerous product.
justification: The heater's defective shut-off mechanism poses a safety hazard, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

I was downstairs when I heard the explosion and upon entering the bathroom, glass was everywhere and my husband was still standing in the shower bleeding.  I gave him a towel to wrap his hand and placed a mat on the floor so he could exit the shower.

I contacted Basco regarding the incident, and their response was "tempered glass may spontaneously shatter for no apparent reason and that it is a characteristic of tempered glass".

We never realized this to be a characteristic of tempered glass -- spontaneously shatter for no apparent reason!
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (punctured hand and bleeding), and the description suggests that spontaneous shattering of tempered glass is a known but unlikely occurrence.

incident_description:
California Air Resources Board (ARB) staff recently measured ozone emissions from 17 consumer products and home appliances and published a journal article on the results, which can be found at http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/ina.12307/pdf. We found that five products in three categories produced ozone at levels that may result in adverse health effects. 

Ozone is a reactive gas comprised of three oxygen atoms. While ozone high up in the atmosphere protects us from the sunÃÂs harmful rays, at ground level, ozone can cause adverse health effects such as coughing, chest tightness and shortness of breath. Exposure to ozone may both induce and worsen asthma symptoms and worsen lung disease; it might also increase the risk of premature death. Some consumer products and home appliances are designed to emit ozone either intentionally, or as a by-product of their functions.

This study measured ozone emissions and impacts on indoor ozone levels and associated exposures from 17 consumer products and home appliances that could emit ozone either intentionally or as a by-product of their functions.  Nine products were found to emit measurable ozone, one up to 6,230 ppb at a distance of 5 cm (2 inches). Five products in three categories produced ozone at levels that may result in potential health effects, including a residential ozone laundry water treatment appliance, two fruit and vegetable washers, and two [REDACTED]. Use of some of these products increased ozone concentrations in a small room to concentrations that exceeded the level of 1-hr California Ambient Air Quality Standard (CAAQS) for outdoor ozone (0.09 parts per million [ppm]). The greatest increase of room ozone concentrations during typical use of the products resulted from use of the laundry water treatment system. During one wash cycle, this product increased the room ozone concentration by an average of 0.11 ppm.

Due to usersÃÂ close proximity to this product, the concentration of ozone that users might actually be exposed to (the personal exposure concentration) can be even higher than the room concentrations measured. During one wash cycle, users of the laundry water treatment system may be exposed to an average of 0.42 ppm ozone potentially for 1 hour. This level of exposure is equivalent to about one-quarter to one-half of the ozone that a typical California resident may be exposed to in one day.

For some products, one use does not increase the room ozone concentrations markedly, but repeated use can result in high personal exposure concentrations for the user. For example, when a fruit and vegetable washer was used for three continuous wash cycles with reused water, the average personal exposure concentration was 2.55 ppm, over 28 times higher than the level of the 1-hr CAAQS. For the remaining products tested, their average ozone emissions were low, but surprisingly high peaks were commonly observed. When using a [REDACTED] were reached. 

Although their market share is unknown, these products can easily be obtained due to their low unit price and widespread advertising via the Internet and television. Thus, the exposures associated with the use of such products may be widespread. However, none of these products are regulated for their ozone emissions, which is a critical gap in consumer protection. Actions should be taken to protect consumers from potential exposures to high levels of ozone from these products.
justification: The study found that several products emit ozone at levels that can cause adverse health effects, including worsening asthma and lung disease, which qualifies as injury (severity 3). The widespread availability and use of these products make occurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I originally noticed a bad smell emanating from the Samsung top load washing machine, despite running self clean and sanitize cycles, and using white vinegar and bleach to clean, per Samsung's product manual and trouble shooting guidance. This did not diminish the odor. I then noticed brown and black spots on the bottom of the washer, as well as on the clothing after the washing load completed. I conducted additional research into the cause of the mold/mildew and discovered that this is a design defect in Samsung top load washers. Multiple consumers have reported this exact problem and complete lack of responsiveness from Samsung online. After conducting research, I removed the cap from the agitator plate on the bottom of the washer and observed black sludge. Please see attached picture. I also removed the agitator plate, per the guidance from other affected consumers online, and observed more sludge/mold/mildew. I cleaned the interior of the machine thoroughly and continued to run self clean and sanitize cycles, all to no avail. My husband and I purchased this expensive washer in the summer of 2016, after our son was born. He is now a toddler and this is a definite safety issue, given that his clothes, bedding and stuffed animals are being placed into a washer that is full of mold/mildew that cannot be eradicated. My son has now developed watery eyes, congestion/stuffy nose and other allergy symptoms that I fully believe are caused by this unsafe condition. Samsung is well aware of this design defect, yet does nothing proactively to protect consumers from their product.
justification: The incident involves a design defect causing mold/mildew in the washing machine, leading to allergy symptoms in a toddler, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
We purchased a Samsung top load washing machine in 2015. A recall for possible "forceful release of the top cover or other parts from the unit" was issued in 2016. We only received warning label overlays to place on the outside of the washer that warned not to use the high spin cycle for bedding and waterproof materials. A rebate of $150 credit toward the purchase of another Samsung machine was the only recourse. The retail value was close to $1,000.
Meanwhile, brown irregular flakes appeared in every wash load that had to be picked or shaken off each piece of laundry. The live chat Samsung representative said to use the "self clean" cycle but clothing stains kept appearing. We noticed over 50 posts on the Samsung community website that complained of the same problem, MOLD, in inaccessible areas of the machine. We wish to purchase a different, not Samsung, washer but have already spent hundreds of labor hours on cleaning. How can this company ignore health issues?
justification: The incident involves product defects and mold issues causing inconvenience and extra labor, but no direct injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I had problems with lights flickering in my home.After checking outlets and switches I went to the main entrance in the garage. I have a 200 amp siemens entrance panel with a100 amp amp sub feed to the house. As I was checking the incoming voltage on the main breaker , I noticed stray blue voltage coming from under the 100 amp sub feed breaker. incident_description: After several months of non-use, I walked over to the 2006 Heatilator propane fireplace in my lower level and turned on the switch that triggers the igniter.  Immediately the fireplace exploded.  The glass bent inward bending the frame on both sides.  Surprisingly, the glass did not shatter.  The access panels flew more than 10 feet into the rec room along with pieces of decorative lava rock.  I contacted Amerigas, our propane provider.  They came out and tested the valve.  It failed the pressure test.  I ordered and replaced the valve assembly with what appeared to be an exact replacement.  Amerigas returned and retested the new valve.  It passed the test and we have used the fireplace for a few minutes.  My concern is if the new valve fails in 10 years, will it blow my family up.  Not to mention could other people be at the same risk.  Had the old valve leaked at a faster rate, the entire basement may have exploded.  I have the old valve and would like to send it to you for testing and study.  I understand it could be simply a defective part, but it could be a flaw in the design or materials used.
justification: The incident involved an explosion with no reported injuries, but significant property damage and potential for severe harm.

incident_description: On March 27th, 2018 my husband and I purchased the Samsun top loader front washing machine. I originally noticed some small brown spots on our clothes after they were washed. They seemed to come out dirtier than they went into the washing machine. I then did every self cleaning imaginable. I did this several times and still found the small brown spots. I cleaned every nook and cranny I could find. Still spots... I then took off the cap on the agitator plate on the bottom of the machine and noticed a ton of black sludge! Then I did more research and found a community of people with the same issue (50 pages of complaints regarding this exact same Samsung product design flaw with nothing being done. One of them instructed to take off the agitator plate and clean under it. When I took it off I was completely disgusted! This is the washing machine where I wash my family's clothing, bedding, etc.! They are 7 months old and chew on everything! My husband and I have been having breathing problems in bed probably as a result of this mold. IÃÂm extremely disgusted by this. IÃÂve always done any regular maintenance of the machine that is recommended. I never use too much detergent, it's always HE, and I rarely if ever use fabric softener. Also, I have babied this product. I run the self clean often. So appalled by Samsung as it seems according to the community on their website that they do not back their products and blame the consumer for improper care. I just want them to take responsibility for this issue as it is not a consumer problem but a flaw in the design of their product.
justification: The incident involves a product defect causing health concerns (breathing problems) and hygiene issues, but no direct injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
My concern is with the 200 fluid ounce container used by Proctor & Gamble for their TIDE product.
The container is designed to lay on its side with the valve pointing down allowing the consumer to fill a measuring cup
with the fluid.
The previous design of this package was "FLAT" on the side that was intended to be facing down.
The new design has a contoured shape on the designated down side.
The problem is that the contour forces the consumer to position the container further out over the shelf in order to access the dispenser.
This location is dangerous because the contour acts like a cam and actually moves the 200 ounce container out far
enough to fall from the shelf.
This condition happened to me twice before I understood the problem. Luckily it missed me but its only a matter of time
before someone gets hurt.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw causing containers to fall, but no injury occurred, only potential risk.

incident_description: Heater started smoking and sparking
justification: The heater smoking and sparking is an incident with potential for harm but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung Electric Dryer model number DV50F9A8EVP/A2 and it exploded. On the 27 March 2018 at approximately 3100 hrs, I was using the Model Dryer mentioned above. After a 15 minute cycle on a medium heat setting it stop due to overheat; we clean the filter, behind the dryer, the exhaust hose and the escape shout and let it rest until the following day. On the 28 March of the current at approximate 1100 hrs, we started the to use the Dryer once more and after 10 minutes the washer exploded without warning. The explosion was loud enough to be heard at the Master Bedroom. When we approached the Laundry room it was full of black smoke. 
As a side note, ever since we had a recall from Samsung we decide that when we used the dryer not to have a big load, to have the fewer items in the it as possible and to always use the lowest setting and time possible in retrospect to the clothes being dried at the time.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and black smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We have 8 total Smoke Alarms, three are smoke & CO alarms combined. All are made by First Alert and are models BRK SC-9120B (combo) and BRK 9120B (Smoke only). We purchased a b rand new home in November 2016 and already 4 of the detectors have failed. I have changed batteries, checked the power supply yet they do not receive power from the mains and for all intents and purposes appear to be non-functioning.  As a retired arson investigator I find this totally unacceptable and a serious fire safety hazard.
justification: Multiple smoke alarms have failed, posing a serious fire safety hazard but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:

Home Depot refused to replace it.

Ryobi text messaging was a waste of time and they refused to warranty the defect!

Someone must make this recall known or people will be killed!

incident_description:
Washing Machine has been lately malfunctioning in a hazardous manner; During the spin cycle, it will bounce around violently and cannot be shut down. The lid is locked and cannot be opened, even if the unit is unplugged. If unplugged while running, it can cause an electric arc an possibly an electrocution and fire.
The excessive vibration can possibly cause injury or death to the housewife. Formerly, when this vibration occurs, the lid could be opened and the spin cycle would stop. the imbalance could be corrected by simply rearranging the clothes and restarting the machine.
If this dangerous condition is not corrected , sooner or later someone, probably a housewife, may be injured or killed and/ or the home and plumbing destroyed.
 I have tried to contact the Whirlpool and Roper people to no avail, but perhaps your office can reach the. I urge you to use to use your influence to remedy this potentially dangerous situation. A national Recall of all Whirlpool and Roper models as named in this complaint should be done, and all Whirlpool/ Roper customers be provided with safe machines free of charge.
justification: The washing machine's malfunction poses a risk of injury or death due to violent movement and potential electrocution, with a high likelihood given the described conditions.

incident_description: We had an electrical fire - our Rheem Performance Platinum water heater's control panel started an electrical fire.  I have numerous documents on it - fire department report, photos, etc. if needed.  It caused smoke damage and carpet damage to our home.  We are out a $2500 home insurance deductible due to the faulty appliance.  After the incident I searched online regarding the particular make and model of this water heater and found out there is a recall for this very same reason.  We were never notified by the manufacturer of this recall/defect.  I had sent in my warranty card the day we had the water heater installed, but still did not receive notification.  Notification could have prevent this fire at our house.  I have tried contacting Rheem several times and have not received a response.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recall indicating a known defect.

incident_description:
My partner bought a small bucket with 2 handles from the local Dollar Tree Store.  When she got home should told me that there was a bucket in the trunk of the car.  When I opened the trunk, I immediately noticed an strong odor unlike any smell that are common to cars.  It caused me to have an immediate response, like my olfactory senses had been overwhelmed.  I left the bucket on the front porch and went inside.  I felt like I was getting a headache.
  After 5 minutes or so still feeling some discomfort from the encounter.  The bucket was brought into the bathroom next to the bedroom.  I again could smell the odor emanating from the bucket.  My partner could not smell it.  I went outside for fresh air while she used it.  The bucket remained on porch outside, overnight.
  Today I checked her car trunk for the smell.  None present.  She had since moved the bucket to the side of the house for disposable but I have elected to report it.  I went and got my phone to photograph label and scan the barcode.  I moved bucket about 10' ft. to take pictures.  When done, I moved bucket back to side of house.  I then went and sat to use computer and I could smell an odor that was not in the room when I left.  I immediately went and washed my hands.  I feel currently as I type, that my taste buds and throat are having a reaction and start of headache.  BP 134/87 P 103.  I have a acute sense of smell so much so that I judge cooking times by smell among others.
justification: The incident caused discomfort and a mild physical reaction (headache, throat irritation) but no serious injury.

incident_description:
(09/30/2018) The submitter stated that his son was using the product for the first time to vacuum the carpet in his home. In under a minute, the son got an electrical shock. There was a shooting pain up his right arm. Also, the lights in the home flickered.

The son was taken to the emergency room at the Pottstown Hospital in Pottstown, PA. He was treated and released.

(10/01/2018) The submitted contacted the manufacturer to advise them of the incident. He was advised that the cause was static electricity because there is no metal in the handle. 

When the submitter asked the manufacturer about paying for his son's medical bill, he was advised that he would have to send the product back to them first.
justification: The son suffered an electrical shock requiring emergency room treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that her washing machine emits a foul odor, more so when she has to drain the unit. Upon inspection, the consumer noticed that both the outside and the inside of its tubing contain mold.

The consumer has contacted the Manufacturer several times and explained the situation; at first she was told not to use a lot of laundry detergent and that pods were not advised. The consumer indicates that her washing machine is used four to five times per week.

The consumer plans on keeping her washing machine for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

incident_description:

incident_description:
On September 20, 2018 I ran normal load of laundry in my Samsung washer, using the normal cycle I have used many times in the past. Nearing the apparent final medium spin cycle, I heard what seemed a very loud banging and shaking of the machine. I have never heard such a loud racket as this before. After a few minutes the cycle ended. When I went back to remove the clothes from the machine, I noticed a pool of water extending out into my basement area. I found it odd. I checked the back of the machine to see if a hose was loose or something was detached. There was nothing appearing to be disconnected at that time and nothing seemed wet on the floor under the washer. The following week I decided to see if the machine was broken by attempting to fill it with water. As soon as the machine began to fill an error message appeared and it stopped filling. But all the water came pouring out onto the floor and back into the basement. I called for service to the unit and was told that the pump was shredded due most likely due to the excessive vibrations that happened.
The machine was subject to a recall regarding the incidents of lid failure. I had that recall notice addressed by having repairs made to the lid on11/22/2016. I personally did not have a lid failure fortunately.
I have scheduled a new pump to be installed on the washer in the coming weeks, but now I am concerned about the future safety of using this washer again.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning washer causing water damage but no injury or death.

incident_description: My front load clothes washing machine continues to have the smell of mold and mildew after washing clothes.  I have tried bleach, does not work; Clorox wipes on the inside seal, does not work; dryer sheets, does not work; removing the seal and cleaning it, does not work; and finally replacing detergent with different brands, does not work.  I purchased the product based on the knowledge that it was the most effective resource for the loads of laundry I do every week with a family of 5.  However it has been nothing short of a nightmare.  Our youngest children have allergies that we continue to battle and we believe the washing machine is the source of problems.  It is not reasonable to expect a consumer product to be broken down and cleaned after each use to keep it safe from contamination.  Even with an extended warranty it is not enough to keep the product safe.
justification: The persistent mold and mildew issue is causing allergic reactions in children, indicating an injury-related severity, and the problem occurs frequently despite repeated cleaning attempts.

incident_description:
I purchased Samsung Top Load Washer only 3 years ago. The past several months I started to notice little brown spots on my cleaned clothes. It looks like someone through dirt into the washer. So, I then self cleaned it, which then made it worse!! I then realized how much mold and mildew was in their. It was ll over the bottom of my machine!!! We self washed it and cleaned 5 times just the last day or so. We took apart the machine to find the location of this mold and clean it. There was a ton of black sludge in the agitator in the bottom and all inside the walls of the basin. I decided to go online after finding this to do some research and see if others have had problems. To my surprise, disgust and disappointment I have learned this is a VERY VERY common issue with this machine that Samsung is not taking care of and is ignoring most consumers. There are hundreds and thousands of people that have wrote to Samsung and requested action.  Community blogs and social media pages have been created about this disgraceful product and the zero accountability by Samsung. 

I have a 13 month old daughter and I wash all her cloths, blankets and toys in this washer! This is a tremendous health hazard!!!! This mold and mildew can possibly be causing breathing and health issues!!!! I am sure it is also breading a ton of bacteria!! 

I have done all I can to rectify this issue! I have always done regular maintenance and self cleaning. I do not use too much detergent or any fabric softener. This is disgusting that Samsung is trying to blame the consumer. It is really a tremendous fraud! Samsung needs to take responsibility for this product being poorly designed and stop blaming the consumer! There are thousands of people with this issue!!!! DISGUSTING.
justification: The incident involves mold and mildew in the washer, posing a health hazard, but no direct injury or death is reported. The issue is described as very common, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

I ended up falling and twisting my ankle on the ground, which sent me to the [REDACTED] hospital, where they gave me some medicine and an ankle strap.  They said I did something to my ligaments and my ankle is actually still swollen and hurt from it and that was weeks ago.

incident_description: On June 30, 2017, we purchased a Samsung Washer and Dryer set from Home Depot.  While we elected not to buy the extended warranty, we didn't anticipate the lid of the washer machine breaking apart with pieces flying.  Around mid July, 2018, these lid of the washer machine started to bend and break apart with sharp plastic pieces flying.  The lid started breaking apart on the right back corner.  I've never seen anything like this in 58 years of being alive.  I contacted Samsung and Home Depot.  Both stated the warranty was out (by two weeks).  I ended up paying for a new lid (340.39) on August 3, 2018.  I was in the throws of some medical conditions and couldn't follow up.  Since I'm home recuperating, now is the time to do so.  I've done research this am prior to this report.  Two other consumers have written comments on the same problem.  This lid is dangerous.  I know Samsung has other recalls in effect and I do believe they are for some of the same problems.  Washer machine lids coming apart and sharp objects flying = dangerous.

incident_description: Rowenta Powerglide 2 Steam Iron.  I've had this product for about 4 years.  I had plugged it in and was in the process of ironing some clothes.  I had only been using it for about 5 minutes.  I rested it on the ironing board and all of a sudden sparks started coming out at the base of the iron by the wire and in less than 10 seconds, it burst into sizeable flames at that part of the iron.  The flames took seconds to burn a hole in the ironing board cover.  I immediately unplugged the iron and took it off the ironing board.  The flames died down once I unplugged the iron.  It was a frightening experience and frightening to think that if I'd left the ironing board for a few minutes when that happened I would have had a serious fire in my house.

I found that the HVAC unit malfunctioned igniting the combustibles where the heating elements were located. I spoke to the lone occupant of the unit. He told me he was chilled so he turned the unit to make it warmer when it started sparking and smoking. He called maintenance to report the unit. The unit then burst into flames. No one was injured.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant smoke but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. HVAC malfunctions leading to fires are possible but not common, warranting a likelihood of 3.

incident_description: Back in June I started noticing "dirt" on our clothes as they came out of the washer.  Light colored clothes were coming out with smears of "dirt" all over them.  A load of sheets were ruined and plenty of nice white blouses and dressy pants.  I thought maybe dirt or food had gotten into the washer and that was the cause.  After cleaning out the washer thoroughly however, this kept happening to new loads of wash.  I ran the Pure Cycle at least 6 times in 24 hours to try to clean it and the dirt/mold just keep coming out and collecting in the basin.  I also wiped out/cleaned/scrubbed the detergent pull outs and everything else I could get to inside the washer.  Since none of this was helping the problem, I contacted Samsung support looking for suggestions, or to have it repaired.  I never heard back from them.  In an attempt to problem solve this myself, I came upon the Samsung Community online and found a long thread (38 pages!) of people having the same problem as myself.  It was then that I realized this was a mold problem, not dirt!  Quite disturbing!!!  My son and husband have had terrible "allergies" lately and my son recently had to start using a preventative inhaler.  I'm sure having his clothes/sheets/towels/everything washed in mold for who knows how long contributed to that problem!  After finding the community, and since I still hadn't heard a word from Samsung, and couldn't get ahold of them I took the bottom of the basin out and everything was caked in mold and build up (see pictures)!  We thoroughly scrubbed everything off that we could get to under the basin, and in the hose and soaked it all in bleach, but I cannot be sure it's not hiding somewhere else that we couldn't see or reach.  This seems to only be a temporary fix, as it will likely build up again over time since you can hear the water sitting under the drum.  We have always used the proper HE detergent on this machine and it is very disappointing that after only a few years we will need to purchase another new washing machine.  We spent a lot of money on this machine and it's going to have to be trash, unless Samsung can fix it!
justification: The incident involves mold contamination in the washing machine leading to health issues like allergies and the need for a preventative inhaler, indicating injury.

incident_description:
Prior to getting sick I was exercising 6 - 7 days a week; teaching at least 4 [REDACTED] classes a week and swimming twice a week. I was growing my business and hired a couple of instructors. Plus I was involved in a project for filming for [REDACTED]. I was healthy and fit and rarely got sick. If I did get sick, symptoms were mild and usually only lasted a couple of days. But it all changed after we got our new hardwood floors placed with Glitsa Swedish Finish by a local hardwood floor company (Goss Floors).

Because there were multiple other stressors occurring, it took awhile to figure out why I wasn't getting better. After what initially seemed to be a cold continued to manifest with worsening fatigue and lung pain, I was diagnosed with reactivation of EBV (mono virus). I thought maybe I had done too much with multiple work projects as well as renovating the upstairs of our home and dealing with a cat who had been sick for months. I started to question whether I had the capacity to do a large scale project and work alongside well-known professionals.

My illness was initially blamed on pneumonia, but even after antibiotics, normal lab results except for EBV, I felt something was wrong. The one thing that concerned me was that my lung capacity when tested with an Incentive Spirometer was abnormal. Though it was blamed on inflammation. But what was causing the inflammation? Pneumonia continued to be ruled out by multiple providers. And yes, there was the reactivation of EBV, but something else seemed wrong. The final straw was waking up early on a Monday morning and having difficulty breathing. I felt I couldn't take a full deep breath and started getting anxious. After an hour of not being able to sleep and struggling with breathing, I had my husband take me to the ER. However, my vital signs were stable and since my previous lab work and Chest X-ray were normal, the doctor didn't know what else to do. I remember starting to cry, because I knew something was wrong, but I wasn't getting the answers I needed. He sent me home with a prescription for steroids and antibiotics (though he thought infection was unlikely the cause).

When we returned home from the ER, I noticed the floors seemed to be smelling more. I didn't think further about it and just went back to bed. However, the next day I started doing more research trying to figure out what was going on and realized the worsening of symptoms was occurring because the floors were off-gassing more with the rise in temperatures. After talking with a couple of providers they confirmed that this was the likely cause of my symptoms. I moved outside and started sleeping in a tent (inside our tipi) and started spending most of my time outdoors. I would only go inside to shower, grab clothes, or get some food. While my symptoms didn't go away, they stopped getting worse (which was huge). Then I started focusing on ways to help heal from the damage caused from the Glitsa Swedish finish which we later found out contained formaldehyde. Two months after I began having symptoms which I now know was from formaldehyde, we finally discovered the cause. When I reflected back I realized the first symptoms I experienced were difficulty sleeping, nausea, poor appetite, and headaches. 

We were never told about the risks of this finish by Goss flooring company or that it wasn't recommended to be used around young children. My daughter who is 6 years old was getting headaches and we now know why. My 9 year old son was having stomach aches and my husband was having increasing muscle pain (which he blamed on all the labor he had been doing). Our family then moved outside into our tipi for the summer and limited our time upstairs. We even had a sitter come to our house for a day and she was spending some time upstairs cleaning up. She noticed chest tightness and the next day was completely exhausted.  Over 3 months after our floors were placed, I bought a detector to monitor formaldehyde levels and discovered that the levels were above the WHO recommendations. We continued to track levels and eventually towards mid-August they started decreasing. However, my daughter's room was staying the same and we realized it was from her new furniture. We cleared out her new furniture and bought some used furniture and the levels in her dropped significantly.

Five months after this all began, I continue to work on healing the damage that occurred from my body. While we ate fairly healthy before, we have drastically changed our diet. I mainly eat fruits and vegetables and a low-fat diet to eliminate foods that can worsen my symptoms. While I am teaching 4 [REDACTED] classes a week, there are days where I definitely need to modify more. I am not able to swim at this time as it is a lot of work on my body and I need to conserve my energy. I had to cut back a lot on my business during this time and am still limited on my ability to market and grow my business. Family activities are generally limited based on my energy. I've actually just hired a "mother's helper" to come in the home a couple of times a week to relieve some of the burden from my husband who has had to pick up a lot more on the household duties.

I am concerned that a product that is not allowed to be sold in 18 other states is allowed to be sold and used in Washington. I can't help but ask how many others have gotten a chronic illness from Glitsa Swedish Finish and not even know it. Formaldehyde is known to cause health issues by the CDC, yet consumers are not required to be informed about this risks of this product. We were told it would be safe to move back into our home 3 days after the product was applied.
justification: The incident describes multiple health issues including reactivation of EBV, lung pain, and formaldehyde exposure leading to chronic symptoms, which qualifies as an injury.

So I brought the ole ladder around the house, opened it out all the way straight and ensured the clips locked in place, and then I extended the telescoping on each side equally to achieve the desired height I needed. I got almost to the top of the ladder as I began to feel something give and then completely release. The aluminum metal broke and bended at one of the ends where the telescoping part comes out. It's kinda hard to explain through a message so I took pictures. 

I was lucky that I was able to fall over to the right side where there was nothing in the way like the wooden fence on my left. To be honest, I didn't feel the missing chunk at all due to the adrenaline; it wasn't until I realized I had gotten blood all over my pants that I looked and saw my thumb.

I feel relatively lucky that this is all the injury I sustained. Maybe I'll feel a little bruised tomorrow but at least I'm not dead. Also, I do want you to know that I'm a 220lb 6'3" average sized male, I did not come close to the 375lb weight limit.

incident_description:
In 2015, my clients purchased a pack of Safety 1st Cabinet & Drawer Latches from Lowes to
prevent their one-year old daughter from having access to their knife drawer. The product was
installed as was specified in the instruction manual, and at no point did the daughter ever see
her parents successfully unlock the latch and gain access to the drawer. Moreover, at no point
did the parents have any reason to believe that their daughter had reached an age that she could
successfully disengage the latch on her own. On December 8, 2017, after being locked out of her
older sister's room, the daughter - who at this time was three years old - attempted to access
the knife drawer in order to cut a piece of tape in hopes that she could lock her older sister in
her room from the outside. Her parents merely stepped away for a few seconds in order to get
the telephone that was ringing. Although she had never witnessed anyone ever disengage the
Safety 1st cabinet & drawer latch, she was able to easily disengage the product by using minimal
force to depress the latch. Once she gained access, she attempted to cut the tape with the knife,
but overcompensated the amount of force necessary to cut the tape, and accidentally stabbed
her right eye with the knife. The three-year-old daughter was then flown to the hospital where
she underwent emergency surgery to save her right eye. Months later, the daughter is still unable
to see out of her right eye. She has undergone multiple surgeries and will continue to undergo
surgeries in the future. There is a chance that the daughter will never regain vision in her right
eye, and there remains the possibility that her eye may need to be removed.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury to the child's eye, requiring multiple surgeries with potential permanent vision loss, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
Fire department was dispatched for an activated smoke alarm and found a smoke alarm that had failed internally and nearly caused a fire which triggered the alarm so they contacted my office to make me aware.

I met the home owner the next day, he and his family are hearing impaired so they have BRK 100S strobe alarms throughout their single family home. All are hardwired and interconnected.  He advised the alarms went off and when he was not able to reset them he began investigating. Upon opening a bedroom door he encountered an odor of burning and some smoke around said alarm.  The fire department arrived and removed the device from the ceiling.  It was hot to the touch and had some obvious melting and discoloration so they sent me a photo and contacted me.

While meeting with the owner I took photos of the smoke alarm, the mounting bracket, and the electric box it was wired from.  The electric box showed no signs of damage or failure.  The only visible damage was to the internal components of the smoke alarm.  I asked the owner if I could have the alarm to send it to CPSC for further evaluation.  He said he called BRK Electronics and they were shipping him a new one free of charge but they too requested the alarm.  I advised him that I was concerned that they may get the alarm and never report the problem.  He agreed to let me take possession of which I did.  

My plan was to give it to [REDACTED] at our next state fire marshal's meeting but I learned today he will not be attending that meeting but he asked that I submit this report.
justification: The smoke alarm failed internally, causing smoke and a burning odor, but no injuries or deaths occurred.
