incident_description:
While away for a weekend trip, a family member found the gas (propane) fireplace insert in our living room to be on with full flame and two items near the fireplace where melted or scorched due to the high heat.  Fireplace had been turned off, by remote control, since February 2018 and pilot light was also turned off.  Family member was advised on how to shut the fireplace down completely and removed the burning items from the house.  Damage is contained to approximately $300 including the cleaning of curtains, brick and other items in the living room.  The installer of the insert, Country Side Stove and Chimney will be inspecting insert and chimney for any defects or damage.  The insert has been installed since 2012.  Upon our return home I found the batteries on the remote control to be exhausted and no display was present on the remote's digital screen.  When last used, the fireplace was in manual mode (not controlled by thermostat) and the remote control was completely turned off.

A previous incident also occurred in November of 2017  when I returned home from work and entered an extremely hot living room and the fireplace insert was on with full flame.  No items were located near the fireplace at that time as it was during the season when we would begin to use the insert.  At that time, the batteries in the remote control were also exhausted and the pilot was not turned on.

During both occasions, the brick surrounded the fireplace and the living was much hotter than when we actually use the fireplace.

Had I not returned home, or had not the family member checked on our home, I believe that a fire would of have started due to the intense heat generated by insert when it self-ignited while turned off.  The brick surrounding the fireplace remained hot for almost 10 hours after the fire was turned off.  A very dangerous condition exists for users of the fireplace insert.  

To clarify the remote control, it can be left on a thermostat mode in which the insert regulates itself based upon the room temperature that the user sets.  When in this mode, the temperature can be seen on the LED screen on the remote.  As we do not heat our home with the fireplace, we have never used this mode and kept the remote on manual mode.  This way we can control the size of the flame, which we kept minimal for looks only and not heating purposes.  For the past several months, since we last used the insert, there has no been no display on the remote control, the remote was turned off and we did not find any fire in the insert.

The fireplace insert in question is a Travis Industries Avalon insert model 34 DVL GS.  I have not made any contact with the manufacture yet, only the installer who will be sending a technician out to examine and inspect the insert.

I believe this to be a great danger for the potential of fire, property loss and the the loss of a life.  I have turned of the propane leading to the fireplace to limit the danger our family and home.
justification: The incident caused property damage and posed a significant fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I use this heavy-duty router in my shop.  It is not used frequently, but is required for special radii in wood projects and plastic projects.  It is used in an aluminum router table, the router is also aluminum cast.  Last week when inspecting the router and planning to put a shorter cord set on it, I found degraded power wires with cracking wire jackets.  These were found on both the ground and power wires from the plug all the way to the internal switch block.  The wire jackets were falling off which meant that any slight contact would have created a serious short on the machine and since it is not a grounded machine by design, it could have been a very serious issue.  The router is kept inside in a cabinet, never subjected to the outside or misuse.  It still looks brand new, but may have been purchased approximately ten years ago by myself.

Porter Cable contacted me to take it to a repair facility if it is still under warranty.  This is not acceptable and it should have been replaced and shipped back to the manufacturer for inspection.  Note that PC has also sent me a new insulated handle a few years ago to handle any potential shocks as a result of short circuit - again, I'm just curious if this was related.
justification: Degraded power wires with cracking jackets were found, posing a serious short risk, but no incident or injury occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased the Generac 2800PSI power washer from [REDACTED] warehouse store in November, 2016.  

It has been used to clean my outside deck(approx.10'X40') twice since I purchased it.  The length of time I used it is approx 8-10 hours.

I cranked it up on or about May 15, 2018 to wash my deck.  After about 2 hours the spray started to weaken.  
I turned it off to check things out and the first thing I checked was for adequate oil in the crankcase.  Upon loosening the filler plug to the crankcase, oil started to gush out so I screwed the plug down so I wouldn't get any more oil on my deck.  

I got a frying pan and put it under the unit and unplugged the oil filler plug.  More than one cup of fluid gushed out and into the pan.  It had a strong odor of gas and oil.  To confirm there was gas in the oil I took a candle lighter and put the flame to the frying pan.  The oil/gas mixture flamed confirming there was gas in the oil.

I called both the manufacturer and the warranty company to report the problem.  I was told to take it to 
Wainwright Lawn Equipment, 
10304 Cathell Road, Berlin, Md. 21811
410-641-2646.

[REDACTED] told me the problem is, "the damn gas/ethenal mixture is the problem where it deteriorates the gaskets in the fuel system allowing the gas to leak into the cylinder chamber where the gas will leak past the piston rings into the crankcase.

He in essence could not fix it because of the gas but he did "test troubleshoot, cleaned fuel system, cleaned carberator and changed oil" as written on the work order presented to me when I picked it up.

Without any definitive repair or correction I now have a gas powered piece of equipment that I will not use for fear of an explosion resulting in possible injury to myself and others or fire damage to my property.

Contacting the factory their attitude seemed to focus on, "this problem has not been reported by others", to, "take it to an authorized dealer to have it checked out".  NOTE: I did take it to an authorized dealer.

It is my opinion that some day, someone is going to be hurt by this piece of equipment.

Final note: I have a gas powered snow blower, leaf blower, trimmer and lawn mower and this issue of the gas eating away at the gaskets is/has not been a problem with any of this other equipment, ever!!

Regards,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning power washer with potential safety risks, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

There was a code on the digital screen, "dc". I checked the user manual and it said it was due to an uneven load. I checked the load and it did not appear to be uneven. I spoke with Samsung and they will replace the top with more secure latches, but I dont believe that it corrects the issue as to why the tops of the machines were coming off so violently.

incident_description:
Hi, 

I hope you are doing well. I wanted to write to you about the Molekule air "purifier" product that was recently approved for sale in CA. 

I wanted to reach out to you to let you know that there are many customers out there who have had a fairly negative experience with their device. The main concern being that the device continues to emit a foul odor / VOCs for many weeks after purchase. The company literature says that the unit is expected to off-gas for 24-48 hours. However, many of their customers (myself included) noted that the smell actually didn't go away for weeks. The problem is not just the smell, but the uncertainty around what actually is being emitted by the unit and whether it is harmful in any way.

The Company refuses to provide any info about why there is smell or whether there is any danger in inhaling that air. I, for one, can speak from experience that every time I entered the room where we were running the device I would break into incessant coughing. So there is something wrong in the gases being emitted from the unit but I am not sure what it is and dont have the means to test.

There have been folks who have been enterprising enough to do their own home tests. Many have found that Molekule has almost no impact on VOCs. In fact here is a link to a thread on forum, where a user "[REDACTED]" posts about his experience of thoroughly testing the unit and finding that it doesn't work. He then got in touch with Molekule and got their tech team to use sophisticated equipment to test his unit and they concurred with him that somehow his unit was defective. 

1: (http://hvac-talk.com/vbb/showthread.php?2254881-MoleKule-Update
"The technical folks at MoleKule took an active interest and contacted me in short order. I've been working with them for the last couple of weeks. After extensive testing at their facility, including Gas Chromatography (the gold standard for measuring VOCs) they determined my catalyst was defective")

2: (http://hvac-talk.com/vbb/showthread.php?2272161-Latest-MoleKule-Austin-Air-Test
Test 1:
At 70^F ~45RH with VOC levels ~300 ppb the 
MoleKule didn't register a significant change.
Austin Air showed a decrease of about 15 - 28%. I tested in a couple of rooms.

Test 2:
Same as above but added a small bowl of [REDACTED] equidistant from both devices.
MoleKule registered ~15% decrease.
Austin Air registered ~ 20 - 30 % decrease.

Test 3:
Same as test 1 except increase heat to ~ 80 - 82 ^F
Molekule didn't register a significant change.  )

This is most concerning to me and should be to CPSC too, and that is why I wanted to point it out to you. There was and is no indicator on the unit or the mobile app to detect whether the unit is working or defective. Most consumers aren't going to go to the lengths that [REDACTED] went to test their unit. So Molekule could very well be selling defective units without any oversight under the garb of being approved to sell these units.

I reached out to CARB earlier and they said they had no authority over them and they suggested I reach out to you instead. I have since returned my unit. 

Thanks,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a foul odor and potential VOC emissions causing coughing, indicating a health impact but no severe injury or death.

incident_description:
On August 3, 2018,  at about 3:45 PM we were driving back from a hike in the Valles Caldera National Monument on High 4 near Los Alamos, N.M. when my wife heard a "pop" in the rear of our SUV and our vehicle immediately filled with dense white smoke. My wife yelled "stop the car and everybody get out". I was driving and thought the vehicle had caught on fire. Our son, my wife and grandchildren got out of the stopped vehicle immediately. Our son raced to the back of the SUV and opened the rear door which released a cloud of white smoke and one of our dogs. The other had jumped over two rows of seats and out the front passenger door. Our son saw the smoking Micro-Start XP-10 on the floor in the back of the SUV and grabbed a strap on it and threw it from the vehicle to the ground. It was still smoking. We had pulled over on this two lane road through the forest and were fearful the Micro-Start XP-10 might start a fire. We called the fire department and asked for help. They and the police arrived to direct traffic and inspect our vehicle and the "Jump-Starter". We had thrown it into our emptied cooler on ice packs and covered it with water. The firemen determined it was out and no longer a fire hazard then told us the smoke from the Lithium Ion battery was toxic. He suggested we monitor our dogs as they were close to the source longest and if they became sick we should seek care for them and ourselves. The firemen suggested we have the interior of the vehicle scrubbed out and replace the air conditioning unit air filters after we got home. We notified Antigravity Batteries by phone and left a V.M. about the episode and also sent an e-mail the night of August 3rd. They responded via e-mail August 6th and answered my phone call to the warranty desk. They e-mailed a Micro-Start Warranty Claim Form which we completed with all the requested information. We provided receipts for the expense of cleaning the SUV interior and the A/C Filter replacement. We have not shown any ill effects to the smoke nor have our dogs. 
The initial moving smoke filled vehicle and emergency exit from it could have resulted in more serious consequences.
justification: The incident involved a smoking lithium-ion battery in a vehicle, causing dense smoke and an emergency exit, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a VIGO frameless shower stall #VG6051STCL48WR from Lowe's (Home Depot also sells these, which is where I originally saw it on display) two years ago.  A licensed and insured contractor installed the unit while following directions and using all necessary parts.  While I purchased the 36x48 size, but there are multiple sizes and models that I'm confident have this same, very serious, and dangerous, issue.

The issue is that Vigo has a new design where they have eliminated two of the metal brackets on one side of the shower (attaching pictures to show), which leaves only 2 very tiny screws on the bar and one flimsy metal piece at the bottom, to hold an 80 pound glass panel.  These are absolutely not capable of holding anywhere near 80 pounds. 

The end result is that my stationary glass panel fell- very fortunately my children were not in the bathroom, as it broke a tile AND cracked the granite countertop- I know for 100% certain that if one of my children had been standing in the bathroom (as they often are), it would have killed them.  I have never been more certain of anything in my life.  To be clear- this ONE panel is 80 pounds- not the entire shower.

I contacted Vigo Industries, during the first call the customer service rep indicated that the NEW version has two less brackets, and that he could send me the "old version" panel which has the holes drilled to screw in the brackets to the wall (and the two extra brackets).  

After several days of not hearing back, I called to check the status and the story has completely changed, he connected me to a manager who first insisted we used a different base than what the kit came with (patently untrue, this shower was an entire kit), then they accused of using different  screws, not true, then said not installed properly- we had a licensed and insured contractor install.  At the end of the day- these are all distractions from the truth- Vigo Industries has reduced costs  by no longer drilling the holes in one of the panels, and providing two less brackets.  I would have paid $100, $200, or more for a safe shower.

I no longer feel comfortable with this shower and will be writing to Lowe's for resolution.  My reason for writing to your organization is in hopes to protect future customers from this same issue, and to hopefully have the opportunity to warn other customers.  I urge you to review this product's safety issue, and I strongly recommend that anyone who has purchased this shower be given an option to receive some type of bracket to hold this 80 pound panel in place- I realize that Vigo is never going to recall and provide a whole new panel with holes drilled, but there has to be some type of bracket that will make this shower safe.

Again, considering the weight of this glass and the fact that it cracked tile and damaged a strong granite countertop- I am 100% certain that my child would have died if she had been in the bathroom on the day that this fell.  It is very scary, and eventually someone is going to be seriously injured or killed by one of these showers.
justification: The incident involved a heavy glass panel falling, causing property damage but no injuries, though the potential for severe injury or death is high if someone had been present.

Our stovetop is a glass stovetop with touch controls.  The cat stood on it and turn on a burned to high that had a silicone hot plate on it and a bread knife with a wooden handle.  My wife and I were outside when the cat did this.  We came in the house and it was filled with smoke throughout.  Neither of the 2 Nest Protects detected smoke nor were alarming.  If we hadn't come in when we did, the whole house could have burned down.

I contacted Nest Support the next day and were concerned to hear it and said they were escalating to their product safety group.  After a week of no follow up I called today.  I want to understand how 2 products could have failed.  The support tech told me they were over a year old and may not work. What?  Throw them away after a year?  I have requested this again be escalated as the response is not acceptable.

If these are in fact not detecting smoke and are giving people a false sense of security, consumers need to be informed.

incident_description: We purchased a Kenmore (Sears) Elite Large model Washing Machine in November 2017 with full extended warranty.  On May 14, 2018 after a loud "thumping" sound was heard,  loud "explosion" type sound occurred: the lid of this washer made of glass had shattered suddenly and violently for no apparent reason.  The lid, made of a type of safety glass had blown slivers of glass all over our laundry room, and inside the bowl of the washer itself.  The majority of the glass remained in the frame, cracked into hundreds of pieces.  I called Sears service  and initially they did not want to "cover" the incident under warranty, essentially claiming we had somehow dropped something on the lid or otherwise negligently caused the breakage, a completely incorrect assumption.  After insistence that they do something to honor the warranty they agreed to send a serviceman to inspect the washer.  He came out the next day.  His assessment was that the washer was exhibiting a problem he characterized as a "Manufacture's Design Defect" and remarked that he had encountered this problem two months previously on the same model washer.  He added that the lid latching mechanism, both the mechanical elements and/or electronic control board and associated electronics were at fault and had caused the explosive shattering of the glass by stressing the metal frame of the lid at the time of breakage.  He also reported that he had ordered a full set of components to replace the various latching elements  and that DURING his installation of the new control board that same thing happened--the lid exploded right under his face, and but for his wearing of glasses would have possibly showered glass into his eyes.  He ordered the same exact replacement part for our machine as he explained that Sears had no "fix" or recall for this machine at this time and he had no other options for the repair of the machine.  He provide me with his business card which also had a phone number for a "Resolution Hotline" if, as the card stated:  "Concerns about your service call today?"  He also told me the parts were on back order with no delivery date predicted at this time.  As my wife and I are both busy professional people we need our washer, and I called the "resolution hotline" where I received NO help.  I called a second number the serviceman had written on the card which is the phone number listed on the "Master Protection Agreement" to request replacement of a unit due to the "lemon" clause of the MPA, but only after 3 separate incidents requiring service within 1 continuous year, upon the fourth incident requiring repair.  I called this number and the representative refused to replace the machine due to dangerous design problems, and in fact denied that the warranty clearly states one "continuous' year of three incidents...this was my SECOND INCIDENT from November 2017.  She insisted the agreement only provided for 4 service calls within one CALENDAR year and as such she denied my request for a refund or replacement of the machine.  I have tried twice more to get help from Sears and the latest person told me on May 20 or thereabouts that an Escalation Response Team for Safety would call me in two days.   This was a total lie, as I found out today after calling and insisting on talking to a second supervisor who guardedly admitted that they have no Sears Safety Team, and that the phone number she would provide me was the phone for YOUR AGENCY of the US Government!  In other words Sears has refused categorically any responsibility for this excessively dangerous product at this time.
justification: The incident involved a violent shattering of the washing machine lid, posing a significant risk of injury, though no actual injuries were reported in this specific case.

incident_description:
I purchased a GE clothes washer on 01/31/2017 from The Home Depot.  Model Number:  GTW680BSJWS.  It was delivered new to my home on approximately 02/07/2017.  I began to experience some issues with the washer including increasing noise and continuous dripping water from the inlet valves.  I had requested service through GE Appliances service scheduling website on 02/10/2018.  Unfortunately there were some delays in scheduling with an authorized servicer.  A GE authorized service provider came to my home on 03/05/2018 and performed no repairs, despite the visible dripping of water and noise issues as described.  I continued to use the washing machine after this service visit date.  I had last used the washing machine the afternoon of 04/10/2018.  The washing machine sat unused and powered off in my main floor laundry room, with the lid open, for more than 36-hours.  I awoke the morning of 04/12/2018 to the sound of the washing machine motor running and the display panel powered on.  None of the buttons on the display panel worked and the only action that stopped the machine was to unplug it.  My husband and I are the only people in the home and the washing machine was found to be running in the early morning hours with neither of us having used it in more than 36-hours.  After this incident, the washing machine remained unplugged, and unused, until a GE Appliances Authorized servicer could come and attempt to repair it.  Any attempts to plug it back in resulted in the same unstoppable motor running and non-functioning control panel.  Therefore, for our safety and that of our home, the machine remained unplugged.  Another repair service request was submitted to GE Appliances on 04/12/2018.  The GE Appliances Authorized Servicer came to my home on 04/26/2018 and replaced the failed controller, water valve, and gear case.  
Because the washing machine motor and control panel started without any human intervention and because the only way to stop it was to unplug it, this posed a serious fire hazard to my home.  I am relieved that I was home when it happened, and woke up to hear it; however, I am frightened to think of the outcome had no one been home to unplug it.  I have since found internet message boards and other online resources describing these same problems in other GE washers of the same model. Consequently, even though the above noted repairs have been made, I am afraid that the same problem could reoccur.  I now unplug the washing machine or switch off the power at the wall outlet, in addition to the power button on the washer itself, when the washing machine is unattended.
justification: The washing machine malfunctioned without human intervention, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

I called Electrolux and informed them of what was happening. they said my warranty had just expired, however all parts would be included but not the labor. They sent their certified Electrolux repair company. They proceeded to take apart my entire dryer. I was supervising as they were still asking questions. When they finished removing all of the outside casing of the dryer they came across with the motor and blower wheel. the blower wheel was completely full of lint. They proceeded to comment that they had never seen that particular design and cleaned out the blower wheel, they could not figure out what caused it. No parts were replaced. After a hefty $300 invoice, I contacted Electrolux explained everything that was said and they sent me a new lint holder, they seemed to know that this was an issue. I emphasized that this was a fire hazard especially considering that it is a gas dryer. A few months later I noticed that the blower wheel which is sort of visible from the lint holder is full again. I contacted Electrolux they basically told me to have someone service it and they could not do anything about it. I have had dryers prior to this and never had a problem. This is a severe Fire HAZARD, and they are not willing to do anything about it.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard due to lint accumulation in a gas dryer, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
The product was included in Recall Release #13-073- LG Recall Top-Loading Washing Machines Due to Risk of Injury

The consumer stated that a repairmen came out to do the recall repair in 2013 but the problem was not fixed.

(6/22/2018) The consumer stated that his wife was washing his son's full size sheet and a light blanket in the machine. During the spin cycle ( he's not sure which spin cycle) the machine became unbalanced. It sounded like an explosion. The top of the machine came completely off and put a hole in the wall. The drum punched a hole in the back of the machine. 

The machine continued to spin. The consumer had to hit the power button to turn the unit off.

(06/22/2018) The consumer contacted the Kenmore Recall center. He was advised that the issue would be turned over to Product Safety and he would be contacted in three business days.

(06/27/2018) After not hearing from anyone, the consumer contacted Kenmore and was advised to wait for a call from the Repair Team.

(07/02/2018) The consumer went to the Sears store in his area. He was given a number to call (department unknown). When he called the number he was advised that the product was not under warranty. The consumer was transferred to another department. He was advised that a repair technician would be out on July 17 to determine if the machine can be repaired or replaced.

The consumer stated that he does not know what to do at this point.
justification: The incident involved a washing machine malfunction causing significant damage but no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents (6927 of 10427).

incident_description:
Jack stand locking mechanism failed. The release lever is supposed to require significant force to move while under tension. The release on TWO of these jack stands can become disengaged by lightly touching it.

The release lever was touched with similar force to tapping someone on the shoulder to get their attention. This caused the extension bar to slip off the lock and fall. Luckily I had the car supported with redundant stands so I was not seriously injured.

After this I compared and tested the stands my applying force to the saddle with my hand and gently touching the release mechanism. On my "good" set of stands from a different manufacture, the release lever would not move, even when significant force was applied. On the bad set of stands I barely touched the lever and the locking mechanism gave out so abruptly that I damaged my finger from the extension falling on it.

I removed the extension bar from the base of the stand and inspected it. It appeared the teeth on the extension bar were poorly manufactured and could easily slip off the lock.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (damaged finger) due to the failure of the jack stand locking mechanism, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the poor manufacturing of the stands.

incident_description:
A Vornado VH101 Personal Vortex electric space heater was purchased for me on Amazon.com 5 years and 5 months ago on November 27, 2012. I use it almost 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, however, because of a situation that caused me concern, I try very hard never to leave the unit running unattended without first turning off the heat.

1. When the unit tips forward onto its face, a safety switch located on the bottom always cuts the power as expected. This safety feature has never failed me.

2. When an object is placed too close, restricting the air flow, a thermal switch located inside cuts the power, and the power is not restored until the unit has sufficiently cooled. As far as I can tell, this safety feature appears to work consistently as well.

3. However, one day, after having owned this heater for approximately three to four years, the smell of burning plastic caught my attention, and I suddenly realized that the fan had stopped turning. I quickly turned off the unit which had become very hot to the touch. I later took the unit apart, lubricated the motor shaft and continued to use the unit. Within a year, the same situation occurred again. Since then, I have learned to continuously pay close attention to the sound of the fan, and whenever I hear it slowing down, I lubricate the motor shaft. I have not had any problems with the unit since. (Note: During both occurrences, there were no nearby objects obstructing air flow.)
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing overheating and a burning smell, but no injury occurred. The issue was resolved by user intervention and maintenance.

I then saw an another ENT who looked at the Yale CT (the 1st one) which clearly showed the wire bristle and from there 3 surgerys ensued and were all unsuccessful at removing the wire bristle.

6-19-18 was the 1st of 3 surgeries and as of today, I am slowly recovering but still have te bristle lodged in my throat; and I am still looking for someone who can help me.
Products are recalled for being significantly less of a danger to the public than these steel-bristled grill brushes.  

These brushes NEED TO BE REMOVED FROM THE MARKET!

If you have any information on the  physician who successfully removed the bristle from the base of the patient's tongue (from the case reported in 2011), please contact me!
Thank you so much for your attention to this matter.
justification: The incident resulted in a lodged grill bristle causing severe pain, multiple surgeries, and lasting physical impairments, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung top load washing machine (model number WA52M7750AW/A4) one year ago. After 6 months I noticed small black specks all over a washed load of laundry. At first I thought that my kids were putting dirt in their pockets. Recently the specks covering a fresh load of laundry have been dime size and larger. My husband and I have been trying to figure out what it is. I decided to do an online search and found a large group of people all having the same problem and they said it is mold. They complained of reaching out to Samsung and getting no help. Several of them suggested taking off the agitator plate and removing the pulsator so that the mold could be cleaned off of all the internal parts. I called for a technician to help me remove the parts and I have attached images of what we found. I scrubbed all of the parts that I could reach with a scrubber, toothbrush and q-tips. Although it was impossible to remove all of the mold I did clean off a lot of it. incident_description:
Several years ago I purchased a three outlet plug-in electrical adaptor from Home Depot.  This device is also known as a "current tap".  After using it for years, with various power tools, the male ground prong came out of the adaptor while I was unplugging it.   Later, while looking into the empty hole left by the missing ground prong, I noticed that there was no metal in there, only plastic.  In other words, the adaptor as manufactured, never had any connection/continuity between the male ground prong and the three female outlet grounds.  I also probe tested this device with a multi-meter and thereby confirmed the absence of any grounding paths through the adaptor.  If any of my power tools had developed a ground fault while plugged into this adaptor, there would have been no protection against the resultant shock hazard.   No doubt, there are more of these defective adaptors out there.  And no doubt the people using them, like me in years past, have no clue about the hidden danger.

The adaptor is a LITESUN Model LT-8A.  Additional identification embossed on the plastic adaptor body states E241182 Made In China.   There is also an attached sticker that says UL Listed Current Tap No. AM653714  L115040H3 copyright 2013 UL LLC.
justification: The incident describes a defective electrical adaptor that could have led to a shock hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

This failure (cord breakage and arcing) was observed in a "Rival" brand "Steam Iron" model:ES280 which was sold through Walmart stores.. but any clothes iron with this "360ÃÂ° Pivoting Cord" design will have this flaw. A quick survey online of clothes irons for sale on [REDACTED].com and Walmart.com show many clothes irons use this "360ÃÂ° Pivoting Cord" design.

When using clothes iron in a normal manner the design feature described as a "360ÃÂ° Pivoting Cord" concentrates the stresses on the electrical cord onto a portion of the cord hidden within the clothes irons housing. Normal use repeatedly alternates flexing a narrow radius bend on the cord in one location (hidden inside the housing) until failure occurs.

ETL (Intertek), 3025655, actually put their mark on this product and stated it conforms to UL STD.UL60335-1&-2-3.

How could ETL put their mark on any clothes iron with "360ÃÂ° Pivoting Cord - Easy ironing at any angle the smooth-moving pivot cord never gets in your way"? This is not a stress relief component but one that concentrates the stress/bending to a small portion of the electrical cord, a portion which is hidden inside the housing so cord fatigue/failure/arcing is not apparent to the consumer (well, not until the arcing glows through the housing and/or smoke/fire appears.) Couple that with the guillotine-like clamp used to hold the wire in place and you have a line of products that are designed to fail.  I believe any reasonable engineer (electrical/mechanical) or electrician/technician would immediately flag this design as flawed. I can't comprehend how a testing laboratory could put their mark on any product incorporating this design feature as its shortcomings are immediately apparent to anyone who examines it.
justification: The description indicates a design flaw leading to cord breakage and arcing, which can cause smoke or fire, posing a risk of injury or property damage.

justification: The heater is malfunctioning with visible soot, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: Excessive shaking and vibrating with uneven loads. Hoses leak due to vibration. Water on floor. Been doing this a long time, just noticed recall and to report.
justification: Excessive shaking and leaking hoses indicate an incident with potential for injury, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
DeLonghi TRH0715 Oil-Filled electric radiator Type KH770715P  Serial 08218514

I purchased the heater on Amazon on September 7, 2017. It worked satisfactorily through the winter.
On Saturday June 23, 2018 the plug burst into sparks and flames, though the unit was turned off at the time.  I put out the fire with a hand-held extinguisher. Had I not been home my apartment would have been destroyed.

A professional electrician checked my outlet and wiring.  He said the fire was caused by the heater's un-grounded plug. He said the plug and its connecting wire were inadequate to the power requirements of the unit. It should have been sold with a grounded plug and a thicker wire.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by the heater's faulty plug, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it was a specific defect in the unit.

incident_description: Shower door spontaneously shattered.
justification: The shower door shattered, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
I discovered many defective electrical outlet from Pass & Seymour after new installation.  When a electrical plug was first plugged into the outlet, the metal contact deform and remain in contact. They heat up and arc.  The situation is complicated by missing ground washers on some receptacles that allow the ground wire to lose contact.  This is a fire and electrocution hazard.  

The product number is 26352-WCC8 and other product numbers showed the same defect.
justification: The defective electrical outlets pose a fire and electrocution hazard, which could lead to injury or death.

incident_description:
My LG window unit air conditioner spit out sparks, very strong smell of burning and smoke when my wife attempted to change temperature 2 nights ago.
It is about 5 years old. It is model LW1214HR
It was purchased from Home Depot in Austin Texas on hwy 620 and 2222.
justification: The air conditioner emitted sparks, smoke, and a burning smell, indicating a hazardous electrical malfunction that could cause injury.

incident_description:
Samsung front loading washer exploded.  Sides and top of washer burst and pieces of drum and plastic shot across laundry room.  Explosion of washer made a dent in neighboring Samsung front loading dryer.  Because of the dent the dryer drum now rubs against the side of the dented housing.  Washer is mangled beyond repair.  Both washer and Dryer were purchased at the end of August 2017.
I have reported incident to Samsung, I am waiting for Samsung to send someone to my home to take a look at my damaged washer and dryer.  I feel that both washer and dryer are unsafe and I want a full refund.
justification: The incident involved a washer explosion causing property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: windows have burning plastic smell but really bad problem is hard to open and then the upper sash falls down  very fast could severly hurt some one also almost impossible to put back up and aslo hasto be locked to stay up which means it can not left opened.
justification: The window's fast-falling upper sash poses a severe injury risk, and the difficulty in operation increases the likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I was doing a load of laundry in the washer. About half way through the cycle I heard a loud noise and found out that it was the washing machine. It sounded like a spark/static noise that lasted about 10 seconds. I went to the laundry room and it smelled as if something burnt and there was smoke. I opened the washer and it was sparking inside and causing more smoke. I grabbed the fire extinguisher to be safe; I honestly thought it was going to start a fire. Once the sparking stopped, I unplugged it. My husband took a look and saw that something had blown up inside the machine.
justification: The incident involved a washing machine sparking and producing smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Federal Pacific Electric Stab-lok panel showed evidence of arcing and smoke according to my electrician.
justification: Evidence of arcing and smoke indicates an incident occurred, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a total of 8 kidde smoke alarms (Model P4010DCS-W) and Smoke/CO combo alarms (ModelP4010DCSCO-W) and installed them between 1/28/18 and 2/2/2018.  These are 10yr alarms with wire-free interconnect.  
Since installation, I have had 3 alarms with batteries that failed.  Also, the alarms regularly disconnect from each other and no longer alarm as a network.  There is no warning or signal when an alarm disconnects.The first failed within 60 days.  The second through fourth have failed within 5 months.

I now have to test almost daily to ensure the alarms are powered.  The "end of life" or "dead battery" or other failure alerts do not work or are non-existent.

Kidde has replaced two of the alarms (after nearly 10 weeks of waiting), but has not acknowledged that there is a problem with their equipment.  I was told they are a new technology and all of the bugs aren't worked out yet.  They did not assure me that these actually work and will function in an emergency.
justification: The incident involves repeated failures of smoke alarms, posing a potential safety risk but no actual injury or death reported.

incident_description: Was cutting A piece of wood when the table saw stand dropped suddenly flinging the piece into my face. It left a piece of wood in my forehead that is now scarred and another piece broke a tooth out of my mouth.
justification: The incident resulted in a scar and a broken tooth, which are injuries.

incident_description: I purchased the usual Purex Laundry Detergent from Walmart in Tallman-Suffern, New York, using it many times.  I was diagnosed as suffering from Xerosis Cutis after the usages, which went away after I discontinued using the laundry detergent.  The laundry detergent mentioned herein smells different from what it's normal scent is.  I had to rinse my clothes vigorously many times with cold water.  Note that I still have in my bedroom the suspicious detergent bottle.
justification: The user suffered from Xerosis Cutis, which is an injury, and it resolved after discontinuing use of the detergent.

incident_description:
2015  The consumer received entry doors through the "Residential Sound Insulation Program" program and she has experienced issues with them.  

Three of the doors were interior doors and 3 exterior doors are connected to them. 

The doors also have windows which can slide up and down.  Due to the weight of the windows in the doors, the consumer cannot lift them up.  Additionally, they can fall down unexpectedly and injure a person.  She said that her neighbors have experienced issues with the door windows falling down unexpectedly and it presents a potential safety hazard

(date unknown) The consumer became locked out of the side door of her home, because she said that the locking  mechanism slipped.  Her neighbor had to break into her home to let her back in.  She said that as a result of this incident, it presented a safety hazard.

The dead bolt on the front door cannot be locked from the outside and she believes that this presents a safety hazard.
justification: The incident describes potential safety hazards with doors, including unexpected window falls and locking issues, but no actual injuries are reported.

incident_description:
I have a Delonghi "Rapido" room heater.  Model DR18TG, Serial Number 24610.  Last night when the heater was on, the control panel started to burn, melting the plastic.  I happened to be in the room at the time and unplugged it.  I'm not sure if there's a recall on this item.  

I've reached out to the manufacturer, but haven't heard back from them.
justification: The heater's control panel burned and melted, but no injury occurred as it was unplugged in time.

incident_description: I BOUGHT A DYSIN V6 ANIMAL CORDLESS VACCUM AND IT SHOCKED MY 9YR OLD DAUGHTER WHILE SHE USED IT...THE CHARGE PORT IS DIRECTLY IN THE PALM OF YOUR HAND ON THE HANDLE OF THE UNIT. I'M 228LBS, 6FT TALL, AND IT GAVE ME ONE HELL OF A SHOCK AS WELL..I CALLED DYSON AND THEY SAID IT WAS STATIC ELECTRICITY...NO IT WAS NOT.!!!! I GOT A LONG SHOCK AND CONTINUED TO GET THE SHOCK UNTIL I LET GO OF THE UNIT AND DROPPED IT ON THE FLOOR.!!! THEY SAID TO COVER THE HOLE WITH TAPE OR WIPE THE UNIT DOWN WITH A DRYER SHEET.!! ARE YOU KIDDING ME.!!!!???  I PAID OVER $430.00 FOR THIS ITEM AND IT'S ABSOLUTELTY DANGEROUS TO OPERATE.!!..I WENT ONLUNE AND THERE'S PEOPLE IN MULTIPLE WEBSITES COMPLAING ABOUT THIS SAME SHOCKING HAZARD.!!!...I WANT YOUR DEPT. TO INVESTIGATE THEM ASAP.!!...DYSON REFUSED TO REPLACE OR REFUND MY MONEY THAT I PAID FOR THIS UNIT...THIS IS VERY DANGEROUS.!!!!

incident_description: Aerosol spray can exploded causing damage to the storage cabinet and cabinet contents.
justification: The aerosol spray can explosion caused damage to property but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a product called super switch which is a remote controlled on off device to turn on lighting and other low wattage devices.  My product is about three years old. I had a remote module plugged in. The device is a grounded three prong device, and it was plugged into a grounded three prong extension cord in my house. There was nothing connected to the device at the time of the incident. The device exploded and caused a fire in my house. The extension cord was fairly new no frays or open wires. 

I understand that these products have wattage limitations but nothing was connected at the time of the incident. It was only powered up.

I am reporting this because I donÃÂt want this to go unreported.
justification: The device exploded and caused a fire, which is a significant incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This hand truck is a convertible cart which can be used 3 different ways.  It was in the position where the back of the cart is at an angle. This is the assisted 4-wheel position.  My child was moving it over when he lost his footing.  He grabbed the cart from the front to catch himself, when it gave away folding shut.  Both the ring and pinkie fingers on the left and right hand were trapped inside the sliding railing mechanisms.  The latch had to be lifted to allow the cart to open so the hands could be pulled out.  The fingers were all disfigured and bleeding. They were flattened so much I thought they had been sliced off.  By the time we got to the Emergency Room, they had begun to plump back up and looked much better. The right hand was not injured as badly as the left hand.  He had an appointment with the hand orthopedic specialist on 6-11-2018.  At this appointment the Dr. told us he would have surgery to repair both the left ring and pinkie fingers.  His surgery was on 6-12-2018.  
After he had the surgery and was getting better, I went to check out the hand cart to try and figure out what had happened.  I was able to convert it between all the positions with no problem so I just assumed I didnÃÂt have it latched properly when the injury happened.  Then on 6-14-2018 I was moving a shipment of boxes I received from FedEx when it slammed shut again.  Thankfully there were no injuries this time.  I once again started to question myself, did I latch it? I thought I made sure it was latched.  It was during this check that I found out the latch was in the correct position but was not fully securing the plastic hook part of the latch around the metal tubing that itÃÂs suppose to secure to.  I tried it several times and sometimes it worked and other times it didnÃÂt.  I found out that I had to force the latch down and then it stayed latched.  The second latch seems to be working great, IÃÂve had no problems with it, only the latch for the 4-wheel assisted position.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries requiring surgery, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the latch mechanism failed multiple times.

incident_description:
My LG top loading washer never makes it through a larger load without becoming unbalanced. The tub spins unevenly causing the machine to travel; as the tub rotates it increasingly sways from side to side, banging the sides of the machine and moving across the floor.  

It has not worked properly since it was purchased in 2013; it has been serviced several times without permanently resolving the problem. I saw the recall for LG top loaders manufactured earlier, and realized this is the same problem, but not being addressed.

My machine's model is 5070CW; serial 304KWWW28F953. I am hoping this machine will also be recalled to address the same safety issues.
justification: The washer's imbalance causes it to move and bang, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I am a fire investigator with the Village of Palatine (Illinois) Fire Department.  We had a small basement fire that originated in a dehumidifier.  The dehumidifier is a SoleusAir by Gree.  The model number or serial number was not identifiable due to the extent of damage to the device.  Fire Cause and Origin photography has documented the incident and photos are available.
justification: The incident involved a small basement fire with no reported injuries or deaths, and the likelihood is possible given the description of the event.

incident_description:
A Samsung Dryer which is only 18 months old, and purchased new, almost caused a fire in my wash room.  The dryer had been working normal but lately, now and them started to make a squeeking noise.  It would come and go.  Well last week the dryer would not work, it would only click when I tried to turn it on.  Called Samsung, they walked me through some steps, nothing worked.   They said to contact their repair center, no luck, so I called Sears repair who came out the same day and they found where the Idler bracket roller bearing had locked up and the idler puller was still trying to turn the dryer drum.  What shocked me was the idler pulley had melted on both sides and looked like it could/if not caught on fire.  If there was a lot of lint, it could have burnt the dryer or my house.  Luckly we clean the lint filter out all the time.  

My main concern besides the idler pulley melting is the fact that this dryer was only 18 months old. 

I have the parts that were taken off.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to a malfunctioning dryer, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was running a load of towels in a ten-year-old GE gas dryer.  It blew the circuit breaker and when I came back in from the garage after resetting it, I smelled something burning.  When I opened the dryer door, black smoke poured out.  I slammed it shut and ran for the fire extinguisher.  When I returned and opened the door, there was a growing fire in the dryer drum.  It took most of a good sized extinguisher to put the fire out.

The vent duct and rear of the machine were clear of lint.  The fire department suspects it was an electrical issue such as a short or overheated motor.

We had a remediation team at our house for two days wiping, washing, scrubbing and shampooing every room on two floors.  

Thank goodness the fire was contained to the inside of the dryer.  Can't say the same for the smoke that likely contained toxic particles from the burning plastic parts.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dryer, but no injuries or deaths were reported, only property damage and smoke exposure.

incident_description: I have a portable generator made by Briggs & Sratton. When I try to start  it,  the gas will leak from the carburetor  which is unsafe. I have contacted the co. and they refuse to help me
justification: Gas leaking from the carburetor is an incident that poses a safety hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
We purchased a generator a few years ago.  It was very expensive and between the unit and installation we paid about $12,000.00.  For the past few years it has been serviced by the same business that worked with LOEWS store to install the unit.  We have not had an emergency since we purchased the unit.  We made our purchase to be ready for power outages.  However, on March 2, 2018 during a power outage we experienced system failure on its very first test run.   Shortly after our generator turned on we noticed our lights would flicker and remained flickering for the next few hours our generator was running.  My husband and I was then alerted by our carbon monoxide detectors in our home of high levels of carbon monoxide rapidly rising.  We immediately called the fire department who confirmed high levels of carbon monoxide in our home with the highest reading upstairs where our bedrooms were.  After a thorough search they found the problem could be coming from our outside stand by generator.  They advised us to turn it off.  We were evacuated from our home and instructed to ventilate the home.  They also instructed us to call the gas company and have them check and make sure there were no gas leaks present.  We called our gas company and  our generator service technicians the following morning. The gas company met with us at our home later in the afternoon to run their check.   After turning on our generator during their check for gas leaks the gas technician also confirmed smelling fumes from our generator.  Later explaining to us that there is a difference between propane fumes and exhaust fumes.  He found no gas leak.  The generator technicians came the following day to perform their check.  In our absence he got our generator up and running, later explaining that there was condensation in the unit and that was the cause for the carbon monoxide.  We are still working on getting a solid work order from them for the work performed because we are questioning the findings.  

We are concerned and have questions about our unit.  Is this a manufacture defective unit?  Why didnÃÂt our unit shut off?  Should our unit be equipped with a shut off when itÃÂs malfunctioning?  Is it safe?  Why did the servicing contractor did not handle this as a warranty issue?  Our unit is up to date on routine services and still under warranty.  We even invested on a three hundred dollar warming kit suggested by them as a preventive measure.  Yet on its first test run our generator failed to run safely and properly.  Can someone please contact us regarding our issues?  Our unit is still under warranty and we are trying to get our generator running safely and the way it was intended to run.  We were very lucky to have carbon monoxide detectors in our home, grateful to be well and happy to have the opportunity to address this issue and bring safety awareness to other that this can happen.
justification: The incident involved a generator malfunction leading to high carbon monoxide levels, requiring evacuation but no reported injuries.

incident_description: My son was using our cordless DCD980 1/2ÃÂ (13mm) Type 1 20 volt DRILL/DRIVER serial # 999669 when it caught fire.
justification: The drill caught fire, which poses a significant risk of injury, though no injury was mentioned in the description.

incident_description: Was climbing ladder to inspect the flat part of my roof. ladder was place on level brick walkway. ladder collapsed when I was 7-8' up. The bottom aluminum frame of ladder bent. I fell approximately eight feet onto the brick patio landing on my left shoulder. I now cannot move my arm above my shoulder.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (inability to move arm above shoulder) from an 8-foot fall, indicating a severity level of 3. Ladder collapses are possible but not frequent, warranting a likelihood of 3.

incident_description:
Craftsman 1/4 Sheet Pad Sander. Model 315.116900. 

I was sanding a drawer front and the motor of the sander "exploded" and broke through front plastic covering of sander. Metal fragments of the motor burst through and were ejected up to four feet from my work space hitting the garage door and floor and the drawer front I was working on.

The sander was kept in the original box and stored properly. I had been using the sander for a small project and it was only in use for less than ten minutes when this happened. I was holding the sander at the time of the incident and it was not hot or did not have any type of smell indicating that it was about to over heat or blow up. 

I checked the recall list and did not see any recall notice for this tool. 

I have pictures of the sander and pictures of the metal fragments that were ejected. 

I was not injured. The fragments that hit the drawer front did leave small nicks in the wood. The other fragments hit a steel garage door and cement floor with no damage.
justification: The incident involved a tool malfunction with no injury, but potential for harm due to ejected fragments.

incident_description: Kenmore Elite electric washer is defective.  Ours is less than 6 months old purchased at Sears.  Today, while mid-cycle washing a very small load of delicates, the top glass lid exploded.  There was a loud "bang" sound when the lid shattering.  On opening the lid, much of the shattered glass fell inside the washer.
justification: The incident involved a defective washer lid exploding, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On February 11, 2018, we were having a linear gas fireplace, Enviro C44, manufactured by Sherwood Industries, installed in our home.  This is a permit process for Boulder County, new installation.  My husband oversaw the final install and ignition. The installer used the remote to start the unit. In less than one minute, the unit exploded with extreme force. My husband sustained 17 stitches in his face (including a hole right into his mouth), glasses ruined, and major dental issues (swollen face and pain for 1 week, infection, loss of work). The installer had 7 stitches on his neck and arm. Fireplace Warehouse of Denver put us in touch with the manufacturer. Fireplace Warehouse will not refund the unit. Sherwood will not pay for any damages, including a refund. We hired a forensic expert for $1047 out of our pocket.  They will need another $4500 to test the unit. Xcel Emergency was here right after the explosion and isolated the explosion to the unit. We feel we are owed compensation and would like to save the life of the consumer of the next explosive unit. Sherwood and Fireplace Warehouse will not pay for the 3rd party expert testing.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring stitches and dental issues for the husband and stitches for the installer, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the specific circumstances of the explosion.

incident_description:
On the night of 2/27/21018, I was awoken when a fan blade broke off of a ceiling fan. The fan was not running at the time.  The metal bracket holding the fan blade to the fan motor broke.  It is a clean break. The fan had been operating normally, without any wobble, in the day preceding the event.  The fan was manufactured by Monte Carlo Fans.  They are part of Generation Brands.

I contacted the manufacturer and they have been unresponsive.
justification: The incident involved a fan blade breaking off but no injury occurred, and the fan was not running at the time.

incident_description: Although we had been noticing and worrying about a "burning plastic" kind of smell in our home for a year or more, it wasn't until May 2017 after discussions with neighbors that we realized that the smell was coming from our windows!  These are PVC windows, manufactured by Sound Solutions, Inc., and were installed in our home in October 2011 through the Chicago Department of Aviation (CDA) Residential Sound Insulation Program (RSIP).   CDA representatives came to our home in May and confirmed that our windows were off-gassing.  They led us to believe at that time that it was the first they had heard of this problem.  Since that time, hundreds of homes in the RSIP program have been confirmed with the off-gassing windows. My husband began suffering with extremely severe headaches about three years ago, my sister who has some respiratory problems came for a visit but was not able to stay in our home due to the strong odor.  The CDA did replace our windows in December 2017 with windows manufactured by Harvey Windows.  I guess time will tell whether or not we'll have a similar problem.  While the CDA has conducted  air quality tests in our home and others, as well as laboratory chamber testing which has shown to be within acceptable guidelines, we strongly believe that their testing has been incomplete.  We have told the CDA all along that IT IS THE SUN that erupts the off-gassing into our homes.  They conducted in-home tests on cloudy days and chamber testing without incorporating the UV element.  It is our understanding that some additional testing will soon take place and we've urged them to include the UV element!   We deserve to know for absolute certain whether or not the windows pose a health risk!  ALSO, the mechanics of the windows deteriorate causing great danger.  Just trying to operate them or clean them is HAZARDOUS.  On many occasions, I've almost lost fingers because of mechanics snapping loose and windows crashing down! Window frames pull apart at corners and insulation slips out - it's just a nightmare!  What we thought started out to be a good program has turned into an absolute disaster!
justification: The incident involves off-gassing from windows causing health issues like severe headaches and respiratory problems, and hazardous window mechanics leading to near injuries.

incident_description: Plugged in my Ryobi 1/4 sheet Sander(model number S6510 - Identifying number - AJ0549 112689) after not using for several years. Turned it on and metal pieces exploded from one side of it it, lacerating my scalp and causing massive bleeding. Needed 4-5 staples in my scalp at the emergency room. Found multiple metal chunks that had flown out from inside the sander. The metal chunks also made small dents in my metal workbench.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring medical treatment (staples), which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) because such mechanical failures in power tools are uncommon with proper maintenance and usage.

incident_description:
Caller reported that the washer while in use started to vibrate violently moving across the room  he unplugged it to cancel the operation.  He stated that he took the unit apart  and noticed that the arm that hold the bearings together was broken.  He stated that the metal piece had split that held the shaft.     

Caller stated that there was no property damages only the washer was damaged.

Caller stated that he was not able to reach the manufacturer because each time he call there was no response.

Caller feels that this washer is unsafe and should be recalled.
justification: The washer malfunctioned violently but caused no injury or property damage, only damage to the washer itself.

incident_description: When in use the machine vibrates and shakes very hard. Caller had to place a piece of wood in front of the product to stop it from moving forward. Caller believes that the product is a entrapment hazard.
justification: The machine's vibration and movement pose a potential hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: PTAC being used for heat/cool, while on heat unit began smoking. Maintenance staff unplugged unit, but found melted components inside. Removed from service, currently no replacement. This is an Amana PTAC, model PTH123E50A, serial #1007627354. This unit is included in a safety recall for fire hazard that we did not receive until 3/13/2018.
justification: The PTAC unit began smoking and had melted components, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
10" Sliding Miter Saw

Saw has two flaws:
1.  Blade guard does failed to close and cover blade after cutting & release of saw.  Spring is weak and Mfg said no serviceable parts or adjustments.
2.  Sliding arm has no springs or retraction mechanism allowing the saw to lunge forward.

BOTH happened to me at the same time.  Blade guard failed to close and saw slide toward me after the saw was released cutting my hand.
justification: The incident resulted in a hand injury due to the saw's blade guard failure and uncontrolled forward movement.

incident_description: The washer was in use on regular cycle. Caller smelt gas and went to investigate. Flames were coming from the machine. Caller was able to put out the flames on the outside of the machine but there was still a fire inside of the machine. Contacted the fire department who came and put the fire out inside of the machine. Fire marshal informed caller that there was an electrical fire that started in the engine of the machine. No property damage.
justification: There was a fire incident with flames, but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description: Started using Earth Friendly liquid laundry detergent brand named ECOS about a month and a half ago. Developed a blistery painful rash and excessive swelling of legs, feet, hand and arms. Was sent to the ER by the Veterans Administration as a doctor questioned me about what new house cleaning, bathing or hygiene products I've added to my home recently and ECOS laundry detergent was the only product. After an online research concerning this product I was horrified to see so many complaints so similar to mine and these comments go back for over 2 years! Definitely going for a legal consult first thing Monday.
justification: The individual developed a painful rash and swelling requiring ER visit, indicating injury (severity 3). Online complaints suggest this is a recurring issue, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: Samsung washing machine shaking violently and extremely loud on spin cycle.   Dented sides of washer and almost came apart. Only had one light twin size bed sheet in washer.
justification: The washing machine shook violently and was extremely loud, causing damage to the machine but no reported injury.

incident_description:
I bought at Walmart a Mainstays stand steamer model BG503B
 unpacked followed the instructions as I was using it for the very first time the handle started to heat up to point you could not hold it and steam would exit at the bottom of the handle. Very poorly made and could be deemed a burn hazard . My Wife went on Walmarts website and saw there where more than 20 reviews most with same issuse handle to hot handle steam coming out the bottom of the handle etc....
justification: The description indicates a hazardous condition (hot handle and steam leakage) but no actual injury is reported, and multiple reviews confirm the issue is common.

incident_description:
New Boyertown hot air furnace installed to replace original fifty year old furnace in house. Furnace was installed by a licensed plumbing and heating contractor October 19. 2017. The day of installation my wife and I noticed that the furnace seemed loud and my wife also detected an odor discharged from the hot air vents. The contractor came back with the representative from the distributing outlet. They did not detect the odor but did recommend two remedies for the noise. A cover was installed over the burner housing and a different section of fuel line was attached to the burner. The noise was reduced but at intervals continued throughout the time the furnace has been in operation. The odor has been continuous and progressively worsened until the furnace was shut down. The fuel nozzle fowled in mid January 2018. This was found after I went down to check on the furnace because it was running continuously and very little air was being discharged through the vents. I checked the air filter and found it to be obstructed with a black carbon color. I removed the filter to allow air to flow. The odor from the vents woke my wife and she asked me why it all of a sudden had become worse. The contractor came in the following day and replaced the defective nozzle. The house was checked by two different fire departments detection equipment for hazardous materials and neither found any. The fumes continued and on February 15, 2018 I removed the side panel from the furnace and discovered the holes from the combustion chamber into the air distribution system. I notified the contractor, he notified the distributor, and they came and viewed the took pictures of the combustion chamber and surrounding area. The matter has caused the distributor to stop communication with contractor. The manufacturer has not communicated with us or the contractor or the contractors insurance carrier. The insurance company has sent an adjuster to record the damage. 
Since February 15, 2018 we have been providing heat with electric space heaters, provided by the contractor, to keep our pipes from freezing and a wood stove which we typically use to heat the end of the house that was added that had no ducting. 
From the beginning of January 2018 to now both my wife and I have been experiencing sinus and throat problems. My wife has also been experiencing chest  and arm pains. Since turning the furnace off we both appear to be recovering although not completely at this time. We both were treated for the flu in February and I wonder if it may also be caused by the carbon particulates we have been inhaling since the date of this furnace installation. If so that is a cumulative affect of four months exposure. We have both had out of pocket expenses for medicine. [REDACTED] has lost wages due to illness. We have lost money deposited on vacation reservations. We are not able to leave our house unattended with electric space heaters as the only source of heat.
justification: The incident caused sinus and throat problems, chest and arm pains, and required medical treatment, indicating injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the continuous exposure to fumes over several months.

incident_description:
I purchased a home in April 2015 that has a California required fire protection system installed in it.  It has come to our attention that the materials used, specifically the Viking VK457 sprinker head, is possibly defective and can initiate when not subjected to fire conditions.  There have been 4 instances of this in my community in the past couple of years causing considerable damage to homes.  Viking has been sued by other contractors in southern California for this specific defect and have been working to replace these heads for them.  They have not considered a similar program in our community.  

The sprinkler heads have been discontinued by Viking but have not been recalled.  It appears that the defect in some of the heads is due to manufacturing processes for heads that were built between 2013 and 2015.  Not all heads are defective but it is reported that it cannot be determined which is impacted unless it fails and floods a home.
justification: The incident involves defective sprinkler heads causing property damage without injury or death, and there have been multiple occurrences in the community.

incident_description:
Samsung Top Loader washer confirmed under recall model WA48H7400AW/A2
 Serial 0BHH5AEG606601X vibrated into me and over a course of time also disconnected from the hose causing leakage into my floor (2nd floor) and ceiling.
justification: The incident describes the washer vibrating into the person, which implies potential injury, and the leakage suggests possible property damage.

incident_description: Our ceiling fan failed (professionally installed, two years old) and the motor and blades separated from the bottom of the stem and fell approximately 20'  down onto our wooden coffee table and broke it in half. Luckily this happened at 3am, as its quite often during daylight hours my young daughters are leaning over that table coloring, or someone is sitting on the couch with their legs on that coffee table. Had this fans motor hit one of my daughters they most certainly would have sustained catastrophic injuries.
justification: The ceiling fan fell and caused property damage (broken coffee table) but no injuries occurred, as it happened at a time when no one was present.

incident_description: I have defective fire sprinklers throughout my new home which go off without warning and it has nothing to do w heat sensitivity. The model is Viking VK457 and it is throughout my Lennar home built in 2016. Already 4 homes, neighbors have had their house damaged to great depths. I have 4 children, all under the age of 5, one being just 7 months, plus animals. As the fire sprinklers goes off and ruins/destroys not only personal but property damages but can also cause personal injury.  Not only to myself, but my 4 helpless children, one having autism and my small kittens. I need these defective fire sprinklers to be replaced throughout the house immediately. I have contacted 3 times Lennar builders and have failed to get a response. I will be contacting Viking Corp., Scott as well. This is an ongoing issue,  with  all the homeowners in WEST PARK area of Roseville as the fire sprinklers are a ticking time bomb.... wait to exploded.
justification: The defective fire sprinklers pose a risk of property damage and potential injury, especially to vulnerable individuals like children and pets, but no actual injuries or deaths have been reported yet.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that when he pulled the attic ladder to unfold the ladder broke causing it to graze his head, which caused lacerations.  He stated that it was installed in the home approximately 10 years ago by a professional.  He stated that the hinges might have broke.   He stated that he administered first aid to his wounds.  Caller did not receive medical attention as yet

Caller feels that this ladder is a safety hazard which can cause serious injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer states that there was a fire in her home however the smoke and carbon monoxide detector did not alert her or her family of said fire. The consumer notes that the smoke detector is also supposed to send an alert to 1) the consumer's cell phone, 2) the consumer's friend's cell phone, and 3) the Manufacturer however not one party received the alert.

The consumer indicates that her mother inhaled smoke, which aggravated her condition as she has medical illnesses.

The consumer states that the fire was caused by a carpet that began smoldering and eventually caught fire. The consumer notes that the other smoke detectors in her home worked.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative she spoke with informed her that the smoke and CO detector must have had a faulty sensor, and so they would provide a replacement unit, which the consumer has since received.

The consumer plans on keeping her unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (smoke inhalation aggravating a medical condition) due to a faulty smoke detector, but no death occurred.

February IS, 2018
U. S. Food and Drug Administration
I 0903 New Hampshire Avenue
Silver Spring, MD 20993

RE: CHEMICAL IN AEROSOL SPRAY FOR HOME USE

Thank you.

incident_description:
I have a Trion by Fedders High Efficiency Console Electronic Air Purifier purchased in 2005. The manual is labelled 157251-001 6/05 Rev. B.

I am contacting you because the Air Purifier started to spark and smoke earlier today. My home quickly filled with smoke which, fortunately, set off the smoke detector.  When I went upstairs to investigate (the unit is in my master bedroom), I found flames starting to shoot out of the casing, I unplugged the unit. 

My wife and have spent most of our day dusting, vacuuming and wiping down surfaces (My wife and I both have asthma). The smoke and black soot has exacerbated our asthma. The house is a mess and smells from the smoke and singed plastic casing.

I have lovingly maintained the pre-filter, charcoal filter and electronic filter, precisely following the manual instructions. I carefully wash the pre-filter and electronic filter on a monthly basis and have replaced the charcoal filter every four months. 

Please advise me of any recalls or notifications regarding the safety of this product. I believe it is important to notify other consumers of the problem I encountered despite proper use and maintenance of this product. 


Thank you.
justification: The incident caused flames and smoke, exacerbating asthma for both individuals, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
We had a local spray foam contractor spray foam our new addition to our home in 10/2016.  From early on after spraying the foam I noticed a fishy smell but was told that the smell was normal and would dissipate. The brand of spray foam used is Demilec closed cell heatlock xt.
justification: The description reports multiple health issues including dermatitis, delayed speech in children, and frequent headaches, indicating injury (severity 3). The persistent smell and health effects suggest the occurrence is likely (4).

incident_description: I finished a load of laundry and removed it from the dryer at 4:30 p.m. Six hours later, before going to bed, I checked if anything was still in the dryer because my son was packing up to go on a trip. Luckily! The dryer had been off but had somehow kept heating. It felt warm on the outside, and the tub was hot on the inside.
