incident_description:
My daughter received a chemical burn on her back under her right shoulder from a Tide pod that did not dissolve
and was on her blouse. We have the blouse, pictures and medical documentation. She went to the ER and
dermatologist. The dermatologist said she will have scarring from the chemical burn.
After the pain of the burn subsided the wound is Improving. The hyper pigmentation will be the concern. How bad
will the scarring be.
The Tide pod was used In her wash load. She had the blouse on when her work manager said there was something
on her blouse. She tried getting it off by putting a damp towel on the spot. The next day, my daughter had a large
red spot that grew larger the following day. We have pictures. When she went back to work, the manager said it was
!Where the Tide pod was on the blouse that they couldn't get out. My daughter's work sent her home and said she
should go straight to ER. She did and was treated for a chemical burn. She was instructed to see her primary
provider If the burn continued to spread. It did. Luckily, we had a dermatologist yearly appointment already
scheduled 2 days after the ER visit. The dermatologist gave her a prescription of silver sulfadiazine 1% cream and we
were told to keep it covered.
This product should not be on the market when it doesn't dissolve properly and causes the severe chemical burn
and scarring of the skin!
justification: The incident resulted in a chemical burn requiring ER and dermatologist treatment, with expected scarring, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
We have had an Emerson heating/cooling thermostat in our home for several years. On Sunday, Oct.15, we came home after dinner at a restaurant and noticed an odd smell in the house. My husband checked the thermostat & it seemed to be working fine in the heating mode. About 40 minutes later, our smoke detector went off. I didn't have the oven on and when I went into the dining room I saw fire/flames shooting up the wall from the thermostat. I grabbed a kitchen towel off the stove & smothered the flames & my husband pulled the thermostat off the wall. We called the local fire department to come out & check for fire in the wall & everything was OK. They took a picture of the thermostat and they called us later to say they had found a recall notice for it. We never registered our thermostat so we didn't get a recall notice.
I have included a picture of the thermostat. We had a new Honeywell thermostat installed today after spending a chilly night in the house.

incident_description:
(09/29/2017) The consumer had an allergic reaction to the product.
The tablet hits the water in the unit when it is halfway through the wash cycle. When the tablet liquefied, the perfumed scent filled the consumer's living room. The consumer had to exit her home because she is sensitive to some scents. 

The consumer went to her car to sit down. The consumer stated that her airway started closing off, and her chest started going up and down. Also, her heart rhythm was blipping and her mouth was tingling.

The consumer had to blow the car horn because she was not able to call 911. Her husband came out to the car and called 911. While waiting for the ambulance to arrive, the consumer took two Benadryl Dye-free gel tablets.  When the consumer was in the ambulance, she was given a Solu-Medrol 125 mg IV.


Report No.20171016-58C48_1705391

There are 4 issues that need to be addressed for Consumer Product Safety:

1.   The labeling or lack of labeling on this product is dangerous and needs to be changed in particular for consumers who have allergies to perfumed chemicals. Neither the 85 count nor the 54 count boxes have anything on the label of their boxes to alert the consumer that a perfumed chemical scent has been added to their product. The Company representative told me on the phone that both of these products are made with what they call "Fresh Scent."
However, nowhere is that stated on the box for these products.(See attached pictures.) When I questioned another representative about the use of this perfumed scented chemical not being labeled on the box he said, "It's there but we just don't tell you on the box." To add to the confusion, when I spoke with a nurse on their Medical Emergency line, she initially said the products were the same but then she said on further investigation the  one I had not reacted to did not have perfume and the one I did react to did contain a perfumed chemical.
2.   In addition, it is my belief that there was indeed some perfumed chemical that was chemically different either in concentration or chemical from the 54 count product that I had used safely and the 85 count product that filled my living room with a perfumed chemical odor that I had never smelled with the 54 count product. This new and different perfumed odor from the tablet in the 85 count box caused an allergic reaction that sent me to the ER. Unfortunately, my body
is 100% accurate on this. The Company refused to tell me what that difference was. When we purchased the 85 count box,other than the difference in the # of tablets in the box, there was nothing on the label to warn me as a consumer that this product would emit a different perfumed odor that would fill up my living room which never happened with the 54 count product. That difference should also have been noted on the label and was not.
3.  The Company has listed on their MSDS sheets (which do not necessarily contain the complete list of chemicals in a product) the chemicals which are the same in these products but they do not alert the consumer that something is different from the 54 count product and the 85 count product, nor  do their labels. That omission on the label and the MSDS sheets can potentially have deadly consequences for consumers like myself who have allergies to many perfumed
scented chemicals. I am not asking for proprietary information, however when something has been done to a product that will cause a perfumed odor to fill your living room that did not happen with the prior product the customer has a right to know that something in this product Is different  or has changed. People with allergies to perfumed chemicals cannot avoid them if they are not informed on the box that they have been put into a product or that something they had used safely before has changed.
4.   Finally, the question has to be asked from a Consumer Product Safety point of view, "Why are manufacturers putting perfumed scented chemicals in dishwashing tablets?"
"Would anyone in their right mind as much as they may like the smell of their perfume, spray
their perfume on their dishes and glassware and then eat off of it?"

While in the ER, the consumer stated that her heart was doing something. There was also the feeling of soft tissue swelling below the nose at the back of her throat. 

The consumer stated that this is the first time that she used this product.

(09/29/2017) The consumer contacted the manufacturer's Medical Emergency Team around midnight. The consumer's information was taken.

The consumer requested to know the difference in the chemical concentration in this product (05170089229 UPC code 051700897 85 ct)  Her request was denied. 051700810505 (54 ct) which consumer had used safely with no perfumed chemical odor filling her living room. compared to their other products.
justification: The consumer experienced a severe allergic reaction requiring emergency medical treatment, including IV medication, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I have a Heat N Glo SLR-B model fireplace, which was installed in 2010 by Fireside Hearth and Home in my Model Townhouse.  I purchased the Townhouse in 2013 and have lived there since, using the fireplace every year.

Last night the glass front exploded into a million pieces with glass shards flying all the way across the entire 30 foot length of the townhouse.  My wife and five month old daughter were sitting only feet away.  The glass actually shattered 5 to 10 minutes after I had turned the fireplace off.  I ran the fireplace for about 30 minutes before turning it off.

I'm not sure what the sound of the explosion has done to my daughter's ears or the glass dust that they both had to inhale.  I have glass all over my furniture, rugs, and floors.  It's large pieces and as small as dust particles.
justification: The glass explosion caused significant property damage and potential health risks from glass dust inhalation, but no immediate injuries were reported.

After wearing an article of clothing from this wash for approximately 10 hours, I woke up in a lot of pain on part of my skin covered by the clothing. When I examined the area in pain it was red and appeared as if my skin had rubbed off. I realized I had chemical burns that were apparently caused by the OxiClean product. I do not have sensitive skin and have never encountered any issues with the use of any other detergents, lotions, or any skin products. I purchased the product at a Kroger grocery store in May to treat a furniture stain, but had never used the product as part of a laundry wash until now.
justification: The incident resulted in chemical burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Such occurrences are rare given the user's lack of prior issues with similar products.

incident_description:
In July, 2017, we were notified by our builder, Lennar, that our joists in our basement may be off gassing high level of formaldehyde. Weyerhaeuser Co, is the manufacturer for the trujoists in our home and indicated for us to just stay out of the basement and we will be fine.  

On August 2, 2017, I requested air chamber test to ensure other levels on our home were safe for our family.  Weyerhauser performed tests on our main level as well as basement to determine the exact level emitted.  Weyerhauser did not release test results until November, 2017 showing results were over 90 times above the exposure guidelines for residents.  We chose to leave our home the end of August after having an attorney perform the tests since Weyerhauser chose to not let us know the exact poison released in our home.

My daughter lived in the home for over three months, that resulted in respiratory issues not seen prior to moving into the home that resulted in her adenoids to be removed.  Weyerhauser should be held responsible for putting these toxic product in over 2,500 homes across the nation.  Weyerhauser issued a statement about the "potential" of this off gassing and will surpass.  This is incorrect and falsifies the real danger the product brings to consumers homes.
justification: The incident resulted in respiratory issues requiring medical intervention (adenoid removal), indicating an injury.

They have failed to respond since.  I don't want my house to catch on fire and/or me die from a defective product.  What do I do now?
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly contained without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood of recurrence is possible given the defective outlet and lack of response from the manufacturer.

incident_description:
The dryer is a Whirlpool WED5800BW0 S/N: M40301713.  Our smoke detector went off.  We smelled smoke coming from our dryer which was running.  We unplugged it, emptied it and made it safe.  Upon examination, the screen inside and at the back of the drum was black and there was a piece of burned lint on the other side of the screen.  The exhaust vent and sides of the machine were not hot.

The next day, I took the machine apart and there was about 3/4" of lint on the entire floor of the machine which appeared charred and there was charred lint on top of the box containing the heating element.  We clean the lint screen prior to each use and I have brushes which I use to clean out the area inside the machine below the screen along with using a vacuum cleaner on it.  You can not get to the back of the drum as the back of the machine is welded to the sides and bottom.  The exhaust duct had some lint but it was nowhere near being blocked.

We are getting rid of this piece of... but I do have pictures which I can forward if contacted.  This could have been a lot worse if we had not heard the smoke alarm.

PS - I am using the latest version of Firefox but your website will not let me upload my pictures.  Also, when I tried the spell checker on the first or second page, I lost all my info.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard from the dryer, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Smoke Detector, First Alert Model P1200 manufactured 2014 DEC 16.
Bought 2-16-2015 along with several other detectors for my residence from Lowes Home Improvement..  I placed a new 9 Volt battery in this detector and within minutes before I got to reinstalling it in a  bedroom ceiling, I pushed the test button and it sounded one time. Within about 15 seconds I smelled something, electrical smell, burning. There was a bright orange glow on the cover and it became extremely hot to the touch and the cover started to melt at the orange glow point. It was to hot to touch. I removed the battery and put in a sink and ran water over it.  I've no doubt that it would have been in flames if I had installed the device and left the room.  
I notified the Raleigh NC Fire Department and got no response, which was somewhat surprising, possibly because my residence is not located in a 'high rent' area nor am I politically involved in the City.  
I sent a notification to the First Alert manufacturer using their web site but again no response from them. 
I notified the NC State Fire Marshall's Office and they advised me to report the issue this this web site.  
I still have the device.
justification: The smoke detector malfunctioned, causing overheating and melting, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Black mold growth in Maytag washing machine MHW8200FC.

Eight months after purchasing the Maytag MHW8200FC washing machine, I discovered an incredibly nasty growth of black mold in the dispenser cavity (see photo).  There was no way to clean the area; Maytag had to replace the entire cavity and dispenser unit.  Maytag could provide no method for either preventing the mold from recurring or for removing it once it had formed.  Once the unit is out of warranty, I will be responsible for replacing the parts myself on a routine basis, or else just living with the mold.

The unit is located in a large laundry room with the door always open and a hepa air filter running 24-7.  I leave the door to the washer open when not in use, as well.  I do not live in an excessively humid climate (Oregon) and the house is air conditioned in the summer.  I never had a problem with mold growth in my old front-loading washer which lasted over 15 years.

Since black mold is a known health hazard, I feel the CPSC should be aware of this product and its potential for causing sickness when used according the manufacturer's instructions.

I purchased the machine on 11/18/2016 and the parts were replaced on 9/6/2017.

I have attached a photo of the mold; please contact me if you did not receive the photo.

Thank you.
justification: Black mold is a known health hazard, but the description does not mention any actual injury or death, only potential risk.

incident_description:
Last week I was filling a bucket of water with the shower head and when I went to test the temperature of the water by dipping my finger in I got a mild electrical shock. Initially I thought maybe it was static so i touched it again and it was definitely AC electric (a feeling that I am relatively familiar with.

Immediately I went and shut off the power to the house and then the water (since I didn't want to risk touching the tap again). Then using a non-contact voltage detector I checked for live current on the shower head. With power to the house off there was no live current. 

I flipped the breaker for the washing machine off and then turned on the master breaker again. Still no live current on the shower head, valve, or bucket of water. When I flipped the washing machine breaker back on there was initially no current. Then when I turned the washing machine on (using the soak cycle + a little bit of bleach and soap) both of my non-contact voltage detectors were triggered when checking the shower handle (a metal part). At this point I was fairly certain that the issue was related to the machine machine so I started to try different things. I used an alligator clip to connect the live (red) lead of my multimeter to the drain of the washer (before the airgap) and connected the neutral (black) lead to ground. When the cycle began there was initially no current for a few seconds then when a solenoid inside (I assume it was a solenoid, it wasn't the lock) clicked, the multimeter detected 100 VAC (likely not 120 because of resistance) on the drain. I have not yet tested for voltage or continuity on the water input lines.

I realized that the washing machine was not on a GFCI, so I installed and tested a GFCI outlet (with both the built in function as well as a dedicated GFCI test tool). I tested the washing machine another time and again detected 100 VAC on the drain, the GFCI was never triggered.

There is continuity between the body of the washing machine and the ground, so it is definitely grounded properly. 

I have unplugged the washing machine and put a warning label and ziptie on the plug (so it cannot be plugged into a receptacle).  I have also attached another warning label and a lock to the door that prevents it from being closed by anyone who tries to use the washing machine while there is still a fault.

I contacted Whirlpool support and let them know about the issue. I have also ordered a new pump for the machine since that seems to me like the most likely cause. Multiple safety features failed here or did not exist, and had I decided to to my laundry an hour earlier I'd have killed whatever family members that were showering. In the mean time I'll be using a laundromat until I find the definite cause. and implement a ground connection between the water input and the GFCI.


The water inside of the machine should have been grounded, however, it was not. The machine either did not include any safety mechanism to prevent this, or the features failed. 

If WhirlPool would like to take this machine to diagnose the issue, I'm okay with that provided they do so for free and provide a washing machine to use in the meantime.
justification: The incident involved a mild electrical shock, which constitutes an injury, and the potential for more severe harm was present.

After this issue occurred in my first unit which had been purchased in 2009, in 2013 I was contacted by LG Electronics Liability department after posting here regarding mold buildup in the detergent drawer and wash tub.  At that time I was told to go buy the equivalent newer model by LG that would still match my dryer and they would send someone to pick up the old unit.
It has been nearly 4 years, but the machine has periodically had a mildew odor and some signs of mold and mildew in the same places again over the last year.  Now, the machine is at the point where I cannot get rid of the smell.  When I called LG Customer Service they told me I would have to pay to have a technician come disassemble my machine and clean it thoroughly as it was out of warranty.  They also informed me that the "recommended cleaning process" is to run the Tub Clean Cycle with a chemical additive repeatedly, multiple times in a row, to eliminate smell and contamination.  A washing machine is meant to clean clothes and in turn I expect it would also be a fairly clean device overall so this is unacceptable.  
This is now the second machine where mold and mildew seem to be pervasive to the cleaning areas of the machine and I am scared to even place my infant son's clothing in the machine at all.

incident_description:
The unsafe product is a ""Stanley 5000 Watt Generator with 6000 Surge/Peak Watts" portable generator.  The product was/is sold by SEARS.  The manufacturer of the generator is GXI Outdoor Power LLC.  The product uses the American brand name "Stanley" but is actually made in China by third-parties. 

This product caused a sudden and spontaneous gasoline leak which lead to a fire and decedent's death from 3rd degree thermal burns/injuries. Decedent's wife sustained first and second degree burns and also the emotional trauma of seeing her husband burnt alive, among other things. 

The accident took place on 10/27/14 at approximately 11:30 PM in [REDACTED].  The generator was in decedent's garage and NOT IN USE on the night of the incident. 

When retiring to their bedroom at night, decedent & wife smelled an odor and traced it back to the garage on the ground level.  In the garage, decedent and wife witnessed gasoline leaking from the generator.  Wife tried to obtain rags in the room next door and, upon exiting the garage to the room, the pilot light of the boiler next door ignited the gasoline vapors. 

The New City Police Department, Fire Inspector and Fire Department determined the cause of the fire as being the leaking generator. Thereafter, in Nov. 2015, experts for the estate, SEARS & GXI conducted multiple days of joint inspections, including physical inspection, microscopic testing and chemical testing, among other things.  The joint inspection found a defective, fractured bolt in the carburetor.  The Estate's experts determined the leak was caused by a sudden fracturing of the brass bolt in the fuel reservoir bowl, in the upper portion of the carburetor.  The fracturing of the bolt had caused the fuel reservoir bowl to fall, thereby causing the sudden and immediate leaking of all the generator's gasoline contents.  The experts found that the bolt was made of low quality yellow brass alloy which is prone to corrosion, cracking and dezincification.  The experts also found the bolt had intersecting perpendicular bored holes which also caused the fracturing of the bolt.  All of the above, among other things, constitute dangerous defects in the product.  The experts also found inadequate or non-existent warnings, among other things. 

This report is being submitted as three years have passed and SEARS/GXI have still not reported the incident.  The product is still being sold in the USA, via SEARS, Home Depot, Loews and Kmart.  There is a high likelihood that other American consumers will be injured.
justification: The incident resulted in a death and injuries, with a high likelihood of recurrence due to ongoing sales of the defective product.

incident_description:
Around August 15, 2017 I noticed my dehumidifier was not functioning correctly.

Around June 1, 2017, I started running the dehumidifier for the summer months in our basement. When I first plugged it in and started it, I thought the compressor sounded normal. The unit seemed to be running fine since I noticed water draining from the bucked to the floor drain. I have a basement office and I started noticing a kind of a low pitched "metallic" sound coming from the unit if I happened to be within earshot. It was one of those things you notice, but assume it is just "normal". 

Then around the 15th of August, I came downstairs and noticed the basement humidity was up and it had that "basement" smell. I could hear the unit's fan running, but the compressor was not on. I rotated the unit and kneeled down to check the floor drain to look for water coming out of the hose. There was none. I immediately noticed a "burnt, ozone, melted plastic smell" at floor level. I quickly unplugged the unit and began investigating. After taking the back panel off, I managed to pull off the black plastic compressor cap and found a horrendous site. One of the power leads had completely been melted, burnt, and was broken off of the compressor terminal. You can see in the pictures the melted wire, black scorching, and the melted plastic inside the cap. This is a complete fire hazard. I am lucky I was there when I noticed the unit not functioning.

incident_description: We purchased a Samsung top loader washer two years ago and within the last 3-4 months have been noticing black flakes on our laundry; the total cost of the washer at the time of purchase was $1,279.98, plus the extended warranty of $249.99.  We have run the self clean cycle as recommended by the manufacturer, we have tried running baking soda and vinegar and the more we do this the worse the problem is getting.  We have come to find out that the black flakes are an accumulation of mold.  We have called Samsung and reported the problem and they just tell us that we should run the clean cycle which we have done several times only to have the problem continue and continuing to get worse!  Now they have told us to contact their repair person who informed us that this will cost, to start at least $200, just to remove the part that they had to install because of the washer lid exploding incident, so we get punished because of their fautlty engineering!  The repair person also told us that we have to pay him up front with either cash or a credit card before he will even touch the machine.  When we contacted the extended warranty company about this issue they told us that the extended warranty only covers electrical and mechanical problems, so why were we fools and purchased it, what a rip!  And of course, our warranty with Samsung has expired since we purchased it two years ago.  We are so frustrated with this issue and we have decided to never purchase another Samsung washer again and are now in the process of looking for a new washer, it is either that or we have to end up taking our clothes to a laundromat to avoid having mold all over our clothers, towels and bedding.  This is a health hazard, but Samsung refuses to do anything about the problem.  If you check the Samsung web page and the communtiy blog pages complaints about this issue will appear and yet Samsung does nothing to alleviate the problem!  My whole family has been having issues from itchy skin to stuffiness.  We paid over $1,000 for this washer and it is like brand new and this is the service we get from this company, it is ridiculous!  Please advise us as to what we can do to get either the problem resolved or at least a full price refund!  We will never purchase another Samsung product again!!  We will also spread the word that they sell junk and don't back up their products.  They can take this washer and send it back to Korea where it came from, typical Asian junk!!
justification: The incident involves health issues like itchy skin and stuffiness due to mold exposure, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I was walking up the ladder putting away Christmas presents and the hinge sheared off.  The ladder is rated for 300 lbs, I weigh 180 and was not carrying anything at the time.  Werner SS2208  ladder's hinge fails.  This seems to be a design defect in the ladder.  See https://smile.amazon.com/22-1-ATTIC-LADDER-Werner-S2208/dp/B0001LQZN4/ref=cm_cr_arp_d_product_top?ie=UTF8  and http://futheylawfirm.com/werner  .  The ladder should be recalled.

incident_description:
A Kidde fire extinguisher which I purchased was recalled two years after I purchased it. They sent me a replacement. Now, one year later, they informed me that the replacement is recalled. They said they would send me a new one; it took three months for them to do so. When I received the new fire extinguisher the gauge was on empty. In other words, they sent me a faulty extinguisher to replace the faulty extinguisher they had sent me to replace the original faulty extinguisher.

In addition, I checked the other Kidde extinguisher which I had purchased at the same time as first one, and the gauge is on empty. This extinguisher several years away from the expiration of Kidde's warranty. And this extinguisher was not part of any recall.

It seems to me that this company should be investigated and that all consumers should be advised to check the gauges on their Kidde extinguishers on a regular basis.
justification: The incident involves repeated faulty fire extinguishers, posing a potential safety risk but no actual injury or death reported.

incident_description: I never even imagined this could happen until yesterday. I had the most terrifying experience of my life yesterday. My 3 year old twin boys were upstairs playing in their room. My daughter said she could hear them screaming, so I went upstairs to check. I realized the screams were coming from the laundry room. I found both of them in the washer, it was running & the lid was locked. I hit the stop button but the lid wouldn't unlock, same with when I turned it completely off. I finally ripped the lid open breaking the whole lock off. This could've ended so much worse. All I keep thinking is the what ifs.. what if she didn't hear them, what if I didn't make it in time.. I would no longer have my 2 babies. The older top loading Lg models have a feature where you have to press the start button a second time once you close the lid. The model I own which is only 2 years old does not. My kids must've hit the start button while they were climbing in, closed the lid & it started with them trapped in side. I don't want this to happen to another parent, & the outcome not being as good as mine.
justification: The incident involved children trapped in a running washer, which could have resulted in death, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Product was being used in the basement of residential structure for its intended purpose. The Fire Department was called for a possible structure fire, upon arrival found light smoke throughout the residence. Source of smoke was located at the dehumidifier with smoke coming from the unit.

whirlpool front washer with black mold

incident_description:

incident_description: I purchased a Sears Kenmore Elite Gas Dryer in November 2007.  I recently began to smell natural gas emitting from around the dryer and called Alabama Gas Company.  Their service technician arrived and checked the dryer for a natural gas leak and found that in fact there was a gas leak coming from inside the unit.  His opinion was that it was coming from the internal gas valve.  He checked all of the external natural gas line connections to the unit and found no natural gas leak at any external line or connection.
justification: A gas leak was detected, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that there is a light on the dryer that indicates when the filter and dirty and must be cleaned. The consumer cleaned the filter out however he noticed an unusual amount of lint outside his home.

12/02/2016 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to arranged for a Service Technician to inspect his unit. 

12/09/2016 - The Service Technician inspected the consumer's unit and noticed that a fire had started underneath it.

The consumer contacted the retailer to inform them of the Service Technician's findings. The representative he spoke to informed him that they would remove from the floor any of the same units he owns so as to prevent consumers from purchasing them.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer  to inform them of the Service Technician's findings. The representative he spoke to informed him that they needed to wait for the service repair company to contact them and let them know what the issue was.

The consumer states that prior to the incident, he used his unit approximately twice per week. The consumer plans on keeping his unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: A fire started underneath the dryer, which is a significant incident but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Maytag Bravos high efficiency top load washer has developed a strong mold odor.  This odor developed despite routinely using the clean washer cycle and leaving the lid open when the washer is not in use.  It is now to the point where it causes me to have a tight chest and sore throat.  Washer is almost eleven months old.

incident_description:
This information was taken from the information Center.

Early August 2017 we purchased the above product at our local North Huntingdon Walmart.  We used this product to scrub the carpeting in our living areas on August 3, 4 and 5 in anticipation of receiving a family visit of out of town relatives.  Our dog reacted to this product by coughing and began to experience difficulty breathing.  She passed away overnight unexpectedly on August. 6.  She was 11 years old and had an enlarged heart.  We are deeply concerned that this product may have aggravated her condition and put her at a higher risk of complication of her existing health issues.  The use of this product also caused an irritating rash to appear for several days on my hands.  We read the label prior to use and followed all guidelines indicated.  We feel that additional warnings should be listed concerning possible health risks, particularly since the product is clearly marketed to pet owners.  After contacting [REDACTED] of the PA Office of the Attorney General (file # [REDACTED]) we were advised by [REDACTED], Consumer Relations Specialist of [REDACTED], representing Resolve, that we should send the remaining contents of the Resolve container directly to them.  We are concerned that it would be inappropriate for Resolve to investigate this complaint.  We feel strongly that a neutral party that does not represent the product should follow this up.  Thank you for your attention and advice.

Product: Kidde smoke and CO alarm. Date of manufacture: August 2012

The alarm announced FIRE when there is no fire present. This happened for about 3 minutes and then it stopped. It happened again 3 hours later, stopped, and happened again about 10 minutes later. We have changed the backup battery and it has been quiet for about a half-hour. 

The alarm has been recalled for another reason. I noticed report of a similar situation on this site from August 2017.
justification: The alarm falsely announced a fire, causing concern but no actual injury or damage.

incident_description: My snow blower started on fire (having used starter fluid to try to get it started).  The plastic parts (including the gas tank) ignited and I was at risk to lose my home or great  personal injury.  I got my Kidde fire extinguisher and attempted to extinguish the fire.  The extinguisher failed and the fire raged on.  I pushed the snow blower away from the house with risk to myself if the gas tank blew up - luckily it didn't.  As my exterior water was turned off, drained, and hoses stored for the season, the fire raged on until I could get all of this re-connected and functional to extinguish the fire with a hose / water.  My snow blower is completely destroyed and the Kidde fire extinguisher was a complete failure just when I needed it the most.  I consider the money that I spent on this fire extinguisher to be theft by Kidde.  I'm out $900 for a replacement snow blower.

incident_description:

My 22 year old grandson & I heard a loud popping noise, followed by an intense grease fire with yellow flames at the rear of the grill . Grill is built into a concrete block island located away from any flammable structure.

We immediately removed the First Alert , Model FE1A10G15 , NO. AB-170560, from its wall mount . We verified that the gauge was "in the green" and attempted activation . There was no sound of escaping propellant and no extinguishing agent was expelled  and indicator needle went into the "red" . 

 Fire intensified, and we immediately got the Model [REDACTED] extinguisher from the garage . Extinguisher functioned as designed and all flames were extinguished within a few seconds .Gas supply was turned off and grill permitted to cool .

The malfunctioning FE1A19G15 caused a delay in extinguishing the blaze . Further, the gauge indicated that it was serviceable . The mount was on the wall of a covered porch , behind an arch - protected from the elements and direct sunlight . Storage temperatures were not exceeded . 

Incident was reported to the manufacturer - no response in 48 hours. Defective item held for investigation.
justification: The incident involved a grease fire and a malfunctioning fire extinguisher, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her front loading washing machine that she purchased from a home store around mid 2006.
She had no problems with the unit until sometime between July 11th and 12th, 2017
She was washing clothes and around mid wash during the spin cycle she saw white smoke coming from around the edges of the door.
She turned the unit off then unplugged it from power.
She searched for repair techs around her area but could find none.
Her father in law said he could repair it but when he began taking it apart and viewing it, he stopped working on it and advised her that there had been a fire inside when he saw burned parts inside the rear tub.
The consumer then contacted the manufacturer July 21, 2017 and she advised caller to contact CPSC.

She is asking for this product to become recalled with rebate/replacement as a remedy.

incident_description: Samsung top-loading washer "exploded" during spin cycle. This particular model was part of the recall in 2016. incident_description: We purchased a GE Harmony washing machine model WPGT9350 in 2005. It has worked fine until this morning. incident_description: Samsung dryer drum splits. Have had it fixed three times. Samsung denies there is an issue with their drum but thousands of reports and blogs say they all have the same issue of splitting. Longer dry cycles could cause fires.. Seams come apart in drum creating potential fire hazard and mechanical thumping making dryer not efficient.This is a fire safety and health and security issue of paramount importance. Homes could burn down. Samsung continues to not acknowledge there is a problem. Only resolution is Samsung to pay to put in a drum that does not crack. Consumers should not have to make repairs due to a known manufacturing gross error.
justification: The description indicates a potential fire hazard and mechanical issues, but no actual injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
I have a Shop Vac model K12-300A purchased in 2013. When I turned it on recently the switch shorted, starting an electrical fire. Luckily I was able to disconnect it before anything besides the vacuum was damaged (the switch melted in the closed position). I contacted Shop Vac and was told I could purchase a new motor unit, which I have ordered. I asked them if they were going to respond to me regarding this serious safety defect (a switch shouldn't catch fire, as it's supposed to be within 1 wire, usually the black power line). incident_description:

My son and I followed the directions and set it up in the left corner of the bathtub opposite the shower and bathtub fixtures. It toppled within two days into the shower curtain. All soaps, shampoo bottles, etc., were scattered inside and outside the tub.

If someone had happened to be using the tub, they could have sustained injuries from the metal pole, shelves and/or items in the shelves crashing onto them.  If a child or a baby were in the tub, a serious injury could occur.  The shelves have protruding metal hook-like arms to hold things like wash cloths which could cause injuries. 
     I also went on the web site of the store I purchased it from and 8 out of nine people reviewing it reported that it did not stay up for them either. I saw these reviews after I bought it. Again, I state that this is an unsafe product due to the instability of the pole which topples over for no reason.

incident_description: Approximately 11:30 pm our electrical service to our home switched on and off approximately 10 times over the course of a few minutes.  The power didn't stay off for any significant duration and eventually stayed on the rest of the night.  The next day I checked with neighbors and found out they didn't experience any power outage so I investigated around the house.  I discovered outside at our electric meter box that it was black all around the box and on the brick where the box was mounted.  I notified Ameren Illinois who dispatched a utility worker.  Once he arrived and opened the box he commented he had not seen one burned that bad and he immediately disconnected our underground utility service at the street and I had him call an electrical contractor to come out.  One side of the electrical service was burned completely through the wire and the electrical box and meter had to be replaced.  Both the electrician and Ameren employee were amazed that we still had electrical service coming in the home based on the extent of the damage.  Because it was mounted on brick that helped prevent more serious fire damage.  A relative alerted me to a report they heard about smart meter fires.  The meter involved in this fire was Focus AXRe-SD Landis+Gyr Gridstream RF.  The back of the meter was burned pretty badly, as well as the interior of the box.
justification: The incident involved significant electrical damage and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
We had an Eva-Dry 2200 dehumidifier in 2 large walk-in closets in the second level of our home.   They had worked without incident for over a year.   On August 25, 2017, the one in our guest room totally disintegrated, causing severe damage to the closet and its contents, and also causing severe smoke damage to entire second floor of our home.  The fire chief stated that if the closet door had not remained closed, the damage would have been much greater to the structure, as well as to myself.  The fire chief also stated there was no indication that anything else electrical in the house had been affected and the breaker did not trip.
We looked on the internet for reviews of this product that might indicate someone else had experienced this problem but found none.  Also asked the question on the Amazon web site where we had purchased the product and no one said they had any trouble with it.
We contacted the company and spoke with an individual who suggested we not report it to our homeowners insurance but rather get estimates for repairs and let them know and they would send us a check, as long as it wasn't over $68,000.   They also made some sort of statement that we may have caused this to happen, on purpose.  The next time we spoke, we told them we had filed a claim and we have not heard from them since.  We still do not have the final costs associated with this fire nor do we know how much our insurance will pay to [REDACTED], [REDACTED] for cleaning of all of the clothing and textiles or for the complete rebuilding of the closet and repainting that had to be done in several areas.
We believe this product is dangerous in its design and/or use of certain materials.  I was home when this occurred and would not be here today if I had opened that closet door to investigate a noise I heard.  When I did investigate a few minutes later,  the smoke was so thick and so black in the bedroom, I could not even see light coming in from the windows....just smoke.   The remains of the dehumidifier were taken by someone from [REDACTED] to a lab to see if they could figure out what happened to it.  We have not heard back from them about the results.
justification: The incident caused severe damage and smoke but no injury or death, and similar incidents appear rare based on lack of online reports.

I ran back upstairs to grab some clothes to smother the flames, and began removing oxygen from the base of the fire while attempting not to have the clothes catch on fire.  In the process the flames burned my right hand, but I had to continue subduing the flames.  Meanwhile I was asking her to try different methods or angles with the extinguisher, but to no avail.  Finally, 1 puff of dry chemical came out but it was not under proper pressure, and since my wife was standing back from the oven while I manually put out the fire, the discharge caused no significant reduction in the flames, but instead sprayed my counter, cabinets, sink, etc with a fine layer of dust.

incident_description:
A little over a month ago, the 3 year old water heater in our house started detonating the natural gas that powers it instead of smooth ignitions when the heater would start a cycle to warm up the water.  At it's worst, it was a loud enough detonation that it sounded like somebody slamming a door on the other side of a larger house.

Our plumber came out, serviced the unit and found that the screen that covered the pilot light / burner assembly literally had holes burned through it and indications of hot spots on the assembly.  Presumably these hot spots were causing the detonation when the water heater would first cycle on.  Almost $400 in labor later, a new assembly was installed and the problem was fixed.  A month, almost to the day afterwards, the gas valve freezes in the shut position.

The water heater was a State Water Heaters Co model GS 6 40UOC T G 200

State Water Heaters was only willing to ship out a replacement gas valve via 7 to 10 day delivery ground shipping.  They seemed completely unconcerned about the earlier safety issues with the gas detonation or the inconvenience and expense they caused us in both cases.  We replaced the water heater with a different brand due to our fears for our safety.  That cost us another $920, after our plumber gave us a discount. 

The water heater is a defective product at best and a potentially very dangerous one at worst.  Gas appliances are supposed to have a smooth, even ignition process, not one where the gas initially detonates with a bang when it ignites.  Had those detonations gotten bigger, it could have potentially destroyed our house.  State Water Heater's indifference to whole situation only added insult to injury.
justification: The incident involved a defective water heater causing gas detonations, but no injuries or deaths occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue was resolved but could recur with similar defective units.

incident_description:
I purchased this dryer new from Sears in February 2010.  Shortly thereafter I smelled gas coming from the drum and vent.  Sears came and changed the valve. 

This year the smell has become more frequent and consistent.  Around September 2017 I called Sears for repair (I purchased an extended warranty). I was told that I had to call the gas company before they could come out.  The gas company determined that my vents are clear, the gas lines are in good condition and there were not leaks and the gas smell was coming from the dryer.  I called Sears and they scheduled a repair visit.  Approx. 2 weeks later the repairman came and changed the valve and left.  I ran the dryer an hour later and the gas filled the drum and vent again.  I called for the repairman to return but they scheduled a visit for approx. 2 weeks later again.  

I went ahead and called for the gas company to come out and check the dryer again and they determined it was the dryer and the dryer was on recall.

The Sears repairman came and smelled the gas and ordered new parts from where the gas goes into the dryer to the valve.  3 boxes of parts.  Approx. 2 weeks later he arrived again with an older more seasoned repairman who thought it unnecessary to change all the parts.  He changed some parts and left with the ones he didn't use.  He ran a cycle and didn't detect gas and left.  I also informed him that the gas company said the machine was under a recall.  He was unaware of the recall. The recall recommended a valve change which was done on the first visit.

Approx. a week later about November 11, 2017 I  ran the machine on a 40 minute timed cycle on medium heat and after 30 minutes opened the dyer door and was hit with the strong smell of gas.  My clothes smelled like gas too!

I called for a repairman again and Sears said they will not send someone out if there is a gas leak.  I had to explain again that the smell is there only when the machine is running and the gas company had been out twice already and determined it was coming from the dryer.  I had to insist they schedule a repairman visit.  Another 6 days from now is the date!
justification: The incident involves a gas leak from the dryer, which poses a significant hazard but has not resulted in injury or death.

incident_description:
I'm writing this while some smoke still remains in my home after the Fire Department spent 30 minutes blowing out as much as they could.  My 5 year old Maytag MGC2TC has had serious problems almost from installation.  The furnace failed the first time within 4 months of installation.  The house was barely above freezing when our son stopped by to check on the home.  He brought in 4 electric heaters to keep the home from freezing until American Heating & Cooling of McHenry, IL could fix it.  They stated the thermostat wasn't compatible with the new furnace and installed a temp.
Almost exactly a year after installation, the cooling unit malfunctioned and American installed a new Honeywell Vison Pro thermostat for $245.
The blower motor failed in year 3 and was replaced after several days at no charge.
The heat exchanger burned through in year 4 and American disassembled the furnace and left us with no heat for 3 weeks in late October 2016.  When I complained about them not returning, they said I was rude and wouldn't return to fix the disassembled furnace they had sold me 4 years earlier.
I called the distributor and got the heat exchanger replaced under warranty.  I was charged $475. for labor and shipping of the part.
They furnace failed to work again about 2 weeks ago in early October.  A "high pressure sensor" needed replacing for $145.
This morning I was awakened by our alarm and fire detection system.  The home was filled with grey smoke coming through the heat registers.  There were no visible burn marks on the outside of the furnace, but it was hot to the touch.
When the furnace was opened up by a Maytag repairman, he found the plastic tray under the a/c evaporator coil had melted and burned when it landed on the furnace burner tubes.  He checked all of the high temperature shut off switches and all were operating and none had been triggered.
Had we not had a fire alarm system, the smoke and eventually the fire would have possibly taken our lives.
justification: The incident involved a furnace malfunction leading to smoke filling the home, posing a serious risk of injury or death, though no actual injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
We have a Sloan Flushmate lll and were unaware that this product had a recall. It appears the tank can explode causing the lid and parts of the tank to become projectiles. I noticed my water bill going up and today 10-30-2017 I watched videos on youtube to troubleshoot the issue. I only became aware of the recall by accident after I troubleshot the issue of the toilet hissing (I did not hear it because I am a disabled veteran). I had to put my face next to the tank to find the leak, which I did. It was coming from the top right side of the tank (this pressurized tank is inside the porcelain tank.)
There was water squirting to the rear of the toilet tank and that's when I looked up the part, this is when I found the recall which was dated Jan. 23rd 2014. And it states "Hazard:
The system can burst at or near the vessel weld seam releasing stored pressure. This pressure can lift the tank lid and shatter the tank, posing impact and laceration hazards to consumers and property damage." I had my face on top of this tank !!!
They are sending replacement tank but I could have been seriously injured troubleshooting this problem.
I never received a recall on this product.
justification: The incident involved a recalled product with potential to cause injury, but no actual injury occurred.

This mold started about 2 years ago she has cleaned it thoroughly but the mold only returns.  She believes breathing this can present a serious health hazard.  She stated that she contacted the retailer and was advised that her model was not part of a recall.

Consumer stated that the washer is unsafe and should be recalled.

Actually longer than 2 years but she just kept trying to clean it.

Consumer is quite concerned about this as she feels it can be harmful to her health.  This odor is quite strong.

incident_description: Samsung Washer Model #WA456DRHDWR is only 4 yrs old, washing 2 simple couch throw blankets and 3 towels that were covered in plaster dust from a construction project at the house.  This was my third load in the day - all of a sudden heard loud bang and strange beeps that I had never heard before.  Next in racing to the laundry area, I step in water and water now covered entire room!  Today Sears A&E Service comes stating the pump blew - so a new one needed, they asked about heavy load - I stated I used the right load wash because I WENT THROUGH WITH THE RECALL THAT WAS SUPPOSED TO PREVENT THIS EXACT THING from happening!  IT DID NOT HELP!  The items needing washed were divided into groups as mentioned this was already my third load, and I wasn't done yet.  I asked about why isn't this a covered service when I know this seems to be part of the dangerous symptom these machines were being recalled on.  I am told it is my fault?  How?  I'm washing clothes?  This makes no sense!  The service provider then tells me "oh as it turns out the pump now works but when the original pump busted (I assume he is referring to the famous rod that is supposed to hold the pump in place?) that it killed the board and we now needed a new board put in for a grand total of $636.  How is it that this company keeps getting away with producing faulty products - I got lucky as nothing exploded through the machine and did not cause injury but it could have!  And, how does the company live with its self that a 4 year old machine can be named "scrap" after such little time frame?
justification: The incident involved a machine malfunction causing water damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) given the recall history and user's experience.

incident_description: Purchased the Frigidaire dehumidifier FAD504DWD in July 2014 through Staples. Product will not turn off, compressor continues to run and has to be unplugged. Thank goodness I went into the basement to check on it because it was extremely hot. I tried to turn it off and nothing happened. I have it plugged into a surge protector so I quickly disconnected it before it caught on fire. The heat it was producing was so bad it steamed up my glasses as I got near it. I googled my problem and found the recall website. Mine was not on the list since it was made 2 months later than the recall cutoff date (Feb. 2014). These units are a fire hazard! Thank goodness I caught it before it burned my house down!
justification: The dehumidifier malfunctioned and overheated, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or fire occurred.

I pulled the plug out of the wall and let it cool down.

incident_description:
Cutaneous exposure to a yellow dye on 10-2-2017 that dissolved out of yellow leather work gloves and into my hands, apparently due to perspiration.  Subsequently I found that my wife had some weeks before worn these gloves while doing garden work at home and noticed how her hands had also become stained with the yellow dye that had dissolved out of the gloves after only using them for a short period of time.  I also wore these gloves while doing gardening in our back yard and did not use or come into contact with any other chemicals or other potentially harmful substances. Within 24 hours of using these gloves I began to suffer from headache, eye irritation, urinary problems and severe fatigue.  The dye remained in the skin and nails of both my hands for five days, resisting both immediate and frequent washings with soap and water to attempt removal. These gloves were purchased locally from a Harbor Freight Tools retail store as product item attached and sewn into the glove: Full Grain Work Gloves #63153.  I contacted Harbor Freight Tools of Camarillo, CA by phone (888-866-5797) and spoke with their representative, [REDACTED] about the possible health risks to people wearing these gloves if the bright yellow dye proves to be an aniline dye.  Subsequently, the dye was confirmed by email to me on 10-11-2017 to be aniline dye by HFT Product Support representative, [REDACTED].

I found that other HFT consumers had submitted complaints of yellow staining of the hands from these same gloves, and therefore, I submitted a negative comment to the HFT web page for this product, stating that there was a potential health risk to wearing these gloves, due to the aniline dye not being properly "fixed" to prevent it from being absorbed into the skin via hand perspiration.  I did not complain of the symptoms I had experienced with this comment submission.

HFT screened out my consumer comment from their product web page, of a potential for toxic exposure to consumers that I submitted with this product on or about 10-11-2017.  They did email to me a boiler plate response within 24 hours thanking me for my comment and stated that their screening policy is to allow/disallow consumer comments to their product web pages within a period of 7 days.  It has now been 2 weeks since I submitted my comment, so I am assuming they chose not to let their consumers know of the potential dangers of their product.  However, I did find a few days after submitting my comment, they continue to market this glove on their web site but with a different photograph of these #63153 Full Grain Work Gloves accompanying their product description.  The photograph has been changed to a different photograph of a tan color leather work glove that does not match these bright yellow gloves at all.  Also, for over a year, I have seen a thick cloth work glove of the same bright yellow hue marketed in several HFT retail stores.  I do not know if the dye in those is also able to penetrate the skin. 

I contacted my state office of epidemiology (in New Mexico) within 48 hours of recognizing that my symptom complaints were related to the use of these gloves, and even though I am a medical doctor, the person with whom I spoke was unable to complete their toxic exposure report because I had not actually seen a doctor.
justification: The incident involved exposure to aniline dye causing headache, eye irritation, urinary problems, and severe fatigue, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Samsung washing machine drum spinning out of control periodically making it necessary to stop the machine, hand ring items, drain water in spin cycle. Damage to sides of washer and dryer due to the washer banging against the washer.

incident_description:
Running the Soleus Air dehumidifier Model # GL-DEH-70EIP-6 in my basement to lower the humidity level.  When opening the basement door, I smelled a strong "hot plastic" odor.  Tracking down the area where the odor was the most prevalent, led me to the dehumidifier.  No real warmth on the outside of the housing.  Turned the device off and removed the bucket from the unit. I could see that plastic behind the bucket had begun to deform and melt.

Given, I bought the unit because of the internal pump, I don't need to empty the bucket and visit the dehumidifier often.  Mainly only to clean out the air filter section.  I am glad this issue happened while I was home as I do feel continued operation of the dehumidifier was a fire threat.
justification: The dehumidifier showed signs of melting plastic, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or fire occurred.

Upon further investigation we find a Kenmore de-humidifier with black soot marks on its sides near vents, and melted plastic inside after removing water drawer.  Black plastic behind water drawer has approximately 2" hole melted in it directly in front of coil unit in back, and is located juts above and to the left of aluminum label on unit. To get to the spark plug to remove the spark plug wire you are in contact with the cover.  I attempted to remove the spark plug wire and was cut in my right finger about 1/2 inch.  The fact that the sharp cover is so close to the spark plug approach is not safe and the cover should be modified to make it safe.

incident_description:
In 2015, I had a professional electrician install 2 new hardwired smoke/fire detectors.  
They are: KIDDE Dual Sensor Smoke & Fire hardwired detectors Model #PI2010.
Last evening, I had a small, but smoky, incident in my kitchen - burning food on the stove. I was in another room, unaware of the problem.

Since the ramifications of this apparent product defect are so serious, I am notifying your agency as well.  I hope you are developing an official record of any reported incidents of this model.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.

incident_description:
In October and November of 2016 I purchased and installed Pergo laminate flooring made by Unilin company and also known as Mohawk flooring.  Several months later I began to have cold like symptoms and developed skin pimple like eruptions on my little finger and lower arm that persisted until I tore up the floors in August of 2017.  The upper respiratory distress and green phlegm it produced were supposedly treated by three different rounds of zithromyacin which did not cure the symptoms.  Finally in June of 2017 my physician told me she believed I was suffering from an allergy.  By this time I was no longer able to walk my usual two miles on most days due to chest tightness and difficulty breathing.  So after walking through my house trying to figure out what I had purchased recently, of course the floors became the obvious culprit for causing my symptoms. These symptoms all went away gradually after I tore out the floors.  After very close examination of the flyer that came with the flooring product, in a small print paragraph  at the very bottom of the flyer labeled" For Minnesota Residents Only"  was listed ALL of the symptoms I had been suffering for many months: itchy red eyes, cough,  skin irritation, respiratory difficulty, etc.  That warning was NOT on the flyer the consumer could see, but on the underside of the flyer included with the flooring and not able to be read before purchase of this flooring.  In fact on the flyer that was visible to the consumer in very large bold print it read MADE IN USA so I was tricked into believing it was also safe because of that word choice.  Had the warning and words "contains formaldehyde" been on the visible portion of the flyer I would not have purchased their product.

I spent $1440.00 on the floors and neither Lowe's who sold the flooring nor Pergo (Mohawk/Unilin) will stand behind their product and refund me my money.  They claim that the product meets California Carb regulations and therefore can be legally sold.  But I could not live in my home for months without illness, so how good are the regulations?
justification: The incident describes persistent health issues including respiratory distress and skin irritation, which qualify as injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific circumstances of the product's hidden warning.

Heater used under normal conditions (in a residential home) and in prescribed manner.

incident_description:
During normal use, the battery pack on my Drill Master 18volt cordless drill exploded.  Fragments of the casing were projected at my body at a velocity too fast to see and produced a noise which was mistaken for a gunshot by my neighbors.  
Injury resulting from the failure:

1. Pain was experienced as at least one fragment made contact with my groin.
2. When inspecting the battery pack after this incident, my fingers were burned due to overheating of the battery pack.
3. The battery pack contains cadmium, a toxic metal, which was dispersed into the environment and my home resulting in skin contact with and inhalation of cadmium.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including pain from projectile fragments, burns, and exposure to toxic cadmium, but no death was reported.

incident_description: We purchased Chinese laminate flooring from Floor & Decor last year to install in a house we purchased for my daughter and grand daughter to live in.  Ever since the flooring was installed the house has had a horrible odor and they have had allergies and eye irritation. We have been trying to find out the cause and was unaware that we purchased a product that contained high levels of formaldehyde until we needed a small area of the flooring repaired in July. The installer brought it to my attention that the smell could possibly be coming from the flooring.  I researched the product and SKU# to find out that this particular product was under investigation and had class action lawsuit against Floor and Decor.  I was never informed of the problems and did not get to participate in the lawsuit. I filed a claim with Floor & Decor and they agreed to reimburse me for the materials (no labor). The cost of the materials is minimal compared to having it removed and reinstalled,  plus what we paid to originally have it installed. We can not afford the expenses that are needed to replace the floor. They sent an inspector to the house to inspect the flooring and any other conditions that may be causing the problem They also sent samples to a lab to be tested for formaldehyde.  I ask for a copy of the reports, but they refuse to send them to me.  I am worried that my family is in great danger breathing in the gases long term.
justification: The description reports allergies and eye irritation, which are injuries caused by the formaldehyde in the flooring.

incident_description:
SoleusAir/Gree Model #SG-DEH-45/70  overheated, started to smoke white and black.  Internal flames started within three minutes of the unit turning on.  Within 4 minutes, the flames extended beyond the unit, and within 6 minutes, the flames reached 4-5 feet.  The unit exploded.  

The unit was in the basement when I heard popping sounds, saw the smoke and flames, and ran the unit upstairs.  The flames started as I was unlocking the front door and the unit blew on the front porch. The entire house was filled with black smoke. Three fire departments responded to the scene.  I sustained smoke inhalation and minor burns on the arm.  The porch brick was scorched.
justification: The incident involved flames, smoke inhalation, and minor burns, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the detailed description of the event.

incident_description:
My husband and I build a Westport Home in Commercial Pinot, OH and moved in June 2, 2017. We received a letter from Westport on July 29, 2017 advising us that the floor joists they installed in our home were emitting an increased level of formaldehyde gases. For the 10 wks we were living in the home we experienced dizziness, coughing, heavy chest, burning eyes and throat, & runny noses. Additionally, our pets experienced similar symptoms. We thought it was due to possible allergies. However, since I recently had an allergy test prior to moving in and it was negative, and we hadn't experienced these symptoms prior to moving in,  we knew it was a direct result from the formaldehyde gas emissions. Since receiving the letter, we've been living in a hotel (along with most our neighborhood) for approx. 4 wks now with no real resolution. Westport is only giving us 1 option to remediate, which is to apply a latex type of paint to the floor joists to minimize the emissions of the gases. This is NOT a proven method nor has it been approved by anyone (EPA, etc) to work or withstand the test of time. At this time, only the manufacture, Weyerhaeuser, allegedly "tested" this product and claims it works. However, since it's already been proven that Weyerhaeuser failed to properly test their flak jacket formaldehyde coating used on the floor joists before they sold it to the public to be installed in approx 2200 homes, jeopardizing our health & property values, How can we trust that they properly tested this so called "paint remedy"? How long will the paint minimize the fumes? How long did they test the paint solution? If it fails, how will we know (particularly on finished bsmts) unless we start getting sick again? If what they are alleging that "the formaldehyde gas emissions dissipate in 12-18 months after the paint", then why is there a "lifetime warranty"?, Why is the Dept of Agricultural and EPA saying that Formaldehyde CANNOT be encapsulated?
Lastly, If there's no definitive proof the paint remediation works, why isn't Westport offering alternative options that other builders are offering (scrapping or dry ice-blasting the formaldehyde off or replacement of the joist)? True and full remediation would include the full removal the joists that are emitting cancer causing carcinogens and replace them with a clean safe product to ensure the safety of 2200 families affected. That's what we paid for and that's what we should demand Westport to deliver so we don't end up like the people affected by asbestos who no have cancer.
justification: The description reports multiple health symptoms (dizziness, coughing, burning eyes, etc.) in both humans and pets, indicating injury due to formaldehyde exposure.

With my new home I purchased a range hood Brand is Kitchen Aid model is kxw9736yss. 

The switch that controls the operation of this unit is their part number Item #: 1878923 "control panel". It has all the electrical connection to control the fan, and lights housed in a plastic case. This plastic case failed after 1 year and 3 months of service. It cracked, fell apart and exposed wires. I purchased a new one which failed after 6 months of service. 

This is an electrical shock hazard. I looked at reviews of this product and see several referencing failed control panels.

Kitchen aid needs to issue a recall and get these fixed before someone gets electrocuted.
justification: The incident describes a recurring electrical hazard with exposed wires, but no actual injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Our Rheem Performance Platinum water heater's control unit unexpectedly an spontaneously caught on fire on Sunday, July 9th 2017 at approximately 12:10AM.  Significant damage was done to the control unit and water tank.  Our fire alarm went off and we smelled a burning smell.  After evacuating the family and pets from the house we called 911 and had the fire department come to the house.  While waiting for the fire department I grabbed a fire extinguisher and did a quick look through the house.  I discovered open flames coming out of the control unit panel of the hot water heater in our basement and was able to use the fire extinguisher to put out the fire and disconnected the electrical from the home power panel.  The fire department arrived, inspected the water heater and surrounding area and confirmed that the fire was a direct cause of the water heater control unit.  

After looking online, I discovered that our water heater model has a recall.  However, the manufacture date of our specific water heater is outside of the date range of the recall.  The recall states that it is for manufacture dates from January 2014 to December 2014 and our water heater was manufactured on March of 2015.

I am writing this to make you aware (and hopefully the rest of the public) that the issue described in the recall notice has happened to my water heater which was manufactured outside of the recall date range.

My water heater details:
MFR:  Rheem
Model Description:  Performance Platinum
Model Number:  XE80T12EC55U0
Serial Number:  M131519941
Manufacture Date:  26March2015
Capacity:  80 Gallons
Install Date:  16April2015
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recall context and the incident happening outside the recall date range.

incident_description: On 7/6 my sons were running a load of wash in our LG top load washing machine, the load became unbalanced and then made a weird noise and they thought something snapped. The load of wash then drained and my sons waited until we came home to review washer. I reviewed known issues online and realized the washer was part of a recall which I had not seen before. I called LG and they are sending someone to look at unit but I am concerned as the online reports indicate they just adjust the speed so it doesnt spin as fast. This will not resolve my issue and we dont want anyone to get hurt with this product or damage to my home .
justification: The incident involved an unbalanced load and a potential mechanical issue, but no injury or damage occurred. The recall and online reports suggest such incidents are likely.

incident_description:
I serve in the Fire and Life Safety Division For Rockingham County Fire and Rescue in Rockingham County, VA.  My job responsibilities include Public Safety Education and Asst. Fire Marshal duties.  A member of our department recently brought to me a Smoke Alarm that an elderly family member had in their home.  During a visit he stated he pushed the test button on the alarm and nothing happened.  He inquired to the elderly family members about the alarms and they stated that they were recently purchased from a local Costco store.  They are 10 yr. battery alarms.  First Alert Model No. P1210.  He took the alarms down and found on the back of them that there was a deactivate switch which when operated permanently disables the alarms.  I would imagine the purpose of this switch is that when the alarms get to the end of their life and begin to chirp you can deactivate them before tossing them in a trash receptacle.  The alarms are designed in a way that once the switch is placed in the deactivate position they should not be able to be placed back on the mounting bracket.

Here is the issue... these alarms were somehow deactivated before being placed in service.  The elderly couple did state they had difficulty placing the alarms on the mounting bracket, however, were eventually able to get them mounted to the bracket.  All along they thought they had the protection of smoke alarms when in fact they were disabled.  While I understand the intent of the deactivation switch I feel this creates a problem in providing a false sense of security.  I feel these units provide a major safety issue.  Though as public safety educators we preach that people need to check their alarms using the test button monthly, fact is few follow through with this lesson.  Within that group are elderly and those unable to understand the safety message due to language barrier.  These are the ones that probably need to have the most guaranteed protection.  If a deactivation switch is going to be included, which personally I am not in favor of, I feel there should be some other way that is more obvious in indicating the alarm no longer works or provides the protection those using it may need to count on.

If you wish to speak further with me I am certainly willing to discuss this issue.
[REDACTED PII]
justification: The incident involves smoke alarms being deactivated before use, creating a false sense of security, but no actual injury or death occurred.

They state that after skin exposure, one should ÃÂFlush with water. Remove contaminated clothing.ÃÂ It does not state that skin/inhalation exposure can be potentially life threatening. Encouraging consumers to seek care could also ensure proper follow up with a hand surgeon when appropriate to prevent further morbidity. 
Also, the product lists ÃÂrubber glovesÃÂ as appropriate protection for the use of this product. Latex gloves would not be adequate and further guidance on appropriate protection is not listed. The decision regarding transfer and to perform these procedures would have been better informed if the product were properly labeled.  
	The Carolinas Poison Center discussed this case with the director of the UNC Burn Center as well as the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services. All involved parties involved are in agreement that further action should be taken to prevent this from happening to future consumers.

incident_description:
I used a Harbor Freight Portable band saw (item 62800) for several typical homeowner's activities including trimming oak flooring, galvanized pipe and metal fence posts.  Attempting to cut these materials with the saw led to overheating, rapid deterioration and finally shattering of the included blade.  The 14tpi blade that comes with the saw is the subject of a Safety Warning on page 10 of the Owner's Manual because it should only be used for cutting aluminum, plastic and soft wood.  However, the optional blade kit purchased with the saw contains only 3 more 14 tpi blades. The heavy duty 24tpi blade recommended for cutting steel in the Safety Information is not available and never has been available according to either my local Harbor Freight store or Customer Service at the main office in Camarillo, CA.  

Once the 90day warranty period has elapsed, the saw cannot be returned under any circumstance for either refund or for store credit.  Harbor Freight (Katrina at Customer Service, Camarillo) disavows any responsibility for injuries due to blade failure because I didn't use the appropriate saw blade.
justification: The incident describes potential injury due to blade failure, and the likelihood is possible given the misuse of the tool with incorrect materials.
