incident_description:
Made-in-China Zapals Carbon Monoxide Detector does not function reliably.

Ref.:  https://www.zapals.com/lcd-display-carbon-monoxide-detector-co-alarm.html?geoip_country=US&gclid=CjwKCAjw2s_MBRA5EiwAmWIac9U_IEQD7bUd05r3IAVA_v1p3aw8GkncxjzbPZsiSuf5OWILrpXJxRoCq04QAvD_BwE

The Zapals Carbon Monoxide (CO) detector arrived about 2 weeks after the online order was submitted.  A critical part required for its operation fell out of the box.  This was a sign of shoddy manufacturing and lack of quality control.  I figured out where the part belonged, a spring-like dual terminal used for making contact with two of the three batteries required for its operation.  But when I put it back together the detector functioned intermittently. The spring contacts would not reliably stay in place causing intermittent operability.  I sent seven emails Zapals with photos showing and describing the problem and asking for a replacement.  Zapals refused to replace the faulty CO detector and asked instead for proof of the intermittent operation including a video of the malfunction as it occurred.  Zapals knows well I cannot supply them a video of the intermittent operation, an effort way exceeding the cost $6.99 of their CO detector.
As this product directly impacts safety-of-life I ask you to test this product's reliability and safety of using this product for detecting deadly Carbon Monoxide before allowing Zapal.com to continue exporting this made-in-China product to the U.S.
justification: The CO detector's intermittent operation poses a potential safety risk, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Description of product; Gas Changeover Kit - natural to regulated LP/Propane. Manufacturer; Allied Air Enterprises. Manufacturer's part #13X57.   
    This kit is used on some gas fired residential central heating systems. In my case, furnace model #A96UH2E030B08S-01 installed on 5/05/17.
     The problem is that the gas valve inlet brass fitting supplied with this kit, split open on the morning of 6/18/17,  allowing LP gas to leak into my home.  The installation instructions are quite specific as to the tightness of inlet pipe and fitting and not to use a channel lock pliers or pipe wrench on the brass fitting. I believe I followed the directions when installing it.
My qualifications are that I had my own heating contracting business for 35 years until 2015 and was a licensed plumber for 25 years until 2016. 
     The problem with the brass fitting easily splitting open can be understood by a visual inspection of the failed part. The material used is not substantial to begin with. Then a 1/2" pipe thread is tapped into the fitting at the factory, whereby more of the brass material is removed, thus further weakening the fitting. 
     I believe this fitting should be immediately recalled and replaced by a fitting with a greater wall thickness.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to a faulty fitting, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Purchased a new 11KW emergency generator with automatic transfer switch manufactured by Generac Power Systems Inc, S45 W29290 Hwy. 59, Waukesha, WI 53189.  Model #0064410, S/N 9382786.  In September 2016, notified Generac and the Underwriters Laboratory (UL) which Listed the unit that the factory-installed power conductors from the generator's stater to the unit's output circuit breaker (CB) were not installed according to applicable UL Standards.  The power conductors are #10 AWG (fine-stranded).  The line-side terminals on the CB are UL Listed for a minimum wire size of #8 AWG and not Listed for termination of fine-stranded conductors.  All of the strands of the conductors are not terminated.  This creates high resistance terminations which will heat up and eventually burn off, thus making the generator inoperable for its intended use to provide power to my home for well water, heating, and lighting during a utility outage.  It also creates the potential for a fire within the unit which may cause an explosion from the generator's propane fuel supply.  Since September 2016, UL has investigated this matter; however, neither Generac nor UL will disclose UL's Findings to me.  Generac has recently informed me via email that it has received UL's Findings and recommendations for future manufacture of generators; but, Generac will do nothing to correct the aforementioned defects on any existing generators it has in the field, including mine, even though it is still under warranty.  I believe that UL's initial Listing of the generator was flawed and/or it was not auditing Generac for compliance.
justification: The defect creates a potential for fire and explosion, which could lead to injury or death, but no actual incident has occurred yet.

Usually it doesn't take very long, but this time it was taking longer to heat up. incident_description:
I purchased an upright vacuum cleaner online from Dirtdevil.com on 4/22/17.
It was brand new, not reconditioned.
I had it for 4 months, and soon after using it , it seemed like it was getting harder to push.
And then one of the wheels kept falling off.
To make matters worse, I was vacuuming up slivers of my vacuuming.
It was falling apart as I was using it.
So far, this is not your concern, until now.
I was really curious as to what was going on with my brand new vac, so I investigated further.
On my model, the motor housing sits very low to the ground, almost touching the ground.
The main wheel assembly is located too close to the motor housing.
If you run the motor for about 45 minutes, the housing gets so hot you can hardly touch it.
Bad enough that the motor is already almost touching the ground, but now the heat of the motor softened the plastic assembly that holds the main wheels.
Because the plastic has been softened due to the heat, the wheels tilt inwards like a car when it has Toe In.
The Toe In puts excessive wear on the contact surfaces between the wheels and the main body.
On one side, it looks brand new. 
On the other side, it is almost worn away.
This is a very dangerious situation for several reasons:
-the motor gets extremely hot. Is there no thermal cut-off
-the motor sits too close to the groung. Being so hot, this is very unsafe.
-after a few uses, the wheels develop Toe In, and now the motor actually scrapes the carpet.
TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE
Not to mention that the vacuum is tottaly useless with the motor scraping the ground and the eheel falling off.
All this from a 4 month old vacuum.
I contacted Dirt Devil and described the problem in great detail.
It fell on deaf ears.
They told me to take it to an autherized repair shop, which I did. All Brands vacuum in Lyndhurst Ohio.
They will not honor the warranty, they said it was just cosmetic, I believe.
Cosmetic? With a wheel falling off, and a very hot motor dragging on the ground?
I don't think so.
I was just going to toss it in the dumpster, and chock it up to poor business practices.
But I don't want to see somebody get hurt, or a fire start because of this.
I asked Dirt Devil if I was the only one complaining about this. She skirted the issue.
Its time for a recall.
They have a fee models where the motor is like mine. I bet they all have the same problem.
justification: The vacuum cleaner's design flaws pose a risk of injury due to overheating and mechanical failure, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: I used Febreze Fabric Refresher, the variety called "Free/Nature," in a spray bottle to clear the odor from a smelly co-worker (!!) after he left my office.  I bought it specifically because of this person, who is a smoker.  I sprayed it where he had been sitting and walking, then turned on a small fan and stepped out of the office for about 5 min.  Came back, turned off the fan, and went back to work at my computer.  Within an hour I noticed that my face was feeling numb under my right nostril.  I took some [ibuprofen] in case it was a fever blister emerging, but the numbness spread to underneath the left nostril.  I tested myself for stroke and assured myself that wasn't happening.  About an hour later, my entire upper lip was swollen, and I felt as if my nasal passages were becoming swollen, so I went to the emergency room (St. Anthony Healthplex North in Oklahoma City).  They too evaluated me to rule out stroke, then concluded it was an allergic reaction, gave me some prednisone and a prescription for that steroid and recommended antihistamines.  The Febreze is the *only* change in my use of consumer products in recent weeks, and this incident was the first time I ever used it.  I can provide a photo of my lip, which was swollen 3x the normal size the morning after the exposure.  The swelling and pain began to resolve after more steroids and about 24 hours after the onset of numbness and swelling.
justification: The incident resulted in an allergic reaction requiring emergency room treatment, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rare (1) as this is an unusual allergic reaction to a common product.

incident_description:
The smoke detector in question was noted next door to an apartment fire that occurred in our city on June 16, 2017.  The apartment had a moderate about of smoke inside when fire firefighters entered. This apartment was unoccupied at the time of the fire.  During a routine search of the apartment it was noted that the smoke alarm was not activated.  This information was reported to the fire investigator on scene.  
The smoke detector was examined in place by the fire investigator.  The smoke detector appeared to be properly installed and positioned on the wall of the apartment. The test button was first depressed at which point the alarm sounded.  A secondary test was initiated with a smoke alarm tester. This test also activated the smoke alarm.
justification: The smoke detector failed to activate during a fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred as the apartment was unoccupied.

incident_description: Black mold/mildew problem.
justification: Black mold/mildew can cause respiratory issues and allergic reactions, qualifying as an injury. The likelihood is high due to common environmental factors.

incident_description:
During transport of item from store to destination, my 8 year old picked up the item off the floor of my vehicle to look at it. When looking at the item he pinched his finger in the blade tensioner device integrated into the handle causing a severe skin tear resulting in the need for 3 sutures to close the wound and stop the bleeding. A smaller finger could have easily been partially severed by this product.
Most concerning to me is the product was still in all original packaging and had not been opened. I feel very strongly this product is dangerous as packaged and will result in future injuries to others. While a blade guard is put in place during manufacture, no such safety device is attached to the tensioner device on the handle to prevent pinching. The tensioner handle is under great pressure and snaps closed with significant force if partially opened and allowed to close on it's own.
I assert the current packaging creates a false sense of security and feeling the device is rendered safe as packaged. Sadly, I feel the device would be safer if it had no blade guard at all, as it would signal a reasonable person to handle the item with extreme care and treat it as a dangerous tool. While I think the overall design is dangerous; it's current "safety" packaging makes it even more dangerous by instilling a false sense of security on the part of the purchaser.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe skin tear requiring medical attention (3 sutures), indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the product's design flaw and false sense of safety from packaging.

incident_description: I purchased a battery operated drill from Harbor Freight some months back the cordless drill "Drill Master" serial number 3633831601 drill has been used and battery recharged numerous times. This routine use was no different than several other times, the battery exploded while in use. The percussion from the batteries explosion knock me backwards, the drill from my  hand sending debris from the exploding battery case into the wall, across the garage to the far wall into the ceiling. The most dramatic and possible injury was to my left arm where a small piece of plastic was lodged into my arm, of which, I promptly removed, with other pieces striking my upper hand and left arm . Being retired military the sound from the battery explosion was if a grenade went off.
justification: The battery explosion caused injury with plastic pieces lodged in the arm, indicating a severity level of 3. Such incidents are rare but possible with faulty equipment.

incident_description: I stepped up onto the center of the step stool with my right foot and the top suddenly gave way. My foot fell through the broken top and the sharp broken edge of the hard plastic sliced my ankle and shin. I want to the emergency room and received wound care including stiches. The max. load specified on the product is 300 pounds, I weigh 116 pounds.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring emergency room treatment and stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The step stool failed under weight well below its specified maximum load, suggesting a possible manufacturing defect, making recurrence unlikely but not rare.

incident_description: I purchased a Great Northern Premium Quality Shaved Ice Machine and it did not come with a safety shield.  Using the shaved ice machine, the big block of ice flew out of the machine and struck me in the torso causing bruising.  The damage could have potentially been lethal or deadly.  A safety shield would have prevented this.  When contacting the manufacturer they say some of the machines now come with a safety shield and that I would have to purchase it.  This doesn't seem appropriate as a safety shield should have been included with their shaved ice machines.  Please help.
justification: The incident resulted in bruising, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the event and the potential for recurrence without a safety shield.

incident_description:
This is a GE Dehumidifier  Model No. AHG40LBG1.  It was not among the two sets of recalls recently issued for other GE Dehumidifers; however, it seems to have the same type of defect.  The unit was plugged in and operating and caught fire internally.  Burned oil and black soot is clearly visible on the unit and it emitted a foul, burning rubber smell.  This fire endangered a 2 year old boy.

incident_description: Whenever I am exposed to Downy dryer sheets I develop headaches, dizziness, confusion, and fatigue. This seems to occur more often with the scented version. I am concerned because these products are in wide use and difficult to avoid. They are also difficult to remove. If I do much as sit on a chair where someone has used this product and it ends up on my clothes it's almost impossible to remove. Please look into the chemicals that are being used in these products and their safety. I am not the only person who has this reaction to said products.
justification: The individual reports symptoms like headaches and dizziness, indicating an injury level severity, and mentions the issue is common and difficult to avoid.

incident_description: Yesterday morning (15 Aug 2017) I was standing on our Werner 6 foot Type II Medium Duty/Commercial use non-conductive Fiberglass stepladder.  When suddenly it collapsed under me in a split second throwing me off to the right.  Both cross braces had bowed with vertical cracks in the fiberglass appearing where the cross braces are attached to the ladder. The skin on the back portion of my right elbow was shaved off  apparently by the bowed out cross brace on the right side of the steps as I fell to the ground.  I also hit my head on a lawn border brick.  I was taken to the local emergency room by ambulance where my complex lacerations were sewed up.  I have always been safety conscience and ensured the ladder was fully deployed and on level ground.  I weighed 231 pounds yesterday which is 6 pounds over the specified weight limit of 225.  I believe I was standing on the third step from the ground and in the process of moving to the fourth step.I do have pictures of the ladder following its collapse, but am having trouble uploading them to your site due to the special Flash Player requirement.  This morning I spoke with an individual in the construction business regarding my accident yesterday.  He informed me the construction company he was with threw out this stepladder as soon as it reached five years old.  Apparently, they were aware that the fiberglass in this ladder tends to lose its strength and fatigue over time resulting in this type of accident.  My ladder was probably about eighteen to nineteen years old.  The individual looked at my damaged ladder and said the same thing had happened to him where the cross-braces suddenly buckle outward, and their attachment points in the fiberglass exhibit vertically running cracks.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring emergency room treatment, and the description suggests that ladder failure due to aging is a known issue.

incident_description:
26 April 2017

To Whom It May Concern:

Please find enclosed, for your careful consideration and inspection, one Rowenta iron model# DZ5080, Ser# 0908.
As you can see, by the enclosed photo's, my wife suffered burns because of your defective product. The burns, although painful, were treated at home.
Rather than running to the nearest law firm, I tried unsuccessfully to reach you via the internet and only recently found a phone number finally reaching you folks.
Our primary concern lies as follows: We are both retired and have no children living with us. Consider a younger women and a small child, standing or crawling near the ironing board. When your iron shorted out, the iron went flying and with a child near by, the outcome could have been catastrophic.
I have my opinion and belief on why this problem happened. The opinion comes from many years of buying and using wire products.
We appreciate you taking the initiative to inspect this iron and what you decide is up to you. I can assure you, after buying and using several Rowenta Irons, my wife does not abuse your product. She uses only distilled water and currently is using a Rowenta Promaster.

Thank you for your consideration in this matter.

Best regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in burns that required home treatment, indicating an injury but not death.

incident_description: Installed Schon Oak floors from Lumber Liquidators in April2016, started seeing black discoloration/ mold spread throughout the entire installed house. Also used Exmore adhesive and moisture control exactly as directed. Mold keeps getting worse. Filed complaint with lumber liquidators. Never received a response after several phone calls and emails over a 3 month period.

incident_description:
Injured party was doing a home inspection, as the injured party is a home inspector.  Injured Party was using a Little Giant Alta-One Ladder.  When injured party was coming down from roof, the ladder collapsed. Injured party fell backward and struck his head on the concrete driveway. incident_description: I have a Hoover Wind Tunnel vacuum model UH70130, MFG Code E10A.  The retractable cord mechanism does not work correctly and catches the cord or the cord get's stuck when trying to pull it out causing the cord to become frayed/worn in areas and the electrical wires to become exposed.  While vacuuming my home on July 10, 2017 I was holding the cord in area where the cord is worn and experienced a small shock while operating the vacuum.  I did not have serious injury but obviously concerned so I looked into similar problems with this vacuum and found that other Hoover vacuums have been recalled for same problem, just not my model.  I contacted Hoover customer service and was told that the cord damage is just normal wear and tear.  My vacuum works just fine other than the defective cord and retractable cord mechanism, which I do not consider normal wear and tear, especially in light of other Hoover product recalls for similar defect.
justification: The user experienced a small shock due to exposed wires, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue with the cord mechanism is a known problem, making recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Glacier Bay touchless faucet model 67536-0508D2 has a design flaw. It burnt my hand. The touchless mechanism only turns off the flow of water to the head. The water valves on the faucet are left on. This allows the hot and cold to mix since the hot water is under pressure. If the handle is left on any temp besides full cold, when you turn on the faucet HOT water comes out. I can explain this further. I've tried to talk to Glacier Bay (Home Depot) about this but they won't let me speak to anybody with authority or understanding on how the faucet works. If you look at Delta's touchless faucets they come with check valves on the HOT and COLD lines to keep this from happening.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury due to a design flaw in the faucet, which allows hot water to unexpectedly flow.

incident_description: I use this tumbler as does numerous others (as I have read about the same problem from them on other websites) to tumble our ammo brass to clean it for reloading. What happens with the Harbor Freight 5lb model is after about 45 minutes of run time the center threaded rod gets extremely hot, I burned my fingers to where I had blisters! Then on the 2nd time I made sure I was not over the weight limit of 5lbs total media and brass, I turned it on, I remained in the area working and the tumbler sounded strange so I turned around, the lid came off, the bowl was spinning, dust and media was going everywhere, I went to turn it off and went into a coughing fit from the dust, the center rod yet again was extremely hot!, the wing nut and metal washer that goes on top of the lid to keep the lid on was hot as well. I waited for 15 minutes to let the rod cool, as far as I could tell the motor was not overheated, but it is completely covered so have no idea, I tried to move the bowl it was secured and did not move as it should. As hot as this gets so quickly I feel it is a fire hazard, other companies build these tumblers are very similarly made but they are ran for hours a day, as like 2 hours, 4 hours, some report they tumble for 6 hours at a time and have no problems. All that own Harbor freight tumbler have these problems I described to you, some fixed theirs by replacing the small center rod with a larger sae threaded rod and use a nut to lock down the wingnut for the lid. I have owned this tumbler for about 2 weeks, I am to try to replace it tomorrow.
justification: The incident resulted in blisters from burns and a coughing fit from dust, indicating injury (severity 3). The problem is reported by multiple users, suggesting it is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
For my toddler I researched window protections for the second floor of my home. This research led me to the Andersen Window website that offered as a child safety device the window opening controls for the casement windows in my home.
https://parts.andersenwindows.com/LearningCenter_WindowSafety.html
https://parts.andersenwindows.com/detail_9051542__w_safe.html

I ordered these items for all my casement windows upstairs. Unfortunately, as soon as they were installed my child was immediately able to depress the button for the device that releases the window limits. This button is another safety device to allow an adult to quickly open the window completely to escape through the window during an emergency. Sadly, this safety feature creates a situation where the child safety feature is now removed. A child that pushes this button and successfully releases the limit will now be able to open the window and fall out.  

I immediately called the president of the company's office to tell them about this problem and the potentially devastating consequence. Another "executive" returned my call but concluded that he was unable to help me because the company was required to have the release safety button. I believe that a parent unaware of how easy it is for a child, mine is 17 moths old, could override this window limit and be seriously hurt or killed.
justification: The incident describes a safety device that can be easily overridden by a child, posing a risk of serious injury or death, though no actual incident has occurred yet.

GE service tech inspected the machine on 5/22/17 when the motor began to smoke, spark, arc, and catch on fire when power was applied. incident_description: This incident concerns a Leviton Decora dimmer switch/stepped fan speed control #6620. This switch has been installed in my home with no problems for over 10 years until last night's(June 2nd) incident. The fan was operating on low speed and the light was on; when my wife went to turn out the light she noticed the switch was hot to the touch. Upon investigation, I saw that the fan control no longer worked and I was unable to turn off the fan; I also smelled burning electrical. I immediately turned off the breaker and removed the switch from the wall and capped off the wires. At this point the switch was still hot enough to burn my hand. I feel that we were very lucky to have found this problem before the house caught fire. Luckily the only damage is the Leviton switch in question and repairs have been made. The fan/light switch was wired correctly but it did not trip the breaker when it failed, I had to turn the circuit off. curious, I removed two small screws to examine the inside of the failed switch. The outside case is melted and the inside components look like someone attacked it with a welder; completely burned up. I still have the unit.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning switch that caused overheating and potential fire hazard, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
Once in 2014 and now, two Rheem thermostats failed closed on this water heater keeping the element continuously on creating scalding hot water dramatically overheating the thermostat area. In 2014 it was the lower thermostat and now it was the upper thermostat.

I reported the safety concern about this overheating failure mode to Rheem in writing both in 2014 and now and asked whether the thermostats had been redesigned for a safer failure mode e.g. open circuit. Rheem failed to answer those questions and based on this recent second dangerous failure it's evident that they have not corrected the safety issue.

I have photos of both failures including the charred heating element head in 2014. This time we detected the scalding hot water and I disconnected the upper element fed by the defective thermostat in time to prevent a possible fire.

Today [REDACTED] from Rheem ([REDACTED]) told me that our 2 closed circuit thermostat failures were rare and usually caused by a electrical surge that welded the contacts closed. I told him that was not the case with us because we have a whole house surge supressor and no other device was ever damaged by any surge.

He said Rheem uses the same bimetallic thermostat design everyone else uses with two exceptions for this plastic tank water heater;
   1. They use a brass rod to transfer heat from the water to the thermostat
   2. The Marathon thermostats are calibrated differently for the plastic tank
justification: The incident involved overheating and scalding hot water, which could lead to injury or fire, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
GE Top Load Washer Model #GTW460ASJ2WW- Serial #VF193086G has a chronic problem which, in my opinion, is a shock hazard and a fire hazard.  For the last 6 months the spin cycle has been faulty. Service was called 6 months ago, 2 months after that and now again.  The situation is the spin cycle stops working. This requires the user to manually turn the machine to the rinse/spin directly. Sometimes this works and sometimes it does not. The hazard part occurs when the machine, after sitting untouched for up to 12 hours, decided to turn on all by itself. The machine bypasses the input panel, turns off all lights and doesn't allow input, then turns on the pump. There is no water in the machine but the pump runs until the user unplugs the machine. Even if you let the machine sit for hours unplugged, then plug it back in, the pump starts pumping without the presence of water. The pump gets extremely hot and the smell of electrical wires overheating is noticeable. Fortunately, we were home each time this occurred or had arrived home to find the machine pumping nothing but in time to prevent a short circuit and/or fire. The most recent incident occurred in the early morning hours while we were still sleeping. We woke up to the sound of the pump actively pumping away and almost overheating. Had this occurred during the night, it could have caused a fire and/or death.

There should be an immediate recall of this model, as there has been a recall of similar GE models due to the fire hazard and potential loss of property and/or life.
justification: The incident describes a chronic issue with the washer that poses a fire hazard and potential for death, though no actual injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Whirlpool Electric Dryer motherboard burned and melted.  We had just run two loads and then there was no power to the dryer. Upon further inspection and removing the control panel it was discovered that the motherboard had burned and melted.

incident_description: I put a normal load of whites in my Samsung Front Loading washer Sunday afternoon, June 4th.  It ran.  I came upstairs to check it as it was unusually loud.  When I saw it it seemed to have an unbalanced load and was jumping around, which was unusual.  The timer indicated 4 minutes left until complete.  I walked away and came back immediately and the machine indicated off.  I opened the door to pull the load out and put it in the dryer and smoke began pouring out of the machine drum and the back of the machine.  I frantically pulled the clothes out of the washer.  Smoke continued to pour out faster and filling up our utility room.  My husband helped me pull the machine away from the wall and we immediately unplugged it.  The smoke continued for a good 30 minutes or more after we unplugged it and did cause our smoke alarm to go off.
justification: The incident involved smoke pouring out of the washing machine, causing the smoke alarm to go off, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung clothes washer several years ago that has since been recalled. Last year we had someone come out and repair one of the parts that was on recall, after the part fractured and large amounts of water leaked out on our laundry room and kitchen floor. The washer has also been shaking excessively for over a year. Last week we filed a service request through Samsung, and someone came out to install stabilizer bars in the washer to fix the excessive shaking. That same day, after the repair was completed, the washer overflowed while performing a cycle, and part of the washer broke during the spin cycle. At the same time, the washer started to fill with water and flooded my entire laundry room and kitchen, and ruined the drywall and flooring in the laundry room and part of the kitchen. This is my second time having the washer repaired--the first time being last year after a similar situation occurred--though not as severe as last week's account (as mentioned above). I now have a laundry room and kitchen that isn't usable and we have to have the floor and drywall replaced. We recently had two contractors come and give estimates for the repairs, totaling over $15,000.

Please note that as of last weekend my family and I had to vacate our home for an emergency flood restoration company to come in and extract excess water from the floor and wall surfaces in hopes of saving some of the insulation and foundation. This was also a necessary step before contractors would begin any repairs. We we will be living with friends, family, neighbors, and in hotels for the next 3-4 weeks until the work is complete.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and displacement, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: While in use on regular setting, steam valve on Maytag dryer failed flooding the drum including load. This caused eventual overheating and actual fire.
justification: The incident describes a failure leading to a fire, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: We bought a gree dehumidifier model # GDN70AI-A3 BB2A. It started to make a weird noise, as if short circuit. We also noticed water leaking (a small pool by the time we saw it) and ice building in the back of it so we stopped using it right away.
justification: The dehumidifier malfunctioned with noise, leaking, and ice buildup, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
My Hamilton Beach Iron Type 186, Model 19800 Series A1621DX caught on fire while it was plugged in and turned on. On June 3rd, 2017 I went to use my iron like I normally would do. I plugged the iron into the outlet; turned the iron on and poured water into the dispenser at the top of the iron. 

Immediately after which the top of the iron plate began to get real hot. The tiny holes started shooting out the water and the water was spattering on the wall. Then some grayish smoke came streaming out too. Of which caused my smoke derectors to sound off. 

Just aproximately 2 weeks prior to this incident. I went to use this same iron at the same location. After I had plugged the iron into the outlet, the red light came on and the iron heated up like normal. After I began ironing the shirt most of the way. Then the iron's light went off and the light inside my closet blinked out completely. 

So I unplugged this iron and plugged it into another outlet inside the same bedroom. The iron's light came back on and I was able to continue using the iron and complete my ironing. However, the iron had blown the fuse to the previous outlet. I had to reset the breaker inside the fuse panel. I had to run out and buy a new iron. Which is working just fine in that original outlet that the Hamilton Beach iron caught on fire.
justification: The iron caught fire and emitted smoke, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
Model WGD9750WW0  Whirlpool Duet Steam Dryer

During the course of regular laundry, I noticed a burning smell when I went into the laundry room.  In the dryer were blankets used for our dogs, so no chemicals or anything like that ( as when washing cleaning rags).  The smell was profuse, and I opened the dryer for further inspection.  I could still smell a smokey smell, but the lint collection was clean and thought maybe something caught and resolved itself.  Later, though, the smell remained in the dryer, and upon further inspection noticed the rear vent or stainless grate on the back wall of the interior was covered in brown/black burn such as you would find on a stove burner.   Checked online for recalls, and although a big mess in the UK, I did not find one for the US.  I have never had this happen before, and am disheartened to see several complaints about this happening on this forum, and yet Whirlpool does nothing?  It was quite the investment a few years back for this washer and dryer set, and I would expect better quality. Quite the hazard in a second-floor laundry room for a gas dryer.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and visible burn marks, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The first time I used my GE gas dryer, I smelled gas.  The dryer is in the basement and gas was smelled in the bedroom above the dryer.  I called factory service, and  they said it is normal to smell gas when the dryer starts up but if I smelled it more than that, I  should call my local gas company.  I called National Grid and they came to the house and the technician said the gas dryer was hooked up correctly and that there was no gas leakage anywhere in the gas lines of the house.  The dryer cycles on and off, and each time the heat cycles on, I smell gas.  This is not normal.  I feel that no gas appliance should emit a gas odor at any time.  I have had gas dryers for 50 years, and never have had this problem.  I am waiting for an appointment from the Factory Service to come and look at the dryer and give me a solution to this problem.
justification: Gas smell was detected but no leakage was found, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Purchased Infinity-Z 56 in. to 60 in. x 72 in. Semi-Framed Sliding Shower Door in Brushed Nickel// 
Door Glass Thickness (in.) 1/4" from Home Depot on July 22, 2017 and picked up the door on August 5th in the morning from home depot.   Installed the door frame and non movable glass side on morning of aug 6th.   All of it was installed and my son and husband were putting the door that slides in,  when the door exploded in their hands.   Glass was on top of my cabinets, on top of the door,  stuck in the stone tile in the shower, glass behind the door,  glass in the bedroom,  up on the bed, under the bed,  it was even inside the baskets in the bathroom on the shelf.    .Husband and son sustained cuts... had to dig glass out of many of the cuts.   Did contact Home Depot...insurance claim filed.....  waiting to hear from Home Depot's  insurance  ( manger told me it was Liberty Mutual).
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the husband and son, requiring medical attention for glass removal from cuts.

incident_description: Tumble dryer went on fire.  Seen smoke coming from it and flames in drum.  Dealt with ourselves as small fire due to spotting it straight away.  This is an indesit model that was modified during there programme.  A while later my dad did another repair on machine, unconnected.  During this repair he found burnt fluff on heating element so again contacted indesit who sent a 2nd engineer out who again did further modification.  Fire occurred after two modifications.  Reported to indesit who plan to come out this week to investigate.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the tumble dryer but was dealt with immediately without injury.

incident_description: My BernzOmatic propane torch started to leak propane through a small hole on the gas valve.  The manufacturer claims that this is a safety in the event of an internal seal failure.  I purchased this torch approximately 8 years ago and used it less than 10 times and it failed.  The manufacturer seems to have no issue with their product failing after minimal use and feels that venting flammable gas in the direction of the operator is a good safety practice.  After I discovered the failure I discontinued use and detached the propane cylinder.  I have read on-line about others having the same issue.  The torch is black plastic with a blue plastic grip and a red gas valve and ignition trigger.  The blue handle says BernzOmatic and the number 307 is stamped near the ignition trigger.  There are no other markings on the torch and no safety instructions or mention of the safety relief on the gas valve.
justification: The incident involved a propane leak but no injury occurred, and online reports suggest it's a recurring issue.

incident_description: Our Maytag clothes dryer, model MGDB835DW has a very sharp, pointed protrusion that is part of the door latch mechanism. It is triangular in shape and resembles a knife blade in appearance. I have been scratched by it several times, but this morning I received a deep cut with substantial bleeding on my forearm as I transferred laundry from my washer to the dryer. I would suggest that Maytag redesign the door latch using a more rounded protrusion. I can provide a photo of the item if desired.
justification: The description reports a deep cut with substantial bleeding, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
This report is about the Samsung washing machine WA422PRHDWR/AA.
I own a summer home in [REDACTED], I usually rent it for a few  weeks out of the year mostly on the summer season, meanwhile I stay at the little cottage at the back of the property. 

Only a couple of months after we bought the appliance, it exploded awhile the cleaning lady was doing the laundry, at that time I didn't think was an accident because she quitted at the same day, afraid I'd accuse her for breaking the machine, since she knew it was brand new.

 This past Saturday, July 29, 2017 my guest (she is a public figure and for that reason she doesn't want to be identified), was laundering the 2 months baby clothes (on quick washing settings), prior their checkout;
 "AT the spinning mode" as she describes; the machine started making a loud noise and the entire first floor was shaking like there was an earthquake going on, she ran to check what was going on as she stood up in front of the machine to turn it off it sounded like an explosion and the machine jumped and turned sideways towards her as someone just flipped the machine against her. She has breast feeding and now is so fering with her right side breast got infected on the past few days. She just shared the Samsung washing machine incident with me today as I inquired about the damaged appliance and mentioned deducting the repair amount from her security deposit, other than that she'd never have told me, and the poor women still don't get that fact is not her to blame; Since I didn't know about the incident or about the recall I had the local appliance store technician to put the top together again; the machine is throwing all kind of codes, it's dented, it restarts over and over again at the spinning circle, the drum is totally detached and unbalanced , it's wasting my expensive water and sewer, and mostly is ruining my rental business, I have seasonal contracts for the rest of summer,I need my machine fixed ASAP, so I called my local appliance guy again, after charging $50 a visit he told me there are several recalls for several models of Samsung washers with the very same problem and he's not certified for Samsung recalls and "GOOD LUCKY TO HAVE IT FIXED BY SAMSUNG"!
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the guest, specifically an infected breast due to the washing machine explosion, and the machine's malfunction is described as a known issue with recalls.

incident_description: One year after we moved in our Rheem 80 gallon water heater failed.  It was replaced under warranty with a RH Q361304515  80 gallon unit.  4 years later we have no hot water (5/27/17).  After investigating the circuit breakers and the unit, we found that the control panel had caught fire and almost completely melted.  Since it is still under warranty, Rheem is replacing it however, they only make 50 gallon residential units now.  They would not upgrade us to a commercial unit which is what we need for our size house.  Our options were to install a 50 gallon unit an modify it with a mixing valve or upgrade to the commercial 75 gallon unit with $700 out of pocket expense.  Their customer service and warranty center were of no help!!! So frustrating.
justification: The control panel caught fire and melted, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
After completing my shower, I proceeded to glide open my semi-frameless, tempered glass shower door to reach for my towel.    

While standing inches away and facing my shower door to exit, I was frightened by a load bang (sounded like a gun shot) followed by an intense propulsion of glass fragments and shards towards my body that completely covered me and entered my mouth.    My feet and hands began to bleed profusely.  

After contacting the store where purchased (Lowe's) and the manufacturer, I was made to feel that I did something wrong.   

The manufacturer acknowledged that this type of incident does occur, but does not know how to prevent.   The manufacturer is aware of the potential failures that can occur but choose to withhold the information from the consumer.    There are no warnings on their products or website.   By withholding information, I was not able to make an informed decision about my safety.  

 I learned after the fact there is an after market safety film that can be applied to glass to prevent it from "exploding" in the event of the product failing.    The manufacturer failed to inform or offer such product resulting in my injuries.
justification: The incident resulted in bleeding injuries from glass shards, indicating a severity level of 3. The manufacturer's acknowledgment of such incidents suggests an occurrence likelihood of 3 (possible).

incident_description:
I have had a 120 volt First Alert Carbon Monoxide Alarm in my 40 foot diesel motorcoach for several years as a backup for a similar battery operated product.  I keep it in the coach to provide a margin of safety when I am operating a permanent propane powered Onan Generator on board. The model number for the Alarm is FCD2N and the serial Number is A549265.  The order replacement for the Alarm is "B".

This week while the motorcoach was in the Parliament Motorcoach facility in Clearwater, Florida for maintenance, the Alarm suddenly started smoking on the wall next to the stove while workers were coming in and out of the unit. They grabbed the unit and tossed it out the door and could only pick it up when the electrical board inside had finally cooled.  The heat was so intense that a small section of the rectangular plastic box was melted....but otherwise there was not indication of any problems, like at the electrical plug on the wall or the electrical prongs on the device.  An electrician quickly checked the wall plug for problems and found nothing.
justification: The incident involved a smoking alarm but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the likelihood of such an event is unlikely given the lack of prior issues.

incident_description:
Delta Bathtub Shower Door Model # SDGT060-CL-R , consists of 2 clear sliding glass panel doors within an aluminum frame.  Glass panels slide using small wheel assembly at the top of the panel that fits into the top frame, as well as the bottom of the glass panel is guided by a small plastic guide installed on the bottom frame.  The frame and doors were professionally and correctly installed according to the instructions provided with the unit, leveled, etc.  However one of the glass panels (the one that is used the most) consistently comes off the track, causing the person using it to have to replace the glass panel door wheels back on the track at the top of the frame.  

This time, while attempting to replace the panel back on the frame, the glass panel "exploded" into a zillion pieces, causing personal injury from glass cuts on hands and arms, accompanied by a fair amount of fright and shock (emotional, not electrical).  This happened without the glass panel being subjected to any undo stress, impact or other "reason" that it should have disintegrated as it did.

While I am able to purchase a replacement door, they are only sold in pairs - not convenient or right.  Besides that fact, I am unsure as to whether these tempered glass panels are safe!
justification: The incident resulted in personal injury from glass cuts, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the glass panel consistently coming off the track and the unexpected explosion.

incident_description: Purchased a Harbor Breeze fan from Lowe's a few years back and had it installed in my daughter's room. She used the fan every night when she slept but one morning when the fan was off the paddle broke at the metal leaving a jagged metal Edge at the end of the fan blade. She was unable to use the fan after that but we still used the light on the fan. One night while she slept another paddle just broke again when the fan was not on and hit her while she slept.
justification: The fan blade broke and hit the daughter while she slept, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: at 6:00 am this morning the Combination Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm on the third floor went off.  It went off three times within a half hour.  I vacuumed the unit because I'd had the windows open earlier in the week  and there was a lot of pollen in the air.  Later in the day it went off again.  At 4:00pm it went off again and I called my electrician, who made the installation two years ago.  A short time later it went off again and continued beeping and alerting "fire" for over a half hour.  My electrician showed up and he removed the outer twist of casing from the unit and pushed the hush button.  He advised that I should inquire if there was a recall on this model.  I did.
justification: The alarm repeatedly went off, indicating a potential issue, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
While cutting with the saw positioned in the bevel angle of 45deg. The part known as the Fence in its default out of the box position can cause a collision between the blade and the Metal Fence (See user manual for definition of fence ), 

The interference between the blade and the fence caused the Plastic Lower guard to shatter and to cause the guard screws and a spring to separate from the guard area and act as a projectiles.
The Saw blade was able to interfere with the guard and to shatter the plastic guard.


I returned the saw to Harbor freight and they replace the saw. Before I started to use the saw I tried all of the difference angle and this is when I identified the potential issue.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage and potential projectile hazards, but no injury was reported.
