incident_description:
The shower door was being installed.  The first panel was installed, and when the second panel was lifted  and getting ready to install, the door shattered in the contractor's hands and literally exploded.  The glass dropped  in segments while shards flew everywhere shooting sharp glass into all the areas in the vicinity.  It pitted the first panel of glass that was installed, but that panel did not break.  It deeply pitted the aluminum track on the bottom.  It put a gouge in the newly installed vinyl plank flooring.  And most importantly, it cut the hand of the contractor.  He was able to pull a piece of glass out of his hand.  He is okay.  No stitches were required.  It was a very frightening experience!  There were three of us in the room.  Fortunately no one else was injured, except for myself a few days later when I stepped on a small shard of glass in my heel, but was able to remove it without incident.  I shudder to think what would have happened if I would have been taking a shower at the time!  And I thank God that none of us were seriously injured.  The panel that was already in place shielded the two of us standing outside the shower when it exploded.

The door was approximately 74x60", with thicker glass.  Arizona Shower Door brand from Lowe's.
justification: The contractor suffered a cut on his hand from the shattered glass, which qualifies as an injury, but no stitches were required.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the laundry detergent made her ill.  She had used it to wash her bed linen and after lying on the linen, she developed a rash, became dizzy and had to go to the emergency room 7/3/17.  She was advised by the physician that she had an allergic reaction, she was treated and released.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller stated that the warning on the product advised to wash thoroughly if the contents touch skin and feels that this detergent is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The caller experienced an allergic reaction requiring emergency room treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
While at work, my Universal plug in carbon monoxide alarm began beeping that the battery was low.  I live alone but my daughter happened to stop by at lunch time and heard it sounding.  She went to the plug and found the device smoking and burned and the wall outlet was melted and burned as well.
It looks as though the alarm overheated and would have caught fire had my daughter not stopped by.
justification: The device overheated and caused damage to the outlet, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Samsung washer exploded and blew the top off. Researched and found out that it was recalled. 
The incident caused a hole on the wall, also crushed the exhaust pipe connected to the dryer, and also knocked off the vacuum cleaner that was in the room which is not working at the moment due to the incident.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description:
Shopping at home Depot, put a piece of metal edging on cart, piled mulch on top so metal edging would not slide off the cart.  ( had that problem the last time purchasing this product)
The product is sold in 8ft. lengths and the carts to transport the metal are 3ft to 5 ft. long.
So the product overhangs on any cart to transport.  The product is "RAZOR SHARP"  on one side of the edging.  No warning signs saying this is sharp.  No gloves provided, no SAFETY GUARD on the very sharp edge.  I walked away from my cart, went to get more items, upon returning to my cart, I walked into the metal edging and sliced my leg to thew bone.  I was taken to the hospital via ambulance, and received 6 stitches in my lower leg.  I am scared for life, and have over $3000.00 in medical bills both Home Depot (seller of the product) and Collier Metal Specialties, LTD( manufacturer) REFUSE to take responsibility for selling a dangerous product.  It is concerning as a consumer to experience an incident with injury In-which could of been avoided if a PLASTIC GUARD was on the SHARP METAL EDGE.  The product cannot be transported from shelf to cash register WITH OUT sustaining an injury.
Please investigate the sale of this product.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring hospital treatment and stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is assessed as 4 (likely) due to the inherent danger of the product and lack of safety measures.

incident_description:
Utilizing the Skilsaw 3800 compound mitre saw and making a straight-cut on a piece of 1x3 whitewood, the lower guard assembly broke and came in contact with the blade during use causing shrapnel to fly in all directions.  The potential was that severe lacerations could of occurred - fortunately no medical injuries were incurred 

Reading a similar recall, the notice for the Skilsaw 3316 sounds identical to this models issue.  https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2012/bosch-recalls-skilsaw-miter-saws-due-to-laceration-hazard

I have owned this specific model for some time and was purchased from Lowes.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure causing potential for injury, but no actual injuries occurred, and a recall notice indicates this is a known issue.

incident_description: Washer model Samsung WF 328AAW/XAA 02, serial no. W01F54AZ200115Z got in fire on 07/14/2017. It happened at the last spin. I called proffesional appliance specialist and to repair I need to change the drum and it will cost $ 600.00 to $700.00.
justification: The washer caught fire, causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: Brown Hampton Bay ceiling fans that I just purchased have stopped working after a few months and a couple of the light bulbs burst and broke. The ceiling fans are installed in my living room and bedroom. When turning on the fan in my bedroom the light burst and sent glass flying everywhere. And the unit in my living has stopped working all together.
justification: The incident involves broken light bulbs and non-functional fans, but no reported injuries.

incident_description: This about the Samsung washing machine recall. I had the first step done, protecting the top of the washer from flying off and hurting me. But it continues to shake violently and does a poor job on heavier items that need to b e washed. Towels and sheets. I called them and it seems because I had the cover secured they will not continue to support their product and I can not get a replacement. So they did not fix it completely. Not Fair
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washing machine that shakes violently but no injury is reported.

incident_description: Was washing clothes on heavy duty cycle of our Samsung top loader washer model WA48J7700AW/A2. I heard you colostomy. During wash the top exploded off of the machine- moving machine at least a foot. The impact also caused severe damage to dryer. Dryer was pushed on its size by impact. Frame of washer completely destroyed by impact.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
I was retracting the power cord on the steamer using the button with one hand and it wound too fast, causing the cord to fly up and the prongs to strike my head between my eyebrows, causing a small gash, swelling, and pain.  

My Little Steamer Deluxe 
Ingenious Design
justification: The incident resulted in a small gash, swelling, and pain, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: The top loading washing machine shakes excessively during every spin cycle due to the load being off-balance, This causes the drum to hit against the insides of the washing machine and causes the whole unit to scoot along the floor.
justification: The washing machine shakes and moves, but there is no mention of injury or harm, only potential for minor property damage.

incident_description: I was standing squarely on top of the two step gorilla ladder while cleaning a kitchen cabinet when the ladder collapsed. After a sudden whoosh  I was on the floor facing the opposite direction. My foot was bent sideways and looked very distorted. I dragged my self into the living room and called 911 as I felt that I may go into shock. I was brought to the emergency room and give pain meds, and x-rays and crutches which I was too wobbly to use. At home I realized I had a giant bruise on my breast and a small bruise on my thigh. I was told to follow up with a podiatrist. Turns out that my foot was dislocated, a lys-franc injury and my breast had an apple size bruise. I was unable to return to work as an occupational therapist due to being nonweightbearing. I have post traumatic arthritis and unresolved lemon size hematoma and smaller cysts in my right breast. My son brought the ladder back to Home Depot and they put a sticker on it an told him they would send it back to the manufacturer. He then called the number on the ladder and was told over the phone that the company would pay for time out of work and medical expenses. Since I did not know what to ask for or the extent of my disability I sought the assistance of an attorney. Currently the company Tri cam is offer very minor compensation for a serious and life altering injury. Subsequently I found out that the three step ladder had been recalled with the same defect, the top platform cracks and the ladder falls completely flat, I fell three feet! I hope you can prevent others individuals from serious injury by looking into recalling this two step ladder.
justification: The incident resulted in a dislocated foot, hematoma, and other serious injuries requiring medical attention and time off work, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the ladder defect was known and similar models had been recalled.

incident_description:
The submitter said he installed 80 units, 1 on each condo porch, at the address below. The submitter said he began installing them in September 2016 and stopped in early January 2017.

The submitter said approximately 25 units have burned up or stopped working. He said the first incident occurred in September and then a few weeks later a few more burned up.

The submitter then contacted the firm and informed them of the incidents. The submitter said the firm was unresponsive.

In early January a firm local sales Rep., [REDACTED] witnessed the submitter remove one of the units that had burned up. The submitter said the Rep. advised him the unit was properly installed. The Rep., sent he unit to their testing lab and received notice that the unit was too damaged to determine a cause of failure. 

(April 2017) The submitter said he filed a complaint with National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) regarding the defective units. He said shortly after he filed the report the firm contacted him to obtain more information and denied receiving a complaint about the issue. 

The firm asked the submitter to send them the units but the submitter only sent 5, some that were burned and others that just stopped working. The firm advised the submitter that their findings showed the units had been excessively wet and caused the failures. However, the submitter states these units are water resistant and are intended to be used in outdoor outlets. The submitter believes the firm is denying that there is a defect with the units. The submitter believes the units should be tested by CPSC and recalled. The submitter said he removed all 80 units and has 5 in his possession. 

The submitter said he installed another brand GFCI receptacles on the condo porches approximately 5 weeks ago and there hasn't been an incident.
justification: The incident involves units burning up or failing, but there is no mention of injury or death, only property damage and potential safety concerns.

incident_description: The main control panel on my home Maytag Electric Dryer, Model MEDX700XLO, purchased in 2011 shorted out and caught fire. Lucky it did not cause damage to the laundry room or my home other than soot staining on walls and very strong electrical burning smell. I have pictures of the dryer and the burnt control panel.  Most concerning is happened when the dryer was not in use and only our two dogs in the house! I have submitted a complaint on Maytag USA customer support website.
justification: The dryer's control panel caught fire but caused no injuries or significant damage, only soot staining and a strong smell.

incident_description:
On the 4th of July we had family visiting us.One of the family members used the shower and as she was getting out of the shower and opened the shower door (Tempered glass),the door shattered  and crumbled down within seconds into multiple small pieces spontaneously..she sustained severe laceration to the wrist ,barely missing the nerve and arteries,multiple small laceration on forearm, and on both lower extremity.she was bleeding profusely, was rushed to the emergency room by ambulance where her bleeding was controlled, and the laceration was sutured both on her wrist and lower extremity.She continues to have persistent pain and numbness in her Right hand, and being a right handed person has difficulty to do her daily activities.This incident has traumatized her not only physically but emotionally, and has put a burden on the family economically as she is not able to do her job.
These are expensive glass shower enclosures , the manufacturer does not mention anywhere there is risk of spontaneous shattering of these doors.Since we have small children at home we do not want this incident repeated , and want the public to be aware of the possibility of of  glass shattering  and severe injuries.
Kindly make sure that this message gets out  to the public, and the manufacturers keep their customers well informed regarding the risks.
justification: The individual sustained severe lacerations requiring emergency medical attention and continues to experience pain and numbness, impacting daily activities.

incident_description: GE top loading washer model # GTW460ASJ6WW caught fire under control panel during initial period of wash cycle.
justification: The washer caught fire, which is a significant incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Purchased approximately 60 of these First Alert smoke detectors model #P1210 from Costco between Feb 2015 to June 2015.  Right out of the box we tested each unit and 8 of the 60 did not sound the test alarm.  We returned those and got new ones from Costco.  Installed the product in 30 different units.  Got a complaint within a couple months that 1 unit didn't go off only 10-15 feet away from a kitchen fire but fortunately the detectors further away went off.  Started testing the units with smoke and found many (maybe 1 in 4) took 2-4 minutes to go off when placed in a covered bucket with smoke and some didn't go off at all.  Took those back to Costco and got replacements.  Starting within months of install and over the last 2 years tenants have complained about the units beeping for no reason and not being able to stop the noise so they take them down.  We have replaced approximately 50% of the units now and are no longer replacing with First Alert.  I recently called the company to see if the units were recalled and apparently they were not recalled but they are sending me replacements of an updated model to replace the most recent batch that we picked up from tenants.  I will test them to see if they work out of the box but I'm not sure I will risk using them with tenants.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning smoke detectors, which could have led to injury or death but did not in this case, hence severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reports of failures over time.

incident_description: The glass enclosing the shower area in the Master Bedroom bathroom shattered with no warning.  It was installed at the time the new home was finished, 7/23/2015. (The glass was in place for about 2 years)
justification: The glass shattered unexpectedly, posing a potential injury risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: At approximately 1:00 p.m. the emergency dispatch received a smoke alarm activation call to a residential home.  Upon arrival FD personnel did not observe a fire.  During the examination of the hardwired smoke alarms, black soot was observed around the base of the alarm.  The alarm was removed and the internal components appeared to have short circuited.  A new alarm was installed in the old alarm location.  The old alarm had a replace by date of 2016.
justification: The incident involved a smoke alarm malfunction with no fire or injury, but required replacement of the alarm.

incident_description:
This consumer and her son each purchased a propane use space heater in December 2016 from in Gallipolis, Ohio.
She  never set her heater up, however her son did sent his up in the garage under his apartment set on the 21' x 21' concrete floor in the middle of the floor.
The heater was hooked to a 5 ft propane supply via copper tubing and had already used two tanks of the propane but during the third tank and the heater running approximately one week the caller's son came home to see that the heater was burned and had approximately 6 to 8 inch flames coming from the bottom of the heater.  He ran and turned the propane supply off which extinguished the flames.
The caller is reporting this as a severe fire and burn hazard due to the fact that if he had not come home when he did then the flames could have become much hotter, their three vehicles in that garage could have exploded and the house could have caught fire.
There are no injuries to report
The caller and her son took both the heaters back to the seller and received refunds for both heaters.
The seller contacted the manufacturer but has at this time not heard back from them.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the potential for significant damage if not for timely intervention.

incident_description: I have a front load washer that has mold on rubber seal.  It is hazardous & unsafe to my health.  I had contacted co. & Better Bus. Bureau few years ago.  The co. only said I can pay for replacement at my own cost.  I also contacted a lawyer for class action suit but nothing ever was resolved.  I cannot afford to replace so I still live with this condition.  I simply wanted it replace at no cost to me.  after the fact they suggest to leave door open but it is too late for that!  I think it is a safety hazard too leave door open for young kids & pets.  I have tried all suggestions to clean with bleach & vinegar but nothing works.  Even wipe it down after each use which is time consuming & doesn't work.  I would appreciate any help in this product defect.
justification: The presence of mold is a health hazard, but no injury or death has been reported. The issue persists and is likely to continue affecting the user.

incident_description: Found a melted down Federal Pacific panel in a residence.  Breaker failed to trip causing the main service cable to melt down along with the breaker. The wire reached temperatures hot enough to weld the main lug to the copper wire.   Active sparking and glowing wires when arriving at the property.
justification: The incident involved significant electrical damage and active sparking, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: A homeowner had an unattended cooking fire in a pan.  She stated the house was filled with smoke from burning oil. The fire produced both smoke and flames, But it was the thick smoke that alerted her.  She stated there was so much smoke, that after smothering the fire in the pan, she had to open every door and window in the house and "air it out"  She stated that neither one of her smoke alarms ever activated.  The alarms were First-Alert P1210 that were installed in 2016. I had tested the alarms prior to the incident. This was done the first week of January 2017 and then again on January 10, 2017. Both times the alarms sounded when the test button was depressed.  On May 3rd, after being notified of the incident, I manually tested the alarms again.  They sounded.  I then sprayed the units with canned smoke.  I tested each alarm.  With the one by the bedrooms, when I used the normal amount of smoke that is usually used for testing, it did not alarm.  I then sprayed what I felt was excessive smoke, and it finally alarmed.  No matter how much smoke I used, I was never able to get the other unit to alarm.
justification: The incident involved a cooking fire with significant smoke but no injuries or deaths, and the smoke alarms failed to activate properly.

incident_description:
My Samsung washing machine is part of the Samsung safety recall. I purchased the washer at Home Depot in [REDACTED]on July 6, 2014 and had it delivered to my summer home in [REDACTED] on July 28, 2014. At the time of the recall announcement last November, there wasn't much I could do about it except to register with Samsung, because I was already in [REDACTED], my state of residency. When I spoke to someone at Samsung, I asked how long I had to request a rebate. I was told they would kindly extend my deadline to June 1, 2017. Later, I read on the paperwork they sent me that I really have until next November, one year after the recall announcement!
I arrived back in [REDACTED] on May 2, 2017. I am afraid of my Samsung washing machine due to reports that they may explode at any time. It makes terrible noises and really has never gotten my wash clean even though it takes over an hour. I purchased it because it was advertised that it could wash a king size comforter. Samsung now says you can only wash bedding on what was the delicate cycle. That will not get it clean or wring out the water. 
I purchased a matching Samsung washer and dryer set. I do not want another Samsung product. I need to purchase a new washer ASAP. Another brand will not match my dryer. I am not happy with the performance of the dryer either. It does not sense when the load is dry as was advertised.
I feel Samsung should refund me for the total purchase of the set. They knew about the issue the washers were having even before my purchase.
justification: The description mentions a safety recall and fear of explosion, but no actual incident or injury has occurred.

incident_description: The lip (edge around the top) cut my finger rather severely resulting in a trip to the urgent/emergency care. The pad of my ring finger was sliced and fell off - doctors were unable to sew/glue and had to use bonding "fake skin" to heal. Finger was in a cast for a week and may have little/no feeling for several weeks or months.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe finger injury requiring urgent care, fake skin bonding, and a cast, indicating significant harm.

incident_description: After taking an evening shower, I went to open my shower door and upon moving it slightly it shattered into thousands of pieces.  I have had the product since June of 2015 and have used it without issue.
justification: The shower door shattered but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: In June of 2016 NRG HOME SOLAR Co. installed solar panels on my homes roof. During the following winter after every snow storm snow would avalanche from my roof onto my front entrance without warning. Weight of the snow and speed and height of the fall was so dangerous that I could no longer use my front entrance. NRG after many calls and contacts refuses to correct this danger.
justification: The description indicates a dangerous situation with potential for injury due to snow avalanches, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
On Sunday evening, January 29, 2017 I put two sets of sheets and pillow cases into my GE top loader to be washed and went into my kitchen (which is next door to the laundry room) to get some bills paid.  After a while I began to smell a terribly offensive odor coming from the laundry room. I opened the laundry room door and the smoke was so thick you could not see.  I immediately opened all the doors and windows and called the fire department.  The fireman pulled the front panel of the washer off and showed me where oil which had leaked from the washer had caught fire from the motor and was burning the rubber belt causing the heavy smoke. They extinguished the fire and told me to leave the windows open all night.
The next day I call my insurance company to report the fire. They sent professional cleaners out to suck out the smoke (which took several days), remove the damaged clothes hanging in the room, the smoking washer and assess that else needed to be done.  A week or so later, a friend told me to check the internet because she had read that since 1998. GE has had problem with washers catching fire. I did and saw the info about GE washers catching fire. I called the telephone number listed to report such happenings and told the gentleman to whom I spoke what had happened.  He asked for the model and serial number of the faulty washer, which I gave him.  He was very upset that the washer had been removed and told me if I had the burned, smoked up washer brought back, had it re installed and let GE uninstall it, they would give me a new GE washer.  I didnÃÂt know whether to laugh or cry.  I had not asked for a new washer and would even consider installing another GE, but to suggest that after days of coughing from the smoke, that I re-install the faulty washer, was ludicrous.  I did however want them to see the faulty washer. The firm that had removed the washer sent GE pictures and offered to let them send a service man to see it, but GE declined. 
In the interim GE has sent a credit for $76 which I could, but wonÃÂt use to purchase another GE washer. I have since learned that several people where I live got rid of their GE washers because they smelled when they operated.  I just want other people who have a GE top loading agitator washer to be wary when they use them. The washerÃÂs model no. is WCXR1070/TAWW.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing heavy smoke but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) given the reported history of similar incidents with GE washers.

incident_description:
The submitter said she moved into the home (address below) a week ago and the washer was already in the home. The submitter believes the washer was purchased from Sears.

When the submitter went to use the washer she noticed mold all around the rubber rim. She said she has cleaned the rubber rim but the mold and mildew will not come off. The submitter believes the washer poses a health risk and it should be recalled. 

The submitter called the firm today and informed them of her safety concerns. The submitter was told that her washer was not recalled and they have not heard about a mold problem with their washers. The firm offered to send a technician at the submitter's expense but the submitter refused. When the submitter asked to file a complaint she was given the number to the CPSC Hotline.
justification: The incident involves mold in a washer, which poses a potential health risk but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: A Nutone brand bathroom fan Model 696N-R02 B Unit likely caused a house fire. No injury occurred.
justification: The incident caused a house fire but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: Washing machine "exploded" while in use causing damage to walls & ceiling.  Owner was not near the machine and not injured.
justification: The washing machine caused damage but no one was injured, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
On April 12, 2017, 2350hrs, there was a kitchen fire I investigated.  The occupant of the residence attempted to use a Kidde 3lb disposable fire extinguisher and it failed to operate.  The date stamp on the base of the extinguisher was "2015" The extinguisher was rated for ABC type fires and contained a number on the label of "A99014677".  This model extinguisher appears to be the same type of a recall previously issued on extinguishers made up to 2014.  I attempted to use the extinguisher to see if I could get it to operate and I was unable to squeeze the handle to activate the extinguisher.  The pin had been pulled.  I obtained photos of the extinguisher and it is currently being safeguarded by the property owner.  As a result of the inoperability of the extinguisher, an occupant of the residence used water to attempt to extinguish a cooking oil fire and as a result spread the fire.  

Further, upon my examination of the extinguisher I noticed a piece of plastic on the upper handle that is to extend into a hole in the lower handle; in my attempt to activate the extinguisher I had to manually manipulate this protruding piece of plastic into the lower handle.  This utilized a fine motor skill that, I believe a normal person would not be able to perform under a high stress situation as a fire.
justification: The fire spread due to the inoperable extinguisher, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
A routine inspection was performed 01/30/2017. The carbon monoxide testing came back with emissions of forty parts per million. The installer contacted the Manufacturer and was informed that this specific boiler was not recalled. The Manufacturer advised the consumer to install a gasket or replace the induction motor.

03/27/2017 - The gasket was replaced at the expense of the consumer. The carbon monoxide testing performed came back with emissions of twenty parts per million. The installer informed the consumer that he could replace the induction motor however there was no guarantee that this would solve the problem. The induction motor would cost the consumer approximately nine-hundred dollars. The consumer's other option would be to replace the entire boiler.

03/28/2017 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and left a voice message.

The consumer is unsure if he will have the unit for at least the next thirty days.


Update to Report Number 20170328-41583-1648955

3/28/2017-The Manufacturer, Weii-Mclain, 500 Blaine Street, Michigan City, IN 46360-2388, confirmed that there are no recalls on this boiler model with this serial number.

3/29/2017-The consumer called the Manufacturer Warranty Number at 1-800-654-2109. The boiler is not under warranty for replacement parts.

4/19/2017- The installer, Reimer Home Services,255 Fire Tower Drive, Tonawanda, NV 14150 (716-
694-8524) agreed to install a new inducer motor at dealer cost, approximately $500, rather than the retail cost.

4/26/2017 -New inducer motor installed. CO monitor recorded zero CO levels during unit operation. 

Cost of inducer motor to consumer was $553.54 including tax plus the cost of the gasket replaced on
3/27/2017 for $164.21. Total cost was $717.75.

BOTTOM LINE- The CO leak was mainly due to the erosion of the original caulking material which is an integral part of the inducer motor. This material is found where the inducer motor exhaust connects with the venting system. Additionally, the inducer motor gasket also loses its effectiveness over time. Manufacturer has not issued any warnings to consumers that this will occur over time due to NORMAL OPERATION of the boiler. This is a critical safety issue for all users of this product and can potentially lead to CO buildup in residences.
justification: The incident involved a carbon monoxide leak due to boiler issues, but no injury or death was reported. The problem was resolved with repairs, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he noticed that the dishwasher capsule soap did not completely dissolve in three different occasions and hence left a lot of residue in the machine and on the dishes and silverware.

The consumer read the back of the packaging and it stated that ingesting the product causes serious harm to consumers' health.

The consumer plans on keeping his dishwasher capsule soap for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

The consumer enclosed poor quality pictures of both sides of container.

The consumer will save the container and 3 soap packets for your reference if required.

What he is concerned about is a soap deposit left on forks etc that might not be observed.  I saw deposits  O <- This size!  I have never seen that before on other soap brands!
justification: The incident involves residue from dishwasher capsules but no reported injury or ingestion, hence severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as it happened on three occasions.

incident_description: I was using the air compressor to run tools while working on my vehicle. While it was running, it started smoking so I turned it off. A few minutes later I noticed it was dripping burning plastic from under the shroud so I quickly pulled out out of my garage and removed the shroud to find the motor on fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The carbon monoxide alarm on our upper (sleeping) floor activated on 4/28 as a "warning". It was old so I bought a new one that also went off at 3 pm on 4/29; the fire department was called and after much searching, the highest readings were near a basement dryer. I had the vents thoroughly cleaned within a few hours, but the alarm went off again at 3 am on 4/30. The fire department came out again and found the highest readings to be near the furnace(also in the basement); unfortunately, they didn't take readings outside, or they would have known it was the furnace the first time. When I called a HVAC company in the morning, he informed me that he had seen several problems with high efficiency Carrier furnaces that had horizontal plastic vent pipes having faulty heat exchangers. We had no heat from Sunday to Wednesday, when a new heat exchanger was installed. Carrier will refund $325 of the $800 cost to replace the defect. I want to know why I wasn't contacted about a recall on this furnace earlier, and, as a result, my family (including a 3 month old) was put in harm's way.
justification: The incident involved repeated carbon monoxide alarms and fire department visits, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Couple of weeks ago my front loading Samsung washer (WF218ANW/XAA) all of a sudden started shaking with loud banging noise. 3 days ago my wife noticed smoke along with strong burning odor coming out from it when she opened the washer door. We are reluctant to use it fearing that it may cause sparking and may explode. With small kids around the house we don't feel safe using it. I hope Samsung will take care of the issue plaguing this particualr model. There are numerous incidents like ours for this washer. I am surprised Samsung hasn't issued a recall yet.
justification: The incident involves smoke and a burning odor, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
Late January, 2017, I installed a Kohler R706009L-SH glass door during master bathroom remodel in preparation for the arrival of out daughter in late June or early July. This door was purchased from my local Lowes.

My wife gave birth on 6/20/17, we got home on 6/22/17. and hired a housekeeper to help clean up around the house due to us wanting to care for our daughter. On 6/25/17, upon entering the shower and closing the door, one of the panes of the shower door exploded. Our housekeeper was cut and glass showered into the bathroom and our master bedroom.

Late morning 6/25/17, after cleaning up the glass, I took back some of the door framing to Lowes and explained the situation. While I was there, one of the employees that worked in plumbing and sold us the door originally, said "we've had two this week." That's 3 doors of the same model that exploded on your customers from one store, so I asked to speak to a manager to make sure that they were aware of the issue. The manager on duty said he knew about the issue and had spent 1.5 hours on hold with the manufacturer, kohler, trying to escalate beyond simple customer service but couldn't.

I relayed this to kohler's facebook page, and I was advised by their page administrator to private message them and customer service would be in contact. Kohler wanted to do a warranty replacement on the door and asked how the housekeeper was doing. I declined the replacement because of the uncertain safety status of the product.
justification: The housekeeper was cut by the exploding glass, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
We purchased the Hot Headz Personal Water Mister on 6/25/17.  We used the mister that day.  During the night, the mister was placed on the nightstand and exploded.  After a loud noise, shards of jagged plastic flew all over the room and bounced off the walls.  I have a photograph of the pieces.  Prior to the explosion, it had been a few hours since the mister was used or touched.  

The mister works by pumping the device to cause pressure, and then pressing the button releases a fine mist.  The product worked throughout the afternoon.  No one was hurt, but someone definitely could have been.  

I have photos of the plastic shards and the packaging labels, but am unable to upload to this report.
justification: The mister exploded, causing shards to fly, but no one was injured, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the product worked initially but failed unexpectedly.

incident_description: Small fire inside home oven (overheated food in broiler). Operated portable fire extinguisher but after less than 1 second, discharge stopped and could not be restarted. Manually extinguished fire using cup of water and transporting items to kitchen sink. Minor burn to hand in this process.
justification: The incident involved a small fire and a minor burn to the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the event.

incident_description:
On June 16,2017 after reviewing use directions,cautions and first Aid Treatment label ( after showering) I cleaned shower glass doors with Magic Shower Glass& Mirror cleaner.
I used no other cleaning products on this day.
Later in the day my hands started itching,by morning on June 17 2017 my hands and fingers were experiencing redness ,itching , blistering /small bubbles, inflammation .
By June 18 2017 blistering became more severe and growing,from June 19 to June 21,2017 blisters at base of palms/thumbs area became very large( about 1inch diameter)and hands became painful.
I e-mailed my physician on June 22, 2017 for advice,Acting fill in  Physician informed me my Physician was out of office until June 26,2017 was it possible to e-mail pictures,I was unable to send pictures and made appointment to be seen on June 26,2017 by my Physician.
On June 26,2017 I visited my Physician,I was diagnosed with chemical burns to my hands and treatment began,I was advised to not use this product again.
As of July 5,2017 I am still being treated,there is severe pain,scaring and skin peeling at base of palm/thumb area,at this time it is not known how long recovery will be or if there will be any long term scaring.
I have photo's documenting injuries to hands.
The caution label on Magic Shower Glass&Mirror had no mention of harm to skin or protection needed.
I would like to see Magic Shower Glass &Mirror cleaning have better caution warnig label regarding hands and skin damage and protection needed and first aid treatment.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in chemical burns requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
(03/09/2017) The consumer stated that his wife was sitting in the eat-in area near the laundry room. She heard a noise and a sizzling sound. She checked the laundry room and saw sparks and smoke coming from the top of the dryer. She unplugged the dryer. The dryer continued to smoke after it was unplugged.

(03/13/2017) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. A dispatch is scheduled for a technician to come out to inspect the unit.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the dryer, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I was using a Little Giant Ladder Type 1A ,hinged folding ladder opened strait and extended to 11 ft.The right leg was extended a additional 8 in. over a step using a Little Giant Leg Leveler attachment.While I was standing on the ladder the central ladder hinges suddenly failed,allowing the top section of the ladder to rotate left and the bottom half to rotate right!The ladder fell to the deck surface with me landing on the ladder and deck from a height of about 9 ft.

I consider myself lucky that my injures were limited to bruising,swelling and lacerations, but no bone fractures! The hinge locks worked ,but both hinges show severe torsional distortion and mechanical damage.The ladder was set up and being used properly,and I weigh 240 lbs which is well within the 300 lb. ladder rating.  This mechanical failure occurred without warning and should not have been possible,I want to know how and why this ladder failed!
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including bruising, swelling, and lacerations, but no fractures, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the ladder was used properly and within its rated capacity, suggesting such failures are not common.

incident_description:
This caller purchased a wall heater approximately three years ago from retailer in [REDACTED].
The heater is connected to a gas line on a wall in a Sun Room.
She had no problems with the heater until March 29th, 2017 when her son who informed her that he had been standing around the area where the heater is placed on the wall, he walked away and the heater just exploded.
There is a tempered glass insert at the front of the two foot wide heater that shattered all over the front of the heater, on the floor directly in front of it and went out onto the area of three feet from it.
She states that she is reporting this as a severe hazard of laceration due to the force of the explosion as well as the larger pieces of glass that flew out from it.
There are no injuries being reported
She did try to contact the Pro Con Heating, numerous times since the  day after the incident when she spoke with [REDACTED] 
[REDACTED]  took a report but did not provide a report number although this caller sent pictures also.
justification: The heater exploded, causing glass to shatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was shocked while holding the handle of my Shark Navigator Lift Away (model NV352 26). While researching this online, I found that this is a known problem and that there was a recall a couple of years ago. Unfortunately though, my model was not included in this recall.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock, which is an injury, and the model was not included in the recall despite being a known issue.

incident_description: Ratcheting gas cap on brand new unit won't seal and leaks large amount of gasoline every time you tilt or move it. Hot engines and gas cap spewing gas all over is a life safety hazard. Impossible to transport unit in a vehicle without gas sloshing over. These are going to cause injury and damage. Ratcheting cap is worthless.
justification: The description indicates a significant risk of injury due to gasoline leakage and potential fire hazard, especially with hot engines involved.

incident_description: My two year old son was taking a bath and the Kohler glass shower door spontaneously exploded on him, causing injury.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a two-year-old child due to the shower door exploding.

incident_description:
My daughter had been doing her laundry at. My house for several weeks. I had become I'll every time she did this. She used a free and clear type detergent, but she was using suavitel fabric softener. I would get a.migraine headache, nausea, vomiting, each time she did her laundry. I have used various brands of softener before, but this made me physics!!y I'll!. I felt like I was smothering  until the fragrance dissipated.  I have asthma, so I have to be careful about these these things.  The symptoms get worse each episode.

Thank you
justification: The individual experienced severe physical symptoms including migraines, nausea, vomiting, and asthma exacerbation, indicating an injury level severity.

incident_description:
I was using a Cascade Complete (by Procter & Gamble) pod to put into my dishwasher. The covering of the pod split so that the liquid  squirted  into my eye at lose range with great force. I could feel it burning and it was very painful. I instinctively rinsed my eye in cold water for 5 minutes. then I read the warning on the pkg. that said to rinse it for 15 min. If I got some in my eye. I did that, but it was still very painful with a burning feeling so that I could not keep my eye completely ope.

I called the company phone number on the box. The first person I talked to took a report with my name and what happened. Then he transferred me to their medical dept. Again, I told what had happened and that I still was not ok. she said to go to a doctor or emergency room.

I did that and was diagnosed with "burn of cornea and conjunctival sac. They flushed my eye with 1 liter of saline, which took about 1/2 hour, and was a painful treatment in itself. 

Please recall this product - this could happen to anyone.
justification: The incident resulted in a diagnosed burn of the cornea and conjunctival sac, requiring medical treatment, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
(05/19/2017) The consumer stated that he was preparing to do the wash. He noticed that some of the pods in the container were leaking. He was separating the pods that were leaking when some of the liquid from the pods got on his hands causing chemical burns.

The consumer contacted 911. An ambulance crew was dispatched but the consumer did not receive any treatments on his hand.
justification: The consumer suffered chemical burns from the leaking pods, which qualifies as an injury, but no death or severe treatment was required.

incident_description: Building product manufactured by Railing Dynamics, inc., is dangerously ineffective.  I had built a deck on my home using the RDI Endurance Original Railing made of PVC and the railing brackets are spontaneously developing cracks.  The brackets are a crucial element of the structural integrity of the railing.  There has been one minor injury directly attributed to the failure of this railing system due to poor design engineering of this product.
justification: The description mentions a minor injury due to the railing failure, indicating a severity level of 3. The spontaneous cracking of crucial structural elements suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I had purchased a waring pro shaved ice machine at frys electronics. when i returned home my daughter and i begain making snow cones.during the second use i took a bite of a snowcone and my teeth met something metal, i tasted a lttle blood, i fished the object out of my mouth only to discover the thing i had in my mouth was a blade that had fallen out of the machine and into the shaved ice. what if my daughter ended up with it in her mouth? this product is unsafe, should not be on the market. also in the shaved ice container i found two little bolts.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (tasting blood) due to a metal blade in the snowcone, and there was potential for more severe harm to the daughter.

incident_description: While using the Craftsman Table Saw (Model Number 137415030) I was cutting a length of oak wood weighing approximately four pounds when the stand suffered a partial failure on the left side, dropping downward and tipping the surface of the table saw at about a 30-degree angle. When I felt the stand begin to give way, I released the piece I was working on and moved away quickly. I suffered some impact injuries to my left arm and shoulder as the part was flung back at me by the blade. I then turned the unit off, treated my injuries, and have avoided using the saw since.
justification: The incident resulted in impact injuries to the arm and shoulder, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such equipment failures can happen but are not frequent.

incident_description:
(04/10/2017) The consumer has a safety concern about stones that have been installed on the front of his home.

The consumer stated that the stones are a grayest brown color scheme. The consumer bought seven boxes, 5 small boxes and one large box. When he opened the boxes to mix the stones, he noticed that one of the stones was black. He then noticed that the manufacturer date on one of the smaller boxes was 2015. He looked at the other small box which had a date of 2016. The largest box had a manufacturer date of 2017. The consumer also noticed mold on the top of the small boxes and mold was on the inside.

The entire front of his house have been covered with the stones and some of the stones are covered with mold.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer. He was referred to  a representative and was advised to contact the retailer. 

The consumer was advised that they will clean the mold as a courtesy. The consumer was advised that the mold would be cleaned with [REDACTED].

The consumer stated that [REDACTED] will not remove mold. 

The consumer will email pictures.
justification: The incident involves mold on stones installed on a home, which is a health and safety concern but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I was using ladder while pressure washing a home. And have had this problem on a few other times. We are one of how many similar stories you've heard over the past decade or so.   How many of these injuries could have been prevented.   Where's are we at now?   I'm sure rods all comes down to politics and money.   It really makes me ill.  

I've read articles on injured parties suing and getting settlements from the saw manufacturers.   The problem is that all the injured parties deserve the same treatment but they don't get it.   We are being turned down from everyone because we live in a state that makes product liability cases difficult and not worth the law firms time.

I wonder every day how certain parties can sleep at night knowing how many lives could be very different based on their decisions.

incident_description:
I have a ceramic oscillating space heater by Lasko, model 5362.
There is a recall already for this model number due to cords overheating but Lasko says my unit isn't included in the recall (I have exact same included model number but they say mine was manufactured 2006 and affected units were manufactured in 2005).
My unit power cord had apparently overheated an unknown number of times causing the outer covering of the power cord to disappear/burn away, exposing the metal wiring inside the power cord. This has caused the metal to spark and arc wildly when the cord was moved, which caused slight burns to the carpeting it was sitting on as well as my hands/fingers when I attempted to move the unit to unplug it.
The unit overheated where the plug enters the base of the housing/grommet.
The unit has not been damaged due to abuse or misuse.
This unit *should be included* in the recall regardless if it was manufactured 2005 or 2006 as my unit OBVIOUSLY has the same issue that prompted the recall.
I was told by Lasko to stop using it and throw it away and buy a new one  (I personally believe they just do not want to cover this one with a free replacement even though it is the same model number as the recall with the same issues).
I have photos showing charred metal of the wiring/power cord but am unable to upload as I'm on mobile device (Note 5)... I can send via email or upload to file sharing website and share link(s) if needed.
justification: The incident caused slight burns to the carpet and hands/fingers, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
This is a safety problem concerning the ÃÂAce Light Dimmer Foot ControlÃÂ. Multiple units are failing over time in a way that separates the plastic casing and exposes bare wires with the 110 volt mains supply. This was discovered when my 11 month old son was playing near to one of the units. ItÃÂs unclear whether he played with it but nonetheless my wife and I both noticed the exposed unit barely a foot away. My son would only needed to have reached over with his hand and he could have electrocuted him so very easily.

Fortunately no harm came to him. I immediately disposed of the broken unit. I then retrieved another spare unit of the same type that had remained in itsÃÂ packaging since purchase approximately 1.5 years ago. After removing the packaging the unit fell apart in exactly the same way!!!! This means itÃÂs a consistent manufacturing issue and not just an aberration. That second unit which failed in the same way has been kept. Annotated images of the second unit are attached to this report.

I suspect that this a 3rd party manufacturing issue but it is Ace Hardware on the packaging. Given that the screws are still locked in place, it appears to be an issue with either the plastic material or the injection moulding process. Given that 3 joints failed in the same manner, IÃÂd suspect a material defect but IÃÂm not an expert. As far I can see, the failure was identical to what I saw with the first unit.

My wife is confident that she purchased both units from Cole Hardware at 2254 Polk St, San Francisco, CA 94109. SheÃÂs reasonably confident that she purchased them while pregnant around a year and-a-half ago.

We have zero interest in any lawsuit or refund. Our overriding concern is another child which could be at risk for the same issue. We may be able to gather further information such as a receipt but wanted to make sure this was being taken seriously before we spend the time to do that.

Areas of Investigation:
* What combination of material, bonding and time causes this problem?
* How many units did this affect?
* Should the unit be redesigned as an added precaution so that if it separates, no 110v wires are exposed?
* Should it have more material around the joins to reduce likelihood of separation?
* Is a recall merited?

Thanks for your consideration and I hope this is taken seriously.
justification: The incident involves exposed wires posing a risk of electrocution, but no injury occurred. The consistent failure across multiple units suggests a likely occurrence.

We aired our home out continually during the install and thought it was just a new floor smell, not knowing these floors were under any investigation. We called lumber liquidators to report the concerns we had and were told the flooring was discontinued and they would do nothing about the quality concerns we had. We filed a claim and they denied it even though we did not finish the install due to the quality and once we found out about the investigations into the flooring toxicity we left the remaining 1100 sq ft of our purchase unopened and uninstalled.
Our new son was born healthy and active. Within a short time of the flooring installation he began getting chronic congestion and ear infections. Our 15 year old daughter who has never been unhealthy has had 4 boughts of pneumonia and degenerating health since 300 sqft of this flooring was installed in our living area.
This has continued and Drs have no answers. We have ordered the test kit and will also be calling a third party test company to document their finding. These findings along with our children's health records will be submitted to all health dept agency's in our locale as well as  federal gov health agency. Considering the test results this product should have been recalled immediately by Lumber liquidators and consumers should not have to fight to get an unsafe product out of their homes to protect the health of our family.
justification: The incident describes chronic health issues (congestion, ear infections, pneumonia) linked to the flooring installation, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the direct correlation between installation and health deterioration.

incident_description:
This is a very serious safety issue concerning a Briggs and Stratton power washer engine.
My power washer was purchased at Sears , in Canada, under the Craftsman brand equipped with a Briggs and Stratton engine .
The washer was purchased on Dec 14/2014 and used so far no more than 10 times, only for domestic purposes.
On Apr 9/2017 I tried to use the washer, it took a while to start, much longer than usual.
After about two minutes of usage, the engine exploded with a very loud bang an a cloud of black smoke..
Fragments of very sharp metal were spread around on the deck, together with hot oil.
Only the fact that my BBQ was between myself and the power washer saved me of being hit with those very sharp metal fragments.
When the smoke went away, I looked closely at the machine and I noticed a big hole on the side of the engine block, about 4 inches in diameter.
We are talking about a power washer working perfectly fine just one week ago.
The washer was stored over the winter in our sun room, cover with a protection cover, with a temperature way above freezing level. 
During the storage the gas tank was emptied and anti freeze fluid was added.
I definitely believe that Briggs and Stratton and Sears  should issue a recall notice for all of these engines or at least a warning to the customers who bought machines equipped with this type of engine.
I find it very disturbing that an appliance used only several times a year could potentially hurt people, not only the users but also the families around them, children, pets etc. 
Not to mention the potential of the windows broken or other damages to the property.
I would like to know what is your official position regarding this and if you have prior complains about similar issues.
justification: The engine explosion caused sharp metal fragments and hot oil to spread, but no injury occurred due to the BBQ acting as a barrier.

incident_description: In 2011, I purchased the Generac GP5500 portable generator (model# 0057360).  I had purchased the generator to provide power back-up to my house whenever there is a power outage.  I didn't even wind up using the generator the first 2 years that I had it because we were fortunate those years not to have severe enough weather that knocked out our power.  Once I did use it, I only used it 2-3 times.  There are only a few hours actually on the generator.  Fast forward to 2016 when I go out to my garage only to smell strong fuel odors.  I was shocked to find the gasoline in my generator leaking all over my garage floor.  There wasn't that much gas in the tank because of the simple fact that I don't use it that much.  I always tried to make sure I only had enough fuel in the generator to run it for each situation.  At the end of each summer/fall season, if there was any fuel left I would either drain it out or actually just let the generator run until the remaining fuel was used up.  In 2016 when the fuel was leaking all over, it was fuel that had only been in the tank a short time - it was not old gas.  Once I was able to clean up the gas, I checked my shut-off valves & all my connections.  Everything appeared to be okay - I couldn't see any visible damage but not being a mechanic, I couldn't tell if things were okay internally.  Being on a fixed income, I didn't have the money to take it in to have it serviced because, naturally, it was out of warranty.  Now this spring 2017 season, we got our first storm of the year where we lost power.  I went to get the generator started & I got NOTHING.  As a result, the sump pumps in my basement wound up backing up & I had water all over my basement.  A neighbor of mine who works on small engines was kind enough to look at the generator for me & advised me that even though the generator was like brand-new, the carburetor was completely gummed up.  I would need a carburetor repair kit.  I called Generac & they were of absolutely no help.  Not only did they inform me that they don't sell parts to their own equipment, but they couldn't tell me who did or what the part #s were that I would need.  Upon doing some further research, I was extremely surprised to see that there are TONS of people who have posted complains of this very same problem with this particular model of their generator.  Many of these people suggested filing a complaint here with CPSC because going through Generac was of no help.  I'm just really shocked that with all the complaints I've seen, that there has not been any type of recall or class action suit.  I assume nothing will come of this based on the other responses I've seen but I want it on file that yet one more consumer is dealing with a defective Generac product.
justification: The incident involved a fuel leak and generator failure causing property damage (water in basement), but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: In the month of April, 2017 I acquired a second hand aluminum hand truck, Costo Mod. 12-302 ABL  3in1 (multi position). One of the handles was broken so I contacted Costco by email 3 times to get the "handle" (safety bracket) replaced. They sent me the wrong handle 3 times, the upper one, when I insisted I needed the lower handle. The Lower handle supports 2 positions. Regular upright, where the hand truck is in an upright position as any other handtruck would be [handle carries 0 load]. Also, the lower handle can be unlocked and 2 extra wheels lower making the truck roll at an angle (leaning back) carrying the FULL load for the human [that part of the handle was operational]. This truck is labeled for 1000lbs upright and 800lbs leaning back on the extra 2 small wheels (4 wheels total).  Since I was having hardships carrying a FULL load of sodas or plastic water cases where the load was being carried by my arms & back... the leaning position was the excellent solution for me. The lower broken handle was fully operational in that SINGLE position.  I wrote Costco CS, and like I said, they sent me the wrong bracket 3 times despite my excellent communication capabilities. On 2017/05/24 (May 24th) the hollow plastic bracket broke off and the 5 cases of water, each 5.25 gal. were sent to the sidewalk together with me. I received 2 nasty gashes on my left leg and bruising. Another long bloody gash on my right leg that I saw the next day. I sent pictures to Costco CS and asked them to fedex me the correct handle or a truck capable to handle the weight they claim their hand truck could carry. incident_description: We are a federally funded housing authority using a Kidde safety product, a combination detector model # KN-COSM-IB which has been recalled by the manufacturer. incident_description:
I own an ecobee3 smart thermostat that was installed about 6 months ago. It has operated fine until a few days ago. I happened to notice the thermostat said the house was over 90 degrees, but it clearly wasn't. After closer inspection I found the face of the thermostat to be very hot to the touch. I removed the thermostat from the wall for safety. 

I contacted ecobee's tech support and did some troubleshooting with them. Since this is a smart thermostat it keeps temperature logs for history. The tech said he saw the thermostat got to over 100 degrees the night I noticed the problem. The logs showed the temperature rising at about 1 degree a minute before I disconnected it.

With their tech over the phone we concluded it was not a wiring issue. I happened to have a second ecobee that was still new in the box to replace a different thermostat. We connected the new one and it operated fine. They are sending me a replacement.

While I really like this product, I'm concerned about its safety given this incident. I feel lucky to have caught the problem when I did. I'm concerned the thermostat would have caught fire if left unnoticed.

incident_description:
We recently purchased a couple of handheld showers as part of a home remodel. They are manufactured by Watermark Designs, Ltd.   350 Dewitt Avenue Brooklyn, New York 11207.

The product is a solid brass handheld under the Blue line.  The handheld being solid brass is really quite heavy.  It prior was manufactured with a holding bracket that would hold nearly 1" of the handle.  This was the bracket we expected to receive on our order and was the bracket listed in the manufacturers product book at the retailer.  The shower holder we received is apparently an updated version, but is defective in that the hole to hold the shower handle is too small.  This results in about 1/2 inch less depth of the shower handle being held.  As a result, when the water is turned on, the handle due to water pressure and weight can work its way out of the holder and spontaneously fall. 

This presents a significant risk due to the weight of the product.  Not only can it damage the shower structures, but it poses risk to the user, especially smaller children who could be hit in the head by the falling handheld shower.  We have stopped allowing our children (ages 7 and 3) to use the shower due to the risk.  

We have contacted the manufacturer directly, as well as through the local retailer about the concern and have requested the old holder which functions correctly.  We have advised them to make a simple fix, drilling out the holders in the future to a slightly larger diameter to adequately hold the handle, but despite this they continue to refuse to address the issue or change their design.  They remain adamant that their current design functions correctly.

Our retailer (Chown Hardware, Portland, OR 503-243-6500) has informed us that they have received multiple concerns from clients regarding this bracket. 

I remain mystified that the company remains so resistant to a simple manufacturing change, but I am concerned about the risk this product presents.  I have pictures of the old handheld holder and the new that shows the difference in fit.

As a physician, I see the results of head injury and know very well the potential long term health risks that something of this weight falling from height could have on a child.
justification: The handheld shower can fall due to design defects, posing a risk of injury, especially to children, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
2/25/17: Purchased Kohler Levity Bypass Sliding door from Lowes in Concord, CA. Kohler model #706009-L-SH, Serial # [REDACTED]. It was installed following the instructions provided a few weeks later. We had no issues until 5/7/17.

5/7/17 around 6:15pm: My 5 year old daughter asked to take a shower with me when I returned home from work, something young children sometimes enjoy doing with their mama, especially after we had been apart all day. At the end of the shower, my daughter opened one of the doors, hopped out, closed the door behind her and dried herself.  After she was dried off, I asked her to hand me the towel, as I was still in the shower. When my daughter opened the door, it slide over to the other side and then entire door shattered! Glass flew everywhere- all over me and all over my terrified daughter. We had tiny shards of glass all over us, but then we noticed my daughter was bleeding. She had three major cuts: one on her foot and two on her hand/wrist. The one on her hand looks like it may require stitches but to avoid traumatizing her more tonight, we have decided to wait until the morning to reevaluate the severity of the cut, as we are thankful it has stopped bleeding. I was left standing in the glass filled shower until my husband had taken care of our inconsolable daughter and made sure her wounds were given first aid as priority. I couldnÃÂt move because of all the glass everywhere I couldnÃÂt move to hold and comfort my traumatized daughter. My husband had to find his rubber boots to put on to get to me, and he had to carry me out of the shower and into our second shower where my daughter and I had to rinse the tiny pieces of glass off ourselves. I had several tiny pieces of glass in my wrist which had to be removed with tweezers and a needle in some areas. After the adrenaline wore off and the glass was cleaned and my 5 year oldÃÂs blood was scrubbed from our bed and carpet below I began to think of what could have happened. What would have happened had my daughter been a few inches closer to the glass when it broke? What if those large pieces of glass had hit her head or her face or her NECK instead of her hand? My daughter could have died! My two year old son had been playing right outside the shower just a few minutes earlier. What would have happened had he been there? 

5/7/17 around 11pm:  I emailed Kohler stating the above details with pictures begging for someone to follow up. 

5/8/17 around 9:06am: I called Kohler and was given a case number (#[REDACTED]) and transferred to someone else who was supposed to be able to help me. [REDACTED] stopped me quickly as I was telling what happened and he said, "to best help you, please tell me what your expectations are of Kohler in this situation." I was caught off guard by that. No empathy. He showed no care at all in the injury my daughter and I experienced. He offered no solutions to rectify the issue. He wanted no details of the incident. I told him I wanted an explanation of how this could happen and he simply said that glass can break and that he understood it was "not a fun thing to go through." I asked, begged, to send pictures to someone's personal email at Kohler so that our experience could be documented and reviewed and I could get some sort of response or explanation. If nothing else, wouldn't Kohler want to document when their products fail and cause injury to their consumers so that they can work on making better, safer products? I wanted to know what safety measures Kohler uses so that these things don't happen. He said I could send photos to the general Kohler email but that I should not expect any explanation or follow up. He basically said when I figured out what my expectations were of Kohler aside from wanting an explanation that I could call back. He did not care about documenting my and my daughter's injuries or the incident whatsoever. 

5/8/17 7:45pm Still no response from my email to Kohler, no follow up after my initial phone call conversation.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to both the daughter and the mother, with the daughter suffering significant cuts that may require medical attention.

This caller is reporting the electrical light switches in his home that was installed when being built around 2012.
The caller had seen sparking at various times from different switches.
His home and approximately 40 other homes in his development were built by the same electric company at least on his entire block and they are the contractor hired for electrical installations.
He has at this time established only that the house to the left of his and the house to right of his had sparking coming from the switches also.
During the first week of February 2017 eight of the switches were replaced by the same electrician.
These eight appeared to be the worst and the caller observed that the wiring was charred with melted plastic. 
He then stated to the builder that he was now very leery of the rest of the light switches and the builder since then isn't talking with him.
He has only that the switches are part# WH4300-WH, Manufacture 610578 sku# 76335610665.
He said that each switch supports only one light or one lamp etc.
There are no injuries being reported.
He is reporting this to CPSC as a severe fire hazard and is asking that they become investigated, recalled and replaced.

Note:  There are pictures embedded in the storyline.  High resolution photos are available of the burnt switches.

The builder, [REDACTED] Residential, built my home in 2011.  While the home was within the 1-year warranty, I reported to the builder that my light switches smelled burnt and were arcing when toggled.  I have a sensitive nose and could smell this clearly.  He sent out the original electrician from Thompson Electric (in 2012) who said they are "fine" after a bit of debate.  Fast forward to late 2016 and now the majority of my light switches have signs of black burning that is clearly visible when the light switches are in the ON position.  The light switches that carry the higher loads (more lights) seem to burn first.  But, these loads are normal and proper for a UL rated switch.  The switches are rated at 15 amps and are operating on a 15 amp circuit.  The load for the bathroom for example is a fraction of the rated load (6 x 60w bulbs = 360watts or roughly 3 amps of load on the switch or 20% of what is was rated to do by UL)

At my request, this February 2016, I showed the builder via email pictures of the "scorched" light switches (above) and let him know that one was tripping the circuit breaker and the others appeared to arc or shoot a spark when toggled.  There are more examples in the home but only a few pictures were provided.  He expressed concern as did the electrician (they are good people).  The original electrician came out and replaced 8 switches that appeared visibly burnt as indicated by the black area in the photos.  We all agreed that maybe a bad batch of switches existed and that a few were defective.  This was a kind gesture and very much appreciated.  I then took the burnt switches apart and was stunned at what I saw.  

Internally, the switches are melted, scorched, the contacts burnt, and there is clear evidence of a high-heat environment sufficient to melt plastic (read: fire hazard).  It is clear that the contacts are defective causing an arc which was melting the white plastic on the back of the switch.  As the plastic melted, the switch become more unreliable and arced more since.  The switches that are most burnt also had some ÃÂplayÃÂ in the switch vs. a nice clean on/off toggle feel like a new switch.   Every switch I took apart looked the same.  I did not take all switches apart to preserve any evidence that may need preservation.  

I then began to wonder if the switches that weren't visibly burnt may be internally burnt.  This had me concerned.  I then chatted with a neighbor.  We live in a condominium community and many homes were built in a row at the same time by the same builder using the same electrician and the same switches.  My neighbors switches are visibly burnt also (see picture below, it mirrors my bathroom identically).  Notice below the left switch that has the highest load is visibly burnt and the other two, the vent fan and single light over the tub (low loads) are not visibly burnt. 

It seems the switches that carry the larger loads (kitchen lights, bathroom lights, etc.) burn up internally first.  The switches that carry a lesser load (a single light in a closet) seem to do better.  But, the switches are all working well under their UL rated capacity.  

My questions - how many homes have these defective switches?  They are clearly a fire hazard and the problem is bigger than I thought. 

Some internet research of switch today found the following: 

The switches appear to be made by [REDACTED] Brands under the [REDACTED] product label.  The label shows the switch as item [REDACTED] , MFG# [REDACTED] Single Pole Switch White, with a SKU of [REDACTED] .  There is a UL stamp, a rating of 15 amps, and a Made in China label.  Do note in the photos one switch is a three-way switch (kitchen).  This is a different SKU but the internal parts are the same and they were likely manufactured together. 

Please let me know if you need higher resolution photos.
justification: The incident involves sparking and charred electrical switches indicating a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description:
RE: Report of Unsafe Product

Dear Sir or Madam:

A plastic part covering the thermostat in the gas valve on my 4 1/2 year old AO Smith Gas Water Heater split without warning allowing gas and water to mix making water leak with the potential for a water heater and/or gas explosion.

I believe the potential harm from the use of this product is so catastrophic that all AO Smith gas water heaters with plastic thermostat covers in the valve should be recalled and replaced by the manufacturer without charge to the owner.

This incident involved the AO Smith FVIR Gas Water Heater installed by Webb Plumbing July 2012. The Model is GCV 50 300. The serial number is: 1223A009605

The water heater is in the basement near the gas furnace. We have no pets or small children that may have bumped into the water heater valve. The valve was not damaged in any way.

At 2 a.m. on December 15, 2016 my husband heard a hissing sound from the basement. He found water leaking from the water heater through the gas valve assembly. He turned off the water and gas supplies to the water heater and drained the water heater with a hose, but water continued to leak.

Our plumber, [REDACTED], found the plastic thermostat cover in the gas valve had split. He said that gas was going into the water heater. Water was going into the gas line. It took him an hour to dry out the line enough to allow the burner using the replacement valve to light.

The replacement gas valve (provided under warranty) had a metal part instead of the plastic part that split. This indicates to me that AO Smith knows this part can split and has made a manufacturing change.

We were very lucky to have taken action to stop the damage when we did. We were a day away from being away from home for 4 days. I shudder to think what would have happened if the gas and water continued to leak from this valve. If the water pressure had been low, or the water turned off for a repair, would the gas have leaked into the water heater causing it to blow up? Or would gas have leaked into the room, 3 feet from our gas furnace, causing an explosion? Needless to say a water leak that went on for 4 days would have damaged a lot of items in our basement.

I tried to talk to AO Smith about my request for a recall. The Technical Support Division said that Honeywell made the valves for AO Smith (using AO Smith specifications). The Technical Support Division said that I needed to talk to Honeywell. I tried to do so. Honeywell said I needed to talk to AO Smith.

In my opinion, AO Smith gas water heaters with plastic part containing valves are a risk of injury or death to others. AO Smith should recall these valves.

I give permission to share this report with others and publish it in the Consumer Product Safety Commission database.

This is a true and accurate account to the best of my knowledge and belief.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a gas and water leak with potential for explosion, but no actual injury or death occurred.
