incident_description:
While using my Brownie F390X Gas-powered direct drive hookah compressor unit on a recent dive trip, my son-in-law and I experienced a sudden loss of air pressure.  Fortunately we were in shallow water and were able to return to the beach without incident.  Had this failure occurred a few minutes later after we had reached our intended dive depth, the consequences would have been much more serious, if not fatal.

I purchased this unit new from the Brownie corporation in June of 2013 and by the time the above listed incident occurred in December 2016,  the unit had less than 20 hours of total run time on it.  I notified Brownie Corporation of the compressor failure and was informed the unit was no longer under warranty and I needed to buy a "rebuild kit" to fix the problem.  I was told, the problem was probably due to a flapper valve which is considered a "consumable" and not covered under warranty.  

 purchased the rebuild kit but expressed my concern over the serious danger of this type of failure.  I advised Brownie that I would be getting back in touch with them with photos and details once I had disassembled the compressor, determined the cause of the failur and installed the rebuild kit.

Upon complete disassembly of the compressor, I discovered the problem was indeed due to failure of one of the compressors four flapper valves.  I took photos of the broken flapper valve and sent them to Brownie along with a brief report indicating the flapper valve failure was due to a poor design which allowed sea water to enter into critical parts of the compressor which could not be accessed for cleaning without removing the engine/compressor from the housing, and then completely disassembly of the compressor. 

Brownie responded by saying the failure was due to lack of proper maintenance, even though the photos I provided reflected an area within the compressor that could only be accessed by total disassembly.
justification: The incident involved a sudden loss of air pressure but no injury occurred, and the divers were able to return safely.

incident_description:
We are a Church Scouting group.  The spindle sander was purchased about 2.5 years ago.  It has seen very limited use with only our group of Royal Rangers using it less than 30 hours.  Most of the time the tool will sit for 8 months with out use.  Then be used for  a hour every few weeks and maybe 2 times a year be used off and on for 6 hours during a crafting event.

Sunday evening 3 of leaders were in the shop room working on some craft projects.  One of the men used the sander for the first time that day.  He used it shortly then went over to the band saw and was cutting some other things.  

We have a Springfield, Missouri Fire Marshall as one of our Leaders and he said I smell smoke.  I asked him if he was burning wood on the bandsaw he was using.  We looked around and spotted the Grizzly spindle sander had some flame coming out just below the switch.  

The 3 of us quickly unplugged the machine and tried to smother the flame and burning plastic and used some water in a bucket to put the fire out. 

We removed the bottom of the sander and found that where the motor brushes contact the motor that part of the copper part had broken off and had caught the unit on fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire was quickly contained.

We have a LG washing machine at home on the second floor. A couple of days ago, our nanny was doing laundry as our 6 month old baby was taking a nap, and asked me to check the washing machine as she thought that it should have already stopped the cycle. The screen displayed an error (FE error) and it seemed as if the water was still running inside the machine. I called my husband immediately and he suggested that I closed the water valves that go to the machine. As I tried looking for them, the water started overflowing. It was so much pressure from the water that the machine door opened (it is a front loading machine) and water started coming out. It was very scary. incident_description:
10 January 2017

Samsung TL W Rebate Program c/o Stericycle
6026 Lakeside Boulevard
Indianapolis, IN 46278

Dear Samsung Rebate Office (or whomever at Stericycle that helps "Protect People and Brands,
Promote Health and Safeguard the Environment").

Dealing with this recall has been one of the most frustrating interactions I have ever had with a
company. First of[ after hearing about the exploding washers. we did not want to take the risk of
using ours. so we went out and bought a new one (a Samsung believe it or not) Trust me that it
would not have been a Samsung except for the fact that we paid $899 for the original washer
ONLY four years ago. and could hardly afford to pay for another high-end washer again now. So
we bought a floor model that has a bash in the side but still worked. But there was no deliver~
option. so we had to pay to get a hand dolly from [REDACTED] and pick up and install the washer
ourselves. (I know that your rebate pays---ostensibly---for delivery, but sadly I don't have a
receipt for the $85 bill from [REDACTED] for the hand dolly rental.)

That's just the beginning of my saga with Samsung and Best Buy (half the time I wasn't sure
who I was getting connected with). The fact that there is now a third party (Stericycle) involved.
makes me even more wary that my consumer plight will ever reach anyone who may be able to
make the slightest decision that changes even one nano-portion of one cog in the wheel.

Regardless, my interactions regarding what should have been a simple transaction have pushed
me to the limit where I am writing this letter. You don't know me, but if you did. you would
know it took a great deal to get to this point. Believe it or not. I have better things to do. But
regarding this issue, to note:

1) I got a call from someone named [REDACTED] on October 19, 2016, saying he was from the Best
Buy/Samsung Recall, who I made a deal with for a new washer and pickup of my old one Dec. 7
(I still have his original call messages on my phone). No one ever came. (Sec #3 below for my
follow up on this.)

2) On November 4, 2016, I received an email stating:
  "Because you have already registered your washer. a Home Label Kit will arrive to the address
provided within 14 days."

I never received the labels I was promised. Oh, but I got an email yesterday (January 7, 2017)
stating:
"Thank you for your submission. Your home label kit will be shipped to you within 14 days."

3) When no one arrived for my Washer pickup on December 2. 2016. (which l had to make sure
I was home for), I called my local Best Buy and they knew nothing about it. I then called the
number from that [REDACTED] had left me (800-303-5518) and got a recorded message saying that Iine
was no longer in operation and that I should call 888-237-8289. I called that number and got
stuck in a phone tree until I finally got and someone who said they would connect me with
Delivery.

The next person I got was from Sales. She went to connect me with Delivery and then I get into
another phone loop telling me Samsung is working with the Consumer Products Safety
Commission to resolve this and that, because of high volume, to go to the website or hang on for
assistance. I hung on. Then I got a message saying Samsung has reached an agreement with
CPSC. Go to our website or hang on for assistance. I hung on. I finally got someone who told
me-after I say why I am calling-they would try to get me a Delivery number.

He said he will try to find a phone number. He gives me the number 800-[REDACTED]. I tell him that
doesn't make any sense, and explain the problem and that I don't know what department he's in,
but he should put an email up the chain that the loop saying that the Recall department needs to
revisit its phone tree in that the phone loop has dated messages about the status of the recall and
there is no easy way to get to a representative.

I finally asked what department this person worked in and he said ... wait for it. .. the Recall
department. Um, might that not have been a good idea to mention when l was complaining about
the recall line and for him to let someone know about it? In any case. I ask him to find out what
happened with the pickup and says he can't find anything and that he can' t help me. I ask if he
can at least find out who I talked to: that surely there must be a record of the call.

He could find no record of my initial call and says again that he's sorry but he can't help me.
When I asked this customer service representative his name he wouldn't give it to me, when I
asked to talk to a supervisor, he wouldn't connect me. When l insisted on talking to a supervisor,.
he hung up on me. He ... hung ... up ... on . .. me. Are you kidding me? Are you hiring high school
freshman to fill recall lines? I didn't try calling back because based on the above. I'd probably
never find him or his department again.

3) I went back to the original message from [REDACTED] and found that my caller ID showed a non-
800 number ([REDACTED]). I called that number on December 13, 2016, to find out about
getting the washer picked up. The person was as helpful as possible, and directed me to someone
else. I called someone else (a lovely, helpful woman named [REDACTED]). who actually told me
whom I should contact and also informed me that I could also get a rebate. She told me to have
my washer picked up by calling a certain number, and that I could get a rebate on the washer 1
had bought if I sent the receipt and serial number tag from my old washer-and the receipt from
my new one- with a form from the website.

This was first I'd heard about this. It 's ironic(?) that I only reached this helpful woman, and
found out about the rebate, after I sleuthed to through my incoming calls to find the above
number. I had received no contact from Samsung about the recall via the email the company,
even though they knew how to contact me (as they had once already per #2 above).

So, after calling the number she gave me, and telling someone at that number about my problem.
I was told they would look into who could help me. Very quickly after, someone from [REDACTED] 
called me---someone named [REDACTED]. Finally! A really helpful person
(THANK YOU [REDACTED] for being professional, helpful, and actually able to solve a problem).
Because of [REDACTED] the washer finally gets picked up on January 7, 2017 (though this letter is
tedious, the alert reader will note that the washer gets picked up the same day that I get a second
notice about soon-to-be-delivered home label kit I should use to label the washer as potentially
dangerous).

At this point. you might think I would just be happy to have the recalled washer gone and a
dented working washer in my home (after all. I could have bought three high-end washers were I
being paid for all my time spent getting to this juncture). But no. I've gotten this far so I want to
cross the finish line.

So off I go to the Samsung website. where it takes a hit to find the rebate form. I print and fill it
out (am even willing to go through snail mail to get my rebate---although this seems to be
another hurdle cast in the road to consumer justice-really, Samsung, even though you populated
the snail mail form with my address and washer information. you are not able to create a form I
can fill out, save, and easily send by email? Gosh. given the technology of your washers. that's
kind of surprising).

But then, when filling out the form I had to print, I discover that I have to have 2 serial tags, or 1
tag and a photo of the tag from the back of my washer in order to be eligible for a refund. My
machine only had 1 tag, and I was not told I by the woman who informed me about what I had to
do to apply for the rebate that I had to take a photo of the 1 tag in addition to including it with the
from. So I've only included the I tag.

Oh, and I also learn that my form and receipt have to have been submitted 30 days within buying
the new washer. Given the timeline above, that would have been impossible. In fact, I'm still
waiting on my home label kit. But if l didn't apply for my rebate within 30 days I'm not eligible
for the negligible (and varying based on whether I bought Samsung again) rebate?

I will wait to hear about how you process my claim before deciding whether to contact the
Samsung and Best Buy hoard members, or posting on social media, about my experiences with
both companies regarding this recall.

Regards,

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes frustration and inconvenience but no physical injury or death.

incident_description:
This started one day at Home Depot when I was stopped by an employee and asked to do a survey about my water. I agreed to the survey. I was called a few days later by Home Depot stating that I won a gift card and a free water test for doing the survey. I agreed to the free water test. The salesman from the company RainSoft came to our home and did the water test. He told us that their water treatment system could clear up eczema and this was a main reason why we ended up purchasing their system.  Initially, I was excited about the product but after about a week of having it installed, I started to notice some physical symptoms such as muscle cramps and weakness which led me to start researching how the RainSoft system works.  It is removing calcium and magnesium from the water and replacing it with sodium and then further filtering the water at the filter in the kitchen sink.  The water is being demineralized by the RainSoft system. I came across this article from the World Health Organization which outlines the health risks from drinking demineralized water: http://www.who.int/water_sanitation_health/dwq/nutrientschap12.pdf

From the article:
"The possible adverse consequences of low mineral content water consumption are discussed
in the following categories:
ÃÂ Direct effects on the intestinal mucous membrane, metabolism and mineral homeostasis or
other body functions.
ÃÂ Little or no intake of calcium and magnesium from low-mineral water.
ÃÂ Low intake of other essential elements and microelements.
ÃÂ Loss of calcium, magnesium and other essential elements in prepared food.
ÃÂ Possible increased dietary intake of toxic metals."

I asked my doctor to write a letter for RainSoft to explain this to them and she has provided the letter. I have given the letter to RainSoft and have asked them to return the product, as I am not going to take these health risks by having the product in our home. RainSoft has refused to return the product and threatened to place a lien on our house if we do not pay them an 18% return fee. [REDACTED] from RainSoft told me "I am going to cease these emails" in his last email to me.

I want to return this product to RainSoft at no additional cost and expose the potential health risks of their product as well as the practices of this company to the public.
justification: The incident describes physical symptoms (muscle cramps and weakness) linked to the water treatment system, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is considered possible (3) as the health effects are documented but not universally experienced by all users.

incident_description:
X-Tronic Model 5040-XTS product burst into flames while in use in my home.  Product was destroyed by fire.  Because I was in the room when it happened, there was no property damage or injury.  X-Tronic USA Model 5040-XTS. 5040-XTS Hot Air Rework, Soldering Iron Station & Preheating Station.  Imported from China by X-TRONIC USA https://xtronicusa.com 
X-Tronic International, Inc. 
2159 Magnum Circle
Lincoln, NE 68522
Email: Info@XTronicUSA.com
Phone: (402) 742-2586
Toll Free: (844) 861-4762

Purchased from Amazon March 2017.   This is a hobbyist-priced device that looks like a professional tool to work on circuit boards.  It includes a infra-red heating plate to warm circuit boards, a hot air gun to melt solder (soldier), and a soldering iron.  Manufacturer states that the hot air gun and the soldering iron are thermally protected (which I observed to be true on previous uses of the hot air gun). Thermally protected means that when the heat gun is set down in the holster, the internal fan continues to run until the heating element is cool, at which time the fan shuts down and goes into standby.  When the heat bun is picked up again, the fan and heating element turn on and the unit is ready for use.  

 On the day of the mishap, I plugged the 5040-XTS into the 120 volt 60 hz 15 amp three-wire (grounded) USA wall outlet, and turned on the main power switch at the rear of the unit.  About 10 seconds later, the hot air gun burst into flames.  The plastic handle of the hot air gun was burning with open flame.  From the time I plugged the unit into the wall, until the fire began, the hot air gun was sitting in the manufacturer's holster.  The holster was attached to the main unit with the provided screws.  The hot air gun cannon plug collar was properly screwed to main unit.  

The control unit (main box) has user-adjustable heat control and user-adjustable fan control for the heat gun.  The control circuits include feedback sensors, so the unit knows when the hot air gun is set down, and when overheating (according to X-Tronic).  

The Chinese instruction booklet is hard to decipher.  Troubleshooting guide is limited.  On the day of the mishap, I am assuming that when the unit was powered up, the fan inside the hot air gun did not turn on to keep the heating element under control. Assuming that temp sensor inside the hot air gun did not kill the power to the heating element.  

On a previous day, the soldering iron from this unit failed and was disconnected from the unit.    Inside the soldering iron handle, the electrical solder connections on the circuit board had melted.  Also, the ceramic heating element had a chip or chunk missing.  I am assuming the soldering iron assembly is unregulated, and overheated.  

I am reporting this to the CPSC because it appears the safety sensors in both the hot air gun and the soldering iron failed.  The soldering iron "failed safe" (cut power).  The heat gun failed and started a fire.  

The X-Tronic Model 5040-XTS is not marked with a safety certification from a third party safety certification company, such as a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (NRTL).
justification: The product burst into flames, causing property damage (the product itself) but no injury or other property damage, indicating an incident without injury. The occurrence likelihood is possible given the reported failure of safety sensors.

incident_description:
Purchased an LG Gas Dryer Model DLGX3002P S/N S/N 908KWZH00061in 2009.
In March 2017 the gas valve began emitting raw, un-burned natural gas into the dryer drum.
After a survey of products like this on the Internet and actual testing of the dryer I determined that the problem was most likely the control board which would prevent the igniter from lighting the gas after the first heating cycle. Once the dryer cools the first cycle of any run works normally but subsequent heating cycles emit raw, un-burned gas. Although there was a recall of similar models in 2012 (http://www.lg.com/us/public-notices/general/lg-electronicsgas-dryerpr-final-20120816) LG has so far avoided adding any further dryers to the list even though they appear to have this sever safety problem. LG only offers a $250 cost to consumer repair option for this out of warranty product. Since the release of un-burned gas into a residential structure is a safety hazard I am requesting that all models with this problem be recalled and repaired free of charge to consumers or credit be given toward a new appliance.

Instead of mA, it should read "ohm" or have the omega symbol.  There is a
200 mA position, but that should not be used for measuring resistance.

2.  The bottom of each page states,
"For replacement parts, please call 1-800-444-3353.
But at the bottom of page 7 (last page) is
"NOTE:  No replacement parts are available for this tool."
  and below it is

incident_description:
Our Model WPGT9360E0WW GE HE Top Loading Profile Washer caught fire 18-May-2016. It appeared that the fire originated at the main control board, P/N WH12X10281. When this event occurred, we immediately unplugged the washer from its electrical supply, but smoldering continued for a few minutes. When the smoldering and smoking had slowed, we removed the backsplash and used a fire extinguisher as an additional safety measure as there did seem to be heat generated from the control board area.

The Washer had been loaded with laundry, which then had to be taken to a laundromat along with all of our laundry as we of course would not reconnect the defective GE Washer to the electrical supply. We researched having the main control board replaced, but learned that a new washer could be obtained for a lower cost than the parts and labor for repair. We purchased a new washing machine of a different brand and paid to have the defective GE Washer hauled away at the time of delivery of our new machine.

GE issued a Recall Notice dated 28-Nov-2016 for this defective washer citing that there is a risk of fire. By that time, six months following the recalled defective GE washer catching fire, the defective GE washer had been removed from our home and replaced with an alternate brand.
Upon receiving the Recall Notice, I immediately contacted GE to request reimbursement for the replacement washer that I purchased, plus the expended fire extinguisher and laundromat costs, a total of $522.50. GE failed to respond and so I re-transmitted my request on 13-Feb-2017. Finally on 03-March-2017, GE called to advise that since I no longer have the washer for their "verification", my request will not be considered. I had provided photos indicating charring of the washer backsplash above the area where the fire originated, but GE used this weak excuse of the washer having been removed from our home nine (9) months earlier for not reimbursing for the replacement washer. The washer was no longer under warranty and I saw no reason to contact GE prior to my receipt of the Recall letter. And who in the world would keep a burned out washer at their home for months after it had been replaced?

Our home is still loaded with GE Appliances including dishwasher, clothes dryer, refrigerator, cooktop and range and vent hood. Hopefully these items will not catch fire, and as they reach the end of their service life, they will certainly not be replaced with GE products.
justification: The washer caught fire, causing property damage and inconvenience, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Ran out of laundry detergent - have used "kirkland" brand from 
Costco for over 5 years with no problems. Brought home Kirkland signature Ultra Clean premium laundry detergent, refreshing scent with "Patented catch release technology aka "odor eliminating technology" safe for HE washing machines. Because we stock up on Costco products, we later discovered in our research that a new formula was introduced by Costco in March 2016, that we had not bought until February 2017. The size of the container is 194 fl oz for 126 loads.  Information on scan label was ITM./ART.845613 above - and 096619316540 below.
On February 2, I did a load of whites with the above described detergent, and during the process of pulling out the clothes and folding them, I was shocked by the overpowering and nauseating "perfume" smell on the clothing to the point where I called and asked my husband if he had spilled his cologne and wiped it up with a tee shirt or something?! His answer was no and I could find no other reason - so went ahead and put clothes away figuring odor would subside. Odor did not subside AT ALL!  Husband called from work next day saying his tee shirt reeked of "cheap perfume" and to wash all tee shirts again. 
On February 5th, we rewashed said white load, in addition to all of our bedding - still strong perfume odor - permeated the entire house!
The night of the 5th - I crawled into bed with the sheets and pillow cases, etc., that had just been freshly washed with the Kirkland detergent, and immediately felt nauseous and started wheezing (I have mild asthma) and moved into the guest room to sleep (I felt better in about 2 hours). The next morning I walked into my bedroom where the sheets had been washed in the new detergent and immediately started coughing - left the room - went in again - started coughing more violently -  and had a severe asthmatic reaction where I had to use rescue inhaler and take 2 benadryls. This rarely happens with me - maybe 3 other such reactions in 20 years.
I was scared and called husband at work - he stopped by store and bought TIDE and came home to immediately start rewashing everything.  Over the course of a week - my husband washed everything that had been contaminated at least 4 times before odor and residue gone. I spent the week in the guest room. My husband returned Kirkland brand to Costco and received credit, but employees didn't seem too interested in my horrifying experience.
justification: The incident caused an asthmatic reaction requiring medical intervention (rescue inhaler and Benadryl), which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
We have a 6 yr old Hunter ceiling fan model 23903.  It has three lights with glass globes.  One of the glass globes fell off hitting our daughter in the head (the fan wasn't even running).  It shattered the bulb as it fell.  We had to pick bulb glass out of her hair.  Thankfully, she wasn't cut by it.

Each globe is held on by a 'globe assembly nut' -- a 2" diameter threaded flange that screws onto the threaded plastic bulb socket while the globe is held in place.  I assumed the nut had come loose.  I found that the nut could be slipped over the threaded light socket with minimal pressure and without turning the nut, as if the threads were stripped, but they weren't.  The nuts on the other two globes are the same way.  I can grab each nut and pull it right off the threaded light socket.  Of course I have no clue about whether they ever fit properly or the nuts had expanded or the plastic light sockets had shrunk.  Appropriate 60W bulbs had been used.

All Hunter fans that I now see have the globes retained by three radial thumb screws.  My guess is that they were all changed to correct the design flaw.  I contacted Hunter regarding a revised light assembly to replace my original one, and they said they don't have any of the newer design that would fit -- though, aside from the thumb screws, they look the same.  Newer model 52044 appears nearly identical.
justification: The glass globe fell and hit the daughter but did not cause injury, indicating an incident without harm. The design flaw suggests this could happen again with the remaining globes.

I have a picture of the dark smoke/ash at the edge of where the control panel meets the body of the dryer.  No damage or issue at the 220V plug or wiring or interior of the dryer. On December 12, 2016 we had a notice on the panel which indicated in our owners manual to call Samsung which we did.  The Samsung person said that a service person needed to come check the circuit boards - a service rep came and deemed the dryer to be operating fine. We purchased a new Garage Door Opener from Sears Model 139.54931 built by Chamberlain. We followed all instructions in the manual. On page 32 Adjustment Step 2 Test the Safety Reversal System they tell you to place a wood 2x4 flat under the door, activate the door in the downward direction when it touches the wood the door should reverse. The door did not reverse we checked all settings and installation many times. We found if you jam the door down using the adjustments then you can preform the test successfully. The problem is the force necessary to do this causes the travel rail to bow and keeps a load on the system at all times when the door is down. We called Sears twice the next  call connected us to Chamberlain technical. We went through all settings several times the service tech said to place the 2x4 on the 2 inch side which means it was sticking up approximately 4 inches. The door now reversed. The tech said it is now fixed. We asked what would happen if our 2 year old grandson stuck his arm under the door (it would not reverse) his arm is about 2 inches in diameter. 
We then tried using a paper towel roll under the door it reversed after crushing the roll. We then got our bathroom scale and brought the door down on it (not very scientific) the results of several times lowering the door produced a minimum 160 pounds and a maximum of 250 pounds of force. The tech tried to tell us this was caused by the weight of the door we asked why the travel rail bowed if the weight of the door caused the issue. This door opener is a disaster waiting to happen and needs to be looked into. There are no force adjustments such as can be found on older openers. According to the manual the force is set by the internal electronic circuits.
justification: The garage door opener fails to reverse on objects smaller than 4 inches, posing a significant risk of injury, especially to small children.

incident_description:
The smoke alarm is manufactured by Kidde, model P3010H, a photoelectric smoke alarm with a 10-year lithium battery. According to the label, it was manufactured July 5, 2014. I purchased it from a large retailer and installed it in March, 2016. 

Not quite one year after activation, the alarm sounded in the middle of the night. The "hush" button did not function as advertised. The detector was removed to another room and stopped sounding.

Today, it sounded again in the middle of the night (of course!), the "hush" button had no effect,  and was removed to another room, where it stopped. Two hours later, while on a table in another room, it sounded again. No response from the hush button. 

In each instance, none of the other five alarms in my home sounded (one is an identical model). I had a 35-year career in the fire service, and now six more years as a licensed and certified expert witness in fire investigation, and I'm pretty confidant that there were no products of combustion in the home during any of these alarm activations.

A quick check on the internet found numerous instances of consumers complaining of the same issues with this model alarm. No information about recalls was found.

Here is my concern: consumers dealing with this same issue might choose to deactivate or discard their smoke alarms as a false alarm is unsettling and annoying. If they do this, they will no longer have the protection of smoke detection in their homes. Over my fire service career I took part in investigating more than 60 fatalities from fire, and it is well known that the single most important thing that any of us can do to prevent a fire death is to have a working smoke alarm in our homes.

Additionally, if there is an issue with false alarms, I have no confidence that the detector will actually detect smoke. I have not yet tested this unit, but will if you choose not to.

I request that the CPSC investigate and evaluate this model smoke alarm to determine if there is any wider problem than my own detector failing. My faulty detector is still operational and available for evaluation and testing if necessary. I have, however, removed it from my home and will replace it before the end of the day.

Thank you for your consideration, and thank you for the work that you do to keep us all safer.

[REDACTED]
justification: The smoke alarm's false activations and potential failure to detect smoke pose a risk of consumers deactivating or discarding their alarms, which could lead to lack of fire detection in homes. No actual injury or death occurred, but the potential for harm exists if alarms are not functioning correctly.

I bought a wood burning stove December 2013 from Tractor Supply in Savannah Tennessee. I moved from Tennessee in September 2014 and brought the stove to Dahlonega Georgia where we installed it.

We would constantly have to watch and tap them back in when we added wood to the stove. Every time you open the door the pins rise. On one occasion I forgot to check the pins while putting wood in and it fell and hit my arm and broke the tile under the stove. I wasn't burned bad, as the door only hit the tip of my arm and fell to the floor. 

I contacted the manufacturer of the product and they first sent me glass only for the door. So I called them back and told them it is the pins and what I wanted was new pins with a hole on the bottom to put a cotter pin through or something. They agreed to send me a new door. Since I was driving truck and in their vicinity they agreed for me to pick up the door and met me and gave me a new door. That door has no problems with the hinge to date. 

I feel Tractor Supply sold many of these stoves. As I had seen them in the stores in Georgia and I remember the ad for the sale of them. I am concerned someone might get severely burned and concerned for fire hazard, as if the door fails, then there is no protection from the fire itself.

About two years ago I purchased a Bonaire Electric Fireplace heater Model BFH5000.  I used it intermittently but about two weeks ago I heard a repetitive clicking noise after it was powered down.  I unplugged it to reset and then tried powering it up again.  Everything seems to work fine so I powered it down again and after a short delay of about 20 seconds the clicking sound returned.  I unplugged it and contacted Bonaire, who informed me it was not under warranty.  Despite this, I asked the representative to find out if they had other complaints similar to mine.  She talked with her supervisor and informed me they had no reports of any problem like this.  She did suggest I discontinue using the product for safety reasons.  Today, I opened the product to expose the element, circuit board and fan, plugged it in an turned it on.  Everything seemed to work fine and after about one minute I turned it off and it did the typical 10 second power down and then turned off.  Everything turned off including the fan but the heating element did not turn off and started glowing red hot!  I quickly unplugged it and the element of course shut down.  

I find it very disturbing and dangerous that the heating element continued to stay powered up even after the unit is powered down and the risk of fire is obvious.  I will contact Bonaire and report the problem but I thought the CPSC should be aware of the problem since the is a wall mount electric heater which makes the risk of fire even more dangerous.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning heating element that poses a clear fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Our GE washing machine, model number GTWN2800D1, purchased in March 2015, overflowed in the fill cycle and flooded several rooms of our house.  The cause of the overflow was a defective Load Size switch.  The switch has a RESET position that it is turned to by hand and then released to select a "super size" load, or turned further counterclockwise to select a smaller load size.  The load size that is selected determines the amount of water allowed into the tub before it automatically stops filling.  The load size switch is spring-loaded to cause it to spring back from the RESET position when the hand is released.  The Owner's Manual states (p. 4) under Load Size:  "Loosely load items in the washer basket.  Overloading may negatively impact wash performance.  Adjust the load size accordingly."  And, under Reset it says: "If you decide that you want a higher water level, move the Load Size first to Reset, and then to the higher water setting."
Nowhere is a warning or caution given to stay with the machine while it is filling, or that it will continue to fill if the switch becomes defective and becomes stuck in the RESET position instead of springing back.  That is what happened in our case.

The overflow and flooding that occurred caused a serious slip and fall hazard because of the water on the floor and because of detergent and other wash additives in the water.  Also, there is the electrical shock hazard if the overflowing water reached an electrical outlet, which can readily happen if there is a power strip located on the floor of any of the flooded rooms.

GE was at fault for designing a switch on a washer that could fail and cause flooding.  There was no fail-safe designed into the machine to detect and stop the water at a certain fill level or when it was overflowing.  An appliance service technician replaced the defective switch and confirmed it was the cause of the overflow.
justification: The incident caused flooding and created slip and electrical hazards, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung 4.5 Cu. Ft. Top Load Washer SKU #: 4115597 Model #: WA45H7000AW from RC Willey on 12/1/2015 for $533.22 plus tax and delivery fees. In November 2016, it was recalled. Although I had not experienced any trouble with my washer, and in fact, recommended this model to others because I was so satisfied, I had the recall repair performed. 

After the repair was done, my washer started vibrating violently and making a lot of noise during normal use. I called Samsung and told them about the new issue and asked if I could have a refund because I am not happy with the repair. They told me that because the repair had been completed, I was no longer eligible for the refund (or "rebate" as they are calling it). I expressed my displeasure with this, and they said they would send my case to escalation and I would be contacted. No one ever contacted me, so I called again. That time, I was put through to escalation, and the representative told me that I can not have a refund or rebate and another repair is my only option. 

After reading the manual, I now realize that the advertised features of this washer no longer apply. It boasts of VRT (vibration reduction technology), which it no longer has. It is incapable of washing bedding (expect on the gentle cycle, which does not get it clean enough, nor does it spin out enough water). Waterproof items are no longer to be washed in this machine. If I had known all of these claims were false, I would not have purchased this product.

In addition, I have learned that this machine is still unsafe, even after the recall "repair." 

I feel that I have been deceived by Samsung, as the product (and features) I was sold is not what I currently have. I would like a full refund of my purchase price, including tax and delivery fees.

In doing so, I purchased a new machine (same model) from JC Penney, a site listed on the Samsung web site, indicating that the model was available for purchase and would be delivered from a Samsung warehouse. 
I ordered the washer on 11/9/2016, 5 days after the recall announcement.  It was delivered on 11/15/2016.  I
initially, we thought we had a new and improved model because the serial number on the packing slip was not recognized in the Samsung data base.  Later that day, we noticed the serial #, now located on the lid and not on the rear of the machine, had on digit (a 'P') at the end of the serial number.  When I entered it into the Samsung database, sure enough, it was a recalled model sold after the recall.  
I contacted Samsung and was told, that since it was purchased within 30 days of the recall, I would be entitled to a full refund.  OK, that's nice, but what about my first machine that was removed by JC Penney and what was I expected to replace the 2nd one with?  The call was sent to an escalation manager. At that time, there was no other replacement within my delivery area. A DISH Satellite repairman 'repaired' the machine on 11/23/2016.  It was at that time that I realized that it was not a root cause repair, he simply secured the lid from becoming a missile.  
Since that time, the machine has not functioned properly.  At times, it stops with a dC indication, noting an imbalanced load, even though the laundry is evenly distributed.  Also, there are times when the rinse/spin cycle repeats and there is a lot of shaking of the machine.  I have contacted Samsung and have not received one cent of a rebate.  I also have been told that I would not receive the rebate since I chose to have it repaired, it voids the rebate.  It is now covered under the warranty.  That makes no sense.  They sold me a re-called model after the re-call announcement.  The repair created more problems and didn't address the root cause of the problem with the machine.  The machine is not repaired as it was intended to be used.  It's reliable and unpredictable.
3 months ago, I had a 1 year old machine that was supposed to be a high-speed, large capacity washer with vibration control technology.  I bought the large capacity and expected it to function as it was intended.  I now I have a washer that is unstable and unpredictable.  I also bought a matched set.  Please help!  There are thousands of us that are not being treated fairly by Samsung.  I want an new washer and dryer that is reliable and not a threat to the household.

HD has refused to post my revised recommendation and asked me to post a better one. I will not. I sent them a email in response telling them that the saw is dangerous, that my revised recommendation is public and if they get sued HD is guilty of a coverup.  This chop saw has at least 3 major defects. 1. motor is too weak, 2. there are no clutch brakes, or shear pins on the blades to protect the motor. 3. the motor failure mode is prone to starting fires and exploding. Please alert the public before someone dies.
justification: The saw malfunctioned severely, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The submitter purchased the washer for his son (located at [REDACTED]).

The submitter contacted the firm to request the recall remedy and made an appointment to have the washer repaired.

(12/10/2016, Approximately) The washer was repaired by [REDACTED]. The submitter states that the technician did not test the wash cycle. The technician advised the submitter to contact the firm if there is any issues with the washer.

incident_description: Fire crews responded to a residential structure fire within a single-family dwelling. The fire originates in the basement utility area, near the base of the electric hot water tank. Fire progression is vertically and horizontally into combustible basement contents and structural members, traveling beyond the area and level of origin.

incident_description: Purchased Earthwerks Engineered Wood Flooring.  After about 1 week I started to develop symptoms of Formaldehyde.  Nausea, Vomiting, burning nose, burning throat burning eyes and burning skin.  I've reported the issue the dealer place air movers into the house to remove the fumes but they did not help.  The floors have been in two months and my family and I have had to move out of the house.  I am getting estimates to have them removed and to get the house cleaned from the Fumes that have coated everything in the house.
justification: The incident resulted in physical symptoms (nausea, vomiting, burning sensations) requiring the family to move out, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe reactions to flooring materials are not common.

incident_description:
Health Concerns over Allure Flooring
In 2014, I purchased allure flooring.  I believe it was traffic master.  I could look back on my home depot card account and check for sure.  Anyway, a few months after it was installed I developed an autoimmune disease related to m.s.  The doctor kept asking me if I had been exposed to toxins.  I had not had a flu shot in years.  But, I had recently installed this flooring, which still gives off a weird chemical smell to this day.  I don't know who to contact or if I need to get it tested.  I understand there has been some concern with the flooring due to the chemicals in it.  Who do I need to contact?  Halstead, Home Depot Corporate?
justification: The description indicates a potential link between the flooring and an autoimmune disease, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I have Generac Standby Generator. it is controlled by a Transfer Switch. We lost power from Tillamook PUD. Normally the generator is supposed to automatically start and switch the power from PUD to the generator. We did not have power from the generator even though the generator was running. I checked the circuit breakers and everything was OK. I smelled burnt wires and removed the cover from the transfer switch. I noticed burnt wires and the Generator Closing Coil was burned. It was damaged quite badly.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure (burnt wires and damaged coil) but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased the washer and dryer Maxima Xl on December 23, 2013, yesterday the dryer started vibrating make a noise also. I am a retired firefighter and for 20 years have done repairs on Gas appliances also. When I started to trouble shoot the dryer I found an excess of lint build up in the blower wheel. Some of the fins had a quarter of an inch on each fin. After each use we always clean the lint screen. However, the lint duct always has large amounts of lint, which we clean with the vacuum and brush. 
 
Of great concern is that my brother has the same washer and dryer. After calling him he said he had the exact same problem when his was about 3 years old. He had an extended warranty and when the repairman came out he watched the man not clean the blower wheel , but replaced it. He has always had the same experience with the lint build up that the screen DOES NOT CATCH. Over the many years in fire fighting, dryers were some times involved in the cause of the fires. Which is our concern on this Maytag dryer, that apparently many others on the Internet have experienced the same problem.
 
For the lint screen NOT doing properly what it should be doing is the problem and the reason I am asking for someone with Whirlpool to address.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to lint buildup in the dryer, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
We live on the [REDACTED] a sparsely populated area of the State. We have a whole house Generac generator, 20 kw, fueled by propane gas, that ÃÂexercisesÃÂ once a week and automatically goes on when the electrical power Is interrupted. It was installed by a certified Generac Installer who is also a certified electrician. On Wednesday, January 4, 2017 at about the time the generator was due to exercise there was a considerable explosion and a fire ensued. We as owners, were not home at the time but we had cleaning people In the house who heard the noise, could not find a reason for the explosion in the house, so looked outside and saw the fire. They were able to alert maintenance workers who were in the area, who came to the house and using an outdoor garden hose, put out the fire. Eventually the local volunteer fire department arrived on the scene, using a chemical extinguisher, sprayed the generator, shut off the propane gas to the house and the generator and as a precaution entered the house and threw several circuit breakers. They are in the process of preparing a report. Fortunately the extent of the damage was limited to the generator itself.
After visits from the propane gas supplier, the certified installer and from talking with a neighbor In this same area, we learned that ours in not an isolated incident and are concerned that other generator owners who have this same type of generator may be at risk.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Purchased a 1500W Ceramic Tower Heater on 12-16-16 as a supplemental heater for my son's room.  He lives with his girlfriend nearby but was planning on staying in his room on Christmas and New Years. He also used it on occasional days he stopped by to help us with tasks around the house. The heater ran just a few days.  Last week, my son complained about a plastic smell coming from the heater. Yesterday I found the heater had melted on the bottom and melted the carpet beneath it. If this heater had been used more frequently, and possibly, a normal amount rather than sparsely as my son it, it would have caused a fire and more damage.  This is dangerous product
justification: The heater melted and damaged the carpet, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I purchased 3 hydro-sil baseboard heaters in 2010. Two of them would have the control box get very hot and then they quit working. The last one: model #hhp15002 from Santech industries inc in ft mill sc, caught on fire tonight. It was by the control box. If we had been sleeping our house would have caught fire. There were actual flames. I'm concerned that other people with these same heaters could be in danger.  I have a photo of the burned heater but didn't now how to add it. Thank you

incident_description:
I am the unfortunate benefactor of a Samsung dryer that recently caught fire. It filled the whole of the house up with smoke and did damage to the laundry room. I called the fire station and they removed the dryer outside, shut off the gas line and inspected the dryer.

It appears that the dryer ignition switch caught fire. More concerning was there was lint inside the machine where you can not clean regularity. Both my wife and I clean the lint screen after every use. In addition I would also clean the back exhaust pipe and have a lint remover that attaches to my vacuum, which I would use to clean the lint trap when the screen was removed.

In dealing with Samsung, they had a technician come to inspect the dryer. In his own words he said that this should NEVER happen and was shocked at the damage to the unit. He took multiple pictures of the unit and dismantled the dryer to see the source of the fire. 

It appears the ignition switch started the fire. We also noticed lint within the machine where it is simply impossible to clean, unless you were to completely dismantle the unit.

After dealing with Samsung for the last two weeks with this issue, I got a call today in which they stated that the cause of the fire was a dirty lint trap and that they are not responsible for the cause of the fire.

I can tell you that the lint trap is completely free of lint, as I was diligent in its cleaning. It is very concerning and I fear that this particular model may have a inherent design flaw, and would hate to see other people experience this or worse lose propertyÃÂÃÂÃÂ... or life.

What can I do to move forward into getting a second opinion on this issue, as I feel Samsung is simple not taking responsibility for their product. 

In addition not only is the dryer concerning, but I just finished paperwork for a matching washer that is on recall. I had to go out and buy a new washer, fill out paperwork and wait to get reimbursed. This does nothing but raise my suspicion on the safety of their dryers.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the described design flaw and previous recalls.

In September, 2016, I contacted your tech department and they offered to send out a new charging baseÃÂwhich solution I questioned, if it would be any better.  After many weeks, I called, as I had not received the base. I was told that the base was on back-order and may be available in November. Once I returned the requested part, Royal could refund my money.  Your agent and supervisor, both told me that this was unacceptable. But more importantly, I explained that this 3.28 lbs. unitÃÂmore if it is filled with debrisÃÂcan land on the head of a child, would that I mounted it higher. incident_description: The product was brand new out of the box and was then plugged directly into the wall outlet in my room away from any flammable surfaces. It was placed on the concrete floor. incident_description: I have a Fabulous Home Fireplace Heater that was purchased from Ingles Market in Griffin GA.  I actually have two of them. I believe these heaters are a fire hazard. These heaters have two 750 watt heating elements that are seperate from one another. Meaning each has a functional on/off switch the elements are both 750 watts each. incident_description:
Several years ago, we purchased a Bosch Axxis front load washer and dryer. Our extended warranty has ended although I don't believe it would've covered this problem.

I read an article about front loading washing machines having a problem with mold. I checked the areas they mentioned and it's there in spades.

No one told us this could be a problem or what to do about it when we bought the machine. Since learning about the mold, I've researched how to get rid of it, and the health effects. Cleaning didn't work although I followed the directions that were consistent on each site twice.

Health wise, I've been suffering from stuffiness and horrible itching. These symptoms have been going on for years and hadn't been identified.

incident_description: Comfort Zone heater Model number CZQTV007BK melted in 2 places on the front of the heater leaving 2 holes in the plastic. The plastic ended up inside the heater. Heater was being used in a large master bathroom with a tile floor.

incident_description:
Reaction to laminate flooring from Balterio, a Belgium manufacturer.  Laminate type or model is called Burnt Pub Oak.  
Even though produce was certified as being in compliance with CARB Phase 2 for formaldehyde, I experienced an overpowering chemical odor (like a mixture of smoke, smog, bleach, and gas) as soon as unopened boxes of laminates were brought into the house.  Following the installation of laminate flooring on Jan. 13, initial symptom was a tingling sensation around the mouth/lips, followed by burning sensation around the eyes (even though we had lots of windows open in effort to try to air it out) and then face that would get better or go away when I was out of the house.  Contacted nurse on Jan. 17 who suggested that I go to Urgent Care.  Urgent Care doctor reviewed my symptoms and recommend that the flooring be removed.  By then I was feeling sick (air was difficult to breath, burning sensation of the nostrils, tightness of the chest, and heart seems to race).  As soon as flooring was completely removed on Jan. 19, breathing became easier and air felt better.  There's still a tingling sensation around my face and a bit of burning sensation in my nose when I'm in the rooms where the laminates were installed so maybe there's still some residual that needs to be aired out.  We're contemplating of having the laminate tested by a lab to determine source and level of exposure.  We suspect it was the formaldehyde.  Please feel free to contact me at [REDACTED] if you have any questions.
justification: The incident caused physical symptoms like burning sensations, difficulty breathing, and chest tightness, which required medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
We have a Samsung Washing Machine.

We had the recall repair done by a DISH employee in December 2016 and we have been very careful with the machine ever since.  Today  whilst on a medium spin the machine made a huge boom 3 times and my husband quickly turned it off. It then leaked water all over our kitchen floor. After inspecting underneath the machine we found several brackets were broken and a pipe that held water was disconnected. We have a 2yr old toddler and she was playing in front of the machine at the time.
justification: The incident involved a washing machine malfunction causing a leak and broken parts, but no injury was reported despite the toddler being nearby.

incident_description: My Samsung washing machine just exploded.  I bought a new home about 30 days ago and the old home owners told us they had a brand new washing machine due to a recall.  I later learned that it has just been repaired by a Samsung technician on11/15/2016.  We moved on on 12/22/2016.  The washing machine exploded 1/24/2017.  There was a loud explosion and the entire machine flew to another wall.  The sides are all popped out.  I have young children and they could have been seriously injured had they been anywhere near it.  This is terrifying.  I can't believe they fixed a faulty machine and it exploded again.  This is not safe at all.
justification: The washing machine exploded, causing significant damage but no injuries, though the potential for serious harm was high.

incident_description: On Sunday, September 25, 2016 I did my laundry using Tide Pods.  Two pods were stuck together.  As I have done many times in the past, I once again attempted to pull the pods apart rather than placing both in the wash or throwing them away.  As I did this, one of the pods burst open, spraying a stream of the liquid detergent up my shirt.  I took the shirt off, set it aside, and put it back on again about twelve hours later.  It smelled good, and since it was dry I decided to wear it.  I woke up several times in the night, noticing a pain/burning on my upper right hand chest and shoulder.  I was very drowsy and fell back asleep until about 4 am when the pain/burning was too great to continue to ignore.  When I check myself in the bathroom I noticed that there was a very large red mark where the pain was.  That day, September 26, I went to the local walk-in clinic and told them I had a burn.  There I was told it was a chemical burn and was sent to the Emergency Room where I was treated for a second-degree burn that took about 10 days to heal.
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree chemical burn requiring medical treatment, which qualifies as an injury.

With the clothing item in a vertical position, the steam is to get rid of wrinkles.  I bought the item on 10/17/16.   On 12/1/16 I used the Xsteam for the 2nd or 3rd time. incident_description: I have a two year old ventless propane heater in our second home in North Carolina. It is made by Empire Comfort Systems in Belleville, Il. It is a HearthRith model HR 15 TL2. Yesterday, at about 6:30 PM, it was cold in the house so I raised the thermostat and activated the switch to turn on the fan. Within seconds the fire alarm went off and I saw flames and black smoke coming from the vents at the top of the heater where the fan motor is. I quickly turned off the gas and got the flames out. This was a very unsettling event. If this fan went on automatically while we were not home it would have burnt down our cabin.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but was quickly controlled without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the potential for recurrence if the heater is used again without repair.

incident_description: Was using a Lasko space heater, model CC23155 (from CostCo) in my kitchen/family room area when I noticed a small amount of smoke in the air.  I couldn't determine exactly where it was coming from but I immediately turned off the heater and unplugged it.  The space heater appeared fine, no melting or smoke marks.  It wasn't until later that I realized that several electrical outlets in the room were not working and when I examined the outlet the heater had been plugged into I noticed a blackening of the outlet.  No breakers were tripped.  The electrical wiring in our home is up to date and meets all local codes.  I am returning the product and am concerned about its safety.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical damage but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the observable damage and potential for recurrence with similar products.

incident_description:
I purchased a Jiffy Ice Auger Propane model generation 2.  I was told upon purchase this was an updated model, the updated model apparently addressed some serious issues the model one had.  Come to find out after owning it for two years the propane line started leaking, I purchased a new line and installed last year around this time of the year.  Went to start it up this year and the propane started leaking again from the new line.  I called the manufacturer after finding several other people online in forum talking about they were having the same problems with the product.  I called Jiffy at [REDACTED] and talked to the customer service rep there.  He told me the product I was inquiring about is not under warranty, and I was out of luck . He explained why the ice auger leaks, because of bad design and that is why they changed the design to what is now called a gen 3 propane auger. The Gen two has the propane bottle mounted sideways making the propane go into the unit as liquid propane instead of gas, and the liquid drys out the seals in the line quickly and can malfunction easily in cold weather under 10 degrees.  THIS IS very dangerous as the propane starts leaking and could ignite and cause an explosion if you were near an open flame or smoking.  
I asked the manufacturer to help with the issue with their product and they said sorry, we can not help you without me in any way except by selling me the same faulty hose.  They said I could convert it by buying a bunch of new parts but it would be near the same price as a new one.  I pleaded with them to help, they said no. I sent another email asking if there was anything they would be willing to do before I sent this complaint.  It is very unfortunate a company that admits they have a faulty product and design but are not willing to do what is right and to fix their product.   Another side note, I just called a local Jiffy authorized repair facility and they have sold over 20 hoses for this same unit so far this season.  It is not just me that is experiencing this issue.  Sooner or later someone will get hurt using this product.  The Manufacturer should do a recall.
justification: The propane leak poses a significant risk of explosion, which could lead to injury or death, though no incidents have been reported yet.

incident_description: I currently own a samsung recalled washer. incident_description: I conducted a fire scene exam of a residence and concluded that a fire originated in either a plug and/or in a oil filled heater. The occupant further advised me that he had another unit by the same manufacturer that malfunctioned approx 1 year earlier. The occupant received burns to his face as a result of searching for his wife in the fire, who did escape.

incident_description:
Only two days after Thanksgiving, we arrived home from a day of running errands, to find the whole side of our closet ripped out of the wall and the contents spilled onto the floor. The shelf that was under the clothing rod was broken and there were very large holes left in the wall. The things that had been on my side of the closet were now across the center of the closet floor. Thank God I was not
in the closet when these bolts gave or I likely would have been seriously injured. I wrote
to the distributor/manufacturer about this issue three times to no avail. They never even gave
it due attention to send an automated reply indicating receipt of our letters.

After a few weeks i did contact both for one last time. At that time Lowes took a report
indicating they felt it was a serious enough matter to warrant such a report,
however i have heard nothing since from Lowes and to this day have never heard
from the company whose questionable advertising policies have cost us a lot of money to repair damages and reinstall something that could have been done very differently in the first
place had they not been so dishonest as to make unsubstantiated claims. 

We are thankful that there were no personal injuries yet even purely financial injuries inflicted on people on fixed incomes can be substantial, especially when those injuries could have been avoided had the truth been told in the first place.

We don't want anyone else to be injured in any way, either financially or physically so we are making
this report to your agency at this time.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, and similar incidents are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description:
Samsung sent recall notice on clothes washing machine instructing me to purchase a new machine and they would refund a portion of the purchase price.
I purchase new machine an disposed of old samsung machine that caught fire in my house.
Now they won't pay the rebate that they promised.
justification: The incident involves a financial dispute and breach of promise by Samsung, but no physical harm or injury occurred.

incident_description: A Cadet model 4F1000-1 baseboard heater (120V, 1000W) was being used to heat a bedroom. It was not the main source of heat for the apartment, there were other heaters that heated most of the apartment and this heater was only used at night to keep the bedroom at a tolerable (but still fairly cold) temperature. There were no flammable objects or debris of any kind around or near the heater. Overnight a small section of the unit's heating element burst into flames. The open flame died down after a short time, but the section of the heating element that failed (and the nearest heat spreaders) continued to visibly glow white-hot and were visibly melting. Power was cut to the unit from the apartment's main circuit breaker, and the unit cooled off. Closer inspection later revealed a visible hole in the side of the heating element, where the unit had apparently burst open. There was no damage to the property other than to the heater itself, but the force of the initial explosion is evidenced by a "shadow" of soot that had been propelled out of the gaps in the heater, that marked the floor black up to about 3 feet away from the point of failure. The unit failure easily could have burned down the apartment building had somebody not been present to immediately cut power and deal with the situation.
justification: The incident involved a heater bursting into flames but resulted in no injury or property damage beyond the heater itself.

incident_description: noticed bad air quality in house, opened air tunnel panel and found loose insulation which has obviously been loose and breaking away when the fan blows air into the ductwork system, for a long time. it is not normally visible and not a standard maintenance point. i could feel the grit in my teeth similar to grit felt when working with fiberglass on construction projects. several children who have resided here have had unexplained bloodied noses that we attributed to lack of humidity, but seemed particular to my house. the unit was installed new in 2003. there was foil backed insulation in the top portion of the unit that came loose right away and was obvious when top filter cover was removed. i took as much of that out as i could right away and assumed that was all of it.  the unit is a coleman dgaa077bdta and is made by johnson controls. im waiting for suggestions, but about to tear it apart and remove the insulation. i dont want to freeze or choke to death.
justification: The description mentions unexplained bloodied noses in children, indicating injury, and the presence of loose insulation causing grit in teeth suggests ongoing exposure.

justification: The glass shower door shattered, but no one was injured as the elderly mother was in bed at the time.

incident_description: I purchased Fabuloso Passions of Fruit cleaner and used it a week ago.  I used it to clean the floor.  I started vomiting and felt sick for 2 days.  I thought it was a virus of some sort.  So, this Saturday I was cleaning some ceilings and walls with it and started vomiting.  Dry cough, breathing backed up and choking. incident_description: He bought a washer from a local store. The brand is an LG. We reported an issue with mold to the company via 1-800 number. incident_description: We purchased a new Samsung washer and dryer in April 2016 at Best Buy. We were in need of a new washer and decided to go with this particular Samsung set. Even after hearing reports where some Samsung washers have exploded and caused property damage and even bodily harm. I called Best Buy to ask about this issue at which point they stated not to be aware of any issues. I then called Samsung to ask the same question and was told they were not aware of such issue. I had seen news reports where this issue was reported but none in Texas where I reside. In November 2016, Samsung officially recalled several of their washing machines due to excessive vibration or the top detaching from the chassis. In some cases reports of property damage and serious injuries have occurred. After discovering our washer was on the recall, we were terribly concerned about our safety. The remedy offered by Samsung is a free home repair or a rebate toward the purchase of a new Samsung washer. After much research I have found that Samsung is sending a DirectTV technician to make this repair and in many cases the repair fixes nothing. Samsung states to give you an additional one year warranty on the washer which I think is still not good enough. The second option is a rebate toward a new Samsung washer which is not enough to cover the purchase of a replacement. They give you the option of purchasing a different brand washer but they will give you a much lower rebate amount. We are a single income family of 7 which is why we decided to with this particular set that will accommodate the loads of laundry we accumulate. For that same reason we can't afford either one of these options given by Samsung. I went online to make this recall claim and was offered the above mentioned options which I was not satisfied with either one. I contacted Samsung over the phone and was told those were my only options available, the only other thing they could do is send the claim to corporate. They stated it don't guarantee anything but they could possibly offer another option. I was told someone from corporate will contact me within 24 to 48 hours, it has been well over 48 hours and still haven't heard anything. I don't think it's fair that we have to choose between these two options that don't rectify the fact that these machines are defective and they refuse to make things right. At this point we feel they are blaming us for this major issue. If we take this rebate we will have to make an additional purchase for another washer which we aren't getting a rebate to cover and still be left with the balance of the defective washer to pay. In many cases I've hard we have to wait as long as six weeks to get such rebate, which is unacceptable. Samsung needs to take responsibility for their mistake and replace these washing machines for their customers.
justification: The description mentions serious injuries have occurred due to the defective washers, and the recall indicates a significant risk of harm.

incident_description: Purchased a top load washing machine from SAMSUNG sixteen months ago and the drum stopped spinning adequately a few weeks ago and then started violently banging the housing. incident_description:
Our Samsung Dryer, Model DV448AEG 02555A 10, started on fire inside our home on November 13th, 2016.  It is a gas unit, that was purchased in December of 2010.  

The fire initiated near the gas flame trench, apparently by igniting residual LINT that had accumulated INSIDE of the metallic case, which had settled on the bottom.  Over the period of use, the lint appears to have accumulated to approximately one fourth to three eighth of an inch in depth.  The fire subsequently propagated forward to the gas valve assembly, wiring harness assemblies, and then laterally over to a plastic duct which burned a large hole through all the way through it.  Thankfully, the fire subsequently self extinguished, apparently due to oxygen starvation.  I am amazed that it did not propagate further, as there were some dry clothes near the base of the unit that could have easily caught fire.  The unit was installed into a corner, right next to the baseboards, and easily could have burned our entire house to the ground.

Subsequent to discovering the fire, I inspected the ENTIRE vent pathway, and verified that there wasnt any blockage that contributed to the fire.  Up until that point, the dryer had been working perfectly.  
The venting duct was installed with hard points for all corners, and was sealed with aluminum tape and large hose clamps to preclude any air leaks.  Further, I have religiously completed semiannual maintenance on the dryer vent by checking both the ducting at the back of the dryer, and the exit of the vent at the roof line.  Surprisingly, the dryer caught on fire ALL BY ITSELF, without any issue with the venting.  Thankfully, the normally closed valve assembly did shut off the flow of gas to the burner. 

I immediately contacted Samsung corporation to discuss the incident.  Even though it was out of warranty, they initially told me to hold onto the dryer so they could send someone out to investigate the fire.  Apparently, they wanted to make sure they didnt have a design or manufacturing flaw.  So, I kept it in my garage for 6 weeks trying to coordinate their appointment to have a technician come and look at it.  After dealing with at least 4 to 5 separate phone calls, all attempting to coordinate an inspection, I received a call from someone in their Executive Customer Service.  They asked me what I wanted, and I explained to them that I honestly didnt expect any money, but as an engineer and trained failure analyst, I expected that they would at least want to come and inspect the unit to investigate root cause.  They eventually refused that request, and told me that they didnt even care to receive pictures of the fire to review internally.  The dryer was out of warranty.  Case CLOSED.

I was absolutely SHOCKED and appalled, and told them I honestly couldnt believe they wouldnt follow up.  I told them I would file a report with the consumer product safety commission, and I would also contact the Better Business Bureau.  

As an engineer, I would want every bit of data I could retrieve from relevant failures to resolve any future hazards associated with design and or manufacturing flaws.  This dryer started on fire as a result of lint build up INSIDE of the case.  We clean our lint filter RELIGIOUSLY, with EVERY SINGLE load of laundry.  The lint duct in my home was performing adequately.  There isnt any instruction in their manual informing owners that they need to periodically take their dryers apart to vacuum out any residual lint INSIDE the case.  This is a design and or service FLAW, that is not being acknowledged by Samsung or other dyer manufacturers.  I believe Samsung is negligent in both this design flaw, in their lack of instruction regarding this specific and necessary maintenance to reduce the hazard, and in how they have handled my specific case.  We were incredibly LUCKY THAT SAMSUNG DIDNT BURN OUR HOUSE TO THE GROUND.

I have photographs of the evidence should you like to see them.  Further, please contact me with any follow up questions via email at [REDACTED].  Or, please contact me by telephone at [REDACTED].

Thanks for your time.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

BTW, I have been formally trained in the art of failure analysis, and perform such root cause investigations as a part of my professional job at [REDACTED].  On occasion, I have personally supported failure investigations requested of [REDACTED] by the [REDACTED] office of the [REDACTED].  I still cant believe that Samsung handled this issue in such a pathetic fashion.
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have caused significant damage but self-extinguished without injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased a set of the Samsung top loading washing machine and matching dryer in June of 2012. The washing machine is under the recall from Samsung since November 2016. However, I was not sent any info and did not know about this recall until I called to have my dryer fixed. The dryer quit drying on December 25, 2016. I however NOT aware of the dangers involved in this machine would 'help' the machine balance and spin correctly so not to waste more water by standing in front of it and bracing my legs against the front and holding the top part of the machine to help stabilize it. They sent out a tech form DISH Satellite TV to do the 'safety' repair which consisted of the tech taking off the top of the machine and placing bolts and nuts around the underside of the lid, and then he said he had to [REDACTED] the drain hose anchoring it to my other water hoses because it could come off and flood my house...I was given no paperwork and no 'stickers'. All I want is for my washing machine to be made safe to use, and if that's not possible I want it replaced free of charge with a washing machine that is safe.

incident_description:
Responded to the recall notice for Samsung top load washing machines. Request was made on 11/23 and email notifying of 11/27 fix date arrived. The following day email arrived that Appt. was canceled and to call. I called back and next appt was made for 12/10 between 8am and 12pm. 

Dish TV network person showed up, removed the top and replaced plastic retaining clips with metal ones and put top back on. Wife tested machine and same issue with violent shake in spin mode no clothes in washer. She asked for repair work order and was refused, technician stated they are not allowed to give work order or repair order numbers and there was nothing he could do about that. He said he was trained by watching a 1 hour video. 

Wife did laundry in small loads 1/4 fill tub and even on low spin cycle tub hits the inside wall of the washing machine cover. 

We have called our extended warranty company whom told us that Samsung touched it they won't honor warranty and refused to service us saying Samsung owns it now.

Since 12/10 we have got 8 different ticket numbers, have called at least 5 times following up with only being able to speak with initial phone takers, no one higher. Asking for supervisor mean sitting in a hold for 88 mins, while being told there is no supervisor queue.

Finally got a hold of a repair person and they promised to call back exactly on 12/28 at 5PM EST to check some things out (I took off work early based on our conversation while I had her on the phone) and then no phone call. 

Seems to  me Samsung is fixing the after effect of the lid or clips breaking when in fact they should be focusing on the cause of the poor design of the barrel/tub and why it gets so out of balance with nothing in it.

The washer is not usable in any spin cycle and its too bad that being on the recall list meant no one now will cover it under a warranty nor will Samsung own up the issue.  Maybe a class action lawsuit should be in order here. Just throwing away money like this is something most can not do.

So far we now have a $730 dollar lump of coal and are left in the cold.. Really?
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washing machine and poor customer service, but no injury or death occurred.
