The drum has fractured at the weld about 3-4 inches long and multiple sharp protruding edges.  While there have been no injuries past the extent of a small laceration, I have a small child that loves to assist with laundry, potentially risking serious injury.  Samsung is making me replace the drum out of warranty, despite the very searchable facts that this is a common enough issue that a quick search for Samsung dryer drum fracture returns hundreds of results.  There is thankfully only minor injuries and only damaged clothing at this point, however this prevents an investigation recall from the government.  
What, if any, action can I pursue due to a serious injury inducing manufacturing defect?

incident_description:
We purchased a new Samsung Washing Machine on November 25, 2016. It was delivered to our home on December 10, 2016. It worked fine until the morning of January 9, 2017 - one day short of a month old. A single mattress cover was placed in the machine to wash prior to taking our kids to school. Upon returning home 20 minutes later, the washing machine was found about two feet out into the room still running. It was assumed that it just got off balance and no further inspection or thought was given. The machine was paused and moved back into place and then resumed the wash cycle. Left the room for about 5 minutes and came back in to find water pouring out of the bottom of the machine. Apparently, sometime during the commute to school and back the machine had exploded the top of the washer loose and the whole drum had separated from the rest of the machine on the inside. 

This washer is not on the current recall list, but has done exactly what the other machines are being recalled for even though it was not yet a month old. The sales person assured us that this machine was not on the recall list and therefore ok. 

We are fortunate that I returned home that morning, else our wood floors would have been flooded by the machine. Also fortunate that nobody was hurt. The recall needs to be widened to include this model as well and seems like all top load washers should be taken off the sales floor until the problem is resolved.
justification: The incident involved a washing machine malfunction causing water leakage and potential property damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We puchased a Samsung Front Load Washing Machine in 2010 or 2011.  Model # is WF328AAW/XAA 02.  Manufacture Date on label is June 2009.  Last Saturday we noticed it was suddenly much louder than usual on the spin cycle.  Then last Monday morning smoke began to fill the drum.  It smelled like burning metal.  I noticed the odor around 6:00 a.m. upon entering the room to move the clothes into the dryer, not realizing that my husband had stopped it from running in the middle of the night due to the same odor.  (I had set it to run at 2:00 a.m. while I slept, and fortunately he was up while it ran and noticed the problem.)  When I opened the drum to get the clothes out, smoke poured out of the drum.

I've since found multiple reports by other consumers on YouTube and the like, stating the same problem, in some cases with videos.  The serial number on our machine is W01F54AS600701E.

I was disappointed to learn that existing recalls from Samsung on its washers do not include a recall for this problem.  I have ordered a non-Samsung replacement, and I feel that the app. $1000 we paid for this machine should be refunded to us to cover the replacement.  We feel fortunate that our house did not catch fire as a result of this problem.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell from the washing machine, posing a fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: samsung came to my house to do a washer recall but the tech was a dish network tech i told  him about the problem that i was heaving an he told me that he doesn't know anything about washers he just came to perform the recall, since them my washer can't do a single load i start to hear cracking noises. and unit spend more water than my complete family. i call Samsung to report the problem and they ware going to send me a dish network  tech. still not hear from samsung.

incident_description:
I have been told Everthing must be washed on the delicate cycle to avoid malfunction.  .

On Sept 3, 2016 I purchased a Samsung top load washer along with the matching dryer.  It was delivered on September 4, 2016.  On September 29, 2016 I saw on the news the top load washers were reported as exploding & the there was a recall.  Naturally, I called Samsung to inquire if my brand new set was on the recall & was advised the issue was fixed prior to mine being manufactured & therefore I had nothing to worry about.  The agent then advised me to registered the washer & dryer on Samsung.com, which I immediately proceeded to do & received an email documenting the registration.  On Friday, 12/30/16 the washer began to make a loud grinding noise followed by a violent clanking sound.  I then called the technical # listed on the machine itself, 866/726-7864 & was then advised the washer is "actually" on the recall.  You can imagine my frustration.  They offered me a rebate & bonus of $150 if I purchase another Samsung washer.  After speaking to a friend who also had a SS top load washer on the recall & who chose the rebate option, it took much longer than the 6-8 weeks promise her to receive the actual rebate check, in fact she just last week received her rebate check after filing in Sept.   Not to give a sob story but I'm a single mother & don't have extra money to all of sudden go purchase another w&d set & wait months for a refund.  Ultimately, I chose the repair option & the Dish Network (yes Dish Network) technician did come out today to repair however it wasn't until today that I realized the repair is not actually a repair, it is in fact a work around.  They provide a sticker for the machine which eliminates the bedding setting & in turn the bedding setting on the replacement panel sticker corresponds with the "gentle" cycle on the original washer setting.  I explained this is not what I paid for & would like a refund or a rebate check now to replace the defected set.  I have spent several hours on the phone with them & have 3 ticket #'s.  They attempted to reach me Monday afternoon at 4:46 & but did not leave me a voicemail so when I called them back this am I was advised the ticket was closed because they were unable to reach me.  Therefore, I had to start the process all over again basically from the beginning.  I feel they are wrong on so many levels & Samsung has not truly attempted to truly justify this matter just a work around which in turn only benefits the company not the consumer who is greatly inconvenienced with this matter.  I would like to bring this to light in attempt to warn others from this nightmare.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washer and poor customer service, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a recalled Samsung Washer. It's a 700 dollar washer that the extended warranty was still good on when this all started. Was told to wait and see what they would be doing. Now that extended warranty has expired, and their idea of a fix is Dish Network coming out and installing 2 bolts, and stickers going on the machine, changing the bedding cycle to the delicate cycle which in NO WAY spins heavy bulky items enough. Or they offered me 256 dollars towards another Samsung washer or 156 dollars on a non-samsung washer. This is NOT ACCEPTABLE!  I have seen several people still have issues after the "fix"   The inside of my drum is chewed up from this issues, and I was told I could address that with the repair tech when they came out, only DISH was coming out and said they couldn't do anything. 

I've seen recalled machines still in the stores. I don't think I should have to suffer because I refuse another of their washers!
justification: The incident involves a recalled washer causing inconvenience and dissatisfaction, but no injury or death is mentioned.

My Rheem hotwater heater started on fire and filled my laundry room with black smoke. I learned the control device was on voluntary recall.  I do not recall being told about any recall and if I had not been home and responded to the smell of smoke when I went downstairs I might have had a serious house fire because I discovered it just in time. Serial Number: RH A311408993

Rheem apparently told the service contract provider not to contact customers (this is what I was told) about this voluntary recall.  Home Depot sold over 45,000 of these devices with the controller and I want this device placed on Mandatory recall and repair.  Why risk the lives of thousands of people.  I was home and if I had not gone downstairs this could have been tragic.  I am glad we were not sleeping at night in our beds. 
Your reporting system for attaching photos does not work.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injury or death, and the recall issue suggests a potential for widespread occurrence.

incident_description:
My husband went to nap on December 26, 2016. I went food shopping. When I came home he was up and said, I could not sleep something is on fire and I think it is in our unit. We searched our condo and the building and finally I went to utility closet.  Our water heater had large scorch marks and smoke coming out of the control panel.  Our heating unit with return vent is right next to it and the heating unit was pulling the smoke into the return thus causing the smoke to be blown into our heating system. 

We turned main circuit breaker off and called fire department.  They removed the panel and found that the insulation had caught fire and the mechanisms were completely fried. The unit is older but the fire marshall said he has never seen something like this.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the water heater with smoke spreading, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

able to shut down before it caught fire, these machines are fire hazards!

abused or used on a regular basis.
Prompting report, After researching Online there are hundreds with this model and thousands with GE models all
having the same type of issues. GE recalled some models but passed this one up for recall.
After I took ours apart I found the cause but GE will not stand behind it.

incident_description:
One Harbor Freight item number 61970 (aka other stock numbers)
12" Double-Bevel Sliding Compound Miter Saw with laser guide.
This item was purchased and used AS PER PROVIDED INSTRUCTIONS AND SPECIFICATIONS.
The item has no minimum length of material specified it can cut.
During cutting of tall short wood blocks, the upper fence deflects.
This is an inherent design flaw.
When this occurs the wood will twist causing binding with the blade.
The result is the wood piece is ejected at high speed behind the saw, breaking the upper fence in the process.
A [REDACTED] from Harbor Freight was contacted at [REDACTED] and notified of this flaw.
He denied any such flaw exists with it and offered an exchange of the product.
He never followed through to honor the exchange.
This flaw can be seen in any existing floor model on display in any store.
Simply apply rearward pressure to the top half of the fence nearest the area of cut.
Unacceptable deflection will be seen.
Please intervene before a child watching his father work is hurt or killed by insisting they recall existing models for modification and/or ban further sales of it in the US (Imported product).
justification: The incident describes a design flaw that can cause wood to be ejected at high speed, posing a risk of injury, though no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
Product in question is the Black and Decker Cordless Lithium Hand Vacuum Model No. HHVJ315JD10.

My daughter (7 yo) was using the vacuum to clean up tree needles from the carpet after taking down the Christmas tree.  The panel that you take off to empty the vacuum (and which I've found to be prone to coming unexpectedly unlatched) came off, and my daughter's long hair was sucked into the fan area and wound around the motor.  Either she somehow managed to turn it off, or it became so jammed that it bound up and shut off before it got as far as pulling against her scalp.  She was understandably upset and distressed.  I took a photo, if that is ever helpful.  I had to dismantle the vacuum, but I managed to get it far enough apart to unwind the motor and extract it from my daughter's hair without cutting it.

Their customer service rep spoke broken English and was very hard to understand.  Since this washer has already thrown items off and hit my foot I am not going to keep it.  It is my understanding I will take a substantial loss (from the rep) if I do not replace with a Samsung model.  I am not sure how the washer will be disposed of.  I asked that question and the rep could not answer.  My washer was bought a year ago and has only been used a couple of months.  This is a second home that we own and we live here four months of the year.

I am going to proceed and buy a [REDACTED].  I am very disappointed that Samsung was not "PINNED DOWN" with exact instructions on how the consumer proceed and get the defective product removed.

incident_description:
Armstrong Ultra SX 90 Furnace leaking massive amounts of CO into living spaces.This is a very dangerous situation. The Armstrong/Lennox J vent trap part number 41093-001, caused serious harm to a family. The resultant CO gasses pumping into the house could have been lethal. It sickened a house full of people. The part was apparently leaking for years. Several symptoms in the family over the years indicate this was failed for some time. It finally lead to the total failure of this part. When this occurred (total failure) the amount of exhaust gasses pumped throughout the house was enormous. I did a quick search and found that the symptom of leaking water from this part is common. When this part is leaking water it is also pouring out CO gas! It splits at a poorly designed seam joint. This part needs to be one piece or, at the very least made from stainless steel. It should not be cheap glued together plastic. It is the main exhaust exit from the furnace. It is SAFETY RELATED. I cannot believe Armstrong/Lennox has avoided a recall on this. I will certainly keep an interest up for persons complaining of CO poisoning with Armstrong/Lennox furnaces that use this J vent. There are many of these under various brands. It has been around for years.This needs to be a Safety Recall. I am absolutely positive there are many people currently being exposed to CO gas from this. This failure is documented several times.These furnaces have been around for at least 15 years in various form, all using his very dangerous, poorly designed part. They will all most likely fail to some degree if they haven't already.

I will await your response.
justification: The incident describes serious harm to a family from CO poisoning, with symptoms over years and a potential for lethal outcomes, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description:

I immediately went to the emergency room where I received approximately 25 stitches on the top of my left foot, 5 stitches on my left wrist, and numerous derma bond and steri-strips applied to close other cuts on other parts of my hands, arms, legs, and feet. In addition, I was no longer able to move three toes on my left foot, including my big toe, and had no sensation in the top of my left foot.

On May 25th, I had an MRI and immediately after underwent surgery to repair one tendon in my left foot that had been severed in two places, and a second tendon in the same area severed in one place. In addition, a severed nerve in the same area on the top of my left foot was reattached.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries requiring stitches and surgery, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) due to the unusual nature of a shower door exploding.

incident_description:
Kidde PI2010 smoke detector failed and was the root cause that GENERATED smoke/fire and then detected its OWN smoke/fire to sound the alarm in my home around 2:30 am Dec 22, 2016. 

Luckily, we were home (and awakened) to keep house from catching on fire and were able to remove the AC plug and unit (unit was generating smoke - my son-in-law unplugged unit from AC plug and also removed battery; smoke was in the bedroom; after fan turned on, I had safely removed the short AC plug unit /wires from rest of AC wiring in electrical ceiling box since plug was burnt/melted).  Detector was installed on a bedroom ceiling; a few other detectors in house are interconnected (red wire) to also sound in event one detector goes off (other units DID sound, and only source of alarm was burnt PI2010).  

I have NOT yet determined what to do with (1) original failed unit regarding evaluation and (2) the other PI2010 dual AC/battery units I have in the house. I do have other battery-only smoke/fire and CO detectors in the residence. 

No confidence in PI2010 units at this time... put a different PI2010 back in bedroom where original was located, but did not hook to AC.   I feel it may be necessary to eliminate risk and take all KIDDE PI2010 units off of AC power.  

I do have pictures of burnt AC connection on unit and AC plug which will be posted to this SaferProducts.gov site; I have NOT opened up unit to take internal photo to view any internal components in the detector. For sure this was a concerning event for me and my family, and smoke was quite unpleasant/toxic (daughter and son-in law were sleeping in particular room, I was exposed to smoke as unit was removed and room air cleared; others in home (children) were in room down the hall). Unit was purchased at Home Depot, with MFG date 2011 Jul26; installation AC (w/red wire to sound other units) + battery; battery replaced May 5, 2016, so neither battery nor AC plug were touched before December 2016 event.

Thank you for your attention regarding this concerning event.
justification: The smoke detector failed and generated smoke, but no injuries were reported despite the concerning event.

incident_description:
I purchased Samsung Gas Dryer Model Number: DV50K8600GW/A3 June 2016, by the end of October we were seeing reduced performance, taking longer to dry, sometimes requiring multiple cycles for dry clothes.

This dryer has a defective design of the lint trap will lead to exhaust blockage, wet clothes, and water in the exhaust. The lint trap has a flap that we have seen consistently not functioning. I have found that the lint trap is defective by design and will drop lint into the bottom of the unit. This will lead to an Exhaust blockage outside of the dryer, which will then start to collect water in the exhaust pipes. My house was as new as this dryer. Now I need to re-drywall the ceiling where it fell through due to the moisture collection.

I took apart the Dryer in order to check the unit for faults. I found that the Dryer had become an imminent fire hazard; Lint in the combustion chamber where the Gas fires, Lint all over the front of the machine. The imminent fire hazard occurs because the majority of customers are re-running cycles. I found other customers running this unit multiple times just like I did. If I had not taken the unit apart to clean, it would have started a fire, as I am using Gas.
justification: The defective design poses an imminent fire hazard, which could lead to injury or death, but no actual injury or death was reported in the incident.

incident_description: On July 18,2016, I was using a 12 oz. can of Rust-Oleum paint. I purchased the product in April or May of 2016. From the time I bought the aerosol can of paint until the first time I used it, I kept the can stored in my shop. My shop is insulated and never gets above 90 degrees Fahrenheit or below 40 degrees Fahrenheit. I have used Rust-Oleum products for years without incident. The can was not near a heat source of any kind while in my shop. The first time I used the product was the day that it exploded into my face. On this particular day, I was just outside my shop repainting the rims of one of my lawn mowers. I removed the plastic cap on the aerosol can, gently shook the can to engage the agitator ball to mix the paint, and began to spray the lawnmower rim. Suddenly and without warning, I heard a loud pop, felt extreme pressure on my face, and could no longer see out of both of my eyes. The can had exploded and shot like a rocket into my face. My left eye was protruding from my orbital socket. I was rushed to the hospital. I suffered many injuries as a result of the can exploding in my face, those injuries include, but are not limited to, the following: bilateral fracture of the frontal sinuses, cribriform plate fracture, left orbital roof fracture, non-displaced fracture of the right orbital floor, fractures of the medial orbital walls, bilateral fracture of nasal bones and nasal septum, pneumocephalus (traumatic), subarachnoid hemorrhage, temporary left eye blindness, lacerations to the left brow and left eyelid and face requiring hundreds of stitches, extreme facial pain, loss of smell, loss of taste, and lower back pain.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including fractures, blindness, and other significant trauma, but no death was reported.

incident_description: I was using my new Gorilla Ladders brand  Gorilla Slim Fold Work Platform Model GLA-47WP, which I think is a Home Depot brand.  I had older model that was not slim fold, so I thought this would be better version, that was not as bulky, since it was "slim fold".  But when I was opening the work platform to use in my house to check my light fixture in the basement, when you open the legs and rotate them to lock in place, if you are not careful or have not experience what I experienced in using this product you will crimp/crush your fingertips painfully.  What I think is dangerous is that each pair of legs have two sets of cross bars. The cross bar closest to the rotation point is where if you are not careful you will crimp/crush your fingers in opening the legs of this work platform to lock the legs in.  It was extremely painful for an adult male hand fingers, so if your children or wife should think to use it, their hands/fingers are smaller and it was extremely painful when I crimp/crush my fingertips.  That cross bar also serves as a support brace to the platform, so  it is basically as you rotate the legs to use, it acts like a clamp. The problem is, is that naturally when you open this platform ladder product you would naturally place your hands/fingers of your hand right there to hold the platform steady to pull up the legs. So if you are distracted or not aware of this design flaw before, you will definitely crimp/crush your fingers.  Please, please look into this. It was extremely painful and I don't  allow my kids or wife to touch it, and have placed a sticker that says "Finger hazard, do not place hand here", in case they do when I am not at home.
justification: The description details a painful injury (finger crushing) due to a design flaw, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the design naturally leads to finger placement in the hazardous area.

I removed the top panel of the washer so that i could get the door open. What i saw was complete destruction inside. The steel tub has literally ripped from the plastic housing it was in. Ripped completely around. There were shattered pieces of plastic everywhere. Many of the plastic components inside were broken or crushed as well. I say crushed because they would crumble as you touched them, unlike you would expect for plastic that should bend. I took pictures of the outside and inside damage. No one was injured and there was no unusual smell or smoke.

incident_description:
We experienced a gas clothing dryer fire. The appliance technician who came to our home to service the dryer after we noted a burnt smell in dried clothing told us that fire was unusual in his experience because it was not in the venting system but inside the dryer itself. Based on visual inspection of the inside of the dryer after the technician removed the front panel it appears that lint accumulated over time (11 years) in the bottom of the sheet metal box that forms the exterior of the appliance. Immediately before the fire the dryer was tipped in order to move it during a kitchen remodel. It appears that the layer of lint in the bottom slid to the front of the appliance and formed a low mound which was in close proximity to the gas burner element. Likely this drift of lint ignited the next time we used the dryer. The technician speculated that the dryer may have experience excessive back pressure in it's venting system due to accumulated lint in the slats of the exhaust on the outside of our house. He suggested that somehow the dryer developed an internal leak that allowed lint to accumulate inside the appliance housing. No one was hurt and the fire was contained within the appliance. The fire was hot enough to melt plastic parts inside the dryer and discolor the paint on the outside of the appliance. We were not aware of smoke, just a burnt smell in the clothing inside after the run.
Model# GLG02152ES0 Serial# XD51912048 Manufacture Date (?) 05/2005
justification: The incident involved a fire contained within the dryer, causing damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Is this the right place to report a safety hazard?  The product is the Kwikset 2 key point exterior door entry lock set.  The handle portion of the 2 part lockset (dead bolt and handle with key point) can and did have an internal metal part breakage that prevents opening a door from either the outside or the inside of a building.  This happened to me.  I was locked out of my house because the metal piece broke inside of the lock preventing the handle tab from depressing.  This tab is what makes the tongue from retracting into the handle and allowing the door to swing open.  The handle will also not retract its tongue from the inside of the house.  The door cannot be opened from either the inside or the outside of the house.  This is the second door handle that has been a problem.  In the first case, we were told by a locksmith that the handle would soon fail given that the key was getting stuck in the keyhole.  We then replaced the lockset with a new identical product from Kwikset only to have it lock me out of my house on Sunday, December11, 2016. This meant that I had to call a locksmith to drill the door handle in order to open the door.  I then had to purchase a new lockset (which I did but from a different manufacturer as I have had now 2 bad experiences with Kwikset) and had to pay someone to install my new lockset.  Without doing so meant that I could not go in or out of this door without the door locking and stopping the door from opening from either the outside or the inside.  
 I have called the company for a refund.  They tell me that they will replace the handle but have a policy of not issuing refunds though their printed warranty states that they may replace, repair, or issue refunds.  I am awaiting a telephone call from their management.  I do not expect to get a refund much less any compensation for the locksmith drilling open the lock, the purchase of a new lockset, and the installation fee for the new lockset. However, even if the company does compensate me, this lock is still a safety hazard.  When it fails, it will stop someone from getting into or out of their structure via that entryway.  In apartment buildings where there is only one doorway into an apartment, this would be a serious safety problem.  
This may not be the place to raise this issue.  If not, please let me know where to refer this issue.
justification: The incident describes a lock failure that caused inconvenience and financial loss but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of the issue with multiple locks suggests a possible likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
On July 25, 2016, my husband and I purchased our first home. We officially moved into the home on August 1, 2016. Our master bathroom was newly remodeled about 2-3 years before our purchase. In our property inspection report, our master shower door was noted: "labeled as safety glass and operated smoothly and latched when closed." The glass door etching on the master shower door reads:

DECOLAV
TEMPERED
SAFETY GLASS
16CFR 1201 II
ANSI Z98.1-2009
SGCC-3960 1/4 U A
1212

We researched Devcolav, and apparently they do not sell a single shower door on their website. We wonder why they no longer sell them. We used our shower daily and treated it with care, as would any new home owner who just invested their life savings into their home would. On November 30, 2016, around 9:00 PM, my husband, was taking a shower, with the bathroom door wide open. Our daughter, who is 2 years old and about 26 pounds, came into the bathroom to say hello to her Dad. According to my husband, our daughter rested her left hand on the inner glass shower door and waved with her other hand and said "Hi daddy!" and the next second, the glass came shattering down on her, and she fell into the shower onto the pile of glass. My husband quickly picked her up. As soon as I heard the loud crash, I ran into the bathroom to retrieve my daughter and began to treat her wounds in our other bathroom. My husband had multiple scratches on his body, one cut on his right toe, and one cut on his right-hand finger. My daughter was bleeding from multiple areas. Her right wrist had one vertical laceration, streaming with blood, and one laceration on her left palm, also streaming with blood. She had one large cut on top of her head. Her hair was covered with tiny sharp shards of glass, which also found its way into her clothes, down her back, and into her diaper. Her head, face, and body was covered with multiple scratches from the incident. She was admitted to the ER and had to take multiple x-rays to see if any shards of glass entered her wounds, and her left palm needed four stitches. This ER visit left her traumatized of machinery, hospitals, and doctors. It took over 5 hours to clean up all the glass, which we still sometimes find little shards embedded into our carpet, and we have yet had the time to clean up all the blood stains in our carpet. We are left with a mess, a large medical bill, and we are left in fear of glass shower enclosures, to the point that we plan on removing all shower doors in our home. We believe that there was a manufacturer problem in the glass, perhaps during the tempering process. From our research, 

"The problem occurs with tempered glass, which manufacturers use because of its safety value. However, [REDACTED], a window expert, says that pre-existing damage and imperfections are both factors in the doors' spontaneous shattering. "The number one reason glass doors break is because of some form of damage to the glass around the edges of that door," [REDACTED] said. "The number two reason would be through inclusions, microscopic imperfections that grow into a larger crack internally to the pressure layers. Those pressure layers eventually cause the glass to just shatter." 

We do not believe that our daughter was capable of such a mess. Because our door passed the property inspection, and because we treated it with care, including weekly cleaning, we never saw any damage on our glass, therefore the spontaneous shattering must have been due to inclusions. We also believe that tempered glass is NOT considered a "Safety Glass". Granted it is "safer" than it breaking into larger shards, but it is still NOT safe, especially around small children. This label is very misleading for consumers. We demand that all glass shower manufacturers should be required to notify their consumers of this possible danger so that consumers can take proper precautions. It should also be a requirement to be notified of this possible danger when purchasing or becoming a tenant of any property with glass shower enclosures.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries requiring medical treatment, including stitches and x-rays, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
SUMMARY: our furnace firebox overheated causing air intake PVC pipe to partially burn. 

We are owners of a 6-year old high-efficiency Carrier furnace (model 58MVC120-F-10120) installed in the basement of our single-family home. Recently, we began smelling something abnormal in our yard and after some investigation we realized that the smell was coming from our furnace exhaust pipe. We called a local Carrier dealer for service.  When the technician took off the furnace cover we found that an intake PVC pipe inside of the furnace was partially burned on the side facing firebox. The firebox has evidently overheated and whatever safety mechanism this furnace has, it failed to shut off gas supply when temperature rose to the point that the PVC pipe began to burn.  We contacted Carrier directly and it referred the case to "regional distributor" who blamed the problem on improper installation (incorrect furnace pitch and piping) and asserted that there is no fire hazard, but also added that he "did not recommend" that we use the furnace.  We have not used the furnace since we discovered the problem.

At this point we feel very uncomfortable with Carrier representative's assertion that there is no fire hazard and in absence of a constructive remediation to the overheating problem we are probably looking at replacing our furnace with a new one.

What is concerning to us in this situation is that Carrier does not appear to show any real interest to  investigate this incident further for fire or other safety risk (such as possibility of someone inadvertently placing combustible materials on top of the furnace or even touching severely overheated furnace enclosure) - it seems like they are hoping that we simply replace the furnace prior to anyone performing any in-depth investigation (during last call to Carrier on 11/02/16 I informed them that I was planning to report this issue to Consumer Product Safety Commission.)
justification: The furnace overheated causing a PVC pipe to partially burn, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The Carex Toilet Support Rail B36800 is designed to allow someone with limited mobility safely sit on and stand up from a toilet. We purchased this for my wife who will be having hip surgery. This rail design attaches to the bolts at the back of the seat and then the front arms sit on the bowl. The design allows for different styles of toilets by swinging in or out to fit the style. There is no way to lock the front arms into position. 

 I installed this on November 29, 2016. Two days later as she sat down and put her weight on the right side handle it slipped off the toilet bowl and dropped several inches. Fortunately this was pre-surgery and no injury occurred. I dread the thought of what could have happened had it been post-surgery. I also dread the thought of other more physically limited people using this product and experiencing a similar incident. 

I believe a simple re-design could prevent this from occurring, but until then, it should not be used.
justification: The incident involved the support rail slipping, but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the design flaw and potential for repeated incidents.

incident_description:
I purchased an LG Washing Machine from Home Depot on 11/7/2016. On 11/28/2006, I referred to the owner's manual to conduct a Tub Clean cycle. On page 25 of the manual, it states to "Fill the bleach dispenser to the MAX line with liquid chlorine bleach." I looked into the machine, saw the dispenser labeled "Liquid Bleach Only", with a line labeled "MAX". I proceeded to fill the dispenser with liquid chlorine bleach (Clorox), but the bleach did not reach the max line after I poured in 1/2 GALLON. I stopped since I felt it was excessive at that point. I called LG Customer Service to explain, and while I was on the phone, bleach started to run out from the bottom of the machine onto the floor. They scheduled an LG factory service technician to come out on 11/29/16. On 11/29/16, the LG technician arrived and was perplexed. He said it appeared that the factory did not install the bleach reservoir under the dispenser. He then called his technical adviser for consultation. After the call, he told me that this is a new model that LG just came out with, and this does not have the reservoir, but they did not update the labeling on the bleach dispenser or literature. Since there is no reservoir, attempting to pour bleach to the "MAX fill" line WILL ALWAYS overflow into the bottom of the machine where the wiring and motor is housed, and onto the floor. This is a MAJOR fire hazard and health hazard, and time is of the essence to have owners notified.

On 22 NOV 2016 at 19:15 hours the Fire Investigation Unit was requested to respond to [REDACTED] for a fire investigation. Scene access was by exigent circumstances, while fire crews were still working on scene. Weather at the time was 29ÃÂ°F, clear skies with winds from the WNW @ 14 MPH.
Upon arrival I was met and briefed at the scene by the IC, [REDACTED], [REDACTED]. Chief [REDACTED] detailed the WFD response and actions taken to the incident. The 911 caller was located in [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] had called her apartment maintenance person because she had a smoke odor and found soot coming out of her bathroom shower fixture. The maintenance man was [REDACTED] (xxxxxxxxxx). He observed the soot and smelled the odor and dialed 911.
Capt [REDACTED], commander of [REDACTED], was the first arriving WFD unit. He stated that there was an odor of smoke in [REDACTED] which is located on the second floor. After finding no cause for this odor or soot in [REDACTED], he ordered [REDACTED] to check the unit below this unit. [REDACTED] was commanded by Acting Lt. [REDACTED]. Acting Lt. [REDACTED] reported a neighbor said the unit was vacant. He forced the unit door open and observed soot covering all surfaces of the vacant unit. Further investigation revealed an extinguished fire in a bedroom ceiling. The adjoining walls were opened up in units [REDACTED] to check for fire extension until the companies were satisfied there was no active hidden fire.
Statements were obtained from the involved persons. [REDACTED] resident [REDACTED] was interviewed. She stated that she and her children had left the apartment at 05:30 hours. She returned briefly at 08:15 hours and at this time smelled the odor of smoke and heard alarms sounding in the downstairs unit which she knew to be vacant. She called her maintenance person; [REDACTED] who told her there was no concern because the fire department had already checked the property prior to her call and found a problem in the adjacent building. [REDACTED] then left for the day and returned at 17:30 hours to find soot on her shower fixture and the odor of smoke. She again called [REDACTED] who did respond to the unit this time and observed the conditions.
[REDACTED] was interviewed. [REDACTED] is the maintenance person for 22 of the 46 units within this complex. He does not have any affiliation with this fire unit. [REDACTED] has worked at this complex for 15 years and stated that he was aware of several fires that were caused by the ventilation fans located in the windowless bedrooms and common hallways. He reported that all these fans were installed in the same manner and of the same equipment when the building complex was first constructed. He also reported that as a result of his own testing and comparisons these fans did not have a thermal cut off switch within the unit, unlike the bathroom fans with lights that did have thermal cutoff switches. He opined that all the ventilation fans were dangerous and subject to overheating.
[REDACTED] (xxxxxxxxxx,xxxxxx) of [REDACTED] is the unit owner and she was interviewed at the scene. [REDACTED] purchased the unit on this day for $75,750, paying cash with no mortgage recorded. (Wdrd Book [REDACTED]; [REDACTED]). [REDACTED] did not have property insurance for this unit. She was advised that there may be an insurance claim under the master insurance policy, therefore she should not damage the fan or electrical wiring until it was approved and examined by the insurance company. The master insurance policy is held by [REDACTED] through the [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] is the local agent.
A systematic scene examination was then initiated in the area of least to most damage. No exterior damage was found on the building. Smoke staining was visible on the interior window surfaces of [REDACTED]. Interior examination of [REDACTED], located directly above the fire unit showed evidence of soot emitting from the shower head pipe fixture and concentrations of soot on the ventilation fan surfaces. Fire crews opened the walls in the area of the utility chase to check for fire extension. No fire extension was found in [REDACTED].
The interior examination of [REDACTED] revealed smoke and soot covering all exposed surfaces of the unit. Fire crews opened walls in the master bathroom to check for fire extension from the windowless bedroom. Upon entering the fire bedroom fire damage was observed to the carpet that appears to result from melting and pooling of a smoldering fire. The ceiling in the area of the ventilation fan was fire damaged with partial wallboard collapse. Fire crews pulled additional wallboard and insulation down from between the ceiling joists to expose the extent of the extinguished fire. The ceiling joists showed extensive char and fire extension to adjoining surfaces. The ceiling fan showed fire and heat patterns and the electrical wires were also burned.
Closer examination of the collapsed wallboard show smoke only on the interior surface indicating the fire began above the surface of the ceiling. The electrical wires were examined in detail. No beading was located on the electrical wires to signify an electrical arc or fault. Electrical wire damage was consistent with thermal exposure. The bedroom circuit breaker (#23) was found in the tripped position, also consistent with thermal exposure. Fire patterns on the ceiling fan housing indicate a heating event in the lowest portion of the fan motor area. The bedroom electrical switch near the door was in the on position.
MRIRS reports indicate that the Worcester Fire Department did respond to an alarm incident ([REDACTED]) at this building at 06:41 hours. Fire companies noted a smoke condition and alarms sounding in [REDACTED]. As they investigated the smoke condition cleared prior to locating the source. The building alarm was reset by the responding responsible party. The fire department left with no alarms sounding.
Based upon information obtained during this investigation it is believed within a reasonable degree of fire investigative certainty that the origin of this fire is the area of the NuTone ventilation fan and the cause of the fire is undetermined. The ignition source could not be identified. Faulty electrical wiring or a defective fan motor could not be determined without destructive examination. The first fuel ignited is most likely the thermoplastic cover, or dust contained within the grill. The ignition sequence is the thermal runaway of the ignition source. There is no evidence indicating a set fire. The burns on the carpet are caused by thermoplastic resin drop down fire that ignited a slow moving smoldering fire. This fire self-extinguished when it became ventilation limited by consuming all the available oxygen in the room. The incomplete combustion of the smoldering fire covered all unit surfaces with soot.
[REDACTED], xxxxxxxxxx is the Trustee for the [REDACTED]. He was advised of the findings of this fire and it was recommended to him to change all the fans in the common area and windowless bedrooms-24 fans in total and to add CO alarms within dwelling units. He was also advised that several of the emergency lights were not functioning and needed repairs. A complaint was filed with Fire Prevention for an Inspector to follow up with this repair.
This fire has been ruled undetermined and the case is closed pending further information that may
warrant its reopening. All additional names, photos, phone numbers, personal information, witness
statements, full narratives and notes are in FIU file or investigation report.

incident_description:
For the past several years I have operated a Fridgidair model FDL50S1 dehumidifier in my basement.The dehumidifier was set to maintain 50% humidity and was hose drained to the basement sump. The manufacture date is listed as 03/09 which falls outside of the current recall on this particular model by Gree.

I arrived home for lunch to a strong burning odor and found my dehumidifier smoking slightly, but still running, in my basement. I immediately unplugged the unit and let it cool for 30 minutes.The dehumidifier was hot to the touch.I disassembled the unit the make sure nothing was smoldering before returning to work.The compressor was still too hot to touch,the plastic casing near the compressor was discolored, and the insulation on the wiring to the thermocouple (part of the thermal protection circuit) on the compressor was burnt.Oil was found in the plastic tray underneath the coils. Luckily I caught it in time and no injuries were sustained.

I called the Gree recall hotline at 1-886-853-2802 and provided my name,address,phone number,product model number,manufacture date,and serial number. I was told that it was not covered by the recall and that there was nothing they could do.
justification: The dehumidifier was smoking and had burnt wiring, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
On November 15th at approximately 6:30 a.m. I was beginning to take my shower when the frame less glass shower door I was closing suddenly exploded. The doors were tempered glass and the manufacturer is Delta. I purchased and installed these doors almost a year ago from Home Depot. I followed all instructions included with these doors. I'm skilled and installing and doing handy man type of work so I know I installed them properly. 

This door exploded loudly , without any warning at all. I was pushing on the towel bar and the door was not shut when this happened. The force of the explosion sent glass everywhere and knocked the towel bar out of my hand or blew my hand away. Nonetheless and stunned, wet and naked, I wasn't sure what had happened. My feet were covered in glass and my right hand was bleeding. I stood still to gather myself and to see if I had sustained any other injuries. Considering that glass was covering my feet and glass was everywhere, I slowly pulled one foot out at a time. I didn't noticed any injuries to the top of my feet, I had to step out onto glass to get out of the shower and in so doing sustained a minor cut on my right heel. Once out I reached for a towel and put my feet on it as I shuffled out of the bathroom into the hallway to find a towel to stop the bleeding on my hand. I found one in my laundry room and wrapped around my bleeding hand. Once, I did that I saw that I had received 2 gashes in the top of my right hand. I quickly found some hydrogen peroxide to pour into the wounds to clean out and to deal with any bacteria.  I then took some pictures. Once I was composed and bandaged the sight, I found a gash along my right forearm as well. I cleaned it as well. I then got dressed and headed to my primary Physician, Dr. [REDACTED] in Tomball where I live. Dr. [REDACTED] determined that I could probably do w/o sutures and so his assistant, applied the type of surgical tape that pulls wounds together to help them heal. She also treated with some type of topical solution. I also had to have a tetanus shot and then sent on my way.

Once back home I began to do some research into these type of doors and was stunned to learn that these doors due to their manufacturing process have the explosive power of 10,000 PSI and that the breakage is so fast that it exceeds 14 times the speed of sound. In other words, they are ticking time bombs. I will attach a you tube video of an expert witness in Chicago that elaborates on this subject matter. I'm also attaching pics of my hand and the glass breakage. I have not filed any claims with my insurance company, nor have I contacted Delta or Home Depot. I thought it better to obtain legal advice and direction first. 

The wounds have healed up nicely. However this could have been much worse and any part of that glass could have hit a major artery and could have resulted in more serious injury or death. Imagine, a small child like my grand children taking a shower and this happening with glass coming down on them. That situation has occurred to others if you search the internet.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries requiring medical attention, including cuts and gashes, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
My Samsung top-loading washer (model # WA422 -- purchased new in 2012) broke apart while in use (in 2015) and flooded three rooms of my home, including the laundry room. This was a significant electrical hazard as the machine was still plugged in and running while in standing water.

I called Samsung, and they sent their authorized service contractor, who charged me more than $100 for the service call just to look at the problem.  He then quoted me a repair cost almost equal to the purchase price of the washer.  He showed me a plastic part that was completely broken into two pieces (on the bottom of the washer) and said it would need to be replaced with a more durable metal part and bracketed differently to be less vulnerable to vibrations.  He also told me that this was an issue that had occurred repeatedly with this model washer -- and that Samsung was aware of the defect but was not making any recompense or covering repairs.

I was so upset by this (given that it was a safety issue they were neglecting to rectify!) that I declined the repair and instead purchased a new washer of a different brand.  As this was only three years after purchasing the Samsung, my family could not afford ao buy another new washer with the same features and power, so now we have a mismatched washer/dryer set that does not get the clothes as clean, unfortunately.

It seems as though, rather than step up and correct and obvious and known safety hazard in their product, Samsung chose to run a bit of a "racket" in charging consumers exorbitant amounts to repair it.

Even if nothing can be done to recoup the losses in my case, I hope that the CPSC holds Samsung accountable for their dangerous and neglectful business practice!

Thank you very much for your time and attention!
justification: The incident involved a washer breaking apart and causing a flood, posing a significant electrical hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

Description of accident: Using the Cover Mate 1 cover lifter for the Sundance Spa Edison Model, adding chlorine to the spa, I lifted the cover so I could put the chlorine directly into the motor/agitator.  Because I lack to upper body strength, I grabbed ahold of a handle which was conveniently located on the side of the spa tub. This handle as it turns out, was not what I assumed it to be but instead was to prevent the spa cover from falling to the ground when fully opened.  Because my hand was securely braced on this handle the spa cover crushed my right thumb, causing a near complete amputation, crush injury, arterial bleed, as well as a fracture to the base of this thumb.  

Emergency Treatment: My children brought me to the hospital where x-rays were taken and pain medication was thankfully given. I was told I had to go to another hospital to have it repaired or "removed and a flap made."  At this point my husband arrived and took me to the second hospital because I refused transportation by ambulance.  The surgeon at the second hospital was very talented and put my thumb back together and the next day I saw a hand specialist for a second opinion.  The hand specialist reassured me I would heal, may grow a thumb nail again, and have some function.

Long term Effects: One year plus after this injury I continue to have some limited movement, alteration in sensation, and constant feelings of cold discomfort in the distal part of my dominant thumb.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe thumb injury with long-term effects, including limited movement and altered sensation, but no death.

He claimed it was the washer and we were lucky that it happened while under warranty (even though we still had to pay labor!) The washer is like being on a factory floor it's so loud. It is suppose to be quiet! And it is louder than any cheaper washer we've ever owned. We don't stay in the room with it while it is spinning. But after seeing the top load recall, I am really concerned. I thought we just were unlucky and got a lemon but I'm concerned now that it is a similar issue. And worse case, I'm concerned it will harm our families hearing as it is sooo loud. I have 4 children so this is a big concern for our family. I tried contacted Samsung and the rep was very dismissive and said there were no recalls on this machine. When I asked to file a complaint, he said I could put comments in the feedback section of their website. (Dismissive like the repairman who fixed the spin but left us a loud wreck of a machine). I own a ton of Samsung products from phones, TV's and tablets, to the washer, now matching dryer, refrigerator, and dishwasher. Aside from the TV - where the screen literally cracked less than a year after having it - just right in the middle of us watching it!....The washer is the worst investment I've ever made. I spent $1000 on the washer alone. The cheap $250 [REDACTED] I had when I was first married lasted longer than this. And wasn't this loud! The Samsung is suppose to have a dcb limit for quite on it which it obviously is not meeting. I'm furious I was dismissed this long and wish I had complained here sooner. There are many forums with consumers with this same complaint.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washer causing excessive noise and inconvenience, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: After I watched the news I became aware of a recall with this Samsung washer. According to the news it was advised that consumers wash using the Delicate cycle. On 11-08-2016 I was washing a comforter on Delicate cycle. I heard a loud noise from the washing room and went to check on the wash. The noise was so loud i pushed the power button and stopped the wash cycle. At this point water spilled out of the bottom of the washing machine. I have now left the washing machine unplugged and unused.
justification: The incident involved a loud noise and water spillage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: washer vibrates excessively banging into dryer .
justification: Excessive vibration and banging indicate an incident but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: Made a phone call to Samsung who said that although my washer was on the recall list according to the serial number it didn't fall in the recall.  I proceeded to say that this was already the second washer since I bought it 4 months ago.  First one made all kind of weird noises and since it was within 30 days replaced it.Also told the rep. that it was banging at high speeds and that the tub was so loose that I was having to run it at low speeds to keep the washer from sounding like it was going to fly off.  My washer has all the same problems the other washers have but she said call a repairman and hung up.
justification: The description indicates a malfunctioning washer causing inconvenience and potential safety concerns, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
This caller purchased his original top loading washer from a retailer in Pearl City, Hawaii.
This washer was delivered, was damaged January 2016 and it was replaced by the washer being reported. 
The replacement washer was delivered March 9, 2016.  Washer legs were adjusted and leveled.  Subsequently, machine vibration was an issue.

He contacted the installer March 26, 2016 to report that the washer had moved, had shifted position by 0.5 inch, unsure if legs even.

The installer came to the caller's home April 1, 2016 and advised the caller that the right front foot was lower than it was supposed to be, he adjusted the front foot and measured for levelness.  He also adjusted back foot.

September 13, 2016 the caller's sister used his washer and informed him that the washer was rocking.

The caller looked at the right front foot which was off the ground so he adjusted the right front foot to be level with the floor. wobbly.

The caller contacted the customer service line October 5, 2016 when he noticed that the foot was not stable again and he believes had been and had continued to be moving out of where it should be to level the washer.

He did notice that the tub of the machine hit the right side of the washer on several occasions.

October 7, 2016 the service technician came to the caller's home and after informing him that if he rocks his drum front to back there is more play than if it is back to front.

The service technician advised the caller that he has to order four dampers to repair the machine, two in the back and two in the front to repair this condition.  Following 10/14/16 installation of dampers, washer vibration and noisiness continued to be present.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller has been in touch with the manufacturer a few times during the past few months
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washer with repeated issues but no injuries or deaths reported.

incident_description: Our Frigidaire dehumidifier (model #FAD704DWD, serial #KN60501903) purchased on Amazon in July of 2016 was placed in our basement approximately 10 feet from our smoke alarm.  The unit has caused the smoke alarm to sound off due to either heat or smoke approximately 12 times since the purchase date.  We tend to let the unit cool down before use, but given the recent recall involving similar units, we have stopped using it and are inquiring with the company for a replacement.
justification: The dehumidifier caused the smoke alarm to sound multiple times but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The washer been really loud and moves on the spin cycle.

incident_description: GE top loading washing machine less than one year old, was operating normally and at some point in the cycle, literally exploded in our laundry room, causing extensive damage to my walls and the machine itself.  Made no abnormal noises before the incident.  Water and drywall everywhere, along with numerous parts from the machine.  Fortunately no one was in the room when it happened because someone would have probably been injured.

incident_description: My machine started giving me problems a month after my husband purchased it. He couldn't detect the problem but claimed that the machine was not leveled. He ended up adjusting the machine but to this day, the machine vibrates excessively while am doing doing laundry, which forced me to stop using the machine altogether now.

incident_description:
(8/30/2016) The consumer stated that one alarm started going off occasionally but then went off about every half hour. The consumer had to take the product off the wall and press the silent button. 

The consumer stated that the false alarms started about a week or a week and half until she had to remove it completely from the wall.

(08/30/2016) The consumer contacted the mfr. The consumer stated that the mfr did not ask any questions about proper use or anything but told her that they would replace the smoke alarm. 

The consumer received the replacement but is afraid to use it, especially since it has the same mfr date code.

(10/07/2016) The consumer stated that a second smoke alarm, same model she purchased same sate as the first one, went off afterward, but would not stop when the silent button was pressed it had to be immediately removed from the wall and it took a while until the silent button finally worked.  A red light near the silent button started blinking. Several hours later, the red blinking light turned to white and then finally stopped.  The consumer is fearful & other alarms purchase w/ around same time will do the same thing.  Consumer is taking all 4 back to the store for a refund and will purchase diff. CO type of alarms.
justification: The incident involves false alarms and inconvenience but no injury or death.

incident_description: On or about October 27, 2016, my Samsung top load washer, model number WA422PRHDWR/AA, flooded my house.  I placed a load of laundry in the washer, turned it on, and 15 to 20 minutes later water poured from my laundry room into the garage, three bedrooms, three hallways, kitchen, and a  bathroom.  A message error appeared on the washer as it alarmed to the malfunction.  Before water restoration could begin, a formal dining, formal living, hallway, and a second living area were ruined by water from the Samsung top load washer.  A plumber came out and cleared the house of active water leaks.  When he turned the washer on and water immediately poured from the bottom of the washer.  The result was a significant amount of water in the laundry area.  An appliance technician was called out and he found that a pump which connected the water hose to the washer had broken.  He reported that he had specific instructions from Samsung on replacement of the part because there had been cases of this part breaking, causing water damage.  The position of the water pump and hose posed a high risk for malfunction and breakage.
justification: The incident caused significant water damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The technician's report indicates this is a known issue, suggesting a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Samsung top loader washer top shakes and caused washer to jump around while washing and spinning.  I called Samsung to help with this and they said that they were not able to help and that although I thought there was a warrant, I was told the warranty would not cover that action.
justification: The washer shaking and jumping is an incident with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The issue is likely to occur based on the description and the high frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description: washer basket spinning out of balance, dancing around the room dinging matching dryer.
justification: The washer basket spinning out of balance and moving around is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I have an L G top loading washer that dances and goes crazy and seems like it is going to explode. I never bought the warranty  so I never have had some one look at it. Both washer and dryer cost me around  $1700.00  and I am still paying for them. I have been hit by the washers several all times on my feet.  The washer scares me but I have to tolerate it because I have to finish paying it. This is so unfair to continue to pay for a washer when it does not work right and it may explode and hurt me. Is there a recall on my washer.  L G washer WT487OCW. 303PNPD32296.

incident_description: Smelled burning in basement.  Tracked the smell to the dehumidifier.  Unplugged the unit and turned it over.  Found the bottom burned and melted and my carpet was also burned directly under the unit.  Call manufacturer and still waiting for response.  The unit is a Danby model DDR6009REE.  If the unit was left on longer my house could have burned down.  Please beware that this unit could be deadly.

incident_description: I purchase a Samsung Washer and dryer 6/6/14. I notice when I wash my clothes the wash machine get very loud and when it start to spin it spin like it out of control and I can hear it all the way upstairs. Then after it stop I get a error message UE and it keep doing that three or four times after you check and restart and each time when the machine start spinning out of control
justification: The washing machine is malfunctioning and causing loud noises and error messages, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I was home alone and started a load of laundry.  I was upstairs and heard what I thought was construction noise.  It sounded like a boulder being dropped in a dumpster.  I went downstairs and noticed that my washer was about a foot away from where it normally is.  As I was standing there, it started to spin at a very high speed and started to lift off the ground and shake side to side.  I threw myself on to the washer and tried to hit the stop button. It continued to spin violently.  I hit it again and it finally came to a stop, with the results in the pictures.  In person the washer looks much worse. 

Here is where things go wrong, as if the traumatic incident wasn't bad enough.  I called Home Depot (where the washer was purchased) and was referred  call Samsung directly.  I was informed that there was a recall on some of the Samsung washers.  This was the first time I had heard of it.  I called Samsung at 12:45.  I spoke to a agent who showed very little concern about the incident  or my safety.  He was trying to start a claim and told me that I would be contacted within 2-4 hours.  I was extremely traumatized and had been shaking and crying.  I expressed this to the agent and was told again someone would call.  That didn't happen.  At almost 6pm yesterday I started to  reach out to Samsung again.  When I called it was an automated system that told me I had called before and asked if my info had changed, but then there was dead silence and I could reach a person.  I went on the Samsung chat and tried to get somewhere that way.  I was told I needed to wait till someone called me.  I then asked in the chat if I should go to the media and was told that an urgent message would be sent and that I should keep trying the 800 #.  So I tried again and asked for a customer rep this time in the beginning of the call.  I was able to talk to someone.  This was the 4th attempt in calling.  I again was told that someone would call me. It was almost 6:30.  While on the phone a vm popped through. My phone never rang.  It was from a [REDACTED] at 201-982-8897 at Samsung. I called back, but got his vm.  It is 9:30 on Friday now.  I have still not heard from [REDACTED].  

I have a 4 year old daughter, two sons ages 8 and 11 and a dog.  Had they been standing where I was yesterday, I hate to think of what could have happen.  I am still very upset about this.  The timing is so odd because of this being on GMA this morning.  I am lucky that no one was hurt.  I am super disappointed in how his is being handled by Samsung.  I just purchased Samsung range microwave three weeks ago.  I have totally lost trust in Samsung and am going to contact Home Depot about replacing the microwave too.
justification: The washer malfunctioned violently but no one was injured, and the likelihood of such an incident is possible given the recall context.

incident_description: I own one on the Samsung top loading washers.  I have suffered physical injury and did research about my machine prior to the recall.  Samsung denied any problems and blew me off.  Can someone please call me and I will put together a timeline of everything for you.  [REDACTED].  Thank-you.
justification: The description mentions physical injury, which corresponds to severity level 3.

incident_description: Washing machine have been making a lot of noise during spin cycle. Called a washing machine repairman to my house and he said it was okay. Also it moves a lot during spinning like it is going to come apart. Noticed they have a recall on my machine
justification: The washing machine is making excessive noise and moving excessively, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
We bought our Samsung WA456DRHDSU/AA washing machine in December of 2012.  At first it ran so smoothly.
But then over time, It started to shake a little and make a worrisome banging sound during the spin cycle.  At first, it would shake and bang and then that noise would go away as the spin cycle continued. From about 2014 to 2016, we had no idea that we were putting ourselves, our children and grandchildren in danger, but we suspected that what the machine was doing wasn't a good thing.  In the summer of 2016, the machine started shaking and banging much louder and lasted a whole lot longer.  I would be afraid to go check it in case it was about to explode or something.  In September of 2016 it started shaking and banging so bad that an error message appeared on the machine and the machine shut down.   
We were not aware of a recall at that time, and therefore called an appliance repair company to check out what was wrong with our machine.  We were told it was the "shocks" and had those repaired at a cost of $250 to us.

Even though our machine has run better since that costly repair, we don't dare place heavier items in there or fill the machine more than halfway full.  This is unacceptable. We should be able to wash clothes, bedding, towels, etc as we have done for years and years.  Without worry.  We have always just placed things that needed washing in our old washing machines and washed them and didn't worry that the machine was going to go out of control.  Seems technology has made us go backwards, instead of forward.
justification: The washing machine exhibited concerning behavior but did not result in any injury or death, only inconvenience and repair costs.

incident_description: Samsung washing machine WA422PRHDWR. The washing machine starts to make loud noises, shaking and jumping around the laundry room.
justification: The washing machine's loud noises and movement indicate a malfunction that could lead to injury if not addressed, though no injury is reported yet.

incident_description: Heard about the recall of certain models of Samsung top load washing machines on 11/4/2016.  The recall notice states that the top cover of the machine may be blown off when the machine is in use.   My washer is one of 34 affected machines. Although we have not had an incident, we want to have the machine modified in order to prevent any problems.
