incident_description: My washer was going thru the dry cycle spinning and basket hit the shell of the washer and dented the shell now it does it all the time it sounds like a loud banging and sound like it's gona fall apart..
justification: The incident describes damage to the washer but no mention of injury or harm to a person.

incident_description: The washer and dryer were purchased Aug 21 2016.  Neither of the worked properly. The washer sounded like a jet taking off when it spun.  The cloths were all tangled up and a mess.  The dryer will not dry on the first time you have to keep setting the minutes.
justification: The incident describes malfunctioning appliances causing inconvenience but no injury or death.

incident_description: This washer lid popped open and hurt my wrist badly, bruising my arm for weeks!  I was reaching to stop it at the control panel as the load sounded unbalanced.  I yanked my arm back too violently and tore something in my shoulder.  My wife's a doctor so I didn't seek medical attention, but I still have shoulder pain from the incident.  How do I know your next machine isn't going to hurt me?  A rebate of $31 is NOT acceptable to me.  An hour of my wife's time is $210, not to mention the time I spent rehabbing my wrist and shoulder.  DO YOU THINK THIS IS A GAME?  Samsung offering $31 rebate is like them thumbing their nose at those of us their machines hurt.
justification: The description mentions injuries to the wrist and shoulder, including bruising and persistent pain, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such incidents can happen but are not extremely common.

incident_description: Washer was in the spin cycle with just a couple of minutes left and we heard a loud boom, like 2 cars crashing then the machine shut down. There was a loud grinding noise like a tire coming to a screeching halt and lots of banging from side to side, then It stopped spinning but completed the countdown and water is drained. Not sure if we should try another load.
justification: The incident involved a loud noise and machine malfunction, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(10/04/2016) The consumer stated that the dryer was in use. It had been running for a couple minutes. The consumer stated that his wife went past the room where the product was located and smelled something burning.  She turned the dryer off. The consumer went in the room and saw smoke coming the dryer. He turned on the vent and called 911.

The fire department came out and checked the lint trap and the line going out of the unit. The line and the lint trap was clean.  The consumer was advised that it smelled electrical there was no fire.

The consumer called Best Buy to get warranty information. The consumer called the warranty department. A dispatch was set up for a service company called Big Kountry. The technician took the dryer apart and found lint under the drum of the dryer. The entire bottom of the drum between the wall housing and the drum was black.

The consumer will contact Whirlpool.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no fire or injuries, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
My family and I purchased appliances for our new home. Home Depot delivered them on 09/09/16. We only moved into the house the following weekend and started using the washer and dryer. Upon completing the first dryer cycle we proceeded to clean the lint filter and noticed that the screen was burnt in 2 place in on the corners. I immediately contacted Samsung 3 times who gave the run around from the beginning, first saying that the serial number (listed on the product and invoice) were not valid. After several attempts I managed to speak to a representative who told me that I can buy a replacement filter and there's nothing that they will do about this. I managed to speak to a supervisor (on their online chat) who told me that it's normal for the filter to get burnt during normal operation which is mind boggling to me. I threaten to filed a CPSC report and  only then they became somewhat more responsive. Coincidentally, I had to go on an extended trip and received a few calls which I was unable to answer. It's worth mentioning that Samsung requests a back-up number in case the main number is not available but nobody called my wife's number. When I returned and listed to the voicemail; they were all scripted, saying precisely the same thing, that a replacement filter is mailed and assuring me that the drier is fine to use. I am reluctant about using the dryer and we only use it when the children are away so we prevent any incident. 
I had called Samsung again last week and was put on hold for 45 minutes then hang up. I called again and managed to request a technician to inspect the dryer. Finally I got a call this morning advising me that in spite of the time sensitive and safety concerns which are evident, a technician might or might not be available next Monday or Wednesday. I am concerned about this dryer safety and if the filter is burnt, whether delivered burnt or burnt during "normal" operation. This is not normal.
justification: The incident involves a burnt lint filter in a dryer, which poses a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: I own two Samsung washers that have been verified as being included in the defective models (WA50F9A6DSW/A2).  Both were purchased in 2014.  The one machine that gets used regularly has exploded.  The lid has disintegrated and separated from the body of the machine.  Who knows what damage has occurred inside the machine to cause this type of visible outward damage.  After learning that that this was not an isolated case, I have called Samsung three times to try to get a resolution.  The best I can describe the interactions is that I am given the run-around.  On the first call they acknowledged the problem which I appreciated, and said I would receive a call to schedule service.  When that call never happened, I called back and Samsung had no record of my first call.  This time they gave me the number for a service company and a confirmation number.  When I called the service company, they informed me that there would be a $99 service call fee and that I would be responsible for the cost of the repair.  This did not seem right to me since I am dealing with a defective machine.  So I called Samsung back for a third time only to be told that all repairs will be my responsibility.  They made it clear that Samsung has no plans to repair, replace, or be responsible in any way for my washer exploding.
justification: The incident involved a defective washer exploding, causing visible damage but no reported injury, and the issue appears to be a known problem with the model.

incident_description: A cordless Micro Dremel started all by itself last nite at 2am.It woke us from our sleep with the motor revving so high it took me pushing the off button 3 times.When we went to set it down my husband realized it was really hot so instead of putting it in the battery charging cradle we set it on the table in my craft room (where it was when it turned on by itself across the hall from our bedroom)We went back to bed and within a few minutes started to smell an electrical or melting plastic smell got up again and the Dremel was soooo hot my husband had to get a pot holder to move it outside.The smell was so strong we had to put on our fan and spray room spray.The next morning we brought it back inside and the strong smell was still there but it would not turn on or off.If we had not been home I really fear our house would have burned down.I do not recall hearing anything about this on the news but seems very unsafe.It started by itself!!!!!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning Dremel that overheated and emitted a strong smell, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was laying in bed while a load of 1 comforter was washing in the washing machine when we heard an explosion. We walked in to the hallway where the Laundry Room is and the whole top of my washing Machine blew off water hit the ceiling parts flew into the hallway.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and damage to the washing machine, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I own a top load Samsung washing machine that is 3 years old and under the Premium Service Plan sold to me by HH Gregg. This plan has a life span of two more years as of November 1, 2016.
I find that my washing machine is under investigation by Samsung and the CPC, but this does not solve my problem.
The washing machine is the subject matter listed in a recent news article where-in  the machine will vibrate out of control when in the spin cycle. Inspection of my unit reveals that the tub is separating from the side wall on the bottom and the plastic parts which make up the top of the tub are being chewed up somehow. In addition clothing is found to be stuck under the spinning parts on the bottom of the tub making it necessary to pull with force to remove the article of clothing. This is damaging to the clothing to say the least. 
Samsung reports when the CPC and Samsung reach "an agreement" they will notify me as to a solution. The warranty people tell me that if the machine is "still washing clothes" then the protection plan will not cover the problem and we must wait until complete failure of the machine is evident. 
This tells me two things, first the Premium Service Plan is not worth the paper it is written on and  second considering the recent articles on Samsung products they are not worth my consideration in the future.
justification: The washing machine is malfunctioning and damaging clothing, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: When I first started this heater and after several minutes on high a flame started coming out of the control knob and started the plastic knob on fire. I was able to turn the tank off but the control knob continued to burn until it was completely destroyed.
justification: The incident involved a flame and fire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(08/2016) The consumer stated that two weeks after she purchased the adapter, she plugged it into the wall outlet. After about twenty-five minutes she smelled something burning. There was smoke coming from the adapter. The consumer's daughter unplugged the product. The fingers of her daughter's left hand was burned.

No medical attention was required.

The consumer has pictures.
justification: The daughter's fingers were burned, indicating an injury, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description: Our Washer is part of the recall for the top loading Samsung washers.  Since the recall we have been aware of the problem with exploding tubs and we have chosen not to use the washer in the evening due to our children's rooms being located by the laundry room.  On 10/30/2016 we were in the living room while a load of laundry was being washed.  We heard a loud bang from the laundry room.  Went in to inspect and found that our entire washing tub had fallen to the bottom of the washer. The washer will not drain, spin or run a cycle.  I feel very fortunate that it did not spin out uncontrollably as other's have experienced, causing damage and harm to my family. However, this washer is only 5 years old and we have had it serviced when we move  in order to make sure it was balanced right, it seems to me that this should have lasted longer than this time frame.
justification: The incident involved a loud bang and the washing tub falling, but no injuries or damage occurred.

incident_description:

Subject: Fwd: Concerns with GE Dehumidifier

Dear Mam or Sir,

Good morning. I'm writing because i have some concerns regarding a GE dehumidifier ADEL70LRL1.

I have two in my basement. One was running significantly more than the other one so i went to check on it. They are both set up with the hose drain and where set to 50% and connected to a surge suppressor. I removed the bin, so i could see if there was an issue with the hose, i found an area to be significantly discolored. I proceeded to touch the area, and found it to be significantly hot. r/s,

incident_description: I was using our shark press and refresh to dewrinkle some shirts just as I have done many times before. I immediately dropped the steamer and began to run my hand under cold water as my husband ran in and unplugged the steamer.  Two fingers sustained painful burns.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her washer vibrates violently and her clothes is usually twisted and ripped when she takes them out.   This incident has been ongoing for a few months. She was informed by the company to wash her clothing on gentle cycle but that does not work for her.  

Caller feels that this washer is extremely unsafe and something should be done before it explodes and harm consumers.
justification: The incident involves property damage (ripped clothes) and potential safety concerns, but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:

incident_description:
About one year ago when our five year old Samsung front load washer (model WF218ANW) was doing a load of laundry there was a loud clunk and vibration just at the end of the spin cycle.  After consulting the internet it was determined that the flange shaft assembly probably cracked.  The flange shaft assembly is bolted to the back of the stainless steel drum which is directly attached to the motor.  The drum is held inside a two piece plastic tub which holds the water. Once the washer was disassembled it was confirmed that one of the three arms of the shaft assembly had indeed cracked.  Although the washer is five years old the inside of the drum as well as the inside of the cabinet look new.  There are no signs of leaks or any misuse and only HE detergent has been used.  However, the back of the drum and the shaft assembly which have been sealed inside the tub looked like a giant Petri tree dish.  When cloths are being washed they are constantly being sloshed into the same water that is being splashed onto the flange shaft assembly.  In effect washing the cloths with water that contains whatever comes off the shaft assembly.  The shaft assembly is a casting made with a metal other than stainless steel and since it does not have a smooth surface there are various areas where water can settle.  It is also directly connected to the stainless steel drum with six stainless steel bolts.  The different metals in direct contact with each other in a wet environment apparently causes the galvanic corrosion of the flange shaft assemble to the point of weakening.  That coupled with the design of the part with all its nooks and crannies for water to settle makes me question the safety of the design.  
I do not know if this design is peculiar to this model washer or not but, if this problem is indeed real and not particular to our machine it could explain why there are complaints of a moldy smell inside some front loaders even thou the inside of the washer and rubber door ring seal is spotless.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure (cracked flange shaft assembly) without any reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as the issue seems design-related but not universally reported across all models.

I am reporting a problem with an Electrolux Home Products Frigidaire Room Air Conditioner. The Model is FRA064AT7 and the Serial Number is KK25142655.

He smelled a strong musty odor. He looked closely at the air conditioner and saw there was black mold on the vents (located on the front above the air filter), so he removed them and clean them. He also could see inside the air conditioner and saw the fan and other parts inside the body of the air conditioner had black mold, including the white Styrofoam inner shell. We do not know how long this black mold had been growing in the air conditioner.

My husband and I both experienced numerous mold-related health issues due to the mold inside the air conditioner. We didn't realize the health issues we were having were due to mold until we discovered the mold on the vents and in the air conditioner. After cleaning the mold off the vents (and regularly checking and cleaning them since then), the health issues have decreased. The mold still remained inside the body of the air conditioner.

The air conditioner's manual has Care and Cleaning instructions regarding the air filter and exterior cabinet only. It does not indicate that the vents (located on the front above the air filter) and the interior body of the air conditioner need to be cleaned. It is easy to remove the vents and clean them. However, it is quite a process to access the interior body of the air conditioner.

Suggestions: The manual should at least be updated to include the vents as a part that needs to be cleaned on a regular basis. Perhaps the interior components could be made of mold-resistant materials.

The mold that grew in this air conditioner is definitely a health issue for people. My husband and I do not own a pet, but I wonder if the mold could also cause health issues for pets.

Now that it is autumn and the temperatures are cooler, we have removed the air conditioner for the season. My husband took the air conditioner apart, and I took pictures.

I will attach photos of the inside of the air conditioner, pictures of the model/serial number tag on the outside of the air conditioner, and the Care and Cleaning instructions that are in the air conditioner manual. I have also attached a photo of the front of the air conditioner showing the vents that I refer to above. The vent photo shows them after they were cleaned and the air conditioner is ready for winter storage.

For the Incident Date below, I will use an estimated date of when my husband turned on the air conditioner by hand and smelled the strong musty odor.
justification: The incident caused mold-related health issues to the users, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as mold growth in air conditioners is a known issue but not universal.

incident_description:
Our Samsung washer exploded this afternoon. Model WA422PRHDWR/AA, S/N Y01Y5AECC00898M. Yes, it's a recalled model -- one we never received a recall notice about. We called a service number saying we *may* get a call in 7-10 days. This is unreal.

I heard a loud noise and my washer had jolted itself away from the wall, and was making a violent noise. Mind you, the load was normal as was the cycle. I pressed "stop" on the machine, and noted the interior drum looked mangled on the inside. The top of the washer seems to have exploded from the joint. 

This is very dangerous. I've come to find you've already been contacted regarding this issue -- PLEASE HELP. Samsung set up a special hotline to apparently deal with this issue -- the best response we got calling in was that someone would call us in about two weeks! No offer of any solution or help, aside from an email to tell us to wash our clothes on the delicate cycle! Our machine is destroyed! incident_description:
9/28/2016 (4:30pm) The washer was started by the consumer's wife and she left the home.  There were 2 baby towels and baby clothes in the washer.

The consumer came home and found that the washer turned around 180 degrees and was facing the wall.  The electric cord was pinned against the corner.  The outer shell of the front and rear of the washer was bent from the drum banging around inside during the wash cycle.  The entire top portion of the washer was hanging on the side and being held by wires from the control panel.  

The clothes dryer was also damaged from the washer banging against it.  One could see the path that the washer took as it moved around.  There was no damage to the walls or floors.  There were no injuries & no one was home at the time.


NOTE:  The consumer's washer was repaired under CPSC Recall# 13-073, in April of 2016, but he was told that it was NOT included in the recall.    

7/2015:  The consumer noticed that his washer shook during use and it would move approximately 1' to 2' from the original location.  The consumer initially contacted Sears about Recall 13-073, but he was told that he did not have the correct model, because he was not providing enough numbers.  The consumer double checked his numbers and saw the numbers 2972, but there were 3 very small numbers prior to it, which were 796, which he relayed to Sears.  The consumer was told his washer was not recalled.   

4/2016:  The washer continued to move and the consumer looked at the CPSC recall further.  He identified that his serial number matched the range listed in CPSC'S recall.  The consumer contacted Sears again and was told that his washer was not included in the recall.  The consumer then contacted the CPSC and his information was taken.   Approximately a day or 2 later, Sears contacted the consumer and sent the recall-repair parts to his home.   A tech was came out within approx. 3 days, but he did not do the repair.  The tech. told the consumer that based on the numbers on his washer, it was not recalled and he took the parts that were mailed to the consumer back with him.

The consumer followed up with the CPSC, who in turn contacted the firm again.  A technician came out and inspected the washer.  The tech. found problems with the washerÃÂs struts and the barrel.  The tech. checked the consumer's model/serial numbers and indicated that the washer was not included in the recall.  The consumer showed the tech. a printout of Recall # 13-073 with identified model/serial numbers and the tech. agreed to do the repair under the recall.  The tech. ordered the parts and they were sent to the consumer's home overnight.  Once the parts arrived, the consumer contacted the tech. and he came back out and made the repairs.  

The washer appeared to work as it should until this most recent incident.

Although LG manufactured the washer, Sears handles the matters that arise with their brand of washers. 

9/28/16:  The consumer spent 4+ hours on the phone with Sears discussing this latest incident and was not offered a resolution or assistance
justification: The incident caused significant damage to the washer and dryer but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Please see the attached letter for a description of my experience and supporting documentation.


To whom it may concern,

I recently had a painful and scary incident happen while using Jaws Quick Spit product. I am writing you today to share my experience with the hopes that this information can help make changes to the product, package labeling and brand management to ensure a safer consumer experience for others.


I bought at bottle of Quick Spit on September 4, 2014 from Swim Outlet (receipt and pictures of bottle are included below) and have been using the product to defog my swim goggles. On October 5, 2016 I was competing in a one mile open water swim race. I sprayed the product inside the lenses of my swim goggles and rinsed them before the race. About a minute into the race I felt both eyes start to burn and my vision blur. After exiting the water the pain and blurriness continued to get worse to the point that I could no longer open my eyes. I got help from my fellow swimmers to find the bottle and followed the directions to flush my eyes for 15-20 minutes with fresh water. After an hour of flushing my eyes I was
still in excruciating pain and could not open my eyes. At this point, we made the decision to go to the Emergency Room.

In the ER I went through a painful process of having my eyes flushed for an extended period of time to ensure all chemicals were removed from my eyes. After that, a doctor gave me an eye examination and determined I had corneal abrasions on both eyes. To provide me the proper care the ER nurses and doctors searched the product website, MSDS and poison control to figure out what chemicals were in the product however, they were not able to locate them anywhere. After a consult with an ophthalmologist without any additional information about the product, they taped my eyes shut, put
me on pain medications and antibiotics and sent me home.


I was not able to open my eyes for three days and as a result was out of work for two days and relied on care from my husband and friends to perform basic functions. I was in excruciating pain for the first three days with little relief even while taking strong pain medications. When I was able to start opening my eyes again I had extreme blurriness, light sensitivity and constant scratchiness in my eyes. Along with an expensive eight hour ER visit, I've had three follow-up doctor's visits and medications to add to the expense so far and I'm still recovering.

For a product that is intended for surfaces so close to the eye and that is advertised as "natural" and "ECO friendly and non-toxic" I'm very surprised that this happened to me. Also, I find it unacceptable that there is no additional information on the main chemicals in the product. Without an understanding of what was in the product the ER doctor and my ophthalmologist were guessing about the best course of treatment. After wondering if this has happened to anyone else, I've spent time reading reviews of the product. Unfortunately there are many other people that have experienced the same thing as me. In
the negative reviews on Amazon you can read about many others to which this has happened. The DC Tri Club blog is another example of consumers with the same issues.


Again, my hope is that you take this issue and situation seriously and take the appropriate measures to ensure that your product and consumers are safe. It has been a very painful and expensive process.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in corneal abrasions, severe pain, and required emergency medical treatment, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
My daughter in law recently had an extremely scary situation relating to some cabinet and drawer latches and I wanted to report it so that hopefully this and similar dangerous products can be removed from the market. I hope you are the right person to contact. If not, I'd appreciate it if you could let me know who I should refer this to.
 
The situation
My daughter in law was in her kitchen with her 3 year old daughter. The child attempted to get into a cabinet that had a safety latch installed. Suddenly there was a loud scream. The child had pushed her head into the cabinet and one of the "safety" latches had somehow pushed into her eye and had caught under her eyelid. Since the child's head was into the cabinet it was hard to see what the problem was but when the child was finally freed, there was much bleeding that resulted in a trip to the emergency room and two very shaken up parents.
 
The product
The product is called "KidCo" and came in a 12 pack. Their site is: www.kidco.com and the box label specifies: Cabinet & Drawer Lock      #S338.
 
The company
Kidco Inc. 1013 Technology Way, Libertyville, ILL 60048-5349
 
Notes
- The latch portion of the product is very narrow and has sharp edges. A product that is intended to be placed at the head height of a small child should be much larger and much smoother. This product is not suitable for this application and should be removed from the market.
- There may be other such products that should be examined. It would be a tragedy if any child had the loss of an eye or any permanent injury from these products.
- I would be pleased to send the product to whoever could investigate further.
- I was surprised to hear that the emergency room staff did not follow up to gather information on the product and report it directly
- I have not contacted the company. I felt that contacting someone who could rapidly get the product off the shelf was a better way
 
Please contact me if you need further information or provide contact information so that I could contact you.
 
[REDACTED]
justification: The child suffered an injury requiring emergency room treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but possible with defective safety products.

The consumer states that the dryer began working but shortly after the consumer's wife noticed that the dryer was still taking 2 hours to dry their kids work out clothes. incident_description:
Manufucturer: General Electric 
Model Number: DCLR333GTWW

The dryer's lint filter leaves an air gap around the filter that allows lint to pass through the dryer venting system.  I contacted GE to let them know of the dryer design, but the technician I met and spoke to said that was normal. incident_description:
Hello,

I have one of the top loading washers that are affected by the top falling off.  My washer's top shot off completely in the end of February.  On March 1st I called Samsung to inform them of the problem.  The top shot off the washer and the levers on each side that had held it on were rusted and sharp.  I had actually cut my finger on one.  Anyhow, Samsung talked as if it were our fault and said it wouldn't be covered under any type of warranty. We did not do the repair because we knew it was a faulty washer and were going to try Samsung again.  

Since March 1st, the only way I can keep my top on my washer is by using a 20 pound weight to set on top of it.  I have been using the light spin since the top broke off in February but the weight will still fall off onto the floor.  It is not safe.

Not only has the top shot off but the unit around the lid is all rusted and so it part of the lid.  This washer isn't even 2 years old and began rusting within a year's time.  On top of that, the cap on the inside of the washer came off during a load of clothes and tore many of the clothes in the washer.  We tried to repair it and it did it again with the next load.  We have about 15 pieces of clothing ruined because of it.

October 3rd is when I heard about the top loading issue.  I was not surprised at all.  I went onto the Samsung website and entered my washer model and serial number and foudn out it WAS  one that was affected.  

On the same day, I called Samsung customer service to ask if there was anything they could do in the meantime.  It is NOT safe and I shouldn't have to pay hundreds of dollars to have it fixed.  It cost over $1,000 less than two years ago and was a Christmas gift to my husband and I by my in-laws.  The girl I spoke with talked to her supervisor who informed me that I should not use the washing machine at all.  Really??  That is terrible customer service.  We're a family of four with two kids in travel sports.  I wash clothes consistantly and need a working, safe washing machine.  I told her the only way I can stop using it is if they will replace it.  I'd even be happy with them fixing it for now.  When I asked her how long it would take for a solution to be determined she told me she didn't know and it could takes months.  I just can't see where that is ok.

So now I'm using an unsafe washer, because it was made faulty, and there's nothing that can be done to help me.  What a terrible feeling.

I'm in the process of creating a letter to send to several places but wanted to contact you before I did that.  I'm hoping you can do something to help me instead. 

Thank you,
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
Whenever I use my Samsung washer machine, which is about 2.5 years old, it both leaks from the bottom, and vibrates very strongly and unnaturally. When the vibrations start, there are usually very loud, booming and banging noises. The machine usually wobbles back and forth due to the vibrations, and has, on occasion, moved over a foot from where it started the wash. The vibrations seem to occur prior to the last spin/rinse cycle. They also do not cause the machine to register an error, and thereby have the machine stop itself.

Neither my wife or I do a load of wash unless we are at home. That being the case, we are able to stop the washer as soon as the violent vibrations start. I do not know what would happen if we didn't; the vibrations only seem to get worse the longer you let the machine run. In order to successfully do a load of wash, we have to run the machine up until the banging starts, stop the machine, and put it through a manual rinse/spin cycle.

I have contacted Samsung multiple times about both the leaking, and vibration issues. In addition to them being extraordinarily unhelpful, the only time they took me semi-seriously is when I mentioned that I thought the washer leak may have caused water damage to my home. After going through the exhaustive claims process in which I had to resubmit the paperwork multiple times because either "I never sent them anything" or "they lost it" , I never heard back from Samsung on the status of my claim.

This is an ongoing problem as my wife and I still use the washer because we can't afford a new one.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washer causing leaks and violent vibrations, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting a Gyr Landis smart meter that was at one time placed on her home late September/early October 2011 but was moved to approximately 70 feet away from her home in 2015 due to adverse reactions causing illness that began a couple of weeks after it was placed on her home.

She began to hear buzzing in her ears the first two weeks then a couple of months later she began to exhibit neurological symptoms similar to Parkinson's Disease .

The symptoms reduced the dexterity in her hands, limited range of motion of her right arm, she began having tremors and shaking in her entire body.

She believed that if the meter was moved her symptoms would then improve, however because it is a wiring meter it is still connected with communication signals in electrical wiring that it was never meant to carry.

She has been seen by her physician but states that these conditions as a result of the smart meters is so new that doctors are not extremely familiar with them.  Her physician however did draft a letter stating that it would be a good idea to remove the meter from anyone near her living area or property.

Her mobility has recently began to suffer and she states that this is due to the smart meter and the communication signals acting as an antenna damaging her health and quality of life.

The caller has contacted the utility company asking that this meter be changed back to an analog meter but this request has been refused.
justification: The caller reports neurological symptoms and reduced mobility attributed to the smart meter, indicating injury.

incident_description:
Every window in my house is made by a company called Hurd Windows.

They are dual paned windows with Low E Glass and my understanding is that they have some type of gas in between the two layers of glass to help with insulation.

On at least six occasions I have had the interior pane of glass - what I can only refer to as spontaneously combust. This usually occurs during the winter months when the weather is cold and the heat is on inside the house.

These windows are not cheap to repair or replace and pose a danger to anyone who is in the room when the combustion occurs.

On at least one occasion my children had just left the room when one of the windows exploded.

They were not injured but I cannot believe that I am the only consumer that this has happened to. I feel confident that someone has or will be hurt by this flying glass.

On a prior occasion I contacted Hurd Windows by email, never to be contacted in return.

If this is still occurring with their products they should be pulled from the mrket.

Do I have any recourse?
justification: The incident involves spontaneous combustion of windows, posing danger but no reported injuries yet, though the potential for harm is noted.

incident_description:
On 8/11/15, our Samsung Washer leaked gallons of water through our 1st floor laundry area down into our daughterÃÂs bedroom. The model number of the washer is WA400PJHDWR/ AA. The serial number is Y69Q5AECB04812Z. The electricity had to be turned off in the basement due to the risk of an electrical short and fire hazard. The entire ceiling in the bedroom was ruined, her clothes were soaked and the floor in her room was saturated with water. Water was found pooled in a light fixture located in her ceiling tile. The service technician informed us that the drain pump was misdesigned to be under the tub. Vibrations from the tub caused the housing to crack open and the pump leaked expelled fluid under the unit. He told us that it was a flaw known to Samsung but that no recall was issued to pro-actively replace and relocate the pumps to a different location under the machine. Photos showing the water damage were sent to Samsung on 8/13/15. The wet clothes were laundered at a laundromat, the floor dried and new ceiling tiles purchased to replace the ruined ceiling. All of the work was performed by ourselves. On 10/27/15 a receipt for the cost of the ceiling tiles was submitted to Samsung for reimbursement. On 11/26/15, the receipt was resubmitted as there was no response to the first submission. On 12/28/15, I contacted the head of Samsung quality, [REDACTED] directly and asked for assistance with receiving a reimbursement check A reply from an [REDACTED] was received on 1/4/16 stating that a reimbursement check would be issued to cover the cost of the ceiling tiles. On 1/13/16, we received an email stating that a reimbursement check had been cut for the cost to the damages.
Yesterday, we read that the same machine is being investigated for explosion risk. It should be obvious that the design of this machine is truly flawed and dangerous for the consumers. It can lead to water damage and fire hazard along with explosion of the unit. We feel quite strongly that this unit should be eligible for a complete refund that can be used to purchase another machine from a different manufacturer.

incident_description:
Product: Rheem Professional Prestige 50 gallon hybrid heat pump electric water heater
Serial number Q41150054
Model number PROPH50 T2 RH245

My water heater was installed late last year in my garage. Permit was obtained, installation inspected and approved by the City after installation. I have been using the water heater in Heat Pump only ode since installation set to 140 degrees.

This morning I came home from a drive and heard an alarm chiming on the water heater. The service icon was blinking and I found an alert for error code A004 comp.shutdown. I smelt a slight electrical burning smell and the top of the unit was warm to the touch.

I called Rheem's Heat Pump Water heater customer service line at 800-995-0982. I was walked through a couple of steps (confirming what the temperature sensor readings were, performing a test to see if the evaporator fan would spin). The technician on the line said that the compressor had died, could not be fixed, and that the unit would have to be replaced through the vendor that I bought it from. He instructed me to switch the unit to the "Electric-Only" mode so that I could continue using it until it was replaced. I let him know about the electric burning smell and that the unit was warm to the touch on the top, and he said it shouldn't be a problem. Running the unit in electric only mode would bypass the compressor. 

I went inside the house, and ten minutes later I noticed the lights were flickering in the home. I walked out to the garage to investigate, and as soon as I turned the corner and saw the heater from four feet away, KABOOM. A large explosion noise sounded and a gigantic ball of sparks shot out of the top rear of the unit where the compressor is located. My wife heard the explosion and I told the family to get out of the house. Smoke was billowing out of the top of the unit, and I ran to turn off the electricity at the breaker in the garage.

After the smoke cleared and I was sure there was no longer a danger to our lives or property, I called the same customer service number again. I told them what had happened after I followed their directions, and they said, "Well, we already told you this had to be replaced by the vendor you purchased it from". I was incredulous, and said I don't think you quite understand what happened. I was going to leave my house, and I might have come back to it being burnt to the ground. I was calling back to let them know they definitely shouldn't be telling customers to keep a unit in use with a compressor failure and a burning smell like they had told me to do. Somebody could be injured or killed! The technician was more understanding at that point, maybe realizing I wasn't exaggerating what had occurred. She said she would tell engineering about this. At no point during the second phone call was my name, product information, or anything gathered!

I have emailed Rheem customer service. In the meantime, the water heater will be without power until I either get it replaced through the vendor (I will not be installing that model type again, I can promise you that) or get further direction from the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a significant explosion and sparks, posing a serious risk to life and property, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Cut finger during change of the razor blade:
The design of the scrapper was that changing the razor blade required first sliding of the scrapper cover out of a tab, then removal of the cover so that the worn blade can be replaced with a new one.  The cover could be re-installed by re-engaging the tab after installation.  In the process of change the blade, I sustained a cut in my finger about 1.5 cm long and 1.5 mm deep.  I was told that size cut normally would have required at least 2 stitches.  Luckily the cut had smooth edges and seemed to close with little gap, and the emergency staff was able to send me home with a medical tape over the wound.  The accident was caused after the new blade had been installed, the cover had to be secured by re-engagement of the tab lock.  During the re-engagement, the cover had to be pushed which coincidentally expose the blade.  If a finger or body part  was anywhere in front of the blade, there would be an accident for sure.   
Someone else had reported this problem a few years ago (required 7 stitches).  I am surprised this design has not been updated and there is not even a serious safety warning sticker to alert of the danger.  
I am an extremely safety conscious person. I have safely used many powered tools that are potentially  more dangerous than this.  But this design is inherently dangerous.  Worst is that it seems so deceptively harmless.  I urge the manufacture to do something now, either change the design, make it impossible to change the blade, or at a minimum put out a RED warning label.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut requiring medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the design flaw has caused similar injuries before and the hazard is inherent in the process.

Regarding Samsung Top Loading Washing Machine purchased August 2015 and verified serial number as being affected on Samsung website.

Washing machine has severely vibrated and moved on the floor since purchase.  I felt that the vibration and movement was in excess of any machine I have owned over last three decades.  I have decreased the spin speed on every wash cycle to decrease as much as I could the vibration the entire time I have owned this machine....still we have had to move the machine back to it's original sitting position on multiple occasions.  Samsung's current suggestion(to use the gentle cycle) is not a viable solution to properly clean laundry as this setting does not allow for the use of hot water and does not properly remove excess water from the laundry.  It is my hope that this machine will be recalled.
justification: The washing machine vibrates excessively and moves, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I put a load of clothes into the washer and started it about 10 minutes into the cycle the washer started making a terrible noise I was just getting ready to go see about it when my husband came in and heard it when he opened the door to check on it and the washing machine was jumping and the room was filled with smoke.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning washing machine causing noise and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Subject:
 Samsung Top Loading Washing Machine.
Model #WA400PJHDWR/AA
Ser.# Y69Q5AEC703179Z
Date of purchase 9/10/2012

For the record let it be known that in July of 2015 I reported to Samsung that our washing machine was having trouble with it's spin cycle and that the drum was hitting the sides of the washing machine causing it to bounce from side to side.
 Samsung refused to do anything due to it was out of warranty. During the spin cycle the drum would hit the sides of the machine no matter how large of a load it had. In the end, cost us nearly $200.00 in repairs and the repair man informed us it was a common problem and Samsung was aware of it. Over time the springs would stretch due to they are too weak to support the drum and it's load resulting in the drum to hit the sides durning the spin cycle. The repair man could only replace the springs with new factory springs which in the end will result in the same problem over time. 

Repair date 7/21/15
General Appliance Service  State Lic.# [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Repairmen's Comments,
"Washer suspension shocks are stretched, banging the sides of the washer."
Suggestions, "Do not overload washer"

Due to my customer service call and the repairmen's comments leads me to believe that Samsung was aware of the problem and chose not to do anything about the problem.

Thank you,
Ron Santellano
justification: The incident describes a malfunction causing damage to the washing machine but no injury or death, and the problem is described as common by the repairman.

incident_description: I was prompted to report this after the recent news about Samsung top-load washing machines exploding. My washing machine model is listed as one affected. Mine has NOT exploded. However, for the last several months it HAS been been very "off-balance" very often. It is so off-balance that it bangs around with very loud booms and shaking. I often have to re-configure the clothes 4-5 times and sometimes turn it off and on repeatedly to get the shaking to stop and the spin the cycle to finish. This is particularly true if there are any towels in a load--whether one towel or all towels. Originally I thought that his was just very annoying and made me want to buy a new washer.  However, after the reports of explosions I realize this may be even more serious, and a safety issue.
justification: The washing machine is malfunctioning but has not caused injury or explosion yet, indicating a potential safety issue.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased a Maytag front loader washing machine on 1/16/2009.  The Model number is MHWE500VP00; serial # HLW4043148.    Within the first year it started smelling like mold.  I would clean mold from under the seal and from the tray where the laundry detergent went in.  I would run bleach through it, but the mold persisted.  I started having consistent sinus problems starting in 2011 - 2012 and finally in 2013 I ended up having to have sinus surgery.  One month later I was hospitalized for a week for hypoxia and new onset asthma.  My IGE level was over 4000 which indicated it was allergy related.  I now have to take [REDACTED] injections twice a month (cost in $5000 per month to my insurance), use [REDACTED] twice per day, rinse my sinses twice per day with [REDACTED], use [REDACTED] nasal steroid spray twice per day and take [REDACTED] nightly.  I believe this all stems from the mold issue with the washer.  If I leave the door open after using the washer, then I can smell the mold in the house and if I keep the door shut after washing then I only smell the mold in the laundry room.
justification: The incident resulted in significant health issues including sinus surgery, hospitalization, and ongoing medical treatments, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The persistent mold issue suggests a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description: February 2016 I purchased a samsung dryer because my original dryer went bad. I decided to purchase a new washing machine along with thee dryer even though my washing machine was still good. I received my new washing machine and procrastinated on hooking it up since my old one was working perfectly fine. I decided to hook up my new machine and say goodbye to the old one a month after receiving it. I hooked up the machine and it was horribly loud made banging noises and vibrated way out of the norm in the spin cycle, would keep refilling, and takes forever to finish a cycle. I immediately called best buy for a return, they told me since I waited past 30 days it was a manufacture issue. I then immediately called samsung. Samsung sent out a technician and the technician said the machine wasn't level and since we bought a low end model thats how it works. Samsung refused to do anything. Keep in mind my fiance was home when the technician was there. I checked the machine when I got home and it was level. Till this day the machine shakes violently in the spin cycle and now I hear there is a recall. I will never in my life purchase samsung. I feel like my hard earned money was put to waste on an important investment my family depends on to stay sanitary.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning appliance causing inconvenience and dissatisfaction, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Was washing 1 full size quilted blanket on the bedding setting and washing machine suddenly started to violently rock back and forth and sounded like it would come apart.  We thought it might be an unbalanced load but before we could get to it, it banged the wall and stopped with a tub full of water and would not spin out the water.  It would not drain and it would not spin.  I pulled the power plug  and shut down the washer and I had to remove the wet blanket and wring it out by hand.  Then I plugged in the washer, turned it on without the blanket, and put in on drain cycle, then it did spin and drain.  This washer has banged and bumped before on heavy loads like with jeans or sheets but never so violently and never had problems spinning or draining until this time.
justification: The incident involved a washing machine malfunction causing violent movement and operational failure, but no injury or damage beyond the machine itself.

incident_description: My Samsung top load high efficiency washing machine is constantly stopping due to an unbalanced load and shakes violently. I am very unhappy with the product. It also has ruined several of my clothing items  by tearing them.
justification: The washing machine's violent shaking and damage to clothing items constitute an incident without injury.

incident_description: Steel attic ladder that folds up into the ceiling with a 300lb weight rating. It was marketed as being the stronger option for attic ladders. One of the hinges that hold the bottom section of ladder snapped during normal operation. The metal in the hinge simply failed. Neither of the people who has been using the ladder weighs over 200lbs and nothing heavy is carried up into the attic. This failure has been reported by numerous people online. Werner has refused to acknowledge that the hinge was faulty or that the design potentially poses a risk to users.
justification: The hinge failure during normal operation indicates a design flaw, but no injury was reported despite the risk.

incident_description:
On two occasions, my hot tub heated to a temperature of 140 degrees F.  This occurred while my 4 year-old-granddaughter was visiting.  Had she jumped in, it likely would have resulted in death or severe burns. The hot tub is manufactured by California Cooperage, Model 280, and uses electronic controls for the two pumps and the heater.  Obviously, the over-temperature protection controls do not operate in a fail-safe condition to limit the maximum temperature to 108 degrees F as stated in the hot tub manual. After unplugging the hot tub and allowing it to cool to below 108 degrees F, the system appears to function normally again.

I consider this product to be an extreme safety hazard that should be recalled and modified to operate in a fail-safe condition, whereby the heaters and pumps shut down when the temperature exceeds 108 degrees F.
justification: The incident describes a scenario where death or severe burns could have occurred, indicating a severity level of 4. The occurrence likelihood is 2 as it happened twice but did not result in actual harm.

incident_description: My new Samsung top load washer caught fire at the controls panel, the washer had not run for 2 days. I was not at home at the time of the fire.  The receptacle was not burned nor the power cord from the receptacle up to the panel. Fire started at the control panel and burned the lid as well as the tub.  The fire started burning the wooden wall behind the washer at the height of the panel on the washer and proceeded up the wall.  The dryer on the right also burned as well as the wall to the left of the washer, washer was in the corner. My electrical panel box was on the left side of the washer and all wiring coming out of panel box was damaged.  When the room heated up my ac came on and the smoke was sucked into the whole house, new house btw.  I had been living there 6 weeks, I'm now displaced from the home due to $83,000 damage.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I was using a samsung top load washing machine (WA45H7000AW). I was washing bedding at the time and during the spin cycle I heard a loud explosion. I was not in the laundry room at the time. When I came up stairs the frame on the washing machine was all busted up and the washing machine itself had moved quite dramatically. It appeared that the drum had come loose. I contacted samsung and at the time they were unwilling to repair it at their cost because it was 2 months out of warranty.
justification: The incident involved a washing machine malfunction causing significant damage but no injury or death.

incident_description:
I was washing bedding in a Samsung washing machine - Serial number Y0IY54BC201105Z.  When I went to check on the load, the machine had literally exploded.  The basin had come loose.  The lid was still in the locked position, but the entire top of the machine had lifted up.  One of the basin mounts was laying across the room.  It had obviously been airborne.  All four sides of the washing machine were dented.  The drywall was damaged.  There was water everywhere.  The machine had moved so from from its original position that it become unplugged.    
.

I tried to upload pictures, but the webpage wasn't working.
justification: The washing machine exploded causing significant property damage, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: We were using our Samsung Washing Machine  (Model wa45h7000aw) doing a load of bedding and all of the sudden it sounded like rocks were in the washing machine.  We quickly ran downstairs (where the washer is located) and turned it off and unplugged it, to our surprise the drum in the washer was sitting sideways in the washer and the outside case was all banged up due to the drum hitting the sides repeatedly.  In addition the washer turned in place 90 degrees from where it was located due to what was happening.   Lucky no one was hurt, and we contacted Home Depot, as we bought a warranty when we bought the machine, and it is in the process of being fixed, although currently the parts needed are on back order.  I didn't think anything of this until I read and article in the Washington Post today about this issue.  The washer was originally purchased in early July 2015. Please feel free free to contact me if you have any additional questions.
justification: The incident caused significant damage to the washing machine but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) based on the frequency mentioned (6927 of 10427).

incident_description: The drum of our 2003 GE front load washer Model #WSXH208A1WW has separated from the machine just like other GE washing machines listed in the recall. When operating, the spin cycle is so loud it sounds like a freight train and vibrates uncontrollably. I am afraid to run it fearing that the drum during high rpm's will fly out of the machine and injure or kill someone in the area! This problem has existed for a few months. Prior problem was the shock absorbers. Both bottom absorbers died last year and caused the washing machine to bounce all over the washer room!!!  Dangerous as it pinched and trapped my hand between the washer and dryer while it shook and bounced around! Took hours to access and replace the absorbers. I am now awaiting delivery of new washer but must continue to use this one in the meantime. I was quoted $500 for parts alone to fix the drum and bearing problem, labor additional. The recall of this GE Front Loader Washer should definitely be extended to include this model.
justification: The description mentions a prior injury (hand trapped) and expresses fear of potential death or injury from the drum flying out, indicating both past harm and ongoing risk.

incident_description: My washing machine was washing a load of laundry and the top (not just the lid, the entire top) blew off.  It threw it across the laundry room damaging the wall.  We called for service and they told us it would be around $800 to replace all of the parts and that this was a common problem.  We paid the service fee, used other laundry facilities, repaired the wall and eventually bought a new washer.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, and the service indicated it was a common problem.

incident_description: Over the last several weeks have had issues with our Samsung washing machine purchased  Dec 2012. It has been shaking violently during any spin cycle.  After watching the evening news noted there have been reports of similar events also resulting in the machine exploding or catching fire.  At this time we are no longer able to use our washer d/t the fear of injury to person or potential for property damage.
justification: The washing machine is shaking violently and has potential to explode or catch fire, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I have samsung front loading washing machine. Nwf210anw xaa
I have clean dryed seal on front door and covered in mold and mildo.
justification: The presence of mold and mildew on the washing machine seal indicates a hygiene issue but does not involve injury or death.

incident_description:
Air conditioner Frigidaire Serial Number IK80811426   Model FAM156R1A ---- MOLD HAZARD

Internal side of the air conditioner is made of thermal insulation foam , which is PERMANENTLY accumulating mold. Its cell surface makes impossible to remove mold, many particals of mold are blown to the air.  It is real  MOLD hazard.  In our family of 3 kids and 2 adults we are all experiencing symptoms like runny nose, constant cough, tiredness.   I request to open safety recall to this equipment.
justification: The description reports health symptoms (runny nose, constant cough, tiredness) affecting all family members, indicating injury due to mold exposure.

incident_description: On September 22, 2016 I was taking a shower. As I began to exit the shower the Kohler glass shower door model K-706014-D3-ABV anodized brushed bronze Levity shattered. I suffered a severe laceration to my left thumb and multiple lacerations to my feet, legs and right hand
justification: The incident resulted in multiple lacerations, indicating an injury but not death.

incident_description: 18kw and 16kw Generac generators produced with a faulty charging system that causes the battery to explode upon activating the start procedure either manually or automatic. This generator and others like it are unsafe for consumer operation. I have knowledge that this is NOT an isolated incident. I personally saw an exploded battery in a 16kw generator. Luckily no one was injured because it was an automatic start. Several technicians have informed me that this happens very often. I suggested to Generac at the time of the incident to voluntarily recall the product and after more than 2 years nothing has changed. The only solution suggested is to change the battery every 3 or 4 years.
justification: The incident involves a faulty charging system causing battery explosions, which could lead to injury, though no injuries were reported in this case. The issue is described as happening very often, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: On Sunday September 25 2016, a fire was reported at [REDACTED] in Knox County, Tennessee. Fire was determined to have started in a electrical disconnect box for the HVAC unit. 5 other boxes also showed similar damage from a high resistance heating connection where the breaker snaps onto the bus bars. All units were installed in 1990 and were Square D model QO200TR with 30 amp breakers installed.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no reported injuries, and similar damage was found in other units, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
We have a GE 50 pint dehumidifier, model ADEH50LQQ1, serial number FZ053835, manufacture date 03/12.  The dehumidifier is connected to a ground fault interrupter in the basement.  It has been operating normally until recently  Now it now trips the GFI about once a day.  When it is running, it otherwise operates normally.

In about 2001 I had a similar incident with a GE dehumidifier.  At first I did not realize it was the dehumidifier that was tripping the GFCI.  When I plugged the dehumidifier into a non-GFI protected outlet, it started a small fire, which went out immediately when the unit was unplugged. It caused very little damage to the dehumidifier, and no injuries.  GE did send a courier to pick up the unit for inspection and provided a replacement.

I am reporting this incident because others may have the same model dehumidifier and may be operating it without GFCI protection, which may potentially lead to a fire.  

The product will be replaced, but I will save the old unit for possible inspection by the manufacture or the CPSC, as the unit appears faulty, but since it has not burned, it can be examined to determine which component(s) are faulty.
justification: The incident involves a faulty dehumidifier tripping GFCI, with a past instance causing a small fire but no injuries, indicating a recurring issue with potential for minor property damage.

incident_description:
I have an itchy skin rash after using Tide with Febreze. 

Left a strong smell on clothes.  Had respiratory symptoms while clothes were drying inside.
justification: The itchy skin rash and respiratory symptoms indicate an injury, and the occurrence is possible given the reported reaction to the product.

incident_description: Last night my wife was vacuuming the upstairs hallway carpets when the sweeper caught fire. Hearing her screams, I came out of the bedroom and saw the sweeper on fire with flames coming from underneath the sweeper. I told my wife to pull the plug from the wall outlet and the flames subsided. I blew out the remaining fire. Damage was limited to the sweeper itself but did produce enough smoke to set off the smoke detectors in our house. My wife was visibly shaken by this incident.
justification: The incident involved a vacuum catching fire, causing smoke and alarm, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: The Samsung front load washing machine I bought at Lowes has been having an awful smell and has made my clothes smell bad as well. I finally saw a commercial about the mold that grows in these type of washers
justification: The incident involves a malfunction causing unpleasant smells but no reported injury or harm.

incident_description:
My daughter came home from school and noticed a funny smell in her room. She than noticed the charger was really hot. It had melted and turned brown in color. Bought from CVS. I returned it and asked them to make sure there is a recall. 
USB charger. Model LY-06 green/white
justification: The charger melted but there was no injury reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her floor fan blades shattered into million pieces while in use.  She stated  that she had just turn it on and she heard a loud noise and immediately the blades shattered becoming projectiles, if a child was present it could have caused serious injuries.

Caller stated that there was no injury sustained by the incident.

The manufacturer was not contacted because there was no contact info.  She feels that this product is dangerous and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved shattered fan blades but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the event.

incident_description: I was using a Cuboid 150W from Joyetech when it suddenly exploded in my hands and started shooting flames out of the battery compartment. It exploded without notice and was in good working order with no signs of abuse or neglect. It exploded inside my home office, filling the air with toxic fumes and burning my hands. It was quite terrifying. Had this happened inside a moving vehicle, I shudder to think of the outcome. Someone needs to investigate these before someone dies as a result of this product.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and toxic fumes, indicating injury (severity 3). The description suggests this could happen unexpectedly, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
About 3 years ago, I purchased a Samsung dryer, model # DV350AGW/XAA. Recently, it began making a noise.  After clothing got snagged, I discovered that the aluminium dryer drum had come apart at the welding and had a large crack. After some internet research, I found that this is most certainly not an issue related to normal use or ordinary wear and tear, but rather a defect/flaw, as many Samsung customers have complained of similar issues across different dryer models. Samsung has refused to repair my dryer without me incurring either the expense of the labor or the parts.

After several calls to Samsung representatives, each of them made it clear, that customer satisfaction is not important to them, since product is out of warranty. A recall definitely is needed to be done for this product, since it is clearly defective.
justification: The incident involves a defective dryer drum causing inconvenience and potential safety hazard, but no injury or death reported.

incident_description: Son was taking a shower when one of the glass door shattered and cut him over his body. One cut on his hand required 8 stitches
justification: The son sustained a cut requiring 8 stitches, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Dryer drum has cracked exposing electrical and internal components to lint causing a fire hazard.  In addition the dryer now has exposed extremely sharp steel parts making it very unsafe to reach in and grab clothing.  Clothing became caught on sharp jagged edges and ripped.
justification: The dryer's cracked drum exposes electrical components and sharp edges, posing a fire hazard and risk of injury from contact with sharp parts.

incident_description: I purchased mirrored closet doors at the Home Depot in [REDACTED] and had them installed.  The other day we were sitting by the door and the header piece crashed to the ground and shattered in pieces so far that we could not imagine how tiny pieces could get into adjoining rooms in the house.  In any event, come to find out the piece was simply taped to the top of the door with a small strip of what appears to be double faced tape on the backing.  As a result, I went to the Home Depot and observed a header piece on one of their demos and made inquiry of how the product is constructed and should be attached to the door.  The sales person indicated that (synopsis) those headers should be solidified with screws in order to assure adherence to the wall/door.  However, that was not the case here.  I have one other closet door in the house that was purchased/installed at the same time as the master bedroom door and now I am concerned that one will fall.  I have taken measures - as limited as that may be due to my inexperience with these things, to ensure the same event does not take place, but I am still concerned.  I told the clerk at the store that I wanted someone to call me about the product, but as of a week ago I have not heard back from anyone.  I am hoping this does not happen to anyone else.
justification: The incident involved a falling header piece causing property damage but no injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the improper installation method described and the potential for recurrence.

incident_description: Bought Holmes fan 21inch box fan from Amazon. Cord caught on fire during the night. Only had for 5 days.
justification: The fan cord caught fire, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was vacuuming carpet in my house on 9/13/2016 when I saw smoke coming from the connection between power nozzle and the Connection Pipe Assembly. Connection Pipe Assrmby had melted causing smoke and had I continued vacuuming a potential electrical fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting of the vacuum parts, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This razor blade scraper consists of 2 pieces of plastic which slide with respect to each other.  One piece of plastic is mounted a razor blade (the blade piece), the other piece acts as a protector (the protect piece).   In the "open" position, the protect piece moves behind the blade piece, thereby exposing the blade.  In the "close" position, the protect piece goes in front of the blade piece, presumably offering protection from being cut by the blade.  Except it does not work because there is no locking of the pieces in position either closed or opened position.  So if the blade is closed and you pushes the scraper toward a part of your body, you the protector will retreat and the blade will be exposed to cause a cut.  This design is careless and extremely dangerous.  My wife was cut at least 2 times just picking the scraper up.  

I have also reported a more serious accident with this device in No. 20160919-208F0-2147413945
justification: The description reports injuries (cuts) from the scraper, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (5) as the design flaw makes injuries almost certain during use.

incident_description: I have a pocket jump starter approx.  2 years old  used less than 5 times that the battery swelled up and busted the case while charging . I was home and removed from outlet before further damage from being done
justification: The battery swelling and busting the case is an incident, but no injury or death occurred as it was promptly removed.

incident_description:
The vacuum extension wand has a power feed (wire) that comes loose and shorts out against the metal tube, which is exposed to the consumer and causes an electrical shock !!
My Kenmore Progressive model # 116.21714110.
justification: The incident involves an electrical shock from a loose power feed, which poses a risk of injury but no death is mentioned.

incident_description:
During pre-sale safety inspections of single and multi-family homes required in the state of Rhode Island, same model hardwired battery back-up smoke/CO alarms have been found to not activate during testing, although the indicator light on each unit remained illuminated showing it to be energized. I've encountered this situation involving the same model alarms on several occasions over the past two years and subsequently filed reports with CPSC at that time. The manufacturer claims that these alarms are supposed to chirp every 30-seconds at the end of their useful life, however, an all cases I've been involved with the residents report these alarms have not done so.
I'm concerned that that homeowners are relying on smoke/CO alarms that show they're energized and functioning when the units are actually not effective at all.
justification: The smoke/CO alarms are not functioning despite appearing energized, posing a potential safety risk, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Dehumidifier  Model 251.90701010  S/N  WNX5Y50000019

Electrical Shock Hazard

The Kenmore is about 7-9  years old.   Purchased about 2007-2009

 In is in the basement and performed well. 

On 9/14/16, the basement breaker circuit went out.  After repeated tests and disconnecting various electrical equipment the problem traced to Kenmore.  It has not been damaged and has been in the same place for years ... water goes automatically into a drain, so seldom touched or moved.    Electric cord was sound and had no defects.  

When I plugged the Kenmore in the receptacle, the breaker on the receptacle was activated and cut the electricity.

It cut off again when I tried to restart it.  Thinking it might be the receptacle, I ran a extension cord to another receptacle  in the basement.   

 When I tried to connect the Kenmore cord to the plugged in extension cord, there was a very large spark generated at the plug interface and a CRACK.  

 If I had not been holding the two ends at a distance from the connection point I would have been burned or severely shocked.   I was fortunate.

I noted other Kenmore dehumidifier  models have been recalled before due to hazard problems.  This was produced in Korea and might be from the same manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a significant electrical hazard with potential for severe shock or burns, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
My Samsung Washing Machine was on, when I checked the clothes, the power to the washer, dryer and anything else connected to that particular circuit was off. I reset the circuit breaker and restarted the washer. The washer wouldn't start. The lights come on, but the washer will not continue to the next cycle.  I received an email from Consumer Affairs of all the horror stories involved with the Samsung Washing Machine catching fire. Thank goodness my circuit breaker didn't allow this to happen. 

I am asking for a recall on the Samsung Washing Machines. I purchased my machine in March of 2014. 
I called Samsung who says there is no recall as of yet and the machine is not under warranty anymore.
I'm disgusted and have dirty laundry.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning washing machine that tripped the circuit breaker, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: The Trendnet Home smart switch THA-103AC does not shut off the power to the hot side of the plug when selected off using a smart phone or using the switch on the side of the unit.  Instead it electrifies the neutral plug of the unit to stop the flow of electricity.  I contacted the manufacture about this and they confirmed this is how the switch is designed to work.  My concerns are 1) if someone has a lamp plugged into this switch and uses the switch to turn the lamp off, they are at risk of shock when changing a bulb.  the risk is elevated given that both the neutral and hot sides are both electrified.  2) three prong appliances may not shut off if the appliance uses the ground prong as the electrical return.  this is how I found this issue.  I had a small water pump that would not shut off using the switch.  3) this could potentially bypass a ground fault outlet.
justification: The incident describes a risk of electric shock when changing a bulb, which could lead to injury, and a potential for appliances to remain powered, increasing the likelihood of harm.

incident_description: I was charging pocket jump starter  model  ZT50400after less than 5 minutes on charge it literally swelled up and busted apart and was smoking and very warm. I received this as a gift and approx. 2 years ago and this was the first time using it and charging it. Also I have spoken to several people that have the same model purchased thru snap-on tools and they have had the same problem
justification: The incident involved a device swelling, bursting, and smoking, but no injury was reported. Similar issues were reported by others with the same model.

incident_description: I mopped my floor with Zep Hardwood and Laminate Floor Cleaner.  After 20-25 minutes I walked on it and immediately slipped and fell, even tho it was dry.  My foot slipped completely out from under me, bringing me down directly on my head.  The wound required 4 staples to close
justification: The incident resulted in a head injury requiring medical treatment (4 staples), which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Slipping on a recently mopped floor is a possible but not highly frequent occurrence.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Washing Machine: Model number 796-29278000

Imploded, due to unbalanced load and would not stop (King size blanket).  The machine proceeded to  hit the wall of my laundry room  creating a medium hole in the wall.  The top of the washing machine also became disconnected from the rest of the machine.  Luckily no one was hurt.  It has been very difficult for Sears/Kenmore to resolve the situation.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, as stated in the description.

incident_description:
The emergency cut-off circuit tripped due to overheating of the water. The water was hot enough that even after being off all night, the water was still scalding hot the next morning, eight hours later.

Rheem has agreed to provide warranty/recall service.  

Thanks to the CPSC highlighting this issue and making a contact number for Rheem available.  Without this information, I likely would have just reset the device or replaced parts that weren't the true issue, unwittingly risking a house fire or serious burn.
justification: The incident involved overheating water and a tripped emergency cut-off, posing a risk of burns or fire, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Danby dehumidifier ddr7009ree1 runs, but won't remove humidity from room. unit compressor becomes so hot, that if you try to touch it, you would be seriously burned!
