incident_description: Sliding glass shower door exploded/shattered into a million cubes of glass approx 1:30PM on 9/10/2016. Nobody was in the bathroom at the time, and nobody had used the shower since 9AM that morning. Door had no visible damage prior to the explosion. Door was made by Coastal Industries, Jacksonville FL, installed in 2010 (assumption-house was built then, but we were not living here yet).
justification: The shower door shattered but no one was present or injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Hunter All-Fan Control (model 27185, s/n 277076) failed while not being used.  I had this device installed in a fan canopy to control the fan and light kit via a remote controller mounted on the was switch.
On 8/24/16, I returned home from being away for a week, when entering, I noticed a smell of burnt electronics when entering the kitchen (where the device is installed).  A short time later, my wife tried to turn on the fan but neither the fan nor light would work, either with the remote or directly with the switches on the fan or light.
I removed power from the circuit and disassembled the fan and found the remote control unit badly burned and melted.
During the week I was away, there were no signs of a lightning strike to my home nor was there a loss of power.
I contacted Hunter Fan but they have not been very helpful in trying to figure out what happened.  All they have done is offer to replace the device.  
I have the failed device but they have shown no interest in having it returned for a failure investigation.
justification: The device failed and caused damage but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The washer has developed mold around the rubber seal and it causes the rear of her home to emit a mold odor.  The consumer said that she has experienced the problem from the time that the washer was purchased.  The consumer has never had the washer serviced for this issue.

The consumer searched the Internet and saw a video, where others had experienced this same issue.  It also referred people to the CPSC to file a complaint about this issue.

The consumer's husband has developed sinus problems that he has not had in the past and it may be attributed to the mold in the washer.  The consumer's husband has been to the doctor and are attempting to see what symptoms may be causing the coughing that he has experienced, but have not been able to identify the cause so far.

The consumer still uses the washer.

The washer does not appear to be included in any CPSC recalls.
justification: The husband has developed sinus problems and coughing, indicating injury, and the issue is common enough to be documented in videos and complaints.

incident_description:
Dear Gentlemen,
Ser # BDPK7, model: LW45, Job: 16198
Subj: DeathTrap - Jacuzzi Walk-In Tub.

On April 3, 2016, I signed a contract for installation of a Walk-In Tub.  The agent was [REDACTED].  The Fairbanks construction Co. of Ocala Fl., installed the unit 4-1-2016.  I was advised never to use the tub without the 911 alert system in reach.
On July 18, 2016, after finally receiving the 911 alert, I decided to try the Walk-In Tub.
After 30 minutes the tub filled with 50 gal. of water.  I opened the air jets at my back.  At that moment, I was thrushed forward, landed on my knees and my head was underwater.  I was in panic and tried frantically to get a hold of the bar to pull myself up.  I could have drowned.  The Alert 911 would have been totally useless out of reach.  The Walk-In Tub is a death trap.
The tape demonstration and brochures given by the agent [REDACTED] do not compare to the tub installed.  The Tub is an old model.  The new models (copies encl.) require 30 gal of water and are half the size which was actually installed.
It takes 30 min. to fill the tub with 50 gallons.  The shower head is barely in trickle mode and does not work properly.  Numerous calls to the agent, the Fairbanks Construction Co., and [REDACTED], installation supervisor, [REDACTED]; were not returned.  [REDACTED] of the Fairbanks Co, was rude, who returned the phone call stated "you got what you ordered, you do not get another tub!"
The agent [REDACTED], did not return any of my calls.  Details re: water capacity was not disclosed and the publications were misrepresented.
I am a senior citizen, 85 yrs. + and a victim of exploitation of the elderly.  I live on fixed income and invested $15,500.- of my savings for health reasons, because my net worth does not qualify me for a senior establishment.

Please contact me at your earliest at above address or by phone at [REDACTED].  Please, please help!

[REDACTED]

incident_description:
The caller and his wife were asleep May 14th, 2016 when they awakened to their bedroom filling with smoke  then they saw smoke and fire outside their window.
He identified that it was coming from the window air conditioner which was NOT in use at the time. 
He purchased the air condition at an estate sale in New Hampshire around mid July 2014.
The caller got out of bed, unplugged the unit then the fire began dying down with smoke dissipating as he left his bedroom door closed after opening the windows then opened other windows in the home.

There are no injuries being reported.

The caller contacted the manufacturer by email sometime around the last week in May 2016 thinking at the time that his son in law had thrown the unit away but then discovered he had not so he contacted the manufacturer a second time to inform them that it was still in his possession.

He is a volunteer fire fighter himself and has asked that CPSC investigate this unit much due to it NOT being in use at the time of the fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by an air conditioner not in use, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My Bosch dryer just caught on fire and it was not in the vent it was in the back of the drum inside the dryer.  It looks as if debris built up behind the drum liner.  A warning should be posted.  If I was not sitting a few feet away and just happen to hear a strange beep come from the dryer, it could have caught the house on fire.
justification: The dryer caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injury or death occurred as the fire was noticed in time.

incident_description: My husband and I were staying at the Bayridge Condos in Fort Lauderdale, FL. On July 15th, the second night into our stay, I was exiting the shower and the glass door, made by FLEURCO, combusted. The glass shattered everywhere, and as a result, I sustained cuts to my hands, thighs and feet. I now have permanent scarring due to the incident. The property owner was alerted of the accident right away, but we recently just received the manufacturer's name. I reached out to the manufacturer, FLEURCO, today via an online form and I'm waiting to hear how this will be resolved.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts and permanent scarring), warranting a severity level of 3. Glass door shattering is uncommon but not unheard of, leading to an occurrence likelihood of 3.

incident_description: With the power switch fully in the "off" position, my Craftsman shop vac turned itself on, began to smoke from the motor and started to flame.
justification: The incident involved a shop vac turning on unexpectedly and catching fire, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I was using my laptop the charger batter/cord was extremely hot. I didn't think much of it  next thing my power outlet popped and was burnt and my laptop was fried. The outlet has been replaced the computer has not.

incident_description: I purchased a vacuum cleaner from HSN in May 2016 by Joy Mangano called Super Chic upright vacuum.  This product overheats after a few minutes. incident_description:

She has had no problems with this ceiling fan until the night of August 5th, 2016 when the caller went to bed with the fan running as usual then heard a loud sound and rose to find that two of the blades had fallen from the fan and had hit about two feet from her head.

They have asked for any information she has for the fan but they are questioning because she has no receipt from the eight year old purchase.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the cordless rechargeable hand held vacuum overheats to the point he received 2nd degree burns to his right hand.   He applied first aid to the burns.  He stated that his spouse also received 1st degree burns to her hands as well.

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that a replacement would be sent to him, but they did not need the defective one to look at.

Caller feels that this vacuum cleaner is a safety hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description:
I purchased a Singer 4432 sewing machine from Amazon.com and felt a continuous tingling/shocking sensation when in contact with the machine's metal base plate while it was on.  Investigating further, I measured 80VAC on the base plate relative to ground.  I exchanged the unit with Amazon twice and both units had similar issues, measuring 55VAC and 53VAC respectively.  

I've made Singer aware of this issue; however, they contend that it is a coincidence (not a systemic design defect).  Further, they say that since none of their other customers have reported getting shocked, there is no issue.  They have been unwilling to test one of their own units using a voltmeter.

Below is a summary of the 3 machines that I've tested:

* Machine #1 (serial number: ZHC1601911098): 80VAC
Video: https://www.dropbox.com/s/qkhzx82jckczt1q/2016-08-22%2012.19.34.mov?dl=0

* Machine #2 (serial number: ZHC1614515381): 55VAC
Video: https://www.dropbox.com/s/4khk7aollyzqy85/WIN_20160824_145037.MP4?dl=0

* Machine #1 (serial number: ZHC1602111228): 53VAC
Video: https://www.dropbox.com/s/fqq48k5hfbwkcxs/WIN_20160902_130336.MP4?dl=0
justification: The incident involves a continuous tingling/shocking sensation from the sewing machine, indicating an electrical issue, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On September 3, 2016, In purchased the Guerilla Wagon from Home Depot. As soon as I opened the box I noticed the awful smell. I realized it was the tires. The smell gave me a sever headache and caused my face to burn.

I thought the smell would go away after a couple of days but it did not. The smell is strong and can be smelled from several meters away.

I will be returning the product immediately. 

Store SKU 824220
justification: The incident caused a severe headache and facial burning, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I used BEHR paint to paint my new town home. Within 24 hrs I had blisters all over my hands, within days I had a rash all over my exposed skin. My nose had sores and my eyelids swelled up. I felt completely disoriented and extremely sick. I went to the dermatologist and then to the hospital because of airborne contact allergic reaction to BEHR paint. I had several biopsies done and was sent for further testing. After certified patch testing I found out I was severely allergic to methylisozialonone a major preservative in BEHR paint. BEHRs costumer service representative told my dermatologist that MI was "pretty much not in their paint" when I contacted them they gave me a run around answer "it's not an ingredient we use here at BEHR in our paint, but our suppliers of our raw materials use it in the can" so it's in the paint...  Since the MI used in BEHR paint goes airborne once it's applied to the walls it is in the air for 90+ days. This is an unknown fact for many consumers. This type of reaction is rare but worthy of being documented and researched as to why companies can place blame on their suppliers and not take responsibility for what goes into the can that has their brand name on it! Or the effects of airborne chemicals that can cause such horrible effects.
justification: The individual suffered severe allergic reactions requiring medical attention, including hospital visits and biopsies, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
We recently bought this saw from Lowes and the first time my son-in-law tried to use it he receive a very stong shock when he tried to turn off the saw. My son-in-law, daughter and myself all checked the manual and no where in there was a warning not to turn the saw off with wet hands. Since it is a water saw for tile. When you are using it the way it is mean to be used, your hands are going to get wet. There were all kinds of warning about the plug getting wet, but no mention not to touch the on off switch with wet hands. There fore he received a server shock.
Again since this is a water saw and ment to used with water, this really needs to be a warning. he did not have get medical attention, but it should never have happen and there should be warning in the manual.

incident_description:
Re: Serious and Dangerous Product Packaging defect.

Dear Sir/Madam,

I recently purchased the "5 Second Fix" which is Distributed by OnTel, in Faifield NJ 07004.

The package came with no damage to the outer packaging. Also the sealed plastic package, which contains the glue and the UV light (as one unit), was also undamaged.

However, when I cut open the plastic package the glue poured out onto my hands. I quickly washed my hands but I still got a rash from this glue.

The plastic package contains a folded small sheet of paper (8" X 6") which includes several warnings including a First Aid warning, all of which describe the glue as being a cancer and birth defect causing chemical which is a strong irritant
that may require a physician's attention, and that it should be kept out of reach of children.

The problem is that there is no possible way to know that the adhesive leaked out inside the plastic packaging until one opens it. The warning notation on the outside of the package is partially covered up by a product label which prevents it
to be read.

Apparently, the plastic cap that holds the adhesive inside the unit while it is still in its plastic package can easily become loose during shipping thus causing the adhesive to leak out. Yet there is no possible way to know that the adhesive
leaked out as it is clear just like the plastic package.

This is a very hazardous situation especially if a child opens the package as it is heavily advertised on TV.

Personally, I think the product should be recalled and several safety measure should be introduced. One could be a stronger seal on the part of the unit that holds the adhesive. Another could be to make the adhesive a different color so
that one knows that the adhesive leaked out during shipping. 

It would be a great public service if you could bring this to the public's attention.

Sincerely

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a rash from chemical exposure, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the packaging defect could recur during shipping.

incident_description:

incident_description:
The market for USB Type-C (also known as USB 3.1 Type-C) chargers and cables are having significant inconsistencies between cell phones/smart phones (devices) and not following the specifications established by the USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF). Examples of manufacturers doing this are LG and [REDACTED] and they have not taken any steps to address this. Consumers are not readily aware of this practice and may plug their device into a charger that is non-compliant because the charging connector is the same as one that is compliant. What this is causing is a significant risk of shock, fire or injury due to the battery exploding due to these non-compliant chargers or cables sending more power than the device needs. 

Companies like Amazon have already taken their own steps to try and limit this hazard to consumers by banning non-compliant cables or chargers from sale on their site. See here under Examples of prohibited listings: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html/ref=hp_left_cn?ie=UTF8&nodeId=200277240 "Any USB-C (or USB Type-C) cable or adapter product that is not compliant with standard specifications issued by ÃÂUSB Implementers Forum Inc.ÃÂ" Also certain people have taken on the task of verifying themselves if the cable or charger is following the specification to ensure consumers have the right knowledge that a cable they buy or are already using will not be a safety hazard. Example here: https://plus.google.com/collection/s0Inv 

A great video that also details the safety hazards presented by these non-compliant and defective chargers and cables can be seen here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DMPrM0eWPbY . I hope the CPSC can review all of this and realize that as USB Type-C is fast replacing MicroUSB as the way to charge devices, that leaving this situation unchecked may result in consumers being harmed due to gross negligence by manufacturers not following established and available specifications.
justification: The description indicates a risk of injury (shock, fire, or battery explosion) due to non-compliant chargers, and the issue is described as significant with manufacturers not addressing it.

incident_description: We hired [REDACTED] and his company The Right Handyman LLC of Columbus Ohio to refurbish our bathroom.  Included with the refurbishment we purchased a frameless tempered glass door directly from [REDACTED].  The work was completed during autumn of 2015. On 5/22/16 the upper portion of the glass door spontaneously exploded. No one was in the bathroom at the time that the door exploded. We have attempted to work with [REDACTED] on a solution to the problem. We have expressed that we have concerns regarding the safety of the door as well as the quality of the installation job. Through research we have since learned that their is a history of frameless tempered glass doors spontaneously exploding.  We have also learned that the glass door industry is well aware of this history yet they continue to sell these doors and they do not make a disclosure of the risk involved.  We are appalled that this safety hazard was sold to us and installed in our home with no disclosure being made regarding the history of frameless tempered glass doors spontaneously exploding.  We purchased the door directly from [REDACTED] and his company The Right Handyman LLC (158 Eastwood Ave., Westerville, OH 43081 - (614) 357-5154) - therighthandymanohio@gmail.com).
justification: The glass door exploded but no one was injured, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his clothes dryer purchased from a retailer in California around the middle of 2007.
He had no problems with the unit until July 28th, 2016 when the caller was relaxing at his home and around 10:00PM he began noticing that there was a gas odor coming through the room.

He went to his backyard because he was dizzy then once his head was clear he contacted the gas company who came to his home and noted that his dryer was emitting gas.  The gas company turned off the connection to the dryer.
He will attach a copy of the gas company's report.
Other than dizziness the caller has not reported other injuries during the incident.
He said that he did contact the manufacturer July 28th, 2016 and was advised only that there is no recall but that a repair tech can be dispatched at the consumer's expense.
justification: The caller experienced dizziness due to gas exposure, indicating an injury, but no further injuries or death were reported. The incident is unlikely to occur frequently given the specific circumstances.

incident_description:
The market for USB Type-C (also known as USB 3.1 Type-C) chargers and cables are having significant inconsistencies between cell phones/smart phones (devices) and not following the specifications established by the USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF). Examples of manufacturers doing this are [REDACTED] and Huawei and they have not taken any steps to address this. Consumers are not readily aware of this practice and may plug their device into a charger that is non-compliant because the charging connector is the same as one that is compliant. What this is causing is a significant risk of shock, fire or injury due to the battery exploding due to these non-compliant chargers or cables sending more power than the device needs. 

Companies like Amazon have already taken their own steps to try and limit this hazard to consumers by banning non-compliant cables or chargers from sale on their site.  See here under Examples of prohibited listings: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html/ref=hp_left_cn?ie=UTF8&nodeId=200277240 "Any USB-C (or USB Type-C) cable or adapter product that is not compliant with standard specifications issued by ÃÂUSB Implementers Forum Inc.ÃÂ" Also certain people have taken on the task of verifying themselves if the cable or charger is following the specification to ensure consumers have the right knowledge that a cable they buy or are already using will not be a safety hazard. Example here: https://plus.google.com/collection/s0Inv

A great video that also details the safety hazards presented by these non-compliant and defective chargers and cables can be seen here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DMPrM0eWPbY . I hope the CPSC can review all of this and realize that as USB Type-C is fast replacing MicroUSB as the way to charge devices, that leaving this situation unchecked may result in consumers being harmed due to gross negligence by manufacturers not following established and available specifications.
justification: The description indicates a significant risk of shock, fire, or injury due to non-compliant chargers, which could lead to severe outcomes including injury or death.

incident_description:
On June 2015 we purchases wall-to-wall carpeting from Lowes Hardware. The carpet as it ages emits a gaseous odor that takes our breath away at times when we have the house closed up. We expected that for new carpeting, but after 1 year past the odor continues, concentrated, and is now a health hazard for me as I have severe asthma.  We use a whole room air filter system which does little to remove the gaseous oder. We have to keep windows open in all weather to air out the smell. Now after 14 mos past and the carpet seems to be disintegrating, and the gaseous smell sickens us, especially in humid or foggy weather where vapors are concentrated closer to the floor.
 
I have called Lowes several times about this, and continue to be ignored,  The gaseous smell is like burned rubber or plastic, and causes anyone entering out home to gasp to breath our house air.   We keep a very clean home, and vacuum with our Shark vacuum twice a week throughout the house.  Also, since getting this carpet installed, smoke alarms go off often in the night.  We bought new smoke alarms, installed new batteries in them, and still have this problem.  I believe the alarms are picking up the gas smell.

Our house is 15 yrs old, and we had it built.  Our old carpet still remains in the bedrooms and looks better than the disintegrating new carpet. The new carpet already looks old and beat up, My husband and I (age 70) live in the house, and we have a small dog also.  I appealed again today to Lowes to consider the matter, and after I told them I am ready to call a lawyer over this, they said that they will have the carpet manufacturer contacted, and the carpet will likely be tested.

Meanwhile, I seek any information as to what, if any, complaints are issued about carpeting smell and health hazards. I checked for this information online, so much confusing information  for the lay person to sort out. I feel that this carpet is a serious health hazard and needs checking into.

Is there any chance I could have testing done on my carpet, its under padding, and glue used for installation?   Would you please recommend a resource for that.  

Thank you for your consideration of my complaint.  
You may contact me: [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED]
justification: The carpet's gaseous odor is causing health issues, particularly for someone with severe asthma, and is affecting the residents' quality of life.

incident_description:
The flooring was delivered to the consumer's home and her husband installed the flooring himself.  The flooring is in their kitchen and hallway, which stretches to their foyer/front door (approx. 274 square feet).

12/2015:  The husband was in the kitchen, when he said he noticed that his symptoms were primarily present when he was in their home.  The husband wondered If their flooring was part of the group that was being investigated by CPSC.  The consumer said that they had heard about this issue in the past, but did not connect their flooring with the issue until recently.

12/31/2015:  The consumer called the mfr. and spoke with [REDACTED] (last name unknown) and inquired about the possibility that their flooring could contain excessive formaldehyde.   [REDACTED] checked the consumerÃÂs flooring information and said it was on their list of impacted flooring and suggested that she contact their Customer Care Department, Tel:  1-800-427-3966.  The consumer called that number and spoke with [REDACTED] (last name unknown), [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] sent the consumer a formaldehyde test kit.  The consumer asked [REDACTED] if their flooring had excessive formaldehyde, but she told the consumer that she could not comment, since there was an ongoing investigation.

The consumer was concerned about the accuracy of the manufacturerÃÂs test kit, so she ordered a second kit from an online-retailer, who was independent of the mfr.  This test kit was manufactured by [REDACTED], but there was no phone number the consumer could provide.


1/10/2016:  The consumer conducted the manufacturerÃÂs test and she indicated that it takes 24 hours to run.  She then has to pack up the test kit and send it to the manufacturerÃÂs recommended testing lab.   She said that the test would be completed by the time she returns home this evening.  

1/10/2016:  The consumer also conducted a second test with a kit that she purchased separately. incident_description:
Glass shower was purchased and installed by Schererville Glass and Mirror in October 2011 shortly after closing on the house that I built.

incident_description:

I'm furious and physically sick right now from this overpriced piece of junk I want a refund and a new washer that doesn't make me sick. Heck, I wish I had our old top loader that worked just fine!!!

Lid would not open for removal of small load, & electronic panel began making loud popping sounds when I attempted to open it, & almost immediately began burning & emitting thick black smoke. incident_description: We purchased this washing machine in 2011. Around 2014 we filed a complaint because the lid was cracked and would not operate. After doing some research we found many sites that listed this issue as a serious and repetitive problem with Whirlpool Cabrio washing machine. Whirlpool contact us and resolved the issue by installing a new lid at no charge. However, this time the lid shattered and glass was everywhere including in the clothes. This is a serious problem that is happening to the majority of whirlpool cabrio owners. These lids are not safe. Had myself or my children been injured by the washer while it shattered we could have been seriously injured. I received cuts on my hands and arms while trying to get our clothes out of the glass filled machine. I do have photos of the machine as I found it. The lids are breaking and shattering approximately 1-3 years after use.

The consumer sent a picture of her injury with her reply to the 2nd email.  The consumer followed up with a call to the mfr. and she spoke to a rep. (name unknown).  The consumer asked to speak with someone else and she spoke with [REDACTED].  The consumer asked [REDACTED] about the report she sent, but [REDACTED] told her that she could not locate the report. The consumer estimates that the problem with the sweeper started sometime in May/June 2016.  The lock would work intermittently, but became worse over time.

When the package was opened the rug had a very strong odor of chemicals.  It did not have the expected "new rug" smell.  Instead it smelled like some kind of solvent or other chemicals. It was melted at the middle of the handle and bent in half.  The top of the plywood it was setting on was slightly scorched leaving the outline of the battery.  This could have very easily burned the unoccupied home !!!!!

incident_description:
In [REDACTED], we had an electrician install a Generac 11KW standby generator. A flexible hose for gas delivery to the generator was included with it. Our propane company installed the gas line and used the flex hose that came with the generator. About two weeks ago, we noticed the strong odor of gas around the generator. The gas company discovered that an animal, probably a squirrel, had eaten a hole into the flex hose and gas was pouring out of it. We have no idea how long it might have been leaking. We were fortunate that no-one was injured and there was no property damage. This incident is costing us more than $1000. We estimate that we lost about 300 gallons of propane.

I contacted Generac customer service and was informed that the warranty only covers manufacturers' defects and they don't consider animal damage a defect in the product. I understand their point, however, an animal-proof hose should have been provided in the first place. I am aware that there was a recall of metal mesh-covered hoses in 2006. Apparently, this is not an adequate replacement.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to animal damage, but no injuries or property damage occurred. The likelihood is possible as animal damage to hoses can happen but is not frequent.

incident_description:
We were awakened to the house filled with smoke last Tuesday morning as we had left a pot of soup on the stove in the kitchen.  The food completely charred and burned the smoke had  traveled upstairs and moved under our closed bedroom door to awaken us.

We ran  downstairs and turned off the stove and began airing out the house astonished as to why our hard-wired smoke alamrs (all four) had not gone off.  We called Oakland Fire Department's non-emergency number.  The fire crew arrived and tested the smoke alarms which appeared to be working, but were surprised they did not go off.

The next morning, I saw on your website that the specific Kidde model on recall show the manufacture dates of October 22, 2013.  However, our model's manufacture date is October 21, 2013. Our unit is clearly defective.  We lit a sage bush and held it under the unit and it did not go off.

We called Kidde and they sent us replacement units, but we have not yet returned the old ones to them.  After installing the new one, we did the same "sage" experiment and the new one went off within one-minute of lighting the sage.
justification: The incident involved smoke filling the house due to a burned pot of soup, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I recently purchased an Air Conditioning Manifold-Dual-Gauge-Set supposedly designed for air conditioner connections and use with R404A R410A R22 HVAC units as a Diagnostic AC Charging Tool.  Mine was purchased through eBay and manufactured in China by ARKSEN.    http://www.ebay.com/itm/371234780439?_trksid=p2057872.m2749.l2649&ssPageName=STRK%3AMEBIDX%3AIT .

There are about 5 different sets of these units manufactured by ARKSEN and I suspect that all of them suffer from the same defect which potentially may serious meme / life threatening.   I was fortunate that I was not seriously injured by the product when it failed.   After the failure, and in searching the internet for consumer complaints, I found that similar failures have happened to other people with similar potentially fatal incidents.    

The units, used for testing, evacuating, and filling AC with various [Refrigerant].  They are built with plastic based valves which are attached to (screwed into) an aluminum manifold to regulate the [Refrigerant] flow and act as shut on/off the valves for evacuation and addition of Freon.   The safety hazard when filling [Refrigerant] into the system is that the valves get potentially extremely cold (sub-zero).  While apparently manufactured to service 800 psi (according to the specifications), they cannot tolerate the extreme cold created by restricted [Refrigerant] flow and they crack, allowing sub-zero [Refrigerant] to shoot as a spray from the unit in any random direction.   In my instance the [Refrigerant] shot out at a 90 degree angle from the front and hence did not hit me in the face, but the potential of -150 degree [Refrigerant] at high force and volume was there.   Instantaneous 3 degree freeze burns would have resulted had I been positioned a few feet to the left.   

The knobs once frozen, having been chilled below 0 degrees by a restricted [Refrigerant] flow through them during  a recharging / filling,  should not cause them to crack.   The pressure of [Refrigerant] from the tank, in my case R410A, is about 250 psi which chills to subzero instantly and could potentially be lethal when the valves crack.   Clearly this inexpensive product is / contains a manufacturing defect hazard and should be removed from the market.
justification: The incident involved a product defect that could have caused severe injury but did not result in any actual harm this time, though similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description: My wife [REDACTED] weighing 130 lbs, while using a Warner 6 Ft Type II Fiberglass Stepladder on a sturdy wood base platform, to build an outdoor metal shed, the stepladder metal frame buckled at the non-step base causing the ladder and my wife to fall.  The fall caused three broken ribs and substantial emergency hospital bills and ambulance charges.

incident_description: I was in the process of installing a glass wall panel for a frameless glass shower enclosure in the basement bathroom of my home.  The acrylic floor pan and fiberglass walls had already been installed and it was time to install the two glass side panels and door.  My son and I were tilting one glass side panel up on a corner to remove a small rubber gasket from the panel that had become stuck to the bottom edge of the panel during the installation process.  The protective corner cap was installed on the corner of the glass panel.  As he was standing over me slightly tilting the panel, suddenly the panel shattered in my son's hands and glass fell in a pile on the floor and fell on me as I was kneeling beside the panel to remove the stuck gasket on the bottom edge as described above.  I received cuts on my head, hands and leg as it seemed like the glass was falling to the floor in slow motion - it just kept coming.  This incident could have been tragic - we were lucky that no cuts were extremely serious.  I think that the manufacturer could be blamed, MAAX Bath Inc. in Canada, and Menard's in Evendale, OH USA.  Firstly, MAAX packaged the shower with the three glass panels and the shower base in one box - this weighed well over 100 pounds and was awkward to move.  I had purchased the shower enclosure online at Menard's.  When I went to pick it up, I found that the workers in the shipping area at Menard's had broken open the shipping box (possibly with rough handling) the glass panels were touching the concrete floor through a gap in the slats of the shipping pallet that it was standing up on.  However the glass panels had the corner caps on and did not appear to be damaged.  But just to be sure that there was no damage we completely removed the shipping box to check the contents - it all appeared to be okay, so I hauled it home.  Little did I know that the glass probably had been pre-stressed from the rough handling at Menard's and could have shattered at any time.  This could have been horrific.  I have plenty of pictures of the shattered glass and injuries I received.  I am going to ask Menard's for a refund - this was an expensive unit at well over $1,000.  Now I need to figure out how to dispose of the two remaining glass panels in my house without them shattering.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts on the head, hands, and leg, indicating an injury but no death.

incident_description:
I purchased a convection space heater at Home Depot, manufactured by Holmes Products, a brand of Sunbeam Corp doing business as Jarden Consumer Solutions, on March 5, 2015.  It is model HLH4422M.  When turning the heater on for the first time, it emitted a noxious, choking odor that also burned the eyes.  I placed it outdoors and ran it on a high setting for two hours.  The odor subsided significantly after this first operation, but it remains to an extent that causes coughing and airway irritation.  I am not overly sensitive to allergens or other environment conditions, and my workmates in the office also complained about the noxious fumes.  I use the heater sporadically, once every few month, and hoped that it would eventually ÃÂburn offÃÂ the irritant.  However, after a year and a half the noxious fumes continue.  After using it a week ago at a low heat setting, my throat became raw and my sinuses were irritated.  I decided that this product will never ÃÂclean upÃÂ and presents a consumer health danger.

I tried to return it to the place of purchase, Home Depot, but the 90 day return period expired and Home Depot said that the issue must be pursued directly to manufacturer, Holmes Products.  The manufacturer web page does not readily give contact information, I am still trying to make contact.  However, I feel that the CPSC should be notified of the health hazard.
justification: The incident caused throat and sinus irritation, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The issue persists over time with each use, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: I was using the Aquarug in the bathroom when I had lifted my leg to wash under my feet, the mat slipped out from under me and I tried to grab the something to hold on to and when I reached out to grab a hold of the plastic soap holder that is built into the tub, the plastic broke and sliced my hand and the right side of my head and ear hit the tub hard and started to bleed.  I decided to report the incident a year later due to my move and finding the box to complain about the product mildewing and not being non-slipping as advertised when I went online and saw the recall posting.  I had purchased the product last September I believe.  I had taken a picture of the tag on the box which had the date on it.

incident_description:
I bought a Magnum 2 HP 5 Gallon Twin Tank air compressor from Harbor Freight in Huntsville AL. I do not have proof of purchase but it was about 6 or 7 years ago. I used the compressor occasionally. I will guess that the actual running time was less than 24 hours. On the morning of Monday June 27, as I was pressuring up the compressor the back pressure red valve blew up. If I would have been near the compressor it would have blown my head. The top of the valve hit a table that was over the compressor, avoiding further damage. It was shear luck that nobody was injured..
I have the parts of the valve that I was able to recover and it is obvious that it was a metal failure. The walls of the part where the valve is screwed on is very thin and obviously under-designed.
I can provide the parts or send you images as proof of this incident. When I reported the explosion to a Harbor Freight employee today, he just look at me as if this accident was of no concern to him or to the company. 
The product is unsafe and it should not be sold in our country without comprehensive overhaul of safety measures to prevent this accidents to happen.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous equipment failure that could have caused severe injury or death, but no one was actually hurt.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kitchenaid stainless microwave in October 2008.  In the middle of the night while sleeping, were were awakened by a violent noise.   Our microwave's vent cover unit detacedh and fell with such force on our stove top below it severely dented the stainless strips on the sides of our cook top and woke us out of a dead sleep.

While inspecting the unit, the cause of the unit detaching and falling off was the plastic casing broke around the screws on the vent insert (black plastic unit inside the stainless steel cover). 

Had this detached and fallen while cooking it could have easily caused an oil fire, or severe burns to my family.

When I contacted Kitchenaid they basically told us our choices were to pay out of pocket for a service call or pay nearly $90 for the part.  There are numerous complaints online about this part failure, yet there was no recall notice.
justification: The incident caused property damage and potential risk of injury, but no actual injuries occurred. The likelihood is high given the numerous complaints about the part failure.

The consumer did not identify exactly when the symptoms started the symptoms included shortness of breath, wheezing, continuous tearing, coughing, headaches, extreme itching and loss of hair.  The odor in the home has been so extensive that it is affecting the consumerÃÂs voice.  Callers sometimes think that the consumer voice sounds raspy over the phone.  The consumer now wears wigs due to loss of hair. She also experienced Pneumonitis (a lot of mucus in her lungs).
The symptoms improve when she leaves the home and in particular, the tearing and shortness of breath.  Other symptoms have become chronic.

incident_description:
On June 26, 2016, smoke started coming from my washer. I was alerted by the issue because my dog started barking and would not stop. I smelled smoke and notice smoke vapors coming from my laundry room. I go to the laundry room and noticed smoke coming from the back of the washer. I tried to turn the washer off but the control buttons wouldn't work. I had to unplug the washer to get it to stop. I had my work clothes inside and could not open the door. My kitchen filled with smoke and smoke started spreading to my living room. I had to turn on the exhaust fan in the kitchen and laundry room. I had to open all kitchen windows as well as living room windows. I opened the washing detergent receptacle and smoke came from there as well so I knew the inside of the washer was filled with smoke. I plugged the washer back in the outlet to try to get the control buttons to work so I could open the washer and remove the clothes. The power did not come back on. I waited about 10 minutes and the control panel lit up. I was able to open and remove the clothes. My work clothes smelled like they had been in a fire. Of course I couldn't wash them again to get rid of the smell because I was afraid the washer would catch on fire as well as my house.

I performed an online search of the event to see what may be the cause. To my dismay, there were several consumers who had the exact same issue and complained about this model and the lack of response from GE to recall this model. I completed a recall search on the GE website and found a recall for a similar washer (which look exactly like my model with the exception of the water pump being in a different place). GE's website states - "GE Front Loading Washing Machines Recall (2006ÃÂ2010 models)....The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission and the General Electric Company (GE) have announced a recall of 181,055 GE front load washing machines, manufactured from December 2006 until February 1, 2010. These units are white, have a round door and can be identified by the control panel unique to these particular models. Submit the information below or call the GE Recall Hotline to determine if your washer is included in the recall."My washer model is WHDVH660HWW. My washer fits the description of the washer above - white, round door, and appears to be same control panel . The washer model pictured that was recalled which is similar to my model is [REDACTED]. I am concerned that there have been so many complaints about this particular model smoking and burning clothes. There are even youtube videos showing smoke emitting from this exact model. However, there is no recall for this model. Is it just coincidental that so many consumers with this exact model as mine are having or had the exact same problem. My washer was purchased in 2008. I am quite sure it was manufactured in between 2006-2010 as GE website states for the recalled washer. 

Does someone's home have to catch fire and burn or become seriously injured in order for GE to recall this model? If I had not been home when this event occurred to immediately act, the washer would have caught fire and my home would have burned down. Not only that, but my dog would have burned as well not being able to exit the house on her own. If that would have happened, I would have filed a suit against GE given the overwhelming complaints about this issue going back to at least 4 years. GE needs to issue a recall on model number WHDVH660HWW before consumers become seriously injured. It poses a safey concern and is hazardous. A consumer even complained on their website about the model emitting smoke and gave a poor review of the model on GE's website.  

It is my hope that the matter will be investigated and GE is mandated to issue a recall of model WHDVH660HWW before anyone is seriously injured, if they refuse to do a voluntary recall.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission from a washer, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

To verify that we had correctly identified source of smoke, I removed screws on back cover of dehumidifier to look for ignition source and observed melted insulation on wiring and other electrical components.

It does not appear that Home Depot made any attempt to contact us, which is unacceptable; given that the unit was purchased with a credit card, and given the extensive data mining performed by companies, they should have been able to contact us, if they cared to.  This appears negligent to me.

incident_description:
While unplugging an item from an outlet that had the outlet cover on it, sparks flew out of the outlet, the plate cover was blown across the room (approx. 8 feet), the circuit threw and the power in the entire kitchen was blown out. I was shocked (electrically - my hand and arm were numb for hours) and knocked backward. I hit the floor and hurt my ankle/foot (I found out a few months later that it was actually a fracture after many doctor visits, x-rays and wearing an air-cast for 6 weeks I still have problems with the ankle swelling. However, I feel extremely lucky that I wasn't electrocuted/killed.). I had taken pictures and showed them to some of my co-workers (I work for an electric power utility) and family members to get their opinion on what the problem may be (unfortunately I lost those pictures). They were as astonished as I was and couldn't believe I wasn't seriously injured or killed. I have had one person out to change the outlet and that did not resolve the problem. I was told it will most likely require rewiring the affected line an possibly the entire kitchen.
I received the recall letter on the outlet cover a few weeks ago, a little late for me, but, it all makes sense now.
justification: The incident resulted in a fracture and ongoing ankle issues, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rare (1) as such severe outcomes from electrical incidents are uncommon.

incident_description: I purchased Dreamline Infinity-Z shower door online from Home Depot and installed it in February 2016. On June 6 2016 a single roller supporting the door broke and the entire sliding piece fell down, and exploded onto my wife as she exited the shower. She received two large lacerations on her foot, which severed two tendons as the glass broke into large chunks. The piece that was responsible for the collapse is made of cheap plastic, but is made to appear as if it is metal. The door is advertised as being made of glass and aluminum and this is deceptive as the most important safety piece is actually not aluminum or metal at all, but is cheap breakable plastic. This puts consumers at unnecessary risk, as I believe this would not have happened if the hardware were metal. There needs to be more oversight for these companies as they are allowed to sell products that have the potential to kill and are cutting corners to save a little money. Our family is only beginning to heal.
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations and tendon damage, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
The product is a dimming light switch maufactured by Cooper Industries and purchases at Lowe's home improvement.  I bought several of these switches and had them installed for awhile before I finished my project and went to put cover plates on them.  When screwing the cover plat on, one of the switches short circuits, and burnt up.  At first i though this was a fluke, but the second switch did the same thing.  After this I looked closer, this switch has a terrible design and what happened to me was an inevitable result.  The holes for mounting the cover plate are not thru holes, as with many other electrical devices, if the screw that came with the cover plate is too long, it will short out.  

The part number from Coooper is TAL06P-C1-K-L  
The Lowe's number for the item is 480248 

Cooper makes many similarly designed switches sold at Lowe's.  An electrical device that is made to have a screw inserted should not short out if that screws is barely too long.  Even if this switch is installed without incident, it is entirely possible that years later some unsuspecting homeowner would change out the cover plates, and the new cover plates would have a slightly longer screw.
justification: The incident describes a short circuit and damage to the switch, but no injury or death occurred.

I went exploring one day and examining my washer and found that under the rubber seal around the tub there was black mold and lots of slimy black goo. At that time I started to leave the door open to see if that would help and still today I leave the door open or you can't stand the smell. It has been 6 years now and I try to clean it out, but you just cannot get it all out nor can you get rid of the smell.

incident_description:
Ace detergent - used as intended to wash clothing.  This product is produced by Procter and Gamble.  This caused severe inflammation and nerve irritation.  The safety data sheet is listed on the company's website at 

http://www.pgproductsafety.com/productsafety/sds/SDS_2015/TIDE_ORIGINAL__ACE_ORIGNAL_powder.pdf

It says it contains sulfuric acid and is a skin irritant.  The MSDS also says fumes should not be inhaled.  It says personal protective equipment should be used.  It says do not get in eyes, on skin, or on clothing.  The MSDS says the container should be tightly closed in a cool and well ventilated place. The product was sold in a plastic bag with no measuring device to measure the product and no way to reseal the bag after it is opened.  The MSDS also says it contains silicic acid.  It says for prolonged use gloves should be worn.  The MSDS says it contains sodium hydroxide which is regulated as a hazardous substance under the Comprehensive Environmental Response Compensation and Liability Act and a regulated pollutant pursuant to the Clean Water Act.  Why are these components not listed in the 'ingredients' on the Procter and Gamble website?  

The "ingredients" of this toxic product are on the company's website at 

http://www.pgproductsafety.com/productsafety/ingredients/household_care/laundary_fabric_care/Ace/Ultra_Ace_Powder_Detergent.pdf

It says it contains oxygen bleach (sodium percarbonate), bleach activator (nonanoyloxybenzenesulfonate and B62 agglomerate).  

Why are these toxic chemicals not listed on the packaging?  Why does the packaging have no warning that the product is a skin irritant?  The MSDS states to never return spills to original container for reuse.  Why is the product being sold in a bag that is not resealable and can spill very easily?  Why is no measuring device included in the packaging?  The product is toxic so why would the instructions give measurements by the cup (a unit of measurement to measure food) instead of by the cap?  Why is it being sold under different names?

The product is very dangerous.  Procter and Gamble have their own poison control center staffed with health care professionals on call around the clock.
justification: The incident caused severe inflammation and nerve irritation, indicating an injury (severity 3). The product's hazardous components and lack of proper warnings suggest a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description: I used Febreze fabric refresher, original scent, to deodorize bed sheets for approximately six months. I began having respiratory problems, including bronchitis, persistent coughing, shortness of breath and panic attacks after about three months. Multiple doctor visits, a trip to the emergency room and lung and heart tests did not reveal a possible cause for my ailments. My doctor and I discussed environmental changes, and Febreze came up. I stopped using Febreze and replaced the sheets and noticed an almost immediate improvement in my health. Though I still have a little bronchial congestion, all the other symptoms have stopped. I believe Febreze, with many unlisted harmful ingredients, caused my illness.
justification: The individual experienced respiratory problems and required medical attention, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) since the symptoms resolved after discontinuing use of the product, suggesting a plausible but not certain link.

justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts) to the husband's legs and feet, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) due to the unusual nature of a sink exploding under normal use.

Below is an email correspondence I had with Lumber Liquidators; the letter details our experience of my son's diagnosis with acute myeloid leukemia, a cancer that is associated with formaldehyde exposure, which I believe is the result of the flooring that we had installed in his room when he was 2 years old.  I have also included the response from Lumber Liquidators.

Ultimately I had the flooring testing done on my own, and the tests reveal there are high levels in the flooring material as well as elevated levels of formaldehyde off gassing.  I am now getting quote from a contractor to remove and replace the flooring.

I had a piece of the floor material tested, which it revealed levels of 1,100 mg/kg(PPM) of formaldehyde.
I also had two air tests performed, one revealed 55ngL(44PPB), the second 54ngL(43PPB)

All test results are included in the attached documents.

========== Original Message ========== 

From:    [REDACTED] <>

June 8, 2016 


[REDACTED], Chairman

Toano, VA 23168 


Dear [REDACTED], 

I am writing with serious concerns about the flooring that we purchased from Lumber Liquidators.  It has become clear to me that it is unfit for human habitation and I would like compensation 
for the cost of removal, a replacement of my choice including a replacement subfloor heating system if necessary, as well as for the cost of the testing I have already conducted and any needed in the future.  Although the flooring we installed is bamboo and not included in the study published by the CDC in early 2016, it prompted me to research and ultimately to initiate testing that has confirmed that there continues to be unsafe levels of formaldehyde in my sonÃÂs room.  This is especially concerning because the report indicates that there is a connection to high levels of formaldehyde exposure and myeloid leukemia. 

In 2005, we purchased and installed Lumber Liquidator Morningstar Bamboo Flooring along with approved subfloor heating in my then 2 year old sonÃÂs bedroom.  In 2013, my son at age 
9 became extremely ill and was diagnosed and hospitalized with acute myeloid leukemia, which is the exact type of leukemia that is associated with formaldehyde exposure.  After reading everything I could find on the issue, I am convinced his leukemia was caused by the flooring.  Thankfully, he survived the treatment and is doing well at this point.   

In the attached folder you will find all relevant information that I have accumulated up to this point.  I had a piece of the floor tested from wood that we had remaining from the installation; test results show high levels of formaldehyde in the material.    Subsequently, I had the air in my sonÃÂs room tested two times, once comparing it to our living room, a second time comparing it to the outside air.  Both tests taken from my sonÃÂs room are consistent and reveal elevated levels of formaldehyde.  I am extremely disturbed that after 11 years, the flooring is still off gassing at rates that could cause health issues.  I am even more upset that my son, who has already experienced such an 
extreme health crisis continues to be exposed, as am I and my other son. 

Upon reading the CDC report in February, I immediately removed my son from his room, and he has been sleeping on the couch since that time.  This has been a huge hardship in itself. 
The bigger picture is that we have had to experience the nightmare of his treatment, and the fears of what the future holds for him.  Because of the type of chemotherapy he received, he has a greater risk of other cancers, his heart health has been jeopardized and he has to go for heart screening tests annually for the rest of his life, and there is a chance he could have fertility problems. This is in addition to all the expenses involved in having to deal with an extremely expensive medical crisis. 

I have tried upon several occasions to contact Lumber Liquidators to gather more information about our specific flooring, but no one was able or willing to help me.  I emailed you once, but got a rote response email referring me to the website, which really does not yield much specific information.  I had one customer service person claim that my flooring was not made in China, even after I told her I had packaging that is clearly marked Made in China.  I also tried to acquire one of the air test kits Lumber Liquidators is offering to customers, but because this flooring is not one of the ones involved with the CDC report, nor is it part of any class actions suits, I was denied a test.  Considering 
all the information that has come to light in the past several years, it is reasonable to suspect that Lumber Liquidators as a company is aware of the defects with their flooring, but has not taken any steps to acknowledge or remedy the issue and has failed 
to warn me as a consumer. 

As of Sept 2015, my employment situation has finally stabilized, but I have no funds to rectify the problems that have occurred because of the Lumber Liquidator flooring and am looking 
to your company to take financial responsibility for making my sonÃÂs room safe.  As a retailer/wholesaler, I believe Lumber Liquidator should be held liable for the imported defective products that they manufacture and promote. 

I look forward to hearing from you soon so that we can start taking steps to bring this to a resolution. 

Sincerely, 

[REDACTED]

Our bamboo floors are an entirely different product.  They are made differently, and with different materials. On 6/6 2016 I ordered a brand new shark navigator lift away vacuum, model NV352, from Home Depot.  June 14, 2016 was the first time I used it. After going over the rug a few times I started getting electrical shocks! They are coming from the top part of the handle where it curves. Not the part you hold on to, but the curved part of the handle that is underneath the part you hold on to. I didn't have to actually even touch it, but it was arcing from there to my hand. This is not just small static shocks, but very strong electrical shocks, my hand and arm were tingling for about an hour after I stopped vacuuming. One was so strong that I actually let go of the vacuum handle and almost fell backwards.  This is extremely dangerous. After this happened I checked on-line and found out that Shark has had other vacuums that have been recalled for a shock hazard. I contacted Shark and this was their reply to me:

Dear [REDACTED],

Thank you for your email.

I am sorry to hear that. It is a normal occurrence and can be prevented by keeping hands moisturized, not wearing wool/polyester clothing while vacuuming. I apologize for the inconvenience this has caused. 

If we can be of further assistance please feel free to contact us at 1-800-798-7398, Monday to Friday, 8:00 am - 10:00 pm EST, as well as Saturday & Sunday from 9:00 am - 6:00 pm EST.

With regards,
Customer Service Team
SharkNinja Operating LLC


NORMAL OCCURANCE?!! Are they crazy??!! I have been vacuuming 40+ years and this is NOT normal. I can't emphasize enough how strong these shocks were!! Plus, I moisturize my hands and I was wearing cotton. I never wear wool or poly. To suggest this will fix this problem is insane. I'm hoping you can get a recall on this before some gets seriously injured. I will be returning it to Home Depot with a warning not to re-sell it!
justification: The incident describes strong electrical shocks causing tingling and almost causing a fall, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the user's experience and similar past recalls.

incident_description:
I purchased a Frigidaire FAD504DWD 50-pint dehumidifier on Sept 1, 2014 through Amazon. I maintained the unit as suggested in the use and care manual (i.e., cleaning filter, dusting the cabinet, and clean the water bucket). On June 4, when cleaning the filter, I noticed a mildew smell emanating from the appliance. I disassembled the appliance and found that the front coil was covered in 1/8 inch layer of mold and sludge. As I started to clean the unit, I realized that there was also debris etc between the two coils and that there is no way to disassemble the coils from the appliance to clean/disinfect. 

My husband called Frigidaire (June 4, 7:15 pm) and was told that the appliance was still functional/not broken, so they could not issue a replacement under the 5 year limited warranty. On June 5, I emailed product support reporting what I had found and stating that I was shocked that Frigidaire considers this product functional in this state, rather than a product/health liability. On June 6, I received a response that "When the filter and coils of the dehumidifier are choked with dirt, it may not pull out moisture from the air properly. The efficiency of the dehumidifier gets decreased and the only solution is, to clean it thoroughly. In order to assist you with the cleaning procedure of a dehumidifier, following are a few tips..." One of these cleaning tips suggested that I "Use a vacuum cleaner to clean the evaporative coil/hot coil. Scrub off the dirt using a brush but make sure that you don't bend the fins while cleaning. Clean the condenser or the cold coil the same way." Given I didn't think the appliance could be dissembled allowing access to both coils, I requested detailed information on how to do this on June 6th. On June 8th, I received a response stating: "Do not try to remove the coils of the dehumidifier as this will ruin the appliance. You may use a vacuum cleaner to clean the evaporative coil/hot coil and condenser coil..." On June 8th, I responded and specifically asked for a refund given there is no way to adequately clean the unit without removal of the coils and removal of the coils would ruin the machine. In response, again on June 8th, I was told "I was happy to review your case with my supervisor. Regretfully, mold is not covered by your Manufacturer's Warranty, so Frigidaire will not be able to provide you with a replacement dehumidifier." I disagree. Given the current state of the appliance, it is not capable of performing its intended function without serious health ramifications. I contend that this is a direct result of the "defective materials or workmanship" (i.e., poor design) of the product.

Additionally, when purchasing this appliance, the website claimed (as does Frigidaire's current website) that this appliance "protects your home from mold and mildew caused by excess moisture" and "helps eliminate bacteria in the air that can make breathing difficult." Instead, this appliance became a major source of mold and mildew within my home. Further, I suspect that it was emanating bacteria into the air for months without suspicion as a direct result of these advertising claims. Given the design of this appliance is prohibits repair (i.e., cleaning), it is not feasible for the unit to function according to these claims, yet Frigidaire considers the unit to be functional in its present state.

I am currently working through the BBB to ideally obtain a refund/resolve my complaint, but think it is important that more people are warned so not adversely affected by this product.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning dehumidifier causing mold and potential health risks, but no actual injury or death is reported.

May, 13, 2016

To: Consumer Products Safety Commission
From: [REDACTED]
Re: Patriot Power Generator Recall

To Whom It May Concern:

Attached please find pdf scans showing that I purchased a Patriot Power Generator from Patriotpowergenerator.com a.k.a. Power4Patriots. They indicate their mailing address as: POB 121709, Nashville, TN 37212, with phone number 800-680-8504.

On November 15, 2014 I purchased a Patriot Power Generator for a price of $1997.00. This unit is a battery-powered rechargeable power generator that can be recharged either by pre-charging it using an AC outlet OR with the included solar panels. The unit arrived in what I believed to be normal working condition & was then stored after completing an initial battery charge as directed by the enclosed instructions. I did not use the generator after the initial charge. I have not been physically injured by the product.

On February 24, 2016 I received both an email & mailed letter indicating that the referenced generator was being recalled because the lithium batteries posed a fire hazard. The seller's communications advised that they are cooperating with the manufacturer (Lekker, LLC of Lindon, Utah) as they implement a recall with the Consumer Products Safety Commission. I contacted the seller with my serial number & they confirmed that my generator was included on the recall list. They then advised me that they would contact me soon to arrange for return of the unit for a full refund & that the return shipping would be at no charge to me. During the initial call I advised the seller that the shipping box arrived with multiple slashes, thereby preventing me from returning it in the original shipping box. I also advised that I had found a very sturdy box and packing material that would be more than adequate for the return. They advised that they would be responsible for all aspects of the return, including shipping costs & providing a box if necessary.

When I had not heard back from the seller by the first week of May, I called the number they provided. During that call, I received conflicting information from the seller's customer service representative. The responses included that the CPSC was still processing the recall, then I was told that the CPSC needed to give them authorization to have the units shipped back to the seller.

As the seller's customer service representative seemed to be confused in her responses, I asked to speak with a manager. I was advised that a manager from the seller's company would call me back within 48 hours. To date, I have not heard back from anyone associated with the seller. Instead they mailed me a complimentary packet of instant coffee, while apologizing for the ongoing delay.

A few days ago I called the CPSC. The CPSC representative was very helpful. She first checked into the recall & was unable to find any such matter either under the seller or manufacturer's names. She then advised me to send this email, including scans of any documentation associated with the purchase of the generator & the recall. The names that the CPSC representative investigated included: Patriotpowergenerator.com; Power4Patriots; Lekker, [REDACTED]. I also later noticed the name of [REDACTED] of Shenzhen, China.

I would appreciate your help to resolve this matter. My goal is to return the unit at no cost to me & the seller should also provide me with a full refund. I would NOT be interested in any type of repair or exchange as I no longer have faith in the seller.

Sincerely,

The consumer immediately rinsed his eyes for approximately fifteen minutes; this was repeated once again thirty minutes later.

05/16/2016 - Because the consumer's eye was still irritated and red, the consumer visited his ophthalmologist, whom after treatment with steroids, antibiotic and sterile water drops told him he had received a grade two corneal injury and should follow up two days later.

05/18/2016 - The consumer followed up with his Doctor; his eye has improved much and that he should continue his treatment. The Doctor informed the consumer that he was lucky his injury was not worse.

The consumer believes the packaging of the product is faulty and should not be sticking together or packaged under pressure.

State Farm is our insurance company and the damages are being assessed. Major smoke and soot damage. Have already received an estimate from an electrician to repair, replace affected house wiring. Air Conditioning people to make estimation for damage to Daikon unit. ServPro still working on restoring/cleaning house to normal.

incident_description:
RE: Amazon Order# [REDACTED]

I ordered a replacement power supply for my HP Pavilion laptop (Laptop/Notebook Power Supply
Sold through Amazon by C.W.K.} because the first one I purchased overheated and the casing deformed, emitting
the smell of melting plastic.

I was given a replacement that I have used since. When I was asked for my opinion about the replacement power
supply, I said that it was not overheating but my computer's battery was fully charged. I suggested that buyers be
careful to monitor the heat if they were re-charging a partially or fully depleted battery because the chargers could
overheat.

Yesterday, for the first time since I started using the replacement power supply, I used my laptop without plugging
it in. When the battery power dropped below about twenty percent, I plugged in the power supply. A half hour
later, I smelled melting plastic and saw the casing deforming like the first one I had replaced.

Follow my reasoning for a moment. Let us assume that the probability of receiving two identically defective power
supplies is low.lf we assume quality control measures are designed to prevent customers from receiving defective
products, then the probability ought to be vanishingly small. But of all the many thousands of people ordering this
product, I get two with the same defect.
justification: The incident involves a defective power supply overheating and deforming, but no injury or death occurred.

Thank you

incident_description: Using a SoleusAir powered by Gree Dehumidifier Model GM-DEH-45-1q3.  Unit was in basement utility room.  Turned on previous day and ran for approximately 24 hours. On Friday, May 27 2016 the unit overheated and was emitting smoke.  We were home at the time and smelled smoke through the HVAC vents in home.  Went downstairs to find the unit very hot to the touch, the breaker to the home wiring circuit was tripped. The unit was still emitting smoke.  House circuit breaker prevented much worse from happening.  Looked up the recall information online with Gree and they state that this serial number is NOT affected by the recall.  We had a previous unit that we replaced when it was recalled and this was the replacement.
justification: The dehumidifier overheated and emitted smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The house circuit breaker prevented further damage.

incident_description: I used Tide Washing Machine cleaner in my machine around 10:30pm and the smell went throughout the house. It gave me a bad headache which didn't respond to [REDACTED]. It woke up my husband who was in bed asleep with the door closed on the other side of the house. He wanted to know what the horrible chemical smell was. It was so bad it woke him up. incident_description:
I bought the house in 2004 and the air exchanger failed by 2006 within the warranty period. The air exchanger fan motor stopped. When this happened, the unit was hot enough to partially deform the airtight seal. A noticeable smell of outgassing material occurred upon entry in the utility room. A 60 Hz hum was audible simultaneously. The unit was hot to the touch.

The unit was new with the house, installed in accordance with the manufacturer recommendations, and inspected by the City of Saint Paul. It also failed within the warranty period. Previous communications indicated that a repair person would be dispatched at no cost. However, that did not occur. We received an embedded 3 ampere non-replaceable fuze after the unit quit and were notified of a recall. This service does not meet our expectations.

Model HRVBBLHU1150
Serial Number 1504V00705
justification: The incident involved equipment failure and safety hazards like overheating and outgassing, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
We have a LG DLG2702 Gas clothes dryer. (purchased 11/2009)
After drying a load of bedding in our gas dryer, the dryer caught on fire.  I first noticed a burning smell at the end of the cycle. Shortly after smoke came into the drum and from behind the unit.  The fire department responded. They removed the dryer from the home and extinguished the small fire inside by removing the top. They confirmed that something was burning inside. It was NOT a fire caused by lint in the hose or by anything placed in the dryer.  The interior drum was fine as well as the hose. We regularly remove/clean lint from the machine.

I inspected the interior of the dryer by placing a flashlight in the exhaust.  There was the remains of a small booklet (something from the parts mgfr??) in a plastic bag on the gas line which started the fire. This should have never been in the inside of the dryer.  It wasn't something a consumer would have access to and is a fire hazzard.  

Luckily I was home and caught it. The damage was isolated to the dryer.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dryer but no injuries or deaths were reported, and the damage was isolated to the dryer.

I tried to push the power button to shut the unit off, but it would not shut off. Had to unplug it from the outlet to get it to shut off. This seemed like a very dangerous situation so I decided to contact the manufacturer. Went to their website and found out the unit was recalled because it causes fires. Typed my units information and my complete contact information in to their form and it verified that the unit was recalled and that they would contact me. This was three weeks ago and I have not heard anything. This company needs a big fine! They obviously build defective products and do not take their recall obligations seriously. Caller stated that the furnace has a burning problem (flashback) and is very noisy.  He feels that this furnace is unsafe.  He contacted the company, a technician was sent out and he was informed that the heat exchanger needed to be replaced.

Caller stated that he has this problem since installation and he does not feel they are willing to replace the furnace.

Caller bought and installed an American Standard brand furnace for a homeowner. Upon commissioning the furnace, caller found out that the furnace burners have excessive noise and abnormal flames that felt disturbing and unsafe for the homeowner and worrisome to caller as the service provider. After hours of investigation and trying things that could possibly correct the problem, the problem  remained unresolved. At the same time, it gives the homeowner some heat even with a degree of risk. This furnace needs a thorough factory testing for finding the exact cause of the issue for the sake of correcting the manufacturing process and public safety.
