incident_description:
The consumer stated that the rubber hose that connects the propane tank supply gas to the generator has no place to lay while the generator is in use. Leading to the rubber supply hose from the LP gas laying on the hot generator exhaust.

The consumer stated that the rubber hose lays on the hot exhaust regardless of if the propane  tank is hooked up and in use or not. The consumer stated that there is no place to hang the hose on the generator  at any time even when it is not in use. The LP gas stays attached to the generator at all times even when the generator is running on the alternate  fuel "gasoline".

The consumer stated that while he was running  the generator on gasoline not LP gas, noticed a strong smell from the generator. The consumer did not notice anything the matter at first but then later found that the rubber hose that goes to the LP gas tank had melted in half with a small piece of the hose falling to the ground.

The consumer stated that the hose did come curled up on top of the motor from the factory out of the box. Consumer stated that there is no place to hang the hose while the generator is running on LP gas or on regular gas.The consumer stated that there is no place to hang the hose while running the generator or moving the generator on its wheels. The only logical spot to place the hose is curled up on top of the motor when you are trying to move the generator or not using the LP gas tank. It's not logical to lay the open end of the hose in the dirt potentially leading to dirt in the line and possible damage to the fitting on the end of the hose where it would attach to the tank. This leads to damage to the LP hose whether
it is in use or not. Huge risk of the hose being damaged, partially melted or possibly having a hole melted in the hose from it coming into contact from the hot exhaust.

The consumer stated that the generator hose should never easily come in contact with the hot exhaust. Possible solutions would  be a different high temp hose,or have the LP gas line come out on the opposite side of the generator than the exhaust does. In any case there should be either  a retractable hose installed or a safe secure place to hang the gas hose away from the exhaust while in use,not in use, or while the generator is being transported.

Being that the generator is mobile, the LP hose also stands a huge risk of unnoticed damage while it is being wheeled or transported from location to location.

The consumer  believes that there is a huge risk of fire,injury and or damages due to the fact that at any time the LP gas hose can come into contact  with the hot exhaust leading to someone potentially hooking up and using a damaged or leaking hose. If a leaking hose was put into use without someone realizing it and started the generator,it appears that there is a very high likely hood that it will cause a fire or a personalinjury of some kind.
 
The consumer states that he is thankfulhe found the melted hose when he did. Consumer believes that not everyone  would notice this problem before an accident could happen.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer about the issue. They informed him that he shouldn't have had the rubber hose laying on the exhaust. The consumer was informed that a new hose would not be covered under the warranty. The consumer had to pay around $20 for a new hose and shipping.
justification: The incident involved a melted hose but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is high given the design flaw and frequent contact with hot exhaust.

incident_description:

incident_description: Approximately one month ago, I began using my Lasko Ceramic Floor Heater (Model 5521) for the second time. I purchased this heater on 10/21/2014, as the weather cooled. The heater was used extensively for about four months. After the weather warmed, it was unplugged and put away. Last month, I began using it again. This however, I noticed its outside portions near its base, the "skin" of the heater, was warped. Upon inspection, it became obvious to me that excessive heat had caused this. The plastic was warped and it had rippled and had split the casing open. Immediately, I quit using the heater and checked to see if it had been recalled. I discovered many similar heaters from Lasko had been recalled--but not this model. Of the recalled heaters, many had shown defects identical to the ones I had experienced. I immediately contacted Lasko through their online messaging system. I never received a response. No phone call. No e-mails. Nothing. Lasko completely ignored me and completely ignored what might be a lethal defect if this results in a house fire, which I believe it could. This heater was purchased from Overstock.com and has approximately four months of use on it.
justification: The heater's casing warped due to excessive heat, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Letter to AO Smith:

I purchased an AO Smith 50 gallon propane water heater in April, 2014.  Since that time I have had a recurring problem with the water heater overheating.  Initially the problem was diagnosed as a faulty gas control valve, but after 3 valve replacements it became obvious that was not the case.  Fast forward to today and I find myself at an impasse with your technical support department.  

I live in [REDACTED] and have a second home about 1.5 hours away that I visit 3-4 days a week.  During the time I am away it has become apparent that turning down the temperature setting on the heater does not prevent temperatures of 150-160 degrees (a potential risk of scalding) being exhibited when I return.  [REDACTED], the head of your technical  support, has told me that the pilot light alone is causing the excessive heating and the only solution is for me to shutdown the heater when I leave and relight it when I return.  In my opinion this is a ridiculous solution to the problem.  The inability to keep the heater in a nominal temperature range with the proposed solution would result in tremendous inconvenience on a weekly basis, and potential impairment of the heater's functionality (igniter wearing out and excessive repeated temperature changes).  This condition indicates to me that the heater does not have proper temperature control.
justification: The water heater's overheating poses a scalding risk (150-160°F), but no injury has been reported yet.

The consumer had not used the shower today. The middle panel is a glass door which shattered, however the other two outer panels which are stationary were not damaged.

incident_description:

Removed tank from its generator mount and inspected the area where the leak was dripping down from which was a mounting port.  Did not see any significant  cracks or breaks around the port beneath the tank.

Took a flashlight to look at the inside of the tank and discovered that three of four ports have a dome shaped cap on the inside end of the port.  The fourth port, the leaking port does not have a cap.

I then decided that the missing cap on the leaking port is causing gasoline to leak out and leak is due to a factory defect in construction and assembly.

incident_description:
Re: Possible Unsafe Products- Stabil Concrete Pavers, LLC-Sarasota, Florida
To Whom It May Concern:
By way of this communication and Its attachments, I respectfully request the review and
possible intervention of the commission. My concerns specifically relate to products which were
and continue to be produced by STABIL CONCRETE PAVERS, LLC of Sarasota, Florida.
As a point of Information, I am a retired forensic construction defect/product defect consultant
with over 35 years of forensic experience. 1 am degreed in the four (4} major engineering disciplines
of civil, mechanical, electrical and chemical engineering as well as having been exposed to the
commission's interventions in the past.
The products of which I have concern are swimming pool coping stones and concrete paving stones.
My initial exposure to the defective products were when coping stones were installed on my pool
circa March 2014. At that time, the stones exhibited excessive edge chipping. The forensic signatures
were quite clear that I may be dealing with a substandard production product. But, hoping that I was
dealing with an anomaly, I approached the manufacturer with a warranty claim. Though they
attempted to offer what was, in their view, a fair settlement position. In my view, their offer fell short
of being equitable. The recalcitrant nature of both the manufacturer as well as their attorney urged me
to utilize the forensic skills God chose to entrust to my care.
The new question was whether the defective products installed at my pool were just an isolated
situation or, in the alternative, evidence of a more pervasive production problem. If the defects were
pervasive, they could pose a threat to the health and welfare of the public totally beyond aesthetic
appearance issues. Based upon the need to be objective, I temporarily ignored the coping stones
installed on my pool. I sought out and obtained standard supply chain samples, maintaining as normal
a chain of custody as possible for my initial forensic investigations.
Initial forensic research indicated that the manufacturer claimed to " .ÃÂ. MEET OR EXCEED THE
REQUIREMENTS OF ASTM C-936". This standard has specific production requirements including, but
not limited to, requirements for compressive strength and absorption. The supply chain samples were
subjected to test procedures defined in the referenced ASTM standard by an independent laboratory
with extensive experience with matters of this type. ASTM C-936 references test protocols defined In
ASTM C-140/140M. The test results for the limited number of samples tested were devastating
though quite dispositive. The supply chain samples tested failed to even come close to the ASTM
standards for compressive strength and absorption which the manufacturer claimed to "MEET OR
EXCEED". More importantly, the test results profile a product which could potentially pose a threat
to the health and welfare of the public.
The test results clearly explain the edge chipping found In the coping stones Installed on my pool.
Of greater interest to the commission is that the Initial test results support a theory that the standard
supply chain production products of this manufacturer could be unsafe for use by the public. Please
consider that the absence of the published compressive strength could have significant consequences.
1) It could cause ongoing chipping of pool coping stones which would create sharp edges with the
potential of being a cut/abrasion hazard to pool users.
2) A relatively minor impact could cause a brittle fracture of the pool copings in cases where the
stones are installed In a cantilever fashion on the pool shell top edge (Typical installation). This
event would expose a "Cutting Edge" to the pool users with the associated cut/abrasion hazard.
3) Lack of published compressive strength could also cause a compressive failure (Pulverization) of
the pool coping stones and paver units if exposed to loads equal to or even less than their
claimed capacity but above their actual tested compressive strength (Claimed Strength-8000 psi,
Actual Test Data-approx. 2000 psi). If Stabil's products fall in walkways, driveways or any other
ambulation surface installation where their claimed strength Is assumed, the deformed stones
would present a significant trip and fall hazard.
Also, please consider the high absorption rates found in the test results. Obviously, they exceed the
ASTM standard claimed by the manufacturer and provides a clear reason why the manufacturer
needs to exclude efflorescence from their warranty. Of greater Interest to the commission should be
the fact that high absorption rates will negatively affect the existing inadequacies In compressive
strength over time. This alone could further compromise the strength of Stabil's production products
since the high absorption rates could lower their already poor compressive strength values.
To assist the commission In the investigation and possible recall of the involved products, I
have enclosed the following:
1) "File A Report'' form-OMB Control Number 3041-0146 with relevant sections completed
and referencing this correspondence as appropriate.
2) Copies of the Manufacturer's published limited Warranty as well as their published tutorial on
Efflorescence. Their warranty specifically references conformity to ASTM C-936 and
specifically excludes Efflorescence as a valid warranty Issue. The tutorial document basically
attempts to exculpate the manufacturer from blame regarding efflorescence Issues. In my
opinion, it is an affirmative effort to "short circuit" valid claims caused by the high absorption
rates of their standard production products.
3) ASTM C-936/C-936M titled "Standard Specification for Solid Concrete Interlocking Paving Units"
4) ASTM C-140/C-140M titled "Standard Test Methods for Sampling and Testing Concrete Masonry
Units and Related Units"
5) FORENSIC TESTING REPORT prepared by J.A. FREZZA & ASSOCIATES, LLC of Flemington, NJ.
dated July 24, 2015.
If there are any open questions, I can be reached at (Home) [REDACTED]and (Cell) [REDACTED] Since I have both a personal as well as professional interest In this matter, any Information that the
commission can share with me regarding any Investigation and/or conclusion would be greatly
appreciated. My professional skills are offered to the commission as a courtesy, if needed.
justification: The description indicates potential safety hazards from defective products, including sharp edges and trip hazards, but no actual injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
I am an accredited U.S.EPA instructor and University research member.  As such parents from around the states contact me when they have concerns over Lead.  Recently, a parent from Florida contacted me because her child had a lead level of 11ug and her house was not painted with lead paint.  The home was constructed in 1978.   Interviewing the parent I discovered that they recently had a bathroom remodeled and no one controlled the dust.  A certified inspector was called to the home and discovered that the remaining tile (just like that remodeled) registered over 20mg/cm2.  It is possible the child was contaminated by the remodeling dust because he crawled on the carpet close to the area remodeled and only normal house cleaning (not abatement cleaning) was used.   The parent's, now being aware of lead and its hazards panicked and had everything in the house tested.   The child's school project painted with "Coloration" Green Glitter Paint registered (.4mg/cm2).   This product concerns me.  Many teachers buy this product from "Discount School Supplies" on line. Can CPSC test the product as purchased from this online service or do you want me to get the actual bottle from the preschool where the Florida child attended.

(Issue 2)... Several years ago, the Southern Nevada Health Department closed down some [REDACTED] shops for excessively high levels of lead dust in the shops.  The shop owners were made to abate the shops and asked to purchase un leaded ceramic paints.   I thought they would comply but a student in one of my lead classes brought in a freshly painted ceramic plate made by his granddaughter in one of our local Las Vegas shops.  It registered 8.6 to 5.6 mg/cm2.  I thought ceramic paint (hobby paint) was now limited to 100ppm.    Thank you for any help in this matter.  Please let me know what else I can do to help. [REDACTED]
justification: The child had a lead level of 11ug, indicating exposure likely from remodeling dust, which can cause injury. The occurrence is possible given the context of uncontrolled dust during remodeling.

incident_description:

incident_description:
The "rip fence" that was provided by Ryobi with this product Model RTS20 10" portable table saw has two plastic "sliders" that allow the fence to lock onto the table saw top.  The sliders appear to be very poorly made and one or both can easily become cracked and break off.   The left slider for my rip fence did in fact break within 2 years of use and also within the 3 year warrantee period for this product.   I discovered that without both sliders intact, the rip fence cannot lock and may move unexpectedly while the saw is being used.  If the rip fence moves it can allow the wood piece being cut to shift and permit severe operator injury.    The two plastic parts in question are described below with their Ryobi Part numbers.   I contacted the company to inform them of this problem and discovered that they have discontinued these parts and don't offer the consumer any other option for replacement.  To me, this compounds the problem since consumers may continue to use a defective rip fence, attempt a home made fix or use another brand rip fence not made for the table saw.   I feel strongly that these rip fences should be recalled to check for damage to the sliders and that the company provide a safer, more stable design for the rip fence.    Please understand that I have not been injured by this defect but it seems very likely that someone could easily become injured if it is not corrected. 



Rip Fence Slider - Left  #089037008156
Rip Fence Slider - Right #089037008155
justification: The rip fence defect poses a risk of severe injury if the fence moves unexpectedly during use, though no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Table saw from Delta which was purchased at Home Depot or Lowes several years ago started on fire and almost caused a fire in the garage. The fire was electrical and it was INSIDE the saw housing box which is sealed and not serviceable to the consumer. The fire caused severe smoke inside the garage which also made it's way into the house. Had to be put out with an electrical extinguisher. Fire could of been worse if it had spread to wood that was being worked with saw. It was a complete product failure and had nothing to do with my side of the electrical. The circuit protector inside the saw also failed as it did not reset or trip. I contacted Delta first but their corporate offices will no help with the product claiming it was before they (Dewalt / Black Decker)purchased Delta in 2004 relieving them from any responsibility. Only offered a small % discount on an online item which is not what is needed to rectify the situation. 

Model Saw 36-540 Type 2
justification: The incident involved a fire and severe smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: 46 year old male and 16 year old son were waterproofing their boots in their house.  I do not know what kind of ventilation was used.  that same day,  he had respiratory difficulty and went to an Urgent Care but was discharged home.  Son developed chest pain. Next day, both cats were dead.  Father had difficulty breathing and could not get out of bed.  Wife was not home during the waterproofing process.  Son has improved but husband has had an additional ED evaluation and seen by PMD requiring steroids for his respiratory symptoms.  Cats were taken to the MSU Veterinary College where they wanted to do necropsies but family could not afford the procedure.  I have been unable to obtain the specific ingredients in the aerosol but it is highly suggestive of the prior episode of Bootmate which led to a recall because of nanoingredient used for waterproofing.  This is Heelix Foot and Shoe Care aerosol bout at Rocky's Outdoors: 810-742-5420.  the only ingredient they could give me was the propellants: propane, isobutene and hexane.  It also contains mink oil.  I am unable to locate this product on the web.
justification: The incident resulted in respiratory difficulties and chest pain for the individuals, and death of the cats, indicating injury and death, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the incident happened but is not a common occurrence.

incident_description: My five year old dehumidifier started on fire.  It did not cause home damage because I was able to stop it with a fire extinguisher right away but there was about 6-8in Flames coming out the back of the unit.  It was well maintained, the filter was clean, it was not full of water, and had plenty of air flow around the unit.
justification: The dehumidifier caught fire but was quickly extinguished without injury or property damage.

incident_description: The product in question is an indoor/outdoor ethanol fireplace.  This incident involved two people, the victim and her male friend.  The victim was sitting at the end of a dining room table.  Located in the middle of the table was a Moda flame Vigo indoor/outdoor ventless fireplace (see picture).  The friend stated that they observed the flame going out so he grabbed the bottle of fuel (see picture) and poured more ethanol in the fireplace.  When he did this he said the fireplace flashed on fire and in turn, there was also a fire on the table.  He grabbed a towel and put the fire out, but he mostly described the fire as being a flash fire.  Shortly after the fire was out on the table and fireplace he said the victim told him that she was on fire.  He reported the front of her dress was on fire and the flames rapidly traveled up to  her face.  She stood up and tried to pat it out, he ran over and helped.  She went up to the shower to cool the burns and he called 911.  The victim sustained 40% partial thickness burns mostly to her torso.  She passed away at the hospital several weeks later due to treatment complications.
justification: The victim sustained severe burns and later died due to treatment complications, which constitutes a death.

incident_description: We were using heater in room blowing straight on us and smelt plastic burning it was on about a hour or 2 there is a tilt vent which was blowing a little less then straight looked over and it was melted under neath vent they should of made vent so you could only move it a little when i called them about it they said you're not supposed to angle vent all the way down why would they make it so you can and also the automatic switch should of shut it off before it had a chance to over heat and melt so i sent it back to them they have to investigate it whatever that means.

incident_description: Turned on Dimplex Electric Fireplace using remote control unit APT-1315.  It made a static noise, then started smoking and burst into flames.  Luckily the breaker popped and the flames went out.

incident_description:
1st Hot Water Tank (04/23/2015)The consumer stated that she purchased a Bradford White hot water tank on April 23. The consumer stated that after using the water a white substance was left on her skin, scalp and eyelashes. There was a terrible metallic odor when the hot water was turned on. It also left deposits around the tub in the bathroom and the kitchen sink faucet. The consumer also suffered hair loss and her eyelashes turned white. 

The consumer contacted her water conditioner company. The representative came out and check the water conditioner, which was fine. The consumer was also advised that other people were having problem with the sacrificial anode rod that is in the  water tank. The consumer gave the representative permission to pull the rod.  It was discovered that the rod was pitted and magnesium had gotten into the water line. 

Removing the rod did not change the condition of the hot water. The consumer uses well water. 

The consumer stated that she does not use the hot water in her home anymore.
justification: The consumer experienced hair loss and discoloration of eyelashes, indicating physical injury from contaminated water.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire dehumidifier model #FDL50S1 serial #KN90602955 with date code Feb 2009 manufactured by Gree.  There was a recall in 2013 for their dehumidifiers overheating and catching fire.  I called Gree on 9/12/13 and they said my dehumidifier was not part of the recall.  They gave me a reference #[REDACTED].  Last week I went down to my basement and smelled something burning.  It was the dehumidifier and it was smoking. When I tried to turn it off by the button on the unit it would not turn off.  I had to pull the plug out of the outlet to turn it off.  I called Gree today and told them what happened and she said the year 2009 dehumidifiers are not part of the recall, the recall only goes up to the year 2008.  I told her the same thing is happening with my dehumidifier as the ones already recalled, and she said she would have to send something to their other department and for me to call back in four weeks!  I think they need to put another recall out for year 2009 also!
justification: The dehumidifier was smoking and required unplugging to turn off, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On 9/5/15 the consumer used the saw to cut pieces of wood. The consumer cut 10 2x4 and 10 2x6 pieces of wood. While he was using the saw one of the screws that hold the safety guide in place came out and caused the safety guide to fall. The consumer reached to lift up the safety guide and the blade cut through the safety guard cutting the consumer's left thumb. The consumer was wearing gloves and the blade cut through the glove as well. The consumer did not seek medical attention. 

The consumer states he used the saw only 2 times prior to the incident.

There are no prior incidents.

The consumer plans to contact the firm. 

The consumer believes the saw is dangerous and should be recalled. The consumer is concerned since the saw was barely used.
justification: The consumer suffered a cut to the thumb, indicating an injury, but did not seek medical attention.

incident_description:
When I got this drillmaster 18 volt cordless 3/8" Drill/Driver out of my tool box to use, I felt the handle was hot.  I did not understand this.  I then began to use the drill/driver, unscrewed 1 screw with it and then I put the drill/driver down into my tool box again.  15 seconds later, the drill/driver was excessively smoking and I couldn't touch the handle due to the heat.  It was smoking, black and white smoke mixed together and had the smell of burning wires.  I managed to pull out the battery.  After pulling the battery out the drill/driver stopped smoking approximately 3 minutes later.  The handle of the drill is melted where the switch is located.

This drill/driver item number is 68239 from Harbor Freight Tools.
justification: The incident involved excessive smoking and heat, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The Pelonis Oil-Filled Radiator Heater, Model HO-0221 was plugged in before sleep to warm the bedroom.  UL Listed E190384.  It was unplugged in the middle of the night as the room was warmed.  In the morning, we noticed the plug was completely charred, melted to the point that one of the prongs remained in the outlet.  This is a frightening fire safety hazard, not only with regard to the charred remains but with regard to the potential to start an electrical fire.   

In looking up this product to see if it was previously recalled, I find that this UL Listed product is still on the market and has not been recalled.  Yet, I find that the very same manufacturer has had this problem before with the plug.  Why didn't the manufacturer and UL take extra care to ensure that the same problem didn't repeat itself?
justification: The incident involved a charred and melted plug, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

Upon examination, I realized that there were some broken copper wires inside of the wand and residue caused by heat and or scorching. Afterwards the vacuum was unusable due to the handle kept separating from the wand and not realizing why the inside appeared to be burnt, I felt that it was unsafe.

incident_description:
I had an Old Castle tempered glass shower door installed less than three years ago (16 CFR 1201 - I, II; ANSI Z97.1-2009; SGCC 3096; 5/3UA) and this morning (8/28/15) the small side panel of glass (approximately 10 inches X 6 ft) spontaneously shattered.  At approximately 6:30am this morning my wife was in our bedroom with our two small children and I was in our kitchen, no one was in or near the bathroom nor had been for several hours, when we heard a loud 'pop'.  When we went to investigate we found that the side panel of our shower enclosure had shattered.  The tempered glass shower door itself is still absolutely fine and un-shattered, only the side panel shattered.   Though still in place (not all over the floor), the side panel was shattered into a thousand tiny pieces.  I have pictures and video if you would like to see for verification.  Nothing comes into contact with that area of the glass enclosure and no one was around, near, or even in the same room when it shattered.  It spontaneously shattered.  I have contacted the manufacturer (Old Castle) regarding any warranty information.  When I called your 1-800 number a few minutes ago (apprx. 8:25am CST on 8/28/15), I spoke with an Oldcastle representative who said that sometimes tempered glass gets bubbles, maybe 1 in 100 pieces, and they have the potential to spontaneously break, but OldCastle offers no replacement or warranty.  It just happens sometimes and there's nothing that can be done.  I can't believe that is the official viewpoint of a company like OldCastle.  No one was hurt in this instance, but if anyone had been in the vicinity and the glass had fallen, it could have caused significant injury to myself, my wife, or my children.  I will also be contacting my installation contractor, At Ease Remodeling LLC, but I had hoped that the manufacturer would be more interested/responsive to this incident and the safety concern that it poses.  

Thank you,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved spontaneous shattering of a shower panel with no injuries, and the manufacturer's representative indicated such events are rare (1 in 100 pieces).

incident_description:

He had just finished his shower and was preparing to get out, he had not turned the water off but was opening the shower door when it exploded, cutting both of his hands, his left foot with the heel of the left foot receiving a deeper cut.
The glass went from inside and just outside the shower to the end of the six foot floor.
The caller states that the surprise of the incident causes him to believe that he was temporarily in shock and this is substantiated by his wife who returned to the home 45 minutes after the incident and stated that he appeared to her to be in a state of shock.
The consumer treated himself for the cuts and did not require a physician.
The caller has not contacted the manufacturer yet but does intend to contact them.
He is asking that the product involved in this incident be inspected and recalled with reimbursement as the remedy.
justification: The caller sustained cuts on both hands and his left foot, requiring self-treatment but no medical attention, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the specific and unusual nature of a shower door exploding.

incident_description: I have owned 2 husky electric powerwasher that I purchased at home depot over 5 years ago. I also own an gas powered by sears. The problem is with the lance on both the husky units. The lance has a red tip that is threaded but made of plastic unlike the gas powered one. I have used both units about 6 times each. The problem occurs when the machine builds up power that this red tip goes flying off. The tip and lance are made of cheap plastic that can't withstand the pressures that it is designed for and causes the unit to be just a garden hose. I contacted home depot who directed me to husky directly. I contacted husky and told me that the unit was past the 1 year warranty.  They offered to replace the lance for $30 with the same type but I refused to buy it stating that I knew for certainty that it would fail again . The problem occurred on both my units and rendered them uselesss. I was told that there was nothing more they could do .I told them they were selling a flawed and possibly dangerous unit. I was given additional info on the actual parts which I contacted via email to express my concern. I would like a complete refund and recall of the lance or replacement made of aluminum or metal and not some cheap plastic threading.

The consumerÃÂs wife and both his daughters have been experiencing frequent headaches. The consumerÃÂs wife has visited the physician and she has been advised to take headache pills. The consumerÃÂs daughters have not seen a physician. 

On 08/19/15 the consumer called the firm (800-HARDWOOD) and spoke with a rep (name unknown) about his concerns with his flooring. incident_description:
Initially purchased 3 of these units for the bedrooms in our newly purchased home. Noticed a wisp of smoke staining the wall from one of the units. Assumed it was a defect so replaced with a 4th unit. These units were less than 18 months old when a second one failed. Fortunately there was someone home to unplug the unit before our home burned down. I contacted Eco-Heater along with pictures and spoke with an "I don't give a damn" rep, [REDACTED]. All they wanted was:

1. Please provide the serial number of your heater. The serial number is located on the carton and on the rear of the switch junction box. 
2. Please provide a copy of your proof of purchase.
3. Please let us know which model you have

I could not provide a complete serial number since part of it was burned off. I could not immediately provide a proof of purchase as I was out of state for 4.5 months. And the model was an easy one. Within the first 3 emails, all they asked for were those 3 things above and they tried to take possession of the burnt heater in an attempt to take away the only evidence. I told them I would not be sending them the unit unless they repaired my wall. After 17 emails, they refused to repair the damage to my wall and offered to replace the 3 units instead. Why would I want to replace the units when 2 out of 4 caught on fire (1 was in the master bedroom and the other in my infants bedroom)? They gave me the run around and I can only assume they were hoping I could not provide a proof of purchase (the accountant at the business I purchased them from was kind enough to go back into their database and provide the original receipt and purchase order). They have stopped replying to my emails and my numerous requests to repair the damage to my wall (not even both, just the one that is burnt in the picture).

I'm sure their customer service is great for little things. But when it comes to accountability and the well being of others, they could care less. I brought up the request to repair my really burnt wall in every email but they refused to acknowledge that it was their unit that damaged my walls. Dishonest, no accountability, do not deal with this company!
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On Monday Oct 5, at approximately 8:15pm, I heard a violent sounding commotion coming from my laundry room. I yelled for my husband and ran to the room to find my brand new, 2 month old Samsung Activewash washing machine lying on its side, the lid completely blow off, the sides of the machine expanded outward, the internal drums now thrown behind the machine on the floor, the machine itself thrown across the room, and shards of metal and plastic lying everywhere, in addition to my floor being covered in water. The entire metal backing of the machine had flown off and was crumpled like paper, and water and flown out into the hallway floor and also floor to ceiling (8ft ceilings) on the wall diagonally across from the laundry room. Our dogs food and water stands are also located next to the washing machine, and they had been thrown about and flipped over as well. The garage door across from the washer is metal, and has multiple dents in it from the force of the metal and plastic shards exploding outward.

incident_description: Please help fix this potentially lethal Kohler Shower door (Model # R709062-L-SHP) hazard with either newer handles, protective covers, or better yet recall this shower door. I am going to notify the CPSC and regret buying/installing this Kohler shower door. Shameful of Kohler...frequently putting profits  over customer safety. I can live with my recent painful experience installing this defective door but when my family member also gets hurt I take this personally and will NOT let it pass quietly! Shame on you Kohler!  I have pictures clearly explaining the dangers of this shower door but basically, there are numerous sharp corner edges on either side of this shower door which pose a immediate safety hazard to all owners of this shower door.  The tub/shower area is already a hazard for senior citizens but is made worse with this shower door which I just installed as part of a bathroom renovation.  during installation by my contractor he mentioned these new shower doors had extremely sharp edges posing a serious safety hazard to people who bath or shower.  I have already been injured cleaning this door and while painful it has reoccurred again for family members.  I can clearly provide picture which will help...please advise if I can send them to assist with my concern

incident_description:
I plugged the converter into a European wall outlet (240VAC). I then plugged a USA surge-suppressor power strip into the converter's 110VAC outlet. (Note: As the converter's outlet was for 2-pronged plugs, I put a plug adaptor on the power strip's 3-prong, grounded plug.) Immediately after I flipped the power strip's switch to "on" there was a bright blue flash and a "poof" sound. The circuit breaker protecting that European outlet had tripped, apparently by my actions. The converter's internal fuse was not blown. I suspected that the power strip had been damaged, so I discarded it.

I acknowledge possible user-error. However, Samsonite should provide warnings to preclude such configurations. In my opinion, the converter's internal fuse should have blown first, preventing possible harm to the user/equipment/electrical supply. That the circuit breaker tripped first seems to indicate existence of some electrical sneak path that effectively shorted the outlet.
justification: The incident involved a bright blue flash and a tripped circuit breaker, but no injury or harm occurred.

incident_description:
Wiring that was used to install electric baseboard heaters and thermostats has both a soft coating on the wires and
on the outside cover shield. Today, Aug. 26,2015, I was cleaning my basement when I touched the two main boxes
installed for the division of the heaters and got shocked. I measured the current and found that it had 124 volts on
the outside of the metal box. I loosened the wire from the holder and it showed exposed copper. The metal clamp
holding the wire had squeezed through the outside plastic/rubber covering and also through the wire allowing 124
volts into the metal junction box. In 2010, I had a similar problem. I am enclosing a copy of my letter to Mr. [REDACTED], an employee of Southwire Company who handled my complaint then and decided there was not an issue
with the wire in question. I also called them today, got an answering machine and left a message. I have not heard
back yet. I found another wire in the other box beside it that appears to have been arcing. If you are wondering why

incident_description:
The Maytag Bravos XL electric dryer, model # MEDB880BW, electric heating element failed and fused itself to the frame of the dryer, meaning the body of the dryer became a 240 volt potential instead of a 0 volt potential and was an electrocution hazard. Instead of failing outright, the dryer continued to function in this condition for months meaning the risk of shock or electrocution was present each time the dryer was used.

The failure of heating element was cleary due to a manufacurting defect. The lead wire of the heating element had everal "crimp" marks on the pieces which were recovered from the failed component, and it is clear that when the heating element was hot, normal expansion of the wire caused the lead end to separate at one of these crimped locations. See attached letter which I sent to both Maytag and Sears about the problem.

Fortunately, no one was injured.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous condition (electrocution risk) but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the manufacturing defect and prolonged exposure.

incident_description: The glass on our Heat-N-Glo gas fireplace, Model # SL-750TR-C, shattered for no apparent cause.  The fireplace has a continuous pilot light; however, the unit was not in use nor did the glass shatter when the unit was turned on; it happened without warning and without anything being done to the unit or near the unit.  We only use the unit around 4-5 times per year because of the amount of gas it burns; it was not an option when our home was built by the developer.  However, I have closely followed all recommendations in the unit's Owner's Guide with keeping it cleaned and inspecting the vent.  Although the glass remained intact, no shard was larger than approx. 1/2" in two dimensions, the broken glass showered from the frame with a slight nudge.  I contacted the manufacturer and although they were very cordial, there was no explanation provided.  I was given two recommendations:  purchase a replacement glass assembly ($250) and have the unit inspected by a service representative working for one of their approved vendors ($145).  I have no explanation for what I consider to be two serious safety issues:  broken glass and an open unprotected flame with the possibility of broken glass falling inward to extinguish the flame = gas leak.  What would have happened had no one been at home?  Instead of the manufacturer expressing enough concern to at least investigate why their product failed; I must pay to make certain their product functions in a safe manner.

incident_description:
I have a residential gas water heater Low Nox emissions, Model PG38T09AXK00, made by Rheem/GE.
Purchased 2011. Since 2014 we have had problems with keeping the pilot lit.  A plumber replaced the thermocouple in 2014.  This did not fix the problem.  We continue to have "pre ignition" with a very hot flash of hot burning natural gas within the heater which blows out the pilot light.  On 9/26/15 we had a small EXPLOSION at the water heater.  This time it could be heard all over the house and upon going to the heater we found it "surging" gas, sounding all the world like a blow torch. Flames could be seen via the pilot view hole, the area around the burner is burnt. I have pictures.

 I shut it off, let it rest and then relit it and it is working fine so far.  

I feel this is a extremely dangerous situation.  If sufficient gas builds up in the heater before ignition I could have a very bad explosion and resulting fire could destroy my home and possible kill someone.

I contacted Rheem about the problem and they seemed to think that it is "no big deal".  Hire a plumber to get it fixed.  They could not recommend any plumber in my area, so I am at the mercy of whatever predatory plumbers out there.

I feel this should be addressed as someone, somewhere is going to die because of a this faulty water heater.
justification: The incident involved a small explosion and ongoing dangerous conditions, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have an LG gas dryer. the dryer does not function properly. It is a major safety hazard. In many situation the danger of this dryer may go un noticed. If functioning; when the flame on the dryer goes out or fails to ignite the gas valves on the unit should close automatically. In this case the dryer does not close the gas valves, instead it continues to pump gas into the fire tube even though there is no flame. This is not brief, it will actually continue to pump raw un-burned natural gas into the unit for however long the dryer cycle is set for. In the beginning of my statement i mentioned that this can go un-noticed. Here is how. 

1) if the flame does not go out no one will ever know that the safety shut off is not functioning.
2) the dryer is generally vented to outside the house and if vented properly the gasses will simply flow out of the house almost un-detectected, that does not mean that it not present incredible danger. For instance if there was an ignition source by the dryer vent it would surely ignite. If something was to block the vent it would fill the house with deadly gas. I am sure you can use your imagination. 

LG has several other models with similar issues where the unit keeps pumping fuel with the fire lit after the cycle is finish I am sure if you researched it you would find the same parts exist.

my dryer is an LG TROM
 model # is DLG7188rm
S/N 701KWRE02814
justification: The dryer's failure to close gas valves when the flame goes out poses a significant risk of gas accumulation, which could lead to explosions or poisoning, potentially causing death.

It was ordered from Amazon, July 02, 20125 and received July 06, 2015, unpacked, plugged in, and I set humidity level to 45%. The unit worked flawlessly until today, September 13, 2015, when this exact unit, Frigidaire Serial Number, KN50700665, appears to have experienced an electronic control failure accompanied by a mechanical failure, of some kind. Operating for several hours today, around 5:30 p.m., Sunday, September, 13, 2015, it suddenly began making a loud, low frequency, drumming kind of sound. I immediately investigated and discovered the unit's fan was no longer operating, the display read 30% instead of the 45% it was set for and it could not be turned off. The On-Off switch was unresponsive despite being pressed repeatedly. The unit continued making the noise described above and began to smell like it was overheating and very hot. The filter was perfectly clean and was not a contributor. The bucket was virtually empty and not a contributor. The only way to turn it off was to unplug it. The back panel of the unit felt hot and the entire unit smelled hot. The back panel is easily removed by loosening 7, highly visible, chrome plated, Phillips screws and simply lifting it off. I removed the back panel and the interior was spotlessly clean but the compressor was extremely hot, too hot to even lightly touch. I stood the unit up and let it cool down for about 15 minutes, then replaced the rear cover and all of it's screws, plugged it back in and pressed the On/Off switch. The unit immediately started up and operation was normal for approximately one minute when the display again reverted from the preset 45% to 30%, the exhaust fan again coasted to a stop, the loud, low frequency drumming sound returned and the On/Off switch was again inoperative and again it was not possible to switch the unit to an Off condition with the On/Off switch. This dehumidifier had electrically and mechanically, locked itself up in a way it could not be turned off, reset, or stopped, without unplugging it and the sound it was making is consistent with a motor driven mechanical device that has mechanically failed but the motor is still trying to drive it. Because the On/Off switch was again inoperative, I had to again unplug the unit to shut it down and it again smelled like it was overheating and excessively hot. I checked the exhaust fan for freedom of movement and it spun very freely when I used a small stick to move the squirrel cage, accessing it from the grill opening on the top of the machine, thus eliminating the fan as a potential source of the problem. 

We had received a rebate for a prior Frigidaire dehumidifier recalled by the Consumer Product Safety Division for causing several fires and were informed the unit had been redesigned and was no longer a fire hazard, so we used the rebate to purchase this replacement. However, the same fire hazard condition appears to still exist. If we had not been home to unplug the unit when it overheated from an obvious electronic and mechanical failure, I am 100% confident it had every potential to set itself on fire and potentially burn the house down. I have now completely lost confidence in the Chinese manufactured Frigidaire brand of dehumidifiers labeled as Frigidaire and sold by Electrolux, believing the unit we currently have to again be a serious fire hazard and a threat to occupant safety, not to mention property damage with the potential for catastrophic loss. In my opinion, based on real life experiences with these Frigidaire dehumidifiers, these units are a fire hazard, a threat to family/public safety, and should be removed from the market place.
justification: The dehumidifier experienced a mechanical and electronic failure, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

Despite this defect/flaw the dryer should no Error code (Trouble code as we call it in the automotive world) and the dryer continued to operate and operate at excessive temperatures! This in my mind put my family at risk for a fire and or shock hazard. 
There is no way in my mind that this dryer should have continued to operate without a warning or thrown a circuit to stop this dryer.
I took the pictures to my local Fire Department H/Q in Londonderry, NH and there the battalion chief was equally shocked (no pun intended) about this device being melted and suggested that I report to the manufacture and Consumer Product Safety Commission.
justification: The incident involved a significant defect (melted electronic module) that posed a fire and shock hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Product: LG Dryer Model number DLGX2802W

A few months ago my wife noticed a gas smell/odor coming from the dryer after drying clothes. The dryer operates normally yet seems to be leaking gas. We requested that the gas company inspect the dryer and gas lines to ensure there are no leaks in the line or connection. The technician verified that the lines and connections are fine but that there is something wrong with the dryer. He tagged the appliance as a safety/fire hazard and rendered it inoperable until fully repaired. He recommended contacting LG directly to inform them there is a safety/fire hazard issue. And he also recommended getting our dryer duct cleaned.  We did have our dryer duct cleaned however the gas odor persists.

I contacted LG about this today (Case # [REDACTED]) and they are unwilling to take any action on behalf of the consumer. They kept referring back to the point that the unit is out of the 1 year warranty period (I bought this 5-6 years ago) and that it is now my responsibility. I pointed out many times that this is not a warranty issue and is a major safety issue and fire hazard, yet LG continually ignored this and responded with the typical "it's outside the warranty period" response. All they could offer was providing a list of authorized dealers who could come out and look at the appliance at my own cost and that it was ultimately my responsibility.

Furthermore, I am not the only one who has experienced this issue:
http://forum.appliancepartspros.com/dryer-repair/29971-lg-gas-dryer-heats-but-smell-gas-after-heat-cycle.html

LG supervisors stated that they have to get a certain number of calls about a particular issue before issuing a recall. While I understand that metrics are involved, that should never override the potential of a serious issue that may cause disaster and harm. This issue is particularly dangerous because there are likely many customers who may either not notice this issue or if they do, may think it's completely normal. 

LG is blatantly ignoring this issue and should be held liable for their neglect should any future incidents occur, leading to damage, injury or death. As mentioned, this is not the kind of issue that may be particularly noticeable to many people, or even if it is many may not actually do anything about it because the dryer works and dries clothes. But there is an eminent danger and LG should be prompted to re-evaluate and address this issue.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak in a dryer, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has been reported yet.
