incident_description: I did not know about the recall.  I purchased 3 of these units and gave 2 of them as Christmas presents to my children.  I just today needed mine, so I plugged it in to charge it about 2 pm today.  I noticed it hadn't charged at 5 pm, but just thought it needed 24 hours.  While back in my bedroom, I heard a popping noise in the kitchen around 9 pm.  I went out there and the unit was on fire.  The flames had also caught some papers on fire.  I used a fire extinguisher on it.  My counter top has a burn spot on it, and some recipes, dishes, and papers were lost, but fortunately that is all.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the described scenario of a recalled product causing a fire.

incident_description:
June 6th, 2015 this caller was home when a repair tech from the electric company knocked on her door and advised her that her smart meter was about to catch fire and it was due to her wiring.

(She had an electrician at her own expense to check the wiring of her home ten years prior to this time because she was having problems with so many appliances and the electric company said it was her wiring but inspection by the electrician then proved that  her wiring was excellent.)

The tech from the electric company knocked on her door a second time and advised the caller that he tightened too tightly and had broken the bolts to connect the meter to her house.

She was informed that she would have to wait until a new smart meter to be brought out and connected.

She is reporting this incident because the smart meter was overheating and could present a fire hazard.

She lives in a wooded area in a wooden home.

There are no injuries being reported.

She was contacted by [REDACTED] from Talquin Electric on June 18th, 2015 and she states that he spoke with her as if she was a nut.

The Smart Meter 530x Flex Net Icon sensus meter has arcing problems.  Several people have died as a result of this model of smart meter due to fires.  They are defective & have arcing problems.

Talquin Electric is not regulated by the Florida Public Utility Commission.  They are a co-op & received federal money for this project.  People in Talquin should not be endangered by their smart meters.  June 18 Mr. [REDACTED told the caller she could replace with old fashioned meters but it would cost $40.00 (forty dollars) per month extra.  That's extortion!

The meters have been banned in many states across the country, Australia, Canada.  There is a class action starting against them in FL but due to Talquin being a co-op they cannot fall under Florida Public Utility perview.

Please assist.  If the caller's home catches on fire from outside she will be dead before fire alarm goes off.

Please research this meter.  A gentleman was "laid off" from Sensua, an Engineer, for not continuing to look the other way.
Truly yours,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard from a defective smart meter, but no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated the burner cleaner when his spouse used it causing her to become ill.  Symptoms included hoarseness, respiratory problems etc.  7/16 Caller stated that his wife received medical attention from her physician, and was informed that the chemicals she inhaled caused her to receive burns to her throat.  The victim was treated and sent home.

Caller stated that the company was contacted about the incident and he was informed that he would be sent the chemical information through the mail.  He inquired of the representative why there was no label on the container to indicate the chemicals and the dangers they posed.  He was advised that the company does not have to display that information.

Caller feels that the oven cleaner is a health hazard and should be reported.

This product has left the caller's wife with a voice very horse
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burns to the throat and respiratory problems) requiring medical attention, but no death occurred.

incident_description: Using step stool on top step easily rolls owner an fell bruised back. Ladders to to narrow at base rolls over. Plastic feet do not level as well, air space between feet and floor. Very dangerous design.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruised back, indicating an injury, and the description highlights a dangerous design that makes such incidents likely.

incident_description: My wife plugged the Ipad 3 wall charger into her Ipad 3 a couple of evenings ago as she has done before, and when she returned the connector that connects to the Ipad 3 port had begun to melt and was very hot.  There was also a burning smell in the room.  I still have the cable.  The Ipad 3 doesn't appear to have been damaged because we caught it in time.  If this had been charging overnight, the damage would probably have been much worse.  Nothing was done differently in charging the Ipad 3 this time versus other times.  A different charger seems to be working fine so far for charging it, although much slower as it is a Iphone charger and apparently charges slower.
justification: The charger melted and produced a burning smell, but no injury or damage occurred as it was caught in time.

incident_description:
We have a one year old Samsung top-load washing machine with a 5.0 cubic foot capacity.

We began a load of laundry before going to bed. As the washing machine entered the spin cycle, the entire machine exploded and burst into pieces. The entire top of the unit separated and flew into our hallway, and the unit continued to spin violently around the laundry room, ripping holes in our walls, dryer, cabinets, flooring, etc. 

If we had not been home, I'm not sure how long this would have continued.

Shards of metal and large peices of plastic were lodged in the walls and hurled into other rooms of the home with great force.

A quick search of YouTube indicates that this same incident has happened to several other consumers. If we had been in the room or even in our hallway at the time of the explosion, it is very likely that we would have been seriously injured or killed.

I have photos that I can send.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and posed a serious risk of injury or death, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description:
At 0400 on 30 March 2015, my wife and I awoke to a the loud sound of shattering glass.  We got up, turned on the bathroom light and found that one of the glass doors on the Kohler (Fluence 44-in to 47-in W x 70 in H Brushed Nickel Sliding Shower Door) had shatter into  thousands of little 1/4" pieces.  This door was purchased at the Lowe's Store in Clay, New York on 3 October 2012 and installed within a few days of the purchase.

As directed by the Lowe's Customer Service Representative, I contacted Kohler and asked about the doors.  I was told the door was out of warranty and had to pay $98.90 to get a replacement door.

Based on what I have read on this spontaneous shattering of these doors for what was referred to as "Micro Flaws" during the manufacture process for a variety of shower door models sold by Kohler, some of which have been recalled (except for the model I purchased), something does not seem right that a consumer has to pay for a replacement door for something that known to have a problem.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous shattering of a shower door with no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3, as the issue is known but not widespread for this specific model.

incident_description: Today, I noticed the smell of smoke in my house, and I traced it down to my basement. When I entered my basement, I found it heavily engulfed in smoke. I was able to trace the smoke back to our dehumidifier, which we purchased from Sears approximately 4 years ago. It has been 12 hours and we are still running fans to empty the smoke from the basement. I am extremely agitated that it would break in such a manner as to cause harm to myself and my family. If we werent home, the house would have burned down.    It is a Kenmore Elite Dehumidifier Model Number 42-99701. Thank you and we would appreciate a response.
justification: The incident involved heavy smoke but no injury or death, and the likelihood of such an event is possible given the description.

incident_description: I have used Dawn dishwashing liquid for years! Now I can't use it because it contains Methylisothiazolinone. I have developed a severe allergy to this preservative. My hands and arms break out in small blister-like bumps that are very itchy. Eventually they dry up and leave my skin peeling and flaky. The dry skin then cracks and I have sores. Each time I am exposed to this chemical the reaction gets worse and the healing time takes longer. At first it only was on my hands, then included my wrists. Now it goes up to my elbows! It is painful and itchy! It makes my life miserable. I am terrified of a new outbreak. I have stopped using Dawn, but so many products have it, it is almost impossible to avoid it.
justification: The description details a severe allergic reaction causing injury (itchy, painful blisters and sores), and the likelihood is high as exposure to the chemical is common in many products.

incident_description:
Saturday, August 30, 2015 at about 10:00am, I began painting on my house. I had a bucket and brush in one hand and used the other hand to climb the ladder. When I reached half way up, the rung located next to the middle hinge, pulled out of the frame. The resulting twisting motion caused the frame to tear and rip, causing the ladder to collapse with me on it.
   The nature of the damage resulted in my dropping straight down and landing on my feet. I stumbled off to the side, bucket sloshing but still in hand. 
   The only injury appears to be a soreness in one ankle that disappeared by the next day.
   There were no indications, beforehand, that the ladder rung would pull loose.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (sore ankle) that resolved quickly, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since there were no prior indications of ladder failure.

incident_description:
1. My sister was renting my condo from May 2013 to August 2014. During that time, a ceiling mounted track lighting fixture with four lights "blew up". She also reported having repeated electrical problems with kitchen outlets not working.  No irregular use. No Injuries.
2. I moved into my condo in August 2014. I also experienced kitchen outlets not working. Also my FPE box has loose circuit breakers. One of them was so loose, that when turned back on, the outlets connected to that circuit, remained dead for several minutes. The FPE box would cause that circuit to fail. I therefore replaced my panel box in June 2015.
justification: The incident involved electrical issues and a lighting fixture failure, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Was transporting 8 - 40 lb. bags of water softener salt, when I went down two stairs the wheel shattered. Fortunately, I wasn't hurt but could have been.
justification: The wheel shattered during transport, but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: When power button was pressed to turn of the tool, the tool failed to turn off. The rotary engine began spinning at a greater rate of speed than under normal operation. Device continued out of control unitl parts began to rattle around inside the case. The case then began to heat uo rapidly and spew smoke. When the device had finally burned up and stopped spinning, I attempted to pick it up and began spinning again.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning tool that caused smoke and overheating but no reported injury.

incident_description:
We have an Kohler acrylic shower base, Archer model (K-9397-**).  The center shower drain is covered by an acrylic plate, roughly 8 inched by 10 inches (part number 1062356**).  The cover plate is held down by two small suction cups.  The cover plate must be periodically removed for cleaning the drain and over time the suction cups can break free from the cover plate.  The best demonstration of this can be seen on the You Tube video EzQd9wC2vT4.

A week ago my wife stepped on the cover plate while exiting the shower.  The plate came loose and her foot went into the drain hole, causing her to fall.  Fortunately the glass shower door was open and she did not fall through it.  She did however suffer multiple bruises and an injured knee that required a trip to the emergency room.  

I reported this event to Kohler.  I suspect that they know that the cover plate needs more robust suction cups because they replaced the plate at no charge even though it was out of warranty.  This is a disaster waiting to happen
justification: The incident resulted in multiple bruises and an injured knee requiring emergency room care, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the design flaw with the suction cups and the fact that the plate must be periodically removed, increasing the chance of failure.

incident_description: My home has light switches with Bar Code UPC 85007 66013. Has 660-WG on label below UPC.  So far every light switch I have checked are broken and it is not from installation.  My home was built in 2000.  This is a serious safety concern, after fining a light still on when it was switched off due to arching.  Thankfully, I was home at the time or my home could have burned down.
justification: The incident describes a serious safety concern with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: my glass tempered sink shattered on its own..
justification: The sink shattered on its own, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: product turned on by itself, and regularly over-heats in use.
justification: The product turning on by itself and overheating is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Sometime after April 2015, I was going to do some homework on my Dell Inspiron Lab Top and went to plug in my power supply to the wall and felt an electric shock near my palm. I had quickly notified my dad about this and he instantly came over to look at what I was shocked from. He had noticed that the copper wires were exposed on the male plug end of my power supply; the end that you would plug into the 120 volt residential receptacle. At that point my dad had to locate the circuit breaker to shut off the power. He then removed the plug from the wall and noticed the insulation over the copper wires where they meet the male plug end of my power supply, the insulation was cracked allowing the bare copper wire meaning the hot and neutral wire were exposed without any protection. My dad told me to no longer use that cord; I told him that I had to finish my work, which at that time he had an older lab top that he was not using, therefore we swapped out that part of the power supply. My dad had said to contact Dell to see if there is an exchange or warranty being that the item itself is only 2years old. My sister and I received our lab tops as graduation gifts around September 2012 but Dell tells us they are out of warranty to just buy new ones. My sister too, we found a crack in the insulation on her power supply also on the 120 volt side. My sister is currently using one of my mom's old cords that appear to be much heavier as I am using one of my dad's. My main complaint here is my sister's and my lab top computer and power supply's were received on around September 2012 and here my incident occurred on March 2015 but currently our units are only about 3 years old and now I am using my dad's 10 year old cord, we have a 15 year old vacuum and a 20 year old iron all that the cords are in perfect shape no breaks or cracks nothing. I personally cannot believe that no one else has had this problem with the very light gauge wire and what appears to be minimal insulation on our damaged cords. Dell should at least make a replacement cord available because my power supply works just fine. The inlet voltage side of the power supply that cord is removable. It has a male on one end and female on the other similar to an extension cord.  My most serious concern is that I was shocked from the cord and is worried that someone younger than me may carelessly get electrocuted. My sister and I are 20 something twin college students and take very good care of our belongings.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock due to exposed wires, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My Kenmore Elite washing machine exploded.  During the spin cycle, there was a catastrophic failure of the attachment between the top and the base. The top flew off (staying connected only by a few hoses) and the entire machine continued to spin around, banging into and damaging the wall and the dryer.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description: We purchased and installed a shower door from Lowe's in Jackson, MI in April of 2013.  July 3, 2015 one of our house guest was showering, we heard a loud CRASH and he was standing and bleeding in a pile of glass.  I blamed him for "slamming the door too hard".  He stuck to his story that he barely touched it and it just broke. I didn't believe him.  Well, this past weekend on 8/23/15 a little 10 year old girl was using the new replacement shower and we heard a CRASH and then her screaming at the top of her lungs.  Another exploding shower door.  She was also bleeding with glass in her hair and cuts from head to toe.  It was then I realized it was a faulty door or bad design.  I find it hard to believe a 10 year old girl could fling it open to the point it breaks all over her.  I apologized to the young man who broke the first one and told him I was going to call Lowe's.  Lowe's in Jackson, MI initially told me they will NOT refund me for either door nor will they accept any responsibility. I just got a call that they are "working on a refund".  I requested (on the first call) they pull the doors off the floor and quit selling them and he said we were the only complaint, so I'm sure they will continue to sell them.  These doors are a HAZARD.  Unfortunately, we did not get any pictures of the 2 incidents because, quite honestly, we were in EMERGENCY MODE and taking pictures was never on our minds.  We are very fortunate both victims didn't end up in the ER since both were covered in cuts.  Something needs to be done.  Please help or advise.  [REDACTED] in Brooklyn, Michigan
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to two individuals, including a 10-year-old girl with cuts from head to toe, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of the incident with similar outcomes suggests an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
(09/2011)The consumer stated that the unit was plugged into the outlet in the bathroom. The unit had been in the outlet for about a month. The consumer stated that her sister was out at the barn. She heard the fire alarm go off on the inside of the house. Her sister called the fire department. They came and put the fire out. No one was in the house at the time. The house was completely burned down.

The consumer's sister was advised by the fire department that the heat from oil in the plug-in unit short circuited the wires in outlet.
justification: The house was completely burned down, but no one was injured or killed.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern:

We received the enclosed electric drill as a consumer complaint. The drill was purchased at Harbor Freight Tools, Salem Oregon. The drill was used approx. 6-8 times over a six month period.

As you can see the obvious reason we are sending it to your attention.

The consumer stated that he had used the drill the night before and in the morning he stated there was a foul burning smell emitting from the battery and the drill itÃÂs self-had begun to melt. The drill was located on the battery pack; however it was not plugged into the wall.

Thank You

---------------------------------------------------------

Drill was purchased approx.4-6 month ago at Harbor Freight Tool in Salem Oregon.

I believe I paid somewhere around 25.00 for it.

Used it again on May 27th. On May 28th my wife ask what was wrong with the drill as it
appeared to have melted. The battery charger was emitting a powerful burning smell. The
power pack was not plugged in to the wall outlet but the drill was on the battery pack
overnight.

I feel this could have been a health hazard and possible could have started a fire if it had gone unnoticed.
justification: The drill emitted a burning smell and began to melt, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Craftsman air compressor model# 921.164710 purchased in late 2011. The motor caught fire during operation, had to be put out with a fire extinguisher.
justification: The motor caught fire, requiring a fire extinguisher, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I recently purchased Hunter brand ceiling fans from my local Lowe's store and after installation, the product is emitting a smoky/electrical smell/odor whenever the fan is turned on. This odor is making my pregnant wife and I dizzy and we fear there may be health hazards. I called Hunter's customer support line and the gentleman on the phone told me that they get this call often. Their recommendation is to run the fan on high for 24 hours to "burn off" the chemical used to "seal the motor." This is very concerning because there is a definite physiological effect on humans from exposure to this chemical as it is "burned off." I worry about neurological damage or long-term side effects.
justification: The incident involves a physiological effect (dizziness) on humans due to exposure to chemicals, indicating an injury-level severity. The occurrence likelihood is high as the issue is reportedly common per customer support.

incident_description: After a shower, when opening the door, it suddenly shattered. There was no visible damage to the glass prior to this occurance.
justification: The glass shattered unexpectedly, which could potentially cause injury if someone was nearby.

incident_description:
The consumer states that the fan has 3 blades that can separate from motor assembly and fly off. The consumer states that the product is really dangerous.

The plastic assembly holding the fan blades to the spindle of the motor breaks off. This allows the blades to go flying off. 

The consumer had the fan on high. All blades separated from the spindle when the plastic assembly broke in half. The blades flew around in the cage of the fan. One of the fan blades almost came out of the cage. 

The consumer contacted the customer service of the retailer about the incident. They were unable to assist the consumer.

The consumer will go into the store where he purchased the product.
justification: The incident involved fan blades separating and flying off, posing a danger, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On 07/22/15 the consumer used the product to clean a bathroom sink in her recreational vehicle (RV), located at [REDACTED]. The consumer states it took her about 2 minutes to clean the sink. The consumer did not use gloves. 
On 07/24/15 the consumer noticed that her skin on both hands was peeling.  

On 07/27/15 the consumer called the firm (800-448-5281) to inform them of the incident. The consumer spoke with a rep (name unknown) and was transferred to the Biotech Lab Poison Control Center. The consumer was told by a female rep (name unknown) to visit a physician for treatment and she would call the consumer back within a few days to follow up (case # [REDACTED]). The consumer was also given the number to the firm's consumer affairs dept but when she called the number it was incorrect. The consumer called the firm back and was transferred to the consumer affairs dept. The consumer spoke with a male rep (name unknown) and she expressed her safety concerns. The consumer was told that her concerns would be discussed in their next meeting. 

On 07/27/15 the consumer went to her primary care physician, Dr. [REDACTED]. and was told that she had chemical burns on both her hands. The consumer was prescribed medication to apply to her hands and treat her burns.

The consumer states the product did not have a strong chemical odor and on the bottle it did not indicate to avoid contact with skin. The consumer believes the bottle should have a label to clearly warn consumers about using protective gear. 

The consumer states she has used other cleaning products without gloves and has never had chemical burns. This is the first time the consumer used this product.
justification: The consumer suffered chemical burns requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that when he walked down in the basement, he noticed that the dehumidifier was running when he had shut it off. The unit was plugged in but the power was not on. The consumer stated that none of the indicator lights were on. The consumer stated that the compressor was running but does not remember if the fan was running.

The consumer stated that when he pushed the power button, instantly, heavy amount of smoke (dark colored) started emitting from fan vent on top of the unit. The consumer stated that there was an electrical burning smell to the smoke. 

The consumer pulled out the power cord and moved the unit to the outside of the house. 

The consumer's unit does not appear to be under any recalls.
justification: The incident involved smoke and an electrical burning smell, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the unit is not under recall and the issue was isolated.

incident_description: I recently purchased a Holmes 31" Tower fan from Target. After assembling the fan per the instructions, I noticed it was very unstable on its base. For lack of a better term, it wobbled badly. I tested the fan at all of its speeds and the wobble seemed to get worse. When I had the fan on its highest speed and activated the oscillation feature the fan tipped over when the fan pointed towards the near wall. I believe it was the air bouncing of the wall back at the fan that tipped it over. Of course, if it had a sturdy safe base and didn't wobble precariously this wouldn't have happened. I contacted the manufacturer of the fan and they are doing everything they can to discourage my reporting this issue.
justification: The fan tipped over due to instability, but no injury was reported, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: In 2012 we requested service on our HeatNGlo GEM 36 gas fireplace.  The technician found a single crack in the ceramic surround enclosure.  We asked at that point to have it replaced.  We were assured the crack was normal and it was no problem to continue using the fireplace.  In 2015 my wife began having headaches when using the fireplace.  We shined a flashlight in to the fireplace and found the crack has "spider webbed" everywhere on the top, sides and back of the ceramic enclosure.  We immediately visited the local HeatNGlo distributor and requested a visit.  They came the next day took some pictures and stated the fireplace probably needed to be condemned, but that they needed to confirm this with the factory.  The factory emailed and stated there was a patch kit to solve the problem.  We took more pictures, forwarded these to the local distributor (Groth Gates Inc.) and the HeatNGlo rep. along with several questions concerning the patch kit and application.  We then received an email stating the damage was beyond repair and not covered by warranty.  This unit has become very dangerous and unsafe.  This began within the warranty period, but we were lied to about this problem.  We have since found out from another distributor in Salem Oregon that they have had a number of customer with the same issue and the response has been the same from HeatNGlo.
justification: The incident resulted in headaches (injury) due to a cracked ceramic enclosure in the fireplace, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as multiple customers reported similar issues.

incident_description:
In October of 2014 purchased Andersen model 3000 storm door. I had it installed professionally by contractor for Home Depot from whom I purchased the door. Unfortunately, although installed correctly, the door slams shut with such force and so quickly that guests and family members have been hit on the back of the leg and or ankle causing severe bruises...fortunately no medical attention has been needed so far. This is a significantly heavy storm door and it slams to within a foot and a half or less of the door jamb before the 2 pneumatic cylinders stop the door and then slowly close it. This does not allow enough space or time for the person entering to do so without getting hit on the legs by the door.

In researching this situation on the internet I have found quite a few purchasers of Andersen storm doors have the same complaint. My opinion is that Andersen is trying to avoid having to design a different pneumatic closure which stops the slamming of the door further away from the door jamb giving the person entering the space and time necessary to enter safely.

Other then this situation the door itself seems to be well made and I prefer to find a way to overcome the stated problem but my contact with the manufacturer to date has been to no avail. They state that the door is working normally...even though injury to people entering is a destiny possibility.

I would welcome further contact from Andersen to find a way to remedy the situation.
justification: Severe bruises have been reported, but no medical attention was needed, indicating an injury without serious consequences. The issue is common among users, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: My husband and I awoke to a crash at 1:30 a.m.  When we went into the bathroom, we saw that one of the Kohler Fluence sliding glass doors had spontaneously shattered.  Glass was everywhere.  Pieces of the door were still in the railing at the bottom of the slide so the door didn't fall; it just shattered in place.  The shower hadn't been used in a couple of days, it was only two years old, and was typically used only 3-4 times a week.  Thank God everyone was asleep when this happened or someone could have been seriously injured by the shattering glass.
justification: The glass door shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I was using my Ryobi SA 1802 drill when I noticed an odor coming from the drill, I looked at the drill while it was in use and observed sparks inside the handle (through the vented area), followed within a few seconds by smoke coming from the motor area of the drill.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the drill, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: yes I brought a Hamilton beach iron less than a year ago.model number-142104-series-A0721DA.AND THE RETRACTABLE CORD HAS A SHORTAGE IN IT. PLEASE HELP.I WOULD LIKE TO TAKE BACK TO KMART FOR A FULL REFUND.
justification: The incident involves a retractable cord shortage in an iron, which poses a potential hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
on 2/2015 I purchased a white space heater from rite aid in Sebastopol, California.  I took the first
one back  because of a humming noise.    I exchanged it for the same model and type a few days later.   The 2nd on made a humming noise.    On 3/30/2015 I woke up to find the optimus space heater  on fire..   the fire quickly spread to engulf my entire  RV in flames.    The fire  ruined my life,
damaged my car and caused  damages to both my  neighbors  trailers.   I have filed  complaint
with  the  rite aid in Sebastopol  and  sent  pictures of my burned rv to  optimus ent.  I Have yet to 
receive any type of  recognition or  settlement  from  Optimus.    The  fire left   homeless and
I lost my job to this incident.    I have had to seek  medical  care  and psychological  care.   I still
have  no  compensation for this  needless  and  undeserved   way  of  life.

please  help
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage, homelessness, job loss, and required medical and psychological care, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that they had noticed burning/smokey odor in the last couple of weeks.

The consumer went down to his basement and noticed some smoke. The consumer touched the dehumidifier unit and felt that it was really hot. He turned off the unit.

The consumer took out the water bucket and saw faint white smoke being emitted. The consumer stated that all of the plastic around the condensing unit/motor had come down and melted. 

The consumer unplugged the unit. 

The consumer contacted SoleusAir the same day that he discovered the issue. They had a recording asking to contact Gree. The consumer spoke to a representative at Gree and filed a claim [REDACTED]. The representative informed the consumer that his unit is not recalled (under recall #14-179). The consumer was informed that his claim will be sent to their review board and someone will contact him in a week. The consumer stated that it has been over two weeks and he has not heard from Gree yet.

The consumer called Gree again on  07/23/15 and provided the claim # to the representative. The representative informed him that his unit is not recalled so there was nothing they could do in this case. She informed the consumer to call SoleusAir back and deal with them regarding the incident.

The consumer contacted SoleusAir on 07/23/15. They informed him that they do not deal with Gree anymore and that he should contact Gree for this matter since they manufactured the unit.

The consumer has not been able to receive assistance from either SoleusAir or Gree in this matter.
justification: The incident involved a burning/smokey odor and melted plastic, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: During annual fire extinguisher training we are required to put out a controlled fire. I pulled pin and gave a short burst of extinguisher, I then proceeded to approach base of fire and attempted to discharge the remainder of bottle but nothing happened. Squeezing the handle did nothing, it appears the valve is stuck. I had fire fighter personal try also and nothing.
justification: The fire extinguisher malfunctioned during a controlled training exercise, but no injury or actual fire incident occurred.

incident_description: I went into the garage about 5:30am this morning and the garage was full of smoke and had a strong odor.  After searching the garage I found my Kawasaki cordless drill, model #691761 on my work bench with a hole melted through the plastic near the trigger.  The battery was quite hot, so I removed it to prevent any further issues.  The battery and drill have brown burn marks on them.  The drill was located under a wooden shelf which now has a burn mark on the underside as well. I took photos of the drill, battery, and burn on the shelf.  No people were injured.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burn marks on drill, battery, and shelf) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My Dimension One, Amore Bay Hot Tub produced smoke and steam after water had spilled onto the hot tub's power pack which is the 240VAC power input and electronic distribution hub for the pumps valves and electronics for the hot tub. This could have been a fatal situation if someone was in the hot tub at the time of the incident.
justification: The incident involved smoke and steam production due to water spillage on the power pack, posing a potential fatal risk if someone was present, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: robertshaw water heater gas valve leaks. both whirlpool and robertshaw claim no responsibility. this valve has leaked off and on for several years but I was not able to find it. I guess due to hot weather, the valve has leaked for the last two weeks and bubble testing showed nothing. I did a web search and found out the valve leaks from a control knob that is very seldom ever moved once set. the robertshaw model is: 64-LF8-376R110RATSPL . WEB SEARCH TURNS UP THIS TO BE A PROBLEMATIC DESIGN WITH LEAKS OVER SEVERAL BRANDS. in the past, the r110 was subject to recalls but I guess the problem still exists in the newer valves. news recently reported houses exploding due to gas leaks and maybe this could be a source.
justification: The gas valve leak is a known issue with potential for serious consequences, but no injury or death has been reported in this specific case.

incident_description:
I was operating the quick-release lever on a Bosch MX30 oscillating multi-tool.  The lever will lock in the open position so that the blade can be inserted.  As I began to close the lever, however, it snapped shut suddenly with the force of a mousetrap, cutting my finger badly.  The lever itself is cast aluminum with sharp edges.

I am a very experienced user of power tools and I would say the operation of this mechanism is unexpected and dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in a bad cut to the finger, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The unexpected and dangerous mechanism suggests this could happen to other experienced users (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description:
I cleaned my grill with a wire bristle grill brush. Cooked some chicken and ate it. A bristle from the grill brush was dislodged and stuck to the meat I ate. I wound up in the Emergency room with severe abdominal pain to lower left quadrant. 
A CT scan revealed a 1.5cm long, piece of metal protruding through my intestine. An emergency bowel resection was performed to remove the section of intestine.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury requiring emergency surgery, but no death was reported.

incident_description: A ceiling fan blade separated from a ceiling fan.  The fan was operating normally in an outdoor setting at a temperature of 110 degrees fahrenheit. The fan was not impacted by external objects nor was there any wind. The fitting holding the blade completely severed causing the blade to come crashing down into a seating area. Nobody was injured as a result of this defect. The fan in question has been in use for 2 years. It is the Harbor Breeze Freeport 52-in Bronze Outdoor Downrod Mount Ceiling Fan purchased from Lowes on 7/28/2013. The model specifics are Item #: 204534 |  Model #: LP8079LAZ. Pictures are available of the unintended separation.
justification: The fan blade separated and fell into a seating area, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
On August 6, 2015 my Chamberlain garage door opener started on fire.  We caught it in time to put it out with a fire extinguisher before it ignited the ceiling and other items in proximity to it.  The garage door opener was the only thing that was damaged (some minor smoke and fire extinguisher dust damage).  We were fortunate to not have cars in the garage as burning plastic and battery acid/goo was dropping on the floor.  

Chamberlain Garage Door Opener info:
Model Number:  WD962KPEV
Serial Number:  07546100190
Manufacture Date:  02/2014
Purchase Date:  03/12/2014

Model description:  This is a belt drive unit that has a battery backup and therefore a DC motor.  The unit also has an LCD wall switch with a motion sensor so the lights on the unit turn on from motion in the garage.

The unit operated normally for over one year.  It was installed as per the manufacturer instructions.  My home is 12 years old ÃÂ there are no issues with electrical.  I only use incandescent bulbs (100W) in the garage door opener.  This particular Chamberlain model is rated for incandescent bulbs up to 100W and CFLs up to 26W.  Interestingly, the light bulbs were relatively undamaged from the fire.

I have been in contact with Chamberlain and their response and help has been good.  They are concerned about this incident and are replacing the unit.  They have also requested to have the burned up unit sent to them so they can investigate what caused the fire.  I have no issue with how Chamberlain has responded ÃÂ their response has met my expectations.

I am submitting this report so that there is record of this incident.  Since a 911 fire call was not made, the fire department will not be reporting on this incident.

I have photos of the garage door opener that I took just a few minutes after we put the fire out.  If these are of interest I will be happy to provide them.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was contained without injury or death, and only the garage door opener was damaged.

incident_description:
Homelite 18 volt electric pole saw model #UT 34020 handle started getting hot & I smelled something burning, so I took it apart to see what was wrong. Half the wire & all of the coiled wire had cracked off the insulation. I've never seen anything like that. 

Seems like to me a recall is in order since this might could cause the battery to explode.

Also a better design would be two power strips inside the pole where the power rails would remain in contact with each other.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage and a potential safety hazard (overheating and burning smell) but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung Washer (model # WA456DRHDSU/AA 0001. serial
# Y6BP5AEC701884L) on May22, 2013 from Sears of Lufkin, Texas. Since the purchase 
date, I have had to schedule several service calls for repairs-always for the same problem.

The drain pump on the washer has continuously broken, often coming disconnected from the
drain hose so that water pours out the bottom of the machine. The wire connector that
operates the drain function gets disconnected from the terminal during this activity, causing 
the unit to stop draining so that the pump is either pouring water onto the floor, or not
draining the water out of the machine at all. 

After four service calls and repeated attempts to resolve this annoying and now costly, issue
It has become apparent that this machine and/or the drain system is faulty and that the 
defective unit can only be temporarily repaired before it breaks again. This proves that the 
warranty given on the appliance was ineffective and inefficient.

I therefore, I am requesting that the washing machine be replaced at the sellerÃÂs or
 manufacturerÃÂs expense with a better quality machine, that has passed all applicable quality
 control tests on itÃÂs parts and assemblies, as well as all applicable safety regulations.

This machine cannot be considered safe to operate , under the circumstances, as the faulty
mechanism involving the water and the electrical connections create a potentially fatal 
situation for possible electrocution, and is subject to cause extensive water and or fire
damage at the least.

As I am within my rights as a consumer, in accordance with the Magnuson-Moss Warranty 
Act, the Uniform Commercial Code, and the Texas lemon Law Statutes to request the
replacement of this product which is also subject to numerous other product liability laws, I 
trust that you will consider this letter to be the first step in exercising hose rights and 
respond accordingly.

Sincerely yours,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a faulty washing machine causing water leakage and potential electrical hazards, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I ordered this unit the end of March 2013 and used it during the spring and summer only to avoid any chance of freezing.  I realize it is out of warranty, but I think you ought to know of a safety issue.  The unit was never misused or placed in any unusual situations.  The plug that attaches to the unit semi-melted down and the unit quit working.  There were burn marks around the plug at the unit.  I had noticed the adapter always seemed hot to touch.  There was no other damage unless it is inside of the unit.  I recommend you review this product as I see others have found the same damage to their units (see saferproducts.gov report # 20130209-ACB4E-2147458946).  I am surprised there is not a recall as it could easily have created a fire.
justification: The incident involved a melted plug and burn marks, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Purchased SoleusAir (portable air conditioner/dehumdifier / 60 pint) Model: HCB-P13HP-D,
S/N 1005110103001400068, on 8/11/2014 from our local Fry's Electronics. On 7/02/2015, at approximately 7:30pm, we noticed a slight burning smell of melting plastic and tendrils of smoke emitting from our electrical outlet. Immediately I turned off the Soleus unit and pulled the GFI plug from the outlet. At that time, the GFI outlet belonging to the unit had burn and melt marks around the prongs along with an extremely hot electrical cord. While removing the plug and cord, I received a burn mark on my arm.

I have attempted to contact SoleusAir for many days at the number listed as (888) 876-5387 to no avail. I have called morning, noon, and evening and have never been connected as the line called resumes to a constant busy signal.

I believe this product to be a fire hazard and if we were not at home at the time, fire damage to our home would have most definitely occurred.
justification: The incident involved a burn injury and potential fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the clear evidence of equipment malfunction and burn marks.

incident_description: I am a wallpaper hanger.  For 45 years, in using various 3 and 4 foot stepladders, the occasion arises where one must jump clear of the ladder in a tip over incident.  In using the Werner ladder T-6203, I faced the need to get clear of the ladder.  This ladder collapses in an unsafe manner.  All things break, and they should be engineered to break safely.  This ladder is so designed to collapse the opposing side in a failure.  This is dangerous. A ladder can break on one side, and yet give enough stability for the user to save them self.  This ladder does not.  To my misfortune this defect caused a broken arm, and 3 months of lost income.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken arm and lost income, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests that while such incidents occur, they are not extremely rare or frequent (likelihood 3).

incident_description: Munchkin wipe warmer was plugged in through the AC adapter to the wall outlet (110V). Immediately next to the wall was the mattress, so there was not a lot of air circulation around the power adapter. Adapter was in continuous use for about 6 months. At the end of 6 months I decided to unplug it. It was extremely hot to the touch, i had to put it down to cool, it was painfully hot to handle.
justification: The adapter was extremely hot but did not cause injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I purchased a Honeywell Air Genius 4 Air Purifier at Walmart. I read all directions and operated the 
purifier as directed. Within 24 hours of turning the air purifier on I began to cough and had a tightness in my 
chest. I did not associate the symptoms with the air purifier until the next day. The coughing got 
painful, my chest and lungs felt inflamed, my sinuses felt burned. I searched the internet to see if 
there was any problems with using an air purifier when I discovered the ionic air purifiers have 
been identified for years to have caused similar symptoms, and are banned in some states. Why is 
there not warning labels required on these product? Why are they still for sale to the public? 
I took the produce back to Walmart and complained to the store manager and she said that there was 
nothing she could do to remove these dangerous products for there store and that it had to be 
removed by the manufacturer. How many more consumers have to have their lungs destroyed before this 
product is removed?
It's now been over ten days since I stopped using the air purifier and all of the symptoms have 
remained. How many others have had their health effected because if these products?
justification: The user experienced painful coughing, chest and lung inflammation, and sinus burning, which are clear signs of injury.

incident_description: I purchased an air compressor from Harbor Freight 6 or 7 years ago because they were basically dirt cheap compared to everyone else. Well it developed an air leak at the 125 psi check valve. There was a large nut that holds the spring (internal) against the check valve (also internal). The leak was at the gasket under the nut as checked with soapy water. I barely moved the nut when it (the entire valve) exploded with my hands on the wrench and near this nut. Shrapnel went everywhere. Lucky for me I was not injured or blinded. My son's neighbor had a similar incident (involving the same model compressor) when the check valve was banged accidentally by a piece of wood that fell over and it sent shrapnel everywhere. I bought a new check valve from Harbor Freight and attempted to make one good compressor out of two since he gave me his old one. Now comes the bad stuff. The fittings for the copper tube from the compressor cylinder to the check valve shattered when a minimal pressure was applied and it turns out that the copper tube is not copper at all- it is nothing more than copper plated aluminum! There is no other reason to use copper plated aluminum than deception. The fittings along with the check valve were chrome plated pot metal- also deception. Anything that you try to remove to install better parts, will break off or strip. In short, when these air compressors are fully charged with air they are ticking time bombs just waiting for something to fall or even brush up against them. I noticed that all of their compressors are built the same way. I do not know how that they are allowed to be imported with this type of hardware on them. Someone is eventually going to be killed or seriously injured by one of these Chinese built Harbor Freight air compressors.
justification: The incident involved an air compressor exploding and sending shrapnel everywhere, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a case of ESL/Interlogix 541NCSXT hard wired smoke detectors, and had them professionally installed in my home by my alarm company. The units all had a manufacture date of 14155 which meant they were constructed on the 155th day of 2014.  Of the case of ten, we've had
3 malfunction with numerous false trips. My repeated calls to ESL/Interlogix tech support has yielded
no explanation as to why 30% of my newly installed smoke detectors would fail. Since these units activated improperly for no credible reason, I can't assume the other units will operate as designed.

Here is a quote from the distributor I purchased the units from: "they haven't gotten back to us on what could be the issue with them. it may be a bad lot but if you have this many going bad on after the other I would assume they never fully corrected the issue that the units had that put them on manufacturer hold to begin with".

As a retired fire fighter, I urge you to look into this situation as the company has a history of
selling defective units that resulted in recalls!
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning smoke detectors with false alarms, posing a potential safety risk but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while using the power washer the exhaust from the unit burnt her leg, causing the skin to peel.  She contacted her physician who advised dressing the wound with antibiotics and bandages.  The caller then saw her physician & was treated for a second degree burn.

The power washer was in use for approximately 1hour and 30 mins when the incident occurred.  Caller stated that she had purchased the unit 2 months prior and there had been no prior incidents.

(Unit was used once before for 30 minutes)
(6/29/15) The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that the warning stated that there should be 3ft of clearance to prevent burn.  She stated that the warning is not clear because
1) the picture of a fire and a hand implies not to touch the muffler area and
2) you could not operate the unit if you had to be 3' away from it


Caller feels that this power washer is unsafe and should be reported.  Exhaust is too hot & too powerful

The caller followed up with Dr for 2nd degree burn approx. 5" x 3"
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he is experiencing similar problems of Recall#14-179.  Hazard: The dehumidifiers can overheat, smoke and catch fire, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers.  Caller stated that he smelled a burning odor and when he pull out the water container for the unit he noticed that the plastic had melted.  He also researched and found that his model was not part of the recall when he contacted the manufacturer (7/1).



Caller feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be included in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and melted plastic, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was using a Husky Powerwasher Model H 1600 to clean my patio.  Without warning the spray gun separated from the high-pressure hose.  Since the unit was still on, the hose was whipping around me and could have caused serious injury.  The spray gun and high-pressure hose are sold as a single component and not designed to come apart.
justification: The incident involved a high-pressure hose whipping around, which could have caused serious injury but did not result in any actual injury.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased the laminate flooring from Lumber Liquidators and the sales order number is "[REDACTED]". The consumer states he installed the laminate flooring in his home by early May 2014. The laminate flooring is in the kitchen, dining room and laundry room. 

Sometime in May 2015 the consumer was informed by his son that there were allegations about the laminate flooring sold by Lumber Liquidators containing high levels of formaldehyde. The consumer contacted Lumber Liquidators and was offered a testing kit. The consumer received the testing kit within a few days and performed the test. On 05/29/15 the consumer sent the testing kit to Environmental Diagnostics Laboratory (EDLab), located at 4911 Creekside Drive, Suite C, Clearwater, FL 33760 as instructed by Lumber Liquidators. 

On 06/24/15 the consumer's wife contacted Lumber Liquidators to inquire about the results of the test. The consumer's wife was told by a rep (name unknown) that the formaldehyde limit is .081 ppm and their results were .243 ppm (we are not sure who set the limit that the rep was referring to).  The consumer has been calling Lumber Liquidators to request some assistance and information about how to proceed but the consumer has not been able to speak with anyone that can assist him. The consumer last called Lumber Liquidators on 07/13/15 and filed a report on the matter and the consumer was told that someone would get back to him but no one from Lumber Liquidators has reached out to him as of today 07/20/15.

The consumer contacted EDLab (855-982-9797) to request a copy of the results (reference # [REDACTED]) and is still waiting to hear from them. 

The consumer states he and his wife have been experiencing sinus issues and headaches for some time. The consumer is not sure when the health issues began. The consumer is not sure whether the symptoms are from the high levels of formaldehyde in the laminate flooring but he is very concerned about their safety since he became aware of the test results.
justification: The consumer and his wife are experiencing sinus issues and headaches, which are potential health effects from formaldehyde exposure, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her glass shower door that was already in home that had been newly renovated when she purchased it in 2011.
This home was used only as a vacation home until the caller moved into it in December 2014.

June 8th, 2015 the caller heard a loud noise coming from her bathroom, went to check and saw that her glass shower door had exploded sending glass into the shower, the bathroom floor, into her bedroom, and bedroom closet.

No one was in the bathroom at the time.
There are no injuries being reported.

She is reporting this product as a potential laceration hazard stating that if this incident were to happen with someone in the bathroom it could be a very hazardous injury issue.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does plan to contact them today.  (June 9th, 2015).

The shower door that exploded has been removed from the area and placed in the garage.
justification: The glass shower door exploded but no one was injured, and the incident was reported as a potential hazard.

incident_description: I had just gotten into the shower and closed the shower door behind me when I heard a pin drop.  Then CRASH!!  The right shower wall completely shattered and fell all around me along with the shower door (which was still intact).  Yes, I know exactly what caused it.  The pin fell off the shower door hinge and the weight of the door could not be held, so the right side of the glass wall completely shattered.  I had to walk out of my shower and bathroom over shards of glass (barefoot of course) and all the while shaking from the shock of what had just happened.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass and walking barefoot over shards, posing a clear risk of injury, though none was reported.

incident_description: This is supposed to be a quick release for easy cleaning product.  However, the caps that are supposed to keep the release mechanism from releasing aren't strong enough and they release unexpectedly.  My son was thrown forward and fell in the bathroom.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall, indicating an injury, and the product defect makes recurrence likely.

incident_description: My husband was taking a shower and suddenly and without warning the shower door shattered. Glass all over him and the bathroom and shower. He sustained cuts on his back, shoulders, arms, and feet.
justification: The individual sustained multiple cuts from shattered glass, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
PRODUCT: Cosco Big 3-Step Folding Step Stool with Rubber Hand Grip 
Purchased at Walmart, product # : 552846254
Fell off backwards.
Steps are hinged at front edge for folding.
When unfolded and locked in use the step is stabilized by the rear edge support.
BUT the step is FLEXIBLE PLASTIC so if your balance starts to move, the step hinges with you and you get no feedback until you start to fall.  With a rigid step you would immediately feel your imbalance and respond.
justification: The description indicates a fall occurred due to the step's flexible plastic design, which suggests potential for injury.

incident_description: We were given 3, Holmes window fans last summer that were purchased from Walmart in Butler Pa.  2 of our 3 window fans have gone bad and nearly caused a fires.  The first (which was in my toddlers bedroom) stopped running and began to produce a burning electrical smell which woke my son who then alerted us, this was apriximataly 2 weeks ago (July 2015).  Today (2 weeks later, August 4, 2015) the second of the 3 fans began to produce a electrical fire smell that filled out entire residence.  This unit was still running.  Both units, the plastic foam insulation around the motors was discolored on and appeared to be starting to melt and were isolated to be the the source of the smell.  The plastic fan slats at the motors were extremely hot to the touch, actually too hot to touch for more than a second or two.   With both incidents the walls around the electrical outlet became hot over where the wires run through the walls however we caught the problem prior to the breakers tripping.  I attempted to contacted the manufacturer today and am awaiting contact back from the company.  After reviewing product reviews on the manufacturers site and various other sites searching for possible recalls I found an identical incident on a review on Target.com website from a person who also purchased 3 and had 2 fail similarly to ours shortly after purchase.
justification: The fans nearly caused fires but no injuries occurred, and similar incidents were reported by others, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that although his unit sounds like it is working properly, for the past two weeks it has not been removing moisture from his home. The unit runs twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week.

06/16/2015 - Curious as to why his unit was not working properly, the consumer proceeded to check his unit. At first, he had to wait for it to cool down as he noticed how hot it was to touch. When he opened the unit, he noticed several components inside it that were either losing their form from excessive heat; the compressor was so hot that the housing was melting because it was touching the compressor. The water pump was also affected.

The consumer indicates that he never noticed any smoke surrounding the unit. He informs that the fan was working properly.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained to a representative the issues he has been having with his unit. Upon looking up his specific model, he was informed that his dehumidifier is not included in a recall. Because his unit is not recalled, he was not offered a remedy but was informed that he should unplug and stop usage of his unit, as well as that he will be receiving a call from the manufacturer the following week.

The consumer has no injuries nor previous incidents to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction without injury, and the likelihood is possible given the described overheating and component damage.

incident_description:
The consumer lives in an apartment and states the furnace in the complex is causing her adverse health effects. The consumer has been renting the apartment for approximately 11 months. 

About 2 months ago (05/15/15) the consumer changed the air filter in her apartment and since then she has been experiencing the following symptoms, bad taste in her mouth, chest pain, skin irritation, sore throat, nose irritation and coughing.

The consumer believes the furnace in the apartment complex is emitting a chemical through the air vents that is causing her adverse effects. The consumer has spoken with the property manager of the apartment complex about her health issues. The property manager contacted Clean Aire to have the consumer's apartment tested.

On 06/19/15 there was a test conducted by an indoor air quality specialist from Clean Aire (803-776-1117) and the results were inconclusive. 

The consumer has visited a physician and underwent tests. The consumer was told by the physician that the test results were normal. 

black, wool-like debris found in exchange air shaft?  while changing 30-day filter.  Particulates now dispersing through apartment, onto all surfaces, and high dust build-up to filter and shaft.  Breathing the in-door air leaves a chlorine, bitter taste in mouth; nasal drainage with particles?; have also experienced flu-like body pain.
- chest pain (lungs)
- eye irritation
[REDACTED]
justification: The consumer reports multiple health symptoms including chest pain, skin irritation, and flu-like body pain, indicating injury.

incident_description: 4.5 inch cut off wheels sold by Harbor Freight are rated for 13500 RPM, but even with a 11000 RPM motor (theirs, #69645) they fly apart. One cut my face, another cut my abdomen after cutting through my shirt, a third hit my son about five feet away but did not cause any damage. I reported this to Harbor Freight and have received no acknowledgement, concern, offer to replace, or any other response. Other wheels have delaminated without flying apart. This product is commonly known to be hazardous to use, but this specific product goes beyond that.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the user and a near-miss with another person, indicating a severity level of 3. The description suggests this is a recurring issue with the product, making occurrence likelihood high.

incident_description: We purchased a Shag Moroccan rug from Rugsusa.com, they only say their carpet sheds. Does not offer a warning the shed cumulates and posses a choking hazard to small animal or children. This Sunday 8/2/15 shed from the rug that cumulated was picked up by our infant son who began to gag on it. We had to call paramedics and luckily our son vomited up the chunk of shed from the carpet.  This could have been deadly for us. We already contacted Rugsusa.com several times about this and they simply said we should have known after 14 days the rug was unsuitable for our family. The rug shed so much, even after getting rid of it , the shed was all over the house and still was a choking hazard.
justification: The infant gagged on rug shed and required paramedics, indicating a significant choking hazard that could have been fatal.

incident_description:
This caller is contacting the CPSC regarding her daughter's Kenmore dehumidifier which was purchased September 15th, 2013 after her previously owned unit was recalled.
Her daughter had no problems with the new dehumidifier until her father went to her basement Monday, June 22nd, 2015 to empty the water container and found that it had overflowed and that the dehumidifier was overheating.  The unit was not smoking, however the fan was not running and the top of the unit was very hot.

With the thought that the unit may reset and work properly it was left plugged in but it continued to overheat and so the caller's husband unplugged their daughters dehumidifier Wednesday, June 24th, 2015 and it remains unplugged for fear of fire.

The manufacturer was contacted around June 22nd, 2015 but was believed to be unconcerned.

The submitter added when she turned the unit off the compressor continued to run, and the only way it completely shut off was when it was unplugged.
justification: The dehumidifier overheated and malfunctioned but did not cause injury or fire, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the unit was installed in the house that he purchased new from K. Hovnanian Builders.

The consumer stated that the fireplace comes on by itself. The consumer stated that this happened on three occasion.

After the first two times, the consumer contacted the manf. They sent out a technician. The technician informed the consumer that some of the remotes have an issue. They informed him that the remote control is susceptible to picking up interfering signals. The consumer was informed that the only way to solve this would be to have a remote that only turns on or off the fireplace and not control the other programs. The technician replaced the remote with the same kind of remote.

The consumer stated that few weeks later, the fireplace came on by itself again, twice more.

The consumer contacted the manf again. They informed him that they will come out again in end of July for an inspection. The consumer was informed that their engineering department was working on the issue. The consumer was informed that even if the fireplace comes on by itself, it will auto shut off after 8 hours. The consumer believes that is a major safety hazard for the fireplace to stay on for 8 hours when someone is not home.

The consumer lives in a new built community for ages 55+. The whole community has these fireplaces installed and many of the other people have reported similar hazards to the consumer. The consumer believes that the other people may have reported the issues to the builder.

The consumer added, on 7/16/15, the fireplace manufacturer replaced the remote and the receiver with a new and different remote (1410TH-A) and receiver.  The consumer also noted the manufacturer acknowledged receipt of many complaints with the original remote and receiver.
justification: The fireplace turning on by itself poses a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Complainant purchased newly constructed home in October 2014 and in June 2015 his 8 hardwired smoke detectors started falsely activating during the night and day.  He contacted Kidde customer support and they advised him to trouble shoot them by disconnecting them from the hard wire and running them on battery power.  After conducting the test, he found that 2 out of the 8 units were defective.  He contacted Kidde customer support again and they sent him 2 new detectors.  He asked if he needed to send them back to be examined and they told him no and instructed him to throw them away.

As a Senior Fire Investigator for the Maine State Fire Marshal's Office, I believe that 2 out of 8 detectors being defective is unacceptable, and that Kidde should be examining defective smoke detectors in order to identify the cause of the failure.  It is my experience that faulty detectors can mean the difference of life and death in a fire event, and nuisance alarms cause people to not use their smoke detectors.  The complainant is the Town Fire Chief and had thrown the detectors away before informing me of the issue.
justification: The incident involved false alarms and defective detectors but no actual injury or death, warranting a severity level of 2. The likelihood is 3 as defective detectors are a known issue but not universally prevalent.

incident_description:
I am writing saferproducts.gov to inform you of what we have learned concerning the improperly installed spray polyurethane foam (SPF).

In May of 2013 Demilec APX fire rated open cell SPF was applied underneath the roof deck of my house.  A Demilec Territory Manager was on site for 3 days along with the Demilec authorized installer.  

Due to the foul smelling odor for weeks after installation the installer acknowledged the problem.  Seven weeks later the foam was removed and I collected samples for testing by Eurofins.  They reported the two highest VOCÃÂs are fire retardants: TEP CAS #78-40-0 (emission rate 89.5 ÃÂµg/mÃÂ²*h) and DEP CAS #78-38-6 (emission rate 4750 ÃÂµg/mÃÂ²*h, chamber concentration 4710 ÃÂµg/m3).  DEP fire retardant as reported by Eurofins was extremely high.   At no time during my complaints to Demilec representatives concerning the foul odor did they instruct the construction crew or myself to vacate the house.  I developed a dry hacking cough while working in the house. After removal of the SPF construction was halted and the house remains vacant, toxic, and unlivable.


The Berkeley Analytical certification for Demilec APX reports emission rates of DEP 2237 ÃÂµ/gmÃÂ²*h and TEP 564 ÃÂµ/gmÃÂ²*h.  In the report are ÃÂEstimated Indoor Air Concentrations (ÃÂµg/mÃÂ³)ÃÂ for Classroom at 2152.6, Office at 1203, Residence at 5007.

CRELÃÂs have not been established for these chemicals.  Protective Action Criteria (PAC) is the only protocol to determine the health effects.  PAC protocol is used by first responders and health officials to determine the impacts of a one hour- once in a lifetime exposure. There are three levels of PAC value (1 to 3) where each successive value is associated with an increasingly severe effect from a higher level of exposure. Each level is defined as follows:

PAC-1: Mild, transient health effects.
PAC-2: Irreversible or other serious health effects that could impair the ability to take protective action.
PAC-3: Life-threatening health effects.

DEP (CAS 78-38-6) PAC protocol 
PAC-1                    PAC-2                    PAC-3                    
370                         4100                       460,000  ÃÂµg/mÃÂ³

This puts the Eurofins test in the PAC 2 category and the Berkeley Analytical estimated residential in the PAC 2 category.  Schools estimated is in the PAC 1 category; this means after a once in a lifetime/one hour exposure the health effects are mild and transient if you remove yourself from the school and do not reenter.  This product should have never been released.  It remained on the market for two years 1/13 to 1/15 when Demilec announced they had reformulated the product.  Putting this product to market was fraudulent or negligent by advertising APX as the lowest VOC open cell foam approved for use in schools.  I understand that the fire retardants are on the B side (proprietary side) of the APX mix and therefore donÃÂt have to be disclosed.     

[REDACTED] a Certified Industrial Hygienist, Professional Mechanical Engineer, and president of Indoor Environmental Engineering agrees with the above statements. 

Two follow up indoor air quality studies have been conducted after removal of the foam.  The most recent is August 2014, 13 months (two summers) after removal of the SPF.  The reported concentration of DEP was 210 to250 ÃÂµg/mÃÂ³.

[REDACTED] conclusion for the Indoor Air Quality test (210-250 ÃÂµg/mÃÂ³) in assessing for a non-occupational (residential) exposure to VOC amounts currently in the house would be in the PAC-2 level for non-occupational exposure.  Note, criteria for a non-occupational exposure is significantly lower than the level for a one hour one time first responder exposure as an individual would be exposed for greater than 8 hours per day for their life.  He recommends that all of the Demilec foam be removed including the surfaces that it was applied to (roof deck and truss).  This means removing the roof and truss system as a minimum.  The HVAC system and ducting, electrical wiring, recessed light fixtures, solar tubes and other construction material is coated with the Demilec APX foam. 

The current status of the house is it remains vacant and in litigation.  All contractors who have inspected the house recommend complete removal as it would be less expensive and they could not guarantee a fix if they try to repair.

EPA website:
ÃÂEPA is not currently aware of standard accepted removal and/or remediation practices.  This is an area for further investigation and research as future renovation and deconstruction of buildings where SPF has been applied are anticipated.
ÃÂNote: Removal may not resolve the problem and may create other problems.
When spray foam has been correctly applied and cured, it is usually considered to be relatively inert; however, there are factors that impact curing rates and some long-term concerns for exposure potential.
If SPF was not applied properly, chemical contaminants may have migrated to hard and/or soft surfaces elsewhere in the building and may be the source of residual odors; therefore, removal may not resolve the issue.  Also, disturbing SPF material might generate dust or hazardous materials if done improperly. 

I also need assistance in what type of personal protection equipment for deconstruction, protection to neighbors during deconstruction (SPF dust with the DEP), and transport/disposal of the building materials in contact with the APX foam if this is determined to be a hazardous material.

IÃÂm willing to share all the reports and information I have.

Thanks and hope to hear from your Agency,

incident_description:
Dangerous product: I purchased a replacement home toilet From Lowe's in Arlington Heights, IL on April 22, 2015. The model was an American Standards brand Champion 4 brand made in Mexico.

During the installation, I got a nasty hand cut from the back of the water tank cover. Apparently during the manufacturing process porcelain or glass shards were not removed.

The water tank's chromium plated flush handle was also somewhat sharp but did not cause me injury. Trying to register my purchase and file a complaint. their suggested web site will only handle air conditioners. Very frustrating!

The submitter added after his injury, he took the tank cover and attempted to grind away the sharp edge against his concrete driveway..He noted it helped, but he pities the next unaware buyer.  The submitter also noted American Standard did not reply to his April 25 letter.  The submitter also added he is not asking for monetary recuperation, and the public should be aware of this product defect.
justification: The incident resulted in a hand cut that took two hours to stop bleeding, indicating an injury but no permanent harm.

incident_description:
I worked a long day on my Lenovo T60 laptop (6459-CTO) on July 9, 2015.  Around 7:30PM, I smelled rubber burning and soon after, I saw smoke coming from the power cord (Lenovo AC Adapter 65W, 20V -> FRU P/N 42T5282).  It ignited very close to the connection point with the laptop.  I quickly pulled out the cord from the computer and soon after realized that I needed to unplug it altogether from the power source which I did and eventually the cord cooled off.  And I have not used it since (to be trashed).  

What is disturbing to me, is the attitude of the Lenovo Customer Service representative when I called on July 13, 2015 2:23PM (ET) (call duration 12 minutes 30 seconds).  I wanted to report the incident to make them aware of a problem that could have ended badly like an engulfed house fire.  They would not hear or listen to any of it.  They really showed no responsibility or accountability for their defective product and resulting incident.  The rep basically said that "an accident was adverted, therefore was not a concern" (I paraphrased). 

I think this is incredibly irresponsible for a company that sells electronics for home use where families with babies evolve.  My desk is made of wood and the power source lays on the wood surface by just about 1/5 of an inch. 

Please do your best so families don't end up mourning their loved ones because a company decides that it is OK to risk their consumers' lives as though human beings are as disposable as their defective products. Thank you!
justification: The incident involved a smoking power cord that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:

We needed to clean it up immediately as we have 2 children in the house. Though we wore shoes and gloves we had several cuts on fingers and feet and knees from the clean up process.
