incident_description:
This device is a  5/16ÃÂ cable with a keyed locking mechanism in the shape of a python head in camouflage colors.   The locking mechanism can be moved up and down the cable and locked in almost any position.  

  Attached to the cable is a warning label with the following language: 

 ÃÂWARNING:  Risk of bodily injury or suffocation from tightened cable.  Use only as directed for securing and locking property.  This is no (sic) a toy.  Keep away from small childrenÃÂ.

There is no warning about hazards for children on the printed cardboard backer to which the device is attached when it is sold.
  
Most people would assume that the locking mechanism canÃÂt be moved when it is locked and assess the danger the device poses on that basis.  However, there is an even greater danger which is not readily apparent because the locking mechanism when locked does not stay in placeÃÂit can still be moved to further constrict the cable loop.    In other words, the locking mechanism when locked will not slide up the cable (i.e., the cable loop cannot be expanded) but can still be slid down  the cable (i.e,  the cable loop can be constricted).   The locked mechanism will slide downward  whether or not the key is in the lock.  There is no apparent functional reason for designing the locking mechanism to slide downward after it is locked as it can be slid to whatever position is desired when it is unlocked and then locked in position.  

Here is a hypothetical to illustrate the danger which the device poses:  A consumer might think he is protecting children when storing the device by locking the locking mechanism and removing the key.   He pays no attention to the position of the locking mechanism on the cable or how big the resulting cable loop is.  His ten year old son finds the device and decides it would be fun to scare his 8 year old brother with it.  He sees that the locking mechanism moves downward and assumes it is unlocked.  The loop is big enough to put over his brotherÃÂs head and around his neck and he does so.   He slides the locking mechanism down the cable until his brother is choking,  assuming he can pull it back after he has scared his brother.    He discovers too late that he canÃÂt pull it back.  If someone does not quickly intervene with the proper key or bolt cutters, the other child could choke to death. 
 
It does not appear to me that the warning supplied by the manufacturer is sufficient to warn of this unexpected hazard. 

 The device would be just as functional and far safer if the locking mechanism was designed so it did not move in either direction when locked.

Do other Python devices in different series have the same issue?  It appears that Master Lock sells a number of different Python series devices with different dimensions and colors but with the same general design.   I found some at a nearby store and attempted to check them to see if  their locking mechanisms also slid in one direction when locked.  I first checked a Python device which appeared to be identical to mine (5/16 inch cable) except that the color of the locking mechanism was black and silver rather than camouflage.  It also constricted when locked.  I suspect that all Python devices in the 5/16 inch cable series constrict when locked.  I also attempted to check a device from a different series of Python devices with thicker cablesÃÂ 3/8 inch  cable.  The locking mechanism on the 3/8 inch devices appears to be more substantialÃÂunlike the 5/16 inch device locking mechanism, it had three key positions.  However, the packaging on the 3/8 inch device was such that I could not check the locking mechanism without destroying the packaging so I did not check it.  Perhaps the locking mechanisms in the 3/8 inch series stays in place when locked.
justification: The device poses a risk of suffocation or death, as described in the hypothetical scenario involving children, warranting a high severity level. The likelihood is considered possible due to the design flaw and potential for misuse.

As the best recollection of both my wife and I, my wife purchased the spa from Griffith Pools and Spas in the Spring of 2013 possibly at a show as a special and we asked if they could hold it. At that time I did not think we had a suitable location for the SPA at our home and decided that we would come up with an idea or build out an area to locate it.

Again as best as I recall the unit was delivered by the Griffin Pools and Spa sub-contractor sometime in the Spring of 2014. At that time we filled the spa and started using it. And I might add thoroughly enjoyed it.

In the Fall of 2014 one night when I was stepping out of the spa onto very wet concrete pavers I had my hand in the spa water and my feet on the wet pavers.

I received a very strong stinging numbing sensation. My first thought was that can't be what I think it was. Thinking it may have been what can happen with the body where the body mimics something similar to an electrical shock, I again stuck the tips of my fingers into the spa water and again received a very strong stinging which I then clearly recognized as an electrical shock as having been a Clemson University graduate Electrical Engineer along with 40 years of working with electricity on many levels it was clear to me that I was acting as the grounding path for a spa that has the water in it charged with 120 VAC or some level of that voltage which a professional will always tell you that having your body act as a ground conductor never turns out good for the person.

I did call and advise you of my experience immediately and your response was very rudimentary in that an individual came by an "checked" the spa wiring, however I was not home and I suggested over the phone to him that he simply mimic my test where he soak the pavers in water or use one of my water hoses running on his feet and then stick his hand in the water which he told me he would not do so. So getting to the problem was avoided and let drop.

Myself being not really sure of a good means to test the spa and also not having the spa on my priority list allowed it to languish until recently when my wife started asking me how are we going to "fix" the spa.

Being an engineer for 40 plus years my first thought is before we fix the problem we define the problem and get at least an idea. So recently I came up with a very simply test.

I used a #12 THHN AWG insulated wire and stripped both ends. Having the spa plugged in I insert one end in the water of the spa and the other end in a grounding receptacle point on a receptacle plug. I verified the ground was OK with a simply tester.

The result of this homemade testing was astounding. When the circuit is on a 15 AMP breaker the breaker is tripped every time when I do the short the water to ground. Using a 20 AMP CB it maintains the charged water and will not trip the breaker. The factory installed cord GFI never trips. Recently I had left the tub unplugged for a day and when I plugged it back in my main 200 amp main house breaker tripped for an unexplained reason. Point is the GFI does not work and the spa water will shock the person creating the ground path.

I believe based on my testing that there are two serious shortcomings in regards to the product which has a GFI which is a device that when a fault occurs such as I experienced the power to the spa will be shut off. This device always failed to function. Secondly the spa with the design as it stands can have component failures that will induce lethal voltages into the spa waters and when a person is in the water and touches a grounding surface outside the tub they will suffer a voltage shock causing injury and again possibly death.

Based on that experience I need to ask how you intend to resolve the issue as I called your company last Fall and received very minimal support to date with this situation what I based on my years of experience is a hazard in a product that can result in human injury and potentially death to people using the spa.

Having 40 years of work experience I recognize that no one wishes to build or sell products that can cause harm, however unfortunately as hard as we try the situation does occur. Also unfortunately in my 40 years I have also learned that the first response of nearly every company I have ever dealt with is that the company and their lawyers try to smear the person being victimized instead of addressing the real issue. So let's both stick to what I want and that is a safe spa. I loved the unit but now am gun shy and will not use the product based on the issues.

Again I repeat my only agenda in writing and bringing this problem to the attention yourself and other people is that I like the hot tub and the size was perfect for my family including grown kids and grandkids, however my families safety takes priority over getting my feelings hurt and also the general public who has this spa need to be made aware of the possibilities of what could happen based on my experiences.

I look forward to your reply and a resolution to my problem however I will not be waiting for your reply as this issue needs an immediate thorough investigation and based on that investigation provide both me a response due to the what I believe is unsafe and possible lethal consequences in using the product to not only me but the public.

Please contact me at the above address in writing to provide what permanent safe solution you will provide for both the failure of the GFI to function and the mitigation in the product design which allows live 120 VAC voltage direct access to people using the spa.
justification: The incident involves a severe electrical shock hazard with potential for injury or death, as evidenced by the user's experience and testing results.

They stated that the FEMA federal regulation is 16 ppb...so of course to us almost triple that amount sounds dangerous. We've spoke to the IL EPA, IL Dept of Public Health and most recently [REDACTED], MD from the Chicago branch of the ATSDR. No one can give us a straight answer that we are looking for......do we tear out the flooring because it's making our son sick, or is this nothing to worry about. Lumber Liquidators states they are being cooperative (which they have sent us 2 of their air quality tests as well, but those will take a month for results because they are so overwhelmed with testing) but it's nearly impossible to talk to someone in their customer service department and they can't give me any information on what levels they are considering toxic either. I'm really hoping that the CPSC is able to help us figure this out!! 

Thank you,
[REDACTED]

incident_description: Allure Laminate flooring was installed December 29- Dec.31.  After 5 days I developed a disease called erythema multiforme, an autoimmune disease. A biopsy suggested a medication or chemical caused the problem. As I had been on the same meds for a great length of time it was determined that an environmental cause was probable. It was then that I realized that five days separated my symptoms from the installation of laminate flooring manufactured by Halstead. I performed off-gassing measurements by certified lab analysts who concluded that off gassing was very high. Examination of the laminate components indicated that laminate material contained 7.8% di-sonyl phthalate. This chemical is banned in California under proposition 65. I believe others have developed erythema multiforme but didn't connect the dots, i.e. symptoms with time of installation. The laminate is made in China and it would be difficult getting honest answers as to the material as noted by the documentary on laminate flooring by '60 minutes".  The issue on this documentary was formaldehyde, however, I believe that the real issue is di-sonyl phthalate. Please investigate this flooring as I believe it is unsafe.
justification: The incident describes a case of erythema multiforme, an autoimmune disease, linked to chemical exposure from laminate flooring, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
This generator is used for intermittent power supply at my farm, to run coffee processing equipment.  I purchased it from Costco, and first put it into service in July 2005.  It probably has about 300 hours of run-time, up until this date, (March 2015)  Typically, I roll it out of it's locked storage room in my "barn" to a roofed open-sided work area; check it for fuel, oil, etc.  It is a manual start unit, so I start it, and connect heavy extension cords to it to run a gas-fired roaster, and it's blower, also lights in the barn work-area.  I've also used it to run power saws and other tools, and a small "buzz box" stick welder.

I've had no problems with in before now, except it does not run well on alcohol based gasoline, so I purchase non-OH Gasoline for it and my other small engines.  It has a 5 gallon tank over the large alternator unit with a shut-off valve beneath the tank, and a rubber hose leading to the carburetor of the 10 hp Briggs & Stratton engine.

On Mar. 22, 2015, I setup the generator as usual, started it, and used it to arc-weld a brace from my disc harrow that had snapped, and a heavy-duty grinder to prep and finish off the repair area. Both pieces of equipment throw off a lot of sparks when they're being used.  After I was done, I stopped the unit, by shutting off the valve beneath the gas tank.  I noticed it was wet and dripping but seemed to stop after I turned off the valve.  I cooled the unit down, then put it away in its locked storage room, thinking I'd take a look at it later, believing it was the "ball" valve that was leaking.

The next day, when I went to the barn, I noticed a strong odor of Gasoline.  I unlocked the small storage area, and wheeled the unit out, it still had traces of gasoline on its frame.  I checked the valve, and it was hanging beneath the tank by the rubber hose.  About 3 gallons of gasoline had leaked onto the concrete floor and evaporated over night.  The valve is pressed into a rubber grommet, which in turn has been pressed into a 1/4" hole in the bottom of the tank.  Nothing else attaches the shutoff to the tank,  Upon subsequent inspection, I found that half of the grommet was still around the neck of the valve, but the other half had broken away at its thin spot, and I later found the top half loose inside of the empty tank.

It would seem that something more substantial than a rubber grommet  would be used to secure a main fuel shutoff valve to the bottom of a tank holding 5 gallons of gasoline, especially considering that the tank sits above a brushed electrical generator, and that the entire unit is often used in close proximity to spark creating devices, such as power grinders, and arc welders, and of course it's own heat creating engine.
justification: The incident involved a significant gasoline leak but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the generator had been used without issues for years before this failure.

incident_description:
Re: Safety of Tempered Glass

Dear Sir or Madam:

We would like to call to your attention the fact that one of the tempered glass doors which we had installed in February spontaneously shattered. Our library received a large, private donation which allowed us to remodel the children's room of our library, and we had the construction company pick out tempered glass doors for us, along with the rest of the project, and they recommended doors manufactured by Oldcastle BuildingEnvelope.   These doors were very thick and large, and we had placed some decals placed on them to match the new underwater theme of the children's room. They were held above the doorway by some metal brackets attached to the top of the doors and slid along a metal bar installed above the doorway on each side to open the doors.

About five weeks after the doors had been installed and the children's room was back in use, a lady was gently closing one of the doors, and the door broke into both small and large pieces, which fell to the floor.  A few small pieces remained attached to the metal brackets at the top of the door (see the enclosed photos).  If a small child had been next to the door when it broke, the pieces of glass falling to the floor would almost certainly have caused an injury or even death because some of the pieces were sharp, large and heavy. The glass also rained down several feet because the doors were so large. An Internet search revealed that this type of breakage in tempered glass has happened many times over the last few years to other people and to companies that had installed tempered glass doors or windows, and that there may be a few different reasons for the breakage.

We did not realize that the doors were not warranted by the door manufacturer at the time that the construction work was performed. We also did not realize that there was a chance that the doors could spontaneously break and possibly damage someone. Once the door had broken, we were told that the doors were not under warranty.   If we had know that there was a chance that the door could break in this manner, we would not have installed them in the childrenÃÂs room.  We were told that bumping the side of the door with a metal object could cause the weakening of the glass and be the cause for later breakage, but the door was not hit with any metal object.


We would like for you to add our instance of breakage to the tally you keep of spontaneous tempered glass breakages,  and we  would also  like for you  to consider imposing a regulation to require manufacturers to put a warning label for consumers on all  tempered  glass  sold  in  the  United  States  advising  them  of  the  possibility of spontaneous breakage so that they will be aware of the possibility of the breakage and possible injury from the pieces of glass.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous shattering of tempered glass without injury, but with potential for severe harm if a child had been nearby.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he purchased the water heater and had it installed.

The consumer stated that immediately the pilot kept going out on the water heater. The consumer had to constantly re-light it more and more over the past two months.

The consumer stated he went out for sometime. When he came back he had to re-light the pilot twice a day. 

The consumer stated that there was black soot coming out of the water heater. 

The consumer called the retailer. They informed him that this was normal.

The consumer stated that eventually the pilot stopped lighting. The consumer contacted the manf at that point.

They sent out a technician from Superior on 2/4/15. The technician was asked to take pictures of the chimney and exhaust. The consumer stated that Rheem attributed the soot problem to not having a chimney liner and the right pitch to the exhaust line. 

The technician from Superior stated that Rheem will send out replacement parts (TDR and burner) due to the heavy soot. The consumer stated that he received a call from the technician two days later asking about the parts and if they have come in yet. The technician called Rheem to find out and he was informed that since the consumer does not have the right pitch and chimney liner, they will not provide any replacement parts.

The consumer stated that this water heater was a direct replacement from a previous one.

The consumer contacted the manf and spoke to a supervisor on 2/5/15. They agreed to send the parts as long as the consumer does not hold them liable for any more warranty repairs.

The consumer has a 7-10 years warranty on the water heater. The consumer was sent the TDR but not the burner since it was on backorder.

Technician #2 from Superior was at the consumer's house again on 2/9/15 for few hours taking the product apart and putting it back together. The technician kept running into the same issue with soot regardless of what he did.The technician ended up taking the product apart for the 4th time and found a manufacturer defect. He found that they did not install an orifice in the gas line. The technician stated that this is a safety defect which could have caused his house to burn down. The only thing that saved from the house fire was the TDR that popped over 500 degrees.

The technician proved that it wasn't the pitch or the chimney liner causing the issue. The technician called Rheem. Reluctantly, they agreed to replace the water heater and reinstall it.

This unit will be at the consumer's house for about 10 days. They cannot install a new heater for 10 days due to their work load.
justification: The incident involved a safety defect that could have caused a house fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Both my cat and I had severe reactions after switching from generic Safeway dryer sheets to Bounce Dryer Sheets.  She developed contact dermatitis and I have had respiratory issues since switching to them February 1, 2015.  

After just getting over a bad cold, I decided to wash just my pillowcases and wait to do my entire bedding until the weekend.  After washing the pillowcases, I'd find a few hours after going to sleep, I'd wake up with severe coughing fits.  Thinking I'd just re-infected them with my cold somehow, I washed them again with all my bedding - blankets, cover, etc.  That evening, and every evening since, I continue to wake up within hours of retiring to bed with this severe coughing.  

My cat, who've I've had for about 4 years, is a heat hog and generally sleeps on my legs every night.  I woke up Monday morning, after doing all the linens the evening before, to find she wasn't on the bed but instead hiding under the bed.  She finally surfaced and was running around all over - top speed like something was chasing her.  She'd cower down in the middle of the floor, run, stop, lick frantically at her foot, her back, run, stop, lick again.  I went to pet her and she acted like I was going to hurt her, running from my hand.  Thinking she might have just fallen off the bed and hurt herself, I went to work and returned home to find her in the same condition.  She eventually came to me and sat on my lap for about 2 hours, getting up every few minutes to move like she just wasn't comfortable.  I contacted a vet friend to see if I needed to get her to an emergency clinic, and after discussing everything, she advised giving her a small amount of [REDACTED], which I did.  Before going to bed, I put the old heavier blanket on the bed which I hadn't laundered yet and woke to find her sleeping between my legs again.  Upon waking up, again a few hours after going to bed, in a severe coughing fit, I thought about the dryer sheets and removed them from all of my pillows.  Coughing stopped and I was able to get back to sleep.

I've done a little research online and am surprised to find dryer sheets aren't regulated with regards to what they can put on them (in them).  As both my cat and I had reactions to Bounce Dryer Sheets specifically (which I'd be happy to give up the remainder of the box if you'd like it for testing), 

Thankfully, I'd just spent the weekend at my boyfriend's house and did the bulk of my clothing laundry at his house - with the exception of my bedding.

I like to think I'm an average healthy 40-year old individual this reaction to Bounce Dryer Sheets alarmed me and made me think how many parents may have lost a child to SIDS due to these unregulated dryer sheets?  The babies can't remove themselves or the sheets to get away from them.

My general health is good (aside from that cold), I have a few known allergies to medications where I get hives, but have no known respiratory issues.  My cat gets annual check ups, so I'd say she's in good general health as well.  I don't smoke, I don't live in a high air pollution area and neither of us had any issues with any other dryer sheets prior to introducing these Bounce Dryer Sheets to the household.
justification: Both the individual and the cat experienced adverse health effects (respiratory issues and contact dermatitis) but no long-term injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I am writing to inform you of a product malfunction with the Honeywell Surround Heat portable heater. Last night, 2/28/2015, the heater was in use and the thermostat set at the halfway mark. After about an hour of use, the thermostat triggered the heater to start up. I heard sputtering and then blue flames were visible through the vents at the bottom of the heater. The next moment, flames shot out of the base of the machine as I leaped out of my chair and disconnected the heater from the power source. I only removed this heater a week earlier from the bedroom my two young daughters share, and I can't even imagine the horror that could have possibly unfolded had this happened while they slept.
justification: The incident involved flames shooting out of the heater, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Lasko Brand -- Cyclonic Digital Ceramic Space Heater Model 5841

We have been using this space heater at home for the last few cold months.  Recently it was placed bedside.  Last night, I awoke to a strange, foul smell.  Without turning on the lights, I tried to locate the source of the smell -- and not thinking straight, simply turned off the heater and went back to bed.  Forgetting about this incident, I turned the heater on again tonight.  The odor appeared within minutes, and I immediately turned off the unit and located the odor source.  The heater plug is connected to a heavy duty extension cord which is plugged into the wall behind the headboard of my bed -- and where that connection lay on the carpet, both the plug and the carpet were melting/melted.  What I smelled were the fumes of melting carpet and plastic.  The plugs of both the unit and the extension cord are fused/melted together (unable to be separated) and the carpet has a burn the size of a "cigarette burn."  I am certain if this unit was left in on in an unoccupied room, it would have eventually set fire to the carpet.
justification: The incident involved melting of plugs and carpet, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Shark Lift-Away Pro, Steam Pocket Mop S3901D at Bed Bath and Beyond two years ago and have enjoyed cleaning my floors with this steamer. On October 24, 2014 the Shark Steamer exploded.
Just before the machine exploded my employee said it had stopped making steam. We put more water in it and it seemed to make steam again. A few minutes later when I was in another room there was a loud, terrifying noise that sounded like an explosion. I was afraid to go into the room because I was not sure it was safe or what I would find. I wanted to check on my employee and found him visibly upset by the noise and the force of the explosion. His feet were scalded and the floor was damaged from the boiling water and steam. The Lift-Away water container of the Shark Steamer became unattached from the machine and shot a few feet Also the
cap came off the water container. Boiling water and steam were spewed two to three feet from the machine.
When I went online in Google, I was shocked that there were numerous complaints about Shark Steamers exploding. I have told the above story to some of my friends who have Shark Steamer and tried to warn them of this defective and dangerous equipment only to find that they also had Shark Steamers that stopped making
steam and exploded. I am shocked that this and other Shark Steamers have not been recalled and taken off the market The explosion indicated a clear and present danger. How can you sell products that are defective and dangerous?
I demand that your company pay all of the costs of damage to my property and employees injuries. I also demand that I am compensated for the cost of replacing this steamer with a machine that does not explode.
justification: The employee suffered scalded feet, indicating an injury, and there was property damage from the explosion.

incident_description:
(12/28/2014)The consumer stated that there was on item in the dryer. The setting was on delicate. After about ten or fifteen minutes, the consumer went back to the laundry room. Before she open the door, she detected a horrible smell. When she open the laundry door, there was smoke in the laundry room. The consumer turned off the fuse box and unplugged the dryer. The top and front of the dryer was very hot.

The consumer open the dryer and found no damage on the inside. The consumer had a repair technician to come out to check the unit. The technician advised the consumer that the electronic board had burned.

(01/2015) The consumer contacted Frigidaire and advised them of the problem. She was advised that they were not aware of a fire issue with the model of this dryer. She was also advised that the dryer was out of warranty. The consumer was advised that nothing could be done for her.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burned electronic board but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
18-ga lamp cord bought at Lowe's Glenville NY today. Lamp cord is meant to be separated into two insulated wires to allow attachment to (+) and (-) terminals in a lamp/appliance, and in a wall plug. When you separate the two wires, bare wire is exposed along the length where the two split apart. The insulation is too thin, so pulling the wires apart exposes bare copper along the length of the separation.
Using the wire in this condition is apt to allow bare wire to come into contact with ungrounded parts of the lamp or appliance. Lowes sells this wire by the foot from bulk spools.
[REDACTED]
justification: Exposed bare wire can lead to electrical hazards, but no injury or death is reported in the description.

incident_description: Gas stove fireplace model 8000TR-OAK-IPI glass shattered under normal use.
justification: Glass shattered under normal use poses a risk of injury from sharp fragments.

incident_description:
On October 27, 2014 we purchased a GTUP270GMWW which was delivered on November 11.  I had requested delayed delivery so I could clean and paint the area.
Approximately Feb 5th we noticed the dryer was not heating as it should, called for a service appt which was scheduled for Feb 11th at that time the technician diagnosed a faulty igniter.  He did not have one on his truck, so the order was placed.  
On February 21st the same technician showed up.  He took the front panel off and replaced the faulty igniter with the new one that was shipped to our house.  Before putting on the front panel he verified that the dryer indeed did warm up.  
6:45 PM Approximately 45 minutes after he left I placed a load of laundry to dry,  my wife asked me how many minutes I had put on the timer, I said 35, she then opened the dryer.  The smell of natural gas was starting to permeate the house.  I told my wife and grandson to get out.  I called 9-1-1.  I opened all doors to ventilateÃÂ  Fire Department was on scene quite quickly.  They came in and using a gas meter verified that indeed there was some type of gas leak.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common post-repair.

incident_description:
One year old washing machine exploded during normal use. The top of the washer unit itself separated from the frame of unit which became bent in many areas. Very loud noise and significant movement of washer from explosion. No personal injuries; however, damage to plaster wall behind washer, damage to dryer next to washer, and floor flooded from leaking washer. 

This was a very frightening and unexpected event. Defective product.

Product Information: Samsung top load washing machine for residential use- MODEL WA50F9A6SW/A2
justification: The incident involved a washing machine explosion causing property damage but no personal injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) given the description of a defective product but no indication of widespread occurrence.

incident_description:
Today our  washing machine, GE Front Load Washing Machine WCVH6260,  started smoking during normal use.  Luckily I was close enough to the machine to hear that something was wrong, and when I paused the machine smoke billowed out. 

I saw here that there are many others with similar complaints about the WCVH washers:

http://www.thepetitionsite.com/739/633/604/recall-ge-wcvh-front-loading-washing-machines-due-to-smoking-fire-hazard/

And that a similar model was recalled:

http://www.geappliances.com/products/recall/washer_2010/

If the components that caused the other model to be recalled are also in my WCVH 6260 machine (I don't know if they are), it would seem that my model should also be recalled so I would really appreciate your looking into this issue on its own account and on account of the possibility of the same issue being in my model as in the recalled product.

While no immediate injuries happened during our use, I'm not sure what that smoke's long term effects will be on those in the house at the time and I am lucky to have stopped the machine quickly so as to avoid further issues, which based on the other model's reports might have been actual fire in my home.
justification: The incident involved a smoking washing machine with no immediate injuries, but potential long-term effects are uncertain. Similar models have been recalled, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: I was home on a snowy day in Virginia.  My husband and I were napping when I smelled something funny.  We went around the house looking and smelling when we arrived to the electric heater.  It was the remote box melting and nearly on fire. We where lucky since it was minutes away from starting a fire.  It melted on the electrical outlet and the plug.  I am thankful this did not start a fire.  I was also surprise to see this was on recall. I bought this unit from Lowes and at the very least with the way technology is today I should have gotten letter by mail since my account is active from your company or theirs.  I am glad it a fire did not occur while I was asleep since this is the extra source I use when I do sleep.
justification: The incident involved a near-fire situation with no injury or death, and the likelihood is possible given the recall status and the circumstances described.

incident_description:
The product is a Bionaire space heater, Model: BFH3342M. 
The product was being used as an extra heat source for a bedroom in our downstairs. Our daughter was about to go to sleep with the heater running and she heard it making some noise. It got louder so she got up and it was sparking real bad and turning red and smelling like it was going to catch on fire.  She then unplugged it and came upstairs to show me. She was kind of frantic.  I plugged it in and it stated sparking immediately around one of the coils. It turned bright red and started to smell very bad. I definitely believe it would have caught on fire. If she had not have been in the room, I believe it could have caught on fire and worse case scenario, burned our house down. It's a scary thought. I doubt I will be buying another space heater of any kind for a while, if ever. This is the second winter we have had it. Our daughter is not using it but a few nights a week if that. She is only here a few nights a week because of her job. Scary!
justification: The heater was sparking and could have caught fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Brookstone Towel Warmer model number  647156 at least 8-10 years ago, so it is long out of warranty.  I accept that.

What I do not accept is the melting of the case and, consequently, possible electrical/plastic fire.  A couple of years ago the part of the case began to be distorted (as shown in the photograph attached) as if there was extreme heat underneath.  I can only presume that a heating element or other electrical component was shorting and/or overheating.  

I put it in the garage, notified the company, and, promptly, forgot about it.  When I came across it today, I remembered that I had intended to notify you as well.  Better late than ever, as I still would hate to see and injury or a fire started as a result of the problem in the towel warmer.

Thanks for your attention to this.

Cheers - [REDACTED]
justification: The towel warmer showed signs of overheating and potential fire risk, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I turned the HomeTouch model # PS-250 garment steamer on and it immediately began making a very loud sound. The base ignited within several seconds and shot sparks out, almost catching the floor on fire.  I was able to unplug the machine and it continued producing smoke. It was removed from the home without any further damage or injury. Steamer was approximately three years old and had a half full water tank at the time it caught on fire. It was plugged into a grounded outlet at the time.
justification: The incident involved a garment steamer catching fire and producing smoke, but no injuries or further damage occurred.

incident_description: I have been using my laptop HP Notebook 2000 using the cord provided. I noticed that my hands were red and burning but did not know why. I bought Aloe Vera, sunscreen, and other burn ointments, but it kept staying red and painful. I finally associated it with the notebook being hot and the air being hot, so got a stand with a cooling fan, thinking it was the laptop. This also did not work, so I started wearing  leather gloves with touch fingers thinking my hands were just ultra very sensitive. Finally, I called my landlady  numerous times, thinking her  internal wiring was old and causing overheating. In fact she was about to schedule an electrician. I never realized it was the cord itself that could be the cause of all this, though it does get hot. I thought that is just how it gets. I am so glad I found out and hope the new cord will eliminate the problem, though at this time my hands are still red, and though I wear gloves. I do my bills online and need to use the notebook constantly. I appreciate this coming to light and look forward to having protected use henceforth. I hope the problem goes away as my daughter kept saying to have a doctor see it, and I was due for an appointment so would have shown her it, also. Thanks!
justification: The incident describes red and burning hands due to a hot laptop cord, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Recently I have been having problems with my Lenovo Laptop maintaining a charge. The Laptop is a Thinkpad Edge. I thought that the battery may have had a problem but soon realized that the cord was not connecting. If you moved it ever so slightly it would turn back on. I thought there may have been a loose wire but before I could check it out further it started to smoke. I noticed there is a recall on the power cord already but my cord is not listed. My parents bought this computer for me a few years ago. I think it was in 2011 or 2012.  However upon further research on the power cord recall only the portion of the cord connecting to the wall and the adapter is being recalled. My problem exists between the adapter and the actually computer. The connection to the computer where the smoke started coming from is swollen and kind of bulging. It often got warm but I never really noticed until it sparked and smoked today that this may be a problem. If I had not been trying to figure out why my computer was not charging this could have started a fire in my home. My computer was plugged in and I often leave it unattended in a room where my young son is playing.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and sparking power cord, which could have led to a fire but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: We were using a Sunheat Portable heater to heat our daughters room which is a second story bedroom.  The thermostat was set to keep her room 60 degrees.  The heater did not run often as we burn wood and is used for supplemental heat.  On Sunday, February 15th, 2015, I awoke to a funny smell.  At the time it was faint but I could smell something.  I went to our basement thinking maybe someone laid something too close to our woodburner.  The smell was not in our basement.  I went back up to the main level and awoke my husband telling him something smelled like burning plastic.  He also immediately suspected the woodburner and I told him that I had already checked.  We checked the main floor and was unable to find the source.  I went to the second story, our oldest daughters bedroom.  Immediately after opening her bedroom door I could smell the burning plastic.  I immediately went and unplugged everything that was plugged in.  Plugged in items included an [REDACTED] in one outlet, a TV and DVD player in one, an [REDACTED] in one and the Sunheat heater in another.  The room stunk so bad and our daughter and her friend, both almost 15 years old, were asleep and unaware something was burning.  We woke them up and told them to get out.  We immedietly suspected the heater but when I unplugged it, it was not running, nor warm so we really didn't think it was the problem.  Unable to find where the smell was coming from we were ready to call the fire department but decided to remove the heater from the room and disassemble it.  Upon taking the heater to another room we could smell the same smell inside the heater.  We took the heater apart and realized that the quick connect for The power cord and the thermostat had melted and burned badly.  I called a few local dealers and they seemed to not be concerned.  I contacted the manufacturer and they stated they would send me an email showing us how to remove the quick connects and hard wire it.  No concern that it was a safety issue.  The employee I talked to stated it happens in some earlier heaters that they put the quick connect in.  We received the email showing us how to hard wire it but feel thhis is a major safety issue.  What if we had not been home??
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and potential fire hazard from a heater, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Pelonis portable Electric Radiator Heater model #Ho-0250h

on off switch sparking with melting plastic smell.
heater is 3 months old
justification: The heater's switch is sparking and emitting a melting plastic smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her two step, step stool purchased around October/November 2009. The caller states that she used the step stool to get in and out of her raised bed and had no problems with it until Tuesday, January 13, 2015 when she was standing on the step stool to adjust window shade.  After the window was adjusted she began to step down but the left side of the step stool broke off sending her falling to the right, hitting her wrist. 

The caller's husband drove her to the Tulane Medical Center Emergency in downtown Louisiana where she was diagnosed with a fracture of the right radius of her right wrist.  After approximately five to six hours, her bone was set, a cast was on her right wrist and she was instructed to be seen by an orthopedic physician to be sure the bone was healing properly.

The caller contacted the retailer/distributor January 16th, 2015  (manufacturer is in China).
This does not appear to be one of the stools recalled with release# 12-001.
justification: The caller suffered a fracture of the right radius, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I acquired a Bissell Spot Bot Pet Series carpet cleaner approximately 2 months ago, and have been using it regularly since its purchase, new.  Last evening, I put the appliance into use, as intended, and within a minute began to smell smoke.  I disconnected the unit from the power outlet, and examined it at which time more smoke began to emanate from the unit.  Fortunately, the unit was supervised on this occasion, and there was no loss besides the burned up motor and electrical components of the device.  I am concerned about the product's fire safety since it is intended to be used on the carpet of a home.
justification: The incident involved smoke and damage to the device but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as it happened once in regular use over two months.

incident_description: Smoke was reported coming from a bathroom ceiling ventilation fan. Fire crews found high heat was generated by old operating bathroom exhaust fan. Make and model of fan was same as previous fires in the neighborhood.
justification: Smoke was reported but no injury or death occurred; the same fan model has caused previous fires, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: This complaint is about a Husky utility knife (Model 1000 032 776, UPC # 820909972037) sold by Home's Depot.  I purchased this tool around July 2014.  The design of the knife allows the razor blade to rotate while applying downward cutting pressure, and  then the back side of the blade slides out between the 2 halves of the housing, and cutting the operators fingers in the process.  I tried going to the website listed on the package, but the website is no longer available.
justification: The description indicates the knife design causes the blade to slide out and cut the operator's fingers, resulting in injury.

incident_description: Our General Electric Dryer Model GHDS365EFRR Serial Number GA949178G stopped working January 5, 2015.  We called to have it repaired.  The repairman pulled the front panel and discovered the cause of the failure was a wire harness fire.  We were lucky that the fire was contained by the sheet metal and no clothes were in the dryer at the time.
justification: The incident involved a wire harness fire but was contained by sheet metal, causing no injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer was notified by [REDACTED], her home contractor, that her unit was affected by recall #15-026. The consumer contacted the firm and requested the remedy. The consumer received the part and on 01/02/15 (estimated) the unit was repaired. 

On 01/25/15 the consumer noticed a blinking light on the unit. The consumer saw error code "A7" and according to the manual it means a Gas Valve Failure. 

The consumer has not contacted the firm but she informed her contractor of this issue. On 01/26/15 [REDACTED] spoke with the firm and the company who sold him the unit. [REDACTED] has not been able to speak with anyone that can assist with getting the unit repaired. 

The consumer is concerned about her safety and would like her unit working properly.

The Rep. that sold the unit to Bi Lo Supply has not returned calls to the consumer's contractor [REDACTED] [REDACTED]   The consumer has not had hot water since 1-25-14.  No one is willing to help get this problem solved.  The consumer does not want to put more money in this unit, as she has only heard bad reports on this unit.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning unit with a gas valve failure, posing a potential safety risk but no actual injury or death reported.

incident_description: Kohler glass shower door model# KT02206MXAB shattered when I was in another room.
justification: The shower door shattered but no one was injured as the person was in another room.

incident_description: The DeLonghi oil heater was plugged in the kitchen set on low. When we turned it to high the plug melted down and destroyed the outlet.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted plug and outlet) but no reported injuries.

incident_description: outdoor ceiling light / fan installed at deck area near pool in backyard.  The light shade is made out of glass!  Shade broke and injured family member several places.  I strongly believe it is not safe for outdoors use, especially around the pool area and kids playing around bare foot...
justification: The glass shade broke and caused injuries, indicating a severity level of 3. Given the outdoor and poolside location, recurrence is likely if not addressed.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she plugged in the heater. The consumer was reading the paper and smelled something burning. The consumer stated that the smell became stronger. She looked over to the heater and noticed that it was smoking and sparking. The consumer unplugged the heater right away.

The consumer stated that the heater was on for less than 30 minutes. The consumer stated that she does not use the heater as much.

The consumer stated that she has COPD and the smoke made it hard for her to breathe.

The consumer contacted the retailer and they refused to offer a refund. The consumer was informed by the retailer that her model is not included in a recall. They informed her to contact the manf.

The consumer contacted the manf. They informed her that they will replace the unit. The consumer does not want a replacement heater, she would like a refund. They did not offer a refund.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and sparking heater, causing breathing difficulties due to smoke inhalation, but no direct injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Electric cord on pedestal space heater sparked with a small flame at heated connection site.
justification: The incident involved a spark and small flame but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On February 3 at 4:40 AM, my tempered glass shower door shattered on its own.

It was a frightening experience.

The manufacturer/supplier as well as the installer are brushing it off, saying 'it just happens'.

I don't think it just happens. From articles online, I believe our glass door is an unsafe product. Articles state that a manufacturing flaw, or improper installation are the leading causes of tempered glass doors shattering.

I believe I have encountered an unsafe product.
justification: The incident involved a shattered shower door but no injury was reported, and similar incidents are possible based on the description.

incident_description: House fire with 70% of our house destroyed
justification: A house fire causing 70% destruction is a significant incident but the description does not mention any injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: The power switch on the fireplace kept getting harder to turn off and on more than usual. Yesterday when turning it off it clicked and was very loose. Today when I went to turn it on the switch was still lose and it began sparking, I immediately unplugged the unit before it could have caught fire.
justification: The incident involved sparking and a loose switch, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Newest [REDACTED] XM-L2 Ultra-Portable LED High Bright Work Light on February 8th, 2015.  I plugged the device in to charge and after about six hours one of the three batteries exploded.  Debris was spread over a 15 foot radius around my garage and battery filaments burned through other plastic and wood/paper items.  It appears that the battery exploded, burst out of the device housing, and bounced around the garage spraying hot debris and causing damage. This incident happened on 2/16/15 and I reported it to the merchant, Amazon, on 2/18/15.  I took pictures of the damage and can send them if needed.  I also recommended to Amazon that I not return the item as the remaining two batteries appear damaged and could exploded or catch fire.
justification: The battery explosion caused significant property damage but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My husband and I just had a new bathroom installed. Our tiler put in the new sliding shower doors and they worked fine. Tonight,  Feb. 17th, my husband closed one of the shower doors and it shattered into a million pieces. He closed the door gently, so he was shocked when it burst apart.  The whole family came running to see what had happened, only to see a floor covered in glass. We purchased the doors at Lowe's.  The company who makes the doors is Style Selections.  

Funny, because there were 2 other complaints about these doors exploding on Lowe's website reviews. They are a danger.
justification: The shower door shattered, posing a risk of injury, but no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description: Heater will not shut off and overheats. This is a fire hazzard
justification: The heater overheating is a fire hazard, which could lead to an incident but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description:
ON 2-3-2015 AT ABOUT 1600 HRS, MY GRANDDAUGHTER WAS REACHING FOR A BANANA ON TOP OF THIS PORTABLE KITCHEN ISLAND,THE ISLAND TIPPED OVER AND LANDED ON HER, SHE HAS A BROKEN BONE ON HER RIGHT THIGH AREA, THE ISLAND HAS A GRANITE TOP THAT WEIGHTS ABOUT 40 LBS,PART OF THIS GRANITE TOP LANDED ON HER RIGHT LEG 
THIS GRANITE TOP SITS ON TOP OF THE ISLAND WITH ONLY 2 DOWELS
justification: The incident resulted in a broken bone, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the unstable nature of the kitchen island.

incident_description: Would like to report a problem with a gas clothes dryer, set on sensor cycle to dry clothes and it would shut off after 2-3 minutes.  Detected a faint smell of something burning, called repair service and repairman removed front panel on dryer and determined combustion (fire) had taken place in a sealed area of the unit, wires where melted along with a harness.  We are still going back and forth with Sansung as dryer is only 2years 8 mos old..  We would like one of your field reps to look at it if possible.  We have since replaced the dryer with a different brand.  The old dryer is in the garage for inspection...if you are not concerned we will dispose of the old dryer in the junk yard.  Please advise as we feel this is a product defect and a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard in a dryer, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
(01/02/2015) The consumer stated that he was asleep in bed. He heard a bang and discovered that the shower door had shattered. The glass from the shower door was still popping when he went to inspect the noise. 

The consumer stated that the shower had not been used since earlier in the day.

(1/05/2015) The consumer called the company and advised them of what happened. He was advised that there was nothing that they could do. 

The consumer added that pictures were e-mailed to {REDACTED], the local investigator...
justification: The shower door shattered but there was no injury reported, only property damage.

incident_description: I was at home and the breaker kicked off, I started smelling smoke, found the source, it was the plug that had melted into the plugin. I called the heat/air folks and they came out to replace it cost me almost $200.00 for emergency call, trip fee, and repair.
justification: The incident involved a melted plug and smoke, but no injury or death occurred. Such electrical issues are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description: We had a fire and the extinguisher failed to
justification: A fire occurred but the description does not mention any injuries or deaths, only that the extinguisher failed.

incident_description: While trying to open a reusable ziptie, the blade on my Leatherman Wingman Multitool closed on my left index finger, deeply cutting my left index finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut to the finger, which qualifies as an injury. The likelihood is possible given the nature of handling sharp tools.

incident_description: Performax model #90206, Serial # W071105, switch was activated, switch sparked, motor emitted sparks, motor does not turn off when switch released, no injuries. saw continues to run unless unplugged; plugging saw in causes motor to run, spark and smell. Safety brake does not engage.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction with sparks and a motor that wouldn't turn off, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Purchased walk in bathtub  wife was sitting in possibly half the tub of water, water is lower than seat.

Caller's wife was going to stand, used the bar to brace herself but her feet slid out causing her to fall.

The bar should give her leverage and floor is supposed to be slip free.

The bar held but the floor was not slip free.

The caller's wife sustained minor injuries including left foot and left knee bruising then back and tailbone bruising and pain.

The caller's wife treated herself the first week, just taking pain pills but the pain was too bad for self treatment.

He took his wife to the physician who obtained xrays to be sure there were no broken bones and advised the caller to continue taking the pain pills.

The callers spoke with the manufacturer January 20th, 2015, spoke with [REDACTED] and on the 21st, caller doesn't remember name of representative.  January 22nd, he spoke with [REDACTED] who was a manager but of no assistance.

He will try again but does plan to contact Consumer Protection.

Submitter added [REDACTED] called him on 2/5/15 and said she ordered the part for his tub and as soon as it comes in she will call them to set a date to have it installed..Submitter noted today in 2/9/15 and they have not heard from her.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries including bruising and pain, requiring medical attention, which fits severity level 3.

incident_description: I intended to put away our Rowenta DX1700 iron. It has an auto-off feature that shuts off the iron after 8 minutes, so even though it was plugged in I assumed it was safe to handle. I was picking up the iron to wrap the cord and burned my hand. I asked my wife - and she hadn't used the iron for many days.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, which qualifies as severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the auto-off feature may not always prevent burns if the iron is still hot.

incident_description: I have a LG gas dryer model #  DLG2702V and I started smelling a strong smell of raw gas during operation. I searched the internet for answers and found a lot of people having the same extremely dangerous issue. I can't believe LG is ignoring this issue. the control panel will tell the gas valve to open with out the igniter being on therefore pumping gas into the dryer and out the vent.

incident_description:
Caller purchased an gas fireplace in 2009 and had no problems with it until sometime around the middle of October 2014 while he was conducting a pre season cleaning and noticed a faint smell of gas.
There are two sets of burners in this gas log set, one in the rear that burns high flames then ones in the front are lower flames. 
There is a rock wool fabric that is used to cover the first set of burners.
If there is a smidgeon of a gap then all exposed areas do not light.  If the wool moves very slightly it could possibly uncover one of the holes.
When the holes are not lit or are uncovered then they are still emitting gas which presents a gas leak.

The manual does not impress how important it is to place the wool in order to ensure all holes properly light.  It also does not encourage replacement or monitoring.  The caller's 5 year old wool was deteriorating.  The caller found that properly placed wool will move over the course of several lightings and thus cause a hole to be exposed, unlit, and leaking gas.  It seems like the moveable part (wool) is critical to proper lighting.

There have been no injuries at this time

The caller has still been using this fireplace but being very careful that all holes that leak gas are lit.  The caller checks the wool placement each time!
Caller has been advised that he should consider not using the fireplace at this stage.

He contacted the retailer who sent him extra rock wool.  The retailer indicated how the wool can move & thus not light correctly.  Page 76 of the manual does not clearly explain the placement of the wool and how they must touch to create a chain effect & properly light the holes.
 
He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak risk due to deteriorating and improperly placed rock wool, but no injuries have occurred.

incident_description:
Sunguard is an additive that you add to your clothes in the washing cycle to increase UV protection.  Phoenix Brands markets Sunguard as safe for sensitive skin.  I'd received a box of Sunguard sun protection and also bought some in the middle of July, after internet searching that showed various organizations supporting Sunguard's use and no seeming problems.  

I spent the balance of the summer nauseated with burning skin, sinusitis, cysts, and fatigue.  I thought my sunblock (I'd used for 10 years) was no longer viable.  I tried others and none seemed to work.    I stayed inside; but that didn't matter--just simple trip to the market, outside for 10 minutes and I'd burn.

I covered up when I went out.  Sunblock first and then a Sunguard-soaked gaiter.   Still! burned.

I thought I was going crazy.   My hat (also treated with Sunguard) didn't seem to protect me. Though covered, my forehead was burning.  So I took Sunguard treated material and sewed it into the hat.  My eyes were all burned so I bought new sunglasses.  

I called all companies of products I used. Sunguard reps told me it couldn't be Sunguard as Sunguard was really safe.

I contacted the FDA to see what could be going on.

I continued to try new sunblocks. Nothing helped.

It was after I sewed material under the hat that I developed cysts on my head.   When I developed a lump on the upper part of my neck, I knew I had to see a doctor.   

I was relieved to find out it was just a cyst.   And that's when I knew it was Sunguard.

Within a week of not wearing or touching (because I would transfer the chemical from my clothes to my skin...face, etc...and I was using Sunguard treated material to wipe my skin in the hot sun) I was healed of sinusitis burning and general malaise.  My cysts began to disappear.

Then I did deeper research. The msds sheet on [REDACTED] shows it to be considered a harsh chemical.  The report on file in Australia (1999) shows that this chemical produced skin and eye irritation  in animals (exactly what I experienced) ...and at higher doses, death.

I've continually asked the company through its [REDACTED] agent for studies that support their 'good for sensitive skin' claim.  But none seem to exist.

At this point, my skin has not recovered.  My eyes and other skin parts seem stained and damaged.
And the worst part seems to be dealing with a company that doesn't seem to care about the harm it can do.

I'm not sure about filling out the below.   I was harmed the entire time I used Sunguard but finally figured out it was that the beginning of Sept.(when submitting supportive documents, the cpsc injury clearinghouse reps said that they didn't recognize my report number, so am submitting again)
justification: The user experienced significant skin and eye irritation, cysts, and other health issues directly linked to the use of Sunguard, indicating a clear injury.

incident_description:
In September 2014 I purchased around 70  Step/Down transformers via Amazon.  There were all branded Power Bright and ranged from 100W to 3000w.   As a matter of course, we decided to check these to ensure they were safe.  I had an electrical engineer check them over.   He made the following comments:

"At all times, both the 240v and 110v outlet sockets are live. The power switch and fuse have been placed on the neutral line. Blue indicates neutral; the brown (phase) line should be running to the fuse holder, and from there to the power switch. This means that even if the power switch is turned off or the fuse blows, the full input voltage (240v in this case)) is present on both output sockets (even the 110v socket), and on any equipment plugged into them. Even given that earth is set up correctly for an autotransformer, this is fairly dangerous."

Hi primary concern was that the fuse was not on the phase line in and therefore,  the unit still remained live - even when the fuse was blown etc.  There is nothing to ensure the feed of live electricity is cut in the event of a fault. 

As I mentioned above,  these are branded Power Bright but I understand are made by a company called Gold Source  for Power Bright.   They are sold via Amazon under both brand names.  See the following links

http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0022U0MSQ/ref=s9_simh_gw_p23_d0_i2?pf_rd_m=ATVPDKIKX0DER&pf_rd_s=desktop-1&pf_rd_r=1QACP0WN16EH0ZT2GW72&pf_rd_t=36701&pf_rd_p=1970559082&pf_rd_i=desktop

http://www.amazon.com/Bright-VC3000W-Voltage-Transformer-converter/dp/B000MY02LQ/ref=sr_1_8?s=electronics&ie=UTF8&qid=1423006521&sr=1-8&keywords=Power+bright&pebp=1423006525824&peasin=B000MY02LQ
justification: The incident describes a dangerous electrical fault in the transformers, but no actual injury or death occurred.

A day later the consumer discovered that one of the contacts on the underside of the vacuum had melted into the plastic housing and was depressed by nearly ÃÂ¼ inch. 

The consumer indicates that during charging, one would typically leave the unit alone for an hour or more. He is concerned because if the unit gets hot enough to create a burn blister to his fingers, he believes it could get hot enough to set fire to rugs, drapes, paper, etc. The consumer indicates that he uses his unit once a week but that it is charged six times a week after he vacuums each room (which is when the unit overheats, when it is being charged).

incident_description:
We installed 4 sheets of pine subfloor on January 2, 2015.  The product was sold as "no added urea formaldehyde".  The person cutting the plywood had a low grade fever and nausea for two days after exposure to the sawdust.  A person living in the home experienced low grade fever with increasing swelling over the entire body including shortness of breath by the eighth day when they left the home and showed symptom improvement within two hours.

The product was removed from the home and one person helping with the removal experienced sinus swelling from their brief exposure to the product.  All people adversely affected routinely use building products with no adverse effects.  

The Lowe's receipt shows product
                            12249  23/32  Sturdifloor T&Groov

Sturdifloor website appears to suggest that the product may contain melamine formaldehyde. Any person trying to avoid fromaldehyde could be at great risk.  It makes us nervous that the product can be sold by Lowe's with a product description stating, "Contains no added urea formaldehyde."   The product was also listed as, " Exempt from the world's leading formaldehyde emission standards and regulations due to very low emission rates."

The person living in the home, and home at all times, has a diagnosed allergy to formaldehyde and had no reason to suspect formaldehyde as present in a form other than "urea formaldehyde."  We find the Lowe's listing to be intentionally misleading on the subject of formaldehyde content and potentially dangerous to those with a known formaldehyde problem.
justification: Multiple individuals experienced adverse health effects including fever, nausea, swelling, and shortness of breath due to formaldehyde exposure, indicating injury.

incident_description:
Febreze Inhalation Injury
[REDACTED], Oct. 16, 2014


Additional Comments that may help to better understand the problem:

An exchange student is living with us. He is very sensitive to bad smells and likes to use air fresheners. Since the bathroom that he and another exchange student share opens into his bedroom, he uses A LOT of air fresheners. After the incident, he threw away 7 recently emptied cans: 4 [REDACTED], 1 Febreze Hawaian and 2 Febreze Air effects Linen and Sky, which was the product used when symptoms occurred.
There had been problems in the bathroom a week prior to the main incident. After working on it in the evening, I had tightness in my lungs which I attributed to mold exposure. It went away on its own by next morning. I had to keep walking through the Febreze saturated bedroom to work on the bathroom but thought nothing of it. (No irritating chemicals were used in cleanup, only [REDACTED] water which I had utilized before without ill effect)

On the 16th, I had been working hard outside, walked into the kitchen/dining area and noticed a strong Febreze smell. The student had fixed himself food and was sitting at the table eating. He had sprayed an entire can of Febreze Linen and Sky upstairs and it clung to him (he had not used it downstairs). Almost immediately my lungs (bronchii - I'm a nurse) clenched up (worse than the week before) and I opened windows then left for a brisk one mile walk to air out my lungs. However, that did not help. Then I drank 2+ liters of water with lemon juice to try and flush out the irritants.
By morning, it was not better, so I got worried, called P&G hotline and was advised to go see a doctor.
I went to the ER where I was diagnosed with an inhalation injury.
I was unable to finish the outdoor work I had started, spent a whole day at Urgent Care/ER/Pharmacy and missed another full day due to extreme fatigue either from the [REDACTED] or the injury itself. 
There were 2 milder repeat incidents 10/25 and 10/27 even though no more product was actively used, due to smelly residue on furniture, clothes, book bag. 
Then I spent several hours at my DoctorÃÂs office for a follow up visit.
IÃÂm still waiting to see if this will be an ongoing issue, I have been unable to use certain restrooms which were saturated with air freshener.

I had no respiratory issues, asthma or bronchitis before this; very healthy.

My main complaint against Febreze is that there is no warning against spraying for more than a few seconds or even using the entire can in one shot.
justification: The incident resulted in an inhalation injury requiring medical attention, but no death or long-term effects were confirmed. The likelihood is unlikely as it involved excessive use of air fresheners in a specific scenario.

incident_description:
FIRE HAZARD! - When the ceiling fan was turned on at the wall switch a loud pop was heard.  The circuit breaker was found in the tripped position.  The circuit breaker was reset and the wall switch was turned back on.  The ceiling fan blades rotated but the light did not illuminate.  The voltage at the light bulb socket measured 75 vac.

The metal cap on the metal switch housing was removed.  Soot was observed on the wiring and the inside housing surfaces.  The insulation on the black wire to the light bulb was indented, partially melted, and ruptured.  On the cap, to which the light bulb socket bracket attaches, small metal beads and a pit, indicative of arcing, were observed.  It was also observed that the crimp on the bracket, which attaches to the housing cap, contained sharp edges.  The sharp edges of the bracket along with the tight packing of the wires inside the housing resulted in the abrading of the wire insulation.  As a result bare wire contacted the bracket crimp resulting in arcing and tripping of the circuit breaker.

An identical fan purchased at the same time and used in another room was disassembled and the same sharp edges were observed on the bracket crimp.  The sharp edges on the bracket crimp were created during the manufacturing process.  The electrical short was caused by the manufacturer making a defective crimp on the bracket.

This is a serious problem and could have resulted in a fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to a manufacturing defect, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Late Nov. 2012, I purchased through Lowes Web-Site a Wire stripping/cutting tool to replace my old ones. According the web-site there were NO hazards or warning to this tool purchased from their Electrical dept. The tool look very close to my old one and look insulated. The tool was purchased, ordered and picked up from Lowes (by our employee) and delivered to my desk. I saw this tool later on in the day on my desk. I picked up the tool, inspected the spring, took off my gloves and placed them inside my tool bag. On March 1st 2013 I went to use them for the first time feeling very confident this tool will do the job required, as I trusted products before even by other companies. I was electrocuted with 277volts,  passed out while on a 8 foot ladder as the electricity held on to me. I came to laying on the concrete with my right foot in pain. Was taken to the Hospital, and they stated the heel had multi-fractures needed surgery as soon as possible. The following Tuesday my Wife pick up my tools from Security Office and brought them home. I examined the wire strippers, grab a magnifier and saw small writing on the inside handle written in yellow the same color as the handle itself (yellow) "Warning do not use on live circuits". I called the employee who has delivered the tool to my desk and asked, were there any labels, signage or anything that would have indicated warnings? The answer was No, the way they left it on my desk is how it was picked up from Lowes. The tool was manufactured by Ideal Co. USA. I called Lowes later within 2 months after the incident and man stated it was a manufacturer/product issue and they were not going to do anything about it. So, in my opinion Lowes falsified/failed to warn of this product regardless just to sell a product and not be concerned at all about Safety.
 If anyone knows of a Florida Attorney that would assist me in this issue, please have them contact me.
Thank You, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury requiring surgery due to electrocution and a fall from a ladder.
