incident_description:
On 8-27-14 a metal grill brush wire became imbedded into a hamburger that I had cooked on my grill. The wire was ingested by myself and became lodge in the right side of my throat. The grill brush that it came from was made by the Grill Shop. The brush was only a few months in use. I had used the brush to clean my grill prior to starting it that day.

After the wire became lodged in my throat, I felt a great deal of pain. I have had the following exams, procedure and surgeries due to this.

Visit to Ear, Nose and Throat specialist x 3 visits.  Will have a 4th visit January, 2014. 
CT scan x 3
Xray x 1
Nasal endoscopy & Laryngoscopy x 2
Pre-op examination and lab work.
Attempt to remove a the foreign body with general anesthesia on 12-1-14. This was unsuccessful.
Second attempt to remove the foreign body with general anesthesia and stealth guided CT on 12-4-14. This surgery  was successful,but difficult.  It lasted greater than 5 hours.
Hospitalization for management of pain control and airway monitoring x 1 day.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injury requiring multiple medical procedures and surgeries, but no death occurred.

incident_description: Purchased AC Adapter for Euro-pro V1730 sweeper on E-Bay. Item number 141296611497, AC adapter for Euro-Pro V1730. Seller name utopiadreamglobal. Adapter first sent did not work. The second adapter set fire to my Euro-Pro sweeper. It set the battery compartment on fire, burn, leaked the batteries and melted the plastic on the sweeper. If I was not home my house could have caught on fire. I filing this complaint to let you know of this fire hazard. I E-mailed the seller also.  This adapter in not UL listed.
justification: The AC adapter caused a fire, damaging the sweeper and posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(12/25/14)  The fireplace was in the "off" position.  The plug was in the wall and the consumer was attempting to turn on the fireplace using the remote, but it would not come on.  She then tried moving the electric cord around and she heard what resembled a sizzling sound.  She also saw smoke and noticed a burning odor from the receiver.  The top portion of the receiver has melted.  The damage was definitely limited to the receiver.  The consumer immediately unplugged the receiver.

There were no injuries.

(12/26/14)  The consumer was searching the Internet and she found the recall CAP# 10-167.  Her model number and the date of purchase appear to match the recall.


120 V A/C, 60 Hz output, 120 input, 400 watts, UL Listed 10Z1  E110084.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting but no injuries, matching severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the recall match and the described malfunction.

incident_description: I have an American Standard Furnace model number TXC042C4HPC0 S/N 5222XXY5G I awoke in the morning to a cold home but the furnace was on. I felt over a vent only to feel cold air being pushed by the fan. I went into the utility room to the smell of burnt plastic. I noticed the drain hose that runs long the top of the unit was melted. I shut off power to the unit and opened up the front panel. What I saw was all four burners still lit with flames coming out of the manifold burning the top of the unit. The limiter wires which ran over the top of the right most burner has been burned up by the flames. I immediately shut off the gas at the valve. What I discovered is the gas valve a "Gemini" model 36G24 Type 205 had stuck in a "Open" position which was dangerous. Gas Valve SN: TRANE C341949P01. These valves are supposed to be designed to fail "close". Had it not been for luck that I choose to go to work late this could have burned down my house. I called a local HVAC company and we were able to test and replicate the problem. The manufacturer the technician contacted recommended we replace the valve. These Gemini gas valves are dangerous and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction of the furnace that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
[REDACTED] was severely injured by a washing machine which exploded from suspected mechanical failure in or about October 2013. The washer had been purchased in or about June 2013.

[REDACTED] stood nearby waiting to take clothes out of the adjacent dryer when she was injured. The washing machine was believed to be completing its final minutes of high-speed spin cycle, when suddenly and without warning it violently exploded and the top of the washing machine separate from the bottom. The washer lid flew off the machine and violently slammed into [REDACTED] on her lower left back, causing [REDACTED] to collide into a cabinet, where she struck her head, neck, upper body, chin and jaw, and then fell to the floor.  The entire washer lifted approximately three (3ÃÂ) to six (6ÃÂ) inches off the ground, spun 180 degrees, striking [REDACTED], damaging the wall, and striking the side of the dryer before landing on the floor away from its original location.

[REDACTED] took pictures of her injuries, the washer and the damage caused to the wall.
justification: The description details severe injuries caused by the washing machine explosion, including head, neck, and body impacts, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her vacuum cleaner ordered November 27th, 2014 and received December 9th, 2014.
The caller had assembled it and tried it but was suprised to find that it shocked her.
Three other persons in her household tried the vacuum and it shocked them also.

There are no injuries to be reported.

She contacted the maufacturer 12/15/2014 and was advised to put it away so that no one else could use it.
She is waiting for a return call from the manufacturer after submission to claims
justification: The vacuum cleaner shocked multiple people but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I purchased the HAAN professional steam cleaner for multipurpose cleaning model number MS-35.  On the second day of use the steam exploded from the flexible hose where it connects to the handle.  The steam burned under my arm when it exploded.  I did not need medical attention.  However, if it had been on my face or an area not covered in clothing, it could have been severe.  I did call the company and asked that they let their engineering team know of this incident.  I was told they would be in contact about the incident, but have heard nothing back.  I have since returned it to costco but have kept photos of the damaged hose.
Thanks,
[REDACTED]
justification: The steam explosion caused a burn injury, but no medical attention was required. The incident suggests a possible but not certain likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The glass shower door exploded.  Thankfully, no one was in the room at the time, but I have 3 small children.  The glass was everywhere.  Inside the shower stall and all over the bathroom floor.  There was hardly any glass left in the frame.
justification: The glass shower door exploded, but no one was present, resulting in no injury.

incident_description:
The unit worked fine when performing a testing the power consumption for a few minutes. However, you may run into a problem when was using the Kill A Watt to test or monitor the power used on a  device for an extended period of time. The unit is rated at 1875 watts ( Max Current 15 Amp and Max Voltage if 125 VAC ) 
In my particular case the receptacle on the Kill A Watt began to melt and turn brown when attached to a device that draws about 1,311 watts which is way below the maximum ratings of the Kill O Watt.
justification: The incident involved a receptacle melting, which is a physical incident but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
My Lennox Gas Fireplace was acting oddly.  First it would not come on, thought it was the remote, then it came on and appeared to be working normally.  Then it pulsed on and off several times.
Internet search highlighted the recall

Model
Lennox MLDVT-40NE
Serial number starts with 6412H4
justification: The fireplace malfunctioned but there was no injury or death, fitting the criteria for severity level 2. The recall suggests this issue is not rare.

incident_description: At approx. 3:00 p.m. EST the shower door "exploded" and shattered into thousands of pieces.  No one or animal was in the bathroom at the time and the shower had not been used in 18 hours.  So luckily no one was injured but I can image in the terror and injury if someone had been in the shower at the time.
justification: The shower door shattered but no one was present, resulting in no injury.

incident_description: While conducting a routine pre-sale home inspection, three same model combination smoke/carbon monoxide alarms failed to activate when the test button was depressed and when canned smoke was sprayed. This same scenario has occurred involving the same model alarms during past home inspections I have conducted.
justification: The smoke/carbon monoxide alarms failed to activate, posing a potential safety risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Sunbeam Turbo Steam Master Professional Iron

Model GCSBCS-100
Manufactured in 2011


The unit was plugged in but the dial was set firmly in the "off" position. The unit began beeping at random times. Consumer unplugged the unit to attempt to reset. This is an extreme fire hazard, as the iron should not turn itself on - ever. . This data has been conveyed to the Manufacturer, SunBeam, and theit holding company, Jarden.
justification: The iron turning itself on poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: OEM YELLOW POWER CORD for ProTeam CoachVac vacuums. I bought 2 of these vacuums in 2010. This year, BOTH of their power cords went--one "burned out" the end of the cord; the other bursted into an electrical fire! These cords have a bad knack of twisting tightly, pulling & breaking the wires inside. I've been cleaning for 15 years and never had any power cord issues with other cords. The incident date listed below is for the 2nd one--the one that caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved power cords burning out and catching fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
(12/14/2014) The consumer stated that when she returned from church she discovered that the shower door had shattered. No one was at home at the time that it happened.

The temperature in the room was between 68 and 70 degrees.


The consumer will contact the company.
justification: The shower door shattered but no one was present, so there was no injury.

incident_description:
We were using the Dream Baby "Secure-A-Lock" cabinet locks (UPC = 878931007128) to keep our 2 year old out of our household chemicals cabinet under our kitchen sink and our games cabinet in our living room, which contained many games with small parts such as dice.

My 2 year old broke both of these cabinet locks simply by pulling on them. They both snapped in half, allowing her to gain access to the dangerous items within the cabinets. This safety lock is a hazard because it fails to do its job as we trusted it to do. In both cases, our child was unhurt, but I feel that this product should be removed from the market and improved.
justification: The child was unhurt but the locks failed, allowing access to dangerous items, which constitutes an incident without injury.

incident_description:
First Alert Carbon Monoxide Alarm Model CO606

Attached power module (UNI-SAN New Dynamic Electron CO Model UP-IAD-12A)

Power model is physically attached and converts AC to DC/12V.  Module became overheated,
plastic case holding AC power leads melted.

Fire hazzard.
justification: The power module overheated and melted, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Was using a soda stream penguin carbonation machine.  Have had the machine approx 3 years. Afer the second injection of CO2, the glass carafe exploded into hundreds of pieces.  Even though the carafe is enclosed in a structure during the carbonization process, sharp pieces of glass escaped and hit my wife.  While she was not hit in the face, that was by luck.  There were enough pieces and enough force that she could have been substantially injured.

We reported it to the company last week (via email to their support center) and got no response.

incident_description:
This product is called "The Clapper" and is advertised on television and sold in many retail stores including "As Seen on TV".

The Clapper plugs into an electrical outlet. A light or other small home appliance is plugged into The Clapper. The user can turn the light (or other appliance) on/off by clapping their hands.

We were using The Clapper with a small table lamp (75W incandescent bulb).

The Clapper was purchased new at a retail store. It was given as a gift to my 11 year-old son for use in his bedroom. On the first use out of the box, The Clapper was plugged in as described above. 

The next morning we went into my son's room and there was a very apparent electrical smell. We located the source as The Clapper which was still plugged into the outlet. The Clapper actually melted and appears to have burned the outside housing containing the electrical parts.

The Clapper is a fire hazard. We feel that we are very lucky that the damage was not more significant. My son is scared to sleep in his room.
justification: The Clapper malfunctioned and melted, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: WE PURSHASED THE TIMBER TUFF TMW-10 LOGGING SAW HORSE ON DEC 11 2014, WE USED 1 TIME.  AFTER USING IT THE 2ND. TIME AND PLACING A LOG ON THE SAW HORSE THE WHOLE THING COLLASPED.  HITTING MY LEG CASUSING A CUT AND INJURING MY FOOT, CAUSING SWELLING AND BRUSING.  THIS THING IS A PEICES OF DANGEROUS JUNK, STATED IT CAN HOLD UP TO 150 POUNDS, THE LOG WE PUT ON IT WAS NO MORE THEN 60 POUNDS AT THE MOST, VERY DANGEROUS ITEM.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut, swelling, and bruising to the leg and foot, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The product failed under normal use conditions, suggesting a possible design or manufacturing flaw (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he received the unit on 02/3/12. He followed the manuel for set-up. The consumer plugged in an electric leaf blower and ran it for 10 minutes. The consumer shut it off afterward since the generator was working fine.

In 08/2012, the consumer started the generator and plugged in an electric leaf blower, ran it for 10 minutes and the put it away. The consumer just wanted to check that the unit was functioning.

The consumer lost power during hurricane Sandy. The consumer set up a heavy duty extension cord with the generator. The cord came into the house. The consumer plugged in a light and a refrigerator into the extention cord.  The generator ran for 1 hour. The engine started to rev up and down. The electrical powers began to surge. The consumer unplugged things from the extension cord and shut off the generator. The consumer let the generator cool down and started it up again. The consumer ran the generator for about an hour with the extention cord that had only the light plugged into it. The engine began to rev up and down. The power began to vary. The bulb and the light melted. 

The consumer shut everything down. 

The consumer ended up leaving the house until the power came back on.

The consumer started looking into who he can take the generator into for a repair. The consumer dropped of his generator at Empire Power Tools and Repair (Patterson, NY) on 11/3/12. The consumer stated that they could not figure out what the problem was. The consumer went back and forth with them multiple times. The consumer has in-depth notes from them. The consumer stated that they could not fix the unit. The consumer picked up his unit on 06/01/13.

The consumer contacted Generac in June-July of 2013. The consumer was contacted from Generac Account Manager for Sears, [REDACTED] on 07/23/13. The consumer was informed that he would look into the matter. The consumer had this conversation through text. The consumer was informed to bring the unit into Skid Steer Rental (Danbury, CT). 

The consumer took the unit to Skid Steer Rental on 8/10/13. The consumer followed up with them in fall of 2013. They informed him that they stopped working on his Generac unit because they were not being compensated for the time they spent on this unit even though they are an authorized service center. The consumer was informed that he can pay them for their time to get the unit back, even though the unit was not fixed. They still have the unit.

The consumer contacted the assistant attorney general in CT. The attorney general was contacted by staff attorney from Generac. The staff attorney provided incorrect information to the attorney general. They attorney general contacted the consumer and informed him that she can no longer assist with this since the consumer's unit was out of warranty.

The consumer stated that the attorney general was provided incorrect information about commercial warranty instead of residential warranty. The consumer stated that his unit was under warranty when Skid Steer Rentals had it for repair.

As of 08/9/14, the unit was still with Skid Steer Rental. The consumer is hoping that they still have his unit.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction and property damage (melted light bulb), but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Drill started to get hot seconds after starting to drill, was supporting top, vent area, with 2 fingers, by the time I let go, my 2 fingers were blackened by soot and slightly burnt.
Afterwards drill would not operate, I put battery into charger and now it will not charge.
justification: The incident resulted in slight burns to two fingers, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
We had noticed that a nightlight plugged into a GFCI occasionally flickered or went off when bumped.
This was in a downstairs, guest bathroom, next to a basin.
We decided to investigate, thinking maybe a loose connection.
When we removed the Decora trim plate, the white plastic front portion of the GFCI fell out, leaving dangerous line voltage exposed on internal parts within the grey rear portion.
We noticed that the portions of the front section, at the four corners, were broken at the point of attachment of the four screws which hold the front section against the back section. The plastic had apparently, over time, split due to the torque of the screws.
...
This led us to wonder about a second GFCI in another bathroom, upstairs, also next to a basin. My wife had noted that a device plugged in was no longer charging.
I determined that the GFCI needed to be reset. But it would not hold power on.
We removed the Decora trim plate, and saw the same problem as with the first unit - the front white plastic part of the GFCI had pulled away from the grey rear portion due to split plastic at the corners. This exposes dangerous line voltage.
Both of these dangerous GFCIs were manufactured by Leviton Mfg. Co., "Issue B114956".
The upstairs unit had a sticker, "Assd. 9D54L in Mexico 00575-L4 7".
...
We have replaced these two units with another manufacturer's product. However, there are multiple additional such units in our home, probably about six more. We bought them at Home Depot, date unknown.
justification: Exposed line voltage presents a clear hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The issue was found in multiple units, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: We responded to a small fire that filled the basement to the ceiling with smoke.  The Kidde Smoke Alarm (i9030) didn't sound even though the battery was in working condition.  The detector's date of manufacture was Mar 19, 2014.  After some investigation I found multiple one-star reviews on Amazon that stated the same issue.
justification: The smoke alarm failed to sound during a fire, but no injury was reported. Multiple similar complaints suggest this is a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
The fireplace came with the house the consumer purchased in 2006. The house was built in 2006.

The consumer stated that they have a wall switch that turns on the fireplace unit. The consumer turned on the wall switch and the fireplace exploded about five seconds later.

The consumer stated that the explosion was felt up to about 1/4 mile away.

The explosion blew the upper and lower vent. The consumer stated that it blew the content of the fireplace unit into the living room floor. The consumer stated that the glass of the fireplace is still intact but the lower hinges bent out of shape. This caused the door to swing open when the explosion occurred.

The consumer stated that the pilot light was on when the incident happened. The consumer called the fire department. They shut off the gas line. 

The consumer had the fireplace serviced on 11/3/14. The consumer stated that sometimes when they turned on the fireplace, it did not come on right away. The service tech from Gede (DE) cleaned the fireplace unit. The service tech did not see anything else wrong with the unit.

The consumer stated that she contacted the manf. They informed her to call the dealer (Gedy). The consumer has tried to call the dealer and get what service was conducted on their fireplace before the explosion occurred.

The consumer is trying to communicate with the manf about the incident but they are not being cooperative about it. 

The consumer has had various people look into a replacing the fireplace. They all have provided different ways. The consumer wants to address the cause of the incident so it does not happen again with the new unit.

The consumer's unit is not included in recall #13-744.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: My daughter discovered a burning smell when she entered her room this evening.  Upon a search of her room, I discovered the smell was coming from her humidifier.  The humidifier was on and had run out of water.  I unplugged the unit and had her fill the water tank.  When we put the water tank back on the unit, water began pouring out the bottom onto the floor.  Once we cleaned up the water, I inspected the unit more and discovered the there was brown (burnt) melted plastic on the rear base of the unit.  This unit is advertised as having an automatic safety shutoff feature when it runs out of water.
justification: The humidifier malfunctioned, causing a burning smell and water leakage, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: My son turned on the Vornado Whole Room Space Heater model # TH1 this morning in the bathroom walked out of the room to turn the coffee on when upon returning to the bathroom with in minutes the bathroom was filled with smoke and the heater was in flames.
justification: The heater caught fire, filling the bathroom with smoke, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
I plugged my Lasko heater in to run for the night because the house was cold and the temperatures were going to be below 0 with the wind chill.  When I woke up the heater was smelling like something was burning and the plastic molding around the front is melted in 2 places.  It was sitting in the middle of the room so not around anything to cause it to overheat but it did and it didn't shut itself off.  I am concerned that with the melting of the molding it malfunctioned and could have caused a house fire.  I tried to reach the manufacturer multiple times but just sat on hold for 20-30 minutes and no one answered the phone.  I even left my phone number for them to call me back and I still haven't hear from them.

Lasko Heater 5521
Safety hazard / Fire hazard
justification: The heater malfunctioned, causing melting and a burning smell, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
We have been using our steam mop for about 2 years.  Last night, while my husband was mopping the floor, the bottom of the mop shot out, along with a huge blast of steam.  We weren't hurt, but if my children were standing anywhere close to him -- as they do, since they like to help him mop -- they would have been hit with the steam or the bottom of the mop.  What concerns us is that the bottom shot out as if it was under pressure.  Also, a ton of water spilled out, in addition to the hot steam.

The bottom has never been detached from the unit before, and we have been using the mop regularly over the last two years.  That part is detachable, but you have to press a button on the side of the machine with enough pressure to do it.  We keep our cleaning supplies hidden well out of view of the children, and I know my husband and I have not ever needed to detach it before.
justification: The incident involved a steam mop malfunction with potential for injury, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description: We have a whirlpool energy smart water heater Made by American water heater company/ US Craftmaster/ owned by AO Smith , The Unit was professionally installed a few years back this exact unit states it comes with a lifetime warranty as well, For roughly about the last 2-3 years we noticed no hot water once in a while and you would have to reset the energy smart controls or adjust the energy smart settings up then back down to what was optimal for our usage as i guess it is suppose to learn our usage and adjust itself. Over the last year however we noticed it tripping the circuit breaker and its electrical components becoming intensely hot the other day my oldest son [REDACTED] (30 years old) burned his hand so bad it blistered just touching its components and electrical switches as it has many user selectable options such as heat temperature, energy usage, etc he had then turned down the heat thinking that is why it was so hot a few days later we had no hot water and the breaker was tripped after a quick inspection we noticed all of its electrical components that come preinstalled had ignited it seems to be cause by a faulty energy smart panel and after calling lowes they said they had got many complaints about this happening and a quick search on the net showed other complaints about them overheating , melting, or catching fire. This is a major consumer safety issue.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe burn injury to the user, and similar complaints indicate a likely recurrence of such incidents.

incident_description:
Re: Safety Hazard, Best 48" Stove Vent
P/N: Model K260A, K260A, Rev-G

Dear U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission

The attached memo to [REDACTED] Broan-Nutone describes how I seriously lacerated two of my fingers (total of 19 stitches) on an unprotected, raw stainless steel sheet metal edge inside my Best 48" stove hood (P/N referenced above). This occurred in mid-July 2013 when I was trying to replace one of the four the removable vent baffles after cleaning, and it was catching on some hidden obstacle in the vent assembly (...turned out to be dangling 120V power cord assembly).
 
The unit was purchased from Ferguson Enterprises on 28-Dec-2013 (invoice Nr.2736968), and installed on February 5, 2014 by Greg Georguson Summit, Inc, [REDACTED] of Lodi CA.

Also, be aware that when trying to replace on of the (four) halogen lights, the light socket installed in the hood broke free as I tried to "push and twist'' a new light bulb into place, potentially exposing me to yet another raw stainless steel sheet mental edge, as well as the now exposed, internal120V AC electrical circuits. [REDACTED] sent me a replacement light socket that I self installed. The old one is still trapped somewhere inside the vent unit. This latter event occurred in mid October, 2014.

I believe there is a simple fix to the exposed, raw sheet metal edge on which I lacerated my fingers: simply roll over this sheet metal edge by ~6mm prior to assembly. I recommend that this unit be recalled until the above issues are addressed and fixed.

Sincerely yours,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a serious laceration requiring 19 stitches, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this could happen to others during similar maintenance, making it possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Caller filed online incident report 12/09/2014 that wouldn't complete.

Siemen's 200 amp main circuit breaker, model number and serial number not available at this time but information will be populated by caller before he returns his report.
In 2010 CPSC recalled 2.2 million circuit breakers of various sizes..
Circuit breakers are four years old, installed in 2010 with no problems noted until caller was attempting to power his generator during a power outage on November 27th, 2014 and could not shut the breaker off in order to supply power to his home through the generator.  The 200A breaker was confirmed defective by a licensed Electrician (Navsbaum Electric Perry N.H.)

He is reporting this incident as a fire hazard because the breaker would not shut off.

There have been no incidents of injury known at this time

The manufacturer was contacted sometime around December 1st, 2014 and consumer was informed that he should return the breaker.

He has already returned the breaker to the distributor and so cannot return it to the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a defective circuit breaker posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the electronics on the unit control all of the cycles. The consumer stated that the electronics are malfunctioning and allowing the lid to open during spin cycle.

The consumer stated that the lid becomes unlocked during spin cycle and sometimes during other cycles as well.

The consumer stated that the lid is able to open up while the drum is spinning extremely fast.

The consumer contacted the manf and they sent out a technician for inspection. The technician explained to the consumer that the transmission and the electronic controls in the machine are starting to fail. The consumer was informed that this is a safety hazard. 

The consumer wanted the manf to either replace the unit or pay for the repair cost. The manf stated that because the unit is not under warranty they will not cover repair cost or provide replacement.

The consumer was provided repair cost estimate of $443.
justification: The malfunctioning electronics pose a safety hazard by allowing the lid to open during high-speed spin cycles, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was using my Ryobi 18v Cordless Drill when it began to spark and smoke.  I was using it to fix a squeaky floor and discontinued use out of fear of a fire. I contacted the company and they told me that the drill is out of warranty and I needed to buy a new motor.  I asked about the fire risk and they told me to not use the drill.
justification: The drill sparked and smoked, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred as use was discontinued.

incident_description: Heater stopped working. A few days later it was working when plugged in.  Used for a few days intermittently.  Today it sparked and started smoking. We unplugged it and sparks stopped.  Set in tacked unit outside on metal can.  It fell off  (1 1 foot) and landed in metal/wood garden basket.  Looked outside and saw 2-3 foot flames at doorstep.  Used metal fireplace rod to get it into middle of driveway and used fire extinguisher to put it out. All that was left of heater was scraps of metal.
justification: The heater malfunctioned, sparked, and caused a fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was coming down from the ladder. The consumer heard a loud snap and noticed that the lower left hinge broke.

The caller was hanging on from the ladder and was able to grab a hold to get down safely to the ground. The consumer stated that he was about 4 feet off of the ground when the hinge snapped. The consumer stated that a piece of the hinge has broken off completely.

incident_description:

On Dec. 23 2014 the power cord of the end suddenly sparked and burned the cable; the cable and plug ( connect to the AD adapter) were disconnected into two pieces. the plug:UL 50A 250V LT07  , the cable : CSA   TYPE    SPT-P   LL-1140    ET2    600C     300V    18AWGX3C
justification: The power cord sparked and burned, posing a fire hazard in a paper-filled office, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Had a can of Rust-Oleum spray paint stored in a wall cabinet in my garage. Last Friday night it exploded spontaneously, apparently with considerable force since it blew the cabinet doors open & spattered black paint over a considerable area (including two of my vehicles). Fortunately no one was in the garage when it happened, but there was significant damage to the interior of the garage and its contents. I am a physician and in my estimation there was the potential for serious injury if someone had been nearby when the can exploded. What is baffling to me is why it exploded in the first place. It had been in the cabinet undisturbed for some time, and there were no extreme temperatures to blame for the incident. My fear is that it could happen elsewhere with more serious consequences. I took photos of the damage that morning & have kept the can that caused the problem.

incident_description:
My mother-in-law was using a Eden Pure Model GEN3 manufactured in 2011 to heat her living room. The unit was purchased new last year (2013), and had been used only a few times prior to 12/13/14. The few times that the heater was used prior to 12/13/14, my wife's mother had always commented that the cord was very warm during use. On 12/13/14,  while the unit was operating normally, the circuit breaker suddenly tripped. I went out to reset the tripped breaker and noticed that the panel was warm in the area of the breaker. I felt the breaker and it was hot to the touch. I went back to the living room and began to unplug the heater, when I noticed how extremely warm the cord was. The wall outlet face was warm and also the entire receptacle was giving off a substantial amount of heat. I removed the outlet cover to assure that no burning or arcing had occurred at the outlet. The entire assembly was just warm like it had been overloaded. The circuit in use was a 15amp branch line in a home less than 15yrs. old. No other high draw appliances or lamps were in use at the time of the tripped breaker. No extension cords or any adapters were in use with the heater at the time of the incident, it was plugged directly into the wall. I advised her to not use the heater until I could verify that it was operating correctly and I had checked for a recall. 
Several days later I began to research this product and found some shockingly similar stories from many other customers. It seems that this is a common issue with this product and it has already been attributed to at least (1) serious fire. I also found some recall information involving the same manufacturer with another product. 
Needless to say, I am wondering why this product is still available to the public and why a recall involving all similar types of their products has not been issued. This appliance very well may have caused a serious fire by merely operating under normal circumstances. I am not sure if the appliance is UL approved, but it certainly would not be considered safe. See links below:

http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/edenpure.html

http://edenpure-heater.pissedconsumer.com/

http://www.aboutlawsuits.com/edenpure-fire-lawsuit-20358/

http://www.saferproducts.gov/search/Result.aspx?cid=17179&dm=0&htid=9%2C14%2C30%2C31%2C34%2C39%2C47%2C46%2C49&pcid=354%2C363%2C373%2C375%2C376%2C377%2C378%2C895%2C1924%2C1942%2C2020&srt=0
justification: The incident involved a heater causing a circuit breaker to trip and components to overheat, but no injury or fire occurred. Similar issues have been reported by other users, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:

A couple of days ago, I noticed a smell sort of a smell like plastic burning, then it went away.  Yesterday I noticed the timer on the heating unit was making a humming noise which I thought odd since I didn't have the timer set.  About an hour later, I heard a loud "pop", saw a spark fly out of the front of the unit (where the temperature controls are located), and smoke came out of the front top of the unit (just above the temperature controls and the smell of the smoke was a combination of burnt wires and plastic.  I shut the unit off, and unplugged from  the outlet (the power cord itself was not warm at all which I thought was interesting).  I am thankful I was at home when this happened and that this unit was away from the furniture.  I don't want to guess what the outcome would have been if I wasn't here to shut it off and unplug the unit.

The product claims "Automatically turns off with safety thermal cut-off if heater becomes too warm"  I am not sure what is deemed too warm, I feel smoke coming out of the unit is too warm yet the unit didn't shut off, I had to do it.

This morning the same model space heater plugged in a different location of the house, started to have that same plastic burning smell  I immediately unplugged the unit as I didn't want the same incident from yesterday to occur again.  This is an oil filled space heater Delonghi TRD0715T Safe Heat Oil-Filled Radiator

incident_description: I purchased a Fahrenheat FUH54 5000-watt electric heater from Home Depot in January of 2014 and had it installed in my garage. I turned off the breakers to the heater to shut it off.  I then opened the bottom of the unit where the thermostat and wiring is located. I did some research online and found that the thermostat in the unit is known for this defect...that there is a flaw with the thermostat that causes arcing and overheating.  This is a HUGE fire hazard.  There was enough heat in the wire to destroy the wire insulation which is also enough to start a fire.  The serial number on the thermostat is 5813-11002-000, thermostat model number is ATC-26B SPST.

incident_description: We purchased a new Jotul free-standing gas heat stove to replace a wood stove.  It was finally up and running with a new gas line on December 1.  We had it set on a thermostat to keep the basement room at a steady temperature.  Upon returning from an errand on Dec 3, we entered the room to find the flame considerably larger than it was set, and there was a sound like a blow torch coming from the stove.  It was quite alarming.  My husband set the flame level back, but that did not correct the blow torch sound.  We turned it off, turned it back on and it was okay.  This has happened four times now since Dec 3. Today is December 19, and it happened this morning.  We no longer leave the stove set on a thermostat unless we are in the room.  I did a search online and found a forum where others with Jotul stoves were discussing this issue, and one of them had contacted Jotul and spoken with an engineer.  The first post on this forum was 2005.  Several comments were posted about this issue, in 2007, 2010, and the latest in 2011.  The findings were that the engineers confirmed there is a problem with the burner, and that there could be some damage to the stove from repeated blow torch effects.  So, we shared this with our dealer, who called Jotul and had it confirmed with them by telephone.  A new burner is on order and will be installed as soon as the part comes in.  We are sharing this issue because we see this as at least a costly problem with the stove over time, and possibly a potential fire hazard.  It is alarming to us that this issue was first mentioned in the forum 9 years ago, and that it has been ongoing, and yet our dealer had never been provided information about this.  We believe this is worth some investigation by some organization.  If that is not you, please advise so we can pursue this.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove with potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred. The issue has happened multiple times and is confirmed by others, indicating it is likely to recur.

incident_description:
Uncontrolled heating of the burner tube in a Whirlpool  Duet dryer (model GGW9260PW3) poses gas fire danger.

On the morning  of October 28, 2014  the consumerÃÂs wife ran a load oflaundry in our Whirlpool Duet dryer (model  GGW9260PW3). The dryer finished  the job and she unloaded it. Three hours later she noticed a dark brown scorch mark had appeared  on the interior  of the drver  drum near the front on the right hand side. She touched that spot and found  to be extremely  hot, too hot to touch  without burning  her fingers. The dryer had not been in operation for over three hours. There  was no odor or smoke  and no sign of flames or flame damage to the exterior  of the dryer. The consumer estimated  the temperature of the drum surface near the brown scorch  mark was in excess of 300 F and possibly  as hot as 500F. The consumer unplugged the dryer and shut off the gas supply.

The dryer drum eventually  cooled  off and the consumer opened the front panel to examine for damage. The consumer did not see any sign of damage; no smoke stains, no flame marks, no melted parts. The exterior  of the dryer  drum did show a brown scorch mark directly  opposite of the mark on the interior  of the drum. The exterior scorch  mark on the drum was directly above  the igniter and burner tube assembly.

The consumer set up an appointment with Sears appliance repair service and a repair technician  came and inspected  the dryer.  He said the hand encountered this problem  before and he replaced the dryer's electronic control broad (part# W1 0542001) and the dryer drum (part# W10381481). The technician took the original parts that he replaced.  We have now run four loads of wet laundry through  the dryer and the problem  has not reoccuned.

Evidently the original control  board suffered a failure that allowed  the igniter to heat the burner tube (part# W693140) to an extreme  temperature and maintained that temperature even though the dryer was not in operation. This extreme heat caused the scorch  marks on the drum directly above the burner tube. Apparently this heating would have continued had not the power  been shut off to the dryer. The potential for starting a fire is self-evident. The high heat might eventually  damage  the igniter assembly  and cause a leak in the gas feed line. The gas from such a leak would  be ignited  by the hot burner tube and engulf the entire appliance in a gas fed fire.

This dryer was purchased from Sears and installed  by Sears on August  28, 2006 and  has been  in continual use since that time.  It has never been  repair or modified previous to this  incident.

Three  documentation photos are attached  to the email message used to send this form.
justification: The incident involved extreme heat and scorch marks but no injury or fire occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as the issue was resolved after parts replacement and hasn't recurred in four subsequent uses.

incident_description:
12/14/14 1:30 pm Sunday
A 13 year old female decided to wash her PE clothes. She may have had damp hands and grabbed her PE clothes and put them in the washing machine. She then grabbed a Costco Kirkland Signature Ultra Clean Laundry Detergent Pac (LDP) and held it in her hand, while she decided to grab more clothes from the hamper next to the dryer to fill the machine. She put those clothes in the washer and then went to drop the LDP into the machine, however it was stuck to her hand. 

She could not pull her fingers apart, as the plastic coating melted and began to dissolve on her skin. She tried to pull her thumb and index finger apart with a little more force, about 2 feet from her face. All of a sudden, the LDP exploded and burst.

Less than half the detergent from the PAC covered her face, mouth, eyes, hair and clothes. More was found on the door, on the floor, and blue drops of detergent were in the empty laundry basket a couple feet away.

The LDP must have had a lot of pressure to spray that distance and with such force.

She dropped the LDP and ran in the house immediately to the kitchen sink and began to rinse out her mouth and eyes. The right eye had the biggest hit.

This is where I found her, frantically rinsing the suds out of her eye, from her hair and mouth.

We rinsed at the sink for a few minutes, as she screamed from the pain.

I called the poison control number on the bottle and then proceeded to get in the shower to keep a slow trickle of water running through her eye.

Poison Control advised me to keep running water through her eye for 10 to 15 minutes. They then told me to have her close her eye for 20 minutes and rest.

We did this, and she was in constant pain, both in the shower and while resting. 

She was able to see out of her eye, although she saw a halo effect, had blurred vision and felt like she was looking through fog.

At 2:44 pm, I placed a call to her pediatrician and left a message for the advice nurse.

At the same time, I called my RN relative and asked her advice. She recommended we go to urgent care right away. 

At 3 pm we were on the road.

At 3:09 pm, As we were driving to urgent care, the advice nurse returned our call and said that we did the right thing and should continue proceeding to urgent care.

3:15 PM  We arrived at Urgent Care in Mountain View  to a packed waiting room

3:17 PM - We were called in for care after a very short wait. We learned that chemical burns to the eye are considered quite dangerous and high on the urgency priority list.

She was seen by several doctors and nurses and the main doctor was in constant communication with an Opthalmologist.  Her eye injury is severe and she has been in constant pain.

Her PH level in her eye was 8.5 and the appropriate level is 7.0.

They tested her eye several times - probably 4-5 times or more.

Her eye was rinsed with saline solution 4 separate times, 3.6 liters total to drop the base level back to normal.

The doctor used a dye test where she dyed both her eyes an orange color and then shined an ultraviolet light on both eyes so that she could see the chemical burn locations. The light showed several significant spots on her right eye, especially on the pupil itself, along the bottom and top right corner.

Her eye pressure tested in a normal range. Her right eye was 13 and her left eye was 16. Normal is 20 or less.

They put a patch on her eye to protect it and to keep her hands away from accidentally scratching her eye.

She is taking pain meds, pain eye drops, antibiotic eye drops, and using natural tears as often as possible to help the eye heal.

At 8 pm, we left urgent care, almost 5 hours after we arrived.

The problem with the laundry [REDACTED] is that the chemicals are super concentrated and do not rinse off the eye very well. This is a huge danger!!

Day 2 - Saw the opthalmologist. The ph level of the eye was high again, signifying that there was still detergent in the eye. The Doctor rinsed her eye again with saline and was able to bring the ph level back down again. incident_description:
In the beginning of the year I installed a gas fired Dornback ceiling mounted unit heater model DGH-45 made by Adams Manufacturing Company in the garage. Shortly after the installation I contacted the manufacturer about a hot metal smell the was causing some irritation to my wind pipe tissue. After investigating I found a section of the heat exchanger coating was changing in appearance and I emailed photos of it to the manufacturer and talked to them.

After the summer when I ran the heater again I found the smell had increased in level and would cause me to get a
headache after the unit runs for a while. After I left the space the headache went away. If the metal coating is
burning off the heat exchanger headaches can be a symptom of metals sickness. The area of the heat exchanger is
now all black with another area changing in appearance. I sent current photos of the heat exchanger to the
manufacturer and talked to them again. Photos attached.

I had an HVAC company check out the unit and a carbon monoxide detector reads zero.

The manufacturer has yet to provide any solution to the problem.
justification: The incident involves irritation and headaches caused by a burning smell, indicating potential health effects but no severe injury or death.

incident_description: Iron smoking, potential fire hazard: I purchased a Singer Expert Finish iron from Amazon in December 2011, and have used it 2-3 times per month without any problem since that time.  I use filtered tap water for the steam function, as instructed in the ownerÃÂs manual, and have cleaned the iron regularly using its self-clean feature.  On the afternoon of November 16, 2014, I had ironed 4 or 5 shirts with the iron set on 7 (Cotton) and using the steam feature.  I left the iron turned on, standing upright on the heel rest on the ironing board, while I went to another room to get more hangers. When I returned, no more than 2 minutes later, the iron was beeping and smoke was pouring out from under the soleplate at its tip.  The LCD display read ERR and MAX.  I turned the iron off, unplugged it, and moved it to the ceramic cooktop where I could turn on the hood exhaust to get rid of the smoke.  The iron continued to smoke for 5-10 more minutes, and was extremely hot.  The heat was so intense that the plastic trim at the side of the soleplate was bubbling.  There was water remaining in the reservoir.  There is no mention in the ownerÃÂs manual of any ERR message, but clearly the iron is no longer usable.  When I contacted the manufacturer to notify them about the incident, the customer service representative seemed unconcerned about the safety issue (though she - [REDACTED] - did hasten to tell me that the iron was no longer under warranty).  I am disappointed in the lack of an apology or any explanation from the manufacturer, and feel that consumers should be warned about this potentially hazardous appliance.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred, and such events are unlikely given the user's proper maintenance and usage.

incident_description:
The consumer would like to file a report because she feels her front loading washer poses a safety and a fire hazard. 

08/14/2014 The consumer reports that she was awaken in the middle of the night by the sound of her washer having turned itself on while its door was opened. Because the washer does not have an On/Off switch, the consumer tried to shut off the machine through its Cancel button but was unable to. The consumerÃÂs husband had to switch the breaker off that was supplying electricity to the machine in order to stop it. The consumer indicates that the machine was not set to any particular setting despite it having turned on. 

08/15/2014 (Approximate) The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained what happened. The representative she spoke to informed her that she had never heard that happen before with one of their units. She advised the consumer to try and turn the washer on again to see if it would work or to contact a Technician to inspect her unit. The consumer proceeded by turning her unit on once and reports that it worked fine until now.

The consumer indicates that her washer looks physically fine. She plans on contacting both the retailer and the manufacturer to see if they can provide any assistance with it. 

The consumer first contacted Frigidaire some time un Aug. with this problem.  Since then the retailer has been contacted.  Frigidaire has been called on 10/27-10/30-11/4-11/6.  The consumer was told they would send a new control board at a reduced price.  Consumer contacted retailer on 2 occasions & was told a fax with the amount of purchase price to Frigidaire. incident_description:
On July 21, 2014 we ordered from Hesco Lighting, the [REDACTED] 16 Light Multi-Tier Chandelier by [REDACTED] Lighting. Upon receipt of the chandelier we discovered that the chandelier's rod and its coupling are "standard thread" and our Aladdin Light Lift's rod and its coupling are "fine thread." On [REDACTED] FAQ web page they offer for purchase, via their Customer Service Department, an adapter that would allow their chandelier/light to be hung to an Aladdin Light Lift. 

We ordered our chandelier from Hesco Lighting because customers cannot purchase directly from [REDACTED]. We contacted Hesco about the incompatibility issue which they were not familiar with since rods and couplings are generally fine thread based on Hesco's experiences. Hesco then contacted the [REDACTED] representative and after much discussion among them, it was agreed that we would need the adapter. 

Upon receipt of the adapter kit, we proceeded to attach the chandelier to the lift. The attachment of the chandelier to the lift went terribly wrong because our chandelier fell 23 feet to the floor, damaging the chandelier, the wood floor and possibly the lift but we will not know for sure until we attach another chandelier to the lift. Thankfully the four adults present were not injured because none of us were standing under the chandelier. 

The adapter kit did not contain specific instructions for the installation of the adapter itself, but it did include a second copy of the instructions that came with the chandelier and those instructions read and depicted the male connector going up into the female connector. 

After the chandelier fell, we contacted Hesco who then contacted [REDACTED] who responded, as we were told, by saying they are not responsible if we hung the chandelier incorrectly. We contacted Aladdin Light Lift about the incident and discovered that they are aware of the incompatibility issue with the [REDACTED] chandelier and the Aladdin rep immediately emailed us a photo of the installation for the adapter. The photo shows that we needed to remove the fine thread coupling from the Aladdin lift, exposing the fine thread male connector, and then placing the female end of the adapter into the male end of the Aladdin lift thus changing the original chandelier instructions of male into female. It is our understanding that the adapter is made by [REDACTED], not Aladdin. 

[REDACTED] was negligent for not including, in the adapter kit, instructions/diagram for the installation of the chandelier adapter to the Aladdin Lift
justification: The chandelier fell and caused property damage, but no injuries were reported, making the severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the incident resulted from specific compatibility and instruction issues that are not everyday occurrences but are plausible with similar setups.

incident_description:
On Sunday, November 2nd, I was using the Steam Machine to peel wallpaper.  I had used it in this room during this past week on five days - each time about 45 minutes, without concern.  This is the third room I had used it in since purchasing it at the end of last year, without concern.  I had used it earlier in the day, for about 45 minutes, taking a break for about 1.5 hours.  I had been using it for about 20 minutes, when I suddenly smelled a plastic/electric burning smell.  I immediately turned it off, then unplugged it.  Between turning it off & unplugging it, my sister called.  After unplugging it, I told her to hang on so I could look at what just happened.  When I turned the machine over, the bottom was clearly melted, still quite warm, concave, with one whole area melted completely through.  In this area, it looked like there was what appeared to be a battery (although I know that's not what was in there).  I peeled away the sticker to find that the brown spot on the sticker was a scorch mark.  You could see where the Machine had been resting on a towel as there were "towel" impressions in the melted plastic.  
As this was a Sunday & the Customer Service not available, I called at 9:33 a.m. on Monday, the 3rd.  I spoke with a {REDACTED] (name confirmed on Tuesday, the 4th), to report the hazardous event & that I wanted a refund.  She said they usually just replace it & I told her I would not be interested in that option. I added that it should not be me paying for the postage & registered mail to get back a defective product that they should be concerned about. I said "this cannot be the first time this has occurred?" & she replied, "there have been other times the heating unit overheats."  She said she could not make the determination re: refund or replacement, asked me if I had used it to steam floors or just take off wallpaper, if I had an invoice, receipt or packing slip.  I told her I  did have the [REDACTED] charge info. from when the online Home Depot purchase of it.  She said she would need to ask "upper management" re: next steps & would call me back on Tuesday.  
She did call back on Tuesday to inform me that "upper management" okayed for a [REDACTED]call tag to be issued, that I should box the Steamer/accessories up, along with the copy of the receipt for the item.  When I asked if "upper management" had agreed to a refund, she informed me that  the steamer would have to be inspected first before a refund could be issued.  At that time, I informed her I had looked up on line how to report a safety hazard, that I was concerned that I had not read about any issues in the comments section when purchasing in from Home Depot (pertaining to the concerns she had spoken of yesterday) - if I had, I would not have purchased it.  I re-interated my concerns & added, "what if the next user does not have an acute sense of smell?  There will be a fire."  She said "upper management" was at a trade show & that when the return next Monday & the Machine has been checked by the technician, she would give me a call by next weekend, Friday the 14th.  The Machine was packed up & [REDACTED] picked it up at 1929 on 11/6/14.
On Wednesday, November 5th, she called to say that "upper management" had agreed to refund the purchase amount & a check would be cut right away.  
A letter & check was received from [REDACTED], Risk Management for HomeRight - was sent on 11/6.  In it she states "I assure you that HomeRight is serious about the quality of our products.  As a result, we will be sending your steam machine on to our Quality Department for inspection and resolution as soon as it is back in our possession."  I can make that letter available as well.  Her direct number is [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a hazardous event with a melted and scorched steam machine, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I am writing in regard to a warm mist humidifier model #HWM-340 manufactured for/by Kaz USA that resulted in fire during normal operation last week.   The humidifier was filled during the day and then we had forgotten to refill before we went to bed.  Normally if the water level got too low the unit would shut off and the refill light would come on, but overnight the auto shut-off function failed and all the water boiled off resulting in the unit overheating.  I awoke at 6:30 AM last Tuesday to the fire alarms going off in my house and my living room filled with smoke.   When I went downstairs, the humidifier was in full flames but luckily I had a fire extinguisher handy and was able to put the fire out before my house or furniture caught fire.  The unit has water level indicator that shuts the unit off when the water drops below a certain level, but the unit does not have any type of overheating protection if the unit is run without water.  There are warnings in the manual not to operate without water, but if the fill level system fails, then there is nothing to prevent the unit from overheating and catching fire. The 15 AMP circuit breaker to the outlet also tripped but not before the unit caught fire. The unit is about 1-1/2 years old.
justification: The humidifier caught fire due to a failure in the auto shut-off function, but no injuries or deaths occurred as the fire was extinguished before spreading.

Electrical circuit breaker or distribution bus failure in I-T-E (now owned by Siemens) 2-pole 240V load center, Unit manufactured in March, 1986- same unit was recalled with manufacturing dates of Aug-Oct of 1986.   

Unit fed 240V/ twin 50Amp circuits to electrical resistance heater coils in forced-air heat pump HVAC system.  (electrical resistance heat used as "back-up" heat source to HVAC system)

Circuit breakers within unit evidenced thermal fatigue/ expansion of metal clip-to load bus and resulted in electrical arcing to center load bus; circuit breaker failed to interrupt circuit, which resulted in overheating and eventual small  electrical fire contained within the load center and internal circuit breakers.  

The ITE distribution load center unit had a date code of C1886 (Mar 18 1986)
The Siemens 240V 50A circuit breakers date code is 07/99

Affected Unit: I-T-E Indoor Load Center E0408ML1125F/S-2
Manufactured date: C1886 (March 18, 1986)

Affected Circuit Breakers: Siemens Type QP 50 Amp 240V model Q250; mfr date 07/99


Original Recall published by CSPC, Relase # 88-0091
Affected units are specified as having date codes as:
- H2586-H3186 (H = August, days 25 through 31, 86 = year)
- J0186-J3086 (J = September, days I through 30, 86 = year)
- K0186-K2486 (K = October, days I through 24, 86 = year)

Affected Circuit Breakers: Siemens Type QP 50 Amp 240V model
Q250; mfr date 07/99

Unit fed 240V/ twin 50Amp circuits to electrical resistance heater coils in forced-air heat pump HVAC system.  (electrical resistance heat used as "back-up" heat source to HVAC system)
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire contained within the load center, indicating a significant incident but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I purchased a Bosch Jigsaw model 1584AVS. The saw has a quick release mechanism for the blade. This is supposed
to make the blade easy to change without using tools. The mechanism fails and the blade loosens turns and will fly
out of its housing. While completing a cut the blade has come loose from its housing and has flown into the top of
my shoe. After a few other attempts the blade will loosen and fly out when started. I emailed Bosch's customer
service department and have not received any responses. They have changed the blade mechanism on their newer
models. I have only used this saw twice. I was using the jigsaw to cut out an arch with 5/8 inch plywood the first
time. The second attempt was a failure because the blade continued to fly out when started even thought the
mechanism locked in as the instruction manual indicated it would.
justification: The blade flew out and hit the user's shoe, but no injury was reported. The issue occurs frequently during use.

incident_description: I heard a loud noise while in my kitchen -- it sounded like something very heavy hitting the floor -- when I looked up I saw that my quarter-round Andersen window had exploded. I went outside to see if maybe a bird had flown into the window; no bird, just glass fragments on the ground. The other quarter round window had shattered months earlier, but I assumed it was due to bird or something, although again I didn't find one (the first incident occurred while I was at work so I didn't hear it). I contacted Andersen windows and they told me that the windows were out of warranty but I could purchase replacement panes at a steep price. We purchased our home a year and a half ago and these windows were manufactured and presumably installed in 1992. I'm very concerned that additional windows will explode. So far, both times, the exploding panes have been on the outside, but the glass fragments in my back yard are very dangerous and hard to find (not tempered glass). I have a child and a dog who play outside and I am concerned for their safety and for our own. We have Andersen windows all over our house -- each one now seems to be a ticking time bomb and the manufacturer, Andersen, has offered us no remedy except that we must pay dearly for the replacement of these defective products one by one, after they explode and possibly injury us. We were quoted a price of over $800 to replace the defective panes - without the cost of labor.
justification: The incident involves shattered glass fragments, posing a risk of injury to the child and dog, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: On October 7, 2014 I went to a single family home located in North Kingstown, RI to perform a pre-sale inspection as required by local regulations. This house has two 110 volt, battery backup, interconnected devices.  I went to the bedroom area first, I sprayed a small amount of smoke in the device (Smoke/co), and nothing happened, the green power light was on. I again sprayed a little bit more in the device and nothing happened. I then reached up and pushed the test button and nothing happened. I removed the device to check the date the device was made and found it to be June 2005 and there was a 9 volt battery in it. When I removed the device the power light stayed on after it had been removed from 110 volt power. The same model 110 volt smoke detector in the second bedroom functioned but had a low decibel level when activated. The occupants of this home have lived here since these detectors were installed, and never heard a chirp every 30 indicating they were near end of their functional life.
justification: The smoke detectors were not functioning properly, but no injury or incident occurred as a result.

incident_description:
I went to Pep Boys and was approached by a salesperson.  We (my husband) and I explained what we were looking for.  They were garage mats to be put under our car's tires.  He showed us the product Best Step mat.  BS 120.  I believe they are also sold online at various sites and also Sears.  We used them since December 2013.  We didn't realize they would start to buckle.

One day I was unloading groceries from the trunk of my car.  I had a bag full of groceries on my right shoulder and as I was reaching for a bag of groceries with my left hand my right foot started to slip on the mentioned mat.  I noticed I was barely on the mat, maybe just a few inches.  The mat buckled and made me fall very hard on my left side.  I hit my head and left arm on the concrete.  I needed stitches on my head and my left arm was broken in 7 areas.  I needed surgery to reconstruct my wrist.  

I did go to the Pep Boys store and the manager on duty made me feel very uncomfortable.   He mentioned I was the only one...  He did give me the manager's business card and I have tried to call.  I also tried to go online at the Pep Boys site to make a comment on the product as being unsafe.  They would not take my review.  A review on the Sears site does mention that the mats buckle.  Please note that a picture on the mat 's present day packaging has the mat in the same position as it was on my garage.

They are not made to be put under car tires even though they are the perfect size for that.  They are made in China and need to be taken off the market.

Mats for the garage should be totally safe no matter how they are used.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injuries including a broken arm and head injury requiring stitches and surgery, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as similar incidents are noted in reviews but not widespread.

incident_description: On Sunday Nov. 2, a powerful Nor'Easter knocked power out to customers of [REDACTED]in midcoast Maine. At approximately 3 pm, the power flickered, then went out. I have a 7 year-old Generac Guardian 13K whole-house standby generator, model # 0052420, serial # 4785168, which, as it is designed to do, started and picked up the power load approximately 20 seconds after the power went out. Approximately 30 minutes later, I heard a series of electrical "pops" (I realize now that it was four separate surge protectors blowing out), and then my main audio-video amplifier began smoking copiously. I got it unplugged and then went to the basement, where I smelled an electrical problem near the indoor generator control panel. I immediately ran outside and shut down the generator. The power remained out until late Wednesday, Nov. 5. An authorized repair tech came on Tuesday, Nov. 4, started up the generator, and found it was outputting 400 volts. He diagnosed the problem as a faulty voltage regulator. He said he would have to order a replacement. He also said that this problem would not necessarily been uncovered during a routine service of the unit. When power was restored, I had a master electrician in to go over the house wiring. He found a fried circuit breaker on a bedroom circuit on the indoor generator electrical panel. Meantime, I have discovered several appliances in addition to the A/V receiver that are no longer operable. He also told me that had I not been home and/or had not shut down the generator, a fire would likely have broken out. I have spoken to several people who say they have heard of this problem with this vintage of Generac Generator. That there is not a fail-safe surge protector on this generator that would shut it down automatically if voltage surges, I believe, is a dangerous omission. The company has been unresponsive to my queries. I urge CPSC to compel Generac to issue a recall on these generators, fix the problem safely at its expense, and to reimburse any consumer who has suffered losses and/or suffering (as in being without power for three cold days).
justification: The incident caused property damage and potential fire risk, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

Additionally, they do not respond to e-mails. My question for the CPSC is this:  Has a product recall been issued for these heaters?  This is an extremely unsafe condition and could lead to a fire.
justification: The incident involved a loose power prong and burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I owned an electrolux dryer which caught fire and damaged the home I was renting. Electrolux has given a vague excuse on why not to accept claim on September 18th, 2014 my home was caught on fire by an electrolux dryer. I was able to get myself and the 3 kids out of the home safely. The home as a whole is still intact but much of what we owned was damaged due to the fire or the heavy smoke damage. I was forced to keep my family of 5 in a hotel for one of the weeks that we were homeless, and the other week I spent on the couches of friends/family while I searched for a place for us to live. I contacted Electrolux and started a claim with them as I did not have renters insurance at the time and they came out and did an evaluation of the damages/incident. I received no answer from anyone at the company for 2 weeks, and in fact called and left voice mails for their representatives to no avail. Last Friday on October 24th I emailed [REDACTED] whom is the VP of Risk Management explaining the situation and the treatment I have received from the company. A representative of his called me on Saturday to tell me that they would not be paying out for the claim, but could not tell me what caused the fire only that "it was not something they would cover". An independent investigator, fire marshall, and fire department all determined that it was not the fault of lint build up, clogged vent hose or anything that was preventable and that it was indeeed an issue with the dryer. This particular dryer is also one that is part of the current class action suit against Electrolux for dryer fires, of which is going through settlement as I type this.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage and displacement, but no injuries or deaths were reported.
