incident_description:
The caller stated that he was doing a re-sale inspection on a house. 

The caller stated that he found 3 combination alarms to be non-working in the house. All of them were the same brand and model. 

The caller stated that he tested the alarms with a can of listed smoke and the alarms did not work. The caller also stated that the test button on the alarms also did not function. 

Also, a green light on all of the alarms indicated to the home owners that the alarms were working normally.  

The caller contacted the manf. They informed him that this batch should have reached its end of life at 7 years and should have chirped every 30 seconds. The caller stated that the alarms failed to chirp. The manf asked for the alarms back but the caller did not feel that they would properly handle the safety aspect.

The caller sent in the alarms to UL for testing.
The caller is submitting 3 separate reports for the 3 alarms.
justification: Non-working smoke alarms pose a potential safety risk, but no actual injury or death occurred in this incident.

incident_description:
Kohler shower door exploded. Model #K702200. Shower doors have been used maybe 40 times.  No indication of cracks. No one was injured but if anyone was in the shower they would have been cut. Contacted Kohler and they stated that there was a one year warranty and it had expired. It probably exploded because we have more sunshine in Hawaii and the product was no longer made, yet they are still selling them at Lowes here. They just gave me the run around.
I suggest if they really think this is the cause they should not be allowed to sell their product any where that the sun shines.
justification: The shower door exploded but no one was injured, though there was potential for injury if someone had been in the shower.

incident_description:
We have a Whirlpool 80 gallon ee3z80hd055v hot water tank.
Lack of hot water prompted us to check out the tank.
The plastic housing had melted. One of the 220 lines completely burned
and broke loose. It even melted  the copper. 
I think we were lucky our house didn't burn.
I have pictures I would like to submit. 
I found three other identical complaints at [REDACTED]I feel these tanks are a real fire hazzard.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the water tank and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I plugged the three-prong end of my Apple 60W MagSafe Power Adapter into a wall outlet and the other end into my 13-inch Apple Macbook Pro. The low-voltage side of the cable coming out of the charger shorted out releasing sparks, burning the cable, and emitting a burning smell. The cable stopped working. I unplugged the device and returned it to the Apple retail store at the Jordan Creek Mall 	101 Jordan Creek Pkwy, West Des Moines, IA 50266 (515) 440-9900
justification: The incident involved a short circuit and sparks but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer would like to file a report against the company. 

9/21/2014 The consumer noticed that his unit turns on by itself. When he tried to turn it off the unit it would not shut off.

9/24/2014 The consumer contacted the company and provided the product's information. The representative he spoke to informed him that his specific unit was not included in any recall. Because of this same reason, the consumer was told that there was nothing they could do to repair his unit and that any repairs would have to be paid for by the consumer himself.

The consumer reports no injuries or property damage due to the defective unit. He also states that he has never had any problems prior to this incident with the unit.
 
The consumer believes his product poses both a safety and fire hazard and, therefore, should be included in the recall list.
justification: The consumer reports no injuries or property damage, but the unit malfunctioning constitutes an incident.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that this was the second time he was using the air compressor. He stated that he received a 2nd degree burn on his arm from the air compressor. 

The consumer stated that he hooked up the hoses and started the compressor up. The consumer turned off the air compressor after use. The consumer lifted up the hose by the handle. The consumer went to drain the tank by opening the valve. The consumer's right forearm came in contact with the brass fitting. The consumer realized that his skin was burning and moved away.

The consumer stated that he has a 1-2 inch blister. The consumer went to the doctor for the blister and used topical antibiotics for its treatment. 

The consumer stated that he has not been able to speak to someone at Sears. The consumer has received a runaround.

The consumer believes that there should be some sort of a guard on the compressor to avoid burn. The consumer stated that a passerby can touch it and get burnt if there are no guards on it.
justification: The consumer suffered a 2nd degree burn requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description: We recently had our bathroom remodeled.  We had new sliding shower doors installed.  The doors were called "frameless" and the style of glass was called "rain".   The doors were installed by [REDACTED] . in Wyandotte, MI.  The doors were manufactured by Daiek Shower Doors in Troy, MI.  On September 20, 2014, my husband had just finished taking a shower and was wiping down the shower door when it exploded.  Luckily it was safety glass, but he had numerous small cuts over his arms, legs and feet and a couple of pretty deep lacerations on his hand.  None required emergency care, but the deeper cuts took several weeks to heal.  There was glass and blood everywhere.  Luckily none of the glass went into his eye.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries, including deep lacerations, but no emergency care was required, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but do happen occasionally.

incident_description:
Kenwood Oil filled radiator heater model numberEW7507EK
type#ME75071EP
120v 60hz 1500w serial #72615 Jh

It gets  unbelieveably hot to the touch  burned a spot on my curtain,and tipped over unexpectedly causing me to wind up in the emergency room, falling on my foot. Now I have an ER bill!

It is  unbalanced!!!
It is VERY wobbily!!!!
justification: The heater caused a burn and a fall resulting in an ER visit, indicating injury.

incident_description: Our son plugged it into a cord at the library at college and it caught it fire
justification: The incident involved a fire but no mention of injury or death, indicating a severity level of 2.

incident_description: The top (handle, hose & guage ) of my Kidde fire extinguisher blew off for no apparent reason emptying the entire contents in my pantry.
justification: The fire extinguisher malfunctioned, causing a mess but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
I have 2 ceiling fan switches manufactured by FASCO Industries that were installed 20+ years ago. Three days ago while turning off one of the ceiling fans I noticed the switch plate screws were extremely hot to the touch. The surrounding wall are was warm as well.

Upon further examination I discovered the switch had overheated internally, causing the surrounding gray cardboard casing to become black. This case was burned through in one area and the label had been burned off. Excessive heat caused this. There was no visible fire. I replaced this swith with a new one from another manufacturer.

I checked the other fan switch and found similar damage, but not as severe. It was burned as well. The label was also burned through in one area leaving some of it still legible. The remaining part # appeared to be"--929 Control". Above the "UL" symbol is "A238". Below the symbol is "E13100", and below that is"6129-0499". This switch has been replaced as well.
justification: The incident involved overheating and damage to the switches but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: My husband was home alone on the second floor of our house when he heard a loud crash of glass breaking.  Once he determined that both of our pets were in the room with him, he went into the basement and found the glass door of our front loading washer had spontaneously broke, leaving large shards of glass all over the floor.  The washer was not in use at the time or for at least 24 hours before it broke and there was no sign of anything that could have made contact or broke the door.
justification: The incident involved a broken washer door with no injuries reported, fitting the criteria for severity level 2.

incident_description: The AC Adapter caught fire and began to burn the AC power plug, the table where the laptop was and the laptop. Causing several burn-marks on the wall, destroying the laptop for complete, the outlet and the AC cable itself. We had to wash and clean the burn marks of the wall with an hydro jet, repaint it, substitute the AC outlet and 12 meters of cable, the laptop was completely destroyed and the table where the laptop was had to be disposed because it got unusable.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: I was using my laptop and charging it at the same time when suddenly the cord lit a small flame, burned into two pieces and blew the fuse in my room.
justification: The incident involved a small flame and a blown fuse, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I bought a Champion Generator and when I started to first use it gasoline leaked from the carborator. When I called the company they told me to take it to a nrepair shop. They told me that the Champion did not cover the repairs and I had to pay $150 to get my gernerator back.
justification: Gasoline leakage from the carburetor is an incident but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
I had been using my cordless drill for 45 Mins. or so at my camp in Maine. I set the drill on a counter and left the room for 5-7 Mins. when I returned I could smell smoke and found the the cordless drill was billowing smoke and melting. I took the drill outside and disconnected the battery and the drill cooled  down. The trigger was melted and the grip was melted.
I'm sure if I had not returned when I did the drill would have caused a fire.
I do have pictures of the drill and I have contacted the store where I bought the drill.
justification: The incident involved a cordless drill overheating and melting, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller's 5 year old grandson who weighs only 40 lbs was standing on a Easy Reach one step Gorilla Ladder when the hinge in the middle on the on right as you  open it gave way causing the child to fall to the floor.

Gorilla Ladders

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Model# "Easy Reach"

The 5 year child hit his chin on the counter bruising his chin then fell to the floor bruising his right knee.

The step ladder.

The child was provided with first aid by his mother and grandmother.

The callers have not contact the manufacturer and they do not intend to contact them
justification: The child suffered bruises from the fall, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Purchased Coleman furnace 2 years ago.  We were just getting cool air coming out of our vents.  Service tech came out to service.  "Tech found severe crack in heat exchanger with heavy roll out, burning wires to gas valve and sensor.  Unit shut down. NOT SAFE TO RUN." Coleman had a mass recall on a different model of furnace for this same issue.  Carbon monoxide detector would occasionally go off.    Tech stated if we were to turn on the furnace we could very likely catch our house on fire.     As for injury's we were possibly exposed to carbon monoxide.
justification: The incident involved potential exposure to carbon monoxide and a high risk of fire, indicating possible injury.

incident_description:
A three years old LG Gas Dryer model DLG2302R, Serial Number 005KWMK01147 with strong smell of Natural Gas when operates. It began doing this in the last week.
Description: Unit does dry the clothes but it is producing very strong smell of Natural Gas.  
After some research, I found following video in YouTube ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mJqzwdBavfw ) .
 I decided to conduct the same "exact" test shown in the above video and I found that my unit is experiencing the same failure.  After the unit completes the very first drying cycle that lasts about a minute, the control unit would unexpectedly turn the gas valve back on. It does this while igniter is off therefore, the gas never ignites again and begins leaking into chamber and vent.
justification: The dryer is producing a strong smell of natural gas, which could lead to a gas leak, but there is no injury or death reported.

incident_description: Earlier this year (March 3, 2014) I bought a new Hoover  (also known as TTI Floor Care) vacuum Model # UH70820 from Target. Immediately out of the box the motor made a humming noise. A few months after owning it the vacuum Model # UH70820 it overheated on the bottom and burned holes or roller marks in to my shag rug. I filled out a complaint form on their website June 25, 2014.I did not hear back from Hoover/TTI Floor Care so I emailed them again on July 18, 2014. I didnÃÂt hear from Hoover/TTI Floor Care until late August 2014. The lady who called me was very kind and informative. She knew a lot about Hoover/TTI Floor Care products and explained to me that Model # UH70820 doesnÃÂt have an automatic roller shut off feature. That when you are using the hose feature the rollers continue to roll, causing the bottom of the vacuum to overheat. She explained the damage claim process and that she would send me model that was redesigned with an automatic roller shutoff so that when I use the hose the replacement wonÃÂt further damage my property. I received my replacement much sooner than expected, I was told 7-10 days from the date Hoover/TTI Floor Care ordered it but it was here in 2-3 days. Again immediately out of the box the replacement has a humming or vibrating noise coming from the motor. IÃÂve not yet used the hose attachment feature, mostly out of fear of further damaging my property.Last week IÃÂd realized it had been 5 weeks since I filled my damage claim against Hoover/TTI Floor Care and I was supposed to hear back from Hoover within 2-3 weeks with a determination of my claim. I emailed my Hoover/TTI Floor Care representative and she called my fiancÃÂ© back this morning. The Hoover/TTI Floor Care Engineer could not find anything wrong the vacuum so my property damage claim was denied. I called back and a request was submitted for a supervisor to call me back. I spoke to a Hoover/TTI Floor Care supervisor today and she informed me that the engineer canÃÂt duplicate this in his lab which means I must have used it incorrectly. They claim you have to use the vacuum with the back turned towards the object youÃÂre vacuuming with the hose. This is not in the manual but non sequential because the hose is short and thatÃÂs the only way you can reach the back of the couch I was vacuuming any way. They further claimed that you have to have it tilted slightly back which is contradictory to the manual that states, ÃÂBrushroll continues to turn while product is turned on and handle is in upright position. To avoid damage to carpet, rugs, furniture and flooring, avoid tipping cleaner or setting it on furniture, fringed area rugs, or carpeted stairs during tool use.ÃÂ I assured them that it wasnÃÂt tipped and that it was in the upright position which is what the manual advised. She read the manual with me and noted my use. I requested that the engineer test on a high area rug like mine and not your standard carpeting but IÃÂm not optimistic that will change his mind. Hoover/TTI Floor Care doesn't feel that a vacuuming overheating is a safety or fire issue but I disagree. If it got hot enough to melt my rug and turn it into what feels like hard plastic this definitely is a safety issue. A vacuum has no business getting that hot.

incident_description: I recently bought a Lasko stand heater model CT30750. I took it home to use and noticed that it tripped the circuit breaker for the outlet it was plugged into. I tried another outlet, same thing. I tried the third and it worked but after about a half hour I went to touch the plug and it was burning hot. I spent some time reading blogs and noticed many people have had issues, some causing outlet and plug meltdowns and even small fires. I immediately returned the product and told the store.
justification: The heater caused circuit breaker trips and overheating, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Husky Air Scout Air Compressor Model 41001.  I was using the compressor and the knob that adjusts the air pressure blew off like a bullet.  The metal separated and ripped apart.  It looks like metal fatigue.  I looked and the safety valve was still intact. 

Contacted Home Depot HQ and they did not seemed concerned.  This blew off at such velocity it could have hurt me badly as it is about 1.5 inches around.
justification: The incident involved a high-velocity metal part failure that could have caused injury but did not, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of metal fatigue and the potential for similar incidents.

incident_description:
On the morning of October 4th, at approximately 7:20 AM, the glass wall to our shower shattered.  No one was in the shower at the time and the shower had not yet been used that morning.  

We heard a loud noise (boom)  which we thought came from our upstairs neighbor. After the boom, we also heard what sounded like water dripping from the shower head in the bathroom.  After turning on the light in the bathroom, we found our shower wall shattered and small pieces of glass were falling to the shower and tile floor.
justification: The glass wall shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I built a custom home, completed January 2014.  In May 2014, when the weather warmed up, the house began to smell badly every afternoon.  After searching the home for the cause of the smell it was found to be coming from the attic.  I suspected the Spray Polyurethane Foam insulation (SPF) in the attic was the source of the smell.  On May 28th I moved my family out of the home due to constant headaches, throat pain, coughing, and other symptoms.  I sent some of the SPF to a lab for testing, and also ran Indoor Air Quality tests on my home.  The lab has since confirmed that the SPF is off-gassing chemicals into my home, and that the home is not safe to live in.
justification: The incident caused headaches, throat pain, and coughing, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such incidents are not common but can happen with faulty materials.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his double shower door when his home was built in 2007 and had no problems at all with it until September 18th, 2014 around 4:30AM.
Around 4:30AM when his wife was awakened to sound she described similar to someone dropping a bucket of marbles.
They went to their bathroom and discovered that one side of their glass shower door had shattered.
The glass shattered onto the floor of the bathroom because it had been open and on the outside of the the other side.
The caller stated that the glass on the floor was still stress relieving for approximately ten to fifteen minutes and sounded like ice cracking.

He still has the door and the pieces of glass
There were no injuries to report

The caller contacted the manufacturer September 18th, 2014 and was advised by a female representative that, "These things happen" and that he could purchase another door from a retailer.
He would like to have this door replaced at manufacturer's expense. 
There are no recalls with CPSC for his model.
He has pictures and will include them with the return of  his incident report after proof reading and signing.
justification: The incident involved a shower door shattering without causing any injuries, fitting the criteria for severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of similar incidents happening occasionally.

incident_description: Adapter overheated and burned my hand and arm.
justification: The description mentions a burn injury to the hand and arm, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: The charger heats up when being used. I have lightly burnt myself on it a couple times if plugged in for more than 45 minutes. It also occasionally will not charge my computer when plugged in.
justification: The charger causes light burns when used for extended periods, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue occurs occasionally but not every time, making it likely (4).

incident_description: I purchased a First Alert brand carbon monoxide detector from Sears, model number CO400.  When I tried to install the battery, I found the terminals to be too deeply recessed into the case to make full contact with the battery, and unable to clip to the 9-volt battery in the normal fashion.  The battery door closes and gives the impression that contact is made, but the battery rattles in its housing and does not stay in contact with the terminals.  I find this to be an egregious failure on the part of the manufacturer, as it appears to be a design flaw instead of a manufacturing defect.  I think they need to recall this product.
justification: The incident involves a product design flaw that prevents proper battery contact, posing a potential safety risk but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased HP power cord and used it and about more than a year ago my laptop burned and set on fire and completely damaged. I received an email from amazon today about the recall of that power cord by HP since it caused burns and over heating. I tried to repair it but it costs me more than $300 so I purchased a new one but today I came to know the real reason of the burn which actually burned my hand as well since I was using the computer at that time.
justification: The incident resulted in a burned hand and significant property damage, indicating an injury (severity 3). The recall notice suggests this is a known issue, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: The charger was plugged into a 6-hole extension cord, charging my HP laptop. I was about to the leave the house and ran back upstairs to grab my wallet when I found the charger cord on fire. I quickly unplugged the extension cord and put out the fire with a blanket. The fire was in the middle of the cord. I do longer used the cord again and bought a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury or death occurred, and the fire was quickly extinguished.

incident_description: We have been using the Trisonic universal AC-DC adapter for about 1 year to charge a baby monitor. We had it pugged into the wall (without the monitor attached) and smelled plastic burning. It was the adapter. It began to melt. We found it bedfore it was able to catch fire. No one was injured.
justification: The adapter melted but did not catch fire, and no one was injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with faulty electrical devices.

incident_description: I was using a Black & Decker RO100 5" Palm Grip Random Orbital Sander to sand paint on my house exterior.  I thought the sander might be rotating faster than usual and sounded louder, but was not sure.  Sometime later, as I was sanding, the black disc which holds the sand paper broke off from the sander and flew away.  Since luckily I was not the path of the object, I was not hurt, but the speed at which it flew off had the potential to cause serious facial or other injury.
justification: The incident involved a tool malfunction that could have caused injury but did not, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the dehumidifier compressor runs without being turned after it is plugged in.  It emits heat by the compressor running constantly although it is not turned on.  His model is not included in a recall, however, he is concerned that it can start a fire.  He has unplugged the unit.

The incident has been ongoing intermittently since last year.  He took it to a service dealer and they examined it and told him that the unit was working fine.  He stated that his model was not part of the recall 14-179.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.
justification: The dehumidifier runs without being turned on, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
A 25 pound ceiling fan broke loose from the mount and fell to the floor. It narrowly missed the room occupant. The power wires were broken inside the ceiling but no fire ensued. 
The unit was professionally installed about 20 years ago. The maintenance document makes no mention of checking the mount which is secured by a lockbolt which appears to have loosened over time.
justification: The ceiling fan fell but narrowly missed the occupant, resulting in no injury. The incident was caused by a loosened lockbolt over time, indicating a possible but not frequent occurrence.

incident_description:
False alarms / unit failure from 2 of 5 smoke detectors I recently purchased. Used in bedroom of single family wood-frame construction home. All other units throughout house have worked fine for 10 years, but these new Kidde units have failed within their first year. Concerned about their safety and efficacy in protecting my family.

Kidde PI2010 Ionization & photoelectric smoke detector. Manufactured May 3 2013.
justification: False alarms and unit failures indicate an incident with no injury, raising concerns about safety and efficacy.

9/15/2014 The consumer noticed the unit overheated and smelled of burning plastic inside. It is set to automatic to turn off/ on at 65 degrees. The consumer was away from his home for a couple of weeks and when he returned, he noticed the unit was extremely hot to the touch. 

Consumer feels that this unit is a fire hazard and should be reported. Consumer might be experiencing similar problems of recall # 11-324: The power connector for the dehumidifierÃÂs compressor can short circuit, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers and their property.

incident_description:
Front load washer soap/bleach dispenser replaced.  Original part caused washer to immediately stop if dispenser opened.  Replacement part does not stop washer if opened.  Told this was due to replacements parts manufactured without magnet.

This dispenser is at eye level for toddlers and poses a danger of eye/skin injury if dispenser opened while washer running due to fluids splash out of dispenser.
justification: The incident describes a potential for eye/skin injury due to fluid splash, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
My three-year-old daughter was standing on the stool in front of the bathroom counter. The stool flipped out from under her and landed upside down on the floor (legs sticking up) and my daughter fell flat on the underside of the stool. In retrospect it seemed that she had placed too much weight on the back of the stool, causing it to flip out from underneath her. However, she was using the product in the way specified, was not behaving inappropriately, and there was no reason to believe the stool should flip out from under her like that. She sustained bruising to her chest and both legs, and a large laceration on her armpit near her rib cage. She has scratches and minor bruising to a few other areas, including her face. Had she fallen directly on one of the legs (rather than between them) she could have been gravely injured. We were also lucky she didn't slam her head on the bathroom counter on the way down. 

The product states that the stool should be used for ages 3-7 and up to 55 pounds. My daughter is 3 years old and weighs 31 pounds. Although the product label states that the stool has "Non Skid Pads," there are only small plastic pegs on the bottom of each leg that are hard plastic and no different from the plastic of the stool. They are in no way rubberized as they would need to be to prevent the stool from slipping on the floor. I realized this was a safety hazard after I bought the item so I did not use it for approximately one year. I recently brought it out for my daughter to reach the sink but made a strict rule that the stool was to be used in the bathroom on the carpet ONLY. This incident took place on the carpet and was not simply a matter of the stool sliding (although that is an additional hazard - any safety tester would clearly see that the product is not suitable for use on flooring). The stool flipped out from under her while she stood on it, so as far as I'm concerned it's not suitable for use by any child, on any surface.
justification: The child sustained multiple injuries including bruising and a large laceration, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The incident occurred despite proper use, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely) for similar incidents.

incident_description:
I recently received a Holmes electric space heater as a gift.  The very first time I plugged it up, within minutes the control panel caught fire.  Fortunately I am both a nurse and a volunteer firefighter/officer and was able to remain calm, unplugging the heater and carrying it outdoors to the front porch until the flames self-extinguished.  As I write this, I have extraction fans running to suck the cloud of noxious, choking smoke from my home.  The incident affected two victims, myself and my adult son who resides with me.  Symptoms included coughing, respiratory distress, eye irritation, and headache.  Respiratory symptoms were alleviated by removal to fresh air pending the extraction of the smoke.  Both of us still have headaches and eye irritation but no acute distress and normal vital signs.  Because the event was quickly limited by unplugging the device and removing it from the structure before flame spread could occur, fire/EMS activation was not required. (As a fire lieutenant, however, the incident will be reported as a "near miss.")

I am horrified that in the year 2014 we still have so many poorly made, outright unsafe products flooding the American market.  This is by no means the first space heater I have seen catch fire, but it is the first one I have seen to do so within minutes of its first use and the first one to do so in my own home.  I am just thankful that, as a firefighter, I have a very high index of suspicion when testing any new appliance.  Because I was directly observing the heater when the flames broke out,  I was able to take very swift action before any flame spread could occur.  Had this heater been purchased by a typical American purchaser who naively trusts the safety certification marks to actually mean anything, the outcome could have been tragically different.

The product information follows:

Holmes Products (div. Jarden Consumer Solutions), Boca Raton, FL
Product made in China (*sigh*)
Model number HLP3300B
Date code from plug blade:  D200 TET
Supplier code from plug blade:  GEM
Additional codes from plug molded housing:  KAI HUA KH-9921 E25426
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (coughing, respiratory distress, eye irritation, and headache) to two individuals, but no death or acute distress occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she experienced similar problems of Release #08-134.  Hazard: The booster cables clamps were assembled incorrectly resulting in reverse polarity. This poses an electrical shock and explosion hazard to consumers.

The cables was plugged in for a few seconds and it started smoking and melting.  A hand towel had to be used to pull the cables off because of the heat.

(6/20/14)Caller attempted to contact the manufacturer but the contact number is no longer in service.

Caller feels that the manufacturer is still selling these defective cables that should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved smoking and melting cables, posing potential hazards, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I wanted to report that I had an issue with the Elogic USB Charger model UC4610B. It melted during charging. I was using a wall charge that has same voltage. Luckily I was sitting right next to it working and could smell the plastic buring. This could be very dangerous. I am concerned that when I searched the web there is numerous reports of melting and fire.
justification: The charger melted but no injury occurred, and there are numerous reports of similar incidents indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Monday, September 22nd, 2014 the caller was on his 24 ft ladder purchased in June 2006 picking apples when the ladder broke 5 ft from the top sending him to the dirt ground.

He lost consciousness briefly (possibly 15 minutes) when he awoke his wife advised him to contact his son in law who took him to the VA Hospital in Johnson City TN emergency room.

He was not admitted but was examined, ex-rayed, diagnosed with broken left ankle, badly sprained right ankle.

His knees are scraped up but the right knee and elbow are the more painful.

A few small bruises are on various parts of his body.

He contacted the manufacturer on Tuesday, September 23rd, 2014 and received a return call this morning September 25th, 2014.

He did not obtain the name of the representative that returned his call but she advised him to send pictures of the ladder to her.
He will also send pictures when he returns this report.
justification: The caller suffered a broken ankle, sprained ankle, and other injuries from a fall, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Ladder failures leading to injuries are possible but not extremely common (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Home we purchased in 2012 has various harbor breeze ceiling fans throughout the house, The first year we moved in we had a ceiling fan burned out and we replaced it without a thought. 

Yesterday 09-30-2014 we had another fan burn out that made the entire house smell like electrical wire burning and filled the entire room with smoke. 

I removed the fan to replace it and found that the wattage limiter had burned the wires and started to melt.

My concern is if we keep having lights burn out our home could catch on fire while we arent home.

They inspected the dryer, removed it from the home to the yard, and started running water on it.  By this point the door was starting to melt, along with the dials.  The fire department ran water on it for 30 minutes.

A week later a service technician from the store where we bought the dryer (Abt, Glenview IL).  He said it appeared that the thermostat that controlled the heat malfunctioned.  The gas kept running to the dryer, heating it to the point that it started to smoke and melt.  He said that it was definitely a product malfunction, not a vent fire.

This is a Whirlpool Duet gas stackable dryer, model WGD9151WY0.  We purchased it in Nov, 2012.  The location is a weekend home, and is not used that often, perhaps 6-10 times a month.  We have been in touch with Abt and with Whirlpool.  This model has been discontinued and we are trying to get a replacement that will fit in the space that we have for a dryer.

We have photos of the dryer as it was overheating and of the fire department working on it.

He said I would have to call LG to see if they would cover the cost of replacing the lid since it's outside of the 1 yr. warranty. He was planning on reusing the detector again.

Report Narative (Not full report):

E23 made entrance into the residence to investigate the cause of the alarm and odor. There was no smoke in the residence and negative smoke alarm sounding. E23 was able to locate an odor of burnt electrical in the area of the whole house fan. E23 quickly cleared the rest of the residence utilizing the TIC. With no fire found E23 canceled E28 and kept TR24 coming code 2. BC24 and TR24 arrived at this time. E23 had TR24 stage out front or the residence. BC24 entered the residence and assisted the investigation. With the whole house fan being a possible cause FF **** made access to the attic and cleared the attic with the TIC. No Heat, fire, or smoke was located in the attic. FF **** also cleared the whole house fan of a possible electrical malfunction. With the attic cleared E23 released TR24.

With nothing found in the attic E23 and BC24 began to search the surrounding area of the burnt electrical odor. FF **** located what appeared to be a burnt smoke alarm in the master bedroom adjacent to the whole house fan. Prior to removing the smoke alarm the homeowners stated they had a previous smoke alarm catch fire approximately 3 years prior. E23 removed the smoke alarm in question and found it had in fact just had an electric malfunction and burned up. (See attachments #1,#2,#3, and #4) The Detector is a Dicon model #:370LB Ionization type 120 Serial #: ORQ9 UL Issue #: 38,503.
justification: The incident involved a smoke detector catching fire, which is a hazardous situation, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Shortly after going to bed one night, I heard a "pop" and the sound of running water in the bathroom. I found that the cold water handle and valve cartridge had blown off the top of a 7 year old two handle Glacier Bay vanity faucet. Water was shooting at full force straight up into the air. I was very fortunate to have been nearby when this happened and was able to turn off the water almost immediately. This was in a 2nd story bathroom and could have easily caused thousands of dollars in water damage. If it had been the hot water faucet that had blown off, there would have also been a scalding hazard.
The part that failed is a thin threaded cylinder that screws down onto the faucet body to hold the valve cylinder in place. The faucet parts diagram calls it a retainer nut or "bonnet." Although it had been in service for seven years, the faucet was drip free and the polished brass finish still looked like new. There was no sign at all that it was about to fail catastrophically. It had never required any maintenance other than an occasional cleaning of the aerator. 

I have a 14 year old version of this same faucet in the downstairs bathroom. The only difference is that the porcelain handles are attached with exposed polished brass screws. On the newer faucet that failed, these screws are hidden under snap-in covers embossed with H & C. I though I better replace it immediately rather than risk another catastrophe, but when I pulled off the handles I could see that the bonnets on the older faucet were obviously much thicker and better built than the ones on the newer model. I've confidently decided to leave that one in service. 

The municipal water pressure here is 80 psi. That isn't high enough for the building department to require pressure regulators, but I installed one anyway over 20 years ago and check and maintain it on an annual basis. These usually come from the factory with a default setting of 50 psi, but I have always set mine at 35 psi. It is my sincere hope that my experience was a one in a million fluke and that there are not thousands of Home Depot customers out there who are at considerable risk after having installed what I always considered an economical but well built product from Glacier Bay.

I am including several photos of the faucet and failed part. I found the original Home Depot receipt dated 5/5/20, but it is faded and difficult to read without a magnifying glass. I am also including a copy of the installation booklet that came with the faucet because it has a detailed parts diagram.
justification: The incident involved a faucet failure causing water damage risk but no injury, and the likelihood is low due to the unique circumstances and preventive measures in place.

incident_description: I was using a Shanghai Master Plastic Products high-pressure "bounce house" blower in my basement for airflow to dry a clothing garment.  This unit was purchased brand-new and is less than two years old.  It has only been used intermittently, and has been used less than twenty hours of operation.  Four hours went by, and the basement filled with smoke and the blower was making an odd noise.  I ran down and unplugged it and opened doors and windows to ventilate the acrid smoke out of the house.  The control box, containing a capacitor, switch, and wiring, which is mounted to the side of the motor, was melting and smoking heavily, and fire was showing present inside the plastic housing.  Being near an outside door, I was able to remove the unit from the house and place it safely outdoors.  After the fire was out and the unit had cooled, I cut the power cord to ensure nobody else would plug the unit in.  I disassembled the control box that had caught fire and found burned, melted blobs of wiring and the capacitor was melted into a puddle of plastic inside the control box.  ***the unit is equipped with (and clearly marked as containing,) thermal protection, a circuit breaker, and a GFCI plug, NONE of which tripped.*** If I had not been nearby, the house would have burned down.  My partner was asleep in the bedroom at the time, which is located directly above the spot where the unit was located when it caught fire.  I took pictures of the damage.  I cannot locate contact information for the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard that could have caused injury or death if not promptly addressed, but no actual injuries occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the blower was new and used intermittently.

incident_description: While ironing the iron began to spark and smoke and began to ignite, myy wife imediately pulled the plug. Rowenta representative said that she would email a shipping label and they would like the unit sent to them for evaluation. When asked if it was going to be replaced they said no. We will not ship the iron back to them as I feel they are trying to cover up a safety fault that is potentially dangerous. I feel these units shoulld be recalled. I did notice on reviews that many people have had issues with the Rowenta irons short circuiting. Had my wife left the iron unattended on the ironing board even for a short period of time there would have been a fire. I have photos of the burnt wiring.
justification: The iron was shorted to ground, which could have caused a fire, but no injury was reported.

This is a Rowena steam iron and you must put water in the iron for it to steam.  The problem is the iron does not have a mechanism or a door to open to put the water into the iron. incident_description: Fire/shock hazard: Washer and dryer was set up stacked as designed. I've been using it without incident for a few years (just for myself and my little boy). Suddenly, the dryer seemed to have no power coming to it. After inspecting the breaker panel, etc I pulled the dryer down to look at it and found that the plastic module that the cord end screws into on the back of the unit was melted around the ends of the cord. We took the top off of the dryer and found that the wires in the wire harness had melted together. It appears that the vibration from the washer below has been causing the wires to rub together and has wore through the casing causing the wires to burn and subsequently short out. I have pictures of said wires and upc tags for reference, however my phone won't upload to your site.
justification: The incident involved a fire/shock hazard with no reported injury, and the issue was identified before causing harm.

incident_description: On 2/29/2012 I was taking out trash boxes. I secured the screen door to open so I could be free to move.  I stepped on this rug and it slipped out in front of me. I instinctively grabbed the door to stop my fall, but that just twisted my body around so that therapy landed on the deck head down, left ankle breaking the ankle.  I will attach pictures.  I bought the rug at Christmas Tree Shops and I contacted them asking them to recall the rugs or at least remove them from their shelves.  They refused, so I did file a lawsuit against them.  They totally deny responsibility.  The bottom of these rugs are made of vinyl.  I was not aware of that.  They insinuated that I should have researched the item before I bought it.  Who researches a purchase like that?  If you live south of Atlanta, that is what adults and kids alike use as a substitute sled for rare snow days.  I did NOT trip on the rug, the rug slid out from under my feet.  It was not icy on the deck.  The fire department took me down the ramp.  if it was icy they would not have done that. the ramp is a 20" + recline down to the ambulance.  I was confined to my house for weeks.  The pain in my ankle and leg was at times unbearable.  I had to have safety bars put in my bathroom (3) in order to be able to try to stay safe. I had to have physical therapy, occupational therapy and visiting nurses for 3 weeks.   I missed for 2 months my trip to Hawaii with my husband.  Christmas Tree Shops had zero caring about it. They now sell the same type of rugs in the store plus ones made of rubber marked "reduces fall risk from slips"..  proving they  KNOW the risk from vinyl backing. I am almost 67 years old now and I still have pain in that area.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken ankle, requiring extensive medical treatment and causing ongoing pain, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such incidents can happen but are not extremely common.

Due to a computer snafu, you might already have received this report. Nevertheless, here it goes again:

Certain Sears Craftsman power tools have safety switches which theoretical cannot power the tool with the key removed. The safety switch on my radial-arm saw has a two-pronged plastic key. The tool operates with only one prong inserted in the switch. I was not aware that one prong had broken off the key and remained in the switch when I thought I was removing the key. The prong remaining in the switch was hardly noticeable.

I removed the prong from the switch with a little difficulty but the saw still operates with the single prong remaining on the key. It would have operated with the broken prong still in the switch.

I suggest the switch be redesigned either a) requiring both prongs be present to activate the switch, or b) the key be made of metal.

I had a few superficial cuts on hands, legs, and feet.  I was so glad by 4 year old granddaughter was not in this tub what a mess.  These doors really need to have frames and tracks clear across to keep them from free wheeling on the tub.  The manufacturer was contacted said this doesn't happen very often and is sending me a new door.  I am really afraid to try this again but frame less doors are what is out there to buy.  I checked with home Depot and Lowes and in the bronze finish this is what there is and after remodeling the bathroom with this finish it was what I used.
justification: The incident resulted in superficial cuts, indicating an injury, and the manufacturer stated it doesn't happen often, suggesting rarity.

incident_description: During the last two days, August 12-13, 2014, my wife and I found our Kenmore washing machine had started on its own, several times.  Not only does it waste water and electricity, it could also be very dangerous.  Consider what could possibly happen, if no one was home during these self starts.  The water could over flow and cause flooding or possibly start an electrical fire.  Obviously, there is something wrong with the computerized control board.  The defective control board could also allow the machine to start during the loading or unloading operations and seriously injure a hand or arm.
justification: The washing machine starting on its own poses a risk of flooding or electrical fire, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she turned on the gas fireplace, not an insert, a free standing vented fireplace, and it did not ignite right away, she smelled gas and she was about to power it off when she noticed a fireball inside which caused an explosion which blew off all the metal that surrounded the frame.  After this incident she thought that the unit was inoperable but about 5 mins later after smelling gas there was another explosion she saw another fireball erupting in the firebox, she immediately switched it off with the remote control.

7/30/14  The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that they will contact the dealer to have the matter resolved.

Caller feels that the product is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

The submitter also stated that the unit never ignited correctly from first installation and was serviced twice. Once in May for this problem.
justification: The incident involved explosions and fireballs, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:

The max rpm of the wheel is listed as 20000 and the grinding tool lists the max rpm of 12000. They said that they felt my call warranted only a ÃÂcustomer concernÃÂ as it was an isolated incident even though the wirers came off of two out of the 48 we ordered.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the plastic straps on the lock are grooved . The consumer stated that if you bend the strap, it breaks off easily. The consumer stated that even a child can bend the strap to break them.

The consumer stated that the plastic strap can break into smaller pieces which can cause choking hazard for the child. Also the child would be able to go into the cabinet which can ;lead to other hazards.

The consumer stated that he want to install the product on the cabinet and the product broke off. The consumer stated that the strap broke off into 1-3 inch pieces. 

The consumer took the product back to the retailer. The consumer was provided refund. The consumer spoke to a manager. The manager opened up another package and the same issue occurred with the other package too.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that there is a nipple on top of the latch which locks latch into the other part.

The consumer stated that his 9-month old son was trying to open the door. The consumer stated that when his son tried opening the door few time, the nipple on the latch broke off. The consumer stated that the broken latch allowed the lock to open. The consumer stated that his son was able to get into the cabinet.

The consumer stated that the broken piece can also be an ingestion hazard for the child. 

The consumer stated that in the pack of 14, 4/5 of them have completely broken off and some more that broke off halfway. 

The consumer removed the latches off of the cabinets and drawers.
justification: The incident involved a broken latch allowing a child to access a cabinet, with potential ingestion hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: While sanitizing neoprene clothing, the glass on the front load washing machine exploded.  Glass shot everywhere, both inside and outisde, and everything that was inside has glass shards imbedded in it (several hundred dollars worth of neoprene).  Some items were shredded against the glass window that remained in place.  No one was nearby when it happened.  There is glass throughout the washing machine, likely in the pump and motor.
justification: No one was nearby when the washing machine glass exploded, so there was no injury, but there was significant property damage.

incident_description: After following the installation instructions, we turned the product on to run a test cycle. We opened the door to see if the dryer was working and heating properly, and found the drum did not stop running and continued to spin. The only way to stop the drum is to power the entire dryer down. When speaking with the manufacturer, the representative was uninterested in the potential safety issue. The retailer has been contacted for a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dryer drum that did not stop when the door was opened, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have a Husky 30 gallon upright air compressor model # 835 522. I had just turned the unit on and was unrolling the air line to fill a tire. Came back into barn to get air chuck and the unit was still running but was blowing flames out of the vent holes around the motor and compressor. I unplugged the unit and the fire went out. I am checking with Home Depot about possible warranty before I dismantle and examine unit for ignition source and cause of fire. No injuries or property damage.

* I am a Detective / Fire Investigator with the Florida State Fire Marshal's Office*.
justification: The incident involved flames from the air compressor but resulted in no injuries or property damage, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
I purchased a Genie PowerLift 900, 1/2 HP, Model 2562 from Home Depot in Atascadero, CA. I assembled and installed it on 7/27/2014. During the initial step in setting up the opener, where you push the Down button on the bottom of the motor assembly, the opener closed the door and then proceeded to break the drive screw housing in to two pieces. Two pieces of the track stayed attached to the house/door, while the last piece of the track stayed attached to the Motor housing. Fortunately no cars were hurt and I was not hurt. A photograph of the failed unit is available. 
 
I am a retired mechanical engineer who worked around machinery throughout my career and I can assure you that the three track locking sections were fully engaged at assembly. Also at assembly, I was somewhat concerned about the high amount of force it took to move the screw shaft slider when assembling the last screw section, which required a rubber mallet to a block of wood against the screw shaft. I can only assume that the ÃÂpresetÃÂ down force limit malfunctioned, allowing the stalled trolley to eject the screw shaft backwards thus forcing a disconnect in the track. With two cars in the garage and me standing under the unit pressing the Down button when it happened, the potential for injury or car damage was very high. The track locking brackets should be redesigned or have a couple of bolts added at each connection point to assure positive retention. As I consider this type unit a design hazard, I took it back to Home Depot and purchased a different brand.

I sent a copy of the above, including a photograph, to Genie on 7/30/14, but they did not respond.
 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused equipment damage but no injuries or fatalities, and the likelihood is deemed unlikely based on the description of the event and the user's expertise.

incident_description:

She looked in the back of the unit cleaned the fans, where the water drips. She states that the unit was not excessively dirty.   There were no prior incident with the unit.

Consumer stated that approximately after an hour and a half of use the dehumidifier became extremely hot which can cause burning. She feels that the unit poses a fire hazard. 

The manufacturer was not contacted.

incident_description:

A fire extinquisher was used to contain the fire.  On the fire department arrival their examination resulted in the power cord having a failure. There was moderate fire and smoke damages.

He researched and found similar recalls for the product.

justification: The washing machine fell due to a handle failure, which could potentially cause injury if someone was nearby or handling it.

incident_description: My Garage Door Opener just exploded (it popped twice and sparks shot out of it) and then smoke filled the garage.
justification: The garage door opener exploded with sparks and smoke, indicating a significant incident but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I was attempting to charge my HP dm4-1253cl laptop computer from a wall outlet when I noticed that no charging was concurring.  I unplugged the computer, adjusted the connection between the computer and the power cable, and the power adapter connection to make sure that everything was connected correctly.  Once I replugged the computer into wall socket, I heard a loud buzzing and the immediately the power adapter box on the power cable caught fire between the box and the cord leading to the wall outlet.  I unplugged the cable from the wall as quickly as possible, but significant burn damage to the carpet the power adapter occurred. Because there was no scorching on the wall outlet, the fire was NOT due to a power surge (and no other equipment was damaged during this event), but a defect in the electronics.  Because the computer is no longer under warranty, HP has declined any service.
justification: The incident involved a power adapter catching fire, causing burn damage to the carpet, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

(02/27/2005)The consumer states that the water in the washer doesnÃÂt extract and itÃÂs causing mold around the edges inside the washer. incident_description: I was using mop when it stopped steaming. Waiting for it to reheat to see if that would help and continued to pump handle to start steaming process. No steam released. This could seriously injury a person by the steam released under great pressure, the scolding hot water from the tank, or the mop head shooting off.

incident_description:
I purchased a washer, dryer and stacking kit from Sears in June 2014.  It was delivered and installed.  I noticed thereafter that the 'kit' that is designed to prevent the dryer from falling off of the washer that there was really nothing stopping the dryer from vibrating off of the washer because the stacking kit was either too long or installed incorrectly.  The manufacturer for each piece is LG.    I read in the manufacturer book that it is very dangerous to operate the machines unless the legs are enclosed by the stacking kit.  However, this is not the case.  Sears sent out on 4 occasions some technical staff to evaluate the situation and they all told me there is nothing to worry about and "who told you there was something wrong with this installation?" or "who told you this is the wrong stacking piece?".  
I contacted LG who sent a technician who photographed the units and agreed with me that it seemed dangerous and either the wrong part or a faulty installation, but since LG only service the machines, they would not correct what Sears had done or comment on it further.  
I need the machines for medical reasons due to a skin condition.  Thus it has been a pressing issue to resolve this unsafe situation.  Anyone who has a stacking kit installed by Sears on their LG washing machines are risking life and limb because again, and I can't stress this enough....the dryer can topple over from vibration because either the stacking kit was manufactured incorrectly or the installation was done incorrectly, and neither Sears nor LG want to accept responsibility.  They just blame each other.  Sears say that it's LG's part and that it's my imagination that something's wrong, and LG say that they don't get involved in installation issues and won't confirm or deny the part is the correct one or not.  By phone, LG admitted to me that their part is manufactured too long, but once I mentioned a possible recall situation, a supervisor was put on the phone and said that they would not comment on it.  LG have photos and Sears have photos.  Neither will do anything to make sure that the operation of these machines can be done safely.  They could not care less if it hurts a kid or falls over.  I have given them ample opportunity to address and fix the situation and they refuse.  Finally Sears said they would just come and pick everything up and charge me a restocking fee, which I refused.  I need these machines to function as advertised, and the stacking kit which is featured on their website as a recommended purchase for safety reasons needs to be addressed.  I can't motivate them to do anything else at this point and I'm afraid that as they currently are, they are extremely dangerous as the dryer weighs hundreds of pounds.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation where a dryer could topple over due to a faulty stacking kit, posing a risk of injury or death, though no actual incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: We bought dehumidifier Goldstar DH305 Line H serial # 501TAGH18767 from Walmart to remove the moisture from the lower level of our home. We purchased it mid summer and used it for about a month. The next summer we had high humidity again so we turned it on and were using it off and on for a week. One day we went to empty the canister and could not even hold on to the outer unit because it was so hot! We immediately unplugged the unit and had to wait several hours for it to cool down enough to remove it from our home. It was very scary because if we would have left our house that day as planned before emptying the canister our home would not have been there when we returned. My husband is a former firefighter and said the unit needed to be removed and was very unsafe. I cannot understand why this unit was not part of your recall. The picture of our dehumidifier looks exactly like the one being recalled but since my house didn't start on fire you are not recalling it? This is a very dangerous model and action needs to be taken to have them removed from people's homes before someone losses their home or even worse their lives! Please respond!
