incident_description:
On 8/19/2011, I bought a Central Boiler Maxim M250, serial #M00377 from [REDACTED], Frontier Heating Concepts Inc. On 11/7/13 the product caused a serious fire that destroyed the boiler and threatened structures and personal belongings at my home. The fire originated in the boiler and was contained by the metal enclosure. 
After extinguishing the fire, I contacted the Central Boiler dealer, [REDACTED], who came to my home and took pictures. An investigation was not performed. Pictures of the boiler were sent to Central Boiler (CB) on 11/8/13. I made inquiries about the fire through the dealer on 11/13, 11/20 and 12/4 with no reply from CB to that point. On 12/4, [REDACTED] instructed me to contact the dealer directly. 
I sent an e-mail inquiry to [REDACTED] of CB on 12/12/13. [REDACTED] replied on 12/16, briefly explaining that a determination was made from photoÃÂs that the fire was caused by lack of maintenance and that damage would not be covered by the furnace warranty. I replied to [REDACTED] the same day, stating that recommended maintenance was thoroughly performed just prior to the fire and that close examination of the boiler would affirm that. [REDACTED] has not replied to this message that was sent more than two months ago. 
I sent an additional e-mail to [REDACTED] on 1/2/13 to ask if he would explain the sequence of events he believed would occur from lack of maintenance that would cause a catastrophic failure and fire. I also asked if the Maxim M250 has any engineered features or safeguards to prevent fire from occurring outside the burn chamber? If yes, I asked if he would explain what those features are and how they work? [REDACTED] has not replied to this message that was sent three weeks ago. 
At this point, attempts to resolve this with the manufacturer are being repeatedly ignored. 
I believe this fire resulted from a failure to regulate temperature. The Maxim M250 is a pellet boiler comprised of a 90-gallon water tank surrounding the burn chamber. During normal operation, when the thermostat calls for heat, pellets are automatically introduced to the burn chamber by a feed auger accompanied by fan-forced air. As the fire intensifies and the water temperature rises to a set point (180ÃÂ°), thermostatic control ceases both pellet and air introduction to the burn chamber and the boiler idles down until another call for heat occurs.  
During suppression of this fire with a dry-chem extinguisher, it was found that the furnace had boiled dry as evidenced by large amounts of water on the concrete floor where it is installed. This was confirmed by physically examining the water tank. Additionally, areas around the water jacket are the most heavily charred, indicating an area of origin. Fire eventually burned through auger feed tubes to the pellet hopper and heat caused a propane regulator to fail which then resulted in fire damage to the electronic controls compartment. 
If a thermostat or other burn cycle controller were to fail, tank water would heat to the boiling point and much of it be forcefully ejected from the fill port. As the burn cycle continues, remaining water would escape as steam and the steel water tank itself would heat to the point that foam insulation surrounding chars and burns. Extremely hot metal will conduct heat to ultimately affect anything that is either combustible or can melt. Evidence and examination of the boiler suggest an overheat condition that eventually led to a fire that involved several major boiler components. 
This product is installed in an outbuilding that in addition to the boiler and pellet fuel contains other combustible materials. If the fire had not been noticed when it was, the outbuilding could have been involved in fire which then may have threatened my home as well. I consider this a grave life-safety concern.
justification: The incident involved a serious fire that destroyed the boiler and threatened structures, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer owns apartment buildings and one of tenants informed him about this problem.

The tenants 4 year old female child was able open the storm door and push up the safety latch.  When the door closed behind her, it was locked.  Therefore, the child was not able to get back in.  The tenants child was outside for an unspecified amount of time, but there was no injury.  The tenant damaged the door to unlock it.  The consumer does not have any additional details at this point and the tenants have moved to a different place.  It is unknown how the child was being supervised at the time this happened.

The consumer was not aware of the incident, until the tenant paid their rent.


These particular storm doors do not have a key.  One side of the frame would have to be removed in order to unlock the door.

The consumer owns 11 of these doors and he sees the potential for this to happen with other doors, because these doors are not designed to be used with keys.  They can only be locked and unlocked from the inside of the home.

(1/10/14)  The consumer called the firm, Tel:  800-375-6507; www.larsondoors.com and shared his concern about this issue.  The rep. placed the consumer on hold and went and checked one of these doors in their inventory.  The rep. came back and indicated that this is the way these doors are designed and there is nothing they can do about this.  Nothing else transpired.
justification: The child was locked out but unharmed, and the incident was reported without injury, fitting severity level 2. The design flaw in the doors suggests a possible recurrence, hence likelihood 4.

incident_description:
As my husband was climbing our garage attic ladder (Werner S2210), he was halfway up when it snapped at the hinge and broke.  He fell to the garage floor injuring his head, neck, back, and arms.

When I googled the exact ladder to see if there were any recalls or complaints, I found numerous complaints and class action lawsuits for the exact same thing happening.  I am very upset that this ladder has not been recalled already, it could have prevented my husband's injuries.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the head, neck, back, and arms, which qualifies as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to numerous complaints and class action lawsuits indicating a pattern of similar incidents.

incident_description:

The rubber smell came back, so this time I took the exhaust port filter off and saw the ORANGE SPARKS were shooting out of the back.   The smell came back and the vacuum started to smoke and I could smell electrical burning.  

The vacuum cleaner was purchased by me, brand new, from Amazon on January 8, 2012.   I went back to the Amazon web page and saw that other people were reporting the exact same thing, rubber smell, sparks and then fire.

Also, there is no pre-drilled hole into which to fasten a bolt which secures the seat.  This could result in throwing the driver out of the seat, should the cart hit a bump.     Defects have caused issues with the cart identified by professional horse driving instructor on the below date.

incident_description:
Whirlpool dryer consumers beware of possible fire hazards! 

In 2003, I purchased a Whirlpool Electric Duet Dryer model# GEW9200LL1, SN# MP3406748 for about $800 from Spencer's TV and Appliance in Mesa, AZ. On December 27, 2013, while turned off, this dryer caught the clothes inside it on fire. The smoke from the fire within the dryer was intoxicating and it forced us to vacate the house immediately. Within 20-25 minutes flames were coming out of our roof over the laundry room and the fire rapidly engulfed other areas of the house. 

The fire department was unable to extinguish the fire before it destroyed our house and possessions. The house is a complete loss; it will need to be demolished and completely rebuilt. Thankfully my husband and I were home at the time the fire started and none of our family members or animals were harmed. None-the-less, we are devastated by this tragedy as we did not have insurance on our house. We have been displaced in a small apartment in another city and have had to begin our lives anew with only the clothes on our backs. 

The fire department has confirmed that the Whirlpool dryer did in fact cause the fire. I will never purchase any other products from Whirlpool. We are currently looking in legal counsel on this issue. I have attached a link to a YouTube video that shows part of the fire and its devastation to our house:

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3wh5bYEfwOo

incident_description:
Craftsman (Sears, Roebuck and Co.) 10-in Table Saw Model Number 315.218050 power switch failed while operating under normal conditions (cutting wood).  Switch failed in the closed position (power-on) which allows the saw to run until the unit is physically unplugged from the outlet.  The power switch can be moved from the on-off position and the power will remain on.  Removing the safety pin does not stop the unit from running. This means that even with the safety pin removed, the saw can be plugged in and operated.  This is a serious cause for concern with young children in the house. 

No injuries were sustained but this appears to have the potential for a serious injury to someone using the saw who may need to turn it off in a hurry.  This may be an issues as indicated above with children in the house if the switch were to fail with a curious child playing with the power switch (even with the safety pin removed).
justification: The switch failure poses a serious risk of injury, especially with children present, though no injuries were reported in this instance.

We needed to unplug and stop using.  Tried using again while closely watching and had the same issue.  It took a while to start smelling hot again.  We finally pulled the plug and stopped using it.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased the hot tub in September/October of 2012 and received it in November 2012.


The consumer began to experience a problem within 1 week of having it installed.  Initially, the breaker kept tripping for the hot tub. The consumer called the manufacturer and when their technicians checked it out and found that the control board had caught fire.  The control board was melted and charred and most of the damage occurred at the area of the control board that connects to the hot tub heater.  The technician replaced the control board, but the heater still did not work.  The technicians ordered a replacement heater and control board and it took approximately 2 months for them to arrive.

Once the replacement heater and control board were installed, the hot tub worked for approximately 3 weeks.  The heater began shorting out the circuit and tripping the GFCI breaker.  The consumer called the manufacturer and a technician came out and checked the hot tub.  The technician found that the heater was burned and he ordered a new one.  The replacement heater arrived in a couple weeks.

The consumer replaced the 3rd,  4th & 5th, heater on his hot tub himself.  These heaters failed in a similar manner, when the heater would start short circuit and lead to frequent tripping of the breaker.  The consumer's main concern is that the heaters continue to fail in the exact same manner.  The consumer stated that he installed the last 3 heaters according to the manufacturer's instructions, but they all failed in the same exact manner.  The consumer still has 4 of the defective heaters

The consumer told the manufacturer's rep. that this appeared to present a safety hazard, since there were 240 volts used near water.  The manufacturer's rep. told him that the GFCI served as protection.

The consumer paid an extra $400.00 as an upgrade to the hot tub, which would allow him to use salt water in the hot tub.  The consumer noted that he later spoke with 1 of the manufacturer's representatives (name unavailable), who said that with his upgraded hot tub, the ozonator is not installed, but that a salt/chlorine generator is installed.  However, the consumer also found that the manufacturer of this hot tub's heater does not recommend using salt water with the heater.

The consumer said that the hot tub heaters are made by a different manufacturer (name unavailable at this time).

The consumer followed up with a different company who makes heaters and they recommend that a titanium heater be used with salt water instead of an incoloy heater.  If an incoloy heater is used, that firm (name unavailable) will not warranty the heater.  Based on the consumer's research and conversations with various manufacturer's of hot tub heaters, it seems that several firms "do not" recommend the use of salt water with certain types of heaters.

The manufacturer never wanted to discard of malfunctioning parts and told consumer.  The consumer still has heaters and board.  Manufacturer never took back.
justification: The incident involves repeated equipment failures and potential safety hazards, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: royalSSWW steam shower tempered glass door exploded.

On Sunday, 01-05-13, at approximately 9:30 p.m. my Kenmore washing machine started itself on fire. The model number is 41748102701. The serial number is XC84009111. The washing machine was not in use at the time and no clothing was in it. incident_description:
Friday, January 3, 2014
Approximately 10:55 pm

[REDACTED] was working on her computer in the office (the master bedroom) and [REDACTED] was in the living room (across the house) watching TV. Suddenly there was a very loud, horrendous crashing noise from the master bathroom. The right-hand shower door had spontaneously exploded!! The left door and metal frame appear intact, but we canÃÂt get close enough to inspect it carefully because of all the shattered bits of glass all over the bathroom. These are rimless glass doors installed by Bathfitters less than one year ago.

No one was walking in or around the house at the time. There were no fireworks, jets flying overhead, or any other loud noises or vibrations beforehand. No one had been in that bathroom, even to use the toilet, for more than 12 hours. There were no recorded earthquakes in the area at the time (we checked online afterward) and nothing else in the house showed any signs of movement. Nothing was hanging on the towel rack on the shower door. Nothing was touching the shower door. When [REDACTED] showered last night and [REDACTED] showered this morning, everything seemed normal. There were no visible cracks. This seems to have been completely random, which made it that much more frightening.

After taking a moment to calm down, we began taking pictures and video clips of what had happened. We observed that the right-hand shower door was completely gone, but the left-hand door (i.e. the one closer to the showerhead) was still standing. There was a large pile of glass debris on the bathroom floor immediately next to the shower, with more debris spread outward from there along the shower door track, inside the shower, across the bathroom floor and behind the toilet. A few tiny bits were on the bathroom vanity counter as well. Some small shards had gone past the bathroom doorway into the office. 

We could hear continuing ÃÂcracklingÃÂ and sounds almost like dripping water for at least 20 minutes afterward. Listening and observing carefully from the bathroom door, the crackling sounds appeared to be coming from the larger pieces of glass (approximately six inches in diameter, visibly cracked in a shatter pattern but still holding together in sheets larger than my hand, sitting in the largest pile of debris next to the shower) that were continuing to crack. The dripping sounds were from tiny pieces of glass (approximately the size of kidney beans) dropping from the shower door track onto the floor as the debris continued to settle.

We swept up the few bits that had flown into the office (two went all the way to the office door by the hallway!) then closed the bathroom door. We want the Bathfitters people to see what happened before we clean up the rest. We will use the other bathroom in the mean time. We immediately called Bathfitters and left a message requesting an emergency call-back as soon as possible.

Thankfully no one was in the bathroom at the time, and [REDACTED]ÃÂs location in the office shielded her from all of the little pieces of debris that made it out of the bathroom. This is the time of night that Jennifer would typically have been in the shower! Also thankfully we have a second full bath available for the duration of the repair. 

We did a quick Google search and found a 7 On Your Side [REDACTED] report from November 2013 stating that this is not an unusual incident. YouTube has many videos from people experiencing the same thing from multiple brands of shower doors. The [REDACTED] report said more than 2500 people were injured by similar phenomena from 2010-2012 and that more than 50 complaints have been filed with the CPSC, but no recall has been issued. We plan to file a report with the CPSC as well to help raise awareness of the frequency of this safety hazard. (We are not seeking to complain against Bathfitters specifically, since this seems to have been happening to multiple brandsÃÂ doors in recent years. We just want to help raise awareness so the CPSC can help fix this at the source and keep everyone safer.)
justification: The shower door exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible due to the reported frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description:
I purchased a Whirlpool Duet Washer in May 2013. I have never owned a front loading washer before  this one and asked the sales people about any special instructions. They told me to keep the front  door open when not in use to prevent moisture in the drum area. I have done that. The problem I am having is with the soap,bleach and fabric conditioner area of the washer. There is signs of mold all over the trays and inside the channel to the inner part of the machine. We have used bleach on the mold and we have run a cleaner,called "Affresh," into the machine. The drum appears to be clean but mold in the dispenser area is still evident.

I have noted a number of comments on the web about mold growth in front load washers,specifically in Whirlpool machines. There are articles stating that this "was" a problem with older machines. It appears to still be a problem.

I have contacted the Whirlpool dealer and expect to follow up with a lawsuit for this obvious problem.
justification: The incident involves mold growth in a washing machine, which is a product issue but has not caused injury or death.

incident_description:
This is a GE front load washer, Model WCVH 6800J1MS, approximately 4 years old. On occasion the unit becomes out of balance and has a slight "plastic" odor. With just a visual inspection the washer appears fine. After only a few more uses, and minimal clothing load, the washer shakes violently and fills the room with smoke. We immediately turn off the breaker and clear the smoke. 
After inspecting the washer it is discovered the bellows gasket at the front of the washer drum shows wear in the area the two make contact. After researching the cause online and in several calls to repairman this is believed to be a design problem with bearings and shaft. 
This would have been a house fire had we not been home to cut off the power. I believe these washers pose a huge risk as most laundry in a washer is left unattended. Similar models have been recalled for bearing issues. I believe these should be added as they pose a "FIRE HAZARD" as well as an "INJURY RISK".
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard and potential injury risk due to a washer malfunction, which could lead to injury if unattended.

incident_description:
The consumer noticed a chemical odor after operating the heater for approximately  3 hours. 

 He then also noticed  a few sparks coming from the control panel. The heater was operating on the low setting  when the failure occurred. 

The consumer powered it in the off position. He has not used the heater since the failure occurred.  

On 3/13/2012 the firm was contacted and the consumer states that he was advised to mail the heater back into the firm. The consumer states that he declined in sending it back and knows what he needs to do to fix the failure. 

No further information was provided.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:

Heater is approx. 8 3/4" high and molded feet (front to rear)
light weight
L.H. 2 3/4" long
RH 3 3/4" long
Easily tips over, on hard surface and worse on rug

I am considering adding a board under heater to reduce possibility of tipping over.  There is more than enough room in heater base for some screws and still stay well away from internal parts and wiring.

The odor first noticed appears to have come from charring of heat-shrink tub insulation on the connector- no fire resulted. 

Local retailer had obtained more of this heater and exchanged my heater (with bad connection). I also purchased an extra heater.  These heaters are expensive and have a low setting of 600 watts, which will be useful in warming storage areas.  The heater with the defect may have been a rare anomaly and was not a design defect but was an assembly error and I know what to watch for.  If connector parts are misaligned when they are pushed together the spring tension is reduced and connection will heat up and deteroriate further.

The element wires (that produce the desired heat) do not get hot enough to show any visible light.  Heater should last a long time.  Some radiant type heaters' elements can burn out.

Use of the replacement heater shows no problem to date, but I will add a comment/suggestion.
justification: The incident involved a chemical odor and sparks but no injury or fire occurred, and the consumer took corrective action.

incident_description:
In Sept. 2010, We had a whole house water conditioning/softener unit installed & maintained by culligan. About eight weeks after the installation, my 12yo daughter I began to experience health issues.  Professional Water analysis showed that the culligan -treated water was high in acetone and more than 10-fold the EPA safe levels for copper sulfate.  The untreated household water (city water) analysis was within normal limits.  Our symptoms went away after we stopped drinking the contaminated culligan-treated water.  To this day, culligan cannot locate this faulty unit which poisoned our water. We attempted to sue Culligan, but they refused to take any accountability for their negligent actions which poisoned our family, and we could not afford to continue litigation.

Here is our story...

Keep in mind that in 2009 - Our daughter was treated for benign kidney tumors.  Part of her diagnostic testing included a colonoscopy, which was negative. .

In 2010  We had a whole house water treatment system installed & maintained by Culligan. 

Because of Our daughter's kidney condition, she drinks 2L of water per day  (I do too). 

Very shortly after the install, it was apparent that the system was not functioning properly & culligan made repeated service calls.

Within a few weeks of the installation of this whole house water treatment  unit, my daughter & I both started exhibiting various symptoms, including headaches, diarrhea, stomach aches, fatigue, eczema, dizziness, , nausea, vomiting, unexplained thyroiditis  - symptoms were daily & we had never had these symptoms before. We both started seeing doctors for treatment. 

We never considered that our drinking water could be the cause of our problems. 

My daughter's diarrhea started to have mucous & blood in it. We saw several doctors & tried elimination diets, stress management, low fiber, high fiber, lactose free, etc.  

Eventually, we noticed that our shower heads were caked with a greenish/blue salty substance, and that there was spotting  & cloudiness on our dishes & shower glass. 

I had "Associated Labs" come out & do water testing of our culligan-treated tap water (the water we had been drinking for the past 8 mos.).  The results showed that the copper was 14.9mg/L. This is more than 10-fold higher than the U.S. EPA Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) of 1.3mg/L. Acetone was also present, and the total hardness was 423mg/L(way above normal). 

I ordered a new water treatment unit & had it professionally installed by Culligan. After 2 weeks, I had Associated Labs retest our treated tap water.  Copper levels were below EPA guidelines (0.068mg/L), there was no acetone, and the hardness level was 6.0 mg/L. - this proves that the original unit was faulty & culligan later admitted this. 

This is the very first time that we considered that this water that we had been consuming over the last 8 months (2L/day - 30mg/day of copper) could possibly be a cause for our abnormal symptoms. Up to this point they could not be explained. 

We attempted many times to have the system repaired by Culligan. It had been making weird noises & didn't seem to be working properly, ever since the day it was installed. The company admitted that they did not install a regulator valve (which I had paid for) & that not doing this could damage the system.  

To this day, Culligan cannot tell us where this faulty/damaged system is and that it could be in someone else's home right now. 

Once we took the system out, our symptoms started getting better and eventually completely went away. 

My daughter was treated by GI doctors at CHOC (Children's Hospital of Orange County) Her symptoms improved, but she still had some bloody diarrhea. Once she started medication, her bloody diarrhea completely went away.  Her current diagnosis is "Proctosigmoiditis, copper sulfate in water". 

Dr [REDACTED] (the toxicologist at UCI) said that my daughter's symptoms were consistent with that of copper poisoning, including the bloody diarrhea.   She supported copper in the water as causation of her GI symptoms, anemia, headaches, nausea, fatigue, and most notably the bloody diarrhea.   

After we found out that our water was so high in copper & acetone, we were told to get some blood work done.  I asked Culligan to pay for this & they refused. We also asked them to locate the faulty unit & they refused to do so.  This made us really mad. This is when we consulted with an attorney. 

My daughter and I have been completely symptom free for 2yrs now, since we stopped ingesting culligan-treated & contaminated water. 
My unexplained thyroiditis completely went away without treatment.  My daugter's GI symptoms have also gone away.  Although, now because of this exposure, she is at an increased risk of developing colon cancer and will need increased diagnostic screening. Her GI doctor is keeping her on a low dose medication for preventative measure. 

My husband and I have both worked in healthcare our entire adult lives, and it seemed logical to us, after doing a ton of research and looking at the whole picture, that there was a correlation between the treated water and all of the unusual symptoms that started to appear. 

After two years of attempting to get Culligan to take accountability, we have exhausted our resources.  Culligan remains unchanged in their policies and their practices. And, is likely putting others in harms way or at risk today. 

Our hope is to educate the public about the possible dangers of chemically treated water;  the lack of regulations to ensure the safety of chemically treated water; and in this case, Culligan's woeful negligence. 

Thank you for taking the time to read this.
justification: The incident caused health issues including injury (copper poisoning and related symptoms) but no death.

incident_description:
This problem was first observed while removing non-permitted electrical wiring and equipment associated with indoor marijuana grow operations as evidence within the city of Tracy in 2009. The equipment in question is lighting controllers used for switching power on and off to a group of light fixtures. These controllers are configured for four or eight fixtures; usually 1000 Watt High Pressure Sodium (HPS) OR Metal Halide (MH) and designed to be installed as a fixed wiring method. See attached photos.
Underwriters Laboratories (UL) was contacted on December 3, 2009 and information along with a description of the hazards associated with the controllers was submitted at this time. One of the controllers was sent to UL labs on December 21, 2009 for inspection.  The unit was returned with documentation from UL stating that it was not listed and did not comply with the National Electrical Code (NEC). See e-mail copies 1-4.
Similar Products labeled and sold by a company known as ÃÂ[REDACTED]  were found recently in a group of grow houses. These appeared to have a listing mark from Intertek Labs (ETL). Intertek was contacted regarding the product and code violations with documentation sent on November 13, 2013. As of this date, no reply has been sent from ETL. See e-mail copy 5.
The safety and fire hazards associated with these light controllers fall into two categories; the first being the ÃÂUniversalÃÂ receptacles used in these units. These receptacles will allow a cord cap (attachment plug) rated at either 120 or 240 Volt to be connected to the controller output.  When the light controllers are connected to a 240 volt circuit all of the receptacles are supplied with that voltage. A 120 volt appliance plugged into the 240 volt circuit such as a fan, humidifier or other small appliance associated with the growing activity will overheat rapidly and fire may follow. The National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA) has very specific configurations for receptacles due to the hazards; theseÃÂ UniversalÃÂ receptacles arenÃÂt a listed item. See attached NEMA Charts.
The second hazard associated with these units concerns the amperage available at the 15 or 20 Amp receptacles. These units are called out for connection to a 30, 40, or 50 Amp circuit, there is no overcurrent device (fuse or circuit breaker) installed between the 50 Amp supply and the 15 or 20 amp receptacle. Without this protection an appliance such as a light ballast or other load could develop a short or overload and the current would continue to flow until it exceeded 50 amps and tripped the breaker supplying it or the wiring overheated, melted and burned open. The conductors used in the controller from the receptacles to the contactor arenÃÂt marked properly; there are no provisions for terminating the neutral conductor. If the controllers are used in dwelling units which all have been found in, they need to meet the requirements for arc-fault and tamper resistant receptacles.
As these units are currently being sold and installed, they violate the following sections of the 2010 California Electrical Code.
Section 200.6 (A) Means of Identifying Grounded Conductors. An insulated grounded conductor of 6AWG or smaller shall be identified by a continuous white or gray outer finish or by three continuous white stripes on other than green insulation along its entire length.
Section 210.5 (A) Grounded Conductor. The grounded conductor of a branch circuit shall be identified in accordance with 200.6.
Section 210.12 (B) Dwelling Units. All 120-volt single phase 15- and 20-ampere branch circuits supplying outlets installed in dwelling unit family rooms, dining rooms, living rooms, parlors, libraries, dens, bedrooms, sunrooms, recreation rooms, closets, hallways, or similar rooms or areas shall be protected by a listed arc-fault circuit interrupter, combination-type, installed to provide protection of the branch circuit.
Table 210.21 (B) (3) Receptacle Ratings for Various size Circuits
Circuit Rating (Amperes)                               Receptacle Rating (Amperes)
              15                                                         Not over 15
              20                                                                           15 or 20 
Section 240.3 (D) Small conductors. 
 (3) 14 AWG Copper 15 Amperes 
 (4) 12 AWG Copper 20 Amperes
Section 240.4 Protection of Conductors. Conductors other than flexible cords, flexible cables, and fixture wires, shall be protected against overcurrent in accordance with their ampacities specified in 310.15, unless otherwise permitted or required in 240. 4(A) through (G).
Section 310.12 ( c) Ungrounded Conductors. Conductors that are intended for use as ungrounded conductors whether used as a single conductor or in multiconductor cables, shall be finished to be clearly distinguishable from grounded and grounding conductors. Distinguishing markings shall not conflict in any manner with the surface markings required by 310.11 (B) (1). Branch-circuit conductors shall be identified in accordance with 210.5 (c).
Section 406.3 (D) (3) (F) Noninterchangable Types. Receptacles connected to circuits that have different voltages, frequencies, or types of current ( ac or dc ) on the same premises shall be of such design that the attachment plugs used on these circuits are not interchangeable.
Section 406.11 Tamper Resistant Receptacles in Dwelling Units. In all areas specified in 210.52, all 125-volt, 15- and20-ampere receptacles shall be listed tamper resistant receptacles.
justification: The description details significant fire and electrical hazards that could lead to injury, and the widespread use of non-compliant equipment increases the likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Purchased an RCA USB wall plate charger from Lowe's Home Improvement.  The unit is intended to plug over a duplex and provide a single 110V outlet and 2 USB plug positions to charge electronics.  When first taken out of the package, the unit was plugged in and my son proceeded to plug it in.  He then plugged a laptop charger into the 110V outlet.  He then went to remove the laptop charger and was shocked as he came in direct contact with the plugs prongs.  Upon examination, we determined that there is no physical way to fully insert the plug into the product.  It aligns directly with the plug that goes into the standard duplex and they did not leave enough room.  This allows any person to inadvertently contact the prongs when grasping the plug to remove it from the wall.  It is a very bad design
justification: The incident resulted in an electric shock to the user, which constitutes an injury, and the design flaw makes it likely to happen again.

incident_description:
My wife was sitting on the 2-Step Plastic Stool when it collapsed under her.  It turned out that one of the four horizontal supporting bands had broken, causing the collapse.  She was bruised and had a muscle strain, but there was no serious injury.  Fortunately, since she was sitting, she did not fall far.

My wife weighs about 250 lb, and the step stool's label states: "300 lb load capacity".
justification: The incident resulted in bruises and a muscle strain, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The stool broke under weight within its stated capacity, suggesting a possible manufacturing defect, making recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Dryer drum lost protective cloth that protected it from rubbing against the other metal parts of the dryer drum area.  The rubbing and thumping the dryer made eventually wore the edge of the drum away producing sharp shards of metal that could hurt someone who puts their hand in there.  Not only that but if someone were to use the dryer in its current state (I wouldn't but someone could do this) they could lose clothing inside the dryer resulting in other serious problems.
justification: The incident describes potential for injury from sharp metal shards, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that whenever the cleaning product is sprayed it releases a toxic odor which causes gagging and burning of the throat.   She is not sure if this product has caused health symptoms (lung infection) which her physician had not diagnosed the cause of the  problem. On 1/2013  She had surgery and she was placed on blood thinners for 6 months.  She has has frequent followup with her physician during that time.
She was using the product 3 weeks prior to becoming ill.  She is concerned that this cleaning product might contain chemicals that poses health hazard to consumers. The product labeling also states "no obnoxious odor".
The manufacturer was not contacted.
The product is not involved in a recall.
justification: The consumer reported gagging and burning of the throat, indicating injury, but no death or confirmed long-term health effects.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that they keep the unit in their basement.

The consumer stated that he and his family smelled smoke. The consumer stated that he called the fire department. 

The fire department said that the smell was coming from the dehumidifier. The consumer stated when he tried to move the unit, they saw sparks coming from the bottom of the unit. The fire department asked the consumer to unplug the unit. The fire department took information on the unit and incident.

The consumer stated that he has the product.

This model is not included in any recalls.
justification: The incident involved smoke and sparks from the dehumidifier, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she has been having problems with her top loading machine which was a part of recall 13-073. The consumer stated that she contacted the recall hotline and on July 10th 2013 a technician as sent to her home and they updated that software on her washer.  The consumer stated that after the update she continued to experience problems with the washer. She stated that the machine constantly went off balance, constantly drained, spin, and refill to try to balance itself which would make the cycles as long as 2 hours. 

She stated that on Aug 28, 2013 she spoke [REDACTED] a manager from the firm and he requested for her to send him the invoice for proof of purchase. Also he scheduled a service appoint with Quality Appliance on Oct. 10, 2013 for them to service the washer. The technician informed her that the first service technician did not properly service the washer. She stated that they informed her that they did not do a software update as they stated and that they needed to order the ÃÂUser interface panel.ÃÂ

The consumer stated that the technician installed the part on Oct 30, 2013 and on Nov 1, 2013 she had to contact the company Quality Appliance back because she was still experiencing the same problems. She spoke to a representative that informed her that they needed to order a second part ÃÂsecond recalled.ÃÂ The consumer decided to contact the firm back and she spoke with [REDACTED] and she informed her that there was no such thing as a ÃÂsecond recalled,ÃÂ but there was a third step to follow to correct the problem. 

The consumer stated that once the third repair was completed if she continued to experience the problem they would try to provide another resolution. 

The consumer stated that she hasnÃÂt been contacted for the third repair and today Nov. 14, 2013 she spoke with [REDACTED] and he informed her that he contacted Quality Appliance and they received the part which should solve all her problems once it was installed. 


PLEASE NOTE!  LG removed the washer and replaced it with a new washer; model WT5070CW on 12-6-13.  3rd repair never occured.  In the consumer's opinion, only after she took action contacting CPSC and relaying that info to LG did LG do what they should be doing for all owners of model WT5001CW washers: voluntarily removing them and replacing them.  Model WT5001CW is a dangerous piece of equipment.  The consumer waited weeks for the third repair and was sitting by the washer each washload to prevent constant "self correction" by the machine which involved draining and refilling over and over again if the load was off balance or the maching wouldn't go off balance when it should have and it would shake something awful while it spinned incredibly fast.  When the cycle would end, at times the machine would start to spin again.  It would jump time.  It would suddenly drain.  How long was the consumer to wait for a third repair?  The consumer had had enough and relayed that frustration to LG along with telling them she contacted CPSC abd would pursue reports with BBB and Dept. of Consumer Affairs in N.Y.  The consumer repeats:  This washer is dangerous.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning washing machine causing inconvenience and potential danger, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The Honeywell Oil-filled Radiator (model HZ-690) was plugged-in and placed in a basement bedroom.  After approximately an hour of being on, we heard a pop from the unit and then flames came out of the top, followed by a cloud of ash.  We immediately unplugged the unit and placed it outdoors.  The entire room had a chemical smell to it.
justification: The incident involved flames and a chemical smell, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: 2 Roof Heating & Air Condition units leaking into my home. Mold, dust, insulation, dry rot, structural damage. The units are Comfotmaker, sold by I.C.P. of Lewisburg TN 650 Heil Quaker Ave. Phone: (931) 359-3511
justification: The incident describes significant property damage (mold, dust, insulation, dry rot, structural damage) but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Started smelling an electrical burning smell throughout the house. Tracked it down to the heater. When I attempted to turn it off, the knob had melted, burned and stuck to my fingers. The area around the knob had also melted. I immediately unplugged the unit from the wall. There was no damage to my house, or property but a mild burn on my left index finger, and thumb.
justification: The incident resulted in mild burns to the fingers, indicating an injury, and the heater malfunction suggests a possible recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the system is installed in one of the rooms of the hotel. The hotel went through last major renovation in 1999-2000. The consumer believes that the flush system was installed then.

The consumer stated that they got a call from a guest in the room. The guest reported explosion in the bathroom. The consumer stated that the pressure tank was split in half and the tank lid exploded from the pressure. The consumer stated that the tank lid shattered all over the bathroom.

The consumer stated that they replaced the system. The consumer stated that they discarded the damaged system.

This series is not included in recall #12-201.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
My wife's iPad charger was plugged into an outlet today and the USB port end burned up.  It was not plugged into the device.  I noticed a strong smell of something electrical burning and a haze in the room.  I unplugged everything including the charger and the smell went away.  We later discovered the end which plugs into the iPad was burnt and part of the plastic had melted.  We went to an Apple store and they claimed it looked like the USB end got wet, therefore, causing an issue when it was plugged in.  The charger never got wet. 

We researched the Internet and found we are not the only ones who had issues like this with the charger.  In fact, one of my coworkers had a major house fire from an Apple product charger a few years ago causing his family to be displaced for months.  I am a volunteer firefighter for over 2o years and felt the need to get this out there.  I don't understand why Apple hasn't done anything to remedy this problem.  The amount of people with similar issues is astounding.
justification: The incident involved a charger burning and melting, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Similar incidents are reported, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: I bought a Pelonis Electric Radiator Heater Model HO-0250H.  After 2 seasons, it started smoking and catching fire at the power selector control knob while it was in the off position.  If I hadn't been at home and smelled the smoke and was able to unplug it, it surely would have caused my home to catch fire. The unit looked like new and was always kept in the dry.  This is an unsafe product and I felt compelled to report this.
justification: The heater caught fire but was unplugged in time, preventing injury or death, though it posed a significant fire hazard.

incident_description: I wanted to share with you a light switch I purchased at Menards about 3 years ago manufactured by Eagle Electronic Manufacturing Co. Inc. Long Island City, NY 11101.  This light switch was off (not drawing any power) and in the morning the switch had burn marks where it had shorted.  Very dangerous.  Wanted you to be aware and let you decide to inform your readers.  I have pictures if desired of the light switch.  I tried contacting the company but their phone was out of service.
justification: The light switch shorted and had burn marks, indicating a dangerous incident but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he heard low noise and he walked into the bathroom and found that the glass shower door had shattered. The consumer stated that there was a single glass door and it seemed to have exploded inwards towards the shower. The consumer stated that the shower had been used the evening before the incident. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured and there were no damages to his home structure. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they replaced the shower door with a new one. The consumer stated that the door was installed at no cost.
justification: The glass shower door shattered but no one was injured and there was no damage to the home structure.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the electrical connect of the handle of the hose on his floor cleaner started to emit smoke. The consumer stated that he had been using his floor cleaner for approximately 20 minutes. The consumer stated that he stopped using the cleaner immediately and noticed that the plastic on the handle of the hose was melting. 

The consumer stated that he disconnected the floor cleaner and it immediately stopped emitting smoke. 
No one was injured and that there no damages to his home structure. 
The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that his model was not a part of the recall. He stated that the representative informed him that he would need to pay $175 to repair the floor cleaner. 
The consumer stated that he believes that this product should be investigated due to the fire and burn hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and melting plastic but no injuries or structural damage occurred.

incident_description: Our SoleusAir dehumidifier (model SG-DEH-45-1) (SN 54040000835) (MFG date MD000032510000) was tripping the circuit breaker in our electrical panel.  When I took the water catching structure off the unit, I could see discoloration caused by overheating, and the same area that was discolored was also disfigured due to the heat melting the area.
justification: The dehumidifier caused a circuit breaker trip and showed signs of overheating, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was walking up the ladder to my attic, not carry any other weight, and the lower right ladder hinge broke.  I fell from the ladder but was not injured.  I weigh 175lbs and the ladder states it is rated for 300lbs. I was not going to spend the time to report this until I saw that many others had complained about the same issue.  This could be very dangerous for some consumers.
justification: The ladder hinge broke causing a fall, but no injury occurred. Others have reported similar issues, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I had a febreeze scented candle explode on my kitchen counter which caused a fire.  The counter top was burned.  When the candle exploded three sharp pieces shot off thankfully onto the counter in stead of into my guests. I had three elderly ladies to my house for a lunch and we had just left the kitchen to sit down at the dining room table when the glass exploded. I tried to swat out the flame with a towel but it continued burning and spread to two pot holders which were near by. I finally used a large pot lid to smother the flames and stop the fire.My kitchen counter top was seared in a couple of spots. My insurance adjuster says that the whole laminate counter top will need to be replaced.  This candle is a fire hazard . I have contacted Proctor & Gamble regarding this and hope that they will follow thru and pay for the damages.
justification: The candle explosion caused a fire and property damage but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
11/08/2013) The consumer stated that the heating coils started glowing orange as soon as the heater was turned on. The consumer stated that the paint on the cover of heater started burning. This set off the smoke alarm. The consumer stated that he started using the heater about a month ago. The consusmer stated that there was a recall in 1997, but he did not find out about it 2011.
(rel#98-017)
11/11/2013) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. He advised the technician of the problem. The consumer was advised that the fan was not turning fast enough. The consumer stated that there is not anything to adjust the fan.

The manufacturer offered to replace the heater.
justification: The incident involved a heater malfunction causing smoke and paint burning, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
11/08/2013) The consumer stated that he was testing the smoke alarm. There was no sound. He replaced the battery and tried again. The same thing happened. He set the product aside for two or three days. He tested it again. The consumer stated that the alarm sounded only once out of ten times that he tested it. The consumer stated that he had someone else to test it. They got the same results. 

(11/12/2013) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. He was advised to return the product to the place of purchase to get a replacement.
justification: The smoke alarm failed to function properly, which is an incident but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: Kenmore Vacumn Cleaner Model # 116.35923500.  I turned on cleaner and received a electrical shock in my hand.  Unplugged machine and tried to restart.  Nothing happened.  Machine is dead.  No motor running or suction.
justification: The user received an electrical shock, indicating an injury (severity 3), but the incident appears isolated and unlikely to recur frequently based on the description.

incident_description: I PURCHASED PEPPERMINT TWIST CONCENTRATED ROOM SPRAY FROM BATH AND BODY WORKS.  AFTER FOLLOWING THE DIRECTIONS I SPRAYED TWO QUICK SPRAYS INTO THE ROOM, WITHIN 45 SECONDS, MY HUSBAND AND 4 YEAR OLD GRANDAUGHTER AND I, STARTED COUGHING, GAGGING, CHOKING AND GASPING FOR AIR.  IT MADE OUR THROATS SORE AND EVEN THOUGH WE WENT OUTDOORS AND TRIED TO AIR OUT THE HOUSE, OUR THROATS WERE ALREADY RAW AND SCRATCHY.   THIS WAS UNBEARABLE AND VERY UPSETTING.  IT LASTED FOR ABOUT 20 MINUTES, BUT THE SCRATCHY THROAT CONTINUED FOR ABOUT 4 HOURS.  WHEN I GOOGLED IT ON THE INTERNET, IT SEEMS TO BE A PROBLEM FOR MANY OTHER PEOPLE
justification: The incident caused physical harm (coughing, gagging, sore throats) to multiple individuals, indicating injury severity. The mention of similar problems for many other people suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description: i turned on heater on medium heat at 1200 watts and 20 min later my floor set fire my floor is burned up bad its a huge spot i unplugged imediantly and the cord was hit and i had to throw water on the fire to put it out
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant damage to the floor, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
This is regarding an Optimus Heater Fan with plug burn damage. It is item # H-1382. I purchased this fan heater to use at my work. I use it just about an hour or two in the morning to take the chill out of the air. Yesterday I smelled plastic burning coming from the unit at the electrical outlet and immediately pulled out the plug and I had the electrical engineer examine it. He said it was not the electrical outlet, but rather the plug that was burning up (internally). Part of the burn discoloration extends up the cord for about an inch or so. Most of the burn was located at the end of the plug which even melted the electrical wall socket protector. I have photos showing the burnt plug.

This unit has only been used less than a year and not used but just 5 days a week for about a couple of hours (at the most), and even less usage in the warmer monthsÃÂ It was a good thing that it didnÃÂt happen while I was away from my desk as it could have started a fire. Please let me know if there was a recall or others that had this same issue with their units. I bought this unit because it had the safety features (like tipping and auto-shutoff) but even now, I will try to remember to turn any heater fan off when walking away from my desk, even for just a few minutes, as it was a scary momentÃÂ.

This is NOT an issue with the electrical outlet. It has been thoroughly examined and the issue is the Optimus PLUG, which is shown to be burnt from the inside and even along the cord, as it melted onto the electrical outlet. The engineer that investigated said that the only damage on the electrical outlet is the plastic that melted from the cord, as he physically examined booth the electrical outlet and then the Optimus unit. No spark or fire occurred because I was in my office and was available to turn the unit off and unplug immediately after smelling burnt plastic. This would have resulted in something far more serious had I left my office! 

I contacted Optimus and sent photos showing the cord (burning INSIDE the plug and ALSO burn damage inside the cord). 

I bought a new [REDACTED] unit (in operating order with the red light on) and working just fine plugged into the other electric outlet that was not melted due to failure of the Optimus unit. The burnt remains of the Optimus plug is just below the current outlet used by the new [REDACTED] unit. Optimus stated that is was a faulty electrical outlet that caused their unit to burn up, but this would NOT be possible since I'm currently using the same outlet with another heater/fan unit.

Please let me know if you need photos of the Optimus unit that almost caused an electrical fire!
Thanks for your time in reviewing this.
justification: The incident involved a plug burning up, which could have led to a fire but was caught in time, resulting in no injury or death.

incident_description: Well-McLain Gas Boiler Ultra Model 155 CP5032702 with corroded holes in exhaust of aluminum heat exchanger.  Carbon Monoxide leaking into room.  Contractor reports multiple reported problems with the aluminum heat exchanger in this unit.   Many manufactures are using stainless steel heat exchangers.  Well-McLain is the only one using aluminum heat exchanger that I know of.  Extreme safety hazard!
justification: Carbon Monoxide leaking into room poses a life-threatening risk, and the description notes an 'Extreme safety hazard' with multiple reported problems.

incident_description: Was using an Ryobi Orbital hand Sander  for only two minutes when the plastic housing disintegrated on the left side of the unit, making a horrible rattling sound, and the internal metallic vibrating ring shattered into 3 pieces along with 15 pieces (that I found and picked up) and flew in different directions. Luckily for me, I only had a few minor cuts and one longer minor laceration on my adjacent left hand.
justification: The incident resulted in minor cuts and a laceration, indicating an injury, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such equipment failures are not uncommon but not frequent.

incident_description:
Similar to recall Alert #11-725, our door lock failed on our laundry room door on November 24, 2013. It was a privacy lock, and the button had accidentally been pressed in.  A screwdriver failed to open it, and it was impossible to open the door.  Since 2 neighbors had the same issue, I am concerned this could happen to others.  Luckily I was not on the inside (since my toddler was running around on the outside) but was scary to think how long I could have been locked in, if that had happened.

A handyman came the next day to completely remove the handle from the door and disassemble it.

Our locks were not in the recall dates above, since our condo was built in 2007 (though we were the first to own/live in our condo last May, 2012) we were past the warranty dates as well, though the company agreed to replace all of the locksets in our condo.  

Manufacturer: Stanley Security Solutions Inc.
Lock: 6K/7KC
Date on lock: Sept 26, 2007 
Stainless finish
justification: The incident involved a door lock failure with no injury or death, but it caused a temporary inconvenience and potential safety concern.

incident_description: I purchased one of these washers about two years ago. I received a recall notice and the LG technician came out to perform the fix for the recall.  At that time, my machine was making a grinding noise that the technician said was related to the recall.  The fix he applied corrected the grinding noise, just as he said.   The machine has been working fine until recently when the grinding noise started again.  I called LG, who said the machine was out of warranty and I needed to submit my receipt for a one time extended warranty before they could send someone out.  I told them it was the recall problem again and that they needed to get someone out here.  They said that the recall had been fixed, and the problem was not likely to be related.  I was told that it would be at least a week before they would call me back to schedule a repair.  I was not told to discontinue use of the washer.  Today my washer exploded.  Pieces of the spinner inside broke apart and badly damaged the drum.  Metal was flying around inside.  I managed to turn it off before it broke the glass in the lid, but the washer is probably now a total loss.  I will call LG, but they seem to be less than helpful about this.
justification: The washer exploded causing significant damage to the machine but no reported injuries, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I have a 9000 KW Champion portable generator purchased about a year ago.  

I try to run it regularly for maintenance, and last week I had trouble getting it started.  Finally it started, but with difficulty, and ran very rough.  I let it run, went inside the house, and a few minutes later it was making so much noise I looked out the window and flames were shooting out of the exhaust!  I ran out, and with much trepidation (it was very scary looking!), turned it off.  I called Champion and they said it sounded like a carburator.  They said they would send me a new one and if I could transport it to an approved dealer, would cover labor.  Well, it would probably cost me a few hundred dollars to get someone to come here with a truck, load it, drive it to Norwalk CT (I am in West Redding - about 1 hr away) and then go pick it up again!  They said it was up to me to either cover the cost of delivery and pickup or to install it myself!  
I then googled the problem and found that they had recalled a number of their generators for faulty carborators causing fire - just like mine!  I emailed them and they said that mine was NOT included in the recall, and thus, they would not cover the cost of having the repair transport.  What am I supposed to do?!   I'm 64, disabled woman, 5'2" tall and arthritic hands!
justification: The incident involved flames shooting out of the generator, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased the CritterZone Pet Air Purifier Wall Unit from Litterboy.com and plugged it in and set it on low. It produced an awful metallic chemical smell that made me extremely ill. The smell has lingered in my condo unit and is in my clothes in the closet, couch, bed, EVERYWHERE.
The first night, I woke up in the middle of the night with shortness of breath and an insane headache. When I got out of bed I was dizzy and began to feel nauseous. I immediately unplugged this toxic product. I could not get back to sleep and the headache lasted for 3 days.
This product also made all three of my dogs sick. My dogs were lethargic and did not eat or drink for 2 days and were breathing heavy. My pitbull vomitted. 
The next morning my neighbor came over because the stench had seeped through into her unit. I showed her the product and she said that it was an ozone generator and was illegal to have those in California, that they had been banned a few years ago.
I've done everything to get this smell out out my condo. I've had every window open and have been freezing. I've had to wash EVERYTHING and spent 4 days doing laundry. When I leave and return home I get a headache after being home for awhile and have woken up with a headache every morning since. I can't believe this product caused this much damage in a day and a half. It has  been over 2 weeks and the chemical odor this product produced still lingers in my condo.
What was even more upsetting then the damage this product caused to my health and home was the customer service I experienced from Litterboy.com. I contacted them and notified them of what happened and said that maybe the unit was defective to cause so much harm. I requested to return it and receive a refund. In their reply they refused to refund me because they said the product was used and that it may be defective and I could call and have them trouble shoot it. Why the heck would anyone want to plug that harmful product back in, unless they were suicidal?
I didn't bother arguing with the company because it was clear they did not care and had no intentions of providing the proper customer service to resolve this issue . I did research on the internet and found through product reviews that other customers had similiar experiences from this product. The company is mismarketing this product and should make it known that this product produces ozone which is harmful and even fatal.
justification: The incident caused injury to both the user and their dogs, including symptoms like headaches, nausea, and vomiting, and the product's harmful effects persisted over time.

incident_description: Lasko tower heater model 5397 plug overheats at outlet. Cord also over heats at base of tower. Does this in all outlets including outlets with breakers. Heater gives off noxious smell that causes coughing and sore throat. Concerned fumes are toxic.
justification: The heater causes coughing and sore throat due to noxious fumes, indicating injury.

incident_description:
Regarding:  Lasko Model 5848.  1292 (date stamp info perhaps?) printed above the info of 120 V 60 Hz 1500 watts.  Purchased a year ago from Walmart in Fairfield, CA

My heater's cord kept getting warm and soft to the touch.  After a week of dealing with it and it getting worse, I asked an electrical minded friend why word the cord's end piece do that.  My friend told me it probably has too thin of a cord to handle the power going going through it.  I thought,"Well that doesn't sound right.  Why would a manufacturer put too thin of a cord on it?" Indeed, it has a thin cord as if powering a small portable stereo.  Next day, I noticed smoke and fire coming from the outlet.  Immediately, I turned the unit off, then unplugged it.  

[REDACTED]

incident_description: Bionaire BH3699 portable heater. 120v/60Hz. 1500w. Plugged directly into wall w/o extension cord. Used in occupied room. No obstructions, not covered, not blocked. Nearest furniture 4-6 feet away. Had been in normal use for about 90 minutes without prior interaction or contact since switching unit on. Sudden, loud arcing/crackling/copious, acrid smoke occurred behind plastic end cap near thermostat knob. Unit unplugged within 10 seconds. No injuries, no property damage, occupants were forced to leave room due to burning plastic smoke.
justification: The incident involved a sudden electrical malfunction causing smoke, but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
Included in this statement is an email I sent to Consumer Reports about the installation of a Bradford White Hot Water Tank in my residence and my concern about the safety of the Liquid Propane controller used on the appliance.  The second part of this report is the response from Consumer Reports about the hot water tank and contacting the US Consumer Product Safety Commission.

Dear Consumer Reports,

I write this email about my experience with a new Bradford White hot water tank installed on August 8, 2013 and my doubts about the safety of the Bradford White Hot Water tank equipped with the Honeywell Icon Controller labeled for use with Liquid Propane. 

My old hot water tank failed.  I called a local licensed contractor to install a new hot water tank for my home.  The tank that was recommended and installed was a Bradford White KA17715748 MI5036FSX 50 gallon.

After the installation the smell of raw Liquid Propane was evident not only in our large utility room, but other areas of the house as well.  The smell of Liquid Propane increased dramatically during the first month of service. So much propane at times, that we had to open windows periodically to lessen the smell. The county inspector, that inspected the new hot water tank installation, stated that there should be absolutely no propane smell being given off by the new hot water tank and I should call the licensed installer immediately. I looked on the internet and saw that other owners of the Bradford White hot water heaters using the Honeywell LP controller were reporting similar problems with the smell of propane.  I called Bradford White to ask for their recommendation.  They stated it was normal for the Honeywell controller to vent LP at a rate of 20CC's.  But could not answer my question to whether this was per second, per minute, per 5 minutes or over what time span. I then called the licensed contractor. They called Bradford White. Bradford White gave them the same story. 

My contractor sent a tech specialist to inspect the hot water tank.  After an inspection by their tech he found a leak of LP along the upper edge of the Honeywell controller. This Bradford White Honeywell Icon LP gas controller with LED was changed for a new controller of the exact same type.

Again in the beginning there was a faint smell of Liquid Propane, but as time progressed so did the quantity of propane smell increase.  From the middle of September to the middle of October the propane smell at times was alarming, especially when you walked into the utility room where the hot water tank was located. The smell of propane was extremely strong when the utility room was left undisturbed for a long period of time. Again we had to start opening windows and/or turning on bathroom fans. With winter coming on and the probable use of our furnace I requested our Liquid Propane provider to do a system inspection.  The Propane Provider checked every connection starting with the propane tank. They checked the regulator, all connections within the house including a LP fireplace, furnace, and the hot water tank.  The Propane Provider's tech Red Flagged the hot water tank and stated no amount of raw LP should ever be leaking from any device, especially in the quantity the hot water tank was leaking from the second LP controller. He recommended we permanently turn off our hot water tank.

Again I called the licensed contractor who installed the hot water tank.  They sent a different specialist out to inspect the hot water tank.  He also concluded that he was concerned with the amount of LP being given off by the second new Bradford White Honeywell controller.  The leak from the controller was coming from the area where the heat dial pushes a button into the controller to increase or decrease the burner propane for water temperature.  He wanted me to turn off the hot water tank until a fix could be performed. No hot showers for a possible two week period was unacceptable.  Instead of turning the tank off he allowed me to place a fan in front of the hot water tank to dissipate the LP fumes into the utility room coming off the controller.  The leaking hot water tank is installed next to the LP house furnace. The tech was more concerned with a buildup LP on the floor and the hot water tank igniting causing a flash explosion. He wanted to go back and give a report to his office to see what they wanted done.  Higher ups within the office called Bradford White.  Bradford White sent new controller. 

This controller is of an older style similar to the [REDACTED] controller on the old, replaced water heater.  The older style of controller does not leak LP.   Problem solved!  No smell of LP in the utility room or being evident anywhere within our 3,000 square foot house.  

BUT: Do all Bradford White Honeywell Icon LP gas controllers leak? Where the natural gas controllers do not? Are the Bradford White Honeywell Liquid Propane Controllers on hot water tanks in reality safe without the threat of explosion due to a ground build up of propane? Are the Honeywell controllers really designed to vent continuously?

Is there a major structural defect in the Honeywell Icon LP gas controller for LP? Or was I just unlucky and got two bad new controllers in succession?  The contractor stated that they have installed hundreds of the Bradford White water heaters which used the Honeywell Icon LED Controller with no problem, but using Natural Gas not Liquid Propane. 

I am a subscriber to Consumer Reports.  I do not keep an archive of the publication on hand.  Could Consumer Reports shed some light on this subject?  Have you tested the Bradford White Hot Water Heaters with the Honeywell Icon LP Controller?  Is this hot water tank dangerous with the LP controller? My most important question... What are the laws that govern the amount of raw, flammable liquid propane (or Natural Gas) that can be "vented" into a room or home from a hot water heater or any LP device?  All individuals in the know that I have talked to about this question state that no flammable gas should ever be vented from any device within the confines of a home or dwelling.

incident_description:

incident_description:
Coleman Furnace, Model DGAH077BBSA.
About a month ago my furnace failed to stay ignited. I traced the problem to a burnt off wire from flame sensor located inside heat ex-changer, attached to main burner. Wire had about 2 inches of insulation burned off and was detached from quick disconnect at flame sensor. I replaced quick disconnect and cut back burned section of yellow wire. Two weeks later, wire burnt again. I observed massive flame up through burner window when main blower kicked on. Further inspection of heat exchanger revealed about a six inch crack and about an inch whole in the heat exchanger. The crack and hole are pretty much in line with and opposite of main burner. Removed furnace from service on 11/26/13 pending repairs or replacement.
This furnace was installed new through state/county weatherization program in June of 2001
justification: The incident involved a furnace malfunction with potential safety hazards, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:

incident_description: The dehumidifier was being used in an unfinished basement.  I was in the first floor watching TV at around 11:30 pm on the November 29th when I heard a few odd cracking noises and started to smell burning.  I quickly went to the basement to discover the dehumidifier unit pouring out smoke and flames.  After dousing the unit with multiple buckets of water I was able to successfully mitigate the fire.  Unfortunately the basement and the rest of the house was filled with smoke that I had to open windows and doors on a night that dipped into the single digits. incident_description:

incident_description: Ok, I have to share this because I have several scented-wax warmers (mine are Scentsy) and had no idea how dangerous they could be. Last week my 2-year-old niece [REDACTED] was chasing her kitty under the kitchen table and got tangled in the Scentsy cord that was plugged in. The Scentsy tipped over, and the wax spilled and ran off the table onto [REDACTED] 's neck and back. She has 2nd and 3rd degree burns on her scalp, neck and back, which may need skin grafting in order to heal. She will certainly be scarred. In many of the Scentsy faq's it says "The wax temperature is very low, just above body temperature. The wax never gets hot enough to burn anyone so it is completely safe around pets and kids." I put the candy thermometer in mine just to see how hot it was and it read 140 degrees F. That's hot enough to cause 3rd degree burns in 5 seconds. There needs to be warnings about burns on the Scentsy warmers like there are on some other brands.

incident_description: I purchased a First Alert model CO400 Carbon monoxide detector Lowes. After installing the battery I noticed that it only functioned if the detector was turned on its side. If the detector was in the upright mountable position the test would not work and the alarm would fail to sound. This is due to the fact that  the alarm is designed such that the battery does not make proper contact with the battery leads in the battery compartment unless the alarm is turned on its side. Therefore, under normal circumstances the alarm will not be receiving power from the battery and will not be functioning even when the homeowner assumes it is. As there is no LED to indicate that the detector is functioning the homeowner will not be aware of the problem.
justification: The detector fails to function in its intended position, posing a potential safety risk without immediate injury.

incident_description: My house is all electric and has King Pick-a-Watt electric wall heaters, 240V, model PAW2422. My house is not a manufactured home or a trailer.  I have been vacuuming the dust out of the inside of the heaters once a year as King recommends.  Two of the heaters have caught on fire, one in the bathroom and one in the kitchen .  I did see and hear the kitchen heater fail.  I was sitting across from the heater in the kitchen when I heard a pop noise, like a small firecracker, looked over at the heater and saw the metal rod that goes through the heat fins glowing bright red on the right side, followed by flames coming off the rod for about a third of its length.  The bathroom heater also glowed bright red in the same place, followed by flames, but I did not hear a pop noise.  The heaters did not shut off, I turned them off, and neither heater dropped its breaker in the main electrical panel.  I have wired in smoke detectors, one very near both heaters, and it did not go off.  I have two more heaters that were turning themselves off and was told by an electrician that the heaters have a thermal switch that should shut them off if they malfunction.  I had a licensed electrician replace all four heaters.  One of the new heaters failed after about 3 hours' use and I returned it and bought another one - which is a 25% failure rate for this King product.  The new unit that failed started making screeching noises, like a dry or worn out bearing, and a thumping noise.  It also smelled very strongly  and set off the smoke detector. Eventually there was a tan stain on the grille on the right side and the paper label on the back was scorched.  I had that unit replaced and had to pay another service call for the work.  I contacted King by email through their web site on November 6 because I was and am concerned about the fire danger from these product failures.  I would expect that any malfunction would shut the heater down.  If I had not been at home when the heaters caught fire they likely eventually would have set the wall framing and sheetrock on fire.  King offered to replace four heaters, but by that time I had already bought and paid for the installation of new ones - it is winter and cold where I live.  I asked them to pay for the service call to replace the new out of the box defective heater and so far they have declined to do that.  I was without heat in the kitchen and bathroom for about four days until an electrician could do the replacement work and had partial heat in the living room where the other two heaters were replaced.  There have been multiple emails and phone calls between myself and a representative of King but as of today  their only response has been to ask me to return the kitchen heater that I heard and saw fail so they can examine it and to ask for photos of the kitchen and bathroom walls.  They have not compensated me in any way for the service calls, the defective new product, the four defective heaters, or the danger to my property and my life.   Because no one can tell me why this happened or why the two heaters did not shut off when they failed I live 24x7 with the stress of wondering when the next failure will occur, and I'm reluctant to leave the heaters on at night or when I leave my house.  As it's been almost three weeks since  I notified King and they've been indifferent to or very casual about my situation I thought I'd better file a report in case this happens to someone else or someone's home does catch fire.  I have photos of the kitchen and bathroom walls and the kitchen heater but can't get them to upload or attach.
justification: The incident involved fire hazards but no injuries, making it a severity level 2.

incident_description:
Gas dryer manufactured by Whirlpool, model WGD9400SW0, serial MU3510660, purchased new & professionally installed circa November 2007.

In September I noticed that, after running the dryer, the smell of natural gas was present. As the dryer runs unattended in the basement, I believe that this had been the situation for some time. I contracted the original retailer for repair. Initial diagnosis on September 27, 2013 was a faulty gas valve. The repairman noted that the glow igniter was shutting off prematurely, and the dryer was venting unburned natural gas into the dryer while the dry cycle was running. The gas to the dryer was shut off while parts were on order, as accumulating natural gas in the dryer and/or dryer vent is a fire hazard.

Final repair was done on October 15 when the parts came in. My understanding is that both the flame detector and gas valve needed to be replaced.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak which posed a fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.
