He stated that to shut down the dehumidifier he would have to manually shut it off. The consumer stated that since itÃÂs was not automatically changing modes it would over heat. The consumer believed that his unit was posing the same hazard stated on release #12-240. The consumer stated that his unit was over heating and it was emitting an odor such hot oil. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured and there were no damages to his home structure. 

The consumer stated that his unit was no longer under warranty, but he will contact the manufacturer to file a report. 

The consumer stated that he believed that this product should be investigated due to the fire hazard that it poses.
justification: The dehumidifier malfunctioned and overheated, but no injuries or structural damages occurred.

incident_description: I Was charging my [REDACTED] with a Enercell Micro usb AC charger when my fiance went to sleep. The charger is right behind the bed and had worked fine for a month or so in that location.  I was staying up late and left my Fiance in the bedroom to sleep. I went into the bedroom about 8 hours later myself to go to bed and smelt plastic. I checked behind the bed where the charger was and my hand bushed up against it immediately giving me a small burn. I Unplugged the device instantly and found the device had begun to melt exposing metal (which is what burned me) as well as begging to catch the bed my fiance was sleeping on fire (It was smoldering). This is INCREDIBLY unsafe. The melting is prominent on the top of the top left corner of the device ( with the cord also to the left). It extends out to the N in the text Enercell on the device. Melted plastic and metal is clearly visible where the melting occurred and my bed has melted plastic as well as a hole in it from the heat.
justification: The incident involved a small burn injury and potential fire hazard, but no death or severe injury occurred.

incident_description:
Dryer purchased November29, 2008 from Lowe's.
Caller is reporting that on Friday, May 24th, 2013,  his dryer DOM- unknown caught fire.

The lint trap had been cleaned before use and the dryer had been running between 30 and 40 minutes when the caller heard his smoke detector's sounding.
He began to search for source, found the dryer with smoke and flames a few inches high coming out of the control panel.
There was only about a medium load of clothes in the dryer.
Caller called 911 for the fire department.  Then he used his fire extinguisher, and turned the circuit breaker off.
Caller is reporting this appliance as a severe fire hazard due to belief that if he had started the dryer and left his home or gone outside around his home then it may have burned.
Caller spoke with manufacturer around May 28th, rep adised him that the unit was no longer under warranty to which the replied that as a rule a consumer doesn't think about the units catching fire.
Caller has had the dryer repaired at his own cost of $425.00 and he is asking for reimbursement at manufacturer expense.
There are no injuries being reported.
justification: The dryer caught fire, but there were no injuries reported.

incident_description: We have shower doors made by Kohler, model number K702200-MXAB. Today they spontaneously exploded. Luckily nobody was using the shower,and it had not been used all day. There were tiny shards of glass behind the toilet and sink as well as in the air conditioning unit. Fragments were also embedded in the bathtub.
justification: The shower door exploded but no one was injured, classifying it as an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Elite Washer purchased unit 11/15/2009.

Unit worked fine for the first year then the next year the caller noticed that the machine was vibrating, it was not as quiet as it had been the first six months and that it seemed to be getting progressively loud but she saw no reason for alarm.

During the past six months the washer has become increasingly loud and has begun shaking so loudly until Sunday, July 7th, 2013 caller loaded the washer then started it and the unit seemed to be working at least as well as it had been in the past.

Once it entered the rinse cycle it was literally jumping up and down from the vibrating/banging tub then just stopped working.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them

There have been no injuries
justification: The washer malfunctioned but there were no injuries reported.

incident_description: I was cleaning the top of my washing machine and went to get into the cupboard above it when the stepladder broke it sides cracked and I fell onto my tile floor landing on my tailbone and scraped my shin. The stool states that it holds up to 300 lbs and I do not even come close to that. The stool is approximately 6 years old. I emailed Rubbermaid to see if anyone else had this problem but have not received a response yet. I could have been seriously hurt and this item needs to be recalled before someone else gets hurt. I was using exactly as stated and have never had a problem with it before I saved it and can mail it to you if requested.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall causing injury to the tailbone and a scraped shin, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the age of the stool and the unexpected failure under normal use.

incident_description: I purchased a Skiva PowerFlow QuadFire 4-port USB charger from Amazon on June 23rd, 2013.  It is rated to operate with input voltages up to 240VAC.  So I took it to Europe with me and plugged it in to charge my [REDACTED].  I was in France at the time.  I noticed that when I touched the metal casing of the [REDACTED], I would get a continuous electric shock.  The charging ports seemed to operate sufficiently to charge my electronics, but there was obviously some voltage on the USB-ground.
justification: The incident caused a continuous electric shock, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: electrical cord supplied with product blew up in my hand when I plugged it in resulting in copper particles embedded into my skin, carbon black covering my hand and a slight shock.
justification: The incident resulted in copper particles embedded in the skin and a slight shock, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I own a Shark S3501FS Steam Mop. I have owned the product for about a year and have used it less than 20 times. When using the mop I noticed the steam did not seam to be working as well as previous times I used the mop. The steam builds up pressure and then the head blows off and all the steam rapidly escapes. I tried cleaning the head area. I did not see any obstructions so I tried the mop again and the head blew off a second time. I view this as a dangerous situation that could cause serious injury or burns from the steam.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning steam mop that could potentially cause burns, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
My LG Front Load Washing Machine is continuously developing mold on the inside and frequent cleaning with either available washing machine cleaner (ie. [REDACTED] Front Load Cleaner) or Chlorine Bleach is not effective in removing the horrible smell for more than a day or two.  This is extremely concerning as I am allergic to mold and have seen large amounts of mold (blue and grey in color) forming inside of the detergent dispensing drawer.  The clothing coming out of the machine after washing also smells of the mold or mildew, a very strong musty odor that is only removed with either repeated washing on higher temperatures or drying with scented dryer sheets.
I have experiences hives and other adverse reactions on my chest and legs that my allergist believes may be caused by the mold, as well as chronic sinus and nasal congestion.
We also have a small dog who seems to be having reactions to the blankets/towels she sleeps on after they come out of the wash.  We have eliminated using dryer sheets from her bedding with the thought that it could have been a reaction to them, but it has not stopped the breakouts.
justification: The incident describes allergic reactions and health issues caused by mold exposure, indicating injury (severity 3). The persistent mold problem suggests a high likelihood of recurrence (4).

incident_description: I have had to purchase 3 apple laptop chargers in the last 2 years, and know numerous other with the same issue. The charger overheats and begins to spark. The last one started my couch on fire, and this one began sparking and almost lit my bed sheets on fire. The wires become exposed as the charger begins to overheat, melting the surrounding plastic.
justification: The charger overheating and sparking caused a fire on the couch and nearly ignited bed sheets, indicating a significant fire hazard.

incident_description: I installed the Safety 1st Cabinet and Drawer safety latch to keep my 14 month old boys from accessing kitchen drawers.  In installed the latches by following the instructions on the back of the box.  I am a moderately skilled at home repair, comfortable using tools and able to follow directions.  I opened the drawers myself and noticed that they latch did in fact stop the drawer from opening. After installing the device I became concerned that my child would be able to reach into the small opening permitted by the latch so I conducted a small experiment.  I cleared out the drawer and showed my kid some cheerios that I put in the bottom.  He then opened the drawer until the latch caught and tried to stick his arm in the gap that is provided.  He could not reach the bottom of the drawer so he took his arm out and pulled the drawer open a little harder.  The drawer opened to my amazement but not because the latch failed, rather the latch broke.  The smaller than a penny piece of plastic from the tip of the latch had snapped off at the force applied by a 14 month old baby.  I was able to keep my child from swallowing the piece however that would absolutely be an issue if I had not been there to observe the incident.  Wondering if the problem was my fault or a chance encounter, I tried the experiment with a second drawer and got the same exact result.  The screws did not fail and the drawer did not fail.  The catch portion of the latch also did not fail, it was only the long stem like piece that is designed catch on the lip of the catch portion of the device
justification: The incident involved a safety latch breaking under force from a child, posing a potential choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Hello. I recently had an incident with a Monster Power AC outlet, model AV-700, where the on-off switch heated up and the unit became inoperable. At the time, I smelled a burning odor and the unit felt very hot. I threw that unit away and replaced it with another Monster Power AV-700. Just today (after using the newer unit for a couple months) I again smelled a burning odor, but this time the unit had melted and caused a small fire (the carpet underneath had begun to smolder, leaving burn marks). Fortunately I was in the room and avoided a serious house fire. I have saved this defective unit and have taken photographs (attached to this report).

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a small fire and property damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
tech used product 10 ft away, I begin choking within seconds, had to leave the room, unable to work until air cleared (10 min().
read can, contains a "bitterant"  to decrease inhalation abuse.  Called maker at 800-498-7192.
Intake person on recorded line was very difficult, gave up effort and making report directly.
Did inform her used )Falcon Safety Products, Inc., Branchburg, NJ 08876)Dust Destroyer Model 50-07521, upc 86216 07521   dot 2Q dot sp-11516,
contains difluoroethane CAS #75-37-6.
Throat very irritated, will seek medical attention immediately after closing pharmacy at 6pm.
Asked for name of "bitterant" but she would not tell me.
justification: The incident involved throat irritation and the need for medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Caller's son rested his arm on the charger for his Laptop, fell asleep and when he woke the next morning his left inside portion of his arm was burned.

The burn covered two and a half inches to four inches in diameter.

Mother took him to Kaiser Medical where doctor provided an antibiotic cream then advised him to keep it clean and change dressings regularly.

Caller is reporting this incident as a fire safety issue, the caller's son's charger has been replaced but if the unit could burn her son's skin then it could catch fire.

She had contacted the hotline another date but was advised to confirm whether overheating was coming from the charger or the battery on the laptop.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury requiring medical treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as burns from chargers are not common but have been reported.

incident_description: I have a EZ install shower door from Kohler which I installed approximately 4 years ago. I bought it at Home Depot.  The glass door just completely shattered.  Looked just like the pictures everyone has included in their reports.  I was covered in glass and cut!  Thank God it did not happen to a guest! I am a nurse but for a few minutes I considered going to the Emergency Room as I was bleeding quite a bit.
justification: The individual was injured with cuts and bleeding, requiring consideration of emergency care, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting breakers that are in a house where his girlfriend lived at one time.
He is aware after being informed by others who lived in the split level house twenty five years ago that the breakers were faulty at that time and are still considered a danger.
His girlfriend no longer lives in the house and he is reporting because he said his conscience would give him no peace if he did not report the breakers and someone living there was injured in a fire resulting from the faulty wiring, breakers and box.
The breakers do not flip the power off when they are overloaded and there is electrical tape over them to keep them closed.
He does not have the model numbers of the breakers.
He has contacted various county officials who have rebuffed him and advised him that only zoning can assist him.
He states that zoning and the county officials contacted are afraid of the owner of the home because he owns over ninety homes in the area.
He is asking that someone look at the breakers and estimate the safety level for use of them.
justification: The faulty breakers pose a significant fire hazard, which could lead to injury or death if not addressed.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his wife was taking a shower and he happened to be in the vicinity at the moment. The consumerÃÂs wife informed him that the hot water stopped working after few minutes in the shower. The consumer found that odd because the water heater is supposed to supply endless hot water. 

The consumer went into the bedroom closet, where the water heater is located. The consumer observed flashing fire, smoke and sparks coming out of the water heater. Consumer immediately turned off the hot water supply, which also shuts off the flow of electricity to the heater. 

Consumer stated that if he was not at home, this incident could have set his house on fire. 
The consumer has not attempted to turn on the heater after the incident occurred. The consumer is not reporting any injuries. 

The consumer stated that the mounting board and cupboard are both scorched and the heater has melted.  ÃÂAlso, the circuit board is burned to a crisp.ÃÂ

The consumer contacted the manufacturer, who informed him that his product was out of warranty. The manufacturer also informed him that they have made modified the circuit board in some of their water heaters, but they are not aware of any other incidents like his.

The product is not included in any recalls.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning water heater causing fire and smoke, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that whenever the gas fireplace is turned on, approximately 20-25 mins later the CO detector comes on.  He turns it off to prevent CO poisoning.  This has been ongoing for 3-4 years.  He has not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

He feels that this gas fireplace (free standing ) is a health hazard.
justification: The CO detector activates when the fireplace is used, indicating a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Used ladder last night and noticed it was bending in opposite direction - unsafe!
justification: The ladder was observed to be bending, indicating a potential hazard, but no injury or incident occurred.

incident_description:
My wife was using the vacuum and screamed.  I ran in and grabbed it from her, slightly burning my hand.  She ran over and unplugged it while I put out the small fire with a cloth.

I called the distributor who sold us this product and he stated that it happens all the time.

I would think that ANY product that can start on fire, thru its ordinary use, should be recalled as a safety hazzard.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (burn) and a small fire, indicating a moderate severity. The distributor's statement suggests this is a common issue, increasing the likelihood.

incident_description: I was steaming my clothes with a Shark Press & Refresh clothes steamer.  The model number is G550011.  While steaming as I normally do every day, the steamer exploded with a loud pop of steam and the neck of the steamer got extremely hot and burned my fingers.  It was not the steam that burned my fingers.  I believe that the pressure of the steam caused the steamer to rise to an unsafe temperature.  I was just holding onto the neck of the steamer like usual.  When this happened, I put my hand in cold water and later on ice, but my hand burned for over an hour.  Blisters were forming.  I dropped by a doctor's office to get some relief.  Because I was stressing out, I forgot to take a picture of my hand.  However, I have a picture of the skin peeling off after a couple of weeks.  I left a review on amazon.com to warn people of the danger of this steamer.  I see from the comments that this has also happened to a few other people.  Also, this steamer leaks water.  This item should be recalled.  Using a steamer in the normal way should not injure people.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and blisters requiring medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The mention of similar incidents in reviews suggests this is a possible recurring issue (likelihood 3).

incident_description: On june 3,2013 my husband and i purchased the intex spa.  On july 9,2013 we noticed the water had a blue tint to it but was clear.  I then noticed what appeared to be a small piece of soft plastice hanging out of the return flow.  My husband and my son stuck thier hand in the water to grab it and were electrocuted.  The spa comes with its own gfi plug and it did not trip the unit.  It appeared to be working fine except getting electrocuted.  We unplugged it until the following morning when we plugged it back in the digital temp showed various numbers higher then the spa is suppose to go and the water instantly charged again.
justification: The incident resulted in electrocution, which is an injury, but there is no mention of death.

incident_description: I was using step stool and the step broke. I fell off and landed on floor with no major injuries.
justification: The incident involved a fall from a step stool but resulted in no major injuries.

incident_description:
Used RainX Headlight Restoration Kit outdoors (not in enclosed area) and as directed on package, which involved
spraying lubricant on headlights and 3 polishing pads in 3 stages of polishing as well as use of headlight polishing compound (not airborne) and spray sealant (used very briefly at end of process). Instructions do not mention the need for respirator or mask. No known allergies or asthma, and I am in fine health otherwise. First time, within an hour of use, experienced feeling of pressure on chest that lasted one day. Several weeks later, used again as directed to improve one of the headlights. This time within an hour of use, after having felt in perfect health beforehand, experienced irritation of bronchial passages, pain in sternum, severe coughing, coughing up yellow mucus containing pink streaks. Symptoms have continued unabated for over 1 week. No shortness of breath, no pain in lungs outside of central bronchial area, some fatigue but no difficulty exercising. Suspect subtilisn detergent enzyme that mimics mold spores (since lubricant contains "surfactants") or quartz silica (as in 3M's product). MSDS sheets report only one chemical per product in the kit and company phone representative refused to reveal other ingredients (said they were "proprietary"). Physician cannot treat without knowing cause, and company is refusing to assist. Physician suggested inhaler or steroids but I am not having any trouble breathing.
justification: The individual experienced significant respiratory symptoms and chest pain, indicating injury from chemical exposure.

incident_description:
We own a Sterling Plumbing framed bypass glass door set for a bathtub in our home.  The product was purchased from Home Depot in 2012 and is still sold as "Sterling Plumbing Standard 59 in. x 56-7/16 in. Framed Bypass Bath Door in Silver," model 690B-59S.  We were out of town on Saturday night, and when we returned yesterday we discovered that one of the two doors was completely shattered.  Nearly all of the glass had shattered and fallen out of the door frame.  No one was in the house during our absence, there were no signs of entry into the bathroom, and glass had fallen apparently equally between the tub and bathroom sides of the door, indicating that the breakage was not due to impact from one side or the other.

In looking on-line, I see that such occurrences have happened before, and I wanted to report the accident -- and potential for serious injury -- to the Consumer Product Safety Council.
justification: The glass door shattered without any injury, but the potential for serious injury exists based on similar past incidents.

incident_description:
I have a Hoover vacuum which today started emitting sparks from it's motor. I have had the vacuum for a few years. Today I transmitted this information to the makers of the vacuum. They have refused to offer assistance, other than to suggest that I have the vacuum repaired at my expense. Because of the vacuum is a fire hazard I would have hoped for more assistance from them.

Here is a copy of the message I transmitted to the makers of the vacuum:

sparking/flaming motor on U5018-900

Last night I changed the bag on the Hoover vacuum we have. The changing was uneventful. This morning I operated the vacuum and noticed a burning smell. I took off the belt cover to see if anything was blocking the movable parts from moving. Next I removed the rotating bush and the belt and I was able to see back to where the motor was. A plasma (flame looking) light source could be seen from where the motor was. 

Thus it very much appears to me like the motor for this vacuum is sparking when it's in use. This is a new occurrence for us. The vacuum has worked from before this morning. 

The sparking (plasma flame looking light & burning smell) from the motor is of course a fire hazard. 

Due to the nature of this failure I wanted to request assistance from you in this matter, with either repair or replacement.

Flame type light & smoke is definitely being emitted from the motor for this vacuum.

---end of quote

I received a response from TTI Floor Care North America, the makers of the Hoover vacuum in question, first to call their customer service department via phone. Then when I called they said they could not help with a sparking motor over the phone. 

Here is one thing they could have done "over the phone:" Offer to have the vacuum repaired or replaced. These words could have passed from their mouths into their phone and then into my ears. But, they refused to do this, even though the vacuum is now a fire hazard.

Here is the product info for the vacuum:

Hoover brand, model U5018-900
serial number 050400043453
justification: The vacuum is emitting sparks and has a burning smell, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
My partner and I began using Tide Pods Detergent when we moved to our new house in May.  We both developed a nasty case of contact dermatitis which required medical treatment.  After eliminating every other possibility and discussion with our physician, we determined that either residue left in the laundered clothing and bedding, or some ingredient in Tide Pods has caused the dermatitis.

We also noted that Tide Pods plastic packaging is leaving a buildup of some sort of plastic residue on the drainage system of our washer.

This product needs to be investigated.
justification: The incident resulted in contact dermatitis requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as it affected both users but may not be common for all users.

incident_description: WHIRLPOOL ELECTRIC DRYER WED9600TW1. DRYER OVER HEATS AND CLOTHES WERE TO HOT TO TOUCH.
justification: The dryer overheated, making clothes too hot to touch, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
June 28, and again on July 11, 2013 about 9pm smoke and fire alarm  went off through out my home.   Home was filled with acrdi electrical type smoke.   Found all the electronics inside the air handler were toast, control boards, regulators, capacitors, and the fan motor too.   All the wires were burnt off the controls and connections...there was nothing left inside but ashes.

We were luck was contained inside the unit.   Simpson's the Tampa Fl company who installed new for Ryland Homes 8/2005, said that never should have happened under any circumstances.   In fact their tech said he never saw one do that before ever. 

Lloyds Air and Heating Tampa area, were sent by my home warranty company...the replaced the components...not sure they good job.    10 days later it caught on fire again.  

Simpsons office staff said the Bryant 4ton Puron system had a 10 year warranty, but he tech who called me said it was only 5.   Regardless, this is unsafe product and should all be recalled and/or replaced.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage due to electrical fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
There was an explosion and fire in a residential home in Bonita Springs, Florida.  The Bonita Springs Fire Department responded and prepared an official fire report.

The incident was an explosion and fire caused by a defective (leaking) can of CRL Hi-Sheen Glass Cleaner containing volatile inflammable gases.  The leaking gases filled the undersink area of the kitchen cabinets and was ignited by the "electrical spark (Arcing)" by activation of the [REDACTED] Garbage Disposal..

The exposion/fire blew out the front doors and the rear walls of the kitchen cabinets as the homeowner (woman) stood in front of the sink.  She was blown across the.  Her closing was afire and she suffered first and  second degree burns of the body from the front pelvic area down to her toes.  She was taken to the North Naples Hospital for treatment of her burns and the effects of falling over from the blast;  her burns were first and second degree...  

It is estimated that the damages to property is $1,000.   

This produce is not adequately nor properly marked as an explosive, inflammable or hazardous material.  Yet it contains the most commonly known volatile materials in use.  If the can had been properly marked, it may haver been stored in a better location,
justification: The homeowner suffered first and second degree burns, indicating a significant injury but not death.

incident_description: Went to turn on sander.  After about 2 seconds heard popping sound. Housing broke away, shattered and fan/ flywheels shattered sending plastic and metal parts flying in projectile fashion.  Small piece hit leg and caused minor laceration.
justification: A small piece hit the leg and caused a minor laceration, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
Just learned of the recall. Have followed the instructions provided on web site Confirmation Number [REDACTED] Enclosed are the required stickers and plug :from the machine. Even though I paid $243.79 ($229 + $13.80 taxes) for the machine when purchased in 2006 (copy of receipt enclosed), the web site notes I will receive a $90 refund and a $25 gift card within ten (1 0) days. because the dehumidifier was defective, it would seem 1 would be/should be reimbursed the full amount of my expense or be provided with a new machine of equal value. I am not sure your limited offer makes for good public relations. Additionally, I have looked at some web reviews and remain a bit skeptical that I will receive the "settlement" amount within the promised ten (l 0) day period. I shall see. 
The dehumidifier ran "hot" for quite some time after I purchased it. Finally, it stopped collecting much moisture at all. I was concerned and finally stopped using it. Good thing I did when I think of what could have happened! I never received a recall notice warning me of the potential hazard. Finally, in 2010, I lugged the thing back to my local Sears store (Battle Creek Ml) where I had purchased it. I had hoped they could fix it and save me the cost of a new machine. The "fix" cost me $90.54 (receipt enclosed) and never did fix the problem. Go figure! Two years later, a recall was issued on the dehumidifier. I knew nothing about the recall until going through an old issue (November 2012) of Consumer Reports magazine. A special thank you to them for bringing this problem to my attention. 
On this date, I contacted Sears National Customer Relations at 1-800-549-4505 and spoke with a very pleasant and accommodating representative who, at my request, provided me with the Sears' Customer Solutions address. By copy of this letter, lam asking Sears to fully reimburse me the 2010 out-of-pocket costs ($90.54) I incurred in my fruitless attempt at "repairing" the defective dehumidifier.
Please reference Service Order #[REDACTED]. 
I will note that r have been a loyal customer of Sears for many years. In addition to two (2) dehumidifiers, I have purchased refrigerators, ranges, a microwave, a dryer, vacuum cleaners etc. Whenever I was in need of a major appliance or a small appliance, my first thought was Sears. Your response to my request will clarifY for me how much you value your loyal customers and may very well determine whether or not I continue my relationship with Sears in the future. Hoping I can.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
As promised, I received a $90 check and a $25 gift card toward new dehumidifier if purchased before 12-31-13. Both were received in a timely manner- within 10 days as promised by the mfr.  I receieved a recall notice in the mail on 6-26-13- a few years too late.  While I thought the "settlement" cound have/should have been more (as outlined in my 6-13-13 letter), I am 'satisfied' with the prompt response from the mfr.  The matter has been resolved. I am grateful the defective dehumidifer did not result in a home catastrpohe.  

On 6-8-13 I received a call rfom Sears advising me my credit card would be credited the full amount of the repair in 2010- $90.54. As of this date, the credit has not been applied.
justification: The incident involved a defective dehumidifier that posed a potential hazard but did not result in any injury or death, only financial and customer service issues.

incident_description:
I was stepping down from a Werner 366 stepladder while working in my pool lanai.  It is almost impossible to describe what happened.  It seemed like an explosion.  I was thrust downward, hitting the pool deck and ending up in the swimming pool.  I thrust with my legs to reach a ledge and get my head above water.  I was in excruciating pain which was emanating from my left side.

My wife called 911 and helped me stay above water.  The EMS transported me to a hospital trauma center.  At the trauma center I was diagnosed with acute traumatic multiple left rib fractures (3-9); flail left chest wall, acute; left pneumothorax; myocardial contusion; proximal atrial fibrillation, acute; nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, acute; and pnuemomediastinum, acute.

I remained in the hospital for twelve days.

An inspection of the stepladder shows the left front support buckled 3-4 inches from the bottom.  I suspect this buckling catapulted me off the ladder, causing the injuries I sustained.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries requiring hospitalization, including multiple rib fractures and cardiac complications, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely as such severe outcomes from ladder failures are not common.

incident_description:
My wife and I have recently purchased a new [REDACTED] home, and it came with a washer/dryer combo unit. After using the unit for a month the machine starting maiking a loud scratching noise and upon further inspection (running the dryer with the door open) I found that there were actually sparks coming from the unit. We called GE to schedule a service appointment, the apointment was for 2 weeks ago on a saturday. GE was a no call, no show. We then rescheduled for today. GE claims that we cancelled the appointment, which of course is false (why wouldnt we want a machine fixed which is a fire hazard?) GE refuses to stand behind their unsafe product. I have never expierenced a company with such a lack of commitment to quality or customer service.


Model No:
GTUN275EM1WW
Serial No:
GA008088C
justification: The sparks coming from the unit are a fire hazard, which could lead to injury or death, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: High Price. CHEAP parts.  I paid $850 for this premium dryer (or so I thought) model DLEX5101V.  This was definitely a stretch for my budget, but my wife convinced me to make the investment.  After only 18 months, we started hearing this clicking noise.  A couple days later the click turned into a heavy "thump" sound, like there's 2 pairs of shoes inside.  Obviously, I freaked out and call customer service.  The operator tries to sound technical and says, "Can you put the phone next to the dryer so I can try and diagnose".   He goes on to tell me that there's nothing he can do b/c the dryer is out of the 12 mo warranty.  A few days later, while removing clothes from the dryer, I got cut on a sharp piece of metal.  After doctoring myself, I removed the other clothes carefully and noticed a big gaping hole in the bottom of the drum with a sharp edge.  This is completely unacceptable.  I work in consumer products, and this has to be a known issue that has gone unaddressed.  All I had to do was type "LG dryer thump..." and it auto-fills in google search with plenty of incidents popping up.  This product needs to be recalled.  I need this dryer replaced or repaired by a certified technician WITH A WARRANTY at LG's expense.  As if that's not enough, my wife told me that 2 of her bras got ruined but didn't realize there was a sharp piece of medal protruding from the dryer drum.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut from a sharp piece of metal, indicating an injury, and there are multiple reports of similar issues, suggesting a known problem.

incident_description: LA's Totally Awesome Oxygen Orange. I believe this product to be extremely hazardous to the human and pet respiratory tract. It causes extreme burning of the throat and chest. It is impossible not to inhale some of the fumes while using. I believe it could cause hospitialization of someone with compromised respiratory function. I think this product should be completely banned from the consumer market.
justification: The product causes extreme burning and could lead to hospitalization for those with compromised respiratory function, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description: 3y10mo male bit into an ALL detergent pod. Poison control was called and they said to call back in an hour. Patient became sleepy and began coughing. Dad put him in the car to go to ED. On the way, he started hearing audible wheezing, was more lethargic and had perioral cyanosis. He began drooling and vomiting. He was admitted to the hospital for observation and upper endoscopy the following morning. He was noted to have mild proximal esophageal irritation, no mouth ulcers. Patient was started on medication and will be followed by GI clinic.
justification: The child experienced significant symptoms including wheezing, lethargy, and esophageal irritation, indicating an injury requiring medical intervention.

incident_description: We hired a contractor to install 3" of closed cell polyurethane sprayfoam insulation in a retrofit attic.  The application process went horribly wrong while I was in the home and we were exposed to the chemicals.  We were told by the contractor and manufacturer that these chemicals are safe including to my pregnant wife.   The chemical manufacture confirmed misapplication and said all the improperly installed foam had to be removed.  The contractor refused to follow the manufacture guideline.  We continued to live in the home for 4 years while having 2 children born into the environment .  We are all suffering medical problems which have been confirmed by the medical community.  We were told by numerous doctors to abandon our home and  leave all of our possesions behind.  We have been out of the home since April 4th, 2013.
justification: The incident resulted in confirmed medical problems for the family, including two children born into the contaminated environment, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances of misapplication and prolonged exposure.

incident_description: Soleusair GM-DEH-45-1 dehumidifier, manufacturing date 12/25/2011 has stopped working. The unit is overheating and does not produce water.  Concern - fire hazard.  This unit is included in Gree STOP SALE notice.
justification: The dehumidifier is overheating and poses a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury has been reported.

incident_description:
GE Gas Dryer Fire hazard because of lint accumulations.  

On June 27 or 28th, 2013 GE Repair Tech found that the dryer was so hot that he was surprised that they didn't have a fire and advised them not to use it.  He also said that the lint trap was inadequate and the only way to clean out the lint was to go on the roof monthly.

My parents are in their 80s. Product was purchased at Sears earlier this year.
justification: The dryer posed a fire hazard due to lint accumulation, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Responding for requests for further complaints of LG washer subject to the current recall.  My model number is WT5001CW with a serial number 110KW****.
I have experienced the same unbalanced loads with drum vibration.  My problems were NOT with water-proof or water-resistant materials however but with any small load of items.  At times the machine read "UE" even while still running, most often it would ring the unbalanced alarm and would stop, requiring a rebalance of the small load of items.
I bought this item approximately in November of 2011 and have had problems since the beginning.
I have the recall notice and am planning on contacting LG.
Thank you.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washer causing unbalanced loads and alarms, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Purchased a machine tool of sorts, specifically what is known as a silk screen mesh stretcher. The cost was roughly
400 dollars. The item was imported from abroad and sold on an online factory direct website. Upon delivery, the
item and its packaging smelled odd and when left alone in residence, for lack of better terminology, "stunk up the
entire place." The smell was very strong and very noxious and caused nausea. Left the package outside where the
smell spread, causing a neighbor to complain. lt has been left outside for several weeks, and though the intensity of
the stench has decreased, it is still very present. Feel this chemical stench could be a risk to human health.
justification: The noxious smell caused nausea and complaints, indicating potential health risks, though no severe injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The electric drain cleaner machine, model#46769, that I purchased from Harbor Freight on 9/13/2008, has an electric  floor pedal on-switch enclosed in a rubber boot, which presents an electrocution hazard because under working conditions the pedal sets in an area that is usually very wet. Harbor Freight apparently is aware of this since the current model has replaced the electric switch with an air-bladder pedal that pneumatically pushes air though a tube to the on- switch mounted up on the machine away from any wetness.

I phoned Harbor Freight 3 times last week: 9/17, 9/19, and 9/21/2013 requesting either a refund or replacement with the current improved model. All three times, I was told by the customer service reps that a supervisor would contact me within 24 to 48 hours. On the second and third calls, I told the reps that I had been contacted by no one! They assured me that they would prioritize the case for immediate attention.

I believe they are willfully avoiding me because they already know the danger of this product and also know they are protected because I cannot reach them through their customer service.
This item is dangerous and should be recalled. (I have since found out that someone else has contacted the CPSC for the same reason. Refer to report # [REDACTED])
justification: The incident presents a risk of electrocution, which could lead to injury or death.

incident_description:
Caller purchased her dryer approx. mid year 2001.
When it was installed the service tech converted it from natural gas to propane gas.
She used it very regularly for seven years then she moved from the address where it was delivered and stored it in her boyfriends walk out basement until sometime around January 2013.
In January 2013 the caller moved the dryer into her own basement until she could have it installed.

The washer was installed the week of June 16th - 22nd
June 24th the dryer was installed and another conversion kit to change back to natural gas was installed.
All new venting was placed.
Dryer was plugged in by master plumber, it was plugged possibly twenty seconds, all seemed good, safety tech attached dryer with new venting to the dryer and put it in place.
Tech started the dryer, it ran for approximately 30 seconds when the tech leaned his hand on the top left front side of the dryer just above the hinges but pulled it back immediately due to it being hot to the touch.
He touched it one more time immediately, yelled "fire", "get water" then poured the water into a one inch by one inch square where the fire had blown the plastic plug out.

Another plumber was present to help get water. 
He used a faucet near sump pump and near dryer that is usually used to transfer water to the horse barn to fill buckets more quickly.
He said that because it was an internal fire they had to use more water because there was gas involved and if the fire had been an external fire her would have used a fire extinguisher and instructed the caller to contact 911.
They were able to extinguish this fire successfully with water.

Plumber stated that this was the simplest dryer to work on, you can't obtain the incorrect fittings or parts and these were all installed correctly.
He stated that in his honest opinion this incident is causing the fire to keep going constantly instead of lighting and going on and off and the thermostat wires did catch fire due to the extreme heat.

The gas was disconnected and the dryer was taken out of the house immediately
There were no injuries reported
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he has been experiencing with his washer since purchase.  The washer would shake violently while in use, sometimes it would move across the floor, bang into the wall.  It had punctured holes in the wall.  He feels that he experienced similar problems of Recall number: 13-073.  Hazard: An unbalanced load can cause the washing machine to shake excessively and the drum to come loose during use, posing a risk of injury to consumers and property damage to the surrounding area.

The washer became inoperable around 1/2013, he contacted LG and he was referred to factory service.  1/14/13 The service technician advised that the control panel needed to be replace because of electrical wires were short circuit.  On 2/4/2013, the panel was replaced at his expense.  The washer is now operable, but at times still shakes excessively.


The model of his washer is part of the recall but he was never notified of it, he feels that the firm should reimburse him for the repair done in January.
justification: The washer's violent shaking caused property damage (holes in the wall) but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The recurring issue and recall history suggest a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description:
The consumer says that the timer on the dryer caught on fire.  The dryer was not in use at the time.  The panel was melted and burned.  He unplugged it and poured water on it.  The consumer says that he had never had an issue with the unit prior to this incident.

The consumer says he contacted the manufacturer.  They sent a technician on June 7th.  The tech told him that the mechanism in the timer froze and continued to heat up and catch fire.
justification: The dryer caught fire but was not in use and no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was trying to open the Fiskars Contour Rotary Cutter to cut fabric at my home. Upon attempting to open the packaging the Fiskars Contour Rotary Cutter blade came through the left side of the plastic packaging and at that point cut off the pad of my dominant right thumb. There is not a protective cover over the entire blade to ensure safety while opening this tool. The cutter remains inside the packaging as it was not fully removed during the initial incident. The incident happened so quickly that I felt the pain then looked down to see profuse amounts of blood. The pad of my thumb was half inside the packaging and half outside the packaging when my husband found it. He placed the skin back onto my thumb and we went to the hospital. After an 8 hour wait and excruciating pain, the ER doctor re-attached the pad with 8 stitches on half of the injury but was unable to place stitches on the other side of the pad due to the severity of the injury. I am deeply concerned that this accident could happen again to another innocent person trying to cut fabric at home. This product did not have a protective cover over the blade or a warning for how to open it safely.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring medical attention (stitches), but no death occurred. The likelihood is possible (3) as the lack of protective cover increases risk, but not all users may encounter this issue.

incident_description:
[REDACTED]
Consumer Product Safety Commission
4330 East West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814
Subject: Letter of Complaint
Reliance Water Heater Company
500 Tennessee Waltz Parkway
Ashland City, TN 37015
Letter of complaint
On November 18,2012, I purchased a Residential Gas Water Heater for a manufactured
home from Sun Valley Inc. in Truth or Consequences, NM 87901 (SN:1242A006850).
The subject water heater functioned properly until approximately March 2013 when the
water heater temperature regulation began to malfunction. Water temperature in the
subject water heater is always above 130*F, even at the V AC setting which is suppose to
maintain a water temperature of 55*F. A water temperature above 120*F is clearly
hazardous, especially with children in the household.
On June 3, 2013, I contacted Reliance Tech Support and spoke with Representative
[REDACTED]. I advised her about my concern with the water heater temperature. She
proceeded to ask me several questions about the manufactured home, including the
location of the water heater. She advised me that the subject water heater was a
Atmospheric Vent water heater and that I should have installed a Direct Vent water
heater. Because of this all warranties were thus voided. I proceeded to review the
Installation Manual and could not find any reference to what she was telling me. My
findings were that all manual requirements were being complied with.
On June 4, 2013, I again contacted Reliance and this time I spoke with Representative
[REDACTED]. I advised him that I had spoke with Representative [REDACTED] on the 3rd and that I
disagreed with what I had been told. Representative [REDACTED] once again asked me several
questions about the manufactured home, including the location of the water heater. Again
I advised them the water heater was located in a completely sealed enclosure at one end
ofthe closet in the spare bedroom. He proceeded to tell me that the location of the subject
water heater was not a proper location and thus the warranties on the water heater were
voided. I explained to him that according to my research, I felt the subject water heater
installation was in in full compliance with local, state and federal codes and regulations.
He then requested that I send him photos of the subject water heater location so he could
review them with his Supervisors. I agreed to do that. Approximately 5 minutes later,
Representative [REDACTED] called me back and advised me he had reviewed the matter with his
Supervisor and that the photos would not change anything. I asked Representative [REDACTED] 
to direct me to the manual section that described what they were telling me. He made an
attempt to locate it as he had just reviewed it with his Supervisor but was unable to. He
then asked if he could put me on hold so he could get the information from his
Supervisor. I was on hold for one hour so I finally hung up hoping he would call me back,
however, they never returned the call. Apparently Representative [REDACTED] was directed by
his Supervisors to end all communications with me.
In conclusion, I believe Reliance Water Heater Company did not fairly evaluate this
matter. More importantly, Reliance acted in a very selfish, unprofessional manner, totally
ignoring the safety issues related to this matter. They made no attempt to assist with
troubleshooting the problem or advising me on how I could correct the problem. If
replacement of the gas control valve/thermostat would correct the problem, I would have
been willing to do that, at my cost.
Respectfully,
[REDACTED]
CC: FTC-Bureau of Consumer Protection
Washington, DC 20580
CC: Better Business Bureau
Nashville, TN 37219
CC: Reliance Water Heater Company
Ashland City, TH 37015
justification: The water heater malfunction poses a safety hazard with water temperatures above 130°F, especially for children, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
This is a ShopVac wall hanging wet/dry vacuum purchased from a Lowe's store approximately 5 years ago.  It is used in our garage to vacuum out our vehicles and clean up small messes from projects. However it has never been used as a wet vac. This is the second time this particular problem has happened with this vacuum.  The first time the housing around the On/Off switch got so hot it melted around the switch.  This time it got very hot to the touch and my wife said when she went to turn it off she felt a mild shock.  
After the first incident ShopVac replaced the defective switch, without cost,  no questions asked.  This leads me to believe that they were or are aware of this problem. 
After that incident we always unplugged the vacuum after use.
When it use it did not trip the GFI outlet it was plugged into nor did it pop the circuit breaker.
ShopVac 4.0hp  Model# QPSH400 or Model# 87707-91. I can not locate a serial number on the unit.
justification: The incident involved a mild shock and a history of overheating, indicating a recurring issue with potential for injury but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: 45 minutes before his high school graduation party my 18 yo son was just getting out of the shower when glass door suddenly shattered for no reason. I heard the loud noise and went to check on him to find him leaning against the wall in a sea of glass bleeding profusely from his right leg and multiple other cuts on his arms and legs.  After calling for help I was able to apply pressure to the right leg to help stop the bleeding and assess other cuts discovering one on his left leg was also pretty severe. He was covered with small shards of glass. After several minutes the bleeding was controlled enough we were able to get him to the ER. The deepest cuts were X-rayed for glass, cleaned and stitched up. One deep stitch and 6 outside stitches on the right leg and 1 stitch in the left leg and other cuts cleaned.  I would have never expected this danger in our bathroom. What if he had been home alone?  It could have cut an artery.  It could have cut his face. Glass in his eyes. We were extremely fortunate   I this consumers need to be made aware of these issues.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries requiring medical attention, including deep cuts that needed stitches, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: I rested a white t-shirt on my space heater (Optimus H-5210) and it started smoking and set off my smoke detector. Several months later I get an email from amazon.com telling me this product was under recall. I recently called Optimus for a replacement, but they said it is ok for me to continue using my product and that the recall was really just a warning. Is this correct? How do I get a replacement heater if Optimus is not cooperating with me? Will I have to pay for shipping my heater back to them?
justification: The incident involved a t-shirt smoking and setting off a smoke detector, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Targus USB adapter that expands one usb port into four ports.  I purchased 2 of these devices approximately 2 years ago. I was using one and had one still in the package.  Today I got an error message from my computer saying one or more USB devices were drawing too much energy, then I started smelling burning plastic.  I shut off the computer and attempted to find the source of the burning smell and found that the USB adaptor was melting and very hot.  The case of the adaptor had actually warped from the heat. My partner immediately unplugged the device and burned his finger in doing so.  We will not use either one of these products any more and wanted to notify someone in case there were other people in danger. This could pose a fire and personal safety hazard. The model number is ACH&405US serial number 104003228 Item 50.  The UPC code I included in my report is one I got from looking the product up online.  The spare one I have still in package is still packed since we just moved a little over a month ago and have not unpacked everything.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the partner and potential fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the device malfunction but not widespread reports.

incident_description: 3yo male ingested a tide pod in front of his parents. The rapper was the only thing remaining in his hand. He developed vomiting, drooling and went to Emergency Department. He was admitted overnight. He did not develop respiratory symptoms. He had an upper endoscopy the following day that revealed superficial but circumferential burns throughout the entire esophagus. Patient will be followed in GI clinic.
justification: The child ingested a tide pod, resulting in vomiting, drooling, and esophageal burns requiring medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Switch failed repeatedly. The first time the switch failed, I dismantled it and was able to put it back together so that it worked. I noted that the switch was poorly designed, and poorly built. Further, the switch was designed in such a fashion that when the switch failed, the saw would be on, rather than off, which is a major error.

The second time it failed I ordered a replacement switch from Craftsman. I noted that the replacement switch had the same design as the original. The second switch failed within several uses. I did not replace the switch again, and now use the saw by plugging it in to run, and unplugging it to stop it. Obviously this makes the saw more dangerous, and is very inconvenient.
justification: The switch failure and workaround make the saw more dangerous, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: My washing machine becomes unbalanced and either stops or shakes excessively when a load combines towels and sheets.
justification: The washing machine becomes unbalanced and shakes excessively, which is an incident but does not result in injury.

incident_description: The child safety plugs that insert into wall outlets create an extreme chocking hazard. Pretty much any brand as they are all the same size. My son chocked on one. I had to reach down this throat to get it out so he could breathe. These need to be recalled. If I left the room more than thirty seconds who knows what would have happened.
justification: The child choked on the safety plug, requiring immediate intervention to prevent serious harm, indicating a high severity level due to the potential for death.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the electronic charging device was plugged into an outlet for approximately 1 or 2 days.  He was  alerted by his fire alarm and discovered that there were flames and smoke emitting from the device which caused property damages estimated at $12,000.00.  Blankets and pillows were used to contain the fire.  

The caller's insurance contacted the manufacturer and a case number [REDACTED] was given.  He feels that this charger is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer poured approximately 3 ounces of the cleaner into a 1 gallon bucket of water.  He used the mixture to clean some lawn furniture, for approximately 20 minutes.  Approximately 3 hours later, the consumer's hands became irritated and reddened in color.

The consumer noted that he had a small cut on his finger, so this may have contributed to his reaction.
  
The following morning, the consumer took a couple [REDACTED] pills and later that day, his symptoms were gone.

(6/3/2013)  The consumer sent the manufacturer and email about this incident and shared his concerns with them, but he never received a response.


On the front of the product's label, it indicates that it is family and pet friendly, no harsh fumes.  However, in small print, it also has a WARNING:  Eye and skin irritant, may be harmful if swallowed.  Keep out of the reach of children and pets.  Read caution on back.

The consumer said that the information on the product is contradictory and that if someone were to use the product based on the family and pet friendly information, they could sustain injuries or experience an allergic reaction.

NOTE:  This is the first time that the consumer has used this manufacturer's brand of cleaner.
justification: The consumer experienced skin irritation and redness, which qualifies as an injury, but the symptoms resolved without lasting harm. The likelihood is possible given the product's warning and the consumer's minor cut.

incident_description: Electrical connection between master switch/handle module and wand connection to Powermate head shorts out, blackened contacts, melted plastic. Unit sparks when used and handle connection is very hot and plastic has melted/burned.
justification: The incident involves electrical shorting, sparks, and melted plastic, indicating a significant hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The manufacturer and the representative I have been contacting: 

-[REDACTED]
 Founding Partner
KrausUSA

                Port Washington, NY, 11050
-Tel. 800-775-0703 
-Fax 516-621-8900

I purchased 2 Kraus Bathroom Vessel Sink: GV-103-14 on October 4, 2013. I then installed the two items at a nail salon located in [REDACTED]. However, on June 3, 2013, one of the two sinks underwent an explosion. All of a sudden, without any reason, the sink exploded and glass went fllying everywhere. Fortunately, because there weren't any people around the area, no one was injured; however, if people had been using the sink or had been near the area, they would have been fatally injured. 
As a result, I contacted KrausUSA Inc. and have been emailing them. I have been in touch with [REDACTED]. However, he just claimed that it was a problem with the installation and misuse of the product. He refused to acknowledge that it was a faulty product that needed to undergo investigation, although I clearly indicated that I was willing to send them the videos from the security cameras of the investigation and the debris. I was worried that the remaining sink would also explode and put in danger the people, but they did not conduct a thorough investigation. I clearly asked them to visit the site of the explosion and investigate, but they refused to. Without even conducting a thorough and fair investigation, they placed the responsibility on the consumers. However, I followed the instructions/manuals carefully during the installation and the explosion took place 8 months after the installation. It must have been with a problem with the product. I am deeply worried that other consumers who have purchased this product are placed in danger. I sincerely ask you to investigate this incident for the safety of other consumers. 
If it is helpful, I am more than happy to send you the related videos, pictures, debris, and witnesses. 

Thank you.
justification: The sink exploded but no one was injured, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: We had polyurethane closed cell foam installed. Demilec heatlok soy 200, a supposed "green" product. It is giving off VOC's - and has ruined our home.  the date of the incident is the day it was installed.
justification: The incident involves VOC emissions from installed foam, which has ruined the home, indicating significant property damage and potential health risks.

incident_description:
Glass shattered spontaneously on side fixed panel of fireplace. Came home to find shards of glass scattered throughout the living room and adjacent hallway
No fire burning at time.
No impact to glass
no known other inciting causes
justification: Glass shattered without impact or injury, indicating an incident with no harm but potential for future risk.

incident_description: While using a Lowe's Master Forge Grill cleaner, some of the bristles came out unknowingly. When the raw meat was laid on the grill, the wires become embedded in the meat. When we ate dinner, I thought the meat was just a little too "done" on the edges. So I'm not certain if I ate any or not. But definitely took one metal wire out of my mouth before swallowing. On inspecting the grill carefully, there were metal wires from the Master Forge cleaner all over the grill. We only bought this cleaner a little over a month ago.
justification: Metal wires were ingested, posing a risk of injury, though no severe harm was reported.

incident_description: I have owned a munchkin wipe warmer for 20 months and have used it non-stop (always plugged in).  I do not move this product as it remains on furniture.  I recently moved furniture in the room.  The Munchin warmer started to turn on and off sporadically after moving the furniture.  When touching the electrical cord to check the product the electrical cord fell out of the back of the warmer and began to spark causing a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to a sparking electrical cord, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
My Holmes Oscillating Fan Model HAOF87 "Blizzard" has been working fine since we bought it new several years ago.  However recently I accidentally stepped on the cord barefoot and got a 60-cycle shock in my foot.  (I'm a retired Electrical Engineer and I _know_ what 60 hertz current feels like.)

A visual inspection of the chord shows no wear or breaks in the insulation (but my eyesight ain't what it used to be).  It was plugged in with the polarized plug in the correct direction and the outlet is properly grounded.

I would be happy to mail you the fan if you wish.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (60-cycle shock in the foot), but no further harm was reported.

incident_description: I put water in my steam mop and plugged it in.  Usually it starts steaming within a minute or two.  It didn't this time.  I got closer to see if I could hear it.  Then all of a sudden the mop head blew off across the floor and then the steam came out.  I was not hurt but felt that the product was unsafe to use.
justification: The steam mop malfunctioned but no injury occurred, only a minor incident.

incident_description: I have the 16" Climate Keeper fan in my office cubicle. I have had it for about 3 years. I have only used it a handful of times. Two days ago I was sitting in my office and heard something just shatter. It was the plastic blades on the fan. All the blades just disintegrated as I had the fan on. Which caused the blade pieces to fly everywhere. Even though pieces flew into my hair ,it was a good thing I had my back to it. But my niece was looking at it straight on and she was lucky to be far enough from it that she didn't have a pieces fly into her eyes.  I couldn't believe what I saw. That is absolutely ridiculous that that piece would be so brittle that it would break like that.
justification: The incident involved flying debris but no injuries occurred, and the fan's infrequent use suggests such failures are unlikely.

incident_description: I was ironing a pair of pants using a Pro Steam Products PSP-2001 when I noticed smoke coming from underneath the upper portion of the press. Upon further investigation, there was an actual fire consuming the upper portion of the press and I had immediately unplugged it and took it outside.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was promptly addressed without injury, indicating a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
We purchased a "Swirling Sea Glass Vessel Sink" on 3/11/2012 from DÃÂ©cor Planet.  It was installed by a licensed plumber.

On Saturday, 6/15/2013, the installed "Swirling Sea Glass Vessel Sink" exploded.  I had just walked out of the bathroom and could feel shards of glass hitting my back as glass flew in every direction.  The vessel sink literally exploded, making a very large noise, like a gun shot.  Glass shards and tiny glass fragments were sprayed all around the bathroom and out into the hallway.  The flying glass chipped surrounding wall tiles, damaged the [REDACTED] counter top and surrounding walls.  There was glass everywhere.

Luckily no one was close enough to the exploding sink to be injured by the glass.  I am assuming from the distance glass flew and the force of impact into walls and tiles, that the incident could have caused serious injury.

I contacted the vendor and was led to believe the explosion of the sink was a very unique occurrence.  The vendor indicated that this could only have been caused by a bad installation.  However, I questioned why the sink would literally blow up and not just crack from a faulty install.  So, I did some research and have come up with the following reference links, including uTube video of a similar incident and numerous accounts of the same thing happening.  Also included are some analyses from engineers as to why these Glass Vessel Sinks may spontaneously explode.  Bottom line, as far as I can see, is that this product is not safe.

www.metrowestdailynews.com/x329577973
*******************************************************************************************

justification: No one was injured, but the sink exploded causing property damage.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his ceiling fan was installed 05/28/2013 and after approximately 10 minutes he noticed a burning plastic type smell. The consumer stated that he noticed that the fan was emitting the odor and he decided to turn off the circuit breaker. 

The consumer stated that he tried to make sure it was installed properly and turned the fan back on. He stated that the fan started to emit the same burning odor. 
The consumer stated that he believed that the smell was being emitted from the antique shades. He stated that the glass shades were turning a brown color as if it was burning. 
The consumer suffered irritation to his eyes, sore throat and headaches. The consumer stated that he did not receive any first aid or medical attention, along with a friend who came out that night.  Consumer did contact poison control and they informed himto vacate home.  HIS home.
The consumer stated that the manufacturer informed him that they would contact him back.

incident_description:
Text of consumer's letter dated April 15, 2013 to Rowenta USA, with cc to Pennsylvania Bureau of Consumer Protection and Chairman, President and CEO, Kohl's:

I purchased a Rowenta iron at Kohl's Department Store in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania on April 28, 2012 (copy of receipt enclosed). When I was ironing recently, the iron cord shorted at the base of the iron and the electric spark from the iron hit me at the back of my right forearm. This caused a severe burn on my arm (picture of burn and iron enclosed). I immediately disconnected the iron. Then I washed the burn and rinsed it with cold water. The burn continued to sting and itch for several weeks and at times it would start bleeding again. However, this could have been a much more serious injury. I was very fortunate that the electric spark did not hit me in the face or eye; this could have been a very serious tragedy.

On March 23rd, I returned the iron to Kohl's for a full refund (copy of return receipt enclosed). I explained the above to the Kohl's customer service representative, but she made no comment. In the meantime, I've treated the burn daily with an antiseptic liquid until this morning when the scab finally fell off.

I am writing this letter to alert you because obviously this should never have happened. It's obvious that the cord was defective and there is a serious problem with your company's quality control procedures. Otherwise, this iron would not have passed inspection or been sold to an unsuspecting customer. I've bought irons from other companies, i.e., [REDACTED] and [REDACTED], but this never happened with these brands.

I started buying Rowenta irons several years ago after I saw one demonstrated on QVC. I continued to buy them because they produce more steam than other brands and they have vertical steam and burst of steam. For the past several years I've been buying the Rowenta brand at Kohl's; however, it's been my experience that the irons don't even last for a year. Usually, the way I can tell it's time to get a new one is when the iron starts leaking brown water from the vents. This is the first time I've had one that had an electric spark. This is very dangerous!

You need to look into this matter immediately. You need to ensure that Rowenta is producing safe products. This could happen again and the next time, the outcome could be tragic! maybe these irons need to be taken off the market until this problem is resolved. Please let me know what you decide. Thank you. I can be reached at [REDACTED].

I am also sending a copy of this letter plus enclosures to the Consumer Protection Agency. I don't want this--or something worse--to happen to anyone else!

P.S. I called your customer service number (1-800-769-3682) on April 15, 2013 at approximately 11:30 a.m. eastern standard time. I spoke with [REDACTED] and explained the above problem to him. I also asked him to provide me with the name and address of the President of Rowenta so that I could send this letter to him/her. (l could not locate this information on the Internet.) [REDACTED] advised me that he did not have this information. He told me that he would pass the message to you and that you would call me back within 24-48 hours, i.e., April 16-17th. It is now April 21st. You never called back. I can only assume, therefore, that you do not care about the safety of the Rowenta irons. Also, I can only assume that you are not going to provide me with the name and address of your President and, therefore, do not want your President to be made aware of this problem. My only hope is that the Consumer Protection Agency will investigate this matter thoroughly so that no other customer is injured.
justification: The incident caused a severe burn injury to the consumer's arm, and while the injury was not life-threatening, it required weeks of treatment. The likelihood is possible as the consumer reports this is the first time such an incident occurred with this brand.

incident_description:
I currently own an LG front loading washing machine and feel there is potentially a significant safety issue with this machine.  When the washer is running there is no override option to get the door open.  I have noticed this on several occasions and have had to frustratingly wait until the internal mechanism has cycled down before the door will unlock and open.  This time can range from 10 minutes if there is not much water in the washer to significantly longer if there is a good amount of water.  

Each time this happens, I immediately think what if someone had an emergency and needed to get the door open because a child or pet had accidentally climbed inside.  Unfortunately, there is no override or way to get the door open in an emergency.  The parent or pet owner would have to watch helplessly as their child or pet slowly suffocated or drowned in the washer as they waited the allotted time for the machine to cycle down for the door to unlock.  

This seems like a huge oversight and massive potential death trap that should be addressed with LG and any other potential front loading washers.  I did contact LG and they did not seem very concerned but did file a complaint report for me.  They indicated their washers have passed all federal safety inspections.  If this is the case, someone wasn't very thorough when they passed the machine when it does not have a safety override to open the door in case of emergency.  

All appliances can be a death trap for children and pets getting trapped inside.  But to knowingly have a product on the market that locks and has no option to open except to wait for the internal cycle is an accidental death waiting to happen.  Please look into requiring the manufacturer to correct this oversight in not only the LG front loading washer, but in all front loading washers that do not offer an option to open the front door during the cycle.  

Thank you so much for your time.

incident_description:
This incident occurred with my less than 2 year old, $845 LG HE top loading washer (model# WT 5101HW).  I ran into my laundry room on Monday morning after hearing a noise that sounded like an explosion and discovered my washer, about 15 min into the normal cycle with one king set of sheets, With its top detached and resting askew on the base. It was dented all over, had water pouring from its base and the washing drum was detached from the machine.  I immediately unplugged it because there was an burnt rubber smell in the air. My $845 LG dryer was dented so badly during the incident that it makes a grinding noise if it is turned on.   Aftercalling the HH Gregg warranty dept, I was told that this model was recalled.  I called the LG recall center and was asked if I could try running the machine and told "not to worry" that I would get a call in 3-5 business days with an appointment date and time.  Finding this unacceptable, I had HH Gregg call LG to expedite things.  On Wed. A repair man came to my house, told me that both machines were non repairable (surprise!) and that I needed to email pictures to LG. I did this on Wed and contacted them today having not heard from them.  I was told that I would get a call in 3-5 days from them.  I find their response unacceptable and their lack of concern for customer safety appalling.  I have a family of 7 and after spending more than $1600 on a washer and dryer from LG, I expect better service and a faster response time. 

I am so grateful that none of my children or pets were in the room at the time.  A force strong enough to blow the top off of a washer and damage a dryer is dangerous.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries or deaths, as no one was in the room at the time.

incident_description:
I have a Panasonic steam iron that I bought 4 years ago (I don't have my receipt though). The model number is NI-A56NR. 

On 5/21/13 I was ironing my blouse and the iron began to melt it so I turned the iron down to the lowest setting. I started to iron a second piece of clothing and it burnt that item as well. Immediately afterward the iron started to smoke and it started to melt the plastic around the [REDACTED] plate. I turned the iron off but it continued to smoke and melt the plastic for another 5 minutes before cooling down.

I contacted Panasonic today, 5/25/13, and they said that the warranty expires after one year. I explained the situation to them but they would not acknowledge it as a recall/safety issue. I understand their warranty policy but I feel that this is more of a safety issue than merely a simply defect which I define as a product that no longer functions as designed.

Please investigate this further so a potential fire does not occur in someone's house.

Thanks, [REDACTED]
justification: The iron malfunctioned, causing smoke and melting plastic, but no injury or death occurred.
