The consumer stated that the CO alarm in her home went off and her husband checked it. She stated that he removed her, her son and the dog from inside the house. She stated that he was a fire fighter and he contacted the fire department for assistance in checking the water heater. 

The consumer stated that she and her son were taken to the emergency room to be checked. The consumer stated that they were not admitted to the hospital, they were just advice to get lots of fresh air.  The consumer stated that they had to fix the vent fixed the next day. 

The consumer stated that there were other things that scared her about this water heater. She stated that the water heater would not heat up the water properly due to the fact that the heaterÃÂs heat has melted a mesh screen guard located at the bottom of the water heater. The consumer stated that the ashes fall on the sensors and it continues to turn the heater off and on. 

The consumer stated that she believes that it poses a fire hazard.

incident_description: Our Kenmore electric dryer caught on fire and filled the house up with smoke.  If we were not at home when this happened it could have been a massive fire.  The dryer was purchased new from Sears in Chandler, AZ.  Model # is 796 80272900 and the Serial number is 911KWFN00771.  We are the only owners of the dryer.  It has never been worked on since there were no issues with it until now.  We turned on the dryer and smoke began coming out of the front and the back sides.  After turning it off, smoke continued and got worse.  I quickly removed the dryer from the washroom through the garage and out on the drive way.  The two plastic access panels on the bottom back were on fire and melting.  I sprayed water inside the dryer to put out the fire.  Looking through the access panels showed that the inside of the dryer where the motor, heating elements and other mechanical components are located was full and packed with lint.  The hot air return was clear of lint.  It is apparent that the design is defective or was not assembled correctly to allow such dangerous lint build up outside of the lint catcher and the hot air return and in and around the heating element,  wiring and mechanical components.  See pictures.
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the potential for recurrence given the apparent design or assembly defect.

incident_description:
I was vacuuming with my Kirby G4 vacuum when the power fluctuated a second later a heard sparks and the vacuum power cord caught on fire.  I turned the vacuum off, blew out the fire and ran to unplug it.  I came back to look for fires, and luckily non were discovered.  I looked at the cord and damage to the unit.  Where the cord was manufactured to hook onto the handle of the vacuum in a plastic swivel connection, the cord was burned in half with back powder coming out.  

I called Kirby and they offered no concern about the fire hazard in their power cords.  I was told that I could replace the cord for $31 from them or take it to the local distributor 30miles away.  I said that I was told that I have a lifetime warranty.   I was told that they offer lifetime rebuilding warranties.  They checked my record via SN, then said it would cost over $260 to rebuild it not including shipping to the southern states.  

IÃÂm outraged, not just because of the inherent risk of the manufacturing of their vacuum cord, but for obvious disregard to safety with their G4 power cord specifically modified for hooking into a swivel that over the years causes the power cord to break or fray, spark and catch on fire.  Even if I purchased a replacement cord, it would only take so long for the same thing to happen again.  

Kirby needs to recall this power cord on all units sold and replace it with a proven safe power cord for free to its consumers.
justification: The vacuum cord caught fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire was quickly extinguished.

She could not even was a twin size blanket.  She called and called, then the odor started.  The consumer stated that she had contacted the manufacturer several times and they did not provide any assistance. She stated that she contacted the manufacturer one last time to inform them of the odor and shaking problems that she was experiencing with the machine. She stated that the manufacturer sent a technician to her home on 05/06/2013 and he informed her that her machine was included on a recall.

The technician said he was an engineer for LG. He could smell it. He asked consumer if he washed clothing the person would wear in like a chemical plant/industrial. He pulled the bottom of the tub area, it was coated with what looked like some kind of dark slime. 

She stated that the technician upgraded the software of the machine and he also noticed that there was a bad odor inside the machine. The consumer stated that the technician removed the drum and found that the there was a thick layer of mold underneath the drum. She stated that the technician assisted in removing the layers of mold, but there was still some mold left inside. 

She stated that the technician informed her that it seemed as though the machine was not properly installed. The consumer stated that she was not sure it was the person who installed it because the bolts could have come loosed when the machine was aggressively shaking.  

The consumer stated that her 25 years old daughter has been suffering from respiratory problems and its now on an inhaler. Her grandson also had respiratory problems, was on a nebulizer and has suffered pneumonia twice. The consumer stated that she believes that these problems are due to the mold in the washing machine. 

The consumer stated that she believes that this problem should be investigated, since this machine has more problems and hazards than what is being stated on release number: 13-073.

He scraped as much as he could off into the tub next to the washer, but said there is still stuff there.

incident_description:
Dear Lutron Customer Service,

I am alerting you to a major fire safety issue, and asking for your assistance.

I am a homeowner in Altadena, CA and had numerous Lutron Maestro dimmer controls installed in my two story home nearly 20 years ago. They have always performed well, and been a source of pride. Last night, after I went to bed around 10pm, I was awakened about midnight to a very acrid smell.  At first I thought it might have been coming in the windows.  After several minutes, and noticing that the odor was getting stronger, I got out of bed and went downstairs.  The odor was very powerful, and I traced it to the room below the bedroom where I found the lights ON, and saw smoke pouring from the Lutron dimmer switch.  I tried to switch it off, but the heat was so intense and the switch so deformed, that I could not turn it off.  I then ran to the breaker panel and killed power to that room.  

 

Had I not been home, or worse yet, had I not awakened in time the fire could have been devastating.  I am still shaken by the whole incident, and also feel unsafe in the house since there are many more of these dimmer switches installed throughout the house.  The odor is also very stubborn to eliminate.  The attached photos show the switch and where it had been installed.

 

I eagerly await your support and advice.  The device model is MALV-600.


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a significant fire hazard with smoke and intense heat, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a 12 oz container of O'Reilly brand of Fuel Injector & Carburetor cleaner to clean gummed up ejectors thinking it might be better than lacquer thinner that I have used in the past.  After soaking an ejector, I removed it by hand as I have done with other solvents in the past.  My hand became very sticky and felt different than other solvents.  In the process, my other hand came in contact with the cleaner as well.  I immediately washed my hands.  My hands were still sticky.  I ran a test with lacquer thinner to see if it would cut the cleaner.  Not soluble. Gasoline was then used to try to draw the cleaner out of my skin. After washing, still sticky and the hands starting to fill stiff.  I tried a number of other soaps used by mechanics with no luck. The cleaner is still on my hands and sticky.

On the Internet I found the Material Safety Data Sheet on the cleaner.  Under symptoms: it causes defatting of tissue.  Under Medical conditions generally aggravated by exposure: None Known.  The First Aid section says: Wash with soap and water thoroughly.  False! That does not work!  On the cleaner container caution label: Avoid contact with eyes or repeated contact with skin.  Not true!  It should say NO contact and say how to clean off of hands.

To date, my hands still feel stiff and sore even though they no longer feel sticky.   I am inclined to think that permanent damage has been done.  This product needs to have a special caution label with the procedure for removing from hands.
justification: The incident resulted in stiff and sore hands with potential permanent damage, indicating an injury.

not familiar with how hot my termostat gets. There is no modification for this dangerous product. Reversing the

I leaned over and turned on the tub faucet (just for detail sake..tub faucet was left-sided as you face the tub and shower doors were both completely positioned to the right) and, suddenly, one panel of the shower door shattered and completely collapsed into a million pieces, like a glass waterfall. incident_description:
Caller had been having problems with his 7.+ volts cordless framing nailer and it's dependability to fire as many nails as promised.
He contacted the manufacturer on April 8th, 2013 to inform them that the less than one month old framing nailer advertised that it would fire 6000 nails with each charge, however he was only able to fire about 15 to 20 nails before having to charge again.

He was told that it may be a defective battery and the representative (he did not obtain a name) would look into it.

He hadn't heard anything yet from the manufacturer when he needed his framing nailer for work, on April 15th, 2013 he had fired about 45-60 nails and was preparing to charge the nailer so that he could nail 15 or 20 more, however this time when he plugged the unit in to charge it, he heard a loud pop and the battery with nailer burst into bright sparks and flames.

He extinguished the fire, unplugged the nailer then checked the surrounding area.

He contacted the manufacturer again on April 16th, 2004 to advise that he was reporting a severe fire hazard with fire.
He spoke with [REDACTED] who informed him that she would be sending a replacement over night.

He is reporting this product as a severe safety hazard and would ask that the public be alerted, this incident happened outside of his home, most of his chargers are in his basement and he states that the nailer happened to be on charge while he was working outside of the home and while he was standing there but if the nailer had been charging in his basement and if he had been elsewhere it could have burned his home down causing property and potential human damage.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries, and the likelihood is possible given the defective battery issue.

incident_description:
SUMMARY

Over eleven months ago, I followed instructions on the product container to wear eye ware and gloves, when using the Great Stuff product. Unfortunately, this product dropped from my wrist up to my shoulder. In reading the information indicated on the product container in a separate area on the can titled WARNING/DANGER, I later learned that the product is "sticky" and can only remove it "mechanical means, once it dries on skin.

It also indicated that soap and water be used to wash it off. This does not work.

It did not wash or scrub off. The only way I can remove is to scrape it, thereby also removing a layer of my skin as well.

After damaging my bedding from the bleeding, I went to a dermatologist (at my expense) and learned that this was drying out my skin and that I needed to use a skin moistener Instead.

It is over a year now and not completely removed from my skin. I discovered that the best time to scrape some of it off is when I get up in the morning because; blood tends to flow away from the extremities at night. It definitely does not wear off!

Given the difficulty of removing this product from skin, I believe that the container instructions are inadequate, deceptive and remiss in properly warning the user about this potential situation. Using "sticky" to describe this is woefully inadequate. I notified the manufacture in writing however; they claim that they are in full compliance with Federal regulations.

I would appreciate hearing from you, if you agree that the container is in full compliance, as the manufacture claims.

P.S. I can send you a picture of the product instructions vie e-mail, if you request it. My E-mail is [REDACTED]

[REDACTED]

Text of complainant's letter dated 4/27/2013 to CPSC:


Attached is a complaint form for a Dow Chemical Company product Great Stuff. They are claiming that it is labeled to meet all Federal Hazardous Substances Act and Consumer Products Safety Commissions regulations, therefore both or one of these federal organizations are remiss in making sure that the consumer is properly informed. I also enclosed a copy of my complaint letter to Dow Chemical.

Please let me know if the government believes that given the following potential problems that Dow Chemical Company properly labeled this product.

ÃÂ Extremely difficult and painful to remove from human skin

I am asking that the manufacture change the product instructions and for them to reimburse me for out of my out of pocket expense. I look forward to hearing if you continue to believe that this product has adequate instructions and labeling.

P .S. it you enter Great Stuff via the internet, you will discover that a number of people also have had a problem with removing this product from their skin.
------------------------------------------------

Text of complainant's letter dated 4/10/2012 to The Dow Chemical Company:

The reason I wrote to the president of your company is that you did not respond to my March 1, 2013 memo (copy attached). Out of frustration, I wrote to [REDACTED]. As I indicated to him, I discovered via the internet that a number of additional users of your product have had similar problems, removing this product from skin.

The product container indicates the following:

Instructions: Wear glove and protective eyewear (does not indicate that you should also read the WARNING/DANGER instructions indicated separately on the container).

Therefore, I need from Dow a refund for expenses caused by this and the product container instructions need revision.

Again, I do not believe that Dow has adequately indicated important safety and use instruction on the product container. I do not care or need to know if the instructions are in Federal compliance. I would like to believe that a company with the outstanding reputation that Dow has, is going to make sure that customers using their products are not injured or harmed, due to incomplete product labeling.

If you continue to believe that the labeling instruction are adequate, given the fact that there is no solvent or method that can assist in removing this product, once it dries and that it will not by itself in a reasonable time period wear off of skin; please re-state this.

I look forward to hearing from you, in this matter.

Both safety and manual shut-offs failed to work on a residential Brunman Holiday boiler control.  A Honeywell valve is on the broiler, it failed.  The valve is described as Combination Gas Control for Heating Appliances.  It has three positions: OFF, PILOT AND ON.

Neither of the safety functions to shut off the gas flow functioned when tested.  The two problems identified with the equipment are: 
1)  Gas flows through the control unit independent of the position of the valve control knob, and
2)  Gas flow continues independent of whether or not the pilot light is lit.  

Fortunately this problem was found by the homeownerÃÂs father during a safety check.  We have shut off the gas flow using an upstream manual valve.  We will have the gas company and a HVAC contractor inspect and repair, as needed, the entire boiler control system before using it again.
justification: The safety failures could have led to a gas leak or explosion, but no actual incident or injury occurred as the issue was caught during a safety check.

There were no electrical storms nor service interruption in any way.

No room damage nor structure fire occurred because I was nearby. However a structure fire may have developed if this was not noticed in time.

incident_description:
The exhaust vent collar was replaced on my Navien tankless Water Heater on March 6th per recall Release #12-074 due to the risk of an improper seal and subsequent carbon monoxide venting into the house. In my case the seal as installed was ineffective and exhaust was venting into the house. This was due to the Navien vent collar being made of nylon and being unable to be ÃÂweldedÃÂ to the PVC pipe using the regular adhesive used in the plumbing (and other) trades.

A few weeks after replacement of the Navien exhaust vent collar it was noticed that the Vent Terminator had fallen out of the vent pipe to the ground about 15 to 20 feet below. This was likely due to the increased vent flow (now that it was venting correctly) plus the fact that the Vent Terminator, supplied by Navien as part of the Water Heater installation kit, is made of the same type of nylon material as the original exhaust vent collar covered under the above referenced recall. It is apparent that the Vent Terminator had been installed using the same regular adhesive used in the plumbing (and other) trades for PVC fittings. It was not apparent from any Navien documentation (nor visually at the time of installation) that the Vent Terminator was made of nylon rather than PVC. Also, Navien did not provide any alternative adhesive in the installation kit nor information on what should be used as an adhesive between nylon and PVC.

The Navien provided Vent Terminators are intended to provide a ÃÂscreenÃÂ over the ends of the Water Heater exhaust and inlet vents. Without a Vent Terminator installed on the exhaust vent pipe there is the likelihood that birds or other animals can cause a blockage that may result in carbon monoxide venting back into the house where the Water Heater is installed (in our case). This potential unsafe condition is very similar to the one covered under the current recall notice referenced above.

Should the scope of the recall be expanded to cover this issue?

In my communications directly with Navien they have not taken any responsibility for the issue and they refuse to see it as ÃÂtheir problem.ÃÂ
justification: The incident involves a faulty vent terminator leading to potential carbon monoxide leakage, but no actual injury or death reported.

There was no vomiting or diarrhea at home. Patient was taken to the emergency department; he was awake and lucid but somewhat lethargic on exam. He was noted to be afebrile, tachypneic to respiratory rate of 26 breaths/min, tachycardic to heart rate of 140 beats/min, and normotensive with a blood pressure of 126/71; pulse oximetry was  94% on 3L/min supplemental oxygen. He continued to have coughing, productive of yellow sputum, and expiratory wheezing. He developed a leukocytosis with a white blood cell count over 20,000/mm3 and was started on [REDACTED], but remained afebrile. Supportive management included supplemental oxygen, albuterol, [REDACTED], and IV methylprednisolone. His symptoms improved and subsequent chest x-rays showed improvement of the infiltrates. He was discharged to home on 3/14/13.

Known health hazards from inhalational exposure of this product include respiratory irritation, weakness, dizziness, nausea, loss of consciousness, and asphyxiation, per the MSDS. There is a known association reported in the literature between acute  pulmonary toxicity from inhalation of fluoro copolymers as well as hydrocarbons without a fluoropolymer component.

incident_description:
I have a US Craftmaster water heater (gas) that was installed in February 2004. At the time I was a renter in the home I now own. The water heater was installed by a tech hired by the then-owner.
It is a model MHG1F3031T3NV serial 0346123071 (where 0346 is the year/week code).

The heater has a Robertshaw R110RCTS-PC gas valve with a date code of 0345. Even though by date and model this valve falls outside of CPSC's published Robertshaw R110 recall, there has always been a just faintly detectable scent of gas near the heater, and with the help of a TIF 8800 leak detector it has now been shown that all of the piping is good and leak-tight and the leak is clearly around the control knob at the top of the gas valve itself.

On the Association of Certified Home Inspectors forum there are other reports of Robertshaw R110 gas valves being leaky even with manufacture dates outside of the published recall:

http://www.nachi.org/forum/f22/unitrol-gas-valve-leaks-water-heater-28573/

The photos and descriptions posted there exactly match the location where my gas valve leaks. One of the inspectors reported detecting gas at 40% to 50% of these valves tested, even though outside of the published recall. I hoped that some of those inspectors would have passed their findings along to CPSC, but there was no mention of that in the forum, and I have searched CPSC without finding anything about the R110 except the already mentioned limited recall.

I had wondered whether I should just accept slight leakage at the valve as normal, but the TIF 8800 gives no reading at all for any of the other appliances or fittings in my house. Somehow everything else manages to be gastight but the R110 valve does not. I notice in the forum thread linked above that the inspectors also consider the R110 leak rate remarkably high compared to other valves they test.

At 9 AM EST on 5 March 2013 I spoke with [REDACTED] at the Robertshaw recall hotline, who told me (as expected) that my valve falls outside the recall date range and would not be replaced. I asked whether he was aware of any tendency for valves outside that date range to be found leaky. He said one can always leak, there's a gasket there (quote from memory) but that he was not aware of a pattern. [REDACTED] at Craftmaster/American Water Heater also declined to replace the valve, as the heater is by now beyond the warranty period. It looks like I will be on my own to buy a replacement valve, which is ok, but I still wanted to make sure CPSC is aware of a problem that seems to extend beyond the originally recalled date range, because after seeing those inspectors' findings I do not think my own issue is an isolated one.
justification: The incident involves a detectable gas leak from a water heater valve, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: We own two Maytag Neptune Electric dryers.  Model number MDE6700AYW.  The last digits of the serial numbers are 570840GT and 570855GT.  The first few characters have been worn off the sticker.  These two dryers are stacked on two Maytag Neptune washers.  There is an issue with the metal holder within the dryers that holds the power control board (pcb).  This part is referred to as a pcb-holder and is listed as part # 35001168.  This part became fatigued (I'm assuming from the vibrations of the washer the dryer is stacked upon) and the metal split down the side and the metal box and power control board has fallen onto the rotating drum.  The concern here is that when the holder and board falls onto the drum, the board flips over against the drum rubbing the power wires, etc., against the drum as it spins.  This has the potential to cause serious electric shock as the rotating drum wears away the wiring's insulation or other components on the board.  Since the power cable comes directly from the outside to this pcb, the full 240-volts and current can make contact with the drum and then anyone who puts their hand or arm into the drum to remove clothes.
justification: The incident describes a potential for serious electric shock due to the power control board falling onto the rotating drum, which could lead to injury or death if someone interacts with the drum.

Looking into the interior of the unit through the grill/cover, I observed fire within the unit.  Burning material was dripping out of the unit.  The combustion was audible as a crackling sound.  While I turned the wall heat and light switch off, my wife retrieved a fire extinguisher.  A quick burst of retardant from the extinguisher extinguished the flames within the unit.  While conducting this exercise, some of the melted, dripping material resulted in burns to my hand.  This same material also adhered to the bathroom floor.

Once the fire was extinguished, I removed the unit cover.  The assembly's "B" unit, the heater component, seems to be the cause of the fire.  The electrical wiring and plastic enclosure were charred and melted.  The adjacent fan module showed partial melting.

Since my wife was in the room when the fire started, our response was rapid and the resulting damage minimal.  If the fire had started while the room was unoccupied, I believe the results could have been much worse
justification: The incident involved a fire causing burns to the hand, which qualifies as an injury, and the likelihood is considered possible given the described scenario.

incident_description:
The Kidde i9040 Smoke Alarm has design and product packaging defects that will likely result in the unit being installed without a functioning battery.
Specifics:

1) The unit is shipped with a battery installed; however the battery is installed with the its contacts on the opposite end from the smoke alarm unit contacts. As a result, it can easily be perceived that the unit is ready out of the box when it is not. There is no label to advise that the battery must be flipped to make the unit functional. 
2) When the battery contacts are turned so that they can be touch the unit contacts, there is nothing to prevent the battery from being installed such that the battery's positive terminal is on the unit's negative terminal (and correspondingly the battery's negative terminal is on the unit's positive terminal.) 

In short, a battery can be installed in the i9040 in 3 ways, 2 of which will render the unit inoperable. This unit should be recalled and redesigned.

incident_description:

I was shocked to see the entire interior covered with a scorched layer of lint. This dryer could have easily caused a massive fire. I have since cleaned up all of the scorched lint as thoroughly as possible but I believe the issue is that the exhaust duct is not sealed against the blower housing, which allows lint to escape into the interior of the dryer causing this very serious safety hazard. I have since sealed this joint with foil tape used for sealing furnace ducting. This is the way that it should have come from the factory. I'm hoping that someone will take notice and perhaps institute a change in the assembly process where the sealing of the exhaust duct to the blower housing becomes the norm before someone dies in a fire caused by their Kenmore dryer.

incident_description:
The consumer says his wife turned on the heater.  After one minute  started smoking, sparking out of the front and shooting flames.  She unplugged it.  He plugged it back in and smoke shot straight out and sparking again. 

Their is a hole on the side of the unit where it burned through.  It is in the basement of their home sitting under a wooden desk causing a fire hazard. Has gotten a hold of the manufacturer about a week ago.  They have not returned his emails or phone calls.

He was assured that he would be contacted.  The consumer is upset they they have not been able to get back to them.

The consumer is upset with the manufacturer's inability to respond to what is a severe safety issue.

incident_description: On Feb 14 or 15 my daughter turned our Whirlpool Gas dryer on,  It started to smoke immediately, we turned it off right away.  Opened the windows to remove the smoke and unpluged the item and called whirlpool for service 800 253 1301 confirmation# [REDACTED] they sent a service rep from A E Factory Service, he found that the "board" had started a fire and the board needed to be replaced along with a plastic sheet (cover)  that melted due to the fire.  Both items needed to be ordered.  I called Whirlpool on Feb 25 and spoke with [REDACTED] a second rep for Whirlpool she gave me her direct line and extention 866 640 7146 X [REDACTED] explained that I was waiting for this plastic sheet part to arrived so the dryer could be repaired, she told me she would put my request in on a prioroty basis, do to the fire it caused, told methat A E Factory Service,  would be reimbursed the 311.66 I have spent so far with no repair and that if by Wed Feb 27th I did not rec. the part I should call her again. It is now Feb 28, I have recd. 3 different deliveries on 3 different days that all contain the same part the "board" I now have 5 "boards" and no plastic sheet (cover) to fix my dryer. incident_description:
Caller purchased Linen sachet August 25th, 2012 and while driving home with the sachet still unopened she began having a very bad headache with an acrid taste in her mouth.

Her daughter said it smelled musky to her.

When caller arrived home she placed the still unopened bag of sachet in one room and went to another, then the acrid taste and headache went away.

She has not contacted the manufacturer and has no way to contact them since there is no information other than the country of manufacture.

She has had no medical treatment

She picked the sachet back up to look at it while calling report in to hotline then headache and acrid taste in her mouth began returning so she put it back in the other room.

She would like to have the ingredients tested.

incident_description: The Lakewood 7101 oil space heater caught fire! The fire began where the electrical cord enters the unit.
justification: The oil space heater caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I ve purchased this laundry center on 11/12/2012. After initial instalation the laundry center was working continuosly without stoping. The manufacturer said that they forgot to reprogram it from testing to operation. Now, the dryer starts and stops  by itself every 10 seconds and the only way to stop it is to unplug it and tur off the gas. This is just the third month of operation and there are so many problem with this new computarised model.

incident_description:
Verbiage taken from consumers' letter sent to manufacturer
This is to call your attention to a dangerous exposed part on your generator.
The black metal box around the exhaust should have written on it the word HOT in red letters, and a bar or fence in front of it to prevent accidental skin contact. The word HOT should also include a message of how long, after the engine quits, one should wait before touching it.
I received a severe burn from this exposed surface. This happened after I shut off the generator and was putting it away. While wheeling it with the carrying handles and maneuvering it, I somehow put my leg against that surface in my maneuvering procedure to get it over a bump. Immediately after the initial and severe pain, the area was pink and I did not think the burn was serious. But eventually it blistered, then the blister popped leaving a raw and red wound. See the enclosed photo.
I eventually went to an urgent care medical center where I received treatment. See the enclosed doctorÃÂs report (ÃÂEncounter SummaryÃÂ) and the bills for $136.91 total. I hope you will be considerate and reimburse me for this unfortunate incident.

I sent the letter with delivery confirmation and they did not reply. In November (two months ago) I contacted [REDACTED] their accountant. She was nice and tried to track down my complaint, and then forwarded my message to the company president. I still have not received any kind of reply.

incident_description: Washing machine began to uncontrollably shake almost tipping over, it began smoking, and shut down. It will not turn on now.
justification: The washing machine malfunctioned but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description: I am the co-tenant of a single-family house that recently had a serious fire. The apparent cause was the failure of a Nutone bathroom exhaust fan/light. The fan had started to make make a squeaking noise shortly before the incident. It appears that the motor overheated and charred adjacent ceiling joists until they caught fire. The fan also dropped burning pieces of the plastic from the grill, setting the bathroom rug on fire and in turn triggering the smoke alarm. The more dangerous portion of the fire progressed into the attic. Firefighters stopped the fire and paramedics treated the house occupants for minor smoke inhalation. The Arlington fire marshal indicated his report will designate the fan as the cause of the fire. We have photographs and what we could recover of the fan unit.
justification: The incident resulted in minor smoke inhalation injuries to the occupants, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but can happen with faulty equipment.

incident_description: I am a contractor and have used many types and brands of tape measures. However the tape measure sold at Home Depot with the item number 193 362  and SKU 811187010412  Distributed by Iron Bridge Tools [REDACTED].    The steel tape has RAZOR SHARP edges and created 2 deep lacerations in my thumb and index finger upon retracting the tape measure.  This tape measure is dangerous and should not be sold.
justification: The incident resulted in deep lacerations to the thumb and index finger, indicating an injury.

incident_description: The consumer was using a new Chicago Electric Brand 10 inch compound miter saw. As he was lowering the arm, the aluminum base broke in half, causing the rotating blade and arm to fall and amputate part of his left thumb.
justification: The incident resulted in a partial amputation of the thumb, which is a significant injury.

incident_description: On March 28, 2012 I purchased a Peerless massage/hand shower. Model/SKU 76601SN  8077611994. Last week I was in the shower when under water pressure the hand held became detached from the hose. It flew across the shower, slammed into the shower wall, bounced off and hit me on the back. It then fell to the shower floor barely missing my foot. I was not badly injured. I have a small stall shower so I could not have been standing in the line of fire. However in a full size bathtub/shower a person could be seriously injured or even killed by this heavy flying projectile.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (hit on the back) and could potentially cause serious injury or death in different circumstances, as described.

incident_description: I  had a Lasko Tower Heater model #5119, sitting on my camper counter top. This unit started a fire at the botoom of the heater and then the fire ran the power cord up to a point wher eit met an plastic sink. At this point the fire in the cord stopped. bu the damage had been done. I read where Lasko had another recall on another tower heater unit with the same type of incident. Cord melted out the bottom of the heater and then ran along the power cord. I was lucky that the melting power cord stopped once it reached the plastic sink. I have pictures of the damage and I have the heater.
justification: The heater caused a fire but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the mention of a similar recall and the described incident.

incident_description:
The handle on the heater is poorly designed.
When you grab the handle, it is shaped so that the heather 'squeezes' out of your hand.  We've had a couple of times where we try to move the heater, only to have it fly out of our hands.  The only safe way to move the heater is to use two hands.

The handle needs to be shaped so that you can securely grab the heather.
This is the Lasko Ceramic Tower with Remote Control, Model 5538
justification: The poorly designed handle causes the heater to slip out of hands, but no injuries are reported.

incident_description:

justification: The incident involves excessive noise and shaking during use, with no reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The issue occurs every time the machine is used and is reported by numerous consumers, indicating a high likelihood (5).

incident_description:

The fireplace was off and he realized that the remote was not working, he went to unplug it and noticed that the plug had burnt inside and half of the plug was completely charred into the unit.

incident_description:

incident_description: Family Care Vaporizer model HV 740/745 caught fire at junction of cord and vaporizer motor after being on for 2 hours or less. Vaporizer was used successfully the evening before, but otherwise has only been used sparingly.  No injuries sustained, cord was swiftly unplugged.

incident_description:

incident_description: My Kenmore Elite Washer will not drain or spin without moving out from the wall and makes very loud sounds.  I have had Sears under the recall for this product out to my home twice and they still have not fixed it.  I have been without a working washer for 3 weeks now and they now tell me that LG the manufacturer will now need to ship me a computer board and it will take at least another week. Sears is not standing behind the product until LG has a chance to assist first.

incident_description: THIS KENMORE FRONT LOADING WASHER WOULD SHAKE EXCESSIVELY--TO THE POINT WHERE IT TRAPPED MY 6 YEAR OLD DAUGHTER IN THE LAUNDRY AREA--SO I PROMPTLY MOVED IT OVER TO LET HER OUT. incident_description:
The consumer says that his fiance was sitting on the toilet when it exploded.  He walked in the room and said the lid came down and hit her in the back.  
She went to the Dr. who said their was bruising on her lower back.  The doctor suggested she take a couple days off.  The consumer says their is nothing left of his toilet.
This unit is currently under recall (Release #12-201).
justification: The incident caused bruising and required medical attention, indicating injury (severity 3). The recall status suggests this is a rare occurrence (likelihood 1).

incident_description:
My 6 year old Goodman gas furnace, Model GMH95073BXAA was making a strange noise so my wife called a service person. He inspected it, said the heat exchange was bad, that it was leaking CO and must be repaired - but could not fix it because he did not service Goodman models. It then completely quit working. We then called the Goodman service person (who was also the original installer) who confirmed the heat exchange was bad - there was a hole rusted through and it was apparently leaking CO. It was installed new in my home (new construction - spec) which we bought in Feb. 2007. This was a six year old furnace installed new in a brand new house. Seems WAY too early to be having a serious mechanical failure like this! I have pictures of the part that was removed from the furnace - it shows rust on more than one of the tubes, including the one with a hole in it.

I did contact Goodman. The part was replaced as part of their 20 year warranty on the heat exchange. (Still cost $790 in labor.) I think the bigger issue is the failure and possibility of CO leaking into the house. The service person checked readings on the furnace before it quit running and found a small amount of CO entering the house - most was being vented out through the exhaust vent (255 PPM).
justification: The furnace had a serious mechanical failure leading to CO leakage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:

There was a service call placed in 2/2009 for the same problem.

(6/2012)The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that the gasket could be removed at a cost to the caller. 

The caller feels that the mold in the washer is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident involves mold in a washer causing damage to the gasket, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I bought a Lasko Ceramic Element heater about 2 months ago. I had it plugged in using a heavy duty extension cord. I use it in my basement workroom. I wanted to unplug it from the extension cord and it wouldn't come apart. Using a screw driver (it was unplugged from the wall), I had to pry it apart. Consumer stated she plugged in the heater at night. Just to warm up the room and it was on for about 15-20 minutes. When she came back in the room she smelled something burning. 
So she turned off the heater with the remote and went to unplug it, but the cord was too hot. So she grabbed something to pull the cord with.

incident_description: While my wife was ironing clothes last night, a burst of sparks came from the rubber tube that holds the electric cord at the back of the handle, causing her sleeve to catch fire. incident_description: Bought the SPT Mini Dehumidifier Model: SD-652 circa September 2012.  The unit was used almost daily from November until February 2013 during the day only. It was used in a small bedroom closet during this time. On February 7, 2013 the unit would not turn on.  After close examination it was discovered that the plug that inserts into the unit had "shorted" causing the rubber/plastic of the plug to melt onto one of the prongs. The plastic around one of the holes on the plug was melted and blistered. There were no injuries or fire damage cause by the unit. It was always used in a safe manor and in a dry closet. In fact, it was rarely moved other than emptying the water tank which would take well over a week to fill halfway. It should also be noted that during the last month to month and a half of use, I did notice the motor running louder than usual when first turned on. However, after several minutes, the motor would resume its normal sounds.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dehumidifier that caused a short and melting of the plug, but no injuries or fire damage occurred.

incident_description:
We own a Morso cast iron wood stove model 3610 serial No. 092. The  stove was purchased new from The Stove Barn on 12/19/2009 in Winslow, ME.  We are now unable to use the stove due to it being a fire hazard!  On Dec. 12, 2012 we observed a crack in the cast iron base of the stove extending from the right side toward the left side. The crack was about an 1/8th of an inch at the right side and proceeded to become smaller as it proceeded to the left. The crack becomes obscured by a metal plate bolted under the stove base at approximately six inches from its beginning at the right side base. Accordingly, We are unable  to ascertain how long the crack is at this time.The stove is unsafe to use for two related reasons: first, hot coals could could fall through the crack and possibly cause a fire; second, the crack could continue to open up to the left side of the stove (should we continue to use it) which could cause the entire stove to collapse - again an extreme fire hazard. Should they be needed, we have many photos of the crack and the stove installation.

I have discussed the forgoing matter with a [REDACTED] , proprietor of The Stove Barn (Ph. 207 859 9773). [REDACTED] tells me that he has sold six of the  Morso Model 3610 stoves since he has been in business. To date 3 of these six stoves have experienced cracks in their bases - a 50% failure rate Two of these stoves have had their bases replaced by the manufacturer under warrantee - our stove is the third of the three now awaiting a new replacement base (as has been agreed to by the manufacturer) since on or about Dec. 16th, 2012. After recent numerous calls to the manufacturer by [REDACTED], which now go unreturned, we have yet to receive the new replacement base and have accordingly have consumed to date over $800 in #2 heating oil and propane gas in order to stay warm here in sub zero Maine. 

Reflecting on this matter I find that  I have no confidence in a stove with a replacement base installed performing any more safely or reliably than the original unit (given the 50% failure rate experienced by this local dealer alone - who knows what the failure rate is across the USA - this should be investigated!).  Accordingly, I think the the equitable solution to this problem is for Morso to buy back the stove at the original purchase price of $2205 plus damages costs in added fuel expenditures until such date as the funds have cleared in our bank account. As we here are retirees, once we receive the forgoing monies we can then proceed to purchase a new reliable wood burning stove that will provide adequate heat for our home. In the mean time we will continue to accrue costs of at least $250 per week in added heating oil/gas costs plus any attorney fees incurred by us here regarding these matters until such time as this deal is completed. Morso can be reached at: stoves@morsoe.com     

Thank you for your attention to these matter. We look forward to hearing from you. Our home phone number is [REDACTED] and our email address is: [REDACTED]
justification: The crack in the stove base poses a fire hazard but no injury or death has occurred. The 50% failure rate among the dealer's sales suggests the issue is likely to occur.

incident_description:
I am reporting an accident with and LG LP6011ER low profile air conditioner.  The air conditioner was professionally installed in my window, and was held into place with a metal cross bar and a number of self-tapping screws.  On Monday, February 11, 2013 the bulk of the air conditioner fell out of my window down five floors with a big crash.  The front of the air conditioner was still securely attached to my window.

It appears that the plastic casing for the part of the air conditioner exposed to the elements suffered some sort of fatigue and just sheared off from the secured part of the air conditioner, causing the "guts" of the air conditioner and the bulk of the casing to fall down.

Luckily, no one was injured.

The air conditioner had been in my window for approximately seven years.
justification: The air conditioner fell from a height but no one was injured, and such failures after seven years of use are unlikely.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a Kobalt compound miter saw to install some crown molding.  It is a 7 1/4 inch sliding compound miter, Model #SM1850LW.  The saw is equipped with a blade guard which automatically retracts when the blade is lowered to cut, and then automatically deploys to cover the blade when the saw handle is raised. The handle rises automatically by spring action.  I was using the saw to cut a small piece of molding with a 45degree miter.  I had cut several pieces (enough to thinks I knew how to do it safely) when I goofed and cut off the end of my right middle finger when retrieving the short  cut piece before the blade had stopped. 
After my trip to the emergency room and two days of recovery so that the nausea and pain had subsided enough to look at the saw, I found that the saw was still in the down position with the blade fully exposed at the bed of the saw instead of having spring returned to the up position where the blade would have been covered.  After a little checking, I found that when the saw is tilted left to perform a miter cut, the cutter head lock incorrectly slides by gravity and vibration so that it engages and prevents the handle from rising.  Since I use my right hand to push the saw head down I had foolishly relied upon the spring return to have moved the saw blade away from the work and deploy the blade guard.  That was how it had worked for several previous operations before the cutter head lock had inadvertently engaged and locked the head down leaving the blade still exposed at the workpiece I had cut.
justification: The incident resulted in a finger injury due to a malfunctioning saw mechanism, indicating a moderate severity. The likelihood is possible as it occurred after several safe operations before the malfunction.

incident_description:
I purchased a shower door from Home Depot in January of 2010 when I moved into my house.  On January 31, 2013 at 5am I heard a shatter.  It was my shower glass door. Sterling 690-CA is the model number and it is made by Kohler.  I don't know why it shattered, but had it been 45 minutes later I would have been in the bathroom and it would have shattered on me.

I contacted Home Depot and they said they cannot do anything because it is out of warranty and they did not install it.  My dad builds space crafts that have flown to Mars and are out in orbit, it is not his installation but a poorly made shower glass door.

I am contacting Kohler as well, but this is a safety issue because I have read of other shower doors shattering without notice.
justification: The shower door shattered but no one was injured, and the incident is reported to have happened to others as well.

incident_description: Federal Pacific Electric panel. C120-30N1 is the model number.  The breaker went out for the dryer. Electrician came over and identified the panel as a dangerous Federal Pacific Electric panel.  The gentleman could not do anything regarding repair. Would be $3200 to replace.  We do not have the money.  I live in a dangerous house.

incident_description: i have an apple Mac Book Pro 15 inch laptop that came with the power cord (85W).  I noticed my laptop was running low on power, so I plugged it in.  After about 5 minutes I smelled something burning.  I looked around and within about 3 minutes I noticed that the power cord was melted.  The internal wire was not exposed and the outer sheath had melted off.  The next day I went to work at ESU, east stroudsburg university, where I am a [REDACTED] & a faculty member brought in her power cord (the exact same one as mine) and gave it to one of my co-workers who is the technical specialist.  It was burned and melted in the exact same place as mine.  It looked almost identical.  I took photos of both cords.  I called apple to get a replacement and they told me I had to turn in the faulty one to get a new one.  I believe there is a serious problem.  If I had been sleeping (it was 10pm) at night, both my 5 year old son and I might have perished in a fire.

incident_description: The connector between the power supply and the iphone 5 burned through the plastic sheeting just proximal to the tiny 16-point iphone connector. The other end of the connector is a standard USB connector that goes into the port of the power supply, which then plugs into the wall socket. The tiny 16-point connector burned through the plastic sheeting while connected overnight to the power supply which was plugged in. The connector was NOT attached into the iphone at the time. Had anything flammable been sitting near the connector, it would have started a fire.
justification: The incident involved a burned connector but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is considered possible given the description.

incident_description:
We purchased a Back&Decker Dust Buster Model  CHV1410 and hung it on a wall at a convenient height of approximately 54 in.  The hook provided was used, and the included instructions were followed.  When the Dust Buster was lightly bumped, it disengaged from its hook and fell on the foot of the user, resulting in a broken bone. Medical treatment, and therapy were required to restore optimal function.

On examination, the hook and it's mating slot on the Dust Buster do not provide a secure connection.   A minimal move from true vertical allows disengagement from the hook, resulting in this incident.  
This design does not prevent any sideways movement of the Dust Buster in relation to true vertical.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken bone requiring medical treatment and therapy, indicating a severity level of 3. The design flaw makes disengagement likely with minimal movement, suggesting an occurrence likelihood of 4.

incident_description: After cleaning my grill grates approx. Nov 8th or 9th, I grilled a London Broil. Ate London Broil on Nov. 8th or 9th with family at dinner time.  Stomach and abdomen had severe stabbing pain next day.  waited for pain to go away but it did not. went to see family doctir who took an x-ray and saw nothing.  He gave me a prescription to help ease stomach pain.  Did not work. Pain returned.  Went to the ER Nov. 11, 2012, Sunday morning.  They took 2 CAT scans.  Film and report stated metallic pin or object lodged in small intestines, poking through somewhat- hung up.  Admitted for surgery.  8 days in hospital. Surgeon removed wire bristle and later told me the hospital pathologist had it and it did look like it came from a grill cleaning brush.  Wife checked out grill later and found several wire bristles stuck to the grill grates. She also picked off loose bristles from the brush. We still have the grill brush.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring surgery and hospitalization due to a wire bristle from a grill brush, indicating a severity level of 3.

There were no injuries

incident_description: About December 8, 2012, my wife was using her Kenmore vacuum cleaner when it caught fire around the wand/cord area. incident_description: Soda stream maker blew up on my 11 year old boy while I supervised. The bottom blew out of the soda bottle and water shot everywhere. It made a  loud blast and scared us all to death. The plastic piece luckily did not hit anyone. This is very dangerous. We followed directions and this was a newer carbonation tank. There needs to be a WARNING: PRODUCT CAN COMBUST UNDERCERTAIN SITUATIONS PLEASE READ! They just say important info .........Very upsetting!

incident_description: At 3:50 am on January 29, 2013, I awoke to the sound of my shower door exploding. I was so loud and forceful that we thought someone had crashed thru the window in our bathroom. The shower door had not been touched since 9pm the night before. Luckily, no one was awake in my house when this happened. Had this happened at 9pm or 6am there would have been injuries.  We were told that the maker of the glass was Cardinal.
justification: The shower door exploded but no one was injured, and such incidents are rare.

incident_description:
Century grinding wheel 41/2" diameter, 1/16" thickness and 7/8" arbor, rated to 13,200rpm.
120lbs of air pressure, grinding is rated at 13.4 so never came near where it states wheel is rated.
Safety was on at the time of incidents.

Caller's husband has used these wheels for over 20 years but these most recently purchased, shattered into several parts while in use with pieces flying off in all directions.

The first time this happened was Friday, November 16th, 2012 or Saturday, November 17th, 2012 when a piece flew between caller's husband and friend but was dismissed as this being one wheel that may have a defect.

Another incident happened with a different grinding wheel shattering during use Friday, November 23rd, 2012 but this time the pieces cut a groove in the palm of his hand from close to the wrist and ending under the smallest "pinkie" finger.

Caller drove her husband to the Jewish Hospital Emergency Room after finally convincing him that he needed to go for treatment.

Doctor [REDACTED] with the emergency room diagnosed his laceration, placed two stitches inside, four outside and prescribed antibiotic to prevent infection.

Callers have not contacted the manufacturer, they did contact the retailer who told them that they would contact the manufacturer.

Callers have been unable to find all the pieces but have saved the one's that they have found.
They have one that has not been used and one that has been used and shattered.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The recurrence of similar incidents suggests a possible likelihood (3) of future occurrences.

incident_description:
I was using an HP dv6500t laptop when I smelled an acrid burning odor. I looked around for the smell and  hearing this clicking noise. found the source was my laptop ac adapter, which I picked up to investigate. Once I picked it up, the cord began sparking and caught on fire, at which point it frayed.
I immediately went to the wall and unplugged it, after which the fire went out quickly but generated a lot of smoke which I had to open a window to air out.

Apparently there are a lot of customer reviews on online merchants about these power adapters or batteries overheating or in some instances catching on fire. A quick look on google also reveals some news articles in which houses have burned down due to battery fires.
I believe this is extremely dangerous and anyone still using these laptops should be aware. I have replaced this adapter several times due to the cord melting, but this is the first time it actually caught on fire and I am extremely frightened from the occurrence. I looked to see if my battery or the power adapter was on the recall list but it is not. I was lucky that I was home to witness this. I hope no one gets hurt from an incident like this.
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting his fire extinguisher, he does not have size available.
Caller was cooking on November 8th, 2012 (he doesn't remember at which temperature setting) when a small grease fire began building with flames of approx 6-12 " high, causing caller to grab fire extinguisher to put it out.
He removed the safety pin, verified the pressure indicator was green pressed on the lever but nothing came out, he kept trying for approximately a minute longer pressing on lever over and over but nothing was coming out to end the fire. 
Caller states that the lever used to press is soft, so when he pushes the lever it bends instead of pushing the pin.
He and his wife finally got a wet towel and threw it over the fire extinguishing it.

He contacted the manufacturer in mid November who advised him to return he container to them, however he has chosen to retain the fire extinguisher until report is complete with CPSC and he has heard from our investigative or compliance officers.

There have been no injuries, but there was about $1000 worth of fire damages that could have been averted hadthis fire extinguisher worked.
justification: The incident involved a fire extinguisher failure during a small grease fire, causing $1000 in damages but no injuries.

incident_description:
(11/20/21012) The consumer stated that the child was in the room on the floor. She heard the child choking. She turned and saw the child on the rug on his belly. She picked his up and saw a string from the rug in his mouth. She pulled the string out of his mouth. 
The string was about 2 inches long. She also discovered that there is plastic and cotton materials that weave the rug together.  The consumer also stated that  this is not the first time that the child had played on the rug.

The consumer stated that the label on the rug only addresses the care of the rug


(11/21/2012) The consumer spoke with a customer service representative and explained what happened. She was advised that the product could not be exchanged or returned because it was a final sale item.
justification: The child was choking on a string from the rug, indicating an injury occurred, and the incident has happened before, suggesting it is likely to recur.

incident_description:
Saturday, November 17th, 2012 while caller was in his deer blind and just after he changed the propane then lit the portable heater being used he heard what sounded like a mini explosion.  He looked down and saw that the propane heater was on fire with the flames being small but hot enough not to catch him afire.
He grabbed the heater and threw it out to the blind then stepped out and poured his coffee over the fire to put it out.

If he had not been right in front of the fire or the heater had actually exploded he could have been burned severely.
He is reporting this product as a fire hazard.

He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involved a small fire with no injury, but potential for severe burns if conditions were different.

incident_description: About 1 am in the morning my 3 year old daughter woke up crying and screaming. I ran to her bedroom only to find the Sunbeam SWM-5251 humidifier was on fire with flames about 2 feet high. My wife was right behind me,she grabbed her I unplugged the unit and ran for an extinguisher and put it out. We bought it at Walmart about 2.5 years ago and only used it a few times when she was sick. It melted a large hole into the carpet and itself, filed reports with the local fire department and an attorney.
justification: The humidifier caught fire, causing significant damage but no injuries, warranting a severity level of 2. Such incidents are rare but possible with faulty appliances.

incident_description:
We recently had to call the fire department a second time for a dryer malfunction with our Samsung dryer. The first call was about a year ago when the dryer did not shut off the gas flow in between heating cycles, thus filling our basement with natural gas. A Samsung appointed technician came to service the dryer and nearly replaced all of the internal componentry because his testing indicated a few parts were not functioning properly.

The most recent call to the fire department was on 1/15/13 when a strong burning smell and a light smoke condition was coming from the laundry room. We have a Service Notification from the Ramsey NJ Fire Department that the dryer should not be used until it is looked at by a qualified technician. The burning smell took a few days to dissipate from the basement and kitchen, indicating a significant "overheating" condition inside the dryer.

This is now twice that this particular dryer threatened to cause loss of property and / or life. Fortunately we were home both times to notice the conditions before they got out of hand.

I reported the latest issue to Samsung Customer Support the next day and although they indicate that they have escalated my issue to their claims department, I have yet to hear from them.

I have gone ahead and purchased another dryer because with a family of four I can't wait any longer to be able to wash and dry clothes in my home. 

This dryer clearly does not have the proper functioning mechanisms in place to prevent it from becoming a threat to property and life so I have decided to report it to you.
justification: The incident involved a significant overheating condition and gas leak, posing a threat to property and life, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have had two shower doors shatter on me. The first time was six month after I purchased the door and the other was just the other day. It is made by Sterling a Kohler Company. Noone was hurt in the shattering, both were in the morning hours. Was rudely awaken by both.
justification: The incident involved shower doors shattering twice without causing injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as it happened twice within a short period.

incident_description: I was using my Sharp Steam Mop yesterday and it was working properly and then stopped and unplugged the mop.  A little later tried I plugged it in and pumped to get it to start steaming in order to clean the laundry tile floor.  Anyway it blew up and thank goodness I was not close to it.  Really dangerous!
justification: The steam mop exploded but no injury occurred as the user was not close to it.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore HE2 Dryer that is a little over 4yrs old.  Maintenance is well kept knowing I am a Service Specialist who takes care of the products as a consumer and a professional.  With this said, on January 22, 2013 my wife was doing laundry.  She felt the clothes were dry so went to our laundry room, pressed Stop on the Dryer, opened the door and started to pull clothing out to fold.  Within seconds she noticed smoke coming from the Dryer so immediately pulled out all the clothing.  I was away so she called me to ask what to do.  She unplugged the Dryer and pulled it forward to assure it was on the ceramic floor so nothing under it would catch fire.  I returned home within an hour and removed the lint filter to see it was not burnt but had smoke smell.  I took off the kick plate in front to view the damage. The electrical print which was taped to the plate was in ashes.  Note this is within inches of the burner duct.  There was no lint or dust collected in the area except minor amount on the floor area away from any hot surfaces.  I took numerous pictures and only notice one flash burn on the kick plate excatly at the lower right of the electrical plate.  I had charred wiring and door switch plus smoke stains throughout where I feel it will be next to impossible to get out.  Note my clothing was not smoke stained so the fire started  when the unit was stopped.  I took my findings and researched to see if there were any recalls on this product or other complaints on the Web.  I found a recall on LG and Kenmore Elite but my model was not on the list.  I question whether the faulty gas valve is the same for my unit, whether the electrical print was to be encased in plastic to protect it or was it truly poor wiring that caused the arc then a burn. Airflow was not an issue with the blower duct due to good care and duct run is less than 2ft.
justification: The incident involved smoke and minor fire damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) given the specific conditions and maintenance described.

incident_description:
I don't recall when we purchased the Whirlpool Duet FL Washing machine.  However, I followed all of the manufacturer's maintenance reccomendations.  I "clean" my washer twice a month and the front door is left open after every load and is left open "24/7, 365".  We've found black mold in a very unexpected place.  In the dispenser area above it.  My husband found a massive black mold build-up today.  It then occurred to me that this may be why my daughter has been chronically ill for the past 4 years (will be calling her pediatrician today to make an appointment and discuss).  This is utterly unacceptable as I have my grandson who lives with us who was a preemie and has asthma.  It also occurred to me that the black mold could be aggravating his asthma.  You need to do something about this. 

Consumer found a massive black mold build-up in the dispenser area of the washing machine.  Consumer feels that may be mold was the cause for their daughter being chronically ill for the past 4 years & also could be the reason for aggravating their grandson's asthma.

incident_description:
Consumer assembled the generator in his garage and put a half gallon of gas inside to start it. The consumer made sure it worked and turn it off, then shut the off valve, which is a secondary device. The generator was then put away for storage and the consumer placed the gas cans outside the garage. The consumer went to add more gas and notice a gas odor inside of the garage.  The consumer moved his van, because he thought gas was coming from it.  After the van was moved he still smelled the gas odor.  Additionally, some plywood near the generator was covered in gas.  The plywood was a short distance from the generator, but it was sitting on the floor.

Consumer noticed the tank emptied itself after about 2 days of being topped with fuel. Consumer also discovered the gasket had completely crumbled. The generator is currently not used.  The consumer devise a homemade gasket to enable him to use the generator temporarily.

Consumer stated there was no property damage and no physical damages
justification: The incident involved a gas leak and potential fire hazard, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
Caller happened to look up while walking through his hallway and noticed that sometime before last night the fire detector alarm had at some time caught fire.
There were black scorch marks out from all sides of the alarm but there was no odor of fire.

Fire Detector Alarm runs on hardwired A/C burned up 120-11828 DOM _ there were six of these detectors placed in his home in 2006 as a compliance requirement, all five others have a small light still lit & showing operational.

The ceiling must be repainted and there was wiring damage.

He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
There were no injuries.
justification: The fire detector alarm caught fire, causing damage to the ceiling and wiring, but there were no injuries reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the portable heater was on for a couple of hours, she smelled an odor of something burning.  She noticed that the electrical cord was melted at the location where it was plugged in. The heater was unplugged to prevent further damages. There were no prior incidents.

The manufacturer was not contacted because there was no contact number on the unit.

The caller is concerned that this heater is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a melted electrical cord and a burning odor, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On the AC/DC adapter, the plastic/rubber insulation on the 120v cord cracked and separated at the location where it enters/connects with the molded strain relief.  This creates a 1/8"+ length where both copper conductors (live and ground) are exposed.  This would easily allow a narrow foreign object (e.g. paperclip, etc.) to bridge both conductors and create a short.  It could also easily allow for a finger to touch both conductors if the cord was bent back. 

This product was purchased new on August 15, 2012 - it is less than six months old and has not been exposed to any harsh or unusual handling or storage.
justification: Exposed live and ground conductors pose a risk of electric shock or short circuit, which could lead to injury if contacted directly.

incident_description: I bought two packs of cabinet slide locks, each of which contained two locks.  I opened both packs and discovered one lock in each pack didn't work/lock at all.  I decided to give the others a try, but as I was opening one of the locks, I caught my skin in the plastic teeth.  I returned both packs to the store for a refund.  If I got a blood blister while correctly using the product, I can't imagine what it would do to little fingers playing with it or attempting to open it.
justification: The incident resulted in a blood blister, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the product's potential hazard.

incident_description: We use space heater in a unheated family room. It is used often, so I make sure it gets a couple hours off each day. Realized it was getting cool in room, went to turn heater on, thermostat was up and heater was on, but no heat was coming out. Thought I was doing something wrong, turned off, and unplugged to reset. Would not turn on. Unplugged again, and realized the entire plug was black and a burned looking. Wow. Glad we were home.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning space heater with a burned plug, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Installed a ceiling fan by a licensed electrician in a home addition.  Started using the fixture on 1/8/2013.  On 2/4/2013 Noticed there were two bulbs that appeared to be burnt out.  Upon further inspection they appeared to be operating on a reduced voltage and were very dim. 

I proceeded to change the lightbulbs and the lights started to flash in a weird pattern and made an arching noise from the fixture.  To stop the flashing I moved a bulb, and the unit sounded like it was arching a little louder which then burnt out the fan motor.

The unit is unsafe and I am lucky I was not electrocuted when handling the metal parts of the fixture. Fan was harbor breeze  item number 44622. Crosswinds ceiling fan with light kit installed
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning ceiling fan with electrical arcing, posing a risk of electrocution but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Centurion (Generac) 5000 Watt Generator. It was purchased in January 2011. Every month I run it for 15 minutes to test functionality, then shut the fuel valve off and run the carburetor out of fuel.

On February 4, 2013 I started my monthly run when fuel began POURING out of the backside of the carburetor and air filter. I quickly shut the generator and fuel supply off. The unit is out of warranty so I investigated by disassembling the carburetor. The needle valve for fuel supply was stuck open because the plating on the valve had "flaked off" (see picture). I will probably have to buy a [REDACTED] needle valve, since what I've seen on the internet indicates this has been cloned off of them. Theirs is made entirely of thermoplastic. 

Please also reference a prior complaint on this site...

http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1243222

I always use fuel with <5% Ethanol and add [REDACTED] to the fuel supply. This is a very dangerous situation, especially when this piece of equipment is left unattended. There could be a major fuel spill and ignition.
justification: Fuel leakage from the generator poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred in this incident.

incident_description: A state inspector was conducting an annual inspection of a day care facility. The inspector instructed the owner to test a ceiling mounted, battery operated, single station smoke alarm. The owner depressed the test button and shortly after the unit started to smoke and then caught fire with part of the smoke alarm  falling to the floor. The smoke alarm was extinguished with a fire extinguisher preventing a larger fire. The smoke alarm was battery operated type only and purchased from Costco. The make and model was a Family Gard #FG888D. The battery type [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a smoke alarm catching fire but was quickly extinguished without injury or death.

justification: The shower glass shattered but no one was present, so there was no injury or death.

incident_description:
In January of 2012, we purchased a frameless glass shower enclosure by Basco (Roda) through our dealer (Agean Marble). It consists of two pieces: a door and a stationary panel. Each piece mounts to its respective tile wall with two brackets. Additionally the stationary panel mounts to the cast marble floor base with a "U" channel.

On Saturday, August 18, 2012 at 4:15 p.m. I was in the downstairs kitchen, directly beneath the bathroom, when I heard a loud "boom." I immediately ran upstairs to find the stationary glass shower panel had exploded and glass squares covering the bathroom floor and littering the hallway up to 10 feet away. The force was so concussive that there were glass shards embedded in the painted wall. Also, the broken glass had taken chunks out of our cast marble shower base.

I immediately called Agean but they had already closed for the weekend, so I left a (frantic) message. We took many photos and then proceeded to clean up the huge mess. I was very shook up as I was five minutes away from taking a shower.

When I finally spoke with Agean Mon. morning, they connected me with Basco, who ordered a new glass panel based on the specs they already had on file for us. The installer was there within a week to replace it. They also sent out a contractor to repair the cast marble base. There was no charge to us for any of this work.

Luckily there was no one in the shower at the time as injuries would've been serious if there had been.
justification: The glass shower panel exploded, causing significant damage but no injuries, as no one was in the shower at the time.

incident_description: Washing machine shakes excessively with an unbalanced load similar to problem described in [REDACTED]/Kenmore machines recall.  Not clear whether machine should shut off automatically when unbalanced but this does not occur.  Machine shakes violently until turned off manually.  Not sure if these washers are involved in the recall.

incident_description:
My Kenmore upright vacuum would periodically turn off for no known reason.  At last use, it shut off. As I bent down to check the outlet, I put my hand on the machine and was shocked.  Upon closer inspection, the power cord (where it enters the vacuum housing) had come apart and was sparking.

Upon checking the internet to see how to replace the power cord, I discovered several people who have had the same problem.

incident_description:
I have a space heater, an upright Lasko. Tonight I plugged it in. It started to smell, and then I found brown marks above the outlet. I turned it off. ~10 minutes later, I unplugged it. One prong of the plug is black, and the rubber part of the plug is partly melted. 

The space heater was the only item at that outlet. It was ~3 feet away from the wall, and at least 18 inches away from anything. There was no extension cord or power strip; the unit was plugged directly into the wall.
justification: The incident involved a space heater causing a burning smell and melting, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The issue involves mold formation which appears to be an ongoing issue with this product that is known by the manufacture.

My wife and I owner a Whirlpool Duet front loading automatic washer and dryer.  We have been very happy with the performance of the appliances thus far but have a major issue with the washer door seal.

Initially we called your service center and were told that a problem that was common was mold formation on the door seal but that it could be minimized and controlled by following the recommended maintenance procedure which involved cleaning the seal and using [REDACTED] on a regular basis.

All preventive and routine recommendations have been followed but the mold on the door seal remains and is getting worse.  Aside from the horrible aesthetic appearance of the seal,  I believe that this poses a potential health problem from the family.  We have owned numerous washing machines over the years and have had to address mechanical breakdowns or wear and tear but never had a problem of this nature that could affect the health and well-being of family members.
justification: Mold formation is an ongoing issue with the product, posing a potential health risk, but no actual injury has been reported yet.
