incident_description: Range Kleen SS2 Double Step Stool.  It needs a child safety warning.  It folds open and closed.  There are rods inside the legs that that pieces rotate along.  It doesn't attach to the rods in one solid piece.  There hinge pieces with spaces in between them all up and down the sides.  When closed, these gaps are wider than when open.  It opens and closes by having you pull up a handle sharply, causing it to quickly snap open and lock into place.  You pull another handle similarly to close.  My three year old daughter was opening it, but was holding onto it with her thumb inside one of the gaps.  She opened it quickly, and her thumb became crushed and trapped inside.  It captured her thumb very tightly, and it immediately began to swell.  We weren't sure if we could close it (thereby widening the gap) without hurting her more, so we cut through the plastic.  At first I thought we might need the ER.  It had cut into her thumb so deeply and swelled around it so much that it looked like deep cut rather than a crush injury.  She was only trapped a few minutes.  As the swelling reduced with the help of ice, it became clear that the skin was not cut, but it is deeply bruised.  I checked, and my finger fits in the gap when open, too.  I think it would have been worse if she had been 5, because the bigger the finger the more tightly it will crush down on the finger.  Presumably there is a point at which it simply can't close down on the finger, because it is too thick, but I'm not going to test that.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep bruise and swelling, indicating an injury but not requiring emergency medical attention.

incident_description:

We located the smell in a utility closet where the hot water heater is, opened the door, odor was very strong of electrical and plastic burning. Turned the light on, hazy smoke in the closet, took us a few minutes to realize the plastic cover on the "Smart Saver" unit on top of the heater was melted and distorted on top with little curls of smoke still coming out.  I quick rush to flip the breaker. 

Whirlpool Electric Hot Water HEater  Model EE3Z80HD055V,  PURCHASED 9/27/2010

We contacted Whirlpool, they are sending parts overnight (2 days) and covering shipping. The [REDACTED] with their water heater, what if my house had burned down. 

Wife says she smelled it the night before but very slight odor.

Whirlpool clearly knows that they have aproblem with this unit,  the customer service phone rep was awfully familiar with this issue as soon as we gave her the model number.

The tank unit was smoking inside the cabinet. The cord was laying in water that had leaked from the unit so my husband immediately unplugged it.

The callers husband grabbed the heater and threw it out of the deer stand, then climbed down and extinguished the fire by kicking snow on it.

incident_description:
On August 11, 2012 and again on January 26, 2013 the City of Carrollton Fire Department responded to [REDACTED]  to reported residential fires.  On both of these responses the bathroom exhaust fans had overheated or had a fire inside their plastic enclosures.  The plastic enclosures themselves were melted causing considerable smoke inside the apartment buildings.  On January 30, 2013 I made an investigative visit to the apartment complex and with the owners permission checked several of the apartments to determine fan manufacturer, model, and condition.  The majority of the fans that I checked, which was only a small sample of the 50 or so apartments, showed signs of poor maintenance with heavy dirt and dust accumulations inside the fan housings.  The fans involved in the fire incidents were not recovered at the time of the incident and it is not possible to determine if poor maintenance could have been an issue with these fans.

Aubrey Manufacturing
Model # 7550 Vent Fan

incident_description:

During an interview, the tenant reported smelling natual gas in the basement the night before the fire occurred.  I took the information from the water heater and reserched for any recalls on the water heater.  I discovered that there was a recall for that make and model for the gas control valve.  When try to match the valve to the specific items listed under the recall, the only item that did not match was the date code.  However, the manufacturer, model, and failure described in the recall was the same.

The valve in question is a Robertshaw R110 gas control valve with a date code of 0006.  

The CPSC release # is 05-274

My concern is that the recall may not have encompassed enough of the faulty valves posing a risk to consumers with this valve.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no reported injuries, but the faulty valve poses a continued risk.

incident_description:
I bought a Sears Craftsman model 21833 table saw in 2010.  Many of these saws, including mine, have a manufacturing defect (widely reported on woodworking web sites) that causes the blade to become significantly misaligned when the blade height is raised or lowered.  This is a serious safety problem because it can cause kickback,  Kickback is an event in which the work piece is lifted by the back of the blade and thrown forward with great speed and force.  In addition, it can cause the user's hand to be drawn into the blade, causing very serious injuries, including severed fingers.

Normally, there is a process that can be used to align the blade so that it is parallel to the saw's miter slot and rip fence.  However, this process is only effective if the blade height is never changed, which is totally unrealistic.  The problem is that the trunnions were not machined correctly, so no matter how many times the adjustment procedure is performed, the underlying problem is never corrected.

I have not been injured, but there have been times when the wood I was cutting became bound against the rip fence, even after the rip fence was properly aligned.  It is a serious safety issue and I would appreciate your investigating it.

Thank you.
justification: The user reports a manufacturing defect causing potential kickback and serious injuries, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I own a Generac GP5500 generator purchased in May 2011.  
The problem I have experienced is massive fuel leakage from the carburetor after the unit has been stored for several months and then put into service.  Storage of the generator was in a conditioned space (garage).  

The procedure issued by the manufacturer is to run the unit with fuel shut off until the generator quits running.  I followed this procedure before storing the unit.  Having been trained to work on small and large engines and after the fuel spill occurred, I removed and disassembled the carburetor.  I found that the float needle was stuck in the open position due to heavy corrosion of the needle valve, which caused it to remain in the open position, allowing fuel to continue to fill the float chamber.  

This corrosion is definetly a defect which deserves an immediate recall by the manufacturer.  If an open flame or ignition source had been present when this occurred there is no doubt in my mind this would have been a serious fire and likely explosion of the fuel tank.
justification: The incident involved a fuel leak due to a defective carburetor, which could have led to a fire or explosion if an ignition source was present, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: We purchased a new set of C.R. Lawrence porcelain mirror pivots from Glassware Pro (an on-line supplier) on December 9, 2012 and installed the pivots to hang a mirror on our main bathroom wall on December 28 2012. The C.L. Lawrence sales information states the pivots are rated to hold a mirror weighting up to 30 pounds.  A mirror, weighing 22 pounds, was installed with hangers that exceeded the manufacturers requirements.  The mirror was up approximately 2 weeks when on January 10, 2013 at approximately 9:30 at night the entire mounting assembly suddenly gave way from the wall and the mirror fell to the floor.  Large pieces of razor sharp plate glass and glass shards were propelled through the air upon floor impact.  We were fortunate that no one was injured when the mirror fell.  Sharp glass shards and glass pieces were thrown up to 10 feet from where the mirror impacted.
justification: The mirror fell and shattered, but no one was injured.

incident_description: charging my [REDATED] with this Sharper Image Dual USB AC Wall Charger (TSI-4002). then it started glitching. it became really hot and then started sparking and caused a small fire. after turning off the fire. i noticed that my [REDACTED] was not turning on. i used a different wall charger but still my [REDACTED] did not tun back on. the next day i took my [REDACTED] to [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] told me my motherboard was fried because of the wall charger i used.
justification: The incident involved a device malfunction causing a small fire and damage to the device, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My washer continues to easily become unbalanced with any large load or small load with an article that becomes heavy when wet.  For example a bedspread for a kingsized bed may require an adjustment on my part to rebalance the load two or three times to get through a wash cycle.  The same thing happens with a small load if there is a shirt that retains a lot of water that one article will cause the entire load of five or six items to become unbalanced multiple times during the wash cycle. It will cause the shaking noise or stop the wash cycle.   This has happened too many times to count and until I saw the recall I thought this was SOP for this type of washing machine.
justification: The washer frequently becomes unbalanced, causing noise and cycle interruptions, but no injury or damage is mentioned.

incident_description:
I own, or have owned, 2 Holmes Model HLP3300B heaters.  Both heaters were purchased in 2012.   In 2012, one of the heaters caught fire.  I thought it was a fluke and continued to use the second heater.  Today, they second heater started smoking and the control knob melted down into the heater.  I would think that this heater would have some type of safety feature that would cause it to shut off if it started to short out.  Maybe it does, but it's not working.  Based only on my own experiences, I believe that these heaters are dangerous and should be recalled before someone is killed.  
I threw the first heater away, but I kept the second heater and took pictures.  My hope is that Holmes might want to see why their heaters are catching fire.  I'm assuming that they don't already know this.
justification: Both heaters exhibited dangerous behavior (fire and smoking), but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Our Sunbeam Model SQH310 Portable Heater tends to overheat and trip off. Now I notice that the cord is getting quite hot. Almost too hot to touch. I found similar complaints at WalMart.com and other sites. One person at viewpoints.com wrote that one unit's cord melted while another unit caught fire.

My heater is over a year old, so it is too late to return it, but I think with the number of problems reported, the product should be investigated.
justification: The incident involves overheating and tripping off, with reports of cords melting and catching fire, indicating a significant hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description: My GE Profile High Efficiency Top Load Washer Model number PTWN8050MWW fell apart during the final spin cycle.  It ttore the machine wide open and had enough force to smash through a portion of one wall and hit my dryer hard enough to dent in the side and the insde drum along with forcing the dryer against another wall damaging that wall and actually making the wall loose.  If anyone was near the machine when this happened they could have been killed.  I have numerous pictures of the washer and the damage created I have also uploaded a video to you tube showing some of the damage caused.  I have never seen or heard anything like this before, so I want to get the word out before someone gets injured.  Here is the link to the you tube video of the damage.[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and had the potential to cause death, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have two Shark Euro-Pro floor steamers and they both have the exact same issue. Once they are turned on and warmed up you push up and down in order to force steam out of the end onto the floor. What frequently hapens is the unit become clogged and the steam continues to build as there is no exit for the pressure. I have tried on multiple occasions to remove the head and if yoiu have not allowed at least 20 minutes for the unit to cool down it will literally explode with great force. This was the worst ever and it sprayed my foot, through my socks and slipper causing a burn. The fact that there are multiple compaints about this steamer and BOTH of mine do it should be a huge cause for concern. This could seriously injure somebody's face, child or pet. I cannot believe that these are still being sold!
justification: The incident caused a burn injury to the user's foot, and there is potential for more severe injuries to the face, children, or pets.

incident_description: Using a Eedenpure 1000 heater I noticed a plastic smell in the house and investigated and found that the heater was melting on the front face plate and the top also was melting.
justification: The heater was melting but there was no mention of injury or death, only a plastic smell and visible damage to the heater.

incident_description: About a week ago my living room in wall cadet electric heater unit was functioning normally when all of a sudden my toddler said Mommy, look! and pointed to sparks and then almost immediately flames jumping out of the front vent. I turned it off immediately and thankfully avoided a real fire but it made some electrical smoke. After it cooled down I turned off it's breaker and took the faceplate off. The resistance coil was mangled in one part but not broken. It didn't have very much dust as I routinely vacuum it out. I have 2 others just like it in my bedrooms and another Cadet unit but a different model in my bathroom. The bathroom unit is rarely used but the bedroom units are used daily. So far the bedroom units are still fine, but they are the same exact model as the living room unit. I am very worried about them as I see they have many, many recalls. I used to leave them in the on position to automatically run and maintain a good temp in the house but now I never leave with them on nor do I leave them on a night. The all have C202 listed as the model but searching the cadet site does not show any that are this model, the closest are models RMC202W (the Register Plus series) and CSC202TW (the Com-Pak Plus series), which also have the same voltage, 240V. The one that caught fire shows a mfg date of April 21 2003. I cannot tell from the info on the cadet site if these are units included in a recall or not.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks from the heater, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible due to the presence of similar units in use and recalls mentioned.

incident_description: On January 14, the Beverly Fire Department responded for a fire alarm activation at a commercial Structure. Upon arrival, crews found an odor of electrical burning in office area. After a thorough search, the source was determined to be an Innowave water purifying dispenser. After closer observation, it was determined that wires passing through a round cutout of a metal partition had chafed against the cutout and shorted out. There was no protection around the interior of the cutout.
justification: The incident involved an electrical short with no injury or death, and such electrical issues are possible in commercial settings.

incident_description: My kenmore oasis has been giving the infamous f1 code and when on the high rpm spin cycle the machine will not balance and moves around violently. The machine  actually smashed my fingers between it and our door frame as I tried to push myself out of its way. This issue is the same for small and large loads.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (smashed fingers) due to the machine's violent movement, indicating a severity level of 3. The issue occurs consistently with both small and large loads, making the occurrence likelihood high.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his baseboard heater caught fire after using it for the third time at the highest heat, it was in use for 10 hours.  There was an odor of electrical fire and he noticed that there was burnt hole near the control panel.  The electrical cord was still intact. 

The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that he would received a prepaid label to return the heater.  It has been 5 business days and he did not receive anything.

The caller is concerned that this product is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The heater caught fire, causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Our realtor informed us that we would need to change our Federal Pacific Stab Lok electric panel circuit breaker box in order to put our house on the market.  We contacted an electrician.  He confirmed that these panels are "deadly" and "scare" him.  We will need to replace the unit.  However, this item continues to be sold on-line even though the manufacturing is no longer in business.  There has never been a recall for the product and consumers are spending significant dollar amounts out of their own pockets to replace these malfunctioning circuit breakers.
justification: The description indicates a potential hazard with the electric panel, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
(01/07/2013) The consumer stated that the space heater was in the kitchen. The consumer stated that she plugged the heater in this morning around 4 am for the first time per the instructions. She turned to her husband and told him that something smelled funny. Her husband told her that the heater was on fire. The heater was in flames. The flames were coming from the grill on the front. The consumer unplugged the heater. She picked it up and took it out the door. The heater was still in flames but the flames had died down. Eventually, the flames went out.

(01/07/2013) The consumer called the manufacturer. She spoke to [REDACTED]. He asked her to send the space heater back to the manufacturer. The consumer refused. [REDACTED] advised that he would send someone out. the consumer told him no one would be there until 1/9/2013. She asked him to call before coming out.
justification: The space heater caught fire, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description: We had two "touch n brush" dispensers mounted on a large mirror over a vanity.  (The mirror was approximately 4'x3', and properly mounted with brackets and anchors.)  My 10 year old child, who is very small, was attempting to clean her mirror.  She pulled on the dispenser to try to release the suctions cups.  The mirror pulled completely out of the wall, fell on her, and shattered.  She is very fortunate that she sustained only a large bruise on her arm.
justification: The child sustained a large bruise on her arm, which is an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a refurbished uninterruptible power supply originally manufactured by APC from excessUPS.com through Amazon marketplace. excessUPS.com replace the batteries in these devices with their own generic brand when the original batteries expire. The product was powered on November 16th in a well ventilated office with three windows.

I developed the following symptoms after powering the unit

extreme difficulty breathing, dizziness, giddiness, nausea, confusion and disorientation, loss of balance to the point that I fell. I had chest palpitations and vision changes and felt so faint I could not stand in the ER. 

In all I was in the emergency room on six occasions from November 19th through November 27th. They performed various tests including CAT and MRI scans of my head, neck and chest.

After a few hours I would appear to somewhat recover at the hospital then after returning to my apartment I would become ill again. Eventually it was discovered that this product was emitting odorless fumes that were the cause of my condition. This gas was exceptionally potent. Briefly smelling the air around the unit almost knocked me out and I was delirious for two hours afterwards. It was able to poison me from an adjacent room with the door closed. Even cleaning the floor where the device was placed made me ill a week after it had been removed.

I am writing this report January 13th and have still not recovered completely from this exposure although I have gradually been improving. The UPS is in storage and I am searching for a lab to have it tested in the hopes of finding out exactly what I have been exposed to. 

I have not worked during this time and have substantial medical bills as a consequence. Since this incident it has been a daily struggle just to live. My health has taken a substantial hit. I was so ill at the hospital I had a will written during this time.
justification: The incident caused severe health issues requiring multiple ER visits and ongoing recovery, but no death was reported.

incident_description:
A product I purchased (The Aloha Fan Heater) Model 05100....date 06/05 from the label on it. Caught on fire while in use. It was a small fire and I noticed it right away. No damage occured because I unplugged it and blew out the small flames.

It was on its high heat setting.

Have not used it since obviously.
justification: The heater caught fire but was quickly extinguished with no damage or injury.

incident_description:
Maytag Dryer model#MED850WQ0 serial#2823089:
Purchased July 2010, within 8 months, the dryer would run for an extended time , inside the drum would become dripping wet with dust stuck all over inside the drum and the clothes would not dry. I called Maytage and authorized tech opened up the dryer and saw the vacuum pulley nut came off and the belt to the vacuum was laying loose next to it. 7 months later the exact same thing happened; same symptom, same same cause, same solution, screw nut back on and reattach belt to vacuum. December 2012, now 3rd time it has happened. This is a fire and electrical hazard; fire hazard because dust can accumulate within the dryer and inside under the drum and electrical hazard because excess moisture dripping. Maytag suggested I buy an extended warranty because they will not cover manufacturer defects outside the warranty period even though the issue was initially discovered within the warranty period and the same defect has cause the dryer to malfunction now a total of 3 times. As well I have to pay $149 each time service comes out. Dryer should be recalled because vacuum malfunctioning could be a fire hazard. My telephone number is [REDACTED] if you need more information.
justification: The incident describes a recurring mechanical failure posing potential fire and electrical hazards, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: On numerous occassions, my one year old daughter has unlocked the Safety1st push and latch cabinet locks. I made sure I was tightening them the first few times it happened and then I realized she could still unlock them. Luckily, I stay on top of her so she has not ingested anything or hurt herself with heavy pots and pans. There was a recall in 2012 on a different model number of the same locks but we assumed we were safe because we had the newer model number the company said they were replacing them with. However, once my daughter became mobile and stronger, we realized she could open these as well. The name is Safety1st push and latch cabinet locks. They are manufactured by the Dorel Juv. Grp. and the model numbers are HS158 and HS159.
justification: The child has unlocked the cabinet locks multiple times but has not ingested anything or been injured due to parental supervision.

incident_description: Five and 0ne-half year old furnace started having operating problems-wooshing sounds and intermittent shut downs. Repair personnel discovered that tubes had disintegrated causing potentially dangerous levels of carbon dioxide to enter residence.  Particulate matter was found as well as large hole in one of the pipes.  Pictures are available for viewing.  Per the direction of repair personnel we were instructed not to utilize heat until unit could be replaced.  Outside temperatures are below freezing so replacement of furnace was necessary as parts are difficult to come by and repair costs were close to full replacement.
justification: The furnace malfunction led to dangerous levels of carbon dioxide entering the residence, posing a significant health risk, though no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased my home in April of 2011.  Shortly after moving into my home, slate roofing tiles began breaking off and sliding off the roof.  The roofing tiles are a simulated slate roofing tile product called "Lamarite", produced by Tamko Building Products, located in [REDACTED].  The Lamarite tiles are a 18" x 12" synthetic slate material.  Each tile weighs approximately 10 pounds.  

I contacted a roofing contractor to inspect my roof.  The roofing contractor performed an inspection and  reported that the majority of the roofing tiles on my roof were cracked, crumbling and/or in high risk of failure.  The roofing contractor contacted a local Omaha roofing supply company to find our more about the roofing tiles.  He discovered that the Lamarite product had been released in 2003 and 2004, stating a 50 year service life.  The Lamarite product began to fail within a few short years after installation.  

My roofing contrator discovered that Tamko had been replacing the defective tiles on a case by case basis, after filing a claim with Tamko's residential warranty services [REDACTED].  In July of 2012, I proceeded to call the warranty number, file a claim and submit sample roof tiles.  Since July, the Lamerite tiles have been failing a rapid rate.  Cracked and broken portions of the individual tiles are falling off of my roof on a weekly basis.  A UPS delivery driver recently met me at the door with a failed and fallen broken tile, which he suggests fell on my front porch as he approached my door.  

5 months after submitting my claim to Tamko, along with my required submittal of ownership documents, physical samples and photographs, Tamko denied my claim outright.  Tamko's sole reason for the denial was that I was not the original homeowner.  Tamko refused to even respond to the roof samples and pictures that I supplied, even though they clearly demonstrate the impending failure of my entire risk.  For them, this is about saving money, by denying warranty coverage.  For my household and guests, this is about the danger of heavy roof tiles crashing down unexpectedly.  There is no question a person could be struck and killed when the roofing tiles fail and come crashing down.  

As such, I am left with a roof that is cracking, crumbling and crashing down to the ground.  The roofing tiles fail unexpectedly and end up crashing down on my sidewalks, driveway, porch and patios.  Tamko is fully aware of the high risk posed by their defective product.  I can supply the name of a representative from Builders Supply, here in [REDACTED], who was Tamko's exclusive dealer in the Omaha area.  

While Tamko believes it can hide behind its limited warranties, I feel like I am at great risk from a dangerously defective product.  Tamko refuses to do the right thing, which is the purpose of this report.
justification: Heavy roofing tiles are falling frequently, posing a clear risk of injury or death, though no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description:
(11/10/2012) The consumer stated that she sprayed the cleaner on the shower wall and in the tub of the bathroom. The consumer stated that her eyes started watering and her nose started running profusely. She stated that she wiped down and rinsed the walls and tub with  clear water. She stated that this took about 15 minutes. The consumer stated that afterward she could not breath. She stated that she was wheezing and coughing. The consumer stated that the vent fan was on and the bathroom door was open. 

The consumer stated that she was coughing and had shortness of breath all night. She stated that she went to Associates in Family Medicine Urgent Care on !0/11/2012. The address is [REDACTED] The telephone number is[REDACTED]. She stated that she was seen by Dr. [REDACTED], Urgent care doctor on duty. She stated that she was given an albuterol sulfate nebulizer treatment because she could not breath. The he did an xray. The xray indicated reactive airway dysfunction symptom (RADS). She stated that it was caused from inhaling one of the chemicals in the product. She is being treated for inhaled irritant induced asthma. She was prescribed prednisone and albuterol nebulizer treatments at home. 

(11/15/2012)The consumer stated that she followed up with her health care provider, [REDACTED]. PA at[REDACTED][REDACTED]
She was given an albuterol nebulizer treatment in her office.
justification: The consumer experienced severe respiratory symptoms requiring medical treatment, including nebulizer treatments and medication, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I picked up a white plastic container of Spray Shield and did not realize that this item 'sprayed'.  I inadvertently sprayed it directly into my eyes.  The product is called Zagg Shield Spray  Application Solution.  It reads "Do Not Spray into eyes, Swallow, or Inhale".  There are NO ingredients listed on this package so I have NO idea what went into my eyes and caused severe burning.  I have flushed my eyes with cold water and have minimal relief.  20 minutes later and my vision is hazy.
justification: The incident resulted in severe eye burning and hazy vision, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Circuit breaker panel bus bar tabs "melted" partially where circuit breaker pushes down onto the bus bar.  This was a Westinghouse panel installed when my home was built in 1993.  A video of the problem is posted on YouTube at  http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NCqGjqoc_Ts Since I posted the video about a year ago, it has had over 11,000 visits and several people have commented about having the same problem.  I reported this to Underwriter's Laboratories, but they chose to take no action.
justification: The incident involves a potential electrical hazard with no reported injuries, but multiple reports suggest it is a recurring issue.

incident_description: I was using the vacuum to clean my floors.  The vacuums electrical was shorting off and on.  The vacuum starting smoking and the plugs burnt up.
justification: The vacuum smoking and plugs burning up indicate an incident with potential for harm, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(11/06/2012) The consumer stated that the dryer was on the permanent press cycle for about 36 minutes. The consumer stated when she attempted to take them out of the dryer, they were too hot to touch. The consumer said that she could smell that they scorched and not wearable. She stated that she threw them out. The consumer stated that she noticed it before on cotton materials. She stated that the synthetics clothes have melted. She stated that the problem is more frequence than before. The problems have happened on the cotton and permanent press settings.


(11/09/2012)The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and was told that the dryer was not a part if the recall (REL#12-251). She was advised that she would have to pay out of pocket for the repair.


The consumer stated that she is having the same problem that is mentioned in the release.
justification: The incident involves property damage (scorched and melted clothes) but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: After a year of usage (and proper maintenance as per manufacturers instructions) the AC adapter shorted out and I realized it had begun corroding at the insertion point.  I had two of these wipes warmers and this happened to both units within months of one another.  When the second one broke, I started thinking it was not just a fluke and did some investigating/inspection.  I realized that when the unit is in use and open, condensation that has accumulated on the lid leaks through to the back of the unit and onto the power cord where it inserts into the unit.  This water damage leads to shorts and corrosion over time.  Both of these units were kept away from water sources and that is the only water damage that occurred.  They were also used in GFCI protected outlets in a 10 year old house with a whole house surge protection system in place (as well as a whole house generator as a back-up power supply). I unplugged the units immediately and continued use only as a dispenser and not a warmer, realizing I did not want anything that could be a potential fire hazard in my home.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure (shorted AC adapter and corrosion) but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Found that the plug on my Lasko model #6252 electric space heater had been on fire. It melted the outlet cover, the outlet itself, and the plastic around the plug. The space heater was in the "off" postition at the the time.
justification: The incident involved a fire that caused damage to the outlet and plug but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that she followed the instruction to use the heater, however there was fumes and an overwhelming odor emitting from the heater which caused her to be nauseous.  This incident left an unusual taste in her mouth.  No medical attention was received.  [REDACTED], made me sick.

The caller returned the heater to the store and received a full refund.  She requested that the retail store removed the item from the shelf because the heater was a health hazard.  The manufacturer was not contacted as yet. The caller feels that this heater is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident caused nausea and an unusual taste, indicating physical discomfort but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was using the washing machine and when it was on the ÃÂspin cycleÃÂ he started to smell burning rubber. The consumer stated that he walked to the washer machine and found smoke all over the room. The consumer stated that he pressed the power button to turn off the cycle, then opened the door to the washer machine and smoke came out from the washer. 

The consumer stated that there was also water on his floor. The consumer stated that he dried off the floor and unplugged the washer machine. 

The consumer stated that the water in the washer machine was not draining. The consumer stated that the basket became detached and broke the gasket or rubber boot which caused the water not to drain. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. The consumer stated that there were no damages to his home structure. 

The consumer stated that he believes his front loading machine was experiencing the same hazard discussed on recall #13-003. 

The consumer believes that this product should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved smoke and water leakage but no injuries or structural damage, aligning with severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) given the recall reference and described malfunction.

incident_description:
In November, 2012, my husband and I bought a new Moen Onehandle Pullout kitchen faucet, model number CA87316C, which was installed on November 13, 2012.
Several days after we had it installed, I started smelling a chemical smell, when the cold water was being used.  I am very sensitive to certain smells and it has made me feel ill whenever I smell it.  I have looked online and many other people with Moen kitchen faucets seem to have the same problem.
Because I wash my hands at the kitchen sink many times a day, make coffee with water from that faucet, as well as use it for cooking, I am very concerned as to what is causing the smell and how dangerous it may be.  I have read that people who have complained to Moen about this, have been told that it is the hose that is causing the problem, but people who have replaced the hose still have the same problem.

I wanted the CPSC to be aware of this (I believe other people have also written of this problem) and find out, if you know, what follow-up, if any, has been done and what has been found out about this product.
justification: The chemical smell from the faucet has made the user feel ill, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The issue is reported by multiple users, suggesting it is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Comfort Zone CZ499R Oscillating Tower Heater
I bought this heater in the fall of 2010. It had a made on 8/2010 sticker on the bottom. It worked very well. Always kept the room nice a warm. However, in November 2011 I started noticing a burning smell. Then power button (not the on off button) stopped working. Then today it just stopped working all together. I noticed on the bottom a burn mark and hole. I looked around the area where it was sitting and sure enough my carpet has burn marks on it now. I took the bottom plate off to find that the coating around the small wire connecting to the power button had burned off and the wire disconnected. The wire was lying on the bottom of the unit, hence the burn mark. This is why you should never leave these space heaters on unattended. So in summary, it works great until the it starts to melt down!

Read the Amazon.com reviews, several say they started smoking or had the same issues that I did.
justification: The heater caused burn marks on the carpet and had a burning smell, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: MrHeater Big Buddy heater started on fire
justification: The heater starting on fire is an incident with potential for harm, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
I had a Antec EarthWatts EA-650 GREEN 650W computer power supply catch on fire. Luckily I was at the computer when smoke started coming out. Flames started coming out the back and I pulled the power plug. The power supply is at the bottom and back of the computer so it would have caught the drywall on fire if I was not there. I bought this power supply last spring when I built the computer. It was working fine until it started burning. I contacted the company but have not heard back. I also found others having the same problem:

http://www.newegg.com/Product/Product.aspx?Item=17-371-044&SortField=0&SummaryType=0&Pagesize=100&PurchaseMark=&SelectedRating=1&VideoOnlyMark=False&VendorMark=&IsFeedbackTab=true&Keywords=%28keywords%29&Page=1#scrollFullInfo

Thanks, [REDACTED]
justification: The power supply caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injury occurred as the fire was promptly extinguished.

incident_description: Dealer called and told us their might be a gas leak in the valve.  I contacted the manufacturer and   they said they are discussing what to do with the CPSC.  They told us to either keep the pilot lit all the time or shut the gas off totally.  We have been afraid to use the fireplace.  Apparently in 2007 and 2008 they had a recall with a similar problem.  It is now 9 months and there is no fix announced.   The fireplace is the 1080 Clean Face made by Fireplace Xtraordinaire owned by Travis Industries.  Can you help me?
justification: The description indicates a potential gas leak (incident) but no injury or death has occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the historical recall and ongoing discussion with CPSC.

incident_description: I own a Venmar air exchanger, model Solo 2.0 HRV.  Recently the motor started to  vibrate and was very hot to the touch.  I have unplugged the device.  While I had nothing serious happen, I have read that there have ben fires caused by the motors in these unit overheating, and I wanted to report the motor failure.  It appears that these motors are seriously unreliable and dangerous, and Venmar should replace them with a reliable and safe motor.  I was fortunate to have found mine before the unit overheated and caught fire.  Regards, [REDACTED]
justification: The motor was hot and vibrating but no injury or fire occurred, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: Clothes dryer was running under normal operation. When the dryer alarm went off my wife opened dryer the door to the smell of warm natural gas. From what we have been able to determine the igniter stopped working but gas continued to enter in to the dryer chamber. My concern is if gas continues to fill the dryer chamber and the igniter starts again the dryer will explode.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with potential for explosion, but no actual injury or explosion occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she purchased a generator and when she went to turn it on it started to leak gasoline from the carburetor. The consumer stated that she decided to turn off the generator immediately and also turned off the fuel switch. 

The consumer stated that she was afraid that if the gas continued to leak if it came in contact with the hot engine it can cause a fire. 

The consumer stated that she searched online and found many reports in regards to these defective generators. The consumer stated that she was upset because she lost $700 on a defective generator that could have caused a fire. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they referred her to an authorized repair services.
justification: The incident involved a gasoline leak from a defective generator, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Two problems that have been reported to the Federal Trade Commission;

Caller purchased a box of five 400 grit belts for his belt sander this past Summer.
Around July or August 2012 he put one of the belts on the sander to etch glass but within minutes the belt snapped at the seam and almost hit him in the face.

He states that this is not an OSHA product because the belts used in the workplace are 120 inches long and his are not only 4 inches wide and 64 inches long but are used in his own garage at his home.

He would like these belts investigated and recalled before someone is injured severely.

Also note:  Consumer checked on Internet & stores wherein sander belts are sold to find no endless belts of any size are sold.  None have a mfg date or expiration date printed on the belt nor do they come with any storage instructions.  This should be there in my opinion.  My belts are used in water environments for glass work - Many others are used in a dry environment for woodworking.

The belts I have from CR Lawrence and failed were made by 3M.  Altho Lawrence will not provide the mfg date and tell me they will last 1 year.  How long did they have them in stock prior to selling them to me?  This mgg date & expiration date is vital for the user as well as any storage info.

Retaping the seam if necessary (wherein they fail) should also be made available to users.
justification: The belt snapped and almost hit the caller in the face, indicating an incident with potential for injury but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
On November 24th, 2012 caller was just getting on his attic ladder to climb up and retrieve Christmas decorations when he felt the left side of the ladder disengage at the first fold metal casting which snapped.
Once he felt the left side of the ladder disengage he began to step off the ladder when the right side also disengaged.
He fell to the ground but was not injured because his wife actually broke his fall, she also was not injured.

The ladder was installed in the house during building in October 2005.
He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

He is reporting this incident because the ladder is just 7 years old and could have caused great injury to persons climbing it.

He is asking that this ladder be recalled and that he be reimbursed for the ladder he is having installed to replace this ladder due to his being very much afraid of the ladder.

Caller is 71 yrs old and his wife is 69 yrs old, they could have been very seriously injured.
justification: The ladder failure caused a fall, but no injuries occurred as the fall was broken by the caller's wife.

incident_description:
On December 1, 2012 I purchased a new Frigidaire laundry pair, top load washer and front load dryer.  Upon preparing to wash clothes I raised the lid and it fell down on my head.  On many occasions after that the lid would not stay securely up and I would have to be careful to make sure it was stable.  I noticed how flimsy and loose the lid was and how easy it was to come down.  Each time I wash clothes I have to pay close attention to the lid.  One time when I was lifting the lid and reaching for the clothes detergent at the same time, not paying as close attention as I should, I almost had my hand slammed by the door falling.

I called the place we purchased the set from and they sent a tech out and said that I needed to contact Frigidaire.  The technician said the problem is in the way the door is manufactured with too big a lip on the back of the lid.  Most washer lids will go back further but this one is not secure.

Upon contacting Frigidaire they said they could not do anything and that this is the way the machine is designed.

Please check this unit out yourself.  It is not safe and is a poor design.
justification: The incident involves a recurring issue with the washer lid falling, posing a risk of injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description:
Issue is with Klein Tools Depthfinder Steel Fish Tape # 56003.  Below, my email to the manufacturer, Klein Tools, pretty much spells out the problem.  My assessment of the cause is a structurally inadequate construction, namely a case made of inadequately stiff plastic that permits the content, always a sprung load, to entangle and jam.  The safety issue is that this happens every five or six uses and, with the spring steel loose end of the tape bobbing and flying about, with its users frequently constrained in tight quarters (because of the nature of the work for which this things is used), there is a very significant eye hazard both to the user and anyone else in the vicinity.

---------------
Email:

From: [REDACTED]
Date: January 5, 2013 7:09:15 PM EST
To: customerservice@kleintools.com
Subject: Depthfinder Steel Fish Tape - Garbage

Today, for the umpteenth time over the last year, my Klein fish tape jammed again.  I've had it apart a number of times, straightened bends in the tape, wound and rewound it carefully onto the plastic reel, giving more TLC to a simple tool than I do to even complicated power tools, yet it never works for more than a few uses before again binding, it's cheap plastic case distorting and causing tangles.  For the tape's intended purpose, it is worthless.  But this isn't the worst.  Being difficult to keep unbound and requiring extra effort and attention, often in tight quarters, it's loose end all too frequently swings dangerously about, risking putting my or coworkers eyes out.  The darned thing is flat out dangerous.

Tonight I discarded it and will never have another, at least never one made cheaply of inadequate plastic.

[REDACTED]
Clinton, TN
justification: The description indicates a significant eye hazard due to the tool's malfunction, posing a risk of injury to users and coworkers in tight spaces.

incident_description: Purchased heater in Nov 2011 from Amazon.con. Have been using during winter months each year since without issue. This morning, turned unit on after being off for 12+ hours. Within several minutes, unit burst into flames for no reason. I unplugged unit and extinguished fire with fire extinguisher. Very scary.
justification: The heater burst into flames, which is a significant incident, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Coleman Powermate Manual Transfer Switch, Model No. PA0650080
30 Amp 10 Circuit

Transfer switch has been installed and functional for around a year. Switch was wired according to manufacturer's instructions. There is a test switch and pair of lights to indicate that line power is available. When I toggled the test switch the last time, it literally blew up with the intensity of a
firecracker. It burned my thumb (which I used to toggle the switch) and
left a black residue on my thumb and forefinger. Both the rocker switch
and light have literally disappeared leaving plastic shells. I found the
switch toggle, a piece of spring wire, and the red jeweled cover for the lights about 15 feet away.

Coleman Powermate addressed this problem by telling me that they subcontracted the manufacture of this device, so they don't feel responsible. They also recommended that I disconnect all power from this dangerous product.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the thumb and forefinger, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the event and the manufacturer's response.

incident_description:
This is in regards to Item #32879, 20 Ton Shop Press produced and sold nationwide by Harbor Freight.   

http://www.harborfreight.com/20-ton-shop-press-32879.html?ccdenc=eyJjb2RlIjoiNDk2NTI0NDIiLCJza3UiOiIzMjg3OSIsImlzIjoiMTQ5Ljk5IiwicHJvZHVjdF9p%0D%0AZCI6IjQ1MyJ9%0D%0A 

The issue is not with the press itself but with the accessories provided.   As part of the purchase, Harbor Freight provides cast iron plates to be used to support items being pressed.   These plates will see up to 20 tons of pressure (rated capacity).   Cast Iron is a poor material for use in a high pressure application.   It has a tendency to shatter sending shards of the plates flying in all directions.    I have not personally been injured by this happening however, there are numerous accounts of this happening where individuals were injured available via numerous internet forums.  

I am reporting this as a proactive measure to prevent future injuries to others as well as myself.    Harbor Freight should recall these plates and replace them with a proper material such as mild/cold rolled steel.   Not Cast Iron.   I have brought this to the attention of Harbor Freight but am not confident they will respond with appropriate measures.
justification: The incident involves potential injury due to shattering cast iron plates under pressure, with reports of injuries but no personal injury reported.

incident_description: King Sound Enterprise Co., Ltd Super Switch Model KSI-293.  After two previous years and ten days this year of using this remotely operated switch for Christmas lights, I noticed an electrical burning odor.  The switch was so hot that it was melting the case as well as the molded plug on the extension cord attached to it.  The switch had been on for approx. three hours today and had no indication of problems when switched off the previous evening.  Pictures available.
justification: The incident involved an electrical burning odor and melting of the switch case and plug, indicating a hazardous situation but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
HolmesÃÂ® HLP3300B-TG Low Profile Heater w/ Manual Controls.
A few months after purchase, unit started emitting acrid burned-plastic/electrical-smell smoke.
Unplugged unit.  
Inspected, verified that switch was melting. 
Called manufacturer.  They are out of stock of replacement units.  Told me to call back in a few weeks, could not retain my order in a queue.
justification: The unit emitted smoke and had a melting switch, indicating a hazardous incident but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Smelled smoke smell coming from laundry room.  Found out it was from a Whirlpool brand Cabrio AccuDry gas Dryer purchased in 2010 (model # WGD5600XW0), after searching the web for similar occurrences (found incident on Safer Products.gov website here). Removed bottom panel from my dryer and saw tons of black burnt lint covering the bottom of the burner compartment. It evidently had a "flash" fire of the most fine lint on top, because none of it was still smoldering nor was there any more smoke.
justification: The incident involved a flash fire in the dryer but no injury or ongoing fire was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Genie PowerLift 900 garage door opener on Sept. 15, 2012, and installed it a couple of weeks later.  The unit passes its safety tests and worked fine until last week when it exceeded its down limit and reversed twice.  I reprogrammed the down limit, and it worked okay a few more times until it again exceeded its down limit.  However, this time the door did not reverse, and the down force continued until (1) the shuttle went to the very end of the screw drive and was possible damaged, (2) the arm connecting the shuttle to the door was twisted out of shape, and (3) the small bracket screwed to the door where the arm connects was bent.  Then the motor shut off.

The Genie tech I talked to today mentioned the possibility of a "bad board."  I (too late, of course) read a reference to a "bad board" in a review of this product on Amazon.  If there are indeed bad boards in these openers, the product should be a candidate for recall, should it not?  There's a real hazard here.

The S/N of my unit is 122164210976JC
justification: The incident caused damage to the garage door opener and its components but did not result in any injury or death.

incident_description:
Purchased two Lasko Ceramic Heaters, Model 5165 from Target in November 2012.  I paid $49.99 plus 8% tax for each device for a total of $I07.98.  plugged one unit in and noticed it began to make a noise.  After one week I noticed the cord began to over heat when in the HI position.  It eventually overheated and melted the electrical outlet. I immediately removed the cord and contacted Target to let them know this device is defective.  I will also contact Lasko via email.

This product needs to be removed from the market before it burns someone's home down.  If left unattended, the electrical outlet will overheat causing internal wiring to catch fire in homes that do not have AFI outlets.  AFI outlets will short the wiring before it catches fire.  Most homes built prior to 2010, do not have these upgraded outlets. 

I took a photos of the burnt cord, the ceramic heater, original box and the damaged outlet.  Did not see a manufactured date on the product or instruction manual.

I will be returning these products to Target for a full refund or give Lasko 7 days to respond to my email.
justification: The incident involved a defective heater causing overheating and melting an electrical outlet, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: A few years ago my husband and I remodeled a bathroom.  We installed new shower doors over an existing bath tub.  The glass shower doors were made by Kohler - product #K-702200.  This weekend one of the shower doors spontaneously burst into thousands of little glass pieces.  The door simply shattered.  No one was home at the time.  As I returned home and entered the house I could hear the grass cracking and popping.  We estimate that 20 pounds of broken shattered glass was all over our bathroom.  We had never seen any cracks or damage on the door.  Luckily no one was in the shower at the time.  Shower doors simply shouldn't shatter with no warning.  A quick google search shows that this is not unheard of...
justification: The shower door shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury. A quick search indicates this is not unheard of, suggesting it's possible.

incident_description: The thermostat caught fire and ignited all the wiring within the wall. The thermostat blew off the wall and landed a few feet away.
justification: The thermostat caught fire and caused damage, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The incident is that my Belkin UPS had failed in a closed state and melted to my carpet.  I believe I was lucky that it didn't cause a fire but wanted to alert Belkin of the issue.  I have not received a response from them about this in 6 weeks and was concerned that this issue could be more wide spread than just me considering I was using the product per manufactures specifications.

I was using it to provide protection and minimal runtime to my Home entertainment center.  It was positioned behind the TV in a reasonably well ventilated area.  

It did cause damage to the carpet but did not burn up any of my electronics.
justification: The UPS failed and melted the carpet but caused no injury or fire, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I am a pediatric ICU doctor and have had 3-4 incidences of ingestion of laundry detergent contained in gel packets such as "Tide Pods."  I just got off the phone with an ER physician for yet another episode of a child playing with one of these pods which ruptured and caused significant and serious eye injuries.  These pods are apealing to children in color, and shape, and have a pleasing fragrence.  They are clearly a problem that has been reported previously, but they have not been removed from the market.  Please remove these products from the shelves, before more children are injured.
justification: The description reports significant and serious eye injuries from detergent pods, indicating injury (severity 3), and mentions multiple incidents, suggesting likelihood is high (4).

incident_description: Plugged in the Soleil Fan Heater to warm up the room. It is the small size electric heater. After a few second, flames came out of the heater. I was able to put out the flames without any injury to me.
justification: Flames came out of the heater, indicating an incident, but no injury occurred as the flames were put out safely.

incident_description: We have frameless, tempered glass shower doors.  One of the glass doors spontaneously shattered.
justification: The glass door shattered, which could potentially cause injury if someone was nearby, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I am very concerned that the Life Smart 1500 watt space heater will cause a fire. When used a few hours, the AC plug gets extremely hot, so much so that the wall plate in my home began to melt. I purchased two of these units at the same time and the second one exhibits the same problem. 
I can supply photos of the damage if needed.

justification: The person fell from a step stool but there is no mention of injury, so the severity is low.

incident_description: I have a Sterling by Kohler Company Bypass Glass shower door.  Product wasn't even a year old.  On the evening of 1-7-13 I was watching TV when I heard what sounded like and explosion then a continued cracking sound.  I started walking around the house to see what caused the noise, as I walked into my bathroom I noticed the one panel of my glass bypass shower door has just exploded.  Glass was everywhere.  I contacted the company via email on 1-8-13 and as of today 1-9-13 I have heard no response.  The item was purchased at Home Depot.  The model number is Model # 660B-48S.  The store SKU # is 320905
justification: The shower door exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using my Shark steam mop.  Suddenly it stopped creating steam, so I unplugged it and waited for the mop head to cool.  I started to take the mop head off of the unit by pressing the release button, when the mop head shot off the unit, followed by a huge stream of blistering hot steam that shot across the room.  I sustained a very minor burn on my left thumb.  Luckily, my children and dog were not in the vicinity when the steam shot out.  I will NEVER use a steam mop of this kind again.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the event.

incident_description: My wife purchased a Bath and Body Works Wallflower, a plug-in air freshener. The scent was strong so she unplugged it and placed in on my bedside stand. The oil leaked from the container and spread over the table, saturating my cellular phone. The oil completely disintegrated the phone. The lining started to bubble, the plastic cracked, and now my flip phone is in two pieces. A small amount of the oil dripped onto the hardwood floor and ate away at the finish, leaving a discolored area on the floor. The leaked oil is noxious, causing irritation to our nasal passages and a skin irritation as well. I read the packages and found no warnings on the labels that would lead me to believe that this would be a problem.
justification: The incident caused nasal and skin irritation, which qualifies as injury, and significant property damage.

incident_description: We have now gone through 8 Apple 85W Magsafe chargers. Each one has heated up to burning temperatures and the pins that attach to our Macbook burn and melt. The original charger that came without Macbook Pro plus 3 we bought out of our own expense were all replaced by Apple. These are now the replacements that have fried up.
justification: The chargers have repeatedly heated up to burning temperatures and caused melting, posing a clear risk of injury.

incident_description: We purchased a Lasko Heater from Lowes and almost instantly noticed problems.  The unit was tipped over a few times and never shut itself off even though the product says it does.  The next incident, I started smelling burning in my home and found the front vent of the heater was burnt.  This smell has continued to this day.  Next, my dog walked by the heater and his fur grazed the front of it.  He instantly jumped away and licked his skin.  I thought the heat was just too hot for him, I did not realize he could have been hurt because the heater says it is safe.  However, last nite, I walked by the heater and my leg grazed the front of it, I was instantly burnt leaving a large red welt from my knee to almost the top of my ankle.  The heater had only been on for a 15 minute period.  I had to ice and aloe my leg and have a large mark.  This heater poses a fire risk, and a burn risk to people and animals.  This model is not on their recall list.  Model 5115

incident_description:
The glass shower door in my middle school son's bathroom spontaneously shattered.  No one was in the room when it happened and the room had not been even occupied in at least an hour.  It sounded like a gunshot followed by raining glass.  There was over 6" of tempered glass chunks in the bathtub, the toilet, and next to the tub.  The door did not fall out of the track, as evidenced by the rollers and slides still being in place with bits of glass clinging to them.  

I was cut up (even wearing gloves) trying to clean up the glass pieces (about 30 or 40 pounds) from the tub, floor and in the toilet.

I can't imagine what the damage and injury would have been to my son had he been naked in the shower or sitting on the toilet next to the shower.  Even the tempered glass would have definitely cut him up.  If he would have been in the shower, his feet would have been sliced to ribbons if he had tried to move at all to walk out of the 6" of glass.

I called the manufacture of the door (Kohler) and they claimed spontaneous shattering almost never occures and that the door must have been hung wrong (it was professionally installed and the frame is still completely level), missing its rubber bumpers (they are still in place) or that it had been struck with an object (never).  However, I found numberous bloody pictures and reports on the internet of this exact model shattering, along with a recall one month ago of another of their shower doors.  The customer support person even said that the doors can get cracks if you "bump" them while in the shower.  How can a product be sold like a shower door that can't even be bumped with your elbow while shampooing your hair!  It is such a forseeable and reasonable occurance in a shower.  She worked very hard to try to make it seem that we had caused the breakage.
justification: The incident resulted in injury during cleanup, and the potential for severe injury was high if someone had been present during the shattering.

incident_description: Hampton Bay Nassau 52in indoor/outdoor ceiling fan blade arms broke off and blades went flying in the air. I have 4 of these fans, all the blades on one them have all broken off and the others have crakes in them.
justification: The incident involved fan blades breaking off, which poses a hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Bionaire space heater from Walmart in October of 2012.  The model number is  BHH7522MX-BWM, Quartz heater.  The first one had sparks coming out of the on-off switch and I exchanged it.  I'm now having the same problem with the seconed unit.  This poses a significant fire hazard and I will be contacting the company.  If you have this unit, cease use and return it to the store.  A recall of this heater should be issued.
justification: Sparks from the heater indicate a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I filled my Shark Steam Mop with tap water and plugged it in to warm up so I could steam clean my floors.  I noticed that the unit wasn't making the usual periodic gurgle or steam sound as it usually did as it heated up.  It was plugged in for several minutes by this time and the power light on the unit was illuminated blue to indicate there was power to the unit.  I pumped the handle to try to produce steam and nothing happened.  I pumped the handle several more times and there was no steam produced by the unit. At this point, I had gently felt the cleaning head attachment with my fingers and it was cool and dry.  I do not think that any steam was making its way to the cleaning pad. 

I sat on the couch and picked the unit up, placing the unit parallel to the floor across my lap with the cleaning head hanging a few inches to the right of my legs to take a look at it.   I leaned forward a bit while I was looking at the unit and in my hands and on my legs I felt that the unit was warm to the touch as I believe it usually was prior to the incident.  While I was examining the unit in my lap, there was an unexpected, sudden very loud popping/exploding sound and steam burst out powerfully from all the seams of the body of the unit in a hot and quick release.  I am not sure what happened internally, but to me it seemed like a large amount of pressure built inside the unit and it caused a mass steam exit from the body of the unit's seams rather than down the unit shaft and out through the cleaning head attachment.  The hot steam exiting through the seams of the unit body caused mild steam burns to my face and by hands.  Luckily, my legs were covered with clothing.  I remember dropping the unit to the floor while screaming and running to unplug it.  There were no external signs that anything was malfunctioning inside the unit.  I never plugged the unit in again after this incident.  

Before and after the incident, the unit was undamaged and never had been dropped.  Since some time has passed since I reported the incident to the manufacturer, I don't remember the use details as much as I did at that time, but  the unit was used lightly in normal residential household use to clean floors in a small 950 sq. foot house (very lightly used) no more than 5 times before this happened.  The unit was never dropped or mishandled.  I believe that I always used tap water and didn't used distilled water inside the water canister.  I was the only one to ever use the product and I received it new as a gift in its original manufacturer packaging.  The attachments were in pristine condition as well.  Water was emptied from the unit following each use.  The unit was stored hanging in a cool, dry place always.

I treated the burns, which equated to mild sunburn on my face and quickly touching a hot stove top on my hands at home using ice packs for several hours following the incident.  My face was sensitive and sore for a week or two after the incident.  Fortunately, no scarring occurred from the burns.  

I remember that the incident happened in 2010 or 2011, but I don't have the exact date.  I reported it to the manufacturer over the phone.  The representative took a report of the incident including description of injury sustained, coordinated the return of the malfunctioned product via UPS, replaced the product with a same, equal product, and gave me 2 free Shark products and additional Shark steam mop replacement head cloths of my choice.  If I recall correctly, the free products were in exchange for not pursuing a product liability suit for the burns, but I can't 100% recall if this was expressly stated to me by the representative. 

Because I returned the product before knowing this resource was available to me to report consumer incidents, I don't have the serial number, the incident date, or model number.  However, the manufacturer does have a detailed report from me and would hopefully willingly share my report with the US government.
justification: The incident resulted in mild steam burns to the face and hands, which aligns with severity level 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) due to the unique malfunction described and the lack of prior incidents with the lightly used unit.

incident_description: I just found out that the Aloha 1013 fan heater should be returned to Walmart. I am glad to hear this because today my unit sparked from where the line cord exits the back of the unit. After investigation I found that the two wires exiting thru the plastic cord clamp on the rear of the unit were melted thru to the wires and they shorted against each other. The reason for this is because the wires heat up and are compressed so tightly by the clamp that over time the wire insulation gets soft and melts which in turn exposes the wires. The more pulling and yanking on the cord will accelerate this break down. Fortunately the unit was not on flammable material and the sparks did not ignite. I will return the unit to Walmart so that they can destroy it appropriately.
justification: The incident involved sparks and melted wires but no injury or fire occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the described design flaw causing repeated incidents.

incident_description:
(08/31/2012) The consumer stated that she put a load of clothes in the washer. The consumer stated that it took a such long time to complete cycle that she went to see what was wrong. She  found that the wash cycle was stuck on fill. This cause the washer to over flow onto the floor. 
The consumer stated that the washer is on the first floor. Her carpet was soaked and had to be replaced. The water had seeped through the sub flooring into the basement causing water damage to the  ceiling.

The consumer stated that she turned the machine off. 

The consumer stated that she called ServPro to clean up the water. 

(09/01/2012) The consumer stated that she called GE and they told her that they would send out a technician. The technician came out on the next day. He pulled the washer out to check. He advised the consumer that it was caused by a defective pressure switch hose and chamber inside of the washer which he replaced. 

The consumer  stated that the technician ran the washer for a short time to see if it was working properly. She also stated that she have not used the washer since the incident. 

UPDATE:
we had   electric cords as well as a power strip on the floor. If  the water depth had reach much  higher  it could  have  posed  a  serious  risk of injury
justification: The incident caused property damage (soaked carpet and water damage) but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) given the described scenario and potential for similar incidents.

incident_description: DeLonghi ("micathermic") SafeHeat electric room heater, model HHP1500, used in kitchen. Had not been used since last winter.  Soon after turning on, sparks started to shoot out from random locations on the heater's flat panel; several landed on floor, which was fortunately ceramic tile.  Same occurrence on next 3 uses of the heater, then stopped using due to concerns regarding fire hazard.
justification: Sparks shooting out from the heater pose a fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
The product of concern is a Kenmore washer / gas dryer combination machine.  While using the clothes dryer function of the unit, the unit caught fire internally in two areas located near the gas blower that was unaccessible to be cleaned for excess lint build-up by the consumer.  The first area was the area housing the gas discharge and the second area is a few inches below that. Additionally, although this unit was already present in the home when I purchased this house, I had located an online version of the unit's user manual and I didn't see anything listed about consumers having to take the unit apart to clean inside the machine to prevent fire.  

The fire remained localized to inside the unit and appears to have extinguished itself once the lint that was fueling the fire was mainly burned away, but the unit and items within the unit smelled like burnt popcorn for almost a year thereafter.  I ceased using the unit after it went on fire because I noticed the intense burning smell when I unloaded the dry clothes after the drying cycle was over.  I couldn't confirm a fire at that point, but I suspected one occurred although I didn't see any obvious signs on the outside of the unit and didn't see any smoke rising from the unit.  Within a week or two of the incident, I called to have the unit serviced by a Sears Home Repair specialist.  When the technician arrived, he disassembled the unit by taking off a diagonal metal piece that is located between the washer loading door and the dryer door.  Inside he showed me a large amount of burnt lint and told me that the unit went on fire due to lint accumulation inside the sealed area near the gas discharge.  I told him that I regularly cleaned the unit and he sold me a long brush designed to clean under the lint trap chamber as a precaution.

Prior to the fire, I maintained the unit's lint trap by cleaning it out after the completion of every dryer load and periodically sticking a vacuum attachment in the area underneath the lint trap.

On 9/17/10 or 9/18/10, I again had the unit serviced by Sears for an unrelated problem with the dryer function.  When the technician serviced the unit, it required him to open areas that are inaccessible to the consumer again and he appeared startled when he called me over to show me a mass accumulation of lint in the same area of the unit that caught fire back in 2008.  He took a small orange shop vacuum of his and vacuumed the inside of the sealed area near the gas discharge.  There was a lot of lint build up in the area.  I don't know if the shop vacuum previously had anything inside it prior to the cleaning of my unit, but the vacuum filled to capacity during the cleaning and I offered to empty it into a plastic supermarket bag and it filled the entire bag with lint.  Prior to this discovery, I had not opened the unit to clean this area.  I watched the technician put the unit back together and watched how he accessed that internal area with the lint build-up  and since this time, about every six months I use a screw driver to open the unit carefully and remove the lint build-up that continues to occur in this inaccessible area.  

I want to report this condition since the unit has previously been on fire from the lint build-up, I feel that it is a little unsafe to be working inside the unit around a gas line, but the consequences of not cleaning it could be much greater, I didn't see instructions to the consumer that this type of maintenance is required per the user manual.  I think that Sears products are becoming very unsafe and that this issue warrants a closer look for a possible recall.
justification: The incident involved a fire inside the dryer unit but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire extinguished itself without spreading.

incident_description:
In April of 2006, I purchased a rug from Pottery Barn online. The Palampore 10x14 rug for $1099.  Soon thereafter I noticed a burning electrical smell. I realize that wool rugs have a distinct odor once they are wet.  This particular smell is not the same.  We have our rugs professionally cleaned at least 2 to 3 times a year. It took my husband about a year to notice the smell. We would have the rug cleaned and it would smell fine for a while and suddenly the odor would return.  I told my husband I was ready to get rid of the rug. His argument was the amount of money we have spent and how wasteful it would be to dispose of the rug.  I argued how the smell was unbearable and an embarrassment when we have guests.  

I decided to put the rug on Craig's list, but was not sure how much I should sell it for. So I googled "how much should I sell my Pottery Barn 10x14 rug for."  What I found has made me furious, to put it mildly.  

I read 2 blogs with several consumer's complaints about an electrical, rubber, burning smell coming from their carpet.  Through investigation, the manufacturer in India used a latex glue that emits an electrical smell. And there is a concern that this odor (gas) is releasing carcinogens.  After reading this I have no doubt that my 10x14 Palampore rug came from the same manufacturer in India. My $1099 rug now sits wrapped and sealed in my garage. 

Although I have not researched the effects of this particular latex glue, I do have medical records which substantiate the claim of migraines and other illnesses ( soon after the purchase of the rug) that could be a result from inhaling the gas fumes.  I also have a concern for my kids who would crawl and play on this rug as I have a daughter whom three years ago was diagnosed with Asthma.

I have continued to purchase items from Pottery Barn not only because of the quality, but because of the customer service.  I don't understand why Pottery Barn did not issue a letter to those who purchased the rugs. I would have immediately removed it from my home. 

Please send me any information about lab results and or other consumer complaints against Pottery Barn rugs made in India. 

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes potential health issues (migraines, asthma) linked to the rug's fumes, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as multiple consumers reported similar issues.

After ironing or in between clothes, the iron is placed in the upright position, a puddle of water forms beneath the iron which is a shock hazard.
