incident_description: I have a Dimplex Remote Receiver APT-1315 that quit working.  I looked at where the fireplace cord plugged into the receiver and it had melted.  When searching for a replacement, I found that there was already a recall on it so I have ordered it.  Just wanted to let you know that there was indeed an issue with this product.

incident_description:
On December 22, 2012, my Kenmore dehumidifier, model # 251.5070 1010, overheated and started smoking, emitting noxious fumes. Fortunately, I was downstairs at the time, so I unplugged it and put it outside, and was able to avoid a catastrophic fire. When I called the hotline, however, I was told that my unit was not recalled, and that I would have to bring it in for repair. I mistakenly assumed that it would be repaired for free, since it was an expensive unit, and was unsafe. When we brought it in to the Sears store, we were told that it was out of warranty (it was purchased in May 2010), and we would have to pay for the repair. We brought the unit home, rather than having it repaired, since I would rather spend the money on a newer, safer unit. I am greatly disappointed that Sears management would not make this right.

I used one last January when i noticed that the prong on the power cord from the heater had gotten hot and melted and burned the plastic around the prong on the plug. incident_description:
I purchased a Craftsman drill bit set from Sears in Hicksville 6 years ago.  I am not expert, but I believe the drill bits are made of metal and the set contains all different sizes from very thin to very thick bits.  The drill bits have been lightly used only a handful of times by me in a residential setting over the duration of ownership.  

On 11/30/12 I used one of the thinnest drill bits in a Craftsman rechargable power drill that was full charged and fully functional, but as I was using the power drill correctly in a safe manner and lightly drilling a hole into a soft plastic gutter on a mark designed per the manufacturer instructions to be drilled, the Craftsman drill bit snapped approximately in half while the drill was in use.  Since there was no safety measure in place to disengage the drill power upon snapping of the drill bit, the drill slipped out of control at the moment of the drill bit breakage into two pieces with the bottom jaggedly broken half still inside the drill spinning.  The moving broken spinning bottom half of the drill bit ended up drilling a hole the size of the drill bit deeply into my left hand pointer finger.  It all happended in the matter of one or two seconds.  I just remember screaming at the top of my lungs outside and running inside to the bathroom sink to begin pouring rubbing alcohol, peroxide and water over the mutilated finger.  In the frenzy, I remember seeing a circular plug of jagged, torn, warped sink fall into the sink from the area that the drill tore into.  I had to immediately go to the emergency room for treatment due to this faulty product.  

I don't think that metal drill bits should be made so cheaply that they snap because it can hurt a consumer as it did to me.  My finger is healing from the outside-in, but it is so sore to the touch and is scarred.  This is upsetting because I am a young woman who cares about her appearance and also has a whole host of household duties that have been impaired to be performed as a result of the injury.  

Additionally, there is no warning label on the drill bit case or the drill itself, which are both Craftsman products announcing that the drill bit could snap.  This product is dangerous!  I cannot find any type of identifier on the black plastic drill bit case for a serial number.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring emergency room treatment, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
LG Model WT5001CW   SN#111KW******* PURCHASED 03/2012

This is actually my second washer.  The first machine (purchased 01/2011) malfunctioned, became unbalanced and the spinning drum broke completely lose from the unit.  It broke free of the housing and crashed into the dryer and wall.  LG replaced the unit in March 2012 with the same model.  The newer machine, same model is showing repetitive behavior of the original machine.  The brackets supporting the drum are inadequate.  The machine does not turn itself off if unbalanced.  Violent shaking and banging occur whether the load if off balance or not.  Size of load is also not relevant.  
I see a recall exists for this current model and LG is sending to my home a repair technician to install some sort of new balancing awareness gadget and warning sticker.  (really? a sticker?) 
It is my opinion that a new sensor is not the source of the problem.  The support brackets are inadequate for holding the weight of the drum.  Bad mechanical design is also an issue.  I would hope LG would refund consumers of their purchase amount ($899.00+) to allow the consumer to purchase a better washer.  
I know that it is just a matter of time before this washer breaks again.  The first time it happened no one got hurt and damage to my home was minimal.  I hope I'm as fortunate the second time.
justification: The incident involves violent shaking and banging of the washer, but no injury or death has occurred.

The heater that is used the most is very hot to the touch and shuts itself off after in use for a while.  I believe that its "Thermal Cut-Off Safety Device" cuts the heater off due to overheating. (The other heater is just a backup and is hardly ever used.)

I contacted Optimus which said if I want to ship it back to them in California it will fix it. The problem with that is that the shipping cost is almost as much as the purchase price.

However, I am more concerned with overheating and the safety of this product.

incident_description:
Coated our redwood deck, about 40 years old, with Cabot Silicon Waterproofing product, after thoroughly scrubbing the deck. The day after the application when the surface felt and looked dry, my wife slipped and fell as she attempted to enter the deck from an interior door.  As a result of the fall she suffered a bone contusion on her left knee.  In helping her up, I noted myself just how slippery the surface was and could see how it would be easy to slip.  I carefully checked to see that the surface was dry and it was.  In reading the very fine print on the container label I noted the following:
Under Finishing it says " Use caution when standing or walking on surfaces when still wet after application of Cabot Waterproofing as the surface may be very slippery".  As noted above the surface was dry to the touch when the fall occurred.  Under Drying Time the same label says " Recently applied Waterproofing may remain slick, even when dry, until the surface has been exposed to general weathering ( rain and sun for several days)"
Now I have several comments about these warnings, if that was what they were meant to be?
First the print of all these warning, very small print fonts,  are not in any way highlighted to draw ones attention.  Second the terminology of the second statement that: the Waterproofing may remain slick, is rather vague compared to the first statement regarding still wet coating surfaces, i.e. very slippery.
Also the statement that general weathering has to take place before the surface is safe is vague.  I can tell you from my experience that the surface remained slippery weeks after the application even with rain and sun exposure.
I documented my experiences, with photos, in correspondence to Valspar, the owner of Cabot, but have received no satisfaction.  They believe their label is adequate to protect consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in a bone contusion, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) because the surface remained slippery even when dry, and the warning was not prominently displayed.

incident_description:
I am writing about LG front load washers and dryers which could involve all front loads.

I went to my daughters house to sit her 2.5 year old twins.  While playing they went into the laundry room where the new washer and dryer are installed.  The boy opened the door and the girl crawled in.  The in NOTHING to prevent the door from being closed and the start button hit.

Thank goodness I was there to prevent the death of my granddaughter.

Here the cabinet of dryer was full of lint which somehow ignited.  We clean out lint filter after every use and clean vents frequently.  Have made many calls to Samsung and have received no help at all.  Lucky we were home and awake at time, could have been a devastating event for our family and home.  DO NOT PURCHASE THIS PRODUCT.  Dryer is only a few years old.  Samsung only will say it's out of warranty.  This is a SAFETY issue!!  They did give me a number to call to have someone come "assess the liability"of fire. incident_description:

incident_description: On Tuesday, December 11th, 2012 I was sitting in my kitchen reading the mail when I heard a loud explosion .  I was not sure what it was, I ran upstairs and looked in every room, but when I got to the bathroom I saw glass everywhere.  The tub was filled with glass and it was all over the bathroom.  I could not believe what happened and just felt lucky that my handicapped son or myself were not in the bathroom.  When my husband came home and I told him what happened, he could not believe either, since we never heard of this before.  Anyway, my husband went to Lowes the same night to replace the door and he was informed by one of the salesmen that he had occasionally heard of exploding shower doors and told us to call the manufacturer, Kohler, and tell the what happened.  When my husband called Kohler he was told that it is uncommon but it and happen, shower doors exploding.  A Kohler representative told us that they would send a replacement door within 4 - 6 weeks.

incident_description:
Dear Sirs:                                                                                                                       october, 31,

We purchased a GE clothes dryer about 12 years ago. I have seen safety messages on TV that recommend cleaning the dryer vent pipe to prevent a possible fire due to accumulated lint. I have cleaned the vent pipe from the back several times. Today I dried some clothes and removed the screen that is designed to catch some of the lint that occurs during the tumbling and drying process. When i removed the screen to clean it I discovered that there was a large buildup of lint below and to the left of the screen. I reached down into the cavity as far as I could reach and was able to remove some lint but much remained. I utilized a strong piece of wire and was able to remove even more. I think I removed nearly a pound as was pleased that we did not have a fire form the accumulated lint.
I believe that there should be an easy access panel that the average homeowner should be able to open to check for accumulated lint as well as being able to remove that lint. I know that there would be a cost involved in making an access panel but i truely believe that it could prevent dryer fires.
I do not know the statistics regards dryer, and resulting house fires, that occur around the country. I have seen fires blamed on such type fires in articles in the newspaper. I would hope that those type fires could be prevented and would save not
only homes but also save lives as well. I hope that your office would give this suggestion serious consideration as I believe that you can convince the dryer manufacturers to incorporate an access panel in their products.
[redacted]

There were obvious char marks on the wiring at the junction of these wires.

While there was no fire with the failure of the unit, charring of the plastic did occur. I am not in a position to determine if greater damage would have arisen if the wiring had not completely charred.

incident_description: I decided on Sunday 18 November to place Glade plug-ins in my bedroom and closet.  On Monday 19 November I broke out in a rash that comprised small red dots, as well as large boils/pimples that looked to be infected.  My first thought was that I had been bitten by fleas or bed bugs.  I inspected the house, in particular our bed and could find no evidence of fleas or bed bugs, but washed and disinfected all of the bedding and towels etc in the house, as well as the dog's blankets and toys.  On Tuesday, the boils/pimples had spread.  Again I searched for bugs, but could find none and my husband did not have the problem.  By Thursday I knew that I would ahve to see a doctor as I had no idea where the boils/pimples were coming from and they were multiplying.  In addition, the rash had tunred from red dots to red streaks that looked like an infection of my blood vessels.  All boils/pimples also had red circles around them indicative of an infected cyst.  After racking my brains to think what I could have done differently in the past week to make this reaction/disease occur, the only thing I could think of was the Glade Plug-In.  I hadn't changed soaps, laundry detergent etc and was starting to think I might have  aparasitic infection.  Thinking it a long shot, I removed the Glade Plug-Ins and by the next day, Saturday 24 November the rasj had disappeared and the boils/pimples had gotten considerable smaller and looked like they were starting to heal.  As of today, Monday 26 November, I am completely back to normal, with just a few faint red spots where the boils/pimples had been, but they are healing nicely.  This seemed to suggest that it was the Glade Plug-In that caused this reaction.  As background, I have never been allergic to anything before, including seasonal allergies.  I have certainly never had a reaction like this to anything, and while I am glad it was not a horrible disease, I felt that someone should know that this type of reaction is possible when using these devices.  Thank you.
justification: The incident describes a severe allergic reaction (injury) caused by Glade plug-ins, requiring medical attention but no death occurred.

The rubber outer insulation is breaking away from the harder rubber going into the handle. This exposes the the white and black wires inside as well as some strings that we are guessing they use to prevent the wires from being bent inside the cord.

We took the vacuum back to the dealer and he reluctantly said we could leave it with him for a few days and he would attempt to repair. He really didn't seem like he wanted to repair the vacuum.
We contacted Oreck customer care and they only referred us to a different dealer in Nashua, NH which is a 30 minute drive from here.

What are you supposed to do? Go and buy another vacuum while they repair a basically brand new vacuum that could cause electrocution? We don't even know how long the power cord has been like this as the place where it is falling apart is under the handle and hard to notice. 

We believe other people must have seen similar problems with their Oreck XL power cords (near the handle).
justification: The incident involves a frayed power cord exposing electrical wires, posing a potential electrocution hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Heat n Glo Vienna II green cast iron gas LP stove. I bought it in December 2001 from the dealer Frederick Block in Winchester VA. It was installed in January 2002 by an HVAC/plumbing/electrical contractor into a new home that we built. We moved into the house in March 2002 and since winter was over, the stove was not used for the first time until the following winter in 2003. It is located in our family room. This stove has had normal use - primarily for pleasure - it was never the main heating source for the room it is in. Since 2003 it has been used maybe a total of 20 hours a week during the winter months of November - February, operating via a remote control/thermostat setting that turned it on/off automatically based on the temp setting. In the past week I was having trouble with it not lightning properly when I used the remote to turn it on, and pilot light went out for no reason, and I noticed that it also looked like the logs had moved inside the stove. I called a technician who looked at the stove on Friday, Nov. 23rd. He found the following:

* The metal plate the logs rest on is rusted very badly - tech said due to the condensation of the water in the LP gas before it burned off. I would have thought Heat n Glo would have taken that into account in the stove design and would have used a metal that would not corrode from the water in the gas. One of the pieces that was designed to hold a log had completely rusted through and a chunk had broken off, which is why the logs had moved. 

* The pilot light kept going out when the tech tried to light it. Upon investigation, he found that the burner pan had many cracks in it and the gas was seeping through the cracks with enough force to blow out the pilot - instead of coming through the holes in the pan as it should have. Tech said WE COULD HAVE HAD A CATASTROPHIC EXPLOSION! He said the stove was totally unsafe to use, was at high risk for an explosion, and he turned off the gas to it. Where did the cracks come from? We didn't do anything to cause it. It had to be defective from the manufacturer.

Tomorrow I will be calling Heat n Glo and also the dealer who sold it  (they were both closed due to Thanksgiving till 11/26) to see if there is any warranty or recall on this stove. I wonder if there aren't other Vienna I and II stoves out there where this is also occurring, which is why I am filing this report with you. I am very sad about this because I loved that stove, but I believe it is a disaster waiting to happen to someone - could have already happened for all I know. And even if under warranty and the parts or stove itself can be replaced, I don't want another stove with the same faulty design that might blow us up. So I may just be out my $2000 I paid for this stove, unless there is a newer stove with a better design that Heat n Glo is willing to give me to replace this one. 

I also have 2 of the Heat n Glo 6000TRI gas log units in fireplaces - 1 in living room and 1 in master bedroom - that I am having checked out to see if they might have burner pad/leaking gas defects. They were also installed new when house was built in 2002 but have rarely been used. FYI all the Heat n Glo units are vented to the outside and are plumbed directly into the 1000 gallon underground propane gas tank in our yard that also provides gas to the hot water heater, house furnaces, and backp generator. 

I have seen that there are recalls on some Heat n Glo units - but I don't know if there are any recalls on the ones I have. Are there recalls on the 6000TRI fireplace logs or Vienna II stove? 

Does a manufacturer have to stand behind a defective product, such as this stove that could have blown up and killed us, or am I just out the money and left with a green cast iron piece of junk that I'm afraid to use, and Heat n Glo walks away without any responsibility to make it good? I have seen some dealers online that are still selling Vienna I and II, although the stoves are no longer listed under those names as available products on the Heat n Glo web site. Are they perhaps still being sold, but under a new name?
justification: The stove had significant defects that could have led to a catastrophic explosion, but no actual incident or injury occurred.

Cummins should honor their remedy posted in their recall so I can purchased a unit that is not defective and does not cause a risk to my personal property or life of my family.  How many other consumers are out there that may have this unit with an "R" on it and not realize that it was manufactured with a defect, repaired and put back on the market as a new unit with no disclosure?  I was never contacted by anyone about this unit being recalled.

incident_description:
I purchased LG Waveforce Top Loading Washer WT5001cw and Gas Dryer Set on 7/9/11 from Best Buy. I had a little issue of leaking that out of nowhere was resolved. On 10/31/2102, I went to the washer to get my whites out. I couldn't open the washer because it was locked. I pressed the power button & it would not turn on. I pulled out the manual to troubleshoot the issue. There was nothing in the manual to address this issue. I then called LG. I talked to a rep out of a call center in the country of Panama. The person told me to unplug unit for 30 seconds to reset. I did this. That did not work. The person then told me to check the circuit breaker to see if the outlet tripped. I checked the circuit breaker & everything checked out normal. That did not fix issue. They told me to plug it into a different outlet. I did this. That did not fix issue. I told rep that I smelled a burning smell coming from unit. The rep told me to unplug unit. I immediately unplugged unit. Rep stated that since the unit was a bit over warranty, I would have to send my original receipt to them to be approved for an extended warranty.

I faxed LG the documents they requested. As we waited days to see if this warranty was going to be approved, on Sunday, 11/4/12, my husband went down to basement to see if washer would turn on. He plugged it back in & smelt a burning smell & saw smoke coming from the back of unit. He took off a small white cover in the back to see what was happening. We found out that the main power source in the washer had caught on fire and this wasn't the first time since 10/31/12. We immediately called LG to report this & they seemed uninterested in helping us. This call center was in Asia.

We also took many pictures. This rep told us we needed to contact LG on Monday to find out what to do next. On Monday, we called & talked to a rep in the USA by the name of [REDACTED] **, a supposed supervisor for LG. She wasn't helpful whatsoever and she was extremely rude. She made us re-fax and email another copy of original sales receipt to call us a few hours later to tell us that we were not approved for the extended warranty. She said her superiors told her that because we took off the back panel, we voided the warranty or any option for an extended. We were like "Are you ** kidding us?" This was an emergency situation of an LG appliance on fire in our home and it caught on fire previously days before this.

Then this [REDACTED] rep told us to go to Best Buy to see if they could do anything for us, which we did that same night, which was tonight. The Best Buy manager pretty much laughed (not at us) as they were shocked LG told us to go back to them. Now, we are in a situation of being without a washer. We are trying to figure out what to do next. This appliance cannot be repaired. Even if it could, we don't want a fire hazard in our home or have to worry about it re-catching on fire in future.
justification: The incident involved a washer catching fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I have been experiencing repeated remote control failure with this stove.  So, far I have had 4 units.  The first was at the recall of the Gold Banded remotes & exchanged for the Red Banded units.  Since then, each Red Banded unit has lasted for less & less time. The last one was received November 9th 2012 and became inoperable within 2 days  Nov 11th, 2012. 

Dimplex Traditional Stove
Model DS55804 Mod C
Ser No 1604D6  472
Part No. 6900331000

Failing Component:
Power Remote Module Model No. 47-1010-R*
FCCID: ELY547-47-1010-R


The problem is always the same.  The plug in unit evidently overheats and melts internally around the power plug coming from the stove.  I surmise this as the stove plug needs to be pried out of the remote control box.  That, and the strong smell of burnt bakelite.  

The remote plug in boxes appear normal from the exterior, with only a slight melting around the smaller of the two holes.  At this point, they are totally inoperative as tested by plugging in a 40 watt lamp which fails to light up.

a breaker been tripped.  The stove continues to operate normally when plugged directly into
this circuit using only the manual controls.  

I have safety concerns about the these units and feel they need to be investigated.  Towards that end, I have retained the last two units, should you desire to inspect them.

(9/30/2012) The consumer stated that she was coming down her attic ladder, which is located inside her garage. Approximately at the 3' foot section of the ladder, the consumer stated that it gave out. The consumer was dangling mid-way. In order to get down safely the consumer swung one of her legs to a near by stool and got ahold of it. The consumer was able to balance herself on the stool and make her way down to the floor safely.  The consumer stated that she did not receive any injuries.

Consumer contacted the manufacturer by telephone and was informed that the ladder was mfr'ed by the old Werner company and parts were no longer available.  The Werner company rep, [REDACTED], advised her that Werner would send a $200 gift card for Lowe's or Home Depot towards the purchase of a replacement ladder.  Werner company followed this up with a letter (see attached).  When I asked how a contractor would be paid she stated that Werner company could instead send me a $100 gift card towards replacement and pay by reimbursement up to $100 towards the labor cost.  After more thought I again contacted [REDACTED] and asked about reimbursement for labor as well as the mentioned $200 gift card towards product replacement.  She then stated that they would send $200 towards replacement and reimburse up to $150 towards the cost of labor.  However, a new letter would be sent stating that Werner company faxed the letter, sent the gift cards and as of this writing, consumer is awaiting reimbursement for the cost of labor and some materials for removal/new installation of an attic ladder (see atttached documentation).
justification: The consumer experienced an incident with the ladder but did not sustain any injuries, and similar incidents are possible given the context.

incident_description:
I purchased a Hampton Bay (which appears to be HomeDepot's store brand) ventilation fan, Model #BPT18-34A-1

The included quick connect spicing connectors are a fire hazard. When I received the unit, one of these connectors was falling off the internal cable and couldn't be put back on. I tried the other one which when in use, heated up and partially melted before I shut the fan off. I tossed these garbage connectors and used tried and true quality wire nuts instead. This is typical poor quality Chinese manufacturing, with Home Depot putting profits over safety.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to faulty connectors, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the air compressor turned on auto and immediately he started to hear crackling sounds being emitted by the motor. The consumer stated that he looked at the motor and noticed that it also emitted sparks. He stated that he unplugged the air compressor and took a second look at the motor and noticed a (1ÃÂ tall) flame inside the motor. The consumer stated that he blew out the flame inside. 

The consumer stated that he did not notice any other visible damages to the air compressor. The consumer stated that he hasnÃÂt use the air compressor since the incident. 

No one was injured.

The consumer believed that this product should be investigated since it poses a fire hazard to the consumer. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they requested for him to contact them back at a later time due to a system update.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with visible flames, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
Me and my daughter was watching tv last night, in our family den. We have a little forced air space heater we purchased last winter. This is an item we use off and on. It's a PELONIS Model HF-0020T with I think serial number:3068797.

We had it on the highest setting and it was working fine. All of a sudden a loud fizzling noise came from the heater, with a big sparking flash inside. All of a suddne it caught fire inside where the cord wiring inside meets with the outside cord. It smelled like rubber burning so I unplugged the device and extinguished the flame. I looked underneath the item and there was a small hole from the arcing wire inside.

The item in my opinion just simply sparked and caught fire inside.

I called the manufacturer, whose phone is listed on the item. They are supposed to call me back with answers today, Nov. 14th.

I do have pictures.
justification: The heater sparked and caught fire, but no injuries were reported, and the fire was quickly extinguished.

incident_description: I purchased a step stool in 2010 for my son and my grandchildren.  On October 6, 2012, my 6 year old grandson as sitting on the stool and the stoll collapased , taking a one inch piece of his middle finger with the stool. He was immediately taken to the Emergency room, treated ad continues to be treated by a hand surgeon.  The stool is in my possession as I did not want any more accdents at my son's home.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring emergency and ongoing medical treatment, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it's a single reported incident with the stool.

incident_description: I was standing on stool doing some house work and my foot went through the middle of the stool and broke the stool.  I fell backwards and hit my back on the door frame.  I was standing in a small hallway.  I had a bruise on my lower back for about a week.  My ankle bone was sore because it went thru the stool.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruise and soreness, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: A Champion portable generator - model number 41532, serial number 11Oct2000605, caught on fire while in use outside our home on the night of November 7th 2012.  While some serial numbers of this particular generator are under recall due to fires, this particular serial number is not and is supposed to be acceptable for use.
justification: The generator caught fire, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Bionaire BCH9221 Heater smoked and when opened up found white wire going to hear element melted and frayed.  Also found melting wire melted plastic case of heater.
justification: The heater smoked and had melted wires, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: 3 day old Carbon Monoxide detector failed to sound alarm with high CO levels. (Separate secondary alarm sounded. Fire department notified).  Fire department found high CO levels, verified suspect CO detector was inoperative.  Unit self-tests okay, but does not actuate during actual event.    Unit Details: Kidde Single Station Carbon Monoxide alarm (Issue No 4477)  Model KN-COB-B-LPM, Assemblt number 9CO5-LP. Date of Manufacture 2012, June, 25.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but the CO detector failed to sound an alarm, which could have led to serious injury or death.

incident_description: I was using an electric circular saw when it suddenly sucked in my hair.  The entangled hair caused the saw to jerk upward slamming me in the head.  I was unable to free the large chunk of hair the saw sucked up and had to cut the hair to get free of the saw.
justification: The incident resulted in physical harm (head injury) due to the saw jerking upward, but no death occurred.

incident_description: We purchased a Bionaire heater.  We used it sparingly to heat our bedroom.  We noticed a steamy burning smell before we fell asleep.  Then noticed that the unit was burning and had sparks emitting.  Luckily it was not close to other objects and we were able to turn it off in time.  I've read other reviews and people have had fires from this device.  It costs $70 and only lasts thru several uses.   They should not be allowed to sell this.
justification: The heater emitted sparks and a burning smell, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Honeywell oil-filled digital radiator heater
Model HZ-709
Produced by KAZ Inc. - sold by Honeywell at Wal-Mart

I own several Honeywell oil filled digital radiator heaters. One of them nearly burned my house down yesterday and I thought you should know what happened.
I had run the heater overnight and in the morning turned the unit off my pushing the on/off switch as usual. The unit clicked off, all the lights went off as usual and the unit appeared to be off. I left home for several hours, came home and went into the bedroom which was very, very hot and had a strange smell. I went to the heater which still had all of its lights off, still appeared off, and yet the unit was too hot to even touch. Obviously the on/off switch had shorted out and so too had obviously the thermostat. The unit was stuck on and was heating all day. This was a very dangerous situation and I an afraid to think what might have happened had I not come home early.
justification: The heater malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The is a sticker on the inside of the Goodman furnace that i bought in 2009, We (family) recently started to hear a sounds from our furnace. I decided to look into and noticed the sticker was coming off and going into the fan. It also looked as though it was getting a bit hot as the sticker was warped.
justification: The sticker coming off and going into the fan poses a potential hazard, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Coleman Furnace Model # DGAAO77BDTA
Cracked heat exchanger
Carbon monoxide hazard
Expensive repair, although part warrantied, due to labor
8 years old
Trailer
justification: Cracked heat exchanger poses a carbon monoxide hazard, which could lead to injury or death, but no incident or injury is reported yet.

incident_description:
On Saturday 9/15/2012, I was washing my kitchen floors with Fabuloso Citrus Cleaner. As we have no children, the bottle was sitting on the counter incase I needed to use an additional amount. My husband remarked as to why I had left a bottle of juice sitting on the counter and not put it in the refrigerator. When I pointed out it was cleaner, he stated how would anyone know? I pulled a bottle of a name brand juice product from the cupboard and place it side by side with the cleaner. The shape and size of the bottles were almost identical. Additionally, the cleaner is a pretty red color, has a very fruity fragrance and the label displays large slices of fruit. 
Reciently we have red several atricles about children mistaking laundry products and dishwasher soap for candy. I believe Colgate-Palmolive might want to rethink the packaging and appearance of the Fabuloso before some child makes the same mistake and assume it is a juice drink as my husband did.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard due to product packaging but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was on the step ladder when a support arm rivet failed, causing the ladder to twist and collapse.  
Of course I fell and the 2X4 lumber I was putting up fell on me.

The method of using a rivet to hold a support arm is unsafe.
Rivets don't have the inherent physical strength to handle the support arm load.
This has happened before(see the lawsuit) and will happen again.

The ladder was a Husky manufactured by Tricam Industries, Inc.


Plaintiffs [REDACTED] filed a complaint in Indiana state court alleging that [REDACTED] was injured while using
a ten-foot Husky ladder manufactured by defendant Tricam Industries, Inc. (ÃÂTricamÃÂ)
and sold by defendant Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. (ÃÂHome DepotÃÂ). (DE # 1 ÃÂ¶ÃÂ¶ 4-7.)
ÃÂ..[REDACTED] allege that [REDACTED] was properly using a ten-foot
Husky ladder on October 31, 2008, while constructing the roof of a porch on a house.
(DE # 1 ÃÂ¶ 4.) They allege that while he was on the ladder, the rivets holding the support
arm on one side of the ladder failed causing the ladder to collapse. (Id.)
justification: The incident resulted in injury due to the ladder collapse and falling lumber, and the description mentions a prior lawsuit indicating recurring issues.

incident_description:
While using a EuroPro Shark steam Pocket Mop, the steam channel melted and became clogged.  Upon inspecting the unit as to while it was not functioning and releasing steam, the mop head exploded away from the unit, and steam was release in an uncontrolled fashion.  Luckily, no one was hurt, but the steam jet was about 1-2 feet in the air as reflected off of a tile floor.  Any hands in the way would have been scalded and burned.  Small pieces of the melted plastic steam channel had broken off, and were found on the floor after the steam had finished releasing.  If the mop had been pointing up as opposed to at the floor when the explosion occurred, these may have become projectiles.

This mop had been replaced under warranty for a similar clog which resulted in the non-function of the unit.  The first mop had internal tubes rupture, without outward explosion.  However, that unit was broken at that point.  The replacement unit failed outwardly, which is considerably more dangerous.  Both units had been filled with tap water with each use.  I would believe that calcification due to tap water minerals would have clogged the first unit, but a melted steam channel in the second would not be caused by minerals in water.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and uncontrolled steam release, posing a risk of scalding and burns, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: During a routine washing of clothes in a GE front loading washing machine, we smelled a burning like an electrical type fire, we checked around the house, saw smoke coming from the laundry room.  Smoke was pouring out of the washing machine.  We hit the stop button, pulled the power plug, started clearing the smoke.  Did not see any obvious flames visible, but maybe inside the machine someplace.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential electrical fire but no injuries or flames were observed, and the situation was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a sheet of insulation made by K-Flex USA. It was a 36"x4'x1/2" sheet of their Insul-Sheet insulation and it is supposed to be safe for indoor use in general and it's supposed to be safe for schools as well. The product is [REDACTED] constantly emitting a burnt rubber smell. The longer the product is exposed to the air, the more [REDACTED] it's off-gassing. I only had it installed in a room for 36 hours before I had to remove it since it was causing nausea and airing out the room wasn't getting rid of the odor. The room was aired out for another 12 hours after the insulation was removed, but the odor won't go away. This was a very clean, odor-free room before. Now I have no idea how to get rid of the odor or how dangerous it is to continue breathing the air in this room. 

[REDACTED].
justification: The insulation caused nausea, indicating an injury, and the persistent odor suggests a possible recurrence if the product is used again.

incident_description: I was trying to figure out why my medium room ceramic heater from Sunbeam was just blowing out cold air.  I took the front panel off and saw that the middle (black) wire that connects to the heating element had burn marks on it.  I lightly pulled it and the wire broke off of the terminal.  Upon closer inspection the other wires that come into contact with the black heating element wire were also scortched.  I believe this could have caught fire if it had been left on for a long period of time.  The product was made in China, Manufacturer is Sunbeam Products, Inc. doing business as Jarden Sonsumer Solutions.  The model number is SCH2100.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to burnt wires, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Dear sir,
I have had a problem with my makita sander, type electrical, model bo5000. The pad came apart while using sander without causing injury but some surprise. I purchased it in france, Paris in 1993 approximately. Before I have it repaired for ballbearing problem. I would appreciate to obtain a new pad to be installed at the closest factory service center. In France the plate for serial number is removed, I canÃÂt give the information.
justification: The pad came apart during use but no injury occurred, only surprise.

incident_description: Duraflame Ceramic Desktop Heater with Thermostat DFH-DH-14-T almost caused a fire in my home last night, the power cord has melted, there were sparks flying. I'm concerned about the safety of this product. No one should have to go through what I witnessed last night.  The cord melted where it connects to the unit, there is no reason for wear at this location as the device was sitting stationary on the dresser top.
justification: The incident involved a melted power cord and sparks, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
2000 we built a home.  We installed a heat recovery system HRV by BRYANT. The system worked for about 3 years, we notice it was running all the time and it did not work right with the wall control. 

(1) 2004 We called a heating guy out, was the same one that installed the system, the board in the HRV was bad and had a burnt spot on it. He check out all controls and replaced board, it worked fine for two years. 

(2) 2006 We notice again it was not working, this time we called the wholesaler and Venmar in Canada about the problem along with pictures; All Air put that board in. He checked all controls everything good. 

(3) 2008 We had the same problem and again we put this board in. We pulled out all controls to check is there was a short; everything was clean. 

(4) 2009 Again the unit was not operating by the control. We again talked to the distributors also Venmar they sent me a recall part to have installed on the motor by the heating guy and a new board. T and T Heating did the work. I shipped the board to Venmar for inspection, did not hear from them for a year, we called them and they had no information for me. Our home is very tight and needs the HRV to bring in fresh air, again the part went. 

(5) The system worked for just over a year and now has quit working. We are stump on this Bryant HRV, have called T and T Heating to come out, they are avoiding usÃÂsmall town only a few heating guys here, have no faith in them. I had electrical out to check my box...everything clean, I am suspecting something is causing the board to blow, could it be motor, I think we replaced that a wild back. The place where the board was seem very warm. I am calling Venmar in morning, my concern is the air quality and the tightness in home also possibly fire. If you can give me any info I would appreciate it.
justification: The incident involves repeated failures of a heat recovery system without any reported injuries or deaths, but with potential air quality and fire concerns.

incident_description: 2003 Werner Co. Made in China Attic Ladder, part# 62460-02, model# S2210 MK 2.   Call [REDACTED] for service.   Ladder is rated 300lb capacity but lower right swing hinge broke in half suddenly and without any prior signs, warnings, or indicators of a defect under a total load of 225lb.  Break sent climber holding only a tape measure from second step to floor so suddenly and off balance that tape measure was dropped to avoid injury from fall.   Swing hinge broke in half without any stress marks or twisting of metal indicated.   Steel used for hinge appears to be of very poor quality and not strong enough for 300lb rated ladder.   It is cast steel that broke like china would under the same type of load.  Broken hinge has a dull grainy appearance inside of break area.
justification: The ladder hinge broke suddenly under a load below its rated capacity, causing a fall but no injury.

incident_description:
On November 17, 2012 at approximately 1:30 am I was awoken by all three of our smoke detectors upstairs going off. When I went upstairs, I noticed a funny smell. I went into all of the rooms and storage closets as well as into the attic.  I then went into the storage area where our air handler was, turned the breaker off and removed the cover. I couldnÃÂt get any continuity from the bottom (old) element, so I slid the blower unit out. I then saw the element burnt up about 8ÃÂ melted and burnt in two pieces. 
This is the second time this has happened to this same unit. I had to replace the top element about 2 years ago with the same problem.
There was a recall:   Release # 99-061   The date codes for that are 3592- 4595. My date code is 3095.

I hope this continuing problem can be corrected so no one else will have fires or scares like this in the middle of the night. 
Thank you for any information you can give me on this.

Model :  Rheem RBHA-14 J 10 NFAA	
Serial #   T M3095 92

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a burnt element and smoke detectors going off, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The Sears Craftsman 10" Table Saw, model number 315.28462, has a plastic pad, part number: 089037008040, that provides pressure to hold the blade angle once it is set. 

I released the lock lever, adjusted the blade, then locked the lever. The plastic pad broke into two pieces and flew across the room. I did not apply excessive force.

Had this part failed while sawing, the blade would tilt and jam possibly causing serious injury.

The saw is about a year old and has had very light use. This is the first time the blade has been tilted.
justification: The plastic pad broke during adjustment, but no injury occurred. The incident highlights a potential hazard if the part fails during use.

incident_description: While investigating why my garage unit heater (natural gas) was not turning on I discovered a tripped breaker.  The Venmar Heat recovery/ Ventilation unit was plugged into the same circuit as the heater.  through process of elimination I found the Venmar to be the cause of the breaker tripping.  I then removed the front cover of the Venmar AVS Duo 1.9 as in performing the annual cleaning, and found the motor to be ~150 degrees F.  I verified that the fan was free to turn (though somewhat stiff) and tried to run it while observing.  The motor appeared to get power, move a few degrees, and lock up.  I isolated the power, removed the motor and lubed the bearings with a couple of drops of oil and was able to free up the shaft to spin freely.  I reassembled and tried powering it up again without the fan cages on the shafts and it immediately bumped, froze up, and heated up.  I did not let it go long enough to trip the breaker.  the motor is apparently not as thermally protected as it should be, and though I haven't disassembled it yet, it may not be designed to be used in a vertical installation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning motor and tripped breaker, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: We recently moved into a rental home...the first time in over 20 years and didn't think twice about the electrical panel box.  We were gone for the weekend and came home to a furnace that wasn't working.  Called the landlord and he sent out a heater repairman.  He said the unit wasn't getting any power, so they called in an electrician.  The electrician came and preceded to open the electrical panel box and discovered the fuse (if that's still what it's called) for the heater was completely burned up.  He told us that this could of caught the house on fire.  He also told us that the whole panel box should be replaced as they were known to malfunction.  He said look up "GTE Sylvania Zinsco Electrical Panel" on [REDACTED] and said we would find all sorts of scary info. The electrician took an unused fuse in the box and replaced the one that was burnt.  I am in the process of notifying our property managers about this safety issue and am hoping that they replace the whole panel.
justification: The incident involved a burned-up fuse in an electrical panel known to malfunction, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: We've owned and used an Arrow Hot Melt Mini Glue Gun (model MT300) for about 10 years.  It has seen limited use.  Tonight my son was using the device for a school project and it apparently arced and exploded in his hand.  The fire ball scorched his hair and eyebrows  which were about 1.5 feet from the tool.  It has the UL listing stamp.  This is a seriously dangerous product and we are extremely fortunate that he wasn't hurt any worse then he was.
justification: The incident resulted in scorched hair and eyebrows, indicating an injury, but no death or severe harm.

incident_description: smoke coming from drill; stopped using before got hot; attempted to register witll Alltrade but they would register because I told them the drill did not have a serial number on either the battery or the drill body which they do no and never did
justification: Smoke from the drill indicates a potential hazard, but no injury occurred as the drill was stopped before overheating.

incident_description:
On Monday, November 5, 2012, Dartmouth Fire District 3 responded to a fire at [REDACTED] in Dartmouth, MA.  Upon investigating, we found a small fire located in a ceiling fan in a bathroom unit.  This is the second similar incident involving these units in this building.  The fire was extinguished and the unit was removed.  It appears that there is inadequate room for venting dust and debris.

The unit is located at:

REDACTED
justification: The incident involved a small fire with no reported injuries, and it is the second similar occurrence in the building.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Model 116.27514 vacuum cleaner in Feb 2010.  This is a cannister vacuum with the sweeper mounted on a handle.  The sweeper can be detached to allow different attachments to be fitted to the handle.  In Aug, 2011 I noticed that the light and vacuum were turning on and off on the sweeper as I pulled it back and forth.  When I investigated I found the insulation on the electrical cord that connects the sweeper to the handle completely worn through.  There were wires bundled in that sheath and the insulation on the wiring was also worn though.  There was a black area as if something had arc-ed.  I called Sears and ordered a replacement part figuring that the cord had been damaged or mishandled by me.  I installed the replacement part and have used the sweeper roughly 50 times since then.  Last week I noticed that the same wear had occured.  I caught it early enough that the insulation on the wires is not worn.  I know that I have not mishandled the vacuum or done anything unusual that would have caused this.  I attribute the wear to poor design and feel continuing to use this product poses a risk. 

I sent an email to Sears today alerting them to this problem.
justification: The incident involves a potential electrical hazard due to worn insulation, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore Dehumidifier  Model 580.54701700  Ser # 705TAAC33584

This model is not in the recall.  However, my unit got extemely hot and burned the outlet.
justification: The dehumidifier got extremely hot and burned the outlet, indicating an incident with potential for injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description: Outlet expander was feeding 2 appliances, a CO2/smoke alarm, and a dehumidifier that draws approximately 850W with te compressor engaged. Upon noting the dehumidifier was not operating, closer examination of the outlet expander revealed the disintegration of 1 of the copper prongs. The expander was removed from service and the outlet replaced.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage but no injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a portable generator by Champion Power Equipment, model #41311, at Costco.  I am experiencing fuel leaking from the carburetor after the unit has been shutdown by turning off the ignition key and then immediately turning off the gas line control.  This is the same problem reported in CPSC's Release #13-026 for model #s 41332 and 41532.

Note: I do not experience fuel leaking from the carburetor if I first turn off the gas line control and let the unit shutdown itself down a few minutes later when it's out of gas.  There's nothing in the instruction set which addresses this problem.
justification: Fuel leakage from the carburetor poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
We purchased 2 portable electrical heaters made by Soleus Air company about 2 seasons ago.  Today one of the heaters went "poof" and smoke started to come out of the unit.  If the unit is shorting out
then something is wrong.  I spoke with the company, told them what happened and asked if a recall was on these units, they said no.  I advised that this issue is bad and if we were not there it could have caused a fire.  Their answer was "could have, would have, but a fire didn't happen". You are not under warranty so all we can do is tell you to buy another heater.

These heaters are not the $29 heaters, they cost about $100 a piece.  If they are faulty, it needs to be corrected, there are enough fires in homes throughout the winter.

Thank you for your assistance.
justification: The heater emitted smoke but no fire or injury occurred, indicating a potential hazard without immediate harm.

incident_description: On the night of November 3rd 2012 (around 11:30PM) the glass in the shower door shattered for no apparent reason.
justification: The shower door glass shattered, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My house came with Pass & Seymour light switches, which was built around 1995.

Within the last 3 or so years, I've had to replace several of my light switches due to safety concerns.

Nearly all of the light switches arc and you can see light when you turn them on.  They also create a crackle type of sound when you turn them on or off.

The more severe issue is that a couple of them have smoked and caused a breaker to throw.  After taking off the wall plate and removing the switch, the switch fell apart in my hands.  It was split in half.  This particular switch powered my 40watt light bulb in my closet.  So there wasn't a lot of load on it.

Since then, I've been going around and replacing any that make noise.
justification: The switches arc and create a crackle type of sound, and a couple of them have smoked and caused a breaker to throw, but there was no injury.

incident_description: My Bionaire BCH9208 purchased last year sparked and smoked this morning. It would probably have caught fire if I had not unplugged it.
justification: The device sparked and smoked, which could have led to a fire if not unplugged, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Kenwood model ew7507ebk  type:kr750715ep  ser#03618 jn  oil filled space heater overheated and softly exploded spewing hot oil onto carpet and nearby bed.  Melted carpet and sent smoke and fumes into house.  luckily no one was standing close or they would have been badly burned.
justification: The heater overheated and exploded, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
Vacuum cleaner experienced intermittent power to the carpet cleaning head.

Upon removing the attachment connector, I observed that there was no insulation on portions of both high voltage power lines from the connector to the carpet cleaning head.

This allows the two power lines to short.
justification: Exposed high voltage power lines pose a risk of short circuit, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: The Diaper Sprayer was correctly installed for about two weeks with no problems. During the night, we woke up to a house full of water. The plastic pipe had burst and was flooding the bathroom and adjacent rooms. We live on a third floor and the water traveled through the floors and destroyed our neighbors ceiling and walls.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Dryer cycle ended and clothes were removed. Closed dryer door and left house for 2 hours. When we cam home the dryer had started on its own and had been running for an unknown amount of time. This is an ongoing problem and after researching the internet we found numerous other buyers of the same product are having the exact same problem.  There is obviously an electronic malfunction that could cause a serious fire.
justification: The incident describes an electronic malfunction causing the dryer to start on its own, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
The caller stated that she was using the iron for approximately 5 mins, there was a sizzling noise and then there were flames erupting from both sides of the iron and near the electrical cord.  The flames were at least 12 inches long, she immediately unplugged it and used a shirt to smother the fire.

The  caller noticed that the incident left a burning odor in the room, she then place the iron outside.  This was the first incident.

9/2012 The manufacturer was contacted the following day and she was advised to return the product so that they could make an evaluation.  They told her this would take about 4-6 weeks to make a determination of what caused the incident.

The caller is concerned that this iron is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved flames and a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My home was built with Summit windows, since acquired by Jeld-Wen. The balances on the windows, which keep the windows from falling, continue to fail. Jeld-Wen replaced some of the units, and their repairman has since indicated that they no longer make these units due to a history of failures. I am fearful of the heavy window falling on me or on a child, as when the units fail, the windows fall with no resistance, potentially hurting or killing persons near the windows. Jeld-Wen is asking me to pay for the replacement of these units, though they appear to me to be quite defective and dangerous.
justification: The description indicates a history of window failures with potential for injury or death, but no actual incidents reported yet.

incident_description: Macbook Pro charger, 60W MagSafe charger heated up overnight and melted at the base, resulting in exposed wire and high heat.

incident_description:
On Sunday morning April 8, 2012 I was using a Steamfast SF-275 (serial number C2275-247262) canister steam cleaner.  After around 10 minutes of use, the steam started coming out very slowly then stopped.  At this point I was done cleaning so I turned off the unit off. 

I checked for pressure in the unit by squeezing the trigger for the cleaning nozzle.  Nothing came out so I assumed the unit was not under pressure.  I decided to remove the hose and unscrewed the knob attaching the hose to the main unit, suddenly without warning the hose blew off and sprayed steam and hot water on my forearm, wrist and thumb.  

I immediately put my arm under cold running water but every time I removed it from the cold water, the pain was unbearable, so I had to return it to the water.  I got an ice pack wrapped in a towel but the texture of the towel was also very painful on the arm.  I ended up keeping my arm in a bucket of ice water for the entire day until I decided to go to the Palo Alto Medical Center Urgent Care facility.  The doctor dressed the wound with and gave me codeine pain medication.  

Since there is no warning label about removing the hose, I thought there must be a one way valve on the main body of the SF275 to prevent the discharge of steam from the unit when the hose is removed, and because the hose is attached with a simple unsecured knurled knob, it seemed like a user friendly device, not a accident waiting to happen. Even though I was careful in checking for steam pressure by squeezing the trigger for the nozzle I needlessly suffered 1st degree burns on my arm.

If the SF-275 a 2 cent warning label or a $3 check valve on the output port this accident never would have happened.
justification: The incident resulted in first-degree burns requiring medical attention, which classifies it as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the lack of warning labels or safety mechanisms.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she purchased a space heater and she followed the instructions for usage. The consumer stated that nowhere in the instructions did it notify the consumer that the heater could emit a chemical odor. 

The consumer stated that she aired out the heater for approximately 8 hours and it continued emitting the strong chemical odor. The odor was like burning plastic. The consumer stated that the smell was so strong that she had a severe asthma attack. The consumer stated that she did not have to go to the emergency room. The consumer stated that she took her asthma medicine to control the attack. The consumer stated that she had been ventilating her home for since 10/07/2012 and the smell had not dissipated. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that she should place the unit by a window, for the fumes to ventilate. The consumer stated that the representative also informed her that she could mail the heater to them and they would replace it to her. The consumer refused because she feels that other units are being sold and the manufacturer would not investigate the problem.
justification: The consumer experienced a severe asthma attack due to the chemical odor, which constitutes an injury, but did not require emergency care.

incident_description: I purchased a Poulan Pro 6500 generator just over a year ago.  I purchased it to use during power failures only, as of this date I have not needed to use it.  I do start the generator once a month and let it run for about five minutes just as a preventive measure.  A few days ago I brought the generator out of my garage for it's monthly start, when I turned on the gas valve, gas began leaking out of the valve itself at a fairly good rate.  I immediately turned the gas valve back off and the leak stopped.  I returned the unit to the retailer that I purchased it from for repairs.  When they turned the gas valve on, it did not leak.  I left the unit with them to check it over.  I contacted Husqvarna to see if there was any product recalls in regards to the gas valve, they indicated that there was none just one for the carburetor.  In checking on line I have found other Poulan Pro owners with the same problem.
justification: Gas leak occurred but was promptly stopped with no injury or damage reported; similar incidents found online suggest possible recurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased this plastic sports court flooring.  The flooring is from Rhino Sports (or ProPlayer Source.com).  The salesman and installers all could clearly see that on 3 sides of the court is water.  One side a pool, a hot tub, and a lagoon.  I had no idea that this surface was NOT indeed an All Weather Court, as they state on their website.  In fact, the weather must be absolutely desert dry.  We have two teenage sons, and the first time we had multiple kids over to use the backyard, 3 kids slipped and fell from wet bathing suits just walking by the court surface.  I called the company several times and complained that my backyard is now hazardous, and I would prefer NOT to wait to file an injury lawsuit.  I informed them how dangerous this flooring is, and that I would like it removed.  One of the injured was my 15 year old son, and he now does not feel safe on the court.

We also live in the San Francisco Bay area.  We have fog frequently.  The court is slippery then as well.  I had no idea this flooring surface was so dangerous and should not be sold as outdoor flooring.  I am still fighting with them to have it removed and refund my money.  I cannot believe they are permitted to sell a product as All Weather, when it is clearly dangerous in anything other than sunny, dry weather.
justification: Three kids slipped and fell, including the user's 15-year-old son, indicating actual injuries occurred.

incident_description:
The product is a driveway repair sealant, consisting of a solid rubber compound that is to be melted before pouring over cracks.  It is packaged in a canister, similar to a 1gallon paint can but smaller.  Directions call for heating over a camp stove on High for 1 hour, stirring it after 15 minutes.  

The canister lid was removed, and I _loosely_ placed a sheet of tinfoil on top since it was windy.  I skipped the step of applying tinfoil on grate to prevent any spills.  The canister was then placed on the campstove.  The flame was initially set to High as the instructions indicated.  After a moment, I adjusted it to Medium/Low to save fuel, then approximately 3 minutes later the canister burst open from the bottom, and it sprayed hot, liquified rubber over my garage door (see attached photos).

The canister was stored in an unheated garage, and the ambient temperature was 48 degrees.  Power of the campstove is advertised as 10,000 BTU/hr at maximum setting.  I noticed very shortly after the explosion, that the top portion of the rubber was still solid in the canister.  No warnings are given, in the instructions or packaging, about the potential for this product to burst and expel hot, liquified rubber.  Nor are there specifications regarding minimum operating temperatures or campstove limitations.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2.  The occurrence likelihood is 3 as the incident was caused by user error and not a product defect.

incident_description:
I use Tide Pods to do my laundry.  My 3 year old got a hold of one of the Pods, squeezed it, and it went directly into her eye.
After calling Poison Control and reading the back of the container, I was told to wash out her eye for 15 minutes.  After doing that I took her to the doctor, had her eye flushed and was told to come back for a recheck.  The next day her eye was flushed out again and she seemed better.  Several hours later she was in pain again and I took her to a pediatric opthamologist.
Her eye suffered a severe corneal abrasion.  She basically burned off the top layer of her cornea and the Doctor said it was similar to a chemical burn.
With some treatment and a weeks worth of pain, she will be fine.
However, people should be aware, and the labeling which states "May cause some eye irritation" should be changed to seek medical attention immediately.  
These pods are fairly new, and even Doctors are not aware of the damage they can cause.
justification: The child suffered a severe corneal abrasion requiring multiple medical treatments, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: The lid on my washing machine for like the 100th time would not unlock after it said washer was finished. I pushed the power button 3 times before it finally went off and the lid unlocked. I reached into the washer to pull clothes out and realized the clothes were still very heavy and full of water, the washer then went into cycle with my hands still inside!! I jumped scraped my arm on the lid, my leg on the shelf behind me from being startled. This washer has been nothing but trouble since I purchased it and ways bad it was a replacement for the previous washer I had that also was defective!!! Very unhappy with both lowes and whirlpool and now I am going to be permanently scared from this machine's poor design. I am gathering I'm not the first person to have problems with this machine. It needs to be recalled!!!!

incident_description: My twelve year old son was carbonating some water using his soda stream appliance. He is very familiar with the appliance and the instructions and warnings.  He was operating it within the written parameters and the entire appliance exploded.  The top of the appliance, including the charging canister rocketed to the ceiling. Water was sprayed all over the room, dripping from ceiling and covering the walls.  The explosion shot the appliance with such velocity that he would have been seriously injured had it hit him in the head.  It turns out the the bottom of the bottle which came with the device failed.  There is a big hole in the bottom of the bottle.
justification: The incident involved an explosion with potential for serious injury, but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as it was due to a rare equipment failure.

incident_description: My Nutone Bathroom ceiling fan [located in my bedroom bathroom] started making a squeaking noise about a week ago. I took it down and cleaned as best I could, what appeared to be dust. It was not as noisy, but still made a bit of a squeaking noise; like a squeaky fan belt. I left my home about 2:45, for a 3:00 pm appointment. I returned about 4:20. When I went into my bedroom, I heard a low humming noise. I thought it might be the hallway bathroom fan, or, the basement bathroom fan, which are directly next to and beneath my bathroom. When I stepped into my bathroom, I realized that although I didn't hear MY fan, the noise was coming from my bathroom. I looked and the switch was in the ON position. The humming was coming from my ceiling fan. I immediately turned the fan off, and went to get a screwdriver to remove the fan. Upon removing the fan, it was so hot that it burned the tip of my left ring finger; I almost dropped the whole unit on myself. I have a minute blister on my fingertip as a result of the heat on this unit's motor. [REDACTED].  It took the unit about 45-60 minutes to cool down. I attempted to do a search for this unit on the CPSC website and do not think it is on there, however, someone should look into this. I am saving this unit, and will contact Lowe's tomorrow.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (a blister from the hot motor), which qualifies as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) since such incidents are not common but can happen with faulty equipment.

incident_description:
Smoke detector false alarms.  I replaced all 8 of the smoke alarms in our house with the Kidde i12080 smoke alarms and we have been experiencing false alarms ever since.
I contacted Kidde via phone a couple of times regarding this matter. The first time I was told to have an electrician come out and install a whole house line filter as power spikes in the middle of the night may be causing the false alarms. This is not a reasonable solution due to cost.  Also my previous smoke alarms never gave false alarms.  My second call to Kidde I was told to disconnect the offending alarm from the system and see if they still go off. I tried this and a month or so later a different detector went into alarm mode. This detector required an 8ÃÂ ladder to reach, which is not the safest activity to engage in at 3am.  
I reached out to Kidde via their web site, as I did not want to wait on hold for twenty minutes.  I filled out their form, and typed out the issue and received no response.  I also did a web search and found this is a wide spread safety problem with the Kidde smoke detectors.
There are several safety aspects to this issue that Kidde is choosing to ignore; 1. Kids and adults are learning to ignore the alarms. 2. The level of protection is compromised when you have to unhook the detectors to stop false alarms. 3. Forcing consumers up on ladders in the middle of the night is dangerous.
Please help Kidde realize they have a quality and safety problem before someone gets hurt or killed.

[REDACTED]
justification: False alarms and the need to climb ladders at night pose potential safety risks, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

He turned and saw that the garage door was continuing to go down although it was no longer moving down.  The door bent/buckled about center as if to fold itself in half. Three windows completely shattered, exposing sharp ragged edges. He was able to get the door to retract back up by crossing the light sensor beam.   Glass was on the ground outside the door, inside the garage on the floor and covering our personal belongings.  The Genie garage door opener  located on the ceiling of the garage was broken as well.  [REDACTED] called Easy lift door company at 916-922-7123; he left a voice message explaining that there was a problem with our door and that we would need someone to come look at it and do necessary repairs.

[redacted] proceed to clean up the mess and secure the door.  The glass was sharp and shattered.  The glass was not tempered.  He was able to pull out the pieces that remained in the small window frame.  Disposed of the broken glass and screwed plywood to cover the open windows.  The door was able to manually close.

History of the garage door and opener:
There was nothing blocking the garage door, hinges, brackets or opener.  The door is the original door installed by Easy Lift Door Company via KB Homes in 2004.  We took possession of the brand new house October 7, 2004.  [redacted]installed a Genie Excelerator Model 15D995 ÃÂ½ HP as per the instruction manual.  [redacted] does not wear glasses and is competent to do such an installation.  The Genie Excelerator was purchased by us from Lowes; unable to locate original receipt.  Called Lowes they only have records 5 years back.  We still have the original manuals.

It continued to go down and bend in the middle.  This door was also installed by Easy Lift Door Company and the same Genie Excelerator Model 15D995 ÃÂ½ HP was installed by [redacted].  This event was not reported because I thought it was an isolated event.

Also, several times our neighbor [redacted] has had trouble with his door falling of the track.  We have helped get his door back on the track.  I believe he had to get a service person out the last time it fell of the track.

9/13/12 see incident above

9/14/12 Easy lift door company returned our call.  The scheduled a technician appt for Monday 9/17/12 between 1-4pm.

9/14/12  I called [redacted], Investigator, CPSC b/c he was recently out for another claim. I asked him if I should report the garage door.  He instructed me to do so by reporting the garage door opener as product one and that product 2 the door was damaged.  He told me that it was fine that the garage door company was coming out to investigate the problem.  He instructed me to get as much information from them as possible to include in my report.

9/14/12 I called Genie at 1-800-354-3643.  I provided my model number 15D995 and asked if there was any recalls on this item.  I was told not on this model.  I explained the above situation and I asked if there was a technician that could come out and figure out what happened.  I stated that the product was going to be reported to the CPSC.  I asked again if they had any similar complaints about this product, again I was told not on this model.  My information was collected for a damage claim and that my call would be forwarded as a level 3.  I should expect a call back either ÃÂtomorrow or Monday.ÃÂ  I provided both my home number and call phone number; I explained that it was ok to leave a msg, but please try both numbers.

9/15/12 I received a message on my home phone. No calls to my cell. I was told to call Genie back on 1-800-354-3643 with access code [REDACTED].  I called this number as instructed and entered my access code. Unfortunately, I received a prompting that business hours were M-F & to please try my call again.

9/17/12 I called Genie at 1-800-354-3643; entered access code [REDACTED]. Spoke with  we can file a damage claim fill out paper and send it back proof of purchase, picture of damage.  Send out Genie manufacturer defect coverage only.   If there is any sign that it was something other than the unit like installation or the door the damage will not be covered.  I was instructed that a genie authorized dealer must be the ones to come out first to assess the damage, but the garage company can come out after this authorized visit.   The damage claim paperwork is being sent to our email.  I should hear from a Genie authorized dealer within 24-48 hours.

9/17/12 I called Easy Lift Door Company and canceled my appt for today.  I said I would call and reschedule after the genie authorized dealer appt was made.

9/17/12 I called KB Homes to confirm that yes Easy Lift Door company did install the doors in 2004 on our new home.

Sept. 2012 [redacted] came out from Overhead Door Company of Sacramento, Inc. as authorized by Genie.  He found that the force control only worked when set to an eight to quarter past low and it did not retract otherwise.  When he tried other settings it would not retract.  This  force control setting was set at high prior to the malfunction of the unit.
He stated that the Genie Excelerator operates too fast and has his technician disable to high speed by cutting the high speed wire.  This is not the wire that controls the force setting.  This is the general speed of the unit moving the door up and down.
He also stated that the door will crush objects that are under it, but it is made to retract so the item does not become entrapped.   

Sept. 2012 Easy Lift door company came out.  They assessed the door for replacement parts.  Helped to straighten the damage.

Oct. 19, 2012 Incident claim report has been filed with Genie via [redacted], Customer Service Group via email [REDACTED].

We are now waiting for a response from the manufacturer.

incident_description:

justification: Gasoline leakage poses a fire hazard, especially when the generator is hot, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:

Upon receiving service from Sears, it was discovered that the burner was laying in the bottom of the unit along with the 2 screws that were supposed to attach it to the gas tube.

incident_description: I bought a foam carpet cleaning product on 10-10-12 from the Dollar Tree in Manchester, Tn. It is called The Home Store carpet cleaner and deodorizer. Made in China and imported to Greenbriar International  on Volvo Pkwy, Chesapeake, Va. I used this product for the first time on a floor mat from my car. I sprayed it on the front porch and so was not in an enclosed area. I evidently breathed in a chemical from this according to my Doctor. I was in the ER for 4 hours on Wednesday. [REDACTED]
