incident_description: Retractable Razor Blade (purchased from DaisoJapan in Torrance, CA) was used to remove a clothing tag.  Razor blades are assumed to be made sturdy and durable (like cutting boxes), but this particular razor blade are not entirely safe.  The razor blade was new and when using it the blade chipped and flung, causing an injury to my eye.  As I was admitted to the emergency room, the doctor classified my injury as Subconjunctival Hemorrhage (bleeding in the eye).  I am concerned with the quality of these razor blades as consumers who use these razor blades may come accross similar injuries.  I was lucky to only sustain injury to my sclera (white of the eye) and risked suffering damage to my cornea & pupil.
justification: The incident resulted in a Subconjunctival Hemorrhage, requiring emergency room treatment, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the blade chipping and causing injury, though it may not be a frequent event.

incident_description: Venmar constructo 2.0 motor seized 3 years ago and nearly started a fire it got so hot. incident_description:
I just bought "the Mat" and put it on my bathroom floor outside the bathtub.  I took a shower on Friday, stood on it, dried myself off and went into the other room and got dressed.  I went out of town.  When I came back home and decided to shower on Sunday evening, I stepped on the mat to get into the bathtub and almost fell as the mat slide on my linoleum floor.  I just thought I had stepped wrong as the corner edge was raised up a little bit against the door jamb.  I fixed it so it was laying flat on the floor but had to go and grab my other shampoo.  When I came back to the mat to step into the bath tub, it again slide and again, I almost fell.  So I picked up the mat and it was still damp on the bottom from where it got wet on the earlier Friday.  Plus it left the floor all wet as well.  This is not acceptable in any way, shape, or form.  The mat should have dried on its own.  So I put it on the counter and dried it off with a towel.  I put a regular bath mat on the floor after wiping up the dampness still on my floor. 
 
So I wanted you to now that this thing is a safety hazard.  If I can't stand on it and dry off and have it dry on its own--well it is not a product that should be on the market in my opinion. 

I will be taking the two mats back to Costco where I purchased them and I will warn them of this issue.  

It is comfortable to stand on, but if it can't dry rapidly on its own, it should not be on the market.
justification: The incident describes a near-fall due to a slippery mat, indicating a potential for injury but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Items: 2 Whirlpool 50 Pint Dehumidifiers Model AD50USL3
Serial Numbers: QP1820933 and QP1821048

Both units were in use in my basement. When I went into the basement I noticed an electrical burning odor. I eventually determined that it was coming from one of the dehumidifiers. I looked up any recalls on these units and found that a recall Release #02-096 was for serial number beginning with QL, but not for units beginning for QP like my units. Seeing that the recall stated that the units were overheating and causing fires. I also found a Whirlpool document that stated "certain internal components including wire terminals and switches can overheat.  This can result in fire and cause personal injury or property damage."

I was concerned that my dehumidifiers might have the same problem, so I took the cover off the units to see if there was something that needed to be cleaned. I also took the cover off the compressor and found that the wiring on the overload switch on both units was brittle and bare and had shorted against the metal rod coming from the top of the compressor that it was tightly pulled against (I have photos showing both overload switches). I assume that the burning odor was from the bare wire that was shorting against the metal rod, which I believe is an electrical and fire hazard. On both units this wire as so short that it was pulled tightly against the metal rod. In addition, other wires and terminal plugs on both units were brittle, cracked, and broken - which are also electrical and fire hazards. That area was also very hot.
justification: The incident involved an electrical burning odor and visible damage to wiring, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
3 - 4 months ago I purchased a GE combination electric washer dryer (model GTUP270EM1WW) from Lowes. Unit operated fine for the first three months before the problems started. The unit started vibrating and shaking violently. It shook so hard that it actually dislodged the exhaust ducts from the machine. I took out the level and made sure everything level. That was OK so I contacted GE and they sent out a repairman. I won't get into how clueless this guy was as that's a different issue. He said the drum was defective and ordered a replacement. If the drum was bad it should have been a problem from day one. Crew came and installed it a week later ran a test with nothing in it and said it was fixed. Not the case. Now the machine shakes twice as hard and moves on the floor. Once again checked and made sure it was level.

During these service calls I discovered a couple of other issues. The first one is that the unit that the softener goes in constantly dislodges itself on a regular basis and rattles around the inside. GE rep said that's because the softener is too heavy. No the problem is that it doesn't lock into place properly.

The biggest concern is yet to follow. It seems that when the washer hits the spin cycle small items such as socks and underwear get tossed out of the drum and fall into the bottom of the unit where the still wet items lay across the electrical components. I can tell they weren't accidentally dropped in there because the items were clean.

So as I see it there are two major issues.

There something wrong with the component during the spin cycle. This causes the exhaust duct work to become dislodged. This would be an even more extreme problem if you had a gas version of the product as lint is so easily combustible. 

The second issue is that you have wet clothing being dispersed into the inside bottom of the unit and laying across the electrical contacts which I'm sure you know could be a real problem.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning washer-dryer causing violent shaking and potential electrical hazards, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Product is a Sears Kenmore Top Load Washer Model 11028002010, purchased 03/25/2011.  On June 2, 2012, while the washer was completing a cycle, I noticed a burning smell coming from under the washer and that the clothes had not spun down.  When I lifted the bottom of the machine, further burning smell was evident.  I called Sears Appliance Services and a technician came to the house to examine and repair the product.  The technician removed the lower insulation/sound deadening panel, and we could see that the housing covering the two drive pulleys was warped, broken, and partially burned and melted.  The insulation layer was also blackened and partially melted.  The technician removed the housing and stated that the nut holding the large drive pulley had come off the shaft, the pulley had detached along with the drive belt, and friction had caused the damage and burning.  Due to a lack of parts, the total repair could not be completed and parts were ordered.  On June 12, 2012, another Sears Technician completed the repair by installing factory parts and was of the opinion that the problem "would not happen again".    The repair cost me $265.79.
However, on September 24, 2011 the machine again broke down in the same fashion.  Sears was called again, and a Sears Technician made a house call on September 24 and October 2, 2012 to  install replacement parts of the same design that had failed previously.  The Technician and I observed that the breakdown was due to the fact that the manufacturer had used an ordinary nut to hold the large pulley on the drive shaft, without any means of securing the nut in place over time (such as a lock washer mechanism, cotter pin, or threading in the reverse direction of shaft rotation).  As a result, the nut would and did fail repeatedly to secure the pulley in place by simply coming unscrewed under normal use.
This was an inherent design flaw that could have been and should now be remedied to preclude both breakdown and the chance of causing a fire under the washer.  
As I had purchased some myself for this purpose, the Sears Technician applied "REDACTED" glue to the shaft to help hold the nut in place, but I view this as only a temporary fix at best.
I am concerned that this appliance is inherently dangerous as constructed, has not been repaired despite several visits by Sears qualified technicians, and requires a safety recall to repair it using other parts now not available.  Failing that, the company should totally recall the product and refund my original purchase price.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing a burning smell and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The issue recurred multiple times, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
12/2011 The caller stated that she used the fabric freshener to spray on her bed linen.  She stated that she started to have health symptoms including, headaches, dizziness, respitarory problems, etc.  She was taken to the Nazareth hospital in PA by the rescue squad for a heart attack, where she was hospitalized for a week.  There was no diagnostic that she had a heart attack and she was released.  

2/2012 The caller had a followup visit with her cardialogist and he was unable to diagnose the problem.  

6/2012  The caller was still experiencing problems.  She removed her bed linen, washed them thoroughly and threw out her pillows which seemed to resolve the issue.

The manufacturer was not contacted because there was no contact number.

The caller feels that this fabric freshener contains chemicals which is a health hazard.


UPDATE:

In November 2011 after moving to this current address, I began using Power House Fabric Freshener on my bed.  I have a rather unstable bladder so I was concerned about smelling up the bedroom.  I sprayed a lot and often.

Toward the end of December, I began waking up light headed, unsteady on my feet, short of breath, and generally out of focus. These problems worsened during January and the 'out of focus' often lasted most of the day.

February 5, 2012 my breathing became very labored and the chest felt tight and heavy. I was rushed to the hospital with a possible heart attack.  After a week in the hospital and many tests, no heart attack.

Shortly after returning home the syptoms returned, and I returned to spraying.

In mid-April, my daughter (a nurse) wondered if my problems were caused by a concentration of carbon monoxide. Possible, we'd gone through a winter, windows closed, drapes down, low ceiling.  So monitors were bought, and someone to check the house.  No carbon monoxide.

However my daughter's words resonated with me.  They only thing going on in the bedroom besides sleeping and dressing, was spraying.

I immediately striped the bed and washed everything in hot water.  The pillows went into the dryer and out in the hot sun.  I thought I was going to have a miracle cure.  Then I even threw the pillows out.  Of course, no more spraying. But no miracle.

Gradually, through June and July, the symptoms were less frequent and not as intense.  

We are now through August and I do believe that my system has finally cleared out.  I'm feeling normal again.

I do, however, have one remnant left from this experience- red, red lips.  This too is beginning to fade.
justification: The caller experienced significant health symptoms requiring hospitalization, though no heart attack was diagnosed, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue resolved after discontinuing use of the product, suggesting a possible but not certain link (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
On June 22, 2012 lightning hit two trees bout 200ÃÂ from the building I had converted from a barn to a recreation room and workshop. The trees were near my Invisible Fence buried a couple feet away. That fence conducted the lightning to my building. Within minutes, there was heavy smoke coming from the peak of the barn. The building was a total loss. $25,067 of the replacement value of $79,207 was covered by insurance. The depreciated value of the building was $59,120.
The Fire Marshall, [REDACTED], who is a former fire chief with Eagleville and was a fire officer at UCONN did a thorough investigation. He concluded that the fire had started at the spot where the Invisible Fence was plugged into an outlet and that the Invisible Fence was the cause of the fire. I enclose a copy of the Fire MarshallÃÂs report.
A few days later, a representative from Canine Fence who sold and installed my fence, also looked at the building, the scarred trees, and so forth. Their representative acknowledged that the cause of the fire was the Invisible Fence his company had installed.
[REDACTED] of Canine Fence says that Canine Fence has no responsibility for what happened. I disagree for the following reasons:
1) Nowhere in the installation manual and ownerÃÂs guide is there indication that having an Invisible Fence connected to a building puts that building in danger from lightning. I enclose a copy of the installation manual.
I mentioned this to [REDACTED]. His response was that it is "common knowledge" that buried wires can conduct lightning into buildings, so I should have known. I have done some informal research, asking various acquaintances whether they were aware that buried wires could do this. Out of ten people eight of them were surprised and amazed. This is not common knowledge, although IÃÂm sure it is obvious to people installing buried wires.
2) After my event a friend who also has an Invisible Fence told me that the men who installed the system advised him to unplug the charger when there was an electrical storm. So, the installers are aware that lightning is a danger to the building in which the charger is plugged in.
If the installers were aware of this, it seems that those writing the warnings on the installation manual were aware of this as well.
In any case, I was not given that bit of advice.
This is not a rare occurrence. I am aware of at least one other event just like mine that happened in Columbia about a week after my building was destroyed. A quick [REDACTED] search finds many more such events, some of them captured on [REDACTED] videos.
3) There are plenty of warnings on other topics in the installation manual. The only warning about lightning, however, is that an electrical storm may damage the buried wire, so that one should check the perimeter of the fence after a storm. There in not word about fire danger to oneÃÂs building.
4) A company that sells a product has a responsibility to inform buyers of a product of dangers associated with the product. Drugs, pesticides, and almost every other product come with appropriate warnings. In the present case it is pretty clear that Canine Fence was well aware that their product involved this danger. They have a responsibility to let customers know of this danger. I should re-iterate that everyone Invisible Fence owner I have spoken to has been surprised and frightened.
5) The "common knowledge" excuse for not informing me doesn't hold up. When you buy coffee, the cup says "contents may be hot." Well, duh! Even if it were "common knowledge" that buried wires connected to buildings can burn them down, that should be in the literature among the other warnings.
6) I live on top of a hill, in an obviously lightning-prone location. My House and out-buildings are the highest point for hundreds of yards in every direction. I had lightning rods on the building which burned down, and I have lightning rods on my house. Canine Fence has to know that installing an Invisible Fence in this location is exceptionally dangerous.
            So, my opinion is:
1) Canine Fence should be required to warn past purchaser and potential future purchasers of this "common knowledge" fact that installing an Invisible Fence could conduct lightning into the building into which it is plugged and burn it down.
2) Given that Canine Fence was well aware of the problem with their dog containment device, and continued to sell their installations without any warning, some kind of fine should be imposed on the company. This situation akin to the tobacco companies covering up the dangers of smoking and to Ford ignoring the dangers of their Pinto. It is beyond belief that their installers knew about the danger and the management of the company did not.
3) Canine Fence should compensate burnt: owners who suffer fire losses due to their product. At least up to the depreciated value of the destroyed property.

Sincerely
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (building loss) but no injuries or fatalities, and similar incidents are documented but not extremely common.

incident_description:
Bought Hoover Platinum Collection Carpet Cleaner about 1 1/2 years ago.  Used about 5 times since then.  Cleaner still like new.  

On 9/18/2012 began to clean carpet in bedroom 1.  Cleaner began making a really loud rumbling noise.  I stopped the cleaner to make sure that I had all containers for solution, water, and dirty water in properly.  They were.  Turned cleaner back on.  Noise began again and grew even louder.  

Then machine began bellowing out white - horrible smelling smoke - enough smoke to fill up the second level (2300+ sq ft) of my home.  Just as I thought "what in the world?" here come some flames shooting out toward me and then toward the drapes.  Scary!  

I immediately turned off the machine, ran and unplugged it, and began to move it away from the bed and drapes and toward the tile in the master bath.  As I was doing this I noticed the carpet in this bedroom was charred black!! 

The machine was so hot that - as I was attempting to get it into the master bath - it even charred the carpet in the master bedroom just by rolling over it!!!!   

I finally managed to get the machine into the bath, turned it on it's side to get the "hot portion" of the unit off the floor and into the air and the ran to the windows to open them and turn on the ceiling fans to get the smoke and the smell out of the house.  

God was with me.  There is no other explanation.  Otherwise the drapes, the bed, the carpet, and me would have caught on fire!!!!!    Plus the smell...oh my.  I get migraines and needless to say this scare and smell triggered a fantastic one that stayed for two days.  

Once I had done these steps, I called the 800 number for Hoover to report what just happened.  They could have cared less.  They told me to take photos - I did.  They asked if I wanted to file a claim on the damage.  I do.  They then stated that I should get a repair/replace estimate.  I have.  They also stated they would contact FedEx and have FedEx email me a shipping label to send the machine back to them.  

To date I have NOT received the label yet.  I have called and emailed Hoover several times.  They ignore me.  The only response I get is one rep did leave a message and said the label was sent to me last Tuesday and if I did not have it I must have deleted it.  

I received 2nd and 3rd degree burns last year from a brush fire on both my legs.  Needless to say when this carpet cleaner did this I nearly went into shock!  I want this dangerous machine out of my home.  However, Hoover is doing nothing to help this process along.  

I sincerely think something should be published on these machines and this company should take responsibility for making such a dangerous piece of home cleaning equipment.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction causing smoke, flames, and property damage, but no physical injury was reported.

He noticed that the unit was overheating and immediately powered off the unit and unplugged it. Later when he retrieved his clothes he noticed that they were burnt. The consumer has black scorched marks on his wall and the rear of the dryer.

 (12/2010) The manufacturer was contacted and a Rep. (name unknown) advised him that there was nothing that could do about it.

The consumer was unable to use his dryer since 2010. He heard about the Release #12-251. After calling the recall hotline he was informed that his serial did not fall within the range, but they would send out a tech to diagnose the unit at a cost to him.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burnt clothes and scorched marks) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer says she was washing clothes when the machine went into the spin cycle, when it started spinning out of control.  It sounded like lightning bolts coming through the wall.  The consumer went into the laundry room and saw the washer jumping out of control when it shot forward off of the wall and cracked the granite countertop underneath.  The door flew open and the latch to the door is now broken.  The washer was on approximately 30 minutes prior to the incident.  She contacted the manufacturer the next day on 8-14-2012, who offered to send out a technician for a fee. 


Incident Date: 8-13-2012
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 as it is a common occurrence for incidents to happen.

incident_description:
We were drying a shirt that had water spilled on it.  After 15 minutes, we removed the shirt and it was dry.  We turned off the dryer and did not notice any problem.

A few minutes later we noticed strong smoke smell and called 911.  My wife left with the kids while I waited for the fire department.  The City of Novi firefighters arrived and determined that there was a fire inside my dryer.

I removed the back of the dryer and the bottom left half of it has burned lint throughout.  This is a major fire hazard.  After searching online, there are many people with this exact same problem!  This product should be recalled and fixed at no charge to everyone who owns one of these dryers.  We are lucky we were home during this incident!
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard in the dryer but no injuries or deaths occurred, and similar issues are reported by many users, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
First, I would like to say that with each passing day both property and people are at risk charging their Amazon Kindle. I am very concerned and feel that there should be an immediate recall on the Kindle power cord (cable) manufactured for my device, the 2nd generation keyboard, at least this is what the Amazon customer rep called my device. I called Amazon to notify them of the scary incident we experiened, and they offerred to replace the power adapter/charger. I explained that this was not the true purpose of my call and continued to explain the following incident. I urged them to recall the cord immediately in order to prevent electrocution,shock, and fire that could cause loss of life and property as well. They told me that this is the first they had heard of this but would send my concerns to some team at Amazon. 

I later went online and googled kindle power cord defective, or recall or somthing similar to these words. I was taken to Amazon where comments were posted and replacement cords were for sale. There were many comments stating similar experiences to ours concerning the cable. Amazon had to have known about this problem because others have alredy contacted them and posted comments. The reps I spoke with previously did not hesitate to offer to replace the cord but wanted to charge me for shipping. I now believe they were aware of the problem. 

I then spent about 40 minutes composing a comment on the Amazon product review section concerning the power cord and urging anyone reading  my post to file a report with you, and to call and urge Amazon to take the responsibility to issue a recall. I guess Amazon intercepted the message as I never saw my comment that I spent much time composing and felt such urgency to post. I was told by two seperate Amazon reps yesterday that someone from Amazon would contact me today by phone. I have not heard from Amazon. The incident is described and follows.

We were packing to leave on vacation last week. The Kindle had been plugged into a surge protected power strip where we charge telephones as well as the Kindle. [REDACTED] wanted to take the Kindle and charger with us, she reached to unplug it by pulling on the plug to release it from the outlet. As she did this she noticed that part of the wire was bare and small pieces of the cable's insulation had fallen off and onto the top of the console where the power strip sits. As she held the cord to determine how bizarre this was, more of the cracked pieces fell away leaving large and small sections of bare wire!  The insulation was cracked all along the cord and just a slight touch caused pieces to break away and fall off. The pieces of cable insulation material upon inspection appear to be brittle as well. If [REDACTED] had pulled the cord from the outlet by using any part of the cord to assist its release, like most children and teenagers often do, she would have been shocked or electrocuted completing this action. If papers had been laying near or in contact with the bare wire, we may have not made it to our vacation the night it was charging. I can assure you that this charger has never been used by children, been in extreme conditions, or exposed to extreme temperatures or harsh conditions of any kind. It has been in a climate controlled environment and only used by adults. The Kindle and charger will be 3 years old this Christmas.

I can honestly say that I have seen and used  many appliance cables and cords over my lifetime but have never seen a power cable's protective insulation on any appliance break down like this. There is no melting of the plastic. It just appears to be a substandard material not sufficient for this application used to manufacture the cable. I would be more than happy to send the power cable to you for inspection and testing but only if you agree to pursue this because I may need to send it to a future contact if you do not choose to act.

I have no idea how many Kindles are in American homes. I am guessing that millions have been sold. I am very concerned and feel that I have a personal responsibility to not only report this to you but to insure that Amazon proceeds with a recall. It is important that I hear from you concerning the actions that you are willing to take. I will excersise every resource available to prevent innocent people from being harmed or killed by electrical shock and from having a house fire possibly causing loss of life due to the use of this inferior  and dangerous product. I informed the Amazon rep that they could send me a new cord but the Kindle will not be used unless I know for sure that this new cord is safe. I have no idea that the replacement cord will be safe, especially if they are still having this product made in China with inferior materials.

I am including  information printed between the plug prongs of my power cord. I feel this may be beneficial to you to identify my power cord and others out there in American homes. I AM SURE THERE IS A POSSIBILITY THAT OTHER MODEL NUMBERS MIGHT BE INVOLVED AS WELL.! I bought this kindle as a Christmas gift for my roomate, [REDACTED] I consider both of us to be victims. I am so glad she was not hurt.I filled out this entire form and the page disappeared after I loaded photos. I had to do it twice. I was not sure which of the numbers below were serial numbers when trying to fill in the blocks on the form.

Input 100-240V-0.15A   50-60 Hz/Output 4.9V=0.85A/ 54pt  EZ233466/flextronics pin  09500043-200

model no. A00810   MADE IN CHINA 

My phone number is [REDACTED]

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
While otherwise operating normally and drying clothes, the LG gas dryer model DLGX7188WM pumps raw, non-ignited natural gas into the machine (and the room in which it is located). The odor of natural gas was so strong in my house and backyard that I assumed I had a leak from a broken gas pipe and called the local utility to check the situation. Their technician came and found the LG dryer was the source of the gas, and shut the appliance down. The appliance repairman who came a few days later ran the machine and told me that the following was happening: the igniter heated the gas to the set temperature and then turned off. Then, after a few second delay, the gas valve opens and raw gas is pumped into the drum and out the exhaust hose, hence the gas odor in the backyard where the dryer exhausts. The flow of raw gas does not stop, and the dryer continues to run and dry the clothes because the igniter is operational.

I informed LG of this situation and they took a "report" and said I was the only consumer who had reported this problem. A simple search of the internet proves this to be untrue, as several people have had this problem and reported it to LG. A video of the exact nature of the defect is also posted : http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mJqzwdBavfw

The defect in this product poses a serious threat to life and property. I believe it should be recalled.

If there is anything I can do to help this investigation, please contact me. This is a dangerous product that people should be made aware of.
justification: The incident involves a gas dryer releasing raw natural gas, posing a serious threat to life and property, but no injury or death was reported.

It was apparently due to some form of a "solvent" that the cylindrical pleated filter element was treated with at the factory.

incident_description:
I was attempting to put a new plug on a lamp cord.  I purchased a current product, LEVITON's Flat Vinyl Plug No. 48643 (package of 2, white, 2-prong, rated 15A-125V, also marked 1B22Y0, CPC 7847784648), UL listed Plug 257B.
This plug is designed with two ramped tabs on opposite sides of the core piece that are designed to slide into and then lock into slots in the flexible shell, retaining the core in the shell.  The connections are screwed posts on the core piece.
The core pieces are supplied already inside the shells so that you have to disassemble the pair before the plug can be used.  The instructions state "Pry body out of cover." and there is a drawing of a flat-blade screwdriver being used for this.  Because there are two opposed tabs, and prying on one side tends to re-close the already pried other side, you either have to use two prying tools or repeatedly pry alternating sides while trying to pull the core out of the shell, which is awkward.  I had to repeatedly reorient my hands and the screwdriver.
During this process, I impaled my hand with the screwdriver, drew blood, and damaged the first couple of layers of skin.
Supplying these preassembled is not necessary and adds the disassembly step and adds the risk of injury.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (impaled hand, drew blood, damaged skin), which corresponds to severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the awkward disassembly process described.

They engineered a insulating padding to prevent electrical current flow to metal housing by moisture conductivity,  He said that there is just not enough insulation to prevent this overheating.

Caller attempted to contact the manufacturer August 13, 2012 but has not at this time been successful.

He is reporting dangerous overheating that could be alleviated with an insulated padding.
justification: The dryer's overheating has caused property damage (melted laundry baskets) and poses a burn risk, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description: On Sunday 09/09/2012 we purchased a new electric Kenmore Elite Steam Dryer model number 796.81473. The dryer was delivered and installed on 09/11/2012. The delivery crew connected the power and the exhaust ductwork. Our exhaust duct goes through and up an internal wall into the attic and then exits out through a roof vent. The house was built in 1990 and has a three wire 240-volt, 30-amp circuit with the neutral wire also used as the ground for the dryer connection. The delivery crew installed the power cord on the dryer as/per the three wire instructions on page 13 of the manual supplied with the dryer. Except they did not use a UL listed strain relief. The power cord just went through the hole in the sheet metal wall on the back of the dryer. They test operated the dryer and it appeared to work fine. As they were leaving they noticed smoke coming out of the roof vents above the room where the dryer was installed. They notified my wife and a small fire was discovered in the attic next to the dryer exhaust duct. The installers put out the fire with a garden hose while my wife called 911. The City of Fresno Fire Department responded and cleared out any fire or water damaged insulation in the attic. They discovered that a flexible metal duct that supplies combustion air to my zero clearance fireplace had been in contact with the dryer duct and a water pipe. There are electrical arc marks on the dryer duct and the water pipe indicating that somehow the exhaust duct for the dryer had become energized and the flexible metal duct for the fireplace had completed the circuit to ground and caused the fire. Please note the lack of the UL listed strain relief was not the cause, the wires were not cut where they went through the hole. I do not know how the exhaust duct became energized but it didn't happen until the new dryer was installed and operated. Our previous dryer, of 12 years, was a natural gas unit and did not use the 240 volt circuit. Prior to that we did have an electric dryer and never had any kind of problems. This dryer is installed right next to a new Kenmore Elite Front Loading Automatic Washer. Had the short circuit in the attic not occurred, when someone touched the washer and dryer while the dryer was operating they may had completed the circuit instead with deadly results.
justification: A small fire occurred in the attic due to an energized dryer exhaust duct, but there were no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: On 8/11/2012, @ 6:37AM, I awoke to a popping noise, thought someone was popping popcorn. As I was getting up to check the noise out, I then was hearing a sparking type of noise too and both noises was getting louder. I ran downstairs to see that our [REDACTED] was on fire. I yelled "FIRE" to wake the family and grabbed the fire extinguisher. By the time I was going to put it out, it was out but the smoke was so bad of smelling like rubber and smoke, that my husband grabbed the power tap and threw it outside. This power tap has 5 plug outlets and we were using only 4 of them. And what we had plugged in doesn't draw allot of current for this to just start on fire. We have had this for about a yr or so now and never had any reason to think it would catch on fire like it did. We also don't have the receipt anymore because it has been this long before anything happened. We bought at our local Walmart here in Milwaukee WI. We have damage to our floor lamp that was plugged in, the cord is burnt and singed. We also have our home surveillance system (Swann DVR4-950 tm) that has (4) separate power supplies, all cords are burnt and singed. We won't use our surveillance system because of the condition of the cords. We don't feel safe using any of the cords damaged. One power supply is for the DVR, one for the flat screen monitor and one to run the camera. Also the floor where all were is burnt. (we aren't too concerned with the floor, as we were tearing it out this winter anyways). If I didn't wake to this, whose to say that my family and I and our 3 pets would not have been hurt or worse killed by this fire. There should be no reason for this to have happened since we have had this for over a year. This is a defect as my husband is pretty smart on stuff like this and he feels that the "surge protection circuit failed"? This was definitely a defect of this product and not human error on our part.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, and the likelihood of such an event is considered rare given the description of the product's history and usage.

incident_description:
I purchased a new HEPA filter insert ([REDACTED]) and charcoal pre-filter (HON38002) for my old [REDACTED] air purifier. The products came from AllergyBeGone (866-234-6630) via Amazon.com.  I am reporting the HEPA filter insert (HON24000) as unsafe. It came with a small identifying sticker: RPS Products / BestAir / 847-683-3400. The new HEPA filter insert is white overall. All previous HEPA filter inserts I have purchased for the air purifier have been black outside. I first used the new HEPA filter on 8/13/12. 

I have operated my air purifier with the new HEPA filter in place three times. All three times when I turned on the unit I immediately noticed a strong organic chemical sort of smell, a smell too objectionable for me to remain in the room. Never before have I experienced any sort of smell when using the air purifier (I have owned it since it was new, perhaps more than 10 years ago, and have purchased and used several replacement HEPA filters and charcoal pre-filters through the years). 

I ran the air purifier for 3 hours each time on two different days and in two different rooms. The smell was just as strong after each time, so I turned off the air purifier, opened the windows and, after a time, was able to return to the room. On both occasions the next morning I awoke with a sore throat, which was gone by later that morning. 

A third time I ran the air purifier in my bedroom for 1-1/2 days while I was out of town. The same strong smell was immediately present, and remained as strong after 1-1/2 days of operation. I turned off the air purifier, opened the windows and, after a time, was able to return to the room. I later went to bed in the room. The next morning I again awoke with a sore throat, but this time by midday I was experiencing such low energy that I spent much of the rest of the day lying down. I developed a runny nose and scratchy throat during that day. All my symptoms worsened over the next several days, and I developed a significant cough and experienced much-interrupted sleep as well. 

One week after the 1-1/2 days of running, with continuing bad cough and very low energy, I realized that if the replacement HEPA filter were related to my symptoms, perhaps my paper hepa furnace filter had picked up contaminants and was continuing to spread them through my home. I replaced the furnace filter with a new paper hepa furnace filter and, on lying back down, had the sense of breathing more easily for 20 minutes or so (though I had not previously been aware of breathing difficulty). That same evening I had more energy and my cough had improved. I noticed significant improvement in both by the next morning, though my energy level was still at perhaps 50% of normal. 
After two more days I realized that though I had washed my sheets since the 1-1/2 days use of the air purifier in my bedroom, they had not been washed since I changed the furnace filter (my sheets are left open to the air during the day, and the air conditioning ceiling air ducts in the bedroom discharge directly onto them). I washed the sheets and that night my sleep was dramatically improved. 

Now three days later I am still experiencing fatigue ÃÂ improved though still significant ÃÂ I spend much of each day lying down. I sought help from my medical doctor yesterday, and it was her opinion that I am dealing with a two-fold trouble: a viral infection AND the effects of using the HEPA filter. I sincerely hope that no one else will need to suffer such effects.
justification: The incident caused physical symptoms including sore throat, fatigue, and respiratory issues, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the detailed account of repeated exposure and symptoms.

incident_description: The lady I care for who is 95yrs old very much still able to do things for herself was asked by a lady who was there to try and make things in her home safe so as to prevent falls etc to get a suction cup handle for her shower so she would have something to help her get into the shower safer. I went and tried to put it on myself and I did I also pulled on it and hung on it myself to make sure it was secure but i did tell her  I really don't think you should trust it and to be careful. I am very concerned this product could do so harm to a person who is depending on it to get in to the bathtub or shower
justification: The handle fell off but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is high given the product's unreliability and the vulnerable user group.

incident_description: I purchased a Coleman Perfect Flo Instastart camping stove (model # 2000006510) and used it for the first time while camping over the Labor Day weekend, Sept 2012.  The instructions that come with the stove indicate that the ignition button may need to be pressed several times before the burner will light. By the time the burner lights, there is a lot of propane in the air and there is a big burst of flame that could easily burn the person trying to light the burner or someone standing nearby.
justification: The incident describes a potential for burns due to propane buildup, indicating a risk of injury but no actual injury reported.

(6/2012)  The consumer called the manufacturer and told them about the incident.  The manufacturerÃÂs rep. (name unknown) did not ask the consumer any questions about the incident.  The rep. told the consumer that his model was no longer manufactured, but he indicated that he did not have any other information for the consumer.

The consumer uses the dehumidifier for approx. 3 months out of the year in his cellar.


The consumerÃÂs dehumidifier was not included in Recall CAP# 12-240, but he believes that it presented a problem similar to the ones identified in the recall and that the recall may need to be expanded to include additional models.

incident_description: I purchased an Onan-Cummins Homesite 5500 generator for our home and kept in in an enclosed trailer behind my shop so that I could take it up to the house if the power was interrupted which it is from time to time.  From time to time I start the generator to be sure it is ready when it is needed.  Last fall I started the generator and after it ran for a few minutes the bowl  on the bottom of the generator fell off and the spilled gas caused a small fire in the trailer.  It might have been larger but I was near and had a fire extinguisher handy.  The brass bolt that held the bowl in place on the carburetor snapped at a place in the bolt where there are small holes.  I contacted Cummins to get parts to fix it but they said that I couldn't  and would have to let them do so.  Since they wanted what I thought was a high price for this I thought I could find the parts on the internet.  This has proved fruitless.  I asked if there was a recall on the generator as it seems the bolt was poorly make but they said no and would do nothing.  I tried brazing the brass bolt but the brass seems of a poor quality.  I've only ran about 15 gallons of gas through the generator so it hasn't enough hours on it to be wore out.  In fact it looks new.  I would have made pursued this sooner but shortly after the incident I hurt my foot an had surgery.  On a plate on the frame it shows the model number as Mdl# 4EGMBD-5269 and Ser# J06E002760 and it was made in China.
justification: The incident involved a small fire due to a generator malfunction, but it was quickly controlled with a fire extinguisher and no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I have a Hampton Bay HB50 dehumidifier that I run in my basement in the summer with a hose
to a sump pump. I never have it set on the highest setting. Last week a switch and wires caught fire and set off my smoke alarm at 1 am, filling the first floor and basement with smoke. When we got to the dehumidifer, the wires were burning, smoke was coming out the back, and the grill was starting to melt. I rushed the dehumidifier out the back, but the wires continued to burn, so I put it out with a fire extinguisher.

No injuries, but I had to run the fans all night to rid the house of smoke, and the basement still stinks of electical fire. We were out of town the weekend before, so if had happened then
there is a chance the house would have burned down.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the potential for recurrence and significant damage if unattended.

incident_description: My wife complained ceiling fan was noisy, and some lights not working. When I started to change the bulb THE FAN FELL ON ME!  It knocked me from the ladder, and I think it injured my hand and arm, my neck is also sore.
justification: The fan fell and caused injuries to the hand, arm, and neck, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Vacuuming furniture product began throwing sparks out of the motor
justification: The incident involves sparks from a motor, indicating a potential fire hazard but no injury reported.

incident_description: I was mopping with my Shark Steam Mop.  I had just started.  The mop was not producing steam like it usually does at start up.  I pushed the handle in a couple of times and it started to make the steam noise, but nothing came out.  After about 5 seconds there was a loud pop and steam and hot black liquid came out.  Had I not been wearing pants and shoes, I would have been burned by the steam and liquid.  I immediately unplugged the mop and have not used it since.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning steam mop that released steam and hot liquid, but no injury occurred due to protective clothing.

incident_description:
Shark Steam Mop  Model S3501  While using the product their was an explosion.  Steam started to come out of the body of the product.  No one was injured fortunately.  But hot steam could cause serious burns. 
An inspection showed that a steam hose failed. It blew apart send a spring that was inside the hose into the unit near electrical connections.  
Internet research show this is a common failure for these units. 
Contact with Sharp determined this is a common failure and they will not sell repair products for this failure.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and steam release, but no injuries occurred. The failure is described as common by both internet research and the manufacturer.

incident_description:
I used the Barbecue Genius 2 Way grill brush to clean my grill prior to grilling chicken. 

While eating dinner my husband discovered a piece of metal in his tongue. After closer inspection we discovered that the piece of metal was a brass bristle from the wiry side of the grill brush. We looked at the grill brush and discovered more wire bristles were loose.

The brush was purchased at the end of May and has been used between 5 and 10 times.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (metal bristle in tongue) and the brush showed signs of wear after limited use, indicating possible recurrence.

incident_description: This form is very difficult so as to not get futher furstrated I will summaryize my issue . We bought a Hoover # Uh 70201 Vac with retractable cord the cord melted fron the motor resulting in a shock to a heart patient. Hoover knows they have a problem as I ended up talking with a loss prevention person.
justification: The incident resulted in a shock to a heart patient, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
I am writing this in connection with your dated : July of 2011  Release # 11-281  Regarding Homelite Recalling Pressure Washer Surface cleaner attachments due to a laceration hazard.  Model # on recall was AEZ231022.
  On July 24, 2012 I purchased a Model # AEZ31022 EZ Cleaner attachment from a wholesale outlet on Ebay. The unit was listed as " used " (open box) with all parts etc.  When the item arrived it appeared to be in "like new Condition",  no signs of damage to plastic dome top and all metal fittings tight and in order.  I didn't get around to field testing the item until last week.
   I hooked my [REDACTED] gasoline powered pressure washer up to the attachment and started in to cleaning my flat ,broom- finished, concrete patio.  In about 10 minutes the attachment had done a teriffic job of cleaning about a 6-8 square foot area ,gliding over the surface as smooth as silk.  Suddenly, with out a warning,  and no where near any obstruction, the unit gave a shutter and self destructed.
   One of the spray arms had detached and shattered through the all plastic top dome. I am happy to report there  were no injuries or property damage, but plastic from the shattered top flew more that 150 feet, and it took an hour of searching to recover the wayward spray arm & nozzle.
   I have a healthy respect for pressure washers, and had carefully gone over the attachment and my pressure washer before starting out. Wearing work pants ,shoes and safety glasses proved to be a smart way to go.
   The instruction sheet lists Techtronic Industries North America, Inc in Anderson, SC as the manufacturer, not Homelite?   The instruction sheet shows a date of 11-24-09 (Rev:01)
    Have there been any other reports on this model (AEZ31022) EZ Clean ? This model number did not appear on July 2011 Recall List?
justification: The incident involved equipment failure but resulted in no injuries or property damage, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as the issue was unexpected but not common.

incident_description: primo flavor station home soda maker machine. The bottles that come with the unit are not vented, If you leave soda made in the bottle with the top on it will explode. The first time it happened I was asleep and the bottle was on my nightstand, I was woken by loud boom the sounded like gunfire. The top flew up and hit the ceiling, the bottle flew across the room. I called the company to see if I was using it incorrectly, I was told the bottles are not vented and change in temp from cold when it was made to room temp causes pressure in the bottle because they are non vented tops. Knowing this I continue to vent the bottle myself as I am using them, however today I was driving and it happened again after I had just vented the bottle like I was instructed. It exploded all over my car, thankfully I was stopped and was not hit by the flying cap, I have learned always point the cap away from me at all times. I worry someone will be injured because the cap is very forceful then it comes off.
justification: The incident describes forceful explosions of the bottle cap causing property damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The repeated occurrences despite precautions suggest a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
My front loading GE washer wbvh6240fww started making a lot of noise and smoke started coming out. This is a fire hazard that should be recalled. 

I tried calling GE Answer center and they told me I had to pay 79.95 to have a certified technician come and diagnose their faulty product.

Not only they put in danger my life, they want me to pay to have the appliance checked.

I want them to be aware that their products are defective before there are any injuries.
justification: The washer produced smoke, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high given the reported defect.

incident_description:
I had a new Goodman furnace installed in October 2006.  In December 2010 a motor had to be replaced.  Now April 2012, I once again have had to call for repair and this time it involves the replacement of the mother board and heat exchanger as the unit is registering unacceptable carbon monoxide levels.  I have made the decision to replace the entire unit with another brand as opposed to fixing the problems, which would cost me almost as much as an entirely new furnace.

THIS BRAND OF FURNACE IS JUNK!!!  AND IT IS UNACCEPTABLE THAT I HAVE TO REPLACE A UNIT THAT WAS LESS THAN 6 YEARS OLD!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!11
justification: The furnace had unacceptable carbon monoxide levels, posing a potential health hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Fire hazard:  I was issued a Verizon eco-charge suitable for my mobile device. It is called Verizon Wireless ECO Micro-USB Wall Charger for [REDACTED] or Other Devices with Micro USB Charging Port. 

It worked fine for a few months and then suddenly started smoking. I unplugged it. If I had been away from my office for more than a few minutes, my office could have caught on fire. 

Other people have had the same experience, based on amazon.com reviews:  
http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B004Z1WXW8/ref=cm_cr_mts_prod_img
justification: The charger started smoking, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: wher e the vacuum cleaner lifts off n  there is a plug that melted and almost started fire
justification: The plug melted and almost started a fire, indicating an incident with potential for harm but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Our LG Gas dryer started to leak gas into our home when it was not in use.  Kind of scary.  We had it fixed.  The valve assembly failed and needed to be replaced.  Not sure if this is a widespread problem.
justification: Gas leak poses a potential hazard but was fixed without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: The saw is a 10" craftsman table saw, model #137.218072 Serial # RPV3009.  This saw was purchased in January of 2012 and used only a handful of times prior to this accident.  The saw is sold by sears as a craftsman saw, however is made by Rexon Manufacturing in Taiwan.  During the normal course of ripping a board in half, I placed the board on the table top and while doing so placed both of my hands on the saws table top and it shocked me badly.  The shock knocked me to the floor and either the shock itself or my hitting my head on a concrete floor in my garage rendered my unconscious for a period of time.  I contacted Sears who advised me that they could do nothing about the saw and referred me to Rexon manufacturing. Rexon had an attorney, (a third party claims administrator in the US)  contact me via email however offered to do nothing about the serious malfunction of this saw.  At my request, Rexon did arrange for an engineer to come to my home to "check out the saw".  I requested this as no other action appeared to be taking place.  The engineer came to my home and did not check anything on the saw but instead only checked the wiring in my home and the outlet that supplied the saw to determine if the shock was the fault of my homes wiring.  This accident occurred nearly 4 months ago and no action has occurred to remedy this malfunction, replace the saw, investigate the cause,  or determine if this is a widespread problem with its.  To date, the saw is still in my garage and I do not even receive follow up email from Rexon's claim administrator.  I have since been diagnosed with sensorneural hearing loss in both of my ears and tinnittus resulting from severe shock/trauma caused by the accident.  This product, for one reason or another, is a massive safety concern for anyone using it.  Aside from being shocked, I could have just as easily been thrown into the cutting blade of this saw injuring me much worse than I was.
justification: The incident resulted in unconsciousness and diagnosed hearing loss, indicating significant injury.

incident_description:
Washing Machine:  30 minutes into the normal cycle, with a medium load.
Smoke alarm sounded, went to inspect and smoke was pouring out of the washing drum.
Heavy smoke accompanied by a strong chemical smell.
Clothes are possibly ruined, by an oily film and strong odor.
justification: Incident caused smoke and potential property damage (ruined clothes), but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My husband and I have a 2 year old Kenmore Front-Loading Automatic Washer, Model 796.  While on the spin cycle it began to smoke heavily filling my bathroom and the rest of our condo.  Accompanying the smoke was a strange metallic smell almost like burning rubber.  We have placed a service call to Sears but they won't come out for another week!  And, we have had to turn the circuit breaker off to the Washer to avoid a possible fire.  I have done some cursory research on the internet and this seems to be a common problem with the Kenmore Stackable units.  I wish we had known this before we bought it.
justification: The washer emitted smoke and a burning smell, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My nook charger was plugged into the wall and I noticed the USB end had melted.
justification: The charger melting is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My wife fell on a wrought iron railing and injured her arm and knee.  The step stool collapsed while she was standing on it.  This step stool is collapsable for storage.  The side locking hinge broke away from the stool.  The name of the product is E-Z FOLDZ, distributed by B&R Products, Denver, CO.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the arm and knee, warranting a severity level of 3. The step stool's failure suggests a possible design or manufacturing issue, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: Grill brush losing bristles within a month of purchase.  Third such grill brush and all three lost their bristles, which have the potential to stick to the grill and get stuck to food.
justification: The incident involves bristles falling off and potentially contaminating food, which is a hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description: electric smoke alarm caught fire
justification: The smoke alarm caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I have owned this charger for about five months.  Today the cord shorted out (visible sparks) and melted.  Near the charging tip a short developed.  No safty device stopped the shorting and melting of the cord.  The shorting continued for about ten seconds after the power was removed.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit and melting cord but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible (3) given the description of the event.

incident_description:
I have a Siemens Load Center Model # M1020MB1100F in my home. I have had to replace three breakers (all three were quad breakers) due to the spring clips on the back of them losing connection with the buss bar and arcing. This breaker box has aluminum bus bars. The most frequent  completely burned up the stab on the breaker box to the point it can not be used again. It also destroyed the breaker. I think this is directly related to the recall that I have read about but the recall does not list this breaker as one of concern.  I do believe that this is a concern worth checking into.
Thanks
justification: The incident involves repeated breaker failures and arcing, posing a fire hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
I was using my Shark Pocket Steam Mop model S3501-N as I normally do when I clean my floor when it stopped producing steam, I lifted the mop head off the floor to see what was going off and it exploded off, shooting about 5 feet across the room with a rush of hot steam and water, all over my hand and right at my dog. I got the beginning stages of a burn on my palm and pinkie, but nothing that would need an ER visit. Had my kids been in the room or my dog literally 6 inches to the right, we would have been in big trouble.
Once it was cooler, I looked closer at the head, none of the holes were clogged. I reattached the head, plugged it in with a new  and tried it again, same thing happened. I immediately looked online and saw many reports of the exact same problem with this particular model. I called Shark and they're sending out a replacement, but I'm afraid of the same problem occurring again with no warning.
justification: The incident caused burns to the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3), and the recurrence of the issue with the same model suggests the likelihood is high (4).

incident_description: Hand burn from handle (switch overheated) on a eureka upright bagless vacuum model 5893 avz.
justification: The description mentions a hand burn, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire Clothes Dryer had a fire in the control panel.  Fortunately, the fire self extinguished with no damage to my laundry room.  I had smelled an odd smell and went down to the basement laundry room to investigate.
The dryer is ruined.
Frigidaire Model #LEQ215ESO
(Item purchased Winter of 2008 from Lowe's, Seattle, WA)
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dryer control panel but self-extinguished without injury or property damage beyond the dryer itself.

incident_description: Bosch aqua star tankless water heater has faulty sensor. Results in water tempratures fluxuating between scalding hot and cold resulting in potential scalding injuries.
justification: Faulty sensor causes fluctuating water temperatures, posing a scalding risk, which is an injury hazard.

incident_description: When using vacuum area behind and below power switch became extremely hot causing plastic to melt/smoke. Cord also became hot. This happened in less than 10 minutes from when I started using the vacuum. There was no fire or property damage. Plastic did get hot enough to burn skin.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic and potential for skin burns, indicating a risk of injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description: CO incident with injury to young children. Local investigators suspect leak and possible product defect associated with vent pipe to gas boiler.
justification: The incident involves injury to young children due to a CO leak, indicating a severity level of 3. The mention of a possible product defect suggests a likelihood of recurrence, rated as 4 (likely).

incident_description: Vornado space heater was being used in a bathroom.  It began to spark and smoke.  It was turned off and the plug was pulled from the electrical outlet.  Investigation revealed a badly corroded wire in the wiring harness had shorted and started to burn.  There were no injuries, and fast action prevented a fire.
justification: The space heater sparked and smoked due to a corroded wire, but no injuries occurred and a fire was prevented by quick action.

incident_description: I own at GE front load washer, Model Number WBVH 5300 K0WW.  I have had problems with mold 6 months after it was installed.  I had a GE service specialist come out and all the recommended was a "[REDACTED]" front load cleaner.  I was given instruction to wipe the interior of my machine with a bleach soaked towel after every use, leave the door open all the time when not it use, and to run a clean cycle once a week.  None of this has helped, it very incontinent and time consuming. More importantly the mold is getting worse.  The GE customer service refuses to help.  This is becoming a health issue as we have notice more "cold" and "allergy" like symptoms is our children over the past 6 months.  Our clothes and towels have a noticeable odor.
justification: The presence of mold and associated health symptoms in children indicates an injury (severity level 3). The ongoing issue and worsening condition suggest a likely recurrence (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description:
When I went out to start my generator, I noticed that the gas had leaked for the fuel shutoff gas housing. I've been trying to locate a shutoff valve to replace it due to the storm in the gulf. (Isaac)
I won't be able to use the generator due to the leak from the housing and no one seems to carry the fuel shutoff valve.
justification: Gas leak from the generator's fuel shutoff housing poses a hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Was using Home Touch portable steamer (item PS-150) when a large amount of water came through the hose shooting at neck and face. A burn was left on neck. Steamer left a pool of water on the ground and also sprayed door that was in opposite direction.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the neck, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the event.

incident_description: On several occasions the Ritetemp vent free gas heater thermostat has caused the gas to come out of the burner without igniting even though the pilot was burning.  3 times I was not in the room at the time and when I returned to the room it was filled with gas fumes - the pilot was burning in each occasion.  On several other occasions I was present - sometimes the burner lit with a woooofffff.  Other times I turned heater off by lowering the thermostat then when I turned it back up it lit correctly.  It is certainly an unsafe situation and I feel lucky my house didn't explode.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation with gas fumes filling the room, posing a risk of explosion, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I bought a garage door from HOME DEPOT IN ROCKFOR, ILLINOIS. I had it installed by them, along with a Genie opener. 20 days ago, after working perfectly for 4 years, a broom handle got in the way, usually if a small object or any incidental object,even a spider web, gets it the way, any pressure it meets, the door reverses. This time it made a horrible churning noise. I was in the garage, am permanently handicapped and got the bright idea of going, and removing the broom handle that usually any pressure or object it touches as I said it reverses, but this was a frightful noise and sight. the door was going sideways, it was pulling towards the right, roller flying all over, the right railing twisting like a pretzel.. tried to put my arm to hold it up, and got a hematoma from my wrist to my elbow, then tried waving my foot in front of the eye, and the door kept grinding horribly and coming down. My doctor told me I was crazy, I could have fallen and got crushed, and I live alone .. who would find me, but dead. The lady who has been stringing me along, a woman who was nice as pie for 20 days told me today, you never almost got killed, as if she knew me or my situation, my doctor does. and she had seen pictures of the damage to my arm done the first day. I was not seeking any legal recompense, I just wanted my rail fixed so I could get in and out of my house in some comfort since it pains me to walk, i NEED 3 SUP.BELTSTO WALK have an impact fracture on my right wrist, and a torn shoulder, and now the crushed left arm. Since she sent her boys over to make sure it was not her fault her attitude changed . .from fairy to witch of the North! Go get whoever sold me the Genie .. well they brought it with them, it mist have been acquired by their company. Incidentally, the handle was not in the railing it was across the path,!
justification: The incident resulted in a hematoma and other injuries, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such severe mechanical failures are not common.

incident_description:
I would like to report an iron.  yes the plain kind that she used iron your clothes. The brand is shark the model number is G1408Z. What has happened is that the electrical cord has broken just past the court support and is a shock hazard. It's obvious that the cord material was/is very defective. We have owned this iron for 2 maybe 3 years and like most people don't iron  a lot.  my wife is careful not to put a lot of stress on the chord joint using an extension cord to keep it from pinching.

I don't know if you want to hear the sort of things but I thought I would put my $.02 worth in on this defective product. Besides being defective it is also dangerous because the cord broke in exposing the copper wires within.

Thank you [REDACTED]
justification: The exposed copper wires in the iron's cord present a shock hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Purchased a Eureka AS1000A Upright vacuum cleaner from Walmart. 

After less than a week of using the vacuum, I tried to use attachments, and attempted to lift the vacuum to get wand to higher area to use on top of chair and drapes. The vacuum was extremely hot to the touch around the bottom front, and when I lifted it a bit to reach the higher area, the bottom of the vacuum burned a hole in my upholstery. I filed a complain with Eureka/Electrolux customer service and was told that the following Warning is in product manual:

ÃÂ Do not place vacuum cleaner on furniture or stairs as the brush roll may cause damage. Use
extra care when cleaning stairs. Place vacuum cleaner on floor with the handle in storage
position while using attachments.

This is very helpful information.However, having a product that can easily burn your skin and furniture poses a hazard and danger. This is not acceptable, and a product recall should be considered.  Elderly individuals and children can be easily burned by this vacuum.

Company claims that I did not use it as intended/recommended. A child putting through their head through crib slats that are too wide, is also unintended use. 

I would like the CPSC to look into this particular product to ensure all precautions are in place to avoid injury to children and others due to the design flaw of the spinning brush continuing to spin 
and getting extremely hot while using attachments.
justification: The vacuum caused property damage and posed a burn hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Using Maytag Neptune Dryer model no. MDE9700AYW Serial No (S) 12278380GE yr 2005. Using on sensor dry mode smelt fire it was coming from the dryer. The electrical wires from the dryer were smoldering down to the plug! called maytag. They are sending service tech but because it is not under warranty they cannot fix only get a free evaluation for me to have fixed. I m thinking it was a good thing I was Home!  There was not lint not vents clogged. I have read up alot on this dryer and this is a common complaint of many consumers and there has been no recalls! I could've had some serious damage to my home or children if I had not been home to smell the fire. Very upset consumer. replacement cost is above $1000.00 and I am A single mother of two. Dryers should not be catching on fire for no reason. The dryer is very clean lightly used and no lint clogged anywhere.
justification: The incident involved smoldering electrical wires, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The description indicates this is a common complaint, suggesting a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
Purchased a Utilitech model 0320778 500 Watt portable halogen work light from Lowes.  Assembled in accordance with manufacturer's instructions.  Set unit on ground in accordance with manufacturer's instructions.  Used in driveway in dry conditions.  Approximately 2 minutes after plugging the unit it, the protective glass lens shattered explosively.  Small, sharp shards of glass were thrown outwards from the device.  I was approximately 4 feet away and was struck by the glass.  I received minor cuts in two places.  Glass shards were very difficult to clean up because of their small size and their "sharpness".  Most of the lens remained intact but cracked like automotive safety glass.  I don't know if the glass lens was defective or whether the entire design is defective. The unit generates alot of heat.

My specific concerns are the force with which the glass shattered, the distance the shards were thrown, and the "sharpness" of the glass residue.

I tried to contact the company to report the problem, but nobody answered their phone.

I have no dog in this fight.  I'll bring it back to Lowes and get a refund.  I sent a note to Lowes and told them that I thought they are stocking a dangerous product.  Maybe you can get them to pull the product too.

Thanks and regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in minor cuts from glass shards, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific conditions described but lack of broader data on frequency.

incident_description:
Our On-Base Fire Department responded to a fire in an enclosed oven. The resident had turned on the "self cleaning" feature but inadvertently forgot there was a pan of grease in the oven. The heat inside the oven ignited the grease, the resident tried to open the oven but could not due to the safety latching feature of the oven. 
Upon arrival of the responding fire crews, none of the smoke detectors (Kidde Nighthawk KN-COSM-1B) in the residence were sounding, despite heavy smoke. The oven was disconnected and relocated to the exterior of the residence. Afterward, fire crews went through the house and tested every detector by pushing the test buttons, and every detector worked (sounded) at that time.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the smoke detectors failed to activate during the event but were found functional afterward.

incident_description:
I HAVE A SEARS KENMORE DEHUMIDIFIER MODEL 580.54501400 PURCHASED MAY 26, 2004 FOR $159.99 FROM THE LOCAL SEARS.  I CONSTANTLY MONITOR THE HUMIDITY IN MY BASEMENT.  LAST WINTER, THE UNIT DID NOT SEEM TO WORK PLUS IT  DID SEEM TO BE QUITE HOT ON TOP.   I THOUGHT THE ROOM TEMPERATURE WAS TOO LOW.  I PURCHASED A DIFFERENT BRAND, LARGER UNIT.  AS SPRING BROUGHT WARMER TEMPS, I DECIDED TO RETRY THE SEARS UNIT.  AGAIN, I KEPT A CLOSE WATCH TO ITS PROGRESS.  GOOD THING, AS ON ONE TRIP TO THE BASEMENT, THE UNIT WAS SO HOT ON THE TOP, I COULD NOT TOUCH IT.  WITHIN SECONDS, I SMELLED SOMETHING LIKE IT WAS BURNING INSIDE.  I QUICKLY SHUT IT OFF AND UNPLUGGED IT.  I KEPT THE UNIT TO RECYCLE THE PARTS THIS SUMMER WHEN I FOUND OTHER SEARS BAD UNITS ON THE NET.

I THINK SEARS SHOULD REFUND MY INVESTMENT ALONG WITH THOSE OTHER UNITS.  OTHER CONSUMERS NEED TO CHECK THEIR UNITS AND FILE A REPORT LIKE I HAVE.  THANK YOU U.S.CPSC.
justification: The dehumidifier overheated and emitted a burning smell, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Smell of gas and burning metal in laudry room.   Open dryer to investigate.  Touched black spot and received severe burn (instant blistering and malformation of skin).  Appears to be very similar to similar recall involving Kenmore Elite Dryer 796.90512900.  Recall does not include our dryer...it should.
justification: Severe burn with instant blistering and skin malformation indicates an injury, warranting a severity level of 3. The similarity to a recalled model suggests this issue is likely to recur, hence an occurrence likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
In June, 2010, I received a Craftsman air compressor (#00915215000
Mfr. model #15215) as a gift.  I have used it very sparingly at my "up north" home. It has been used less than a dozen times all told.  My son needed it (July 4th) to inflate a tow tube for the boat.  when he turned it on he was shocked so hard that he collapsed to the ground - even the GFI didn't trip.  My electrician friend came over and, not believing me, tried it and got the exact same reaction.  the then put his meter on it and told me that the circuitry was running thru the metal outside parts.  When I contacted Sears repair, their only concern was that I did not purchase the "insurance policy" for mechanical failure.

I am concerned that some one will get killed.  Both my son, and the electrician were barefoot, on the cement basement floor.  If a person is not going to ground, they are safe, but if they are "grounded", they are in mortal danger.  Thank God the floor was dry!  

Sears, obviously needs to be prodded in to action.  If you need my correspondence with them, email me and I will forward it to you.
justification: The incident caused severe electric shocks to two individuals, indicating a clear injury risk, but no death occurred.

incident_description: the iron has a gap between the soleplate and the body of the iron.  A belt loop from a pair of pants became entangled and I was burned trying to extricate it.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, which qualifies as a severity level 3. The likelihood is considered possible (3) given the described scenario.

incident_description:
A Fisher & Paykel model DE04 US2 electric clothes dryer Serial Number SZ713977A burned up in a bathroom laundry 8/6/12.  The dryer was purchased new 5/18/2001.  The fire started when the dryer was in operation.  The power cord was disconnected and fire destroyed the dryer causing considerable smoke damage to the bathroom laundry.    Apparently what burned was lint.  The dryer had been kept in very clean condition. 
An insurance adjuster estimated cleanup damages at $4000.

The fire department personnel discovered charred wires and melted plastic casings inside the housing unit of the dryer. Fortunately, the circuit breaker to the unit was tripped because of this and no flames were discovered. Model #WSM2700DAWWW Serial #ZL603803W
