incident_description: The plug-in base of a motion sensor lighting system caught on fire all of a sudden. I happened to be around that outlet and husband was able to stop the fire from spreading. Otherwise, our house would have been burnt down.
justification: The plug-in base caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Husqvarna model K950 power saw.  While using power saw to cut rebar above firefighters head, gas cap  appears to have come off spilling gas on ground and fire fighter. Sparks ignited fumes which in turn ignited fire fighter burning him on face, hands, and abdomen. At no time was gas cap touched or was product refueled prior to incident. Gas cap appears to be weak and no safety mechanism on cap itself to prevent from coming off. This problem was found to have happened before, industry wide, after further investigation.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the firefighter's face, hands, and abdomen, indicating an injury (severity 3). The problem has occurred before industry-wide, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: the water heaters ,were not kicking off after the valves were shut off ,causing hot water to back up,where cold water goes in,the water was so hot it melted the pipes and bursted the water pipes.these were set at luke warm ,tempuratures ,We had three,they all did the same thing over a two year period.
justification: The incident caused damage to the water heaters and pipes but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Over the past two and a half years I have replaced 6 light switches in my home. After having replaced two in the past, today I flipped a switch, there was an arc and the lights went out.  A breaker was blown.  I removed the cover plate and found there were two bad switches in this box of 4 switches.  Curious I removed a cover plate in an adjacent room that was not turning the exterior flood lights on.  I had tought the bulbs were burned out.  I found a bad switch there too and the hot wire had backed out of the friction fit hole.

The failure mode is the same in all the switches.  The plastic back shell of the switch propogates a crack until the switch falls apart and the internal componnents are displaced. 

Made in China. UL listed mark. Manufacturers mark is PS. Part no M495B.  SPST 15A 120V for CU or CU clad wire.  Bar Code SKU 85007 66013.  Has 660-WG on label below SKU.
justification: The incident involved electrical failures and a blown breaker, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I'm am writing you regarding a safety concern I've become aware of with the gun locks provided through the Project ChildSafe program. As I understand it, the City of Canyon Lake, California  received a donation of the Project Child Safe gun locks through the Riverside County Sheriff's Office. A portion of these locks were then donated to the [REDACTED]. These locks were then intended to be purposed to assist with the Quagga Mussel Inspection Program as a means to physically lock a contaminated boat to its trailer to prevent the boat from launching within the lake. Upon inspection of the approximately 60 locks we received it was discovered that a large amount of these locks were malfunctioning and would open without the use of the key. A small amount of vibration or tapping on the frame of the lock would cause the locking mechanism to jar loose and the cable to run free. 
My concerns do not lie in the area of what the locks were now intending to be used for, but for the original purpose of securing a firearm from endangering a child. I currently serve as [REDACTED] and I have extensive training in firearms safety and responsibility. I own several guns which I store responsibly in my home to prevent my children from accessing them as required by law. I believe that proper education is the first and foremost deterrent to children improperly handling firearms, and that a dependable means of locking the weapon is critical to ensuring this.   After seeing 1 in 5 of these locks fail to maintain a secure connection, I would never trust nor allow any of my firearms to be secured with these locks. I am urging you to take a hard look into this claim to find the cause of the malfunction. I think the purpose of this program is commendable and worthwhile, I would regret for the reputations of the agencies involved to become tarnished by just one of these gun locks failing in the most unfortunate of circumstances. 
After conducting some research on the subject it seems this is not the first time the National Shooting Sports Foundation have experienced this type of malfunction with a gun lock they have provided. I found a recall notice from the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission Release # 01-078 which details a recall on a similar product on February 07, 2001. I hope this will not continue to be an issue with the locks they are currently providing and I trust that they verified the quality of this product before issuing it as a replacement for the previous failed gun locks.  
I am available to assist with any information you may need of me and I have several examples of gun locks that have failed which I can forward to you for inspection.  

Sincerely,
[REDACTED] 
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning gun locks that could fail to secure firearms, posing a potential risk, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
I have been using a Prince Lionheart Wipes Warmer #9002 for our new baby since October 2011.  On July 21st, 2012 Guests in my house noticed the GFCI outlets in our second bathroom no longer worked.  I investigated and determined that the GFCI fuse had popped, and would not reset.  I checked to make sure everything was unplugged from the GFCI circuit and then it would reset. The Prince Lionheart Wipes Warmer was unplugged from a GFCI protected outlet at this time.

Shortly after Plugging the Wipes Warmer back in, the GFCI outlet tripped again.  At the time, the only thing plugged into the GFCI outlets were a small lamp on the bathroom counter and the Wipes Warmer.  Upon removing the power plug form where it plugged into the Wipes Warmer, I observed water in the DC power connection plug.  I then emptied the Wipes Warmer of baby wipes, and turned it upside down over my sink.  A significant amount of water (maybe 10-20mLs) ran out of the device.  It was rust colored, so it had obviously been accumulating for some time, as well as been in contact with metal inside the Wipes Warmer itself. 

It was obvious to me without opening the Wipes Warmer to look at the circuitry itself that the device had filled up with water, apparently either entering through small cracks in the wipe holder itself, or through condensation dripping through the holes where the lid of the device connects to the body of the device.

Without a GFCI outlet protection, I am very concerned that either the Wipes Warmer would have shorted out, perhaps creating a fire, or represented an electrical shock hazard to myself or my wife as we removed a wipe from the warmer.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning device that could have posed a fire or shock hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was steam mopping my floors with the product, and my older child let my one year old through the baby gate.  When I saw him coming towards me I stopped mopping and put the handle upright, reached to get him a cookie off the counter.  He slid on some water as he came towards me and his toes slid under the edge of the steam mop.  I grabbed him up immediately, and ran cool water over his toes, but the damage was done.  He sustained 2nd and 3rd degree burns to both feet.  After a trip to his pediatrician, then a pediatric surgeon in a neighboring town, we were sent to a burn center in Augusta, Georgia (about 4 hours away).  [REDACTED] (my son) was admitted and had surgery to debride his burns and apply gamma-overlying silver grafts.  He was bandaged, redressed, and assessed once a week, requiring multiple drives back.  He has handled this ordeal better than his parents, we are thankful that his grafts did well, he does have  keloid scarring on one toe, the others fared better.  We are unsure of the nerve damage he has sustained, but are hopeful to not require any further treatment.  The safety feature of the steam vac is that the steam stops when the handle is upright- clearly, that did not function properly, and the warnings in the manufacturer book are not adequate in my opinion.  It never occurred to me that anything could slide under the edge, since it appears flush with the ground until close inspection.  I just hope the warning labels can be adjusted to adequately warn future consumers.  I do not want this traumatic event to happen to any other child or family.
justification: The child sustained 2nd and 3rd degree burns requiring surgery and ongoing medical treatment, indicating a severe injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was using her vacuum cleaner and the handle became extremely the hot. The consumer stated that she was using the vacuum cleaner for approximately 5 minutes. The consumer stated that she was using it on a carpet surface. She stated that there was nothing stuck in the vacuum to make it overheat. 

The consumer stated that when it became hot she immediately turned off and let it cool down. The consumer stated that it took approximately 30 minutes for the handle to cool off. The consumer that she did not see any smoke of sparks, she stated that it only becomes extremely hot. The consumer stated that she used the vacuum in other surfaces and the same incident happened. 

The consumer stated that she was not injured. 

The consumer stated that she had been experiencing this issue for approximately 6 months. 

The consumer stated that she researched online this particular model and many reports are available online stating that they were experiencing the same issue of the handle becoming extremely hot. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that they had never heard of the problem. The consumer stated that she should take it to one of their company authorized repair locations. She stated that the representative informed her that she would have to pay for the repairs (amount of the payment was unknown). 

The consumer stated that she contacted the local repair place for the company and they informed her that they were very familiar with the problem and that they had replaced and repair many of this model vacuums. 

The consumer believes this product should be investigated due to the burning and fire hazard that it poses.
justification: The incident involved the vacuum handle becoming extremely hot, but no injury occurred. The issue is recurring and widely reported, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: While washing a load of towels the washing machine started making a horrible thumping noise.  I  stood beside it for a few minutes and just figured it was off balance.  When the cycle finished, I opened the door to get the towels out and a huge piece of glass slid out on top of my foot.  Luckily I had just dropped some other dirty laundry on the floor and my foot was under some of it, other wise it could have easily sliced right through my ankle.  This is VERY dangerous and VERY sharp!! Maytag should replace this piece and issue a recall if this has happened to anyone else.  We don't even put tennis shoes in the washer so I am at a loss as to what could have caused it to crack/break unless it was the temp of the water, and considering we shower in it, that would be ridiculous.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous piece of glass but no actual injury occurred due to protective clothing.

incident_description:
Subject: Amana washing machine fire

July 6,2012
I attempted to report online. However, very difficult with your website to put in purchase date over 10 years. I have an Amana washing machine purchased May 18, 2001 from [REDACTED], True Value in Blue Ball, Pa. [REDACTED] installed the washing machine in my home. machine lid and smoke came out. I unplugged machine.
I believe I had electrical fire.

incident_description:
The consumer says the unit has a strong odor that is making her sick.  She didn't know until today that the machine creates mold.  This is according to a representative of the retailer.  Her brother went online who saw numerous reports of the same thing happening.  She was told she has to keep cleaning the drawer with mold.  

She says that she cannot continue to do this as it effects her asthma.  The retailer is telling her that she needs a cleaning agent along with the washer.  The consumer says it is wrong to knowingly sell this machine to someone.

incident_description: Bought a new Master Forge grill brush at Lowes on 6/22/2012. Have used perhaps 12 times since. Last night I grilled two steaks. I felt a sting in my mouth. Inspected and pulled a brass bristle out of my tongue. There was monor bleeding. Traced it to the bristles on this brush. Later found another under my bridge. I am worried and found another report on your site after googling for master forge grill brush. LG Sourcing is apparently a division of Lowes. Same address in North Carolina. This product should be pulled. I hope I did not swallow other bristles. My husband apparently is OK.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injury (a bristle stuck in the tongue with minor bleeding), which qualifies as severity level 3.

incident_description: The second time using my shark steam mop, it quit steaming and all of a sudden exploded with scorching water coming out the sides and onto my feet where it left blisters.
justification: The incident caused blisters, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
At around 5:00 am, the downstairs area was found to be flooded with about a half-inch of water.  Upon inspection of the women's restroom it appears that the toilet tank pressure vessel ruptured.  The toilet was not in use at the time, and does not see heavy usage.  No personnel were injured, however the tank was destroyed along with the vessel scattering shards up to 15 feet away.  

After looking up the recall information, this is a different series than is currently under recall for the same issue.  This is the Flushmate Model M101526F, Serial # 050498F011838.

This unit is located in a Fire Station along with 8 other of the same model from varying years 1998-2006. This is the first catastrophic failure noted although a few have been replaced over the years.
justification: No personnel were injured, but there was property damage and a hazardous situation with scattered shards.

incident_description:
Caller has iron she inherited from her aunt and that was new in condition.

She was ironing on June 28th, 2012, sat the iron down to turn the fabric when flames shot out from area where cord meets the iron.

The flames were possible one and a half inches high.

She immediately unplugged the iron and the flames extinguished.
She estimates that seeing the flames and unplugging the cord took possibly 15 seconds or less.
Guide for cord is charred black and handle is cracked..

Caller has not contacted manufcturer yet but does intend to contact them.
She thought that she was calling them when she contacted the CPSC hotline.

Caller would ask that the iron be replaced at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved flames and damage to the iron but no injury was reported, indicating a moderate likelihood of similar incidents occurring.

incident_description:
The consumer says the heating element in the back would be fire red even when the unit is in a low setting.  Two days ago her outlet was smoldering, melting and smoking.  She says that her wall was blackened as if ready to catch on fire.

She contacted the manufacturer yesterday who said it is not under warranty.  They offered to send out a technician for a fee.  Her brother is an electrician who came out yesterday who tested the outlet where the unit is plugged and the outlet.   

Her brother said it was so hot when he opened it up it was if it were on fire.
justification: The incident involved smoldering, melting, and smoking of an outlet, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that while the fan was in use, the metal arm that connects the fan blade to the base of the fan snapped in half.  The fan blade projected across the room.  Fortunately no one was hit because this could have caused serious injuries.  The blade landed against the drapery on the wall.

My son [REDACTED] (16), was in the bed at the time.

6/2012  The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that someone would contact her.
7/9/12  The caller contacted the manufacturer again and she was informed that the fan would be replaced but that the incident was rare and there was nothing else that could be done.
The caller feels that the failure of the fan is a safety hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The fan blade projected across the room but no one was hit, indicating an incident with no injury. The manufacturer described the incident as rare.

incident_description:
GE High Efficiency Washer Model WCVH6260HWW Serial Number AM2050247 installed new August of 2007 was reported to GE Consumer Relations as a product safety issue for fires.
A case number [REDACTED] was opened by GE and later disregarded as an out of warranty product despite having a fire risk.

The fire risk occured when after only 5 years the basket bearing failed.  This resulted in the basket tumbler unit to rock back and forth.   The rubber gasket between the washer basket tumbler and access door heats up from friction during the spin cycle and begins to smoke thus presenting a fire risk.   If the consumer is not home to monitor wash cycles the fire could spread without consumer knowledge while they are away from the home or sleeping.

The estimated cost to repair the washer was $1300 and provided by a GE appliance repair service (Chambers Services, Inc. 1102 1/2 MacArthur Ave., Bloomington, IL 61704 PH [REDACTED] GE was only willing to provide a minimal discount on another GE unit and was not concerned about fire risks.

The washer will be scrapped on 8/17/2012 and replaced by a non-GE made appliance.
justification: The incident describes a fire risk due to mechanical failure, but no actual fire or injury is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that there was a defect on the dryer that the lint goes inside the dryer. The consumer stated that is 2008 she had to contacted the retailer and they sent out a technician to clean out the lint from inside the machine. 

The consumer stated that on 07-02-2012 (est.) she decided to contact the retailer again because she smell smoke coming from the dryer. The consumer stated that the technician went to service the dryer on 07/12/2012 and he informed her that the lint was still going inside the machine. The consumer stated that the technician informed her that she would need to have someone service the dryer every 6 months to clean the lint that was going inside the dryer. 

The consumer stated that the lint inside seems to be burning and it does not matter on what cycle she uses the dryer. The consumer stated her clothes come out of the dryer smelling like smoke. 

The consumer stated that this product needs to be investigated because it poses a fire hazard. 

The consumer stated that she will be contacting the manufacturer to file a complaint.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard due to lint accumulation, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I read over the instructions given with the Nostalgic Cotton Candy machine and I proceeded to use the machine as directed.  I turned the machine on, let it heat up first, turned the machine off to pour the sugar in just as directed, leveled the sugar by spinning the machine by hand and turned it on.  When I turned the machine back on sugar flew out every where.  When the sugar flew out it burnt my daughters face but the worst spot was about an inch under her eye.  This was 3-4 days ago and the burn still has not healed completely.  Even after telling the company what happened and telling them it could easily happen again to someone else they didn't seem to care.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the daughter's face, which has not healed completely after several days, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: We were given the electric heater for Christmas 2006.  Today, my wife smelled a strong burning plastic smell!  She found the electric heater with a big hole burned in the top plastic housing with flames shooting out higher than the toilet seat.  If she had not been home, the heater could have stared the entire house on fire!  It was just inches from a wooden cabinet that had hair spray, alcohol and other flammable items in it.
justification: The incident involved flames and potential for a house fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
74 yr old caller is reporting that she is unable to read directions/warnings on label of sealing product purchased for concrete/brick.
She used this product inside her office to seal a wall where mortar is coming down.

Caller wears glasses, states that she can usually read most containers warnings or directions but could not read them on this one gallon plastic container because the type is so small.

She believes that she may be alright but would like to report while requesting that labeling be required to be larger.

She has not been seen by any medical professional, does not feel ill.

She spoke with the manufacturer today, July 23rd, 2011, did not obtain the name of the representative she was speaking with the representative said she would note and tell her people.
  
Caller has Asthma and hopes that she didn't do any harm to herself.
justification: Caller reports no injury or illness, but there was an incident involving difficulty reading product labels.

incident_description: I have a whole house Generac Guardian generator with a GTS 12 breaker load center.  This uses a Generac Transfer Switch Part # C2237.  At 4:45am on 8/14/12 i was awoken by a very loud pop from the basement and my fire alarm sounding.  The power had gone out over night and the generator ran all night without problem, when the power came back on at 4:45 the switch must have failed and overloaded causing it to burst into flames.  I opened the smokey extremely hot box to flames and melting wires.  The flames would not just blow out, i had to use a fire extinguisher.  I contacted Generac customer service and was informed it is not longer under warranty, "Sorry".  My house could have burnt down and my family could have died, "Sorry" does not seem to cut it.
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant damage to equipment, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Found screws loose on gas valve for Weil McLain Ultra230 gas heating boiler.  There was a previous Recall Alert on this model boiler on MAy 13, 2003.  This boiler was manufactured in 2007.  I notified Weil McLain tech support of what I found but they seemed uninterested since it did not fall into the time frame of the earlier recall.
justification: Loose screws on a gas valve pose a potential hazard, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: black plastic clamps after clamping within minutes will break , shattering and send pieces flying. This happened on several clamps. Luckily I was not standing near them.
justification: The incident involved clamps breaking and sending pieces flying, but no injury occurred as the person was not near them.

incident_description: I have a frigidaire affinity front load washer. rubber gasket and area where detergent goes in constantly have black mold growing and accumulating. i have 2 small children at home and feel like we are constantly brething in and wearing mold now because its so hard to get rid of. based on my research it seems as though i am not the only one with this issue. its clearly a big problem. they design flaws are putting everyone at risk for serious illness.
justification: The presence of mold poses a health risk, but no specific injury or death is reported. The issue is described as common, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Several months ago, the Kenmore Dehumidifier model #580.54501400 (50 pint capacity) started to start and stop more frequently. Then it the extension cord circuit breaker began to pop everytime we used it. I replaced the extension cord. 

Two days ago, the unit began making a strange smell, like ozone and burnt plastic. My wife felt the unit and it was extremely hot to the touch. We turned it off, fearing a fire.

I saw that a similar unit (Kenmore model #580.53509300, made in 2003) was the subject of a recall. We bought our model in 2004 or so. I suspect it is very similar to the recalled model and may be suffering the same product defect that prompted the recall.

We believe the unit is dangerous and likely defective. There should be an investigation and the unit should be recalled if there is in fact widespread defects -- people could die and houses could burn down otherwise.

I still have the unit, as well as photos.
justification: The unit was extremely hot to the touch, smelled of ozone and burnt plastic, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Purchased a Chef Master Grill Brush for the restaurant 2 weeks ago...the bristles started falling out , they ended up in food cooked on the charbroiler....was served to 2 customers who notified us and we found the source.
justification: Bristles from the grill brush ended up in food served to customers, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore Dehumidifier 580.5435.1500 got very hot started smelling burning checked the compressor which was too hot to touch. Turned off and removed from service
justification: The dehumidifier got very hot and smelled burning, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(7/17/12012) The consumer's box fan had been sitting on the box spring to the bed for approximately the entire day (exact length of time unknown). While in another room he and his wife began to smell strange odors, as if something were burning. As the consumer and his wife walked around their home and opened doors, his wife located the room with the fan in it and yelled out fire. They immediately grabbed the fire extinguisher and also threw water on the fan to put the flames out. When the consumer went downstairs to shut off his breakers, he saw that they had already tripped (wondering why the fan caught fire if the breakers were down). 

Several items from the home such as the fan, bedding, curtains, blinds and the carpet were burned due to the fire.  The consumer placed those items outside.

The fire department was also called shortly after the incident. When they arrived, they examined the home and advised the consumers that there were no other hot spots in the room.
 
The manufacturer was not contacted, but will be contacted later.
 
The fan model was listed in Release#11-183, but his fan was dated 2000-2001, which was prior to the ones dated in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, as confirmed by the fire department's assessment.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his dehumidifier was on.  He smelled an odor of smoke and discovered that the unit was emitting smoke, which had triggered his smoke detectors.  He immediately unplugged it and place it outside to prevent further damages.  He noticed that the capacitor had melted, which he believes prevented the unit from safely turning off.

The consumer feels that he is experiencing similar problems of Release # 02-096.  

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.


The consumer feels that that this dehumidifier is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The dehumidifier emitted smoke and triggered smoke detectors, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The product is a household cooling fan that mounts on top a pole held by a pedestal on the floor.  The AC power cord runs up the interior of this pole, which is made of 2 telescoping steel tubes.  In my sample of the product, and the upper tube has a sharp flake of steel at the top that could cut through the plastic insulation of the power cord.  This flake of steel is probably a scrap of leftover welding rod.

I have not assembled nor operated this product.  No injuries have resulted.
justification: The description indicates a potential hazard (sharp steel flake) that could damage the power cord, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I was a first time user of Alpine Roof Paint Semi Gloss, when after applied on a metal roof, I slipped and fell off that roof and suffered serious head trauma, and shattered elbow.
The manufacturer states my failure to wear fall protection caused my fall, but as I explained to the retailer I had never painted a metal roof prior to the incident. Also, I was not a roofer nor had knowledge of the OSHA REQUIREMENTS.
I walked on this metal roof for 5 days preparing it for paint prior to the incident; even during a period of pressure washing. I slipped off the roof the day (20 hours) after I applied this roof paint in warm sunny weather, well within parameters of the label's instruction for recoat. Common sense and reason dictates the the slippery condition of this roof paint caused my fall. The slippery condition of this roof paint makes for a dangerous situation.
I certainly did not expect nor was prepared for the slippery condition of the roof paint!!!
The manufacturer failed to warn me of the product's dangerous propensities. They did not require me to have knowledge of or certification in OSHA roofing safety standards.
justification: The incident resulted in serious head trauma and a shattered elbow, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described conditions and lack of warnings.

incident_description: We have a SoleusAir 30 pint/day Model: SG-DEH-30M-1 S/N: 51610000317 dehumidifier. On 7-12-12 this humidifier started producing a noxious smell that made our family ill. I contacted the company (numerous times) and was told that it was out of warranty and honestly they couldn't care less. I believe the odor being produced could be harmful.
justification: The dehumidifier produced a noxious smell that made the family ill, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: My child is 2 years old and can open the Safety 1st Push 'n Snap Cabinet Lock. She has accessed chemicals, medicine, ect. We are very fortunate that we have been able to get to her before she has done any harm to herself. This is almost an everyday occasion. I have the same model that has already been recalled, however mine was manufactured at a later date. This model and date NEEDS to be included in the recall.
justification: The child has accessed hazardous materials multiple times without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The incident occurs almost daily, making the occurrence likelihood 5.

incident_description:
My ceiling fan remote control unit has a resistor that burned/melted the case and quit working.  This unit is manufactured by RHINE  (model UC 7067RC) and is used in many different brand ceiling fans.  My online research has led the part number Harbor Breeze , [REDACTED]  and many more.  The unit is also available separately and could be added to other devices.

This heat and potential fire hazard could burn down homes.
justification: The burned resistor could potentially cause a fire, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This incident relates to a Kidde Model 1276 Ionization Smoke Alarm.  This device has a manufacture date of November 22, 2004.  

Around 12:20 AM on Sunday August 5, the smoke detectors in our house (integrated Kidde system) went off.  After getting everyone out of the house, we discovered that the alarm had stopped.  I located the detector that started the alarm and discovered that the smoke detector itself had char marks on it from excessive heat and determined that the smoke detector was the source of the smoke.  We have since replaced the faulty detector, but his is a serious safety issue.  The very device that is supposed to alert you to a fire could possibly start its own fire!

When reviewing the CSPC website I discovered that another consumer had a similar issue with a Model 1275 smoke alarm.  Is this a sign of a larger issue wiht the 197x series of smoke alarms?
justification: The smoke detector malfunctioned, causing a false alarm and charring, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a power cord for my [REDACTED] from Battdepot.com, part# AC19V90K3. When I plug the cord into the wall socket it produces a big spark. It does this on any electrical wall outlet I have tried.

This is a shock hazard and potential fire hazard. If a young person were to use this, they would be at great risk for electrical shock.

Contacted Battdepot and advise them of the hazard. They were not responsive and showed no concern over the safety of their product.

Please look into this product before somebody is injured by it or it burns someones house down.
justification: The power cord produces sparks and poses a shock and fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: On Saturday, 7-28-12 I lost partial power to my pole barn.  I went to my main fuse panel in the house and heard electrical sparking.  I removed the face panel and could hear it was coming from a 60 amp breaker which fed my pole barn.  I put a screwdriver on one of the screws and tightened and the sparking went away.  On 7-29-12 at appx 6pm my compressor in the barn kicked on and I heard a loud crack.  All of my power in the barn was out.  I went downstairs to look at my panel.  There was black residue on the panel cover.  I removed the panel cover and noticed that both of the legs were black and the 60 amp breaker was tripped and angular.  I checked voltage and there was none at the 60 amp breaker.  I pulled the 60 amp breaker out, for replacement purposes, and the panel began to arc.  I tried to pull the main, 200 amp breaker but it would not move.  The panel is on fire and electricity continues to flow into the panel.  The wires and breakers were burning.  I used two fire extinguishers on the fire.  The fire department responded and pulled the meter.  If I had not been home I am sure the house would have caught on fire.  Luckily the damage, smoke, was confined mostly to the basement of my home.  I still have the damaged panel in my possession.
justification: The incident involved a significant electrical fire that could have caused severe damage if not for immediate intervention, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have a Keller 36ft extension ladder possibly manufactured on 4/20/88. I belive it to be manufactured wrong, The rungs are D shaped and are slanted in as your climbing up, I think they should be flat. I would like someone to tell me if it is safe to use this ladder
justification: The ladder's design may pose a risk, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Our Casablanca ceiling fan just fell from our ceiling and hit the floor of our living room.  No one was hurt but it was very dangerous.  It looked that the fan unscrewed itself from the metal pole that attaches the fan to the ceiling mount.
justification: The fan fell but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm. The occurrence is unlikely as it appears to be an isolated mechanical failure.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that with no warning on June 30th, 2012 his approximately 52" in diameter ceiling fan came apart and fell to the floor in the middle of the night.
Caller estimates the fan to weigh approximately 25 lbs.

The fan did not fall with the base but rather came apart and fell, leaving wires dangling that then shorted out and blew the breakers.

The fan fell very close by the place his one  year old grandchild normally sits.

It is now a necccesary for caller to contact an electrician to cap off the live electrical wires.

If repair and replacement takes place before compliance can get back with consumer then he would ask for reimbursement of repair and replacement.
justification: The ceiling fan fell but no one was injured, though it posed a significant risk to the grandchild.

incident_description:
The "thumb latch" on our Andersen sliding glass door (installed only 7 weeks ago) has experienced a mechanical failure exposing three small plastic ball bearings creating a risk of choking. The product includes a retaining ring which is snapping, subsequently exposing the internal components and rendering the latch useless.

Two replacement latches were received from Andersen.  One of the latches arrived broken, the second shows signs of initial degradation and is well on its way to being broken.

When I outlined to the Andersen customer service representative that there is an apparent fundamental design flaw in this product I was told that I should utilize the ten year warranty to receive replacements.  I find that ongoing replacement of a defective product is an unsatisfactory solution.

Furthermore, the customer service representative indicated that this is a familiar problem and that their supplier has been advised of the issue and has taken steps to change their manufacturing process.  I find it odd that the replacement product I received today has the same design flaw.
justification: The incident involves a mechanical failure exposing small parts posing a choking hazard, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I was using my table saw and when I reach for the power switch, if wouldn't turn off my table saw.
justification: The table saw not turning off is an incident with potential for injury, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says last night her son was working when he called her stating his roommate told him of a strong odor in the home.  

She went to his home and noticed fumes and smoke had engulfed the home.  The consumer called the Fire Dept who said the fire was caused by the compressor in the air conditioning unit.  They sat the unit outside.

The consumer says she called the manufacturer today who told her the unit is not on recall.  The retailer also said the same thing.  

There was no other damage done to the home.
justification: The incident involved fumes and smoke but no injury or death was reported, and the fire was contained without further damage.

incident_description: A/C Fan failed resulting in the compressor overheating and catching fire.  Unit was not manufactured with a safety system in place that would shut down the system in the event of failure.  If the system would have shut down, then there would not have been a fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire due to a failed A/C fan and lack of safety system, but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description:
A kohler shower door exploded into 1000's of tiny glass pieces while we were out of the house.
The door was bought brand new from Lowe's on April 22,2011 and professionally installed by Lowes. It was not damaged nor in need of repair.
justification: The shower door exploded but no one was present, resulting in no injury.

incident_description:
July 11th, 2012 around 8:30AM caller heated bread with drippings that had been grilled the day before to prepare a sandwich for his wife and himself.

Around 9:00AM Pacific Time on July 11, 2012 the caller's wife contacted him via cellphone asking if he was alright and to warn him that bristles from the brush used to clean the grill the day before had gotten into the drippings and a bristle had lodged in the soft upper tissue in the roof of her mouth.

She removed the bristle and at this point appears not to have been harmed, however she will keep an eye on the area.

The bristles of the brush are very fine and cannot be seen easily.

The caller and his wife are reporting to alert public to be aware of this potential safety hazard, especially children and the elderly.

He has notified newspapers and television stations.
There is a warning on the handle of the brush stating that the  bristles may come out.

Callers have not contacted manufacturer yet but do intend to contact them.
justification: The incident resulted in a bristle lodging in the wife's mouth, which constitutes an injury, but no long-term harm was reported. The likelihood is possible as the bristles are fine and not easily visible, posing a moderate risk.

incident_description:
Product:
Kobalt 3/8" x 50' Rubber Air Hose, Item #: 336414 |  Model #: SGY-AIR155 purchased from Lowes in La Habra, CA
Product Description:
3/8" x 50' Rubber Air Hose

    Contractor-grade air hose
    Remains flexible from -30ÃÂ°F to 200ÃÂ°F
    Oil- and abrasion-resistant
    Will withstand intense daily use
Incident:
The rubber in the hose and inner shielding cracked and degraded over the length of the hose within 1 year with home owner use (several hours per week).  The degraded hose blew apart projecting the steel fitting at the end of the hose into a parked vehicle with enough force to dent the vehicle.  Had the fitting hit me I could have been seriously injured.  With the hose blown, if I had not been home and left my air compressor on, the compressor could have run until the motor burned up, such situations can possibly start shop fires.  No injury or damage occurred.  I felt inclined to post a review on Lowe's website stating this hose is hazardous to warn other buyers and Lowe's refused to post my review nor did they respond to my safety complaint.  I will email them my complaints and they should be investigated or fined for not taking my safety complaint report seriously.  
Thank you
justification: The hose degraded and caused damage to a vehicle, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is possible given the description of the hose's failure.

incident_description: I have a Campbell Hausfeld CC 2300 Portable Inflator which I keep in my garage. I have had the inflator for between 1 and 1-1/2 years. I normally plug the inflator in to charge the battery a few hours before I need to use it. In May 2012, I plugged the inflator in to fill our bicycle tires. A few hours later I noticed a burnt plastic smell in the garage. I traced to the power supply from the inflator. When I unplugged the power adapter, I was shocked at how hot it was. I immediately dropped it because it was so hot it actually hurt to touch it. I called Campbell Hausfeld, and the support tech told me that it was probably the battery that was the problem. He said he wasn't able to send me a replacement but offered to send a new ac adapter to try. The new ac adapter was smaller than the original. I tried charging with the new adapter, but after a few hours had the same problem. This time it was even more hot to the touch. I was worried about it being a fire hazard and have not plugged it in since. Campbell Hausfeld refuses to replace the battery, which seems to be the problem. I do not recommend using this inflator without checking it often. If anything flammable was near this product, I would be very worried it would ignite.
justification: The incident involved a hot power adapter causing discomfort but no injury, and the repeated occurrence suggests a likely issue.

incident_description:
08/2010  The consumer stated that her friend was taking care of her home while she was overseas. The consumer stated that the friend informed her that they had experienced a power outage and that the generator had not worked.  

The consumer stated that she contacted that manufacturer and they send a technician to service the generator. The consumer stated that the technician informed her that the battery on the generator had exploded and that was the reason why it was not working. The consumer stated that the manufacturer charged her for the replacement of the battery. 

07/01/2012 The consumer stated that she contacted the fire department and they informed her that there was oil all over the bottom of the generator. They advise that she turn it off because it poses a fire hazard. 

07/02/2012 (Est.) The consumer stated that at the moment the generator was not working.  She had experienced a power outage and the generator did not work properly. The consumer contacted the manufacturer and informed them that she was experiencing problems with the generator and that it was giving an error message warning about the oil. The consumer stated that the technician that looked at the generator stated that nothing was wrong with the generator. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that she was concern because of the fire hazard that it poses. The consumer
believe that this product should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a generator malfunction posing a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We smelled electrical smoke, went down to the basement, and found our LG dehumidifier burning hot with meltdown in progress but not shutdown.  Had we not been home and smelled it, it presumably would have caused a fire.

We called LG.  The model is not part of their recall but we suspect it should be.  LG wasn't interested in hearing about it.  Pathetic response on their part.

The model # is LHD65EL.  Meltdown of parts is very visible on the unit.  We're planning to dispose of it imminently, so please tell me if you need us to keep it.
justification: The dehumidifier was overheating and melting, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was using my Ryobi S651D 1/4 sheet sander this afternoon and the interior metal fan piece sheared off and broke through the front of the unit. Basically, it looks like the entire front of the sander exploded. Model #AJ0638211365. Thankfully I was wearing eye protection and I ended up with only a small scratch on my face and no one else was near me as I was working since pieces flew everywhere. It also helped that I have been using similar tools for a long time and did not panic when it happened. However, it is not unusual for other family members to be in the adjacent area when projects are being worked on. 

It there is some place that I can either send photos or the sander so that you can evaluate it? I could not find all of the pieces, but saved the large ones that I could find. 

I did find out that this was recalled on 5/5/2011 due to the fan breaking issue. Until today, I was unaware that there was a recall.
justification: The incident resulted in a small scratch on the face, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the recall indicates a known issue, but the user was unaware and others could have been nearby.

incident_description: I just read an article by Marc Weber Tobias detailing how the Stack-On safes can be opened with a paper clip (search for his name and "thesidebar" and/or "Security Labs" and/or "Forbes"). So I tried it myself on the Stack-On PS-514 I have. I have a short video if you want and I posted it on Amazon under "DANGER !!! Easy to pick !!". I've never cracked a safe in my life and I did it on the second try. The video is my 5th time opening it with a paper clip. I showed my wife how to do it and she got it open on the first try. These are sold as gun safes. The California DOJ has approved them. A child can get into them, get a gun and kill or injure themselves or another person (this has actually happened).
justification: The safe's vulnerability can lead to unauthorized access to firearms, posing a risk of death or injury, as evidenced by past incidents.

incident_description:
Panther Computers purchased 100 ATX molex to SATA power adapters that are used for computers that have no or too few SATA power connections available from the internal power supply. It has come to our attention that these items may pose an immediate fire hazard.

We purchased these items from a wholesaler called Evertek who also sells direct under the name Geeks.com. These are generic in nature and have no UPC codes on them nor any manufacturer immediately identifiable on the packaging. They are approximately 4 inches in length and milk colored plastic on the ATX or molex end and black plastic on the SATA connector side. The SATA side has the words Serial ATA on one side with the word Amphenol on the other.

We have an article with pictures on our website shows at least 4 computers that have had melt downs and one fire that did not traverse the computer case, but could have.  This can be sen at www.panthercomputers.com   We have instituted a voluntary local recall for the product we used, but suggest a national recall be considered since this could be a more serious issue.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard with potential for property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I was using the stool to put up a curtain in my shower when it broke and caused me to fall. I stopped using the stool and placed it in the closet.
justification: The stool broke and caused a fall, but there is no mention of injury, so it is classified as an incident with no injury.

incident_description: The consumer wanted to illustrate his concerns about a  wooden work bench he recently purchased. The size is designed to be 48X24 inch. The consumer feels the product is unsafe because the legs of the workbench have very sharp corners and poses a potential safety concern. The consumer stated that the packaging gives a false sense of how the product will appear upon assembly. The consumer has not been harmed by the product. The consumer has been in contact with the firm about the issue and was told that the design was changed six months to the current format. The consumer was directed by the firm to call the retailer for a refund. The consumer called the retailer today and they are aware of the problem, but is unsure if they have removed their stock from the shelf. The consumer also feels this product is unstable and could fall on a nearby child.
justification: The consumer has not been harmed, but the sharp corners and instability pose a potential safety risk, especially to children.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the ladder was a 17ÃÂ ladder that has hinges that lock in place to change the height of the ladder. The consumer stated that he had folded the ladder on the ÃÂAÃÂ shape where he could climb on either side of the ladder. The consumer stated that when he tried to climb on the ladder, he got to 4ÃÂ high and the ladder collapse and folded inward. 
The consumer stated that he felled backwards and the ladder fell on top of him. The consumer stated that his right thigh and right knee were bruised. The consumer stated that he has not sought medical attention. He stated that he was unsure if he was going to seek medical attention. 
The consumer stated that she tried to find the contact information for the manufacturer and was unable to find it. 
The consumer stated that he research online and found many reports on incidents with this same product. 
The consumer stated that he believe this product should be investigated.
justification: The consumer suffered bruises from the ladder collapsing, indicating an injury without the need for medical attention.

incident_description:
on April 28, 2012 i purchased a cramer task it 50051pk-82 from amazon.com and on july 30, 2012 i used this stool for the first or second time (i can't remember if used before) and as i was hanging a shower curtain liner it broke and caused me to fall. when i fell i hit a piece of wooden furniture and hit my left side right on my rib cage, at the time i did not think it was very serious but as the day and night went on it became more painful so i went to the emergency room on the 31st of july and they took xrays, luckily nothing was broken and i was just badly bruised, which i am still very sore and it is now the 8th of august. i returned the stool to amazon as they instructed but i did take pictures of it before i sent it back . i did receive a refund from amazon less a restocking fee but not sure why i had to pay that as it was pulled from their website until this was investigated and besides that it was broken how can they restock it. 
if you need additional information please advise
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bruised ribs) requiring emergency room visit, but no broken bones or death. The likelihood is 'possible' as such incidents are not uncommon with faulty products.

incident_description:
The consumer says that his son was going camping.  He was coming down the ladder when the hinge broke and he fell to the side of it.  His son says everything was fine with the ladder prior to the incident.  

His father was not sure if he was seriously injured.  He returns from camping today. The consumer called the manufacturer today who offered a $100 gift certificate.  The consumer purchased it for 3 times that amount.
justification: The incident involved a fall from a ladder, but the injury status is uncertain, suggesting a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as ladder failures can happen but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
We do not use our dehumidifier continuously, but we had plugged it in to run in the basement because we were having hot humid weather. Soon after we went out and returned about 3 hours later. We were sitting on the porch and heard our smoke alarm in the basement go off. The dehumidifier had caught on fire and the basement was filled with smoke. I called 911 and my husband managed to get to it, felt that it was not too hot on top to touch, unplugged it and dragged it out through the garage into the driveway where the smoke continued to pour out of it. It had caught fire inside where the cord comes out from. The heat had melted a hole through it and there was a black patch on the floor where it had been standing. When the fire chief arrived, he checked the outlet in the wall where it had been plugged in and found no problem. 

Thankfully we were home when it happened and we were able to avert disaster - our home could have burnt down.
justification: The dehumidifier caught fire, causing smoke damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I noticed that there were scorch marks above 3 of my 6 Honeywell RLV430 thermostats.  I had a licensed electrician come look at the the wiring, thinking that it was the wiring in the wall that was causing the scorch marks.  He said there was nothing wrong with the wiring, it was the thermostat unit, possibly a battery within the unit going bad.  I now have the breakers to all the units shut off.
justification: Scorch marks indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Flushmate Mod 503, SN #111705-F3G-1846, in recall series, burst at rear seam inside tank spraying water out overflow/vent hole on rear and onto walls.  No lasting damage.   Called Flushmate recall hotline and they are sending a replacement tank (but not a plumber).  Hopefully it arrived soon...
justification: The incident involved a burst tank spraying water, but no injury or lasting damage occurred, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
Cotton towels ignited while drying inside a Hot Point model DLB1550BBLWH electric clothes dryer at a hair salon.  Fire damage was confined to the clothes dryer.  Damage was estimated at approximately $500.  There were no injuries.

The exact cause of the fire is undetermined.  Possible causes are contamination of the towels by a hair dye product causing directi ignition or spontaneous combustion; or a malfunction in the dryer.
justification: The incident caused fire damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) given the undetermined cause and potential for recurrence.

incident_description:
04-13-2012, My kitchen caught on fire twice within a few days of each other. The first time it had happened, the fire department came and left after the fire was put out, giving us no definite source of the cause. Because of this. We had no idea how to prevent it and once again another fire started later on 04-18-2012. After some investigation, we have concluded that the outburst of the two fire were caused by our gas water heater. The fire disasters worried my ex-husband so much that he died from anxiety with phobia.

The water heater is an imported item that we purchased, made and produced in the US. And the incidents occured overseas in China. Can we instituting a lawsuit go to Los Angeles Superior Court for compensatory damages, and other related actions? We would like to know how the instituting a lawsuit length of time we have in doing so.
justification: The incident resulted in a death due to anxiety and phobia caused by the fires, which elevates the severity to level 4. The occurrence likelihood is considered rare (1) as the fires were caused by a specific gas water heater issue.

incident_description:
My Sears Kenmore Dehumidifier filled by basement with smoke. I immediately unplugged this unit.
I recently heard about a recall, but my model was not included. I sounds like it should have been.
Model # 580.54501400 purchased at Sears 7/17/2004 for $169.59.
justification: The dehumidifier filled the basement with smoke, indicating a hazardous incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The caller is a Medical Director at the California Poison Control System.  

He says the product is brightly packaged and they look like candy.  It is wrapped in a plastic film.  Children pick this product up, which is the size of a golf ball and bite into it.  He says they are very attractively colored, inviting, and are getting children really sick.

The caller says this has been happening mostly since March 7th.  He has seen incidents of 139 children get into these products since that time.  Almost all of them are 3 years of age and under.  Five have been admitted to hospitals.  Three to critical care units.  

9 of these kids have had moderate affects and one major affect according to the Poison Control Centers codes.  

The children have experienced significant vomiting and nausea.  Secondly, is respiratory distress.  

Thirdly is Lactic Acidosis and eye injuries.  When children open the pods with their teeth, the substance sometimes gets in there eyes.  

The caller feels that 139 exposures in 3 1/2 months is troubling.  Lactic Acidosis is a risk that they don't understand why it is occurring but it doesn't usually stem from getting into laundry detergent.  

The caller feels CPSC should step in and require more labeling and also the way that it is packaged differently to not be so inviting for children.
justification: The incident involves 139 children experiencing significant health effects, including hospitalizations and critical care admissions, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the high number of incidents in a short period.

incident_description: I read about the dehumidier recall today and wanted to say that my dehumidier also gets extremely hot. Too hot to touch. I have the Kenmore 580.54701801 Serial number 903TAEJ15292.
justification: The dehumidifier gets extremely hot, posing a potential burn risk, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description: When washing clothes in a HE washer using Tide Pods Mystic Forest we experienced headaches and some nausea.
justification: Headaches and nausea indicate physical discomfort, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such reactions are not uncommon with chemical exposures.

incident_description: Fire extinguisher exploded in our apartment.
justification: An exploding fire extinguisher is an incident that likely caused injury, given the force involved in such an event. Such occurrences are relatively rare, hence the low likelihood score.

incident_description: I have had a Guardian 7kW Standby Generator by Generac generator for about 4 1/2 years. Last night (7-31-2012) when the generator was starting, the battery exploded. I have since read numerous accounts on the Internet that this has been a common occurrence.
justification: The battery explosion is an incident with no reported injury, and the description notes this is a common occurrence.

incident_description:
On approximately 4/4/2012, the consumer stated that when pulling the 3 way splitter cube tap out of the wall the plastic cover separated (screw failed to hold unit together) and half of the unit remained in the wall. This led to sparks, burn larks on the unit, and destroyed the circuit breaker.  The consumer was not injured.

The manufacturer was not contacted.

The consumer feels that the product may be a fire hazard.
justification: The incident caused sparks and damage to the unit and circuit breaker, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Product was Ortho Home Defense Max Insect Killer, in the 1.33Gal/5L bottle, with a hand held sprayer. Bar code was 7154901974, and the printed (lot number?) was I11343/FI/3/2. Purchased 1-2 months ago at Lowes in Augusta, GA. Bottle was appx. 2/3rds used at time of incident.

The hand held sprayer wand has a large, spring loaded plunger, which is drawn back to build pressure for continuous spraying. While using the sprayer, I drew back the plunger, and the red plastic hand piece split/burst open, resulting in a few ounces of the product spilling out. In addition, the spring inside the sprayer released suddenly, causing some of the pesticide to splatter on me and the surrounding area.
justification: The incident involved a sprayer malfunction causing pesticide splatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We purchased a Navien Tankless water heater CR-210 in Feb. 2009.  It was supposed to supply hot water on demand and save us a bundle in energy costs.  It cost us about $1500.00 and $700 to install.  From the beginning , the water heater did not work properly.  We had to run the water 5-10 minutes just to get warm water.  Although it wasn't set to go on all the time, the tank never stopped running.  We called the vendor and were told that it was supposed to work like that and there was nothing we could do.  Our bill went up a hundred dollars a month instead of down.  We put up with it until we no longer got any hot water. About that time, there was a recall on the product, so the plumbers came out to fix the unit.  They found out that the wires on the mother board were crossed and the unit was put together wrong.  Apparently, the unit had not been U.S. certified and was quite dangerous. The plumbers fixed the water heater, charging us several hundred dollars. We requested that Navien refund our money as they were supposed to pay for the recall and pay for the excess energy charges the defect had cost us.  They refused to do either.  I reported them to the BBB and they received no response.  They are rated F on the Better Business Bureau website.  We feel that this water heater should not have been put on the market uncertified and defective.  The Navien America company did not honor the recall or the 12 year warrantee on this defective unit.
justification: The incident describes a defective product causing financial loss and inconvenience, but no injury or death.

incident_description: Kidde 10 lb fire extinguisher dry chemical had the nylon valve separate and explode in my garage. No injuries, just a huge mess. Found out item has been recalled, and for good reason. Parts found all over garage.
justification: The fire extinguisher exploded but caused no injuries, only a mess, fitting severity level 2. The recall suggests this issue is not rare, warranting a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a Maytag stacked washer/dryer unit, model MGT 3800XWO. The washer tub is made of plastic and has a sharp, square edge along the top. The other day when I was adding clothes to the washer, my hand rubbed along this edge, scraping off enough skin to cause bleeding.

I attempted to post this comment to the Maytag product web site, but my comment was rejected. It seems that a simple manufacturing change would solve this problem. Instead, I'll need to file down the sharp edge myself. Pretty frustrating to pay over $2,000 for a new product and find out that it has been so poorly designed.
justification: The incident describes a physical injury (bleeding) caused by a sharp edge on the washer, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The pot metal bracket that held the ceiling fan broke and the ceiling fan came crashing to the floor. It fell about 11
feet to the floor. My wife usually sits right there so she can watch the TV. Thank God no one was in the Den or they
would have been killed. The metal bracket broke where the company had drilled a hole and it made that spot on
the bracket weak.
justification: The ceiling fan fell but no one was injured, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: While doing routine ironing, the Rowenta powerguide 2, Model DM253, iron started smoking then caught fire inside the iron.  We unplugged the iron and stuck it in a sink full of water.  The smell was horrible, but fortunately no one and nothing was hurt.
justification: The iron caught fire but no one was injured, and the situation was controlled without further damage.

incident_description:
Black mold is growing inside my front loader Kenmore washing machine.  Always keep the door open to the washer after a load, so I don't see any mold in the washing area, but mold grows in the soap dispenser, I keep it cleaned, but yesterday, I pulled out the soap tray for the first time and looked inside and see quite a bit of mold growing inside the machine where I can't get to it. Enough to not want to use it again. I tried the cleaning cycle with bleach, but after running this cycle twice, I see the mold is still there inside the machine.

Most of my clothes are line dried (so they won't shrink or fade in the dryer) and I believe I've been carrying around mold in my clothes for God knows how long.

I spent around $990 on this washing machine, because the front loading is better on my back than pulling out a load from a regular washing machine, but I'm going to have to get rid of the mold. Contacting Sears, but I bought this Kenmore from them 3 or more years ago, without any additional warranties, so I expect I will get nothing from them on this.
justification: The presence of mold in the washing machine poses a potential health risk, but there is no direct evidence of injury or illness caused by the mold.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was using the air compressor for approximately 10 minutes and suddenly starter hearing a popping sound.  The consumer stated the safety valve was making that noise alarming him that the pressure had increased to high. The consumer quickly proceeded to press the off lever, the lever failed to turn the compressor off. The consumer had to turn it off from the circuit breaker. 

The consumer stated that normally the compressor goes up to a pressure of 135 psi and shuts off, and then it decreased to approximately 110 psi and turns back on. The consumer is concern because that product should let the consumer turn off the compressor, and it failed to do that. 
The consumer was not injured and there were no damages to his home. 

The manufacturer stated that the compressor switch fused together and thatÃÂs the reason why the machine stayed on. They informed him that there is a new design switch that the consumer was supposed to upgrade to. They informed him that he needed to upgrade to the Kit # 46818555. 

They are informing the consumer that he would need to pay 117 dollars for the new kit. 

The consumer believes that this is dangerous because it could be a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning air compressor that failed to turn off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Polder 90401 Mini-Step stool.  The stool has a plactic handle which one uses to pick up the step stool when it is closed. The metal is sharp and the plastic handle breaks. The step stool fell on my foot. It injured my foot. A very poorly designed handle.
I'm sure this happens all the time with this step stool.
justification: The incident resulted in a foot injury due to the step stool's poorly designed handle, indicating a severity level of 3. The description suggests this is a common issue, making the occurrence likelihood high.

incident_description:
Power cord with L-shaped connector for Apple Macbook Pro Mid 2011 model. 85W Magsafe adapter.

The cord has been continuously used (but rarely moved from its in-use position), with a constant flex angle of about 30 degrees near the the point where the connector attaches to the power port on the laptop. Over time (10-11 months), discoloring of the cable possibly from being near to the hotter parts of the laptop has occurred. After this, the thin rubber-like coating covering the wire has started to disintegrate at the point where the cable undergoes the 30 degree flex, exposing metal wires and sheathing.
justification: The incident involves damage to the power cord exposing wires, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: husband sat on it and it made cracking noise.  father stepped on it and it caved in
justification: The description indicates an incident (cracking noise and caving in) but no mention of injury, so severity is 2. The likelihood is high (4) as it happened twice in the description.

incident_description: I purchased a Powermate 5500 generator less than a month ago from Home Depot during a recent power outage and used it for approx three days and haven't used it since. Today, my wife called me at work informing me that there is a very strong gas odor in the garage and in the house. I left work and identified the problem as the generator so I wheeled it outside and went back to work. When I came home I could smell gasoline as soon as I got out of my car (meanwhile the generator was in the backyard). From inspecting the generator, it was now obvious that it was leaking gasoline. I identified that the leak was coming from the fuel filter. I am writing to identify a defective fuel filter and a potentially very serious fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves a gasoline leak from a generator, posing a fire hazard but no injury or death reported.

incident_description: Lower right hinge of Werner S2210 MK3 attic ladder cracked and broke while I was on the ladder.
justification: The ladder hinge broke while in use, indicating an incident but no mention of injury.

incident_description: While installing the "Philips Power multiplier SPS1060T/17 6 outlets Wall tap", I discovered that the supplied screw is too short to secure the unit to the outlet. This creates an unsafe condition, so I removed the unit from service before use.
justification: The incident involved an unsafe condition due to a short screw, but no injury occurred as the unit was removed from service.

incident_description: Purchased Soleus Air Portable Air Conditioner, Model LX-100,  in July 2011. Concerned with lack of safety shutoff when submerged in water.  Used item approximately 200 hours before water began leaking on carpet.  Attempted to use drain with a hose to catch water in a shallow pan, however no water accumulated at site of drain. Discovered that water was leaking from somewhere inside air conditioner. Placed unit in a small wading pool to catch water, and over 8 hour period accumulated 7 1/2 gallons of water and the unit never shut off. My concern with unit is the risk of electrical shock. The unit's cord is located at the bottom of unit and I do not understand how anything electrical could continue to run while submerged in water. I have seen numerous complaints on the internet pertaining to the same issue of massive water leaking in same model of air conditioner.  I am not an electrician, but I would be concerned with anything electrical, extension cords, lamps, etc that would be near this unit when it is pumping out 5 gallons of water on the floor.
justification: The incident describes a significant safety concern with the air conditioner leaking water and not shutting off, posing a risk of electrical shock, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I installed a Brica baby-in-sight mirror on the headrest of the seat (2nd row, right seat behind shot gun of 2011 [REDACTED]) where my baby (14 months) sits rear-facing in her convertible car seat.  I was involved in a frontal crash accident that caused all airbags to deploy.   When I checked my baby if she was alright, I also noticed the mirror facing her had big cracks and the upper left corner (where the air bag might have hit) had disappeared (chipped off).  The product description claimed that the product is flexible and shatter resistant but if so, the corner  shouldn't have broken off.  (another brand of mirror that i got for my older child was not damaged at all)  We were lucky that the broken piece of mirror didn't hurt anyone in this accident  and I hope it won't hurt anyone in any future accidents.
justification: The mirror was damaged in the crash but no one was injured, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: re sloan flushmate III series503 one unit burst in 2011. factory replaced at no charge but we had to provide labor to install. now they recall units as a personnel safety issue. factory tells us unit already replaced has no defects but 8 others we have are defective. further they advise a repair kit consisting of a metal strap to be secured around the existing defective tank and a pressure reducing valve will also be supplied. they have redesigned tanks that are not defective so that's what they should be compelled to send out. the "repair kit" puts a "[REDACTED]" around a defective product and the valve reduces pressure so consumer does not get the flush capabilities of a non- defective product. the CPSC should not save the maker of the defective product but should protect the CONSUMER. you are the CONSUMER psc right?
justification: The incident involves defective units that could pose a safety risk, but no actual injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description: Light fixture portion of the fan began to operate intermittently and to flash on and off.  Then the fan stopped turning. When resetting the remote control in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions a loud pop came from the fan and the fan ceased to function.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning fan and a loud pop, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: a metal bristle from the master forge grill brush fell off the brush onto our grill and got lodged into my hamburger. I swallowed the bristle and it got lodged into my esophagus which caused me to have to rush to the emergency room to get it removed
justification: The incident resulted in a physical injury requiring emergency medical attention, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
I am the administrative fire chief for a fire district. One of my retired volunteer firefighters has a Drill Master 19.2V 1/2" battery powered drill. It was lying on his workbench when it began to smoke, and melted a hole through the handle. It was so hot he had trouble picking it up to move it outside. Definitely enough heat was produced to start a fire if it had been nearly readily combustible materials. I have photographs of the drill that I can send. You can contact me at: 

[REDACTED]
justification: The drill overheated and melted, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Health spa sauna fire. The sauna heater in the men's locker room sauna malfunctioned and ignited the wood cabinet housing the heater. The heater is an electric infrared portable heater. It is plugged into an outlet in the sauna. The sprinkler head located in the sauna above the heater activiated and extinguished the fire. Fire damage was confined to the sauna.

The heater is a Sunburst 3000. It is manufactured in China by Diam Chiang Chia Technology Co. Ltd.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the sauna, but the sprinkler system activated and extinguished it without causing injury or death.

incident_description: On July 20, 2012 at 9am I stepped on a stool purchased from Christmas Tree Shops and it shattered causing me to fall. I sustained bruising and lacerations to my wrist, elbow, left shoulder and lower back.  There is no weight limit stamped on the stool and I weigh 125lbs.
justification: The incident resulted in bruising and lacerations, indicating an injury, but no death.

incident_description: I recently purchased a PVC hose for an air compressor from Lowes. Clearly marked "Made in China". Wherever it was made, when I put it (unwrapped) in my garage, it omitted a very strong, offensive, chemical, toxic odor. I placed it outside in extreme heat for 3 days and nights before bringing it back inside; thinking it would 'air out'. It didn't. It was just as offensive when I brought it back in and soon the smell permeated the area. It only took a very few minutes for my eyes to water and my dog would not even come into the room!!! Needless to say, I took it back and was told it was not the first one to be returned because of the smell! I know we can't stop giving China our jobs or our money, but shouldn't there be an enforcement to protect our health??
justification: The incident involved a strong, offensive odor causing discomfort (watery eyes) but no reported injury, and similar returns suggest this is a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
I purchased a Mainstays bathtub mat at Walmart on Monday 7-16-12. Tuesday morning I put it in my tub and began taking a shower before work. As I was washing, the surface of the mat became slippery and caused me to fall hitting my head on the tile wall, the faucet or handle. I'm not sure what I hit because it happened so fast. I went to my doctor's office and she said I had a concussion. She did a cat scan and it was negative. I had/have a headache, slurred speech, blurred vision, short term memory problems, lightheaded, and nausea. I went to work and was there about an hour and had to leave. I went home and slept for hours. Wednesday I went to work and felt so bad i had my husband call my doctor's office and they seen me again at 1:45. I felt like I could not think. The doctor wrote me off work for the rest of the week. I have also had severe neck and shoulder pain. The doctor said it could take a month for me to start thinking straight. My job requires a LOT of multi tasking and quick thinking. She also said it should take a week or so for my neck and shoulders/back to feel better.
