I believe the bath mat caused to happen exactly what it was supposed to prevent. And thankfully it was not one of my children that were the first to use this mat. I have saved everything, the mat, the receipt, and the packaging if any of the numbers would help at all. II wrote a message to Walmart online and I have been contacted by a woman at my local store in Fenton, Michigan where I purchased the mat. I gave her the numbers from my receipt and she said I will be contacted by someone else. I believe this bath mat has a design defect and the smooth texture of the surface is dangerous.
Thank you.
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion and other injuries requiring medical attention, fitting severity level 3.

incident_description: I was attempting to install a brand new SATA/IDE to USB 2.0 Adapter Model: CB-ISATAU2 manufactured by Vantec (http://vantecusa.com/). I followed the instructions on the disc that was enclosed and plugged the power cord (E-65849 ABU-033) into my surge protector and the other end into the power adapter. As soon as this happened, the power cord exploded, shocking me, burning my hand, starting a small fire which left a scorch mark on the wall, and filling the room with smoke, which I inhaled.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burned hand and smoke inhalation) and property damage, but no death. Such incidents are unlikely but not rare.

incident_description:
On 6/16/2012 The consumer stated that a dehumidifier was on for approximately an entire night inside a church. The following day someone entered the church and then into their office. The person began to smell smoke. After going to inspect the cause of the odor they saw that the unit was smoking, but did not emit any flames. The consumer immediately unplugged the unit.  

The person whom works in the maintenance department of the church was called and he inspected the unit. After removing the top and looking inside he saw that the sensor on the evaporator coil was melted and may have possibly had a small fire inside the unit.

The manufacturer has not been contacted yet.

The consumer feels that this unit model should have been included in Release #11-324.
justification: The incident involved a smoking dehumidifier with a melted sensor, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or flames were reported.

incident_description:
Text of Conmuner's Complaint in a Letter to the Retailer:

An LG dehumidifier I bought from [REDACTED] went on fire April 21, 2011 in my home in [REDACTED]. The fire caused more than $50,000 in damage. The home was insured by [REDACTED], which may or may not have undertaken action against LG.
As a result of this fire, I removed from service the three other LG dehumidifiers that I had bought from [REDACTED] and which were operating in my homes. I replaced them with [REDACTED] dehumidifiers, two of which were bought from [REDACTED] and the third from [REDACTED]. With the known record that LG has had with faulty dehumidifiers and their history of causing fires (record enclosed), it is appalling that [REDACTED] still sells this brand to the public.
Enclosed are copies of my purchase receipts for these LG dehumidifiers bought from [REDACTED]. My total cost was $887.42, including tax. The dehumidifier that caused the fire was included in the settlement I made with  [REDACTED]. The balance is $695.89, including tax. I expect that [REDACTED] will pay me for my purchase of these three potentially dangerous appliances. The three remaining dehumidifiers are now in my barn and can be brought to your store in Johnson City, NY.
If you choose not to make good directly on the dangerous appliances you sold to the public, [REDACTED] will find its name and its record posted, with photos, endlessly on the internet and in letters to major media where [REDACTED] has stores.
justification: The incident involved a dehumidifier catching fire, causing significant property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Friday night 7/13/2012 I was in surgery to remove a wire bristle from my intestine.  It was seen on a CT scan and was sent straight to emergency surgery.  Had bbq some pork chops on Monday 7/9/2012 and started have pains on Wed.  when the pain would not go away I went to an Urgent Care facility that sent me straight to the ER.  After confirming with a CT scan, the bristle was removed by the surgeon on staff at Cedar Park Regional Medical Center in Cedar Park, TX.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring emergency surgery to remove a wire bristle from the intestine.

incident_description: The Culligan Waterbed heater was no longer heating our waterbed so we drained the mattress to replace the heating unit.  We immediately noticed that the heater pad had overheated, melting/burning into the wooden base of the bed.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage (melted/burned heater pad) but no reported injuries, warranting severity level 2. Overheating of waterbed heaters is a known issue, making occurrence likelihood 'possible' (3).

incident_description:
We bought the THE ROCK EXCAVATOR FIELD KIT (Backyard Safari) from [REDACTED].  The heavy, steel head of the hammer came off when my daughter was using it.  Luckily, she was not hurt.

This is a link to their web site.

http://www.backyardsafari.com/patch-program/the-rock-excavator/

[REDACTED]
justification: The steel head of the hammer came off during use, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Through the Pa. weatherization program I received two window air conditioners. They are Kenmore by Sears. They both are installed properly.They are filled with mold. I have to have them taken out to clean them.They are back int he windows a day or two and all the mold is back.  I called Sears and was told to call the store they came from, the weatherization program doesn't know which store they came from. I have been having them cleaned because of the severe heat.I can't just stop using them.Please help,me and I'm sure many other low income and disabled people in Pennsylvania who received these items. Thank you .[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves mold in air conditioners causing inconvenience and potential health risks, but no direct injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Upon opening our gas dryer after the 3rd load of laundry, we immediately noticed a strange almost chemical smell and noticed that the dryer seemed extremely hot, even on the outside wall.  We left the door open for about 15 minutes, but the smell and heat did not dissipate.  At this point I noticed a brownish discoloration in the dryer drum and (OK, [REDACTED]!) reached in and touched it.  I burned my finger, badly enough that it hurt for a couple of days afterward.  The entire drum was very hot.  At this point we unplugged the dryer, but the burn mark continued to get bigger and it was clear that there was heat continuing to reach the drum.  Eventually, we realized that we needed to shut off the gas.  After that the dryer cooled down.  

Other facts that may or may not be relevant:  
1.  This dryer had a gas leak that was repaired by the manufacturer (just after the dryer was out of  warranty).  This was done at no cost to us.  We reported this to CPSC also.  
2.  About 4 months ago, the control board for this dryer was replaced because the dryer did not seem to shut off when it should (this happened intermittently).
3.  We found no clogs in the vent. The installers of our new dryer confirmed that the vent was clear.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury that caused pain for several days, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the history of gas leaks and control board issues.

incident_description: I have had ge front load washer for about three years and from the third month have been battling mold. I have tried to eliminate with over the counter washer cleaning products, bleach, and vinegar. All these methods were suggested by GE, however none have been able to prevent or eliminate the mold. I have a family with three children, my husband and myself and we have been suffering from allergic reactions because of this mold. Our linen and clothes smell strongly of mold and is never clean. My youngest daughter  and I suffer the most from constant rhinitis, a cough that never goes away and occasionally skin irritation.  I have been doing my laundry at my mothers house and she has much less maintenance of her top load washer than I with my front load. It's more than just a health issues our whole lives are affected.
justification: The description indicates allergic reactions, constant rhinitis, cough, and skin irritation due to mold exposure, which qualifies as injury.

incident_description: I tried to clean my shower with fantastik all purpose cleaner with bleach (UPC 054600105689).  The bleach concentration is way too high. The fumes burnt my eyes and hands and bleached the hand towel I was using to wipe it off.
justification: The fumes caused burns to the eyes and hands, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Fire inspector believes that fire at rental property may have been caused by clothes dryer issue related to recall.
justification: The fire inspector identified a potential cause related to a recalled clothes dryer, indicating an incident occurred but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
While turning the pedestal fan, the fan blades hit the safety shroud, the tip of the blade came through the back side of the cover and cut open my left hand.  

The fan shakes violently, vibrating and shaking, with the blades sometime hitting the safety shroud.  The fan is impossible to point or aim because of the violent vibration.  

Product is sold by "Tractor Supply Co."
Item: 
KU Number: 5002308

Manufacturers Number: CL-30P-DDF
Brand: CountyLineÃÂ®
Stand Type: Pedestal
Fan Blade Diameter: 30 in.
Overall Width: 27-4/5 in.
Overall Length: 27-4/5 in.
Overall Height: 83 in.
Case Material: Steel
Current Rating: 2.6 A
Power Rating: 120 V
Air Flow: 8500 CFM
Number of Speeds: 2
Warranty: 1-Year Limited
Color: Black
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the hand, which qualifies as an injury, and the fan's violent shaking suggests a recurring hazard.

incident_description: When I turned the humidifier off, it started smoking and smelled of burning plastic.  I turned it back on to make sure it hadn't been happening through the night in my children's room and it seemed to be functioning normally again but as soon as I turned the humidifier off again, it started smoking and smelling badly again until I unplugged it.
justification: The humidifier emitted smoke and a burning smell, indicating a malfunction, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Wired Smoke Detector with constant beeping, running battery down and also giving off false alarms.

The caller states that in the past year and more the battery wired to his home has gone off when he has been home and able to turn it off but that if he was not at home it would cost him money due to police responding to his unit sounding as well fire and rescue.

He states that this problem with his smoke alarm does make him believe that he is not as safe due to not being able to depend on the alarm.

He contacted manufacturer on May 22 or 23, they advised him that he could pay for another alarm or ship this one back for trade at his cost of $15 plus shipping.

He would like CPSC to assist him with receiving a replacement alarm at manufacturer expense.
justification: The smoke detector's malfunction causes false alarms and potential financial costs, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: While using my Smart Living Steam Mop it made a loud "explosion type" sound, started spitting out hot water.  The plug became very and the silver metal handle rod became red hot and would not turn off.  I immediately unplugged the unit from the wall receptacle and when I picked the unit up to empty it I burnt the tips of two fingers when they touched the handle rod.  This product carries a one year warranty and is sold at fairs throughout the country.  I contacted by email Ocean Sales out of Calgary, Canada and was told to contact the person I purchased this mop from, impossible.  I feel this product is both a safety and fire hazard and should be investigated.  There are numerous reviews online that indicate the same problem.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the fingers, indicating an injury, and there are multiple reports of similar issues, suggesting a recurring problem.

incident_description: a Safety 1st one step step stool used in the kitchen while in use by a 160 lb person. It broke at the pivot points of the lock for one of the legs. The unit was about two years old and being used on a flat surface
justification: The step stool broke during use, which could have caused injury to the person using it, though the description does not mention any actual injury.

incident_description: I have an Eureka Vacuum model 4870GZ upright, while using the unit the on and off switch caught fire, melting the electric wire.  I reported it to Eureka and they told me that the vacuum was out of warranty.  I did not call them for the warranty but to warn them about the hazard with the switch, thank god I didn't put it back in my closet as the wire was smoldering, it could have caught my house on fire or even shocked an burned me.  The company could care less and said basically oh well.  I am concerned for others if this model switch is still being used in their other products.  I have pictures and even sent the pictures to the company.  Something needs to be done to protect the consumers using this product or any product with this faulty switch.
justification: The switch caught fire and melted the wire, posing a hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was merely standing on the step stool when the lid that lifts to reveal the stool's storage compartment collapsed.  I fell off the stool, but was not injured.  Upon looking at the lid, the corners that pivot cracked in half.  This was caused by the support piece of wood that is along either side of the stool falling off, placing too much weight on the corners.  I have since sealed off the storage area and secured the lid with screws through the side, but never thought about reporting the problem until now.
justification: The incident involved a fall from a stool but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described failure mechanism.

incident_description:
The consumer says the control panel caught on fire.  He says no one was home and the unit was not in use at the time of the incident.  
The consumer says the last time it was used was Saturday afternoon.  The incident occurred later that night.  He says the inside of the unit is blackened and there are burn marks on the top through the outside.  
He contacted the manufacturer today 6-4-12 who is going to send out a service technician to diagnose the problem.
justification: The control panel caught fire but no one was injured as no one was home at the time.

incident_description: The 12 volt lead acid battery in our generator exploded.  The generator is made by Generac Power Systems, model 04389, 7kw air cooled automatic standby generator.  The s/n is 4299489.  The unit is about 6 years old.  The battery is used to automatically start the generator in the event of a power outage.  Luckily the enclosure contained most of the acid that was blown out of the battery, and no one was near the unit at the time.
justification: The battery explosion was contained by the enclosure, and no one was near the unit, resulting in no injury.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting washing machine that he believes he purchased sometime between 2000 and 2002, but states that he really doesn't remember.

He has had problems with it in the past, repaired it himself by replacing the timer and repairing the connector that hooks to the harness because it either doesn't connect properly due to connectors being burned inside from arching.

He doesn't remember when the washer began arching at the connector.

He states that he wants to report this washer because it has the potential to cause a fire or shock users.

He would like to request repair at manufacturer expense but mainly would like to register alert that this situation is occurring with this model number.

no one has been injured

Manufacturer was contacted June 12th, 2012, was advised that the washer was not recalled, they are aware of no problems.
justification: No injury reported, but potential for fire or shock exists.

incident_description:
This fan was "stuttering" as it oscillated and occasionally comes to stop on its own until is gently tapping it.

I removed the exterior plastic motor housing to investigate what was happening and found that the electrical cord was cut because it was not properly routed away from the sharp plastic head of the base.  I believe this is what caused the fan to intermittently stop operating.
justification: The incident involves a fan malfunction due to a cut electrical cord, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Cooked a tuna steak on the grill.  Upon eating the tuna, had a wire from the grill brush that lodged into my soft palate on the roof of my mouth.
justification: A wire from the grill brush lodged into the soft palate, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he purchased range hood that while being wired made a loud noise  triggered some electrical effect that cause the fan controller to no longer work.  

The consumer stated that the next morning, he had it completely installed and he reached up inside to unplug the power plug that when inside range hood. The consumer stated while trying to unplug the power cord he received an electrical shock. The consumer stated that he looked and realized that the plug that connects to the range hood has 120 volts all the time. The consumer stated that this was unsafe because it was exposed to the consumer and a women while cleaning the hood could easily be electrocuted.  
The consumer stated that there were no injuries and there were no damages to his home structure. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they replaced the range hood for the consumer. The consumer stated that on 06/12/2012 he received the replacement and was unhappy to see that the wiring is the same and would cause the same hazard. 

The consumer believes that this product should be re wired and should be investigated.
justification: The consumer received an electrical shock but reported no injuries, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
I received the product Magic Mesh for Father's Day.

The product contains magnets that automatically "close" the door after passing through the mesh.

The problem I have is that when standing too close or sometimes when passing through the mesh it causes my implanted pacemaker/Internal Cardiac Defibrillator to malfunction sending out an audible alert tone.  This happened multiple times over several days.

I needed to make a visit to the Cardio Lab for testing of the pacemaker.  Everything checked out okay, thank goodness.  It was very disconcerting.  

There is no warning label on the box or in the instructions to warn users of this problem.  I was lucky.  The next user may not be.
justification: The incident caused a pacemaker malfunction requiring medical testing, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Shark s3501co stopped producing steam, but stayed hot.  Mop was full of water.  When I pushed the handle a loud pop was heard and steam came out around the tank burning my hand.  Minor burn for me, however we have small children in our home who could have been severely burned by this.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn (injury) and there is a potential for severe burns to small children, indicating a higher severity level.

incident_description: The consumer wanted to express concerns about the dryer in her renters home. The consumer stated that the renter was operating the dryer on June 3, 2012. She stated while her renter was operating the dryer the power knob on the front panel fell off. Her renter noticed that flame came off of the empty compartment. No one was injured and the flame went out on it's own. The renter had a repairman come to inspect the product on June 11, 2012. The repairman concluded that the back panel melted. The consumer called the firm today and was offered no further assistance but was able to file a report. The consumer has not called the retailer. The consumer has not called the fire department or her home insurance company. The consumer has not sustained any further property damage.
justification: The incident involved a flame from the dryer but no injuries or further damage occurred, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
Monday, May 21, 2012 caller's 3 yr old son was standing on step stool to wash his hands when the stool gave way and broke.
The three yr olds left foot became entrapped in the broken stool.

The caller took him to the pediatrician then to  (child's South Jersey Radiology Associates where it was verified that it was broken.  
The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia put a cast on child's foot which will remain on for four weeks.
Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The child suffered a broken foot requiring a cast, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: The Kennedy International folding step stool unexpectedly collapsed when being used.
justification: The step stool collapsed unexpectedly, but the description does not mention any injury or death.

incident_description: Unpacked the generator for the first time, decided to try it out before putting it in the shed until the power went out. I filled the engine with oil and the fuel tank with gasoline, and turned on the fuel shut-off switch to ready the generator to be started. I noticed after a few seconds that gasoline was streaming out of a seal on the carburetor. I turned the fuel shut-off back to the off position, and the fuel stopped streaming on the ground. Turned it back on, and the fuel streamed out again.
justification: Gasoline leakage from the carburetor poses a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I own a Kawasaki cordless drill model # 691220.  While using the drill in my garage to drill through thin plastic, I started smelling a burning smell.  I thought it was the plastic burning around the drill bit and kept drilling the holes.  The smell became very strong, and I noticed a lot of smoke coming out of the vent holes at the back of the drill.  I stopped using the drill and switched batteries, and made sure the forward, and speed switch were fully engaged.  I used the drill again and brown smoke started coming out of the drill.  I have not used the drill since.

The drill motor turns, but slower and makes a weird sound.  The closest thing I can relate to it is when you attempt to use the drill with a battery that is almost dead.  But these batteries were fully charged and hold a charge for hours.  I don't feel the batteries are the problem at all.

I bought a new drill and was going to sell the batteries and charger since they are still good.  When I did a search online I noticed a recall for Kawasaki drills model # [REDACTED].  The reason was for a bad switch.

I researched my model drill online and found that many have failed for the same reason, although I don't see complaints of smoke like mine.

My concern is where there is smoke, there is fire, or about to be fire.  I feel a person who is working outside in a breeze won't notice the smoke, and the drill may catch fire.

I bought the drill at Costco.  I thought it was about two years ago.  I tried to return the drill without the receipt and was told that they couldn't find a record of my purchase, and assumed it was purchased over 4 years ago.  They don't maintain purchases past 4 years.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard from a malfunctioning drill, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On Monday July 2nd at 4 AM our carbon monoxide alarms alerted us to evacuate the house due to CO .We called the Fire Department who responded and found over 100 ppm CO in the house. They determined the cause was the Water Heater power vent was inoperative and the water heater gas burner was still operating. They turned off the gas electric power to the heater and gas.

The Water heater was installed in 2010 when our Condo was built.
The water heater was an A.O. Smith Promax  model GPVH 50 100 and it was date coded 8/4/09 with serial # 0931AO12365.
When the plumber came to investigate and turned the power and gas on the vent motor appeared to be working OK - he did not test the vacuum safety switch or CO levels. The plumber has replaced the power vent assembly.

I have a VERY signifigant safety complaint about your NextStep toilet seat.  I purchased one from my local Home Depot around 6 months ago.  The magnet that is used to hold the seat up FELL OFF the seat.  This magnet poses a signifigant choking hazard.  Also, if it's swallowed with another magnet, a signifigant stomach/intestine perferation hazard.  I did not notice that the magnet was not molded into the lid and it sits freely on the exterior of the lid.  If I had noticed that, I never would have purchased this product.  The magnet is gone, and I can't find it anywhere.  My hope is that it was flushed.  But now, I'll be spending tons of time ripping my kids bathroom apart and digging through toyboxes to make sure it's not in there.  POOR DESIGN.  DISSAPOINTED CUSTOMER.  My friends have an older model of this seat that had metal hinges and I think that the magnet was embedded in the lid and not able to be separated.  MUCH SAFER DESIGN FOR KIDS!!!! incident_description:
To Whom I May Concern:

On this last Monday, XFINITY put me through the worst nightmare any company has ever put me through.  A week or two ago I had their new security system installed.  They had sent out a salesman from a subcontractor.  He was very knowledgeable and very professional.  The companyÃÂs installer was just as great.  They gave us the kind of service and professionalism we are use to getting from Comcast employees.

We had also purchased a thermostat from them.  It was not good at all.  From the very beginning it did not work properly.  The hold function did not work.  It would kick off in the middle of the night and I would wake up in the middle of the night sopping wet.  I am a very sick Veteran.  They have classified me as 100% disabled.  They see my condition as permanent and total.  The most I can do is stay home most of the time and try not to die.  I get out once in a while but I have to be very careful and my wife has to be with me at all times.  She hates to leave me at home all by myself because I have all most died more than a couple of times.  She will not be able to stay home with me fulltime until she can retire two years from this coming February.  She has had to call in sick because of an immediate family member (namely me) to many times as it is.  So far her employer has been very understanding but I am sure that their understanding has its limits.  On Monday XFINITY caused it to happen again and put my life at risk.

Monday morning we called and told them about our problem.  They were able to determine that I understood how to use the control panel and their thermostat was indeed not functioning right.  A few hours later it went crazy.  It turned on our furnace and started pumping hot air into an already overheated house.  I was able to turn off the furnace using my circuit breaker box but their unit then stopped working all together.  The way their system is set up we could not just turn off the thermostat and use the fan to try and keep the house cooler.  Like you can with most thermostats.  I started to get sick.   When I become overheated it can very quickly become life threatening.  If I had been home by myself napping I may have never woken up.  My wife would have come to a corpse.  If this had happened to someone with a crated dog they would most likely also have come home to a corpse.  As anyone can see their system has to major design flaws.  They said they could not get out to us for a couple of days.  We had turned down a next day appointment at first when the hold problem was the only problem we seemed to have.  We disparately needed to go shopping the next day.  My wife kept crying and telling them that the situation was quickly becoming life threatening.  She told them she would already have to lose a days work because of the malfunction.  She said she was close to having to call 911 and take me to the hospital.  She said she would put me in bed and have all our portal fans blowing on me but that could put me in danger of catching pneumonia.  I have been told by my doctors that I may not survive another bad case of pneumonia.

Finally someone was contacted within the company who new they have emergency service.  We were told that their on-call person had been called in.  He was helping another customer but he would get to us right after.  We are of the opinion that if the people that we first contacted had been properly informed about the emergency on call service he would have been sent to us first.  That would have prevented so much anxiety for myself and my dear wife.  One of my major problems is I can not deal with stress very well and it can make me very ill.  Dealing with Comcast over this matter continued to cause me nothing but stress.  The man who arrived turned out to be the person who will be responsible for our over all security system.  We now have his card and can call him directly.  That is first positive thing that resulted from this whole mess.  After he showed up it was determined that he could do nothing.  The thermostat was not repairable at all, not even for the short term.  The only thing he could do was replace the thermostat.  We had been informed by the person who said he was coming out that he was coming out to install a new thermostat.  The problem was he did not have one and did not know how to get one.  He said that he had just finished the training necessary to be certified to install and repair thermostats as part of the overall security system.  The company that had been doing the installing had all the thermostats.  They had been pulled out of the equation before the in-house service people like him had been supplied with thermostats to install.  In fact a man from the installation company who heard about the problem through the grapevine called me.  He was very upset and said he should have been called in the first place.  It just happens that he personally is capable of servicing furnaces and air conditioners.  He had not been hired to do that by Comcast but he was pretty sure he could do that if his company was able to allow him to do that even though he had not been hired by Comcast to give that kind of service.  We came to realize that is the kind of company you buy a thermostat from.  One that can service your entire system and not just part of it.  Because of health and property concerns heating and cooling problems need to be dealt with as quickly as possible.  It is bad enough that we are at the mercy of the electrical company.  People do not need another weakness to deal with on top of that one.  The kind man called me right back.  He said he was told by his supervisor to stop and come back.  He had been in route to our home.  Comcast had told him that they were now handling the service end of thermostats and they already had a man dealing with the problem.  Their service man told me he was helpless to help me.  Because of that I had already called our handyman.  He said when he had finished his current job he would pick up a good thermostat and come by to install it.  He was able to recommend a good heating and air company.  They are sending out a tech today, Wednesday.  He will check the installation of the thermostat and train us on how to use it.  He will also service our air conditioner and furnace.  We will know be their customers.  They have 24 hour emergency service if we have any problems in the future.  That makes us feel so much better because of my health concerns.  The man from the installation company called back yesterday to make sure everything was ok and that we had gotten some help.  I had the feeling if we had not he was prepared to get us a new thermostat and come install it himself.  That shows you the kind of people you deal with when you do business with XFINITY, even their subcontractors.

The way I see it, the problem comes from the top.  The type of organizational machine you normally deal with when you deal with Comcast is not up and running.  Good people can not do their normal good job if they are not given the tools and information they need to do that job.  While waiting for the repairman to come out I tried to get in touch with a person in authority who could talk to me about reimbursement.  Our serviceman said he would leave the thermostat in for our handyman to remove so we could return it.  He did not want to leave a bunch of bare wires hanging out.  I wanted to find out if that was going to be ok with Comcast.  I also wanted to know if they as a company were concerned at all about my wifeÃÂs lost wages and all the emotional stress the problem had put us both through.  The person I was finally able to talk to said she could not understand why I was calling Comcast at all.  She said I was calling a Cable Company.  She said I needed to call a furnace company to have a thermostat installed.  She said she had worked for Comcast for fifteen years and they did not install thermostats, even though I tried to tell her I had one in my wall that had XFINITY on it.  

This morning I tried calling Comcast again.  I was reluctant to talk to someone at the new security section because of the fact that they did not seem to know what was going on in their own department.  I gave them one more try and was able to talk to the right person.  His supervisor is suppose to call me this afternoon and tell me how to return the thermostat.  They are still trying to figure out how they want to go about it.  I personally feel that this product was offered to the public way to early.  They are still working out to many major problems.  I am happy to say that they still have the great Comcast employees trying to do a very hard job without being provided the proper resources and information.  Because of that this new department is not living up to the high XFINITY standards.  At least that is my opinion.  I am sure this wall change given the needed amount of time.  We are willing to be patient and work with them so that can happen.

The man that was suppose to call us back on Wednesday never did.  I called the serviceman that gave us his card Thursday morning and so far and has not called either.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning thermostat that caused significant distress and potential health risks, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I write to report an unreasonably dangerous bath mat product sold by Bed Bath and Beyond, the "Microdry Ultimate Luxury Memory Foam Bath Mat."  If the bottom of the mat gets any moisture on it, such as can easily happen from the tub, shower, condensation, steam in the bathroom from the shower, etc., it slides out under the users feet causing a very dangerous slip and fall situation.  The bottom of the mat is a rubber like material, but if it gets even a little bit moist, it will slip, like being on ice.  In the product reviews section for this mat on the company's website, countless consumers have reported the exact same thing.  Now, the description of the product on the Bed Bath and Beyond Website contains a sentence telling the buyer to place on a dry surface, but this is not reasonable because it is certainly reasonably foreseeable that a mat, even if placed on a dry floor in a bathroom initially, will end up getting some moisture under it -- one stands on it dripping wet as part of its normal use!  To me, this shows that they know of a problem and are trying to take the easy way out rather than fix the situation.  I personally fell, straining my neck, back, and nearly injuring my knee, before going online and learning this.  I have since removed the mats, but I am sure there are many out there in homes that pose a very serious safety threat.  If an elderly person were to fall in a bathroom he or she could early suffer very serious injuries because of this dangerous mat.  Thank you for your attention to this problem.
justification: The incident describes a personal injury (strained neck, back, and nearly injured knee) due to a slip and fall caused by the bath mat, and highlights potential for serious injuries, especially for elderly users.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a safety concern regarding the Hitachi G12SS 4-1/2 In. Angle Grinder.   

After sustaining a deep-cut on my right knuckle of my index finger using this machine (required stiches), I examined my actions and other contributing factors that led to this incident.  I believe that several of the items I identified were directly attributed to the tools design.  These items are listed below with a description:

1) Switch Position:   

The switch is positioned on top of the tool and all the way forward on the tools barrel.  The barrel is used as a handle to grip the tool.  The location of the switch, and its use by the thumb to operate, places the index fingers knuckle forward on the underside of the barrel in a bent position and directly adjacent to the horizontal blade which is located on the underside side. 
When switch is operated by the thumb, it is pushed forward.  The index finger is intended to be protected by the shroud on blade, provided that it is rotated in a position to do so.  If not, when the machine is turned on, it can jerk slightly, thus causing the blade to touch the knuckle on the index finger.  
I have another model of Hitachi angle grinder and have used other manufactures angle grinders.  the others, as well as many I have looked at, all position the switch elsewhere.

2) Barrel Shoulder:

The tool has a very short "shoulder" on the plastic housing near where the switch is located.  The shoulder is not sufficient to keep the operators fingers from being forward near the blade.  
3) Shroud Position:

There are no "stops" to keep the shroud from being rotated in a manner to allow the blade to be exposed to the operators lower index fingers knuckle.  

In addition, I will add that injured me instantly when I first turned on the machine.  This occurred while I had the shroud off.  I did not recognize that an action of gripping the tool in a normal position and turning it on would directly expose the index fingers knuckle to the blade.  I have also found that the shroud must be in specific position so as not to expose the finger.  Note, when holding the tool, the finger is on the underside and out of normal view.

Recently when I used this tool, I again found the design to be very concerning in regards to safety and am thus looking to dispose ot it, even though it has been only used a few times.   This use, and the fact that this tool and its design is still for sale, prompted me to submit this complaint.

Sincerely, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut requiring stitches, indicating an injury, and the design flaws suggest a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
I believe CPSC has a file already activated for the OE -34 Solar Roofing Tiles. The original manufacturer was Open Energy. Applied Solar LLC acquired this company. In 2009 Applied Solar LLC declared bankruptcy and to my knowledge is now out of business. The distributor of our solar roofing tiles is Eagle Roofing.

Riverside Ave, Rialto, CA phone 909-355-7000, the OE-34 solar tile distributor, and roofing installer, Leonard Roofing, Inc. 43280 Business Park Drive, #107 Temecula, CA 92590, phone 951-506-3811, and Suntech America, Inc. San Francisco, CA 888-770-7122. We believe that these companies  can and are obligated to contribute to a corrective plan of action. incident_description:
The smoke ventilation hood is over a cooktop. It has two halogen lights in the center to illuminate the cooking area. Grease collected above the filters and the lights and dripped over an extended period of time onto one of the light sockets. Eventually, one socket abruptly "blew" with a flash. Upon examination, the bracket, socket, and bulb base were coated with black grease. The manufacturer (after a few false starts) sent me the 2-bulb light panel assembly. When I replaced it, I noticed that that the other socket/bulb also had burnt wires, although it was still operative. It appeared that grease was collecting and liquifying above the sockets/bulbs, perhaps due to the heat or inefficiency in removing the smoke and grease. 

I noticed on their website that the company has a substantially similar produce with the lights located at the edges of the hood rather than in the center. A re-design?
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning light socket due to grease accumulation, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My family and I were shopping at Home Depot on June 3, 2012 close to 1:00 in Indianapolis, IN. I intended to purchase the Rust-oleum universal advanced formula satin paint and Primer in one spray paint in white. It was in the back of the shopping cart. incident_description:
I purchased a home in the summer of 2011 that was built around 2002.  As soon as I moved in I noticed that some of the light switches weren't working properly so I opened up the wall plates to take a look and found that some of the light switches were cracked and the wires were loose or coming out of the back of the switch.  In addition I found additional switches next to the ones that were giving me problems that were starting to "fall apart", too.  I replaced the bad switches and decided to check additional switches in the house.  Upon opening more of the wall plates and found that many of the switches were starting to crack.  I decided to replace all the switches in the house that were manufactured by this company.  While replacing the rest of the switches I continued to find cracked switches and even found a couple switches that were completely broken in pieces (with wiring and bare metal switch components exposed).  I was lucky that the house hadn't burned down.  After replacing all of the switches I found that over half of my switches were either cracked or falling apart.  Out of 35 switches, 19 were bad (14 of 29 two-way switches and 5 of 6 three-way switches were bad)!  It seems as if there must have been a manufacturing issue with the plastic when my switches were manufactured.

Today I investigated what brand the switches were and found out that they were all Pass and Seymour brand switches (white lever and white front with grey rear housing).  The two-way switch were all Model 660-WG, though I could not find a model number for the three-way switch.  I did some Internet queries and did not find anyone else that had reported the same problem I had.  I mentioned the problems I was having to other homeowners in the subdivision to see if anyone else was having similar problems.  One or two people said that they had light switches that didn't work, but hadn't checked into the reason why.  At this time I do not know if anyone else had the same issue I did with their switches.
justification: The incident involved faulty switches with potential fire hazards, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On Sunday June 10, 2012, the electronic control board on a ~ 4 year old 40 Whirlpool Electric Water Heater caught fire.  The unit was purchased from Lowe's on July 15, 2008 and installed on August 8, 2008.  The fire melted the plastic cover, the wire nuts connecting the main power supply to the control board, and some of the insulation on the wire.  The unit was a 40 gallon standard electric water heater with an "energy saving" control board mounted on the top of the water heater.  Conversation with a professional plumber (friend) indicated that he has seen others melt, but was not aware of any that had burst into flames.
Whirlpool/Lowe's replaced the water heater and now have the defective heater/control board in their possession; I did, however take pictures of the aftermath of the fire.
There were no injuries. The potential for serious injury existed, however.  Due to the fact that I happened to be within about 3 feet of the heater when it starting popping (sounded like someone hammering on the adjacent wall) and the my local power shut off was right above the water heater, I was able to quickly kill power.  i.e. I'm not sure how long it would have kept on burning nor how far the flames could have spread if I had not been present.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no injuries, but potential for serious injury existed.

incident_description: I purchased a Genie Powerlift 900 garage door opener at a local home improvement store.  Installing the opener was not difficult, but I could not complete the programming - the unit would not pass the control limit test and reverse when I closed it on a board.  I found an addendum page with new instructions for setting down and up travel limits that was separate from the instruction manual, but those new instructions were not very clear.  I finally looked at the manufacturer's website, which offered a file called "Programming Instructions-New."  The third set of instructions indicated that at the end of the down limit step, the door would be fully open.  Instead, when I followed the last set of instruction, the opener traveled too far and bent the top panel of my garage door.  I am very concerned that other purchasers may get to the point I did in following the original instructions in the manual, which worked up to the point of the control limit test, and skip that important safety feature because the door goes up and down.  Quite apart from the damage it caused in my home, I believe that The Genie Company's negligence in distributing these unworkable instructions may put other families at risk.
justification: The incident caused property damage (bent garage door panel) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to unclear instructions potentially affecting multiple users.

incident_description:
A Centurion model of a Generac generator (7000 watts) was installed in late 2005. A car battery was needed in order to exercise the generator on a weekly basis. Approximately two years later the car battery exploded. The auto supply store replaced the battery at no cost. We thought it was a bad battery. In May 2007, we called a generator service company, Wooldridge Heating, Air, and Electrical, from Lynchburg, VA to service the generator on a routine basis. The second battery exploded in May 2010. Wooldridge installed a new battery, and continued to service the equipment once per year. The last service call was in December 2011.

The third battery exploded today, 06/20/2012. The service technician from Wooldridge called Generac to report the incident. He was told that the generator's battery charger was "too heavy" for this unit. They gave him a replacement part number for a more appropriate battery charger. They informed him that there had not been a recall on this item, although they were familiar with the problem and had obviously come up with a fix. They informed him that I would be responsible for replacing the battery and battery charger. I believe Generac should be made responsible for selling a faulty product with an obvious safety hazard and for compensating owners for the expense of replacing batteries and faulty parts.

Why do I think this is a safety hazard? Because the battery blew up in my face when I turned the generator on! I was not injured simply because the battery was beneath the control panel, but I did suffer temporary hearing loss, and for the third time I was forced to clean up the battery electrolyte, which again caused damage to the concrete pad the generator sits on.

The serial number of Centurion unit is 4097635. The item (model) number is 0046793. The part number for the replacement battery charger is OJ77030SRV.
justification: The incident caused temporary hearing loss and repeated property damage, indicating an injury and a likely recurrence due to the faulty battery charger.

incident_description: I was exposed to a low-level, injurious concentration of carbon monoxide (CO) over a 4-month period by daily use of a gas-log fireplace heating system installed in the un-vented mode.  I believe this system lacks sufficient safeguards to maintain the high efficiency necessary to be used un-vented.  I learned that a change in position of the logs results in sooting, which is a visual indicator that CO is being produced.  In my case, a fairly heavy soot coating on the walls and windows finally alerted me to the hazard, but it was not until after I suffered a sudden 90-percent loss of hearing in my left ear on December 23, 2011.  I subsequently learned that long-term exposure to low concentrations of CO can lead to health problems because of the cumulative effect, with a retention time in the bloodstream of several hours.   In my case, it was four months of daily exposure each evening to a low-level of CO (our CO detector, with a threshold of 100 ppm, provided no indication).  The result, as verified by a physician, was nerve damage that caused hearing loss along with unsteadiness and vertigo.  I've attached a technical paper that describes the link between CO and hearing loss.  When the heating season began, I moved the logs to relight the pilot after turning it off for the summer.  The owners' manual presents vague warnings about moving the logs and an incomprehensible diagram of log placement, but there is no warning that directly relates to a specific hazard of CO.  Later, after the logs were reset and cleaned by the original installer, they shifted on their own to again cause sooting.  There is no way to lock the logs in place.  Had this been a vented installation, there would have been no problem, but the dealer's selling point was that the high efficiency of the burner makes it perfectly safe to be un-vented.   When it is vented, of course, it provides substantially less heat to the room/home.  Beyond the direct effect such as I experienced, it is known that CO exposure during pregnancy can lead to fetal poisoning or death.
justification: The incident resulted in nerve damage causing hearing loss, vertigo, and unsteadiness, verified by a physician, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
On January 13, 2012 a Cosco step stool  collapsed suddenly when the right leg assembly broke. I was sent crashing to the floor onto my right shoulder. I immediately iced the shoulder and took Advil. On January 29 I consulted an orthopedic doctor-was told I may have suffered a deep bone contusion. On March 27 I consulted the doctor again, was advised to begin therapy, which i did. On April 9 I had an MRI which disclosed a full thickness tear of the Right Supraspinatus tendon with 2.5 cm of retraction. On May 7 I had surgery to repair the tendon. 

The pain was the most severe I have ever experienced. It is necessary to wear a sling for 6 weeks 24/7; following, one month severely restricted movement, 3 months guarded activity, and at 8 months a hopeful return to normal activity.  I cannot engage in ANY activity which loads the arm.  It is difficult to sleep in one position for more than 1.5 hours..Eating and putting on clothing is difficult. Showering is a challenge. 

I am 71+ years of age. I have a lifelong activity with horses on our ranch. I engage in all aspects of ranch work, including doing my own farrier work for 40 years. I will not be able to engage in normal and necessary ranch work for MONTHS. At this time my husband is carrying the entire burden of ranch work. I cannot clean my own house-having to hire help. Our annual maintenance trip to our ranch in Montana cannot happen. We have had to hire help to mow meadows for fire safety, and road maintenance.

Now, Cosco was sent a Certified Mail letter on May 22, 2012, describing the situation, my injury, and my concern for the safety of this product. No response. Not only do I resent being injured because of a faulty product, have my  participation in  lifelong activities threatened, I resent  Cosco Company's lack of response to a valid concern about a product's safety.

Cosco has experienced recalls in its history and a large civil penalty. Time for accountability.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring surgery and long-term recovery, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such severe injuries from step stool collapses are not common.

incident_description:
I had to replace the thermostats in my home (about 10) two years ago when one caught on fire, literally burning and melting off the wall in the middle of the night, fire trucks, the whole works.
The electrician used Honeywell RLV430 models as replacements for all locations.

Just noticed that over half or more of them, there is a small soot-streak on the wall over the "vents" above the control panel.  This is evident on at least the ones on light-colored walls (at least 5).  The others may have the same marks, but the walls are dark so it is hard to tell.

The model that caught fire previously was a Honeywell CT1650A1017N (and I wish at the time I had realized the electrician used the same manufacturer) and now researching online, I realize that what I thought was an isolated incident at our home was more likely related to the incidents that led to last-year's recall of some of their thermostats.

It was very expensive to have so many thermostats replaced (including the labor) and now it looks like I will need to repeat the process as these appear to be experiencing a similar issue.

If they are smoking under no load now (summer time) I fear what will happen come winter when they are being used again.
justification: The incident involves visible soot-streaks indicating potential smoking, but no injury or fire has occurred yet. The likelihood is high given the history and multiple affected units.

About 1/2 hour into continuous use and the pump housing began to smoke. Unplugged device and smoke increased. Housing and handle were extremely hot to the touch. Did best I could to spray water inside housing through vent openings. When smoke stopped I removed housing to examine pump. Once housing opened a disk shaped fan blade fell out. It appears this fan blade was supposed to be fitted in rear cowling of electric motor and it came loose causing the overheat. Several components of electric motor are scored and blackened. Portions of motor housing are melted as well.

incident_description:
A resident reported their home was vacant after 8:30 a.m. on the day of the incident.  About 8:00 p.m., a neighbor heard the smoke alarm sounding from next door.  The neighbor investigated the alarm, found a fire burning in the neighbor's residence, and called 911.  After the fire was put out, a cause investigation was conducted.  The investigation revealed the possible cause to be a malfunctioning button on the door bell assembly, which remained stuck in the depressed position, caused the wires leading from the button to the transformer to remain energized.  The continued current is suspected to have burnt thru the wiring which in turn caused radiant heat to spread to the plastic chime housing of the door bell cover located on the wall above the stairway.  The door bell cover eventully melted, dripping hot plastic onto the carpeted stairway below.  The supposedly flame-retardent carpeting ignited causing the eventual damage involved in this fire.  A check of the identical door bells in adjacent units revealed similar circumstances.  (See attached fire report.)

No injuries or deaths occurred as a result of this  incident.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, and similar issues were found in adjacent units, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
ProClean DRYER LINT REMOVAL KIT (Dundas-Jafine) - This 3 component system provides helpful brush/vacuum attachment tools to remove excess lint from dryer trap and vent duct line. However, the recommended procedure, troubleshooting info and manufacturer contact info is incomplete and poses a SAFETY hazard. While initially removing much lint and believing we would restore drying efficiency, our dryer failed to exhaust air to the outside when starting a new load. Hence, after following the limited instructions, it left us with a dryer that did not work and a DRYER OVERHEAT/FIRE RISK HAZARD.

The laundry room became warm/moist, the dryer external surface become very hot, there was no air exiting the vent from the outside. We turned the dryer off and suspected that the lint trap brush may have jammed something inside the dryer to block the internal exhaust. However, and after contacting the kit manufacturer for guidance, we discovered that we actually created a COMPLETE BLOCKAGE in the >10 ft duct line (running underneath the floor) by using the 10 ft. spiral duct brush. We were able to clear that out by aiming a leaf blower from the OUTSIDE into the vent entering the house. We blew out COMPRESSED LINT that filled a 3 gal trash can and had a major mess. NOTE: We used the gas blower from the outside, NOT the inside to avoid sparking the airborne lint in the laundry room (explosion hazard!).

When initially using the long spiral brush in the duct line, my wife and I were able to "pull out" much lint USING IT FROM BOTH SIDES of the duct. It was too short to "snake" all the way through. What we were actually doing in this process was also jamming/compressing the lint in the middle to create the blockage without knowing it (cannot see nor access the middle). So rather than restoring dryer efficiency, the kit process created a VENT BLOCKAGE and DRYER OVERHEAT/FIRE RISK. We were fortunate to observe the overheating/failure to vent, but know many consumers start a load and leave the house or go to bed. Should the dryer over-heat sensor fail, this poses a significant fire hazard.

The manufacturer's Product Development rep was actually very helpful in resolving this issue for our particular experience. Prior to his call, we felt we were going to have to repair or replace our 10 yr old [REDACTED] dryer (which was running OK prior to using the kit, just a little slower to dry). HOWEVER, it was not obvious how to contact the manufacturer for help, and the instructions were sparse. They should call out "post cleaning CHECKS" to confirm the dryer air is venting properly before using again plus trouble-shooting guidelines. There was no manufacturer contact info (e.g., name, phone, etc.) on the instructions, just a name/web address on the carton (which I suspect many would discard since it's hard to fit everything back into the box after 1st use). If no internet access, there is no way to contact them.

I am a retired PRODUCT DEVELOPER of laundry products and familiar with DRYER OVERHEAT/FIRE RISKS. I am filing this report to flag the hazard to others using this product PLUS ANY SIMILAR PROCESS they may use in clearing out the dryer duct line.
justification: The incident describes a significant safety hazard (dryer overheating/fire risk) but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I own a Sears Power washer model number 580.752200. While using this product to power wash our deck the protective sleeve that surround the power washer nozzle flew off hitting the glass patio door. This is the second high pressure nozzle that has failed during use. The nozzles I have had issues with are labeled "general" purpose and "max". I contacted Sears, both at the Appleton, WI store and through the internet, and they will not recognize the product as defective and will not replace the units. I feel this product is defective because it could fly off hitting somebody in the face or worse, in the eye.

Thank you in advance for investigating my issue.
justification: The incident involved a nozzle flying off and hitting a glass door, but no injury was reported. The likelihood is considered possible as it has happened twice.

incident_description:
The ON/OFF switch on my Craftsman Table Saw model 315.218050 has failed for a second time.  The switch allows the saw to be turned on, but not off.  I consider this a safety hazard in that I am unable to stop the blade from spinning which could be catastrophic in the event of an emergency.  The only way to stop the blade is to disconnect the power switch from the source, an inconvience in that the power cord plugin is remotely located from the saw itelf.  Each time this has happened I have had to order a replacement switch from Sears.  This same switch appears to be common amongst numerous other similar Craftsman power tools.  The fact that two have failed on my seldom-used power saw suggests there may be numerous similar incidents.
The Customer Service representative from whom I ordered the second switch provided me with a telephone number for their customer complaints.  When I called the number, the recording said the phonemail box was full.  A call to the Sears Customer Help Line provided a different telephone number.  The response (phonemail message) from that number was that the office was closed and to call back later.  This call took place at approximately 11:30 AM Eastern.
justification: The switch failure poses a safety hazard by preventing the saw from being turned off, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: The product is the Sears Craftsman 10" table saw, model #315.284620.The incident occurred while changing the blade on the saw for the first time. As instructed, I checked the bevel locking lever to make sure it was secure. This was the first time I had touched it. When I released the lever I heard a snapping sound and the blade immediately swung to the left. The plastic washer that serves as the locking device for the lever had snapped cleanly in two. Had I been operating the saw at the time, pushing a piece of wood through the blade, I could easily have been seriously injured, either by the blade running in to my hand or by the piece being cut jamming and/or flying in to the air. I believe this is a serious safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure that could have led to serious injury, but no actual injury occurred.

 The consumer feels that this product have too many unsafe features and should be investigated.

The other day I was using my laptop and noticed that it was not charging, even though it was plugged in.  I pulled the cord up from the floor to check to make sure it was working correctly, and noticed that part of the cord was sparking and smoking, and it also formed a brief small flame.  I immediately unplugged the cord and it stopped sparking and smoking.  When I looked at the cord, the outside was all melted away and the wires are exposed.

Last week on May 22 in the late morning, I was cutting a concrete tile, I had finished the cut and when I set the grinder down, the switch stuck, not really sure what happened then, if the grinder hit a piece of the tile or the ground, it kicked back striking me in the right knee, causing a very deep laceration. I went to the emergency room, received several sutures and medication for pain and infection. I have been off work since and still in a lot of pain. I hope this doesn't happen to anyone else.

incident_description: I've had my Toshiba Portege R835-P56X laptop for roughly 10 months. About a week ago I noticed the AC adapter/power cord was being sensitive when I connected it to charge (sometimes I had to rotate it slightly). It is the original cord from when I purchased the laptop Model # PA-1650-21. Today, May 30, 2012, while sitting here with the laptop plugged in, the cord began smoking and shooting sparks approximately 1.5 inches from the end where it plugs into my laptop. I'm talking real sparks and a lot of smoke out of no where. I immediately removed the adapter from my laptop, however it continued to spark until I unplugged it from my wall outlet. Had I not been there and left my laptop charging this would have definitely started a fire. I've read the reviews on the Toshiba power cords and how many have stated the inferior quality and short length of use they get from them, but after what's just happened I'm genuinely concerned. I bought this laptop because of the rave reviews it got from several credible web sites.

incident_description:
I was using a Milwaukee cordless drill, product no 2601-20, s/n B288C111303269, on Monday, 28 May 2012.  Unexpectedly, the chuck partially detatched from the drill housing when I operated the drill in reverse, leaving a 1/2" gap between the drill housing and the chuck.  When I reversed direction on the drill, the gap closed and pinched the skin on my left palm and pinky finger.  My palm was slightly cut, but my pinky finger was severely lacerated.  If the bleeding does not stop today my doctor has advised me to seek additional medical attention.

I puirchased the drill new in 2011. This is the first time the drill malfunctioned in this manner, normal operations over the last year or so since I've owned this product did not result in this malfuntion.  Now, normal drill operations always result in this malfunction.
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations and potential need for medical attention, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: it is a campbell hausfeld air compressor hu350100 and there is a air hose that runs from the tank to the air guage on the right side that touches the engine.  while using the compressor the engine burnt a hole in the hose which caused a back leak of air.  the part number for the hose is hu002500av.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his portable generator as the fuel gasket deteriorated, breaking on the inside of the gas tank and now the is model is leaking gas. The consumer stated that yesterday morning he came outside and attempted to power on the generator and there was gas leaking in his driveway. 

The consumer stated that the gas tank has a 6 gallon capacity and would assume the tank had leaked out 1-2 gallons of gas. The consumer further inspected the model and found that the fuel gasket deteriorated. 
The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product but discovered that his model is similar to the ones cited in release 09-305. The consumer called the firm today and he received no assistance. The consumer has not called the retailer as of yet. The product does not have to be operating in order to leak the gas.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak but no injury or harm occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased this generator from Electric Generators Direct and just after the warranty ran out, the carburetor started leaking fuel badly whenever I start it. I stared my genrator monthly and let it run for an hour. All fuel was fresh. Upon investigation, my repair shop says the float value chrome platting was defective and has failed, thus causing the float value to fail to cut off the fuel when then bowl is full. Fuel then overflows the carburetor and spills out and onto the ground creating a pool of raw fuel underneath the generator. 
The generator was a Honeywell HW7500E 7.5 KWatt electric start model.
justification: The incident involves a fuel leak creating a hazardous condition, but no injury or death is reported.

The consumer feels fortunate that there was not a fire in the home because of it.  The repairman ordered a new board and parts for replacement. incident_description:

The room had not been used in a few days.  There was no moisture, lint dust, or any other contributing factor anywhere near the outlet which could have caused it to short-out.  The unit was in that exact location for at least 3 years.  (In an adjacent outlet was another ac adaptor to a small hand vac.  This has been there for about 10 years w/o incident.)

Shark Steam Mop. Model S3501CO. 120V, 60Hx, 1550 W. The mop is gray (gold?), with interchangeable heads, microfiber replaceable pads, adjustable-height handle, a 180-degree swivel steering, a 15-ounce water tank, and a 25-foot power cord.

He opened the package and noticed a real strong odor.  Microban embedded into the product.  While installing the pad he noticed a strong odor coming from the pad, and it made him sick.  He took the product back to the store.  The consumer says the odor was severe and that several friends noticed the smell.
