incident_description:
I received a Kenmore canister vacuum cleaner about 5 years ago.I very seldom used it because of the weight of the wands. It came with power beaters etc which I didn't need because of hard wood floors only. If I used this machine more then 20-25 times that is a lot.  Mainly I used my old 30+year old vacuum or electric brooms. On May 17th I got out said vacuum...placed it on the floor in the room to be cleaned.  I extracted the electric wire from the machine, plugged it into the outlet. I then proceeded to turn the machine (on switch is in the handle). I felt a tremble in my hand and immediately saw several sparks coming from the hose connector to the machine.I dropped the wand handle and quickly ran to unplug the electrical wire from the outlet   I could smell something burnt. After awhile I moved the canister to a safe spot,afraid it might start a fire. When my son came to visit he checked it out to discover that the connector hose had dislodged from its covering exposing electrical wires which in turn shorted out the start up wiring. The covering was still in the machine but the connector hose (with the electrical wires) was touching something which caused it to shoot sparks as it had.  I have pictures of the defective parts. We purchased a new handle, hose, connector unit in an attempt to replace the defective unit and that  is when we found out the start up unit burnt out also. 

I called Sears repair number and was told there was nothing they could do for me... since the hose connector  was not a recall.  Upon further investigation I found that in 1987 there was a recall for a Kenmore vacuum cleaner hose problem very, very similar to mine.  That is why I am writing to you.  I know it has been several years since the recall and even though different companies are manufacturing these machines for Sears perhaps their design plans are still flawed.   I think it should be looked into before there is a house fire or some injury occurs.  I  think I  was lucky enough to escape both.
I wonder how many other people have had this problem and just passed it off as a lemon of a machine. As I previously stated ... the machine was not abused or over used  for this to happen.
I will be glad to share any other information that you require.

Respectfully yours,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved sparks and a burnt smell but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Quick & Hot water dispenser from Costco.  Model AH-780,   
Serial no. B-0G8-05736-3.    The rubber hose attached between the faucet and hot water tank burst.  The hot water dispenser is installed under the kitchen sink.  The rubber hose burst and water damaged the kitchen cabinet.  My greatest concern was Water was spraying at the electrical outlet socket. This may have cause a fire and electrical shock to anybody  near the the sink. The rubber hose is defective and cannot handle the hot water. Should not use rubber hose for hot water. Not a very good idea.  I called Waste Kind and Westbrass about this dangerous problem.  No luck business as usual.  In addition, I noticed individuals who own this product have the same problem.  I need some answer?
justification: The incident involved a burst hose causing water damage and potential electrical hazards, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I have 3 packs of the Safety 1st slide cabinet lock.  All six of the locks have broken after less than 6 months of use, allowing my child to easily access contents of cabinet.
justification: The locks broke, allowing child access, but no injury or incident occurred.

incident_description:
Caller's wife was sitting in their family room when she heard popping and crackling sound.
She looked up and saw flames coming out of the fan and flaming upward 6" to 8 " inches around the fan.

She jumped up and turned the switch off then ran to her husband who was working just outside.

Caller turned the breaker off, viewed the fan which was extinguished.

He contacted the manufacturer April 26th & was told that there is nothing they do for him 

He is contacting the CPSC to inquire  he can obtain assistance obtaining a replacement for his fans due to having two more of them and that he doesn't want someone else's home to catch fire.                                                                           

He purchased his house in August 2005.
These fans were never recalled due to fire, however they were recalled in 1993 for a fall hazard.
justification: The incident involved flames from a fan but no injury or death occurred, and the fire was quickly extinguished.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was using the ÃÂcarpet attachable featureÃÂ of her canister vacuum and it was working properly while she was pushing it forward. The vacuum is made up of three components, the canister, the hand held and the wand where you can attach other features. 

When she tried to pull the vacuum backwards, it completely stopped working.  The consumer had the vacuum on for approximately a minute, before it stopped working.  The consumer saw sparks, smoke and an electrical burning odor being emitted from where the two (hand held and the wand) components meet. The flames came up almost to her hand.

The consumer unplugged the vacuum immediately and the flames when out. The consumer stated that the components were melted and chard. The consumer stated that nothing was stuck inside the vacuum, to force it to overheat.  She stated that the vacuum is no longer usable. 

She is not injured and there were no damages to her home. 
The consumer is concern because this is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and flames, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
Ryobi SA1802 Cordless Drill.
Drill overheats causing motor to smoke and fail during normal use. Incident occurred during light drilling of wood lasting 3-4 seconds in duration for each hole drilled. Flames were visible through the motor ventilation slots. White smoke was emitted from the motor area and motor functionality degraded quickly. Incident signs are similar to that of a previous recall for Ryoi cordless drills catching on fire.
justification: The drill overheated and emitted smoke and flames, but no injury was reported. The description mentions similar past incidents, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
Harbor Breeze Ceiling Fan Bellevue model E-BE44ABZ5C.  Purchased at Lowes 8/4/11

Wattage Limiting Device Heated up, Smoked, Created a small fire in the Fan Light kit.

LiteX Products customer service said it happens and is sending a new device.  My house smells of bad smoke.  Wires to the device were fried and burnt.  Inside of light kit black with soot.

Stock installation.  Nothing different, except a light dimmer on the lamp kit only (not motor).

Thanks
justification: The incident involved a small fire and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Last week, while cleaning, the hand held portion of my Ergorapido turned itself on.  When it would not shut off, I set it on the counter to let the battery run itself out.  A short time later I smelled burning plastic.  It had burned a spot through the paper towel it was set on and burned a small spot in my butcher block counter top.  I tossed it in the sink and ran water over it.  It stopped running so I turned the water off.  In about 30 seconds, the water on the machine started to sizzle.  Then it came back on and the battery element on the back of it turned red and started to burn again.  I soaked it in water for about 5 minutes.  It stopped.  Once I turned the water off it started up again.  It  finally put it outside, in the middle of the driveway where it eventually burned itself out.  I wrote to Elerctrolux asking them about this but, other then acknowledging my e-mail, I have not had a reply.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning device causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
Product: Stihl SR 400 (backpack mist/blower)
SN: 247775041
Date of purchase: 09-13-2000
Following fueling and operation over various times the engine begins to ÃÂbog downÃÂ.  Upon loosening the fuel cap fuel spews out of the two vent holes in the cap for a distance of approximately 2-3 feet. If the cap is further loosened fuel under pressure comes out around the threads. The total amount discharged is estimated to be ÃÂ½ to 1 pint. 
Once the pressure is relieved the engine operation returns to normal, until the pressure rises and has to be relieved. If the pressure is relieved while the unit is on the operators back there is great risk of fire and serious/catastrophic consequences to the operator and others nearby.
The fuel cap was replaced with a factory manufactured cap, however, the problem persists. The unit was returned to a factory authorized repair shop on two occasions where no defect was found.  Following both occasions the unit was placed in service again with the same problem re- occurring after being refueled several times. 
The userÃÂs manual states (page 15):  ÃÂWarning: In order to reduce the risk of burns or other personal injury from escaping gas vapor or fumes remove the fuel filler cap carefully so as to allow any pressure build up in the tank to release slowly.ÃÂ The above events far exceed ÃÂvapor and fumesÃÂ.
The unit is not serviceable due to the extreme hazard to its operator.
I have attempted to contact Stihl via E-Mail (the only way I know how, however, they have not replied). The authorized dealer says that nothing can be done as they are not able to duplicate the event in their shop. 
The unit sitting in their back lot running is obviously not equivalent to normal operating conditions in the field.
Any assistance you can provide will be greatly appreciated.
justification: The description indicates a high risk of fire and catastrophic consequences to the operator and others nearby, suggesting potential for death. The problem re-occurs after being refueled several times, making it likely.

incident_description:
The safety concern is on an LG Steam Dryer -- model #DLGX2502W purchased in February of 2010.  The first incident was in February of 2012, where I smelled a gas leak.  After confirmation from a gas professional that the leak was not in the line or at the connection, we called an appliance repairman.  The leak was at one of the valves.  It was replaced and there was confirmation through testing that there was no further leak.  3 months later we smelled gas again.  The valve has already burned out... new theory is that there is a defect in the control board that is causing the valves to burn out.  A video demonstration on youtube (link attached) demonstrates EXACTLY what is happening to my dryer (this is the exact same model).  THIS IS A POTENTIAL FIRE HAZARD.. THE WAY THE DRYER IS OPERATING IS TO RELEASE GAS BETWEEN THE FIRE CYCLES.  I called LG again (5/22/12) and they claim that there is not a defect (without even bother to investigate my claim or without speaking to my repairman that can provide exact details) and that NO ONE else has called regarding this issue.  I find this EXTREMELY hard to believe for 2 reasons:  1) there is a youtube video that documents the issue - filming exactly what I'm seeing in my dryer, and 2) replacement control boards for this model are on back order from LG until June 2012... indicating a part that is in high demand

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mJqzwdBavfw

This is a defect in the product that has the potential to cause significant injury or death.  LG needs to investigate at the very least, and I think, will find that a recall is in order
justification: The incident involves a gas leak and potential fire hazard, which could lead to injury or death, but no actual harm has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore canister vacuum with carpet attachment C50XDDY0B047. I have recently noticed that the short cord which brings power from the wand to the carpet attachment has frayed. The cord bends over a sharp corner of the attachment, and also moves across this bend when the attachment is angled for cleaning. The fraying has caused a short, and I will replace it, but I think this should be reported.
Photos are enclosed
justification: The frayed cord has caused a short, which is an incident but no injury has been reported.

incident_description:
I was using an ACDelco Hydraulic 2-ton Trolley Jack (model 34136) this weekend to check my brakes and rotors.  I would jack up one side of my car, put a jackstand underneath the vehicle, then lower the jack and move to the other side of the vehicle and repeat -- would have the front end of the vehicle on jackstands, take care of the brakes and rotors, then lower the vehicle and do the rear brakes and rotors.

The jack worked fine on the front of the car.  I jacked up the rear of the vehicle and was moving to put the jackstand in place when the jack failed.  The car dropped, but I had the jackstand in place...but it missed my fingers by about 2 seconds, and if it had failed 15 seconds earlier the jackstand would not have been fully in position, and would have probably gone flying and/or damaged the vehicle.  The gas tank of my vehicle is less than 6 inches from the jack point...you get the picture
justification: The jack failed but no injury occurred, though there was potential for serious harm.

incident_description:
The caller stated that her spouse is experiencing problems with the pocket folding knife not locking.  The incident occurs very often since he purchased the product.  She feels that this knife displays similar hazard of Release #12-163 and is very unsafe.

The caller stated that her spouse at times had to fiddle with the switch to close it.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The caller feels that this is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning knife that poses a safety hazard but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I purchased a frigidaire front load washer about 3 years ago, I started to smell a foul odor coming from the washer and immediately called the frigidaire representatives.  I was told to replace the bellow which is a large grey casket that keeps the water from spilling out of the machine, I replaced that part, yet a smell was still coming from the unit.  I was then told that after each wash I needed to wipe out the washer because keeping the door closed would keep moisture inside and allow mold to build up, (very difficult to keep the door open at all times with a toddler).  After two weeks of doing that, the foul, musty, molding smell still has not gone away.  I again called the frigidaire reps again and they told me to now buy a product called Aafresh, and use these cleaning tabs to get rid of the mold.  to no avail, the foul, musty, molding odor is still there, and now it's starting to make my clothing and my children's clothing smell of mold.  I again called the frigidaire reps and they informed me that the only thing they could do for me was to issue a 40% discount on another frigidaire product...Short of dismantling this washer I have done everything they have asked of me.  My husband is currently deployed to Afghanistan, we are a family of six and I am constantly doing laundry, but having to keep the washer door open it has led to our small military housing unit to smell of must and mildew, not to mention that my two year old is constantly trying to climb in the machine.  I am also concerned that  the mold  will start to make my children and myself sick.    I feel the least that frigidare can do is replace the defective washer.  
Thanks for your time in this matter 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a persistent mold issue causing foul odors and potential health concerns, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I have a Goldstar dehumidifier that when operated, sounded like an air conditioner going on and off and wasn't pulling in water and was shutting off abnormally. I initially did research for repair instructions only to find my Goldstar Dehumidifier has a recall on it due to wiring to the compressor. It has been reported to have caused numerous house fires, injuries, etcÃÂ I contacted the company and they agreed the model/serial numbers fall in the recall, however, they refuse to help me because they do not like the format of my address. I live in a somewhat rural area so I offered to drive to Albany, NY (the capital of the state) which is 2 hours out of the way to bring it to a service center. The company maintained their refusal to help simply because they did not like my PO Box address. IÃÂm not sure what to do. The PO Box is my physical address. Please help.
justification: The dehumidifier has a known recall for causing fires and injuries, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I am writing this letter to advise you of a major problem with the plastic wall hanger used on your 5 pound ABC
Kidde fire extinguisher. I was at a pizza store in Parsippany, NJ the other evening with my grandsons and their
parents to enjoy a Friday evening dinner. One of my grandsons, a little over 2 years old, had walked away from the table followed by his mother. He went over to the entrance door, where one of your 5 pound extinguishers was hanging. When his mother reached him he put up his arms to be picked up and in doing so his little hand tapped the bottom of the fire extinguisher.
At this point there was almost a real tragedy. The extinguisher fell out of the bracket, slid by the bridge of his nose and landed on his foot. You can imagine the screams, and chaos that developed after this event. Luckily, the extinguisher did not hit him flush in the head, he probably would no longer be here, as well as that it did not hit his foot with the bottom edge, his foot was hit by the side of the extinguisher.
The bracket used on this extinguisher is totally inadequate. It should have a strap to make sure it stays in the rackunless needed. You should consider recalling these brackets and stop using them immediately, little children lives are at risk as well as adult toes and feet. All you have to do is bump it and it is falling.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the child's nose and foot, and the description suggests the bracket's design makes such occurrences likely.

incident_description:
We have a Kikkerland Easy Fold Step Stool.  The model is ZZ09-BK.  The stool has been manufactured in China.  This product closely matches the [REDACTED] Folding Step Stool that has recently been recalled.  From the pictures, the two products are identical.
We have had the step stool for about six months.  Within that time, the step stool has cracked on the top portion by the handle.  While I can snap the pieces back in place, we have to regularly check the cracked area to make sure the pieces have not misaligned again and pose a laceration hazard.

[REDACTED]
justification: The step stool has cracked, posing a potential laceration hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
A 17 mo old child was found by mother after having bitten into a Purex ulra pack of laundry detergent. Soon became ill with vomiting, drowsiness and respiratory distress. At a community hospital, he was nearly unresponisve with severe respiratory distress and required emergency endotracheal intubation, and transfer to our children's hospital ICU. Recovered markedly over 24 hrs, but the rapid onset of severe depressed level of consciousness and respiratory distress is disinctly unusual after laundry product ingestion. And this form of packaging seems to be not very child resistant, and very attractive and accessible.
As a pediatric toxicologist and assoc director of the Phila area posion control center, i described his case on our  list serve of US PCCs, and have discovered 3 or 4 other US cases and 1 Canadian  case in past 2 weeks. A physician from the Milan, Italy PCC wrote in to say that more than 500 cases have occurred in Italy over past year since the product was introduced ( introduction  was only ~ 2mos ago in the US, apparently), and they have embarked on a large public health and media campaign to reduce further pediatric exposures.
justification: The child required emergency intubation and ICU care, indicating severe injury, and the incident is part of a pattern with multiple cases reported, suggesting likelihood is high.

incident_description: Bought a Firenze bathtub and matching enclosure for my own remodel. It has been in for 9 or 10 months. It was pointed out to me that I have a crack in the bottom of it towards the back where it slants. Its a 4 1/2 inch crack that can be pushed in with the fingers. The water leaks out and runs under the tub and into the basement. I talked to the Home Depot where I purchased it and they were surprised at what was happening to the tub. It can't be fixed because it is Acrylic (plastic). I was told that it would need to come out and be replaced. I was not happy with their answer. Now my walls, surround and tub with fittings has to be cut out with a sawsall. Now I must decide on what to replace it with. plastic again or fiberglass. I have heard nothing but good about this tub, this is why I purchased it. I just didn't expect to be destroying my bath again to replace it because of defective merchandise. Now I read that others have and are experiencing the same problems.
justification: The incident involves a defective bathtub causing water leakage and property damage, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Initial incident description replaced with consumer's description included with the Consent Letter, as follows:

On 5/5/12 consumer put on a load to wash. Closed the door. Set the cycle. Heard a loud noise as if a gun went off. Washer tripped the breaker. Door locked and would not open. Contacted repair technician and was advised 5/8/12 was the earliest for service.

On 5/8/12 Technician attempted to re-start washer. Heard a number of sparks and machine tripped breaker again. Re-started again, heard more sparks. Was advised it was not good. Looking at over $1,000 in repairs or more and should look at a new washer. Was also advised that parts are not available for the Bosch Nexxt appliances.

On 5/14/12 consumer contacted Manufacturer and advised the unit had burned out. She also advised manufacturer that an electrical problem was not repaired by Extended Warranty while unit was under Warranty. Manufacturer asked consumer to provide copies of the repair docinnentation and they would see what they can do.

Consumer feels unit is unsafe and could have potentially caught her house on fire. Parts are not available by the manufacturer for repairs. Extended Warranty was made aware of an electrical problem and did nothing to repair it. Consumer was advised by the technician for Extended Warranty to plug unit in a regular receptacle and not a GFCI, which is against ALL building codes.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning washer causing sparks and tripping breakers, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
TVH500 by Vornado Air LLC caught fire internally. Serial number 10253. Date of Manufacture: AUG09. No property damage. No personal injury. Vornado contact information: 415 E. 13th Street, Andover, KS 67002. PHONE:(800) 234-0604. FAX: (316) 733-1544.


The space heater was returned to Kohl's in West Springfield, MA on Sunday, May 20, 2012 at 2:32pm. "[REDACTED1]", the manager, oversaw the return. "[REDACTED2]", another manager, was also there that day. Store Information: West Springfield, 935G Riverdale Street, West Springfield, MA 01089, Phone: (413)731-0991. Store Number: 639.
justification: The space heater caught fire internally but there was no property damage or personal injury reported.

incident_description: The screw holding the hinge to my Werner S2210 attic ladder broke off last week.  I called Werner who told me the ladder was made by old company who has gone bankrupt.  Werner offered me $100 towards a new ladder at Home Depot.  I declined and started searching online for info.  I found multiple threads on same issue with these ladders. What is the CPSC doing to recall these ladders?
justification: The incident involved a broken screw on a ladder with no reported injury, but there are multiple reports of similar issues, indicating a potential widespread problem.

incident_description:
Plug-in chime device (part of wireless doorbell extension system) overheated and failed. There are obvious discolorations in the white plastic housing that were apparently caused by a very hot resistor labeled "R2" inside the unit, which was plugged into a power strip. My concern is that the heat could easily have cause a fire had it not been located on top of a metal filing cabinet, which dissipated the heat. The device carries a UL rating and was located indoors.
The device bears the information "DIMANGO by Lamson Home Products, 25701 Science Park Drive., Cleveland, OH 44122", "Model 3730DR" and was purchased sometime in 2006.
justification: The device overheated and failed, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: Power/charger cord for my Kindle, which is only 3 years old, has disintegrating rubber casing all through out.  There is bare metal wire showing and I am concerned that this is a safety concern.  I have reported it to Amazon and did not feel that it was acknowledged as a problem previously reported or a safety issue.
justification: Bare metal wire exposure poses a potential electrical hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Local fire department was dispatched to a residential dwelling for the report of a building fire. I responded as the on-duty fire investigator. A moderate smoke condition was found in the basement of the dwelling. The investigation revealed that an unknown malfunction in the dehumidifier resulted in heat damage to the unit and smoke in the dwelling.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dehumidifier causing heat damage and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Elite washer purchased September 2010 Redmond Washington. While washing clothes on mother's day the interior glass shattered. A loud thumping noise brought our attention to the problem. The machine was on the wash tumble cycle when this occurred. The contents of the washer were 2 towels, 1 cotton blanket and many pairs of a child's underwear and socks. The glass gouged the stainless steel drum and had splinter throughout the contents. We have not run the machine since as the glass front is gone and there are shards of glass everywhere.
justification: The incident involved the washer's glass shattering, causing damage to the drum and contents, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I received second degree burns when a Joy Mangano steamer was knocked over and the water poured from the steam holes like a geyser. I believe there is a defect in the design. There should be some kind of safety on the machine that does not allow boiling hot water to pour from it if it is tipped or knocked over. I was shocked and horrified when after steaming my clothes I was severely burned and had to receive medical treatment. My fear is what if a younger person had been using the steamer? I am just perplexed as to why a product is sold to consumers and it has the possibility to injure and permanently scar people.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I have a Solar system on my roof with  eighty eight 34 watt tiles producing electricity. The system is 3 years old.  I was advised by the manufacture of the 34 watt solar tiles to turn my solar system off as there is some kind of fire hazard associated with the solar tiles.  The manufacturer, Applied Solar also indicated they were going to do a voluntary recall through the CPSC in conjunction with [REDACTED], another manufacture of similar 50 watt solar tiles.  This happened last May 23rd, 2011.  No fix or other information about the supposed problem has been supplied from Applied Solar since the original notice.  Recently [REDACTED] has gotten a fix for their 50 watt tiles and is in the process of repairing their customers tiles.  This month a call to Applied Solar [REDACTED] gets a recorded message to the effect that Applied Solar advised the CPSC that it has ceased operations and does not have assets or funds to fix the 34 watt tiles  and that they will not be involved in repair efforts.

So my questions are;

1. Do I really have a fire hazard on my roof?
2. Was or is this a problem only with the [REDACTED] 50 watt tiles??
3. Did Applied Solar do a voluntary recall?
4. If there is a recall on the OE34 watt tiles what is the procedure to get the problem fixed now that the original manufacturer has ceased operations?
5. If there is a fix for the OE34 watt tiles how will I be notified if the manufacture, Applied Solar, has ceased operations?
justification: The description indicates a potential fire hazard but no actual incident, injury, or death has occurred.

incident_description:
Product:  Rowenta DX-8800 Clothes Iron.

Iron cought fire at power cord entry point.  Smoke and flames burning cord's protective gromet.   There was no stress on cord - iron just sitting there plugged in.  Cursory (non tear-down) inspection of Iron and Cord show them to be in good condition.   Flames would have spread to home if someone not there monitoring.  I am a USAF safety officer / incident investigator.


Internet search revealed multiple instances of this event to others.
justification: The iron caught fire without injury, but flames could have spread if not monitored. Internet reports indicate this is a recurring issue.

incident_description: On May 1, 2012 my Samsung Gas Dryer caught on fire. (The model is DV448AGW/XAA and it was purchased on July 18, 2009.) The fire was caused due to the igniter breaking off of the causing the flames to build around the gas line. I caught the fire in time to keep it within the dryer. When I contacted Samsung about this, they immediately directed me to their Product Liability team even though the dryer is technically out of warrantee. I have had both my personal repairman and the repairman sent by Samsung claim that even if the dryer is fixed, it is unsafe to use. Both repairman said that we were lucky the dryer did not explode in our home. Neither have seen this happen before but I am concerned this could happen in other Samsung dryers. Today is May 15th and I am still fighting with Samsung to address this problem. After 14 days, they now refuse to acknowledge that the root of the problem was the igniter breaking off in the unit. (I have photos and proof of these). They claim the problem was due to lint blockage. I clean the internal lint catcher in my dryer after every load and we vacuum out the hose leading the the dryer at least every 6-8 weeks. I also had a vent specialist come into my home who also told me my vents were clean. Samsung has a very dangerous product out there and if someone doesn't address them about it, someone will get hurt. I have tried. I am just one consumer and they hope to brush me under a rug. Please help so someone doesn't get hurt!
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dryer with no reported injuries, and the likelihood is unlikely as it was described as an uncommon occurrence by the repairmen.

incident_description:
I own three portable heaters with fan made by a company called Howard Berger Co called Comfort Zone Model # CZ40 Date code: 1105CX and recently the side of one of unit fan had melted but before I knew that we had smelled a burning smell in the home but could not find it, I noticed the heater was not working and when I grabbed it to look at it I burned my had and also believed I was shocked before I dropped it on the floor.

I have contacted the company and spoke with a [REDACTED] and it would appear they don't care because all they wanted to do was replace the unit for me with a more costly one.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and a potential electric shock, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue was identified after noticing a burning smell and malfunction.

incident_description: Our Crane brand Blue Bear humidifier started smoking and almost caught fire. Thank god we were in the room at the time. I would hate to think what may have happened if it was overnight when our child was sleeping. The humidifier was less than one year old and only used on occasion.
justification: The humidifier started smoking and almost caught fire, but no injury or death occurred as the incident was noticed in time.

incident_description: I was steam-mopping the floor as I usually do, using a back-and forth motion. Suddenly the mophead blew off and exploded with a great burst of steam. I was very lucky that this happened when the mop was away from my body and no pets were in the vicinity, as the unit was very hot. After I got over my shock, I looked at the area where the pieces had come apart. Nothing appeared broken, so after it cooled down I put the pieces back together and tried to resume mopping. But I wasn't hearing the normal stem noises, and I could not generate steam pressure by pumping the handle. As I was about to give up, the mophead again exploded off the unit. This time water poured out of the handle end in addition to steam. This was obviously a very dangerous defect and I began looking online to see if this model had been recalled.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous defect with the steam mop, but no injury occurred as the mop was away from the body and no pets were nearby.

incident_description: The consumer says that she smelled something burning.  Went downstairs and saw the laundry room was filled with smoke.  They unplugged the washing machine.  She says that the washer was on for about 30 minutes prior to the incident occurring.  She says the unit was repaired in November 26th,  2006 for replacement of the control board.  The consumer tried to contact the manufacturer but has not been able to reach a live person.
justification: The incident involved smoke but no reported injury or death, and similar incidents occur with moderate frequency.

incident_description: I have a Kikkerland 9" plastic step stool, extremely similar to the [REDACTED] version currently being recalled. I weigh only 145lbs, but when I stepped in the center of it, it cracked and I lost my balance and fell. The stool is rated to 300lbs, but obviously not when placed all in the center. I sustained no injuries, other than a bruise to my arm where I hit the granite counter top and the broken glass to clean up from the dropped tumbler.
justification: The incident involved a fall but no significant injury, only a minor bruise, and the stool's failure under expected conditions suggests a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Purchased early in year 2012 from Menards: OPTIMUS oscillating heater with fan, 2 heat settings and thermostat.  I discarded box and receipt after 3 months as thought working well.  Yesterday when cleaning carpet in my mother's bedroom, I saw that the plug (without ground) had melted into the extension cord.  They are now fused (melted) together.  My mother used this heater daily, and I'm glad to have discovered this before disaster struck.
Thank you.
justification: The plug and extension cord melted together, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Shortly after I purchased the Kennedy 13-inch step stool, I sat on it to groom my dog and the leg connections started popping loose.  As it was unusable after that, I threw it away.  Now I just received a notice that the stools have been recalled, so I thought I would report mine also since I now have an opportunity to make a difference.  Purchased July, 2010.
justification: The stool became unusable but no injury was reported, fitting the criteria for an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
I purchased the recalled Kennedy International step stools in a pack of two at TJMaxx.  I have both the 9 and the 13 inch stools.  I have had the stools for about 2 years.  I used them for reaching in tall kitchen cabinets and my 4 year old used the 9 inch stool to reach the bathroom sink.  After about 1 year of use, the 13 inch stool broke at the foldable handle and came apart at the "folding seam" while I was standing on to reach something.  I was able to catch myself and only obtained a cut on my ankle (other than the shock!).  
Only a few months later, my son (who only weighs 35 lbs.) fell through the same spot on the 9 inch stool while brushing his teeth.  He busted his lip on the counter top during the fall.  I have not used the stools since and am not surprised at this recall.  I just assumed that I bought a cheap product and learned my lesson about plastic folding stools!
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (a cut on the ankle and a busted lip) from the stools breaking during use.

incident_description: The first service call in 2010 was to replace the thermostat and a portion of attached red wire. 4 inches of red 12 gauge wire attached to the heating element has melted to the point of release from the clip allowing it to hang freely inside the unit. This has happened twice prior. Property damage was limited to a burnt odor permeating the clothing.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burnt odor) but no injury, and it has happened twice prior, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
On May 5, 2012, I purchased a hand truck from the Tractor Supply Company in Dixon, CA.  The hand truck label indicated that it was rated for 1000 pounds.  After I got it home, I wanted to properly inflate the tires so that I could use it to move a 30 cu foot fire safe I had just purchased.  While looking at the tires, I discovered that they were labeled, "Max load 353 pounds".  The unit has two tires, thus the max load (tire limitation) is 706 pounds.  I called customer service and they said, ask the store.  I went to the store.  The manager called the same customer service that I had called.  This time, customer service told her that the only thing they could go by was whatever the label said.  The store was unwilling to take the item in return or make a price adjustment.

Tractor Supply Company Model#:  011118
SKU#: 3893949

I will not use the hand truck to move more than 650 pounds.  I am unaware of any injuries from this product.
justification: The incident involves a product mislabeling issue with no reported injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as the user has decided to limit the load to a safe weight.

incident_description:
Pass and Seymour model 660-WG: Back of switch breaks off at quick connect causing switch to not operate properly.  Occasional arcing occurs if not replaced.  This is the fourth switch that I have had to replace with the same failure.  original equipment for house that was built during 2006-2007 time frame.

This is the same failure that occurred in incident 20110829-B28DF-2147475816 and noted on other online retail feedback.
justification: The incident describes a recurring equipment failure causing operational issues and occasional arcing, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: Had a can of Krylon Clear Glaze on work bench, and went back some time later to find it had leaked and stuck itself to the bench and damaging the bench top. Thought it may have just been an old can so bought 3 more from Michael's Crafts. Put the cans into storage drawer in basement till needed. Not long later came home to find paint smell in the house but had not been painting.  Found basement filled with fumes to the extent it was difficult to get air, and discovered 2 Krylon cans had leaked, filling bottom of drawer with liquid glaze. By chance I had shut off the furnace before I went to work or I believe I would have come home to find it had exploded from the fumes, or had been destroyed by fire!  I contacted Krylon about the problem and they  only said they would replace the products if I supplied them with my information and the numbers from the bottoms of the cans. I supplied the information requested and said I could send a can back if they wished to examine it to determine the problem.  It has been some months and I have not heard from Krylon nor did they ever send replacements.  If I had not shut down my furnace I am sure I would no have a house.  Not only was there the fire or explosion danger but I am sure the basement filled with fumes was a health danger as well.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and potential health hazards, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Product:  DELL AC power adapter Model NO: D12-50 
Input:  120V 60Hz 15W
Output: 12VDC 500mA

Power adapter was being used with a pair of DELL speakers model no: A215 

On 5/10/2012 I was informed by an employee that her power supply for her speakers was burning hot. Upon inspection, the ac adapter had melted its casing and burned a dark area (2"x3") into the linoleum floor underneath it.
justification: The power adapter melted and caused damage to the floor, but there was no reported injury.

incident_description: my daughter was able to take the plug protector from the wall and was almost shocked.
justification: The child was almost shocked, indicating a potential hazard but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Please SEE ATTACHMENTS for information about how the clamp for attaching the neutral wire to a GFI circuit breaker was screwed down so tight that no human could get it loose with hand tools. The electrician (new construction 5 years ago) apparently got inventive and jammed the wire in between the circuit breaker body and the screw head. This finally led to heating and crisping of the neutral wire's insulation, a fire hazard that I discovered just in the nick of time.
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard due to improper installation, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased three NightLock door barricades from:

http://nightlock.net
Taylor Brothers Door Lock, LLC
1400 E. Coldwater Rd.
Flint, Michigan 48505

The door lock consists of a base that is fastened to the floor and a bar that slides into a groove in the base.  I cut my finger pretty badly on the upper edge of the groove in the base.  I checked all three nightlocks that I purchased and all of them had razor sharp edges.
justification: The user cut their finger pretty badly on the sharp edges of the door lock, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purshased a Regency wood buring fireplace insert model Hampton HI300 from a local dealer and had it installed by the local dealer. The manufacturer states they have a lifetime warranty. After one season of burning wood. The top side of the fire box is rusting. This could lead to a carbon monoxide issue in the house and a potential fire. Tired to contact the manufacture  which is in BC Canada and no response. The dealer will not help and the manufacturer will not help.
justification: Rusting could lead to carbon monoxide or fire hazards, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: The hammer I purchased at 99 CENT ONLY STORE, on Clairemont Mesa Blvd., San Diego, Ca., for my grandson, came apart after one use.  It turns out that the very heavy iron head is attached to a flimsy steel tube with only a brittle plastic band that shattered on first use!  It could have caused serious injury had anyone been standing where the head landed.  I called the 99 Cent Only Stores customer service, but they hung up on me and I received recorded messages when I tried to call back.  They have never returned my call, even though I left a detailed message on their answering machine, so I don't think they intend to acknowledge the information.
justification: The hammer head came apart but no one was injured, though it had the potential to cause serious injury.

incident_description:
I installed a General Electric  Time Switch model 15207 NEMA Indoor BM-A301US5-12 for control of a water heater on or about December 15, 2011.  It worked perfectly for about a week or ten days.  I began smelling an odor which resembled chlorine or ozone, but could not isolate the source.

On December 26, 2011, I noticed the hot water heater, to which the Time Switch was wired was not turning on and thus not heating water.  Upon opening the timer, I discovered that there had been an internal melt-down on the connection panel.  Specifically, where the load 1 is connected by the supplied jumper wire to the 1 Com input.

I have no idea why this melt down did not start a house fire.
justification: The incident involved a melt-down in the time switch but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she started having problems with washer approximately 2 years after it was in use, with water filling up in the drum and when the door is opened , water is spilling on the floor which could flood her home.  She stated that she has had several local service call done to the washer.

Consumer stated that she has attempted to call the manufacturer but was unsuccessful.

Consumer feels that this washer is unsafe due to the fact it can flood her house and damaged her property.
justification: The incident involves water spillage that could flood the home, posing a risk to property but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: We purchased a Whirlpool Duet Washing Machine in 2006 and we have noticed a large amount of mold build-up in the boot of the washer.  So far we have tried everything to remove the mold but we are having no luck in removing the mold or the mildew smell.  I believe this is a serious health issue because of the mold and the spores being released into our "clean" laundry.
justification: Mold build-up in the washing machine poses a health risk due to potential exposure to spores, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
The rubber drain hose between a Maytag MAVT446AWW washing machine tub and the pump slipped off of the plastic drain spout of the washing machine tub assembly.  When the hose came off, the water in the tub spilled onto the floor causing serious water damage to the house.

The drain spout of the tub assembly appears to be thin and slightly tapered and the barb is slight.  These deficiencies allowed the rubber hose to simply slip off.  

I ordered a new tub and find the spout of the new tub is not significantly different than the original.  This looks like a defective design.  

[REDACTED]
Unified Investigations and Sciences
Clinton, WA
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused serious water damage but no injury or death.

incident_description:
We recently purchased a humidifier made by Vicks.  (A Vicks Cool Mist Humidifier from Target)

The humidifier was very loud on the highest setting and still pretty loud on the lowest setting.  The real problem with the humidifier was its horrible design.  It leaked water everywhere when we plugged it in and left it in our 2-year-old's room. I am concerned that this product could electrocute someone or catch on fire if the water all leaked out and the humidifier continued running.
justification: The humidifier leaked water but no injury or death occurred, though there is concern about potential future hazards.

incident_description: Our 4 year old GE High Effiency Washer stopped running and the smoke was coming out the closed washer door.  I unplugged the unit and called 9-1-1 not knowing if it would go up in flames.  The laundry room filled with smoke as did the whole downstairs.  The firemen came and pulled the washer away from the wall.  They determined that the motor had burned itself out.  They instructed me not to use the washer again.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The electric heat pump water heater was installed on 7/15/10.  On 12/6/11, water started spraying out of the top of the water heater, resulting in flooding in my basement.  

Upon investigation, it was discovered that the outlet pipe had corroded through.  There were also signs of corrosion on the rest of the tank.  I contacted GE, and they told me that corrosion is not covered by warranty, even though there is no mention of that in the warranty language.

Corrosion failure in a water heater that is only a little over a year old is a design defect.
justification: The incident involved flooding due to a corroded water heater, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: My Bosch electric dryer caught on fire in the house.   The fire was not in any of the normal places that dryer fires might be expected and it was because of a design flaw.   The back of the drum has holes in it and little bits of debris collected there over the two years I had the dryer.   On the morning of March 30, 2012, it caught fire and began putting out black smoke.   My housemate and I got a hand truck and removed the dryer from the house after disconnecting it from the vent. etc.  I will never put that dryer back in my house because it is a definite fire hazard.   I used to like the Bosch brand, but I am no longer a fan of their appliances.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dryer, which posed a significant hazard but resulted in no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
found water on kitchen floor and under sink - from the INSINKERATOR INSTANT HOT WATER DISPENSER, Model #H-990-2 - Serial #05048961424

WATER IS LEAKING from the INSINKERATOR INSTANT HOT WATER DISPENSER, Model #H-990-2 - Serial #05048961424

I have unplugged it.

I noticed the leaks on or about January 19th.
justification: Water leakage from the dispenser poses a potential hazard but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: This is the 2nd water heater from A.O. Smith that has failed via rusting in less than the warranty period.  Both water heaters were model # GVR 50 -100 with a stated 6 year warranty.  The first water heater was installed by the developer in Oct 2004 and put into service on November 2004.  The original one had a serial # J04J007021 and failed by rusting through on Sept 2007 it was replaced by another A.O. Smith heater GVR 50 100 model # H07J010171 on Sept 2007 and this one failed for the same reason on April 2011.  This water heater is installed in a residence with only two seniors in the household using [REDACTED] soft water and temperature set for the normal hot water setting.  The water is only used for domestic purposes.  Not only did the tanks rust out but both ignighter units had to be replaced due to failures.  Seems to me that there is a serious quality control issue during manufacture.  Fortunately I was home both times when the garage was flooded and was able to shut off the water to minimize and serious damage.  If this happened when we were away for any extended period of time could have caused not only physical damage to the home but an awfull waste of water.  Both tanks were flushed within the recommended time period.
justification: The incident involves repeated water heater failures causing property damage (flooding), but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
In June of 2011 she noticed that the hot water heater was leaking and had corroded  on several areas of the hot water heater.  She hired a plumber  to come out to make repairs to the unit to stop it from leaking. 

The plumber (name not provided) advised the consumer that the unit could possibly blow up. 

She spoke with the firm and they did not offer any assistance. The hot water heater has been in the home for approximately two years and the consumer purchased the home in December of 2010. 

She has not made any final decisions on replacing the unit and or repairing it. No further information was provided.
justification: The hot water heater is leaking and corroded, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or explosion has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Last fall I purchased a Black and Decker iron, a First Impressions Cord Reel Iron (Model No. ICR505), I think it was at Target. I tried looking for a place to file this complaint on the Black and Decker website but didn't see any area to do so.

I am a quilter, which means I have to press a lot of cotton calico, which requires a high heat setting and steam. I've noticed with this particular iron that the handle area gets really hot, uncomfortably so. While I haven't actually burned my hand yet, it's not something I want to continue using. I've never had this problem with irons before, and am wondering if there is something wrong with my iron or if it is the design of this particular model.  

This problem started with the first time I used my iron, but I managed to finish the project I was working on last November. I hadn't used the iron since then until this past weekend, when I noticed the painful heat again. Obviously, this is a problem that is not going away.

I will be purchasing a new iron as soon as possible and discarding this one, but I wanted to make someone aware of the problem with this iron. I have also filed this complaint with Consumer Reports.
justification: The iron's handle gets uncomfortably hot, but no injury has occurred yet, indicating a potential hazard without actual harm.

incident_description:
Tonight for sunday night dinner we cooked burgers.

My 5 year old found a piece of metral bristle in her burger. We consider ourselves lucky since the bristle is probably small enough not to be noticed while chewing it with the burger's bread and lettuce but could also find itself in the stomach and create a performation.

Prior to putting the burgers on the grill, we cleaned our grill with a brush made by Brinkmann. The name of the product is "Grill Scrub Brush". It appears that the bristle in question broke loose from the brush while we were cleaning the grill surface. When my wife put the burgers on the grill, the bristle lodged into the meat, which eventually ended up on my daughter's plate. We consider ourselves very lucky that the sharp bristle did not end up being swallowed by her. Upon closer examination, the bristle in question was found to be brittle and could have easily broken in half. It appeared to be sharp enough, if swallowed, to potentially perforate the stomach or intestines.

The brush in question was bought last year and still looks functional, but we will definitely discard it and use a new one. It seems consumers need to be made aware of the potential danger of this brush.
justification: The incident involved a metal bristle in food but no injury occurred, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as it's possible for bristles to break off during grill cleaning.

incident_description: An Amana Washing Machine was operating and filled basement full of smoke. There was no fire associated just smoke
justification: The incident involved smoke but no fire or injury, indicating a non-injury incident.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that her Kenmore washer poses a safety risk because her house can become flooded. She stated that she washing clothes in the kitchen where the washer is and left the room for a short time to clean the bathroom. When she came back to the kitchen the floor was completly all over her floor. She had hired a water damage company to come clean up the damages.A technician stated that the issue is derived from a malfunctioning water sensor. This unit is matching set with a dryer. The dryer has no problems. She spoke to the manufacturer the same day and spoke to a representative. They offered to pay her $1500 dollars of she waives her rights. She has yet to speak with the retailer. The incident cause no fire and no one was injured. She has spoken the attorney general in hopes that can make the manufacturer pay for her damages. The attorney general in turn told her to call the CPSC for further detail. She stated that the product has a patent pending. She felt it was imperative to report this incident.
justification: The incident caused property damage (flooding) but no injuries or deaths, and the issue was identified as a malfunctioning water sensor.

incident_description: The consumer says the unit started leaking.  He noticed it when he got close to it he could hear water boiling on the inside.  He would run more water to it and it would stop.    His wife last week smelled something burning.  The consumer says he tried to turn down the thermostat but that didn't work.   The consumer says the dispenser is starting to arch from the inside and he feels it is a definite fire hazard.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer on Friday,  but he did not have his serial number at the time.  He will call back.  The consumer says that he does not feel it is safe to leave it plugged in.  He does not use the product.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard with visible arcing and burning smell, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a small space heater from Meijer store in Flint, MI last fall.  The brand name is Touch Point Model number HT 708B.  I noticed today the cord going into the housing of the heater was showing bare copper wires.  The insulation had separated from the wire.
justification: Bare copper wires pose a potential electrical hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: I purchased and use a Bostitch fine wire stapler (part number 21680B).  I was shocked to learn that it has no safety to prevent inadvertent firing of the staples.  This is extremely dangerous because the trigger is very sensitive and easily bumped.  Once the stapler fires a staple it is propelled with sufficient velocity to deeply penetrate hard wood.  If the staple hits human flesh it easily penetrates to the full depth of the staple.  If it hits an eye, blindness could result.  The lack of a safety is reckless and easily fixable by Bostitch because a similar tool (part number HP118K) has a safety and the total retail cost of the parts is $2.53.  I contacted Bostitch and they refused to retrofit the 21680B despite the danger to the consumer and the ridiculously low cost.
justification: The stapler can cause deep penetration injuries, including potential blindness, due to its sensitive trigger and lack of safety.

incident_description: T8775C1005 Honeywell "round" digital Heat/Cool thermostat installed fall 2011.  Recently left home for two weeks and turned thermostat down to an unoccupied temperature of 45 degrees.  Returned to find it had malfunctioned - while still dialed in at 45 degrees, the thermostat electronics failed/shorted and turned on the oil furnace "constantly" and with no regard to temperature, raising the internal house temperature to over 99 degrees, consuming 1/2 of fuel oil in 275 gal tank.  HVAC contractor responded, diagnosed and replaced defective Honeywell thermostat head.  Extremely dangerous in my opinion - took almost 2 days for home to cool down.  I suspect a fire hazard had I not returned when I did.  I have reported this incident to Honeywell as well.
justification: The thermostat malfunction caused excessive heating and fuel consumption, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I used the bottle brush a handful of times because the soap dispenser didn't work. Mid April I went to use it and clumps of the brush bristles were coming out. Yesterday when I went to pick it up to dispose of it, the plastic center of the brush disintegrated into small bits of plastic and bristles. As I was moving the brush more chunks of plastic bits kept falling off of the brush. I then placed a call to the Munchkin corporation to report and they said they have instructions on their packaging to discard after 45 days. I used it under 5 times total and also thought there was a lack of regard for this incident which could have harmed my baby if she swallowed the bristles or plastic bits from the brush head. Amazon.com never posted any such information in the description of the product.
justification: The incident involved a product failure (brush disintegrating) but no actual injury occurred, though there was potential harm if the baby had swallowed the bristles or plastic bits.

incident_description:
I own a ROTO ZIP model RZ10. The serial number is 2430. Recently I was going to use my  ROTO ZIP tool to do some work on the roof of my home.When I turned the tool on, all of a sudden the handle separated from the motorized part and the tool fell onto the roof and was spinning wildly out of control with the cut off blade spinning at a very high RPM. While spinning on the roof top the blade hit my shoe and put a gash in it. Furthermore the electrical cord began to wrap itself around spindle attached to the tool.It burned part of the cord.I had a very difficult time trying to pick up the spinning tool as it was jumping all over the place.I finally manager to get hold of the tool and secure it enough to turn it off. I then reattached the plastic handle and had just once again turned the tool on when the handle once again for the second time came off.
 The handle attachment of this tool is extremely insecure and unsafe! I could have easily had a badly cut hand or even a severed finger because of this poorly designed handle attachment. I will not use this tool again with the handle because it is blatantly dangerous and unsafe.
justification: The tool malfunctioned and caused damage to the shoe and cord, but no injury to the person was reported.

incident_description:
Heat gun smoked after being turned off. The smell of burnt wire insulation was strong. I returned the product to the store and exchanged it. I tried the new one while in the store and the same smoking occurred. Bought at harbor freight. 1500 Watt Dual Temperature Heat Gun (572ÃÂ°/1112ÃÂ°)
Drill Master - item#96289
justification: The heat gun smoked and emitted a strong smell of burnt wire insulation, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My Rowenta hand iron caught fire while I was ironing.  The small electrical fire appeared to be caused by a faulty cord near the handle.  My hand was injured during this incident.
justification: The incident involved a hand injury due to an electrical fire, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Electrical fires from faulty cords are uncommon but possible.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased a grill brush that is approximately 15" long and the bristles are coming off of the brush. The consumer stated that he used it to clean the grill. As he was eating his hamburgers the consumer felt something sharp in the back of his throat, as he started to swallow he felt somthing sharp in his front teeth.  After he swallowed the hamburger his wife noticed blood in his mouth and lips, he rinsed his mouth and pulled a piece of shart wire from between his teelth.   He was having pain on the back of his throat and he was gargling salt water to treat it. He examined the grill and the steel brush he used to clean the grill, the wire bristles were all in disarray. He believes he ingested a piece of the bristles. 
The consumer did not see a doctor, but he will be scheduling a visit. The consumer did not contact the retailer, but he plans to contact them to request a refund. 
He realized that he had to notify somone about this dangerous brush with loose bristles.  He called MD consumer Protection and was told they had received complaints from two doctors who had treated with bristles in their mouths.  He was told to contact CPSC   When I purchased brush and tool to lift grill from Bed, Bath and Beyond they were loose in a basket-type box with no warning attached, when I went back to store and inspected brushes he found them to have dangerous warning on them.  He feels that it is a safety hazard that could lead to choking.
justification: The consumer experienced pain and bleeding from ingesting a wire bristle, indicating an injury, but did not require immediate medical attention.

incident_description:
Insinkerator hot water dispenser started leaking water under sink.  Upon removal and disasasembly to see why it was leaking, discovered that a plastic water line from the tank to the top reservoir is routed on top of the tank half lip and surrounded by [REDACTED] insulation.  The plastic water line melted from the heat of the metal tank lip and scorched the [REDACTED] but the melted line caused the water to leak and apparently prevented further fire damage.  The water went all over the interior of the unit including the power connection & temperature setting thermostate and could result in a shock or short hazard.  Upon contact with Insinkerator, they advised there were no safety recalls on the unit and claimed no design defects reported but that the plastic line has been replaced by a different material since my unit was made and the tank unit is essentially the same as my unit for all models.  They did offer to send me a new unit and requested that I send mine back-all w/o any warranty period discussion.  I believe there may still be a design defect in this product regardless of replacing the water line with a heat proof type and consumers should be aware and product be redesigned.
My Model is Insinkerator Instant Hot Water Dispenser 'SST', SN 08038703807, 2/3 gal 115V, 6.5 Amp, 750 Watt
justification: The incident involved a water leak and potential shock hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was again removing another ruined shirt from my GE Adora dryer model DHDVH52GF1WW (there is a design flaw with this model, so clothing frequently gets caught between the drum of the dryer and the wall of the dryer surrounding the door, and when the dryer turns and pulls on the clothing it frequently makes holes in the clothes, which I complained about under warranty and GE could not care less). This time, the shirt was really stuck fast, and I had to get a chair to stand on to get part way into the dryer (it is stacked on the washer). As I got into the dryer, I noticed the smell of smoke. Lint had built up around the exposed incandescent bulb and was smoking (the stuck shirt was likely touching the bulb as well, but does not appear scorched, just a hole in it from where it was caught). Fortunately, I noticed the smoke and removed the build up of lint touching the bulb without having a fire in the drum of my dryer. 
I did not notify GE this time, because I had extended warranties for the dryer and matching washer and neither worked well and the problems were never solved under warranty despite numerous attempts on my part and repeated service calls. If they would not fix problems covered by a warranty (e.g. the washer leaking water much of the time), I'm sure they are even less concerned now.
justification: The incident involved a smoking lint buildup near an incandescent bulb, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer states that there was a power outage in  the area (due to some repairs )  that she resides in.  There was a loud popping sound smoke and arching coming from cord.   The consumer unplugged the cord from the outlet immediately and the arching and smoking stopped.

The consumer noticed that when the failure occurred it tripped the circuit breaker. The consumer powered the circuit breaker back into the on position.  The consumer then plugged the plug to the a/c unit back into the outlet when he noticed the cord going to the outlet had fallen part.

She contacted the firm  and they sent someone out from Murray Service around 2/22/2012. The technician replaced the cord and indicated that he believes a power surge caused the failure. GE Contacted the consumer on 3/27/2012 and they offered to buy the product back from the consumer. The consumer also stated that the firm offered to exchange the a/c unit for another one.

The consumer stated the GE has not made any final decisions and has been using the a/c unit since the failure occurred but indicates there have been no problems with it. The consumer reports that he had installed the a/c unit in the window himself in July 2011 and had used it a day or so prior to the incident occurring. 

The Consumer Added:  GE offered us a replacement A/C--We had to choose between AEQ 24DQ and AM 25DP.  We selected AEM25DP, then GE said those two models were not available and offered us an 18,000 BTU A/C--We know than 12 18,000 BTU is not large enough to cool the reoom that the defective A/C model (AHM 24 DHI) is currently installed in because the AHM 24 DHI was purchased in July 2011 to replace an 18,000 BTU A/C that was not large enough unit after we had shade trees cut down.

We are satisfied with the performance of this Air Conditioner.  GE keeps calling saying that they want the Air Conditioner back.
justification: There was an incident involving a power surge and cord failure, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We purchased a Patton Utility Heater model PUH680 1500 watt from Wal-Mart approximately 4 months ago and have only used it 10 to 15 hours.   The unit started making a hissing noise and started emitting red and white sparks and with a brighter than normal red and orange glow.  Thank goodness my wife was near by and turned the unit off and disconnected it from the power source.  Had she not been in the room the unit would surely have caught fire and destroyed our home.
justification: The heater malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description: I have a Shark Steam Pocket Mop model 3501. I have had it approximately 3 years. I only use it occasionally. I have always made it a priority to clean it properly as I paid a lot for it and cannot afford to just ruin it. I was using the mop as usual yesterday. You have to pump the handle to make it have steam. I had been using it for probably 5 minutes and I was pumping the handle and it would not pump, then it exploded! There are two windows on each side and one window on the front where the water goes in. Hot water came flying out of each window. incident_description:
I purchased a Eureka brand upright vacuum, model AS1000A.
Issues are as follows:

1. Regardless of carpet height setting on the vacuum, the brush continues to spin, even when using the hose with attachments in "Tool" mode. 
As all other vacuum cleaners I have purchased have an automatic brush shut off feature when switching to use hose and cleaning tools, I assumed this vacuum would do the same. It does not, and there is no warning regarding this in the user manual. I fortunately noticed a burning smell while cleaning upholstery, and looked at the vacuum cleaner to find the cord underneath the beater brush. 
Had I been a minute longer, it would have burned through to the bare wire. The insulation was burned almost completely through.
I called customer service and was told that, to help avoid the issue, I should change the height adjustment on the vacuum cleaner to "High Carpet". To make that change, you have to unlock (tilt the handle down) first, or the brush height will not change. I didn't know that, but it isn't in the owners manual either. 
Regardless, if I'm vacuuming high carpet (which I am) and the same situation presents itself, the brush still turns, and the potential for a burnt cord is still there, so the customer service persons "fix" is useless.

When reading the owners manual on how to use accessories on page 5, the first thing you read at the top of the page says: 
"How to use Accessories" ! "Handle must be in the upright position"
The next line: " Before Using Accessories" 
                        1. Raise Height Adjustment to "High Carpet".
                        2. Turn Air Path Selector Knob to "Tools".
**Notice the instruction to "tilt the handle back first" is not in the instructions**

If another consumer didn't know this (to tilt the handle back first), and followed those instructions to the letter, the height adjustment would not change. If the same situation that happened to me (3 times now) happened to them, they would suffer the same result or worse.

In my opinion, Eureka should recall these vacuum cleaners because there is a serious potential electrical safety hazard. I consider myself to be a fairly safety conscious person, and understand the importance of not running over a vacuum cord while vacuuming a carpet or floor. 
But if I'm using an attachment hose, and looking up while vacuuming drapes, or the back of a couch, or whatever, I shouldn't have to worry that if I accidentally pull the hose too hard, it could cause the vacuum cleaner to turn, and provide opportunity for the constantly spinning brush to come in contact with the cord.
justification: The incident describes a potential electrical hazard with no actual injury reported, but with a clear risk of injury if the issue is not addressed.

incident_description:
I just wanted to see if you can give your organization a warning about the product Magic Mesh Instant Screen Door that killed my beloved dog. 

I have a 2,000sq ft home.  My home sits on 3/4th an acre; all fenced in.  I have a 200sq ft covered back porch; it is open air on 2 sides (backstopped by the rear sliding glass door and the brick wall of the house).  I have 2 large outdoor dogs and two indoor dogs.  When the temperatures become extreme, all the dogs reside indoors.  The back porch has a ceiling fan and I install seasonal fans all around the dog houses in the summer.  I monitor them closely. 

However, this week I noticed quite a few bugs invading.  I was seeking something that would prevent the black flies from invading the back porch during meal times (the dogs eat outside).  So I purchased four (4) Magic Mesh Instant Screen Doors for $19.99 each at a local Walmart store to go across the opening of the back porch.  On Thursday, I installed them correctly in accordance with the enclosed instructions using the tacks and [REDACTED] pieces.  The dogs had no problem accessing the opening; however, the rear of my house faces south and the southerly wind (5-10 mph) kept blowing them open so I had to keep going outside to connect the magnets in order to keep the mesh closed.  Friday night 4/27, I let my smallest dog out, a 13 year old AKC schipperke named [REDACTED] (paid $1,000 in 1999).  Schipperkes are commonly known to live upwards of 20 years and this one was in perfect health.  IÃÂve had him since he was 4 weeks old.  I loved him dearly, as him and I were the only two to make it out of an abusive relationship with my ex-husband 10 years ago.  He slept in my room for 13 years and was a much loved member of the family.  

On Friday night, unbeknownst to me, as he attempted to walk through the Magic Mesh to go potty out in the backyard, the mesh came apart and the bottom ribbon caught around his throat.  Unfortunately, and very quickly, as twirled around trying to get it off his neck, the mesh became tighter and tighter so that in a few minutes time from when I let him outside and returned to let him back in, I found him hanging by the neck, dead.  He had bitten off his own tongue and I had to get a knife to cut the mesh from his neck and un-twirl it from around his throat because it was so tight.  The mesh did not pinch on his collar; it was just twisted around his neck above the collar.  I did not hear him struggle because it happened so quickly and he could not bark as his air supply was immediately pinched.
	
I have attempted to call Magic Mesh at the below contact information: 
Magic MeshÃÂ Door Cover  @ 1-866-649-0146
P.O. Box 3179 
Wallingford, CT 06494 

But as it was a weekend, I had to leave a message on a full customer service mailbox.  Sadly, I know nothing will bring back my beloved [REDACTED].  I am sorely grieving and am having him cremated at an expense of almost $300 this week because my town will not allow pets to be buried in the backyard.  But I do have a purpose in writing you this: I also have a 10 year old daughter.  What if she had walked through the mesh and it dislodged from the ribbon frame and ensnared her neck too?  Next time it may not be a pet but a small child. What if this product choked a smaller child?  Or a crawling infant?  I do not want someone else to go through the agony I have. 

I do not expect, nor will any kind of reimbursement make my grief for my dead family member better.  But I do want some kind of return call on this matter.
