incident_description:
We hired a contractor to make our house (built in 1963, a large addition added in 1995 and our home since 1986) more weather-tight, improve the insulation, install new storm windows, etc. They used low-VOC foam due to my daughter's asthma and allergies and our concerns about chemical off-gassing and fumes. The contractor did the work or organized subcontractors to do it. Fiberglass was used above and around our bedrooms in the second floor.  

After most of the work was done, one spot in our large, open attic over a one-story portion of the house containing a family room and garage that we use extensively for storage (plus the attic area opens up to the space above two other rooms where the attic ceiling is non-existent or too low for storage), did not get as much insulation as was needed and we continued to observe heat loss in that area when it snowed. Agreeing that some areas were missed, the contractor returned. The attic ducts and furnace were to be insulated and taped (done) and fiberglass batts installed on top of existing insulation and fiberglass put in areas near our furnace where insulation was missing or inadequate. At the last minute, when the insulation sub contractor had arrived, we were asked to substitute [REDACTED] for the fiberglass. After some hesitation, but after being assured it was better and would cause less dust and debris to be in the air and tracked in and out of the house in the future as we or workers when to the attic, we agreed. Due to the name and assurance that this was not dusty, I thought we were getting a rock wool insulation product. When I returned home, I found, much to my surprise, loose cellulose-like insulation dust all over the area to be insulated and loose in my garage, attic storage area floor, and on top of the ducts leading from the furnace, etc. We called the contractor back and some work was done to better contain the materials, although there remained large open areas with the material easily able to become airborne. There is insulation dust all over portions of the area where we have active storage and very near our gas furnace.

Several weeks later I went to the attic to remove some building materials stored there.  After about 10-15 minutes I could not stay in the attic due to shortness of breath, a pounding heart, and a feeling of "heaviness" in my lungs, unlike anything I have ever experienced. I am in excellent health and exercise regularly, but occasionally have some spring allergies that causes rhinitis and had already taken a precautionary allergy medication well in advance, since it was spring and the attic, well, it's a dusty attic. Once out of the attic and some time passed, my symptoms disappeared. Since I could not continue in the attic, I asked my husband to help me. Within less than 10 minutes in the attic, he was coughing excessively and he also stopped. (He used to experience spring allergies when younger, rarely does now. He is in excellent health and does a vigorous workout almost daily). 
 
After discussing our symptoms with the contractor and the [REDACTED] manufacturer, it turned out that the subcontractor, Valley Insulation in Cleves, Ohio, had not installed [REDACTED] as we and the contractor were told. After sending the MSDS sheet for [REDACTED] to the contractor (and then from the contractor to us), Valley then said that it did not install [REDACTED], but a different product, manufactured by Advantage Fiber Technology 100 Crossroads Blvd, Bucyrus, OH 44820, 419-562-1337. Unlike [REDACTED] , this Advanced Fiber cellulose product contains ammonium sulfate as a fire-retardant. The exact amounts and formula are not spelled out on its MSDS. (We previously lived in an older home where we contracted to have cellulose blown into the walls and did not experience any adverse symptoms from the installation or home. We also frequently vacation in a home with cellulose insulation, again without any problems or symptoms. Thus, we do not think that we have any special sensitivity to cellulose properly constituted and properly installed). We suspect that the ammonium sulfate is the cause of our respiratory problems. 

We want to move forward to have this product removed so that we can again safely access our attic storage space and ensure that the product does not harm our house, health, health of workers who must access the space for furnace maintenance and repairs, electrical repairs, etc. , or our hvac system. Valley does not want to do the work. The contractor says the Advantage company has been very uncooperative and other than the MSDS sheet, will not reveal the content of its cellulose product, which it calls "AFT Cellulose Insulation."
justification: The incident caused respiratory symptoms in two individuals, indicating injury (severity level 3). The likelihood of recurrence is possible (3) given the presence of the problematic insulation material.

incident_description:
A little over a year ago, on November 23, 2010, we replaced our 30+ year old electric tankless, electric water heater, made by the prior owner of your company, with a Bosch Powerstream Pro. I cannot give you the serial number, because it is hidden behind its internal pipes. I cannot see it even crawling under the sink with a flashlight in hand.
When the Bosch heater works, it is wonderful, but when it does not work, and I am reduced to heating water on the kitchen stove to wash dishes or hands, it is a curse. And, it is an intermittent curse, the worst kind. When the plumber who installed it comes, it works. When he is gone, it may, or may not work. 
This device has given me pause about my very long time admiration of German engineering~ (GeI1nan cars from 1961 to and including the present.) This is now the second episode of outages. My prior, American made model always worked during its long lifetime. I find myself grieving over its death and its subsequent replacement with your Bosch.
In addition to not being able to read the serial number, which is inside the cover behind piping, etc., one cannot access the restart button without opening the protective cover. When the cover is opened, the inner wiring and piping are exposed, and they surround the  restart button, and that is how I received a strong electric shock yesterday, attempting to push the restart button.
The danger of your heater has thus been dramatically demonstrated to me. While I hesitate to give someone of your status and expertise advice, it seems obvious, that to protect consumers, both the serial number and the restart button should be placed in a safe and easily accessible location.
Since I have wisely switched from trying to push the reset button with my finger, ever hopeful, trying to get it to restart, using instead the wooden handle of a spatula in a move toward self-preservation, I have concluded that the restart button seems not to push. It does not restart. The red light comes on only when the heater is working and the water is flowing hot. That may be correct functioning. My instruction book is with the plumber at the moment as he was testing the unit in his stop, at which point it was working. At that time, he also contacted your customer service representative who, I was advised was not helpful. How could he have been? The unit was then, diabolically, working, and we had not yet realized that the problem was intermittent. It was guessed that the problem was that we had changed the water pressure. We had not. Your representative did complain, however, that we had not mailed in the registration, which we subsequently did, however, without the inaccessible serial number.
It is my opinion that there is something wrong with the electrical function of the Powerstream Pro. (We have checked circuit breakers, etc., and all is well with the building's electrical system.) It is expensive to get a plumber or an electrician to come out, especially for an intermittent problem. Who knows when to make the request for service? The plumber was scheduled to come today, but this morning the unit is working, at least when I was last in the kitchen, so I must quickly and hopefully get some dishes done.
Therefore, I am asking that you either replace my unit with a safe, dependable, functioning one, and pay for the plumber to uninstall the existing one, and install the replacement. Otherwise, I would like a refund of what has been invested in the existing heater including purchase, and installation, and service, $978.00, receipts enclosed.
CONSUMER ADDED:  The manufacturer has replaced the unit with full warranty, no pay for installation.  Had to write to CEO of BOSCH; Customer Service completely disfunctional.
justification: The incident involved a strong electric shock when attempting to access the restart button, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: Honeywell MS4120F 1006 actuators were being used in the Lincoln Tower fire suppression system in Bellevue, WA.  During an annual test for the fire department, a majority of the actuators that were supposed to fail open to allow relief air out of the building, failed to operate properly.  Out of 9 actuators tested, 6 exhibited the same failure.  The failure was occurring at the main gear shaft.  This metal shaft was intended to be mechanically pressed into the spring case and become displaced and loose.  The shaft had been only partially pressed into the spring case with allowed the shaft to 'rock' in the improper joint which eventually lead to the shaft coming free.  Once the shaft joint was compromised, the interior cover bore the eccentric loading from the gear shaft which it was not designed to withstand.  The gear cover then broke loose as well, causing the gears to move out of place, grind on each other and eventually causing the gears to become stuck and unable to move.

incident_description:
My family purchased a new Holmes HM5305 Humidifier at Target approximately 3-4 months ago. Today while cleaning the unit I noticed what appears to be rust dripping from the inside control panel down into the water reservoir. Upon closer examination the internal controls are badly corroded and rusting. This is a concern for several reasons. Those that immediately come to mind are:

1) This is a fire hazard. The product was designed to handle water and electricity. It should be able to operate without the humidifying function interacting with and destroying the electrical components.

2) I suspect that rusty water from the corroded control panel dripping into the water reservoir contaminates the water being vaporized into the air we breath.

incident_description:
Our State Select gas water heater (model #GS650YBRT) purchased and professionally installed on12/29/07 by CAPPS plumbing and sewage, ruptured at the seam on 3/17/12, leaking gallons of water into our finished basement, causing significant property damage. 
Damage included, carpet, drywall, furniture, photos, albums and scrap booking materials.
The water heater was still under warrantee, so we got it replaced, but had to pay installation/labor.  The likely diagnosis was the pressure gauge was ineffective, causing pressure to build up.
CAPPS replaced the unit, and took the damaged one back to return to the manufacturer.
We have contacted State Select (State Industries Inc.) several times, but they have not gotten back to us.  Our concern is for others who may have this issue and not realize it.  We are grateful no one was hurt (my 9 year old was in the room above when it happened, so luckily the side seam burst rather than the top exploding into the room above!).
Also, we are concerned about getting reimbursed for our property damage and installation costs.

thanks you.

The consumer was glad, in this instance, they could be readily available to immediately treat the children with water and petroleum jelly, and that the children had not sprayed themselves in the eyes while "horsing" around like kids can do in an instant. I requested one after the installation for reasons I will explain.  I was not told when to enter the house, but was told by the installer that day that "it would cure in 2 and 1/2 hours, sheet-rockers work right behind us!" The contractors arrived at my house approximately 8 a.m., and were gone by 5 p.m. that day.  I returned to the house at 5 p.m., it was a rainy, damp, and chilly day so I put the heat on low and left immediately.  While I was there I noticed a subtle sweet/burning odor.  I called the installer on Wednesday to tell him that I was please and the smell didn't seem so bad, but would it go away?  I had asked him prior to the agreement, if there would be an odor and he said, "After it cures there will be none."  On the day of the phone call he said, "It will cure in 24 hours, and after that there will be no odor."  Two weeks later, and after airing the house out with a fan and all doors and windows open, the odor remained.  A worker complained that there, "was a burning smell" in my house.  It was when I overheard him telling a mutual friend later that day, that I became alarmed and knew that I had to call Upstate Spray Foam Co., to report the odor again. [REDACTED] came out and claimed that he, "didn't smell anything".  The electrician working in my house reported that he did smell something strong in one of the lofts.  The owner of Upstate Spray Foam Co., and a representative from the manufacturer; Certain-Teed also claimed that they "did not smell anything."  Meanwhile other people have described it as a "sweet or burning" odor.  [REDACTED]  Meanwhile, I had to cancel work on my house, although I planned to move in by October 2011.  The company who claimed they wanted to help, has not responded to my request to remove it based on the smell alone, which after you are in the house for more than 5 minutes is sickening.  I can also smell it when I am standing outside near an open door.  Another representative from Certain-Teed who I spoke to on the phone told me "there should be no odor after 24 hours and there is something wrong with the installation."  A representative from the Polyurethane Foam Alliance also said the very same thing.  I never paid them because they did an unsatisfactory job and they had promised me prior to the installation, that there would be no smell.  They have put a lien on my house, and have not done a thing to remedy the situation.  I am very concerned about not only my safety, but the safety of the public at large. incident_description:
Beginning in October 2010 through May 2011, I rented a cottage which had been newly winterized by the landlord prior to my moving in. The landlord, acting as the contractor, hired a company to install Icynene closed cell polyurethane spray foam insulation. As a member of the unsuspecting public, after a short time I started developing headaches, a runny nose, acid reflux and then allergic-like reactions to food.  This was followed by respiratory and gastrointestinal problems, which went unexplained for over eight months, despite blood tests, chest x-rays, CT scans, and the like.  Eventually, I was diagnosed with a serious inflammatory gastrointestinal condition and a respiratory condition, specifically hyper-reactive airways (which my MD refers to as ÃÂisocyanate asthmaÃÂ) During my occupancy, I had noticed an ammonia type of musty smell at times, especially along the stairwell leading to the 2nd floor. By the spring of May 2011 with the windows closed, after three days of heavy rain and then heat, a very strong odor of ammonia, polyurethane type paint, and other noxious smells pervaded the cottage interior. I vacated immediately. The suspicious odors were confirmed by five different friends/neighbors and the cause of my health problems became clear.  From the time I moved into the cottage to present, I have had over 60 medical appts.  Although my respiratory symptoms have improved since vacating, I continue to cope with substantial health problems, including acute sensitization and autonomic nervous system dysfunction from this chemical exposure.  I was always healthy before moving into the cottage, never realizing spray foam insulation under floors, in walls and the roofline of a small building could offgas disocyanates, amine catalysts, ammonia by-products and other chemicals.  No ventilation had been installed.  I was informed by three highly respected medical professionals in Boston-a research physician at Brigham & WomenÃÂs Hospital, an occupational health clinic physician and instructor at Harvard School of Public Health, and a pulmonologist affiliated with the Beth Israel Deaconness Hospital- that spray foam insulation poses significant health risks, as it is often not mixed properly, not applied properly, does not cure properly in the wall, and often is not properly ventilated. One of the physicians stated "even if Icynene works perfectly, it sometimes does not cure properly and can offgas."  Each of these medical professionals knew about the deleterious effects of this product, including respiratory effects and cases of ÃÂisocyanateÃÂ asthma.  

Also of note, many of the protocols established for the product application- certification of applicator, ventilation required for safety and adequate air exchanges, checking of R values for building inspection and occupancy permit- were not properly followed in this case.

This product should not be on the market- without adequate knowledge of its effects on human health and/or any established scientific methods to test air for isocyanates or the human body for metabolites.  I have major concerns about the widespread use of this product and believe it poses a significant public health risk.  Action must be taken.
justification: The incident resulted in serious health conditions including respiratory and gastrointestinal problems, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the improper application and lack of ventilation mentioned.

incident_description: I was trying to use the My Little Steamer Go Mini to steam out wrinkles from my shirt.  The directions indicate that you have to pull on the shirt while steaming it to remove the wrinkles.  Since I do not have an outlet near an area where I could hang my shirt while standing, I hung the shirt on the door handle and sat on the floor to begin steaming my shirt.  In order to get the full effect of the steam, you have to put the product close to the fabric and slightly tilt it even though the direction tell you to keep it upright.  As I proceeded to try to steam out the wrinkles, I tilted the steamer too far, and boiling water poured out onto the inner area of my left leg near my knee ( I was sitting cross-legged on the floor).  I had jeans on and quickly tried to remove them, but was unable to do so before I sustained first and second degree burns (pain, swelling, redness and large blisters).  I have taken photographs of the injury.  The boiling water in this product can very easily dispense which makes it an extremely dangerous product.
justification: The incident resulted in first and second degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described ease of boiling water dispensing from the product.

The 1 year old boy received routine testing in July 2011 & had high levels of lead (17 micrograms per deciliter). Local officials examined the home, checked for leaded products & found the double door, cast iron wood burning stove in the living area. The child played around this stove in the summer & pulled himself up using the stove. Flakes were coming off stove door. A lead check swap suggested it contained lead. Child's lead level decreased to 10 - 12 micrograms per deciliter. Local/State officials feel the stove's door was the cause of the child's high lead level

incident_description:
We were removing a platform hanging by four upright boards from ceiling rafters.  Our use involved attaching the straps to support the weight of the platform while the upright boards were removed one at a time and then, using the ratchet to gradually lower the platform to the floor.  After all but one of the straps had been removed and the entire platform was hanging by a single one, mechanism let go, causing the platform to rapidly fall and crash to the floor.  After this, I did some tests and found that all of the ratchet mechanisms were prone to such failure.  

The lifting mechanism worked fine but the gradual release failed.  I do not know why, and have no time at the moment to find out.  There were no specific warnings on the package.  These are prominently displayed near the check-out stands at Home Depot: obviously, the results of using these Chinese-made product could be disastrous.

Please note that while the incident occurred at the below address, that space is now empty and we have relocated across the same street.
justification: The platform fell rapidly but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the ratchet mechanisms being prone to failure.

incident_description: At approximately 5:15am on February 3, 2012, a houseguest turned on the Majestic Vermont Castings gas fireplace in the living room of our home.  Approximately 2 hours later, my 9 month old son put one of his hands on the glass front of the fireplace, sustaining what the doctors ultimately concluded was a second, bordering on third, degree burn on his palm and areas of his fingers.  My husband and I immediately took him to the Emergency Room at the Children's Hospital in Denver.  First, my son received intravenous pain medication from a team of nurses.  Next, a team of surgeons assessed the wound to determine whether they believed a skin graft or other surgery would be immediately necessary.  Next, were taken to the burn clinic for further evaluation.  The burn clinic team assessed the injury, preliminarily concluded a skin graft would not be necessary, cut off the very large blister that had formed on his palm, and proceeded to clean, treat and dress the wound with a soft cast.  My son returned to the clinic two more times, on February 10 and February 17, for additional wound evaluation and dressing changes.  We have been instructed to moisturize and massage his hand several times a day for the next six months.  The doctors said it is unclear at this point whether he will have any permanent scarring, discoloration, loss of feeling or effect on the dexterity of his hand.
justification: The incident resulted in a second to third degree burn requiring medical treatment, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Our GE gas dryer (model DPXH46GA4CC) cought on fire inside the housing and under the drum.  From my observations this was caused by a build up of dryer lint in the area of the combustion tube.  This lint is a product of poor design on GE's part by attaching the outlet pipe (metal) of the dryer to the outlet of the blower (plastic) that draws air through the dryer drum.  This 'seal' was made with a 3/4" wide rubber band.  This band was not positioned properly over the joint nor was it secured by any type of adhesive.  With slight back pressure on the blower and an ill fitting 'seal' on this joint lint was forced out of the exhaust duct into the inside of the dryer housing.  Over several years this accumulation of lint ended up getting to a critical mass near the open flame within the dryer's fire tube and ignighted the lint.  A flash fire occured within the dryer burning the top layer of the lint deposits in the dryer.  The dryer continued to run even while it was being burned on the inside of the housing.  Fortunately the underlying lint was packed down enough that it did not catch on fire too.  Had this been the case I am sure that the dryer would have started the surrounding areas on fire causing the house to burn down.  My wife fortunatley smelled the burning and found the dryer to be smoking and shut it off.
justification: The incident involved a fire inside the dryer but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire was contained within the dryer.

incident_description:
We have a Regency Hampton wood burning fireplace.  It was installed by an official Regency dealer.
The fireplace is fitted with Regency's blower kit.  This was purchased with the fireplace and installed by the dealer.  
During the incident in question, a small ember that was on the hearth was sucked underneath the cover of the blower kit and sucked into the fan blade.  It was small enough to fit under the cover, but just too small to pass through the blades.  The blower blades are made out of plastic.  The blower blade partially melted and there was a smoldering fire in the blower.  What we saw when we entered the room was burning particles being blown out of the top ducts of the fireplace all over our family room.  The lights were low and the scene was akin to a firework display and very scary.  The burning particles were blown several feet across the room, some landing on soft furnishings.  We immediately stopped the blower, however there was still a smell coming from the fan.  We removed the blower kit and found the ember lodged in the fan blade.  We removed the ember, but the plastic continued to smolder.  We had to pour water into the fan to stop the smoldering.  We never saw flames once the fan was stopped, however it was still smoldering.
An ember entering the fan is a credible event.  Plastic components, hot embers and high speed air currents do not mix.  I am concerned that these blades are not made out of metal  Had this been the case, the ember may have just burnt out with no consequence.
I contacted my local dealer, but he was unable to help other than supply new parts.  I contacted Regency and they at first told me to consult my local dealer for parts, then ignored further communications when I raised safety concerns.
justification: The incident involved a smoldering fire and burning particles being blown into the room, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Harman Home Heating 300i Woodburning Fireplace Insert on October 16, 2011. Shortly ofter installing this insert I realized that it has major design flaws which make it impossible to operate in the manner it was designed to do. 

The 300I Insert is a down draft stove and when in the "clean burn" mode it can and will backfire with enough velocity to blow smoke and ash backwards through the draft controls out into the living area of the house. This usually happens when first closing the by-pass damper when smoke and gas accumulate in the fire box. It also happens when the fire starts to die down and the temperature in the firebox drops below the temperature needed to maintain a clean burn. 

I did write to the manufacturer, Harman Home Heating, they in turn contacted Hearthside Patio, the dealer, 790 Bald Hill Rd., Warwick, RI 02886, and a dealer representative was sent here in mid-December 2011 to inspect the stove, check the quality of my firewood, and inspect the installation of the stove and chimney liner since I did the installation myself. He determined that he could not find any issues with the stove installation or the quality of my firewood. He stated that he would contact Harman and get back to me in early January after the holidays. I have called Hearthside Patio three times and visited the store where I purchased the Insert and to date have not heard back from anyone. 

The 300I Insert has not fulfilled its advertised claims: it states that it can be used as an open fireplace, but with the door open, smoke back drafts into the house; it states that the stove has a 12-15 hour burn time, the most I have gotten is six hours; it states that you must reach the "clean burn" stage for proper stove performance, but it is extremely difficult and dangerous to raise the temperature high enough to reach the "clean burn" stage and maintain it. I am only able to use this extremely expensive stove like an old Franklin style stove with the damper open. If I close the damper to put the stove in the "clean burn" stage, the fire goes out, and if I leave the damper open it burns wood extremely fast making this a very expensive stove to own. The most dangerous fire is in the "clean burn" stage when the burning of smoke creates the "secondary burn" which can back fire and the pressure of this burn can force smoke and gas from the stove into the living quarters.

Another major fault is in the fire box. The draft to the fire can be impeded with one inch of ash in the bottom of the fire box. This stove has no ash pan, therefore, I must remove ashes daily or the stove cannot maintain a burn. The placement of the logs in the fire box can also impede the burn since the draft is at the bottom rear of the fire box and if a log rolls against the draft opening,  it will cause the fire to go out.

The stove requires constant attention to just keep a fire burning, and is impossible to maintain a safe fire in the "clean burn" cycle. 

I do not believe the dealer, Hearthside Patio, is acting in good faith. They are well aware of the problems I have described above and agree that the stove is not working properly. To date they have not addressed the issue that the stove has major design flaws that could result in the safety of anyone using this stove. 

I also believe that Harman Home Heating knows of these problems and chooses to ignore these real and dangerous design flaws. 

Please refer to SaferProducts Report No.: 20110311-6B7FC-2147481644, Report Date: 3/11/2011 
Product Description: Harman Oakwood Freestanding wood stove. I believe that this persons description of the "smell of smoke in the house" and the problem with the "gaskets" are due to the same basic  design flaws that I am experiencing with my 300i Insert. I have not found a Response Report on your web site from Harman Home Heating concerning this report.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove that can backfire, releasing smoke and ash into the living area, posing a potential safety hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
In December 2009, I had Icynene spray foam insulation installed in a home under construction. I had worked in this house for nine months without any kind of health issues. After working in the house on four different occasions in the first week that the foam was sprayed, I was in the emergency room in a local hospital with severe chest pains. I was checked for heart problems but had no problem there. I told the doctor that I had been in this house and smell of the foam was quite strong. She said that maybe I had a chemical burn. This product was advertised as being inert and did not off-gass. Icynene finally had a company do an air sample in May of 2010 and the VOC's were almost eleven times the allowable amount for new construction yet the company said that the VOC's were coming from some other source. There was nothing else in the house except the sub-floor that was not covered by their foam insulation. Like I said, I had been in the house almost daily for nine months doing electrical and assorted construction work without a problem until the insulation was installed in the building. Other people that had been in the house several times earlier also had problems. The house is still sitting as it was the day the foam was sprayed in it in 2009. Each time that I have gone into the house since for just a short time, I have had to go to a doctor. I had an analysis done on the product and it was still showing isocyanate, one of the sensitizing agents, still present seven weeks after the product was sprayed. The company says that the product is supposed to be safe within twenty four hours. The last time that I contacted the company, Icynene Inc., about my problems, the engineer, [REDACTED], hung up the phone on me. I have tried to get the installer to see if he could take the product out of the building but he too is of no help. 

The EPA is looking at isocyanate related problems a little closer now. Anyone can go to http:// epa.gov/pbt/ and look at Methylene Diphenyl Diisocyanate (MDI) and Related Compounds Action Plan [RIN 2070-ZA15] for more information.
justification: The individual experienced severe chest pains requiring emergency room visits and ongoing health issues, indicating injury (severity 3). The recurrence of health problems upon re-exposure suggests the likelihood is likely (4).

Repairman informed us of a factory problem where the vent belt pully was incorrectly tightened and they were having a lot of problems with the belt coming off.
About 3months later same problem occurred. Called Sears again. No warrenty left, no warrenty left on previous repair. No recourse offered for an admitted factory problem.
Called Whirlpool with same results as Sears.
I repaired dryer myself. The pully for the vent belt had fallen off again.
My concern is that the clothes become so hot that I feel there is a definite fire hazard. If this happens again and no one notices how do we know that there will not be a fire
justification: The incident involves a recurring mechanical issue causing overheating, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
I recently noticed problems with light switches in my home not working or working intermittently. While replaceing the ones I was having problems with I decided I better check the others. Upon further inspection I ended up replacing all my switches in the upper part of my home (basement used a different switch) due to about 75% being broken in the same way. I replaced about 40 switches, they were all wired in using the slide in connection on the back (rather than the side screws), and it appears the black backshell can't take the stress and cracks. Some of these switches literally fell apart when I was removing them. I am writing becouse I feel this could really be a fire hazard for other users of these switches. I have kept many of them if you would like to see them. I notified the manufacture of these switches (Leviton) and have surprisingly received no response. These switches are original to my home which was built in 1997. I am not interested in reimbursement of any sort from them, I just think this issue needs to be addressed. 

The switches are made by Leviton the three way switch is P/N 218,602-1453, and the single pole is P/N 218/632-1451.

The following is from a web search I did to see if others have had any problems like this. It doesn't appear I am the first to see this problem. The following is cut and pasted from DIY chatroom :

UPDATE:

Well I did follow up with the Leviton, who asked me to mail them the defective switches, which I did.

Today I got a box UPS from Leviton, with 24 new 3-ways and a 3 pack of GFCIs. 

There is a letter from them saying that there was indeed a manufacturing defect where some 3-way switches produced in 1997 had the top rivet rolled too tight, which can cause the breakage pattern like I found. Their files say that none of the defective switches actually got shipped, but apparently I got a few of them. They said I'm only the second report of this "in the wild" so they still believe the problem was contained pretty well.

So I'm happy with this. It's good of them to admit there was a defect, and to send me a box of stuff to make up for the time I spent dealing with this issue.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard due to defective switches, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Complaint involves "Comfort Zone" heater, model cz792, manufacture date 07/10, purchased at Tractor Supply in St. Albans VT in fall of 2010.  I recently noticed that when the heater was set to it's lowest heat setting, the heater would stay on continuously instead of cycling on and off.  I unplugged the heater and stopped using it.  I disassembled the heater and found that the weighted (plastic) arm that is supposed to mechanically open a circuit on the thermostat had melted and was laying in the bottom of the heater (pictures available). This would cause the heater to remain "on" if it were tipped over.  I do not know if this melted arm somehow interfered with the operation of the thermostat causing the heater to stay "on" all the time when the thermostat was set to it's lowest setting.  

I also noted that the thermostat is wired to interrupt the "neutral" side of the incoming power instead of the "hot" side.  

Additionally, during troubleshooting I found that the main power/mode-select switch had several hundred ohms of resistance between the "hot" side contact and the respective outgoing contacts.
justification: The heater malfunctioned but was unplugged before any injury occurred, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Problem with Danby portable air conditioner  - improper routing of wire caused wire insulation to be chafed through and short against compressor pipe - arcing burned a hole in the pipe and [REDACTED] escaped. I was told by someone servicing Danby units what the problem likely was before the unit was opened and that the company had been advised some time before. I contacted Danby and they didn't consider this a safety problem - CSA was helpless.

incident_description: My son was severly injured by the Banshee Bungie.  This product is used with skim boards.  There is an anchor attatched to a bungie cord.  The anchor is set and the cord is pulled tight.  The resistance should send you into the surf on your board.  The anchor dislodged and flew towards my son.  It struck him in the foot, exploding the bone.  It also hit the tailbone, breaking it in two places.  It missed his spine by a fraction of an inch.  His foot was so badly damaged that we were initionally told he may lose his foot.  He spent 5 days in ICU.  Surgery was required to rebuild the foot.  Due to the injuries, we had to have a hospital bed in our home for him.  He did not walk for three months after surgery.  He has lifelong limitations due to this injury.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries requiring surgery and long-term limitations, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
The product is a " FlowPro", Utilty Heater, 1500 Watt, Model #83030. Distributed by Aloha, Arlington,TX.  The PO# is 001204 and the C/NO. is 02325-3600 of 3600. Also marking on  the box label "44200JX100106".
It bought to replace an old 1500 watt heater in a seperate garage. It did a good job of heating, but did not cycle on and off. Today was a warm day and the heater was still on and no setting of the temperature control would turn it off. I then turn it on each side and front and back without it  stop heating. I am a retired EE and took it apart to see what was wrong.
I found the points were burnt away and signs of over heating. The weight could not move the "arm", which had become very stiff. Turning the temperature control could not move the "arm".
If the heater had been turn over, I belivethe way the "arm" warped, there would have been NO SAFETY THERMAL CUT-OFF from the thermial arm.  Potential for a fire would be very great if laying on the front with the heater coils less than an inch away from a contact point.
justification: The heater malfunctioned with potential for fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Here is the full name of the product: MicrodryÃÂ® Ultimate Luxury Memory Foam Bath Mat
The manufacture is named: Mindsinsync.

They say it is only sold at Bed, Bath and Beyond. I highly recommend that you check out this link: 
http://www.bedbathandbeyond.com/product.asp?SKU=120822&RN=1078#BVRRWidgetID

I did not have the product long, I would say no more than 2 weeks. As it was a bath mat I was using the product by having it sit on the floor of my bathroom, outside my shower. When I purchased the product it was marked as slip-resistant. 

I had gone into my shower to gather up some items to take out before taking my shower for the night. I placed my right foot outside of shower onto the mat, and the mat slipped. It caused me to fall straight back and hit my head onto my ceramic tile floor.

I went to the ER and was diagnosed with a concussion (mild traumatic brain injury) and a cervical sprain. I was out of work for one week and worked part time for an additional two weeks.

I received after-care from a general general practitioner (details available upon request) and a neurologist  (details available upon request). 

I suffered from moderate post concussion syndrome for many months some to this day.

The manufacture's claims that the mat is "slip-resistant" is false. They do claim that the mat should not be used around water. It is a BATH mat.

Look at the description on the website and tell me they mean that it should not be used around water.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion and cervical sprain, which are injuries, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the product's slip-resistance claim was false and it was used in a typical bath setting.

incident_description:
Ladies and Gentlemen:
On the evening of Wednesday January 4, 2012 my wife and I smelled a noxious, putrid, burning odor in our house. After frantically inspecting all nooks and corners of our house we determined the odor was emanating from our heating ducts. We immediately tried to shut the heater off from the thermostat control but it would not shut the system off. I then went to the basement and switched-off the breaker, for the heating and air conditioning, in the electrical distribution box.
Upon switching the breaker off the smell dissipated. Since the temperature was to drop to the low 20's that evening I reset the breaker to see if the heater would run without emitting the foul odor. The odor returned approximately 10 minutes after resetting the breaker, at which time I turned the breaker off a second time.
The next day we called Haller Enterprises, Inc. (717-625-1500) to come and service the unit. We have lived in our house for 4X years. The house was new when we moved in. We chose a heat pump system since we enjoy the type of heat and air conditioning the heat pump produces, from our previous home, which we lived in for 25 years.
The heater Manufacture #RXBH17A15J and the Serial #PB1907.
The Technician showed me the problem, which was a hole burnt through the circuit breaker, located internal to the inside heating unit. The question I have is why didn't the breaker trip, like it should have, before burning a hole through the plastic cover? The other question I have is what toxins did it produce and emit when it burned the plastic? And could this have caused further damage, i.e. a fire, by not shutting down the system like it should have? In other words was this a potential safety issue/hazard?

Secondly, the technician also discovered that the electric fan motor was leaking fluid, which caused him to replace the motor as well. The unit is only 4 years old. I can understand one major problem occurring to the unit but two indicates major design problems and/or cheap components used in manufacturing. Since the unit was still under warranty it saved us the cost of parts, however, the cost to remove the old and install the new cost us $565. I find this outrageous for a unit that is only 4 years old. Further, I need to know if my wife and I were exposed to any toxic fumes/chemicals emitted when the
breaker was burning and spewing the noxious odors into our home. If this is the type of product Rheem manufactures we will not be purchasing anything further from your company. I am also sending a copy of this letter to Consumer Reports, the Attorney General's Office, and the Consumer Protection Agency's.
At a minimum I would hope you will respond with information on the toxicity of the fumes emitted from the burning breaker. I would also request reimbursement for the labor costs associated with the replacement of the equipment. I have enclosed a copy of the Service Order and bill for the parts and labor to repair parts that should have lasted for 10 -15 years without major repairs, let-a-Ione two major parts (breaker & motor).
justification: The incident involved a noxious odor and potential safety hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
In mid January 2012 the McDonnell & Miller RB-24 low water cut off on a barely 6 year old Burnham 203PVNI hot water boiler shorted out due to water leaking into the electrical circuit from the plastic threaded section that screwed into the water pipe. The electrical short overloaded the 24 v circuit causing the transformer (fan center) to burn out and generating a significant amount of smoke in the basement. More serious damage was prevented by the tripping of the Fuse panel circuit breaker. 

Plumber that repaired the damage noted that the Rb-24 units were "cheaply made" and had a history of unreliability. 

As to be noted was that the 24 v circuitry of the boiler does not have any fuses to protect from any circuit overloads which I consider a notable design flaw by Burnhan's. Electrical malfunctions are only protected by fuse panel circuit breakers.
justification: The incident caused significant smoke but no injuries, and the plumber noted a history of unreliability with the RB-24 units.

incident_description:
Subject: Jacuzzi bathtub

I am writing this in regards to an incident that happened in our Jacuzzi bathtub. My 2 grandaughters, ages 6 & 7 were in the tub taking a bath and relaxing in the tub with the jets turned on. All of a sudden both girls started screaming to the top of there lungs. I was in the room next to the bathroom, and immediately ran to them. My oldest grandaughter couldn't talk because she was scared terribly. I asked what was the matter, and she pointed to the pump inlet, which had sucked her leg against it. The girls were sitting facing each other when this happened. They had their legs between each others legs. The water level in the tub was just a little above the jets. Both girls have severe bruises on their legs and thighs. I am enclosing the pictures we took of the bruises. I know that the girl with the bruises on her left thigh was stuck on the inlet when I shut it off, but the other girl had bruises more between her legs, but both girls had marks that matched the inlet cover. This is the strangest thing that I have ever seen in my life. I cannot figure out exactly what transpired. We have had this tub for quite some time, but never had any problems other than a lot of black junk coming out of the jets after running cleaners through it. I can't determine if somehow the pumps suction had increased or what. After you look at the pictures, you will see what I mean by serious bruising. The model # is H526000, name-Cetra wp/r, Mfg. # 0008-08, serial # T68737. Are there any recalls or anything else that addresses this issue? Any ideas or help determining what happened will be greatly appreciated. You can contact me at : [REDACTED]. Thank you.
justification: Both girls suffered severe bruises from the Jacuzzi tub's suction, indicating physical injury.

[REDACTED] took my information and stated someone from Black & Decker will contact me within 2 days, she gave me a reference number [REDACTED]. This product injured me severely, I feel and believe I will have facial scars and future issues.  I also took photos of my facial injuries and of the broken Black & Decker RO Sander.

incident_description: Purchashed two westinghouse lighting 7876400 alloy two-light 42 inch reversible three blade indoor ceiling fans, gun metal with opal frosted glass. Ordered about the 24th of Oct. 2011 and recieved them about the 16th of Nov. 2011. So I contacted the dealer that I purchased the fans from thur Amazon. He gave me the number to Westinghouse and I called them twice and both times they gave me the brush off by telling me there supervisor was busy and they would call me back, which they never did. I contacted the dealer again and told him my problem with westinghouse and he refunded my money and said he would try and deal with them. But told me under no condition I was to use the fans again.

incident_description: Bought a Kiddie smoke detector from Walmart on Tuesday 01/17/2012.  Installed it per directions in our master bedroom.  Same models were installed in 2nd bedroom and utility room.  Had a fire that started in the master bedroom.  The smoke became visible coming down the stairs prior to the smoke detector activating.  It sounded 3 times and stopped.  Post fire inspection found that the smoke detector melted and was across the room from the fire.  The 2nd bedroom smoke detector NEVER sounded.

The heating element melted through the plastic housing and burnt a hole in carpet through to the sub floor.  It was probably smoldering for some time before eventually catching fire and setting off our fire alarm.  It was put out quickly without injury.

incident_description:
I own a HP Pavillion dv6000 laptop. I hadnt used it in several months because I bought a new HP laptop recently.  I put a DVD in to view and after less than 10 minutes into the DVD, I went to pickup the AC adapter external battery pack to move the whole laptop from the table to the floor and nearly burned my hand on the battery pack, so I quickly put it back down on the table and as I put it back down on the table I was burned by the end of the cord that enters the A/C pack.  The cord just outside of the adapter was very very hot. I could smell burning electrical wires and hear a buzz or sizzle coming from inside the A/C adapter. I quickly unplugged the adapter from the laptop and shut down the laptop for fear of a fire.
I visited this site to see if this product had been recalled, but they only thing HP has recalled on HP dv6000 laptops was the internal battery, and NOT the A/C adapter that you plug into the wall.  This is a major fire hazard. You can see where the cord has started to melt. If I left my laptop unattended it most certainly would have caught fire.  After only 10 minutes of a DVD playing the adapter was sizzling inside, and too hot to touch.  If the whole movie played unattended my house wouldve burned to the ground!
My internal battery is one of the non-recalled batteries CT: 6294102AXUWBJK, this internal battery was not hot at all during operation.  Only the external A/C adapter battery pack and the  thin cord leading from the laptop to the A/C adapter was extremely hot.  The thicker cord going from A/C adapter to the wall outlet was just warm.

My A/C adapter number is: CT: 592C40EMFUT1JW.
justification: The incident resulted in burns from the hot A/C adapter and cord, indicating an injury, and the description suggests a high likelihood of recurrence due to the hazardous condition.

incident_description:
This is for: Todco GR301-SS Stainless Steel Roasted Garlic Express

When I used my Roasted Garlic Express model 301-SS for the first time it was a painful experience. Upon the completion of the cycle and a 2-3 minute wait I carefully opened the lid whereupon I received a burn from the trapped steam and oil vapor which escaped.

I consider myself to be a careful person and I did read the instructions. I sent the manufacturer an e-mail strongly suggesting they modify the instructions,namely the last sentence in Step 7 where it reads: "Let set 2-3 minutes for best results,then grasp the front handle and carefully lift the lid." I would add: *with tongs or an oven mitt.*
I have not yet received a response.

I also noticed some smoke coming out of the unit for the first few minutes which I kept a watch on since I did follow the BEFORE USING THE FIRST TIME cleaning instructions. Perhaps this should be mentioned in the instructions as well.
justification: The user experienced a burn from trapped steam and oil vapor, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the incident happened on first use despite following instructions.

incident_description: My wife has enjoyed the Shark Steam Mop for a while now. Recently when using it, it became clogged with no steam coming out . As she examined it the head exploded off & the steam burned her wrist.She had 2nd degree burns covering approx. a 5in long & 2inch wide path, which required medical attention. EURO-PRO (manufacturer) has sent us a claim form but has been uncooperative in sending a new unit & assisting with payment for medical & loss/restriction of daily activities.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns requiring medical attention, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: Fire in a gas range oven on initial use after installation. Gas was immediately turned off but fire continued. Damage was minimal and any injury is not known at this time. However, the source of fire gave off vapors which may have been toxic. Cause of fire was a sample packet of stainless cleaner placed in oven compartment by the manufacturer and somehow, perhaps during shipping, worked its way through vents in oven floor and underneath a burner. When the oven was turned on, close proximity of the packet to a burner ignited allowing contents to give off noxious fumes. Oven had to be partially dismantled to determine cause of fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire and noxious fumes, but no injury was reported, placing it at severity level 2. The cause was a rare manufacturing oversight, making recurrence unlikely.

incident_description: My washer leaks water out front, only does wash cycle, then shuts down and reads NF every load.
justification: The washer leaks water and malfunctions, which is an incident but does not cause injury or death.

incident_description: The heaters plug and cord have melted.  The plug was very hot and it was melting the socket.  I shut it off just in time.  I was just going to throw the heater away, but thought I should let someone know that this can happen.  I only use this heater occassionally in my bathroom when it gets very cold.

incident_description: We own a Filter Queen Vacuum and two Defenders systems, purchased in 2005.  We paid thousands of dollars for these 3 items.  The Filter Queen Vacuum has now started on fire in our home TWICE.  Once after the initial purchase and we received a new hose, wand and cleaning head in 2008 and now again the other night November 16, 2011.  We contacted the 800 # on the vacuum who directed us to a "company" 800#.  The individual we spoke with who finally called us back on Friday, November 18 said that we were part of a recall and they'd send us all new parts AGAIN.  I explained that it had this time burned my sons hand, ruined a 5ÃÂ X 7ÃÂ area rug and we no longer trusted ANY of these products in our home.  We had trusted them twice now and this was no longer acceptable, not to send us the new parts, that we wanted to return these three products and get our money back.  It is not fair to us that we would pay this much for their products, only to have them start on fire on us TWICE!!!!  We asked about why we weren't notified of any recalls??  I was originally told they had no idea and later told we must have thrown the notice away!. I then stated we must have been under TWO recalls OR they sent us faulty products the first time it caught on fire... they didn't know.  No one returned my call on Monday, however on Tuesday, November 22 when I got home from work there was a box with the new parts sitting outside my home.  I called and left a message for [REDACTED] to please call me first thing this morning, Wednesday, November 23... During the Christmas season I purchased a Mini-Humidifier from Target, sold as a house brand for $19.95. 

I used it for the first time this weekend, and left it on for a while because it appeared to be functioning normally.  I then realized that the product had a crack where the case had been improperly sonically welded, causing water to leak all over the dresser and on to a TV that was below it.  

Upon inspection, I saw that the manufacturer had not properly sealed the water champed, allowing water to leak out, onto the 24V DC power supply, potentially causing an electrical shock and/or fire hazard. 

I took the unit back to Target, and they refused to refund my money or replace it as it was considered a "seasonal" item.  

There are no UL / CSA or FCC/ CE compliance markings on the device itself, and in fact it was only the following: 

Mini Humidifier
Input Power DC24V 1A 24W
Model No. PNH01
Import Marketing Solutions
August, 2011

At the very least a product that uses water and input voltages above 12VDC are, I believe, required to have UL approval.  The fact that it leaks water due to poor design and manufacture is an potential fire and shock hazard for the consumer, and I recommend that Target be forced to issue a recall on this device, especially given their unwillingness to stand by the product.
justification: The incident involved a leaking humidifier posing a potential fire and shock hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

I have a Scan 60 woodstove that is about 2.5 years old.  Made by Scan, a subsidiary of Jotul.  The top baffle can come down and block the flow of gasses out the flue when the side pieces crack.  This has happened to me twice.  I replaced the two side panels once already.  It has now happened again.  This situation is potentially hazardous.  The Skamol, which is vermiculite (like styrofoam) was never designed to support a lot of weight.  Expansion and contraction, etc. over time seem to make the supporting pieces crack (#6 & 8).

incident_description:
Dear Sir or Madam,

	We had a small electrical fire. It was caused by a Zinsco electrical circuit breaker panel and Zinsco circuit breakers. I wish I had seen this site before I discarded some of the evidence (mostly burnt wiring and charred lumber I still have the panel). I knew there was a problem with the Zinsco electrical circuit breaker panel in our house because sometimes I could hear arcing in the panel. I had vacuumed out the panel because sometimes the sound of arcing can be insects such as ants or termites being fried like a bug zapper, but I saw no insects. Ruling out insects and water intrusion made me very wary of the panel.
	About a week later the Zinsco 60 amp circuit breaker for the water heater failed (I donÃÂt know why someone used a 60 amp for a water heater). When I tried to remove the Zinsco 60 amp circuit breaker, I couldnÃÂt because it was welded to the aluminum bars. I started gathering materials to replace the panel, circuit breaker, and some wiring that I felt was troublesome. Then there was a small electrical fire. Thankfully nobody was hurt (it was during the day, I was home alone). We were very lucky because I smelled the electrical fire and found the source very quickly in an unfinished section of the house upstairs. I used the proper fire extinguisher and we didnÃÂt even have to call the fire department. The Zinsco circuit breakers did not trip. They malfunctioned continuing to deliver electrical power to the melting wiring (more fuel to the fire). I ran downstairs and turned of the breaker manually. I ran back upstairs to the melting wiring and found that shutting off the breaker manually did not interrupt power supply to the fire. I hit it again with the fire extinguisher and ran back downstairs to the panel. Due to my experience with 2 breakers not working, I wasnÃÂt going to chance it by shutting off the main breaker. I pulled the meter and cut the wires at the panel before restoring power to check the other breakers. I found another Zinsco circuit breaker that did not interrupt power supply to the circuit and decided to immediately replace the panel.
	While removing the Zinsco electrical circuit breaker panel we found 4 Zinsco 20 ÃÂ 30 amp circuit breakers that did not interrupt power supply to circuits. There may actually have been more defective breakers because we removed most of them before we started checking them. 
	 I am saying the following to convey that I get the gist of what we are discussing even though I am not a licensed electrician. Wiring is not something that I enjoy. I have completely re-wired several dilapidated 24-unit apartment buildings and then hired a licensed electrician to pull a permit and check my work. They always passed inspection without any red-tags. I have also wired a few houses. Additionally I have hired attorneys to conduct 3 different patent searches only to learn that [REDACTED] holds patents on my concepts.
justification: There was a small electrical fire but no injuries occurred, and the situation was quickly controlled without needing emergency services.

incident_description: a dangerous situation occurred when I started the washing machine which created a call for hot water. I heard the water heater clicking at least 10 seconds followed by a burst of flame. Apparently this was caused by a buildup of natural gas which occurred after the delayed ignition. It seems the gas valve opened despite no flame sensed by the flame sensor of the device. Upon further inspection, the pilot tube failed to produce sufficient gas to be lit by the ignitor which continued to  spark. After 10 seconds of sparking the gas valve opened and a miniblast occurred..Immediately the device was shut off...I took it apart to see if there were any user serviceable parts but this is an engineering wonder and I noted how easy it was to remove the pilot assembly. There appeared to be 2 solenoid gas valves which I removed from the housing to inspect. I suspect that somehow one of these valves failed which prevented gas from entering the pilot tube..I put everything back together and everything seemed ok..However. this is an extremely unsafe condition which needs to be recognized and I would like some assurance that this condition never reoccurs. I need to have the safety devices checked on my unit
justification: The incident involved a dangerous gas buildup and a miniblast, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Generac 6.5 KW portable generator about 10 months ago. I was surprised and disappointed to see a Made in China label inside the fromt panel instead of made in Wisconsin, USA, but I had already made the purchase. Last week we lost power and I hooked up the generator and started it up. I began smelling gasoline and looked back at the generator and gasoline was flowing, not dripping, flowing from the carbuerator, pooling all around the generator. I crossed my fingers and turned the ignition switch to off. I turned the fuel valve closed and the fues stopped flowing shrtly after.  My neighbor purchased a [REDACTED] generator early last summer, it was also made in China. The second time he turned the fuel valve on gasoline flowed freely from the carbuerator to the ground, pooling all around the generator, fortunately he didn't try to start it. I witnessed the leaking gasoline. Apparently many name brands companies have imported Chinese made gernerators and placed their names on them, Generac, [REDACTED], [REDACTED], and others.  I have looked at several generators made in China and they all have one thing in common, the same engine style and carbuerator. I had my carbuerator replaced today under warranty and asked the mechanic how many similar problems he had seen and he said only a couple. He said Generac has a 90 day right to request the faulty parts so I couldn't get the old carbuerator. An emergency stand-by portable generator doesn't get started very often and many owners may not turn the fuel valve on but once per year. It appears the float valve does not work on these carbuerators allowing fuel to flow freely without shutting it off. Extremely dangerous. If I had started my generator and went back into the house, I am certain I would have lost everything to a fire. Please investigate this matter with all Chinese made generators which are sold under most well known brands at a low cost. There is no doubt a real problem with these engines, it is more than a coincidence that 2 new generators of different brands, seperated by 3 houses, would have the same problem. Thank You, [REDACTED]
justification: Gasoline leakage from the generator poses a significant fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred in the described incidents.

incident_description: The fan had been working that day, up until we noticed it wasn't and the power switch was still in the on position.  My husband shut off the switch and then tried going to a different speed, but that still didn't work.  The bedroom , where this fan is located in, also had a terrible oder; liked burnt plastic.  We aired out the room, which helped somewhat and just left the power to the fan off until our small grandkids left to go home.  My husband then disconnected the fan and took it down, only to find the capacitator had started to melt, which is what we were smelling. All 7 fans were installed by a licensed electrician, during the construction of our home, back in 1996.  This was an incident that could of resulted in our home burning down and/or lives being taken.  We will never buy Emerson ceiling fans again ! incident_description:
Approximately 5 months ago a contractor installed approximately 10" of Biobased spray foam insulation on the roof deck and gable ends of our main attic and 4 knee wall attics.  We noticed an immediate ammonia and latex-paint like odor after installation.  This odor has persisted to a lesser extent despite attempts to ventilate the attic with fans.

After inspecting the main attic space 2 days after insulation I developed a headache that persisted for one week.  Since then my wife and I have experienced very frequent tension headaches and neck muscle stiffness that are often triggered by exposure to fumes in the attic.  I have also developed a cough that has persisted for several weeks and only occurs when I am in the house.  I am a physician and I am very concerned that I have become sensitized to the diisocyanates which are part of the spay foam formula.  The insulation continues to outgas as an strong odor is still present in the attic spaces.  

I am in the process of having a medical evaluation of my symptoms.  I am also attempting to arrange testing in the home of air samples for isocyanates and perhaps volatile hydrocarbons

I have very serious concerns about the safety of spray foam insulation
justification: The incident involves persistent health symptoms (headaches, cough, muscle stiffness) linked to exposure to insulation fumes, indicating injury.

incident_description:
GE Electric Clothes Dryer had an internal wiring issue that during use caused a short and large blue sparks were seen from the front of the dryer. 

GE Electric Clothes Dryer
Model DPSB620EC4WW
Serial GL764073A 

People in the room saw the sparks in the door of the dryer and the lights in the house dimmed when the sparks occurred. The dryer was turned off, unplugged and it was examined.

There was no visible damage to the outside of the dryer or in the tub. I disassembled the dryer to determine the root cause. Once the top of the dryer was removed it was evident what the root cause of the problem was - the two wires providing power to the light in the dryer tub when the door was open had shorted out. The wires and area on the drum were scorched and parts of the drum and surrounding areas were damaged.

It appears that the two wires providing power were rubbing against the drum for quite a while and the insulation on the wires had been worn down. After the hot wire had worn down all insulation it was shorting out against the drum. 

We were very fortunate to have been in the room at the time of the sparks and were able to address the problem prior to a fire starting and that no one was injured.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit and sparks, but no injury or fire occurred, and the issue was promptly addressed.

I took it out side and it continued to smoke. We had to open the doors and windows for over two hours with snow and temps in the low 30s. incident_description:
Report of design defect
When replacing water in a "Cool Mist Ultrasonic Humidifier" Model HUM-CM50, distributed by HoMedics, http://www.homedics.com/?gclid=CNbljMi_ua0CFYUZQgodNnO0nQ I followed the instructions filling the water tank at the fill location on the bpttom of the tank and ther replaced the cap.  I then inverted the tank.  Again following the instructions, I picked up the water tank using the handle on the top as illustrated in the instruction manual.  The handle broke away from the water tank and crashed to the floor and broke.  Fortunatley it did not fall on my foot as the sharp edge of the bottom of the tank could cause serious injury.
This is a design defect that can easily result in the tank with sharp edges on the bottom side dropping with the weight of the water.  That sharp edge of the plastic tank could damage exposed flesh or if falls on the electric cord during the reinstallation of the tank potentially sever the insulation on the electric cord, the tank break and flood the floor with water causing and accidental electrocution of the product user.
The plastic foldable U-shaped handle is attached to the tank only by two small tabs approximately a 1/4 inch in length.  The installation of the handle at manufacture is simply by expanding the handle and then it returns to original shape.  With the added weight of the 1 gallon of water in the tank, the handle readily disengages from the retaining slots.  With the shape of the handle being U shaped and approximately 3 and 1/8 inches wide and only approximately 1 and half inches deep even a person with small hands  when inserting four fingers and picking up the tank will cause the width of the handle to expand and disengage the handle tabs from the slots.
justification: The incident involved a broken handle and potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is high due to the design defect.

incident_description:
On 12/20/2011 the heater made by Bionaire model # BCH9221 stopped blowing warm air. I removed the back panel looking for a blown fuse. There is no fuse in the unit. What I found was a burned neutral wire, melted case, and arching marks within the unit.

The unit has a single 16ga wire acting as the neutral for 2, 750 watt heat elements.
A single 16ga wire is rated for 13 amps

The heater is a 1500 watt heater
1500 watts / 120 volts = 12.5 amps

The 16 gauge neutral wire is under sized and has the potential of causing a fire within the unit.
justification: The incident involved a heater malfunction with potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

Summary: On 12/30/11 [redacted] was preparing to wash clothes in her new Whirlpool washing machine. She poured bleach into a glass measuring cup. She then placed the glass measuring cup on the dryer while putting the top on the bleach bottle and placing the bleach bottle in the overhead cabinet.  Because of the curved downward slope of the top of the dryer sloping from back to front, the measuring cup containing bleach slid to the front of the dryer and fell to the floor, splashing bleach onto the floor, the rug in the laundry room, clothes hanging several feet away in the laundry room, and onto [redacted]ÃÂspecifically onto her legs, arms, hands and body.  She sustained bleach burns and swelling to her hands, arms and legs.  Property damaged included her shirt and pants, the rug in the laundry room, and clothes hanging in the laundry room.

Defect/Hazard in dryer and washing machine design: Forward downward slope of the tops causes objects placed on the tops to slide down and fall to the floor.  No warnings on any materials or on the washer or dryer warned against putting objects on the top of the dryer or washing machine.  No rim or other design feature prevents objects such as containers of liquids, clothes baskets, detergent boxes or containers from sliding forward down the sloping top and falling to the floor.  The risk is exacerbated by any moisture present on the top of the dryer/washer or on the bottoms of containers placed on the top of the dryer/washer.

Comment:  It is pure luck that the splash from the bleach did not enter [redacted] eyes. It is only a matter of time, however, before serious bodily injury results from caustic substances or objects slipping down and falling from the sloping tops of the Whirlpool Cabrio washer and dryer.
justification: The incident resulted in bleach burns and swelling, indicating an injury, and the design flaw suggests a likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
i purchased a Milwaukee drill model 3/8 close quarter angle drill #0370-20 in late 2010 to use on installing kitchen cabinets and for other close quarter uses.  i was a California licensed contractor, now retired, and am very familiar with small tool handling.  (I am typing now with one hand so please be patient with my typing style.)  

On December 9, 2011 while using the 0370-20 angle drill my right index finger was caught by the drill's cord almost wrenching my finger off.  I am currently still in a cast and the injury was broken knuckles.  

 I've used the tool before and had a few close calls with it when changing a drill bit or screw bit.  The angle drill can only be held one way to use the key to open the chock.  during the process of changing a bit the trigger can be accidentally engaged with a slight slip of a finger or thumb.  In my case my left thumb slipped slightly touching the trigger while I was holding the key in the chock.  The drill started abruptly spinning its cord around my right index finger.  The chock key slammed into my right hand palm and the drill cord spun around my right finger almost ripping it off.

I have another Milwaukee drill that is the pistol type which has a safety feature where the plug can be removed at the drill handle to ensure safe changing of bits with the chock key.  The 3/8 0370-20 angle drill does not have any safety features to avoid an accident similar to the one I had.  IT IS A DANGEROUS TOOL THAT SHOULD BE REDESIGNED OR REMOVED FROM THE MARKET.
justification: The incident resulted in broken knuckles, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the user's previous close calls and the lack of safety features on the tool.

If this is the correct analysis, then many of these units will FAIL SPARKING in similar way after several years of use -- and go from being very safe to very unsafe.

I will keep this unit for your investigation. I maybe able to send you a video of it sparking.

incident_description:
While washing a load of laundry in my Staber wash machine, I noticed the machine had stopped & the GFI receptacle needed to be reset. I pushed the reset button and heard a sort of zapping sound and immediately stopped the machine. It smelled like something electrical was burning. My husband took the machine apart and saw that the "Motor Controller" board had burn marks on it. He started the machine to try to determine what was happening and the controller board started to smoke. We unplugged the machine and had to leave it as such until we could contact Staber Industries because they were for the weekend. 
We contacted Staber Industries on the following Monday to find out how the Motor Controller could have ignited - an obvious safety hazard. They had no answer for us at that point and waiting for them to call back Tuesday we finally got their answer. We were told a speck of dust or even a pet hair could have caused the board to ignite. This was shocking to us considering the motor controller board is located on the back, interior of the machine and covered with plastic. We were concerned that something else might have been malfunctioning to cause the board to start on fire but we were told thatÃÂs not the reason and that we could purchase a new board. 
A motor controller board igniting on a home appliance is a major hazard and we deemed it necessary for the public to know. We bought this machine new in 2005 and have taken good and proper care of it. We are thankful the machine was plugged into a GFI outlet as if it wasnÃÂt we more than likely would have had a fire.
justification: The incident involved an electrical malfunction causing a motor controller board to ignite, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.
