Yesterday morning upon entering daughter's room, I asked why it was so cold. She responded by using her remote at her bedside to initiate DeLonghi Heater, purchased last fall at a local retailer.
The unit turned on with fan and heat. I commented to her that her mouth did not appear as swollen as she'd just had braces applied 2 days before, a rather unpleasent experiance. We then both exclaimed,"What's that SMELL!?"!  Because the heater had just been turned on, I turned to look down and saw smoke billowing out  from the bottom rear left of the unit and less smoke wafting out the top of the unit, the whole time the unit continued operating as if all systems were "go". I quickly unplugged the unit and we both left the room to be able to breathe. The stench was toxic, simular to an electrical fire in my apartment in 1976, of which a stereo that had recently been repaired from a lightning strike, was identified as the culprit. Had I not been called into work that night, its probable I would've died in my sleep. I came home from working NICU to my windows completly blackened with toxic soot, my door warm to touch. I woke my neighbors on both sides and tried to climb from one's balcony to mine in attempt to rescue my 2 kittens, Gypsy and Jessica, but my neighbors kept saying I couldn't make it ( 3rd floor apt). The firemen arrived, they had head gear, and went in to rescue them, but it was too late. 
It was that kind of toxic stench that was billowing into my daughter's room from this "Delonghi SAFEHEAT" heater.
It was that unavoidable memory of sheer anguish, of their limp, lifeless bodies in my arms, that motivates me almost exactly 35 years later, to put my many other priorities aside (and 2 weeks before Xmas, there's plenty I need to be doing, believe me). 
For it maybe, that some good can come from the horrible death my kittens must have experianced so many years ago. I know how blessed I am to still have my child, braces and all, here with me today. And if my relating this alarming event can alert and perhaps prevent someone else's loved one from a simular tragic occurance, then some good will be done.
There is obvious plastic meltage on the unit.
Should pictures or the unit itself be desired, please advise.
justification: The incident caused smoke and a toxic stench, but no injury or death.

incident_description:
We built a new home in 2009 and 10-15-2009  I installed a 10kw GE whole home generator model 040316  s/n 1017504211with automatic weekly exerciser.  We are 2 hours south of Canada border so ran heavy  (#6 AWG stranded copper) 12v battery cables in underground conduit to 12 volt automotive lead-acid maintenance-free sealed battery stored in warm basement.  The GE installation manual insisted that a 12v 350CCA  AGM battery be installed, however none of the local auto parts stores, nor Sears, Wal-Mart, K-Mart, Autozone, NAPA stocked AGM type.   Installed accessory GE (Briggs and Stratton model 359775 engine) engine oil heater #6030  Standby Generator Cold Weather Kit 6-10-2010 for easier winter starting.  Operator's Manual page 20 advises not to charge battery higher than 13.7 volts if battery needs recharging, at a rate not to exceed 2 amps.

On 12-8-2011 after working normally and weekly automatic exercising (set at 40 minutes per) we had a utility company power failure and noticed the generator did not turn on.  I checked voltage at the battery at 13.8vdc and was convinced the battery was OK.  I observed no "fault lights" on at the basement transfer switch box.  I observed a FC-5  "Low Frequency" fault at the display on the generator itself.

The local generator repair tech came on 12-20-2011, opened the generator service door, removed the 15 amp fuse, pressed manual start override and simultaneously the engine just started to try and turn over as a loud bang was heard from the house basement where the battery was kept.  We went to the battery and the air was overpowering to breathe with battery acid vapor in the air.  The battery entire top was embedded in the ceiling insulation, one end was blown off the battery, and acid was everywhere.  We left the room, disconnected the 12v cables at the generator outside, brought in a new charged 12v car battery and using jumper cables the tech tried to start the generator to see if the generator had any problems.  The tech could not get the generator to run for more than several seconds at a time, but while doing that he did some voltage tests and said it was not putting out any voltage.  He checked the windings on the stator beneath the engine and said their ohms was correct.  He commented that he saw some "mud-wasp nests" and that maybe they had gotten inside the stator and are causing the "no voltage output" condition.  I told him of the 13.8vdc I had measured at the battery, and he remarked that would be affected by the generator's constant trickle charger that never turns off.  I commented that if the maintenance-free battery had boiled off from constant trickle charging (no float cycle) then that would mean built up hydrogen gas inside the battery, and when he got it to try and crank over the generator, the inrush amps from the battery triggered the explosion.  He said that I should have used an AGM battery, not a lead-acid battery, that he learned that at Briggs and Stratton Tech training.  He further stated that they want you to use AGM batteries because they can take the vibration better inside the generator housing.  I asked if they always use AGM batteries when doing the whole installation themselves, and he said "We didn't use to, but now we do".  He stated he had never seen a battery explode in his time as a generator tech, that this was the first.  I pointed out that I had kept mice out of the generator with 1/4" screening, but to keep wasps out would require building a larger enclosure using house screening.  His cell phone went dead waiting on hold for GE tech help, and was not able to fix the generator, leaving with "I'll let you know what I find out".  

I read all I could online about generator batteries exploding, about AGM batteries, and learned that AGM batteries require special charging strategy, and cannot tolerate overcharging.  Read that AGM batteries can be ruined from one overcharge event, "drying out the battery" and doing permanent damage.  So I phoned GE customer support to ask about the exploded battery and their charging strategy.  I was told that they always are trickle charging but that as the battery voltage rises, they lower the current from a maximum of 2 amps down to as low as .33 amps.  He assured me that would not damage an AGM battery.  He advised selecting one with higher than the recommended 350CCA was fine, that the larger the better because it puts less stress on the battery, and I agreed.  When I asked if mud-wasps could damage the stator or windings below the engine I was told "No, they are too soft and would get wiped off on start up".  He said they could interfere with running of the engine if they built a nest inside the atmospheric vent of the fuel regulator, which would not be a warranty situation.

I ordered an AGM battery rated at 850 CCA online, and await the technician coming back to work on the generator when he gets the information he needs from GE.
justification: The incident involved a battery explosion causing significant damage and hazardous conditions, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
A.O Smith Water Products
Gas Water heater
Model: GVR 50 300
Serial #: 1114J014035
Mfg Date: 4/08/2011

The water heater pressure tank ruptured. I can't see where on the tank because of the insulation and outer jacket.  The water was running out the bottom of the unit.  The rupture was large enough that the water was running out almost as fast as it was flowing in.  This is NOT a pinhole leak it is a rapid onset catastrophic failure of the pressure tank structure. The catch pan was able to direct the water outside and flooded my side yard.  

The gas control has positions for OFF, Pilot, VAC, Low, Hot, A, B, C, Very hot.  We keep the control set on A.  The water heater is installed in the garage 19 inches off the floor in a three sided niche.   The garage walls are drywall on the inside, ÃÂfinishedÃÂ.  This is a new house built in June of 2011.

There was no problem when I left for work at 7:30 am. As I said the unit is located in the garage and I had to pass near it to leave for the day.  My wife did hear a loud bang around 11:30 am.  She assumed it was workers working on the house down the street.  At 5:22 PM I received a call from her.  She had gone out to take the trash to the curb and discovered the side yard was flooded.  Water was running out of the drain pan outlet pipe on the side of the house. When she investigated further she saw the indicator on the gas control was blinking, and that the catch pan under the water heater had water flowing through it to the outside.  The blink cycle was a 4 blink pattern indicating ÃÂTEMPERATURE EXCEEDEDÃÂ.  She immediately turned the control to off and also turned off the gas at the shutoff valve.  About that time I arrived home.  I reached up to the top of the unit to see if the pressure relief valve was open.  It appeared to be closed however when I looked outside there was water coming out of both the catch pan drain and  a little out of the relief valve drain.  I then turned off the water supply to the tank.  Water continued to flow into and out of the drain pan until the unit appears to be empty.

We called our builder and they had the original plumber come out to see what was wrong.  He believed that it is a crack in the tank.  They are ordering a new unit and will install it tomorrow. I assume they are taking the failed unit with them.
justification: The water heater pressure tank ruptured, causing flooding but no injury or death.

Then, during the following summer, we noticed that the air had a constant odor and we felt ill when in the home.  As our exposure lengthened we found that we were constantly sick with congestion, frequent sinus infections, dizziness, headaches, and general malaise.   We found that when we left our house for extended periods of time we got better.  We also found that when spend time in or near the attic the symptoms are much worse.   We have spent thousands of dollars on testing and incremental remediation efforts, but nothing has helped.  The installer and the manufacturer have been of limited help.  Industry experts have said that the foam was installed cold and did not mix properly, and that it needs to be removed.  The problem is that no one is willing to remove it.  The manufacturer and installer are not willing and I have not found another contractor that is interested in performing removal.
justification: The incident caused prolonged health issues including congestion, sinus infections, dizziness, and headaches, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the symptoms persist and worsen with continued exposure.

incident_description:
We purchased Karastan Smart Strand carpet for our home (4 bedrooms, office, loft area and stairs) from Merkel Carpet in Ann Arbor.  It was installed on November 7 & 8, 2011.  Despite our having the retailer open and air out the carpet for several days prior to it being installed, the odor of the carpet was very strong.  After the installation, we kept our the windows open and an attic fan running around the clock for 7-8 days.  During this time we slept in the basement of our home because the smell was overwhelming.  The odor made us nauseated, dizzy, short of breath and resulted in a significant cough.  We contaced the retailer and were instructed to purchase fans to 'exhaust' the smell from the rooms.  This did not remove the small.  Approximatley 10 days after the installation, Merkel had a catastrophic cleaning company come out and steam clean the carpet and place an industrial air scrubber in our home.  After 3 days the smell remained and the retailer finally agreed to remove the carpet.  At this point we were living in a hotel, where we remained for approximately 2 weeks.  
After the removal, Merkel indicated they sent the carpet to an independent lab for analysis, but to date we have received no confirmation of this, nor have we been notified of the findings, if any.
I would like to note that I purchased Karastan carpet for my last home in approximately 2001, and we re-carpeted the entire basement in our current home within the past 4 years and had no problems whatsoever with the carpet. The hotel we stayed in was also carpeted and caused us no difficulties.  I am 44 years old and have never lived in a home or apartment that was not carpeted and have never had a problem with carpet prior to purchasing the Smart Strand.
justification: The incident caused nausea, dizziness, shortness of breath, and a significant cough, indicating injury. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as the issue was specific to this particular carpet installation.

incident_description:
The other night, our electric [REDACTED] dryer overheated/caught fire and filled the basement with smoke. The smoke alarm alerted us to this danger. When we went into the laundry room, the dryer was still running and the air was thick with smoke. The dryer was too hot to touch on any of the metal surfaces (sides and top). We opened the door to stop the cycle and yanked out the clothes which were also too hot to touch. In retrospect, that was probably the wrong thing to do in case they had actually been in flames. Most likely, lint got on the elements and burned. 

However, the dryer KEPT RUNNING even after it overheated/caught fire. We had to unplug it with a pot holder. The breaker DID NOT TRIP. We now know that it is probably because we have  Federal Pacific stab-lok panel #945776. 

My concern is that the purpose of the circuit breaker is to stop the electricity to an overheated or burning appliance to stop the electricity. In this case that did not happen. I have no way of knowing if this will ever happen again or if I am in constant danger b/c the panel does not alert us to the danger that is there.
justification: The dryer overheated/caught fire, but no one was injured, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 because the dryer was still running after the fire, which is a rare but possible occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased a whirlpool dryer on 3/3/2010. A gas dryer from Sears model number WGD915OWWO and serial number M01205793.  In December of 2010 I called and was sent a replacement part for my dryer lint screen.  There is a felt gasket on it that when you pull it out of the dryer, to wipe it off before use, it pulls up the lint with it.  The gasket becomes detached and tears its way off the vent.  I have just had my second (the replacement to the original) gasket fall off the vent.  Now my dryer screen comes out of the dryer almost lint free because there is no gasket to gather it onto the screen and secure it when you pull it out of the dryer.  And there is lots of lint in my dryer venting system that I can see with a flashlight.  I contacted Whirlpool on 12/6/2011 and requested a second vent screen because the replacement part had also broken in the exact same way.  I was told that I could purchase a replacement part.  I asked if it broke again in the same way would it be covered and I was told only within 30 days of shipment.  I was also told that the problem was identified in September of 2011and fixed but since so few people had the issue that a recall was not issued and replacements will not be sent out.

I can"t believe they know about a problem, have fixed it, and won't issue the parts to everyone who has purchased it.  The amount of lint that could build up is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard due to lint buildup, but no actual fire or injury has occurred.

Ever since the first load of wash i have had a mold problem in this washer. Since it is a front load washer there is a rubber gasket around the door; this gasket grows black mold and mildew at an extremely fast rate. We clean our washer twice a month with bleach wipes but the mold comes back almost immediately. Also there is a drawer in the front of this washer, in which you put the soap, and the drawer and compartment it slides into also becomes covered in black mold. I am  highly allergic to black mold, it causes asthma attacks and promotes sinus infections, black mold is a very serious health risk. In order to try and prevent this mold from growing we allow adequate air flow into the washer by leaving the door open and soap drawer open. I contacted whirlpool about this and they were very unconcerned about the potential health risk this poses. the incident date is the beginning of this problem and it has continued from years. when searching online i found hundreds or thousand of people with the same problems. this has also caused my clothes to stink and some had to be put in the trash due to being ruined
justification: The incident involves persistent mold growth causing health issues like asthma attacks and sinus infections, indicating injury (severity 3). The problem is widespread and recurring, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
I was using an Eureka Boss Upright vacuum cleaner, model # 5902BVZ, and noticed that the handle near the switch was getting progressively warmer. As I finished up the vacuuming it was down right hot to the touch and in switching it off it sparked from within the handle at the switch. When I tried to turn it back on to trouble shoot the problem it would spark and the power to the vacuum would cut in and out without the rocker switch moving sparking each time.

When I opened up the handle after I let it cool the wiring had melted through its insulation in 2 wires and the slide on "quick connect" connectors attached to the 3 way switch was charred. The handle was also melted where the wires were touching the inside plastic of the handle.

  As well as being charred in the connectors, the wire going into the connectors on two wires were also frayed and there was a pale greenish looking residue on the metal of the wires, like the metal was corroded which was also evident on the inside wall of the wire's insulation.

  I don't know if it's the wire's fault(improper gauge, low quality), the switches fault causing the wires to over heat or the connectors. Reading online I've come across many experiencing the same exact problem but all having different theories as to the culprit.

  I see this as a large hazard and a design flaw more than a "wear and tear" issue and Eureka should address this issue.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is a common issue with this model.

The "thermostat" mechanism carries the full current of the heater coils, and is a fire hazard due to contact pitting, resultant series resistance, and final always-on operation.  If left unattended, temperature will rise to dangerous levels.

The consumer stated that the drain cleaner he was using has an insecure packaging. The consumer was hold the 64 oz. container trying to open it when the plastic film surrounding the top allowed the bottle to slip out of his grasp. The bottle fell vertically to the floor about 3 feet below breaking, resulting in the drain cleaner to spill on to the consumer's legs and feet. The consumer suffered some burns and injuries. 

The consumer cannot fathom as to why the plastic bottle was not more durable to sustain that fall without breaking. The consumer called the company in March 7, 2011. The consumer was asked for an account of what happened. The consumer went to the doctor that he had first degree burns on his lower legs and feet with second degree on both of his calves. The consumer went to his physician and dressed his legs in medical gauze and left the same day. The consumer went to [redacted]. There was no follow up treatment. The consumer called the firm within the week (date unknown). The consumer mentioned the visit and the firm asked him to send the bottle of the product. The consumer sent the bottle in to the firm in May 2011 at his own expense.

 The consumer called back the firm a week or two later (date unknown). The firm concluded that their product was just fine and there was no issue. The consumer has yet to call the firm. The product has not caused damage to his house. The product did destroy his shorts and footwear. 

The Consumer Added:  I purchased a bottle of Rooto Corp drain cleaner, named "Professional Drain Opener", from Ace Hardware in Piedmont, CA on Feb 28, 2011. On March 6th, as I have done dozens of times, I was holding the bottle of drain cleaner, which has a plastic outer covering (picture attached), and opening the plastic packaging at the same time. I put a hole in the top of the outer plastic packaging to pull the bottle of drain cleaner out. When I put a hole in the outer plastic packaging the bottle of drain cleaner leaned on the outer plastic packaging and split the vertical seam and the bottle fell out ofthe packaging. The bottle fell to the floor and the safety cap popped off of the bottle and the contents of the bottle, acid, splashed onto my feet and legs. I have issue with the safety cap coming off of the bottle. Is the safety cap supposed to keep children safe from opening the bottle? If a child dropped the bottle on the floor the safety cap would prove to be useless against a child from opening the bottle and possibly getting burned or worse by the acid in the bottle. I strongly advise the safety caps be tested and evaluated to see if they are actually safe. I also advise the plastic packaging be tested for strength and that there be opening instructions on the packaging. If there had been instructions telling the consumer the safest way to open the packaging, I probably would not have sustained the 2nd degree burns on both of my legs. It has been over 7 months since the accident and I still have unhealed scars on both legs (pictures enclosed).
justification: The consumer suffered first and second degree burns, indicating an injury, but no death occurred. The incident is possible but not highly frequent based on the description.

When I discovered the heater not producing heat, I traced the cord back to the wall and found the wall completely scortched above the plug. Photographs of the damage may be supplied if requested.

The insulation is flaking off, the cord is kept inside in a drawer,never exposed to the sun.  Reading the comments on Amazon's web site this seems to be a very common problem.  The peeling of the insulation causes the bare wires to be exposed and could cause a shock or fire problem.  I have e-mailed Amazon with my complaint but have not heard back from them as yet.  It seems a recall is in order.
justification: The peeling insulation exposes bare wires, posing a potential shock or fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his solar power inverter caught fire at his home. The consumer stated that he got the product from the original firm in a Warning Exchange from March 4, 2004. The original firm went out of business and was bought by another company. The consumer called the manufacturer (the new firm) on March 31, 2011. The firm offered a case number and said they would get back in contact with him. The consumer had to get back in contact with them April 2, 2011 since he never was contacted. That same day he was told they would call him back but never did. 

The consumer is not sure if was in March or April of this year but he called the firm and they told him they would offer to sell him the same product that caught fire at a discounted price. The consumer put out the smoke by disconnecting the power to the solar inverter and the smoke timed itself out. 

The product was mounted on to the wall of a shop building outside of his barn. The product scorched the backside of the barn where the steel cage meets the wall of the barn. The power inverter has melted on the interior. The consumer was not harmed by the product. The consumer has noticed the recall of other power inverters similar to his but have different model numbers. The consumer opted not to call the fire department.
justification: The solar inverter caught fire but the consumer was not harmed, and the fire was contained without injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased the Elmo Bathmat made by Ginsey Industries last year (2010) at my local Walmart. The bathmat provides help with skid resistence in the tub for my small children. While it serves its purpose, and the characters are entertaining for children, the bathmat itself is a safety hazard. The mat is less than a year old, and the elmo characters and beach balls that are affixed to the mat will peel off. They are very small pieces, and will not only pose a choking hazard to small children but also clog your drain for the bath. My 1.5 year old son was coughing on a piece of the rubbery material and I had to pry it out of his mouth. Luckily I was there to catch it happening. I have retained several of the pieces that have come off the mat, and saved the mat itself in case you would like to request pictures. This is a safety hazard to children that tend to put things in their mouths, and also to people that are relying on the elmo pieces *the only actual skid resistent pieces on the mat* to aid children from slipping.
justification: The incident involved a choking hazard for a child, but no injury occurred as the parent intervened in time.

incident_description: I own a Craftsman air compressor; I had seen a list of recalled air compressors that someone at my workplace had sent out to me; I checked my Model number against the ones listed on the recall. my compressor was not there, but the model number was only digit different from one that was listed; the number on my compressor is 919-166442, the recalled compressors number is 919-16644. Everything about the compressors is the same except the one digit, and the manufacture date; my compressor was made in 2006, and the recalled compressors were made from 5/2004 to 3/2005. the reason the compressors were recalled was that they had a defect that made the motor overheat and made them a fire hazard. My compressor has just recently stopped shutting itself off when it reaches capacity, which would make the motor overheat and create a fire hazard. I believe that my compressor is, or should be part of the recall.
justification: The compressor has a defect that could cause overheating and fire hazard, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: I own a Ryobi model BY3100 table saw, serial # X054698909. While using it today, the power switch suddenly stopped working, leaving the saw 'on.' The only way to stop the blade was to pull the plug. This happened during routine use, but the problem could easily have resulted in a dangerous situation had it involved a jammed board, kickback, etc.
justification: The power switch failure could have led to a dangerous situation, but no injury occurred in this instance.

incident_description:
Caller purchased Oak electrical fireplace in 2009, had no problems with it 2009 or 2010 and was so happy with it that she has ordered 13 more and given them as gifts.

This year around October 6th, 2011 she plugged the fireplace in and instantly flames came out of the outlets about 8 inches long.

Caller's husband immediately unplugged the fireplace and blew on the outlet, flames extinguished with these two actions.
Callers assumed that fire was also extinguished within wall.

Caller doesn't remember exact day, she called him the week of October 17th, 2011 she contacted electrician but he came out to her home before the end of the week.
Electrician checked wiring, replaced outlet and said that the stove/fireplace caused the fire in the outlet.

She contacted the manufacturer after attempts all week on Wednesday, October 26th, 2011, she spoke with [REDACTED]  who gave her reference#  [REDACTED] and referred her to  [REDACTED]  who told her that if she sent old insert, they would send another after she paid $179.

Caller would like to report danger, she said two of the fireplaces that she purchased and sent as gifts also had electrical problems but that as far as she is aware the other 11 are fine.
Caller would like to have the insert in her fireplace replaced at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident caused flames but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is not rare but not frequent either.

incident_description:

The citizen states that he noticed an odor of smoke, smoke and flaming combustion coming from the plug-in unit (believe it maybe associated with the remote control of the insert) that the insert power cord is plugged into and then the unit is plugged into the house electric wiring outlet.

There is obvious internal damage to the plug-in unit and to the cord associated with the insert. It has heat damage to one of the plug blades/prongs and the insulating material around this connect.

There was smoke carbon on the wall and the outlet. The resident witnessed this event and intervened. If he hadn't been home there is a distinct possibility that this would have evolved into a house fire.

The insert will need the cord and plug repaired.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung Model DV2C6BEW electric clothes dryer in August 2007. Every 3-4 months, I have disassembled the vent tubing from the dryer - through the basement ceiling - to the outside house rimboard and vacuumed the lint out of it. On the evening of 11/18/2011, the unit started to give off a lot of smoke as if it was on fire. I turned it off (it was drying clothes at the time), and dragged out of the house to my driveway outside. I did not see any open flames at that time. A few minutes later, I took the screws off the backpanel, and noted that there was indeed an open flame inside the unit, along with a thick coating of charred/burnt lint covering the inside components.

I intend to report this to Lowes (place I purchased it), showing them my sales receipt and 4 year extended warranty - which should initiate after the 1-year manufacturers warranty expires: making it good until August 2012.

This Samsung electric clothes dryer should NOT have lint accumulating inside of the unit, and covering everything. I believe there to be some kind of design defect(s) allowing lint to accumulate inside of the unit, instead of being properly expelled out of the exhaust.

I am NOT interested in joining some class-action lawsuit to enrich a group of lawyers, but rather some kind action from the Manufacturer (Samsung) to remedy this situation for consumers.
justification: The incident involved smoke and an open flame inside the dryer, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
In January 2010, we avoke to a house filled with smoke around 2 a.m. We had 3 newly installed smoke detctors, 2 Family Gard FG200 and 1 First Alert Model SA710. These were less than a month old and all had new batteries. The First Alert went off about 20 or 30 minutes after the fire department arrived. Had I not awakened just by the grace of God, the ceiling would have fallen in on our bed in a matter o minutes. 
This fire resulted in lost work  time, a very inconvenient move, personal trauma, and of course, loss of things. Insurance only covered a fraction of these costs but I am more concerned that other households may believe they are safe when they are not.
justification: The incident involved a house fire with significant property damage and personal trauma, but no reported injuries or deaths.

justification: The incident involved a steam mop tank exploding and spraying hot water, which poses a significant risk of injury due to scalding.

After a short time I heard it start up & was running when I ran out to the kitchen & pulled the plug from the extention cord.  It had been sitting on a drop cloth for a while when a self-started.  I checked the on/off switch and it was solidly in the off position, not hovering between.  There were no injuries and because the sander was sitting on drop cloth, no damage occurred to the floor.  It could have if obviously on the floor and I wasnÃÂt near enough to hear it.

incident_description:
On June 11, 2009 Woodman Insulation in Atlanta installed Icynene foam under the roof in our attic at {REDACTED]. The installer did not tell us to be out of the house and didn't create a negative air pressure in the attic. The vapor and mist from the installation permeated the whole house and made us sensitive to something in the product. 
    A couple of days after installation, we started living in the houses of friends who were on vacation and ventilated the house in hopes that we would be able to return. Within a few weeks, my wife found that she was sensitive to clothes and other possessions we had taken with us from the house. We ultimately realized that we would not be able to live in our house again and bought another house in the same neighborhood. And we put any possessions we thought we might be able to decontaminate in storage. 
    Although my symptoms have not been as bad or consistent and persistent as my wife's, we both experienced eye irritation and headaches. My wife also experienced chest pain. She remains sensitive to possessions brought from storage, and I get headaches from latex paint and lacquer odor, symptoms I have never experienced before even though I have used those products.
justification: The incident caused eye irritation, headaches, and chest pain, which qualifies as injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described circumstances.

incident_description: I was operating my Yanmar YDG 3700 Generator during hurricane Irene.Machine is small diesel powered 3700 watt generator (2007).   On the second day of operation machine became loud, exhibited heavy smoking and expelled 6-8 inch flames from exhaust. I was asleep and was awakened early by the noise.   Generator was powering my home during the massive state wide power outage.  When I arrived at Generator flames were shooting from the exhaust and entire muffler was cherry red.   This generator was operating in the doorway of my garage.   If I had not awoken generator could have easily burned down my garage and possible adjoining house. I Innately thought that gen set was merely suffering from engine problems.   Upon tear down of the generator it was revealed that Rotor winding were rubbing on stator from improper winding process from Yanmars generator assembly plant in Japan.   Windings were at the same levels or protruding past the base of the magnet fields. the windings eveually rubbed and ground off. (they literally melted to stator)  I did purchase new rotor which revealed the proper tight winding process.   This generator was doomed to fail from day one.   It operated at total of 16 hours.   I am concerned that other generators are out there with similar dangerous windings.   I also feel lucky that I noticed condition before catastrophe struck.   By winding rubbing on stator it caused generator to go into a series overload condition, burning muffler and shooting flames.   I attempted to notify Yanmar of condition but they did not appear interested in studying defective rotor.   I have documneted process with pictures and have also saved unsafe rotor for verification.
justification: The incident involved a generator malfunction that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore Elite Oasis ST gas dryer that I purchased from Sears in 2008.  On Sunday, Nov. 13th, 2011 my dryer started having a burning smell again.  I say again because back in March of this year I had a lint fire in the back of this same dryer.  I unplugged it and called my independent repairman.  He confirmed that it was the lint  that was burning again.  [REDACTED] told both my mother and myself that this was the WORST lint collection design he has seen.  He also told me that the fan was very poor as well.  He has been in the repair business for over 40 years.  
     This is the second time in 8 months that the lint has caught fire INSIDE my dryer, not the outside vent.  I clean the lint screen after EVERY cycle and fortunately never run the dryer when I am not home.  I also have pulled the screen out and tried to vacuum down the lint screen hole.  I probably do about 6 loads of laundry a week. I have never had this problem with any other dryer I have owned in my life.  I am 46 years old and have done more than my fair share of laundry. 
     I am VERY fearful that someone will be hurt, die or lose their home because of this dryer. Please investigate this dryer as I could not locate any recalls for it.  I cannot be the only one who has had this problem with this clothes dryer.  If you need them I took pictures this time of the inside of the dryer before it was cleaned out.  Thank you so much for looking into this.  

Kenmore Elite Oasis ST Gas Dryer
Mod  110.78062801
Ser    MW3501430
Type  DSSA-NAT-1206006-EL20
justification: The incident involved a recurring lint fire inside the dryer, posing a risk but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Monday, October 24th, 2011, caller's 5'6" wife was vacuuming when a large fireball approximately 7" in diameter came out of the area where the hose attaches to the vacuum.

The fire came fairly close to the caller's wife's face, however she was not injured.

She dropped the wand, went to kitchen grabbed baking soda and water then put the fire out, however while she was getting the baking soda and water the heat burned an approximately 8" by 8" circle in their carpeting.

Caller contacted the manufacturer through the retailer on October 24, 2011, does not remember who he spoke with at either source of contact but was told by the manufacturer to send pictures which he did and sent UPS payment slip to return vacuum to them.

Manufacturer has stated to caller that they will replace vacuum cleaner, repair his carpeting and assured him that they had no recalls since the 1980's.  (This fact was verified by this representative.

Caller is filing this report to alert the public, in attempt to generate a recall and to assure himself that the manufacturer will follow up on their promises.

This rep has explained to caller that CPSC does not become involved in the legality of personal issues. 
Provided Consumer Protection contact numbers to caller.
justification: The incident involved a fireball from a vacuum cleaner that caused property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
Having a party by the pool and in the late afternoon it was getting cool.  I lit the patio heater, using the knob (which creates a spark to ignite the pilot light).  It lit on the fourth or fifth try and then I turned the knob further to the low position.  Once the burner was lit, I turned it further to high, which was fully CCW.  I closed the lid covering the knob.  Many of the women at the party gathered around and started talking (four or five) and this went on for about 30 minutes.  
As they were standing there, the lower portion of the patio heater (where the propane tank is stored) exploded.  Flames shot out the lower vent holes at the very bottom of the unit and everyone jumped.
I ran over to the unit (I was about 15 feet away, facing the unit) and saw the propane cylinder was on fire, but still enclosed in the lower cylinder cover.  I first tried to open the burner valve cover to access the knob and shut off the upper flame.  The fire was shooting out of the grid and burning the entire upper section.  My finger burned as soon as I touched the cover, so I could not access the valve.
My attention turned to the burning propane cylinder.  I told everyone to get away, far away.  I blew hard through the hand-hole of the cylinder cover and was able to extinguish the flame.  I then opened the cylinder cover, which burned my hand further.  I then turned off the gas valve on top of the propane cylinder, burning all five fingers on my right hand (through my shirt I was using to protect my hand).
There was molten metal on the regulator that must have dripped down from the inside of the upper burner area.  I have no idea what melted.
Someone handed me a bottle of water, and I used it to extinguish the upper flame, that was still burning without propane feeding it.  
An hour or so later, I opened the door to the knob in the upper burner area and it was melted beyond recognition.
The patio heater is still sitting exactly as it was during the fire.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the hand, indicating an injury, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
I believe my Venmar Constructo 2.0 may be defective and a definite fire hazard...apparently the motor has seized and is too hot to touch, as reported by the service man today.  It is 10 years old. It was installed by Enbridge and  we are not sure it ever worked efficiently, but started asking questions finally when we discovered that the intake vents were totally clogged...and NEVER  cleaned by companies every year, particularly for the last four years.   I am now wondering where I can find a second opinion because I am leary of replacing the motor without verifying that indeed the motor has seized...( we have two systems and when the second system was checked he said the same thing about the motor, but the words were hardly out of his mouth when the system came on!  We went back to the first system, but it actually would not start.

He also initially said the second system was too hot to touch and if so, I am wondering whether it is about to go as the first one apparently has gone.  FYI  he pushed what I believe is a white reset button on both systems and it seemed to work on the second, albeit a few seconds delayed.

So what is my next move before I spend an inordinate amount of money, gladly so, if the equipment is unsafe, but also wondering why a 10 year old motor on these systems would fail....I read somewhere that they can run for several years without having to be serviced.
justification: The motor is reported as seized and too hot to touch, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: The product is a hot liquified rubber crack filler for home use filling cracks in asphalt driveways.  The product comes pre-filled in a can like a metal paint can and comes with a handle that clamps onto the can.  You are to heat the filler on a camping cookstove or grille to melt it, and then stir before pouring in the cracks. I used a small camping gas burner that fit onto a 1 lb. propane bottle to heat it.  The instructions said to heat it on medium heat, then begin stirring after 15 minutes.  In following the instructions and doing that, the product did not melt as it was supposed to, it began to raise in the can but the top layer did not begin to melt.  I began to get concerned and kept checking it, and I could see the bottom of the can beginning to swell. Expecting the top to melt, I left it on the heat longer.  The filler continued to raise in the can with the top not melting, so I sensed something was really wrong.  I then grabbed the handle of the container with my right hand that had a glove on, raised it off the heat and turned off the camp burner with my left hand.  At that point the bottom of the can exploded down, spraying the hot crack filler down onto my left hand and up onto my face.  I received 1st and 2nd degree burns on both my face and hand, requiring going to the hospital emergency room to remove the tar and treat the burns.  I have needed recurring visits to a burn center to continue to treat the burns. The instructions did not have any warning about the possibility that the can could could blow out spraying hot filler, or what to do when the filler did not melt properly.
justification: The incident resulted in 1st and 2nd degree burns requiring hospital treatment and follow-up care, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the instructions lacked warnings about potential hazards.

incident_description:
I bought a home generator about 1 year ago and have operated it for a total of about 30 minutes. It has been kept dry and dust-free in a shed, so it is essentially brand new.

Yesterday (November 5, 2011) I started it and a large flow of gasoline immediately flooded out onto the ground. I shut off the engine and stopped the gas flow with the valve on the engine. I have repaired it and the cause was a rubber gas line becoming disconnected from the nipple it was slid over. My opinion is that the gas line was too short and the ring clamp that was supposed to hold it in place was too weak to provide any significant clamping force.
justification: The incident involved a gasoline leak but was promptly controlled without injury or further damage.

incident_description: Bionair 1500 Watt Tower Heater w/remote Control.  The tower oscillates.  The plug on the unit gets extremely hot that it melted a surge protector it was plugged into.  The wall plug with the unit plugged directly into the outlet also became extremely hot.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
In May 2008, I purchased an installed steel insulated residential garage door for the house I was building from Lowes of Jacksonville, NC.  Lowes and the manufacturer, AMARR, contracted with Griffin Garage Doors of Goldsboro, NC.  The garage doors were installed in Dec 2008.

The manufacturer's installation instructions state "Torsion spring and opener applications require 2" x 6" minimum spring anchor pads".  AmarrÃÂs instructions are based on the guidance and standards published by the Door & Access Systems Manufacturers Association, International (DASMA).
Griffin Garage Doors, AMARR's chosen installer, attached the center bearing plate of the torsion spring assembly onto a 1"x6" torsion spring pad mounted on a drywall base.  While the installer used the correct 5/16" x 1 5/8" lag bolts provided by the manufacturer they effectively only had 3/4" of the lag bolt imbedded into the spring pad. Griffin has stated that they frequently installed torsion spring assembly pads onto 1"x6" anchor pads.

On November 20, 2009 while inspecting and opening the door, the lag bolt anchors suddenly failed causing the torsion spring assembly center bearing plate to violently become detached from the anchor pad which struck me in the right hand causing severe physical and permanent damage to my right hand. Physical injuries included a crushing injury coupled by severe lacerations. These injuries required emergency vascular surgery with a 3 day hospital stay.  2 more additional day orthopedic surgeries were required to minimize the degree of permanent disabilities. 
An independent professional engineer judgment places the cause of the anchor failure on faulty installation practices.

Based on statements of Amarr's installer that they frequently have installed garage doors utilizing a 1"x6" anchor pad, it is recommended that AMARR issue a recall, conduct inspections of all installed garage doors, and correct any deficiencies identified.

This issue, if not corrected, places the consumer at a high risk of serious injury or possibly death.
justification: The incident resulted in severe physical and permanent damage to the right hand, requiring multiple surgeries, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The installer's frequent use of incorrect anchor pads suggests a likely recurrence (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description:
I plugged this space heater into the outlet and set the temp to 72.  In a minute or two, after heating up, it began sparking and blew the fuse.  It first made a small spark, then a really big one before tripping the breaker.  Looking inside the grate you can see several of the wires and connections are scorched black.

I still have the heater and have not, and will not, try plugging it in again.
justification: The incident involved sparking and a blown fuse, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Black & Decker - Steam Advantage Iron   Model IR1070S   Sold by Walmart.

Open Box, add water, plug it in, heat it up and press the steam button.  You get one large drop of water inside the housing for each surge of steam from the iron when you press the steam button. (Although the steam out of the iron is great).   Set the iron up vertically after a horizontal steam pass on your shirt and it runs out of housing seams and out of the power cord penetration.   Hold it vertical and press the steam button and it leaks out of the steam button, over the power light and across your hand.   Going back before it electrocutes me.

After seeing this I checked product reviews.  They all leak.   Water and 120VAC is a hazard and B&D should recall the product.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation with potential for electric shock due to water leakage near electrical components, posing a risk of injury.

incident_description:
Ryobi 18.v cordless drill Model P200. I was using the drill when it began to smoke. The area around the trigger began to get warm. I know another model was recalled because of possible "problems" in trigger area. Ryobi (800-597-9624) says this model isn't under recall and mine is out of warranty.

Since the drill is no good I took it apart. An area around the black wiring connection to the trigger switch is burnt and melted. The corresponding area on the hand grip is also melted. 

I believe the trigger switch may be a defective part and a safety issue due to the burning.

I have pictures I can send.
justification: The drill began to smoke and caused melting, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Have had problems with it holding water in the soap dispenser, mold mildew smells, not draining out all of the water, leaking after putting in a new seal around door. Why has there not be a recall on this item? Or a fix to the problem, I have tried everything to make the smell go away and I have cleaned out the hoses and it still is having draining issues.
justification: The incident involves functional issues with the soap dispenser and drainage, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: I purchased this dryer in 08/2008.  This dryer has never worked properly with regard to drying clothes.  We have had it serviced as it was covered under an extended protection plan. It still did not work after the service.  I asked the technician why the lint screen does not capture lint in the screen and he did not have an answer.  The lint obviously had been accumulating inside of the dryer posing a serious fire hazard.  This is referring to May 2011:  The dryer started to smoke a few days ago and the fire department was called to my home.  There was the possibility that the dryer vent in the wall was on fire.  Upon further investigation, the dryer vent duct work had no lint accumulated in it.  I did find a substantial amount of lint in the well which holds the lint screen.  There was also a substantial amount of lint in the back of the dryer that did not reach the dryer vent hose.  As I mentioned, the lint screen has never captured the lint and this excess lint accumulates in the well of the lint screen.  The lint then accumulates inside the dryer around the heating element box, etc.  This is a poorly designed lint screen.  It requires a special kind of duct cleaning brush to dig out the lint from the well, as well as using a powerful vacuum.  It is not convenient and it is a very time consuming chore.  The lint screen collects a very minimal amount of lint with the majority of the lint getting trapped in the back of the dryer around the heating element box.  I called a technician to service this dryer after it nearly caught on fire.  He opened the back of the dryer and removed the burned, black lint that was in the dryer.   The smell is horrible and I doubt if it will ever go away.  I was required to pay for this service even though it is covered by an extended protection plan.  I will likely purchase a new dryer because of the smoky smell.  More importantly, I will likely purchase a new dryer because this dryer is a serious fire hazard.  The technician suggested that I remove the back panel of the dryer and do this service routinely.  I have never owned a dryer that required this kind of maintenance to be performed by the consumer.  It is unfortunate that the consumer of this dryer is required to open the back of the dryer and remove the excessive amount of lint that has accumulated to prevent a fire in the dryer.  The lint screen should not allow this amount of lint to back up into the dryer and cause this fire hazard.
justification: The dryer posed a serious fire hazard and started smoking, but no actual fire or injury occurred, indicating an incident with no injury. The recurring lint accumulation issue suggests a likely occurrence of similar incidents.

incident_description: On, October 19, 2011, Sears Electric Clothes Dryer Model 110.66972500 caught fire.  Dryer was working and then we smelled an electrical fire. Determined after running around the house it was the dryer. Saw soot on top of the control panel.  Fire started inside with the controls.  Immediately unplugged dryer and fire smoldered out.  Dryer is not even 6 yrs old - only 2 people in house.  Dryer should not have caught fire.  Called Sears on 10/20/11 at 1-800-469-4663 - then the fun began.  The Sears representative was not sympathetic to hearing that the dryer caught fire, but was ready to sell me that Service Protection Agreement!!  She never even noted anywhere on our information that the dryer caught fire per one of the "numerous" Sears Customer Solutions representatives I spoke with over the last 20 days.  I specifically asked her if the parts would be new or refurbed.  She said new.  She told me that if the cost of the repairs would be over $500 they would provide to me a certificate for $500 for a new dryer.  I was lied to - this was not a misunderstanding.  I specifically asked if the parts would be refurbished and was told they would be new.  After numerous calls and refurbed parts being order.....it is 11/8/11 and I am still waiting for the final repair - which now I am being told will be 11/11/11.  We'll see what happens.  Sear's is a very big disappointment.  Sad.  They were always a good company - very customer oriented.   They are so big now - nobody cares.
justification: The dryer caught fire but was unplugged before causing injury, and there was no mention of any injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Purchased a Craftsman 10 inch Table Saw Model No. 315.284620. The saw has a plastic pad that is used to change the Blade Angle.  The pad cracked when I was moving the blade to a 10 degree cut. With the loss of the pressure pad the saw would not hold an angle and as a result the blade moves freely.  If a person is feeding wood into the blade when the pad cracks there is the potential for injury.  The saw is under warranty and I am contacting Sears to see what can be done.  The pad is plastic and probably should be made out of metal.
The part number is 089037008040.
justification: The incident involves a cracked plastic pad causing the saw blade to move freely, posing a potential injury risk if wood is being fed when it fails.

incident_description:
In-Sink-Erator Counter Top Hot Water Dispenser
Model SST
Manufacture Date: Jan. 2007
Serial #: 07068725313
Tank leaked causing water damage and possible shock hazard.  Water leaked into heat control electronics (110 volts) and spilled into kitchen cabinet causing wood damage.

Disassembly of major tank revealed an overheated, degraded and fractured hose leading from over flow tube to internal overflow tank.  This hose is mounted against tank and obviously, the hose material is not adequate to withstand temperatures of the environment in which it operates (tank temperatures.)

There was a previous recall for similar problem.  Refer to http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml02/02189.html
Previous recall is for previous models manufactured 1972 thru Dec. 1996.
This incident is for a later model but hazard is the same.
justification: The incident involved water damage and a potential shock hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: shower door shattered in the middle of the night , lucky there was no one close to it , found glass 6' away and even in the toilit , read online about many issuses with this happening
justification: The shower door shattered but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm. Online reports suggest this issue is not rare.

incident_description: Report of an electrical fire in the single family home. Units arrived to find a FireX smoke alarm burning. The unit was removed from service.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire and a burning smoke alarm, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated after he had used the spackle to patch holes in preparation for painting the room, approximately 1 hour later he and his spouse smelled a chemical odor which he believed caused them to develop severe headaches, difficulty breathing and chest pains.  They were not able to spend the night at the house.

6/25/11 Consumer took his spouse to the Emergency room at [REDACTED] in [REDACTED]  where she was given oxygen and some kind of treatment (not sure what kind) by the physician and released. There was no diagnosis.
Consumer stated on 7-12-2011 his spouse took him to the emergency room at the same hospital for treatment, where he was treated and released.

Consumer stated that because of the fumes that this product released, he and his spouse were not able to live in their home since 6/24/11.  He has had surface and air samples for the interior of the house tested by a company and he was advised that there was formaldehyde 20, sodium silicote 4000 ppm and sodium borate(not sure of the levels).

Consumer contacted the manufacturer on 7-8-11 and 8-3-11 and was advised that they did not believe that he and spouse illness was caused from the product.
Consumer feels that the Spackle is a health hazard and should be investigated.

10-11-2011 Consumer added:  The chemical(s) in the spackling was unknowingly transferred to my daughter's apartment.  The chemical(s) are in my clothes and truck as well as my wife's clothes and car.  My granson has become sick and my daughter became sick and had to go to the hospital emergency room.
justification: Multiple individuals required emergency room treatment due to chemical exposure, indicating injury.

incident_description: i have a black and decker cordless drill, i was about to start setting a screw into my deck, the switch was set to the foward, screw position, when i pressed the trigger, the drill jumped and and went into reverse, automatically. i was set and positioned for a foward drill and lost my balance and fell on my left shoulder onto the deck and twisted my right knee. i contacted black and decker and sent back my defective drill. i have not heard back from them and that was over 2 months ago. i have to seek medical attention for my knee and shoulder but thay have not authorized this also no one has even communicated with me regarding this injury , please help
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the shoulder and knee requiring medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described malfunction and resulting fall.

incident_description:
Babies R Us Brand -Cabinet & Drawer Latches

Design of latches is faulty and does not provide sufficient protection from young child opening drawers and cabinets. When installed correctly a drawer can be opened with a swift tug, easily applied by a toddler. When examining the product and installation, the falt is with the catch not being long enough to account for deformation in the plastic latch. Most importantly, in real applications the Babies R Us brand cabinet & drawer locks do not provide intended protection.

[REDACTED]
justification: The faulty latches can lead to incidents where children access cabinets, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: Have baseboard heater in livingroom to supplement home heat and noticed that the on light was no longer lite. Prompted me to make sure breaker didn't go off, unplugged heater, plugged in lamp and lamp turned on. This morning I found product manual and took screw out of baseboard heater exposing internal wires connected to on switch. The wires were melted to the point when I touched them with screw driver they crumpled. There was no odor of melting wire covering. Product is about 2 years old only use it periodically. I'm just glad there was no damage, no fire, I'm just not sure that someone else will be as lucky as I was using this product.
justification: The incident involved melted wires in a heater, which could have led to a fire but did not result in any injury or damage.

incident_description: boiler runs, cuts off, and then won't restart.  Inside of boiler is flaking apart.  I understand the boiler is involved in a recall by weil mclain for CO.  My problem is addition to the problem with CO.
justification: The boiler is malfunctioning and involved in a CO recall, indicating a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

justification: There was a spark and flame, but no injury or death occurred, and the flame extinguished on its own.

incident_description:
While using my Ryobi model BD0532 cordless drill it became vey hot and started smoking, I stopped the drill and allowed it to cool, when I tried it again it ran slowly and started to smoke. I was using the drill to drive a drywall screw so it wasn't under a heavy load.

I spoke to a person in the tool dept at Home Depot where it was purchased and was told it was a common problem and its under a product safety recall.

I contacted Ryobi and was told that the recall covered a different model. In looking at the recall notice the drills look identical but it is a different model #. The fack that they look identical makes me wonder if the BD0532 should be included in the product safety recall as it appears to be a safety hazard.
justification: The drill became hot and smoked, but no injury occurred. The issue is known and similar models are under recall, indicating a possible safety hazard.

incident_description: Hampton Bay dehumidifier ModelHB50L caught fire. I had to put it out with an extinguisher.  Lucky I was home.  Looks like the product was recalled for this.
justification: The dehumidifier caught fire, which is a significant incident, but no injury or death occurred as it was extinguished in time.

incident_description: Heater was plugged into wall outlet and heating the room (8x12) from an initial chilly state.  Heater began to make a fizzling sound and release wisps of smoke, then the control panel lit up with bright light and a loud sizzle for about 10 seconds. The sensation was similar to a sparker on July 4th.  I thought the unit was afire and moved the unit towards the middle of the room after the first few seconds, but it stopped eventually and the unit was dead (no lights).  Unplugged the unit and checked the wall outlet for heat or scorching, but there were no signs of damage or overloading, and the outlet appears to be functioning normally.
justification: The heater malfunctioned with smoke and sparks but caused no injury or damage, fitting a severity level 2.

incident_description:
Was using Shark steam mop model # S3501 and unit suddenly popped, there was an electrical flash from the unit and steam began shooting from all around the main body of the unit.  The steam caused some superficial burns to my fingers and hands.  Thankfully the burns weren't as bad as some I have been reading about online after "Googling Shark steam mop exploded".

This unit was purchased through Amazon.com (no reflection on them) as new on January 27, 2010 and the incident happened on 6-27-2011.  This steam mop was only used by myself and approximately once per week for about 15 minutes per usage.

As you can see by the attached photos, something caused the line that attaches to the heating unit to burst.  When the line burst, it actually shoved what appears to be an internal hose support spring out of the hose completely.  On further investigation of this ruptured line, I have found that it is assembled with an extremely sharp bend, almost a kink, in the routing of the line in order to attach to the heating assembly.  Also, the lines used inside of this unit seem to be of a very low grade quality.

If this unit had not assembled with such a sharp bend in the line and/or a higher grade material of line used, I suspect this problem would not have occurred.
justification: The incident caused superficial burns to the hands and fingers, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The description suggests a design flaw that could lead to similar incidents, making occurrence likelihood possible (3).

incident_description: The consumer says she set dryer for 10 minutes and after it was done the gas smell was overwhelming.  Her husand tightened the gas line but the smell persisted.  The consumer contacted a repair shop who told her the issue was with the gas valve.  He said the valve was not shutting and staying open.  The technician told her that they should just buy a new unit altogether because this brand is a piece of junk and none of them work.  The salesman when she bought a new dryer told her the same thing.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak which could have led to injury or death, but no actual harm was reported.

incident_description: Targus laptop power adapter overheated and melted.
justification: The power adapter overheated and melted, which is an incident but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
My long time friend and neighbor was at my house yesterday and her two year old child grabbed my liquid potpourri holder that was on the table and took a sip. He started screaming right away, and his mother brought him to the kitchen to wash out his mouth. We washed out his mouth and washed off the residue left on his face. Because my husband called the poison control number, we did recieve help and were told to call the ambulance. Poison control needed to know the ingredients that were listed on the bottle and there were none! There was no information on the website (dollar general), where I bought the bottle and poison control could not find any MSDS forms either.

At the Emergency room the doctor called poison control immediately per their instructions. In the ambulance the childs mouth swelled up and at my home he was throwing up and coughing. Thankfully he is ok now after being observed for six hours at the emergency room. However, we still don't know what was in the product to cause the reaction. Because this little boy vomitted, it was diagnosed as an accidental poisoning. I am very cautious with my decorations, but this has caused both families much pain, anger, and fright. Please let the store and the manufacturer know that we have hired a lawyer, and that listing the ingredients along with the number for poison control, would have saved this baby a lot of unnecessary pain.

Thank you!
justification: The child experienced vomiting, swelling, and required emergency room observation, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident was accidental but highlights a clear hazard with unlabeled products (likelihood 3).

incident_description: Bought a Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm from First Alert with voice.  The alarm goes through its test alarm several times per week, often in the middle of the night.  It is very loud and wakes everyone up.
justification: The alarm's frequent false alarms disrupt sleep but do not cause injury or death.

incident_description:
I bought four Kidde smoke alarms model PI2010 and integrated carbon monoxide/smoke alarm.  They arrived October 22, 2011 from Amazon.com.  Two of the units are defective. Neither unit will respond to pushing the test button. This is a 50 percent failure rate and Kidde does not adequately support their customers.

On one unit, the test button will not release on its own; I have to bang the unit in the palm of my hand to get the test button to release.  Even though I do this, the unit will not respond as documented in the manufacturer's documentation.  There is no help for this problem on the manufacturer's website.

On the other unit, there is a loose piece of plastic rattling in the inside.  It looks to be a piece of molded plastic which might be part of the linkage from the button to a switch inside the unit.  I have not disassembled it.  This alarm will also not respond to the test button.

I removed my previous smoke alarm system and I am replacing it with Kidde alarms.  Unfortunately, Kidde's telephone support requires their customers to wait through a 30 minute hold time and when presented with the information about their defective product product, the agent agreed to ship replacement units to me which would arrive in 7 to 10 days.  I told the agent that they needed arrive within two days or I would return them to the retailer and would report this incident to the CSPC.

I requested to talk to a manager but was unable to do so.

In my opinion, Kidde falls well below the standard required of a company that manufacturers and distributes safety products.
justification: The incident involves defective smoke alarms that fail to function as intended, posing a potential safety risk but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
On October 14, 2011 at approximately 11:00 a.m. at a seasonal pumpkin patch lot on the corner of Peyton Dr and Grand Ave in Chino Hills, Ca 91709, an electric air mover was plugged in to fill an inflatable jumper. At approximately 1:00 p.m. a fire was discovered in or near the electric air mover, inflatable jumper and a blue tarp. The fire was extinguished with a nearby fire extinguisher.

Damage was to the electric air mover, inflatable jumper and blue tarp. No injuries were reported and no one was in the jumper at the time of the incident.

Notes: 
Both the electric air mover and jumper were new and used only a few hours the day before.

The only remaining portion of the electric air mover was the metal blower and a section of the cord.

A blue tarp is used at night after closing to cover the jumper and electric air mover to prevent dew from accumulating on the equipment.

Eye witness accounts state it appeared the blower had tipped and was covered by the blue tarp when the fire was discovered.

Equipment information:
Advance Air Movers
www.advanceairmovers.com
Mode: AA-1 N.W. 30 lbs G.W. 33 lbs MEAS: 18"x 13.5" x18" Made in P.R.O.C.
justification: The fire caused damage to equipment but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was drying my clothes in the Kenmore Elite Washer and Dryer Set and I heard a low "Boom" so immediately I opened the Dryer and Fire was blowing out of the inside of the Dryer and so I proceeded to unplug the Dryer.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dryer, which is a significant hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Electric Dryer. Model 110.66722690. Unit was not heating properly. Removed rear panel and inspected. Thermostat was faulty and one wire to it was melted so severely, it was disconnected. Evidence of melting insulation on the wire was noticed up to 3 inches from the terminal on the thermostat. No injuries.
