incident_description: I bought this Lysol floor steam cleaner back in 2008 or 2009. Just used it again after putting it aside for a while and it just exploded while I was cleaning. The hot water and chemicals sprayed everywhere including on myself. I had no idea that there was a recall on this item since I never registered it when I bought it. I have several little pieces that I gathered...springs....broken off plastic...the entire top water compartment blew off. I would like my money back and would like to know what I have to do.
justification: The incident involved hot water and chemicals spraying on the person, indicating potential injury.

incident_description:
Hello,

I have owned a Bosch model 4410L compound miter saw for about four years in addition to other woodworking tools manufactured by Bosch.

I found what I believe is a safety flaw in the miter saw.

I performed my first bevel operation and ran the blade into the sliding fence destroying both.

I have been making miter cuts for years without sliding the fences out without incident thereby I never gave it a thought to pull these sliders out for the bevel cut.

The shrapnel is what I feel might cause an injury to some one else that owns this or similar product.

The shrapnel hit the steel garage door denting it and ricocheted and hit the back garage wall where the large piece of the fence came to rest.

There was an awful amount of energy needing to be dispersed by this shrapnel and if an individual were in the path of this shrapnel a severe if not fatal injury would have occurred - my opinion.

Additionally, I feel that the safety labeling could be improved to help "idiot proof" this function and would like to share my opinion as an end user.

One of which shows what I believe would be a perfect place for a "fence" warning that could be integral to this existing mechanically fastened protractor scale - no adhesive to fail.

Every time that the bevel function is utilized one has to affix their view on this protractor to gauge the angle that is trying to be acquired thereby viewing the included fence warning.

I shared these photos and my experience with other engineers in my department and they concur that at the very least the labeling must be improved.

The safety labeling on my unit has a defect with the adhesive - that is failing also.

I have photos to share which are attached showing the damage that occurred including the failing adhesive on the labeling but this form does not offer any method that I can see to do so.

No injury has occurred just damage to the unit and my garage door.

I have worked in mechanical engineering my whole career and have been involved with safety labeling projects for dangerous equipment.

It is/was my fault but engineering must do their best to "idiot proof" (yes, I'm the idiot) their products and safety label as best they can.

I am not seeking compensation but it is my duty to inform others of a potentially dangerous condition.

Best Regards.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused damage to the equipment and property but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the potential for similar incidents if safety labeling is not improved.

incident_description: We purchased a Bissell Model 92l3-W vacuum cleaner and whenever you use the hose attachment the vacuum falls over.  I was not overextending any of the times and it has hit me in the head, the arm 2 times and this final time fell on my dog who was asleep on the couch.  I contacted Bissell and they maintained I had to be overextending the hose but it is so tight it is impossible to extend at all.  The first time I was sitting on the floor doing the case boards and it was less than 1 foot away from me and as I bent my body over it fell on top of me and hit me in the head and hurt very badly.  It is like if you turn or make any movement with the hose extended the top is so top heavy and the bottom of the vacuum so light it will fall over.  The last time I was right by my dog who was on the couch and I has using the house attachments to clean beside the couch and it fell on top of him.  He was shaken up all night long and went to the vet the next day.  No obvious injury but now one dog who completely freaks when he sees a vacuum.  I will never use this vacuum again and Bissell refused to do anything about it so I guess we are looking for another vacuum.  My hope is that this piece of junk gets taken off the market before someone, human or pet, gets seriously injured.
justification: The vacuum caused injuries to a person and distress to a pet, requiring a vet visit, but no death or serious injury occurred.

incident_description: Small fire occurred.
justification: A small fire is an incident with no reported injuries, warranting a severity level of 2. Fires, even small ones, are possible in various environments, hence a likelihood of 3.

incident_description: Shark steam mop, exploded with loud pop and bursts of steam from sides of water tank.
justification: The steam mop exploded with loud pop and bursts of steam, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Son's "plug and Play" charger for his xbox video game overheated.  It got so hot that it melted a hole through the charger.  I've called Microsoft several times regarding the issue, but each time they just tell me that they will have someone call.  My son received a minor burn when unplugging this, but if we hadn't noticed it I believe it could have started a house fire.
justification: The charger overheated and caused a minor burn, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Maytag Front Loading washing machine in 2007, and have continuously experienced a mildewy smell which comes from mold which grows around the door opening of the washer. Eventhough I continue to clean it with bleach, it has become worse as time has passed.  If you lift a large round gasket which lines the door of the washer which is open on one of its sides, you find moisture and mold consistently, whether you clean it once a week or once a month.  I called Maytag and was told that I had to purchase something to help with the smell, call a repair person to try replacing the gasket (which is still the same design), or check with problems with the drainage.  I have owned 4 sets of Maytags and have never had "drainage" problems which cause the smell.   I also have never had mold growing in any of my washers.  From going online I have learned that this is a consistent problem with most frontloaders.  I cannot have mold growing in my home as my daughter suffers from NTM (non-tuberculosis microbacterium), which is a chronic lung disease that was diagnosed in November of 2009.  I explained this to Maytag and was told they are not aware of this mold problem in their front loaders, which is definitely a false claim, since there are pages and pages of articles online from magazine, consumer pages, etc., which detail the length to which some consumers have had to deal with the problem.  Refused to assist in any way.
justification: The incident involves persistent mold growth in a washing machine, posing a potential health risk, especially to individuals with chronic lung conditions, but no direct injury is reported.

incident_description: Fire department responded to a call of smoke in a home.  Homeowner said that her hard-wired smoke detector had started to smoke when she replaced the battery in it.  Removed the detecotr from the wall and upon opening it found that a power resistor inside the unit was burnt, and the area around it on the circuit board was blackened.
justification: The incident involved smoke from a smoke detector but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but do occur occasionally.

incident_description:
The consumer's husband works in the basement and sometimes uses an electric heater.  Their basement developed an odor and they believe that it started around 3/8/2010.  The consumer had the installer check her furnace and hot water heater, but they did not find anything.

The consumer noticed a burning odor in her home and a dead-mouse like odor around September 2010.


(9/16/11)  The consumer had an electrician come out to her home and he checked the breakers in the home.  The consumer electrician was familiar with this problem and he was able to identify that the circuit breakers were the problem.  The electrician removed 4 of the breakers, but he plans to come back out on 9/19/11, to replace all of their breakers.  The electrician said that the consumers could have had a house fire.  The corners of the breakers were burned, but damage was limited to the breakers.

The consumer also check www.saferproducts.gov and she said that someone reported a similar problem on 4/27/2011, with this same exact mfr's breakers.
justification: The incident involved burned breakers and a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire, injury, or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to report that her washing machine produces a high level of mold and mildew under her washing machine. The consumer feels that this is the byproduct of a design flaw. The consumer stated that the gasket inside of the machine is about 5 inches wide and it causes a pocket water that causes mold and mildew to accumulate. The consumer has done some independent research and found that this is a persistent problem with this model. The consumer stated that the washing machine does emit a smell. The consumer has had this problem soon after buying the machine in 2007. 

The consumer called the firm a month ago and was directed to the executive assistant. She spoke to her 2 weeks ago and her response was that the consumer had fabricated the complaint and she had not taken proper care of the product. The firm stated that they have never heard of this issue. The consumer stated that the issue has caused an odor to her clothes. The consumer stated that no one has gotten sick as a result of this issue. The product is a front loaded washer. The consumer has yet to contact the seller of the product. The product shows no physical damage to the product and has not damaged her home. The consumer has not consulted an indoor air quality specialist.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw causing mold and mildew, but no injury or sickness has been reported.

incident_description:
My 17 month old pulled on interior wooden grille of Andersen sliding door.  The grille is designed to pop out, but grille stayed in and arm of grille splintered in baby's hand.  Fortunately he was not injured.

We have contacted Andersen and opened a file to report this incident.  They said that they do not know of any reports of this happening and offered to replace the broken product (although the first broke).  

The doors were purchased with the grilles as a unit, we should have been advised that the grilles could be pulled out by a child.  There are similar models with permanent grilles, but we were not made aware of this.
justification: The incident involved a child pulling on a grille that splintered but caused no injury, fitting the 'Incident, No Injury' severity level. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 'unlikely' since the manufacturer reported no prior incidents of this nature.

incident_description: My Shark steam mop exploded while using and burned my foot.
justification: The steam mop exploded and caused a burn injury to the foot, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I have owned a Euro Pro Light and Easy steam mop by Shark for a little over a year. Recently, it stopped emitting hot steam through the cleaning pad and just slowly dripped cool water. A few minutes after plugging it in today, the water tank exploded with hot steam bursting out of the seams. While I was lightly burned by the steam, I was not injured.
justification: The user was lightly burned by the steam, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident involved a malfunction leading to an explosion, which is unlikely but possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
My neighbor was using Scented Fabric Softener sheets and since their dryer exhaust is next to my front door, which was open at the time, the fumes entered and permeated throughout my home.  I had difficulty breathing, my eyes turned very red and were burning.  Subsequently, I awoke in the middle of the night with severe Vertigo.  Upon arising in the morning, I had to hold on to the walls to walk as I was dizzy, nauseous and very sleepy (I always wake up full of energy and bounce out of bed so this was very unusual for me).  Unfortunately I was supposed to have surgery that day and the doctor had to cancel due to my reaction.  I made an emergency visit to my Internist, and took an allergy pill (Allegra) and within an hour and a half of taking the pill, I was fine.

I then Googled the "dryer sheets and dizziness" and was shocked to see the extreme toxicity of these products.  I had the symptoms they listed as well.

It is appalling that this product has been approved.  Whenever I walk in my neighborhood, I have to hold a tissue up to my nose because there are so many exhausts spewing out this poison into the air as I pass by.  I'm sure I'm not the only one reacting like this.  People who have a general feeling of malaise (not as bad as mine) may just have no clue as to why they are not feeling well.
justification: The incident caused significant health issues including difficulty breathing, vertigo, and dizziness, requiring medical attention and cancellation of surgery, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Really this is two reports in one. I bought two Honeywell Oil Filled electric Heaters model HZ-709-WM from WalMart in 2009. I gave one to my mother and kept one. The one I kept smoked and the venthole in front melted so I quit using it. My mother reported hers smoked with electrical smell and became afraid to use it. I contacted Honeywell and they are planning to replace them with them with identical units. I think I would rather have the $72.73 each I paid for them, but that was not offered.
justification: The heaters smoked and melted, posing a potential hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Ryobi brand Random orbit sander Model RS290, Serial Number AJ1116 42086

I purchased this tool from Home Depot on August 1, 2011.  I used tool for the first time today (October 20, 2011) to sand the glossy surface off of walls in preparation to repaint.  After using the tool for between 30 and 45 minutes, tool began smelling hot.  I turned off the switch and smoke began coming out of the vent holes closest to the power switch.  I immediately unplugged the power cord.  The handle below the switch was very hot to the touch and smoke continued to come out of the vent holes for several more minutes.  I am afraid to try to use tool again for fear of it starting a fire.
justification: The tool emitted smoke and became very hot, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I needed to replace 35 light switches made by the Leviton company from my sister's home due to electrical arcing concerns.  These switches were installed as original equipment in her home when it was built new in late 1997.  The switches all have a crack along the back plastic portion of the assembly.  The crack is the exact same shape and size on each switch, which suggests to me some sort of mold or cast error.  The switch assembly is warped and bowed at the area of this crack.  These switches were also installed in other homes throughout the subdivision.  There have been at least 3 fires in this subdivision within the past few years.  One home suffered minor damage.  Another, next door to this home, suffered moderate damage and was repaired.  Another home was fully engulfed.  Speaking to insurance adjusters who visited the area, the suspected cause of the fires were defective switches.  I have saved one of these switches for your review should you wish to examine it.  The information on the switch is as follows:

Liviton Made in USA
15 A 120 VAC Only
CU and CU Clad wire only
110M 057
218/632-1451
9H17E
UPC 0 78477 15143 3
justification: The incident involves defective switches leading to fires, with one home fully engulfed, indicating significant property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I had a Marineland Visi-Therm 150 watt aquarium heater explode and catch fire.  I heard what sounded like a muffled fire cracker followed by rushing water.  When I ran into my living room I found water leaking out from below my aquarium.  When I opened the cabinet doors I saw the heater had exploded and cracked the compartment of my sump filter where it was located.  As the water rushed out and the heater was exposed to the air it ignited into a brief fire that self extinguished.  Overall I lost about 8 gallons of water onto the floor before I had a chance to shut everything down.  The water seeped through the floor and soaked some insulation, ceiling panels, carpet and drywall.  Had I not been home or if the heater was placed directly in the tank things could have been a lot worse.  I have a second Visi-Therm 100w that I have stopped using.  These are a dangerous product.  Marineland had a recall of a similar heater this year but not for this model.  It took 3 days of trying before I was able to reach someone at the customer service department to notify them of this incident.  I was told in order to file a claim I would need a letter on company letterhead from every vendor I purchased my items from stating replacement value.  Needless to say that will be impossible to get as most of these items were purchased online.  I am sending them the remains of the heater along with pictures and documention to support the replacement costs of the items damaged.  I fully intend to contact my Attorney General's office if they do not honor my claim.
justification: The incident involved an exploding aquarium heater causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported but are not extremely common.

incident_description: Purchased new Honeywell portable power generator model HW2000i in September of 2010, and upon first use in October of 2011 the plastic fuel filter came apart and created a fuel leak inside the generators housing. The generator was only run for a total of one and a half hours before this happened. I was in close proximity to the generator and smelled the strong odor of fuel and quickly shut it down preventing a possible fire and eventually an explosion when the plastic fuel tank melted and added another 1 and 1/2 gallons of fuel to that which was leaking.
justification: The incident involved a fuel leak that could have led to a fire or explosion, but no injury or death occurred as the situation was quickly controlled.

incident_description: Sunbeam Quartz Heater Model SQH310 Purchased 1 year ago at WalMart in Cleveland Ohio. Heater smelled burnt , kicked circuit breaker off and quit working. I opened the back and found 2 burned wires that had melted and burned in half. The cord was fine the internal wires were smaller gauge than the heater cord. Could have started a fire but I had it hooked up to a ground fault circuit that tripped.
justification: The heater malfunctioned with burnt wires but no injury or fire occurred due to the ground fault circuit.

incident_description:
The Maytag Washing Machine that my Mother and Father owns has an issue with the paint.
The paint began peeling and blistering within two years of purchase.
The paint is peeling and blistering inside the lid cover and on the edge of the drum
Top cover which is internal to the process of the washer.
The pieces of paint are a skin irritant and in addition will damage certain fabrics
If not removed prior to drying.
When the clothing is worn that contains particle of paint it will cause your skin to itch.
justification: The peeling paint causes skin irritation and can damage fabrics, indicating an injury risk.

incident_description:
I am disappointed with both the engineering and customer support received in response to an issue concerning my Bosch Nexxt Washer. My prior experience with Bosch has been with automotive products where they have consistently performed at a high level. Unfortunately that expectation of the same quality is present in your Home Appliance line has not been met.
When I reported black mold forming on the washer door seal your customer service department stated I should "wipe down and dry the rubber seal" after each use. For a product that operates in a wet environment this does not feel like a reasonable request. I even escalated in an executive response area, and person confirmed the washer needs to be wiped dry after each use. I expect adequate drainage and drying capability to address the moisture in a washer. I think the product, as designed, is not functional and also creates a health hazard.
Doing some research (googled "Bosch washer mold") I found this to be a common complaint about your front load washer products. I am surprised no action has been taken to correct this defect as it poses a health risk to consumers in my opinion. In addition to eliminating any Bosch Home Appliances from future consideration you are also damaging the Bosch brand with shoddy products and poor customer service.
I am your target customer and so are my friends. By not acknowledging and addressing this issue you are destroying Bosch's "high quality technology" reputation and alienating customers.
justification: The incident describes a product defect and poor customer service, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: I have a cerona Heat & Glo Gas fireplace Ser# 0021184384. The unit is a brand new house that was built in 2009. This unit has never been run. The first time I tried to run it the unit lit then the flames lifted off the burner filling the gas fire place with natural gas then it relit again with a large woof as the bottled up gas ignited then proceeded to do the same thing again. I shut the gas off and called a tech. He says that the unit has a bad gas valve. I e-mailed heat and glo to address my concerns and they told me the unit is out of warranty. OK fine but my issues is if this would have continued this cycle it could fill the fireplace up and cause a huge fire or an explosion.  Someone needs to look into this as I feel this is a very dangerous issue and could even blow the front glass all over people sitting in the living room.   [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas fireplace that could have led to a fire or explosion, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I bought a Briggs & Stratton Portable 4000 watt Generator Model # 030319 Serial number 
# 101363666  in 2006, and started it up about every 3 months to do whatever maintenance was required, and to make sure it worked properly in case of an emergency situation.
    In October 6, 2011 when I started the Generator, I noticed it was leaking gasoline from the plastic (4) gallon gasoline tank, I turned it off and discovered the gasoline tank had a crack at one of the (4) holes where it bolted to the generator frame. I drained the gas tank and removed it from the frame and discovered the mounting holes of the gasoline tank did not line up with the holes on the Generator frame.  It appears that  the people at the factory forced the bolt through the gas tank into the frame and thus withing (4 + ) years caused a stress crack in the Gasoline tank  at the bolt location that would not align. 
    The Generator has a total of approximately (5) hours run time since I purchased it.
I called Briggs & Stratton and was told to take it to Harvester Small Engine Repair which I did on October 10, 2011.  The location of the repair shop is  1430 Jungs Station Road  Saint Charles, Missouri Telephone Number 636-441-6116.
The manager: [REDACTED] called me on Monday October 17 and told me he talked to their Briggs * Stratton  area Representative and was told, without him even looking at the problem they would not pay to have this safety problem repaired. 
   I believe this to be a very serious Safety Problem. If I had just started the Generator and walked off and let it run without seeing the leak it could have been a disaster, with possible loss of life and or property.
   I have pictures of the alignment problem if needed
   The repair cost to have this repaired will be between $150-$200
justification: The incident involved a gasoline leak due to a cracked tank, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My wife and I smelled a "hot" smell. I discovered my Fisher&Paykel clothes dryer heating coils were powered on when the main power switch and panel was switched "off". The only way to stop the coils from heating, is to unplug the dryer. I was a safety engineer for McDonnell Douglas, and analyzed electrical circuits on the [REDACTED] for "fault" analysis. Any design that allows power to heater coils with the control circuit switched off, is unacceptable. Given the catastrophic possibilities of hot coils, no air flow, combustible clothes, and a false indication to the consumer that the system is powered off is design incompetence. 

I called the company to report the failure and asked to see a schematic of the electrical design, to see where the failure was and analyze it from a system safety viewpoint. I told customer support that I was an engineer and would like to see the "technical" design of the system. I was transferred to technical support, who admitted they knew of this failure, but I was not privy to the technical information as a consumer. He also said I presented myself as a "technician", when I wasn't. He did not think the matter was a safety matter and said I just needed a technician to come and change the control module that contains relays that probably failed. He did not agree with my position, and it was obvious that trying to go through Fisher&Paykel to fix a design flaw, wasn't going to happen. If bothers me that they knew of this failure, and did nothing to notify me of the possibilities.

In my mind, this design is a safety hazard, and the company should recall and re-design the control circuit preventing power to the coils with the system showing power "off". 

Please contact me and let me know this report has been read at least. I would like to know who makes the decision and the administrative level it gets made at.

Thank you for making our homes safer for all consumers...

[REDACTED] 
[REDACTED] 
[REDACTED] 
Military Instructor Pilot, Major, USAFR retired
Retired Northwest/Delta Airlines Pilot
justification: The incident involves a potential safety hazard with the dryer's heating coils remaining powered on when the unit is switched off, posing a fire risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Plugged in the Sharp Steam Pocket Mop Model S 3501 and was waiting for the mop to heat up prior to use. After waiting the minimal 30 second period to heat up and noticing steam was not being generated yet, allowed the unit to continue to heat. The time sequence was less than 3minutes when the unit suddenly popped and expelled hot steam from both sides of the water tank. Apparently there is no auto shut off trip mechanism if the unit overheats or builds up too much steam pressure. 

Fortunately there were no injuries but the potential for serious burns was present. 
This is the second unit I have owned and they have a tendency to periodically clog up but in the past the unit basically self cleaned itself and steam would flow normally into the steam mop head. This did not occur on 10/15 and as noted, the water tank unit exploded, expelled hot steam from both sides and is no longer functional.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning steam mop that expelled hot steam but resulted in no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the user mentioned this is the second unit with similar issues and a tendency to clog periodically.

incident_description:
had to use Kidde ABC fire extinguisher (Kidde Home 110) on an electrical oven element fire.
the dry powder did not stop the fire.

I breathed in a great deal of the "non-toxic," dry chemical (Monoammonium Phosphate).

I have Asthma.

The breathing of the dry powder exacerbated a completely controlled, for 10 yrs asthma,
 into a crisis Asthma. It is the 3rd day out & I am still having problems.

Although the chemical is "non-toxic" for most people, it is toxic and can cause severe, even death situations for people with Asthma.

Had I know this I would have not used it.

Nowhere on the label or in the instructions does it indicate people with repository problems should avoid breathing this product.

Because of this, I have to use many asthma medicines, as well as oxygen, just to breathe. Breathing with this chemical in the lungs is not easy.  It caused my lungs to fill with fluid along with shortness of breath and other asthmatic symptoms.

I feel the label on the product as well as on the box and in the instructions should indicate that it will be harmful if breathed by people with Asthma.

That would have saved me from going through what I am now suffering.

Also, I called Kidde to ask for instructions on how to best clean the powder. The answer I got was unsatisfactory. I was told the product is "non-toxic" and "it sounds like you have health issues not related to the product."  and goodbye.

I have HEPA filters going, trying to pull it out of the air. It is so fine that it gets airborne easily. It is on everything: the burnt stove, the floor, table, chairs, walls, papers, even got into silverware drawers and cabinets that were closed.  I need help to clean this so I do not get sicker.

I would have like and expected Kidde to work with me to get an answer to the problem, instead of telling me I have a health issue and goodbye.
justification: The incident resulted in severe asthma exacerbation requiring medical intervention, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific conditions of asthma and exposure to the chemical.

incident_description: I have a may tag washer that is causing smoke when washing cloths.  It happens this year in January and I call Maytag, so they sent someone to repaired it.  Now this is happening again so I call Maytag again they said as long as it is not causing fire, they will not take care.  The agent from Maytag said they can send someone to repaire it, but I have to pay for all the cost.  For the past 10 months after it happens first time I have to be alert when I wash my cloth.  If I fix it this time and it is going to cause smoke again.  If I am not home or in sleep, this could kill my entire family.
justification: The washer is causing smoke, which is a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: I have a Rowenta clothing iron.  The Model is the Professional Luxe, DM860.  When I plugged it in, the electric cord, nearest to the iron and inside of the tubing that encloses that area, started sparking, smoking and burning.  I unplugged it immediately.  The iron has not been dropped or damaged and has been working fine up to this incident.
justification: The incident involved sparking, smoking, and burning of the iron's cord, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: April 12, 2010, in Madison County, Illinois, [redacted], age 56, died and his son, [redacted], age 24, was injured while sleeping in a camper from carbon monoxide from a Coleman PowerMate 5045 propane heater.
justification: One death and one injury occurred due to carbon monoxide poisoning from a propane heater, indicating a high severity but relatively rare occurrence.

incident_description:
June 21, 2009, in Cache County, Utah, [redacted], age 28, and [redacted],  age 10, died in a tent while using a
Coleman Powermate 5017 propane heater.
justification: Two deaths occurred due to the use of a propane heater in a tent, indicating the highest severity level.

incident_description:
We had a faulty testing panel, no voltage output. So one of our electrician open up the panel and tested the voltage at the input of the panel, no voltage. He was to try to go by hand checking the connections. I told him not doing so and asked him if he is sure is tester is good. He told me yes, he worked with it all day long. I told him to try with another tester, just to make sure. So he did, and there was 600V at theis point. His tester was faulty. 

The capacity at this point is a 600V / 1200A feeder. If he has touch this with his tools, this would have been desastrous.

I called Greenlee, and they told me they have a recall on this model number for this same problem, but the serial number of our machine is not part of the recall. 

So the only recommendation they gave me is to report this incident to cpsc.gov.
justification: The incident involved a faulty tester that could have led to a severe electrical accident, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer indicated that he had the dehumidifier plugged into the wall outlet on a low setting in a basement for estimating twelve hours when approximately  1 a.m. on 9/12/2011 the fire alarm went off alerting the consumer there was a fire in the home. 

After waking his wife he noticed that smoke was pouring from the basement door. He powered on the light to the basement and went down stairs where he noticed that thick black smoke was billowing from the from the front of the dehumidifier.

The consumer unplugged the plug from the wall outlet and while doing so it tripped the breaker. He noticed a orange glow so he grabbed the 
Dehumidifier by the handle and bean to take it outside .

While in going through the kitchen area to go outside the flame inside of the dehumidifier  and blew out approximately 5 feet high in the area. The consumer quickly grabbed a bowl of water from the kitchen sink and put the fire out. No proper authorities were contacted. 

The dehumidifier is placed outside of the home near the garage. While doing some research online he noticed there was a recall (see Release #11-088) and his model number was affected. The consumer went into the retailer on 9/11/2011 and the representative that he spoke with (name was not provided) advised the consumer to contact the firm for further assistance.

The representative then decided that he would honor a refund for the consumer. The consumer advised the representative that he did not want to accept the refund and instead took the dehumidifier back home.

The basement is full of smoke damage and has a strong plastic burning odor. The consumer indicated that he would contact the firm and that he may also contact his home owners insurance.
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant smoke damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
This is to report a problem with the Kidde 1275 Smoke/Fire Alarm.

For 2 days, there was a smell of electrical smouldering in my home.  We thoroughly inspected the house and could not find the source.  After 2 days, my smoke alarm sounded and even though there was no fire or smoke condition, the smoke detector would not silence the alarm beep.  I removed the Kidde 1275 and took it apart and to my surprise, there was black char inside the smoke detector.  Since removing the smoke detector, I never smelled the electrical smouldering scent since.

There are simiar reports on the interenet.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning smoke detector with internal charring, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: I have a Whirlpool Duet Sport washing machine.  I;ve been following the care instructions (leaving the door open after every cycle, using the bleach only maintenance cycle/month) and still I have black mold growing on and around the gasket and the washer smells.  I contacted Whirlpool but they wouldn't replace the gasket b/c my washer was not under warranty anymore.  My son is allergic to mold.  THis machine is a health hazard.
justification: The presence of black mold poses a health hazard, especially given the son's allergy, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: I have a Samsung washer that I purchased an extended waranty on.  Among other things, a horrible, moldy smell was coming from the washing machine, even though I always leave the door and the soap door both open to prevent this.  I cannot find the source of the smell, but we have horrible allergies to mold.  We called in the extended warranty, and a technician came out.  He said it was normal.  He moved around the machine a bit to level it out because it was shaking really bad during the wash cycle.  He said there was nothing he could do about the smell.  He must have moved something around because now the mold smell is 10x worse.  It permeates through the entire 1st floor of the house.  We can't smell anything in the house but mold, no matter what we do.  Running bleach through the cycle helps only temporarily.  We can't live with this amount of mold, but the repair guy says our warranty doesn't cover mold.  Now, we're out of warranty, even though we were under warranty when we called him.
justification: The incident involves a persistent mold smell causing discomfort but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: The consumer opened the product and noticed right away that they were oily and had a really strong smell.  He washed them and then noticed a tingly numbing sensation around his hands and fingers.  After three cleanings and two degreasings the smell was still a problem.  He sent the product back to the retailer for a refund.  His wife experienced a headache while on the screen porch, and said that she had to go back into the house.
justification: The consumer experienced a tingly numbing sensation and his wife had a headache, indicating minor health effects from the product.

incident_description: Recently my husband & I were experiencing multiple electrical problems throughout our house. My husband heard electrical zapping coming from the circuit box. Upon checking the circuit box, we discovered electricity arcing several times a minute while we stood & watched. The circuit breaker had sustained burn damage & the red dividing clip had melted quite a bit. The breaker has been replaced & we haven't experience any more problems. The date code on our bad breaker is 0501. We experienced the same issues as the recently recalled 2010 breakers.
justification: Electrical arcing and damage to the circuit breaker were observed, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: I think it is extremely important that a nation wide warning or alert be issued regarding the replacement of older model smoke alarms that may tie into a sprinkler flow switch (on any home that is equipped with a sprinkler system).  Many of these types of alarms switched 120 VAC household current onto the interconnect wire.  Modern smoke alarms utilize a 9 volt transistor battery as a backup.  This is not a problem for new construction, but anyone contemplating a replacement of an older style smoke alarm should confirm the manufacturer type or model number.  One very popular smoke alarm (that is no longer being sold or manufactured) was the Firex 428C.  In fact this device was the unit of choice for anyone with a sprinkler system up to three (3) years ago.  If you were to replace this unit with a modern [REDACTED] smoke alarm (as an example), wired it up in accordance with the instructions, and the flow switch tripped you would destroy all the interconnected detectors in the home and may even cause a fire.  It may also be prudent to issue a warning about ensuring any alarms you do replace are compatible with each other and from the same manufacturer.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard due to incompatible smoke alarm replacements, which could lead to property damage but does not mention injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Electrical fire occurred in dryer wiring harness.
justification: Electrical fire in dryer wiring harness is an incident with no reported injury.

incident_description:
My samsung washer leaked a puddle of water and produced an electrical smell, then found out that my washer had been in a recall. called samsung and was transfered 3 times to different people then hung up on. customer service was horrible....

washer ruined my hardwood floor..
justification: The incident involved property damage (ruined hardwood floor) and poor customer service, but no injury or death.

incident_description: My Nostalgia Electrics CKM-100 Electric Cupcake Maker has only been used twice.  The first time, after being plugged in for only a few minutes, it produced a great deal of smoke and a toxic smell like burning plastic, only stronger.  The second time, some eight months later, after only being on for a few minutes (not even enough time to cook the muffins I was making fully) it basically burned itself to the point where it no longer functions.  The inside lid has melted, the plastic closure has melted, the exterior paint has melted, and the light indicators on the top of the machine have melted.  The appliance was so hot when I used it this second time that it nearly burned my fingers even through oven mitts, and it produced the same intense toxic smell and a great deal of smoke.  I have tried to contact both the company that made it (Nostalgia Electrics, LLC - http://nostalgiaelectrics.com/) and the company that sold it (Best Buy), and neither has offered me any relief.  After reading a number of similarly negative and scary reviews of this product on Amazon (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00472MMZI/ref=cm_cr_mts_prod_img), I believe this product demands an immediate recall, and that the manufacturer and/or seller should be required to issue refunds.  Particularly in light of my own experience with the machine, I fear that this product is a fire or a serious burn waiting to happen, and it is important to take it off the market before that occurs.  I would be happy to provide pictures of the device and/or its packaging if necessary.
justification: The appliance caused significant damage and nearly burned the user, indicating a high risk of injury or fire, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: This is not a single incident, so there's really not a date attached to it.  Relatives have purchased a Hoover "Windtunnel Anniversary Self-Propelled Bagged Upright Vacuum Cleaner", model #U6485900.  I have been around when it has been used.  Having previously owned a number of brands of vacuums, including very powerful, modern units (e.g. Dyson), and various Shop-Vac and similar industrial models, I am shocked at the noise level near this unit while it is running.  It does not sound like there is something wrong with it, so I would presume that this is the normal noise level for this product, not a faulty unit.  I will say from experience that the noise level is comparable to, for example, an electric angle grinder, which requires use of hearing protection apparatus.  There is absolutely no way that this is a safe noise level for anything more than momentary exposure.  Perhaps there needs to be more strict monitoring and regulation of noise levels from home appliances, including vacuums, blenders, and other potentially-offending devices.
justification: The vacuum's noise level is described as unsafe for prolonged exposure, comparable to an angle grinder, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
While using my Shark Steam Mop S3501 yesterday, it worked normally for about 1 minute.  Then it ceased producing steam through the mop head.  I pumped the handle in an attempt to get it back to normal.  The mop head was cool to the touch (not hot as is normal when the unit is on), but the unit was plugged in, the power light was on, and the water tank full.  I unplugged it and went to eject the mop head to troubleshoot, but when I pressed the eject button, the attachment explosively shot off and steam started blasting from the bottom of the unit.  My fingers got slight steam burns, but if a person or pet had been standing in front of me and the mop, they would have been seriously burned.

We were able to replicate this scenario, but the second time, the mop head flew off on its own after just a few seconds, without the release button being pressed, and steam again started shooting everywhere--about a 2 foot long jet of steam.  This mop is seriously hazardous and seem to have some design flaws.  Mine is 8 months old and has been used fewer than a dozen times.
justification: The incident caused slight steam burns to fingers and poses a serious burn risk to people or pets, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue was replicated, suggesting it is likely to occur again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: While standing on the step stool with storage from target the back portion of the lower step broke apart causing my bare foot to fall into the storage compartment cutting my ankle and causing me to fall to the ground.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the ankle and a fall, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a bottle of Pro-Tek cleaner from a door-to-door sales person after he demonstrated the cleaning capability of the product.  It was very expensive @ $89 a bottle.  The salesman said that it was a concentrated cleaner and was non-toxic.

I stored the cleaner in the undersink cabinet in my kitchen.  The bottle leaked and ruined my cabinet!  Upon discovering the leak, I pulled up the shelf liner and moved the cleansers out and found that about 1/4 of the bottle leaked out.  Because the sales person emphasized the non-toxicity of the product, I did not put on PPE such as gloves to clean up the mess.  Upon contact with the bottle, the product immediately began to burn my skin!  I pulled out some pH paper and tested the liquid, and its pH is approaching 14!  How is this purported to be non-toxic??

I called [REDACTED] at Pro-Tek customer service twice and reported the problem.  I asked her what could be done about my damaged sink and asked why there is no warning on the bottle about needing to use PPE when using this product.  [REDACTED] said that the product is non-toxic and she has used it for 13 years with no problem.  She said to pour the remaining product in a milk jug and send the old bottle back for replacement.  I told her that maybe her product is not compatible with the bottle that they sell it in.

I told her about the burning sensation on my skin and she said that diluted, the product is non-toxic.  I told her that the product that leaked out under my sink is not diluted, but concentrated, so the product as it exists in my house right not, has a very high pH.  She said that the product is non-acidic.  I said that I totally agree - the product is EXTREMELY BASIC, very caustic!

She said that she could send me a replacement bottle and that is all she can do for me.

This does not seem right!
justification: The product caused skin burns upon contact, indicating an injury, and the misleading non-toxic claim increases the likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: This product fabric softener is being used by many people in the belief that they are somehow making their clothes softer and more pleasurable smelling. When in reality they are exposing themselves and others to many chemicals that make those of us sensitive/allergic to it sick. I have suffered many symptoms from the exposure to this product, including, headches, nausea, asthma like symptoms of restricted breathing and chest congestion, inflamed sinuses. After many years of suffering with these symptoms have come to the conslusion with absolute certainty that these fabric softener products are the culprit.
justification: The description reports multiple health symptoms including headaches, nausea, and breathing issues, indicating injury (severity 3). The widespread use of the product suggests a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description:
To give a full detail of the acceptance and use ofthe wood burning stove -AVELON,
model: 1750 Spokane, I will attempt to explain what was entailed. The stove was installed by OrIey's installing crew and about three days later an inspector from OrIey's came and inspected the installation. At no time was there any instruction
as to how we were to clean out the stove when the chimney was brushed clear of soot that builds up. About a year later a rep from the local county South Central Oregon Economic Development District and a EPA inspector came out and looked at the stove and asked if we were happy with the stove. I told them that I was not because it did not draw air very good when first lighting the wood off. The inspector said to talk to Orley's about getting an extension on the flue above the roof. OrIey's said that was normal air draw and to keep the door ajar to let air in. Once the wood got started it burned fine with the door shut.
After I brushed the chimney this spring the stove would not draw air up the chimney and when paper was burned the smoke did not go up the chimney and instead came into the house. On checking inside the stove I could see that none ofthe soot had entered the stove and the
chimney was plugged above the draft pipes and brick on the top of the stove. I went to OrIey's and asked about the soot and how do you clean it out as there was not a door to enter to clean out the soot that came down the chimney after brushing. I was instructed on how to prepare the stove before brushing. The OrIey rep showed me how to remove the metal brackets and bricks from inside the top of the stove. This opened up the top inside so that soot could fall into the bottom ofthe stove. I would not have had a soot mess and no smoke in the house if I had known how to take the stove apart before brushing. Also, there are no instructions in the owners manual telling how to remove soot.
What makes this dangerous is that elderly folks would not be able to remove the metal brackets
and bricks before brushing and if they tried to burn wood they would have unhealthy smoke in
the house. The stove needs to be re-designed so it has a cleaning device on the side to enter the brick area where the soot fills up the air space. This devise could be a metal scraper that is controlled by a shaft that passes through the side of the stove and when the shaft is pulled out and pushed
back it would sweep the soot from the air space above the bricks. This would clear the air space and allow the draft to go up the chimney with out taking the stove apart.
When the stove is working right it is efficient and does eliminate smoke particles from the atmosphere.
justification: The incident describes smoke entering the house due to improper cleaning, posing a potential health hazard, especially for elderly individuals, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer said that he was upstairs two floor from the basement when he felt a strong burning odor.  Consumer rushed to the basement and found out that his dehumidifier was hot at touch.  Consumer was unable to turn off.  

Consumer unplugged the dehumidifier from the electric out.  Consumer did not had the product he disposal.

Consumer feels that his dehumidifier could pose a fire hazard, he also said if he wouldnÃÂt be at home it would caught on fire.

09/10/2011 Consumer e-mailed and explained incident to mfr.  He hasn't here from mfr yet.

No Injury.

Further clarification of incident: Sears Kenmore Dehumidifier Model # 580.54701, (this is the model number given in the User's Manual. The number provided in the Parts Manual is 580.54701400). Dehumidifier is a 70 pint capacity model that can be used in cool temperatures. I owned the unit for approximately 7 years, setting it to cycle on and off every 3 hours during the warmer months. It was located in the basement with a hose attached that drained into a sump pump. Humidity setting was usually at 40%. Quite suddenly one evening, I began to smell something burning. I was on the second floor. Eventually traced problem to the dehumidifier which was extremely hot to the touch and emitting a strong, acrid smell. Unit was clearly turned "On"; the switches were illuminated but it was not running. Perhaps dehumidifier was in between cycles. I noticed small amount of water, perhaps condensation, on the upper part of the front grill. I immediately unplugged unit and when it cooled, threw it away. Unfortunately, it didn't occur to me to save my dehumidifier for future examination. I believe I caught this incident at the very beginning. Had I gone to bed or left the premises I have no doubt a fire would have ensued. I notified Sears Customer Service weeks ago but have not heard from them.
justification: The incident involved a dehumidifier overheating and emitting a burning odor, but no injury occurred. The consumer acted promptly to unplug the device, preventing potential fire.

incident_description:
I purchased Olympic Premium interior, eggshell, latex paint at Lowe's. The batch number is 02v36486. P.P.G. says the paint was made in February 2011 and there should be an "M" at the end. The Material Safety Data Sheet, provided by Lowe's was prepared on November 7, 2000, (Product Code 72401). Has the paint's formula changed in 11 years?
I painted a bedroom on September 1. The next day the painted walls smelled stronger than when the paint was wet. I went online and found about 9 cases involving Olympic zero -VOC paint with the same problem. Some said the smell was still there a year later. So I complained to the store on September 5th. By this time, the odor was burning my nose and mouth.
On September 9th, Lowe's manager and Loss Prevention Officer came to photograph the room and collect the leftover paint for testing.
On September 13th, I moved out of the house, and received medical attention for acute sinusitis. Other people said the smell was very strong, like formaldehyde, but not burning. The problem was gone when I left the house.
I don't know what happened to my leftover paint. It was not tested. P.P.G. sent an e-mail saying that they tested "retains" from the same batch and other batches of paint. All of them came out pure and clean, all the chemicals are E.P.A. approved, and I am the only one with a problem. What's more, they said, the loss prevention people didn't smell anything at all.
Is it safe to shellac over the offending smell, or better to tear out the walls? Many other brands of zero-VOC paint have had this problem too. It doesn't happen with every can, what's going on?
justification: The incident resulted in acute sinusitis requiring medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as the issue appears isolated with no widespread reports.

incident_description:
on first time of use, the new humidifier set off fire alarm waking two adults from sleep. after silencing the alarm and looking for the source, discovered the humidifier had produced smokey-appearing particulate haze in the bedroom. the hazy material in the air caused a feeling of raspy throat and bitter taste in one adult and mild asthma reaction in another adult.

inspecting the humidifier after the incident, there was a brownish discoloration to the water collected in the ultrasonic base unit and demineralization cartridge and some foreign material on the outside of the unit.  the foreign material on the outside of the unit had been noticed when the unit was un-boxed.

this humidifier was filled with clear tap water prior to its operation on this occassion, as well as another model humidifer in a second bedroom which operated without incident.

previously, Vicks brand humidifers as well as other brands have been operated in this same bedroom location for several years without incident

Vicks Model V5100N (on unit) or V5100JUV (on box), 1.5 gal capacity
Mfg by Kaz, Inc
Purchased at Drug Mart, Independence, OH on October 2, 2011
justification: The incident caused a raspy throat, bitter taste, and mild asthma reaction, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue appears to be specific to this unit, making recurrence unlikely (likelihood 2).

The supervisor told the consumer that they were acquired by Whirlpool, but she did not specify when.  The consumer asked if she could get a discount on the purchase of another washer, but the supervisor said no. The supervisor offered to send a technician out at the consumer's expense, but the consumer declined that for fear of future problems with the washer.  Nothing else transpired.

Smoke alarm goes off randomly in the middle of the night.  This is our second unit.  It is a replacement unit because we had similar problems with the first unit.  This is only 7months old. And there should be design requirements for alarms that require they be maintenance free.

incident_description:
My Dimplex electric fireplace Model DF2608) caught on fire.  The electric fireplace was on and suddenly I heard several noises sounding like a "PFITT" emanating from the fireplace.  I looked at it and the faux flames where pulsing very bright with each PFITT and black smoke was flowing from the fireplace vents.  I was able to shut it off after several attempts with the remote control, then shut off the circuit breaker, pull out the plug and open the doors to let the smoke out and avoid smoke damage to my home.

I usually sleep with the fireplace on and wonder how bad the fire could have been had I been sleeping.  It is certainly not inconceivable that it could have been catastrophic, resulting in a major fire and serious injury or even death to myself and/or others.

I reported the incident to the manufacturer and was surprised when they expressed no concern whatsoever, advising me that the fireplace was no longer under warrantee and emailing me a service manual, so I could take the fireplace apart, determine which parts had caught on fire and order replacements.

Equally disconcerting is the fact that I have no way of knowing if replacing the burnt part(s) will fix the problem or if I am just setting the stage for another fire, where the end result might not be so fortunate.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke emission from the electric fireplace, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood of recurrence is high given the device's malfunction and lack of manufacturer support.

incident_description:
I own a Generac Guardian Whole House Stand-By Generator, model 43903, serial # 4319281. I purchased this genset new in the spring/summer of 2006 and had it installed by a Generac Dealer - Crandford Electric.

This genset has always cooked/overcharged batteries, causing me to have to buy a replacement about every year or so. The charging voltage was WAY too high - like 14 volts.

Roughly a year & a half ago, I was standing right beside the genset (just finished cutting the grass) at the time it is supposed to crank for its weekly exercise run. When it tried to crank - it didn't turn over or anything - the battery exploded!!! I cleaned it out, purchased a new battery and installed it and the genset cranked and ran normally. 

Now flash forward to the date referenced, the genset will not stay running. It cranks and runs for ~15 seconds, then cycles back off. Then cranks again, runs, then back off. etc. Eventually, it shuts down with an "OVERCRANK" led flashing. Apparently, the exploding battery sent shrapnel into the stator, and damaged the run windings, which provide run voltage indication to the control circuit board.

Despite a tremendous amount of evidence online that MANY other people are having/have had this same problem with Generacs, their initial reply to me was that they were unaware of any issues with their chargers. That is completely unsatisfactory in my opinion. Which is why I am contacting you folks.
justification: The incident involved a battery explosion but no injury was reported, placing it at severity level 2. The recurring issue with battery overcharging suggests a likelihood of 4 (likely) for future occurrences.

incident_description:
Friday afternoon, 9/23/11, around the time that our Generac Model 5243 emergency generator starts its weekly exercise cycle, I heard a very loud boom, like a cannon going off. 

I went outside to see what happened but couldn't locate the source of the sound. There was, however, a slight smell of sulphur or gunpowder in the air.

A while later, I noticed that the generator hadn't started. I went out to try a manual start but no joy. I assumed it must need a service call.

Sunday, for whatever reason, I decided to take a closer look at the generator enclosure. Upon removing the front cover panel, this is what I saw in the battery compartment. 

The battery was completely disintegrated. There were bits of plastic and pieces of filler caps all over. 

The top strap was basically just holding the side plates together. If you tried to lift, more pieces would fall off.

I've never seen a battery do this before. I'm glad it didn't happen when someone could have got hurt. 

There are many online complaints about battery explosions with this product. The manufacturer does not seem to be responsive to providing a fix.
justification: The battery explosion caused significant damage but no injuries, and similar incidents are reported online, indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description:
Last year, I purchased a new Little Giant ladder (Type 1A)  from Costco.  The product was demonstrated by a Little Giant employee who made it appear safe, simple and easy to use.

incident_description:
On June 16, 2011, my 6 year old daughter was seriously injured on our Larson Screen Door.  She was using the door properly.  She had gone out the screen door and as it shut behind her, it sliced across the back of her leg, just above the ankle.  This caused a serious laceration, slicing all the way through the skin and all the muscle, all the way to the achilles tendon.  The tendon was completely exposed and the tendon was also damaged as well.  Because of the severity of the injury and the damage to the tendon, her ankle had to be immobilized for four weeks.  The first two weeks were spend in a half cast and on crutches.  The next two weeks were spend in a medical boot.  The laceration resulted in eleven stitches and a 2 inch scar.  Although the scar does not sound big, my daughter is very small, and so the two inch scar literally runs from one side of her leg to the other. When the injury was viewed from the side, the slice through her leg ran about a quarter of the way through the leg.  The night of the incident, she was rushed to the emergency room and treated there.  For her follow-up care, she was treated by an orthopedic surgeon.  

The screen door has a protective rubber edging along the INSIDE bottom edge, to protect against the inside of the screen hitting the leg.  The OUTSIDE corner of the bottom metal edging has a sharp pointed corner.  This outside corner is what caught my daughter's leg as it swung closed.  This corner comes to a sharp point, there is no rubber edging and the corner is not rounded.  It cut through my daughter's leg like a knife.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious laceration requiring emergency treatment and follow-up care, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
This concerns a DOCUMENTATION ERROR leading to incorrect 120 VAC connections.

The product is TrippLite Model 1250ULHW, a Recreational Vehicle inverter/charger.

The Tripp-Lite OWNER'S MANUAL calls for the external AC input to be wired with LINE (Hot) to the BROWN internal wire; NEUTRAL (earth potential power lead, not grounded) to the BLUE internal lead, and the source electrical protective ground wire to the Green input lead.  Some engineer at Tripp-Lite must have been unfamiliar with non-US power wiring standards.

The Chinese who actually build the unit apparently never got the memo, [or, being Chinese, couldn't read it] and instead wired the internals of the unit according to INTERNATIONAL WIRE COLOUR STANDARDS.  BROWN is the earth potential power lead, BLUE is the Hot lead, and the electrical protective ground is GREEN/YELLOW STRIPE.  The use of BROWN and GREEN wire insulation is tightly defined.  "Hot" wires may be just about any color other than either of these two.

The consequence of transposing the input power leads is that the inverter will regularly trip any GFIC receptacle into which it is plugged.  It will not connect the input power to its LOAD OUTPUT on a pass-through basis.  If connected to a non-GFIC receptacle, the inverter will work but its output
leads effectively will be reversed, which results in putting the Hot connection onto an output wire which is supposed to be the ground potential power return.  This could increase the risk of shock if a double-insulated tool undergoes failure.  Reversing the supply connections eliminates repeated GFIC trips and results in the inverter operating as designed.  The stated date below is the date this was corrected on the unit installed in my RV.

This situation does not warrant a recall of product. There is nothing wrong with the product. However, it does warrant correction of the Owner's Manual and a good faith attempt on the part of Tripp-Lite to notify registered owners that the manual they received with their unit contains an error in the wiring instructions
justification: The documentation error could lead to incorrect wiring, increasing the risk of shock, but no actual incidents or injuries are reported.

incident_description:
This safety concern request is to expand and include all generators using the gasoline tanks that were involved in previous recalls 00-047 (December 30, 1999) and 00-067 (May 6, 2001) regardless of date of manufacture. Even though these recalls do not currently cover our generator, we have discovered that other owners as well as ourselves, have experienced the identical problem as noted in these recalls. Our research indicates cracks in these gasoline tanks seem to appear after about 100 to 150 hours of generator usage. Since this product is used mostly for backup emergency electrical power, it will depend on the userÃÂs number and duration of power failures, as to how soon these gasoline tank cracks will appear. Our generatorÃÂs tank cracks appeared at 108 hours of proper usage. In short, these tanks are very likely to fail due to a design flaw and the way they are attached to the generatorÃÂs frame. Therefore, at some point it appears that gasoline will leak onto the engine below. If this happens to occur during otherwise normal generator operation, a fire and/or explosion is the most likely result. Although we were lucky to have caught our tank problem while our generator was cool and not running, we find this an unacceptable situation. We feel the manufacture should replace, at no cost to us, the defective designed tank with a tank designed to not have this problem. incident_description:
I have an emergency generator which has never been used except to periodically start to verify that it will start if needed.  

With Hurricane Irene heading this way I decided to check out the generator.  The generator has always been kept in my garage.  I pushed it out of the garage to start it.  Since it did not start with first few pulls of the start cord I realized that the shut-off valve from the tank was probably closed.  I found the shut-off valve and when I just touched the valve, it fell into my hand leaving an open hole in the bottom of the tank.  Gasoline poured out over my hands.  I tilted the generator so the gas would stop flowing out of the tank.

I checked in my garage where the generator had been stored and there were stains on the floor indicating that there had been some leakage.

The tank opening is sealed by a rubber grommet pushed up into the opening in the bottom of the tank and then the end of the shut-off valve is pushed up into the rubber grommet.  This rubber grommet protrudes up in the bottom of the tank making it impossible to completely drain the tank.  There is no mechanical attachment of the shut-off valve to the bottom of the tank.  Gasoline causes the rubber grommet to deteriorate over time.  In my case the portion of the rubber sealing the opening was completely gone leaving nothing to seal the opening or to secure the shut-off valve to the bottom of the tank. 

If I had not decided to check the generator that day the shut-off valve would have eventually fallen out of the connection to the tank dumping all the gasoline in the tank on the floor in the garage where I have an open flame water heater.  Had this happened it could have resulted in an explosion and fire which could have destroyed my home and resulted in injury or death of my family.

The generator should have had a mechanical attachment of the shut-off valve to the tank, an attachment which would not deteriorate due to contact with gasoline.  

This is extremely serious safety defect since many of these generators are stored in garages and the owners are not aware of this design defect.

I think there should be a recall put out on these generators for the tank shut-off valve connection to the tank to be changed from the rubber grommet connection to a mechanical attachment to the shut-off valve that would not deteriorate with contact with gasoline.

I contact DeVibiliss, the manufacturer of the generator, and asked to speak to their technical department.  Instead they connected me to a local service representative here in Charleston.  The representative was aware of this problem but did not have the grommets in stock.  I order on the internet and installed it on 8-30-2011.  I intend to not put gas in the tank until the generator is needed.
justification: The incident involved gasoline leakage and a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I own a single family residence with an oil fired hydronic heating system.  In December 2008 my heating oil dealer (Fred Fuller Oil and Propane Company [Fred Fuller] of Hudson, NH) installed a new controller for my boiler.  The controller was a Honeywell R8182D 1079 Combination Protectorelay Primary Control and Aquastat Controller.  The previous controller, which was the same product and of unknown age, had failed.

The new controller worked without incident until September 8, 2011.  On that day I noticed an acrid smell near the boiler; and on further inspection, I saw smoke coming from the enclosure around the controller.  On opening the enclosure I saw a hole burning through the controller's circuit board.  It was about the size of a dime and growing.  Behind the hole there was a red spark or small flame.  I immediately shut off the electric power to the controller, which stopped the burning.

I called Fred Fuller to ask what had happened, explaining that I'd never modified or tampered with -- or really even touched -- the controller.  Their head of service said the controller was probably faulty; he'd seen similar failures in the past.  I then contacted Honeywell (via a form on Honeywell's customer support website) to ask the same question.  I have not yet received a response to my inquiry.

I'm filing this report because if I hadn't caught the burning when I did, a serious fire could have resulted.  The controller was quite close to the oil supply line for the boiler; and wires (with flammable plastic insulation) led from the controller to junctions and conduits in the wood framing of my house.  If, as Fred Fuller's head of service implied, the Honeywell R8182D 1079 regularly fails by catching fire, it should be taken off the market.
justification: The incident involved a burning controller that could have led to a serious fire, but no injury or death occurred. The service head indicated similar failures have happened before, suggesting a possible but not certain recurrence.

In this case all the smoke alarms were ionization. (The CPSC should not be surprised since CPSC estimates that 90% of all alarms are ionization.)   In this fire the occupants appear to have been awakened by the smoke alarms.  According to the one survivor, [REDACTED], he heard smoke alarms after being awoken by [REDACTED].  It appears that many if not all occupants acted in an altruistic and proper manner but did not have enough time to safely escape.  It is highly probable that they did not have enough time because the ionization smoke alarms did not operate in time to provide adequate warning from smoke build-up.  The 2 most important alarms were found in areas (living room and stairwell) which would indicate that they were properly located and should have provided adequate warning since there were not any closed door between the fire and the smoke alarms.  It is also highly likely that since photoelectric smoke alarms are sensitive to all kinds of smoke they would have gone off much earlier and probably several minutes before the smoke developed to the point that egress was impeded.  As a consequence, precious warning, which would have been provided by photoelectric alarms, did not exist. I am highly confident that if this house had photoelectric smoke alarms that these young people would not have died. 

Vermont, Massachusetts and the International Association of Fire Fighters have recently passed legislation/ resolutions that recognize the limitations of ion alarms to provide timely warning. Why doesn't the CPSC recognize this?

It is my understanding that there are multiple unresolved issues concerning ionization detectors' inability to detect smoke or sound an alarm. *In fact, it is my understanding that the CPSC expressed serious concerns regarding ionization detectors as early as 1995. These concerns mirror those put forward by [REDACTED], an outspoken advocate for removing ionization detectors from the marketplace. Yet, the CPSC still has not acted to remove the alarms from the market, nor has the CPSC warned consumers as to the potential drawbacks of ionized detectors. * The issues that appear to be the most prescient and that were addressed by [REDACTED] in his letter to you, still remain unsettled. I ask that you address, the questions in [REDACTED]'S letter in detail, and respond to the following concerns: 1. The National Institute for Standards and Technology (NIST) has found that, on average, a photoelectric detector is 30 minutes faster in detecting a smoldering fire than an ionized detector. The highest percentage of deaths caused by smoldering fires occurs while people are sleeping, when the operation of a smoke detector is critical. In fact, this percentage may be as high as 100 percent. Four years ago NIST reached the conclusion that ionization detectors sometimes fail to alarm in smoldering fires, even when visibility is significantly degraded by smoke. 2. While ionized detectors alarm sooner in "ultra-fast" flaming fires by an average of 50 seconds, those seconds appear to be negligible considering that most people are awake when flaming fires occur. In addition, in what appears to be the most common type of flaming fires (i.e. cooking fires) the photoelectric detector was providing more than enough time for an occupant to escape. 3. Several studies show that the ionization smoke detector is many times more likely to be disabled than photoelectric detectors. 4. The ionization smoke detector is being used by the vast majority of Americans. The ionization smoke alarms susceptibility to nuisance alarms (leading to disablement) and inadequate response to smoldering fires could be responsible for hundreds of needless deaths each year. Recently, due to the efforts of [REDACTED] of the Boston Fire Department to educate the authorities to these facts, the states of Massachusetts and Vermont have taken steps to restrict the use of ionization smoke detectors in residential occupancies. This odor is so strong and pungent (my opinion toxic since it made three people ill with diarrhea and headaches, and for all I know could either be carcinogenic or toxic to some organ in the human body.) that when I asked a Home Depot Store Associate to help me locate the item in the store, she commented she even hated to walk down the aisle because of the "odor" and she didn't think Home Depot should be selling them. i returned it and found another brand of shower heard. The hose also has this very acrid smell. It fill the whole room and is very nauseating to me.

incident_description: Our LiftMaster 2220 garage door opener was pulling the garage door open. When it got to about half-way open, it let go of the door and the door came crashing down. This is a screw-drive model and the part of the opener that connects the door to the screw rod is called the "rack". This piece is made of plastic and when it broke the door came crashing down. Such a critical piece that connects the door and is under a lot of pressure should not be made of plastic that can break so easily! If someone was trying to walk under the door when this happened they would have been seriously injured. I fear for my small children with this issue.

incident_description: We had a propane water heater replaced in our home.  Almost immediately after it was installed we began smelling propane coming from the unit.  We call the plumbing company that installed the unit and they came out, checked for leaks, made some adjustments and felt they had fixed the problem.  We continued to smell the propane.  Sometimes it was just very close to the control unit and other times we could smell it when we entered the garage.  We called the installer back out.  They did some more testing (spraying soapy water on the control unit and surrounding joints and piping)  never finding any visible leak. After several trips to our house they agreed to replace the unit with a new unit.  Once again we began noticing the propane smell in the garage.  We had our propane provider come out and inspect their equipment and they found nothing.  We called the fire department out and they did smell the propane, but were unable to pick up a reading on the meter they had.  They advised us to replace the unit as soon as possible.  The longer this goes on the less cooperative the installers become.  Our main concern is the faulty control unit.  We have had two units and both had the same problem from the same connection.
justification: Propane smell indicates a potential leak, posing a risk of fire or explosion, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

They told us not to use the iron until we replaced the cord.  Now 2 years later the cord is making sparks.  We called Rowenta again.  THey sais that they didn't have any other complaints about this.  I know there was at least one complaint because we complained 2 years ago.  The covering of the cord is getting worn where it is attached to the iron - in fact it has a small hole in it.
