incident_description:
Washer started banging (Internally) and moving violently.  Upon inspection it was observed that the frame that supports the spinning assembly had one of its 3 members completely severed, and the other 2 had suffered severe stress cracks. (The spinning assembly consists of the washer drum along with many gallons of water spinning at hunderds of revolutions per minute.)

Adjacent to the spinning assembly and unprotected is the 120volt wiring harness that rins the motor/pump assembly for the washer.  if the washer had continued to run this way it could have caused a flood, contact with 120 vols and water and the potential to start a fire in my opinion.

I have owned many washers including Maytags in the past.  This component is clearly underdesigned for this purpose.

Although I have a 10 year extended warranty, this part is not covered. If the perception of the Maytag corporation is that this part should not fail then clearly this leads me to believe that its design is flawed. 

Imagin if this had failed and flooded the basement and there was a toddler in close proximity...
justification: The incident involved a washer malfunction with potential for severe consequences, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Maytag washer (MAH2400AWW, Serial #14112672JX) from Home Depot on 2/16/2007.  It was delivered and installed on 2/24/2007.  On 2/14/2008, I had a technician from A&E Factory Service troubleshoot the washer under warranty because it was making a clicking noise and smelled like something was burning.   Upon diagnosing the problem, he discovered that the wireharness was burnt.  He had to order a replacment wireharness and motor since the female end of the wireharness also burnt the interfacing male end of the wireharness attached to the motor.  On 2/26/2008, the technician replaced the wireharness and motor. I saved the wireharness from this first incident.    

On 9/2/2011, a similar noise and smell began occurring and I immediately stopped using the washer.  Today, 9/5/2011, I investigated the problem and noticed that the wireharness burned in the same location as the original one that was replaced in 2/2008. Upon review of both wireharnesses, it appears that there is a inherent design flaw as the plastic body of the wireharness is melted/ burned in the same location from what appears to be a short-circuit, posing a fire hazard.  

Luckily, on both occasions, I was home at the time the washer began malfunctioning/ short-circuiting, and was able to stop the washer immediately.  I believe this wireharness design in use in this Maytag washer is a serious fire hazard for anyone that currently owns and uses this specific make and model washer.  I am appalled to see that this specific model is still being sold.   This make/ model washer should be immediately recalled by Maytag.
justification: The incident describes a recurring electrical fault causing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
On 8/28 my 50 gallon water heater stopped working.  I called Sears Home Service since I have a repair contract and the technician came on 8/30.  He attempted to install two new parts, one of which was a "Water Heater Control Source 387," part F-145-1293.   When he attempted to get it started, it leaked gas and there was a flashback that blew the flue pipe off the top of the water heater and stunned the technician momentarily.  He commented to me that this was the second such part recently with which he had had that experience.  Fortunately no fire started, but it seems to me that if these defective parts are being used by Sears in repairing Kenmore 50 gallon water heaters, then this is a potentially dangerous situation for many unsuspecting consumers.  I still have the defective part in my possession.

The part in question is apparently manufactured in Mexico for the White Rodgers Division of Emerson Electric Co. of St. Louis, MO.

As a result of this fiasco Sears has been unable to repair my water heater and I am still waiting for them to address the situation.
justification: The technician was stunned by the flashback, indicating an injury, and the incident involved a gas leak and flashback, which could recur with similar defective parts.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Washer and Dryer was purchased with the stacking option.  This product was purchased and installed by Sears.  The Dryer sits on top of the Washer.  While using both units, the Dryer came crashing down to the floor without any indication or notice.

We had three repair companies look at the unit.  They all said the there isn't anything holding the dryer secure on top of the washer.   We looked at a newer model being sold by Frigidaire which does have a bracket bolting the dryer to the washer.  This is the same for all other brands we looked at.  

This unit has two guides placed at the rear of the washer that the rear feet of the dryer sit.  This is open-faced and does not have any mechanism to keep the dryer from sliding forward and off.  The front end has a bracket that is screwed to the Dryer and then sits on the front top of the washer with some type of adhesive tape.   When we found the dryer on the ground, the bracket had a screw laying on the ground the the bracket was not in position any longer.  The adhesive tape did not have the ability to hold the dryer on the washer.

This is a very dangerous situation and without notice, a small child can be killed.   Any person could be hurt or worse if they were caught between the falling dryer and floor or wall.  It appears from the multiple discussions we've had that this stacking solution was not well thought out and designed with safety in mind, or ability to do it's intended roll.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation where a dryer fell due to inadequate securing, posing a risk of death or serious injury, especially to small children.

As soon as I got home with it my husband began to comment that something in the room was making him cough and had an odd smell.  It took us a little while to put together that the smell was coming from the rug.  We then set it outside in the sun to let it "air out" for a couple hours. We were thinking the people we had purchased it from just had an odd smell to their house the rug had picked up.  However this airing out did nothing for the smell and as people came over to see the nursery they also commented how the rug had an odd chemical smell.  At this point I got online to see how to get a wool rug not to smell, still not suspecting that it was this pottery barn rug specifically just wool rugs in general.  But after finding your site as well as many others with people sharing there stories of pottery barn rugs we have decided to just throw the rug in the garage rather than risk using/selling it to someone else.

incident_description:
EXTENSIVE FLOOD DAMAGE  caused by "Maytag Performa Oversized Capacity Plus Washer"
 Model # PAV3360AWW Purchased in June 2003.

Water overflow occurred due to a pressure sensor hose (approximately 3/8 " in diameter connected to the inner drum) disconnecting during a rinse cylce. Water continued to flow into the washer and overflowed from the 2nd floor to the first floor causing extensive celing and floor damage, within 30 minutes.

The male/female connection of this hose to the drum is extremely short and held in place with a flimsy "spring clamp". Vibration of a normal wash cylce can cause the hose to dislodge from the clamp. Without the pressure hose in place, the water flow will not shut off.

A Maytag Service Rep was called in to diagnose the failure and indicated that this is a common problem with the Maytag Performa. This machine had been serviced twice this year without any prior indication of a problem with the hose. The User's Guide does not make any reference to the hose or indicate any maintenance requirements for this hose. 

MY CEILING AND FLOORING HAS TO BE REPLACED DUE TO DAMAGE AND POSSIBLE MOLD CONTAMINATION.
COSTLY DAMAGE THAT COULD HAVEN BEEN PREVENTED WITH A BETTER QUALITY CLAMP.
justification: Extensive property damage occurred due to water overflow, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I am a member of the [REDACTED] of Boca Raton.  I am not alone in this complaint.  I am the one submitting it. It has taken me this long to get the 28 signatures needed to show you and the carpet company owner that this is a significant number of people complaining of this health problem. We know of at least 50 people unofficially but this is vacation time. The card room holds around 250 people.

The new carpeting was put down overnight by using glue to adhere to the floor. The next day we smelled strong odors of formaldehyde and something that has a distinctive type odor. Management had big fans and the doors open. This is the only room in the entire building that has ever had to experience this. We complained so Management had two companies test the room. They found it was normal. Yet, our complaints continued. These include; headache, red eyes, tearing eyes, running nose, sore throat, coughing, tightness in lungs, and nausea. Then management bought several filter canisters. Some say it helps but others continue to suffer.

I met with the President of the Board and the Manager for three months bringing them new information as I spoke to County Health Dept .officials, medical professionals and other carpet companies. All said that although the cause may never be known, the fact that so many people were complaining and some were unable to use the room at all, the carpet should be removed. So far, for a reason they will not share with me or others, they refuse to call the carpet company to tell of the health problem even though the President did say he would agree to negotiate. So far the Manager will not contact him. When I asked why, I was told they couldn't until they found the cause. I told them that the cause might never be known as I was told by those mentioned above. So far, nothing has been done. It doesn't make sense not to contact the owner.

After the formaldehyde was gone, I tried to use the card room but within a very short time, I had all the symptoms mentioned above. I left but that night I had an attack because my immune system is effected by my disease of Hyper-IgD (HID) syndrome. I did not need to call the doctor because my fever didn't go above 101.5 degrees. He puts me in the hospital when it reaches 102 degrees or higher. The attack lasts seven days. I have not returned to play. I do walk in on occasion to see if the symptoms return and have found I can't be in there even five minutes. Others have as severe a reaction as mine and others can play in there but suffer one or more of the symptoms. They say it slowly goes away after they leave the room.

There is something wrong ever since the carpet was put in the ladies card room. The room is used twice a day with air conditioning on. The people using the room are male and female and are 60-90 years ofage. The room holds around 250 people. The Manager has not taken an official accounting of who is affected by the carpet but we have an unofficial
count of 50+/-.

The symptoms include headache, red eyes, watery eyes, running nose, sore throat, coughing,
lungs, and nausea. There are several who can't go in at all and others who play in there but have to endure one or more of the symptoms. I have tried to go in the room but immediately begin to feel the symptoms. This means there are several of us who have no use of the room at all.
justification: Multiple individuals reported health issues including headaches, respiratory problems, and immune system reactions, indicating injury (severity 3). The widespread complaints and persistent symptoms suggest a high likelihood of occurrence (4).

incident_description:
We had a solar water heater installed in Dec. 2009.  The system is mounted on the water heater.  It has two loops.  One pumps water to the roof to panels where it is heated.  The water returns through a heat exchanger.  The second loop takes water from the water heater and runs it through the heat exchanger, then returns it to the water tank.  This system won't heat the water tank past 160F, but the individual pipes can see temperatures well above 200F.  For this reason, the pipes should all be copper or stainless steel (per the installation manual).

The contractor, contrary to the above, used plastic (PEX) pipes on the water tank loop. One of the pipes on the water tank side ruptured and spilled about 2000 gallons (before it was detected and stopped) into the house.  It caused about $63,000 worth of damage.  

Luckily, no one was standing nearby when this pipe ruptured because a person could have been sprayed with 200F water.

The contractor reported that he and many other solar water heater installers used PEX pipe up until about 2 years ago.  There are probably thousands of these installations out there, and they will eventually fail in all likelihood.

incident_description:
The defective product is a "Craftsman" Autoranging Multimeter Model 82175 S/N 07030045011 made for Sears by Extech.  A similar meter failed causing severe burns to its user (S/N 20061293403).

I am a registered professional engineer who is required to report public hazards.  I am currently investigating the above incident in my capacity as a forensic electrical engineer.

It is well known that users often apply these meters at the wrong settings and they are designed to protect the user with internal fuses and other techniques.  The exemplar, purchased more than a year after the incident meter, contains a soldering defect that shorts out the protective fuse, eliminating its protection.  This type of soldering defect would readily explain why the plaintiff's meter caused an arc flash and he received burns.  The meter's circuit board is partially "wave soldered" and partially manually soldered.  The exemplar meter that i have shows that the manual connections were made by someone not fully trained in soldering, and it is likely that he was instructed to make the connection in the way that shorts out the fuse.  Although the meters contain a sticker that claims "QUALITY CONTROL - PASSED," this safety related short would not show up in any operational test other than a destructive test.

These meters need to be sample tested to determine if the manufacturing defect is widespread.  I have photographs and diagrams that illustrate the defect.
justification: The incident involved severe burns to a user due to a defective multimeter, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the evidence of a manufacturing defect that could affect multiple units.

incident_description:

The next day, they returned to install a replacement frameless shower door, exactly the same as the one which had exploded. After searching online, however, there seem to be quite a few other people who have experienced this very frightening explosion.  I can't help but wonder why consumers are not warned about the dangers of these exploding doors before purchasing them? I now have to consult a tile restoration contractor regarding the repair of the damaged marble tile.  The owner of the glass door company assured us he would pay for the repair.  More importantly, I would strongly urge this consumer protection agency to alert consumers to this potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
The home standby generator I have is Model 04456-1, 12kw made by Generac Power Systems. It is a "whole house" type, and it starts up automatically when utility power is lost.  The mean it requires a battery to run the starter. 
The problem is with the charging system that Generac utilized to keep the battery fully charged.  It charged the battery at too high a voltage (approx. 14v DC).  the proper voltage should be somewhere in the area of 13.4-13.5 vDC.  When the battery is charged over a period of months, the excessive voltage level causes the electrolye to "boil off", which eventually exposes the plates inside, and results in a build-up of gas.  The battery then actually explodes, sending battery acid and parts of the battery case flying all over the interior of the unit, or on a person if they happen to start the generator manually during servicing or repair, resulting in severe acid burns.
This problem has been discussed on generator "forums", and is not an isolated thing.  Generac Power Systems is aware of the flaw in these charging systems, but refuses to acknowledge any problems, or offer to repair the units....even when they were under warranty. Even after pictures have been sent by owners of exploded batteries.  One way they have "acknowledged" the problem with out actually stating it, is that they have since reduced the voltage of the newer units to the acceptable levels I mentioned above.  There is a very good chance that someone has gotten splashed by this battery acid, and in some cases the flying parts have just missed small children that were nearby.
I am including some links to a well-known generator forum that has this problem discussed quite a bit:
http://zillerstore.com/forums/showthread.php?t=506&highlight=exploding+battery
http://zillerstore.com/forums/showthread.php?t=882&highlight=exploding+battery
http://zillerstore.com/forums/showthread.php?t=531&highlight=exploding+battery
http://zillerstore.com/forums/showthread.php?t=1022&highlight=exploding+battery
www.zillerelectric.com/forums/showthread.php?t=1504
justification: The description indicates potential for severe acid burns from exploding batteries, which qualifies as injury (severity 3). The problem is discussed widely on forums and not isolated, suggesting a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

My three-year-old son's left ring finger was amputated 1/4 inch to 1/2 inch from the tip when he tried to move a 2-step step stool while we were at the laundromat.  My back was turned to him, so I did not witness the amputation.  The step stool had been folded closed and leaning against the counter.  
     I was inserting quarters in the washing machine when I heard a loud bang behind me.  I turned around to find my son lying on top of the folded step stool.  When I picked him up, I saw blood by his mouth and thought he had lost or injured a tooth, but I did not find any damage to his mouth or teeth.  As I put him down to look him over, I saw that his left ring finger was bleeding and that the tip of it was missing.  I yelled that his finger was hurt and someone handed me tissues, which I used to control the bleeding.  I said I needed to call 911 and needed an ambulance, so another customer called 911.  After I had the bleeding under control and my son had calmed down enough to stop crying, I called 911 myself and was asked if someone else was reporting or had already reported the incident.  I replied that another lady was on the phone with a 911 operator at that moment; I was told to let her complete the call so they would not send two ambulances.
     After I hung up the phone, I saw my son's fingertip hanging from the back of the step stool, so I retrieved it and called for ice.  The police arrived shortly afterwards and were quickly followed by an ambulance.  Once we were in the ambulance, the lady who had placed the 911 call stated that she saw my son with the step stool partially open and that he was trying to climb it when he fell forward.  I believe, however, that he had pushed the step stool open and was moving it when he tripped and fell on top of it.  His left ring finger had gotten caught in the closing mechanism, and the tip of it was severed, tearing off all of his fingernail as well, when the weight of his body fell against the step stool.  
     My son was brought to a Trauma Center where he was seen by a pediatrician and a orthopedic surgeon.  The doctors decided to not reattach the amputated tip of my son's finger.

     I have asked to review the laudromat's survelliance video to ascertain exactly what had happened, but the video equipment was malfunctioning and it was not available.
      I am reporting this because my son has sustained a serious injury, and I believe the design of the closing mechanism on this step stool and similar folding products (such as folding chairs) is very dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury (finger amputation) requiring medical attention, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe injuries from step stools are not common.

Upon the inspections of our basement that Eco Tech made, we were told that it was very clean and clear and the spray foam application would not be difficult to do.  Our home is only ~ 6 years old and we keep a dehumidifier going throughout the Summer months to prevent mold and mildew build up.  So that has never been a problem for us. We cannot smell the musty odor in the basement because the spray foam odor is still strong no matter how many days we air the basement out. When this was applied, we were instructed to leave the windows open for like a couple of days and we did that in the middle of winter.  When it got warmer outside, we left the windows open for days.  The spray foam odor has not left yet.  I only noticed the musty odor when I went to use a table that was in the basement in April, and again this month.  I didn't pay much attention to it until I looked further into the odor of the spray foam.  Now I am concerned about our health and well-being as the fumes are still strong.  I feel that this is not normal and it has only happened after the spray foam was applied.

incident_description:
This letter addresses concerns that I have regarding a Kenmore Room Air Conditioner Model No. 580.75151500 purchased from a Sears in Chicago on June 2009.  After two years of using this air conditioner and experiencing some never previously experienced extreme health symptoms, I question if something is wrong with the air conditioning unit.  My girlfriend and I have moved, changed employers and employer locations, and even stayed with family and friends to experiment if symptoms improved.  Based on what we have gone through and measures we have taken, I speculate that something is functional wrong with this air conditioning unit and has caused extreme health issues as listed below.  

I purchased the Kenmore Room Air Conditioner Model No. 580.75151500 from Sears in June 2009 for use in my apartment.  At the time I was living in an apartment on [REDACTED] and currently live in an apartment on [REDACTED]..  Having an air conditioner during Chicago summers is very important for obvious health reasons.  Mid way through the first summer of owning this unit, living in the apartment located on [REDACTED], I began having health issues.  I was in my mid 20s and up to that point in my life had always been a healthy person.  There was no logical reason for me to get sick to the degree that I did; symptoms included dizziness, disorientation, feelings of vertigo, memory recall problems, shortness of breath, respiratory problems, inability to sleep, extreme fatigue, loss of muscle tone and weight loss, and more than usual hair loss.  I experienced most of these symptoms, but some were also experienced by my girlfriend.  Multiple times we cleaned our apartment from ceiling to floor, moving furniture, and ensuring everything was clean, but the health issues did not improve.  From time to time, my girlfriend and I would head back home to stay with our parents or stay with friends that also lived in the City.  During these visits, we would both begin to feel better.  After a day or two of being back in our apartment with the air conditioner operating, symptoms would re-present themselves.  

At first, we both thought these symptoms had something to do with the apartment we were living in at the time,[REDACTED], or my work environment.  Therefore, we cut our lease short during winter and moved over Christmas to a different apartment complex, located on [REDACTED].  All symptoms listed above improved for the first six months of living in this apartment.  Note, we were not using the air conditioning unit as it was winter and early spring.  

Other things had happened at work that caused me to continue my career search.  Plus I was still not thrilled with the work environment indoor air quality and cleanliness.  I continued to try and find other employment with better environmental conditions.  I obtained employment with a new company in a very new, updated, and well ventilated building at the beginning of July.  At this point in time, symptoms were much improved, and we both felt like our health levels were returning back to normal.  

This July Chicago has had its days of extreme heat where an air conditioner is 100% necessary, and there have also been about 15 days where the weather is a perfect 70 degrees Fahrenheit at night time and an air conditioner is not necessary.  One of the instances of extreme heat lasted for a period of approximately one week.  During this week, we ran the air conditioner, and we both began to notice the symptoms were reappearing.  Once the weather became more reasonable, we turned the air conditioner off and opened windows.  We then began to notice that symptoms were again beginning to improve.  

All of this has taken place over a two year period, and everything up to this point leads me to believe there is something wrong with the Kenmore room air conditioner.  I have tried to contact multiple heating and cooling companies to ask questions and inquire what they charge for air conditioner cleaning.  Every company I have contacted instructed me I was better off to purchase a new air conditioner and forget about it.  However, I do not have the income to spend $500 on a new air conditioning unit every year or when something goes wrong.  $500 may not be much to some people, but when I make an investment of that size, I expect the product to be safe to use.  Additionally, when I contacted Sears, distributor of Kenmore products, I did not receive a response to my initial inquiry.  I have since been given short unclear answers to my questions.  I am writing to seek assistance in my quest and also because I would not want anyone else to go through what I have had to over the past two years.  

Please do not hesitate to contact me by e-mail or phone for further communication.  

Thank you

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The description details multiple health symptoms experienced by the user and their girlfriend, which recurred when using the air conditioner, indicating injury due to the device.

incident_description:
About a week prior to March 18, 2011, I came home from work.  My husband had opened the garage door.  When I got out of the car I smelt something that smelled like burning plastic or rubber.  I asked him what was burning.  He said nothing.  I went out the back door of the garage and I could smell it on the patio so I thought maybe one of the neighbors was burning something. 
Prior to March 18, 2011 I usually used the garage door twice a day--once to leave to work and then when I came home. 
On March 18, 2011 I exited my garage door at aproximately 10:00 AM and came back in at 2:00 PM. 
I immediately came into the house.  I had used the garage door opener to close the garage door.  
At about 4:00 PM, I woke up from my nap and my husband told me to go out to the garage and look at it.  I did so.  I did not see anything, but I smelt a heavy odor of smoke, again it smelled like burning rubber or plastic.  He told me to look up.  I did.  The garage door opener plastic cover had melted onto the top of my car.  The top of the ceiling, above the garage door opener was black with smoke.  
When my husband installed the garage door opener in 2004, he had not installed in directly to the ceiling,  He had used a 1x6 and built it to support the garage door opener.  That is what saved our house from burning.  
We contacted Genie  and they had someone from Overhead Doors come out.  The installer was impressed with the way our door openers were installed.  He told us that was the best installation he had ever seen.  
We sent the motor and pictures to Genie.  They told they were not liable because it was not the motor that had caught on fire.  It was external.  
We agree with Genie it was not the motor of the garage door opener.  It was the plastic, opaque cover.
The plastic cover of the Genie garage door opener has an inside lip or small shelf.  
Prior to March 18, 2011, we had seen a small finch in our garage.  It had built a nest on the shelf onthe inside of the plastic cover.  However, we did not know that until after the fire.  The plastic cover is opaque and there is no way to know that anything had gotten into it unless the cover is taken off.  When do you take off the cover?  Only if a bulb burns out.  We could not even remember when we had replaced the bulbs.  
Our contention is that there is a safety issue concerning the opaque, plastic cover.  Because the cover is opaque, it cannot be determined if something--spiders, mice, roaches, (in our case a bird), had gotten into the cover.  It is open enough for anyting, including debris to get up on that shelf on the inside.  
We cannot help but wonder how many fires that may have started in a garage can be contributed to an incident such as ours.  We were lucky because of they way our opener was installed.  If the 1x6 had not been directly installed over the garage door opener, the fire would have caught our ceiling on fire.  Because of what is stored in most garages, it stands to reason that it would be difficult to determine the cause of the fire.  Or, if it had gotten into our attic, it would also stand to reason that someone would have said it was an electrical fire or something causing the fire in our attic.  
Again, we believe the cause of the fire is the way the cover is designed and it opaqueness. It melted very quickly and was very hot.  It melted the paint off the top of my car down to the bare metal.
We do have have photographs of the damage.  
The garage door opener is model H4000 A made by Genie Company.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to a bird nest in the garage door opener cover, causing melting and smoke damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
INCIDENT DETAILS
I purchased an Asko WasherlDryer Combo -model WCAM1812 on March 31,2006 from Albert
Lee Appliances in Seattle, Washington for $1,169.00

After about a year, I noticed that whenever I tried to dry the clothes, after one hour they were
still damp or the other extreme was they were so hot that I had to let them cool down before
reaching in to take them out of the machine. The thing that was most puzzling about this was that
in spite of setting the drying time button to 20/40/0r 60 minutes that it was unpredictable how
dry the clothes were. Often the machine on dry would continue going even after I set it for only
20 minutes drying time.

I called the Asko on 10/27/08 and spoke with a woman name [REDACTED]. She had no record of
proof of purchase, so I gladly faxed a copy of my sales receipt. A month later, on 11/28/08 I
received a call from a woman name [REDACTED]. Her repeated questions to me were how much laundry
was I trying to dry at a time and perhaps I was "filling the machine to the top" which was not the
correct way to use the dryer. I explained to her that I was only using the dryer for sheet and
towels and never had a full load. Also, explained to her that because the sheets were queen size, I
would dry one sheet at a time. Towels were never more that 3-4 and were the regular size bath
towels. After much banter back and forth and her rude, demeaning manner, she agreed to make
arrangements to have a service person come out and take a look at the problem.

A male serviceman did come out shortly thereafter, opened the machine and his comment to me
was that I had a "burned out heat pack". He was even kind enough to show me the pack. I took a
picture of it while he had the top off the machine. He replaced the pack.

Problems continued with no control over the drying time regardless of what time setting I set the
dry knob on, and the clothes continued to come out not dried or the reverse of being so hot that I
could not touch them and sometimes I would pun them out of the machine, in spite of how hot
they were, for fear of a fire.

On June 19,2011, I put a load of clothing in the washing machine and noticed after one hour the
clothes were still on the wash cycle. I immediately called the Asko in a panic because I did not
know what to do since this had never happened before. I spoke with a very kind woman name
[REDACTED]. I explained to her what was going on. She talked me through a procedure that she said
would alleviate the problem, get the machine to go into spin and drain the water from the
machine. I tried 3 times with her on the phone but no results. The machine just kept washing in
the wash cycle. She was at a loss as to why the technique she was walking me through was not
working. She then suggested I pull the drain plug at the bottom ofthe machine and allow the
approx.5 gallons of water to drain. I told her I could not do that because the machine was not on
a platfonn, in other words the drain plug was too low to even slip an adequate bucket for the 5
gallons of water. I also explained to her that I was living in a condo with hardwood floors and
did not wish to damage my unit as well as my neighbors unit below me. She was very
sympathetic, apologized and gave me the number of a few repair companies in the area with the
understanding no one would be available to come out today. I thanked her for her time and we
hung up. The saving grace for me was that I kept repeating over and over the technique she tried
with me over the phone. It eventually worked.

I am very displeased with this product. There are definitely some safety issues and ooncerns as I
have documented. I would have to conclude that not only is Asko WasherlDryer Combo -Model
number WCAM 1812 - not a user friendly machine but that the drying component is a safety
hazard. We as consumers should not have to worry about using a product that is unreliable,
unsafe, or requires rebooting to operate.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning appliance causing inconvenience and potential safety hazards, but no actual injury or death occurred.

Thank you.
justification: The lint buildup is described as a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: FAN WAS ON DURING THE NIGHT AND BURNED. NO INJURIES.
justification: The fan burning is an incident with no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible given the description.

incident_description: Sears Craftsman model # 21829 tablesaw switch failed in the on position.  The tablesaw will no longer turn off and I had to pull the plug out of the wall socket to turn it off.
justification: The tablesaw switch failed in the on position, requiring manual intervention to turn it off, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
The float bowl fell off of the carburetor while generator was running.  This caused gasoline to pour onto the ground under the hot engine, even after the generator stalled for lack of fuel.

There is no obvious mechanical means to hold the float bowl to the rest of the carburetor.  The replacement carburetor sold to me by harbor freight is of the same construction with no obvious mechanical means of securing the float bowl to the remainder of the carburetor.

If the float bowl is glued to the rest of the carburetor, then this failure mode can be expected of any generator equipped with this carburetor.

Harbor Freight generator model number is 98838.  I purchased my generator January 17, 2009 from Harbor Freight store number 177 located in Gaithersburg, Maryland.  The carburetor is part number 14A in the manual that came with my generator.
justification: The incident involved gasoline spillage but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Our Casablanca ceiling fan fell in our bedroom. The fan model No. is 3873A and the serial No. is ASS110022. We purchased the fan 4 years ago from Thousand Oaks Fans & Lighting in Thousand Oaks CA. We had the fan installed by a licensed electrician.

Casablanca Co. sent a representative to our home to inspect the fallen fan. It was the representative's opinion that the set screw was not tightened sufficiently when the fan was installed. We visited Thousand Oaks Fans & Lighting, and the proprietor showed us how easy it is for an electrician to fail to properly tighten the set screw - there are a few different ways that an electrician can unwittingly circumvent a thorough tightening of the set screw. The set screw is approximately 1/8 inch long, and is apparently a single point of failure for the fan.
justification: The fan fell due to an improperly tightened set screw, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Removing cover over  hot water heater to find thermostat. To remove bottom cover (metal plate) you must lift up and out to release cover from latch.  The cover came into contact with electrical connection, which causes small explosive short, and caused insulation inside of panel to catch on fire. It is almost impossible to remove this cover without coming into contact with electrical connection. The foam inside the panel is extremely flammable and not self-extinguishing.  I had to blow out the flames after approximately 10 seconds.  Instruction booklet provided with water heater is not model specific and indicates three different options for where the thermostat could be. Thermostat cover should be marked.  Electrical connection should be insulated against metal cover in case breaker is not turned off completely as in my case.   Foam should be non-flammable. This presents a serious shock and fire hazard to home owners.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and potential shock risk, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was using a Hoover Steamvac carpet cleaner on our livingroom carpet when the machine suddenly began to buzz and emit white smoke.  I turned the On/Off switch to Off but the machine continued to buzz, and billow large amounts of smoke.  I ran to the outlet and unplugged it but the unit had become extremely hot very, very quickly and scorched the carpet beneith where it malfunctioned.  I carried the machine outdoors where it continued to smoke for almost ten minutes.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction and property damage (scorched carpet) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
I use SunBeam Iron plus Steamer that I  bought from Bed Bath & Beyond. The iron worked good for few months and now while ironing, water is dripping from the iron constantly. I consider this as a safety hazard and concerned about safety of my family members using this iron. Model number and details about the iron is Sunbeam iron and Steamer - UPC 0 274571445 7, Embossed number C102JT, GCSBRS103, No. 126272. Earlier version of the Sun Beam iron was recalled but I still believe that even this model is not safe either. You can see the recall information at http://www.walletpop.com/2011/02/03/sunbeam-recalls-irons-from-bed-bath-and-beyond-after-reports-of-f/

I will sincerely appreciate if you can please consider my complain. I have taken pictures of the iron when leaking water and attached to this report
justification: Water dripping from the iron poses a potential safety hazard but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description: I bought a Levition switch UPC 078477772713.   When I installed it in the wall, I noticed that the switch could easilly rest in the middle position instead of flipping to the totally open or totally off position.   I believe this is a fire hazard so I removed the switch from the wall and installed a different one.
justification: The switch could potentially cause a fire hazard, but no incident or injury occurred as it was removed before any harm.

incident_description: the washer will not spin.  makes a buzzing noise gets hot and throws the breaker
justification: The washer malfunctioning poses no immediate injury risk but indicates a potential electrical hazard.

incident_description:
The pressure switch on my old Sears Air Compressor failed. The compressor continued to run and built pressure to 200+ pounds. I noticed it when the belt started to squeal.  

This unit is equipped with a Safety overpressure device (Pop Off Valve) that failed to vent the over pressure.

I removed the device. It was stuck shut, due to rust and contamination inside the body.

This device is installed vertically on the manifold with an opening in the top that allows moisture and contaminants to enter.

This device is, and has been for years, installed on multiple brands of consumer purchased air compressors.

I have pictures
justification: The incident involved equipment failure without injury, but with potential for harm due to overpressure and safety device failure.

incident_description: I purchased the children's bathroom caddy at Target.  It is supposed to be attached to the bathtub wall with suction cups.  Before installing, the plastic caddy fell from the dresser and cut open my three year old daughter's upper arm.  Upon inspection of the caddy, I found that the bottom edge of the caddy, the part that would likely hit a child in the tub if the suction cups fail, is EXTREMELY sharp.  The the hard plastic of the caddy is not rounded to prevent injury.  This thin flat bottom edge of the caddy is what caused the injury. The cut it caused was about 3 inches long and 1/4 inch across. My concern is that since this item is not designed to be attached permanently to the wall it is not safe to install since it is sharp. It fell in a similar way it would fall in a tub, and caused this injury.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury to a child, with a 3-inch cut caused by the sharp edge of the caddy, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the design flaw and the potential for similar incidents if the product is used as intended.

incident_description: Cordless electric drill battery got warm on one side (rear, right when holding drill for normal use) while plugged into drill but drill was turned off at the time.  Drill seemed to operate normally, no unusual or uneven heating noticed.  Battery did not get warm again when drill was turned off.  I suspect the battery, not the drill, perhaps an intermittent short inside the battery (faulty cell or wiring).
justification: The battery warming up without use suggests a potential fault, but no injury or further issues occurred.

incident_description: Fire crews responded to a report of a residential structure fire. Upon arrival, crews locating a smoking electric Galaxy box fan.
justification: The incident involved a smoking electric fan, which posed a potential fire hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
purchashed a Carrier Air Condition had installed in home after 4 yrs ac stopped worked a wire to 
the compressor shorted to one of the copper tubes burned a hole in tube if the circuit braker hadn't tripped could have burned down the home. Was told by corporation representive that they had 
complaints about this and it was an ongoing problem and was the installers responsibility to fis the problem, Carrier should not be permitted to ship a product that has a knpwn problem to consumers that has a problem with the expectation that it will be repaired when installed.
justification: The incident involved a wire shorting and burning a hole in a copper tube, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The problem is described as ongoing, indicating it is likely to happen again.

incident_description: I purchased a 12foot step ladder from Home Depot online.  The ladder was manufactured by Werner Ladder.  The ladder arrived here missing two rivets in the right rear spreader brace ( I later found an extremely mangled rivet on the floor of my garage, I am convinced the damage to the rivet could not have occured in the successfully installed position). Fortunately for me (and all concerned) the "defect" was obvious.  Had this omission occured in a structurally significant portion of the ladder (not readily noticeable) it could have resulted in significant injury or even death.  The missing rivets were the same as used in the rest of the assembly.  I have asked both Home Depot and Werner Ladder for corrective action, such action visible enough to me to allow me to exit this matter.  Thus far neither party has given me an acceptable reply.  I have my e-mail notices and replies if you need them and can assure me that I am legally permitrted to share them.
justification: The defect was obvious and no injury occurred, but the potential for significant injury or death was present if the defect had been in a structurally significant portion.

incident_description:
Regarding LG Front Load Washing Machine

My son and I smelled smoke in the living room/dining room. It smelled like a fire. I traced it to the laundry room. I opened the door and it was filled with white smoke and a fire smell. The washing machine was in the middle of a load of laundry. I immediately unplugged the washing machine and got myself and 3 children out of the home. I called my husband. Once I determined that a fire was not going to spread, I went back in. I opened the door to the washing machine and it was filled with smoke and smell.
We are extremely concerned this may require a recall because only 4 months ago (March 2011) we donated items to a local family who had to move out of their home after it caught on fire from a faulty circuit board from an LG front load washing machine. We are still in contact with them through a close friend.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a fire smell from the washing machine, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Federal Pacific dual pole 220v 30A breaker started tripping when running the clothes dryer. Checked the dryer and it was fine. A current probe on the wire going to the breaker showed that the breaker was tripping at 19 1/2 amps of current being drawn.

Address given is the address of the house. We have moved since then.

Also, we have had that Federal Pacific panel removed from that house and replaced after reading all the horror stories about how many fires they have started.
justification: The breaker was malfunctioning but no injury or damage occurred, and the panel was subsequently replaced.

incident_description:
The glass vessel exploded in my bathroom, sending glass shrapnel everywhere. 

I opened the medicine cabinet when a small bottle about 3 inches tall fell out and landed in the glass vessel sink. As soon as it hit the glass bowl, the sink exploded. The force of the bowl shattering knocked everything right off the vanity counter. I was standing in front of the sink and I had tiny glass slivers embedded in my skin. The slivers were hard to see - I only knew where they were based on the blood droplets that formed around each spot. I was shaking glass out of my hair after the incident.

I've read that these vessel sinks are made with tempered glass and are prone to shatter like this. Had I been a child, I would most certainly have glass pieces in my eye and face.

I wouldn't write to you if the glass sink cracked or dented. Or if it simply broke in half. The way it exploded scared me to death and the sheer force of it knocking bottles off the counter is frightening. This kind of glass should not be in people's bathrooms.

I recorded video of the subsequent damage and what happened:
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dYMKqvJ0wf0&feature=channel_video_title
justification: The incident resulted in glass shrapnel embedded in the skin, indicating an injury, and the description notes the potential for more severe harm to a child.

incident_description:
Earlier this year I purchased a new generator for the purpose of having back-up power in the event of a power outage, which actually happened within 24 hours of my purchase.
I also have a hunting camp which does not have commercial power. I use a generator to run a well pump and charge batteries for approximately 3 hours a day. I should add that I have had this camp for almost 12 years now and have had no electrical issues in that period of time. I am in the process of trying to sell my camp due to health reasons. Because of this placement on the Market I switched my 12 KW generator for this 5 KW generator purely for economic reasons. The 5
KW generator in question is manufactured by Generac Corp. I should also add that prior to the acquisition of the 12 KW generator set that I had a Generac 5500 KW that served me very well for 9 -10 years when it finally failed. During those previous years the generator would run considerably more as I had not perfected my battery system until more recently.  
Now for the problem. As just stated I replaced a much larger generator set with this 5 KW Guardian Generac set. Prior to me taking it to my camp it had less than 2 hours of run time on it. As of this writing it still has only about 20 hours or less total running time, less than a 24 hour day.
My problems began on June 3rd. I was inside my camp doing some painting and had the generator running to provide me with light to paint by. That first day of trouble it ran for about 5 hrs. On the 3rd, while I was painting, I had my stereo playing. Suddenly the stereo just decided to quit operating. I tinkered with it for a short time and simply gave up thinking it had simply gone bad for unknown reasons. For unexplained reasons, a short time later the stereo began working again. Next I got my digital volt/ohm meter out and checked the power at a receptacle to see what voltage was being produced by this new generator. It read 120.6-8 volts. At the time I thought this a bit peculiar as the generator is located between 100 and 150 feet away from the dwelling and there is generally a small voltage loss of 1-3 volts because of the distance. I told my friend what had happened and we both took a look at the new generator to see if there were any problems that may have caused the higher voltage and the stereo acting up. None were found at that time. I resumed painting and a short time later all the lights went out. Now I thought my friend was in the Generator hut tinkering with it still looking for a problem. Then they came back on. A short time later they went out again, same assumption, then came back on again. Then they went out again and this time my friend came in and I asked him why he had turned the generator off? HE DIDN'T, IT WAS STILL RUNNING AND THE LIGHTS WERE STILL OUT! I again checked the voltage and had the same results. 120.6-8 volts. We decided to shut it down and start it again later when we were going to do dishes and take our showers. It functioned perfectly the rest of the time it was on line that afternoon.
On the 4th of June I resumed painting once again with the generator running and the stereo going trying to finish the job. I should also mention that on the 3rd one of the battery chargers we use to recharge our deep cycle batteries was buzzing very loudly. At that time I unplugged it and apparently upon doing so the voltage had dropped back to 120 volts as the other charger was not making any noise I could notice.
I resumed my painting which was going well for awhile until my stereo quit again. I tried tinkering with it again but this time it was never going to work again. Suddenly, from over 30 feet away, I heard the other charger buzzing wildly! I quickly unplugged the other charger. Then suddenly all the lights in the camp got as bright as the sun! I quickly retrieved my meter and check the voltage again. This time, at the same receptacle, I was reading well over 170 volts! Assuming that both phases are producing the same voltage that adds up to 340 volts! We quickly shut it down! To make it short, after a final test and inspection this generating unit has probably ruined both chargers. It did ruin my stereo and my well pump.
Since I had bought this unit from my local Lowe's building center and the directions on the unit state that I should call the Lowe's 800 number provided instead of bringing it back. This I did, and was immediately transferred to Generac Corp.  I was told that my generator was not intended for use in any location where commercial power is not available as is " apparently " stated in the warranty conditions. I bought this unit off the floor and am not even sure if I even received any printed material. And the person selling it to me certainly did not tell me it was not intended for use in special situations only.

All of what I have just stated is my problem and not something you would normally get involved in. "
BUT ", the disturbing thing about all that I have just explained, and also explained in detail to Generac,
is the fact that they express absolutely no concern at all that this style of generator, in all probability,
will cause a house fire and could very well cause fatalities! It mattered not that this unit STILL has only
about 20 hours on it. In normal power outage situations, power may be out for over a week. Most
people I know do not know much at all about electricity and certainly not how to use a meter. Many
people will fill their generators up with fuel and leave them running all night, especially in cold weather
when heavy snow and ice storms take down many power lines. They will leave their generators
running all night just to keep their homes warm and also to prevent water lines from freezing. This is
something I have done myself in past years. I can only thank God that this did not happen under these
circumstances and cause a house fire in my home!
I find Generac's lack of concern for the public's welfare that they are selling these to be absurd and
unconscionable! At the time I bought this unit, I was proud to do so as it is " Made in America "! After
this unpleasant experience I guess that fact is about as good as being made in China as they all have
the same quality.
I feel this is something that needs your attention. My problems are being covered by my insurance Co.
so this is not a plea for money, though I feel they are responsible. My concern is one more of
compassion for my fellow man, and I would hope others would feel the same about a similar situation.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure causing damage to appliances but no injuries or fatalities.

incident_description:
I purchased a portable 3250 watt generator on April 12 2011 from Mr Sparky (704 435-3060). I store the unit in a small barn away from my house. When I went to pull it out to run it a little on July 10 2011 I found that the gas cut-off valve/tank connection had broken free from the tank completely and all gas has drained from the tank. Fortunately I had only a little gas in it to leak out. But it holds up to 4 gallons which would have caused a very dangerous situation and could have lead to a major disaster. I have contacted the company that sold it to me. No response yet. I have asked to return/refund as to the seriousness to a safety issue that I would never feel comfortable with a Generac product that has such a defect in materials used. I have pictures if there is someone I may send them to. 

I have also contacted the manufacturer and have not been contacted according to their response:
From: customersupport@generac.com <customersupport@generac.com>
Subject: Thank you from Generac
To: [REDACTED] Date: Sunday, July 10, 2011, 12:47 PM
Thank you for your request. A Generac representative will respond to your inquiry within 48 hours. If you require immediate assistance please contact us at 1-888-Generac. 
Generac Customer Service
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to a defective part, which could have led to a dangerous situation but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I got up this morning 7/12/11 and heard someting running in the attached garage. It was my Dirt Devil Pressure Washer, model is a Pressure Flex 2000. The unit was plugged in, no water hose attached, and was running. I unplugged it and it quit.  It was turned on but the unit shuts off when the wand lever is not depressed so I did not know it was turned on but not running. It was running hot, lightly smoking with a burnt rubber smell, and leaking blackish oil on the floor ( about 2 or 3 Tablespoons worth, a spot a good foot around) I will take pictures. I think this was close to catching fire. I just read the 6 pages of warnings and instructions in the manual and it says nothing about turning it off when the hose in not attached. This is the first time I have used it and left it plugged in. I have had it about 3 months.It was bought from Menards. I have not turned it of or moved it yet.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction with potential fire hazard but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
My Rowenta iron sparked. My daughter unplugged the iron and left the room. Within minutes the iron caught fire. The fire was at the base of the iron where the plug attaches. I contacted Rowenta and sent the iron in to be inspected. They said it was inconclusive but offered me a new iron provided I sign a release form. After searching the internet I found many other people experienced the same thing with their Rowenta iron and the company either claimed it was normal wear and tear or inconclusive. Fortunately, I had no casualties but my iron and board but it could easily have been very bad had I not seen the fire through my closet window. I feel there is a design flaw or something that is causing all the irons to burst into flames. Here is a site that list tons of people who experienced the same issue http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/rowenta.html.
Thanks!
justification: The iron sparked and caught fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred. The incident could have been worse if not noticed in time.

incident_description:
On 6/9/11, I purchased a small desk fan from Rite Aid Pharmacy on Richmond Ave in Staten Island, NY. The fan worked fine and there were multiple warnings on the proper way to use the fan. However, I did not notice that their was an additional warning on the bottom of the outside of the box until I had already plugged the fan in and started using it. 

The warning read: "Handling this product will expose you to lead, a chemical known by the state of California to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. Wash hands after handling. 

I found this extremely disburbing because I was 8 months pregnant when I brougt th fan. I returned it back to the store, but I don't think anyone should be allowed to use this product because most people will not notice the warning because it only appears on the bottom on the outside of the box. 

Item# 9013735
Distributed by Rite Aid
30 Hunter Lane
Camp Hill, PA 17011
Made in China
justification: The incident involves exposure to a hazardous chemical but no actual injury was reported, and the product was returned.

incident_description:
We purchased a product called Invisible Shield by ZAGG for an Acer Iconia Tablet A500, which is a screen shield.  We did not realize that it was not attached by static alone, but has a chemical spray to use for application.  The sprayer is marked as "Spray Shield" by ZAGG, application solution, and it does not say what is in this, but does have a warning "Do not spray in eyes, Do not swallow, Do not inhale."  We did not open this product as we do not know what it contains.  There are no ingredients shown on outer packaging or on dispenser that we can see.  

It seems that with these warnings, there should be some identification of the product so that if someone gets it in their eyes, inhales it or swallows it, a medical caregiver could advise on treatment.

We are not going to risk using this product and would be happy to mail it to you if you request it, otherwise we will throw it away.  

Please note:  There was no incident - we did not open this product.
justification: No incident occurred as the product was not opened or used, and there was no injury.

incident_description:
I bought and installed a bathroom ventilator fan, NuTone Model #8832SA.  The wiring connection box has an access opening that is too small to work safely with -- even with my medium-sized hands.  And it's too small to wire the connections using tightly-fitting construction safety gloves.  So when I wired the connections, my left palm touched the razor sharp and unfiled sheet metal edges of the fan housing, resulting in a one-inch bleeding gash on my palm.  The electrical connection box also has sharp sheet metal edges that nick and cut fingers.  I would like to send you photos.  

THIS PRODUCT, AND ITS SISTER MODELS 8832WH AND 8833, NEEDS TO BE RECALLED.
justification: The incident resulted in a one-inch bleeding gash, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The sharp edges and small access opening make similar injuries likely during installation (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description:
I own a Maytag washing machine. The plastic liner around the lid of the tub has come serrated all the way around. This not only causes the clothes to be torn as the are removed from the tub
but on several occosians hascaused scratched on our arms.
justification: The serrated plastic liner has caused scratches on arms, indicating injury, and occurs frequently during use.

incident_description:
Ryobi 18 volt cordless drill recently became warm while in storage with battery attached.  The power switch jammed in the OFF position, possibly due to plastic melting inside the switch, and the battery was run down, possibly from the switch not turning off completely.

There is a recall for a similar Ryobi 18 volt cordless drill, model HP1802M, sold during that time period, and that recall appears to be for similar problem (CPSC Release #11-009), but today, Ryobi said my model SA1802 was not affected.  However they could not explain how my drill's power switch differed from the other models or provide any details about the switches, nor could they explain, with any specifics, what usually failed in the switches.

Frankly, I believe the recall should be expanded because some Ryobi drills sold around 2003 may have the same defective power switch.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning drill with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the recall context but no widespread reports.

incident_description: Citizen attempted to utilize an A/C adapter to charge a Kindle.  When the adapter was plugged into the receptacle the adapter began to arc and smoke.
justification: The incident involved an A/C adapter arcing and smoking, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The consumer says she was washing clothes.  She went into the laundry room when she noticed the entire room was smokey.  The consumer says that she opened the washing machine's door and the unit was all smoked up and that it took 30 minutes for the smoke to go away.  The consumer said the unit was on for approximately 30 minutes.  She says the inside and outside of the washer still looked good.  The consumer says that the unit was running even while it was smoking.  The consumer unplugged the unit.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who offered to send a technician.
justification: The incident involved smoke but no injury or damage, and the consumer took appropriate action by unplugging the unit.

incident_description: 15 month old child can easily remove outlet covers from the outlet.
justification: The child can remove outlet covers, which poses a risk of electric shock or injury, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The consumer was using the drill for approximately 3 - 5 minutes to drill a hole in a log, when the drill exploded.  The consumer stated that he had been using the drill off and on that morning and the day before.  When the battery would wear down, the consumer recharged it and started using it again.

The consumer was drilling hole, when the drill exploded in his right hand.  The consumer was using both hands, but the right hand sustained more damage than his left hand.  The casing of the battery blew apart.  The battery is located underneath one's hands, when they are holding the drill.  The battery blew apart into several small pieces.  The consumer equated the incident to an explosive going off.  The consumer's mother drove him to the nearest emergency room (Pocono Medical Center).

X-rays were taken on the consumer's right hand, his wound was cleaned and approximately 3 to 5 sutures were applied his right hand.  The consumer was released the same day.  The consumer had follow-up care, which lasted approximately 2 months.

To this day, the consumer still experiences pain, he has scars and he stated that there is still some swelling to his right hand.


The week after the incident, the consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained the incident to a representative.  Their rep. asked the consumer about his injuries and asked him what amount he would considered as a claim for his pain and suffering.  The consumer said that he did not know initially, but he asked the company's rep. for a figure.  Their rep. did not provide him with a number, but the consumer said that he gave them a figure of $20,000.00.  The manufacturer has never offered the consumer any compensation for this incident. 

The consumer noted that the battery came with the drill and that the battery was made in China.  This product came with 1 battery and it was included in the packaging at the time of purchase.

NOTE:  The consumer said that his battery appears to be identical to the one mentioned in Release # 09-298.
justification: The consumer sustained injuries requiring medical treatment and follow-up care, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific circumstances of battery explosion.

incident_description:
Regarding [REDACTED] Yard Power Products, I believe the problem with the gas gaps distorting due to additives in the gasoline is also happening on my Craftsman Saw.


When new, the gas cap could easily removed (unscrewed) or replaced securely by hand. Now I must use a pair of channel lock pliers to remove the gas cap and more importantly, to tighten it securely so fuel does not leak when it is either in use or stored.
justification: The incident involves a gas cap issue causing potential fuel leaks, which is a safety concern but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated a fire was started by her electric portable heater. The stated that the product was off at the time of the incident and plugged into a wall socket. The wall socket had flames shoot from the outlet. The consumer's husband unplugged the heater from the outlet and the flames stopped. The product does not appear to be damaged in any way. However, the wall socket does have charring and discoloration, and was replaced.

The consumer was not harmed by the product but feels she might have been if her husband was not home with her, as she is disabled and cannot walk. The consumer's son tested the plug and discovered it had wires in the plug that were crossed, creating a short.  The consumer has noticed similar products recalled in release 11-121. The consumer chose not to call the fire department at the time of the incident.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injuries, but potential for harm due to the consumer's disability and the product's wiring issue.

incident_description:
Ryobi Model RTS30 Portable Table Saw.

Attempting to unlock the tilt lock snapped a plastic washer and it flew across the room after bouncing off my arm.

Now the saw is unsafe to use as there is no way to secure the saw tilt.

After checking Home Depot for another saw, it was noticed that all their display models had the same missing washer.
justification: The incident involved a plastic washer snapping and flying off, causing no injury but making the saw unsafe to use, and the issue was observed in multiple display models.

incident_description:
honeywell safe model 2077D manufactured approximately 3 years ago (now it's called First Alert model 2077df)

had to replace the AA batteries after about one year and upon placing new batteries in the inside door for the electronic keypad the unit begin smoking heavily.  batteries started to also melt inside the battery casing.  i had to use a screwdriver to pry loose battery casing out of door and rip the unit with 4 batteries out to stop the smoking which exposed one very hot wire which poked my finger and caused a burn.  

flimsy backup key lock broke off  key when i tried to open it.
justification: The incident involved smoking batteries, melting, and a burn injury from a hot wire, indicating a severity level of 3. Such incidents are rare but possible with faulty equipment.

incident_description: While ironing the morning of June 22, 2011, the cord of my Rowenta iron caught fire.  I heard a pop (the sound of a flame starting) and then saw the flame coming from the cord at the junction of the cord and the plug.  I quickly pulled the cord from the outlet using the other end of the cord.  Thankfully no one was hurt. incident_description: I built a new home which included a Heatliator built in natural gas fireplace. After the first use, the batteries ruptured due to the heat and the fan unit which was running pulled the fumes from the two D Alkaline batteries into the room. I removed the cover of the fireplace to find a pool of acid in and under the battery pack and firebox floor. I called the builder who sent out a repair person who just removed the two batteries and left the acid which had now spread across the floor of the fireplace and had started reacting with the metal floor of the fireplace unit. The repair person advised the batteries should only be used in a power outage due to the heat causing them rupture under normal use. I asked why there is no sticker or label stating the batteries are only for emergency use and the repair person stated there should be as this is a common issue. I have contacted the manufacturer who sent another repair company out to replace the battery box and wiring that was damaged by the acid, and spray painted over the damaged metal floor of the firebox. During that visit I was told I should only use the battery pack during an electrical outage because the heat will damage the batteries installed. I am concerned that Heatilator is not labeling their battery backup product as emergency use only and therefore exposing consumers to fumes produced by ruptured batteries in the fireplaces they manufacture.

incident_description:
We purchased a Shark Steam Mop (marketed by Euro-Pro Holdings LLC) in maybe May 2010.  This is a household device to mop floors with hot steam.  There is a steam generating component in the midsection of the handle (and a water tank) and the steam is channeled to a flexible mop head that is covered by a cloth pocket.

There is a one year warranty.

The mop stopped providing steam maybe last time my wife used it.  She didn't mention that to me before I used it today.  When I used it, I plugged it in to turn it on and waited for it to start producing steam.  You can lift and depress the upper handle to initiate the further production of steam (sometimes when there is low water or other conditions, steam production can be inhibited so patience is required).  I did this intermittently, not aggressively, for maybe a minute or two.

The unit was quiet however, meaning it was not producing steam.

Then it exploded and shot steam all over the floor in maybe a three foot jet.  The mop head broke from the handle, although the break point was actually a release or latched joint, so the explosion itself did not damage the unit.  You could describe it as the mop head explosively detaching.  I was very surprised, and because of the heat, force, and pressure involved I was glad that I was not manipulating the mop head when it explosively detached because I easily could have been scalded.

After unplugging and inspecting the unit and looking for a clog in the steam channel, I repeated the procedure once again, but without purposefully generating steam (I did not manipulate the handle).   The mop head explosively detached again after a short time (30 seconds?).

I then let the unit cool and disassembled the steam channel, as I assumed it was clogged.  In fact, on inspection, I saw that the upper steam channel (which is in direct proximity to the steam production unit) was designed as being plastic.  Part of the plastic had bubbled up like Styrofoam, and part of it had collapsed and melted.  In other words, instead of using a material that was unlikely to melt for the very hot upper steam channel, the designer of the mop used cheap plastic that melted around the time the warranty expired, collapsed around the small steam channel, and caused the unit to explode (or the mop head to explosively detach) in normal use.

I called Euro-Pro/Shark to talk to them.  A rep said that the model probably was out of warranty (by maybe a month or two) and that warranty service was therefore unavailable.  When I told him that I planned to report this to the consumer protection authorities, he referred me to another number 1-866-694-6406 that he said would generate a callback within 34 hours, and made some reference to burns or personal injuries.  I told him that I was not interested in compensation for personal injury, because luckily I was not injured.

However, this unit is basically a ticking time bomb in my opinion and should be recalled.  The melting of the plastic steam channel is a very predictable mode of failure, and it is outrageous that the most predictable mode of failure will very predictably cause the mop head to explosively detach.

I took pictures of the melted plastic piece (which is very small),  which are attached.  The pictures were taken after the channel was disassembled into basically four parts (two of which were plastic and had melted).  There is another choke point in the steam channel, but it is metal and I assume that it is a valve of some sort.  A picture of that also is attached.  I am holding onto the steam mop in case you want it, but it is extremely hazardous in this condition and will not function as intended. It just explodes.

Please encourage Euro Pro to recall all of their units that have an upper steam channel composed of plastic, as it is unreasonably susceptible of melting and causing a resulting explosion.
justification: The incident involved an explosive detachment of the mop head, posing a scalding risk, but no injury occurred.

For the last few years my 2 year old son and I have had what at first seemed to be random allergic reactions that would result in hive breakouts. For the longest time I wasn't sure what could be causing it. My husband would regularly do laundry at his mothers house when he took the kids to visit and so I thought it may be her detergent. I gave him hypoallergenic detergent to use for all our clothes, but of course his mother still used her own.

My son would still break out sometimes. A few weeks ago he had a hive outbreak that was the worst we had ever seen. I got more persistent in asking what she uses. Well one day my husband brought my son home wrapped in one of my mother in laws blankets because he forgot his jacket that day. The blanket remained at my house for a few days and during that time, without thinking about it, I used it while sitting on my couch watching TV. The next morning i woke up covered in hives, the worst outbreak I have ever had in my life, for the first time in over a year. It got the point that I swelled up and had difficulty breathing. As I write this I am taking [REDACTED] and the swelling and hives have calmed down but are still present. 

After this my husband took the issue more seriously and discovered in talking to his mom that she uses this Suavital fabric softener occasionally on the blankets at her home. I say occasionally because the blankets are not washed as often as clothes and she only uses it on the blankets. This made sense to me because when my son was at her house he would nap and use her blankets, which is why his outbreaks persisted when mine seemed to stop, but did not occur as often as they would have had his clothes been washed with the Suavital as well.

I immediately did a web search and found that others had serious complaints about this product as well. I would like to see it removed so that those of us who are sensitive to low quality ingredients don't become victims in this way to this product again.
justification: The incident describes severe allergic reactions including hives and difficulty breathing, which qualifies as an injury.
