incident_description:
I purchased an Eco-heater, model 110400, on April 8, 2011, at an Ace Hardware, in downtown Berkeley, CA. Upon opening the packaging, I noticed a strong odor, similar to a new plastic product smell. I installed the heater and used it for about 3 weeks, All of this time the heater, whether turned on or off, gave off this odor. 
       On May 19, 2011, I e-mailed the manufacturer directly, and their customer rep replied that they had some problems with a few of their heaters off-gassing, and they would replace the unit with a newer model. 
       I received the newer model, NA400S, around May 25, 2011, and replaced the old model 110400. The new model works well and I am having no obvious odor problem with it. I retain the old model 110400, in it's original packaging. 
       I have asked (5/19/11) the manufacturer for information on the source of the odor, with the model 110400, since I would like to know what I and my wife have been breathing for several weeks. 
As of today, I have only heard that the person in charge is unavailable, and that they have been testing their model 110400. Their response to me about their testing is about the efficiency of the model 110400, and some overheating problems, with no comment about the odor or the material causing that odor.
justification: The incident involves a product defect (odor issue) with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) as the manufacturer acknowledged similar issues with other units.

incident_description: This Odorknockout product was given to me by a car dealership to remove a cigarette smoke smell in a used car i just bought.  They assured me that this product was able to get the smell out and this is what they used to get out the bad smells in vehicles(why mine was not done before i bought it is beyond me).  I used the product on a Thursday night which was two nights after i bought the car.  The directions clearly stated to add 2oz of lukewarm water to the plastic container with a white pouch in it, return the lid, and shake for ten seconds.  It then says to run you air for approx. ten to fifteen minutes before actually opening the can and allowing it to sit in your car and do its job.  It did say to leave the area for "not less than two hours" after opening the can and setting it in the car and to allow it to air out before getting into it again.  Well i read the directions and did exactly as they stated and everything was ok until i started shaking the can after adding the water.  I shook it for about five seconds and the can starting fizzing and it blew the top off, a yellow looking smoke/gas was coming from the can.  My nose felt like it was on fire, my eyes burned severly so that they were watered up and i could not see, and i could not have breathed in a breath to save my life as my throat burned severly and my lungs felt paralyzed.  I soon found out that this was in fact chlorine gas being released which of course can be deadly in the proper concentrations.  I work in a lab around pure hydrochloric acid and have not ever been overcome by anything like this stuff got me.  I have been around pure bleach and believe me this was much stronger.  The next thing i did was gagged for a while  when i could finally catch my breath and got inside and ran to get into the shower.  I got to feeling better after i got out of the shower.  The next day i coughed a lot but still did not feel i needed to go to the doctor.  I did notice something that got my attention the next day though, my hand had brown burns on them where i had the can and it got on my fingers.  I also had one spot on my nose and some on my left had where it sprayed out when the top blew off.  I also had a very nice pair of clothes ruined by this stuff bleaching them out.  I did what i thought was best and called the office of the manufacturer of the product and was told that i should have never shaken it with the top on it.  I told him that both his directions and the website video on how to use it say to shake with the lid on it.  The last thing i heard him say was i need to learn to follow directions as he hung up on me.  This stuff could hurt somebody, and to make matters worse, there was not a single warning that i found as to how dangerous this stuff actually is.  I would think there needs to be warnings all over this stuff after what it did to me.  It seems that this stuff is readily available to be purchased by anybody of any age.  I was lucky enough to know what to do when it happened due to my lab experience and training.  I hope that this helps and in the very least that this company has to put an MSDS or a warning label on this dangerous product. The website is www.odorknockout.com.  Thanks.
justification: The incident resulted in chemical burns, severe respiratory distress, and other injuries, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
I cleaned my stainless steel sink with Stainless Steel Magic. My kitchen, dinning room, living room area is aprox. 700 sq. ft. At 3:30 in the afternoon I was walking with a friend. I told her my chest felt heavy and I was having a hard time taking a deep breath as the day progressed I felt worse. The next morning 10-19-2010, I made an appointment with my doctor. I was very uncomfortable taking a deep breath and felt very weak. I showed my doctor the cleaner I used. She asked her nurse to call the Magic American Corp emergency number that was on the can. The nurse asked if there was any
petroleum in their product. The person told her there was not, yet right on the can it says petroleum distillates. The nurse then called the poison control center. They called the doctors office back 3 times to check on how I was doing. My doctor listened to my heart which was beating rapidly, took blood pressure,  took blood, asked me to blow into a devise 3 times, she said I had the breath of a 90 year old.  I am 64. She did an EKG, the top part of my heart was beating out of sync with the bottom part of my heart. She did two chest x-rays which showed the bottom part of my lungs were burned. She ordered a steroid iv drip.

I have never had any problems with my lungs or heart. Previous to this I took a brisk half hour walk 5 days a week. It took me until just recently to be able to walk at my normal brisk walking speed. I would like to go back to the doctor to make sure my lungs are healed but can't afford to with the bill I already have.

incident_description: The Samsung Dryer DV448AEP is a fire hazard waiting to happen and considering they have sold thousands of these there are thousands of fire hazards waiting to happen across the US. This is becoming a well documented problem online and there is obviously a major design flaw with this dryer. The symtoms are loss of heat and an excessive amount of lint that most people only notice in there duct vent on the exterior of their home. However, what most people do not realize is that the majority of the lint that is not being captured by the lint filter is actually ending up on the inside of the dryer itself literally covering the electrical components, motors, and heating element!!! that's right take any one of these dryers apart after 100 hours of use and you will find thick layers of charred lint resting on the heating element. I know because I have to do this every 3 to 4 months so we can dry our clothes properly. Upon inspecting the drum of the dryer I have found that the drum itself is supported by rubber wheels. The design of these wheels allows the drum to sag along the bottom of the felt liner creating a gap of about 1/2 inch. This gap allows lint to penetrate into the dryer box frame where it is blown around until it finds something warm and electrical to cling to. Mark my words, if this one goes ignored someone is going to lose their life taking a nap waiting for the dryer to finish.
justification: The description highlights a significant fire hazard due to a design flaw, with potential for severe outcomes including death, and mentions widespread occurrence.

incident_description: My house in Hannibal, MO had a GE 225 amp main breaker loadcenter installed in approximately 1980 with all copper wire, there was no aluminum wiring in the panel.  The panel was known generically in the industry as a 20-40 panel which means it had 20 full size circuit breaker spaces for GE Type THQL circuit breakers, but will accomodate up to 40 circuits when using the thin Type THQP GE circuit breakers.  The panel caught on fire on the morning of April 24, 2011.  All wiring connections in the panel had last been checked and tightened in 2009.  The nearest interconnected smoke detector was approximately 4 feet from the panel and alerted my renters immediately.  Without delay, my renters ran to the basement assuming the electric clothes dryer that was running was the problem.  They opened the electric panel door to turn off the circuit breaker to the dryer and flames came from the panel.  A nearby dry chemical fire extinguisher was used and extinguished the electrical fire.  I live approximately 110 miles from Hannibal so my renters immediately called me.  I instructed them to call the Hannibal Board of Public Works and have the power disconnected at the pole, the BPW responded immediately and performed the disconnect.  I then called Lampton Electric Co. in Hannibal ([REDACTED]).  The owner of Lampton Electric, [REDACTED], responded immediately to make sure the panel had been made safe.  The next morning, Lampton Electric began work changing the electric service.  There were no injuries and property damage was minor because my renters were home, but this incident could have easily been much worse had they not been there.  I have attempted by email to notify both GE Corporate, asking for them to notify their product liability department, and GE Industrial, the division of GE that manufactures these panels and circuit breakers.  GE has yet to ackowledge my report.  I have pictures of the panel and circuit breaker that apparently caused the fire and also retained the GE burnt panel and circuit breakers.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the electrical panel with no injuries, but potential for significant damage if renters were not present.

incident_description: Was performing routing maintenance (belt replacment) on my Eureka 4870K vacuum s/n UU110827045860. Noticed power switch was not always working (stuck on or off). I removed the housing and discovered the crimp lugs on the power switch showed evidence of overheating (blackened, melting). Further the insulation on the wiring was melted back. Noted the plastic housing was sligtly melted inside in the vicinity of the switch. Also the exposed copper wire was oxidized. Replaced one crimp lug.  This is a safety defect. Either manufacturing (crimp not applied correctly, oxidation on wire prior to crimping) or a design defect (incorrectly sized wire, incorrect crimp lug). Mfr of crimp lug is TYCO, AMP p/n 2-520129-2, which is designed for 18-22 ga wire. Note 18 ga wire is marginally sized (depending on the reference document consulted) for 12 amp (rating on apppliance) for motors (surge currents common), especially when PVC insulation (low melting point, flammable, toxic smoke) is used.
justification: The incident involved a safety defect with evidence of overheating and melting, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Used resovle foam carpet cleaner (UPC 19200-00619-4) to clean spot on the carpet and accidentally sprayed some small amount on right hand. Used product before with good results, but it was first time to spray rather small amount on hand. Bad reaction resulted that seemed immunologic in nature based on kinetics of skin reaction, including rather large edema vesicles in hair follicles and/or erythematous spots all over right hand. The reaction has persisted now since the initial exposure on May 1, 2011, for almost two weeks, with edema gone, but redness still persisting. No previous history of any allergies to cosmetic, personal care or household products. No ingredients on the container, NO WARNING ON THE CONTAINER AS TO ITS SKIN ALLERGY AND IRRITATION POTENTIAL, No warning to handle product with gloves. 
1. Reported incident to company and did not get appropriate response: "Please be assured that all of our products are manufactured from the finest ingredients available, under the most rigid quality control procedures and in full compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.  In addition, all products are extensively reviewed for potential health and safety concerns. The sensitivity of a person?s skin is variable and difficult to predict.  It?s quite possible to develop sensitivities to a product even after years of use.  With this in mind, we ensure that our product is sufficiently labeled for proper use."  
2. Downloaded MSDS and ingredient listing from Reckitt Benckiser product information site. As to the PPE needed symbol B was on the MSDS, but no explanation as to the scale or PPE needed. Picture label shows ungloved hand.
3. MSDS warning was found which does indicate similar type of reaction occurred before to other customers or during clinical testing evaluation of the product: "redness, edema, drying, defatting and cracking of the skin" 
4. INCI ingredients: contains ingredients not found in the PCPC database: "carboxylated polymer" with incorrect function given as "polymer" and "dipropylene glycol phenyl ether", which at least one of its manufacturers does not recommend using in consumer products: "Consumer exposure to products containing dipropylene glycol phenyl ether: not sold for direct consumer use. They are industrial products for commercial applications only. Consumer contact is unlikely.ÃÂ AND from the same product assessment for the ingredient: ÃÂSkin contact ÃÂ Brief contact may cause severe skin burns. Symptoms may include pain, severe local redness, and tissue damage. Prolonged skin contact may cause slight skin irritation with local rednessÃÂ.
5. So-called "Safe ingredients" wrt sodium silicate: in 2005ÃÂs report ÃÂCosmetic Ingredient Review (CIR) Expert Panel recognized the irritation potential of these ingredients, especially in leave-on products.ÃÂ Contains other ingredients with recognized irritation potential, skin allergy potential and contact urticaria potential. Many ingredients do not have their proper function listed on Product Information Site.

Overall, objectively the labeling of the product is NOT in regulatory compliance at the very least. The product caused very unpleasant, long lasting and adverse reaction affecting entire surface of the hand consisting with reactions reported for individual ingredients.  AE was not properly handled by the company within the post-marketing surveillance program, as no follow up with a proper questioner sent out to the consumer was performed upon AE reported to the company.  

I do hope you will eventually investigate this product as to its safety to consumers.

Best regards,
[REDACTED], Ph.D.

incident_description:
The Shark S3501 has the potential to be a "bomb" that projects superheated steam - similar to the kind of soda pop bottle bombs that kids can make.  

My wife has been using the Shark S3501 steam mop for several months now.  After using it for less than a minute, steam stopped coming out.  She "pumped" the handle several times to prime it as the instructions suggest, but nothing.  She unplugged the unit and let it sit for 2-3 minutes to "cool down" as the manual suggests.  She opened the water unit plug to see if pressure had built up.

She then pressed the mophead release button which is directly above the mophead and the head literally shot off across the room along with ejecting superhot steam in a narrow stream. Fortunately, her hands were above the unit not below or in front of it otherwise she would have suffered serious burns.

We then carefully recreated the same circumstances.  The same outcome occurred a second time.  However, when we tried to video it this morning, the seal at the nozzle itself is broken (probably from being forcefully ejected) and steam leaks out the nozzle rather than becoming trapped.

The manual says nothing about this dangerous situation. The final sentence of quick start tip 16 says, "If you live in areas with hard water we recommend using distilled water", but no mention is made of the potential consequences.  Additionally, the advice to "prime the pump" if no steam is coming out absolutely contributes to the dangerous situation.

My wife is a nurse practitioner and has seen steam-related injuries in her practice.  This product creates a very dangerous situation for consumers and the product documentation actually can make that situation worse.
justification: The incident involved the ejection of superheated steam which could have caused serious burns, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) as the issue was reproducible and the manual's advice exacerbates the risk.

a kitchen cabinet catch. The ball catches were supplied with a set of interior double doors, and were mounted by
the supplier (Brockway-Smith Co. ["Brosco"]) in the upper edge of the door with the ball facing up. Several weeks
ago the ball on one of the doors popped out and launched itself across the room, hitting the floor. I ordered a
replacement catch and received two on 3123. On 3/24, when my 5-year-old daughter opened the door, the ball
popped out of the new catch, striking her in the hand and leaving a minor bruise.
I have enclosed the second catch which came apart. The silver ball normally is held in place by the slotted gold
collar, with about 1/3 of the ball protruding to catch on a doorframe-mounted plate. Evidently the slotted collar is
not sufficient to prevent the spring from pushing the ball through.
My concern with the safety of this product is threefold:
1} Risk of injury.
2) Risk of damage to anything the flying ball hits.
3) Choking hazard for a young child who picks up the ball.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (bruise) to a child's hand, and there is a clear risk of recurrence given the product's design flaw.

incident_description: My 25 month old son was standing in the Learning Tower and slid his foot in the space between the platform and the side of the tower.  Neither he nor I could get his foot out.  I ended up dismantling the tower so I could get him out.  This required having someone else hold him so he didn't fall to the ground when I pulled the side of tower away from the rest of the structure.
justification: The child was stuck but not injured, requiring intervention to free him.

incident_description: Safety brake on Performax 90206 sliding compound miter saw stopped working suddenly. Blade continues to rotate after motor stops. Also detected slippage when powering up the saw. This saw was the replacement for an older Performax saw had safety issues as well, and was recalled by the CSPC. incident_description:
Vacuum Cleaner is Eureka model 4870 series upright.  
the on/off switch suddenly stopped working.  the result was that the vacuum could be turned on only by plugging in the power cord (at which time it worked normally) and turned off by unplugging the power cord.

the switch wires were touching and the insulation had fused and bare copper was showing on one

the wires are not the right size for the 12amp rating or the insulation is insufficient.

When I went online to see if I could find a replacement, I discovered there is a recall of a very similar looking engine to mine. incident_description: Consumer purchased a "Brush Hawg" from Lowes a couple of months ago.  Consumer used it to clean his grill approximately 10 times. On 3/19/11, the consumer's wife was grilling chicken for a dinner salad.  When the consumer bit into a piece of chicken that she cooked on the grill, something stuck deep into the roof of his mouth.  The Consumer states that he couldn't get what was stuck in his mouth with his fingers so he had his wife rush to get a pair of tweezers.  Very fortunately the consumer was able to reach in and pull out what turned out to be a half inch piece of wire that broken off the Brush Hawg.  It scared he and his wife very much.  The consumer mentioned his concern if it got lodged deeper in his throat?  The next morning, the consumer examined the Brush Hawg and found a wire that looks as if it was one that broke.  The broken end that was stuck in his mouth is the same size as the missing segment and is the same gauge and color as well.  The consumer further mentioned that is that piece of wire had gone any deeper, he would have needed special surgery to remove it. The consumer said that this product didn't have a warning label on it. There was a large power outage in Johnson City, TN on 4.25.11, when the power came back on, the heater apparently turned itself on and started an electrical fire at outlet where it was plugged in.  The fire started at the outlet and burned back into the outlet (the back of the socket wasn't burned). incident_description:
I often use a small humidifier made by Air Innovations, model number KS30U-06C. This week, as usual, I left the humidifier on while I was at work. I have never had any issue with this product in the past and I have in no way used this product in any way other than for its intended purpose. When I came home from work, my entire apartment was filled with a terrible smell, like something was burning. I immediately identified the source of the smell as coming from the Air Innovations humidifier. Under normal operation the unit senses when the water level in the tank is low and shuts off the internal components. On this day, the unit had run out of water but had failed to shut off its internal components allowing it to become extremely hot underneath the water tank where the operating components are located and to melt the plastic inside the unit. The unit's casing was also extremely hot to the touch. Under normal operation with a full tank of water the unit's LED indicator light is blue, showing that the the unit is in operation and has enough water. When the unit runs out of water, the unit shuts off and the LED indicator light turns red. On the day of this incident, the unit was out of water but the LED indicator light was still blue and the unit was still in operation, it failed to shut itself off.

If I hadn't intervened when I did, the unit would have melted straight through to the carpet and would have eventually started a fire. I contacted the company the next day and they, without any questions whatsoever, took down my address and offered to send me a similar model upon the return of the defective unit. I assume this action was made in an effort to avoid legal action.

I fear that this may happen to others and cause serious harm.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning humidifier that could have started a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:

On July 16y, 2008 they swapped out the unit and charged us for labor not the unit. 

On February 2,2011 the unit let off a burning smell and stopped , a Carrier rep visited the site and determined a repeat event of the first unit. They returned 2 days later with parts and replaced burnt wires, capacitor and other electrical components. Again we were charged for travel and service and labor. 

I contacted Carried on numinous occasions and they promised to address this issue as of this date no action as been taken. 
The unit is now letting off a burning smell once again, smells like something electrical burning.

Carrier continues to promise they will have someone contact me, they also claim I should not have been charged for any of these services but have done nothing to remedy the situation.

Can someone help me as I fear this poses a threat to my family's well being and is a fire hazard.
justification: The AC unit has repeatedly emitted burning smells and required repairs, indicating a recurring fire hazard, though no injury or death has been reported yet.

The Sunbeam convertible iron+steamer [Model: GCSBRS-104 Date Code:C219J-T]  I purchased from a Target store on 12/10/2010 started mildly malfunctioning e.g. not heating up adequately in mid March 2011 and on 04/16/2011 started dripping hot water and shorting out. This accident was accompanied by a loud gurgling sound and hiss, presumably from the leaking steam. Upon setting the product down to cool, I detached the steamer top using the dial at the base, and observed that water had indeed leaked into the heating chamber.

I observed that a similar model [Model: GCSBRS-103] distributed by Bed, Bath and Beyond was recalled as of Feb 11th 2011. I would like to request that the -104 model, sold at Target stores, be also investigated for similar short-outs and the recall list be expanded in investigation results are positive.
justification: The user was singed by sparks, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
I recently had an EASYWATER No Salt Water Conditioning System installed in my home.  The installer recommended putting the device in a closet as it was close to the water pipe.  After the plumber left I went into the closet to prepare to move items back into the closet.  I checked the EASYWATER device and the heat sink on the device was hot to the touch.  It was so hot that I had to remove my hand after about ten seconds.  I became concerned about having the device in the closet next to clothing items, particularly synthetics.

I contacted EASYWATER and asked if there were any safety precautions about installing the device in confined spaces due to the heat issue and was told there were none as the device was meant to be placed in a garage or outside. I was told that the heat sink reaches 120 degrees and that is considered normal.  I believe that this device should have precautions in the installation and owners manual that address the heat issue - 1.  Do not install in confined spaces or near flammable items.  2.  Do not install in areas where children or pets may come in contact withe the device.
justification: The device's heat sink reaches high temperatures, posing a potential fire hazard if installed near flammable materials, but no actual incident or injury has occurred.

incident_description:
On March 8th, 2011, I went to cut a section of steel chain link fence pipe at my home.  I was using a Cal-hawk metal cutoff wheel on a Milwaukee 4 1/2 inch angle grinder (Model 6148).  My complaint is that the Calhawk cut-off wheel came apart while in use on a high speed grinder.  I was not injured.

I installed the Cal-hawk cut off wheel on the angle grinder.  Specifically, a  4-1/2" CAL-HAWK CZCW4510 metal cut-off wheel.  I started to make my cut into the bare fence pipe.  I made about half of the cut when I noticed the wheel becoming wobbly.  I set the tool down and waited.  I unplugged it and then inspected the wheel.  In short, the wheel's cutoff material seperated from the metal ring it was attached to.  

I have pictures which I hope to upload.  The wheel is marked as being good until 14,000 rpm.  The maximum my angle grinder can turn is 10,000 rpm.  I'd be willing to mail you at my expense the wheel and component if you'd care to take a look.
justification: The cut-off wheel failed during use, but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is possible given the wheel's failure under rated conditions.

incident_description: I have a Four Seasons sunroom that was installed in 1998 using Cardinal Code 77 Insulating Glass that has reflected onto my newly installed dormer that has vinyl siding.  The vinyl siding is melting in the area above the sunroom.  There is a safety repair notice for this same product that involves reflecting onto cedar shingles and shakes causing fires.  It is my opinion and concern that if it can cause fires on cedar shingles or shakes it would also be able to melt vinyl siding and possibly also start a fire.
justification: The incident involves melting vinyl siding due to reflected sunlight, with a potential fire hazard mentioned, but no actual fire or injury reported.

incident_description:
I just purchased an

Aloha Breeze 
30" Hugger Ceiling Fan
Syle No 09315

from Walmart in 

Tucson, AZ  85710

I installed it Monday and tested it.  However, last night during regular operation it was emitting a hot smell.  Upon checking it I found the motor casing HOT to the touch.

I checked other ceiling fans to determine if this was usual and all other ceiling fan motor casings remained cool to the touch during operation.

Today, I also sent an email to:

ahitexaslg@aol.com

(an email address listed by you for an earlier recall of a Aloha Housewares product)
justification: The fan motor casing was hot to the touch, indicating a potential hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
This is in reference to a First Alert kitchen fire extinguisher I owned. It was touted as being able to put out a "kitchen or grease fire" On 12/4/10 My kitchen stove caught fire and I attempted to put the fire out using this product. It failed and the result was the entire loss not only of my home and contents, but the loss of our pet dog. People who buy this item should not feel secure about the ability of this product.
I have a fire report about this incident
justification: The incident resulted in the loss of a pet dog and complete destruction of the home, indicating a severity level of 4 (Death). The occurrence likelihood is considered rare (1) as such catastrophic failures are not common.

incident_description: Electric hot water heater seems to be creating hydrogen or other flamable gas which can be ignited at the faucet with a flame, such as a lit match or cigarette lighter.  This occurs when the hot water is not used for about a week, and hot water faucet sputters with gas and water for approximately the first five minutes when it is turned on.  Cold water supply exhibits no sputtering or gas in the water line, only the hot water.  This hot water behavior started about six months ago and did not clear up by itself and continues today.  The hot water tank is in the last year of its 10 year warranty so it is not new, but it is not antiquated.  Contacted GE hot water tank telephone support on 4/9/2011 but they were very unhelpful and disinterested in this kind of problem and said to just get a plumber.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to flammable gas buildup, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says was repairing ceiling in kitchen.  Consumer said when unit sprayed off it went everywhere but the ceiling.  Consumer said unit shot off like a volcano and it went everywhere but the ceiling.  Consumer said he used the product as directed but the product went everywhere but the ceiling.  Consumer said he almost fell off the ladder.  The consumer said he tried to contact the manufacturer but they never returned the message.
justification: The consumer almost fell off the ladder but there was no injury reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: After running this handheld vacuum for about 1 minute, it gets excessively hot. If you're using the shoulder strap that comes with it, the hot vacuum against your side can burn.
justification: The vacuum gets excessively hot and can cause burns if used with the shoulder strap, indicating a risk of injury.

incident_description:
I bought Door Knob Locks by KidCo a couple months ago.  These cover round door knobs and are supposed to deter "child from leaving or entering rooms".  I have a 22 month old who was able to easily open the door using the door knob lock  to do so.  As a note, my 22 month old is a preemie with an adjusted age of 19  months and definitely has no special skills that would better enable her to open doors or defeat safety products.  The design of this lock is round with tabs on one end.  If you squeeze the tabs, it grips the round knob, allowing you to turn it.  The tabs actually make it easier to open than if there were nothing covering the knob.  I contacted the company, this is their response:  

"I'm sorry the Door Knob Locks did not work in your situation. The locks are
recommended up to 24 months but sometimes children like your child are so
smart they can figure out the way to open the lock. Please let me know if
your S352 Door Knob Lock is clear or white and I will send you replacement
to return to the store.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]"

I don't appreciate the company's attempt at flattery to cover up the fact that NOWHERE on the packaging does it say "only good up to 24 months".  If anything, it's very misleading as it specifically says "child", which does NOT exclusively mean "infant".  I really believe these knobs create a false sense of security, creating dangerous situations for curious infants.
justification: The incident involves a child safety product failing to perform as expected, creating a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Hoover P.A.W.S. upright vaccuum with cord rewind.  I purchased this vaccuum approximately 3 weeks ago and used it 4 times.  While using the hose attachment the vaccuum shifted and pulled in an article of clothing.  In seconds, the vaccuum began to smoke and spark as the belt burned through.  Luckily, there was no damage to my home and no one was hurt as I noticed the incident immediately and took action.
justification: The vacuum malfunctioned, causing smoke and sparks, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
Caller purchased new type detergent a bit over a month before this report, had been using it for approximately two or three weeks and had noticed blue dots & blue residue on some of the clothing especially whites and mostly white underwear.
After a two or three week time frame her husband was complaining that he had a rash everywhere that his underwear touched and everywhere his socks touched.
She switched detergents to research source, husbands rash improved and went away in about one week.
Caller would like this researched, investigated and possibly recalled to avoid deeper problems with children's/baby's clothing or someone who wouldn't be able to afford to replace the detergent.
Caller did not go to doctor, wife put first aid cream on him.
justification: The husband developed a rash from the detergent, which required first aid cream but no medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Loaded dryer with twin size mattress cover. Within minutes smoke was seeping out from around the seal of the door. No obvious flames were seen. However, smoke billowed out when I opened the door to the dryer.  Upon inspection, found lint vent piping in back of dryer clogged and lint accumulating in the cabinet of the dryer including, but not limited to, near the heating element.  The top layer of the lint was charred.
justification: Smoke was observed but no flames or injuries occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: GE washing machine spins and rocks violently around room when spin cycle load is off balance, there is no automatic safety switch to stop machine.  Machine moves violently around room hitting other objects and wall, and can only be stopped by a person opening the lid. This is hazardous to fingers and hands and toes and feet or even a child standing near the machine. The noise and violence of this condition not safe and should not be tolerated by design. I have called GE, the manufacture, and this model of washing machine does not have an automatic safety shutoff for this condition.
justification: The machine's violent movement can cause injury to people nearby, making it a level 3 severity.

incident_description:
Smelled a burning smell in the home after starting a load of clothes in our LG clothes dryer
Model # DLG1320W Gas dryer.

Purchased the dryer in 2009.

Dryer is properly vented with a flexible foil hose and cleaned often.

Internal lint trap is cleaned before every load.

Took back panel off dryer and observed a large lint buildup in base (floor) of dryer that had caught fire while dryer was being used.  

Frequently clean in and around dryer and appliance is not in an unusually heavy dust area.

All of the lint buildup appeared to be excess lint that the trap inside the dryer is unable to capture.

Lint dust settles on the internal floor of the dryer, underneath the drum, where a large majority of the wiring and drum belt/motor sit.

Completely vacuumed out and removed all of the lint that could be reached and reinstalled back panel of dryer.
justification: The incident involved a lint buildup that caught fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While using our Euro-Pro Steam Mop this afternoon I smelled rubber burning. I noticed smoke coming from the unit casing where the electrical cord attaches. Part of the casing was to hot to touch and the cord had begun to melt.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting components, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My portable electric heater overheated and scorched the carpet
justification: The heater overheated and caused property damage (scorched carpet) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Targus Universal Wall Power Adapter for Laptops started to smoke my laptop and when pulled from laptop cracked. Model of the adapter is APA23US. Laptop is ruined (Lenovo 8922-C300)
justification: The adapter caused smoke and ruined the laptop, indicating significant damage but no reported injury.

incident_description:
Nov 2010 compressor in back of pickup truck, running only a few minutes when someone else saw the fire flaming from the unit.  They grab it by handle and pulled it to ground before damage and possible explosion.  I called Sears right away and informed them that there was a major problem with this unit and their response was terrible..It must have been our fault and its out of warranty ..very disturbed at their response!!!!  So not a surprise when recall letter came. 
I still have the compressor. I have multi pictures of the damage. I have tried to go through the recall process and an getting no where, they don't seem to know what to do with one already burnt.  They want to rebuilt it, which I will not allow.  I will not have this unit rebuilt after such a fire.  I have requested only a $200 credit from Sears towards the purchase of another compressor (not of that style) from them.  THEY FLATLY REFUSED, but I can have 10% off another.  I need to buy a new compressor and I am not going to continue business with Sears any longer.  Customer satisfaction and safety is not an issue with this company.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was addressed before further damage.

incident_description: I have a Federal Pacific Panel in my home that I purchased in July 2010. Home was built in 1976. I started to notice my son's bathroom and room lights getting dim every now and then. One day one of my son's went to turn on the bathroom light on and the 3 rooms that are connected had their power out. Only thing on at the time was a small tv and a small fish tank motor. I checked the panel, tried to flip the Breaker (The GFI one with a 15 volt) no response. I then shut the main power off, took the panel face off, and saw that the GFI Breaker had caught on fire! This could have destroyed my new home if it got out of control.
justification: The incident involved a breaker catching fire, which could have led to significant damage but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
I'm a building inspector for a municipality and have identified a residential product on many homes in our community, as well as others I've heard of, that are failing and posing a safety hazard for homeowners. The product is a window well that serves as an emergency egress corridor for people needing to get out of a basement in the event of a fire, etc. The particular design, referred to as a Well Install (or EasyWell) Buck Mount system is being sold by Boman Kemp (www.boman-kemp.com, 800.733.7886). I believe they patented this product as I've not seen another manufacturer connected to this type of sytem.

We have responded to complaints or been made aware of numerous homeowners (between a dozen and two dozen) that have their window wells caving in from one or both sides allowing mud and water to enter the well. This creates a compromise of the well's ability to provide a safe exit for residents and even more so when they, in an attempt to stop the failure, install braces across the well that then further prevent it's purpose as an emergency exit. When our residents approach their builders, who then turn to the manufacturer, they are invariably told that it is not a manufacturer's problem. However, when we spoke to a technical person at Boman Kemp he told us that they had a problem with a fastener they were using and had to change it to one that would not shear as readily as the previous screws did. Unfortunately it would appear that they sold them in their inferior state for years and sold many, many of them to variou builders in our community and beyond including Cambridge, Ryland, Town and Country and Pulte Homes.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with window wells failing, but no injuries or deaths are mentioned, only potential risks.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he was working with torch for about 7 minutes when consumer tried to turn off the torch the torch bottom did not work (reason why unknown) the flames was high leading consumer burning his right hand.  Consumer was able to put off the flames by through the torch into the pod of water.

Consumer feels that the micro torch could poses a fire hazard.
justification: The consumer suffered a burn injury to the right hand due to the torch malfunction, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
The receiving unit for Remote controlled Hampton Bays Ceiling fan manufactured for Home Depot overheated and the unit partially melted. This is the third time within three years that the unit and/or replacement unit overheated.

The UPC # for the fan is 7182 1204 9136 and the model number for the receiving unit is UC 7067RC.

I reported this to Home Depot Customer Service and they state that they had not heard of anyone else having this issue. However, when I went online to research the receiving unit model number, there seems to be a number of consumer complaints about the unit overheating. This obviously can be a potential fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves overheating and partial melting of the unit, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: While ironing clothes, the unit began smoking heavily and shut off. I unplugged the unit. There was no apparent fire seen on the outside of the unit.
justification: The iron began smoking but was unplugged without injury or fire, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Several months ago our Amana gas dryer started to sometimes give us a very strong shock when we touched the metal drum inside. We thought that this was just from static electricity and continued to use the dryer.

A couple days ago the dryer made a very bright electrical spark, which tripped the electrical breaker. I am skilled at fixing appliances, so I unplugged the dryer and opened up the front of it to see if I could figure out what was wrong.

There are a set of wires that come through the upper-right hand corner of the dryer to the door area. These wires go to the door switch and the light that is mounted above the door. Three of the wires had not been routed properly through the dryer and were hanging against the drum. Upon further inspection I could see that one of the wires had been worn completely through the metal, one was halfway through the metal, and the third was just starting to wear on the metal. There was a burn mark on the drum where the wires had come into contact with it and made the spark.

Luckily, the only damage done was the shocks we received. Under different circumstances this defect could have caused a fire and/or killed someone.
justification: The incident involved strong shocks and a potential fire hazard, but no serious injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while using the washing machine for approximately 30 - 45 mins she heard a weird noise emitting from the unit, she attempted to turn it off but it became difficult it finallly turned off and she was able to open the door and discovered that the glass on the door has exploded inside and was mixed in with her garments.

3/22/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer at customer support and was advised to contact the Claims department,  and the Claims dept advised that she should provide pictures and a report of the incident.

Conumer stated that the Claims department advised that there had been reports about this incident before.

Consumer feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a washing machine door glass exploding, but no injuries were reported. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) due to prior reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: Steam mop starts and stops and pours out excessive amounts of steam due to mophead getting clogged or otherwise? Also burnt plastic at end of mop handle also could be what caused clogging perhaps.  Not sure exactly.  Could also be too hot.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning steam mop with potential for minor hazards like burns, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Elite, high efficiency washer with the matching dryer 10 months ago at Sears. Each item was priced at $917.99, so this was no small purchase!  Everything went fine until two days ago. I was washing linens (2 king sheets and a bed liner, no comforter), when I heard an earth shattering BOOM in the garage where my units are hooked up. I raced to see if my house exploded and found the washer rotated 1/4 turn from the wall, the entire top of the washer (the part with the lid AND control panel) was on the ground, and the drum has collapsed inside the unit!! I was scared to death!! I had to unplug the unit to get it to turn off. Thankfully, it JUST MISSED crashing into my hot water heater. 

I called the warranty number that is listed in the manual, and a repair technician is scheduled to come out in four days to look at the unit. REPAIR?? Are you kidding?? I am so traumatized by this incident, I don't know if I trust ANY "so-called" high efficiency washer or dryer units, especially of the Kenmore variety. The representative that took the info said she has NEVER heard of anything like that happening. I have done some research online, and apparently a powerful spin cycle can cause a washer to EXPLODE!! I feel very strongly that this product needs to be looked at and considered for possible recall.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and emotional distress but no physical injury.

incident_description:
While standing on the ladder which was on a cement floor, the side rail of the ladder bowed to the outside.  [REDACTED]. The side hinges buckled [REDACTED]. It caused the victim to fall backwards to receive  a laceration to elbow, head and knee (which knee or elbow was not provided).

He went to see his Primary Care Physician a day later where they performed an MRI on his knee, a Cat Scan on his head and since he had broken his elbow previously they monitored that as well.

Consumer believes the ladder is dangerous and could really hurt someone.  

The results were not provided and the firm was not contacted. He currently still has the ladder but no repairs have been made
justification: The victim suffered injuries requiring medical attention, including a laceration and monitoring of previous injuries, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the ladder's condition and the incident details.

incident_description: We purchased the Dylan Rug (8' x 10' wool) from Pottery Barn in January 2005. Over time, we began to notice that the rug smelled like burnt rubber. When the smell became unbearable, we looked on-line to see if we could find out a cause or possible solution. To our astonishment, we found that thousands of people across the country have had the same problem. Our concern is that our daughter developed chronic allergies & cough around the time we put the rug down. We never would have made the connection had we not read of countless others whose children suffered in households with these Pottery Barn/Pottery Barn Kids rugs. From what we've read and been told by Pottery Barn customer service, they are aware of a problem with the break down of the latex backing and have since changed their process. I never received any kind of recall notice about the rugs that they considered to be problematic.
justification: The incident describes a child developing chronic allergies & cough linked to the rug, indicating an injury (severity 3). The widespread reports suggest the occurrence likelihood is high (4).

incident_description:
Hoover has recalled the S3755 vacuum due to short in the wiring.

I have a Hoover WindTunnel S3765, and I believe it has the same issue.  The wand power will not work or connect, and I have the wiggle the hose to get the connection to work.  This is basically the same model as the S3755 that is included in the recall.  I believe this other WindTunnel canister vac has the same problem and should be recalled.

This problem has reported in many online reviews of this product, so this is not an isolated issue.
justification: The incident involves a wiring issue causing malfunction but no reported injuries, aligning with severity level 2. The problem is widespread based on online reviews, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
Sunbeam SFH111 portable electric heater was plugged into 110v wall outlet but turned off, and was on a stand about 1 ft above the floor. Apparently the cat pulled the cord and the heater dropped to the carpet below. Sparks shot out of the front and back (there are black marks on both the front and back of the unit) and caught the carpet on fire (there's a burned and melted spot there now). The unit was unplugged from the wall, the sparks stopped, and the small carpet fire was extinguished. This all happened in a matter of seconds, so the resulting damage to the carpet was pretty insignificant- about 1/2" diameter of carpet damaged, but had we not been in the next room to hear it fall and spark and see the cat running out I imagine the house would have burned to the ground.

The switch on top was in the "OFF" position the entire time. Looking inside the unit, it looks like one of the heating coils is on a metal fan blade.
justification: The incident caused minor damage to the carpet and posed a significant fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Mr. [REDACTED] called me with a concern that his Kidde 0910 smoke detector failed to activate in the presence of a large amount of smoke caused when a pot of hotdogs he was boiling ran dry.

While I often get similar complaints and typically explain how ionization and photo-electric smoke detectors work differently I did tell Mr. [REDACTED] that I could use a commercialized canned smoke product to test his detector . . . after he told me that Kidde had suggested he check with Home Depot where he purchased these detectors to see if they would test the detector. 

Following the directions on the can of CRC Smoke Test I held the can two feet away from the detector and sprayed for 5 seconds with no results. I then sprayed a second time per the instructions for another 5 seconds with no audible alarm. I then checked to insure there was a battery in the smoke detector and tested that the alarm was receiving power and had an audible warning signal by depressing the test button to which there was a positive response.

As a control . . . I tested a BRK brand dual ionization/photo-electric smoke detector in a smiliar fashion and this detector activated within 2-3 seconds. A second test with a First Alert (BRK Brand) smoke ionization detector a little while later also activated within 2-3 seconds.

While many smoke detector issues can often be chalked up to problems with maintainance or the installation I am a little concerned as to whether this is a defective smoke detector . . . or simply a fluke in my testing methodology . . . concerned enough to send this report.
justification: The incident involved a smoke detector failing to activate, but no injury or damage occurred. Similar issues are reported occasionally, indicating a possible but not frequent occurrence.

incident_description: The control box on top of the Heater has overheated twice and fried the wires. This same problem has been reported with the water heater a number of times on Lowes website.
justification: The incident involves equipment damage (overheated control box and fried wires) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Heater was in use for about 3 hours at a setting of 5 (highest is 6).  Cord and plug end became hot enough to start to burn the skin upon touching it, and the plug end was melting.  Room smelled like burned plastic.
justification: The heater caused burns upon touching and emitted a burning smell, indicating a potential injury risk but no actual injury reported.

incident_description: My husband and I installed 6 window guards from Safety 1st (First) and ALL 6 failed.  The window guard is a device that screws in to the drywall or frame next to a window and has two settings, one that allows easy movement and the other that restricts movement of the window at whatever point it is screwed in to the wall.  It is a plastic device marketed as a window lock.  My 3 year-old son was able to lift the window when the lock was engaged and bypass the lock.  The window guard was useless.  We thought we had a defective lock so we bought more.  Every lock we used was broken by raising the window with out any force other than usual pressure to open the window.  This window lock is absolutely a failure and any parent who installs it in their home will have a false sense of security.  This failure can have fatal results.
justification: The window guards failed to function as intended, posing a potential risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: sears air commpressor burned up ............  about 7 years ago my 13 month old compressor,  just out of warranty  , burns up after only 10 hours of operation  i took the compressor /motor to sears to fix  they could not fix it  it would have to be replaced  it was going to cost more than the compressor cost,,  so   i saved the compressor in my shed  and about a month ago i get a recall notice for my model number compressor ,,  i never abused the unit  so i knew there had to be a problem with them
justification: The incident involved a compressor burning up without causing injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the recall notice indicating a known issue.

incident_description:
Cordless drill caught on fire 15 minutes after light use.

Harbor Freight Drill Master Item #40209 14.4V Cordless Drill 

I was using the cordless drill to drive a couple small screws (very light use). I put the drill down and came back about 15 minutes later and picked up the drill and noticed it was extremely hot even though it was not being used. About the same time I picked the drill up, smoke started coming out of the charging port. I attempted to remove the battery from the drill which was difficult because it was actively burning and the plastic was melting. I was able to get the battery disconnected where I ran down the steps of a high rise and got the battery pack outside. It was still smoking as I took it outside and I could see liquid coming from the top of the battery pack.

At the time of this failure the battery was probably half charged. I am completely shocked the battery pack started on fire.
justification: The drill caught fire and caused significant damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
About two months ago I installed several hard wired smoke alarms in my house.  Within two days of the installation, we had our first false alarm.  Since then we have a false alarm at least 5 to 10 times per month.  It is ALWAYS at night, between the hours of 11pm and 5am, usually at 2 or 3 am.

These are not battery chirps.  Often times one alarm will sound one blast, and then no more.  Sometimes an alarm will sound several blasts, but they are random in timing.  Other times it will be a full alarm, which then sets off all the other alarms.

The frequency of the alarms seem to have no pattern.  Sometimes they will sound multiple false alarms in one night, then go several days or a week with no false alarms.  The false alarms originate from different alarms, sometimes our bed room, sometimes the kids' bedroom.

I installed the alarms exactly as the instructions said to.  The alarms are at the proper height.  They are not near any bathroom or the kitchen.  The HVAC vents are on the other side of the room so there are no wind currents.  The attic is well insulated with an R value of 45.  The alarms are far away from all sources of EMF or RFI.

This is a very dangerous issue.  Frequent false alarms are like the alarms "crying wolf".  If they alarm for a real fire they will likely be ignored, creating extreme risk to life.  The false alarms are also likely to cause the removal of the alarm, leaving people at a much higher risk of death from fire.

Upon researching the exact make and model of alarm I purchased, I found an amazing amount of people having the same problem.  The alarm has a rating of 1.2 out of 5 stars on Home Depot's website, and EVERY review talks about false alarm issues.

This is a very serious issue.  I feel it is only a matter of time before a serious injury or fatality happens because people are disabling or ignoring these alarms.  This product, especially since it is a safety product, needs to have some sort of corrective action taken.  It is a safety product required by law, that may actually increase risk.

Thank you
[REDACTED]
justification: Frequent false alarms pose a risk of being ignored during a real fire, potentially leading to injury or death, though no actual harm has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Motor blew up sending pieces of the motor flying all over the place.  One hit a worker on the back of his neck.    No medical assistance needed.

Consumer feels that the sliding compound miter saw could pose an unsafely hazard.
justification: A worker was hit by flying motor pieces but no medical assistance was needed, indicating a minor injury.

incident_description: Plugged in Holmes Ceramic heater model number 4077.  It immediately sparked and shot flames out of heater where hot air escapes.  Sparks shot out from outlet.  Product had been placed on wood surface, and no extension cord was in use.  The outlet is working fine and not the problem.
justification: The heater sparked and shot flames, indicating a significant incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Victim was exposed to carbom monxide due to a faulty furnace.
justification: Exposure to carbon monoxide can be fatal, hence the severity level is 4.

incident_description:
On March 30, 2011, the hinge on the glass door on our IKEA wall-mounted cabinet suddenly released, just missing smashing my wife's fingers as she was withdrawing food from the cabinet.  As she is an arm amputee, any injury to her only upper limb would be very devastating.  The failure of the so-called "Ferrari" hinge, found in IKEA's "[AVSIKT]" cabinet doors (glass doors, mounted to open horizontally upward), has been an ongoing complaint we have filed with IKEA since we installed the cabinets in 2006.  We have been given replacement hinges, which also fail.  What happens is the tension in the hinge, which is like a knee joint, gradually diminishes, causing the door to drop unexpectedly.  Repeated tightening of the hinge eventually causes the hinge to break, spilling small bearings all over the floor.  I have twice written to IKEA corporate, asking that a replacement design be developed.  IKEA no longer sells this model, so they must have realized the folly of the original design.  There is an online site devoted to IKEA customers, where they can share their comments and complaints:  IKEAFANS.COM.  I noted several other negative comments about this same issue, going back several years.

The reported incident is one of several dozen similar incidents, going back to 2006
justification: The incident involved a near-miss injury (severity level 2) and has been reported multiple times over several years, indicating a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I purchased 8 interior ceiling fans from home depot for the construction of my new home. This being the only lighting throughout the house. After installing the ceiling fans (CO in Oct 2009) I smelled smoke and did not identify where the smell was coming from for several months. I contacted Home depot about this as early as Nov 2009 and corporate around Mar 2010, Jun 2010, Nov 2010 and multiple times after that. The ceiling fans began to slow and some had stopped turning all together. I was told that the capacitors were the problem. I paid shipping for new capacitors. When the ceiling fan in the pantry sparked out I called an electrician around Jun 2010. Upon opening the fan it was found that the wiring broke out of the pull switch that apparently the fans internals had gotten hot enough to dry rot causing the switch to fail. My electricity was and has been checked three times and all three times from different electricians stating there is nothing wrong with my electrical wiring. Two of the electricans were sent by Home Depot and King of Fans, one in Aug 2010 and the other in Nov 2010. When the company finally understood the dire problem a representative was sent out on 23 Nov 2010. It was found that all of the fans were becoming hot enough internally to dry rot the fan switches, light switches, reverse switches and other internals. This combined with the capacitors exploding. In the fan that hung above my head in the bedroom, the capacitor had burnt and cracked open burning the internal wiring along with it. King of fans replaced the fan switches, light switches and capacitors in most of the fans. They diconnected the fans that were not replaced with new switches and capacitors. In less than a month the fans again started to slow in speed. The company finally replaced the fans taking the damaged ones on 4 Mar 2011. As the fans were being taken down the opening inspection exposed that the new switches had already bagan to crack and show damage. The capacitors and internal wires were extremely hot internally. The company took the damaged fans. I received word that they were sent to Ft Lauderdale for testing and nothing of note was found. Some of the fans are on the way back to China for further testing.
justification: The incident involved multiple ceiling fans malfunctioning and overheating, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
My son purchased an 8X10 "hand-tufted" 100% wool area rug for his apartment two years ago. I am writing to report my concern about the odor and possible health hazards inherent in "hand-tufted" rugs. From my recent research, I have learned that hand-tufted rugs have a secondary backing of latex and glues, which are often applied in foreign countries in an unregulated and haphazard manner, ultimately rendering many of them useless after a few years and potentially hazardous to human health as well. We were never told at the time of purchase (nor was there any written label or warning on the area rug) that "hand-tufted" means that the rug's backing contains latex and glues. If I had been told this, we wouldn't have purchased that rug. In fact, the term ÃÂhand-tuftedÃÂ is misleading since it positions these rugs in a positive light, avoiding disclosure of the materials in them which often lead to problems. I am particularly sensitive to these issues since I am a social science cancer researcher.

As I am particularly sensitive to chemicals, I smelled the backing of the rug when we purchased it to assure that there was no odor. However, in less than a year, my sonÃÂs apartment developed an acrid burning smell. It was so pervasive that he and his friends were unable to pinpoint the source of this odor which worsened over time. During our recent visit, we finally identified the culprit as the hand-tufted rug purchased at the Raleigh Capel Rugs store. The rug was in the path of a steam radiator, which blew hot air over the rug, possibly hastening the chemical breakdown process.
These odor issues are well-documented on the Internet by people who have had problems specifically with hand-tufted rugs similar to the one we bought, (most often from rugs purchased at Pottery Barn). Ours is not an isolated case. Those people reported the same problem with hand-tufted rugs, saying it often took several years to identify the source of the fumes. Like us, they did not suspect that a rug from a trustworthy and reputable company would have this problem. In all the cases I read about on the Internet, the smell began sometime after the first year they owned the carpet. Those who wrote about their experiences with hand-tufted rugs also were concerned that the pervasive odor equates with adverse health effects as is often the case. Indeed, my son, who has always been extremely healthy and able to fight off viruses, has had an unusually bad year for upper respiratory infections (sore throats, coughs,fevers, nasal congestion). 

When I purchased the carpet, I received no information, written or otherwise, warning of the problems with hand-tufted rugs. Last week, the same salesperson who sold me the rug admitted that the company has been aware of this problem for years. She said that the sales staff ÃÂtryÃÂ to talk to customers interested in hand-tufted rugs about the problem (of the latex breaking down and the rugs falling apart in six years or less) before they purchase them. She added that she has seen so many of these rugs fail that she doesnÃÂt understand ÃÂhow these rugs are allowed to be sold in the U.S.ÃÂ and questioned ÃÂwhy someone doesnÃÂt do something about regulating the process.ÃÂ At the time I bought the rug, however, this salesperson did not have that conversation with me so I was unable to make an informed decision about the rug.  

 I'd like to know if you have any information about any possible short or long-term health effects that can come from exposure to these rugs.
justification: The incident describes potential health hazards from a rug's chemical breakdown, with reported respiratory issues but no confirmed severe injury or death.

They gave me several numbers to call to report this to Coleman.  No one cared!  We had to have this furnace removed and when the technician pulled out the Coleman furnace they discovered that a large hole had been burned through our sheetrock wall in our home.  The furnace had a large break in the metal and was burned throughout that area.  The repairman said we shouuld report this because this is EXACTLY what the recalled furnances had happen in all the other circumstances.

We had to have a new furnace installed by Dales Heating in Pine City and they said they would be willing to confirm what I have just reported.  

We feel Coleman should reimburse us for this faulty furnace and they should add this Model number to their recall list.

Please try to help us in this matter.  Thank you so much for anything you can do.

incident_description:
Zinsco/Sylvania circuit breakers installed in a breaker panel outdoors ignited and caused burns to the breakers and burned a hole through the breaker buss bar.  Lights within the house began to dim and flicker, devices in some rooms shut off, then all power to the house was lost.

The fire wasn't immediately noticeable when opening the panel door due to the cover plate, so I attempted to reset the breaker by moving the switch to the open position (Off) since it had not tripped yet.  Then I switched it back to the closed (On) position and still did not see power restored to the house.  Sparks were visible towards the back of the panel through a very small gap between the breaker front and the cover panel so I immediately switched the main breaker back to Open (Off) and left it that way.

Upon removing the old circuit breakers from the buss bar, burns were visible on the main breaker (100 amp) and several other breakers.  On a few areas of the buss bar, holes were burned through the metal where the breakers previously were.  On other areas of the buss bar, the contact points from the breakers appear to be electrically welded on due to electrical arcing (the welded points breaking apart from the breakers when trying to remove them).  It appears that the deterioration of the breakers happened over the course of many years and was not a single incident.

Looking at the front of the breakers, no damage is visible and the breakers appear to be in new condition, so the severe damage is only noticeable by removing the breakers.  Even when the face plate is removed the damage is not visible, so the very poor condition of the breakers was missed during a recent home inspection.

Fortunately there was no fire damage to the breaker box itself or the side of the house.
justification: The incident caused damage to the breakers and buss bar but no injuries or fire damage to the house, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of deterioration over many years.

Upon return, smelled something hot, traced it to the washing machine, assumed it was a belt slipping since that what it smelled like.  Opened the washing machine and found that a sheet had actually burned.  Some of the surrounding material melted to the tub.  I removed the clothes and unplugged the unit.  Today learned that there had been a recall.  Have scheduled a service call for next week.
justification: The incident involved a burning sheet and melted material, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The Wall Heater overheated and caught fire.  Damaged limited to heating unit due to prompt smoke alarm activation.
justification: The heater caught fire but damage was limited to the unit itself with no reported injuries.

incident_description: I was using a replacement Lysol Steam Cleaning Mop sent to me by the Conair Corp. due to the first recall. The replacement mop was model SM10LR. I was using the mop according to the guidelines and all of a sudden about five to eight minutes into using the mop it erupted. The top was blown off and the rubber water plug was blown out. Hot water sprayed to the ceiling and covered everything in front of where the mop was pointing. I have incurred slight irritation on my left wrist due to the steam.
justification: The incident caused slight irritation on the wrist due to steam, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as it's a specific issue with a recalled product.

incident_description:
Router threw a bit from the collet while in use. 

Porter Cable 8902 Router.  Mounted in a router table.  New.  First use.
Collet : 1/4 inch.

Bit was thrown up and out of the collet while cutting at mid RPM setting.

Examination of the collet showed a manufacturing defect.  2 Webs prevented the collet from closing symmetrically.  The nature of the defect, insufficient depth on a machining cut, suggests a batch of defective collets.   I have pictures of the defect and as of this date, I still have the collet. 

Upon inspection before use, the bit seemed to be firmly seated.
Presumably, vibration while cutting caused the bit to climb out of the collet.  

I reported the problem to Porter Cable immediately.

The bit was contained by the top safety guard.  No injury resulted.  Damage was limited to the guard, the bit shaft and the wood.

If this had been used in a router base, the result would have been a bit thrown free of the router at several thousand RPM.
justification: The incident involved a router bit being thrown due to a manufacturing defect, but no injury occurred as the safety guard contained the bit.

incident_description: Short circuit caused fire below the controls of the heater.  Flame could be seen inside the vent of the device.  Had only been on 30 minutes.  Have owned heater less than two years.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the heater is relatively new and the issue arose quickly.

incident_description:
I've owned both the First Alert "OneLink" Smoke Detectors and "OneLink" Carbon Monoxide Detectors for about 5-6 years now and I've always had problems with the batteries draining very rapidly after replacing (about 2 months +/-).  I've also have had occasional false alarms triggered (always late at night).  Finally after another false alarm tonight, I searched the web for any known problems with my units and found the U.S. C.P.S.C. recall information for both the model of my smoke detectors as well as my carbon-monoxide detector.  I went to First Alert's website, as directed by the CPSC and was surprised to find the following statement that I believe is a false claim (cut and pasted directly from First Alert's FAQ page):

First AlertÃÂ© manufactures our carbon monoxide alarms to exacting standards and rigorously tests each of our safety products. There has never been a First AlertÃÂ© carbon monoxide detector recall.

Here is the link to that page:  http://www.firstalert.com/faqs/co-alarm/has-there-ever-been-a-first-alert-carbon-monoxide-alarm-recall
